venues.longDescription:
Aguasal by Jose Andres opened in June 2025 inside the Andaz Miami Beach in Mid-Beach, the first stage of the Jose Andres Group taking over dining at the oceanfront resort. The name comes from agua salada — saltwater — and the all-day coastal Mediterranean menu draws on Mallorca and Mykonos, running Kumamoto oysters, mussels saganaki and whole snapper served indoors or on the terrace, steps from the sand on Collins Avenue.

Hotel restaurants are usually where alcohol-free drinks are handled worst: the guest is presumed to be on holiday and therefore drinking, and the list defaults to a frozen cocktail and a soda. Aguasal keeps the selection small but deliberate, and the construction is what distinguishes it. The Cardamom & Ginger works cardamom and citrus with sakura and ginger beer. The Mediterranean Milk Punch is a lavender-cardamom tea with pomegranate, fenugreek and mint, dairy-clarified — a technique that takes days and produces a silky, translucent drink, and one almost nobody attempts for a non-alcoholic menu.

Athletic Brewing's Free Wave hazy IPA covers beer, with fresh juices, Per'la coffee and Art of Tea infusions filling the rest of the day. A separate upstairs bar, Bar Centro, extends the group's spirit-free options.

The Greater Miami Convention & Visitors Bureau described the mocktails as Mediterranean-inspired and feeling intentional and refined, which is the right word — two drinks made properly beats eight made carelessly, and a clarified milk punch on a resort menu is a decision rather than an accident.

It is a full-service restaurant with a bar and resort pricing, not an alcohol-free venue. Being inside a hotel means it is open all day, which makes it one of the more usable Mid-Beach options for a lunch or a coffee rather than only a dinner.
venues.pressQuote: Mediterranean-inspired mocktails that feel intentional and refined

venues.name: Albert's Schloss
venues.description: Albert's Schloss is a cavernous Bavarian bierkeller and cook-haus on the ground floor of Manchester's Grade II-listed Albert Hall, pouring tank-fresh European lager beneath near-constant live music, cabaret and its trademark 'Bongdays'. It is no dedicated sober bar, but it is genuinely well-versed in low and no: the fridges hold alcohol-free Paulaner Hefe Weisse and Jever Fun, alongside Hip Pop kombucha and a small named 'No Alk' list of spirit-free cocktails built on Lyre's. Open daily from 9am until 2am, it is a rare big-room party venue where a non-drinker is properly looked after rather than handed a lemonade.
signatureDrinks: 'Not an Amaretto Sour' (Lyre's Amaretti, gomme, lemon, aquafaba)
venues.longDescription:
Albert's Schloss opened in 2015 in the Grade II-listed Albert Hall building on Peter Street, the debut venue of Mission Mars — the group founded by Revolution's Roy Ellis and Neil Macleod alongside the Trof team behind The Deaf Institute and Gorilla. Modelled on an alpine Schloss, or castle, it is an enormous, theatrical 'cook-haus' where long communal tables and timber benches sit beneath chandeliers and a stage that runs a near-constant programme of house bands, cabaret, drag brunches and the venue's own 'Bongdays'. It trades from 9am breakfast through to a 2am close every day, and the format has since been rolled out to Birmingham, Liverpool and London.

For a venue built on tank-fresh Bavarian lager, the low-and-no offer is more considered than most beer halls bother with. Manchester Confidential singles it out — 'Albert's Schloss is well-versed in this area too, stocking bottles of Paulaner Hefe Weisse and the German Pilsner Jever Fun' — pairing an alcohol-free Bavarian wheat beer with Jever's crisp alcohol-free north-German pilsner. Beyond the beer fridge the bar pours Hip Pop kombucha (the Manchester brand formerly known as Booch & Brew) and keeps a dedicated 'No Alk' section on the cocktail list: a No-garita, a virgin mojito and a 'not an amaretto sour' shaken from Lyre's Amaretti, gomme, lemon and aquafaba, with spirit-free spritzes rotating on to the seasonal Sommerhaus menu.

The result is a proper night out that doesn't hinge on drinking. It won't rival a dedicated alcohol-free bar for range, but between the two credible AF beers, the kombucha and the shaken zero-proof cocktails, a non-drinker can settle in for the full bierkeller experience — schnitzel, giant pretzels and a front-row seat for the cabaret — without compromise. You'll find it a couple of minutes from Deansgate and St Peter's Square, at 27 Peter Street.
venues.pressQuote: Albert's Schloss is well-versed in this area too, stocking bottles of Paulaner Hefe Weisse and the German Pilsner Jever Fun.

venues.name: Alcove
venues.description: Alcove is a waterfront restaurant and bar at 50 Lovejoy Wharf in Boston's West End, a few steps from TD Garden and North Station, with a patio on the Charles River that is one of the few genuinely water-facing terraces in the neighbourhood. The kitchen runs a coastal New England menu of line-caught seafood, farm vegetables and locally sourced meats alongside an extensive wine list. The drinks menu prints a named spirit-free section holding five drinks between $11 and $13 — roughly half the price of the house cocktails — including a shandy built on Athletic Brewing's Free Wave non-alcoholic IPA that can be ordered in pitchers for four. Two non-alcoholic beers are stocked at $7.
signatureDrinks: Ginger Shandy (lemon, Athletic Brewing Free Wave NA IPA — pitchers for 4 available)
venues.longDescription:
Alcove occupies the ground floor of 50 Lovejoy Wharf in the West End, directly beside TD Garden and North Station, and is one of the few restaurants in that stretch of the city with a genuine waterfront patio rather than a street-facing terrace — the deck looks out over the Charles at the point where it meets the harbour, which makes it a pre- and post-event room for the Garden as well as a neighbourhood restaurant. The kitchen describes its cooking as coastal New England, working through line-caught seafood, farm-fresh vegetables and locally sourced meats, and the wine programme is substantial enough that the restaurant bottles a Pierre Ferrand cognac under an Alcove Series label for its own cocktails. The Boston Globe included Alcove in its January 7, 2025 round-up of twelve spectacular spots for mocktails, singling out the price point and the use of non-alcoholic beer in the builds.

The alcohol-free drinks are printed on the cocktail page under a spirit free heading rather than tucked at the back, and they are priced at $11 to $13 against $16 to $19 for the full-strength list. Queen's Bee is the cheapest at $11, a light build of botanicals, honey and lemon. The Spiced Tamarind Margarita is $13, using tajin, orange and ginger, and is the most assertive of the group. Ginger Shandy at $13 is the one worth knowing about: it combines lemon with Athletic Brewing's Free Wave non-alcoholic hazy IPA, and can be ordered in pitchers for four, which is unusual — most restaurants will not commit a shared format to an alcohol-free drink. The kitchen also files a Lucano Libre at $13 under that same spirit-free heading, but it is built on Amaro Lucano, an Italian amaro of roughly 28% ABV, so it is not an alcohol-free drink despite where it sits on the menu — worth knowing before ordering from that section. A genuinely spirit-free Raspberry Lemonade is listed at $11 among the frozen and specialty summer sips. Behind the cocktails, two non-alcoholic beers are stocked at $7 each: Athletic Brewing's Free Wave from San Diego and Best Day Brewing's Kolsch from Sausalito, both at 0.5% ABV. Alcove opens at noon on weekdays and 11am at weekends, running to 10pm daily.
venues.pressQuote: In the West End, cozy Alcove does an $11 mocktail menu with unusual offerings like Papi's Punch, with grilled pineapple syrup and Athletic Free Wave nonalcoholic IPA, or a Queen's Bee, made with the herbaceous nonalcoholic spirit Garden 108 and honey.

venues.name: Alden & Harlow
venues.description: Alden & Harlow is chef-owner Michael Scelfo's New American restaurant at 40 Brattle Street in Harvard Square, opened in 2014 in a basement space and known for a vegetable-forward, small-plates menu and an off-menu burger that has drawn national attention. Scelfo also runs The Longfellow Bar upstairs in the same building. The bar keeps a printed Mocktails section of three house drinks, priced $9 to $10, built from the kitchen's own techniques rather than from bought-in zero-proof spirits: cold-smoked passionfruit, ube coconut water, lapsang souchong and a non-alcoholic Giffard aperitif all appear. The result is savoury and smoke-inflected rather than sweet, and reads as an extension of the kitchen rather than a bar afterthought.

venues.longDescription:
Alden & Harlow opened in 2014 at 40 Brattle Street in Harvard Square, in the below-street space that had long housed Casablanca, and made its reputation on chef-owner Michael Scelfo's vegetable-forward small plates at a moment when that was still unusual — the Wall Street Journal cited the restaurant in an October 2014 piece on modern menus shifting focus to vegetables, and its burger has been written up repeatedly as one of the country's notable off-menu orders. Scelfo has since added The Longfellow Bar upstairs in the same building, and the two operations share an address and a kitchen sensibility. The restaurant serves dinner nightly and brunch at weekends. Meet Boston's January 2026 zero-proof guide observed that Alden & Harlow approaches zero-proof beverages from a culinary perspective, with drinks that incorporate both sweet and savoury elements, roasted or herbal notes and layered acidity, sometimes pulling inspiration directly from the kitchen.

That description is borne out by the printed Mocktails section, which runs three house drinks and avoids the standard route of substituting a commercial zero-proof gin into a classic template. Soft Light is $10 and combines ube coconut water with ginger, lime and pineapple soda — nutty, faintly earthy from the purple yam, and the mildest of the three. Golden Smoke is $9 and is the one that best demonstrates the kitchen influence: the passionfruit is cold-smoked before it goes into the glass, then lengthened with honey, lemon, tonic and soda, so the drink carries a smoke note that non-alcoholic drinks usually cannot reach without a spirit. Mocking Bird is $10 and the most bitter and structured of the set, built on lapsang souchong tea with Giffard non-alcoholic aperitif, mango, lime and demerara. All three sit at roughly half the price of the restaurant's full-strength cocktails, and all three are listed on the same menu rather than requiring a request. The list rotates with the seasons alongside the food, so specific drinks change; what persists is the method of building them from tea, smoke, roasted fruit and vinegar rather than from bought-in substitutes.
venues.pressQuote: Alden & Harlow approaches zero-proof beverages from a culinary perspective.

venues.name: AleSmith Brewing Company
venues.description: AleSmith Brewing Company, founded in 1995 and owned since 2002 by Peter Zien, is one of San Diego's flagship craft breweries. Its large Miramar tasting room — a two-story space with a patio, games, and a Tony Gwynn memorabilia museum — pours the brewery's own house-brewed non-alcoholic line alongside its full beer lineup. The NA program centers on AleSmith NA IPA (tangerine and pine, under 0.5% ABV, 75 calories) and NA Speedway, a non-alcoholic take on the brewery's iconic Speedway Stout with dark chocolate, espresso, and roasted-malt notes, plus a Nelson Sauvin hop water on tap — a zero-proof, zero-calorie option. The NA IPA has earned real recognition, taking medals at the California Craft Brewers Cup and the San Diego Beer News Awards.
venues.longDescription:
AleSmith Brewing Company was founded in 1995 and has been owned since 2002 by Peter Zien, making it one of the genuine flagships of San Diego craft beer — a city that has as strong a claim as anywhere in America to having defined the modern IPA. The Miramar tasting room is a two-storey space with a patio, games and a Tony Gwynn memorabilia museum, the last of which reflects the brewery's long association with the late Padres great and his .394 pale ale.

What makes it useful here is that the non-alcoholic beer is brewed in-house rather than bought in, and it is treated as part of the range rather than as a concession. The line centres on AleSmith NA IPA — tangerine and pine, under 0.5% ABV, 75 calories — and NA Speedway, a non-alcoholic version of the brewery's iconic Speedway Stout carrying dark chocolate, espresso and roasted-malt character. That second one matters disproportionately: non-alcoholic stouts are far rarer than non-alcoholic IPAs, because the roasted malt body is harder to hold together without alcohol, and a brewery of this stature producing one gives non-drinkers access to a style they are usually shut out of entirely. There is also a Nelson Sauvin hop water on tap, which is zero-proof and zero-calorie, offering the hop aroma without the beer. The NA IPA has taken medals at both the California Craft Brewers Cup and the San Diego Beer News Awards, judged against the field rather than in a separate category. For anyone doing a San Diego brewery tour without drinking, this is the stop where you are least likely to be handed a soda and least likely to feel like an afterthought. Open daily, to 11pm at the weekend. Miramar is San Diego's brewing heartland, with dozens of taprooms within a few miles, so a designated driver ferrying a group around the area has a specific reason to make this the stop where they get to drink something they actually chose.

venues.name: Alexxa's
venues.description: Alexxa's is a modern Italian-inspired steakhouse and bar at Paris Las Vegas, set on a Strip-side balcony overlooking Las Vegas Boulevard and best known locally for its long weekend brunch service. Its drinks list carries a standing, clearly labelled Zero-Proof section rather than a single token option, and it is one of the deeper spirit-free lists on the Strip: the Zero Royal (Lucano N/A amaro, pomegranate juice, Owen's ginger beer, lime juice), the Flora Botanica (Seedlip Grove 42, grapefruit juice, tart cherry syrup, lime juice), the St. Zita Spritz (Giffard N/A aperitif, non-alcoholic sparkling wine, soda, orange), and a Michenada built on Athletic Brewing's Atletica with michelada mix. Athletic Brewing's Free Wave hazy IPA and Atletica pour alongside them, and the same section carries a matcha green tea latte, freshly squeezed orange juice, the Garden Glow cold-pressed juice (apple, celery, cucumber, spinach, kale, parsley, ginger, lemon) and Ghirardelli hot chocolate. The restaurant serves from 7am daily through to 10pm, and to 11pm on Friday and Saturday.

venues.longDescription:
Alexxa's sits on a balcony at Paris Las Vegas, directly over Las Vegas Boulevard, which gives it one of the better Strip-side vantage points on the block and explains why its weekend brunch has become the thing it is known for. The kitchen is a modern Italian-inspired steakhouse: pizzas and pastas, omelettes and brunch plates in the morning, steaks and seasonal entrees at night, served across an indoor dining room and the open-air patio. Service starts at 7am every day and runs to 10pm, extending to 11pm on Friday and Saturday, which makes it one of the few rooms on this stretch of the Strip that will serve you a properly made drink across that whole span of the day.

What earns it a place here is the drinks menu, which carries a standing section headed Zero-Proof rather than burying a couple of juices at the foot of the cocktail list. It is one of the more thoroughly built spirit-free lists on the Strip, and it uses real non-alcoholic products rather than sweetened substitutes. The Zero Royal combines Lucano N/A amaro with pomegranate juice, Owen's ginger beer and lime; the Flora Botanica is built on Seedlip Grove 42 with grapefruit juice, tart cherry syrup and lime; the St. Zita Spritz uses Giffard's non-alcoholic aperitif with non-alcoholic sparkling wine, soda and orange, which puts a credible spritz in front of someone who is not drinking; and the Michenada is a michelada built on Athletic Brewing's Atletica. The same section carries Athletic Brewing's Free Wave hazy IPA and Atletica by the can, a matcha green tea latte, freshly squeezed orange juice, a Garden Glow cold-pressed juice of apple, celery, cucumber, spinach, kale, parsley, ginger and lemon, and Ghirardelli hot chocolate with marshmallows. The breadth matters as much as the quality: a guest at a long brunch can order four different things across two hours without repeating themselves or reaching for a soda.

venues.name: Alibaba Lounge & Kava Bar
venues.description: Alibaba is an alcohol-free lounge and cafe on Linebaugh Avenue that pairs a hookah programme with fruit-infused kava and an organic wellness drink list, open from noon to midnight and to 2am on Friday and Saturday. It is worth being clear about the balance: this is a hookah lounge first, and the kava is genuine but sits alongside that rather than at the centre. For anyone avoiding alcohol who wants a late, social, dressed-up room, it works — the space is clean and carefully arranged, the music is good and Thursday is Ladies Night. For anyone avoiding smoke, it will not, since hookah is the main draw and the room is not smoke-free. No alcohol is served at any point.
venues.longDescription:
Alibaba is an alcohol-free lounge and cafe on Linebaugh Avenue in Carrollwood, open from noon to midnight and to 2am on Friday and Saturday, pairing a hookah programme with fruit-infused kava and an organic wellness drink list. It is worth being straightforward about the balance, because the name puts kava second and the business puts it second too: this is a hookah lounge first, and the kava is genuine but sits alongside that rather than at the centre of it.

For a certain reader that makes it exactly right. If what you want is a late, social, dressed-up room where nobody is drinking and the evening has some ceremony to it, Alibaba delivers that. The space is clean and carefully arranged, the music is good, Thursday is Ladies Night with half-price hookah, and the venue runs an events programme through the week. It serves no alcohol at any point, which in a category of hookah lounges is not a given.

For a different reader it is entirely wrong, and the reason has nothing to do with alcohol. The room is not smoke-free, and hookah is the main draw. Anyone avoiding tobacco and smoke — including a large share of people who have given up smoking alongside drinking, and anyone with a respiratory condition — should treat that as disqualifying rather than as a detail. This directory would rather say that plainly than have someone discover it after driving across the city.

On the kava itself: it is the ground root of Piper methysticum, a shrub native to the South Pacific islands, prepared as a cold water infusion and drunk socially across Fiji, Vanuatu, Tonga and Samoa for roughly three thousand years. It contains no alcohol. It tastes earthy and bitter, numbs the lips and tongue on the first mouthful, and is mildly sedative rather than intoxicating in the way alcohol is. Alibaba serves it fruit-infused, which is a reasonable way to introduce it to people who have not had it before — the bitterness is the main barrier for most first-timers.

Carrollwood is a residential quadrant of north Tampa, and Alibaba sits close to Ritual Kava Lounge on Dale Mabry, giving the neighbourhood two very different alcohol-free rooms within a few minutes of each other. Ritual is the one built around games and community programming; Alibaba is the one built around a night out with some occasion to it. Which of the two suits you depends almost entirely on how you feel about smoke.

venues.name: All Purpose Pizzeria (Shaw)
venues.description: All Purpose Pizzeria is an Italian-American restaurant at 1250 9th Street NW in Shaw, opened in 2016 by chef Michael Friedman, also behind The Red Hen, and known for crunchy Jersey-style pizza, house-made charcuterie and red-sauce classics. The Shaw original anchors a small group that also includes a Capitol Riverfront outpost near Navy Yard. In January 2025 the restaurant added a dedicated dry cocktail menu at both locations, moving its non-alcoholic offer well beyond the usual sodas. The two named spirit-free drinks are The Golden Boot, made with pineapple juice, basil, lemon juice and soda, and the Positano Punch, built from pomegranate and apple with rosemary simple syrup and grapefruit bitters. It is a lively, social room that hosts a popular weekend drag brunch, and it was named to Washingtonian's 100 Very Best Restaurants 2025 at number 69.
venues.longDescription:
All Purpose opened in Shaw in 2016 from chef Michael Friedman, whose other restaurant, The Red Hen, had already established him in the city. The pizza is Jersey-style - thin, crunchy at the edge, closer to a bar pie than a Neapolitan - and it comes alongside house-made charcuterie and red-sauce classics in a room built to be loud and social rather than reverent. The Shaw original at 1250 9th Street NW anchors a small group that also includes a Capitol Riverfront outpost near Navy Yard. It earned early acclaim from the Washington Post after its debut and was named to Washingtonian's 100 Very Best Restaurants 2025 at number 69.

The reason it appears here dates from January 2025, when All Purpose introduced a dedicated dry cocktail menu at both locations - a real menu rather than an expanded soda list. Resy noted the launch in its roundup of DC bars with superb zero-proof cocktails. Two named drinks anchor it. The Golden Boot is built on pineapple juice with basil, lemon juice and soda, which gives it a herbal edge that cuts through pizza in the way a spritz would. The Positano Punch is the more constructed of the pair: pomegranate and apple with rosemary simple syrup and grapefruit bitters, and the bitters are what stop it reading as a soft drink. Both are priced and served as cocktails rather than as an afterthought, which is the practical difference for a table where one person is not drinking.

What makes the room genuinely useful for non-drinkers is the format. This is a pizzeria with a weekend drag brunch and a consistently busy dining room, so the social occasion does not depend on the bar. Practical notes: dinner starts at 5pm every day, running to 9pm on Monday, 10pm Tuesday through Thursday, 11pm on Friday and Saturday and 9pm on Sunday, with weekend brunch from 11am to 2.30pm. It sits a short walk from Mount Vernon Square and Shaw Metro stations, and Blagden Alley is around the corner if the evening continues.
venues.pressQuote: All Purpose debuted a new dry cocktail menu at both its Shaw and Capitol Riverfront locations this month
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Resy, 10 Washington, D.C. Bars With Superb Zero-Proof Cocktails, January 2025

venues.name: Alley Brews
venues.description: Alley Brews is a small women-owned brewery and coffee shop hidden in the alley between Tennyson and Stuart Streets in Berkeley, taken over at the end of June 2025 by longtime friends Liz Hess and Chelsea Rhoads — Rhoads helped open 4 Noses Brewing in 2014 — who rebranded it from Berkeley Alley Beer Company. The room is designed to work all day: coffee and matcha from the morning, small-batch beer and draft cocktails later, and a stated non-alcoholic line of "non-alcoholic beers, kombucha, coffee, matcha & in-house crafted mocktails". Rhoads told Westword in October 2025 that entire groups had been drinking N/A beer on a Sunday and that there was no stigma around it. Gluten-free brews are also part of the standing offer.
venues.longDescription:
Alley Brews is genuinely hidden — the entrance is off the alley between 43rd and 44th, behind Ohana Yoga, rather than on Tennyson Street itself, at 4342 Tennyson in Berkeley. Longtime friends and industry veterans Liz Hess and Chelsea Rhoads took over the site at the end of June 2025, acquiring what had been Berkeley Alley Beer Company and rebranding it. Rhoads brought serious brewing credentials to the deal, having helped open 4 Noses Brewing Company in 2014. Westword covered the takeover in October 2025 under a headline calling it a tiny Berkeley brewery setting a big example for success, noting how much the pair had changed in a few months.

What makes the room relevant here is that it was rebuilt as an all-day space rather than as a taproom with coffee bolted on. The business describes itself as a place where "beer, coffee, food, and non-alcoholic options all share the spotlight", and lists its zero-proof offering plainly: "Non-alcoholic beers, kombucha, coffee, matcha & in-house crafted mocktails", under the heading "Not drinking? No worries." The house beers cover classic and modern styles — Pucker Nuts, a bright tart ale at 3.3 percent that Westword picked out for packing flavour at low strength; Golden Hour, a cream ale; Sun Drip, a hazy IPA; and Black Dog, a dry Irish-style stout served on nitro — and gluten-free brews are a standing part of the list rather than an occasional guest. The owners have been explicit that the non-alcoholic side is a real part of trade, not a gesture: "We had different groups on Sunday, and everyone was drinking N/A beer," Rhoads told Westword, adding, "There isn't a stigma around it." The venue opens at 8:30am and runs to 9pm on weeknights and 10pm at weekends, and has plans to extend the morning offer further with cold foam flights, matcha tea flights and breakfast burritos. It regularly hosts remote workers who want good coffee, solid WiFi and a space that will not move them along.
venues.pressQuote: We had different groups on Sunday, and everyone was drinking N/A beer. There isn't a stigma around it.

venues.name: Alley Cat Lounge
venues.description: Alley Cat Lounge is a basement cocktail bar reached from Broughton Lane, the service alley behind Savannah's main shopping street, in an 1870s brick cellar. Its menu is a newsprint broadsheet — the Alley Cat Rag — reissued in numbered editions with the whole list rewritten each time, and the bar's standing commitment is that whatever the edition, it carries a minimum of ten low- and no-alcohol cocktails alongside alcohol-free beer and cider. That is the deepest running alcohol-free selection of any licensed bar in the city. It is open from 4pm to 1am Monday through Thursday, to 2am on Friday and Saturday, and closed Sundays.
venues.longDescription:
Broughton Lane is the alley that runs behind Broughton Street, and Alley Cat Lounge is down a stair off it, in a brick cellar dating to the 1870s. The room is small, dim and built for drinking rather than dining, and it has spent years as the reference point for craft cocktails in Savannah — house-made syrups, sodas, teas and infusions rather than bought mixers, and bartenders with a reputation that travels beyond the city.

The menu is genuinely unusual. It is printed as a newspaper, the Alley Cat Rag, issued in numbered editions and rewritten wholesale each time rather than tweaked at the edges. That rotation is why this listing records no signature drinks: any specific name would be wrong within months, and the bar's own format tells you so. What survives every edition is the commitment underneath it. A drinker can always find at least ten low- and no-alcohol cocktails on the Rag, plus alcohol-free beer and cider — a standing floor rather than a token pair of drinks, and by some distance the deepest running alcohol-free selection at any licensed bar in Savannah.

The bar's own staff frame it as a matter of craft rather than accommodation. Bartender Dheeraj Chatlani, quoted by Savannah Magazine in its survey of the city's mocktail trend, said he liked that the non-alcoholic options at Alley Cat were as enjoyable and thoughtfully made as anything else on the menu — which is the argument this whole category rests on, made by someone who has to execute it on a Friday night.

Practical notes: the entrance is genuinely hard to find the first time, and the bar keeps late hours — 4pm to 1am on weeknights and 2am on Friday and Saturday — but is closed all day Sunday.
venues.pressQuote: I love that our nonalcoholic options at Alley Cat are as equally enjoyable and thoughtfully crafted as anything else you'll find on the menu.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Dheeraj Chatlani, bartender, Alley Cat Lounge
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Savannah Magazine, The Buzz on the Growing Mocktail Trend

venues.name: Alley Cat Oyster Bar
venues.description: Alley Cat Oyster Bar is a waterfront seafood restaurant on Old River Road in the Flats East Bank, pairing New England coastal cooking with a Southern Californian lightness and panoramic views over the Cuyahoga. Its mocktails are shaken and built to order rather than pulled off a soda gun, and they are priced deliberately low: the Kitten's Pajamas, a spirit-free take on a classic bubbly lemonade served in strawberry-jalapeño or blueberry-basil, costs $6 — less than half what most composed zero-proof drinks run in the city. It opens at 11:30am Wednesday through Sunday.

venues.longDescription:
Alley Cat Oyster Bar sits on Old River Road in the Flats East Bank, the redeveloped stretch of Cuyahoga riverfront in downtown Cleveland, and is that neighbourhood's seafood room: a raw bar of oysters and shellfish, New England coastal comfort food, and a Southern Californian lightness in the cooking that suits the setting. The restaurant describes itself as having the finesse and beauty of the Cleveland shore, and the river views are why most people book — in summer the outdoor seating runs the length of the building and the whole place turns into a patio.

The non-alcoholic drinks are worth calling out for two separate reasons. The first is care: Cleveland Magazine's 2026 mocktail roundup noted that the team gives them detailed attention, crafting bubbly sips that fit the breezy vibe, and the drinks are shaken and built to order rather than dispensed. The second is price. The Kitten's Pajamas — a spirit-free take on a classic bubbly lemonade, served in either strawberry-jalapeño or blueberry-basil — costs $6, which is less than half what most of the city's composed mocktails run and materially cheaper than the restaurant's own cocktails. That matters more than it sounds: one of the most persistent complaints about zero-proof menus is being charged cocktail money for juice, and Alley Cat is one of very few places in Cleveland where the non-drinking guest is not quietly penalised for the choice.

The kitchen opens at 11:30am Wednesday through Sunday, with a happy hour from 3pm on weekdays, so this is a genuine afternoon option in a part of downtown that otherwise only comes alive at night. For anyone visiting Cleveland and staying downtown, it is the easiest walk-to entry on this list.
venues.pressQuote: The team gives mocktails detailed attention, crafting bubbly sips that fit the breezy vibe.

venues.name: Alley Twenty Six
venues.description: Alley Twenty Six is downtown Durham's serious cocktail bar, on East Chapel Hill Street, and its non-alcoholic list is developed with the same discipline as the alcoholic one. Owner Shannon Healy and his bartenders hold experimental sessions on Thursday mornings building syrups and tinctures specifically for zero-proof drinks, and the bar keeps around twenty house-made tonics that underpin both sides of the menu — the same blood orange or cinchona-bittered tonic that sharpens a gin drink gives a zero-proof build its backbone. The current "Non-Alcohol" section runs four builds, two of them tea-based, and is refreshed seasonally; Best Day Brewing's non-alcoholic Kölsch and hazy IPA sit alongside. Discover Durham credits it with non-alcoholic cocktails with layers of flavour, house-made syrups and real presentation. Open Tuesday to Sunday from four until midnight.
venues.address: 320 E Chapel Hill St Ste 200, Durham, NC 27701
signatureDrinks: Starry Eyed Fig — local garden figs, soda, sugar, champagne acid, lemon
Sunset Sipper — lime, Alley Twenty Six tonic and blood orange syrups, soda
Earl Please — Earl Grey tea, passionfruit, ginger, lime
Conch Shell — rooibos tea, blackberry, rosemary, lime, balsamic

naMenuItems.name: Best Day Brewing N/A Hazy IPA

venues.longDescription:
Alley Twenty Six has been downtown Durham's benchmark cocktail bar for years, and it is one of the few in the region where the non-alcoholic list is a product of the same development process as the rest of the menu rather than an afterthought bolted on for Dry January. The bar runs experimental sessions on Thursday mornings — owner Shannon Healy and his bartenders building new syrups, tinctures and cordials specifically for zero-proof drinks, and holding them to the standard they would apply to anything with spirit in it.

The infrastructure behind that is the tonic programme. The bar makes around twenty house tonics, and they serve both sides of the list: the same blood orange or cinchona-bittered tonic that sharpens a gin drink also gives a non-alcoholic build the backbone it would otherwise be missing. This is the technical answer to the usual complaint about zero-proof cocktails, which is that they taste like juice. Bitterness, acid and tannin have to come from somewhere, and here they come from house production rather than a bottle of syrup.

The current section is headed simply "Non-Alcohol" and runs four drinks. Starry Eyed Fig uses figs from local gardens with champagne acid and lemon over soda. The Sunset Sipper is built on two of the house syrups — the bar's own tonic and blood orange — with lime and soda. Earl Please and Conch Shell are both tea-based, the first on Earl Grey with passionfruit, ginger and lime, the second on rooibos with blackberry, rosemary, lime and a line of balsamic that does the work bitters would normally do.

The list is refreshed seasonally, so what is pouring on any given visit will move. It is worth noting that several published Triangle round-ups still credit this bar with a booze-free hot toddy and a drink called "No Thanks, I'm Driving"; neither is on the current menu. Read the list when you arrive rather than the article that sent you.
venues.pressQuote: non-alcoholic cocktails with layers of flavor, house-made syrups, fresh ingredients and presentations

venues.name: ALO Cafe Hawaii
venues.description: ALO Cafe Hawaii is a plant-based café that opened in Waikīkī in 2021 and has since added rooms in Kakaʻako and downtown. It serves no alcohol. The drinks list is the substantial part of the business rather than a sideline to the food: matcha built to order including the house Aloha Matcha Latte, smoothies made with fresh organic fruit, and cold drinks served alongside açaí bowls and a plant-focused menu. The Waikīkī room on Kaiulani Avenue opens daily from 7am to 7pm, which makes it one of the few genuinely alcohol-free options inside Waikīkī itself — a district otherwise dominated by hotel bars and resort restaurants where a non-drinker is always ordering around the menu.
venues.longDescription:
ALO Cafe Hawaii started in Waikīkī in 2021 as a plant-focused café and has since grown to three Honolulu locations: the original at 159 Kaiulani Avenue, a Kakaʻako room on Auahi Street, and a downtown site on Bishop Street. Nothing on the premises contains alcohol. The menu is built around açaí bowls, smoothies and plant-based plates, with the drinks given more attention than the format usually implies — matcha is whisked to order rather than poured from a pre-mixed bottle, the smoothies use fresh organic fruit, and the house Aloha Matcha Latte is the drink the café is best known for.

Its value in this guide is largely geographic. Waikīkī is where most visitors to Oʻahu actually stay, and it is close to the worst-served district on the island for anyone not drinking: the beachfront is wall-to-wall hotel bars and resort restaurants, where the non-alcoholic option is typically a pineapple juice with an umbrella in it and the price of a cocktail. Of the twenty venues in this guide, only three sit inside Waikīkī proper with anything resembling a real non-alcoholic drinks list, and ALO Cafe is the only one of those where alcohol is absent altogether. That makes it a practical daytime anchor — somewhere to start a morning or break an afternoon without negotiating a bar. The trade-off is the obvious one: this is a café, and it closes at 7pm. It does not replace an evening out, and nobody should arrive expecting a zero-proof cocktail programme. What it offers is a room in the middle of the most tourist-dense square mile in Hawaiʻi where a person who does not drink orders exactly like everybody else in the queue, which in Waikīkī is rarer than it should be.

venues.name: Alo Restaurant
venues.description: Alo is a Michelin-starred blind tasting-menu restaurant on the third floor of a heritage building at Spadina Avenue and Queen Street West, on the edge of Toronto's Chinatown and Queen West. Its own reservations page states the kitchen offers "a refined non-alcoholic pairing" as a standing alternative to its wine pairing across both the six- and ten-course tasting menus, built to deliver "the same level of creativity and balance." A June 2026 review documented that pairing in practice: guests are offered a choice of Champagne or a welcome pour of sparkling Saicho hojicha, a single-origin roasted green tea served chilled and lightly fizzy.
venues.address: 163 Spadina Avenue, 3rd Floor, Toronto, ON M5V 2L6, Canada
signatureDrinks: Sparkling Saicho Hojicha — single-origin roasted green tea (sparkling, non-alcoholic), served as the welcome-drink alternative to Champagne
venues.longDescription:
Alo occupies the third floor of a heritage building at 163 Spadina Avenue, at the southeast corner of Spadina and Queen Street West — an address local write-ups file under Chinatown even though the block borders Queen West and the Entertainment District. The restaurant is Michelin-starred, having retained its star through the 2025 Michelin Guide with a March 2026 refresh, and serves blind, multi-course tasting menus rather than an à la carte format. Seating is split across three areas: the Dining Room offers a choice of six- or ten-course menus for parties of two to four, the Kitchen Counter runs a ten-course menu for one or two guests, and the Parlour Room serves six-course menus at both tables and bar seating. Service runs Tuesday through Saturday from 5pm.

Wine pairings are available for both the six- and ten-course menus, "thoughtfully selected to complement and elevate each course" according to the restaurant's own reservations page — and that same page states Alo runs a standing non-alcoholic pairing alongside it, not a one-off special request: "a refined non-alcoholic pairing" built to offer "the same level of creativity and balance for those who prefer an alcohol-free experience."

What that looks like in practice was documented in a June 2026 review by Carolyn Jung of Food Gal, who was offered a choice of Champagne or a non-alcoholic welcome pour: Sparkling Saicho Hojicha, a single-origin roasted green tea served chilled and lightly fizzy. Jung described it as "deeply golden in color, lightly fizzy, and pleasantly none too sweet," with a "smoky, toasty, roasty flavor" that read as "not remotely like soda, but rather a sophisticated tea drink" — enough, she wrote, that she considered buying a bottle of the tea to take home.
venues.pressQuote: This isn't remotely like soda, but rather a sophisticated tea drink. I loved it so much that I might have to purchase a bottle or two online now.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Restaurant review, "Toronto Dining, Part II: Michelin-Starred Alo" (June 8, 2026)

venues.name: Aloha Beer Company
venues.description: Aloha Beer Company is a brewery and taproom on Queen Street in Kakaʻako, and it keeps a named mocktail list rather than the token soda option most breweries offer. The Cucumber Smash and the tropical Lilikoi Cooler are the two the bar is known for, alongside a house iced tea and a Virgin Mojito. That combination — a working brewery that has bothered to write a zero-proof list — is what makes it useful, because a taproom is the default social venue in most cities and the place a non-drinker is most likely to be stranded. Happy hour runs daily from 2pm to 6pm and brunch at weekends from 10am to 2pm.
venues.longDescription:
Aloha Beer Company brews and pours at 700 Queen Street in Kakaʻako, the warehouse district between downtown and Ala Moana that has become Honolulu's main concentration of independent food and drink. The taproom is the public face of a working brewery, with the range poured alongside guest taps, and it functions as a neighbourhood room rather than a visitor attraction — open 11am most days, later at weekends, with happy hour daily from 2pm to 6pm and brunch service on Saturday and Sunday from 10am to 2pm.

The reason it appears in an alcohol-free guide is that it does the thing most breweries do not. A taproom is, for a lot of people, the default place a group ends up, and the standard provision for anyone not drinking is a canned soft drink handed over without comment. Aloha Beer instead keeps a named mocktail list: the Cucumber Smash, which is the driest and most bar-like of them; the Lilikoi Cooler, built on passionfruit, which is the local flavour that does the most work in Hawaiian zero-proof drinks because it brings genuine acidity rather than just sweetness; a house iced tea; and a Virgin Mojito. None of these are technically ambitious, and the brewery does not produce its own non-alcoholic beer the way some mainland breweries now do. But the list exists, it is written down, and a guest can order from it by name — which is the practical difference between being accommodated and being catered for. Kakaʻako's density helps too: Moku Kitchen at SALT is a few minutes away, Merriman's is in Ward Village just to the east, and Wild Orange and Ground Level Lounge are both within a short drive, so the district supports a whole evening rather than a single stop.

venues.name: Amal Miami
venues.description: Amal is a modern Lebanese restaurant and bar in Coconut Grove, opened in 2022 by Ink Entertainment Group, the hospitality company led by Beirut-born founder Charles Khabouth. It is the U.S. counterpart to the original Amal in Toronto, with executive chef Wissam Baki overseeing a menu of shareable mezze and coastal Lebanese dishes in a 180-seat dining room known for live music and a lively evening scene. For non-drinkers, Amal keeps a named zero-proof list built on Seedlip Notas de Agave and Martini & Rossi non-alcoholic aperitivo: the Habibi Mule (Seedlip Notas de Agave, prickly pear–lime, hibiscus ginger beer), the Yalla Spritz (Martini & Rossi Vibrante, cranberry-mango, Fever-Tree soda), and the Secret Garden (parsley-infused Seedlip Notas de Agave, lime, orange blossom, rose water, tonic). The kitchen also serves Lebanese brunch and a daily happy hour.

venues.longDescription:
Amal opened in Coconut Grove in 2022 as the United States counterpart to the original in Toronto, from Ink Entertainment Group — the hospitality company led by Beirut-born founder Charles Khabouth — with executive chef Wissam Baki running a menu of shareable mezze and coastal Lebanese cooking. The 180-seat room is built for a lively evening, with live music and a scene that builds through the night.

Lebanese hospitality has a useful quality for a non-drinker: the meal is structured around shared plates arriving continuously rather than around a bottle matched to courses, so declining alcohol removes less of the experience than it would at a wine-led restaurant. Amal supports that with a named zero-proof list built on real products rather than juice. The Habibi Mule uses Seedlip Notas de Agave with prickly pear, lime and hibiscus ginger beer. The Yalla Spritz is Martini & Rossi Vibrante with cranberry-mango and Fever-Tree soda. The Secret Garden infuses Seedlip Notas de Agave with parsley and lengthens it with lime, orange blossom, rose water and tonic.

That last drink is the interesting one. Orange blossom and rose water are Levantine pantry ingredients, used in the region's desserts and drinks for centuries — so the mocktail is drawing on the same culinary tradition as the kitchen rather than importing a European cocktail template and removing the gin. Resident Magazine described the Habibi Mule as light, floral and balanced, mirroring the restaurant's modern Mediterranean approach.

The kitchen also serves a Lebanese brunch and runs a daily happy hour. It is a full-service restaurant and bar; the zero-proof list is a genuine section of it. Coconut Grove is quieter than Brickell or Wynwood, which suits a long mezze dinner where the drinking is not the point of the evening.
venues.pressQuote: Light, floral, and balanced, it mirrors the restaurant's modern Mediterranean approach

venues.name: Amara at Paraiso
venues.description: Amara at Paraiso is the waterfront restaurant from James Beard Award-winning chef and owner Michael Schwartz, on Biscayne Bay at the foot of the Paraiso towers in Edgewater. The cooking is coastal Latin American, and the bar keeps two documented alcohol-free builds that are designed to sit with it rather than to stand apart: the Pathfinder's Hand, made with The Pathfinder Hemp & Root, fresh tangerine, lime and soda, and the Miami Mockarita, a margarita-style pour of coconut water, lime, agave, orange bitters, pineapple and coconut. The Greater Miami Convention & Visitors Bureau lists the restaurant among the city's dining destinations with exceptional alcohol-free drinks. Service runs from 11:30am daily and the room sits directly on Biscayne Bay.
signatureDrinks: Pathfinder's Hand (The Pathfinder Hemp & Root, fresh tangerine, lime, soda)
Miami Mockarita (coconut water, lime, agave, orange bitters, pineapple, coconut)
venues.longDescription:
Amara at Paraiso occupies a waterfront pavilion at 3101 NE 7th Avenue in Edgewater, sitting directly on Biscayne Bay at the base of the Paraiso residential towers with a long terrace facing the water. It is the coastal Latin American restaurant from Michael Schwartz, the James Beard Award-winning chef and owner behind Michael's Genuine Food & Drink in the Design District. The restaurant opens at 11:30am Monday through Saturday and 11am on Sunday, closing at 10pm most nights and 10:30pm on Friday and Saturday.

The alcohol-free offering is short, named and documented by the city's own tourism authority. The Pathfinder's Hand is built on The Pathfinder Hemp & Root, the distilled non-alcoholic spirit with a bitter, root-driven profile, lengthened with fresh tangerine, lime and soda — a genuinely dry drink rather than a sweet one. The Miami Mockarita is the counterweight: a margarita-format pour of coconut water, lime and agave with orange bitters, pineapple and coconut. The Greater Miami Convention & Visitors Bureau lists Amara under "Dining Destinations With Exceptional Mocktails" and writes that the restaurant continues to elevate mindful sipping with drinks designed to complement its coastal menu. The Pathfinder is not currently a brand carried in this catalogue's brand registry, so no brand tag is attached to this entry even though the spirit is named on the drink. Michael Schwartz's Michael's Genuine, which runs its own alcohol-free list built on Lyre's and Pathfinder, is listed separately. The setting is worth planning around. Amara sits on the bay at the edge of Edgewater, a stretch that has become one of the denser clusters in this catalogue: Casadonna is a few blocks south along North Bayshore Drive and Joia Beach is a short drive across the causeway on Watson Island, both with documented alcohol-free builds of their own. The restaurant takes bookings on (786) 708-6408 and posts as @amaraatparaiso. Only two named alcohol-free drinks are published, which is why the programme is graded as real but modest rather than serious.
venues.pressQuote: This iconic waterfront restaurant continues to elevate mindful sipping with mocktails designed to complement its coastal menu.

venues.name: Amaru
venues.description: Amaru is chef-owner Clinton McIver's intimate, three-hatted Armadale dining room, where the degustation comes with a full non-alcoholic pairing (approx A$95pp) that reviewers rate as a highlight in its own right. Rather than off-the-shelf mocktails, the drinks are built entirely in-house from infusions, ferments and kitchen off-cuts - a kombucha-like sparkling bergamot shrub with Champagne vinegar and alcohol-free sparkling wine, a feijoa tea perfumed with blackcurrant leaves, and an umeshu-inspired quince drink among them. At the chef's counter, selecting a pairing (wine or non-alcoholic) is required, putting the zero-proof list on equal footing with the cellar.
venues.hours: Mon closed; Tue-Thu 6pm-9pm; Fri-Sat 12pm-2pm & 6pm-9pm; Sun closed
signatureDrinks: Sparkling bergamot shrub - house bergamot shrub with Champagne vinegar, topped with a gentle alcohol-free sparkling wine
Feijoa tea perfumed with blackcurrant leaves
Blood orange and jasmine flower soda
venues.longDescription:
Amaru opened in Armadale in 2016 and has become one of Melbourne's most decorated restaurants, holding three hats in the Good Food Guide including the 2026 edition. Chef-owner Clinton McIver runs a small, precise open-kitchen room seating around 34 guests, where the multi-course tasting menu is delivered and explained by the team of chefs, waiters and sommeliers.

The non-alcoholic pairing is a genuine anchor of the experience, not an afterthought. Priced at roughly A$95 per person alongside the wine pairing, it is composed of house-made teas, shrubs, meads and fermented infusions - many drawing on kitchen off-cuts that are fermented or used in the drinks' preparation. Courses reviewers have described include an apricot white tea, celeriac tea, kumquat leaf mead, quince and pu'er rose, lilly pilly wine, and a melon and native tea tree infusion.

Time Out's five-star review singled out the zero-proof program, describing an opening kombucha-like drink of bergamot shrub and Champagne vinegar topped with sparkling alcohol-free wine, followed by a yuzu skin elixir, a feijoa tea perfumed with blackcurrant leaves, a blood orange and jasmine flower soda, and an umeshu-inspired quince drink. Reservations at the chef's counter require choosing one of the pairing options, so the non-alcoholic list is treated as a full equal to the extensive cellar.

Amaru is at 1121 High Street on the Armadale shopping strip, open for dinner Tuesday to Saturday and lunch Friday and Saturday. For non-drinkers seeking a serious fine-dining occasion, it is one of the strongest alcohol-free pairing experiences in Melbourne.
venues.pressQuote: It's complex and sophisticated, enough to make going off the grog more often at restaurants an appealing idea.

venues.name: Amazonia
venues.description: Amazonia occupies a converted house on Hopkins Avenue in Birdtown, the small Lakewood district a few streets from LBM, and pairs a cocktail bar with a wood-fired pizza kitchen and a short menu of small plates. The rooms are domestic in scale — you are drinking in someone's front parlour, which is much of the appeal — and the bar leans tropical without tipping into tiki kitsch. Everything on both menus is made from scratch, and the zero-proof drinks get the same construction as the full-proof ones: house-made syrups, Seedlip and Lyre's spirits, and the same smoking and charring work. The alcohol-free Coconut Song is $15, exactly what the original costs. It opens at 4pm daily except Monday, runs to 2am on Friday and Saturday, and is 21-and-over, with an early-week happy hour taking $2 off cocktails and half off pizza.
venues.longDescription:
Amazonia occupies a converted house on Hopkins Avenue in Birdtown, the small Lakewood district a few streets from LBM, and pairs a cocktail bar with a wood-fired pizza kitchen and a short menu of small plates. The rooms are domestic in scale — you are drinking in someone's front parlour, which is much of the appeal — and the bar leans tropical without tipping into tiki kitsch. It opens at 4pm daily except Monday and runs to 2am on Fridays and Saturdays, with a happy hour taking $2 off menu cocktails and half off pizza early in the week. The room is 21-and-over, so this is an adults' bar that serves people who are not drinking rather than a family restaurant with a mocktail page — a distinction that matters if what you want is a night out rather than a dinner.

Both the kitchen and the bar work from scratch, and the non-alcoholic drinks are the part of the programme that has drawn the most attention locally. Cleveland Magazine's 2026 mocktail roundup described the alcohol-free versions as nuanced rather than reduced, and used the Coconut Song as its example: the zero-proof build costs $15, the same as the original, and reconstructs the full drink using Seedlip and Lyre's non-alcoholic spirits, the bar's own syrups, a custom smoking step and a charred lime.

That smoking and charring is what carries it. Burnt sugar and smoke supply the bitterness and aroma that rum would otherwise provide, so the result lands as a cocktail with a long finish rather than a fruit punch — the single hardest thing to get right in a tropical zero-proof drink, where sweetness usually swamps everything. Other drinks on the list can be built spirit-free on request from the same components, and the bar team is comfortable doing it, which makes the whole menu effectively available rather than just one line of it.
venues.pressQuote: Inside a cozy, converted Lakewood home, inventive pours and nuanced alcohol-free versions are all crafted from scratch.

venues.name: Amba
venues.description: Amba sits on West 28th Street in Hingetown, the compact Ohio City block that also holds Jukebox, and is the Indian-influenced restaurant in Douglas Katz and Todd Thompson's Edgewater Hospitality group — the same operation behind Zhug in Cleveland Heights. Chef Cameron McCaulley runs the kitchen, and the cooking works through spice, acid and fermentation rather than heat alone, which turns out to be the same logic driving the drinks list. Three named non-alcoholic builds sit as a standing section, each written out with its ingredients the way the cocktails are: the cumin-and-black-salt Nimbu Masala, the colour-shifting Blue Bergamot, and the Spiced Nectar at $13 on a citrus-forward zero-proof spirit. Best Day Brewing's non-alcoholic kölsch is $7 alongside the full-strength taps. Dinner only, Monday through Saturday.
signatureDrinks: Nimbu Masala (cumin, lemon, mint, black salt, ginger, soda)
Blue Bergamot (earl grey butterfly-flower tea, lemon, soda)
Spiced Nectar (zero-proof spirit, cardamom agave, lime)

naMenuItems.name: Spiced Nectar
naMenuItems.description: citrusy zero proof spirit, cardamom agave, lime

venues.longDescription:
Amba sits on West 28th Street in Hingetown, the compact Ohio City block that also holds Jukebox, and is the Indian-influenced restaurant in Douglas Katz and Todd Thompson's Edgewater Hospitality group — the same operation behind Zhug in Cleveland Heights. Chef Cameron McCaulley runs the kitchen, and the cooking works through spice, acid and fermentation rather than heat alone, which turns out to be the same logic driving the drinks list. Service is dinner only, Monday through Saturday, to 10pm on weeknights and 11pm at weekends.

The non-alcoholic section is a fixed part of the menu rather than a seasonal add-on, and each drink is written out with its ingredients exactly as the cocktails are. The Nimbu Masala is the house nimbu pani reworked as a bar drink: cumin, lemon, mint, black salt, ginger and soda water, where the black salt supplies a sulphurous savoury edge that stops it reading as lemonade — the single most common failure of a restaurant mocktail. The Blue Bergamot uses earl grey butterfly-flower tea with lemon and soda, and shifts colour in the glass as the acid hits the tea, which is a party trick that happens to also taste of something. The Spiced Nectar, at $13 and the drink Cleveland Magazine singled out in its 2026 guide, is built on a citrus-forward zero-proof spirit with cardamom agave, lime and a dried lime wheel, and is the closest thing on the list to a conventional cocktail.

On the beer side, Best Day Brewing's non-alcoholic kölsch is listed at $7 next to the full-strength taps rather than hidden in a footnote. Between Amba and Zhug, Edgewater is the most reliable group in the city for printed, named non-alcoholic drinks — useful when booking for a mixed table.
venues.pressQuote: The Spiced Nectar ($13) is a citrusy zero-proof spirit with cardamom agave and a dried lime wheel.

venues.name: American Bar at The Savoy
venues.description: The American Bar at The Savoy, on the Strand, is London's oldest surviving cocktail bar (open since 1893) and a long-standing World's 50 Best Bars name, crowned the World's Best Bar in 2017. Its 2025 'Liquid Moments' menu — 17 cocktails marking the Savoy's 135th anniversary under head bartender Angelo Sparvoli — carries a set of genuine non-alcoholic cocktails, among them the King's Cobbler and Homecoming, mixed with the same craft as the spirituous list. For a landmark grand-hotel bar of this stature, that makes it a rare high-value zero-proof option in central London.
venues.longDescription:
Opened in 1893 inside The Savoy hotel on the Strand, the American Bar is the longest-surviving cocktail bar in London and one of the most storied in the world — the name was a Victorian-era statement that this was a room built to serve cocktails. It was home to Ada 'Coley' Coleman, an early celebrity bartender who created the Hanky Panky, and later to Harry Craddock, whose 1930 'Savoy Cocktail Book' remains a canonical text of the craft. The bar has been a near-permanent fixture on the World's 50 Best Bars list, and under then-head bartender Erik Lorincz it was named the World's Best Bar in 2017.

The room is classic Art Deco: marble pillars, leather chairs, geometric grey-and-yellow carpeting, black-and-white photographs of old film stars along the walls, and a mirror-backed bar with just a few stools. A baby grand piano is played nightly, and the atmosphere leans to old-school Savoy glamour rather than modern minimalism.

The current drinks list, launched in early 2025, is the 'Liquid Moments' menu: 17 new cocktails that distil 135 years of the Savoy's history, curated by bar manager Andrea Di Chiara and head bartender Angelo Sparvoli, who returned to the bar after a four-year absence. Alongside the spirituous serves, the menu carries several genuine non-alcoholic cocktails built to the same standard — Sparvoli specifically names the King's Cobbler and Homecoming as zero-proof options. The offering is modest in number rather than a full dedicated no-alcohol book, but at a World's-best-calibre landmark hotel bar the presence of real, named non-alcoholic builds makes it a high-value stop for non-drinkers on the Strand. The bar is open daily from noon (to midnight Monday–Saturday, to 10pm Sunday); booking ahead is advised.
venues.pressQuote: We have several non-alcoholic cocktails on our menu, including King's Cobbler and Homecoming.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Angelo Sparvoli, head bartender, American Bar at The Savoy

venues.name: Analog Coffee Bar (Carabello Coffee)
venues.description: Analog is the fully non-alcoholic "slow bar" tucked inside Carabello Coffee's roastery-cafe in historic Newport, where baristas apply craft-cocktail technique to zero-proof drinks. Seating just six at a wooden counter, it runs like a chef's table for beverages: the espresso and pour-over gear sits behind the bar so guests watch every step. A brand-new themed menu drops every six weeks — a recent literary-inspired lineup featured The Hobbit, Bear, Blueberries for Sal and Anne of Green Gables — spanning coffee builds, tea-based signatures, hot chocolate and coffee mocktails like the Cold Fashioned (cold brew and bitters, sans the bourbon). Everything is alcohol-free; the venue's own FAQ answers the alcohol question with a flat "No." Open Thursday–Saturday, 10am–5pm, with reservations encouraged, especially on Saturdays.
venues.longDescription:
Carabello Coffee, run by owner Justin Carabello, roasts its own beans at 107 E 9th Street in historic Newport, Kentucky, just across the river from downtown Cincinnati. After a Kickstarter campaign that raised $47,000 in 30 days ("It floored us," Justin told Cincinnati Magazine), the shop expanded and opened Analog in September 2016 during its three-year anniversary — a more curated, experiential space carved out of the cafe. The concept, as Justin put it, is "craft cocktails meets coffee": a slow bar where beverages are built with the deliberate technique of a cocktail program, minus any alcohol.

Analog is entirely alcohol-free — the shop's own FAQ answers the question of whether the drinks contain alcohol with a simple "No." Guests sit at a six-seat wooden counter with the espresso machines and pour-over rigs arranged behind the bar, chef's-table style, so every step is visible. The menu is reinvented from scratch every six weeks, with a few special monthly features in between; a recent literary-themed lineup included The Hobbit, Bear, Blueberries for Sal and Anne of Green Gables. Beyond coffee builds and espresso drinks, the bar pours coffee-free options — tea-based signature drinks, hot chocolate, and coffee mocktails such as the Cold Fashioned, made with cold brew and bitters "sans the bourbon." Desserts and small bites are curated from local bakeries.

Analog runs Thursday through Saturday, 10am–5pm only, and closes the rest of the week. With just six seats, reservations are encouraged (especially on Saturdays) and can be booked through carabellocoffee.resurva.com; the shop suggests planning for anywhere from 5 to 60 minutes depending on how deep you want to go. It's a genuine destination for coffee lovers and for sober or sober-curious guests who want a real, technique-driven alcohol-free experience rather than a token mocktail. Find the bar on Instagram at @carabelloanalog or call (859) 415-1587.
venues.pressQuote: At the six-seat wooden bar, the coffee apparati rests behind the bar, not in front, so that patrons can actually see the processes in action.

venues.name: Anansi Cocktail Lounge
venues.description: Anansi Cocktail Lounge is a Black-owned cocktail bar on East College Avenue in Avondale Estates, on the eastern edge of Decatur. It is a dark, deliberately intimate room — 21 and over, no outside drinks, no flash photography — that trades from six in the evening to as late as 2am at the weekend. Its non-alcoholic menu is not a handful of substitutions but a named list, the Ikenice Choice, built entirely on Lyre's non-alcoholic spirits. The standout is the alcohol-free espresso martini, frothy and bitter without the syrupy finish most versions carry, and there is an amaretto sour given texture with aquafaba. The bar's own site puts it simply: it has cocktails for those who do not consume alcohol.
venues.address: 2700 E College Ave Suite 4000, Decatur, GA 30030
venues.longDescription:
Anansi takes its name from the West African and Caribbean spider-trickster of folklore, and the bar leans into storytelling as its organising idea — its own site describes it as a place where love is poured into every detail, celebrating storytelling and craftsmanship. It occupies Suite 4000 at 2700 East College Avenue, a stretch that carries a Decatur postal address but which the bar itself, and the press, place in Avondale Estates. The room is small, dark and rule-bound in a way that signals what kind of evening it wants to host: over-21s only, physical identification, no outside beverages, no smoking or vaping, and no flash photography, so the lighting stays as designed. It opens at six every night except Sunday and runs to midnight midweek, one on Thursday and two on Friday and Saturday.

The alcohol-free programme is the reason it appears here. Rather than improvising substitutions, Anansi keeps a titled non-alcoholic menu — the Ikenice Choice — assembled entirely on Lyre's non-alcoholic spirits, which gives the drinks a consistent base rather than leaving each one to be reinvented. DiningOut, reviewing Atlanta's zero-proof bars in 2026, called the non-alcoholic espresso martini the standout: frothy, bitter and toasted without the syrupy aftertaste that follows most versions around. The amaretto sour is the other named pour, whipped with aquafaba so that it carries the same foam and mouthfeel as an egg-white sour. Both come out of the same station and in the same glassware as the alcoholic list. The bar is fully licensed and the majority of its trade is alcoholic, which places it at a four rather than a five, but the non-alcoholic list is titled, branded and permanent — a meaningfully higher standard than a bar that will "make you something" if you ask. One practical note on the address: the postal line reads Decatur and the postcode is 30030, but the bar's own website and the local press both place it in Avondale Estates, and we have used the neighbourhood the venue itself uses. It is a short walk from the Avondale MARTA station either way.
venues.pressQuote: Anansi trades bright minimalism for a moody lounge in Avondale Estates, where the 'Ikenice Choice' mocktail menu is built entirely on Lyre's spirits.

venues.name: Andra Hem
venues.description: Andra Hem — Swedish for "second home" — is a Scandinavian-inspired cocktail lounge that opened in November 2022 in a four-story black-painted townhouse at 16th and Chancellor in Rittenhouse. Founded by art collector Paige West, with interiors by designer Ghislaine Viñas built around a fictional Swedish proprietor, the bar deliberately launched with no public-relations push yet landed on Esquire's Best Bars in America list in 2023. Lead bartender Patrick Jennings runs a cocktail program that leans Nordic, alongside snacks like warm bread, pickled herring, and caviar. Its menu carries a dedicated "Low ABV & Non-Alcoholic" section with three named zero-proof builds at $11 each: the Squirt Gun (bitter soda and espresso), The Linc (cucumber water, dill, lime, soda), and Touch Nothing But the Lamp (jasmine tea, fruit, citrus, soda). The NA list is small but real and house-made.
venues.longDescription:
Andra Hem — Swedish for second home — opened in November 2022 in a four-storey black-painted townhouse at 16th and Chancellor in Rittenhouse. It was founded by art collector Paige West, with interiors by designer Ghislaine Viñas built around the fiction of a Swedish proprietor, and it launched with no public relations push at all before landing on Esquire's Best Bars in America list in 2023. Lead bartender Patrick Jennings runs a Nordic-leaning cocktail programme alongside snacks of warm bread, pickled herring and caviar.

The menu carries a dedicated section headed "Low ABV & Non-Alcoholic", and that pairing of categories under one heading is worth noting, because it is honest in a way that matters. Low-alcohol and zero-alcohol are not the same thing, and a bar that files them together is at least telling you they are distinct — which means asking which is which is a normal question rather than an awkward one. Anyone avoiding alcohol completely should confirm before ordering, since a low-ABV drink is not alcohol-free.

The Squirt Gun is the drink the room is known for. Philadelphia Magazine described it as the bar's take on a European favourite and exactly what it sounds like: espresso with bitter soda. That combination — coffee against a quinine-bitter carbonated mixer — is a genuine Italian café habit, and it works because the bitterness of the soda and the acidity of the espresso sharpen each other rather than cancelling out. It is one of very few drinks that is naturally complex without any alcohol at all. The Linc and Touch Nothing But the Lamp complete the named list.

The Scandinavian setting suits an evening without drinking: the room is designed for lingering, the food arrives in small savoury plates rather than courses, and the whole hygge-adjacent premise is comfort rather than intoxication. Open from five in the evening, to midnight Thursday through Saturday; closed Mondays.
venues.pressQuote: Andra Hem's Squirt Gun is their take on the European favorite and it's exactly what it sounds like: espresso with bitter soda.

venues.name: Andros Taverna
venues.description: Andros Taverna is chef Doug Psaltis's Greek restaurant on Milwaukee Avenue in Logan Square, built around a wood fire, mezze and slow-roasted lamb, and its drinks menu carries a dedicated Zero Proof section priced at a flat $14 - the same tier as the low-ABV cocktails and only three dollars under the full-proof list. The section holds four drinks: a St Agrestis Phony Negroni, a Ghia Spritz labeled Lime and Salt, the Root and Bloom built from Seedlip Grove with tonic and lime, and an NA 75 of passionfruit and Roots non-alcoholic vermouth. A Gruvi Golden Lager is stocked at $10 for anyone who wants a beer with the grill. The program has been part of the restaurant since its early days and has grown rather than shrunk.

naMenuItems.description: seedlip grove, tonic, lime

naMenuItems.name: Na 75
naMenuItems.description: passionfruit, roots n/a vermouth

venues.longDescription:
Andros Taverna is the Greek restaurant chef Doug Psaltis opened on Milwaukee Avenue in Logan Square, and it cooks the way a taverna does - over fire, in volume, with mezze to start and slow-roasted lamb as the centrepiece. Resy singled the room out in its 2022 guide to Chicago's non-alcoholic cocktails, noting that guests who were not up for a night of ouzo had alcohol-free drinks built on Seedlip's distilled non-alcoholic spirits waiting for them. In the years since, the section has grown: what Resy described as two drinks is now a four-strong Zero Proof heading on the printed menu.

The current list prices every zero-proof drink at $14, immediately below the $17 stirred-and-boozy cocktails and level with the low-ABV spritzes, which is the clearest signal a restaurant can send that the non-alcoholic list is not a consolation. The Root and Bloom is the house build, combining Seedlip Grove with tonic and lime for a citrus-forward drink that stands up to charred meat and lemon. The NA 75 pairs passionfruit with Roots non-alcoholic vermouth in a riff on the French 75. Alongside those the bar pours a Ghia Spritz labeled Lime and Salt and a St Agrestis Phony Negroni straight from the bottle, and stocks Grüvi's Golden Lager at $10 for anyone who simply wants a beer with the grill. The restaurant is open from 11am seven days a week and runs to 11pm on Friday and Saturday, with weekend service starting at 9am, so the zero-proof list is available across lunch, dinner and late-evening drinking alike. The rest of the list runs to raki, ouzo and Greek spritzes on one side and Pipeworks pilsner, an IPA and a lemon-and-thyme witbier on the other, so a mixed table has range in both directions without anyone ordering off-format. The room itself is built for sharing - spreads, mezze and a wood-fired grill sent out in waves - which is the setting in which a properly made zero-proof drink does the most work, because everyone is ordering in the same rhythm rather than one person nursing a soft drink through four courses.
venues.pressQuote: If you aren’t up for a night of ouzo at Chef Doug Psaltis’ Greek spot, there are two alcohol-free cocktails to pair with the mezze and slow-roasted lamb, both using Seedlip distilled non-alcoholic spirits to deliver that signature alcoholic bite without the booze.

venues.name: Andy's Old Port Pub
venues.description: Andy's Old Port Pub is a waterside pub on Commercial Street facing the working harbour, and it carries a real selection of canned and bottled non-alcoholic drinks alongside house-made mocktails — a combination that covers both kinds of non-drinker, the one who wants something built and the one who just wants a cold can. Its practical advantage over almost everything else in Portland is the clock: it opens at 11am on weekdays, 7:30am on Saturdays for breakfast, and runs to 1am every night, which is a longer useful window than any other venue in this guide. At least one local guide attributes specific mocktail names here that another assigns elsewhere, so ask what is actually on when you arrive.
venues.longDescription:
Andy's Old Port Pub sits on Commercial Street looking out at Portland's working waterfront, which is a more honest view than the postcard version — fishing boats, ferries and the occasional cruise ship rather than a tidied-up marina. It is a pub in the straightforward sense: beer, a long bar, food all day, live music.

Its alcohol-free offering is a stocked selection of canned and bottled non-alcoholic drinks plus house-made mocktails. That pairing is more thoughtful than it first appears, because non-drinkers split into two groups with different needs. Some want a constructed drink — something with balance and a bit of ceremony. Others emphatically do not: they want a cold can, no conversation, no fuss, and nothing that draws attention at the bar. Most venues serve one of those and ignore the other. Andy's covers both.

A note on sourcing: at least one local guide attributes specific mocktail names to this pub while another attributes the same names elsewhere, so this listing deliberately describes the offering rather than naming drinks that may belong to a different bar. Worth asking what is on when you arrive.

The hours are the strongest argument for knowing about it. It opens at 11am Monday to Friday, at 7:30am on Saturday for breakfast, at 9am on Sunday, and closes at 1am every single night. Portland's better alcohol-free drinking is otherwise locked into narrow windows — Hunt & Alpine opens at 3pm and closes Mondays, Arcadia opens at 5pm and closes Tuesdays, Lava Kava runs 5pm to 10pm. A harbourside pub open eighteen hours a day, seven days a week, with something genuinely drinkable for a non-drinker, is a useful thing to have in your back pocket. It is also directly on the waterfront, which makes it the obvious place to send someone who wants the view without the wine list.
venues.pressQuote: The biggest change, they said, is that Andy's is now a soccer bar
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Portland Press Herald, Bar Guide, February 2023

venues.name: Animae
venues.description: Animae is an Asian-inspired fine-dining room on Pacific Highway downtown, led by executive chef Tara Monsod, a three-time James Beard Award semifinalist, and its drinks list prints a Spirit Free section of four. Spirited Away is built on Pentire Adrift with elderflower, honey, Thai basil and black peppercorn; The Malarkey uses a Thai chilli and tamarind syrup with pineapple and lime; and two tea drinks follow — a melon milk tea with jasmine, oat milk and boba, and a cold-brewed single-source iced tea. Prices run from nine to thirteen dollars, against nineteen for the alcoholic cocktails, so a non-drinker is not paying a premium for the absence of alcohol. The Malarkey is the one to order if you would rather avoid spirit analogues entirely. Dinner is served nightly from five, until half past nine on Friday and Saturday, in a dining room built into the base of the Pacific Gate tower on the waterfront edge of downtown.
signatureDrinks: Spirited Away ($11) — Pentire Adrift, elderflower, honey, Thai basil, black peppercorn
The Malarkey ($11) — Thai chilli and tamarind syrup, pineapple, lime
Melon Milk Tea ($13) — honeydew, jasmine tea, oat milk, boba
Kollo Iced Tea ($9) — cold-brewed, single-source tea leaves
venues.longDescription:
Animae occupies the ground floor of the Pacific Gate tower on Pacific Highway, between the Marina district and the waterfront, and blends the spectacle of a steakhouse with the flavours of the Asian American experience — the restaurant's own framing. Its name is a double reference, to anime and to the Chinese American actress Anna May Wong. Executive chef Tara Monsod, who is Filipino American and a three-time James Beard Award semifinalist, cooks over a coal-fired oven and a Japanese robata grill.

The Spirit Free section is four deep and unusually varied for a fine-dining list. Spirited Away, at eleven dollars, is the most cocktail-like: Pentire Adrift, the Cornish botanical non-alcoholic spirit, with elderflower, honey, Thai basil and black peppercorn — floral at the front and peppery at the finish. The Malarkey, also eleven, skips the spirit alternative entirely and builds on a Thai chilli and tamarind syrup with pineapple and lime, which makes it the better choice for anyone avoiding spirit analogues; tamarind supplies the sourness and the chilli the length.

The other two are tea rather than cocktail. The melon milk tea at thirteen dollars runs honeydew and jasmine tea with oat milk and boba, and there is a cold-brewed single-source iced tea at nine. On a menu where the alcoholic cocktails run to nineteen dollars, having a nine-dollar option that is not a soda is the sort of detail a non-drinker notices.

A practical note on the room: this is a destination restaurant with a tasting-menu sensibility and a dining room designed for occasions, so it is expensive and reservations matter. Service runs from five every night, to nine early in the week and half past nine on Friday and Saturday. The spirit-free section is printed on the same card as the cocktails and changes with the seasonal menu, so confirm the four when you arrive. Alcohol is served throughout; this is not an alcohol-free space.

The room is designed to be looked at. Animae sits beneath the Pacific Gate tower and takes its cue from the building above it, with a futurist reading of Art Deco glamour — lush, cinematic, built for celebration in the restaurant's own description. It belongs to the Puffer Malarkey Collective, whose other rooms include Le Coq, and Monsod runs the kitchens at both. Practically, this is a restaurant to book rather than walk into, the tasting-menu pacing suits a long evening, and the waterfront location means parking is easiest in one of the nearby structures rather than on the street.
venues.pressQuote: The restaurant blends the indulgence and spectacle of a classic steakhouse with the dynamic flavors, influences, and cultural perspectives that define the Asian American experience.

venues.name: Anina
venues.description: Anina is a tropical, plant-filled bar on Hayes Street in Hayes Valley, trading to 1am on Thursday, Friday and Saturday and known for a rum-heavy, botanical cocktail list and shareable punchbowls. Its alcohol-free drinks sit under a menu heading simply marked zero proof, and they are priced from $7 to $13 against $15 to $17 for the full-proof cocktails. The section lists Six of Cups, built on Floreale L'Aperitivo with lemon, honey and cucumber tonic; a Pathfinder Spritz made with the fermented and distilled hemp spirit; St. Agrestis's Phony Negroni; and a Juice Shop pineapple mint tonic of sparkling spring water, cold-pressed pineapple and pear juice, mint, blue spirulina and eleuthero. Athletic Run Wild, Best Day Kölsch and Leitz Eins Zwei Zero sparkling rosé fill out the list.
