venues.longDescription:
Anina sits at 482 Hayes Street in the middle of Hayes Valley's restaurant row, and is described by The Infatuation as feeling like a tropical beer garden with a great deal of rum and botanical-leaning drinks. The room runs long hours for the neighbourhood — 3pm to 1am on Thursday and from early afternoon to 1am on Friday and Saturday — and the cocktail list is built around punchbowls, tiki-adjacent builds and a daytime happy hour that discounts beer, wine, house cocktails and, notably, the zero-proof drinks by a dollar.

The alcohol-free section is printed on the main menu under the heading zero proof, and it is one of the better-constructed lists in the city because it covers several different drinking occasions rather than offering three variations on fruit juice. Six of Cups is the aperitivo option, built on Floreale L'Aperitivo with lemon, honey and cucumber tonic at $11. The Pathfinder Spritz, also $11, is served long over ice and uses the Seattle-made fermented and distilled hemp spirit, whose own botanical bill runs to wormwood, angelica root, ginger, sage, saffron, orange peel and douglas-fir. St. Agrestis's Phony Negroni, canned in Brooklyn, is $10 and covers anyone who wants the bitter-orange profile without a build. The Juice Shop pineapple mint tonic at $7 is the lightest option: sparkling spring water with cold-pressed pineapple and pear juice, mint, blue spirulina and the adaptogen eleuthero, made locally in San Francisco. Beyond the cocktails the bar keeps Athletic Brewing's Run Wild IPA and Best Day Brewing's Kölsch, both under half a per cent, and Leitz Eins Zwei Zero sparkling rosé by the glass, so beer and wine drinkers are served as well as cocktail drinkers. The daytime happy hour takes a dollar off the zero-proof drinks along with the beer, wine and house cocktails, which is a small detail that says the bar counts them as part of the same list rather than as a separate accommodation. The bar closes early on Sundays at 7pm but runs to 1am from Thursday through Saturday, making it one of the later alcohol-free options in Hayes Valley.
venues.pressQuote: Anina feels like a tropical beer garden, with a ton of rum and botanical-leaning drinks.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: The Infatuation, The 20 Best Cocktail Bars In SF

venues.name: Anise
venues.description: Anise is a pan-Mediterranean food and wine bar that opened in September 2021 inside the boutique Drey Hotel at The Village, a redeveloped community in central/NE Dallas. The kitchen draws from across the Mediterranean coast with mezze and shareable plates, and the wine program is the centerpiece — roughly 30 wines by the glass, 10 on tap, and about 135 total. Its published Zero Proof section is short rather than deep: the Underserved ($8), built on sweet plum, ginger and lemon with Fever-Tree Mediterranean tonic, alongside a fresh ginger ale ($4) and Heineken 0.0 ($6). Seating runs to an umbrella-shaded front patio for 42 and a quieter back terrace for 26.
signatureDrinks: Underserved (sweet plum, ginger, lemon, Fever-Tree Mediterranean tonic) $8
venues.longDescription:
Anise is a pan-Mediterranean food and wine bar that opened in September 2021 inside the Drey Hotel, the boutique hotel at the centre of The Village, a large redeveloped residential community in central and north-east Dallas. The kitchen works along the Mediterranean coast rather than from one country, running mezze and shareable plates, and the wine list is the reason most people come — roughly thirty wines by the glass, ten of them on tap, and about 135 bottles in total. The room opens onto two outdoor spaces that are the better places to sit in spring and autumn: an umbrella-shaded front patio seating 42, and a quieter back terrace seating 26. Dinner runs Tuesday to Saturday from 5pm to 10pm, and the space has hosted guest residencies, including a Kyo omakase pop-up.

The non-alcoholic offering here is genuine but small, and it is worth being precise about its size before making a special trip. Anise publishes a named "Zero Proof" section, but it holds one house-built drink: the Underserved ($8), made with sweet plum, ginger and lemon, lengthened with Fever-Tree Mediterranean tonic. Beside it sit a fresh ginger ale ($4) and a Heineken 0.0 ($6). The Dallas Observer picked exactly that drink out when it surveyed the city's mocktails in January 2024, describing the Underserved as sweet plum, ginger and zesty lemon all harmonised by Fever-Tree Mediterranean tonic. What Anise offers a non-drinker, then, is less a zero-proof cocktail list than a wine bar that has thought about one drink properly and serves it in a room where not drinking does not feel conspicuous — a reasonable choice for a dinner where the rest of the table is working through the by-the-glass list, and a thin one if the drinks themselves are the point of the evening. The published drinks menu has not been refreshed recently, so it is worth asking what the bar is pouring on the night.
venues.pressQuote: Dive into Anise's Zero Proof Menu, and try the Underserved, made with sweet plum, ginger and zesty lemon, all harmonized by Fever-Tree Mediterranean tonic.

venues.name: Anjou
venues.description: Anjou is a European-inspired craft cocktail bar in East Walnut Hills, opened in June 2021 by Chris Wolfe, Andy Smith and Brad Lauck in a converted former dry-cleaner on Woodburn Avenue. It has built a reputation on inventive, produce-driven drinks, and its standing zero-proof list is repeatedly named among Cincinnati's best mocktails. Two roughly $10 alcohol-free cocktails anchor the menu: the citrus-forward Schamer '94 (non-alcoholic spiced spirit, lemon, grapefruit, honey and NA bitters) and the warmer, aromatic Once An Island (masala, pomegranate, spiced maple, ginger, house yuzu, NA bitters and smoked cinnamon). A lighter Spencer, built on mint, lime, seltzer and a pineapple-mango shrub, has also appeared. Anjou rounds out the option with zero-proof wine and beer, making it a genuine choice for an alcohol-free date night.
venues.hours: Mon closed; Tue-Thu 4pm-11pm; Fri-Sat 4pm-12am; Sun closed
venues.longDescription:
Anjou opened in June 2021 at 2804 Woodburn Avenue, in an East Walnut Hills space that previously housed Woodburn Dry Cleaners. Founders Chris Wolfe, Andy Smith and Brad Lauck named the bar after Margaret of Anjou, wife of King Henry VI, and leaned into a theme of powerful women — grayscale floral wallpaper, minimalist florals and bold bathroom artwork. Wolfe told CityBeat the goal was "familiar flavors introduced in a different way," and the kitchen-minded cocktail approach deliberately avoids a fixed seasonal menu: "We really focus on the ingredients. Are they fresh at the time?"

That produce-first philosophy carries straight into the zero-proof list, which local press keeps singling out. everythingcincy calls Anjou's zero-proof menu "sophisticated," highlighting the Schamer '94 — non-alcoholic spiced spirit, lemon, grapefruit, honey and non-alcoholic bitters — and the Once An Island, an aromatic build of masala, pomegranate, spiced maple, ginger, non-alcoholic bitters, house yuzu and smoked cinnamon. CityBeat's mocktail roundup adds the Spencer, made with mint, lime, seltzer and a pineapple-mango shrub. The alcohol-free cocktails run about $10 and get the same craft treatment as the full bar rather than being an afterthought, and Anjou also pours zero-proof wine and beer.

The room is small, dim and romantic — styled as "a sexy spot" by Wolfe and pitched by everythingcincy as ideal for "a classy, alcohol-free date night." Anjou is open Tuesday through Saturday evenings (roughly 4 p.m. to 11 p.m., a little later on weekends) and closed Sunday and Monday; reservations are wise for the compact space. Because the menu tracks seasonal produce rather than a set list, the exact mocktails can rotate, so it's worth asking what's fresh — the bartenders build them to order. Phone (513) 221-1095, or follow @anjoucocktailbar for current pours.
venues.pressQuote: This European-inspired cocktail bar in East Walnut Hills oozes charm and romance. Their zero-proof menu is sophisticated, featuring drinks like the Schamer '94 (spiced NA spirit, citrus, honey, bitters) and Once An Island (masala, pomegranate, ginger, yuzu, smoked cinnamon).

venues.name: Anna's Place
venues.description: Anna's Place is a hidden bar tucked inside the Hotel Indigo on Dodge Street in downtown Omaha, small and intimate, with a cocktail-party atmosphere and a drinks list that treats zero-proof and alcoholic drinks as equals rather than as tiers. Its specialty mocktails are scratch-made, and the house build is the Rowena Moore — named for the Omaha civil-rights organiser and community leader, which places the alcohol-free drink in the bar's own naming scheme rather than in an annex. Open 5pm to 1am Tuesday through Saturday, closed Sunday and Monday.

venues.longDescription:
Anna's Place is the kind of bar you have to be told about: a small, hidden room inside the Hotel Indigo on Dodge Street in downtown Omaha, run at the volume and intimacy of a cocktail party rather than a bar. It stays open until 1am from Tuesday through Saturday.

Its alcohol-free drinks are scratch-made specialty mocktails, and the house one is the Rowena Moore. The name is the detail worth noticing. Rowena Moore was an Omaha civil-rights organiser and community leader who campaigned for decades in North Omaha, and naming a drink for her puts it squarely in the bar's own house scheme — this is not a drink filed under "mocktails" at the bottom of a card, it is a drink with the same kind of name as everything else on the list.

That pattern recurs across this directory, and it is one of the most reliable signals available. Bars that name their alcohol-free drinks the way they name their cocktails have integrated them; bars that call them mocktails and number them have not. The naming is downstream of how the bar thinks about the customer.

Because the room is small and hidden, it also solves a specific problem for a non-drinker: the discomfort of a big, loud bar where the round is the organising principle. A twenty-seat room where the bartender knows what you are drinking is much easier to spend an evening in without alcohol than a crowded one.

This entry records the one named build. The wider specialty list is not published in a readable form, so nothing further is enumerated here.

Open 5pm to 1am Tuesday through Saturday, closed Sunday and Monday. It is a few blocks north-west of the Old Market cluster, near the downtown hotels.
venues.pressQuote: Tucked inside Hotel Indigo, this hidden bar and Omaha speakeasy offers an intimate atmosphere perfect for relaxing with friends or for a date night in Downtown Omaha.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Hurrdat ONE, 10 Best Zero-Proof & Nonalcoholic Bars in Omaha, Nov 18, 2025

venues.name: Anomaly SF
venues.description: Anomaly SF is an intimate tasting-menu restaurant on a quiet block in Lower Pacific Heights, opened by chef-owner Mike Lanham in January 2023 after nearly five years as a word-of-mouth pop-up, with the buildout funded partly via Kickstarter. Lanham — a Culinary Institute of America (Greystone) graduate who cooked at Spruce, the Michelin-starred Commis, and Bird Dog — calls his Georgia-rooted cooking "Southern-Inspired Modernism," and the restaurant earned a Bib Gourmand in the 2024 California Michelin Guide. General manager and beverage director Francis Kulaga runs a full non-alcoholic pairing alongside the multi-course tasting menu, priced comparably to the wine pairing (roughly $99). Rather than a fixed zero-proof list, Kulaga builds the pairing to each guest's taste across the courses, leaning on dealcoholized and spirit-free products including Free AF, Proxies, and Leitz Sparkling, with an option for a few standalone spirit-free cocktails.

venues.longDescription:
Anomaly SF is a small tasting-menu restaurant at 2600 Sutter Street on a quiet block of Lower Pacific Heights, opened by chef-owner Mike Lanham in January 2023 after nearly five years of running the concept as a word-of-mouth pop-up; the permanent buildout was funded in part through Kickstarter. Lanham trained at the Culinary Institute of America at Greystone and cooked at Spruce, the Michelin-starred Commis and Bird Dog before going out on his own. He describes the food as "Southern-Inspired Modernism" — Georgia-rooted cooking rebuilt with modernist technique, in dishes such as hash brown ice cream with truffle parmesan foam — served across roughly twelve courses in a room of about twenty seats. The restaurant received a Bib Gourmand in the 2024 California Michelin Guide, and service runs Tuesday through Saturday only.

The non-alcoholic pairing at Anomaly is bespoke rather than fixed, which is rare at any price point. General manager and beverage director Francis Kulaga sells it alongside the wine pairing at comparable cost — roughly $99 — and rather than pouring a pre-set sequence of zero-proof drinks, he talks to each guest about what they like and assembles the pairing course by course from that conversation. The backbone is dealcoholized and spirit-free product chosen for how closely it tracks the wine it stands in for, leaning on Free AF, Proxies and Leitz Sparkling, with a few standalone spirit-free cocktails available to guests who would rather have one. 7x7 covered the programme in January 2025 in a survey of San Francisco tasting menus with serious alcohol-free pairings, writing that "beverage director Francis Kulaga conspires with Anomaly SF's chef Mike Lanham to create non-alcoholic pairings driven by individual tastes." The practical consequence for a non-drinker is that the full twelve-course experience is available without substitution or apology, and that the pairing is different for each guest rather than a fixed list everyone receives. Because the restaurant is small and the pairing is built to order, it is worth flagging the request at the time of booking rather than on arrival.
venues.pressQuote: Beverage director Francis Kulaga conspires with Anomaly SF's chef Mike Lanham to create non-alcoholic pairings driven by individual tastes.

venues.name: Antidote at Chemist Spirits
venues.description: Antidote is a three-storey cocktail lounge and coffee bar that opened in 2018 at 151 Coxe Avenue in the South Slope, built as a turn-of-the-century apothecary and attached to the Chemist Spirits distillery next door. Mountain Xpress described it on opening as aiming for a cosy, quiet, upscale vibe with Prohibition-style décor in the manner of a traditional gentleman's cigar bar — though, as the paper noted, happily free of cigars and sexism. The award-winning cocktail team turns the same craft to zero-proof drinks, served all day: an apothecary-inspired menu of espresso, coffee, tea and non-alcoholic mocktails, with the Cold Brew Old Fashioned and Cold Brew Mojito among them. The all-day format is what makes it useful — it works as a morning coffee stop and an evening cocktail room in the same seat, in Asheville's densest brewery-and-bar district.
venues.longDescription:
Antidote opened in 2018 at 151 Coxe Avenue in the South Slope, a three-storey Prohibition-era cocktail bar built as a turn-of-the-century apothecary and attached to the Chemist Spirits distillery next door. Mountain Xpress described it at the time as aiming for a cosy, quiet and upscale vibe, with Prohibition-style décor that feels like a traditional gentleman's cigar bar — though, as the paper noted, happily free of cigars and sexism. That would be the whole story at most distillery bars. What makes this one worth a non-drinker's attention is what happened in September 2024.

When Helene hit, the storm brought severe flooding and left much of Asheville without potable water for weeks. Antidote opened its doors and handed out free water, coffee and Wi-Fi to neighbours who had none — and the bar is explicit that the experience changed what it wanted to be. Serving people who needed a drink that was not a drink, in a city where the taps had stopped, inspired a fresh direction: a daytime café operation and a genuine zero-proof programme alongside the distillery's spirits. General manager Philip Szobody put the intent plainly: part of what inspired him was creating a space where anyone in the community could stop in and find a beverage they enjoy and that suits their lifestyle. The house zero-proof drinks lean on the coffee side of that pivot — a Cold Brew Old Fashioned and a Cold Brew Mojito, both built rather than poured. The bar now opens at 8am daily, running to 11pm on weekdays and midnight at weekends, which means it genuinely functions as a café in the morning and a cocktail bar at night rather than switching identity. It becomes 21 and over after 3pm, takes no reservations for parties of six or fewer, and has a pet-friendly patio and a weather-permitting roof.
venues.pressQuote: A new South Slope bar connected to the adjacent Chemist distillery, Antidote aims for a cozy, quiet and upscale vibe, with Prohibition-style décor that feels like a traditional gentleman's cigar bar (though it's happily free of cigars and sexism).

venues.name: ANTI:DOTE
venues.description: ANTI:DOTE is Fairmont Singapore's apothecary-themed cocktail bar, where Head Mixologist Kingston Chin's 'Cure-All' menu carries genuine zero-proof builds alongside its spirit-forward remedies. Its weekly 'Pretty Sober Night' (every Tuesday from 5pm) puts alcohol-free cocktails such as Virgin Sling, Good Fortune, Golden Reset and Berry Mint Tea front and centre from S$10++, with Heineken 0.0 and other non-alcoholic beers on hand. Year-round, signatures are offered in NA form too - Ammachi's Coffee (S$22) swaps whisky and rum for Lyre's Malt and Spiced Cane, and Deja vu (S$22) leans on a house ginger tonic infused with cinchona bark.

signatureDrinks: Ammachi's Coffee (non-alcoholic, S$22) - Lyre's Malt and Spiced Cane in place of whisky and rum, over a chukku-kappi-style spiced coffee
Deja vu (non-alcoholic, S$22) - pisco-style build with homemade ginger tonic infused with cinchona bark
venues.longDescription:
Tucked into Level 1 of the Fairmont Singapore on Bras Basah Road in the City Hall / Civic District, ANTI:DOTE takes its cues from an old-world apothecary: cocktails are framed as remedies, and the current 'Cure-All' menu by Head Mixologist Kingston Chin is organised into three mood-led sections - Confident, Indulge and Reset. The bar is a fixture of the Singapore drinks scene and is featured as a World's 50 Best Discovery establishment.

The non-alcoholic offering is a real part of the programme rather than an afterthought. Every Tuesday from 5pm the bar runs 'Pretty Sober Night', a dedicated alcohol-free evening with a named zero-proof list - Virgin Sling, Mint Mojito, Good Fortune, Golden Reset and lighter pours such as Berry Mint Tea, Copenhagen Sparkling Tea and Alfonso Iced Tea - with alcohol-free cocktails starting from S$10++ and non-alcoholic beers including Heineken 0.0, Peroni 0.0 and Tsingtao 0.0.

Beyond that weekly night, several of the bar's signatures are built as full non-alcoholic versions. Ammachi's Coffee (S$22), inspired by Indian holistic healing and a medicinal spiced 'chukku kappi' coffee, rebuilds its whisky-and-rum base on Lyre's Malt and Spiced Cane to keep the depth without the alcohol, while Deja vu (S$22) reworks a Peruvian pisco-style drink around a homemade ginger tonic infused with cinchona bark.

The room pairs its remedy theme with vinyl DJ sets, jazz sessions and intimate listening experiences, plus bar snacks, making it an easy hotel-bar destination for drinkers who want a genuine zero-proof option in the same setting as the full cocktail list.

venues.name: Anvil Bar & Refuge
venues.description: Anvil Bar & Refuge is a cornerstone of Houston's craft-cocktail scene, opened in March 2009 by Bobby Heugel in the Montrose neighborhood. Widely credited with launching the city's modern drinks culture, it built its reputation on "Anvil's List of 100 Classics" alongside a rotating slate of about nine seasonal house creations, and has been recognized multiple times as a James Beard Award semifinalist for Outstanding Bar Program (finalist in 2018). Its non-alcoholic offerings are modest but genuine and appear by name on the current seasonal menu: "Double Time," a shaken build of zero-proof tequila, strawberry, vinegar, and sparkling water, and the "Phony Negroni," a bubbly non-alcoholic Negroni served on tap.

venues.longDescription:
Bobby Heugel opened Anvil Bar & Refuge in March 2009 at 1424 Westheimer Rd in Montrose, and the bar is widely credited with kick-starting Houston's modern craft-cocktail movement. Its house menu, "Anvil's List of 100 Classics," began about a month after opening as a laminated training guide for bartenders — a minimal list of recipes every staffer was expected to know by heart — before guest demand pushed it onto the printed menu, where it remains a signature feature today.

The bar occupies a single-story storefront in a small strip center that was originally built in 1959 as a Bridgestone-Firestone tire shop; the space later cycled through the Daiquiri Factory and a bar called Sliders before Heugel took it over.

Anvil has been named a James Beard Award semifinalist for Outstanding Bar Program in multiple years, including as a finalist in 2018, cementing its reputation as a proving ground for Houston bar talent. Early bar manager Alba Huerta, a Speed Rack cocktail-competition winner, helped shape Anvil's seasonal program in its first years, according to a March 2012 Houston Press review that praised the bar's "ambitious cocktail program" for keeping regulars coming back.

On the non-alcoholic side, the current seasonal menu — which rotates alongside roughly nine alcoholic house creations — carries two named zero-proof drinks: "Double Time" (zero-proof tequila, strawberry, vinegar, sparkling water), created by bartender Drew Bennett, and the "Phony Negroni," a bubbly non-alcoholic Negroni served on tap. It's a small but genuine offering rather than a dedicated mocktail list, and the current beer and wine list does not include any 0.0%-ABV alcohol-free beer options.
venues.pressQuote: Anvil's ambitious cocktail program is what keeps its regulars coming in over and over again.

venues.name: Apéritif
venues.description: Apéritif is a cocktail-led restaurant and dessert bar in a second-floor suite in the University Hills complex on Shannon Road in south Durham, open from noon most days, and its printed drinks list ends with a "Mocktails" section of its own — on the current spring menu the Vampire, on fresh blackberries, honey, hibiscus, lemon and soda, and the Passionfruit Fizz, on passion fruit tea, lemon, honey and egg white, both at $9, with Untitled Art's non-alcoholic beer at $5 in the beer list. The winter card added a No-Jito and a hot Apple of My Pie, so the section moves with the season. It is a modest programme at a venue built around signature cocktails, sangria and wine, but it is printed and priced rather than improvised.
signatureDrinks: Vampire ($9) — fresh blackberries, honey simple, hibiscus, lemon, soda
Passionfruit Fizz ($9) — passion fruit tea, lemon juice, honey simple, egg white
Untitled Art Non-Alcoholic Beer ($5) — juicy IPA or grapefruit shandy
venues.longDescription:
Apéritif occupies a suite on the second floor of the University Hills complex on Shannon Road in south Durham, off University Drive, and describes itself to Discover Durham as an upscale neighbourhood bar bringing a downtown experience to its customers' backyard. It is a restaurant that leads with its bar and its desserts: a signature cocktail list, a seasonal one, a page of spritzes and sangrias, dessert cocktails, a long wine list by the glass and a beer list that runs from Allagash to Burial. It opens at noon from Tuesday to Saturday and at three on Sunday and Monday, and closes between nine and eleven.

The reason it is listed here is the section printed at the bottom of the cocktail page under the heading Mocktails. On the spring menu the bar publishes on its site — the most recent it has posted — there are two: the Vampire, fresh blackberries shaken with a honey syrup, hibiscus and lemon and topped with soda, and the Passionfruit Fizz, passion fruit tea with lemon, honey and egg white for the texture of a sour. Both are nine dollars. The winter card that preceded it carried four, adding a No-Jito on lime, mint, pomegranate and soda and a hot Apple of My Pie on cider with a cinnamon-anise syrup, lemon and vanilla, so the section changes with the season rather than sitting fixed.

The beer list is the other half of the offer. Untitled Art's non-alcoholic range is on the printed list at five dollars — a juicy IPA and a grapefruit shandy on the spring card, a mango dragonfruit sour on the winter one — which gives a non-drinker a second category rather than a single line of mocktails.

Be clear about what this is: a licensed restaurant and cocktail bar with a short printed mocktail section, not a destination for non-drinkers, and the kind of place that works for a mixed table where one or two people are ordering without alcohol. The menus were read from the venue's own site in September 2026; the spring card is the latest posted, so confirm the section when you arrive.
venues.pressQuote: an upscale neighborhood bar that brings a downtown experience to our customers' backyard in the University Hills complex

venues.name: Aperitivo
venues.description: Aperitivo is an Italian-inspired bar and cafe inside downtown Milwaukee's historic Pritzlaff Building, built around the European ritual of the pre-dinner drink. Alongside its wine, amari and vermouth, it keeps a standing lineup of house zero-proof cocktails built largely on Great Lakes Distillery's non-alcoholic Junipre spirit. The alcohol-free list runs from a berry-forward Dry Spritz to the winter-favorite Teetotal Toddy, plus an off-menu Lavender Espresso Martini that local press has singled out. It serves lunch, dinner and aperitivo hour Tuesday through Saturday.
venues.longDescription:
Aperitivo opened in 2020 inside the turn-of-the-century Pritzlaff Building at 311 N. Plankinton Ave., a partnership between building owner Kendall Breunig and restaurant-industry veteran Richard Kerhin. The room leans fully into the Italian aperitivo tradition — wine, amari, vermouth and European aperitifs paired with sandwiches, salads, pasta and hand-tossed pizza — served Tuesday through Saturday from 11 a.m. to 9 p.m., with a happy hour running afternoons midweek.

The non-alcoholic offering here is a genuine named menu rather than an afterthought. Managing partner Richard Kerhin and his team developed a set of zero-proof cocktails infused with juniper berries, ginseng, orange zest, cardamom, chili pepper and coriander, inspired in part by Milwaukee's own Great Lakes Distillery and its non-alcoholic botanical spirit, Junipre. The list has featured a Dry Spritz (cranberry, club soda, lime and rosemary), an N/A Mule (Junipre, Top Note ginger beer, lemon and lime), an N/A Tom Collins (Junipre, sour, club soda, lime and cherry) and the Teetotal Toddy (Junipre, chamomile tea, honey and lemon), described as the bar's most popular mocktail in the winter months. Zero-proof drinks run roughly $6 to $10.

Beyond the printed list, Aperitivo will make an off-menu Lavender Espresso Martini that OnMilwaukee highlighted in its Milwaukee mocktails coverage. The venue remains active in 2026, with current posted hours, recent Yelp reviews and Instagram activity through late June 2026, making it a reliable downtown stop for a well-made drink with or without alcohol.

venues.name: Apothéke
venues.description: Apothéke LA is the West Coast outpost of New York's apothecary-themed Apothéke, at 1746 North Spring Street in Chinatown, opened in 2018 by founder Christopher Tierney after a two-year search for the right Los Angeles site. The room is a Biedermeier-revival fantasy — sconces made from scientific boiling flasks holding glowing herbal tinctures, ornate wooden furniture, velvet cushions and curtains, tufted wallpaper, and a glowing 40-inch marble bar at the centre. CORRECTION: we previously listed The Healer and The Baron's Cure as its non-alcoholic drinks. Neither is on the current zero-proof menu, and The Baron's Cure now appears on the regular list as a fully alcoholic cocktail built on milk-washed bourbon, cognac and overproof rum. What exists instead is a printed "Free-Spirited List" of eight drinks, made from house-made ingredients using organic produce, herbs and botanicals: four tea-based Elixirs built on ashwagandha, schisandra, dandelion root and milk thistle, and four Tonics on named non-alcoholic gin, tequila, vermouth and Pentire. No prices are printed. Open Thursday to Sunday evenings; sophisticated attire encouraged.

venues.longDescription:
Apothéke opened its Los Angeles outpost in Chinatown in 2018, after founder Christopher Tierney spent more than two years hunting for the right site for a West Coast version of his New York bar. The room is the reason to go even before the drinks arrive: sconces made from scientific boiling flasks hold infused herbal tinctures that glow in the lamplight, and the rest is a Biedermeier-revival fantasy of ornate wooden furniture, velvet cushions, cascading velvet curtains and tufted wallpaper, with a glowing forty-inch marble bar at the centre. Its whole conceit is medicinal — cocktails are grouped as cures for what ails you, from stress relievers and stimulants to painkillers and euphorics. Head mixologist Nick O'Connor described the local intent at opening: in Los Angeles, juice culture and tonics and wellness are big, and their approach has always been to blend those worlds. It opens Thursday to Sunday evenings only, encourages sophisticated attire, and has paid parking on Naud Street behind the building.

Our previous entry needs correcting on two counts. We listed The Healer and The Baron's Cure as its non-alcoholic drinks; neither is on the current zero-proof menu, and The Baron's Cure now appears on the main list as a fully alcoholic cocktail built on milk-washed bourbon, cognac and overproof dark rum — not something to order expecting zero proof. And we described the bar as one where any cocktail can be made as a mocktail. That was the arrangement a reviewer found in early 2025, when there was no printed alcohol-free list and the bartender simply built to taste. It has since been formalised: there is now a printed Free-Spirited List of eight drinks, headed with the note that ingredients are house-made daily using organic produce, herbs and botanicals. Four are Elixirs, built on medicinal teas rather than spirits — ashwagandha with guarana, orange, turmeric, ginger and honey; schisandra with pineapple, aloe, cayenne and cider vinegar; dandelion root with green apple, aloe and mint; milk thistle with grapefruit, hemp milk and cayenne. The other four are Tonics on named non-alcoholic spirits, including one built entirely on Pentire's Adrift botanical with its Coastal Spritz aperitif, grapefruit, lime and sage. No prices are printed on the menu, so ask. The hemp milk in Elixir #4 is a seed-based plant milk, not a cannabis product.
venues.pressQuote: We appreciate that any cocktail on the menu here can be made into a mocktail. The Healer is similar to green juice with spinach, celery, ginger, and apple, while the Baron's Cure has more intensity with black tea, allspice, and star anise.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: The Infatuation, Where To Drink The Best Mocktails In Los Angeles

venues.name: Arbella
venues.description: Arbella is a globally inspired cocktail lounge in River North with a dedicated six-drink zero-proof menu, dim lighting, DJ sets, and small plates — a full night out that doesn't require alcohol.
venues.longDescription:
Arbella occupies a stylish stretch of W Grand Ave in River North, and for non-drinkers it punches well above the typical 'we have mocktails' disclaimer. The bar launched a standalone zero-proof menu — six cocktails with full ingredient builds — that gets updated alongside the boozy program. That decision signals a kitchen and bar team that treats the NA side as a creative exercise, not an afterthought, making it a rare River North stop where sober or sober-curious guests can order off the actual menu rather than asking what can be made without alcohol.

The zero-proof lineup is where Arbella earns its NA credentials. Smoking Kills layers lemon-ginger kombucha with fresh lime, ginger beer, and infused smoke for something genuinely complex. Secret Window uses a London Dry spirit-free base with hibiscus, Peachtree sipping vinegar, and citrus — tart and aromatic. Glad Matt Is Gone-Lada is the crowd-pleaser: ube syrup, oat milk, pineapple, lime, soda water, and cinnamon in a large-format pour that reviewers have specifically called out as a repeat order. Bartender Eric Trousdale, who has represented Arbella in the bar's Global Guest Bartender Series alongside Chicago luminaries, oversees the cocktail side of the program.

Arbella runs the full River North evening arc — it opens as a lounge with happy hour (Mon–Fri, 4–6pm), then transitions into a club-leaning space with live DJ sets Thursday through Saturday. The interior is dim, decorated with funky art and floor-to-ceiling liquor bottles, and seating is tight enough that walk-ins on weekends are a gamble; reservations via Tock or the official site are accepted for parties of six or fewer. It works equally well for a first date, a post-work debrief, or a late night out, and the globally inspired small plates (pork belly bao, crab rangoon, lamb tacos) are substantial enough to anchor the experience.
venues.pressQuote: The lounge's bold NA drink lineup includes Smoking Kills (lemon-ginger kombucha, lime, ginger beer, infused smoke) and Secret Window (London Dry spirit-free, hibiscus, Peachtree sipping vinegar, fruit).

venues.name: Arcadia
venues.description: Arcadia is a Congress Street arcade bar — pinball, cabinets, a full bar — and its zero-proof list is genuinely composed rather than assembled. The Mock Trial balances bitter Stappi, the Italian red soda that has become a bartender's shortcut to real bitterness, against fluffy pineapple; there is a Watermelon Mojito, and a Coffee Tonic built on nitro cold brew with Fever-Tree tonic and cane syrup. The format matters as much as the drinks: an arcade bar gives the evening a purpose beyond the glass, which is the single most useful thing a venue can offer someone who is not drinking.
signatureDrinks: The Mock Trial - bitter Stappi soda, fluffy pineapple
Coffee Tonic - nitro cold brew, Fever-Tree tonic, cane syrup
venues.longDescription:
Arcadia occupies a stretch of Congress Street in Portland's Arts District and runs on the arcade-bar model: rows of pinball machines and cabinets, a proper bar, and an evening that is structured around playing rather than drinking. That structure is worth more to a non-drinker than most dedicated mocktail menus, because the hardest part of a sober night out is rarely the drink itself — it is sitting in a room where the only activity is drinking.

The zero-proof list is better than the format requires. The Mock Trial is built on Stappi, an Italian red bitter soda that has quietly become one of the most useful products in alcohol-free bartending: it delivers genuine bitterness, which is the quality that separates an adult drink from a soft one and the thing sugar-heavy mocktails always lack. Pairing it against pineapple gives the drink both bite and body.

The Coffee Tonic is the other one worth ordering. Nitro cold brew with Fever-Tree tonic and cane syrup is a combination that sounds wrong and works — the nitrogen gives it a soft, beer-like texture, the quinine in the tonic adds its own bitterness, and the result is dry, complex and nothing like a soda. There is also a Watermelon Mojito for anyone who wants something straightforwardly refreshing.

Hours suit a real night out: 5pm to midnight most days, to 1am Wednesday through Saturday, closed Tuesdays. It is a short walk from the rest of the Arts District and from Tandem's Congress Street bakery, and it is one of the few Portland venues where a non-drinker can comfortably still be out at half past midnight with something decent in hand. The games also solve the other problem with late sober nights, which is having something to do with your hands once the conversation runs down.
venues.pressQuote: Divided into classics, house cocktails and highballs, most drinks were in the $12-$14 range
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Portland Press Herald, Bar Guide, October 2023

venues.name: Arcana Bar and Lounge
venues.description: Arcana is a basement cocktail bar and tarot lounge on West Main Street in downtown Durham, entrance around the rear of the building, and non-alcoholic is one of the four top-level sections of its drinks menu — level with seasonal and signature, classics and twists, and beer and wine. Its own menu index bills the section as inventive cocktails without the booze, and Discover Durham names it beside The Velvet Hippo for a dedicated non-alcoholic menu that rivals anything with a proof. We do not name the drinks here on purpose: the section's individual builds do not render on the bar's website and the menu images it hosts date from 2023, so the honest position is that the programme is real and the list changes with the season. Ask at the bar. Open six to midnight most nights, from five on Friday and Saturday, closed Mondays.
venues.longDescription:
Arcana is a dark, low-ceilinged bar in a basement on West Main Street in downtown Durham, with the entrance around the rear of the building. It runs tarot readings alongside the drinks and has built a following as much for the atmosphere as the cocktails, and its non-alcoholic list is structurally serious in a way that is easy to verify: on its own menu, "non-alcoholic" is one of only four sections, sitting level with seasonal and signature, classics and twists, and beer and wine.

That structure is the strongest signal a bar can send about how it treats non-drinkers. A zero-proof drink at Arcana is not a modification of something else or a line at the bottom of the page; it is one quarter of what the bar publishes. The menu index describes the section as inventive cocktails without the booze, and Discover Durham, the city's tourism board, names Arcana in the same breath as The Velvet Hippo for non-alcoholic menus that rival anything with a proof.

The bar keeps late, consistent hours — six until midnight most nights, from five on Friday and Saturday, closed Mondays — and the room is small, so it fills. Access is worth planning for: the entrance is at the rear of the building, and the bar asks that you call ahead if you need the elevator.

We have not published the drink names here, and that is deliberate. Arcana's menu is not readable from its website — the section exists in the navigation but the individual drinks do not render — and the responsible thing is to tell you the programme is real rather than to invent a list. Ask at the bar, or email ahead; the drinks change with the seasonal list.
venues.pressQuote: dedicated non-alcoholic menus that rival anything with a proof

venues.name: ARCO Cocktail Lounge + Coastal Fare
venues.description: ARCO is a cocktail lounge and coastal-seafood room set inside an 1860 Victorian building on Bay Street, entered off Factor's Walk and framed by the brick arches and vaults that give it its name, with the Savannah River below. It is part of the Ele & the Chef restaurant collection. The cocktail menu is organised into four named categories — Classics, Signature, Light and Moderate, and Non-Alcoholic — so the alcohol-free drinks are a standing section of the list rather than a request, and the low-ABV tier sits between them for anyone moderating rather than abstaining. The room opens in the late afternoon and runs to 10pm, or 11pm on Fridays.
venues.longDescription:
The stretch of Bay Street above Factor's Walk is one of the oldest built environments in Savannah, and ARCO occupies a Victorian building from 1860 on the river side of it. You come through an arched doorway into a room defined by its structure — soaring brick arches and vaults framing the water — which is where the name comes from. It is the most recent opening from the Ele & the Chef restaurant collection, and the food is coastal: seafood-forward, hyper-local, deliberately pared back.

What earns it a listing here is the shape of the drinks menu rather than any single drink. ARCO sorts its cocktails into four named categories — Classics, Signature, Light and Moderate, and Non-Alcoholic — which is a more useful structure than most bars manage. The Light and Moderate tier matters as much as the zero-proof one: it gives a drinker who is cutting down, rather than stopping, somewhere to land that is not a compromise between a full-strength cocktail and a soda. Savannah's tourism board picked the room out for exactly this, and named the Hudson Express, a build of pineapple, orange, coconut water, orgeat and fresh citrus, among its zero-proof drinks.

A caveat this listing carries deliberately: ARCO's cocktail card is published as an image dated 2026 and its individual drink names could not be read from a live text menu at the time of writing, so no signature drinks are recorded here. The evidence for the section itself is solid and comes from three independent sources — the tourism board, the Savannah Chamber listing and the venue's own published menu structure — but the specific names are the kind of thing that rotates, and this directory does not publish a drink it has not seen on a current menu.

One practical note: the lounge is closed Monday to Wednesday and does not open before 4pm on the days it trades, so it is a Thursday-to-Sunday proposition rather than a reliable weeknight stop.

It is worth saying plainly why the four-category structure is the thing being recommended here. Most bars that claim to look after non-drinkers keep one or two mocktails at the foot of a list and rebuild them whenever the menu turns over. A named category commits the bar to filling it every time the card is reprinted, and a Light and Moderate tier alongside it commits to the much larger group of people who are drinking less rather than not at all. ARCO is the only room in this guide that has formalised both.
venues.pressQuote: ARCO - Cocktail Lounge + Coastal Fare is a mood-setting good time offering a sexy take on lounging while sipping.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Visit Savannah, Where to Find Incredible Mocktails in Savannah

venues.name: Ardsley Station
venues.description: Ardsley Station is a neighbourhood restaurant on Victory Drive at the edge of Ardsley Park, away from the tourist blocks, serving Southern plates with local produce from 11am to 10pm every day of the week. Its drinks list prints a section headed Zero-Proof carrying three built cocktails between $8.90 and $9.90 — a rosemary-and-orgeat citrus drink, a seasonal-fruit build on Amethyst's blueberry-ginger botanical, and a cucumber-shrub spritz — alongside Athletic Brewing's New Dawn alcohol-free beer at $4.90 in the beer and seltzer section. The all-day hours make it one of the more reliably open zero-proof lists in the city.
signatureDrinks: Cit-rus Got Real — rosemary, orgeat, lemon, soda
Downshift — Amethyst blueberry-ginger, seasonal fruit, lemon, mint, soda
Garden Party — cucumber shrub, ginger, pomegranate, lemon, soda

naMenuItems.name: Athletic New Dawn
naMenuItems.description: non-alcoholic

venues.longDescription:
Most of Savannah's zero-proof drinking happens downtown, inside hotels or on rooftops that fill with visitors after five. Ardsley Station is the neighbourhood counterweight: a corner restaurant on Victory Drive at the northern edge of Ardsley Park, a residential grid of oaks and 1920s houses about two miles south of the squares, serving locals for lunch as readily as dinner.

The alcohol-free drinks are printed under their own Zero-Proof heading and priced just under the cocktails, between $8.90 and $9.90. Cit-rus Got Real is the plainest and the best-balanced — rosemary, orgeat, lemon and soda, an almond-and-herb sour with no attempt to imitate a spirit. Downshift is the one that changes: it is built on Amethyst's blueberry-ginger botanical spirit with lemon, mint and whatever fruit is in season, so the drink you get in August is not the drink you get in February. Garden Party is a cucumber shrub with ginger, pomegranate and lemon, lengthened with soda. To those the bar adds Athletic Brewing's New Dawn at $4.90, listed in the Beer and Seltzers section rather than sidelined.

The list is a good illustration of how quickly this category moves. Savannah's tourism guide credits Ardsley Station with a House Cherry Limeade and a High Tea built on a pumpkin-spice shrub; neither is on the current menu, and Downshift itself has changed base spirit since the drink was first written up — it ran on a Dhos aperitivo in an earlier version. The section survived; the recipes did not.

The hours are the practical advantage. Eleven in the morning to ten at night, seven days a week, in a city where the better bar programmes do not unlock their doors until four.
venues.pressQuote: A local gem serving mouth-watering dishes with fresh local ingredients is Ardsley Station.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Visit Savannah, Where to Find Incredible Mocktails in Savannah

venues.name: Arizona Wilderness Brewing — DTPHX
venues.description: The downtown Phoenix pub from one of Arizona's most acclaimed breweries — and one of the few anywhere that brews its own non-alcoholic beer rather than stocking someone else's. Arizona Wilderness released ARIZO[NA], billed as the state's first non-alcoholic IPA, with bright citrus, balanced bitterness and a snappy finish, and donates 2 percent of its sales to the Arizona Trail Association every year. The taproom also pours Wild Water, a zero-proof sparkling water hopped with El Dorado and Mosaic. Founded in 2013 by Jonathan Buford and Patrick Ware and named Best New Brewery in the World by RateBeer within months of opening, the company built its identity on water stewardship in a drought state — its slogan is "Drink Like You Care".
venues.longDescription:
Arizona Wilderness Brewing was founded in 2013 by Jonathan Buford and Patrick Ware, and within months of opening a small brewpub in Gilbert it was named Best New Brewery in the World by RateBeer. What it became known for afterwards was less the beer than the water. In a state where drought is the permanent condition, the brewery built its whole identity around consumption — brewing with Arizona-grown Sinagua Malt, and converting an alfalfa farm to malt production in a switch that saves an estimated 100 million gallons a year that would otherwise be drawn from the Verde River. The company slogan, "Drink Like You Care", is the argument rather than the decoration.

The downtown Phoenix pub on Roosevelt Row is where that programme meets a bar. The reason it belongs on a non-alcoholic directory is specific and rare: this is a brewery that makes its own alcohol-free beer instead of buying in a national brand for the fridge. ARIZO[NA] is billed as the state's first non-alcoholic IPA — bright citrus, real bitterness, a dry finish rather than the sweet flatness that afflicts a lot of NA beer — and 2 percent of its sales go to the Arizona Trail Association each year. Alongside it the taproom pours Wild Water, a zero-proof sparkling water hopped with El Dorado and Mosaic, which scratches the same itch without pretending to be beer at all.

That combination matters in a taproom setting more than almost anywhere else. A brewery is the hardest room in which to not drink — the entire social ritual is a flight of the thing you are declining — and being handed a house-brewed pint that the brewers are proud of rather than a can from the bottom shelf changes the evening completely. It remains a working brewery with a full beer list, so this is not an alcohol-free venue; it is a venue where not drinking costs you nothing.
venues.pressQuote: Our focus is on saving the planet.

venues.name: Armadillo Den
venues.description: Armadillo Den is a three-acre outdoor entertainment complex on Menchaca Road in far South Austin, opened in December 2020 by partner Brett Berry. The two-story bar is a neighborhood gathering spot known for live music seven nights a week, five rotating on-site food trucks (including Biggie's Yardbird, Via 313, and Los Danzantes), a large off-leash dog park, yard games, and a 13-foot LED TV wall for watch parties. Visit Austin recognizes Armadillo Den for its award-winning draft mocktail program — a relatively rare commitment in Texas, where most NA options are made glass-by-glass rather than poured from a tap. Signature NA cocktails include the Frescadillo Paloma (pink grapefruit, sea salt) and Ford's Ranch Water (Thai basil sparkling water, cucumber). The space is kid-friendly until 6pm Monday through Friday, and the dog-park-and-food-trucks setup makes it one of South Austin's most family- and group-friendly bars regardless of whether you're drinking alcohol.
signatureDrinks: Frescadillo Paloma (NA: pink grapefruit, sea salt)
Ford's Ranch Water (NA: Thai basil sparkling water, cucumber)
venues.longDescription:
Armadillo Den is a three-acre outdoor entertainment complex on Menchaca Road in far South Austin, opened in December 2020 by partner Brett Berry. The two-storey bar anchors live music seven nights a week, five rotating food trucks including Biggie's Yardbird, Via 313 and Los Danzantes, a large off-leash dog park, yard games and a thirteen-foot LED wall for watch parties.

The thing that earns it a place here is technical: Armadillo Den runs a draft mocktail programme, and Visit Austin calls it award-winning. Non-alcoholic drinks are almost universally built glass by glass, which makes them slow, inconsistent between bartenders, and the first thing dropped when a bar gets busy. Putting them on tap solves all three at once — the drink is pre-batched, carbonated under pressure and pulled in seconds, so it arrives as fast as a beer and tastes the same every time.

On a three-acre site with live music and a queue, that is not a detail. It is the difference between a non-drinker getting a considered drink and getting a soda because the bar is slammed. Very few venues in Texas have made that investment.

The drinks themselves are built for the climate. The Frescadillo Paloma runs pink grapefruit with sea salt — salt rather than sugar, which is what makes a paloma refreshing rather than cloying in August heat. Ford's Ranch Water pairs Thai basil sparkling water with cucumber, a zero-proof reading of the West Texas ranch water that is otherwise tequila, lime and Topo Chico.

The rest of the setup is unusually easy for mixed groups. It is kid-friendly until 6pm Monday to Friday, the dog park and food trucks give an evening somewhere to go that is not the bar, and the whole thing is outdoors. Open from 4pm on weekdays and from noon at weekends, to midnight or later.
venues.pressQuote: Armadillo Den is a year-round favorite for its award-winning draft mocktail program. Grab the Frescadillo Paloma or Ford's Ranch Water for sipping in their expansive back yard.

venues.name: Around the Kava Bowl
venues.description: Around the Kava Bowl is a fully alcohol-free kava bar in Captain Cook, twelve miles up the hill from Kailua-Kona, serving fresh Hawaiian and Pacific kava since 2019. It operates from the back of the Hoʻo Hui wellness centre — the old Captain Cook courthouse building on Mamalahoa Highway, across from the NAPA auto parts store — and trades on being the cooler, quieter alternative when the Kona coast is too hot. Its own stated purpose is to create and nurture ʻohana through community, culture and oneness around the kava bowl. Posted hours are not reliably published, so call ahead. Kava contains no alcohol but is psychoactive and mildly sedating.
venues.longDescription:
Around the Kava Bowl has been serving kava in Captain Cook since 2019, from a room at the back of the Hoʻo Hui wellness centre on Mamalahoa Highway — the heritage building that used to be the Captain Cook courthouse, across the road from NAPA auto parts. Captain Cook sits about twelve miles and a good deal of elevation above Kailua-Kona, and the bar leans into that: its own pitch is that when it is too hot down in Kona you come up the hill to cool off with kava and friends. On an island where most visitor-facing drinking happens at sea level in a resort, that is a genuinely different evening.

The kava is fresh Hawaiian and other Pacific root, prepared from powder, and nothing served contains alcohol. The bar states its purpose directly — to create and nurture ʻohana through a strong sense of community, culture and oneness around the kava bowl — and its own writing about kava is unusually careful for a business selling it, describing the plant as a vital part of ancient and modern Polynesian culture that travelled with Pacific voyagers, and being plain that the effects are mildly sedative, anaesthetic and euphoric and that the taste runs somewhere between cucumber water, potato peels, black pepper and earth. That is a more honest tasting note than most kava bars print.

Two practical notes. Opening hours are not reliably published anywhere we can verify — the website, the listings and the review sites all disagree or stay silent — so this is a phone-ahead venue rather than a turn-up one, particularly if you are driving up from Kona for it. And it is a small room inside a wellness centre rather than a standalone bar, which suits a quiet couple of hours better than a large group.

The usual caution applies and the bar states most of it itself. Kava contains no alcohol but is psychoactive: a mild sedative that should not be combined with alcohol or with sedating medication, and worth planning the drive back down the hill around rather than setting off immediately after.
venues.pressQuote: We are Sage and Jenna, a husband and wife team living our dreams to build a community space where we can share our passion for kava
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Around the Kava Bowl, About page (company statement)

venues.name: Art Haus Bar
venues.description: Art Haus is a downtown Boise cocktail bar whose two named alcohol-free drinks are both built around aromatics rather than sugar — a Chamomile Cordial, and Golden Hour, which layers pomegranate and grapefruit with orange blossom water and cardamom over soda. Orange blossom water and cardamom are the giveaway: they are perfume-adjacent ingredients used in small measures for scent, and reaching for them signals a bar solving the real problem with zero-proof drinks, which is that removing alcohol removes aroma as much as it removes warmth. Note that some local guides list a Grove Street address; the Main Street location is the one recorded here. Open Wednesday to Saturday only.

venues.longDescription:
Art Haus is a cocktail bar in downtown Boise, associated with the Kin group, and its alcohol-free drinks are more thoughtfully constructed than most cities of this size manage.

Golden Hour is the one to read closely: pomegranate, grapefruit, orange blossom water, cardamom, soda. The first two are the body of the drink, tart and slightly bitter. The last two are doing something different. Orange blossom water and cardamom are aromatic ingredients used in tiny quantities — you smell them before you taste them, and they carry a drink's character in the nose.

That matters because of a specific fact about alcohol. Ethanol is volatile: it carries aromatic compounds up out of the glass, which is a large part of why a spirit-based cocktail smells of something from a foot away. Take the alcohol out and the aroma largely stays in the liquid. The bars that solve this reach for intensely aromatic ingredients that project on their own — orange blossom, cardamom, rose, smoked salt, high-oil citrus peel. A menu using them is not decorating; it is compensating for the specific thing that was removed.

The Chamomile Cordial takes a similar route by different means, using a floral infusion as the drink's spine rather than as a garnish.

A note on the address: some local guides list Art Haus at 610 West Grove Street, but the location recorded here is 999 West Main Street. Worth confirming before a trip. Hours are Wednesday to Saturday only, 4pm to 11pm, closed Sunday through Tuesday. That four-night window is the main constraint, so check before crossing town — but within it this is among the more thoughtful zero-proof lists in the state.
venues.pressQuote: KIN's Art Haus Bar is another good spot if you want something crafted with thought and expertise instead of a soda that costs seven dollars
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: City Cast Boise, Bars With Non-Alcoholic Drinks for a Fun Dry January, January 2024

venues.name: Artesian
venues.description: Artesian opened in 2008 as the bar of The Langham, the grande-dame hotel on Portland Place that has been synonymous with London glamour since 1865, and takes its name from the 360-foot artesian well that once drew the purest water in the city from beneath the hotel's foundations. The room was designed by David Collins Studio as a Victorian cabinet of curiosities: a soaring pagoda-topped bar, jewelled mirrored panelling, blue-and-purple faux-crocodile tiling, chinoiserie detail and its signature deep-purple leather chairs beneath high ceilings and tall bay windows. It is one of the most decorated cocktail bars in the world, named The World's Best Bar for four consecutive years from 2012 to 2015. Head bartender Giulia Cuccurullo's "Ultimo" menu includes dedicated non-alcoholic serves: Currant, a booze-free paloma with Smiling Wolf agave and London Essence raspberry-rose soda, and an effervescent Apple built on Lyre's American Malt and Amaretto with Wignac cider.

Cherry on Top (available in a non-alcoholic version)
Bespoke non-alcoholic cocktails made to order
venues.longDescription:
Artesian opened in 2008 as the bar of The Langham, London — the grande-dame hotel on Portland Place that has been synonymous with glamour since 1865 — and takes its name from the 360-foot artesian well that once drew the purest water in the city from beneath the hotel's foundations. The room was designed by David Collins Studio as a Victorian cabinet of curiosities: a soaring pagoda-topped bar, jewelled mirrored panelling, blue-and-purple faux-crocodile tiling, chinoiserie detail and its signature deep-purple leather chairs beneath high ceilings and tall bay windows. It is one of the most decorated cocktail bars in the world, having been named The World's Best Bar for four consecutive years, from 2012 to 2015, in the World's 50 Best Bars ranking. The programme is now led by head bartender Giulia Cuccurullo, who joined in 2018 and took charge in 2021, and who was the global winner of the Patrón Perfectionist competition in 2020.

The draw is a rotating, tightly themed cocktail list rather than a fixed roster. The current menu, Ultimo, comprises 16 cocktails, each built around a single spotlighted ingredient that is preserved, transformed and layered using precise techniques to coax out unexpected dimensions of flavour, with sustainability and the reuse of underused ingredients running through the whole list. It follows a lineage of playfully cerebral menus — earlier serves have leaned on everything from chicory, pumpkin, daikon and marshmallow to rooibos tea, Oloroso sherry and porcini mushroom — so the house style is precise, ingredient-driven and designed to subvert expectations rather than to chase novelty for its own sake.

Artesian is a full-spectrum cocktail bar rather than a dedicated alcohol-free venue, but its low- and no-alcohol options are taken seriously. The standing Low ABV list runs a Seedlip and Fever-Tree tonic (Seedlip being the London-made non-alcoholic distilled spirit) and a low-alcohol Atopia and Fever-Tree tonic, alongside Lucky Saint 0.5% non-alcoholic lager, a London Essence jasmine and white peach soda, and a craft-beer shandy from Shandy Shack. Beyond that printed list the menu states plainly that "we can do several non alcoholic cocktails so please do ask one of our team members," so the team will build bespoke zero-proof serves to order, and several signature cocktails — such as the Cherry on Top, layered around a cherry-pistachio cordial — can be prepared in an alcohol-free version. There is no separately published zero-proof cocktail card, so the surest route to a genuinely good alcohol-free drink here is to tell the bartender what you like and let them mix to order.
venues.pressQuote: Using everything from chicory and pumpkin to daikon and marshmallow, each drink is designed to subvert expectations

venues.name: Arwa Yemeni Coffee
venues.description: Arwa Yemeni Coffee is a late-night Yemeni coffeehouse in Brookline's Coolidge Corner, opened in March 2026 as the first Massachusetts outpost of a small Texas-based chain. No alcohol is served, and the room is built for staying: the kitchen and bar run past 10pm every night of the week and to midnight on Fridays and Saturdays. The list is anchored in Yemeni coffee tradition. Jubani is a spiced blend brewed with coffee husks; mofawer is a kettle-brewed medium roast infused with cardamom, cinnamon and fresh ginger and finished with milk; qishr is the caffeine-light husk brew. Adeni teas are milk-based black brews carrying a warm spice blend and a frothy cardamom syrup. Modern drinks sit beside them, including pistachio, salted caramel and Fruity Pebbles lattes, blueberry matcha and limeade, alongside sweet and savory pastries.
signatureDrinks: Jubani (spiced coffee blend brewed with coffee husks)
Mofawer (kettle-brewed coffee with milk, cardamom, cinnamon, fresh ginger and sugar)
Qishr (caffeine-light brew made from spiced coffee husks)
Adeni chai (milk-based black tea with warm spices and cardamom syrup)
venues.longDescription:
Arwa Yemeni Coffee opened at 1333 Beacon Street in mid-March 2026, taking a storefront in the middle of Coolidge Corner between Lee's Burgers and Maguro. The Arwa brand was launched in Texas by a group of Yemeni founders, and the Brookline store is run by franchisee Zaid Baara, a pharmacist who told Brookline.News he took the site specifically because Massachusetts offers so few places to sit with friends after dark that are not bars. That gap is the whole proposition here: an alcohol-free room with table service, a long counter and a crowd that turns over late, in a neighborhood where most cafes shut by six. The cafe is part of a wider wave of Yemeni coffeehouses opening across American metros, and it is the first of them to land inside Boston's inner ring.

The drinks follow Yemeni coffee practice rather than third-wave espresso convention. Jubani is a spiced blend brewed together with coffee husks; mofawer is brewed in a kettle with milk, cardamom, cinnamon, fresh ginger and sugar until it turns creamy; qishr is a low-caffeine infusion of husks and spice that works as an evening drink. The adeni teas are milk-based black brews built on a house warm-spice blend and topped with a whipped cardamom syrup. Alongside those sit the drinks that pull the student crowd, including pistachio, salted caramel and Fruity Pebbles lattes, blueberry matcha and a house limeade, plus a pastry case of sweet and savory bakes. The Boston Globe covered the opening on May 12, 2026 under the headline 'Arwa Yemeni Coffee opens in Brookline's Coolidge Corner,' and Brookline.News followed on May 26 with a report on the crowds it was drawing on weeknights. The Brookline store is the chain's first in New England; its other locations are concentrated in Texas, and Baara told the Globe he moved on the site because so few places in Massachusetts stay open late that are not bars.
venues.pressQuote: Late night culture in general is very Middle Eastern.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Zaid Baara, Arwa Yemeni Coffee Brookline franchisee

venues.name: Arwa Yemeni Coffee
venues.description: Arwa Yemeni Coffee is an alcohol-free Yemeni coffeehouse on Milwaukee Avenue in Bucktown, the Chicago city location of a chain that began in Richardson, Texas as the first Yemeni coffee shop in that state and has since opened in Illinois, Massachusetts, Connecticut and California. The menu is split into traditional Yemeni drinks, iced refreshers, house signatures and espresso classics: jubani, qishr, mofawer, adeni tea and sana'ani coffee sit alongside a Yemeni latte, a date matcha latte and the Sand Dune latte. Arwa's rooms are designed for sitting and staying, several of them built around jelsa rooms for traditional floor seating. It keeps late hours by cafe standards, running to 10pm most nights and to midnight on Friday and Saturday. No alcohol is served.
venues.longDescription:
Arwa Yemeni Coffee started in Richardson, Texas, where the original store - billed by the company as the first Yemeni coffee shop in the state - roasts on site in the Dallas-Fort Worth suburbs and pairs the counter with an outdoor courtyard. From there the chain expanded across Texas and into Illinois, Massachusetts, Connecticut and California, with several of its rooms built around a private Arabic jelsa space for traditional low floor seating. The Chicago store sits at 1953 N Milwaukee Ave in Bucktown, on the diagonal that carries most of the neighborhood's bar traffic, which puts an entirely alcohol-free room directly in the path of a nightlife corridor.

The menu is organized the way the category tends to be. A Traditional Drinks section carries jubani, qishr, red tea, mofawer, adeni tea and sana'ani coffee - the spiced teas and husk infusions that Yemeni coffeehouses are built on, several of them milk-based and served hot. An Ice Refreshers section lists the Dragon's Blood Refresher, limeade, a manga smoothie and ginger lime. The Arwa Signatures list holds the house-specific drinks: a Yemeni latte, a date matcha latte and the Sand Dune latte. Behind that sits a full classics list of drip coffee, americano, cappuccino, chai latte, matcha latte, espresso, pour over, latte and steamed hot chocolate, so a group that splits between traditional and familiar can order from one counter. Nothing on the menu contains alcohol. The room runs until 10pm Sunday through Thursday and until midnight on Friday and Saturday, which is late enough to work as an actual destination rather than a daytime coffee stop - the reason this category has become one of the most reliable sources of genuinely alcohol-free nightlife in large American cities. Because the room runs until midnight on Friday and Saturday it works as a late stop on a corridor otherwise given over to bars, and because nothing behind the counter contains alcohol there is no menu to interrogate before ordering. The company sells its beans and gift cards through its own site, and several of its stores are built around a private Arabic jelsa room for traditional low seating, with at least one adding a dedicated prayer and reflection room.

venues.name: Assembly Rooftop Lounge
venues.description: Assembly is the rooftop lounge on top of the Logan Hotel, looking across Logan Square to the Art Museum and the Parkway, and it runs to two in the morning on Friday and Saturday. Its menu carries a printed section headed "Non-Alcoholic Imbibements" — a deliberately unapologetic name for a category usually labelled as an afterthought. The Strawberry Ginger Smash at $12 muddles strawberry with ginger and lemon over ginger beer; the Cucumber Mint 'Gin' Spritz at $14 runs cucumber and mint with lime and lemon-lime soda. A rooftop is one of the better settings for an evening without alcohol, because the view supplies the reason to be there and nobody is standing at a bar.

Cucumber Mint 'Gin' Spritz ($14) — cucumber, mint, lime, lemon-lime soda

venues.longDescription:
Assembly sits on the roof of the Logan Hotel on Benjamin Franklin Parkway, with sightlines down the boulevard to the Philadelphia Museum of Art and across Logan Square's fountain. It opens at four in the afternoon and runs until midnight midweek and two in the morning on Friday and Saturday, which makes it one of the genuinely late rooms in this part of the city.

The drinks menu prints a section headed "Non-Alcoholic Imbibements", and the phrasing is worth noting. Most bars file these drinks under "mocktails", a word that carries a faint apology in it — the mock prefix concedes that the drink is an imitation of something better. Calling them imbibements instead is a small thing, but it signals a kitchen that has thought about how the order feels to the person placing it.

There are two builds. The Strawberry Ginger Smash at twelve dollars muddles strawberry with ginger and lemon and lengthens it with ginger beer — a smash in the proper sense, where the fruit is broken up in the glass rather than pre-juiced, so the drink changes as the ice melts. The Cucumber Mint 'Gin' Spritz at fourteen puts cucumber and mint against lime with lemon-lime soda; the quotation marks around 'Gin' are the menu's own, acknowledging that it is reaching for a gin-and-tonic's cool herbaceous register without a spirit in it.

Two drinks is a short list, and it is fair to say so. What compensates is the setting, and this is the real argument for a rooftop as a place to spend an evening without drinking. The view is the event. There is no bar to prop up, the seating is arranged outward rather than inward, and the reason everyone came is visible over the parapet rather than sitting in a glass. The hardest part of not drinking is rarely the drink itself — it is the hours between nine and midnight when a group has run out of things to do except order another round. A rooftop at two in the morning solves that better than a longer mocktail list would.
venues.pressQuote: Assembly sits atop the Logan Hotel and looks down at the busy Benjamin Franklin Parkway, open for happy hour and 90-minute seatings every day starting at 4 pm
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Thrillist, The Best Rooftop Bars in Philly, May 2021

venues.name: Atelier Manna
venues.description: Atelier Manna is a brunch-only "chef's workshop" in the Leucadia stretch of Encinitas, opened in April 2023 by husband-and-wife team Andrew and Larah Bachelier and awarded a Bib Gourmand in the 2025 Michelin Guide. Andrew Bachelier, previously of Michelin-starred Jeune et Jolie, runs the kitchen on a "food as medicine" philosophy — and the defining feature is that Atelier Manna serves no alcohol at all. Instead, its beverage list is a rotating menu of "vitality tonics," spirit-free drinks built like bar cocktails from the same produce used in the kitchen: recent pours include Zanzibar (cold brew, red ginseng, cinnamon, tulsi), Veracruz (dragonfruit, hoja santa, toasted juniper, ginger), Jasper, and Goldenrod. San Diego Magazine called it one of the most ambitious zero-proof drink rosters in the city.
venues.address: 1076 N Coast Hwy 101, Ste 101, Encinitas, CA 92024
venues.longDescription:
Atelier Manna is a brunch-only chef's workshop on the Leucadia stretch of North Coast Highway 101 in Encinitas, opened in April 2023 by the husband-and-wife team of Andrew and Larah Bachelier and awarded a Bib Gourmand in the 2025 Michelin Guide. Andrew Bachelier came from the Michelin-starred Jeune et Jolie, and he runs the kitchen on a food-as-medicine philosophy that shows up in the sourcing and the plating rather than in any wellness posturing. The defining fact, and the reason this restaurant matters well beyond San Diego, is that it serves no alcohol at all — not a reduced list, not a token pair of options, none. For a Michelin-recognised restaurant to make that choice and then win a Bib Gourmand is one of the more meaningful data points anyone can point to about where this category is going.

What replaces the wine list is a rotating menu of vitality tonics: spirit-free drinks built with the same construction logic as bar cocktails, from the same produce the kitchen is already using. Zanzibar layers cold brew with red ginseng, cinnamon and tulsi. Veracruz works dragonfruit against hoja santa, toasted juniper and ginger — a genuinely herbal, resinous drink rather than a sweet one. Jasper and Goldenrod round out a list that changes with what is available. The critical point is that these are designed as the restaurant's actual beverage programme, not as accommodations, and they are priced and presented accordingly. San Diego Magazine's Troy Johnson put the achievement precisely: "Without the breakfast charms of Champagne, they have created one of the most ambitious zero-proof drink rosters in the city." Brunch is the hardest meal for a non-drinker to enjoy socially, because mimosas and bloody marys are so embedded in it; Atelier Manna is one of very few places anywhere that has simply removed the problem. Wednesday to Sunday, mornings only.
venues.pressQuote: Without the breakfast charms of Champagne, they have created one of the most ambitious zero-proof drink rosters in the city.

venues.name: Atlas Bar
venues.description: Atlas Bar is a long-running gin specialist tucked into a Victorian railway arch on Deansgate, run since 2012 by Mark and Elaine Wrigley and now stocking more than 570 gins. Unusually for a gin saloon, it backs that up with a titled Low 'n' No section in its drinks booklet, with serves starting from around GBP 3.50. The alcohol-free spirits shelf runs to Gordon's 0.0, Tanqueray 0.0 and Tanqueray Sevilla 0.0, Warner 0.0, Whitley Neill Raspberry and Rhubarb & Ginger 0.0, Captain Morgan's 0.0, Deadman's Fingers Spiced Rum 0.0 and Myth Coconut Spirit, and the house gin paddle board comes in a 0.0 version - any three alcohol-free gins with a tonic, GBP 8. Alongside them sit six mocktails, eight non-alcoholic beers and ciders, and 0% sparkling wine and Copenhagen Sparkling Tea.

Pornstar (pineapple juice, vanilla syrup, lime, passion fruit puree, lemonade) GBP 7
