Raspberry Mint Fizz (raspberry syrup, mint, lime, lemon, soda) GBP 5
venues.longDescription:
Atlas Bar first opened in 1996 in the railway arches at the southern end of Deansgate, on a site that had earlier been an Atlas-branded car spare-parts shop. In its early years it was a pre-club haunt near the Hacienda and, by local lore, a regular of Factory Records boss Tony Wilson. Mark and Elaine Wrigley took the bar over in 2012 and remade it as a self-styled cafe, bar and gin saloon, opening with 28 gins - then 21 more than anyone else in the city centre and, as it turned out, just ahead of the national gin boom.

Today the back bar holds more than 570 gins, billed as the biggest collection in Manchester and catalogued in the bar's own 'Gin Bible', making Atlas one of the city's defining independent drinking rooms. The long, narrow arch keeps its brick-and-glass railway character and trades all day, from morning coffee through to late-night G&Ts, with a signature gin paddle board that lets drinkers flight three gins with matched garnishes and tonics.

What sets Atlas apart for non-drinkers is that the low-and-no list is treated as a proper part of the offer rather than an afterthought: the June 2026 drinks booklet gives it a titled Low 'n' No section with serves from around GBP 3.50. The alcohol-free spirits shelf runs to Gordon's 0.0, Tanqueray 0.0 and Tanqueray Sevilla 0.0, Warner 0.0, Whitley Neill Raspberry and Rhubarb & Ginger 0.0, Captain Morgan's 0.0, Deadman's Fingers Spiced Rum 0.0 and Myth Coconut Spirit, all available as bespoke alcohol-free gin and tonics - and the signature paddle board comes in a 0.0 version, any three alcohol-free gins with a tonic for GBP 8, so teetotal guests can taste several no-alcohol G&Ts side by side. Six mocktails sit under their own heading, including a Crodino Spritz built from Crodino and 0.0 prosecco, a Dark Mojito on Captain Morgan's Zero, a Pina Colada on Myth Coconut Spirit, and two lower-priced raspberry serves using Double Dutch tonics. Beyond the spirits there are eight non-alcoholic beers and ciders - Beavertown Lazer Crush, Birra Moretti 0.0, Corona Cero, Guinness 0.0, Heineken 0.0, Inches Cider zero, Old Mout and Peroni zero - plus Murviedro 0% sparkling in bottle and 200ml, Luna de Murviedro 0% rose sparkling, and Copenhagen Sparkling Tea 0%. The Seedlip, Everleaf and Tuscan Tree bottlings the bar poured in earlier years are not on the current booklet, and there is no Nogroni on it either; the range has shifted toward the big-house 0.0 expressions instead. Co-owner Elaine Wrigley has leaned into that shift, telling The Manc in January 2022 that the arrival of well-known brands making alcohol-free versions lets the bar push the boundaries of what it can serve non-drinkers.
venues.pressQuote: The emergence of known Gin brands creating zero alcohol alternatives, really does let us push the boundaries.

venues.name: Atlas
venues.description: Atlas is the cathedral-like Art Deco lobby bar inside Parkview Square's 'Gotham Building,' a fixture of The World's 50 Best Bars and home to an eight-metre gin tower. Its 2026 'Daughters of Atlas' menu deliberately moves zero-proof cocktails to the front of the list to include non-drinkers, built with the same precision as the alcoholic serves. Real alcohol-free options include the Vanda Mist (S$12 - grapefruit, almond syrup, salt, cinnamon and cream over crushed ice), the spiced-spirit Miss Rouge, and Hope On The Horizon (kombucha and yuzu), a champagne-cocktail alternative.
venues.address: Parkview Square, 600 North Bridge Road, Singapore 188778
signatureDrinks: Vanda Mist (S$12) - grapefruit, almond syrup, salt, cinnamon and cream over crushed ice
Miss Rouge - non-alcoholic spiced spirit, verjus, basil tea, salt, nasturtium leaf
Hope On The Horizon (S$14) - kombucha and yuzu, a champagne-cocktail alternative
venues.longDescription:
Set within the lobby of Parkview Square in Bugis - the ornate 1990s tower known locally as Singapore's 'Gotham Building' - Atlas opened in 2017 and looks straight out of The Great Gatsby, with soaring ceilings, gleaming gold, and an iconic eight-metre gin tower holding more than 1,300 bottles at the heart of the room. It has become one of the city's most decorated bars, ranking among The World's 50 Best Bars (No. 43 in 2024) and collecting design and industry honours over the years.

In June 2026 the bar unveiled 'Daughters of Atlas,' its first major menu refresh in years, created by head bartender Esmeralda Castrogiovanni, who arrived with more than a decade of experience including a stint at World No. 3 bar Sips in Barcelona. Structured as a seven-chapter collection of 16 signature drinks inspired by the seven daughters of the Greek titan, the menu makes a point of bringing zero-proof options to the front of the list to make the experience more inclusive for non-drinkers.

The non-alcoholic builds are treated with the same craft as the spirited ones. The Vanda Mist (S$12) is a bittersweet, creamy no-alcohol serve of fresh grapefruit, almond syrup, salt, cinnamon and cream over crushed ice, inspired by Singaporean motifs; Miss Rouge blends a non-alcoholic spiced spirit with verjus, basil tea and salt, finished with a nasturtium leaf; and Hope On The Horizon pairs kombucha and yuzu as a champagne-cocktail alternative. Alcohol-free interpretations run across the classic cocktail styles the bar is known for, so non-drinkers get a full parallel menu rather than an afterthought.

Atlas is open Monday afternoon through Saturday late (closed Sundays), and its grandeur, gin obsession and now front-and-centre zero-proof program make it a landmark stop for alcohol-free drinkers in Singapore.
venues.pressQuote: Zero-proof options are brought to the front of the menu to make the experience more inclusive for non-drinkers.

venues.name: Atoma
venues.description: Atoma is a contemporary restaurant inside a 100-year-old Craftsman house at 1411 N 45th Street in Wallingford, opened in November 2023 by chef Johnny Courtney and Sarah Courtney in the space that was long home to Tilth. Its James Beard record, stated precisely: the restaurant was a national FINALIST for Best New Restaurant in 2025, and Courtney was a FINALIST for Best Chef: Northwest and Pacific in 2026 — finalist in both cases, not winner, and both belong to Atoma rather than to its predecessor. Eater Seattle made it Restaurant of the Year for 2024. The cooking is precise and seasonal: a rosette cookie at $7, radish cake with geoduck at $9, grilled squash at $19, halibut at $49, and a family-style duck pot pie at $135. Its zero-proof cocktails are printed as their own section of the bar list — four of them, made by bar director Dillon Raaz: It's Grape(fruit) to See You (house grapefruit soda, DHOS Bittersweet), Forlorn George, Starr Pupil and a St. Agrestis Phony Espresso Negroni. No cocktail prices are published, alcoholic or otherwise. ACCESSIBILITY: the restaurant is not wheelchair accessible — every entrance requires a full flight of stairs.

venues.longDescription:
Atoma opened in November 2023 in a hundred-year-old Craftsman house on North 45th Street, and it took on a considerable inheritance: the building had been Tilth, one of the first all-organic restaurants in America. It has more than held the address. Eater Seattle named it Restaurant of the Year for 2024, writing that there are dozens of new American or Pacific Northwest restaurants in Seattle putting local and seasonal ingredients first, but that Atoma just raised the bar. Chef Johnny Courtney, previously of Canlis, runs it with Sarah Courtney as operations director, with Oscar Galvan on wine and Dillon Raaz behind the bar. The awards deserve stating exactly, because two separate things are often collapsed into one: Atoma the restaurant was a national finalist for Best New Restaurant at the 2025 James Beard Awards, and Courtney himself was a finalist for Best Chef: Northwest and Pacific in 2026. Finalist both times, not winner. Courtney's response to the second was that it was incredibly humbling, that he had dreamed about it since he was a kid, and that more than anything it gave them a bigger platform to keep celebrating their team, their farmers and the simple joy of sharing a great meal. The food runs from a $7 rosette cookie with farmer's cheese and onion jam to a $135 duck pot pie built for a table.

The zero-proof drinks are printed as their own section of the bar list rather than tucked under the cocktails, and there are four. It's Grape(fruit) to See You pairs a house-made grapefruit soda with DHOS Bittersweet — DHOS being a French zero-proof aperitif range, botanical and genuinely bitter, which is what makes the drink work with food. Forlorn George uses DHOS Vodka Free with a "Tang" cordial and a house orange-vanilla soda. Starr Pupil is the bright one, on DHOS Vodka Free with pineapple syrup and lime. The Phony Espresso Negroni is St. Agrestis's bottled version. The shelf also carries DHOS Bittersweet and Orange at $9 and Pathfinder Amaro at $10 by the pour, so the bar can build beyond the printed four. Two practical things worth knowing before booking. No cocktail prices are published anywhere — that is true of the alcoholic list as well, so it is not a slight on the zero-proof drinks, but you will not be able to plan a spend. And the restaurant is not wheelchair accessible: every entrance requires a full flight of stairs, with another step to the patio. Reservations open on the first of each month for the following month.
venues.pressQuote: At the high-end restaurant Atoma in Wallingford, the zero-proof menu features an aperitif mimicking an Aperol spritz, a faux old fashioned with a diamond-shaped ice cube, and a dessert drink fortified with cold brew.

venues.name: Attica
venues.description: Ben Shewry's globally ranked Ripponlea tasting-menu institution runs a full sommelier-curated non-alcoholic pairing in parallel with its wine match, so guests who skip alcohol get the same considered flight rather than an afterthought. The zero-proof drinks are house-made ferments, juices and infusions built largely from produce grown in Attica's own garden - a cold-smoked Granny Smith apple juice poured against paperbark-torched King George whiting is the signature match. Past pairings have run to 'rosella and all-spice', 'riberries and grapefruit' and 'desert lime and apple cider'. Attica gives non-drinkers a full page of house-made alternatives plus a dedicated non-alcoholic pairing, which is what makes a three-hour degustation work without wine.
signatureDrinks: Cold-smoked Granny Smith apple juice - house cold-smoked, paired with paperbark-torched King George whiting
Rosella and all-spice - house-made non-alcoholic infusion
Riberries and grapefruit - house-made non-alcoholic pairing drink
Desert lime and apple cider - native desert lime pairing drink
venues.longDescription:
Attica is chef Ben Shewry's fine-dining institution at 74 Glen Eira Road in the quiet bayside suburb of Ripponlea. Open since Shewry took the helm in 2005, it has appeared on The World's 50 Best Restaurants list every year since 2010 and is consistently rated the top restaurant in Australia. Dinner is a single multi-course tasting menu built around native and locally grown Australian ingredients, served Tuesday to Saturday with guests seated between 6pm and 8pm.

The non-alcoholic program is a genuine parallel to the wine list, not a token gesture. Alongside the alcoholic pairing, the sommelier team offers a full non-alcoholic pairing - and a mixed option - each drink chosen to match a specific course. The zero-proof drinks are house-made: cold-smoked juices, ferments and infusions drawn largely from the restaurant's roughly 1200-square-metre kitchen garden, so the beverage flight tracks the same seasonal produce as the plates.

The most talked-about match is a cold-smoked Granny Smith apple juice paired with King George whiting torched in a paperbark wrapping, where the smoke in the drink echoes the smoke in the dish. Other documented non-alcoholic pours have included 'rosella and all-spice', 'riberries and grapefruit' and 'desert lime and apple cider' - all native-leaning, all made in house. Reviewers have singled out the non-alcoholic list as unusually thoughtful for a restaurant of this level.

The room is intimate and dimly lit, seating a small number of guests each service, with the tasting menu set at A$425 per person from September 2026. The non-alcoholic pairing has been offered at around A$130, curated by Attica's sommelier team.

The reason this matters is specific to the format. Pub With No Booze, writing for non-drinkers, notes that dining at the very pointy end can be genuinely difficult without alcohol — the feeling of not getting the full experience can hollow out the evening — and singles out Attica as the answer, with a full page of house-made non-alcoholic alternatives and a non-alcoholic pairing available.

A full page is the phrase to hold on to. At a long degustation the drinks are not an accessory; they are half the pacing, and a guest given a single bottle of sparkling water for three hours is watching the meal happen to other people. House-made is the second half of it: these are things the kitchen ferments, infuses and bottles itself, which is why they can be matched to Ben Shewry's cooking rather than merely served alongside it. Book far ahead and ask for the pairing when you reserve rather than on the night.
venues.pressQuote: The harmony between the aroma of the dish and the juice is incredible.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Banjo Harris Plane, then head sommelier at Attica, on the cold-smoked apple juice pairing

venues.name: Aulis London
venues.description: Aulis is Simon Rogan's Michelin-starred, 12-seat chef's table hidden on St Anne's Court just off Dean Street in Soho, where dishes are cooked and explained in front of you. Its non-alcoholic pairing is treated with the same technical precision as the food and is curated by sommelier Charles Carron Brown, who ferments house drinks like the Beer Bucha, a hop-fermented kombucha. Club Oenologique calls it one of the capital's leading soft-drink menus, making the zero-proof flight a genuine reason to book rather than an afterthought.

venues.longDescription:
Aulis is the London chef's table from Simon Rogan, the chef behind Lake District flagship L'Enclume. Hidden on St Anne's Court off Dean Street in Soho, the room seats just twelve guests, and each service is a dynamic, interactive tasting menu cooked and explained in front of you, built largely from produce grown at Rogan's own Lake District farm. The kitchen is run day to day by executive chef Oli Marlow and head chef Charlie Tayler, and Aulis earned its first Michelin star in the 2024 UK & Ireland Michelin Guide, which it has since retained.

The non-alcoholic pairing is designed with the same rigour as the wine flight and the food itself. It is overseen by sommelier and restaurant manager Charles Carron Brown, who ferments and infuses much of the list in house. "It's a chance for us to get extremely creative," he told Club Oenologique, which described Aulis as having "one of the capital's leading soft-drink menus." The anchor pour is the Beer Bucha, a hop-fermented kombucha that is the non-alcoholic drink of choice for many diners.

Carron Brown's own favourite is the "Plum Blossom": a Japanese tea brewed with dehydrated plum leaves and freeze-dried blackcurrants from Rogan's farm, served alongside a duck main course with beetroots and raspberry vinegar. The pairings track the seasons in step with the food, so the exact line-up shifts, but the intent stays constant, a considered, fermentation-led zero-proof journey rather than a token mocktail. Booking is by pre-paid tasting menu, with the non-alcoholic pairing offered as an alternative to the wine flight.
venues.pressQuote: Three Michelin-starred chef Simon Rogan's Soho chef's table has one of the capital's leading soft-drink menus, with their Beer Bucha, a hop-fermented kombucha, the non-alcoholic drink of choice for many.

venues.name: AVIV
venues.description: AVIV is the Israeli restaurant from chef Michael Solomonov and restaurateur Steve Cook, both multiple James Beard Award winners, set inside 1 Hotel South Beach on Collins Avenue. The name means "spring" in Hebrew, and the cooking pairs ancient techniques with a Tel Aviv-meets-Miami room. Its documented alcohol-free build is the Almond Blossom, which layers Seedlip Grove 42 with orgeat, yuzu juice and yuzu soda — the citrus expression of the non-alcoholic distiller carrying the almond sweetness rather than being buried by it. RESIDENT wrote in December 2025 that the drink feels layered yet restrained. The restaurant serves breakfast daily from 7am and dinner from 5:30pm, running to 11pm on Friday and Saturday.
signatureDrinks: Almond Blossom (Seedlip Grove 42, orgeat, yuzu juice, yuzu soda)
venues.longDescription:
AVIV sits at 2341 Collins Avenue inside 1 Hotel South Beach, and is the Miami project of chef Michael Solomonov and restaurateur Steve Cook, described on the restaurant's own site as an acclaimed Israeli-born chef and a renowned restaurateur, both multi-time James Beard Award winners. The restaurant's own description explains the name — aviv is Hebrew for spring — and frames the cooking as ancient technique brought into a room that reads as much Miami as Tel Aviv. It keeps an unusual two-part schedule: breakfast every morning from 7am to 11:30am, then dinner from 5:30pm to 10pm, extending to 11pm on Friday and Saturday.

The alcohol-free build documented at the bar is the Almond Blossom. It uses Seedlip Grove 42 — the blood-orange-and-lemongrass expression from the London non-alcoholic distiller — with orgeat, yuzu juice and yuzu soda, which is a considered combination rather than an obvious one: orgeat brings almond richness and body, and the two forms of yuzu supply enough acid and aromatic lift to stop the drink turning cloying. RESIDENT covered it in its December 2025 Miami survey, wrote that the drink reflects the restaurant's ingredient-driven approach, and described it as feeling layered yet restrained and as a refined option for guests seeking clarity and balance. Only one named alcohol-free drink is published, so the programme is recorded here as real but modest. Watr at the 1 Rooftop, the eighteenth-floor bar in the same building, runs a separate alcohol-free build and is listed as its own entry; between them the two make 1 Hotel South Beach one of the more usable addresses in South Beach for a guest who is not drinking. Two practical notes. The restaurant serves breakfast every morning from 7am, which makes it one of very few morning options on this list. And no zero-proof section appears anywhere on the restaurant's published site, so a guest should ask for the Almond Blossom by name rather than expecting to find it printed on the card. Bookings run on (305) 768-1386 and the restaurant posts as @aviv.southbeach.
venues.pressQuote: Seedlip Grove 42, orgeat, yuzu juice, and yuzu soda create a mocktail that feels layered yet restrained.

venues.name: Avo
venues.description: Avo is a fully plant-based, vegan restaurant in Nashville's OneC1ty development on the West End/Midtown edge, tucked beneath the Element Hotel. It was opened in 2015 by raw-food chef Jessica Rice and Hot Yoga Plus owner Susannah Herring, and has been owned by Annie Choo since 2017. The seasonal, chef-driven menu is gluten-free, organic, and locally sourced where possible. Its full bar is also entirely vegan, and alongside cocktails Avo prints a headed Zero Proof section: a Cucumber Ginger Nojito with NA ginger liqueur, an NA Aperol Spritz on Mionetto's alcohol-free aperitivo and prosecco, Lime in the Coconut with NA Giffard pineapple liqueur, and a Lemon Lavender sparkling lemonade, plus Mionetto NA prosecco and two non-alcoholic beers, Wellbeing Brewing's Victory Wheat and Untitled Art's Juicy IPA. Note for anyone avoiding all intoxicants: the same drinks menu also lists THC beverages.
signatureDrinks: Cucumber Ginger Nojito (cucumber, mint, lime, NA ginger liqueur, soda) $11
NA Aperol Spritz (Mionetto NA aperitivo, Mionetto NA prosecco, orange slice) $11
Lime in the Coconut (Alchemist coconut syrup, NA Giffard pineapple liqueur, lime, soda) $11
Lemon Lavender (sparkling lemonade with a floral twist) $8
venues.longDescription:
Avo is a fully plant-based restaurant at 4 City Blvd, Suite 104, tucked beneath the Element hotel in the OneC1ty development on the West End edge of Nashville. It has been trading for about a decade — the restaurant now markets ten years of plant-based cooking — and is run by owner Annie Choo. The kitchen is entirely vegan and leans seasonal and largely gluten-free, working through a menu of kale Caesar, fried cauliflower, nachos, a lentil-walnut burger, penne pesto primavera and a cauliflower steak, with a fried hash brown sandwich and cornbread pancakes on the daytime side. It serves Tuesday through Saturday 11am to 9pm and Sunday 11am to 8pm, closed Mondays. Parking is the one piece of local knowledge worth having in advance: the restaurant recommends the outdoor lot behind the shipping containers, which is free for two hours but requires registering the car by QR code on arrival.

What distinguishes Avo from most restaurants with a mocktail or two is that the bar itself is fully vegan alongside the kitchen — the same standard applied to drinks as to food, which rules out the animal-derived fining agents, honey syrups and egg-white foams that quietly appear in a lot of cocktail and mocktail programmes. That makes it a genuinely straightforward room for anyone who is both avoiding alcohol and eating plant-based, a combination that usually means interrogating a server. The drinks menu, now published in full on the restaurant's own site, carries a headed Zero Proof section priced at $8 to $11: a Cucumber Ginger Nojito of cucumber, mint, lime, NA ginger liqueur and soda; an NA Aperol Spritz built on Mionetto's alcohol-free aperitivo and prosecco with an orange slice; Lime in the Coconut, with Alchemist coconut syrup, NA Giffard pineapple liqueur, lime and soda; and a Lemon Lavender sparkling lemonade. Under a Zero Proof Wine & Beer heading sit Mionetto NA prosecco at $11 and two $6 non-alcoholic beers, Wellbeing Brewing's Victory Wheat and Untitled Art's Juicy IPA — the Athletic Brewing beers listed here in 2025 have been replaced, and the earlier named mocktails (Lil Vamp, Apple Dance, I Love You So Matcha) are gone with them. One thing to know before you go: the same menu lists THC beverages alongside the zero-proof drinks, so anyone steering clear of intoxicants entirely should order from the Zero Proof section by name. What is dependable is the format: a vegan bar in a vegan restaurant, where a non-alcoholic order is ordinary rather than a special request.
venues.pressQuote: AVO is focused on using vegetables to make the dishes delicious rather than relying on imitation products.

venues.name: 'Awa Hou Kava Lounge
venues.description: 'Awa Hou is a kava lounge on South King Street in Mōʻiliʻili, opened by Rami Kayali in the space that used to hold Glazer's Coffee. It serves no alcohol. The house pours fresh 'awa — the Hawaiian name for kava — farmed on Moku o Keawe and Molokaʻi and hand-pressed on site, alongside dry kava sourced from across the South Pacific. Guests choose waka, the lateral root, for a headier effect, or lewena, the stump, for something heavier in the body, and can add ginger syrup or coconut water. Sky Kombucha is on tap. Kava is psychoactive and mildly sedating, which is worth knowing before visiting. A living wall of nearly 700 native plants from Hui Kū Maoli Ola fronts the room.
venues.address: 2700 S King St, Ste D101, Honolulu, HI 96826
signatureDrinks: Fresh 'Awa Hawaiʻi, 8oz 'apu — hand-pressed in house from Hawaiʻi Island or Molokaʻi root (waka/lateral for a heady effect, lewena/stump for the body, or a blend)
Dry South Pacific kava, served with water or coconut water
venues.longDescription:
'Awa Hou occupies Suite D101 at 2700 South King Street in Mōʻiliʻili, in the space Glazer's Coffee held for years, and it is built around a plant that Hawaiʻi has been drinking for centuries. 'Awa is the Hawaiian name for what most of the Pacific calls kava, and the state formally recognised it as a safe traditional food in 2025 — part of a broader restoration of Native Hawaiian food culture. Owner Rami Kayali frames the business around two goals, building community and sharing 'awa, and the room is fitted out accordingly: a living wall of nearly 700 native plants supplied by the Hui Kū Maoli Ola nursery greets you at the door, lauhala mats line the counter sides, and Progress Pride, Hawaiian and Palestinian flags hang in the space. There are books and games, free wifi and parking, a student discount, and a rolling programme of pop-ups and community workshops.

The drinking is genuinely specific rather than generic. Fresh 'awa comes from farmers on Moku o Keawe — Hawaiʻi Island — and Molokaʻi, and is hand-pressed in house rather than reconstituted from powder; guests choose waka, the lateral root, which runs headier and more energising, or lewena, the stump, which sits heavier in the body, or a blend of the two. Dry kava from across the South Pacific rounds out the list, served with water or coconut water, with ginger syrup available to cut the flavour. Kayali is cheerfully blunt about that flavour, describing it to Honolulu Magazine as like "licking a potato" or drinking "pencil-shavings tea." A happy hour from 1pm to 4pm puts an eight-ounce 'apu — a coconut cup — at $5, with regular servings running $7.50 to $8.50, and Sky Kombucha is on tap for anyone who does not want kava at all. The honest caveat matters here: kava contains no alcohol and none is served, but it is psychoactive and taken for a relaxing, mildly euphoric effect, so it is not a neutral substitute in the way a zero-proof spritz is, and some people in recovery avoid it deliberately. Hours run 1pm to 10pm Sunday through Thursday and 1pm to 11pm on Friday and Saturday.
venues.pressQuote: Kava can taste like licking a potato, or pencil-shavings tea.

venues.name: Awafi Cafe
venues.description: Awafi Cafe is a fully alcohol-free, halal Yemeni coffeehouse on Hamtramck's Joseph Campau Avenue, so its drink menu was never built around removing booze — it just never had any. A printed "Refreshers" section carries four virgin mojitos (Blueberry, Mango, Raspberry, Strawberry) plus a Strawberry Mint Lemonade and fruit smoothies, served alongside traditional Yemeni coffees like Sana'ani, Mufawar, and Qishr made from organic imported beans.
venues.longDescription:
Awafi Cafe sits on the south side of Hamtramck, the small Muslim-majority city ringed by Detroit that's home to one of the largest Yemeni-American communities in the country. It's a halal coffeehouse from the ground up: no alcohol has ever been on the premises, so the "non-alcoholic program" here is simply the full drink menu, not a side list added to placate anyone.

That menu splits into traditional and modern. On the traditional side, Awafi pours Yemeni coffees by name — Sana'ani, Mufawar, Qishr, Rad'ai, and Jubani among them — brewed from organic imported beans, with the cardamom-forward Mufawar drawing particular praise from regulars. On the modern side is a printed "Refreshers" section built entirely around virgin mojitos in four flavors (Blueberry, Mango, Raspberry, Strawberry), a Strawberry Mint Lemonade, and a rotating smoothie and boba lineup.

The cafe was opened by Hannan Alzumel, a Yemeni immigrant in her twenties who taught herself to bake at home, started selling pastries to local Yemeni-owned stores, and then opened her own storefront once health-code rules required a licensed kitchen. She built the business quietly, without her family's initial knowledge — a break from norms in a community where few Yemeni women in Hamtramck run their own storefronts — and now employs young Muslim women from the neighborhood behind the counter.

Joseph Campau Avenue is Hamtramck's main commercial corridor, lined with Yemeni, Bangladeshi, and Bosnian-owned businesses. Awafi's grand opening drew city officials, including Hamtramck's mayor and city council, underscoring how integrated the shop already is in the neighborhood's daily life — a coffeehouse where a virgin mojito is just called a mojito.
venues.pressQuote: I broke a lot of stuff from my culture, like driving, work, finish school, open a business...people are going to think, 'This is not wrong.' And they gonna follow you.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Hannan Alzumel, owner of Awafi Cafe

venues.name: Axelrad
venues.description: Axelrad is a Midtown Houston beer garden set in a century-old building on the corner of Alabama and Almeda, sharing a leafy, hammock-strewn patio with Luigi's Pizzeria. It's a casual, walk-in outdoor drinking spot known for live music, food trucks, and community events, welcoming families until its evening 21+ transition. Non-drinkers are well served: the drinks menu carries its own dedicated Non-Alcoholic section with named mocktails like the Elderberry Spritz (Giffard Elderflower, lemon, Lagunitas Hoppy Refresher), the Jalapina Business (Giffard pineapple, mango, lime, jalapeño, mineral water), and the Briney Melon Refresher (watermelon, lime, mint, ginger beer). The NA-beer lineup is extensive — Athletic Upside Dawn and Free Wave, Lagunitas IPNA, Best Day Electro-Lime, and Brooklyn Special Effects — plus kombucha, hopped seltzers, and Topo Chico. CultureMap has repeatedly highlighted its zero-proof offerings.

venues.longDescription:
Axelrad is a Midtown Houston beer garden built inside a century-old building at the corner of Alabama and Almeda — a former grocery store run by the Axelrad family in the 1920s — where it shares a leafy, hammock-strewn patio with Luigi's Pizzeria and Retrospect Coffee. Co-owners Monte Large and Adam Brackman opened the beer garden in 2015, and Axelrad marked its 10th anniversary in April 2025 with weekend festivities and a vinyl live album, "Live at Axelrad, Jazz Wednesdays," recorded with the local artists who play its weekly Wednesday jazz nights. Brackman frames the place in community terms — "We really just try to embrace and support the community," he told CultureMap Houston, describing the concept as somewhere that "is not your home and it's not your work, but it's that place you're going to go to." It has also served as a refuge during Houston power outages: "When a lot of people don't have power, we're open for people to come charge phones."

Non-drinkers are thoroughly served here: the drinks menu carries its own dedicated Non-Alcoholic section, listed alongside — not tucked beneath — the craft beer, specialty cocktail, wine, and liquor sections, and broken into Mocktails, N/A Beer, and Other. The standing named mocktails are the Elderberry Spritz (Giffard Elderflower, lemon, Lagunitas Hoppy Refresher), the Jalapina Business (Giffard pineapple, mango, lime, jalapeño, mineral water), and the Briney Melon Refresher (watermelon, lime, mint, ginger beer). The N/A beer list runs six deep — Athletic Upside Dawn and Free Wave Hazy IPA, Lagunitas IPNA and Hoppy Refresher, Best Day Electro-Lime, and Brooklyn Special FX Hoppy Lager — rounded out by Saint Arnold Root Beer and Mexican Coca-Cola. In past Dry Januarys the bar has run $7 seasonal mocktail specials on top of that, including the "cran you BE anymore merry?" (cranberry, lime juice, and a housemade syrup of apple, cinnamon, and brown sugar) and the warm "not toddy," which pairs that same syrup with fresh lemon juice.

It's a casual, walk-in outdoor drinking spot known for live music, food trucks, and recurring community events, and families are welcome on the patio until the evening 21+ transition — 9pm Sunday through Thursday, 8pm Friday and Saturday. CultureMap Houston has covered the beer garden repeatedly, from its Dry January mocktail menu to its 10-year anniversary.
venues.pressQuote: This vibrant beer garden joins the Dry January movement with $7 mocktails such as the "cran you BE anymore merry?" with cranberry, lime juice, and a housemade syrup of apple, cinnamon, and brown sugar.

venues.name: Azumi
venues.description: Azumi's zero-proof program centers on two named, ingredient-driven cocktails — the Seedlip Garden-based Boketto and the tropical Matcha Colada — each priced at $14, on par with the restaurant's full-proof cocktail list rather than treated as an afterthought. Both drinks are independently confirmed, with matching names, ingredients, and prices, across Houston Dry January 2026 roundups (led by Community Impact), showing they're a standing bar-program feature rather than a one-off mention. Azumi itself is not an alcohol-free venue — it runs one of the region's largest sake lists alongside a full craft cocktail program — but its two zero-proof builds are real, specific, and consistently documented.
venues.address: 4444 Westheimer Rd, Suite G-130, Houston, TX 77027
signatureDrinks: Boketto (Seedlip Garden, jasmine green tea, cucumber, yuzu)
venues.longDescription:
Azumi opened in July 2024 at the Westheimer Road entrance to Houston's River Oaks District, a Houston concept from Atlas Restaurant Group (its third in the city, alongside Loch Bar). The modern Japanese restaurant is led by executive chef Timur Fazilov, who previously worked in Masaharu Morimoto's restaurants in Doha and Miami before taking over Azumi's sushi program. At the opening, Atlas Restaurant Group president and CEO Alex Smith said, "Chef Fazilov and the team have created an elevated Japanese dining experience that reflects the innovation and fusion of Houston's culinary landscape."

The concept centers on a sushi bar serving seafood flown in daily from Tokyo alongside Miyazaki A5 wagyu and a hot kitchen menu, backed by one of the region's largest sake lists and a full craft cocktail program. A daily 3-6pm happy hour, available at the bar and on the patio seven days a week, anchors a lively bar scene.

For Dry January 2026, Azumi's bar team put forward two named zero-proof cocktails at the same $14 price point as its alcoholic drinks: the Boketto, built on Seedlip Garden non-alcoholic spirit with jasmine green tea, cucumber and yuzu, and the Matcha Colada, a tropical blend of matcha, coconut, pineapple and lime. Both drinks were reported with matching names, ingredients, and prices across independent local coverage (including Community Impact), indicating a genuine, repeatable NA offering rather than a single press mention, even though Azumi's drink menu itself is not fully alcohol-free.
venues.pressQuote: Priced at $14, the Matcha Colada includes matcha, coconut, pineapple and lime for a tropical-meets-tea taste. Meanwhile, the Boketto offers Seedlip Garden, jasmine green tea, cucumber and yuzu, a tart East Asian citrus fruit.

venues.name: Bab Al-Yemen
venues.description: Bab Al-Yemen is Boston's first Yemeni restaurant, opened by Ahmed Mahmood on Commonwealth Avenue at the edge of Kenmore Square. It is halal and serves no alcohol, and it opens at 2pm on weekdays and noon at weekends and runs to 10pm every night, which makes it a genuine evening destination rather than a lunch counter. The kitchen works from traditional Yemeni recipes: lamb mandi and haneeth served over rice, fahsa cooked and brought to the table still bubbling in its stone pot, and bread baked to order in a tandoor. The drink to know is the Yemeni cocktail, a layered non-alcoholic blend of mango, banana, dates, strawberry, milk and Vimto, served in a tall glass. Adani tea, the spiced milk tea of Aden, closes the meal.
signatureDrinks: Yemeni cocktail (mango, banana, dates, strawberry, milk and Vimto, layered in a tall glass)
Adani tea (Yemeni spiced black tea with milk)
venues.longDescription:
Bab Al-Yemen takes its name from Bab al-Yemen, the great gate of the old walled city of Sana'a, and it was the first restaurant in Boston to put Yemeni cooking on a menu. Owner Ahmed Mahmood runs it at 468 Commonwealth Avenue, a block from Kenmore Square in the Fenway-Kenmore neighborhood, where it draws Boston University students, the city's Yemeni and wider Arab communities, and a steady flow of people who read about it in Edible Boston's Food Find column in November 2023. The room is halal throughout and there is no bar; the whole operation runs without alcohol, which is unusual for a full-service restaurant open until 10pm seven nights a week in that part of the city. Mahmood has since expanded the concept, adding a Yemeni coffee and bakery project in the South End.

The food is the draw. Lamb mandi and haneeth come over long-grain rice, cooked until the meat gives way without a knife; fahsa arrives still bubbling in its stone bowl; flatbread is baked to order. The drinks are worth ordering on their own terms rather than as a substitute for something else. The house Yemeni cocktail is a layered blend of mango, banana, dates, strawberry, milk and Vimto, the cordial that is a fixture of Ramadan tables across the Gulf and the Levant, and Edible Boston singled it out specifically because the restaurant's halal kitchen means the drink is alcohol-free by construction rather than by adaptation. Adani tea, the strong milk tea of Aden, is the standard finish. For a reader looking for somewhere in Boston proper where a full dinner and a real drink can happen with no alcohol in the building, this is one of the shortest routes to it. Mahmood has a second Yemeni project in progress, C'Yool Yemeni Coffee & Bakery, taking the former Atlantico space in the South End and planning weekend hours to around midnight; it had not opened at the time of writing.
venues.pressQuote: Since Bab Al-Yemen is halal, this cocktail is alcohol-free and truly refreshing.

venues.name: Bacán
venues.description: A Michelin-recommended pan-American restaurant on the ground floor of the Lake Nona Wave Hotel, led by Executive Chef Guillaume Robin in a dramatic open-theater kitchen overlooking the Lake Nona Sculpture Garden. Bacán runs a dedicated zero-proof cocktail menu, including the El Dorado (golden berry-cilantro shrub and citrus-avocado foam), the Havana Habana, and the Bacán-Elazo.
signatureDrinks: El Dorado (honeydew soda, golden berry-cilantro shrub, citrus-avocado foam)
Havana Habana (blueberry-habanero shrub, lemon juice, soda water)
venues.longDescription:
Bacán delivers what it calls 'the boldly seductive flavors of the Americas' from an open, theater-style kitchen on the first floor of the Lake Nona Wave Hotel, with table-side presentations that connect diners to the adjacent Lake Nona Sculpture Garden. The restaurant is Michelin-recommended and spans a contemporary menu across Central and South America with tropical influence, set in a dining room defined by vivid color, soaring ceilings, and a large Amy Rader art installation.

The kitchen is led by Executive Chef Guillaume Robin, a native of northwestern France who spent nearly two decades in Michelin-starred kitchens and four- and five-star hotel properties across the U.S. and Europe - including The Setai Miami Beach and The St. Regis Toronto - before opening Bacán. Robin was honored with the Maîtres Cuisiniers de France title in 2025 and works alongside Sous Chef Ryne Wood.

Bacán's zero-proof menu lists three composed, named mocktails: the El Dorado (honeydew soda, golden berry-cilantro shrub, citrus-avocado foam), the Havana Habana (blueberry-habanero shrub, lemon juice, soda water), and the Bacán-Elazo (passionfruit, cinnamon, lime, demerara sugar) - each built with the same kitchen-driven theatricality as the food menu, and each priced alongside the alcoholic cocktail list rather than as an afterthought.

Bacán anchors the growing Lake Nona dining scene southeast of Orlando International Airport, inside the Lake Nona Wave Hotel.
venues.pressQuote: An exquisite take on fare spanning the Americas.

venues.name: Backbar
venues.description: Backbar is a craft cocktail bar established in 2011 at 7 Sanborn Court in Union Square, Somerville, found through an orange door in the alley between The Independent and Bronwyn. It seats only 39, takes no reservations, and has collected an unusual run of accolades for its size: Boston Magazine rated it the city's best bar in March 2020, Time Out included it among the 28 coolest bars in the world in August 2021, and Wine Enthusiast named it Best Overall Bar in Boston in November 2024. Its non-alcoholic list is a full themed menu that rotates rather than a token section; the current one is Studio Ghibli-themed and headed "Rated NA: Non Alcoholic!", with every alcohol-free drink priced at $11.
signatureDrinks: Means to Fly (Seedlip Grove, Seedlip Spice, raspberry, orange shrub, ginger, lemon, cardamom, chocolate bitters, egg white, NA sparkling wine)
"Baluse" The Spell of Destruction (Pathfinder Hemp & Root, hojicha tea, sakura blossom bitters, rosemary)
Arrietty's Libation (Lyre's gin alternative, prickly pear, Lyre's Coffee Originale, Lucano Amaro Zero, lime)
No Face (Seedlip Spice, Lucano Amaro Zero, cold brew concentrate, demerara, elderflower, cream)
Mockingbirds (bespoke spirit-free bartender's-choice cocktail built to your taste)
venues.longDescription:
Backbar has traded since 2011 from a converted space at 7 Sanborn Court in Union Square, reached through an orange door in the alley between The Independent and Bronwyn, with no sign on the street and no reservations taken. Sam Treadway founded it and has been its public face throughout, and the bar still runs cocktail classes and tastings in its small Closet Bar under his name. For a 39-seat room the recognition has been disproportionate: Boston Magazine rated it the number one bar in Boston in March 2020, Time Out placed it on a list of the 28 coolest bars in the world in August 2021, and in November 2024 both Wine Enthusiast, which called it Best Overall Bar in Boston, and Boston Common Magazine, which put it in the city's top ten, returned to it. Meet Boston's January 2026 zero-proof guide judged the array of flavours structured and nuanced, making this one of the most serious zero-proof programs in the city.

What distinguishes the alcohol-free offering is that it is a designed, themed menu in its own right, redrawn on the same cycle as the bar's pop-culture cocktail menus — a comic-book menu in 2023 carried a spirit-free Wolverine, and the current one is built around Studio Ghibli films under the heading "Rated NA: Non Alcoholic!", with every drink at $11. Means to Fly is the most elaborate, stacking Seedlip Grove and Seedlip Spice with raspberry, orange shrub, ginger, lemon, cardamom, chocolate bitters, egg white and non-alcoholic sparkling wine. "Baluse", subtitled The Spell of Destruction, runs complex, herbal and bitter on Pathfinder Hemp & Root with hojicha tea, sakura blossom bitters and rosemary. Arrietty's Libation is rich and earthy, built from Lyre's gin alternative and Lyre's Coffee Originale with prickly pear, Lucano Amaro Zero and lime. No Face closes the list with Seedlip Spice, Lucano Amaro Zero, cold brew concentrate, demerara, elderflower and cream. Bartenders will also build a bespoke spirit-free drink to taste on request.
venues.pressQuote: The array of flavors is structured and nuanced, making this one of the most serious zero-proof programs in the city.

venues.name: Bad Luck Bar
venues.description: Bad Luck Bar — hidden Capitol Park cocktail speakeasy with a dedicated four-cocktail non-alcoholic menu built around the four elements.

venues.longDescription:
Bad Luck Bar is the speakeasy of the Detroit Optimist Society, the craft-cocktail restaurant group founded by Dave Kwiatkowski (The Sugar House, Wright & Co., The Peterboro, Honest John's). It opened December 8, 2016 inside The Albert building in Capitol Park, accessed through an alley off Griswold marked only by a painted snake and a red neon glow. Kwiatkowski designed and built the 800-square-foot room himself, with 15-foot cherry-wood ceilings cut into hexagonal paneling and a white Silestone bar — a deliberately theatrical, hidden-in-plain-sight counterpoint to its downtown surroundings.

The regular cocktail list runs to elaborate, high-concept drinks built around tarot and folklore themes, so it's notable that the bar treats its zero-proof program with the same intent rather than tacking on a mocktail as an afterthought. The dedicated Additional Drinks menu groups four composed non-alcoholic cocktails by classical element: FIRE (non-alcoholic tequila, non-alcoholic agave, Caribbean spiced pepper, pineapple, acid-adjusted grapefruit, mint, housemade Hellfire bitters), AIR (non-alcoholic gin, non-alcoholic agave, mango, oolong tea, pineapple, lemon, soda), WATER (non-alcoholic gin, dulse, lime, saline), and EARTH (non-alcoholic whiskey, non-alcoholic bittersweet liqueur, rainbow carrot, beet, acid-adjusted grapefruit, ginger). Each uses the same housemade syrups, bitters, and acid-adjusted juices that go into the alcoholic menu.

Beyond the four listed drinks, the bar will build a bespoke non-alcoholic or low-ABV dealer's choice on request, extending the same call-ahead, speakeasy-style service — knock or call for admission, seating is limited and reservation-recommended — to guests who aren't drinking.

Bad Luck Bar sits half a block from Campus Martius in Capitol Park, one of downtown Detroit's densest concentrations of bars and restaurants, and operates Monday through Saturday, closed Sundays.
venues.pressQuote: I designed and built the space, and did all of the carpentry... The 15-foot-tall ceilings are made out of cherry wood and have isometric, hexagonal paneling.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Dave Kwiatkowski, founder, Detroit Optimist Society

venues.name: Bagatelle Miami River
venues.description: Bagatelle Miami River is the Miami outpost of the French-Mediterranean group, on the Miami River just west of downtown, and it trades as a late-night dining room rather than an early one: doors at 6pm Wednesday through Saturday, closing at 1:30am midweek and 2:30am at the weekend. Its documented alcohol-free build, the Dirty Marti-No, is an unusually savoury build — a spirit-free take on a dirty martini made with Osco Original and layered with olive, thyme, grape and rose tea. The Greater Miami Convention & Visitors Bureau describes it as balancing briny depth with subtle floral notes and calls it an option for guests who prefer their drinks less sweet and more complex.
venues.address: 311 NW South River Dr, Miami, FL 33128
signatureDrinks: Dirty Marti-No (Osco Original, olive, thyme, grape, rose tea)
venues.longDescription:
Bagatelle Miami River sits at 311 NW South River Drive, on the working stretch of the Miami River immediately west of downtown, and is the Miami venue of the international Bagatelle group, which runs French-Mediterranean rooms in several cities. The format is a late dinner service that starts at 6pm and does not finish until 1:30am on Wednesday and Thursday or 2:30am on Friday and Saturday, with a quieter Sunday lunch service from noon. It is closed Monday and Tuesday. The Greater Miami Convention & Visitors Bureau describes the restaurant as sitting just on the outskirts of downtown Miami and as proof that high-energy dining does not require alcohol to deliver on flavour or sophistication.

The alcohol-free drink documented at the restaurant is the Dirty Marti-No, and it is worth singling out because it is the only savoury build in this batch of Miami additions. It is made with Osco Original — a non-alcoholic aperitif base — and layered with olive, thyme, grape and rose tea, producing a drink the tourism bureau describes as balancing briny depth with subtle floral notes. It is served in martini format and pitched, in the bureau's words, at guests who prefer their drinks less sweet and more complex. For a reader who has spent an evening being handed sweetened fruit juice in a coupe, that is a meaningful distinction. Osco is not currently carried in this catalogue's brand registry, so it is named in the drink specification without a brand tag. Note that some listings place the restaurant at 400 SW 2nd Avenue; the restaurant's own site gives 311 NW South River Drive, which is the address recorded here. One practical caution: the restaurant is closed on Monday and Tuesday and does not open before 6pm on the nights it trades, apart from the Sunday midday service, so it cannot be used as a daytime stop. The restaurant posts as @bagatellemiamiriver.
venues.pressQuote: Among its standout zero-proof offerings is the Dirty Marti-No, a savory, spirit-free take on a classic martini.

venues.name: Baia
venues.description: Baia is a Roman-inspired rooftop dining lounge above Esplanade Mall with sweeping Marina Bay views, where the Proof & Co-curated cocktail list carries a genuine set of four dedicated zero-proof drinks at S$22 or below. The standout is 'As Good As Corona', built on Seedlip Grove 42 with yuzu and sage, alongside 'Not a Sunken City', the alcohol-free take on the house Sunken City that swaps gin for a non-alcoholic spirit and holds the tomato relish. Bar manager Adonis E. Reyes builds each spirit-free drink to mirror the flavour architecture of its full-proof counterpart, and the team will craft bespoke zero-proof serves on request.
venues.address: Level 4, Esplanade Mall, 8 Raffles Avenue, Singapore 039802
signatureDrinks: As Good As Corona - Seedlip Grove 42, yuzu, sage (S$16, zero-proof)
Not a Sunken City - non-alcoholic spirit, tomato relish, citric and saline solution (zero-proof version of the signature Sunken City)
venues.longDescription:
Baia is a 5,000-square-foot rooftop dining lounge and bar perched on Level 4 of Esplanade Mall, opened in September 2024 by Singapore's ilLido Group under founder Beppe De Vito. Inspired by the ancient Italian resort town of Baiae, the space pairs a warm maroon-gold-green interior seating around 136 with a breezy open-air terrace that looks straight across Marina Bay and the city skyline. It runs from daytime set lunches into high-energy nights with live DJs from Wednesday through the weekend.

The cocktail program is curated by the beverage consultancy Proof & Co and split into three moods: SOL (bright aperitivo-style serves such as the Strombolian), NOX (indulgent after-dark drinks like the Eclipse) and MOSAICS (shareable quick-serve builds). Food leans Mediterranean with Japanese accents, from a caviar-and-oyster raw bar to charcoal-grilled plates, with most drinks and dishes kept accessibly priced.

The non-alcoholic offering is a real, integrated part of the list rather than an afterthought: four dedicated zero-proof cocktails priced around S$16 each. 'As Good As Corona' is built on Seedlip Grove 42 with yuzu and sage, while 'Not a Sunken City' rebuilds the signature Sunken City without booze, replacing the dry gin with a non-alcoholic spirit and adding citric and saline solution to keep the savoury tomato-relish drink in balance. As bar manager Adonis E. Reyes puts it, the team keeps 'all the flavour magic' while swapping out the alcohol, and will mix bespoke spirit-free drinks to order.

Baia has not appeared on Asia's 50 Best Bars or in the Michelin Guide as of this verification; its draw is the view, the Proof & Co program and a credible zero-proof selection rather than an awards pedigree.
venues.pressQuote: We maintain all the flavour magic but swap out the booze for non-alcoholic spirits.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Adonis E. Reyes, bar manager, Baia

venues.name: Bait Shop
venues.description: Bait Shop is a kitschy tiki-and-tackle bar at 606 Broadway E on Capitol Hill, known for frozen cocktails and a room styled after a port town. It opened in 2012 under Linda Derschang, and Mike Leifur and Jonah Bergman — then working for her — bought it in 2016. STATUS, BECAUSE IT IS ON OUR WATCHLIST: the century-old building is slated for demolition and the owners have been looking for a new Capitol Hill home since their demolition clause was triggered; they "technically" lost the lease in December 2025. But no demolition permit has been filed for the address as of today, and Bergman has said construction is not expected before the first quarter of 2027 at the earliest. It is open and trading normally. Its printed non-alcoholic section runs Athletic Brewing Run Wild IPA and Upside Dawn ($6 each), a Phony Negroni and an Amaro Falso ($10 each), a Recess zero-proof margarita ($8), and soft drinks. NOTE: a Rogue CBD ($6) and a Recess Mood soda ($7) also sit under that same heading, with no dosage printed. Open 4pm–2am daily.
venues.longDescription:
Bait Shop has been at 606 Broadway E since 2012, when Linda Derschang opened it as a port-town-themed bar, and Mike Leifur and Jonah Bergman — who worked for her at the time — bought it from her in 2016. The conceit is committed: nautical and tackle-shop clutter, a sailfish on the wall, frozen cocktails, and a genuine sense of humour about itself. One April Fools' Day the team converted several booths into a jail cell and a false-front western building, a nod to the company town that existed when the building went up in the 1920s. The food is proper bar food at fair prices — deviled eggs at $8, tots or fries at $6 for a small, wings at $17, a burger at $22, fish and chips at $21, tacos from $12, and an It's-It ice cream sandwich for $6. Happy hour runs 4 to 6 every day, and the bar is open from 4pm until 2am.

Because this listing sits on our closure watchlist, the status deserves a plain answer. The one-storey, century-old building is slated for demolition, the owners were told so more than two years ago, and in December 2025 they "technically" lost the lease and have been on borrowed time since. They are actively looking for a new home and want to stay on Capitol Hill; Leifur's hope is that it will be uncanny how familiar the new place looks. But nothing is imminent. No demolition permit has been filed for this address — we checked Seattle's own permit records rather than relying on reporting — and Bergman's understanding is that construction could not begin before the first quarter of 2027, and only then if the numbers work. The bar is open and busy. On the drinks: Athletic Brewing's Run Wild IPA and Upside Dawn are $6, the bottled Phony Negroni and Amaro Falso are $10 each, and a Recess zero-proof margarita is $8. One caution. Under that same "non-alcoholic" heading the menu also lists a Rogue CBD at $6 and a Recess Mood soda at $7 — both CBD-based, neither with any dosage printed. Order by name if you are avoiding cannabinoids.
venues.pressQuote: Bait Shop, a Capitol Hill staple, can make many of their cocktails non-alcoholic and have a good list of NA drinks, featuring Athletic Brewing beers, a phony negroni, and soft drinks.

venues.name: Bakaris Pizza & Kava Lounge
venues.description: Bakaris Pizza & Kava Lounge has operated in Atlanta's historic West End since 2013, billing itself as the area's original pork-free halal and plant-based pizzeria paired with an alcohol-free kava bar. The venue is fully zero-proof: its entire beverage program centers on kava, the South Pacific root traditionally used for relaxation. Bakaris serves traditional ceremonial kava, instant kava shots, and tropical "kavarita"-style blends, alongside wellness-oriented kava drinks marketed for "calm, clarity, and social vibes without alcohol." To-go ceremonial and instant kava packs are also available. The kitchen turns out halal turkey pepperoni and turkey bacon pizzas plus build-your-own vegan options with plant-based cheese, making it a draw for the Muslim community and sober-curious crowd alike. The lounge runs late-night, doubling as a community and wellness gathering space in Southwest Atlanta.
venues.hours: Mon closed; Tue-Thu 5pm-11:45pm; Fri 12am-2am & 2pm-2am; Sat 2pm-12am; Sun 5pm-11:45pm
venues.longDescription:
Bakaris Pizza & Kava Lounge has operated at 576 Lee Street SW in the historic West End since 2013, which by the standards of this category makes it an institution — the venue describes itself as twelve years strong, and it long predates the wave of alcohol-free bars that opened in Atlanta after 2022. The pairing is unusual and entirely deliberate: a pork-free halal and plant-based pizzeria with an alcohol-free kava bar attached.

The kitchen turns out halal turkey pepperoni and turkey bacon pizzas alongside build-your-own vegan options with plant-based cheese. That combination serves two groups at once — Muslim diners for whom both pork and alcohol are off the table, and a plant-based crowd — and it is the reason the room has the mix it does. It is one of the few places in the city where abstaining from alcohol is the unremarkable default rather than a request the staff have to accommodate.

The bar is entirely zero-proof and built on kava, the South Pacific root traditionally prepared as a relaxant. Bakaris serves traditional ceremonial kava, instant kava shots, tropical kava blends in the kavarita style, and wellness-oriented preparations it describes as being for calm and focus. Ceremonial and instant kava packs are sold to take away. The lounge runs late, and functions as a community and gathering space for Southwest Atlanta as much as a restaurant.

The venue's own FAQ makes the central point plainly, and it is the right one: kava is not alcohol. It is a plant-based beverage with a long traditional history. But it is psychoactive — a mild sedative — and that is worth stating for the same reason. It should not be combined with alcohol or with sedating medication, it can impair driving by slowing reflexes, and heavy or prolonged use has been associated with liver concerns. Unlike several kava bars in the city, Bakaris makes no mention of serving kratom, which is a genuinely different and more contested substance. If that distinction matters to you, it is worth confirming at the counter.

The practical case for it is the food. Most kava bars serve drinks and little else, which caps an evening at an hour or two before someone suggests moving on to a restaurant — and the restaurant usually has a bar. Being able to eat a full meal and stay put is what makes a venue like this work as a whole evening rather than a stop, and it is the reason the West End has kept it going for more than a decade.

venues.name: Baladi Coffee House
venues.description: Baladi Coffee House is a Yemeni coffeehouse on Lorain Road in North Olmsted that describes itself as authentic Yemeni coffee and tea, with tradition in every cup. It serves no alcohol and keeps the latest hours of the three Yemeni cafes in the suburb, open until 11pm most nights and 1am on Friday and Saturday. The shop says its beans come from a single farm in Haraz, Yemen, are never blended and are roasted to order. Its ordering menu runs from a Baladi House Latte and pistachio, Spanish, Biscoff and tiramisu lattes through matcha, frappes, smoothies, refreshers and tea, with sandwiches at the counter, and it sells its Jubani and Turkish blends and Adeni tea to take home.
venues.longDescription:
Baladi Coffee House is at 24942 Lorain Road in North Olmsted, and its own website announces the shop simply: North Olmsted location now open. Baladi is Arabic for my country or my homeland, and the business presents itself as an exceptional coffee experience rooted in heritage, craftsmanship and genuine hospitality. Its sourcing claim is specific. The beans, it says, are harvested from a single dedicated farm in Haraz, the mountain coffee region west of Sana'a in Yemen; they are never blended; and they are roasted to order with no fillers and no additives. The shop sells those beans by the bag as dark and medium roasts, a Jubani speciality blend and a Turkish speciality blend, along with Adeni tea bags.

The drinks menu is not published on the shop's own site, so what follows comes from its online ordering menu. The espresso bar is long: a Baladi House Latte served hot or iced, and pistachio, Spanish, Biscoff, tiramisu, brown sugar cinnamon and salted caramel lattes. Beyond it the menu is divided into refreshers, matcha, frappes, coffee, mojitos, tea, smoothies and milk-based drinks, with a short list of sandwiches. We have not listed prices, because delivery prices are higher than counter prices, and we have not named individual Yemeni coffees because the ordering menu does not show them item by item. Jubani, which the shop sells as a blend to take home, is the Yemeni style that brews coffee together with its husks and spices; Adeni tea is the cardamom-spiced milk tea of the port city of Aden.

It serves no alcohol. Its listed hours are the longest of the North Olmsted coffeehouses: 7am to 11pm from Monday to Thursday, 7am to 1am on Friday and Saturday, and 8am to 11pm on Sunday. That gives North Olmsted a room where a group can still be sitting at half past midnight on a Saturday over coffee. Qahwah House on Brookpark Road is under half a mile away and Shibam Coffee on Brookpark Extension about a mile and a quarter, so the three can be tried in one evening. The shop also takes catering and event orders through its website.
venues.pressQuote: An exceptional coffee experience rooted in heritage, craftsmanship, and genuine hospitality.

venues.name: Baladi Coffee
venues.description: Baladi Coffee is a family-owned Arabic coffeehouse on George Busbee Parkway in Kennesaw, run by Sarah and Allen, who describe it as "a Middle Eastern/Arabic coffee shop with influences from around the world". Baladi means "my homeland". It is fully alcohol-free and trades 7am to 10pm seven days a week, extending to midnight during Ramadan. The tea programme is the distinguishing feature: Adeni tea, Arabic tea, Yemeni tea and Pakistani chai are listed separately rather than folded into a single chai. Alongside them sit signature espresso drinks, a matcha list, and Peach Mango, Strawberry Acai and Watermelon Kiwi refreshers. The food counter runs to milk cake, kunafa and traditional and modern Arabic pastries, and there are further Baladi locations in Marietta and Athens.
venues.address: 3061 George Busbee Pkwy NW Suite 2000, Kennesaw, GA 30144
venues.longDescription:
Baladi is Arabic for "my homeland", and the shop's stated mission is to bring the flavours behind that word to a Cobb County strip centre. It is family-owned — Sarah and Allen are named as the owners on their listing with Atlanta Coffee Shops — and it has since grown to three Georgia sites, with the original in Kennesaw at 3061 George Busbee Parkway joined by locations in Marietta and Athens. The Kennesaw room trades from 7am to 10pm every day of the week, and extends to midnight through Ramadan, which is when the surrounding Muslim community does most of its evening socialising. There is no licence and no alcohol on the premises at any hour.

The tea list is what sets Baladi apart from the Yemeni coffeehouses elsewhere in the metro. Rather than collapsing everything into one chai, the menu treats Adeni tea, Arabic tea, Yemeni tea and Pakistani chai as four distinct preparations, each with its own spicing, and sells them alongside a matcha and chai section. The coffee side runs signature espresso drinks and a rotating "Wanderlust" list built around flavours from outside the region. The cold options are simple and popular: Peach Mango, Strawberry Acai and Watermelon Kiwi refreshers, which are what most tables order in a Georgia summer. Food is the other half of the draw — milk cake and kunafa lead a counter of traditional and modern Arabic pastries and quick bites, all halal. Because Kennesaw's evening trade is otherwise dominated by chain restaurants and sports bars, Baladi functions as one of the few places in north-west metro Atlanta where a group can sit at 9pm over drinks that nobody has to explain or apologise for. We have not listed an opening year because none is published on the company's own site, and we have not attributed a founding date to the brand for the same reason. The Kennesaw shop is the flagship of the three and the one with the longest hours; the Marietta site on Sandy Plains Road trades as a smaller grab-and-go format, and the Athens location serves the university town rather than the metro. Everything served at any of them is halal and non-alcoholic, and the shop holds no licence.

venues.name: The Lounge at Balanced Being
venues.description: Billed by its own team as Dallas's first plant bar and non-alcoholic lounge, The Lounge at Balanced Being is a fully alcohol-free social space on Lower Greenville — a room to relax and connect, in its own words, without alcohol. Access runs on reservations and memberships rather than walk-ins, with a first-visit fee. It is explicit that plant medicines are part of the offer, including kava and mushrooms, and that intentional cannabis use is welcomed within legal guidelines: alcohol-free, but emphatically not substance-free.
venues.longDescription:
Lower Greenville is one of Dallas's densest drinking strips, which makes the arrival of an avowedly alcohol-free lounge on it worth noting. Balanced Being calls its room Dallas's first plant bar and non-alcoholic lounge, and describes it as a social space to relax, connect and enjoy plant medicines and vibes without alcohol — a plant-forward space, in the venue's own phrase.

The access model is unusual and worth understanding before you go. This is not a walk-in bar: entry runs through reservations and a membership structure, with a fee for a first visit and weekly membership tiers beyond that. It behaves more like a private club or a wellness studio than a bar, which suits some people looking for an evening out and will put others off.

The disclosure here is the most important of any venue on our Dallas page. Balanced Being is clear that its offer includes kava and mushrooms, and that intentional cannabis use is welcomed within legal guidelines. Every one of those is a mood-altering substance. There is no alcohol, and for a drinker looking to socialise without it that may be exactly right — but this is a psychoactive lounge, and anyone whose sobriety means abstaining from intoxicants generally should read it as a venue to walk past. Opening hours are not published; book ahead.

venues.name: Baleia
venues.description: Baleia is a Portuguese-inspired, seafood-forward restaurant at 264 East Berkeley Street in Boston's South End, opened in 2024 as the fourth concept from Coda Restaurant Group, following CODA, The Salty Pig, SRV and Gufo. The restaurant describes itself as a love letter to Portugal — its seafood cooking, its easy-drinking cocktails and bold wines, and the soft lines of its sun-faded architecture — with a global influence layered over it. The drinks list prints a standing Low + No Proof section split between three house mocktails at $8 to $12 and three non-alcoholic wines by the glass at $13 to $14. The zero-proof cocktails are built on real non-alcoholic spirits including Almave and a zero-proof rosso vermouth.

venues.longDescription:
Baleia opened in 2024 on East Berkeley Street in the South End as the newest restaurant from Coda Restaurant Group, the Boston operator that began with CODA in 2008 and went on to open The Salty Pig in 2012, SRV in 2016 and Gufo in East Cambridge in 2023. The name is Portuguese for whale, and the restaurant states its premise plainly on its own site: a love letter to Portugal, to its seafood-forward cuisine, its easy-drinking cocktails and bold wines, and the soft lines of its sun-faded architecture, all infused with a global influence and a creative twist. In practice that means a seafood-led menu with Portuguese anchors treated freely rather than a strict regional reproduction. The Boston Globe included Baleia in its January 7, 2025 list of twelve spectacular spots for mocktails, describing it as a stylish new Portuguese restaurant from the team behind Gufo and SRV drawing a crowd willing to experiment with non-alcoholic drinks.

The alcohol-free drinks are printed under a Low + No Proof heading that is split into a Mocktails block and a Non-Alc Wine block, and — as at the group's other restaurants — they are built with commercial zero-proof spirits rather than juice alone. Dutchess Palmer is the entry point at $8, a tea-led build using MEM's Duchess Grey with grapefruit, lemon and tonic. Bebida Errada at $12 is the most complex, combining a Free Spirit rosso zero-proof vermouth with aperitivo, syrup, Wolffer non-alcoholic sparkling, rose and a lemon twist — effectively an alcohol-free spritz with real bitterness in it. Strawberry Fields, also $12, is built on Almave, the de-alcoholised agave spirit, with elderflower, strawberry, vanilla, lemon, orange blossom and sea salt, and functions as the list's margarita substitute. The non-alcoholic wines are the same three the group pours across its restaurants, all German and all under 0.5%: Wolffer Estate "Spring in a Bottle" rose and Wander + Found "Cuvee Blanc" white at $13 each, and Odd Bird "G.S.M Rouge" red at $14. Baleia serves dinner nightly from 5pm.
venues.pressQuote: This stylish new Portuguese restaurant in the South End, from the team behind Gufo and SRV, welcomes a cosmopolitan crowd eager to experiment with nonalcoholic delights.

venues.name: The Ball & Biscuit
venues.description: The Ball & Biscuit opened on Massachusetts Avenue in June 2010 and is generally credited as Indiana's first craft cocktail bar. It was founded by local attorney Trevor Belden with bartender Zach Wilks, who later left to build the Wilks & Wilson syrup line, and takes its name from the 1930s ribbon microphone nicknamed the ball and biscuit — vintage mics and music gear are part of the fit-out. For a bar of that vintage the non-alcoholic list is unusually developed: seven named zero-proof drinks stand alongside the full-proof menu rather than in a footnote, including the Spritz AF built on Lyre's Italian Orange and Aperitif Rosso with Fre sparkling brut, the Twist of Fate, the New Fashioned and the floral Whole Garden.
signatureDrinks: Spritz AF (Lyre's Italian Orange, Lyre's Aperitif Rosso, lemon, orange juice, Fre non-alcoholic sparkling brut)
Twist of Fate (zero-proof spirit, ginger syrup, basil concentrate, lemon, club soda)
