venues.longDescription:
Bar None launched on 28 February 2026 in the West Loop, an evening concept from Heritage Hospitality Group that transforms Froth — their daytime coffee cafe in the lobby of The Duncan at 1515 W Monroe Street — into a bar from 5pm to 11pm, Friday through Sunday. Founder Michael Salvatore framed the idea in terms worth quoting: we're not removing something from nightlife, he told Time Out Chicago at launch, we're building something entirely new. The drinks are run by beverage director Luke Nevin-Gattle, whose background is in full-proof rooms including Bunker and Larry's, and the cocktails show it. All five are $13 and built on genuine non-alcoholic spirits rather than juice: a Phony Negroni poured from St. Agrestis, an espresso martini combining Ritual's rum alternative with The Pathfinder, espresso and demerara, Good Vibrations with Ritual gin alternative, Giffard elderflower, pineapple, lime and coconut, a spicy margarita using Ritual agave alternative with Lyre's Italian Orange, jalapeño-agave and Tajín, and a Gold Rush built on Ritual whiskey alternative with aperitif, orange bitters, lemon and honey. Behind them sits one of the deepest packaged ranges in the city at these prices — nine non-alcoholic beers and ciders at $6, including Guinness 0, Athletic's Cerveza Atlética, Best Day Kölsch, Untitled Art Orange Peel Wit and an Original Sin blackberry cider, plus Leitz Eins Zwei Zero sparkling rosé, white and red at $9.

One thing needs stating plainly, because the venue's own branding leads with it and a reader in recovery should not discover it on arrival: Bar None describes itself as a THC-integrated sober lounge, not simply an alcohol-free one. Any cocktail on the list can be upgraded for $4 with a 2.5mg THC microdose, and the bar sells 5mg THC seltzers at $9 as a separate line. None of that touches the cocktails themselves, which contain no alcohol and no THC unless you ask — so the room works perfectly well as a straightforwardly alcohol-free bar, and the drinks list is strong enough to be worth the trip on its own. But it is built around cannabis as a social substitute rather than around abstinence, which suits some people avoiding alcohol and is exactly wrong for others.
venues.pressQuote: We're not removing something from nightlife. We're building something entirely new.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Michael Salvatore, founder, Heritage Hospitality Group

venues.name: Bar Nuda
venues.description: STATUS UNCERTAIN — CHECK BEFORE PLANNING AROUND THIS. Bar Nuda is Los Angeles's first Mexican-inspired non-alcoholic pop-up bar, a roving, fully zero-proof operation founded around 2023 by Pablo Murillo and Morris Ellis, owners of the agua fresca company Aguas Locas, with drinks by Bryant J. Orozco. Its cocktails are built on native herbs — Orozco has infused them with chuchupaxtle, also known as osha root — and it describes each drink as having a functional objective such as relaxation or concentration. Its last confirmed run was a Wednesday-to-Friday residency at a Venice café through the summer of 2025; we can find no dated evidence of an event since May 2025, its own site has no menu or events page, and the café that hosted it no longer lists it. Documented drinks include zero-proof cempasúchil carajillos, the Rosa Nuda (non-alcoholic tequila, bougainvillea, rose hips, lemon), the Magón (beets, ginger, hibiscus, grape) and United Ferments' Snow Chrysanthemum non-alcoholic wine. Follow its social channels for any revival rather than travelling on spec.
signatureDrinks: Rosa Nuda (NA tequila, bougainvillea, rose hips, lemon, NA orange bitters)
venues.longDescription:
Bar Nuda was built to do something specific: create a sober, social, safe space where people can go out, make connections and get those deep belly laughs without the pressure of drinking, while celebrating Mexican culture. That is co-founder Pablo Murillo's own description, and the reason behind it is personal — his father died of alcohol-related illness in 2017, three months after the birth of Murillo's eldest daughter and shortly after being deported to Mexico. He wanted, in his words, to change the narrative of his family and help others do the same, creating a space where people can heal while enjoying a night out. He runs it with Morris Ellis; the two also own the bottled agua fresca company Aguas Locas, and Bryant J. Orozco built the drinks. What set the bar apart was that it never imitated: Murillo's view is that people are not really looking for a non-alcoholic version of a margarita, they are looking for something more creative, something they may never have tasted before. The drinks bear that out — zero-proof cempasúchil carajillos, a Rosa Nuda of non-alcoholic tequila with bougainvillea and rose hips, a Magón built on beets, ginger, hibiscus and grape, and a bottle of United Ferments' Snow Chrysanthemum non-alcoholic wine. Orozco has also infused drinks with chuchupaxtle, the native herb also called osha root; the "functional" label here means botanicals aimed at relaxation or focus, not cannabis or kava.

We cannot tell you when to go, and it would be wrong to imply we can. Bar Nuda has never had a fixed address — it is a pop-up that takes over host venues — and its last confirmed run was a residency at a Venice café on Wednesdays to Fridays through the summer of 2025. Since then the trail goes cold. Its own website has no menu page and no events page at all; both return errors. The café that hosted the residency no longer mentions it anywhere, and its events listing is empty. We could find no dated evidence of a Bar Nuda event later than May 2025 — roughly fifteen months. That is not the same as closed, and pop-ups routinely go quiet between seasons, so the listing stays. But treat it as a project to follow rather than a place to turn up at.
venues.pressQuote: At Bar Nuda, a DJ's música tropical beats circle through the air as plates of pollo verde-loaded nachos and sushi-grade ahi tostadas are passed to tables of lively guests, sipping on zero-proof cempasúchil carajillos, mock margaritas, and chrysanthemum-based, non-alcoholic wine.

venues.name: Bar Palmina
venues.description: Bar Palmina is Philadelphia's first fully zero-proof cocktail bar, where everything served — down to the bitters — is alcohol-free. It opened in Fishtown in 2024, founded by Nikki Graziano, who built the bar after a 2022 liver transplant prompted by alcohol-related liver failure and her subsequent path to sobriety. The bar is named for her Italian-American grandmother, Palmina. The menu runs about 22 signature and classic non-alcoholic cocktails alongside 11 NA wines and proxies and 7 NA beers, with house-made and from-scratch infusions throughout. Named drinks include the Yuzu Negroni, D'Argento (rice-washed white tea, cucumber, juniper, yuzu), The Lifesaver (lemongrass, ginger, coconut), and the Limonhattan. The living-room-style lounge also screens soccer matches. It was named Philadelphia Magazine's Best Non-Alcoholic Bar in 2025.
venues.hours: Mon closed; Tue-Thu 4pm-10pm; Fri 4pm-11pm; Sat 2pm-11pm; Sun closed
venues.longDescription:
Bar Palmina is Philadelphia's first fully zero-proof cocktail bar, and the distinction matters: everything in the room is alcohol-free, down to the bitters. That last detail is the one most places skip. Standard cocktail bitters run to 35–45% alcohol by volume, and while a few dashes amount to a trace, a bar serving people in recovery cannot reasonably describe a drink containing them as alcohol-free. Sourcing alcohol-free bitters is harder and more expensive than the alternative, and doing it anyway is the clearest possible signal of who this bar is built for.

It opened in Fishtown in 2024, founded by Nikki Graziano, who built it after a 2022 liver transplant caused by alcohol-related liver failure and the sobriety that followed. She named it for her Italian-American grandmother, Palmina. Philadelphia Magazine's Best of Philly coverage put the origin plainly: having embraced sobriety after the transplant, Graziano found the city's non-alcoholic options lacking, and built what was missing.

The menu is unusually deep for the format — around twenty-two signature and classic non-alcoholic cocktails, eleven non-alcoholic wines and proxies, and seven non-alcoholic beers, with house-made infusions running through the list rather than bought-in syrups. The Yuzu Negroni takes the bitter-forward Negroni structure into yuzu, the aromatic Japanese citrus that is more floral and less sweet than lemon. The Limonhattan applies the same logic to a Manhattan. D'Argento and The Lifesaver round out the signatures.

The scale of that list is the point. A fully alcohol-free bar with four drinks is a gesture; one with twenty-two cocktails, eleven wines and seven beers is a bar, and a group can spend an entire evening there without repeating an order or thinking about what they are missing. It trades Tuesday through Saturday, opening at four in the afternoon and running to eleven at weekends, with a two o'clock Saturday start.
venues.pressQuote: After embracing sobriety following a liver transplant in 2022, Nikki Graziano found Philly's nonalcoholic options lacking.

venues.name: Bar Pigalle
venues.description: Bar Pigalle is a French-leaning cocktail bar in Detroit's Brush Park neighborhood with a dedicated, printed Non-Alcoholic cocktail section on its summer 2026 menu.

Wishful Thinking (NA Amaro Lucano, honeycrisp apple, raspberry, ginger ale)

venues.longDescription:
Bar Pigalle opened in June 2022 inside the Carlton Lofts on John R Street in Brush Park, a building designed by architect Louis Kamper that was the backdrop for one of Detroit's hottest jazz rooms in the 1920s and '30s. The name and concept play off Brush Park's own history as a onetime hub of French immigrant life, once nicknamed "Little Paris." Managing Partner Travis Fourmont, an award-winning mixologist, runs the bar program; the kitchen turns out "playfully modern French fare" under Executive Chef Partner Norman Valenti.

The summer 2026 cocktail menu gives non-alcoholic drinks their own printed section, priced and presented alongside the boozy list rather than tacked on as an afterthought. Clean Slate ($15) is built on Lyre's Italian Spritz with blueberry, lemon, and Casamara Club Alta; Wishful Thinking ($10) mixes NA Amaro Lucano with honeycrisp apple, raspberry, and ginger ale; Plot Twist ($9) is a pomegranate vinegar shrub finished with sparkling lemonade. Hour Detroit's January 2024 mocktail roundup documented a different rotating pair on that season's menu — a Dhos-based Pigalle Bitter Spritz and an N/A Skeleton Key made with Kentucky 74 NA whiskey — confirming the alcohol-free section is a standing fixture that turns over with the seasonal menu rather than a one-off gesture.

Bar Pigalle takes reservations through Resy and sits in the heart of Brush Park, Detroit's fast-redeveloping historic district between downtown and Midtown. It's open seven nights a week: Monday through Thursday 5–10pm, Friday and Saturday 5–11pm, and Sunday 4–9pm.
venues.pressQuote: Bar Pigalle is a lively Detroit hotspot that elevates the mocktail scene with drinks like the N/A Skeleton Key, crafted from Kentucky 74 NA whiskey, elderflower, ginger, lemon, and soda.

venues.name: Bar Please!
venues.description: Bar Please! sits on the third floor at 620 West Idaho Street, directly above Thick as Thieves, and its alcohol-free entry is a Kimchi Michelada served with watermelon shaved ice — which is a genuinely strange and genuinely interesting drink. A michelada is normally beer, lime, chilli and savoury seasoning; building one without the beer and pushing it toward kimchi means going all-in on funk, salt and fermentation, which is the opposite of the sweet default. One drink is a modest programme, but it is a memorable one. The bar keeps long hours — to midnight midweek and 1am at weekends — and Thick as Thieves is one flight down if the michelada is not for you.
venues.address: 620 W Idaho St Ste 300, Boise, ID 83702
signatureDrinks: Kimchi Michelada with watermelon shaved ice
venues.longDescription:
Bar Please! occupies the third floor at 620 West Idaho Street in downtown Boise, one level above Thick as Thieves. The two are separate bars in the same building with the same hours, so a visit to one makes the other essentially free.

Its alcohol-free drink is a Kimchi Michelada with watermelon shaved ice, and it is worth describing properly because almost nobody makes anything like it. A michelada is normally beer with lime, chilli, salt and something savoury — Worcestershire, clamato, hot sauce. Remove the beer and most bars would sweeten to compensate. Going the other way, toward kimchi, doubles down on the parts that were never about alcohol in the first place: fermentation funk, salt, chilli heat, sourness. The watermelon shaved ice then cuts across all of it with cold and sweetness.

That combination is a real piece of drink design. It also demonstrates something worth understanding about the category: savoury and fermented flavours are the most underused tools in alcohol-free bartending, because they deliver complexity without relying on either sugar or the warmth of a spirit. A drink that is salty, sour and spicy holds attention across a whole glass in a way a fruit cooler cannot.

The grade is an honest 3 — one named drink is not a programme, however good the drink is. But the hours are strong, 4pm to midnight through the week and 1am on Friday and Saturday, and the building's double-bar arrangement makes this one of the most convenient stops downtown. Try the michelada first; if it is not to your taste, Thick as Thieves is one flight down with three more options. Between the two floors, this single address is the most efficient stop in downtown Boise for anyone not drinking.
venues.pressQuote: Bar Please will be more of an upbeat neighborhood bar that's offering a unique experience to downtown

venues.name: Bar Pompette
venues.description: Bar Pompette is a French-Italian cocktail bar on College Street in Toronto's Little Italy, ranked #1 on Canada's 100 Best Bars in 2025 and recognized on the World's 50 Best Bars list. Its non-alcoholic program is built around a house-made non-alcoholic aperitif crafted from Ontario and Quebec botanicals, used across the bar's drink menu rather than sitting apart as an afterthought. The zero-proof list includes the named Provence En Fleur, built from pear, lavender, mosaic hops and tonic. It's a walk-ins-only room — no reservations taken.
venues.address: 607 College St, Toronto, ON M6G 1B5, Canada
signatureDrinks: Provence En Fleur (non-alcoholic) — pear, lavender, mosaic hops, tonic
venues.longDescription:
Bar Pompette is a French-Italian cocktail bar on College Street in Toronto's Little Italy, part of a small Pompette-branded group that also includes Bakery Pompette, a French bakery, Bar Allegro, an aperitivo bar, and Pelican Wine, an agency for organic and biodynamic French wine. The bar takes walk-ins only, with no reservations, Sunday through Thursday from 6pm to 1am and Friday and Saturday until 2am. It has drawn outsized recognition for a neighbourhood address, landing on the World's 50 Best Bars list and ranked #1 on Canada's 100 Best Bars in 2025.

The non-alcoholic side of the program is genuine rather than a token gesture: Bar Pompette makes its own non-alcoholic aperitif in-house from Ontario and Quebec botanicals, and it runs through the bar's wider drink program rather than being confined to a single mocktail. Among the named zero-proof cocktails is the Provence En Fleur, built from pear, lavender, mosaic hops and tonic.

Over Here Toronto's guide to the city's best non-alcoholic bars singled Bar Pompette out specifically for the seriousness of its zero-proof list, noting a non-alcoholic Negroni riff the bar once served as "complex and bitter in all the right ways" — a sign that the alcohol-free drinks here are built with the same technique as the bar's better-known boozy cocktails, not treated as an afterthought to them.
venues.pressQuote: Located on College Street, this stylish French-Italian spot is famous for its cocktails, but their zero-proof options are also top-notch. They once offered a non-alcoholic Negroni riff that was complex and bitter in all the right ways.

venues.longDescription:
Bar RBC sits on Minnesota Avenue in the middle of downtown Bend, and it is the most polished cocktail room in a town whose drinking culture is otherwise built on breweries and flannel. The bar runs a proper zero-proof menu — a named section with its own drinks, not a pair of substitutions offered on request — which in a beer town is a deliberate statement about who the room is for.

The two documented builds cover opposite ends of the spectrum, which is the sign of a list designed rather than assembled. The Phony White Negroni takes on the harder assignment: a white negroni depends on the interplay of gentian bitterness and floral gin botanicals, with no fruit to disguise a weak base, so getting it crisp rather than flat is real work. The Shindig goes the other way entirely — pineapple and lime, punchy and bright, the drink for a warm evening on the sidewalk tables rather than a slow one at the bar.

Downtown Bend is compact enough that Bar RBC sits within a few blocks of Deschutes' public house, Zydeco, San Simón, Silver Moon and Dear Irene, which makes an evening of zero-proof drinks genuinely walkable here in a way it is not in most cities this size.

The room opens at four every day and runs to nine through the week and ten at weekends. It takes the food side seriously too, so it works as a dinner destination rather than only a drinks stop.
venues.pressQuote: brings modern, upscale energy to downtown, and their zero-proof menu matches the mood

venues.name: Bar Renée
venues.description: Bar Renée is a natural wine bar and bottle shop on Main Street in downtown Burlington, pouring low-intervention wines from Vermont and further afield with no additives. Its list deliberately runs past wine into the adjacent categories — ciders, co-ferments and a curated selection of non-alcoholic drinks — which makes it one of the few places in the city where someone not drinking is choosing between several interesting bottles rather than between soda and water. Snacks run to charcuterie, local cheese, tinned fish, olives and almonds. Open from noon to 10pm most days and to 11pm on Friday and Saturday, closed Tuesday, and no reservations.
venues.hours: Mon 12pm-10pm; Wed-Thu 12pm-10pm; Fri-Sat 12pm-11pm; Sun 12pm-10pm; Tue closed
venues.longDescription:
Bar Renée is both a bar and a shop: you can drink a glass at the counter or take the bottle home, and the whole selection is built on low-intervention winemaking — wines made without additives, from producers in Vermont and around the world who work that way as a matter of practice rather than marketing.

What makes it relevant here is that the buying philosophy does not stop at wine. The list runs deliberately into the neighbouring categories: ciders, co-ferments, and a curated set of non-alcoholic drinks chosen with the same eye. That is a meaningful distinction. Most wine bars that stock something alcohol-free stock one thing, usually a de-alcoholised sparkling wine that nobody at the bar has tasted. A shop that treats non-alcoholic bottles as part of the same buying discipline — interesting ferments, unusual producers, things worth talking about — gives a non-drinker the actual bar experience, which is choosing.

The room itself is small and informal, with no reservations taken, and the food is the correct kind of unambitious: charcuterie boards, local cheeses, tinned fish, olives and almonds. It functions as an afternoon place as much as an evening one, opening at noon.

This listing carries a grade of three and no signature drinks. Bar Renée's non-alcoholic selection is a rotating retail assortment rather than a fixed menu, so naming any specific bottle would be wrong within weeks — the honest thing to record is the standing commitment to stock the category properly, which is well evidenced and unusual for a wine bar this size.

Open noon to 10pm Monday, Wednesday, Thursday and Sunday, to 11pm on Friday and Saturday. Closed Tuesday.
venues.pressQuote: Four beer, four cider, six nonalcoholic.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Alex Leopold, co-owner, Bar Renée, on what is poured alongside the wine

venues.name: Bar Tonique
venues.description: Bar Tonique is a French Quarter craft-cocktail bar on N Rampart Street, opened in 2008 by Ed Diaz as one of the first stand-alone bars of New Orleans' modern cocktail revival (Neal Bodenheimer wrote its first menu). Beyond classics like its acclaimed Ramos Gin Fizz, the bar keeps a standing "Temperance" menu of non-alcoholic soda-fountain drinks modeled on pre-Prohibition phosphates and craft sodas — an idea Diaz drew from Darcy O'Neil's book "Fix the Pumps." The list includes pineapple and Angostura phosphates and house cream sodas built on made-from-scratch strawberry and pineapple syrups, plus a "milk shake" of cream, strawberry syrup, and a whole egg. Designated drivers can order from the Temperance menu free of charge.
venues.address: 820 N Rampart St, New Orleans, LA 70116
venues.longDescription:
Bar Tonique sits at 820 North Rampart Street on the edge of the French Quarter, and Where Y'at's description of walking in is the useful one: it takes you back to colonial New Orleans, with a beautiful brick interior that seems unchanged for two hundred years — and, the magazine adds, the prices will take you back as well. That combination is the whole proposition. This is a craft cocktail bar in a city full of them, but it is a neighbourhood one, priced for regulars rather than for Bourbon Street, and it opens daily from noon until 2am, which makes it useful at hours when very little else with this standard is serving. New Orleans Magazine noted early on what separates the drinks: fresh-squeezed juices as mixers rather than bottled ones, and most drinks sweetened with organic agave nectar in place of sugar. In a small, dim, brick room with fresh flowers along the bar top, that attention is what you are paying for.

For non-drinkers, the bar uses an older and rather better word than mocktail: temperance drinks. It is a nineteenth-century term from the temperance movement itself, and it fits a room styled after the same era — the drinks are built like cocktails, from the same fresh juice and agave the rest of the bar runs on, rather than being assembled from soda guns. Phosphates in particular belong to this tradition: a soda-fountain format built on acid phosphate, which gives a sweet drink a dry, mineral tartness that plain citrus cannot, and which has been quietly revived by exactly the kind of bar that takes its history seriously. Two practical caveats. The bar's menu is published as a file that cannot be read online, so the current temperance list and its prices have to be seen in person. And its website redirects to a single-page Adobe Express site — that is genuinely its own current page rather than an abandoned one, but it carries little beyond hours and an address.
venues.pressQuote: Walking inside takes patrons back to colonial New Orleans with a beautiful brick interior that seems unchanged for over 200 years—and the prices will take you back, as well.

venues.name: bar Vetti
venues.description: bar Vetti is an Italian restaurant and bar on East Market Street in NuLu, and it runs one of the most technically serious non-alcoholic lists in Louisville. Rather than sweetening juice, the bar rebuilds Italian aperitivo structure without alcohol: the N.A.-Groni is a zero-proof negroni using Ritual Zero Proof alongside Martini & Rossi Floreale and Vibrante, the two de-alcoholised vermouth-style aperitifs, and the Impostore Spritz and Bianca Spritz work the same bitter-and-bubbles register that the room's alcoholic list is built on. Non-alcoholic beer from Athletic Brewing and Lagunitas is stocked alongside. Dinner runs nightly with lunch midweek and weekend brunch.
signatureDrinks: N.A.-Groni (Ritual Zero Proof, Martini & Rossi Floreale, Martini & Rossi Vibrante)
venues.longDescription:
NuLu — the East Market District — is the stretch of Louisville that turned from warehouses into galleries and restaurants over the last fifteen years, and bar Vetti sits in the middle of it at 727 East Market. The cooking is Italian and the room is a proper restaurant bar rather than a cocktail den, which matters for how the non-alcoholic list is built: an Italian drinks programme starts from aperitivo, and aperitivo is a structure — bitter, aromatised, lengthened — rather than a specific bottle of alcohol. That structure survives de-alcoholisation better than almost anything else behind a bar.

So the N.A.-Groni is not a gesture. It reads as a negroni because it is assembled like one: Ritual Zero Proof standing in for the gin, and Martini & Rossi's Floreale and Vibrante — the de-alcoholised aperitifs the Italian house launched specifically to hold the vermouth and bitter positions — doing the rest. The Impostore Spritz and the Bianca Spritz work the same bitter-and-bubbles idea at a lighter proof-free weight. Behind them the bar keeps non-alcoholic beer from Athletic Brewing and from Lagunitas, so a table of mixed drinkers has real range rather than one token option. LOUtoday listed the bar in its Dry January round-up on the strength of that list.

Practically, this is the most useful entry in the guide for a proper dinner without drinking. The kitchen runs nightly from 5pm, with midweek lunch and weekend brunch, and the pricing on the zero-proof drinks tracks the cocktails rather than sitting at soft-drink level — which is the correct signal that they are made to the same specification. NoraeBar, the Korean karaoke bar that also keeps alcohol-free versions of its house drinks, is ten doors down at 717 East Market, and High Stakes Rooftop is two blocks south, so NuLu supports a whole evening without a drink in it.
venues.pressQuote: Some mocktails to choose from include "Impostore Spritz," "Bianca Spritz" and the "N.A.-Groni." Non-alcoholic beers from Athletic Brewing and Lagunitas Brewing Company are also available.

venues.name: Bar X
venues.description: A historic downtown cocktail bar that traces its roots to 1933 and was restored into its current craft-cocktail incarnation in 2011 by a group that includes Modern Family actor Ty Burrell. There's no fixed mocktail menu; instead bartenders take a "roulette" approach, asking what flavors you're craving and building custom zero-proof drinks from house-made syrups, fresh juices, ginger beer and tinctures — sometimes finishing with a flamed-cinnamon flourish for theater. The Salt Lake Tribune singled out Bar X for its non-alcoholic creativity, and as manager Julie Tall puts it, the staff geek out over flavors more than the spirits, so cocktails and mocktails get equal care.
venues.address: 155 E 200 S, Salt Lake City, UT 84111
venues.longDescription:
Bar X sits on the 200 South strip of downtown bars and has become a regular recommendation for the Dry January crowd. The no-menu approach means non-drinkers, designated drivers, and pregnant guests can simply describe what they're in the mood for and trust the bartender to compose something on the spot.

The non-alcoholic program drew local TV and newspaper coverage in 2024, with the Salt Lake Tribune featuring bartender Eric Lewis pouring flamed cinnamon over a craft mocktail for a fiery effect. The bar is open Tuesday through Saturday from 4pm and Sunday and Monday from 6pm, with live music on Wednesdays and Thursdays.
venues.pressQuote: When a lot of people think of a bar, they think of a place where you go to get alcohol, and that's enough of a sales pitch for most people. And so when people come in, and they're asking for something that doesn't have any of that, we see it as, one, a tremendous compliment.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Eric Lewis, bartender at Bar X
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Salt & Seek (citing Salt Lake Tribune, Jan 2024)

venues.name: Barbacoa Grill
venues.description: Barbacoa Grill, near Parkcenter Boulevard on the river side of Boise, pairs a deliberately theatrical dining room with a dedicated mocktail menu it calls Zero Regrets. A named, separately headed section is the thing that matters: it converts ordering without alcohol from a request into a selection, which is the difference between being accommodated and being catered for. The restaurant is one of Boise's special-occasion rooms, which is exactly the setting where somebody at the table is most likely to be pregnant, driving or simply not drinking. It is out by Parkcenter rather than downtown, so it needs a drive, and it serves seven days from 4pm.
signatureDrinks: Zero Regrets - the house dedicated mocktail menu

venues.longDescription:
Barbacoa Grill sits near Parkcenter Boulevard, away from downtown Boise on the river side of the city, and it is unapologetically theatrical — elaborate interiors, tableside preparation, the kind of room people book for anniversaries and birthdays rather than drop into.

Its alcohol-free offering is a dedicated menu headed Zero Regrets. The name is a joke, but the structure is the substance. A separately titled section on the printed menu changes the social mechanics of the whole evening: instead of catching a server's eye, explaining, and waiting while they check with the bar, you read a list and choose from it exactly as everybody else does. Ordering stops being a small negotiation and becomes an ordinary transaction. That single formatting decision does more for a non-drinker than an extra ingredient in any given glass.

The setting sharpens the point. Special-occasion restaurants are precisely where the non-drinking problem becomes conspicuous — a table of twelve, a toast, one person with a soda. These are also the evenings most likely to include someone pregnant, someone driving everyone home, or someone in recovery who came anyway. A room that prints alcohol-free drinks as a proper section has thought about who is actually sitting at its tables.

Hours are consistent: 4pm to 10pm most days, to 11pm on Friday and Saturday, open seven days. Being out by Parkcenter it needs a drive from downtown, so treat it as a destination rather than part of a walkable evening — but it is one of the few Boise venues in this guide that is genuinely built for an occasion. Book ahead at weekends, and mention the Zero Regrets menu when you do if someone at the table is not drinking.
venues.pressQuote: pairs its theatrical dining atmosphere with a dedicated “Zero Regrets” mocktail menu that applies the same creativity to non-alcoholic beverages as the kitchen brings to Hot Rock steaks and tableside guacamole

venues.name: Barlette
venues.description: Barlette is a small cocktail bar in the Arcade Building at 318 Harvard Street in Coolidge Corner, Brookline, opened in 2023 by Rachel Trudel and chef Emily Vena, whose restaurant Cobble sits a floor above. It began as an alcohol-agnostic BYOB bar, where guests brought their own spirits and the bar supplied everything else, and it kept that structure after earning a full liquor licence in November 2024. The result is a menu where the base is a choice rather than a fixture: seasonal and classic cocktails are each offered with bourbon, gin, rum, tequila, vodka or spirit-free, so a non-drinker orders the same drink as everyone else. It is walk-ins only, wheelchair accessible, and open Wednesday to Saturday evenings.

venues.longDescription:
Barlette opened in 2023 in the Coolidge Corner Arcade Building, a small tucked-away room at 318 Harvard Street run by Rachel Trudel with chef Emily Vena, who also runs Cobble one floor above. Its original form was unusual: a BYOB bar where guests brought their own bottle and Barlette supplied the house-made mixers, garnishes, ice, glassware and room. Boston Magazine reported the concept in January 2023 before it opened, the Boston Globe visited in May 2023, and Brookline Hub checked back in after eight months of trading. The bar earned its own full liquor licence in November 2024 and reintroduced itself as a conventional cocktail bar — but it kept the architecture that the BYOB period had forced on it, which is why its alcohol-free offering is structurally different from most. Trudel has framed the intent directly, saying that while Barlette is not a non-alcoholic bar, it hopes to delight guests who choose not to imbibe.

In practice that means the base spirit is a variable rather than a fixed part of each recipe: the menu instructs guests to choose bourbon, gin, rum, tequila, vodka or spirit-free across most of the seasonal and classic list, so the spirit-free version of a drink is the same drink with the same house syrups, foams and garnishes. The seasonals run $17 and change with the produce — recent listings include Knee Deep in the Passenger Seat with lavender honey and fresh lemon, I Curried a Watermelon with watermelon juice, red Thai curry and pickled watermelon rind, Off the Cob with fresh corn, jalapeno, lime and a buttered corn foam, and Coco Loco Yoko with toasted coconut, white chocolate and passionfruit. The classics at $18 include a house espresso martini built on freshly brewed espresso, available regular or decaf, with vanilla bean, plus a negroni, martini, manhattan and old fashioned. Meet Boston's January 2026 zero-proof guide characterised the result as comforting, cafe-inspired drinks that highlight warmth and balance. Food is a short list of bar snacks; entry is walk-in only.

venues.name: Barra
venues.description: Barra is a small Mexico City-influenced restaurant and mezcal bar at 23A Bow Street in Union Square, Somerville, serving aguachiles, tacos on hand-pressed tortillas, and a house mole built from twenty-five ingredients over several days. Its bar holds more than eighty mezcal expressions, but the printed menu also carries a standing block headed Non-Alcoholic Mocktail, offering spirit-free versions of the passion fruit mojito, the paloma, the chamango and the entire frappe collection at $12, or a bartender's build to order. Alongside those it lists Notch non-alcoholic IPA at $7, which can be turned into a michelada, house aguas frescas in hibiscus or tamarind at $6, and Mexican sodas including Coca-Cola Mexicana and Mineragua at $5.
signatureDrinks: Notch NA IPA michelada (NA IPA, lime, salt rim)

naMenuItems.name: Virgin Versions of Passion Fruit Mojito, Frappé Collection, Paloma, Chamango or Make Your Own

venues.longDescription:
Barra is a compact Union Square room at 23A Bow Street that imports the bar-and-dining culture of Mexico City rather than the Tex-Mex format most American Mexican restaurants default to. The kitchen's signature is the Aguachile Amarillo, an original recipe credited on the menu to chef Sofia Garcia Osorio, in which raw white fish is dressed in a passion fruit and serrano emulsion with orange supremes, cucumber and avocado. Around it sit tuna tostaditas, a tetela poblana — a triangular corn pocket stuffed with queso anejo and beans under house mole — enmoladas finished with a mole the menu says takes twenty-five ingredients and several days to build, birria, cochinita pibil marinated overnight in Yucatan achiote, and tacos on hand-pressed tortillas including the quesabirrias and the costra, a flank steak taco wrapped in a crust of cheese. The mezcal list runs past eighty expressions with flights chosen by the bartender. Boston.com covered the bar's alcohol-free work in its January 2025 Dry January round-up.

The non-alcoholic offering is printed on the same page as the cocktails under the heading Non-Alcoholic Mocktail, and it is structured as a permission rather than a fixed list: for $12 the bar will make spirit-free versions of the passion fruit mojito, the paloma, the chamango and anything from the frappe collection — which in full-strength form covers a mint lemonade, a guava colada and a tamarind spicy margarita — or build something to order. That matters because it means a non-drinker at Barra gets the same frozen, fruit-forward, chile-salted drinks the table is having rather than a soft drink. Notch non-alcoholic IPA is $7 and can be turned into a michelada for $5 more, which is a genuinely uncommon offer and one of the better alcohol-free options in the city for anyone who wants something savoury and salty rather than sweet. House aguas frescas are $6 in hibiscus or tamarind, and the soda list carries Coca-Cola Mexicana, Mineragua and ginger beer at $5. Barra opens at 5pm Tuesday through Sunday and is closed Mondays.
venues.pressQuote: Barra can also make other drinks spirit-free, like their mojito and passion fruit margarita.

venues.name: Barrel Bar & Grill
venues.description: Barrel Bar & Grill sits on Whiskey Row, the block of West Main Street that holds Louisville's bourbon-tourism distilleries, and is the bar and grill attached to the Louisville Comedy Club. Its zero-proof list is the most locally rooted in the city: the Zero Proof Old Fashioned is built on Kentucky 74, the non-alcoholic bourbon made in Louisville by Spiritless, so the signature Kentucky drink is served here in a genuinely Kentucky alcohol-free form rather than as an imported substitute. Alongside it sit the Pineapple Upside Down Cake, built on caramel, ginger and grenadine, and the Cinderella — orange and pineapple juice with ginger ale, grenadine and bitters.
signatureDrinks: Zero Proof Old Fashioned (Spiritless Kentucky 74 non-alcoholic bourbon)
Pineapple Upside Down Cake (caramel, ginger, grenadine)
Cinderella (orange juice, pineapple juice, ginger ale, grenadine, bitters)
venues.longDescription:
Whiskey Row is the restored run of nineteenth-century cast-iron facades on West Main Street that now holds most of Louisville's urban bourbon distilleries and their visitor centres. It is, for a non-drinker, one of the harder blocks in America to spend an evening on. Barrel Bar & Grill sits at 110 West Main in the middle of it, attached to the Louisville Comedy Club, and does something genuinely useful: it serves the city's signature drink in a form someone who does not drink can order.

The Zero Proof Old Fashioned is built on Kentucky 74, the non-alcoholic bourbon distilled in Louisville by Spiritless — a company founded here by three mothers who wanted a drink that let them keep their evenings and their next mornings. Kentucky 74 is made by reverse distillation, which strips the alcohol from a finished distillate while keeping the caramel, vanilla and oak the bourbon has taken from the barrel, and it was named Best Non-Alcoholic Spirit at the L.A. Spirits Awards. Ordering an old fashioned made from it on Whiskey Row is, more than anything else in this guide, the Louisville answer to the question of what a non-drinker does here. The rest of the list is deliberately unserious and works for it: the Pineapple Upside Down Cake on caramel, ginger and grenadine, and the Cinderella, which layers orange and pineapple juice with ginger ale, grenadine and bitters.

The comedy club attachment is the other practical point. A stand-up show gives the evening a structure that is not drinking — you are facing a stage rather than a bar — which makes this one of the easier nights out in the city for someone avoiding alcohol, in the one part of town otherwise built entirely around whiskey tourism. Check show listings when booking, since the room's rhythm follows the club calendar. Proof on Main, six blocks west, is the other downtown entry here and also pours Kentucky 74.
venues.pressQuote: Zero Proof Old Fashioned, using Kentucky 74, a non-alcoholic spirit produced by local brand Spiritless.

venues.name: Basan
venues.description: Basan runs a standing "No ABV" section on its drink menu, kept separate from the cocktail list, with four originals: Rise & Shine (Vietnamese cold brew, orange, buckwheat honey, condensed milk, salt), Not This Time (aloe, pineapple, grapefruit, shishito, togarashi), My Neighbor Totoro (coconut, mango, lavender, ube) and Our Little Secret (raspberry, ginger, mint, honey, lime). The Japanese-inspired restaurant, across from Little Caesars Arena in Detroit's District Detroit/Cass Park area, also stocks Sapporo NA, a 0.0% Japanese lager, alongside its sake and specialty-cocktail program. Eater Detroit named Basan one of the city's best spots for nonalcoholic cocktails.
signatureDrinks: Rise & Shine (Vietnamese cold brew, orange, buckwheat honey, condensed milk, salt)
Not This Time (aloe, pineapple, grapefruit, shishito pepper, lime, togarashi)
My Neighbor Totoro (coconut, mango, lavender, lemon oil, lime, ube)
Our Little Secret (raspberry, ginger, mint, honey, lime)
venues.longDescription:
Basan opened in November 2022 in Detroit's historic Eddystone building on Park Avenue, part of a wave of restaurants that filled out The District Detroit around Little Caesars Arena. It's from the Four Man Ladder group — the team behind Brush Park's Grey Ghost and its downstairs bar Second Best — with Chef Eric Lees running a robata-grill-centered menu of Asian and eclectic global small plates. The name references Basan, a mythical fire-breathing rooster, a nod to the live-fire cooking at the restaurant's center.

The "No ABV" category sits on the drink menu as its own section, distinct from Basan's shochu- and sake-driven cocktail list, and it has rotated seasonally rather than staying static: earlier lineups ran drinks like Vanishing Act (oolong iced tea, chrysanthemum, honey, orange blossom) and Holy Shishito (peach, shishito, grapefruit, togarashi); the current menu runs Rise & Shine, Not This Time, My Neighbor Totoro and Our Little Secret. Across versions, the alcohol-free drinks use the same pantry as the cocktail program — togarashi, ube, buckwheat honey, coconut, calpico-style fruit — rather than a separate, simplified syrup-and-juice track. Sapporo NA, a 0.0% Japanese lager, is also on the menu for guests who want a beer instead of a mixed drink.

Basan sits directly across Sproat Street from Little Caesars Arena, pulling a mix of pre- and post-event diners along with its regular dinner crowd. Eater Detroit included the restaurant on its roundup of the best nonalcoholic cocktails in metro Detroit, and Basan has kept the four-drink no-ABV lineup as a fixture of the menu rather than a one-off addition.
venues.pressQuote: Basan has been churning out delicious NA drinks since its 2022 opening.

venues.name: Basic Kitchen
venues.description: Basic Kitchen is a veggie-forward, plant-leaning New American restaurant in Harleston Village, two blocks off King Street, serving a seasonal, locally sourced menu that accommodates gluten-free and vegan diners. Its beverage list, dated August 2026, carries a titled Mocktails & Juice section rather than a full zero-proof cocktail programme: BK Tropic Water (pineapple, mint, lime, sea salt, coconut water and blue spirulina), a Grapefruit Spritz with lavender agave, and Health Insurance, a hot-or-iced turmeric, lemon, cayenne, ginger and honey build. Alongside them sit three cold-pressed juices, a rotating local kombucha, Plus + Minus N/A Pinot Noir Rose by the glass or bottle, and Best Day N/A beer. The bar no longer stocks non-alcoholic spirits, so the earlier practice of building most cocktails alcohol-free on request is not advertised on the current list.

venues.longDescription:
Basic Kitchen sits at 82 Wentworth Street, two blocks off King Street in downtown Charleston, in a bright, plant-filled dining room serving a seasonal, locally sourced menu that leans heavily vegetable-forward without being vegetarian, and accommodates gluten-free and vegan diners across most of the card. For a long stretch it was one of the most reliably non-alcoholic-friendly rooms in the city, and that reputation is well documented: The Zero Proof, which reviews venues specifically for alcohol-free hospitality, scored its drinks menu a perfect 10 out of 10, and the house beet margarita - a bright pink beet, apple, cucumber and lemon juice over lime - was featured in the Post and Courier's Liquid Assets column and was for years routinely ordered without tequila.

The August 2026 beverage list is narrower than that history suggests, and it is worth being plain about the difference. There is no zero-proof cocktail section and no non-alcoholic spirits on the printed liquor list; the beet margarita appears under Cocktails built on tequila blanco with beet, orange, lime and agave, and carries no alcohol-free notation. What the menu does carry is a titled Mocktails & Juice section holding BK Tropic Water (pineapple, mint, lime, sea salt, coconut water and blue spirulina), a Grapefruit Spritz of grapefruit, lavender agave, lemon and an orange juice floater, and Health Insurance, served hot or iced from turmeric, lemon, cayenne, ginger and honey. Three cold-pressed juices sit beside them - Bright Eyes, Super Green and Beets by BK - along with a seasonal local kombucha, bottled mineral water and Boylan soda under Fizzies, and a coffee and tea list running to a golden latte, a chai latte and a Matchaful matcha. The alcohol-free drinking options proper are Plus + Minus N/A Pinot Noir Rose from Australia, poured by the glass or the bottle, and Best Day N/A beer. The Charcoal Latte and Matcha Muchacha named on older versions of this menu are no longer listed, and neither the Virgin Bloody Mary nor the Virgin Moscow Mule appears on the current card. It remains a comfortable room in which to not drink, but the programme is now a modest one rather than the destination it was.
venues.pressQuote: The drinks menu is one of the most zero-proof friendly we've seen in the country.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: The Zero Proof, Basic Kitchen review

venues.name: Bayti Cafe
venues.description: Bayti Cafe is a Lebanese cafe and bakery on NW 41st Street in Doral, built around what its owners describe as a passion for the food culture of Lebanon. The drink list is entirely coffee, tea, juice and blended fruit: macchiato, flat white, cappuccino, americano and espresso from the espresso bar, matcha and chai lattes served hot or iced, iced tea, mango juice, a Lebanese mint lemonade, and a pineapple ginger smoothie, plus milkshakes. The bakery counter carries Lebanese pastries and sweets alongside the savoury menu. It is a daytime room, open 8am to 5pm seven days a week, and its full drink list is published online.
venues.longDescription:
Bayti Cafe trades from Unit 105 at 11402 NW 41st Street in Doral, in the corridor of business parks and residential towers north-west of Miami International Airport. The cafe's own framing is straightforward: the owners write about a passion for the rich and diverse food culture of Lebanon, and the room combines a bakery counter of Lebanese pastries and sweets with a sit-down cafe menu. It is a daytime operation rather than an evening one, open 8am to 5pm every day of the week.

The entire beverage list is non-alcoholic. The espresso bar covers macchiato, flat white, cappuccino, americano and straight espresso; matcha lattes and chai lattes are offered hot or iced; and the cold list runs to iced tea, mango juice, a Lebanese mint lemonade built on fresh mint, and a pineapple ginger smoothie, with milkshakes rounding out the blended options. This is a cafe rather than a zero-proof bar programme, and it is listed here on that basis: for a reader looking for somewhere in Doral to meet over a drink with no alcohol on the premises, Bayti is a documented option with a published menu, which most of its neighbours are not. No founder name or opening year is published on the site, and no press coverage was found at a verifiable URL, so neither is asserted here. The neighbourhood is confirmed as the City of Doral by the US Census geocoder rather than taken from the mailing address. The espresso list is standard European rather than Middle Eastern in format, but the cold drinks are where the kitchen's own hand shows: the Lebanese mint lemonade is built on fresh mint rather than syrup, and the pineapple ginger smoothie is blended to order. Doral has almost no representation in Miami's published alcohol-free coverage, which is part of why the entry is worth carrying even though the programme is a cafe list rather than a bar one. Anyone planning around it should note the 5pm close: this is a breakfast, coffee and lunch room, not an evening destination, and the nearest late alcohol-free options are several miles south around Sweetwater and Westchester.

venues.name: Beachside Social
venues.description: Beachside Social sits on Atlantic Avenue at the Virginia Beach oceanfront, and it keeps mocktails on the menu in a stretch of the city almost entirely given over to frozen drinks and beer. That is the reason to know about it: the oceanfront is where most visitors stay, and it is the hardest few blocks in Hampton Roads to find a considered alcohol-free drink. Beachside Social is a social, ocean-facing room rather than a craft cocktail bar, and it runs late — to midnight on Fridays and Saturdays — which makes it a workable end to an evening for a group where not everyone is drinking.

venues.longDescription:
Beachside Social is on Atlantic Avenue at the Virginia Beach oceanfront, the strip of hotels, bars and boardwalk that most visitors to Hampton Roads actually stay on. Understanding that geography explains why a room with a fairly ordinary mocktail list earns a listing.

The oceanfront is a difficult place to not drink. Resort strips run on frozen daiquiris, buckets of beer and pitchers, because that is what a beach holiday crowd buys — and the drinks are built for volume rather than balance. Someone who is not drinking, whether by choice, pregnancy, recovery or because they are driving back over the bridge, will find plenty of soda and very little else. Meanwhile all of Hampton Roads' genuinely good alcohol-free drinking is in Norfolk, twenty minutes away across the water, which is no help at ten at night.

Beachside Social keeps mocktails on the menu in that environment, and Coastal Virginia Magazine describes it as a classic social spot with crowd-pleasing versions. Crowd-pleasing is the right expectation to set: these are approachable drinks in a busy ocean-facing bar, not the composed builds you would get at Only You or Gershwin's. The grade reflects that honestly.

What it offers is a normal night out in the place people are actually staying. It opens at 5pm midweek, from noon on Saturday and Sunday, and runs to midnight on Friday and Saturday, which covers the hours a beach evening actually happens in. Closed Mondays. For a visitor without a car, it may be the most practical option on this entire list. Anyone with transport should treat it as a convenient fallback rather than a destination, and cross to Norfolk for the region's real depth.
venues.pressQuote: Beachside Social is a classic social spot with crowd-pleasing mocktails and ocean vibes.

venues.name: Beauty & The Butcher
venues.description: Beauty & The Butcher is a Grove Bay Hospitality steakhouse on South Red Road in Coral Gables, a residential stretch well south of Miracle Mile, and its bar list carries two named alcohol-free builds. Both are constructed on non-alcoholic spirits rather than juice: the Skinny Hinny combines Seedlip Spice with a sour mint cordial, ginger beer and watermelon, and the Flor y Pepe pairs Lyre's Agave Blanco with elderflower, cucumber and lime. Secret Miami documented both in its December 2025 survey of Miami zero-proof rooms. Dinner runs nightly from 5pm, with an earlier Friday service from noon, and the kitchen serves until 11pm on Friday and Saturday.
signatureDrinks: Skinny Hinny (Seedlip Spice, sour mint cordial, ginger beer, watermelon)
Flor y Pepe (Lyre's Agave Blanco, elderflower, cucumber, lime)
venues.longDescription:
Beauty & The Butcher trades at 6915 SW 57th Avenue — South Red Road — in the southern reach of Coral Gables, closer to South Miami than to Miracle Mile, and is operated by Grove Bay Hospitality Group. The format is a modern steakhouse with a full bar, and the schedule is dinner-led: 5pm to 10pm Monday through Thursday and Sunday, 5pm to 11pm on Saturday, with an earlier Friday opening at noon that runs through to 11pm. For readers building an evening in the Gables or South Miami without drinking, it and Tea & Poets, a short drive north-east in South Miami, are the two documented options in that corridor.

What earns the restaurant a place here is that both of its named alcohol-free drinks are built on distilled non-alcoholic spirits rather than on fruit juice, which changes what they taste like. The Skinny Hinny uses Seedlip Spice — the allspice-and-cardamom expression from the London non-alcoholic distiller — with a sour mint cordial, ginger beer and watermelon, giving a drink with real warmth under the freshness. The Flor y Pepe is built on Lyre's Agave Blanco, the brand's tequila analogue, and lengthened with elderflower, cucumber and lime, which lands closer to a long margarita than to a cooler. Secret Miami documented both drinks by name and specification in its December 2025 round-up of fifteen Miami venues serving zero-proof drinks, listing the restaurant under Coral Gables. The venue is one of the more southerly entries in Miami's alcohol-free catalogue, and worth noting for anyone who assumes the city's zero-proof programmes stop at Brickell. Two practical notes. The first is that the restaurant is a dinner room on most days, so the Friday noon opening is the only reliable daytime service. The second is that the address is 6915 Southwest 57th Avenue (S Red Rd), Coral Gables, which matches the listing Secret Miami published; the surrounding Census-designated place is Glenvar Heights, but the operating address and the restaurant's own listing both give Coral Gables, which is the neighbourhood recorded here. The restaurant takes bookings on (305) 665-9661 and posts as @beautyandthebutchermiami.
venues.pressQuote: At Beauty & the Butcher, you can choose between the Skinny Hinny, a crisp and energizing drink combining Seedlip Spice, sour mint cordial, ginger beer and watermelon, or the refreshing Flor y Pepe, featuring Lyre’s Agave Blanco, elderflower, cucumber and lime.

venues.name: Beckon
venues.description: Beckon is a Michelin-starred, 18-seat chef's counter in Denver's RiNo neighborhood, opened in 2018 by chef and owner Duncan Holmes, a James Beard Award semifinalist. Diners sit facing the open kitchen for a multi-course, reservation-only seasonal tasting menu that changes through the year, with produce coming in part from the restaurant's own one-acre farm. Beyond the wine list, the beverage menu carries a labelled Zero Proof section built to track the food rather than to sit beside it: First Ascent (passion fruit, almond, ginger beer) and Starry Maid (flowering coriander, hibiscus, Seedlip Grove 42, Ghia non-alcoholic aperitivo, lime, faba), both at $10. Allison Anderson of Beckon won the Michelin Guide Colorado Service Award in 2024. It is a fine-dining counter rather than a walk-in bar; book ahead.
signatureDrinks: First Ascent (NA: passion fruit, almond, ginger beer)
Starry Maid (NA: flowering coriander, hibiscus, Seedlip Grove 42, Ghia N/A aperitivo, lime, faba)
venues.longDescription:
Beckon is an 18-seat chef's counter at 2843 Larimer Street in RiNo, opened in 2018 by chef and owner Duncan Holmes, a James Beard Award semifinalist, and it holds a Michelin star. Guests sit in a single row facing the open kitchen and eat a multi-course, reservation-only tasting menu that turns with the seasons; a good deal of the produce comes from the restaurant's own one-acre farm, and vegetables are usually the part of the meal people remember. It operates Wednesday through Sunday evenings only, with the whole room seated on a schedule rather than run as a walk-in service. Allison Anderson of Beckon won the Michelin Guide Colorado Service Award in 2024, which is a useful signal for anyone weighing whether a counter of this kind will handle an unusual request gracefully.

That matters because tasting-menu restaurants are where non-drinkers most often get stranded between an expensive wine pairing and a glass of tap water. Beckon's beverage menu carries Zero Proof as its own labelled section alongside By the Glass, Sparkling, White, Rose, Red, Sake, Signature Cocktails, Dessert Cocktails, Spirits and Beer, which puts it structurally on a level with the wine programme rather than in a footnote. Two built drinks are current, both $10. First Ascent is the brighter of the pair, passion fruit and almond lengthened with ginger beer. Starry Maid is the more composed: flowering coriander and hibiscus with Seedlip Grove 42, Ghia non-alcoholic aperitivo, lime and faba, shaken to a texture that holds up against several courses. San Pellegrino is stocked at $6. Because the counter runs a set menu that changes quarterly and the drinks are built to track it, the zero-proof list is worth confirming when booking; the section itself is permanent, but the two drinks in it rotate with the kitchen. Service runs Wednesday through Sunday evenings only, and the counter books out in advance, so the drinks question is best raised at the point of reservation rather than on arrival. Reservations are handled through OpenTable, and the eighteen seats mean there is no bar to drift into and no second room to be moved to, so the beverage decision is made once, at the start, for the whole meal.

venues.name: Beer Culture
venues.description: Beer Culture is a craft beer bar and bottle shop at 328 West 45th Street in Hell's Kitchen, with 14 taps and around 90 cans and bottles focused on the New York area. Craft Beer & Brewing described it as an unpretentious beer bar with homey vibes, low ceilings and soft lighting, where amid all the attractions competing for your attention in New York, settling in feels like taking refuge in a friend's basement. Its non-alcoholic beers get their own printed section headed "Non-Alcoholic", currently six deep and unusually well chosen — Guinness Draught 0.0 at a true 0%, Go Brewing's Freedom Hazy at 0.2% (which is also crafted without gluten), Go's Sunbeam Pilsner at 0.4%, and three at 0.5%: Go's The Story, Momentum Brewery's Hazy IPA from Bay Shore, New York, and Athletic Brewing's Upside Dawn. The bar also keeps gluten-free beers in the bottle shop. Prices are not published online. It is 21-and-over after 9pm.
venues.longDescription:
Beer Culture sits on West 45th Street in Hell's Kitchen, a few minutes from the theatres, with fourteen taps and around ninety cans and bottles weighted deliberately towards New York-area brewers. Craft Beer & Brewing caught what makes it work: an unpretentious beer bar with homey vibes, low ceilings and soft lighting, where amid all the attractions competing for your attention in New York, settling in here feels like taking refuge in a friend's basement. The kitchen does smashburgers, bratwurst, crusty pretzels with jalapeño cheese, bar pies and chili. It opens at 3pm most days and 1pm at weekends, running to 2am from Thursday, and it is 21-and-over after 9pm. There is a sister bar, Gebhard's Beer Culture, on the Upper West Side — a different address with a different tap list.

What earns it a place here is that the non-alcoholic beers are a printed section of the menu headed simply Non-Alcoholic, and the selection has clearly been made by someone who cares. Six are on it, and the spread of strengths is the interesting part. Guinness Draught 0.0 is a genuine 0% — the only true zero on the list, and worth knowing if you avoid trace alcohol entirely. Go Brewing's Freedom Hazy is 0.2%, and is also crafted without gluten, which quietly makes it the most accommodating beer in the building. Go's Sunbeam Pilsner is 0.4%. Three sit at the more common 0.5%: Go Brewing's The Story, Momentum Brewery's Hazy IPA out of Bay Shore on Long Island, and Athletic Brewing's Upside Dawn. Three of the six coming from a single specialist non-alcoholic brewer, and one from a small New York State producer, tells you this is a considered shelf rather than whatever the distributor pushed. The bar also stocks gluten-free beers in the bottle shop, and says so plainly in its own FAQ. Prices are not published online — the tap list runs through a live board that carries strengths and breweries but no figures — so you will find out at the bar.
venues.pressQuote: An unpretentious beer bar in Hell's Kitchen with homey vibes, low ceilings, and soft lighting—and amid all the attractions competing for your attention in New York, settling in here feels like taking refuge in a friend's basement.

venues.name: Beer Study
venues.description: Beer Study is a bottle shop, forty-tap beer hall, arcade and the taproom for Starpoint Brewing, in the Rockwood shopping centre on University Drive in south Durham, with The Boot Room restaurant through a connecting door. For non-drinkers the draw is the cooler rather than the taps: around nine non-alcoholic beers, chosen rather than defaulted — Burial's Chaosmachine NA IPA from Asheville, Fremont's non-alcoholic dark, the Deschutes-brewed Patagonia Provisions organic golden and Bellwoods' Jelly King raspberry-blackberry sour from Toronto. Discover Durham credits it with treating non-alcoholic drinks with the same care it gives its wine and beer. It is a beer venue with a good alcohol-free shelf, not an alcohol-free venue, but it opens at 11:30 most days and runs to eleven Thursday through Saturday, and the lounge is a comfortable place to sit while other people drink.
venues.longDescription:
Beer Study is several businesses in one unit of the Rockwood shopping centre on University Drive in south Durham: a bottle shop, a forty-tap beer hall, the taproom for Starpoint Brewing, a video arcade, and — through a connecting door — The Boot Room restaurant. The lounge area has leather sofas, arcade cabinets and a fake fireplace, and it is one of the more relaxed rooms in the city to spend an afternoon in.

For non-drinkers, the draw is the cooler rather than the taps. The shop keeps around nine non-alcoholic beers in stock, and the selection is chosen rather than defaulted: Burial Beer's Chaosmachine, a non-alcoholic IPA from the Asheville brewery that is among the best American examples; Fremont Brewing's non-alcoholic dark, a style almost nobody makes without alcohol; the Deschutes-brewed Patagonia Provisions organic golden; and Bellwoods' Jelly King with raspberry and blackberry, a sour from one of Toronto's most respected breweries. That is a considered range rather than a row of the same three national brands, which is why Discover Durham singles the shop out on the city's official non-alcoholic page.

The honest framing is that this is a beer venue with a good non-alcoholic shelf, not a non-alcoholic venue. Almost everything on tap contains alcohol and the room smells like a taproom. But it is open from 11:30 in the morning, until midnight on Thursday, Friday and Saturday, and it is a genuinely comfortable place to sit with a good alcohol-free beer while other people drink — which for a lot of people is the specific thing that is hard to find.

One note for anyone searching: mapping services frequently resolve this address to Thai Café or Wine Authorities, both neighbours in the same shopping centre. Beer Study is trading normally at suite 4.
venues.pressQuote: the same care they give their wine and beer

venues.name: Beermash
venues.description: Beermash is a Collingwood beer bar and bottle shop on Smith Street with more than 20 rotating taps and 200-plus bottles and cans, run by Kieran Hennessy (co-owner of Rockwell & Sons) and Shayne Dixon (co-owner of Bonny in Fitzroy). Its non-alcoholic range is genuinely deep: a dedicated NA beer collection stocking Heaps Normal, Hop Nation, Garage Project, Molly Rose, Range, Bridge Road, One Drop and more. Beermash was also one of the first Melbourne venues to pour Heaps Normal's Original Draught -- the brand's first true non-alcoholic draught beer -- when it launched in February 2026.
signatureDrinks: Heaps Normal Original Draught -- crisp non-alcoholic Aussie lager, poured on tap
Heaps Normal Quiet XPA -- alcohol-free extra pale ale (fridge)
Hop Nation Mind Ya Head XPA -- non-alcoholic extra pale ale (fridge)
venues.longDescription:
Beermash opened on Smith Street in Collingwood in 2014 and has become one of Melbourne's most respected craft-beer destinations, part bottle shop and part licensed bar. Behind a yellow-tiled counter sit more than 20 rotating taps pouring craft beer alongside cider, kombucha, cold-brew coffee and a couple of wines, with over 200 bottles and cans filling the fridges and shelves. It is co-owned by Kieran Hennessy, also of Rockwell & Sons, and Shayne Dixon, co-owner of Bonny in Fitzroy, who curate the list with their staff. Customers can fill reusable growlers or half-sized squealers to take home, or drink in at high tables inside.

The non-alcoholic offering here is a real anchor rather than an afterthought. Beermash keeps a dedicated non-alcoholic collection running to roughly 50 products, spanning Australian and international zero-and-low brewers including Heaps Normal (Quiet XPA, Another Lager, Third IPA), Hop Nation (Mind Ya Head XPA, Passing Storm West Coast IPA), Garage Project's Tiny line, Molly Rose, Range, Bridge Road Brewery, One Drop, Stomping Ground, Konpira Maru and Weihenstephaner. It is a genuine destination for someone who wants a serious alcohol-free craft beer, not just a token can.

In February 2026, Beermash was one of a select group of Melbourne and Sydney venues chosen to launch Heaps Normal's Original Draught, described by the brewery as a crisp contemporary Aussie lager built with low-bitterness noble hops and toasted malt, and formulated specifically to survive tap service. Beermash poured it from day one and hosted a complimentary sampling on the launch night, making it one of the first places in the city where you could order a non-alcoholic beer straight off the tap.

The room is relaxed and walk-in only, with stools and high tables inside and benches lining the footpath out front. Card games like Cards Against Humanity and Exploding Kittens are on hand, and the venue is LGBTIQA+ friendly with non-gendered bathrooms. No booking is needed.
venues.pressQuote: There's cider, kombucha, cold-brew coffee and a couple of wines being poured here with a dozen or more craft beers.

venues.name: Belles Beach House
venues.description: Belles Beach House is a retro tiki restaurant and bar at 24 Windward Avenue, just off the Venice Boardwalk, opened in late 2021 by restaurateur Nick Mathers of the Wish You Were Here Group, who describes it as Hawaiian izakaya meets tiki bar. Eater named it one of the fifteen most beautiful restaurants in Los Angeles: it took over the former Larry's, with teak sliding doors and no enclosed walls on three sides, so the whole place feels like an open-air patio. Art is by the Venice artist Larry Bell. Its zero-proof section is one of the larger ones on the Westside — CORRECTION: nine items, not eight, spanning $7 to $14 rather than mostly $11. The three fruit-and-herb spritzes are $11 each (Watermelon Mint, Apple Ginger, Thai Basil Cucumber), the Palm Reader is $14, the Red Wing Spritz $14, fresh guava lemonade $9, pure coconut water $9, and an iced mango sencha green tea $7. NOTE: the Palm Reader contains Aplós Ease, which carries 100mg of lion's mane extract per serving — a non-psychoactive nootropic, but worth knowing. Open from noon, to 2am on Friday and Saturday, with DJs at weekends.
venues.longDescription:
Belles Beach House opened in late 2021 a few steps off the Venice Boardwalk, in the space that had been Larry's — a gastropub named for the Venice artist Larry Bell, whose work still hangs here. It comes from Nick Mathers and the Wish You Were Here Group, and his description of the concept is Hawaiian izakaya meets tiki bar; island hospitality, he has said, has always appealed to him, particularly in the culinary sense. Eater put it second on its list of the fifteen most beautiful restaurants in Los Angeles and explained why: the room is surrounded by teak sliding doors with no enclosed walls on three sides, so the entire place reads as an open-air patio, warmed by overhead heaters, with another sixty or so seats across the sidewalk. The Infatuation's summary is the shortest accurate one — a day or night here feels like a tropical-themed party in Venice, with a DJ spinning house records, palm trees by every table and a giant tiki statue up front. Food runs from an $18 poke bowl to a $18 teriyaki cheeseburger and $14 huli huli chicken skewers.

The zero-proof list is genuinely one of the larger ones on the Westside, and worth correcting on detail. It is nine items, not eight, and the prices run from $7 to $14 rather than clustering at $11. Three are the fruit-and-herb spritzes at $11 that the bar is known for — Watermelon Mint, Apple Ginger, and Thai Basil Cucumber, each built on fresh fruit or herb with lime and sparkling water, and all served in the same tiki glassware as everything else, which is most of the point of drinking here without alcohol. Fresh guava lemonade is $9, pure coconut water $9, an iced mango sencha green tea $7. Two sit at $14: the Red Wing Spritz, which uses watermelon Red Bull with lime and mint, and the Palm Reader. The Palm Reader is worth one note. It is built on Aplós Ease, and that product carries 100mg of lion's mane extract per serving alongside L-theanine and magnesium glycinate. Lion's mane is a functional mushroom, not a psychoactive one — there is nothing hallucinogenic or intoxicating in it — but if you are avoiding functional ingredients as well as alcohol, order one of the other eight. Note also that the venue is entirely al fresco with open-air windows, there is no valet, and outside wine may be brought for a $55 corkage.
venues.pressQuote: A day or night at Belles Beach House feels like a tropical-themed party in Venice, with a DJ spinning house records, palm trees by every table, and a giant tiki statue up front.

venues.name: Bellhop
venues.description: Bellhop is Des Moines' tiki bar in the East Village — classy tiki rather than cheesy tiki, by its own description — with elevated takes on the classics and a robust craft beer list. Its alcohol-free builds are the Beachbreeze, of pineapple, passionfruit, coconut and lime with cherry, and Sandy Beaches, which uses blue coconut water with lime, Don's Mix and cinnamon. Don's Mix is the grapefruit-and-cinnamon syrup at the heart of the original Mai Tai-era tiki canon, and a bar using it in a drink with no rum in it is applying its real technique rather than a shortcut.

venues.longDescription:
Bellhop is on East Grand Avenue in the East Village, and it describes its own aesthetic as more classy tiki than cheesy tiki — elevated versions of the classics, a serious craft beer list, and a room that takes the format seriously rather than ironically.

The detail that earns the listing is Don's Mix. It appears in Sandy Beaches, alongside blue coconut water, lime and cinnamon, and anyone who knows tiki will recognise it immediately: Don's Mix is the two-parts-grapefruit-to-one-part-cinnamon-syrup blend created by Donn Beach, the man who invented American tiki drinking in the 1930s, and it is the backbone of the Navy Grog and the original Zombie. It is made in-house or not at all.

A bar putting its own Don's Mix into a drink with no rum in it is telling you something specific: the alcohol-free build is coming off the same station, with the same components, as the drinks it is proudest of. That is the opposite of the usual arrangement, where the mocktail is assembled from whatever is nearest the soda gun.

The Beachbreeze is the more straightforward of the two — pineapple, passionfruit, coconut, lime and cherry — and it is the one to order if you want the full tiki experience without the rum. Both were documented by Des Moines' tourism board in January 2026.

Tiki also does the presentational work this directory keeps returning to. In a room where every drink arrives in carved ceramic under a hedge of mint and fruit, nobody can tell which glass has alcohol in it, and nobody asks.

The hours are narrow: 4pm to 2am on Thursday and Friday, 2pm to 2am on Saturday, and closed Sunday through Wednesday. This is a weekend bar, and a late one.

venues.description: Bellwoods Brewery is a longstanding Ossington Avenue brewpub and bottle shop that brews its own line of named, in-house non-alcoholic beers rather than carrying outside NA brands. The lineup centers on the 0.5% — which started as an internal Dry January joke before becoming a real release — alongside the dry-hopped Stay Classy IPA and several Jelly King non-alcoholic sour and seltzer variants. Co-founder Luke Pestl says the NA beers use controlled, stopped fermentation rather than dealcoholization, an extension of the brewery's long-running interest in low-ABV brewing.
