venues.longDescription:
Bellwoods Brewery runs two adjoining spaces on Ossington Avenue in Toronto's Trinity-Bellwoods/Little Portugal area: a full-service brewpub at 124 Ossington Ave, open Mon-Tue 5pm-midnight, Wed-Thu noon-midnight, Fri-Sat noon-1am and Sun noon-11pm, and a retail bottle shop next door at 126 Ossington Ave. Both carry the brewery's own non-alcoholic beer line, sold through Bellwoods' dedicated Non-Alc collection alongside its regular beers.

The flagship is 0.5%, a 473mL non-alcoholic beer that began, in the brewery's own telling, as an internal joke during Dry January before turning into a real project: "what initially started as a joke inside our brewery, back in Dry January, quickly became a fun side project." The current iteration is described by Bellwoods as having "beautiful hop aromatics, light ice-tea-like flavours, and a spritzy body" — occupying a middle ground the brewery calls "kind of like beer, kind of not."

Co-founder Luke Pestl has said the NA beers are made using controlled, stopped fermentation rather than dealcoholization — equipment the brewery doesn't have — framing the line as a natural extension of Bellwoods' long-running interest in low-ABV brewing: "Low-alcohol beers have long been an interest of ours...NA is really just an extension of that program." He's described the development process as thorough, involving repeated test batches, recipe revisions and taste tests. "If I had to distill it down to one point," he told Some Good Clean Fun in 2023, "I'd say that our NA beers taste just like beer beer."

Beyond the 0.5%, the non-alcoholic range includes the dry-hopped Stay Classy IPA with citrus and grapefruit notes, and several NA riffs on Bellwoods' Jelly King sour: a Dry Hopped Sour with raspberry and blackberry (under 0.5% ABV, tart with peachy notes), a Tangerine, Ginger and Lemon variant, and two Jelly King seltzers — Raspberry Lemon and Tangerine Grapefruit.
venues.pressQuote: Our NA beers taste just like beer beer.

venues.name: Beneath Driver Lane
venues.description: Beneath Driver Lane is a subterranean CBD cocktail den hidden in the vault of the old GPO Money Order Office, down a lane off Little Bourke Street. Alongside its whisky-heavy classic-cocktail program it keeps a genuine run of 100% alcohol-free builds - a zero-proof Negroni, a spiced pineapple Daiquiri, a Winter Paloma and an Americano - documented by Time Out as being 'just as lip-smackingly good' as the full-strength list. Time Out lists four fully alcohol-free builds here — a Negroni, a spiced pineapple Daiquiri, a Winter Paloma and an Americano — so the zero-proof order is a named drink rather than a request.
venues.address: Driver Lane (off Little Bourke St), Melbourne VIC 3000, Australia
venues.longDescription:
Tucked beneath a laneway off Little Bourke Street, Beneath Driver Lane occupies the brick-arched vault of the old Money Order Office, an appendage to Melbourne's General Post Office building. The room is modelled on the grungy blues bars of New Orleans and the late-night music haunts of Paris: black-and-white photographs on the walls, candlelight and low-hanging lamps, arched booths, and live blues on the schedule Thursday through Saturday.

The drinks program is cocktail-forward and technically ambitious, built around an extensive back bar of whiskies and rums and a menu of classics with a modern twist. For anyone abstaining, the bar runs a set of four fully alcohol-free cocktails: a zero-proof Negroni, a spiced pineapple Daiquiri, a Winter Paloma and an Americano - all built without alcohol rather than sweet soda-and-syrup mocktails.

Time Out Melbourne singled the venue out in its 'where to drink when you're not drinking' guide, noting the no-alcohol cocktails are 'all 100% alcohol-free but just as lip-smackingly good.' French bistro-style bar snacks - oysters, charcuterie, smoked octopus - round out the offering. It's an adults-only, hidden-door room that works as well for a soda-and-lime evening as a spirits crawl.

The room does a lot of the work. Time Out describes a subterranean bar of rustic Victorian style: brick arched booths, walls cluttered with black-and-white photographs, and warm light from candles and low-hanging lamps. That matters more than it sounds for anyone not drinking, because a basement lit by candles is a room where nobody can see what is in your glass, and the social pressure that makes a Tuesday night out awkward simply does not arrive.

On the drinks, the same guide names four builds that are 100 per cent alcohol-free — a Negroni, a spiced pineapple Daiquiri, a Winter Paloma and an Americano. Those are bitter, spirit-shaped drinks rather than fruit juice with a garnish, which is the harder thing to do without alcohol and the more useful thing to find on a list. Ordering by name, from the same menu as everyone else, is the whole point.
venues.pressQuote: On the mocktails front, there's a Negroni, a spiced pineapple Daiquiri, a Winter Paloma and an Americano - all 100% alcohol-free but just as lip-smackingly good.

venues.name: Bern's Steak House
venues.description: Bern's Steak House is Tampa's most storied fine-dining institution — a SoHo landmark open since 1956, known worldwide for its dry-aged steaks and a legendary upstairs dessert room. Its bar carries a dedicated "Zero Proof" cocktail section built on Ritual Zero Proof spirits, currently the Lil' Miss (dark cherry, cinnamon, ginger ale), the Solé Sunrise (Ritual tequila, orgeat, tangerine, lime, grapefruit), and the Watermelon Crawl (Ritual aperitif, watermelon, lime, mint, honey). It means a non-drinker can sit down to one of the country's great steakhouse experiences without settling for a soda.  Reservations are essential and often booked well ahead, and the upstairs dessert room is a separate seating after dinner.
signatureDrinks: Lil' Miss (dark cherry, cinnamon, ginger ale)
Solé Sunrise (Ritual tequila, orgeat, tangerine, lime, grapefruit)
Watermelon Crawl (Ritual aperitif, watermelon, lime, mint, honey)
venues.longDescription:
Bern's Steak House has been on South Howard Avenue since 1956 and is, by most measures, the most storied restaurant in Florida. It is known for dry-aged beef cut to order, a wine list that has run to hundreds of thousands of bottles held in its own cellars, and the Harry Waugh Dessert Room upstairs — a warren of private booths built from old wine casks where diners are moved after the main meal. It is the kind of institution where the ritual is as much the point as the food.

That matters for a non-drinker in a particular way. A restaurant defined by one of the world's great wine programmes is, structurally, the hardest possible room in which to not drink: the entire experience is organised around a bottle, the sommelier is central to the service, and the person declining is conspicuous. Bern's answer is a dedicated "Zero Proof" section on the bar list built on Ritual Zero Proof spirits, so the alternative is a made drink rather than an apology. The current builds are the Lil' Miss (dark cherry, cinnamon, ginger ale), the Sole Sunrise (Ritual tequila alternative with orgeat, tangerine, lime and grapefruit) and the Watermelon Crawl (Ritual aperitif with watermelon, lime, mint and honey).

Three named drinks is not a large list by the standards of a dedicated zero-proof bar. In the context of a seventy-year-old steakhouse whose reputation rests on wine, it is a deliberate accommodation, and it is what lets someone join a table at one of the country's great restaurants without spending the evening with a glass of soda.

Practical notes: reservations are essential and often booked well ahead, the dessert room is a separate seating after dinner, and prices are what the reputation implies. This is emphatically a wine restaurant with a zero-proof option, not an alcohol-free venue.
venues.pressQuote: Easily the most iconic restaurant in Tampa is Bern's Steak House, which has been welcoming guests since 1956
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Time Out, The best restaurants in Tampa, November 2025

venues.name: Better Beverage
venues.description: Better Beverage is a fully non-alcoholic bottle shop serving the Columbus metro, founded by Mary LaPlaca and based in Westerville. It has no storefront: the shop trades through pop-ups, event bars, tastings, local delivery and a wholesale programme for bars and restaurants, with orders taken by email. Everything it stocks is alcohol-free, and the buying policy is unusually explicit — LaPlaca curates ready-to-drink brands that are women-, LGBTQ+-, veteran-, minority- or family-owned, or that work to a sustainability standard, rather than simply carrying whatever distributes into Ohio. LaPlaca has written that Al-Anon changed her life and that she started the business after realising Columbus had no shop dedicated to non-alcoholic drinks, bringing two decades of work as an artist to the venture.
venues.longDescription:
Better Beverage is Mary LaPlaca's non-alcoholic bottle shop, run out of Westerville and serving the wider Columbus area. It is alcohol-free in the strict sense — there is no beer-and-wine section behind the zero-proof end cap, because the whole inventory is zero-proof. What it does not have is a shopfront. Instead the business operates as a pop-up and delivery model: LaPlaca runs stalls at markets and events, pours tastings, staffs alcohol-free bars at private functions, delivers locally, and sells wholesale to bars, restaurants and retailers that want to build a non-alcoholic list without sourcing case by case. Orders are placed by email rather than through a checkout.

The curation is the point of difference. Rather than stocking by category alone, LaPlaca selects ready-to-drink brands on ownership and practice — women-owned, LGBTQ+-owned, veteran-owned, minority-owned, family-owned, or run to a sustainability standard — which produces a list weighted towards smaller independent producers rather than the large drinks groups that dominate non-alcoholic shelf space in supermarkets. The founding story is stated plainly on the shop's own site: LaPlaca describes how Al-Anon changed her life, and how she brought a twenty-year career as an artist to bear when she noticed that Columbus, unlike comparable cities, had no dedicated non-alcoholic shop at all. For a city whose only bricks-and-mortar zero-proof retail is an aisle inside a grocer, a specialist operator willing to come to the event is a meaningful part of the picture — though it does mean checking the pop-up schedule rather than turning up at an address. Practically, the way to buy from Better Beverage is to watch where it will be. The shop posts its pop-up and event schedule to Instagram, takes delivery and wholesale orders by email rather than through a checkout, and pours tastings at markets and private functions — which, for a category as variable in quality as non-alcoholic spirits and wines, is more useful than any product description. The wholesale and distributor arm is the quieter half of the operation, supplying bars, restaurants and retailers that want to build an alcohol-free list without sourcing brand by brand. Anyone planning around it should treat it as a schedule to check rather than a shop to visit.

venues.name: Better Luck Tomorrow
venues.description: A Heights neighborhood cocktail bar from chef Justin Yu and bar operator Bobby Heugel with a genuine six-drink spirit-free list — including a Seedlip Grove Sin & Tonic and a Jungle Birdie garnished with a hand-folded origami bird — built by head bartender Sarah Crowl.
signatureDrinks: Sin and Tonic (Seedlip Grove, yerba mate, grapefruit)
Jungle Birdie (fruit-and-citrus, hand-folded origami bird garnish)
venues.longDescription:
Better Luck Tomorrow is a neighborhood cocktail bar in Houston's Heights, opened in summer 2017 by chef Justin Yu (of Oxheart) and veteran bar operator Bobby Heugel (of Anvil Bar & Refuge). Housed in the former Dry Creek Cafe at the corner of Yale Street and West 6th, the bar pairs a deliberately pared-down cocktail list with an unexpectedly ambitious bar-food menu — the double-meat patty melt among its best-known plates — across a dimly lit room where the bar itself is backlit in bright neon, plus two patios.

Alongside its spirited program, the bar maintains a genuine spirit-free list of roughly six zero-proof drinks priced around $9, developed by head bartender Sarah Crowl, who earned a reputation for creative non-alcoholic cocktails at Houston's Coltivare and Rosie Cannonball before continuing that practice at BLT. Featured spirit-free drinks include the Sin & Tonic, a non-alcoholic gin and tonic built on Seedlip Grove with yerba mate and grapefruit; the Phony-groni, made with Kentucky 74 zero-proof spirit; and the Jungle Birdie, a fruit-and-citrus riff garnished with an origami bird that Crowl folds by hand. Seasonal additions have included a cold-brew Old Fashioned, a turmeric-ginger-apricot toddy, and a hot chocolate enhanced with cinnamon, orange, and lingonberry cream.

Crowl has said the current lineup is only the beginning of the bar's non-alcoholic selections, describing drinks built with layers of flavors, textures, and aromas within the season, with or without alcohol. The bar treats its non-alcoholic drinks with the same care as its cocktails.
venues.pressQuote: Down the road this month and beyond we will have more free-spirited drinks available that are unique originals, much like the house cocktails we already create.

venues.name: Beyond Proof
venues.description: Beyond Proof is a fully alcohol-free craft cocktail bar at 597 Centre Street in Jamaica Plain, opened in April 2026 by Krista Kranyak, who converted her own long-running restaurant Ten Tables into what is widely reported as Boston's first zero-proof bar. Every drink is built at 0% ABV and the list is organised into sections headed Florals, Groundings, Rewritten Classics, Awakenings and Simple Sips, with straight $9 pours of zero-proof tequila, gin, vodka, bourbon and mezcal for guests who want something plainer. The kitchen serves a Lebanese and Mediterranean mezze menu of hummus boards, fire-roasted carrots, saffron tahdig bites, knafeh and slow-cooked pots. One drink, the Settle, is made with kava, a psychoactive root, which the bar names openly on the menu.
signatureDrinks: First Light (0% tequila, grapefruit, thyme, lime, sea salt, aromatic bitters)
Abstinence in Bloom (rhubarb, ginger, 0% abstinence, juniper, egg white foam)
Settle (kava — a psychoactive root — lime, strawberry, coconut foam, balsamic salt)
Smoked Old Fashioned (NKD 0% bourbon, orange, smoke, bitters, tableside smoke)
Guinness Espresso Martini (espresso, 0% Guinness, chocolate bitters, cacao)

naMenuItems.description: espresso • 0% vanilla vodka • shaved cacao • brava salt

naMenuItems.name: Guinness Espresso Martini
naMenuItems.description: espresso • 0% guinness • chocolate bitters • cacao

naMenuItems.name: Dirty Martini
naMenuItems.description: 0% gin or 0% vodka • olive brine

venues.longDescription:
Beyond Proof opened in April 2026 in the Jamaica Plain storefront that had housed Ten Tables, the neighbourhood restaurant owner Krista Kranyak ran for years before she stopped drinking and rebuilt the business around alcohol-free hospitality. The conversion was covered closely by the Boston press: the Boston Globe reported the change on April 2, 2026 under the headline that Ten Tables would become Beyond Proof, returned on April 29, 2026 with a piece on a Boston cocktail bar where all the drinks are alcohol-free, WBUR covered the city's no-alcohol cocktail scene on April 30, 2026, and Boston Magazine ran its own feature on May 18, 2026. NBC Boston previewed the opening the week before it happened. Kranyak's own site describes the result as craft zero-proof cocktails paired with Mediterranean-inspired mezze, and the room retains the small, plainly furnished scale of the restaurant it replaced.

The drink list is built entirely at 0% ABV and grouped by mood rather than by base spirit. First Light combines 0% tequila with grapefruit, thyme, lime, sea salt and aromatic bitters; Deep Breath mixes orange, lemon, 0% amaro, honey, ginger and blood orange with sparkling. Under Florals, Abstinence in Bloom pairs rhubarb and ginger with juniper and an egg-white foam, and Soft Blush uses hibiscus, Silver Swallow rose and rose oil. Groundings holds Still Ember (coconut, 0% mezcal, lime, date, sea salt), a roasted blueberry-basil margarita, and the Settle, which is made with kava, a psychoactive root the bar lists plainly among the ingredients alongside lime, strawberry, coconut foam and balsamic salt. Rewritten Classics covers a smoked old fashioned built on NKD 0% bourbon with tableside smoke, an espresso martini with 0% vanilla vodka and shaved cacao, a Guinness espresso martini using 0% Guinness, a dirty martini, a gin and tonic and a lychee mojito. Alcohol-free wine runs $12 a glass and 0% beer $8, drawn from Best Day Brewing, Athletic Brewing and Guinness.
venues.pressQuote: You can build a zero-proof craft cocktail with just as much structure and complexity as a real cocktail.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Krista Kranyak, owner of Beyond Proof

venues.name: Beyond the Bar Bottle Shop
venues.description: Beyond the Bar is DFW's first alcohol-free bottle shop and dry bar, and by its own account the only one in Texas — a zero-proof shop and tasting room in a 1958 mid-century building in Richardson's Core District. The range runs past 280 products, from Athletic, Seedlip, Lyre's and Ritual to Almave, Ghia, Pathfinder and De Soi, alongside dealcoholised wines and functional drinks. The bar pours its own builds, including the Italian Spritz that won the Dallas Observer's Best Mocktail award, and the room hosts tastings and zero-proof cocktail classes.
venues.address: 101 S. Sherman St., Unit B, Richardson, TX 75081
venues.longDescription:
Tucked into a 1958 mid-century modern breeze-block building in Richardson's Core District — one block off US-75 — Beyond the Bar opened in 2023 as the first alcohol-free bottle shop in DFW, and describes itself today as the only one in Texas. Every bottle, can and pour on the premises is zero-proof, making it the rare destination where sober, sober-curious, pregnant or simply dry-for-the-evening guests can walk in and drink on equal footing with anyone else. The shelves run past 280 products: alongside Athletic, Seedlip, Lyre's and Ritual sit Almave, Trejo's, De Soi, Ghia, Pathfinder, Wilderton and Free Spirits, dealcoholised wines from Leitz and Lautus, and a deep functional range including Kin Euphorics, Everleaf and Pentire.

Co-founders Julie and Reid Robinson — who previously owned two traditional bars in Richardson — built the drink menu around genuine mixology rather than simple substitution. The flagship Blueberry Moon Shrub layers a blueberry-ginger-mint botanical spirit with elderberry shrub, fresh lime juice and ginger beer, drawing comparisons to a Moscow Mule without the heat. Julie also makes a zero-proof Old Fashioned that KERA reporters noted carried convincing coffee notes with the ritual feel of the original. The Italian Spritz, meanwhile, won the Dallas Observer's 2023 Reader's Choice award for Best Mocktail — a notable feat for a shop that had been open only months at the time. All three are still in the shop's live drinks catalogue.

The space doubles as a community hub, with tastings and Zero-Proof Cocktail 101 classes that teach two drinks and supply the tools, spirits and mixers, and the team runs a dry bar service for private and corporate events, both in the lounge and off-site. There is no dress code and no reservation needed to visit the bottle shop or tasting room. The clientele skews deliberately broad — Gen Z, Muslim and South Asian communities, expectant mothers, and anyone who just doesn't want a Diet Coke — which gives the room an unusually relaxed, inclusive energy for a drinks destination. One note for anyone avoiding all intoxicants rather than alcohol specifically: the shelves also carry hemp and THC-infused drinks and kava shots alongside the zero-proof range, so it is worth reading labels or asking staff.
venues.pressQuote: Beyond the Bar opened in 2023 and in all its newness, managed to snag our award for Best Mocktail that same year with its Italian Spritz.

venues.name: The Biergarten at Anheuser-Busch Brewery
venues.description: Few sober-curious flexes beat ordering a Bud Zero at the brewery where Budweiser is born. The Biergarten sits inside Anheuser-Busch's historic St. Louis campus — a National Historic Landmark since 1966 — and is open to the public daily, no tour ticket required. Alongside 18 draught beers in signature glassware, the current menu lists five non-alcoholic beers: Bud Zero, Michelob Ultra Zero, Michelob Ultra Lime Zero, Mango Cart NA and Stella Artois Liberté. Add a full food menu, a pet-friendly outdoor patio and a heated tent in the winter months, and this Soulard beer garden is one of the easiest zero-proof outings in the city.

naMenuItems.name: Stella Artois Liberte
naMenuItems.description: non-alcoholic beer

venues.longDescription:
Anheuser-Busch has brewed beer on this South St. Louis site since the 1850s, and the sprawling red-brick campus surrounding the Biergarten was designated a National Historic Landmark in 1966. Today the grounds operate as the Budweiser Brewery Experience at 1200 Lynch Street, where tours run daily and visits with the famous Budweiser Clydesdales are part of the draw. The Biergarten itself — a Bavarian-style beer garden with long wooden tables — is the campus's public hub, and crucially, you don't need a tour ticket to eat or drink there: it's open to walk-ins daily from 11am to 7pm.

For zero-proof drinkers, the hook is irresistible: you can order a Budweiser Zero at the brewery where Budweiser is born. The Biergarten's current menu lists five non-alcoholic beers — Bud Zero, Michelob Ultra Zero, Michelob Ultra Lime Zero, Mango Cart NA and Stella Artois Liberté, the last poured from 12-ounce glass bottles. They sit alongside 18 draught beers served in signature glassware, customizable beer flights and a long packaged list, so mixed groups of drinkers and non-drinkers can order off the same menu without ceremony.

Explore St. Louis, the city's official visitor guide, calls the Biergarten 'a St. Louis favorite any time of year,' thanks to an outdoor patio with urban views, a heated tent in the winter months and an intimate indoor space. The kitchen runs a full menu of appetizers, salads, sandwiches, entrees and a children's menu, and the patio is pet-friendly. Note that the venue posts occasional full-day closures for private events, and no table reservations are taken in the Biergarten — check budweisertours.com before a special trip. It's an unbeatable first stop on a St. Louis alcohol-free itinerary: equal parts brewery pilgrimage, history lesson and low-key afternoon out.
venues.pressQuote: The heated tent in winter months, as well as the intimate indoor space, makes The Biergarten a St. Louis favorite any time of year.

venues.name: Big Bar at Alcove
venues.description: COMPLETE MENU CHANGE — WE HAVE REPLACED THIS LISTING'S DRINKS. Big Bar is the cocktail bar attached to Alcove Cafe at 1929 Hillhurst Avenue in Los Feliz, housed with the cafe in two historic bungalows with one of the larger patios on the east side. It opened on 8 October 2010 from Tom Trellis, who had opened Alcove itself in 2004. The cocktail programme has since been rebuilt entirely around a board-game theme, and none of the drinks we previously listed — Supernova, Tropic Thunder, The Apothecary, Pocket Full of Horses — remain. The current non-alcoholic section is headed "fun & games non-alcoholic cocktails", four drinks at $14, each named for a game: Can Chevy Come Over? (Red Rover) with Plaid Circus kimono dragon, dandelion, lime and corn silk kefir; Sister Sister (Twister) with Plaid Circus vespa rossa, Optimist Cali amaro, dogwood lemon oleo, celery and blueberry; Billie's Holiday (Cat's Cradle) with Seedlip Garden, catnip cream and vanilla bean; and Something Wicked (Ouija) with Pathfinder, sour Fuji apple, green almond orgeat and lemon. Non-alcoholic Best Day IPA and Fremont Dark are $8 each. Open from 8 or 9am daily.
signatureDrinks: Best Day NA West Coast IPA ($8)
venues.longDescription:
Big Bar sits alongside Alcove Cafe in two historic bungalows on Hillhurst Avenue in Los Feliz, sharing what is one of the larger patios on the east side of Los Angeles. Tom Trellis opened Alcove in 2004 with no prior restaurant experience and, in his own words, no concrete expectations other than to create a community within a community; Big Bar followed on 8 October 2010, a 325-foot bar with a deliberately ironic name. Cari Hah has run the bar since 2015, and her framing of the drinks has held up: they do not take themselves super seriously, and while the cocktails are serious, she is not trying to be nerdy and deep or make things too complex to enjoy. The kitchen is a proper all-day operation — a burger at $23, a lobster roll at $32, steak frites au poivre at $34 — and the bar opens with the cafe, from eight or nine in the morning.

This entry has been rewritten from scratch, because the cocktail programme is not the one we described. Big Bar has rebuilt its entire list around a board-game conceit, with each drink carrying a game's name in parentheses and a featured cocktail rotating monthly. None of the four zero-proof drinks we previously listed survives. The current section is headed fun & games non-alcoholic cocktails, and there are four, all $14. Can Chevy Come Over?, playing on Red Rover, uses a Plaid Circus kimono dragon spirit with dandelion, lime and corn silk kefir — kefir being the interesting part, since a fermented dairy drink gives body that fruit and soda cannot. Sister Sister, for Twister, layers Plaid Circus vespa rossa with Optimist's Cali amaro, a dogwood lemon oleo saccharum, celery and acid-adjusted blueberry. Billie's Holiday, for Cat's Cradle, is the gentle one: Seedlip Garden with catnip cream, vanilla bean, soda and mint. Something Wicked, for Ouija, runs Pathfinder against sour Fuji apple, green almond orgeat and lemon. Two non-alcoholic beers sit on the beer list at $8 — Best Day's west coast IPA and a Fremont Brewing dark, both under 0.5% ABV. Because the featured drink changes monthly, expect the specific names here to move on too.
venues.pressQuote: The bar team whips up housemade syrups, oft-rotating concoctions and one of the most cheeky, fun-loving menus in L.A. Puns, drink accessories and non-alcoholic cocktails abound, but don't think they can't do classics; the martinis, margs and spritzes here are some of the best in town.

venues.name: Big Mini Putt Club
venues.description: Big Mini Putt Club is an indoor mini golf bar and lounge at 70 Ionia Avenue SW, billing itself as the Midwest's indoor mini golf bar. It is included here for a specific structural reason: the activity is the point of the visit, so a guest who is not drinking is doing the same thing as everyone else at the table rather than watching. The bar backs that up with stock rather than improvisation, carrying six zero-proof drinks, three mocktails and two non-alcoholic beers. Named builds include the Mulligan Margarita and the Ube Tee, both listed among downtown Grand Rapids' best non-alcoholic drinks in October 2025. It sits directly between Max's South Seas Hideaway and One Twenty Three Tavern on the same block of Ionia.
venues.address: 70 Ionia Ave SW, Grand Rapids, MI 49503
venues.longDescription:
Big Mini Putt Club sits at 70 Ionia Avenue SW, on the short downtown block that also holds Max's South Seas Hideaway at number 58 and One Twenty Three Tavern at number 123, and it describes itself as the Midwest's indoor mini golf bar and lounge. The format is a full indoor putting course wrapped around a bar, open late at weekends — 3pm to 10pm Monday through Thursday, 2pm to 1am Friday, 11am to 1am Saturday and 11am to 10pm Sunday — with tee times bookable in advance.

The case for listing it in an alcohol-free guide is about structure more than about the drinks list, though the drinks list holds up. Most venues in this guide are places where drinking is the activity, which means a non-drinker is doing a lesser version of what the table is doing, however good the zero-proof build. At a mini golf bar the activity is the reason everyone is there, and the glass in your hand is incidental — which removes the social asymmetry that makes sober nights out difficult in the first place. That is the same logic that makes a board game lounge or a climbing gym work, and it is why this venue earns a place over several bars with more elaborate mocktails. The bar does not treat the drinks as an afterthought either: it carries six zero-proof drinks, three mocktails and two non-alcoholic beers as standing stock, and two of its builds were named in the Downtown Grand Rapids alliance's October 2025 round-up of the best non-alcoholic drinks in the city centre — the Mulligan Margarita, whose name does the obvious work with the golf theme, and the Ube Tee, built on the purple Filipino yam that gives it both its colour and a mild, nutty-vanilla sweetness. Eleven zero-proof options in total is more than several dedicated cocktail bars in this guide manage, and it means a group can order a round without anyone defaulting to tap water.

The location compounds the advantage. Ionia Avenue SW between Fulton and Weston is the single most useful block in Grand Rapids for an alcohol-free night: Big Mini Putt Club at 70, Max's South Seas Hideaway and its eight-strong Zero Proof menu at 58, One Twenty Three Tavern and its rebuilt classics at 123, and Cafe Jazzy Rose — the city's only entirely alcohol-free cocktail bar — a minute away at 44. That makes it possible to plan a full evening on foot without ever entering a room where the only option is a soft drink, which is not true of most American cities this size. Between the course itself, the late Friday and Saturday finishes at 1am, and a properly stocked zero-proof list, this is the most straightforward answer in Grand Rapids to the question of what to actually do on a night out without alcohol.
venues.pressQuote: Six zero-proof drinks, three mocktails and two NA beers — including the Mulligan Margarita and the Ube Tee.

venues.name: Bijou
venues.description: Bijou is a neighbourhood cocktail bar in Browne's Addition, Spokane's oldest residential district, with a menu split between house specialties, classic cocktails, warm winter drinks, seasonal coffee blends and a standing mocktail section. The alcohol-free drinks are made from the bar's own components rather than bought mixers — butterfly pea flower tea, house elderflower and lavender syrups, fresh citrus — and the bartenders build to taste, asking which flavours you like and dislike before making something rather than pointing at a list. Open every day from 3pm, to midnight most nights and 1am on Friday, which makes it the most reliably open room in this guide.
venues.longDescription:
Browne's Addition is the oldest residential neighbourhood in Spokane, a grid of Victorian and Craftsman houses just west of downtown, and Bijou is its cocktail bar. The menu is broader than most — house specialties, classic favourites, a run of warm wintry drinks for the months when that matters in eastern Washington, seasonal coffee blends, and mocktails carried as a standing part of the list rather than as an appendix.

What lifts it into this guide is how the alcohol-free drinks are actually made. The bar works from its own pantry: butterfly pea flower tea, house-made elderflower and lavender syrups, fresh lemon juice, soda water, a lemon peel garnish treated as seriously as it would be on a gin drink. Butterfly pea flower is a deliberate choice as well as a pretty one — it shifts from blue to violet as acid hits it, so the drink performs at the table the way a good cocktail does, which is a large part of what a non-drinker is actually missing in a bar.

The service model is the other half of it. Rather than handing over a short fixed list, the bartenders ask what you like and what you do not — sweet, sour, bitter, herbal — and build from there. That is normally a warning sign in this directory, because "we'll make you something" is how bars with no programme deflect the question. Here it sits on top of a printed mocktail section and a documented house-syrup pantry, so it functions as an upgrade rather than a substitute for having thought about it.

Bijou is open seven days from 3pm, running to midnight and to 1am on Friday. In a city where several of the best alcohol-free lists are Thursday-to-Saturday operations, being open on a Monday is a real advantage.
venues.pressQuote: a menu filled with house specialties, classic favorites, warm wintry drinks, mocktails and even seasonal coffee blends
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: The Inlander, on mocktails becoming a menu standard

venues.name: Bike Dog Brewing
venues.description: Bike Dog Brewing's East Sacramento taproom carries three genuinely different alcohol-free options: locally made KC Kombucha on rotating flavours, hop water in passion fruit, orange and guava, and Untitled Art non-alcoholic beer. Hop water is the interesting one in a brewery — sparkling water dry-hopped with the same aromatic hops as an IPA, bitter and citrusy with no alcohol and no calories. Ordering one in a taproom gets you the flavour everybody else came for, from the same tap wall, without the beer. The East Sacramento taproom opens Tuesday to Sunday, from noon at weekends, and is closed Mondays. Three genuinely different options in a brewery is unusual; most manage one dusty can.
signatureDrinks: KC Kombucha - locally made, rotating flavours
Hop water - passion fruit, orange, guava
venues.longDescription:
Bike Dog Brewing's East Sacramento taproom on 66th Street is a working brewery, and breweries are among the hardest rooms for a non-drinker: the entire proposition is beer, the staff are enthusiasts about beer, and the alcohol-free provision is typically one dusty can.

Bike Dog carries three distinct options, which is unusual. Hop water is the most interesting and the most underrated product in this whole category. It is sparkling water dry-hopped with the same aromatic hops used in an IPA — Citra, Mosaic and their relatives — producing something bitter, resinous and citrus-forward with no alcohol, no sugar and virtually no calories. Crucially, it tastes of the thing a taproom actually smells of. Ordering one gets you the hop aroma everybody else came for, poured from the same wall of taps, and nobody looking at your glass can tell the difference.

KC Kombucha covers a different need. Fermentation supplies acidity, tannin and a faint funk — the structural qualities alcohol normally provides — so a kombucha holds up across a long session rather than cloying after one glass. Being locally made and rotating means it changes, which matters if you are a regular.

Untitled Art non-alcoholic beer completes the set for anyone who wants an actual beer rather than an alternative to one; the brand has become one of the more respected NA producers in American craft.

Hours are Tuesday to Sunday, 3pm to 9pm midweek and from noon at weekends, closed Mondays. East Sacramento is residential, so this is a neighbourhood taproom rather than a destination — which is exactly the context in which having real options matters most.

There is a broader point about breweries worth making here. The craft beer world has been unusually quick to take non-alcoholic drinks seriously, faster than the cocktail world was, and the reason is technical rather than moral: brewers already understand that hops, malt and fermentation carry flavour independently of alcohol, so making something good without it is an engineering problem they find interesting rather than a compromise they resent. Hop water came out of that culture. It is one of the few alcohol-free products with no alcoholic original to be measured against, and it is better for it.
venues.pressQuote: Bike Dog Brewing: KC Kombucha (locally made, rotating flavors), hop water (passion fruit, orange, guava), Untitled Art NA beer.

venues.name: Billy Sunday
venues.description: Billy Sunday is an award-winning craft cocktail bar that opened in 2013 in Chicago's Logan Square, part of chef Matthias Merges' Folkart Management group. The bar is best known for one of North America's largest collections of vintage fernet and amaro — bartender Alex Bachman's deeply researched back bar earned a place in James Beard Award-winning author Brad Thomas Parsons' book on amaro. While the cocktail list is spirit-forward, the menu also carries a dedicated "Spirit Free" section. Named zero-proof options include the Lupine Lady (lavender- and thyme-infused verjus, lime, mint, basil, and sparkling water) and an Italian Cream Soda (cola reduction, stewed cherries, cream, nutmeg, and Perrier). The bar also pours a rotating Athletic Brewing non-alcoholic beer alongside house-fermented sodas (note: the house sodas contain trace amounts of alcohol).

Italian Cream Soda (cola reduction, stewed cherries, cream, nutmeg, Perrier) $9

venues.longDescription:
Billy Sunday has occupied 3143 W Logan Boulevard since 2013, part of chef Matthias Merges's Folkart Management group, and it is best known for a bar back that reads more like an archive than a stock list — one of North America's deepest collections of vintage fernet and amaro, much of it bottled decades ago and no longer made. The room is named after the baseball player turned evangelist who campaigned for Prohibition, which tells you the register: the bar takes its own seriousness lightly. Food is built for drinking rather than dining, running French onion dip with kettle chips at $6, pork chicharrones with a barbecue spice blend and hot sauce at $9, a five-cheese plate with Publican Quality bread at $28, and mussels in escabeche with a mezcal-amaro mustard at $28. It keeps genuinely late hours for the neighbourhood, opening at 5pm and running to 2am on Friday and Saturday, with a noon start on Sundays.

The non-alcoholic drinks sit under a heading of their own, "Spirit Free", and the two built cocktails are made with the same fermented-and-infused thinking as the amaro list rather than being fruit and soda. The Lupine Lady ($12) is the more complex: verjus infused with lavender and thyme, lengthened with lime, mint, basil and sparkling water, so it lands dry and herbal where most zero-proof drinks land sweet. The Italian Cream Soda ($9) goes the other way — a cola reduction with stewed cherries, cream and nutmeg over Perrier. Athletic Brewing supplies a rotating non-alcoholic beer at $7, which the menu tells you to ask the bartender about rather than pinning to one label. One detail deserves flagging, and to the bar's credit it flags it itself: the house fermented sodas ($8, in flavours including Dr. Billy, sasparilla, watermelon and a mystery option) carry a printed warning that they contain trace amounts of alcohol, a by-product of fermentation. Anyone avoiding alcohol completely should order the Lupine Lady, the Italian Cream Soda or the Athletic instead — but a bar that discloses this unprompted is being more honest than most.

venues.name: Binge Bar
venues.description: Binge Bar is Washington DC's first 100% alcohol-free bar, in a lower-level space at 506 H Street NE in the Atlas District. Filipina entrepreneur Vergie "Gigi" Arandid founded the concept in June 2020 and opened to the public on 11 February 2023. It works as three things at once: a zero-proof cocktail bar, a Filipino bistro serving traditional bites alongside plant-based Mediterranean plates, and an events room. The drinks are built rather than poured - a Cucumber Mangorita, an Espresso Old Fashioned on Bare Zero Proof bourbon, a Passion Fruit Ginger Sour, a Hibiscus Reposado Margarita - alongside craft NA beer, vegan wines and canned mocktails. It won Best Craft Mocktail in Washington City Paper's 2024 Best of DC reader poll, and runs monthly sober comedy nights and vegan brunches. Nothing alcoholic is served.

Functional Cucumber Gimlet (citrus, Tilden's Lacewing botanical spirits, Little Saints, lychee, basil, cardamom) $14

venues.longDescription:
Binge Bar is Washington DC's first 100% alcohol-free bar. Vergie "Gigi" Arandid, a Filipina entrepreneur, founded the concept in June 2020 and spent nearly three years getting it into a room, opening to the public on 11 February 2023 in a lower-level space at 506 H Street NE in the H Street Corridor, the stretch also known as the Atlas District. It is not only a bar. It doubles as a Filipino bistro, serving traditional Filipino bites alongside plant-based, Mediterranean-influenced plates, and as an events venue, which is what lets it programme evenings rather than simply open its doors.

The drinks are constructed the way cocktails are, and the bar is explicit that this is the point - its own line is that the Cucumber Mangorita is not a mocktail but an elevated spirit-free cocktail. The list runs to six named builds at $12 to $14: the Cucumber Mangorita, muddled herbs and spices with fresh cucumber juice, mango puree, lime and tonic; an Espresso Old Fashioned on Bare Zero Proof bourbon with muddled cherry and orange, citrus and orange cardamom bitters; a Passion Fruit Ginger Sour on Bare Zero Proof gin with fresh ginger, foamer and fig and aromatic bitters; a Functional Cucumber Gimlet using Tilden's Lacewing botanical spirits and Little Saints with lychee, basil and cardamom; a Peach Apple Mule; and a Hibiscus Reposado Margarita built on a house gumamela blend. Behind them sit craft NA beers, vegan wines and canned mocktails, with Seedlip, Free Spirits and Mocktail Club among the brands that have appeared.

What makes it work as a venue rather than a novelty is the programming: monthly sober comedy shows and vegan brunches with live entertainment, and an explicitly recovery-friendly framing. Arandid has described the aim as a comfortable space for people to be vulnerable and have fun at the same time. It was named Best Craft Mocktail in Washington City Paper's 2024 Best of DC reader poll and has been covered by Washingtonian and District Fray. Two practical notes: the bar is closed Monday and Tuesday, opening Wednesday to Saturday evenings and Sunday afternoons only, and the entrance is down a level from the street, which is easy to walk past.
venues.pressQuote: A comfortable space for people to really be vulnerable, to open up to each other, to have uncomfortable conversations and have fun at the very same time.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Vergie "Gigi" Arandid, founder of Binge Bar

venues.name: Bitter & Twisted Cocktail Parlour
venues.description: Set in the historic Luhrs Building downtown, Bitter & Twisted is one of Phoenix's most decorated cocktail bars — open since 2014, and a top-ten finalist for Best U.S. Cocktail Bar at the Tales of the Cocktail Spirited Awards. It takes its zero-proof side as seriously as the rest. Alongside a dedicated spirit-free menu, the team says roughly 60 percent of the full cocktail list can be built without alcohol, and the bar has developed non-alcoholic versions of a dozen or so menu staples rather than a token pair. Named NA drinks have included the Nada Colada, the fizzy hibiscus-sage-cinnamon Miss Nightingale, the Rhubarb-Ba-Arandas, RUM DMC, an NA Pornstar Martini, and Hasta La Vista, Berry! — zero-proof mezcal and Martini & Rossi's non-alcoholic aperitif with a triple-berry shrub and soda.
venues.hours: Mon closed; Tue-Thu 4pm-12am; Fri-Sat 4pm-1am; Sun closed
venues.longDescription:
Bitter & Twisted occupies the ground floor of the Luhrs Building, a 1920s downtown tower that once housed Arizona's Prohibition-era attorney general — a piece of history the bar has never been shy about using. It opened in 2014 under Ross Simon and became, quickly, the most decorated cocktail room in the state: a top-ten finalist for Best U.S. Cocktail Bar at the Tales of the Cocktail Spirited Awards, and a fixture on national lists ever since. The menu arrives as a thick illustrated book, which sets the tone — this is a bar that treats drinks as a subject rather than a product.

What makes it matter to a non-drinker is proportion. The team reckons roughly 60 percent of the full cocktail list can be built without alcohol, and rather than parking two sweet options at the back of the menu, the bar has worked up non-alcoholic versions of a dozen or so of its staples. The Nada Colada is the piña colada rebuilt; Miss Nightingale is fizzy with hibiscus, sage and cinnamon; the Rhubarb-Ba-Arandas works hibiscus juice, rhubarb and strawberry sherbet; RUM DMC layers a zero-proof spirit with lime, guava, grapefruit-cinnamon syrup and a passion fruit foam; and Hasta La Vista, Berry! balances zero-proof mezcal against Martini & Rossi's non-alcoholic aperitif with a triple-berry shrub and soda. There is even an NA Pornstar Martini, which is the sort of thing bars usually refuse to attempt without alcohol.

DiningOut Phoenix put it plainly in May 2026: the zero-proof versions here more than stand up against the alcoholic counterparts. Practical notes — the bar runs Tuesday to Saturday and closes Sunday and Monday, it fills up after work and stays busy, and it is a full cocktail bar rather than an alcohol-free room. The point is not that alcohol is absent but that its absence costs you nothing.
venues.pressQuote: the zero-proof versions here more than stand up against the alcoholic counterparts

venues.name: Black Pearl
venues.description: Black Pearl is a Fitzroy cocktail institution on Brunswick Street that has been named among the World's 50 Best Bars, and its bartenders extend the same craft to their alcohol-free builds. Broadsheet's best-non-alcoholic-bars guide singles it out for giving zero-proof drinks equal billing, from a savoury shaken number with lacto-fermented tomato, lemon juice, honey, ginger and Lyre's Italian Spritz to fruit-forward mocktails. Non-alcoholic beer such as Heaps Normal is also poured alongside the celebrated cocktail list. Time Out rates the alcohol-free cocktails as impressive as everything else the bartenders mix, running from a savoury build on lacto-fermented tomatoes to fruitier work.
signatureDrinks: Savoury shaken non-alcoholic cocktail with lacto-fermented tomato, lemon juice, honey, ginger and Lyre's Italian Spritz
venues.longDescription:
Opened in 2002 and family-run by owner Tash Conte, Black Pearl has spent more than two decades as one of Melbourne's most decorated cocktail bars, a Fitzroy fixture at 304 Brunswick Street that has appeared on the World's 50 Best Bars list (peaking at No. 10 in 2011) and launched a long line of celebrated Australian bartenders. Time Out calls it a bar that has "been a beacon of excellence for decades," while its own team keeps the list "always on the move, keeping step with moods and seasons."

That restless, seasons-led approach is what makes its non-alcoholic offering more than an afterthought. Broadsheet's guide to Melbourne's best non-alcoholic bars highlights Black Pearl for giving its booze-free drinks equal billing with the classics, citing a savoury shaken cocktail built on lacto-fermented tomato, lemon juice, honey, ginger and Lyre's Italian Spritz, alongside brighter fruit-forward mocktails. Non-alcoholic beer from Australian brewer Heaps Normal rounds out the low- and no-options at the bar.

The room itself is classic Fitzroy: a dark, intimate downstairs bar with regulars perched at the counter on quieter nights and a livelier crowd on weekends, plus The Attic, a speakeasy-style space upstairs with table service. It is walk-ins only downstairs, open Wednesday to Sunday from 5pm until 3am.

The range is the reason to come here rather than to a bar with a token zero-proof section. Time Out, reviewing the room, says Black Pearl's non-alcoholic cocktail options are just as impressive as everything else the bartenders mix, and describes the span: a savoury concoction made with lacto-fermented tomatoes at one end, a fruitier affair at the other, with the bar staff expected to have something hangover-free to hand whichever way a guest leans.

A lacto-fermented tomato drink is a specific and useful signal. Fermentation takes days of planning and fridge space, and no bar prepares one for a drink it does not expect to sell. It also produces the savoury, umami weight that alcohol normally supplies — the quality most zero-proof drinks lack, and the reason so many of them read as soft drinks. More than a decade in and still award-winning, the bar treats this as ordinary work rather than a special request.
venues.pressQuote: Tash Conte's family-run bar has been a beacon of excellence for decades.

venues.name: Blackbird
venues.description: Blackbird is a literary-themed neighbourhood cocktail bar on Market Street at the Castro end of Upper Market, open since 2009 and trading to 2am on Friday and Saturday. Its menu carries a section headed Low ABV & Zero Proof, and two of the five drinks in it contain no alcohol at all: Nearly February, at $10, built from fig-infused balsamic with orange, grapefruit and soda water, and Salty Puppy, at $12, made with Aplós Calm, grapefruit, lime, honey and orange blossom water over a salted rim. Aplós Calm is a hemp-derived non-alcoholic spirit and the bar also stocks Wyld CBD cans, which is worth knowing for anyone avoiding psychoactive ingredients as well as alcohol.
signatureDrinks: Nearly February (fig-infused balsamic, orange, grapefruit, soda water)
Salty Puppy (Aplós Calm hemp-derived NA spirit, grapefruit, lime, honey, orange blossom water, salted rim)
venues.longDescription:
Blackbird has been on Market Street between Church and Sanchez since 2009, at the point where Upper Market runs into the Castro, and marked ten years of cocktails in 2019. It is a dark, art-hung neighbourhood bar rather than a destination cocktail room, and The Infatuation names it in its guide to the city's twenty best cocktail bars, saying it is where the writers go for nightcaps and after-work drinks. The bar opens at 5pm on weeknights, from 2pm at weekends, and trades until 2am on Friday and Saturday.

The drinks menu carries a heading for Low ABV & Zero Proof cocktails, and the distinction inside that section matters: three of the five drinks listed under it are genuinely low-alcohol builds using Aperol, Lillet, vermouth or rabarbaro amaro, while two contain no alcohol at all. Nearly February, at $10, is built from the bar's fig-infused balsamic with orange, grapefruit and soda water, and reads as a dry, faintly savoury long drink rather than a sweet one. Salty Puppy, at $12, is the more constructed of the two: Aplós Calm with grapefruit, lime, honey, orange blossom water and a salted rim, a zero-proof reading of the salty dog. Aplós Calm is a hemp-derived non-alcoholic spirit containing a broad-spectrum hemp extract, and Blackbird separately stocks Wyld CBD cans at $8, which is worth flagging for guests who are avoiding psychoactive ingredients as well as alcohol — the two truly neutral options on the list are Nearly February and the bar's soft drinks. Prices for the zero-proof drinks run well below the $12 to $15 charged for the full-proof cocktails. The rest of the bar is a straightforward neighbourhood operation — rotating draught beer and cans, a five-strong wine list, a boilermaker and well cocktails at $10 — and a 20 per cent service charge is added to unsettled tabs. For the Castro and Upper Market, where the drinking options are overwhelmingly built around late nights and full-strength cocktails, having two genuinely alcohol-free builds on the printed menu at a bar that trades to 2am is a meaningful piece of provision.
venues.pressQuote: Ask us where we're going for nightcaps or after-work drinks with friends, and we'll say Blackbird every time.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: The Infatuation, The 20 Best Cocktail Bars In SF

venues.name: BlackSheep Wine Bar & Merchant
venues.description: A wine bar and bottle merchant on San Marcos Place in historic downtown Chandler, at the southeastern edge of the Phoenix metro. It describes itself as equal parts wine bar and conversational destination, and its non-alcoholic drinks are made from real NA spirits rather than soft drinks: the Citrusy Glow is Seedlip Citrus with fresh lemon, and the Spice Girl works berries against Seedlip Spice. DiningOut Phoenix named it among the metro bars worth visiting for a mocktail in May 2026. Open from 11am on weekdays, with a nightly Rebel Hour from 7pm seven days a week, and quiet enough to hold a conversation in.
venues.address: 98 S San Marcos Pl, Chandler, AZ 85225
venues.longDescription:
BlackSheep sits on San Marcos Place in historic downtown Chandler, at the southeastern edge of the Phoenix metro and far enough from the downtown Phoenix cocktail cluster to serve a genuinely different crowd — this is a neighbourhood destination rather than a stop on a bar crawl. It operates as both a wine bar and a merchant, with bottles to drink in or carry out, and describes itself as equal parts wine bar and conversational destination. That is a fair account of the room: it is built for talking, at a volume that allows it, which is not a given in a metro whose bar scene skews loud.

The non-alcoholic drinks are constructed rather than poured. The Citrusy Glow is Seedlip Citrus with fresh lemon; the Spice Girl sets berries against the warmer, aromatic Seedlip Spice. Building on a named alcohol-free spirit instead of sweetening juice and calling the result a mocktail is precisely the distinction that earns a wine bar a place in a directory like this one — a wine bar has the least structural reason to bother, since its whole proposition is the bottle list. DiningOut Phoenix singled the venue out for exactly that in its May 2026 guide to metro mocktails.

The bar opens at 11am on weekdays and runs a Rebel Hour nightly from 7pm, seven days a week, so it works for an afternoon as readily as an evening. It is a licensed wine bar, so the alcohol-free list is one real section of the menu rather than the whole offering. But for a non-drinker joining a table of wine drinkers — the specific social situation a wine bar creates and rarely solves — having two properly built drinks printed on the same list as everything else is the difference between being catered for and being an afterthought.
venues.pressQuote: has a dedicated mocktail menu that keeps sober and zebra-striping guests at the forefront

venues.name: Blank Slate
venues.description: Blank Slate is a woman-owned neighborhood cocktail bar that opened in 2017 in Portland's Montavilla neighborhood, founded by longtime Portland bartender Kierre Van de Veere and Michael Irikawa. Set among lush plants, floral wallpaper, and a deep vinyl collection, it serves craft cocktails, beer, wine, and a seasonal small-plates menu. Its non-alcoholic program is genuine and built in-house: the menu's dedicated "Non-Alcoholic Cocktails" section runs about half a dozen drinks at $10, using house-made botanical syrups, house tea blends, coconut milk, vinegars, and rosewater rather than juice-and-soda shortcuts. Named zero-proof drinks include the Cat Nap N.A. (bitter botanical syrup, chamomile, sherry vinegar), Orange Dream Machine N.A. (orange, vanilla, rosewater, oat milk), Rose Darling N.A. (hibiscus, rose and green tea, lime, coconut milk), and Vacation (coconut milk, passion fruit, lemon, lime, orgeat). NA beer, hop water, kombucha, and CBD soda round out the list.
venues.address: 7201 NE Glisan St, Ste C, Portland, OR 97213

venues.longDescription:
Blank Slate is a woman-owned neighbourhood cocktail bar at 7201 NE Glisan Street in Montavilla, a stretch Willamette Week once described as already equipped with Vietnamese joints, storied dive bars and great Detroit pizza on Tuesdays. Michael Irikawa raised the money to open it with Kierre Van de Veere in late 2015, and Willamette Week reviewed the finished room in July 2017, noting patterned wallpaper carrying a very pretty procession of greenery and lilies, and food with personal touches like fresh Hood strawberries from the owners' garden. The bar still describes itself in those plain terms — a local, woman-owned small business operated by community residents — and the kitchen runs in the same register: oysters on the half shell, deviled eggs with pickled beets and horseradish, a tin fish board built on Matiz wild sardines, shishito peppers in vegan miso butter, and three molasses cookies baked to order.

The non-alcoholic list is a headed "Non-Alcoholic Cocktails" section of six drinks, and what distinguishes it is that four are built from scratch ingredients rather than poured from a bought-in zero-proof bottle. Cat Nap N.A. combines a house-made bitter botanical syrup with chamomile, sherry vinegar, saline and an orange twist. Rose Darling N.A. layers hibiscus, rose and green tea, spiced simple syrup, lime, coconut milk and soda. Orange Dream Machine N.A. is orange juice, vanilla, rosewater, oat milk and soda, and Vacation runs coconut milk, passion fruit, lemon, lime, orgeat and mint. An N.A. Spritz uses the house botanical syrup with peppermint tea, white balsamic, soda and a lemon twist. Five of the six are $10; the one bought-in option is the Phony Negroni at $11, St. Agrestis's bottled sparkling non-alcoholic Negroni. There is no non-alcoholic beer, but the soft-drink shelf is unusually considered for a cocktail bar, including Fort George Fruit Lup hop water and a Wylde blackberry CBD soda. The bar opens Monday to Thursday 4–10pm and Friday and Saturday 4–11pm, and closes Sundays.
venues.pressQuote: A tight list of nonalcoholic cocktails that go beyond fruit juices and sodas — botanical syrups, housemade tea blends, coconut milk, vinegars, and rosewater.

venues.name: Blinker
venues.description: Blinker is a serious-but-welcoming cocktail bar on Spring Gardens in Manchester city centre, opened by industry veteran Dan Berger and named after a near-forgotten rye, grapefruit and raspberry classic. Alongside its seasonal, Top 50-listed cocktail programme it keeps a short, considered low- and no-alcohol list built on Three Spirit's botanical blends. Regulars include a trio of fully alcohol-free cocktails made with Three Spirit Livener or Nightcap, plus zero-proof takes on the Martini, Margarita and Manhattan. The team's obsessive, ingredient-led approach applies just as much to the drinks without booze.
venues.hours: Mon closed; Tue-Wed 3pm-11pm; Thu 3pm-12am; Fri 3pm-12:30am; Sat 2pm-12:30am; Sun 2pm-10pm
signatureDrinks: No Nonsense (Three Spirit Livener, cranberry, orange & lemon)
Three Spirit Livener & Nightcap alcohol-free cocktails
venues.longDescription:
Blinker opened on Spring Gardens, tucked into the Northspring building at the top of King Street a short walk from Hotel Gotham, and is the work of founder Dan Berger — formerly head of bars at Gordon Ramsay Restaurants and The Ned, and the man behind Iceberg Bar Consultancy. The name nods to a long-forgotten three-ingredient cocktail of rye, grapefruit and raspberry, and that same reverence for classics runs through the room: an upscale but unstuffy walk-in bar, deliberately tucked away so the weekend crowds pass it by, staffed by chatty bartenders who are unmistakably in it for the craft. The menu changes monthly and is built around four in-season flavours, with dedicated Martini and Old Fashioned sections, and the bar has earned a place on Britain's Top 50 Cocktail Bars list.

The low- and no-alcohol offering is small by design but genuinely built rather than bolted on. As Manchester's Finest put it, the team have come up with 'a short but perfectly-formed list of low ABV cocktails based around botanical spirits by Three Spirit' — the non-alcoholic Livener and Nightcap blends whose names promise mood-altering, liven-you-up or wind-you-down properties. That runs to a trio of fully alcohol-free cocktails made with Three Spirit Livener or Nightcap, from a raspberry-and-ginger-ale-style long drink to a lime, almond and maple sip, plus a No Nonsense that pairs Three Spirit Livener with cranberry, orange and lemon.

Beyond the Three Spirit builds, Blinker will also pour zero-proof and low-ABV versions of its bar-classic canon — the Martini, Margarita and Manhattan among them — so the sober or sober-curious drinker gets the same considered, seasonal treatment as everyone else rather than a token mocktail on request. It makes Blinker one of the stronger city-centre choices in Manchester for anyone after a properly made drink without the alcohol.
venues.pressQuote: The mixological minds at Blinker have come up with a short but perfectly-formed list of low ABV cocktails based around botanical spirits by Three Spirit, which promise mood-altering properties like the 'livener' and the 'nightcap'.

venues.name: Blood Brothers Brewing
venues.description: Blood Brothers Brewing is a craft brewery and taproom on Geary Avenue in Toronto's Geary Avenue Arts District, set inside a renovated hundred-year-old horse stable. Alongside its rotating lineup of up to 26 taps, the brewery brews and cans its own dedicated non-alcoholic beer line — a 0.5% ABV Zero IPA and several Paradise Lost sour variants — sold through a standalone "Non-alc" collection on its own site. Narcity singled out the brewery's non-alcoholic options as "equally as fun" as its beer, pointing to an in-house strawberry-kiwi lemonade sparkling water and "the occasional non-alcoholic craft beer."
venues.address: 165 Geary Avenue, Toronto, Ontario M6H 2B8, Canada

Paradise Lost Non-Alc Blackberry Crumble Sour (0.5% ABV; berry-forward with vanilla and graham notes)
Paradise Lost Non-Alc Guava Pineapple (473ml tall can)
venues.longDescription:
Blood Brothers Brewing is a craft brewery and taproom on Geary Avenue in Toronto's Geary Avenue Arts District, set inside a renovated hundred-year-old horse stable with indoor seating and a seasonal patio. The taproom pours from up to 26 taps spanning lagers and pilsners, hazy and double dry-hopped IPAs, sour and funky ales, and a dry Irish stout on nitro, alongside a retail bottle shop for takeaway cans. The kitchen runs a Southern comfort food program, smoking meats in-house over oak staves pulled from the brewery's own spent beer barrels. The taproom is open Sunday through Thursday from noon to 11pm and Friday and Saturday from noon until late.

Blood Brothers also brews and cans its own dedicated non-alcoholic beer line, sold through a standalone "Non-alc" collection on the brewery's own site as well as in the taproom. Zero is a 0.5% ABV non-alcoholic IPA brewed with Citra and HBC-638 hops, described by the brewery as carrying citrus and stone-fruit aromas, very low bitterness and an exceptionally smooth finish. The Paradise Lost non-alcoholic sours, also 0.5% ABV, come in several fruited variants: a Spiced Cherry version fermented on cherry and aged on a blend of spices, with flavors likened to homemade cherry pie and mulled wine; a Blackberry Crumble version that leans heavier on berry with hints of vanilla and graham on the aroma; and a Guava Pineapple version sold as a 473ml tall can. The NA lineup is corroborated independently on Untappd and by third-party retailer Collective Craft Beer Shop, beyond the brewery's own product listings.

The non-alcoholic program also has independent press notice: a June 2024 Narcity feature on Toronto breweries serving alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks singled out Blood Brothers, noting its non-alcoholic options are "equally as fun" as its beer, including a strawberry-kiwi lemonade sparkling water made in-house and "the occasional non-alcoholic craft beer."
venues.pressQuote: they've also got some non-alcoholic options that are equally as fun, including strawberry-kiwi lemonade sparkling water made in-house and the occasional non-alcoholic craft beer

venues.name: Bloom's
venues.description: Bloom's is the late-night cocktail lounge just off the lobby of Hotel Ulysses, the maximalist 116-room hotel that opened in the 1920s Latrobe Building on Mount Vernon's Read Street in September 2022. The room commits to the look — crimson banquettes, purple stools, a mirrored ceiling and bar counter — and the list draws on Prohibition-era classics and 1970s revivals like the Midori sour and French martini. The menu carries a short but genuine Zero Proof section: the No Negroni builds Seedlip Garden 108 with Earl Grey tea and Giffard's alcohol-free aperitif bitter, alongside the Naquiri, a daiquiri-shaped mix of Seedlip Grove 42, guava, lime and orgeat (it contains almonds); the earlier Apple Blossom has rotated off, and Peroni's non-alcoholic lager sits on the beer list. It is a two-drink program rather than a deep one, but both are built cocktails on a named menu section, not mocktails improvised on request.

Naquiri (Seedlip Grove 42, guava, lime, orgeat — contains almonds) $14

venues.longDescription:
Bloom's is the late-night cocktail lounge just off the lobby of Hotel Ulysses at 2 E Read Street in Mount Vernon, which opened in September 2022 inside the 1920s Latrobe Building. The room is the opposite of restrained: the Baltimore Sun described a low-lit, velvet-clad lounge with mirrors covering the walls and ceilings, warm pink petal lamps, floral arrangements and plush purple velvet bar stools, and The Baltimore Banner summarised it more briskly as a disco ball of a bar. Esquire named it to its thirty-three best bars in America in 2023. Food is deliberately minimal and salty — house-roasted almonds, marinated olives, rosemary chips — because this is a drinking room that happens to open late rather than a restaurant with a bar attached. It serves from 5pm Tuesday through Sunday, to 1am on Friday and Saturday, closed Mondays, with reservations through Resy.

The zero-proof drinks have their own printed heading and are priced at $14, within a couple of dollars of the full cocktail list rather than discounted into a lesser category. Both are built on Seedlip. The No Negroni uses Seedlip Garden 108 with Earl Grey tea and Giffard's alcohol-free aperitif — the tea doing the tannic work that gin would normally do, and the Giffard supplying genuine bitterness rather than a sweetened approximation. The Naquiri is built on Seedlip Grove 42 with guava, lime and orgeat, and one detail matters more than the rest: orgeat is an almond syrup, and the menu lists almonds in the ingredients, so this is not a drink to order past a nut allergy. There is nothing cannabis-infused anywhere on the menu — the only "N/A" marking beyond the cocktails is on a non-alcoholic Peroni — which is worth confirming explicitly in a state where zero-proof headings increasingly hide THC. Hotel Ulysses lists Bloom's as one of four dining rooms currently operating in the building.
venues.pressQuote: A disco ball of a bar.

venues.name: Bloomsday
venues.description: Bloomsday is a small wine bar and cafe near Headhouse Square, and it does something almost no other bar in Philadelphia does: it runs a $6 non-alcoholic happy hour price all the time, year-round, rather than only in January. Cuddles on the Beach pairs pomegranate with orange; there is a house-made ginger beer, which is worth ordering because a genuine ginger beer is fermented and hot rather than sweet; and the fridge carries Well Being's non-alcoholic IPA, Collective Arts Hazy at 0.5% and Athletic's golden ale. For a wine bar — the venue type where a non-drinker is usually offered the least — a permanent zero-proof price is a meaningful commitment.
venues.hours: Mon-Tue closed; Wed-Thu 4pm-9pm; Fri 4pm-10pm; Sat 10am-10pm; Sun 10am-2pm
signatureDrinks: Cuddles on the Beach ($6) — pomegranate, orange
venues.longDescription:
Bloomsday is a small wine bar and all-day cafe on South 2nd Street near Headhouse Square, named for the day on which Joyce's Ulysses is set. It is exactly the sort of room where being the non-drinker is usually a thin experience: the whole proposition is a curated list of natural wine, and the alternative is normally a soda.

What makes it worth listing is a pricing decision. Bloomsday runs its non-alcoholic drinks at six dollars, at happy-hour price, permanently — not as a Dry January promotion that vanishes in February, but year-round and at all hours. That is rare enough to be the headline. A great many bars produce an excellent zero-proof list in January and quietly retire it; a standing price signals that the drinks are part of the business rather than a seasonal marketing exercise.

Cuddles on the Beach pairs pomegranate with orange, tart against sweet. More interesting is the house-made ginger beer, and the distinction between ginger beer and ginger ale is worth knowing: ginger ale is a flavoured soda, while a true ginger beer is fermented from fresh ginger and carries genuine heat and a cloudy body. A bar that makes its own is producing something with more bite than anything that comes out of a bottle, and it works as a drink in its own right rather than as a mixer.

The fridge covers the beer drinker properly too — Well Being's non-alcoholic IPA, Collective Arts Hazy at 0.5% and Athletic's golden ale, which is three genuine choices rather than a token can.

The hours are worth planning around, because this is not a late room: closed Monday and Tuesday, four to nine on Wednesday and Thursday, four to ten on Friday, and a long Saturday from ten in the morning to ten at night. Sunday is a morning-only service, closing at two. It suits an early evening or a weekend afternoon rather than a late night out.
venues.pressQuote: Bloomsday's general manager D'Onna Stubblefield calls it a “one-stop shop for vibes”
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Visit Philadelphia, A Guide to Zero-Proof Restaurants & Bars in Philly, January 2025

venues.name: Blue Atlas Restaurant and Market
venues.description: Blue Atlas is a restaurant and market in Fulton, east of downtown Richmond, and its bar does two things that separate a real alcohol-free offering from a token one: it makes its own shrubs, and it stocks non-alcoholic wine. A shrub is a drinking vinegar — fruit, sugar and vinegar macerated over days — and it exists precisely to give a soft drink the acidity and length that alcohol normally provides, so any kitchen making one has committed real prep time to the non-drinker's side of the menu. Combined with the market operation and a Wednesday-to-Sunday schedule, it is a genuine destination rather than a convenient stop.
venues.longDescription:
Blue Atlas occupies a corner of Fulton, the neighbourhood east of downtown along the river that has spent the last few years turning into somewhere people travel to eat. It runs as both a restaurant and a market, which gives the room an all-day character rather than a service-driven one.

Two details on the drinks list do the work here. The first is the house shrub. A shrub is a drinking vinegar: fruit, sugar and vinegar left to macerate for days, then lengthened with soda. It matters because the fundamental problem with non-alcoholic drinks is structural — take the alcohol out and what remains tends to be flat and sweet, because alcohol is what normally supplies bite, warmth and length. Vinegar restores the acidity and the finish. It also takes days of prep and occupies fridge space, which means no kitchen makes one casually. It is one of the most reliable signals that a restaurant takes the alcohol-free side of its list seriously.

The second is the non-alcoholic wine, which the market side makes practical to stock. Dealcoholised wine is the hardest category to do well and the one most often missing, so having a few options genuinely changes what a non-drinking guest can do over a long dinner — it is the difference between drinking alongside the table and drinking around it.

The schedule needs planning: closed Monday and Tuesday, then 9am to 9pm Wednesday through Saturday, with Sunday split around a 2:30pm close and a 5pm reopening for dinner. Fulton is a short drive from the centre rather than a walk, so this is a destination visit — but the all-day hours and the market mean it rewards one. The market side also means you can leave with something for later, which no other venue on this list offers.
venues.pressQuote: We are in a historic schoolhouse in the Fulton Hill neighborhood

venues.name: Boca
venues.description: Boca is Chef David Falk's flagship fine-dining room, set behind a famous red door in the storied Sixth Street space that once held Cincinnati's legendary Maisonette. Its Italian-French menu is matched by a beverage list carrying a genuine dedicated "Zero Proof" section: five alcohol-free cocktails, each $12. The lineup pairs house builds — the Caribbean Queen (coconut milk, pineapple, demerara, cherry), the Blueberry Basil Fizz, The Cure (ginger, basil, honey, citrus, ginger beer) and the strawberry-jalapeno Fragola Pazzo — with a St. Agrestis Phony Negroni served over big ice with orange. It's a real menu section rather than an afterthought, letting non-drinkers order with the same intention as the wine-and-cocktail crowd in one of the region's most decorated dining rooms.
venues.hours: Mon closed; Tue-Thu 5pm-9pm; Fri-Sat 5pm-10pm; Sun closed

venues.longDescription:
Chef David Falk opened Boca in Cincinnati's Northside neighborhood in October 2001, moved it to Oakley in 2004, and in 2013 relocated it downtown into the historic Sixth Street room that once housed the Maisonette, long the city's most famous restaurant. A Culinary Institute of America graduate who trained at Chicago's Spiaggia and Charlie Trotter's and in Italy, Falk built Boca into a French-and-Italian destination that has topped Cincinnati Magazine's Best Restaurants list and drawn national recognition from Travel + Leisure, OpenTable's Top 100, Forbes Travel Guide, and Saveur.

The beverage program is anchored by a wine and cocktail list, but it also carries a dedicated "Zero Proof" section of five non-alcoholic cocktails, each $12 — an unusually deliberate offering for a room at this level. Four are house builds: the Caribbean Queen (coconut milk, pineapple, demerara, cherry), the Blueberry Basil Fizz (blueberry-basil syrup, lemon, soda), The Cure (ginger, basil, honey, citrus, ginger beer), and the Fragola Pazzo (strawberry-jalapeno, agave, citrus, soda). The fifth is a St. Agrestis Phony Negroni — a bottled non-alcoholic Italian aperitivo, not made in-house — served over big ice with orange. It reads as a true menu section rather than a token gesture, so a non-drinking guest can order with the same care as the table's wine drinkers.

Boca sits at 114 E 6th Street in downtown's Central Business District, behind its signature red door. It serves dinner Tuesday through Thursday 5–9pm and Friday–Saturday 5–10pm, and is closed Sunday and Monday; reservations are strongly recommended at this upscale, special-occasion room (513-542-2022, @bocacincy). It suits diners marking an occasion who want a genuine alcohol-free option alongside a landmark tasting-menu experience. Note that the beverage list rotates, so specific zero-proof drinks may change seasonally.
venues.pressQuote: Reliable excellence is rare, but Boca consistently exceeds expectations.

venues.name: BODHI
venues.description: BODHI is a 21-and-over Thai craft cocktail bar and bistro at the far end of Massachusetts Avenue, run by Taelor Carmine alongside her mother Nicky Carmine and grandmother Pen Phojanasupan, both of whom spent years in Thai restaurant kitchens. It is women-owned and family-run, with a pan-Thai menu built from recipes passed down through the three of them. The bar treats zero-proof as a build rather than a substitution: the Water Lily Dessert layers Lyre's Dry London Spirit and Fre Rosé over coconut water, strawberry shrub, lychee jelly and soda, and the rotating Secret Garden leans on seasonal fruit and vegetables. Seedlip appears in the seasonal list. The kitchen closes an hour before the bar does.
venues.hours: Mon 5pm-10pm; Tue closed; Wed-Thu 5pm-10pm; Fri-Sat 5pm-11pm; Sun 5pm-10pm
signatureDrinks: Water Lily Dessert (Lyre's Dry London Spirit, Fre Rosé, coconut water, strawberry shrub, lychee jelly, soda)
Secret Garden (rotating seasonal fruit and herb build)
venues.longDescription:
BODHI sits at 922 Massachusetts Avenue, at the quieter northeast end of Mass Ave past the cultural-district signage, and is one of the few bars in Indianapolis where three generations of the same family are behind the counter. Taelor Carmine owns it and runs the bar; her mother Nicky Carmine and her grandmother Pen Phojanasupan, both of whom worked years in Thai restaurants, run the kitchen. The result is a pan-Thai bistro attached to a genuine craft cocktail program — the room is industrial-chic and small, it is 21-and-over, and the food is family recipes rather than a menu assembled around the drinks.

The zero-proof drinks get the same treatment as everything else on the list, which in a Thai context means the aromatic ingredients are already there. The Water Lily Dessert is the signature: Lyre's Dry London Spirit and Fre Rosé layered with coconut water, a strawberry shrub, lychee jelly and soda, so it drinks long, floral and slightly savoury rather than as a sweet mocktail. The rotating Secret Garden is built around whatever fruit and vegetables are in season, and Seedlip turns up in the seasonal builds alongside the Lyre's range. Because the bar keeps its own house shrubs and cordials for the full-proof list, the alcohol-free drinks draw on the same store of components rather than a separate shortcut. Practical notes: the bar stays open an hour past the kitchen, to 10pm Sunday through Thursday and 11pm on Friday and Saturday, and the whole place is closed on Tuesdays. Ball & Biscuit, The Fountain Room and Sundry & Vice are all within a few minutes' walk down the same street. BODHI is also the easiest of the Mass Ave rooms to eat a full meal in without drinking, which is a different proposition from having one good mocktail at a bar. The pan-Thai menu is built for sharing and the heat levels are real, so the zero-proof drinks have something to do — the coconut and lychee in the Water Lily Dessert works against chilli in a way a gin and tonic does not. It is worth calling ahead at weekends: the room seats fewer than most Mass Ave bars, it does not take a large party comfortably, and the 21-and-over policy applies to the whole space including the dining side, so this is not an option with children.
venues.pressQuote: Water Lily Dessert — Lyre's Dry London Spirit, Fre Rosé, Coconut Water, Strawberry Shrub, Lychee Jelly, Soda.

venues.name: Boia De
venues.description: Boia De is a Michelin-starred Italian restaurant opened in June 2019 by chef-partners Luciana Giangrandi and Alex Meyer, who began as a Miami food-truck and pop-up before going brick-and-mortar. Tucked into the Bravo Supermarket Plaza on the Little Haiti/Upper East Side line — marked by a neon pink exclamation point next to a coin laundromat — the intimate room seats roughly two dozen and earned its first Michelin star in 2022, retained through 2026. The kitchen pairs precise small plates and pasta with a curated wine list and a genuine no/low-ABV cocktail program. The menu's dedicated "Zero Proof" section brings the same precision to alcohol-free drinks: the Sober Surfer leans into tropical Miami flavors (coconut, pineapple, Pathfinder), while Strawberry Fields Forever is a clarified, layered build of strawberry-cucumber oleo, lemon, and basil oil. An Aplos Cup and a non-alcoholic Untitled Art IPA round out the options.
