venues.longDescription:
Boia De occupies a small room in the Bravo Supermarket Plaza on the Little Haiti and Upper East Side line, marked by a neon pink exclamation point next to a coin laundromat. Chef-partners Luciana Giangrandi and Alex Meyer opened it in June 2019 after running a Miami food truck and pop-up, and it earned its first Michelin star in 2022, retained through 2026. The dining room seats roughly two dozen.

A Michelin-starred kitchen of that size is where alcohol-free drinks usually get worst treatment: the wine pairing is central to the experience, the covers are few, and there is no room behind the bar for a second programme. Boia De instead runs a named Zero Proof section built with the same precision as the food. The Sober Surfer leans into tropical Miami — coconut, pineapple, Pathfinder. Strawberry Fields Forever is clarified and layered, built on strawberry-cucumber oleo with lemon and basil oil. Clarification is a technique that costs time and yields a drink that looks like water and tastes like fruit; nobody does it for a menu they consider an obligation.

An Aplos Cup and a non-alcoholic Untitled Art IPA round out the list, so a guest who wants a beer with pasta has one.

The Greater Miami CVB has noted that the restaurant brings the same precision to its mocktails as to its food, singling out the Sober Surfer. That is the correct read: this is not a bar with a good NA list, it is a kitchen whose standards happen to extend to the glass.

Book well ahead — two dozen seats and a Michelin star is a difficult combination. It is a full restaurant with a wine list, not an alcohol-free venue. The neon exclamation point beside the laundromat is the only signage — it is easy to drive past, and that is deliberate.
venues.pressQuote: This MICHELIN-recognized favorite brings the same precision to its mocktails as it does to its food.

venues.name: Bokeh
venues.description: Bokeh is a cosy neighbourhood cocktail bar in Albany Park, two blocks north of the Kedzie Brown Line stop, opened in 2019 by a hospitality veteran and former professional photographer who built the room around a photography theme — bokeh being the name for the soft out-of-focus light behind a subject. It was nominated for Neighbourhood Bar of the Year in the Chicago Tribune's 2025 Readers' Choice food awards. Its menu carries a printed "Alcohol-Free Cocktails" section of four drinks at $11, all built from house syrups, jams and fresh juice rather than bought-in zero-proof spirits: Watermelon Man (watermelon juice, mint syrup, lemon), Shinjuku Sweetheart (yuzu, soursop, honey), Echo Mist (chicory syrup, mulberry jam, soda, lemon), and Hi-Potion (lime, lemon, salt, mint), a like-for-like alcohol-free build of the bar's own gin-and-vodka cocktail of the same name. A Deschutes Kernza non-alcoholic lager is $7, and food runs vegetarian-leaning snacks and paninis. The list rotates seasonally.

Echo Mist (chicory syrup, mulberry jam, soda, lemon) $11

venues.longDescription:
Bokeh is a neighbourhood cocktail bar at 4716 N Kedzie Avenue in Albany Park, two blocks north of the Kedzie Brown Line stop, and it describes itself as craft cocktails and community in the heart of Albany Park. It opened in 2019, founded by a hospitality veteran and former professional photographer who built the room around a photography theme — bokeh being the name for the soft out-of-focus light behind a subject — and the result is a dim, warm, genuinely local bar rather than a destination one. Food is bar food done properly and priced accordingly: a house nut mix and marinated olives at $7, goat cheese spread, spinach artichoke dip and giardiniera hummus at $12, and a short list of paninis at $16 including an Italian, a roast beef, a turkey club and a vegetarian G.O.A.T., with a grilled cheese at $12. Much of the snack menu is marked vegetarian. It was nominated for Neighbourhood Bar of the Year in the Chicago Tribune's 2025 Readers' Choice food awards.

The non-alcoholic drinks have their own printed heading, "Alcohol-Free Cocktails", and all four are $11 — roughly $3 below the full-proof list rather than at parity. What distinguishes them is that they are built entirely from house syrups, jams and fresh juice rather than from bought-in zero-proof spirits; no Seedlip, Lyre's or Pathfinder appears anywhere on the menu. Watermelon Man combines watermelon juice with mint syrup and lemon. Shinjuku Sweetheart is the most interesting of them, pairing yuzu with soursop and honey. Echo Mist works a chicory syrup with mulberry jam, soda and lemon, which gives it a roasted bitterness closer to an amaro than to a fruit drink. Hi-Potion is a straight alcohol-free build of the bar's own gin-and-vodka cocktail of the same name, made with lime, lemon, salt and mint — a genuine like-for-like rather than a different drink with a shared name. Beyond the cocktails there is a Deschutes Kernza non-alcoholic lager at $7 and Five Corners salted lemonade and sangrita at $5. The menu rotates seasonally; this is the 2026 spring and summer list.

venues.name: Bolo
venues.description: Bolo is chef Yun Fuentes's Latin American dining room and rum bar in Rittenhouse Square, open since 2023 at 2025 Sansom Street. The bi-level, vividly colorful space draws on Puerto Rican, Cuban, and Dominican cuisine and is named for Fuentes's grandfather, Juan "Bolo" Fuentes; the chef was a 2024 James Beard Awards semifinalist for Best Emerging Chef. While the bar centers on a deep rum roster, beverage director Tony Jimenez — a PUNCH "Best New Bartenders 2024" finalist — builds a genuine spirit-free cocktail menu alongside it. Zero-proof options include the No Jito (Lyre's White Cane, lime, mint, soda), Punch It (Lyre's Dark Cane, mango, coconut, ginger beer), Hibiscus Lemonade (Lyre's Dry London, lemon, hibiscus), and an N/Amaro & Coke (Pathfinder NA Amaro, guarapo, cola). The non-alcoholic list rotates seasonally.

venues.longDescription:
Bolo is chef Yun Fuentes's Latin American dining room and rum bar at 2025 Sansom Street in Rittenhouse, open since 2023. The bi-level room is vividly coloured, the cooking draws on Puerto Rican, Cuban and Dominican traditions, and it is named for the chef's grandfather, Juan "Bolo" Fuentes. Fuentes was a 2024 James Beard Awards semifinalist for Best Emerging Chef.

The bar's identity is rum — a deep roster of it — which makes the spirit-free list more notable, not less. Beverage director Tony Jimenez, a finalist in PUNCH's Best New Bartenders 2024, builds a genuine non-alcoholic menu alongside the rum programme rather than leaving non-drinkers with a soda.

The approach is to rebuild the house's own classics rather than invent unrelated fruit drinks. The No Jito uses Lyre's White Cane — an alcohol-free spirit made specifically to stand in for white rum — with lime, mint and soda, which is a mojito in every respect except the ethanol. Punch It goes to Lyre's Dark Cane, the aged-rum analogue, for something with more molasses depth. Building the zero-proof list from rum substitutes, in a bar whose entire premise is rum, means a non-drinker is ordering from the same idea as everyone else at the table instead of from a parallel menu.

There is a good culinary reason this works. Caribbean and Latin American drinking runs heavily to acid, sugar and aromatics — lime, cane, mint, tropical fruit — and those are the elements that survive the removal of alcohol most intact. A mojito depends far more on the interaction of lime, sugar and bruised mint than on the rum, which is why the alcohol-free version is genuinely close to the original rather than a distant approximation.

Open Wednesday and Thursday from five to ten, Friday and Saturday until midnight, and Sunday from four; closed Monday and Tuesday.
venues.pressQuote: Chef Yun Fuentes' Latin American dining room and rum bar, nestled in bustling Rittenhouse Square
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Visit Philadelphia, A Guide to Zero-Proof Restaurants & Bars in Philly, January 2025

venues.name: Boneyard Beer
venues.description: Boneyard's original tasting room, in a converted auto shop just off downtown, keeps a CBD elixir on tap in two rotating flavours — light, crisp and not overly sweet, and pitched as the drink for when a full pint is too much after a day outdoors. Open Wednesday to Sunday, afternoons only.
venues.address: 37 NW Lake Pl B, Bend, OR 97701
venues.longDescription:
Boneyard started in a small building on NW Lake Place, assembled from second-hand equipment scavenged from other breweries — which is where the name comes from — and grew into one of Bend's best-known hop-forward producers. The original tasting room is still there, an unfussy space in a converted auto shop that the brewery itself brands as the Old Bend room.

Its contribution to the town's alcohol-free options is a CBD elixir served on tap, in two flavours that rotate. Having it on draught rather than in a can is the interesting part: it is poured like a beer, into a glass, at the bar, which preserves the ritual that non-drinkers most often lose. It is deliberately light and crisp rather than sweet, and the brewery pitches it at the specific moment when you have been out on a trail all day and a full pint feels like too much.

The plain flag, as with several Bend venues: this drink contains CBD. CBD does not produce the intoxication that alcohol or THC does, and it is legal and widely sold across Oregon, but it is an added active compound rather than a flavouring, and anyone avoiding all such substances should order something else. The tasting room pours plenty that is simply beer or simply soft drinks.

Hours are the thing to plan around here — this is an afternoon room, not an evening one. It is closed Monday and Tuesday entirely, runs noon to seven Wednesday through Saturday, and closes at five on Sunday. That makes it a stop on the way back from the mountain rather than a night out.
venues.pressQuote: its cbd elixir, on tap at the pub in two rotating flavors. it's light, crisp, and not overly sweet

venues.name: Bonfiyah Kava Lounge
venues.description: Bonfiyah Kava Lounge is a Polynesian kava lounge on the South Main Street corridor in South Salt Lake, and it is a genuinely nocturnal room: doors around 9pm and service to 5am on Wednesday through Friday, 3am at the weekend, with nothing alcoholic served at any point. Utah's liquor laws make most licensed bars close at 1am, so a room running to 5am without a licence occupies a slot in this city that essentially nothing else does. The lounge blends island ambience with a modern space and programmes live Polynesian music — the kava is affordable, available in to-go containers, and the draw is as much the shows and the company as the drink. Kava is a South Pacific root drink, alcohol-free but genuinely relaxing and mildly intoxicating in its own right, and it is served to adults. Hours shift with the events calendar, so check the lounge's social channels before travelling.
venues.address: 3410 S Main St, South Salt Lake, UT 84115
venues.hours: Mon-Tue closed; Wed 9:30pm-5am; Thu-Fri 9pm-5am; Sat 9pm-3am; Sun 9pm-3am
venues.longDescription:
Bonfiyah Kava Lounge sits on the South Main Street corridor in South Salt Lake and keeps hours that make it structurally important to this city rather than merely pleasant. Doors are around 9pm and it runs to 5am Wednesday through Friday and 3am on Saturday and Sunday nights, with no alcohol served at any hour. That schedule is worth dwelling on: Utah's liquor laws require licensed bars to stop service at 1am, which means that for the four hours afterwards there is essentially nowhere in the Salt Lake Valley to sit with other people and a drink in your hand — unless the drink is not alcohol. A kava lounge running to 5am fills a gap that regulation created, and it does so for a crowd that includes both people who have finished a shift and people who do not drink at all.

The room itself is a Polynesian lounge, blending island ambience with a modern space, and it leans on live entertainment — Polynesian music shows are a regular fixture, with named performers booked in. Reviewers consistently mention the service, the shows, and that the kava is affordable and available in to-go containers if you would rather take it away. The Salt Lake kava scene is small enough that a survey of it in August 2026 could name only a handful of rooms; this is one of the two that matter, alongside the Kai Po lounge a couple of miles north. Kava deserves a plain description for an audience that includes people in recovery: it is made from the ground root of a South Pacific shrub steeped in water, has been drunk socially across the Pacific for around three thousand years, and contains no alcohol whatsoever — but it is a genuine relaxant and mildly intoxicating on its own terms, which is a real distinction if you are avoiding intoxicants generally rather than alcohol specifically. One practical caveat: this lounge changes its hours around its events calendar more than most, so check its social channels the day you plan to go rather than relying on a listing.

venues.name: Bonifacio
venues.description: Bonifacio is a modern Filipino restaurant on King Avenue in Fifth by Northwest, founded in 2016 by Krizzia Yanga, a Columbus native who had earlier introduced the city to Filipino cooking through her Red Velvet Café and who was named a Columbus Monthly Tastemaker in 2021. The restaurant is best known for its Boodle Nights, communal kamayan feasts eaten by hand from banana leaves piled with sticky rice, longganisa, lumpia, pickled vegetables and shrimp. The drinks list is written to match those flavours rather than to sit apart from them, and the non-alcoholic side draws on the same pantry: the Ube Colada is built from ube simple syrup with lime, pineapple and coconut cream, using the purple yam that runs through Filipino desserts. Open Tuesday to Sunday, with weekend service from 10am.
signatureDrinks: Ube Colada (ube simple syrup, lime, pineapple, coconut cream)
venues.longDescription:
Bonifacio opened in 2016 at 1577 King Avenue in the Fifth by Northwest neighbourhood, west of the Olentangy and south of Ohio State, and is the work of Krizzia Yanga — a Columbus native who first brought Filipino food to the city through her earlier Red Velvet Café before committing to a full-service restaurant. The name is a reference to Andrés Bonifacio, the revolutionary; the cooking is what Yanga calls modern Filipino, which means the adobo, sisig and lumpia are recognisable but the plating and the produce are contemporary and local. Columbus Monthly named her a Tastemaker in 2021, and the restaurant has since drawn national recognition and grant support for Asian-American-owned businesses.

The format the restaurant is best known for is the Boodle Night: a kamayan feast in which the table is covered in banana leaves and heaped with sticky rice, pickled vegetables, longganisa sausage, lumpia and shrimp, and everyone eats with their hands. It is communal, loud and unusually good for a group that includes people who are not drinking, because the meal itself rather than the round of drinks is the event. The bar supports that with a list written to match the kitchen's flavours — fresh juices, tropical fruit and the Filipino pantry — instead of a separate cocktail programme bolted alongside. On the alcohol-free side the drink to know is the Ube Colada, built from ube simple syrup with lime, pineapple and coconut cream. Ube is the purple yam that anchors Filipino desserts, sweet and faintly nutty, and using it as the base of a piña colada variant produces something that is genuinely of the cuisine rather than a generic mocktail with a local label. CityScene named the restaurant in its December 2025 alcohol-free roundup on that basis. Weekend service starts at 10am.
venues.pressQuote: Known for its authentic Filipino cuisine, Bonifacio complements its bold, comforting dishes with a drink menu crafted to match the restaurant's vibrant flavors.

venues.name: Boone & Crockett
venues.description: Boone & Crockett is a riverside cocktail bar in Milwaukee's Harbor District that trades on the motto "Pretentious Drinks Without the Pretentiousness." It backs up its cocktail reputation with a genuine, separately published non-alcoholic menu of five named mocktails plus a stocked zero-proof bar (Giffard NA aperitif, Lagunitas Hop Refresher, Athletic Lite and Guinness N/A). The bar runs on an order-at-the-bar model with the on-site Taco Moto truck for food and shares its address with sister event venue The Cooperage. Each Dry January it anchors Milwaukee's sober-curious scene by hosting the free after-party for N/A Day, the non-alcoholic beverage festival held next door.
venues.longDescription:
Boone & Crockett is a cocktail bar on the west bank of the Milwaukee River in the Harbor District, operating under the tongue-in-cheek motto "Pretentious Drinks Without the Pretentiousness." It runs on a no-table-service model — guests order craft cocktails at the bar and food from the on-site Taco Moto truck — and shares its 818 S. Water St. address with its sister event venue, The Cooperage, with the Hoan Bridge as a backdrop.

What earns it a place in a non-alcoholic directory is a real, standing zero-proof program rather than an afterthought. Boone & Crockett publishes a dedicated mocktail menu of five named drinks: Backseat Bingo (grapefruit, lime, cane syrup and club soda), Cardinal Punch (muddled mint, cherry, lemon and cranberry), Stranger Danger (pineapple, orange and Top Note ginger beer), The Orange Care Bear, and the High N' Dry, which builds a spirit-free aperitivo from Giffard Non-Alcoholic Aperitif and Lagunitas Hop Refresher. Behind that sits a stocked NA bar including Guinness N/A, Athletic Lite and an Untitled Art sour, giving alcohol-free guests real range beyond a single token option.

The bar is also a fixture of Milwaukee's sober-curious calendar. Each Dry January it hosts the free after-party for N/A Day, the non-alcoholic beverage festival held next door at The Cooperage; the fifth annual edition ran on Jan. 3, 2026. The venue remains clearly active into mid-2026, with posted hours of Wednesday–Thursday 4 p.m.–2 a.m. and Friday–Sunday 3 p.m.–2 a.m., and local tourism coverage has singled it out for its "whimsically titled non-alcoholic cocktails."
venues.pressQuote: Boone and Crockett offers whimsically titled non-alcoholic cocktails, including the Backseat Bingo and the Stranger Danger.

venues.name: Border Brewing Company
venues.description: Border Brewing Company is the original brewery and taproom in Kansas City's Crossroads Arts District, founded by owner and lead brewer Eric Martens, who opened the business after a career as a chemical and process engineer. Open since 2015, it pours a rotating lineup of house-brewed beer, cider, seltzer, and cocktails. In December 2024 the brewery launched Baseline, billed as Kansas City's first locally-owned craft non-alcoholic beer series, brewed in-house to the same standards as its flagship beers. The series debuted in two styles — Baseline Amber, a malt-forward beer with toasty caramel character, and Baseline Pale, a citrus-forward hoppy style — both under 0.5% ABV. The Baseline beers are available on tap at the Crossroads taproom and in to-go four-packs and crowlers. Because the NA beer is house-brewed rather than a stocked national brand, it is a genuine local zero-proof program.
venues.longDescription:
Border Brewing Company opened in 2015 at 512 E 18th Street, on the corner of 18th and Locust in the Crossroads, and founder Eric Martens is refreshingly unromantic about why: he built Border, he says, so he would have a place to drink with his neighbours. Ten years in, he still walks in some Saturdays and recognises half the patio, and calls that the only metric he actually cares about. A chemical engineer by training, he treats every recipe like a problem worth solving twice — which is the relevant detail here, because in December 2024 Border became the first locally owned Kansas City brewery to produce its own non-alcoholic beer. Startland News covered the launch, and Martens was direct about the difficulty: creating a non-alcoholic beer, he said, is no small feat, requiring precision, innovation and an in-depth understanding of brewing processes, regulations and testing. The brewery spent a year getting it right.

That line is called Baseline, and it runs to two beers, both under 0.5% ABV and both pouring year-round at the Crossroads taproom rather than appearing seasonally. Baseline Amber is the fuller of the two, built on rich caramel malt with a smooth backbone and subtle toasty notes. Baseline Pale Ale is hop-forward, carrying grapefruit and tropical fruit. Both are also packaged into 12oz six-packs to take home, and the distribution is real rather than notional — Baseline is poured at other Kansas City venues including KC Bier Co.'s Waldo bierhalle and Cliff's Taphouse in Martini Corner, which is a meaningful signal that other operators rate it enough to put a competitor's can on their own menu. For a non-drinker that makes Border one of the very few taprooms in the city where the non-alcoholic option is not an imported can from a national brand but something brewed in the same building as everything else on the board. The taproom opens at 4pm Monday to Thursday and from noon at weekends, with a patio the brewery calls The Backyard.
venues.pressQuote: Creating a non-alcoholic beer is no small feat — it requires precision, innovation, and an in-depth understanding of brewing processes, regulations, and testing.

venues.name: Bormio
venues.description: Tucked into the lower level of Noto in St. Peters, Bormio channels the Alpine crest — Northern Italy, Switzerland, Austria and beyond — into hearty mountain cooking and one of the St. Louis metro's most serious zero-proof programs. The bar prints a dedicated non-alcoholic menu headlined 'Clear views.': five $13 signature mocktails built on craft NA spirits, from the Ash & Fig (Cut Above zero-proof mezcal, caramelized fig, lime) to a pine-laced Mountain Forager and an NA Espressotini made with Lyre's Amaretti. Best Day Brewing's hazy IPA, Weihenstephaner's NA weissbier and alcohol-removed Mionetto prosecco round out the list. Feast Magazine named the concept — then called Bacaro — its Best New Restaurant of 2024.
venues.address: 5105 Westwood Drive, Suite A, St. Peters, MO 63304

naMenuItems.name: Pom At Altitude
naMenuItems.description: dhos orange essence na, pomegranate, lime, pine simple

naMenuItems.name: Ash & Fig
naMenuItems.description: cut above mezcal na, caramelized fig syrup, lime

venues.longDescription:
Bormio began life in early 2024 as Bacaro, a Venetian cicchetti bar that Wayne and Kendele Sieve opened in the lower level of Noto, their acclaimed Italian restaurant in St. Peters. When a trademark conflict forced a rename that December, the Sieves went further than a new sign: they rebuilt the concept around Bormio, a town in the Italian Alps, and by spring 2025 had rolled out a full menu of Alpine Crest cooking drawing on Northern Italian, Swiss, Austrian, Slovenian and German traditions. Feast Magazine had already crowned the room its Best New Restaurant of 2024 under the old name.

The zero-proof program is printed as its own menu — a section of the house 'drink map' headlined 'Clear views.' — and it goes far beyond token lemonade. Five signature mocktails ($13) lean on craft NA spirits: Pom at Altitude (Dhos Orange Essence, pomegranate, lime, pine simple), Ash & Fig (Cut Above zero-proof mezcal, caramelized fig syrup, lime), Vitality (Little Saints with lion's mane, beet, citrus and orgeat), the Mountain Forager (Saint Heck sumac and Feragaia herbal NA spirits with pine and apple) and an NA Espressotini built on Saint Heck Wierenga, Lyre's Amaretti and cold-brew espresso. Bottles and cans add Weihenstephaner's non-alcoholic hefeweissbier, Best Day Brewing's Hazy IPA and a 200mL alcohol-removed Mionetto prosecco. The restaurant credits its bartender Megan with the list, promising mocktails get the same care as the classic cocktails; past seasonal rotations have poured Seedlip Spice 94 hot toddies and a pine-tea Alpine Elixir.

Critics tracked the transformation closely. The St. Louis Post-Dispatch's February 2025 review ran under the headline 'Noto Italian Restaurant triumphs again with Alpine-inspired Bormio in St. Peters,' Sauce Magazine spotlighted its mini sourdough waffles with caviar, and Feast's April 2025 first look described meticulously crafted cocktails and mocktails threaded with spruce, rosemary, elderflower and berries — with a wave of new diners treating the room like a multicourse dinner destination. Hours run in miniature, Wednesday through Saturday evenings only, out in St. Charles County — worth the drive from the city, with Noto waiting upstairs and a nightcap that needs no alcohol: fig, sumac, pine and espresso, mapped like a ridgeline across the NA list.
venues.pressQuote: The couple has been gravitating towards drinks with savory elements recently, Wayne says; that interest shows up in meticulously crafted cocktails and mocktails with Alpine elements like spruce, rosemary, elderflower and berries.

venues.name: Boston Bottle
venues.description: Boston Bottle is a craft beer, wine and spirits shop on Commercial Street at the harbour edge of the North End, open to 10pm most nights and 11pm on Fridays and Saturdays. It is an alcohol-forward retailer rather than an alcohol-free one, but its non-alcoholic range is organised as a proper department rather than a single shelf: the shop's own catalogue breaks non-alcoholic stock into beer by style, including pilsner, IPA, sour, dark and cider; wine by colour, including red, white, rose and sparkling; and spirits by category, including gin, whiskey, tequila and mezcal, rum and vodka. Non-alcoholic aperitifs, digestifs and vermouths and ready-to-drink zero-proof cocktails sit alongside them, plus bitters, syrups, mixers and bar tools for building at home.
venues.longDescription:
Boston Bottle sits at 372 Commercial Street on the waterfront side of the North End, close to the Charlestown Bridge and the harbour walk, and trades as a full-line craft beer, fine wine and spirits shop. It is included here for the same reason a good general bottle shop earns a place in any city: the range of non-alcoholic products it stocks is deep enough that a reader can furnish a whole evening from it, and the store treats that range as a category with its own navigation rather than an afterthought squeezed between the seltzer and the mixers.

The non-alcoholic section is broken down the way the alcoholic one is. Beer is sorted by style, with non-alcoholic pilsners, IPAs, sours, dark beers and ciders listed separately. Wine is sorted by colour, with dealcoholised red, white, rose and sparkling. Spirits are sorted by base, covering non-alcoholic gin, whiskey, tequila and mezcal, rum and vodka, and there is a separate line of non-alcoholic aperitifs, digestifs and vermouths, which is the part most general bottle shops skip and the part that actually makes a zero-proof cocktail taste like a cocktail. Ready-to-drink zero-proof cocktails, kombucha and functional drinks, craft sodas, sparkling water, wellness shots and juices fill out the fridge, and the shop also carries bitters, syrups, mixers and bar tools. The hours help: 10am to 10pm Monday through Thursday and Sunday, and to 11pm on Friday and Saturday, which is later than the dedicated non-alcoholic bottle shops in the metro keep. Anyone who wants a specialist, alcohol-free-only shop should go to Dray in the South End or Central Square instead; this is the generalist option, and it is the one open latest. One caveat worth stating: this is retail, not a bar, so the listing is for stocking an evening in rather than going out. Anyone who wants a specialist shop where every product on the shelf is alcohol-free will be better served by the two Dray stores, but Boston Bottle is open later and covers the North End and the waterfront.

venues.name: Botanica
venues.description: Botanica is a seasonal Southern California restaurant and natural-wine market at 1620 Silver Lake Boulevard, opened in May 2017 by former food writers Emily Fiffer and Heather Sperling as a home for what they call nourishing hospitality, with a focus on regenerative agriculture, sustainable seafood and responsible animal husbandry. UPDATE TO OUR EARLIER LISTING: we previously had no drinks on file and rated the non-alcoholic offering as minimal. It now runs a genuine printed "Zero Proof" section on both the dinner and brunch menus, seven or more deep, so we have raised the rating. At dinner: a blueberry yuzu shrub ($10), a cucumber, lemon and ginger spritzer ($12), a yuzu spritzer ($10), a Ghia spritzer ($15), Lovely Bunch apple juice ($8), Strange Water sparkling coconut water ($8) and Fermensch kombucha ($9). Brunch adds a sunrise juice of orange, grapefruit, lime, lemon, yuzu and ginger ($8) and a "little tomato", the house non-alcoholic bloody mary ($10). Beverage director Pierluc Dallaire also runs a low-intervention wine programme. Open Wednesday to Sunday, 9am to 10pm.
venues.address: 1620 Silver Lake Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90026
signatureDrinks: Little tomato, NA bloody mary ($10, brunch)

naMenuItems.name: Little Tomato
naMenuItems.description: our n/a bloody mary

venues.longDescription:
Botanica opened in May 2017 on Silver Lake Boulevard, founded by Emily Fiffer and Heather Sperling — both former food and lifestyle writers — as what they describe as a destination for nourishing hospitality. It works as a restaurant and a market at once, and the cooking is seasonal Southern Californian built around the products of regenerative agriculture, sustainable seafood and responsible animal husbandry. The dinner menu runs a bistro burger at $24, steak au poivre at $45, California steelhead trout at $38, braised pork cheeks at $28 and a tomato tonnato panzanella at $19. It opens Wednesday to Sunday from 9am, with coffee until four, brunch from ten, happy hour from three, and dinner until nine.

This entry has been upgraded, because our earlier assessment was out of date. We previously had no drinks on file for Botanica and rated its non-alcoholic offering as minimal. The current menus — both dated this summer — carry a printed section headed Zero Proof on the dinner card and again at brunch, and it is a proper list rather than a token line. At dinner there are seven: a blueberry yuzu shrub at $10, a cucumber, lemon and ginger spritzer at $12, a yuzu spritzer at $10, a Ghia spritzer at $15 built on the Los Angeles-made non-alcoholic aperitif, Lovely Bunch apple juice at $8, Strange Water sparkling coconut water at $8 and Fermensch kombucha at $9. Brunch keeps all of those and adds two more: a sunrise juice of orange, grapefruit, lime, lemon, yuzu and ginger at $8, and the little tomato, which is the house non-alcoholic bloody mary, at $10. The shape of that list tells you what kind of place this is — shrubs, spritzers and small-producer bottles rather than non-alcoholic spirits imitating cocktails, which fits a restaurant whose wine programme, run by beverage director Pierluc Dallaire, has been built on low-intervention producers since it opened. It is not the deepest zero-proof list in Los Angeles, but it is real, current, priced fairly and made from the same ingredients as the kitchen.
venues.pressQuote: Health-conscious, airy and bright (but with a tad bit of grunge), this all-day eatery is essentially Silver Lake incarnate.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Patricia Kelly Yeo, Time Out Los Angeles

venues.name: Botanika
venues.description: Salt Lake City's first all-non-alcoholic bottle shop and gourmet grocer, a woman-owned spot founded by Kate Riser that opened in May 2025 in the historic Artspace Rubber Company building on 200 South. Riser, who spent years in food and beverage across San Francisco, New York and nearly a decade in Europe, built it out with concrete floors, white walls and custom display cases. The shelves run deep on zero-proof spirits, wine, aperitifs, mixers and canned cocktails — roughly 300 products from about 50 mostly small, independent and minority-owned makers, including brands like The Pathfinder Hemp & Root and Aplós — alongside gourmet pantry goods. A small lounge lets visitors open an alcohol-free wine, sip a canned botanical cocktail and linger, making it a sober "third place" for the sober and sober-curious.
venues.address: 353 W 200 S Ste 100A, Salt Lake City, UT 84101

Prima Pavé - Rosé Brut Mini Bottle

venues.longDescription:
Founder Kate Riser describes Botanika as filling a gap in Salt Lake City's sober scene — a place to stock up on better-for-you drinks and provisions without a full grocery-store trip, and where the sober, the sober-curious and people who aren't sober at all are all welcome. Beyond retail, it serves as a community gathering space hosting workshops, tastings and cultural events, and as a small woman-owned business commits to supporting minority-owned and mission-driven brands.

The retail mix spans non-alcoholic spirits, wines, ready-to-drink mocktails and beers plus tinned fish, artisan pastas, single-origin coffees and teas, plant-based milks and specialty pantry items, with local delivery and pickup, curated subscription boxes, and free shipping over $60.
venues.pressQuote: I see Botanika as a love letter to the city.

venues.name: Bottiglia Cucina & Enoteca
venues.description: Bottiglia Cucina & Enoteca is an upscale rustic-Italian restaurant inside the Green Valley Ranch Resort in Henderson, serving Napa/Sonoma, Italian, and French wines alongside seasonal pasta and seafood. Its non-alcoholic side is a defined "Zero Proof Libations" menu ($13–$15 per drink) of crafted, mixology-style mocktails rather than token sodas. The list runs four drinks across the dinner, lunch and brunch menus: the Fiori Nero (Fever-Tree Sicilian lemon soda, hibiscus syrup, mint), the Amore Giardino (Fever-Tree cucumber tonic, mint, basil, lemon, orgeat), the Whata Peach (white peach purée, rosemary, lemon-lime soda), and the Grazi 75, built on Almave non-alcoholic blue agave spirit with agave nectar, lemon and seltzer; earlier seasonal options such as Pomelo Paradise, Lavender Lemonade and a non-alcoholic Milano Mule have rotated off, and Michelob Ultra Zero sits on the beer list. The kitchen leans into the zero-proof category for Dry January, framing the drinks as a way to enjoy the meal without sacrificing sophistication for guests skipping alcohol. The program is supported by the restaurant's own marketing and menus, making it a reliable upscale option for a non-alcoholic night out in Henderson.

Amore Giardino (Fever-Tree cucumber tonic, mint, basil, lemon, orgeat)

venues.longDescription:
Bottiglia Cucina & Enoteca is a rustic Italian restaurant inside Green Valley Ranch Resort in Henderson, roughly fifteen miles southeast of the Strip, which makes it a locals' restaurant far more than a tourist one. The kitchen is Tuscan-inspired and seasonal — antipasti, salads, whole fresh fish, house-made pappardelle bolognese — and the enoteca half of the name is meant literally, with a wine list running through Napa, Sonoma, Italy and France. It serves dinner nightly and brunch at the weekend, and locally it has settled into the role of Henderson's default Italian restaurant for an occasion.

What lifts it into this directory is a defined Zero Proof Libations menu, priced between $13 and $15, which appears across the dinner, lunch and brunch menus rather than only at dinner. Four drinks make up the current list: the Fiori Nero (Fever-Tree Sicilian lemon soda, hibiscus syrup and mint), the Amore Giardino (Fever-Tree cucumber tonic, mint, basil, lemon and orgeat), the Whata Peach (white peach puree, rosemary and lemon-lime soda), and the Grazi 75, which is built on Almave non-alcoholic blue agave spirit with agave nectar, lemon and seltzer. Earlier seasonal builds — Pomelo Paradise, Lavender Lemonade and a non-alcoholic Milano Mule — have rotated off, which is itself a useful signal: a rotating zero-proof list is a maintained one. Michelob Ultra Zero sits on the beer list for anyone who would rather have a beer with dinner. The restaurant leans into the category around Dry January, and frames the drinks in its own marketing as a way to keep the sophistication of the meal intact for a guest who is skipping alcohol, which is a fair description of what the list actually delivers at an upscale table in Henderson.
venues.pressQuote: Even if you prefer to skip the alcohol, Bottiglia's mocktails and refreshments ensure that you don't miss out on the burst of flavors.

venues.name: Bottlehouse
venues.description: Bottlehouse is a wine bar in a restored 1910 house at 1416 34th Ave in Madrona, with a front porch, a bar, a back garden and a patio, and a motto printed on every menu: "dwell, drink, be well." CORRECTION TO OUR EARLIER LISTING: we previously said its non-alcoholic offering included non-alcoholic wine and a persimmon-vanilla soda. Neither appears on any of its recent printed menus, and what we described as a house thyme iced tea is actually a house strawberry-thyme soda. The current non-alcoholic section, headed simply "Non-Alcoholic", holds a house cocktail — Root Ritual at $14, made with Pathfinder, lemon, blackberry and salt — alongside a bottled St. Agrestis Phony Negroni at $9, house sodas and lemonade at $8, Rachel's Ginger Beer at $7, Seattle Soda Co. cola at $6, Saint Aniol sparkling water at $5, a non-alcoholic Fremont IPA or stout at $6, and a loose-leaf tea list from Apolis at $5. The list changes with the seasons — an earlier house cocktail was built on Wilderton — so treat the cocktail name as time-sensitive. Food is seasonal small plates.
venues.longDescription:
Bottlehouse occupies a restored house from 1910 on 34th Avenue in Madrona, and the building does most of the work: a front porch, rooms rather than a dining room, a bar, and a back garden that is the reason to come in summer. Its motto is printed on every menu it publishes — dwell, drink, be well — and it is an accurate description of the pace. This is a wine bar built for staying put. The food is seasonal small plates: a house salad at $16, grilled local asparagus at $18, seasonal burrata at $18, a kale and white bean risotto at $23, house mac and cheese at $16, a petite steak at $32, and a tahini chocolate blondie at $9. Happy hour runs daily in the late afternoon.

We owe a correction here, because our earlier entry for this bar was wrong in two places. We said the non-alcoholic offering extended to non-alcoholic wine, and we listed a persimmon-vanilla soda. Neither appears on any of the printed menus we could check across the past two years, and the drink we described as a house thyme iced tea is in fact a house strawberry-thyme soda. What is genuinely there is a section headed simply Non-Alcoholic, and its shape is worth knowing. There is one house zero-proof cocktail at a time — currently Root Ritual at $14, built on Pathfinder with lemon, blackberry and salt, the salt doing the job that makes a fruit drink taste like a cocktail rather than a squash. Next to it sits a bottled St. Agrestis Phony Negroni at $9, which is the cheapest way in Seattle to have a proper bitter aperitif without alcohol. Then house sodas and lemonade at $8, Rachel's Ginger Beer at $7, a Seattle Soda Co. cola at $6, Saint Aniol sparkling water at $5, a non-alcoholic Fremont IPA or stout at $6, and a genuinely considered loose-leaf tea list from Apolis at $5 — genmaicha, vanilla chai, ceylon-darjeeling, ginger lemon and a tranquility herbal blend. The house cocktail rotates seasonally, so expect the name to have moved on; the section will not have.
venues.pressQuote: You never have that problem at Bottlehouse ... you have options.

venues.name: Bottoms Up Mocktails
venues.description: A fully alcohol-free mobile mocktail bar founded in 2020 by Annali and Cameron Walker, who started the company after failing to find a "high-class soda bar" for their own wedding reception. Every drink is zero-proof — the founders describe mocktails as "mock cocktails" where all the options have 0% alcohol — built into custom, color-matched menus and served from portable bars, with options like a blackberry-jalapeño-salt mocktail, peach-strawberry, and grapefruit-mango. Based in the Lehi/Riverton area, it caters weddings, corporate functions and private events across the Salt Lake metro, and has been featured on KUTV and in Voyage Utah.
venues.hours: Mobile / by booking — events across the Salt Lake metro
venues.longDescription:
Bottoms Up Mocktails is 100% non-alcoholic by design: the founders, Annali and Cameron Walker, started the company in 2020 after their own wedding, when they couldn't find a polished alcohol-free drink service. They build custom, color-matched menus of handcrafted zero-proof drinks served from portable 7-foot bars.

Based in the Lehi/Riverton area of the Salt Lake metro, the company caters weddings, corporate functions and private events throughout Utah, traveling free within 40 miles, with no minimum headcount. It has been featured on local TV (KUTV) and in Voyage Utah, making its NA program genuinely documented rather than incidental.
venues.pressQuote: While planning our wedding, I wanted a high-class soda bar at our reception. As I searched, I only found soda bars serving simple flavored sodas on plastic tables stacked with ugly Torani bottles and plastic cups. I decided that I would create the bar I was searching for.

venues.name: Boulevard Brewing Co.
venues.description: Boulevard Brewing Co. is Missouri's largest craft brewery and the largest specialty brewer in the Midwest, founded by John McDonald along Kansas City's historic Southwest Boulevard, where the first beer was brewed in the autumn of 1989. It has been part of the Duvel Moortgat family since 2014 and took Brewery of the Year at the inaugural Missouri Beer Cup in 2025 with nine awards. It brews four distinct non-alcoholic products, a wider range than almost any brewery in the country manages: Flying Start, a non-alcoholic IPA at 0.5% ABV and a substantial 50 IBU; Space Camper, a second and entirely separate non-alcoholic IPA at 0.5% and 30 IBU, brighter and more tropical; a Non-Alcoholic Wheat with Lemon at 0.5% and 10 IBU; and Quirk's non-alcoholic superfruit seltzer, built on yellow papaya and acai berry juices at 25 calories. All are poured at the Beer Hall at 2534 Madison Avenue, a 10,000 square foot room with thirty rotating taps that is card-only, no cash.
venues.address: 2534 Madison Ave, 2nd Floor, Kansas City, MO 64108
signatureDrinks: Non-Alcoholic Wheat with Lemon (0.5% ABV, 10 IBU)
Quirk Non-Alcoholic Superfruit Seltzer, papaya and acai berry (0.5% ABV, 25 cals)
venues.longDescription:
Boulevard Brewing Co. is the largest specialty brewer in the Midwest, founded in 1989 by John McDonald, a carpenter with a shop on Southwest Boulevard who had come back from a holiday in France taken with European brewing tradition. He converted a historic railroad building into a small brewery and delivered the first keg of Boulevard Pale Ale to a restaurant a mile down the road on 17 November that year. His pitch to sceptics has aged well: I want to do something different, he would say — big beers, a variety of beers, beers with colour and flavour and aroma and body, beers for real beer lovers. The brewery joined the Duvel Moortgat family in 2014 and took Brewery of the Year at the inaugural Missouri Beer Cup in 2025 with nine awards. The public face is the Beer Hall at 2534 Madison Avenue, a 10,000 square foot room with thirty rotating taps, open from 10am on Sundays and 11am the rest of the week. It is card only — no cash is accepted.

What makes Boulevard genuinely useful to a non-drinker is range, because most breweries manage one non-alcoholic beer if any and Boulevard brews four distinct products. Flying Start is the flagship non-alcoholic IPA at 0.5% and a substantial 50 IBU, and the brewery makes the argument directly: there is no reason to sacrifice hop flavour and aroma when choosing a non-alcoholic beer, and you might just trade your NEIPA for their NAIPA. Space Camper is a second, separate non-alcoholic IPA at 0.5% and 30 IBU, brighter and more tropical — worth knowing about, since having two different non-alcoholic IPAs to choose between is close to unheard of at any brewery. The Non-Alcoholic Wheat with Lemon is a zero-proof take on the Midwest's favourite craft beer at 0.5% and 10 IBU. Quirk's non-alcoholic superfruit seltzer covers the non-beer option at 25 calories, built on yellow papaya and acai berry juices. All are poured at the Beer Hall alongside the full taps.

venues.name: Boulon Brasserie & Bakery
venues.description: Boulon Brasserie & Bakery is a French brasserie on Tampa's Water Street, open from morning pastries through late dinner. Its bar builds alcohol-free cocktails on Ritual Zero Proof spirits — the French Caribbean Spritz (Ritual gin, house grenadine, passion fruit, cranberry, lemon, blood orange, ginger beer) and the Next Level Root Beer (Ritual rum root-beer syrup, grapefruit, lemon, ginger beer) — so the spirit-free options read like the rest of the list rather than an afterthought.  Open from 7am daily and to 1am at weekends, it is one of very few rooms in the city serving a properly made drink at both ends of the day.
signatureDrinks: French Caribbean Spritz (Ritual gin, house grenadine, passion fruit, cranberry, lemon, blood orange, ginger beer)
Next Level Root Beer (Ritual rum root-beer syrup, grapefruit, lemon, ginger beer)
venues.longDescription:
Boulon Brasserie & Bakery sits on Water Street, the master-planned district that has reshaped downtown Tampa's waterfront over the past few years. It works as a French brasserie in the full-day sense: pastries and coffee from 7am, lunch, dinner, and a bar that runs to 1am on Friday and Saturday. That span is unusual and useful — very few rooms in the city serve a proper made drink at eight in the morning and again at midnight.

The alcohol-free cocktails are built on Ritual Zero Proof spirits and constructed with the same number of moving parts as the full-strength list, which is the point. The French Caribbean Spritz layers Ritual's gin alternative with house grenadine, passion fruit, cranberry, lemon, blood orange and ginger beer — seven components, which is more than most bars put into a drink with alcohol in it. The Next Level Root Beer takes Ritual's rum alternative into a root-beer syrup with grapefruit, lemon and ginger beer, and lands somewhere between a soda and a long drink without being childish about it.

Water Street is corporate territory — hotels, offices, the arena — which shapes who uses the room and why the alcohol-free list matters. A business dinner, a pre-game meal, an early breakfast meeting: these are all situations where somebody is not drinking for reasons that have nothing to do with recovery, and where being handed a soda is a small professional indignity. A printed spritz solves that.

Practical notes: it opens at 7am daily and runs late at weekends, the bakery counter operates separately from the restaurant, and the district gets busy around events at Amalie Arena. Full brasserie bar and wine list — the Ritual builds are a real section of the menu rather than the identity of the place.
venues.pressQuote: Boulon Brasserie and Bakery is one of the best additions to Downtown Tampa
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: WiLD 94.1, 9 Tasty Mocktails in the Tampa Bay Area, January 2026

venues.name: Bowen House
venues.description: Bowen House is a craft cocktail bar and restaurant set inside Uptown Dallas's oldest surviving home, a folk-Victorian structure built in 1874, offering an intimate speakeasy atmosphere alongside an evolving menu of classic and bespoke drinks.
venues.longDescription:
Tucked inside a 19th-century wood-paneled house on Boll Street in Uptown Dallas, Bowen House is one of the few cocktail bars in North Texas where sober-curious visitors can feel genuinely looked after rather than accommodated as an afterthought. The bar's standing mocktail menu includes a cucumber gimlet that has surfaced repeatedly in guest reviews as a standout zero-proof option — built on fresh cucumber and citrus in the spirit of the classic gimlet format — giving non-drinkers a real reason to come rather than a token concession. The setting itself — candles, chandeliers, dim wood-toned rooms — does the rest of the work before a single drink is poured.

On the alcoholic side, the Laurel Canyon Spritz (lemony and elderflower-bright, a close cousin of the Aperol variant) and the passionfruit-forward Power Hour have become regulars on the ordering circuit, while the back bar's reputation for bespoke, made-to-preference builds means the menu is really a starting point. Owner Pasha Heidari opened the space in 2014 with a pre-Prohibition focus that still anchors the program — think Sazeracs, Ward 8s, and bourbon smashes alongside the seasonal specials. No named beverage director has been publicly documented in press coverage.

Bowen House earns its reputation as one of the better date-night destinations in Uptown precisely because it refuses to feel like an Uptown bar: no TVs, no DJ, no velvet rope energy. The rooms are small and tend to fill up by 7 pm on weeknights, so reservations (made by phone after noon, per their Instagram) are strongly recommended. Dress code is casual but the vibe skews smart-casual — it's the kind of place where a blazer fits without feeling overdressed. Walk-ins are welcome but may end up standing. Patio seating is available for good-weather nights, and happy hour runs daily from 4–6 pm.
venues.pressQuote: In the Victorian-era landmark Ahab-Bowen House, you can brush with a bit of local history while you kick back a few cold cocktails.

venues.name: Bowood by Niche
venues.description: Tucked inside the Bowood Farms garden shop in the Central West End, Bowood by Niche is the greenhouse café from Gerard Craft's James Beard Award-winning Niche Food Group. Plants fill the light-drenched dining room and patio, and the daytime drink list treats zero-proof as a first-class citizen: a dedicated menu section of five $10 NA cocktails — from the NA Blackberry 57 with NA gin and NA sparkling to an espresso-honey NA Cafe Martini — plus Best Day Brewing's kölsch or West Coast IPA and an NA version of 4 Hands City Wide. Open daily 8am to 2pm for brunch and lunch, it's one of St. Louis's most reliable spots for a booze-free morning out.
venues.longDescription:
Bowood by Niche opened on November 4, 2021, when Gerard Craft's Niche Food Group took over the much-loved former Café Osage space inside Bowood Farms, the Central West End garden shop on Olive Street. Craft — winner of the 2015 James Beard Award for Best Chef: Midwest — turned the plant-filled corner of the nursery into a daytime café built on local ingredients, with a greenhouse-style dining room and leafy patio that quickly became one of the neighborhood's signature gathering places.

The beverage menu gives non-drinkers a dedicated zero proof section rather than an afterthought. Five NA cocktails, each $10, mirror the house list: the NA Blackberry 57 (NA gin, blackberry, lemon, NA sparkling) is the alcohol-free answer to the bar's Blackberry 75, joined by an NA Cucumber Gimlet (NA gin, lime, cucumber), an NA Cranberry Margarita (NA tequila, cranberry, lime, sugar), an NA Cafe Martini (NA tequila, espresso, honey), and an NA Bloody Mary. The NA beer picks are just as deliberate: Best Day Brewing's kölsch-style or West Coast IPA from California pours alongside the NA version of hometown favorite 4 Hands City Wide. Melinda Cooper, Niche Food Group's beverage and bar director, curates the non-alcoholic offerings across the group's restaurants, and it shows in how seamlessly the zero-proof list sits beside the mimosas and espresso martinis.

St. Louis Magazine featured Bowood in its January 2025 guide to non-alcoholic cocktails in the city, pointing readers to its 'hefty selection of boozeless beverages' — a lineup that has since grown from a trio of zero-proof cocktails to five. Expect a brunch-hour crowd: the café runs daily from 8am to 2pm, with a morning happy hour Monday through Thursday from 8 to 10am, and the combination of seasonal brunch plates, pastries, and greenhouse light keeps tables busy on weekends. Settle into the garden-shop greenery with an alcohol-free Blackberry 57 in hand — it's daytime drinking, minus the alcohol, done unusually well.
venues.pressQuote: At Bowood, guests can choose from a hefty selection of boozeless beverages, including a trio of cocktails made with BARE zero-proof.

venues.name: Box St. All Day
venues.description: Box St. All Day is a brunch and daytime spot in Hemisfair, the park development beside the Tower of the Americas, and it keeps a named Zero Proof section on the menu rather than a couple of afterthoughts. The list runs to the Topa Chica, Endless Summer, Cabana Cooler and a Hibiscus Sparkler, and the bar builds cocktails with Ritual Zero Proof spirits — including a zero-proof classic margarita. Daytime hours are the point: it opens at 9am and closes at 4pm, covering the window when almost every other considered alcohol-free drink in San Antonio is unavailable. It sits in the Hemisfair park beside the Tower of the Americas, a short walk from the River Walk and the convention centre.
venues.address: 623 Hemisfair Blvd Ste 108, San Antonio, TX 78205
signatureDrinks: Zero-proof classic margarita - Ritual Zero Proof
venues.longDescription:
Box St. All Day occupies a corner of Hemisfair, the redeveloped park at the edge of downtown San Antonio built around the Tower of the Americas, and it trades as a brunch and all-day cafe rather than a bar. Its alcohol-free drinks are a named menu section, not an improvisation, and the bar works with Ritual Zero Proof — one of the better-established non-alcoholic spirit ranges — to build cocktails including a zero-proof classic margarita.

The named drinks are the Topa Chica, Endless Summer, Cabana Cooler and a Hibiscus Sparkler. The hibiscus is a smart inclusion in a Texas context: agua de jamaica is already part of the local drinking vocabulary, tart and deeply coloured, and it holds up against heat and sun far better than a sweet mocktail does.

What gives Box St. its particular value here is the clock, and it is worth spelling out. San Antonio's best alcohol-free drinking is oddly distributed: Hash, the only fully spirit-free bar, closes at 7pm and shuts entirely on Wednesday and Thursday. Isidore and Mixtli are dinner-only. Fermenteria opens Thursday. Almost nothing serious is available in the morning — except here, from 9am, seven days a week.

For a visitor staying downtown, that combination of location and hours makes this the most practical entry in the guide. Hemisfair is a short walk from the River Walk and the convention centre, the park itself is pleasant to sit in, and a properly built zero-proof drink at ten in the morning is not something San Antonio otherwise offers. Note that it closes at 4pm, so it is genuinely a daytime venue rather than an early-evening one. If you need somewhere after work, Double Standard or Idle Beer Hall are the closest equivalents with real zero-proof menus.
venues.pressQuote: Box St. All Day: Hibiscus Sparkler, Ritual Zero Proof Cocktails including classic Marg or Cabana Cooler.

venues.name: Brasserie 19
venues.description: Brasserie 19 is a French brasserie on West Gray in River Oaks with a long-standing reputation for its wine list, which makes the quality of its zero-proof drinks more surprising than it should be. Three builds run on Ritual's alcohol-free spirits: the No-jito pairs Ritual rum with fresh mint and soda, the Spicy Paloma runs Ritual tequila against jalapeño and grapefruit, and the French "O"-75 rebuilds a French 75 on the same alcohol-free base. Houston Press named all three in its January 2026 zero-proof guide. In a room whose identity is built on wine, having three spirit-based alternatives that are ordered by name rather than described to a bartender is the difference between being catered for and being accommodated.
signatureDrinks: No-jito — Ritual rum alternative, fresh mint, soda
Spicy Paloma — Ritual tequila alternative, jalapeño, grapefruit
French "O"-75 — Ritual alcohol-free base, in the French 75 style
venues.longDescription:
Brasserie 19 has traded on West Gray in River Oaks for over a decade, working the French brasserie format — steak frites, plateaux of shellfish, a wine list long enough to be the reason people book. It is precisely the sort of restaurant where not drinking is most awkward, because the wine is not an accompaniment to the evening but a large part of its declared purpose.

Which is why the zero-proof list matters more here than it would at a casual bar. Three drinks are built on Ritual's alcohol-free spirits, and each targets a specific classic. The No-jito takes Ritual's rum alternative with fresh mint and soda — a mojito without the rum's sugar-cane sweetness, which in practice makes it drier and more refreshing than the original. The Spicy Paloma runs Ritual's tequila alternative against jalapeño and grapefruit; grapefruit's bitterness and the chilli's heat together supply the palate-clearing sharpness that a rich brasserie menu genuinely needs, and this is the one to order alongside anything fried. The French "O"-75 is the most interesting choice, rebuilding the French 75 — normally gin, lemon and champagne — on an alcohol-free base, which is a harder trick than it sounds because the drink's whole character depends on the dryness of the sparkling wine.

Houston Press named all three in its Dry January guide for 2026, which remains the best single survey of where the city's zero-proof drinking actually happens.

The practical point for a table is this: when the sommelier comes round and the rest of the party is choosing a bottle, the difference between a restaurant with three named alcohol-free drinks on the printed list and one without is the difference between ordering in one sentence and having a conversation about what you can be made. Brasserie 19 runs to eleven on Friday and Saturday, ten midweek, and serves from eleven in the morning, so it works for lunch as readily as for a long dinner.

venues.name: Braxton Brewing Company
venues.description: Braxton Brewing Company's Covington flagship is a full working brewery, but it earns a spot here for something genuinely uncommon: it brews its own non-alcoholic beer. Garage Beer NA is a 0.0% zero-alcohol version of Braxton's flagship Garage Beer, the crisp, light American lager the brewery is best known for. Braxton describes the NA pour as brewed with a "crisp, light and refreshing taste to keep the engine turning," and CityBeat reported it is available across all three Braxton taprooms, Covington included. That means a sober or sober-curious visitor can sit at the same garage-themed bar, order essentially the same house lager as everyone else, and get a truly zero-proof version poured from Braxton's own tanks rather than a stocked import.
venues.longDescription:
Braxton Brewing Company opened its doors on March 27, 2015, at 27 W. 7th Street in downtown Covington, the flagship of a Northern Kentucky craft-beer operation founded by brothers Evan and Jake Rouse with their father, Greg. The name and the brewery's entire identity trace back to a family garage on Braxton Drive in Union, Kentucky, where Evan taught himself to homebrew; as the brewery likes to put it, "if you want to tell someone about Braxton Brewing Company, you start with the garage." Before opening, the Rouses ran one of the most successful brewery Kickstarter campaigns to date, giving the local community an early stake in the taproom. The Covington space leans into that origin story with a garage-inspired design, a rooftop deck, and rotating house taps.

The reason Braxton belongs in a non-alcoholic guide is Garage Beer NA, a 0.0% ABV zero-alcohol lager the brewery began producing in 2022 as an alcohol-free counterpart to its 4% flagship Garage Beer. Rather than stock an outside NA brand, Braxton brews the beer itself, aiming to replicate the crisp, light, sessionable character of the original light lager. CityBeat covered the launch, quoting Braxton's description of a beer "brewed with a crisp, light and refreshing taste to keep the engine turning," and confirmed it was available at all three taprooms — Covington, the Pendleton location in Cincinnati, and Fort Mitchell. It pours on draft and shows up in cans, so a designated driver or non-drinker can order the house beer alongside friends drinking the full-strength version.

The Covington taproom is open Monday 3–10 p.m., Tuesday through Thursday 11 a.m.–10 p.m., Friday and Saturday 11 a.m.–midnight, and Sunday 11 a.m.–9 p.m., a few blocks from the Roebling Suspension Bridge and an easy walk or short drive from Cincinnati's riverfront. It's a lively, full-service brewery pouring wine and cocktails as well as beer, so this is not an alcohol-free environment — the appeal is a well-made, house-brewed zero-proof option in a room built around beer. Because NA draft and can stock rotates, it's worth calling ahead (859-261-5600) to confirm Garage NA is pouring before you make the trip.
venues.pressQuote: It is available now in all Braxton taprooms (27 W. Seventh St., Covington; 331 E. 13th St., Pendleton; 5 Orphanage Road, Fort Mitchell).

venues.name: Brennan's of Houston
venues.description: Brennan's of Houston is the city's landmark Creole restaurant, opened in 1967 in Midtown as the Houston sibling of New Orleans' Commander's Palace, famous for turtle soup and tableside bananas Foster, with a Courtyard Bar zero-proof menu built on Ritual non-alcoholic spirits.
signatureDrinks: Ginger Pear (pear nectar, ginger beer, lemon juice, cinnamon sugar)
Sparkling Cranberry Apple (cranberry juice, sparkling apple cider, lemon, cinnamon syrup)

naMenuItems.name: French Market Martini
naMenuItems.description: spiced rum, espresso, smoked vanilla, simple syrup

venues.longDescription:
Brennan's of Houston has been the city's landmark Creole restaurant since 1967, opened in Midtown as the Houston sibling of New Orleans' Commander's Palace and run by the Brennan restaurant family. It occupies the former Junior League Building, which the family found to be a near-identical replica of Brennan's New Orleans. The fine-dining institution built its reputation on turtle soup and tableside bananas Foster, and in 1975 it introduced the Jazz Brunch to Houston, the same year the tradition began at Commander's Palace in New Orleans.

The building has weathered its share of Gulf Coast disasters. A tornado on November 16, 1993 tore off the roof and exposed the Garden Room, though the restaurant was fully repaired within a month. A fire during Hurricane Ike in 2008 damaged the roof, second floor, and interior, and the seventeen-month restoration retained 90 percent of the original exterior. The work earned a special Good Brick Award from Preservation Houston, and in 2011 Brennan's was inducted into Nation's Restaurant News' Fine Dining Hall of Fame. Alex Brennan-Martin and Brad Brennan serve as co-proprietors, with Carl Walker as culinary director and general manager.

A renovation completed over the past year enlarged the restaurant's bar into the Courtyard Bar, which the restaurant calls "an extension of our hospitality — fine dining, fine casual, if you will," pairing attention to detail with timeless New Orleans nostalgia. Alongside its classic-cocktail program, the bar offers a zero-proof menu built on Ritual non-alcoholic spirits. As reported by CultureMap Houston in its January 2026 Dry January roundup, non-alcoholic options include the Nogroni (NA gin, NA aperitif, orange), the Ginger Pear (pear nectar, ginger beer, lemon juice, cinnamon sugar), and the Sparkling Cranberry Apple (cranberry juice, sparkling apple cider, lemon, cinnamon syrup).
venues.pressQuote: Snag a spot in the iconic restaurant's newly renovated Courtyard Bar to savor sips such as the Ginger Pear (pear nectar, ginger beer, lemon juice, cinnamon sugar), the Nogroni (NA gin, NA aperitif, orange), and the Sparkling Cranberry Apple (cranberry juice, sparkling apple cider, lemon, cinnamon syrup).
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: CultureMap Houston, "20 Houston restaurants and bars serving spirit-free sips for Dry January" (Brianna McClane, Jan 6, 2026)

venues.name: Brennan's
venues.description: Brennan's is a New Orleans Creole landmark founded in 1946 by Owen Edward Brennan, at its present 417 Royal Street address — a 1795 Vieux Carré building — since 1956. Its kitchen originated Bananas Foster, and it's owned today by third-generation family member Ralph Brennan. Its spirit-free program is built into the cocktail menu under a dedicated section titled "Temperance, 1946 spirit-free selections," with named, seasonally rotating zero-proof drinks on non-alcoholic spirits — current builds include the Catalina Island (Seedlip Grove 42, local watermelon juice, tonic) and the Black Hills (Lyre's NA Agave Tequila, basil purée, lime). Beverage Director Braithe Gill was a 2026 James Beard semifinalist for Outstanding Professional in Beverage Service. The dining room sits around a courtyard in the heart of the French Quarter.
venues.longDescription:
Brennan's has been a New Orleans dining institution since 1946, when Owen Edward Brennan founded it, and it has occupied the pink 1795 building at 417 Royal Street since 1956. It marks its eightieth year in 2026. This is the kitchen that invented Bananas Foster, and it is still owned by the family, run today by third-generation Ralph Brennan. The recognition is current rather than historical: the New York Times put it among the top 25 New Orleans restaurants in 2024, Wine Spectator has given it the Grand Award repeatedly, it was a James Beard finalist for Outstanding Restaurant in 2022, and beverage director Braithe Gill was named a 2026 James Beard semifinalist for Outstanding Professional in Beverage Service. Turtle soup is $13, the Creole tomato tostada $18, redfish Véronique $36, and a chateaubriand for two $120.

The spirit-free section is called Temperance, 1946 — a nod to the year the restaurant opened and to a word New Orleans has a complicated relationship with. It sits inside the cocktail menu, and it rotates by season, which is the right way round: the same kitchen that changes the tomato dish changes the zero-proof drinks. Two are current. Catalina Island is $15, built on Seedlip Grove 42 with local watermelon juice and tonic — citrus-forward and light enough for a long dinner. Black Hills is $14, on Lyre's non-alcoholic agave tequila with basil purée and lime, and is the more savoury of the pair. That the drinks are named after places, priced within a dollar or two of the house cocktails, and change with the calendar tells you they belong to the beverage director rather than to a supplier catalogue. Two practical notes, because this is a jacket-preferred sort of room: reservations open sixty days ahead and parties over six must telephone, and the dress code asks for dressy casual, with no athletic or cut-off shorts, no sleeveless or decal t-shirts, no hats, and no open-toed shoes for men.
venues.pressQuote: Famous for its lavish "breakfast at Brennan's," for bananas Fosters, the dessert invented in its kitchen, and for its Old World ambiance, the restaurant also looms large in the history and culture of New Orleans dining.

venues.name: Bresca
venues.description: Bresca is chef Ryan Ratino's contemporary French bistro at 1906 14th Street NW in Logan Circle, his first solo restaurant, opened in September 2017. It has held a Michelin star since 2019 and sits directly below JONT, Ratino's two-star tasting room on the floor above. The dining room mixes neighbourhood warmth with special-occasion polish - splashes of gold, a living moss wall - and the cooking pairs French technique with local and international ingredients. The bar extends the same care to its non-alcoholic list as to the cocktails: a Citronnade a la Menthe built on a cardamom-lemon cordial, a Pear Collins on zero-proof gin with pear, lemon and ginger beer, and an Old Fashioned riff on American malt with orgeat and aromatic bitters. Dinner only, Wednesday to Sunday.
signatureDrinks: Citronnade a la Menthe (cardamom-and-lemon cordial inspired by southern French mint lemonade)
Pear Collins (zero-proof gin, pear, lemon, ginger beer)
Zero-proof Old Fashioned riff (American malt, orgeat, aromatic bitters)
venues.longDescription:
Bresca opened in September 2017 on the busy 14th Street strip in Logan Circle, and it was Ryan Ratino's first solo restaurant. It earned a Michelin star and has held it since 2019. The building is worth understanding, because it explains the cooking: directly above Bresca sits JONT, Ratino's two-Michelin-star tasting counter, and the bistro downstairs shares its kitchen discipline without the tasting-menu formality. The dining room splits the difference too, mixing the warmth of a neighbourhood restaurant with special-occasion polish - splashes of gold, a living moss wall - and the food pairs French technique with local and international ingredients in dishes like a foie gras negroni topped with Campari gelee.

The bar is a draw in its own right, and the non-alcoholic drinks are made with the same attention as the cocktails rather than being kept on a separate, lesser card. Washingtonian, listing the restaurant among DC-area bars and restaurants with great non-alcoholic cocktails, pointed readers at the nonalcoholic section of the high-concept Myths & Legends cocktail menu and singled out the Citronnade a la Menthe, which combines a cardamom-lemon cordial with mint. That drink is a riff on the mint lemonade of southern France, and it is the one to order if you want to understand what the bar is doing. Alongside it the list has carried a Pear Collins, built on zero-proof gin with pear, lemon and ginger beer, and a non-alcoholic Old Fashioned riff made with American malt, orgeat and aromatic bitters - which is the harder trick, because an Old Fashioned has nowhere to hide without the spirit.

Practical notes. Bresca serves dinner only, Wednesday through Sunday, closed Monday and Tuesday, with both a la carte and tasting options; service starts at 5.30pm midweek and 5pm on Friday and Saturday. Because the cocktail list is themed and changes, the specific zero-proof drinks rotate with it - the Citronnade has been the constant, and it is worth asking the bar what else is on rather than assuming last season's list. Reservations are effectively required at weekends, and the bar seats are the flexible option for walk-ins.
venues.pressQuote: The Citronnade à la Menthe combines a cardamom-lemon cordial with mint and lees

venues.name: BrewDog DogTap Columbus
venues.description: DogTap is BrewDog's flagship United States brewery and taproom, on Gender Road in Canal Winchester at the south-eastern edge of the Columbus metro. It matters to non-alcoholic drinkers because BrewDog brews its alcohol-free beer in-house rather than buying it in: the taproom pours the brewery's own sub-0.5% ABV range, including the Juice Club line made with real fruit juice in Citrus Crush, Raspberry Tart, Lime and Pineapple Breeze. The site runs brewery tours, a kitchen and dog-friendly patios. It should be said that BrewDog's Columbus footprint contracted sharply in 2026: the company was sold to Tilray, and its Short North and Franklinton taprooms both closed abruptly in March that year. DogTap and the New Albany location remained open, along with the bar inside John Glenn airport.
venues.longDescription:
DogTap Columbus is the Scottish brewer BrewDog's flagship American brewery, built on Gender Road in Canal Winchester on the south-eastern edge of Franklin County. It is a production brewery first and a taproom second — tours run from the site, the kitchen is full-service, and the patios are dog-friendly — but it earns its place in a non-alcoholic guide for a straightforward reason: BrewDog is one of the few breweries in the Columbus area that brews alcohol-free beer itself rather than stocking somebody else's. The taproom pours the company's sub-0.5% ABV range on site, including the Juice Club line, which is made with real fruit juice and comes in Citrus Crush, Raspberry Tart, Lime and Pineapple Breeze.

The honest caveat is that BrewDog's presence in Columbus proper has collapsed. The company was sold to the cannabis and beverage group Tilray, and in March 2026 it abruptly shuttered both of its in-city taprooms — the Short North bar and the Franklinton location — announcing the closures on social media without giving reasons, as part of a wider round that cost hundreds of jobs across its estate. 614NOW reported at the time that the Canal Winchester brewery and the New Albany taproom remained open alongside the bar inside John Glenn Columbus International Airport. That leaves DogTap as the surviving destination site, and it is a thirty-minute drive from downtown rather than a walk from the Short North, which is a real consideration for anyone planning around it. Published opening hours load dynamically on the brewery's own page rather than being listed as text, so it is worth confirming by email before travelling out. As a destination the site is set up for a half-day rather than a drink: brewery tours run from the taproom, the kitchen is full-service, and the patios are dog-friendly. The Juice Club range is the clearest expression of what an in-house alcohol-free programme can do — brewed with real fruit juice to under 0.5% ABV across four flavours — and sits alongside the rest of BrewDog's low-and-no range on tap and in can, which is a materially deeper alcohol-free selection than a bar stocking one guest NA beer can offer.
venues.pressQuote: Currently, both locations remain open in addition to the location inside John Glenn airport.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Sav McKee, 614NOW, on which Columbus BrewDog sites survived the 2026 closures

venues.name: Briar Common Brewery + Eatery
venues.description: Briar Common is a brewery and restaurant on the corner of Clay Street in Jefferson Park, a short walk from Empower Field, focused on classic beer styles paired with an eclectic food menu. Its bar list carries a dedicated "Zero Proof" heading with six house non-alcoholic drinks at $7 each — all built from fresh juices, house syrups and teas rather than bought-in mixers — plus a guest non-alcoholic beer shelf at $6 that runs Best Day Brewing's Electro-Lime and West Coast IPA alongside 4 Noses Camp Zero Tangerine Guava Blonde. The zero-proof list includes a colour-changing lemonade made with butterfly pea blossom syrup and a hot chamomile-and-honey drink, so the range covers a full evening rather than one token option.
signatureDrinks: On The Rockies (colour-changing lemonade: butterfly pea blossom syrup, lemon juice, club soda — $7)
Brushfire (blood orange juice, lime juice, clove simple, club soda — $7)
Very Cherry (cherry orange ginger simple, lime juice, ginger beer, club soda — $7)
venues.longDescription:
Briar Common Brewery + Eatery occupies a corner building at 2298 Clay Street in Jefferson Park, the neighbourhood wedged between Empower Field and the Highlands, and describes itself simply as a Jefferson Park brewery-restaurant focused on classic beer styles with an eclectic and well-paired food menu. The bar list is unusual for a brewery in that its non-alcoholic offering is split into two properly developed halves rather than a single line at the bottom of the page: a house-built zero-proof cocktail section, and a rotating guest shelf of non-alcoholic beers from breweries that specialise in them.

The zero-proof section runs six drinks at $7 each, all made from juice, house syrups and tea rather than commercial mixers. Very Cherry combines a house cherry-orange-ginger simple syrup with lime juice, ginger beer and club soda. Pomegranate Zinger is the sharper option, pomegranate juice with lime and ginger beer. Brushfire is built on blood orange juice with lime, a clove syrup and soda, which gives it a spiced, autumnal profile. Cherry Cooler is the lighter cousin of Very Cherry, dropping the ginger beer for club soda. Keep Calm is served hot — chamomile tea, honey, lemon juice and hot water — which is a rarity on a bar menu and useful in a Denver winter. On The Rockies is the showpiece: a colour-changing lemonade built on butterfly pea blossom syrup with lemon juice and club soda, which shifts hue as the acid hits the pigment. Alongside these the bar keeps guest non-alcoholic cans at $6, currently Best Day Brewing's Electro-Lime and West Coast IPA and 4 Noses Camp Zero Tangerine Guava Blonde, so a visitor can drink non-alcoholic beer of two quite different styles as well as a built cocktail. Briar Common trades from 11am daily, to 9pm on weeknights and Sundays and 10pm on Friday and Saturday, and the food menu is designed for full meals rather than bar snacks, which makes it a straightforward dinner option for a mixed group where not everyone is drinking.

venues.name: Brick & Mortar
venues.description: Brick & Mortar is a cocktail bar at 567 Massachusetts Avenue in Central Square, Cambridge, entered through an unmarked door beside Central Kitchen and marked only by a small sign once you are inside. It is known for an adventurous cocktail list and for running craft cocktail classes for groups, and it keeps a standing Zero Proof Cocktails section on the printed menu rather than improvising alcohol-free drinks on request. Three zero-proof cocktails are listed at $15 each, matching the pricing and the build complexity of the full-strength list, and they use commercial non-alcoholic spirits — Landry London Dry, Lyre's Italian Orange, Spirit of Milano and non-alcoholic Lucano amaro — rather than juice-and-soda substitutes. It trades Monday through Saturday and is closed Sundays.
venues.hours: Mon-Wed 3pm-12am; Thu 12am-12pm & 3pm-1am; Fri 3pm-1am; Sat 4pm-1am; Sun closed
