venues.longDescription:
Hilldale is Madison's west-side shopping district, a mall that has been rebuilt over the years into something closer to a walkable town centre, and Café Hollander occupies a corner of it with a large terrace. The format is Belgian café by way of Milwaukee — the Lowlands Group has run several of these across Wisconsin — which means an extensive Belgian and craft beer list, mussels and frites, and an all-day service that runs from breakfast through to late.

The alcohol-free offer here is narrower than most entries in this guide, and it would be dishonest to inflate it: this is a beer café, the beer list is the point, and there is no long printed mocktail menu. What there is, and what Madison Eats Food Tours picked out, is non-alcoholic sparkling wine poured and built into a mimosa with orange juice. That deserves more credit than it sounds like. Brunch is the meal where not drinking is most conspicuous — the mimosa and the bloody mary are effectively the format — and a room that can hand you a flute with something real in it removes the whole awkwardness. It is also, in practice, one of the very few places on Madison's west side able to do that.

Set expectations accordingly. Strength three here reflects a genuine but limited programme: a de-alcoholised sparkling wine and the willingness to use it, rather than a constructed zero-proof list of the sort Nitro Beverage Lounge or Public Parking run. The value is location and format — a large, family-friendly, all-day room on the west side, close to Gates & Brovi on Monroe Street, in a part of the metro where the alternatives are thin. Hours are not published in a form we can verify; check before a brunch trip.
venues.pressQuote: Cafe Hollander serves NA champagne with orange juice, mimosa-style.

venues.name: Cafe Jazzy Rose
venues.description: Cafe Jazzy Rose is downtown Grand Rapids' first fully alcohol-free cocktail bar, opened in January 2025 at 44 Ionia Avenue SW by hospitality veterans Joseff VanHorn and Ben Kaja. The room is built on a Jazz Age conceit, with a menu organised around iconic jazz locales, and the drinks are botanical zero-proof builds the owners call elixirs rather than mocktails. They are made with adaptogens including lion's mane mushroom, ashwagandha, tulsi, valerian root, hemp and ginseng, and non-alcoholic beer and wine round out the list. The kitchen serves Southern comfort cooking with Cajun and global touches: shrimp and grits, mahi tacos, smash burgers, bowls, soups and salads, alongside vegetarian-forward plates such as lion's mane "crab-less cakes" and the Sun Ra Nut Burger. Nothing on the premises contains alcohol.
venues.address: 44 Ionia Ave SW, Grand Rapids, MI 49503
venues.longDescription:
Cafe Jazzy Rose opened in January 2025 at 44 Ionia Avenue SW, and is the first bar in downtown Grand Rapids to serve no alcohol at all. It comes from Joseff VanHorn and Ben Kaja, two longtime hospitality operators who built the business on a specific reading of the market: that a growing share of drinkers, particularly younger ones, want the ritual and the room without the ethanol. A 2025 Gallup study reporting that 54 percent of U.S. adults drink alcohol — the lowest figure since Gallup began tracking in 1939 — was cited in local coverage of the opening. The owners describe the goal as making space for customers to have, in their words, "fun and a fancy cocktail" without "the pressure that alcohol imposes on people." The concept is styled as a Jazz Age restaurant and elixir lounge, with dim lighting, table service at dinner and a drinks menu whose sections nod to iconic jazz locales.

The drink program is where the venue separates itself from a restaurant that simply keeps a few mocktails on hand. Rather than building zero-proof analogues of gin and whisky, Cafe Jazzy Rose leans on functional botanicals, listing its drinks as adaptogenic elixirs built with lion's mane mushroom, ashwagandha, tulsi, valerian root, hemp and ginseng — ingredients in the same family as the compounds found in chamomile tea or kava, and marketed for mood rather than intoxication. Non-alcoholic beer and non-alcoholic wine are also stocked for guests who want something more familiar. The food is Southern-leaning and unusually substantial for a bar: shrimp and grits, mahi tacos, smash burgers, bowls, soups, salads and handhelds, with a vegetarian-forward streak that produces lion's mane "crab-less cakes" and the Sun Ra Nut Burger. Lunch runs as quick service; dinner is fuller table service. The kitchen and bar operate Tuesday through Sunday, 11am to 7pm.
venues.pressQuote: fun and a fancy cocktail — without the pressure that alcohol imposes on people.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Joseff VanHorn and Ben Kaja, Cafe Jazzy Rose owners

venues.name: Cafe La Trova
venues.description: Cafe La Trova is the Calle Ocho bar and Cuban restaurant that put the cantinero tradition back on the international map, ranked #42 on North America's 50 Best Bars in 2024, 2025 and 2026 and #82 on the World's 50 Best Bars list in 2025, with co-founder Julio Cabrera named Roku Industry Icon in 2023. Its bar menu carries a short mocktail section of two named builds, both priced at $10: the Yumislaidy, a long pour of pineapple juice, agave syrup, lime juice, cucumber juice and soda water, and the Mexican Cooler, which uses the non-alcoholic agave spirit Almave Blanco with spicy agave syrup, lime juice and ginger beer. Service starts at 4pm daily and the room stays open to 2am on Friday and Saturday.

venues.longDescription:
Cafe La Trova occupies a corner site at 971 SW 8th Street on Calle Ocho, in the heart of Little Havana, and is the bar most associated with the revival of the Cuban cantinero style. The accolades listed on the venue's own site are unusually deep for a Miami bar: #24 on the World's 50 Best Bars in 2023, #66 in 2024 and #82 in 2025; #42 on North America's 50 Best Bars in 2024, 2025 and 2026; #1 Best Bar in the South in 2022; and the Roku Industry Icon award to co-founder Julio Cabrera in 2023. Service starts at 4pm every day and runs to midnight, or 2am on Friday and Saturday.

The alcohol-free offering is short and honest about what it is: a two-drink mocktail section on the bar menu, both at $10, sitting under a much longer cocktail list. The Yumislaidy is the fresher of the two — pineapple juice, agave syrup, lime juice and cucumber juice lengthened with soda water — and drinks like a Cuban take on a cooler. The Mexican Cooler is the more interesting build for anyone who misses the shape of a real drink: it uses Almave Blanco, the distilled non-alcoholic blue agave spirit, with a spicy agave syrup, lime juice and ginger beer, so it carries heat and agave weight rather than just fruit. Two named drinks is a modest programme by the standards of a bar with this reputation, which is why this entry is graded a three, but they are made by the same bar team and served in the same glassware as the rest of the list. No press quote is attached to this entry because no article naming the alcohol-free drinks could be re-read verbatim at its own URL. The two-drink mocktail section and its prices come from the venue's own bar menu, checked on 2026-08-12, and the 50 Best rankings and the Roku Industry Icon award from its accolades page.
venues.pressQuote: Cafe La Trova honors the community Cubans have created in Miami the best way we know how: by throwing a giant party.

venues.name: Café Roze
venues.description: Café Roze is an all-day café and restaurant in East Nashville's Lockeland Springs area, opened in 2017 by chef-owner Julia Jaksic (a longtime New York chef, formerly of Employees Only and Jack's Wife Freda) with business partner Eric Lincoln. The vegetable-forward kitchen runs from morning coffee and breakfast through afternoon wine and dinner, and was named a Recommended Restaurant in the inaugural 2025 Michelin Guide American South. Its beverage menu carries a genuine, clearly labeled zero-proof selection rather than an afterthought: dedicated "N/A Wines & Kombucha" and "N/A Beer" sections list a Lyre's Classico non-alcoholic sparkling, the St. Agrestis Phony Negroni, Walker Brothers citrus kombucha, and Athletic Brewing's Cerveza N/A. Alongside the bottles, the bar makes a short list of house fizzy drinks at $6 — a Turmeric Cooler, a Beet Root Soda with carrot and lemon, a carrot-and-habanero Firewater, and a cold-brew Coffee Fizz with orange shrub. The Florentina Spritz built on Ritual NA tequila that appeared on earlier menus is no longer listed.

venues.longDescription:
Café Roze is an all-day café and restaurant at 1115 Porter Road, on the corner of Greenwood Avenue in East Nashville's Lockeland Springs, from chef-owner Julia Jaksic. Jaksic came to Nashville with a substantial New York résumé — she has been executive chef of Employees Only Singapore and was formerly of Jack's Wife Freda — and she described the concept before opening in terms the restaurant has stuck to: an all-day café serving breakfast, lunch and dinner, meant to be a communal space, with coffees to go in the morning, breakfast, lunch meetings, meet-ups with friends for a bite, and afternoon rosé. That is close to a literal description of how the room is used now. It runs from 8am to 10pm every day of the week, which in practice makes it one of the few places in the city where the same address works for a morning coffee, a mid-afternoon meeting and a proper dinner, and the kitchen is vegetable-forward without being restrictive. It has been recognised in the Michelin Guide's American South selection.

The non-alcoholic side is worth understanding for what it is, because it is a bottle list first. The menu carries two clearly headed sections — "N/A Wines & Kombucha" and a separate "N/A Beer" — so a non-drinker is choosing from named, labelled products in the same way a wine drinker chooses by the glass. Lyre's Classico non-alcoholic sparkling comes as a 250ml serve at $12, and the St. Agrestis non-alcoholic Negroni is $9 for a 200ml bottle, which is a genuinely bitter, adult drink rather than a sweet one. Walker Brothers citrus kombucha is $8 and Athletic Brewing's Cerveza is $7. The advantage of this approach is reliability: bottled products taste the same on a busy Saturday as on a quiet Tuesday, and they are easy to check before you arrive. The built-to-order side is a short list of house fizzy drinks at $6 — a spiced Turmeric Cooler with lemon and sparkling water, a Beet Root Soda of beet, carrot and lemon, a Cucumber Lime Fizzy, a fresh-ginger Ginger Soda, the carrot-and-habanero Firewater, and a Coffee Fizz of cold brew and orange shrub at $6.50 — so there is something made for you as well as poured. The Ritual-based Florentina Spritz that earlier menus carried has gone.
venues.pressQuote: Ripe and herbaceous, the nonalcoholic cooler is made with a pineapple shrub so robust it's almost a drinking vinegar, a very Southern thing Jaksic mastered and made her own. We need more of that.

venues.name: Cafe Sauvage
venues.description: Cafe Sauvage is a French cafe, kitchen and bar at the Massachusetts Avenue end of Back Bay, cooking modern French food with European and African influences and serving brunch daily alongside dinner. Its drinks card prints a section headed mocktails with five named alcohol-free drinks at $9 to $11, well below the $14 to $16 cocktails. Still in the Bus is fresh blueberries, lavender syrup and club soda; the Ochoa Save is described on the menu as everything you love about a margarita, minus the booze; Le Carre Magique layers pineapple, basil and orange with a coconut-strawberry lime foam; DKR Sunrise combines orange juice, bissap, passion fruit and club soda; and Parisian Sakura is lychee, ginger syrup, lime and club soda. Athletic Brewing's Upside Dawn golden ale is poured at 0%.

Le Carre Magique (pineapple, basil, orange, coconut-strawberry lime foam)
DKR Sunrise (orange juice, bissap, passion fruit, club soda)
Parisian Sakura (lychee, ginger syrup, lime, club soda)
venues.longDescription:
Cafe Sauvage occupies 25 Massachusetts Avenue at the western edge of Back Bay, where the neighborhood runs into the Berklee and Symphony blocks, and describes itself as cafe, kitchen and bar in one. The cooking is modern French with European and West African influences, and the room runs a daytime service from 9am and a dinner service from 5pm every day except Monday, with brunch every weekend and on Fridays. It is one of the venues Meet Boston, the city's official tourism organisation, named in its January 2026 guide to zero-proof drinks.

The drinks card is themed and rewritten regularly; the summer 2026 edition ran a World Cup conceit with sections named Starting XI, On the Bench and Grandes Bulles, and gave the alcohol-free drinks their own block simply headed mocktails. There are five of them and they are built with the same syrups, purees and foams as the cocktails on the facing page. Still in the Bus is fresh blueberries, lavender syrup and club soda at $9. The Ochoa Save is $9 and the menu's own description is the whole tasting note: everything you love about a margarita, minus the booze. Le Carre Magique is $10 and layers pineapple, basil and orange under a coconut-strawberry lime foam. DKR Sunrise is $11 and combines orange juice, bissap, the hibiscus infusion drunk across West Africa, passion fruit and club soda, which is the drink that best explains the kitchen's Paris-to-Dakar framing. Parisian Sakura is $10 with lychee, ginger syrup, lime and club soda. On the beer list, Athletic Brewing's Upside Dawn golden ale is poured at 0% for $7, alongside the full-strength drafts. The restaurant closes on Mondays and runs two services the rest of the week, 9am to 3pm and 5pm to 9pm, with a 10pm close on Friday and Saturday. The Paris-to-Dakar framing printed at the top of the card runs through both halves of the drinks list, which is why bissap turns up in the alcohol-free section and not just in the cocktails.
venues.pressQuote: Cafe Sauvage leans into bold, globally inspired flavors for its zero-proof offerings.

venues.name: Cairo Cafe
venues.description: Cairo Cafe is a family-owned Egyptian coffee and dessert house on County Road 10 in Blaine, established in 2026. Everything it serves is halal and it holds no liquor licence, so the whole room is alcohol-free; it is also open until 11pm on weeknights, 1am on Friday and Saturday and midnight on Sunday. The drinks board runs an Arabic-coffee section with Turkish coffee, a tea and chai section carrying Adeni black tea with cardamom, Cairo tea with mint, Somali chai and karak, and a long list of specialty lattes. Kunafa cups, Egyptian feteer and sweet crepes are made to order at the counter.
venues.longDescription:
Blaine's late-evening options have long been thin for anyone not drinking, and Cairo Cafe was opened in 2026 by a family aiming squarely at that gap: an Egyptian coffee and dessert house on County Road 10 that keeps bar hours without a bar. Its own site states the business is 100% halal, and there is no alcohol on the premises. What it sells instead is the Egyptian cafe format — long sittings, sweet things made to order, and a drinks board deep enough that a group can come back repeatedly without repeating an order. The kitchen's specialities are kunafa served in cups, Egyptian feteer, and sweet crepes; the coffee counter runs alongside them rather than behind them.

The drinks divide into five sections. Coffee and Qahwa covers Turkish coffee alongside the standard espresso builds — americano, cortado-style Spanish, white and dark mocha, caramel macchiato. Specialty Signatures is where the house work sits: pistachio, cookie butter, tiramisu and salted caramel cloud lattes, plus a brown sugar shaken espresso. The Tea and Chai section is the one worth reading closely, because it maps the neighbourhood's own communities as much as Egypt's: Adeni, a black tea with cardamom that comes out of Yemen; Cairo Tea, black tea with mint; Somali chai; regular chai; and karak. Refreshers and blended drinks run through hibiscus, tropical mango, mango dragonfruit, watermelon vimto, guava and lemon mint, and a matcha section covers French vanilla, mango, raspberry, strawberry, banana, lavender and coconut. Nothing on any of those lists contains alcohol. The value for a sober night out in the north metro is the closing time — 1am on Friday and Saturday, midnight on Sunday, 11pm the rest of the week — in a suburb where the alternative after ten is a chain bar or nothing. Two practical notes: the cafe is on County Road 10 rather than on Blaine's Central Avenue retail strip, and it opens at 9am, so it covers the whole day rather than only the evening. Because the entire operation is halal and unlicensed, there is no drinks list to scan for hidden alcohol — nothing on the premises contains any.

venues.name: Calico
venues.description: Calico is a New American neighbourhood restaurant and bar on Main Street with a seasonal menu built around local farm partnerships, and it prints its non-alcoholic drinks as named cocktails rather than burying them. Three mocktails hold the list: the Midnight Sun on non-alcoholic tequila with acidulated blood orange, cherry, pomegranate and lime; An Orange Lovely with orange, vanilla, lime and cardamom bitters; and the Hat Trick, built on house strawberry coconut water with lemon and nutmeg demerara. There is one non-alcoholic beer, a golden ale from Kit NA Brewing in Portland, Maine. It is a full bar serving alcohol, and dinner service only, Wednesday to Sunday.
signatureDrinks: Midnight Sun (non-alcoholic tequila, acidulated blood orange, cherry, pomegranate, lime)
An Orange Lovely (orange, vanilla, lime, cardamom bitters)
Hat Trick (house strawberry coconut water, lemon, nutmeg demerara)

venues.longDescription:
Calico is a small New American restaurant at 95 Main Street with a stated philosophy of doing a handful of things extremely well rather than running a long menu. The kitchen changes with the season and with what its local farm and vendor partnerships bring in, drawing on cuisines from around the world without committing to one, and the fried chicken has become the dish regulars send people for.

The reason it belongs in a non-alcoholic directory is the cocktail page. Calico lists its mocktails by name with full ingredients, on the same page as the spirited drinks, which is a small formatting decision that changes the experience of ordering: you are choosing between drinks rather than asking what can be made without alcohol. The Midnight Sun is the most constructed of the three, built on a non-alcoholic tequila with acidulated blood orange, cherry, pomegranate and lime. An Orange Lovely runs lighter, on orange, vanilla, lime and cardamom bitters. The Hat Trick uses a house strawberry coconut water with lemon and a nutmeg demerara. Alongside them sits a single non-alcoholic beer, the N/A Golden Ale from Kit NA Brewing of Portland, Maine — a dedicated non-alcoholic brewery rather than a big-brand zero, which is a more considered pick than most restaurants of this size make.

Three mocktails and one beer is a modest list in absolute terms, and it is worth being straight about that: this is a restaurant with a thoughtful zero-proof corner, not an alcohol-free venue. Most of the room will be drinking wine. What it does mean is that a table of mixed drinkers works here without anyone being handed a soda gun, which for a town of 16,000 is a genuinely useful thing to know.

Dinner service only, Wednesday through Sunday, closed Mondays and Tuesdays. It is small and takes bookings, and weekend tables go early.
venues.pressQuote: Three former employees of Coco and The Cellar Bar and two area restaurateurs have relaunched the 95 Main St. hot spot under the new name, Calico

venues.name: Callie
venues.description: Callie is a Mediterranean restaurant on Island Avenue in East Village whose drinks list gives non-alcoholic drinkers three separate sections rather than one token line. Five N/A cocktails are priced at sixteen dollars alongside the full-strength list and built on named alcohol-free spirits — Pentire Adrift, the agave distillate Almave, the Scottish spirit Feragaia and a non-alcoholic Amaro Lucano. There is N/A wine by the glass from Lyre's and Leitz, and two Best Day Brewing beers at eight dollars. Every one of those is priced within a dollar or two of its alcoholic equivalent, which is the clearest signal a bar can send about how seriously it takes the category. The kitchen runs Tuesday to Sunday from five until ten and the bar stays open until eleven, so a drink without dinner is a reasonable plan. A four percent service charge funds staff wages and health benefits, stated plainly on the menu.
signatureDrinks: Green Flash ($16) — Pentire Adrift ocean-inspired spirit, cucumber, lime, soda
Falsarita ($16) — Almave agave distillate, lime, palo santo
Dapper in Damask ($16) — Feragaia spiced spirit, pomegranate, rose water, lemon, grapefruit soda
Petulant Giuseppe ($16) — non-alcoholic Amaro Lucano, orange, lemon, orange bitters
Lyre's Classico Grande — non-alcoholic sparkling by the glass, $16
venues.longDescription:
Callie occupies a corner of Island Avenue in East Village, a few blocks from the ballpark, and cooks Mediterranean food built around a wood oven and a long list of dips. The reason it belongs in this guide is a drinks menu that treats alcohol-free drinking as three categories rather than an afterthought: N/A cocktails, N/A wine and N/A beer, each printed in the same type and position as the full-strength equivalents.

The five cocktails are the substantial part, all at sixteen dollars — the same price as most of the alcoholic list, which tells you where the effort goes. Green Flash is built on Pentire Adrift, the Cornish botanical spirit, with cucumber, lime and soda. Falsarita uses Almave, the agave distillate made without alcohol, with lime and palo santo. Dapper in Damask runs Feragaia, a Scottish distilled non-alcoholic spirit, against pomegranate, rose water, lemon and grapefruit soda. Petulant Giuseppe is built on a non-alcoholic Amaro Lucano with orange, lemon and orange bitters, which gives it the bitterness most zero-proof lists lack. A fifth, the Social Spritz, is listed in the same section on a bitter Italian aperitif with passion fruit and lemon.

The wine section is unusually good for a restaurant this size. Lyre's Classico Grande sparkling and a Leitz alcohol-removed pinot noir from the Rheingau are both poured by the glass at sixteen and seventeen dollars, so a non-drinker at a table ordering wine is not stuck with sparkling water. On beer there are two from Best Day Brewing at eight dollars, the Electro-Lime Mexican-style lager and the West Coast IPA, both brewed in California.

Practically: the dining room runs Tuesday to Sunday from five until ten and the bar stays open until eleven, which makes it usable for a drink without a full dinner. The restaurant adds a four percent service surcharge to every check to fund wages and health benefits for its full-time team, which it states plainly on its own menu. Reservations are the safer route at weekends.

One thing to weigh before booking: the pricing. At sixteen dollars, the non-alcoholic cocktails cost within a dollar or two of the alcoholic list, which some readers will find hard to justify and others will read as the point — the same spirits budget, the same labour, the same glassware. The ingredients behind them are genuinely expensive imports rather than syrup, and the section is priced as though the kitchen expects people to order from it rather than apologise for it. The food is built for sharing, with a run of dips, house pita and a five-course family-style option if you would rather the kitchen decide.

venues.name: Camellia Tea Bar
venues.description: Camellia Tea Bar is a specialty Chinese tea bar in Katong Square, out in the east of the island and well away from the central bar districts, and it is entirely alcohol-free. The house sources premium leaf directly from farms in the Wuyi Mountains in Fujian — the origin for rock oolongs such as Da Hong Pao and for lapsang souchong — and the room is built around unhurried brewing rather than takeaway cups. The stated intention is calm tea culture: quality brewing, an emphasis on slowing down, and no pressure to turn the table. It is a daytime and early-evening venue, open Tuesday to Sunday from 10am to 8pm and closed on Mondays.
venues.address: 88 East Coast Road, #01-08 Katong Square, Singapore 423371
venues.longDescription:
Camellia Tea Bar sits in Katong Square on East Coast Road, in the Peranakan heartland of eastern Singapore, and it is a deliberately quiet proposition. The name refers to Camellia sinensis, the plant all true tea comes from, and the bar's focus is narrow in the way specialist operations tend to be: Chinese leaf, brewed properly, with time taken over it.

The sourcing runs to the Wuyi Mountains in northern Fujian, and the house buys directly from the farms rather than through intermediaries. Wuyi is a significant origin — it is where yancha, the so-called rock oolongs, are produced, including Da Hong Pao, and it is also the home of lapsang souchong. These are teas with pronounced mineral and roasted character that reward multiple infusions, which is precisely the format the room is set up for. Guests are given time and equipment rather than a single finished cup, and staff will talk through what is being poured.

The stated philosophy is calm tea culture: quality brewing, a relaxed pace, and space to slow down without feeling rushed out of the seat. That positions it very differently from the matcha counters that dominate Singapore's tea scene, which are largely built around takeaway volume. For a non-drinking visitor the trade-off is location and hours — Katong is a fair distance from the Tanjong Pagar and Chinatown bar clusters, and the bar closes at 8pm and does not open at all on Mondays. It is best treated as a destination in its own right, ideally combined with a walk through the Peranakan shophouses along Koon Seng Road nearby, rather than as a substitute for an evening out in town.

That said, the east of the island is badly served for alcohol-free options of any real quality, and Katong is where a great many visitors stay. A tea bar buying single-origin Wuyi leaf direct and giving guests the time to brew it properly is a considerably better proposition than the mall coffee chains that otherwise dominate East Coast Road, and it costs very little to sit for an hour.

venues.name: Camellias at Hotel Bennett
venues.description: A pink, Faberge-inspired champagne lounge on the lobby level of Hotel Bennett on Upper King Street, with an etched-mirror ceiling, crystal chandelier and reclaimed marble. Alongside its champagne, caviar and afternoon tea, Camellias keeps a printed list of non-spirited cocktails built on zero-proof spirits, including The Charleston (Seedlip 108, celery, pistachio, citrus, smoked salt) and The Waring (Seedlip 42, apple, citrus, Codorniu N/A Brut). Each non-spirited build is $16, and the menu notes a rotating selection of non-alcoholic beer and wine alongside them. Standard service runs Monday through Saturday evenings on a walk-in basis, with afternoon tea seatings Thursday through Sunday by reservation. It is one of the more polished settings in Charleston for a serious zero-proof drink.

The Waring (Seedlip 42, apple, citrus, Codorniu N/A Brut) $16
The Towell (Seedlip Agave, serrano, cantaloupe, citrus) $16

venues.longDescription:
Camellias is the ground-floor champagne bar inside Hotel Bennett, the luxury hotel overlooking Marion Square at 404 King Street. The room was designed around Faberge jewels, with bold pink interiors, a crystal chandelier and an etched-mirror ceiling, and Food Network named it the most Instagrammable restaurant in South Carolina. The core menu pairs champagne by the bottle and glass with caviar service — 30-gram tins of Siberian sturgeon and oscietra served with blini and crème fraîche — alongside lobster roll sliders, a petite charcuterie board, truffled deviled eggs, and desserts from executive pastry chef Rémy Fünfrock, such as the flourless-chocolate Truffle and the lemon-almond Camellias Cake.

For non-drinkers, Camellias prints a dedicated "Non-Spirited Cocktails" section built on zero-proof spirits rather than a single token mocktail. Current pours, each $16, are The Charleston (Seedlip 108, celery, pistachio, citrus, smoked salt), The Waring (Seedlip 42, apple, citrus, Codorniu N/A Brut) and The Towell (Seedlip Agave, serrano, cantaloupe, citrus), and the menu notes a rotating selection of non-alcoholic beer and wine alongside them. A fourth build once listed by local alcohol-free guides, the "Mint To Be" (Amethyst blueberry-mint NA spirit, lemon, blackberry, mint), no longer appears on the menu as of August 2026. The Non-Spirited list sits alongside a spirited cocktail menu of author-named builds at $21 — The Heyward, The Faulkner, The O'Connor among them — and a champagne list running from Crémant and Canard-Duchêne up to Krug and vintage Dom Pérignon; in an exclusive partnership with Louis Roederer, Camellias is currently the only venue in South Carolina pouring Cristal by the glass. Standard service runs Monday through Saturday evenings and does not take reservations, while the separate afternoon tea seatings, held Thursday through Sunday with a Tealeaves tea selection, require booking in advance.

venues.name: Campfire
venues.description: Campfire is a live-fire New American restaurant in Carlsbad Village, opened in 2016 by restaurateur John Resnick inside a converted mid-century Quonset hut with a 12-foot wood-burning hearth at its center. Executive chef Eric Bost leads a seasonal, communal menu organized into "Trailhead," "Kindling," and "The Fire," and the kitchen earned a Michelin Bib Gourmand and remains in the Michelin Guide. The bar program extends to thoughtful non-alcoholic cocktails: San Diego Magazine highlighted Campfire's zero-proof "Thank You, Please," built from yellow corn, jicama, hoja santa, lime, and koji. The NA offering is culinary-driven and intentional — a fine, ingredient-forward option alongside acclaimed wood-fired food.
venues.longDescription:
Campfire opened in Carlsbad Village in 2016, from restaurateur John Resnick, inside a converted mid-century Quonset hut with a twelve-foot wood-burning hearth at the centre of the room. Executive chef Eric Bost — who went on to open the Michelin-starred Lilo behind Wildland a few streets away — runs a seasonal, communal live-fire menu organised into sections named Trailhead, Kindling and The Fire. The restaurant holds a Michelin Bib Gourmand and remains in the Guide, and the camping conceit is carried off without tipping into kitsch, which given the premise is an achievement in itself.

The bar programme extends the kitchen's thinking rather than running parallel to it, and the non-alcoholic drinks are culinary in construction. San Diego Magazine highlighted the zero-proof "Thank You, Please," built from yellow corn, jicama, hoja santa, lime and koji — a genuinely unusual set of ingredients for a drink, and one that only makes sense coming out of a kitchen rather than a bar. Koji, the fermentation culture behind miso and sake, brings savoury depth and a faint sweetness that is very hard to achieve in a non-alcoholic drink by any other route; hoja santa is a Mexican herb with an anise and eucalyptus character. The result is closer to a savoury course than to a soft drink. The magazine's broader assessment of the programme was that Campfire's "alcohol-free cocktails are culinary creations with the same visual appeal and depth of flavor as spirited beverages," which is precisely the standard this directory looks for. For a non-drinker in North County who wants a real dinner out around an open fire, this is one of the strongest options in the region. Dinner nightly. The Quonset hut is a genuinely unusual room to sit in, and the communal format means a table can share across the whole menu — which, combined with the drinks, makes it one of the easier restaurants in the county to bring a mixed group to.
venues.pressQuote: [The] alcohol-free cocktails are culinary creations with the same visual appeal and depth of flavor as spirited beverages.

venues.name: The Campground
venues.description: The Campground is an intimate aperitivo cocktail bar and restaurant in Kansas City's Historic West Bottoms, opened December 3, 2018 in the former Genessee Royale Bistro space. It grew from a 2012 backyard cocktail-party hangout into a brick-and-mortar known for woodsy, foraged-leaning craft cocktails, a natural-wine list, and seasonal small plates. Its zero-proof program is genuine and built into the printed menu: a dedicated "N/A Options" section mirrors the bar's spirit-forward style. The non-alcoholic Gimlet pairs an N/A blood-orange aperitif with wild mint, white sage, and lemon; the N/A Spritz layers that aperitif with non-alcoholic sparkling Pinot Noir and soda; and the N/A Margarita and Paloma are built on Strongwater (Denver) zero-proof spirits. Best Day Brewing NA lager, Topo Lupo hop water, and Casamara Club soda round out the lineup. The Campground was a 2024 James Beard Award semifinalist.

N/A Spritz (NA blood orange aperitif, NA sparkling pinot noir, soda) $12
Topo Lupo sparkling hop water (Alma Mader Brewing, Kansas City) $6

venues.longDescription:
The Campground has one of the better origin stories in Kansas City, and it prints it on its own menu. It began in autumn 2012 as a gathering place for friends in a backyard shed in Midtown. When founders Chris and Cristin had a daughter in 2015 they decided to turn the backyard hangout into a business, and in July 2018 they got the keys to the late and great Genessee Royale Bistro — the room where they had held their own wedding rehearsal dinner in 2012. The Campground opened there on 3 December 2018, at 1531 Genessee Street in the Historic West Bottoms. Kansas City Magazine named it Best Date Bar in its Best of Kansas City 2024 awards, and its kitchen produced a James Beard Emerging Chef semifinalist the same year. The food is small, sharp and reasonably priced: marinated olives at $8, green beans with fermented jalapeño ranch and aged cheddar at $14, a shrimp tostada on blue corn at $16, a double smashburger at $16, ricotta gnocchi with miso-aubergine butter at $24, and a root beer float with hickory ice cream at $9.

The non-alcoholic drinks sit in a section headed simply "N/A Options", and they are built rather than bought in. The N/A Gimlet ($12) uses a non-alcoholic blood orange aperitif with wild mint, white sage and lemon; the N/A Spritz ($12) pairs the same aperitif with a non-alcoholic sparkling pinot noir and soda. A Paloma and a Margarita ($10 each) are made with Strongwater from Denver. The most interesting item is the cheapest: Topo Lupo at $6 is a sparkling hop water from Alma Mader Brewing here in Kansas City, so a non-drinker can order something both local and genuinely made for the purpose rather than defaulting to a soft drink. Best Day Brewing's Electro Lime Mexican-style lager rounds it out at $6. One practical note: the bar does not publish opening hours on its own site, though it flags that the outside bar runs Fridays and Saturdays and that Mondays are burger specials.

venues.name: Campo at Los Poblanos
venues.description: Campo is the restaurant at Los Poblanos, the historic inn and organic farm in the Rio Grande valley north of Albuquerque, and it grows a great deal of what it serves — including the lavender fields the property is known for. Its non-alcoholic drinks come out of that: a Los Poblanos lavender lemonade made from the farm's own crop, and a Morning Remedy on the breakfast menu. A working farm is the ideal pantry for alcohol-free drinking, because the produce is the point and the spirit was never carrying the flavour. Breakfast from 8am Thursday through Sunday, dinner from 5pm nightly.
venues.address: 4803 Rio Grande Blvd NW, Albuquerque, NM 87107
signatureDrinks: Los Poblanos lavender lemonade — made with lavender from the farm
venues.longDescription:
Los Poblanos is a 1930s ranch on twenty-five acres in the Rio Grande valley at Los Ranchos, just north of Albuquerque — an inn, an organic farm and the lavender fields that have become the property's signature. Campo is its restaurant, and it cooks from the farm.

That is the whole argument for the listing. This directory keeps finding that the best alcohol-free drinks come from kitchens with the deepest pantries rather than from bars with the cleverest bartenders, and a working organic farm is the deepest pantry available. The lavender lemonade is made with lavender grown in the fields you can see from the table; it is not a flavouring bought in a bottle. When the raw ingredients are that good, the absence of a spirit stops being the defining feature of the drink.

The Morning Remedy on the breakfast service is the other documented build, and breakfast is itself worth flagging. Campo serves 8am to 1pm Thursday through Sunday, and a genuinely good breakfast room is disproportionately valuable to readers of this site — it is a whole social occasion, with friends, that has never had anything to do with alcohol, and it is where a lot of people rebuild a social life after they stop drinking.

Visit Albuquerque records both drinks in its guide to mocktails in the city.

Dinner runs 5pm to 9pm seven nights a week. Booking is essential; Campo is one of the harder reservations in New Mexico and the property is a genuine destination rather than a neighbourhood restaurant. It is about six miles north of Old Town, in a valley of cottonwoods and irrigation ditches that feels a long way from the city.
venues.pressQuote: Campo at Los Poblanos Historic Inn & Organic Farm offers a Morning Remedy and the Los Poblanos lavender lemonade.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Visit Albuquerque, Where To Find Mocktails in Albuquerque

venues.longDescription:
Canard is a French-inflected bar and bistro at 734 E Burnside St in Portland's Buckman neighborhood, opened in 2018 by acclaimed chef Gabriel Rucker as the casual, all-day sibling to his adjacent fine-dining flagship, Le Pigeon. Rucker is a two-time James Beard Award winner and a Food & Wine "Best New Chef," and Canard quickly became one of the city's most celebrated spots — named Portland Monthly's best restaurant of 2018 — known for playful French bar food like its foie gras dumplings and the Duck Stack.

What sets Canard apart for non-drinkers is a genuinely committed non-alcoholic program, shaped by the fact that Rucker has been sober since 2013 and is a vocal advocate for sobriety in the restaurant industry (he helped establish the Portland chapter of the recovery group Ben's Friends). Canard offers a full menu of zero-proof options well beyond an afterthought, including mocktails, non-alcoholic IPAs and alcohol-free sparkling wine, pouring NA spirits and beers from brands such as Seedlip (served with tonic) and Athletic Brewing. A standout zero-proof drink is the Paul Frank, a blend of cold brew coffee, caramelized banana, Anjou pear and toasted milk powder.
venues.pressQuote: Canard is the third restaurant by Gabriel Rucker, the Portland chef WW has called the most talented of his generation.

venues.name: Canary Club
venues.description: Canary Club calls itself Louisville's first and only natural wine bar, and it is 100 per cent women-owned, run by Sarah Height and Chelsea Moore in a dive-bar room on South Shelby Street in Shelby Park. The non-alcoholic side is treated as part of the offer rather than a courtesy: the bar stocks non-alcoholic beer and wine, builds named zero-proof drinks including the Wild Rose Spritz on Figlia Fiore aperitivo and the Maleficent on NKD LDY non-alcoholic gin, and runs half-price non-alcoholic drinks every Monday as a standing feature. Free live jazz runs every Tuesday, the kitchen serves until 1am nightly, and rotating food pop-ups take over several nights a week.
signatureDrinks: Wild Rose Spritz (Figlia Fiore aperitivo, orange, lemon, simple syrup)
Maleficent (NKD LDY non-alcoholic gin, pomegranate, lime, ginger, house grenadine)
venues.longDescription:
Shelby Park is a small, dense neighbourhood south-east of downtown that has become one of Louisville's more interesting drinking districts, and Canary Club is at the centre of it: a natural wine bar built inside a dive-bar frame, 100 per cent women-owned by Sarah Height and Chelsea Moore, who also run the sister shop The Breeze immediately next door. The wine list is the specialism — low-intervention bottles from small producers, sold by the glass in a room with late hours and a kitchen that runs until 1am every night — but the reason the bar belongs in a non-alcoholic guide is that it has thought about the other side of the list as deliberately as the wine.

The named zero-proof drinks are properly built. The Wild Rose Spritz uses Figlia Fiore, a botanical non-alcoholic aperitivo, against orange, lemon and simple syrup; the Maleficent runs NKD LDY — a de-alcoholised gin — through pomegranate, lime, ginger and a house grenadine. Dry January coverage has also singled out the bar's non-alcoholic Old Fashioned, described as the best riff on one you will find locally, and a fan-favourite Italian Pony, both around $9, alongside stocked non-alcoholic beer and wine. Most tellingly, Monday is an all-day happy hour that includes half-price non-alcoholic drinks as a standing weekly feature — a bar putting its own margin behind the category rather than charging cocktail prices for juice.

The programming makes it easy to spend an evening here without drinking: free live jazz every Tuesday from 8pm, and rotating food pop-ups through the week — Pacaya on Thursdays, Poco on Fridays, a bagel spread on Saturday mornings. Hours run genuinely late, to 1am most nights and 2am on Friday and Saturday, which matters because most of Louisville's better zero-proof lists sit in restaurants that close at 10pm. Pair it with The Breeze next door for bottles to take home.
venues.pressQuote: Wild Rose Spritz: Figlia Fiore Aperitivo, orange, lemon, simple syrup. Maleficent: NKD LDY gin, pomegranate, lime, ginger, house grenadine.

venues.name: Cane & Table
venues.description: Cane & Table is a rum-focused "proto-tiki" cocktail bar and restaurant in the French Quarter, opened in July 2013 on Decatur Street by Nick Detrich with the Cure team (Neal Bodenheimer and Kirk Estopinal). The kitchen leans into Caribbean and Cuban flavors, and the bar — a James Beard Outstanding Bar Program semifinalist, named by Bon Appétit among the best new cocktail bars in America — carries a dedicated "Non-Alcoholic" section rather than a token mocktail. Named builds include the Safe Harbor (a smoky zero-proof negroni on Pathfinder NA aperitivo), the Just Like a Spritz (Giffard non-alcoholic aperitif cordial, sparkling, citrus), the savory-fruity Funky Fresh (strawberry, pineapple, NA beer, black pepper), and a house passionfruit ginger lemonade.

venues.longDescription:
Cane & Table is a rum-led bar and restaurant on Decatur Street in the French Quarter, from the team behind Cure, and it describes what it does as proto-tiki — the drinking culture that came before mid-century tiki rather than the tiki revival itself. Co-founder Kirk Estopinal put the intent well: they wanted to offer New Orleans classics that maybe do not go back a hundred years but might go back to the fifties and sixties. Chef Alfredo Nogueira, a New Orleans native of Cuban descent, cooks food shaped by both halves of that inheritance, Cajun technique against Cuban heritage. The bar has been named a James Beard semifinalist for Outstanding Bar Program. It opens seven nights, 5pm to a 10pm last seating, with happy hour Monday to Friday from 5 to 7.

The non-alcoholic drinks are printed under their own heading and there are five, which is a genuinely deep list for a bar whose entire identity is rum. Safe Harbor is the standout: a robust and slightly smoky Negroni powered by Pathfinder non-alcoholic aperitivo, and the smoke is what makes it work, because a Negroni without alcohol usually loses the weight that gin gives it. Just Like a Spritz uses Giffard's non-alcoholic aperitif cordial with sparkling water and citrus. Funky Fresh is the most inventive — strawberry, pineapple and non-alcoholic beer with black pepper, which uses the beer for bitterness and body the way a cocktail would use a spirit. The other two are deliberately simple: house-made passionfruit syrup with fresh ginger and lemon, and a young coconut cracked at the bar for its water. That last one belongs in a rum bar in a way a manufactured mocktail never would. One caveat worth knowing before you go: Cane & Table publishes no prices at all on its website, for drinks or for food, so there is no way to plan a budget in advance — you will find out at the table.
venues.pressQuote: We want to offer New Orleans classics that maybe don't go back 100 years but might go back to the '50s and '60s.

venues.name: Canni Infusion Bar & Cafe
venues.description: Canni Infusion Bar & Cafe is Walker's Point's pioneering "infusion bar" — billed as Milwaukee's first — where essentially every craft cocktail and cafe drink can be poured zero-proof. The all-day menu of coffee, tea and specialty drinks (OJ & Kush, Cucumber Frost, Riverwalk and more) is built to be ordered straight, spirited, or botanically infused. Important caveat: Canni is an alcohol-free-forward hybrid rather than a fully dry bar — it holds a liquor license and can add alcohol on request, and its optional "infusions" include hemp-derived Delta-9 THC, CBD, kava and functional mushrooms. Treat it as a social-wellness lounge with a deep NA backbone, not a substance-free space.
venues.longDescription:
Canni began in 2018 as Canni Hemp Co., Milwaukee's first dedicated CBD and hemp shop, and reopened its Walker's Point storefront at 810 S. 5th St. in November 2023 as Canni Infusion Bar & Cafe. The concept is "choose your own adventure": a full menu of craft cocktails and cafe drinks that can each be served straight (zero-proof), spirited with alcohol, or botanically infused. Owner Colin Plant told Urban Milwaukee the team "noticed years ago that there was this growing trend of people that wanted to enjoy social experiences, but not have to be in a bar that's focused on alcohol to do so," and later described a rising demographic in Milwaukee practicing abstinence from alcohol.

The non-alcoholic program is unusually deep for a licensed bar. Per OnMilwaukee's Dry January coverage, cafe/bar manager Moonie Swaser designed every drink to be versatile, so any item can be ordered with alcohol, with zero-proof spirits, or with no alcohol at all. The standing named menu includes OJ & Kush (orange juice, vanilla, seltzer), Cucumber Frost (club soda and mint), Riverwalk (black tea, blood orange, lemonade), Mr. Milwaukee Margarita (pomegranate, lime, mint), Elderberry Hot Chocolate and Desert Dream, alongside all-day coffee, tea, taro milk tea and blueberry limeade. That every drink is available fully NA is what places Canni at the high end of the alcohol-free spectrum.

The important qualifier is that Canni is a hybrid, not a dry bar. Shepherd Express (Jan. 9, 2025) reported that Canni holds a liquor license to offer alcoholic versions of its drinks and may be the only bar and cafe in Wisconsin — perhaps the country — to offer both cannabis and alcohol in the same space. Its optional infusions include hemp-derived Delta-9 THC, full-spectrum CBD, kava and functional mushrooms (lion's mane, chaga, reishi, cordyceps), so sober-curious and fully sober guests should order deliberately and be aware of THC/kava dosing. Canni also functions as an events and live-music space, hosting alcohol-free programming such as "Zero Proof: A Dry January Groove."

venues.name: Cannon Ball Lounge
venues.description: Cannon Ball Lounge sits six floors up on the roof of Hotel Indy on East Washington Street, and is the only indoor-outdoor rooftop bar downtown — which matters in a city with four distinct seasons. It is named for Erwin "Cannonball" Baker, the Indianapolis motorcyclist who rode in the first Indianapolis 500 and set transcontinental records for decades afterwards, and the drinks list leans on local reference points throughout. The non-alcoholic drinks are a printed zero-proof section rather than an afterthought: I Miss My Spritz is built on DHOS Bittersweet Aperitif and non-alcoholic sparkling wine, Good Graces runs lemon, guava and honey against New Orleans non-alcoholic bitters and ginger beer, and the Tail of Thyme uses a house plum-lavender syrup.
signatureDrinks: I Miss My Spritz (DHOS Bittersweet Aperitif, non-alcoholic sparkling wine)
Good Graces (lemon, guava, honey, New Orleans non-alcoholic bitters, orange, ginger beer)
venues.longDescription:
Hotel Indy is a Tribute Portfolio conversion on East Washington Street, a block from Monument Circle and across from the old City Market, and Cannon Ball Lounge occupies its sixth floor with 180-degree views over downtown. The pitch is Indianapolis-specific rather than generic rooftop: the room is named for Erwin "Cannonball" Baker, the local motorcyclist who rode in the inaugural Indianapolis 500 in 1911 and spent the following decades setting coast-to-coast driving records, and the menu carries local reference points through the cocktails, the Indiana craft beer list and a kitchen of reworked Midwestern classics.

For non-drinkers the relevant fact is that the zero-proof drinks are a standing printed section, not a request. I Miss My Spritz is the flagship — DHOS Bittersweet Aperitif, an Italian-style non-alcoholic amaro, lengthened with non-alcoholic sparkling wine, which lands genuinely bitter rather than sweet and is the closest thing downtown to an Aperol spritz without alcohol. Good Graces is the long, complex one, running lemon, guava and honey against New Orleans non-alcoholic bitters, orange and ginger beer. The Tail of Thyme is built on a house plum-lavender syrup, which tells you the bar is making its own components rather than buying in mixers. Visit Indy, the city's own tourism body, lists the lounge in its Buzz-Free Drinks guide on the strength of that menu.

Practicalities: it opens at 4pm Monday to Saturday and at noon on Sunday, running to midnight on Friday and Saturday, the indoor-outdoor design means it works in February as well as July, and it takes reservations through OpenTable — worth using on a weekend or around a Colts or Pacers game, since the hotel sits in the middle of the downtown event footprint. This is a hotel rooftop, so expect a mixed crowd of visitors and locals and a price point to match; the zero-proof drinks are costed in line with the cocktails.
venues.pressQuote: Hotel Indy's rooftop cocktail lounge offers "I Miss My Spritz," featuring DHOS Bittersweet Aperitif and N/A Sparkling Wine, one of three mocktails on the menu.

venues.name: Canon
venues.description: Canon is a 32-seat cocktail bar and small restaurant at 928 12th Avenue on Capitol Hill, opened in 2011 by Jamie Boudreau, and it holds one of the largest spirits collections in the world — over 4,000 labels, around 2,500 of them whiskey, shelved along the hallway and even in the bathrooms. Boudreau designed the back bar so guests would feel utterly, lavishly wrapped up in bottles. ACCURACY NOTE: Canon is frequently credited online with winning the 2019 James Beard Award for Outstanding Bar Program. It did not — that award went to Bar Agricole in San Francisco. Canon was a James Beard semifinalist in the same category in 2014. Its non-alcoholic drinks sit in their own printed section headed "Sans", each prepared without alcohol at $20: POG the Magic Dragon (passion fruit, orange, guava, black "horchata"), I'm Longan Ver-Jus (longan, pear, verjus blanc, sparkling rosé), Tropical "Julius" (mango, pineapple, starfruit, passion fruit, orange, vanilla, milk, frozen) and Cascadian Norteño (Pathfinder amaro, Mexican vanilla cold brew, chicory, sarsaparilla). Open Wednesday to Sunday from 5pm.
venues.longDescription:
Canon opened in 2011 and is, by most counts, one of the most serious cocktail bars in the world. Jamie Boudreau built it around a spirits collection that now runs past 4,000 labels — roughly 2,500 of them whiskey — which has long since overflowed onto shelves in the hallway and in the bathrooms, inside a room that seats thirty-two. He designed the back bar deliberately so that customers would feel utterly, lavishly wrapped up in bottles, and his own explanation of why people come is the most quotable line any bar owner has given: people come to be in the room. The food is proper cooking rather than bar snacks — Taylor Shellfish oysters at $30 for eight, a crab and rice bowl at $20, katsu lamb leg at $20, a vegan "foie gras" at $10. It opens Wednesday to Sunday from 5pm until at least midnight, with happy hour at each end of the evening. It will not split your cheque, and says so in the driest possible terms: not until a computerised till exists that can handle its inventory.

One correction is worth making because the internet keeps repeating it. Canon is widely described as the 2019 James Beard winner for Outstanding Bar Program. It is not — that award went to Bar Agricole in San Francisco. Canon was a semifinalist in that category in 2014, which is real recognition and does not need inflating. The non-alcoholic drinks have their own printed heading, Sans, and each is prepared without alcohol at $20 — the same architecture as the rest of the list, which at this bar means something, because Sans sits directly beneath shared and vintage cocktails running from $345 to $750 built on decades-old spirits. POG the Magic Dragon works passion fruit, orange and guava against a black "horchata" and, per the menu, magic. I'm Longan Ver-Jus pairs longan and pear with verjus blanc and sparkling rosé. Tropical "Julius" is frozen and creamy. Cascadian Norteño is the one to order if you want something bitter and adult: Pathfinder amaro with Mexican vanilla cold brew, chicory and sarsaparilla.
venues.pressQuote: People come to be in the room.

venues.name: Cantina Rosa
venues.description: Cantina Rosa is an agave-focused cocktail bar in Hyde Park, opened in November 2024 by chef Erick Williams of Virtue Hospitality, who named it after his grandmother Rosetta. It sits at 5230 S Harper Ave, steps from Williams' other Hyde Park spots, Virtue and Daisy's Po-Boy & Tavern, and was developed with longtime collaborator Jesus Garcia, with the tiki-leaning cocktail menu consulted on by veteran Chicago bartender Paul McGee. Tequila and mezcal anchor the drink list, but the bar runs a genuine "Spirit Free" section that gets the same fresh-juice, house-syrup and garnish treatment as the alcoholic menu. Named zero-proof options include the Verdita (pineapple, lime, mint, jalapeño) and the Horchata Fizz (coconut water, in-house almond orgeat, cinnamon, ginger beer), plus a spirit-free Margarita and non-alcoholic Corona. The room, designed by Erin Boone with nods to architect Luis Barragán, features pink accents, terracotta tiles and mesquite woodwork.
signatureDrinks: Horchata Fizz (coconut, almond, cinnamon, ginger, soda) $12

venues.longDescription:
Cantina Rosa opened on 29 November 2024 at 5230 S Harper Avenue, a few doors from chef Erick Williams's other Hyde Park rooms, and it is the agave-focused counterpart to his Southern restaurant Virtue. Williams named it after his grandmother Rosetta and has been direct about the intent: the concept has deep personal significance, he said at opening, and just as Virtue pays homage to Black culture, Cantina Rosa honours the rich traditions of Mexican culture. The bar is built around tequila and mezcal with a diverse bartending team behind it, and the kitchen sends out roasted poblano oysters with serranos, Oaxaca cheese and crostini at $12, tamales Oaxaqueños with chicken and tomatillo salsa at $9, and barbacoa de borrego — lamb with Mexican rice, adobo and tortillas — at $19. Bon Appétit has named it among the eight best bars in Chicago. Service runs Wednesday to Sunday from 5pm, to midnight on Friday and Saturday, and reservations are held for ninety minutes with a fifteen-minute grace period for late arrivals.

The non-alcoholic drinks have their own printed heading, "Spirit Free", and they are treated as part of the agave programme rather than as an exception to it. The Verdita ($12) is the one to order first: verdita is the traditional green chaser served alongside tequila in Jalisco, made from pineapple, lime, mint and jalapeño, and serving it as a drink in its own right is a genuinely idiomatic way to give a non-drinker something that belongs on this bar rather than something borrowed from a soft-drink list. The Horchata Fizz ($12) works coconut and almond with cinnamon, ginger and soda — WTTW liked it enough to publish a version of the recipe in January 2025. A spirit-free Margarita is $15, built rather than poured from a mix, and a non-alcoholic Corona is $7 for anyone who wants a beer in hand. It is a short list, but every item on it is drawn from the same tradition as the rest of the bar, which is rarer than a long one.
venues.pressQuote: Cantina Rosa's bar staff prepare the non-alcoholic offerings as thoughtfully as the boozy ones, with flavorful fresh juices, syrups, and garnishes adding up to imaginative concoctions that fit their cozy, elegant setting.

venues.name: Cardellino
venues.description: Cardellino is the Italian-American room in chef Brad Wise's group, on Goldfinch Street in Mission Hills, making handmade pasta and pizza alongside a bar that prints a Spirit Free section. Four entries run from a ten-dollar cantaloupe and mint limeade made in house, through Bella Vita on a non-alcoholic aperitif with orange and raspberry at thirteen, to Solar Flare at fourteen — aplós arise with lemon, ginger and turmeric — with Athletic Brewing's non-alcoholic golden ale at eight. The limeade matters as much as the two spirit builds: it is the one drink on the list for a guest who would rather avoid spirit analogues altogether, and it is made to order rather than poured. Dinner runs Tuesday to Sunday from five, until ten on Friday and Saturday, with a happy hour in the first hour of service. The room is small and pasta-led, so weekend reservations are advisable.
signatureDrinks: Bella Vita ($13) — non-alcoholic aperitif, orange, raspberry
Solar Flare ($14) — aplós arise, lemon, ginger, turmeric
Cantaloupe Mint Limeade ($10) — made in house, no spirit alternative
venues.longDescription:
Cardellino trades on Goldfinch Street in Mission Hills and is the most relaxed of chef Brad Wise's San Diego rooms: handmade pasta, pizza from a wood oven, and a menu the restaurant describes as melding a midwest chophouse with a trattoria. It opened in early 2020 and has stayed a neighbourhood restaurant rather than an occasion one.

Its alcohol-free offering is short but properly constructed, printed under a Spirit Free heading on the same card as the cocktails. The cheapest is also the most straightforward: a cantaloupe and mint limeade at ten dollars, made in house, which is the right answer for anyone who would rather avoid spirit analogues altogether. Bella Vita, at thirteen, is built on a non-alcoholic aperitif with orange and raspberry — the spritz shape, without the wine. Solar Flare at fourteen is the ambitious one, using aplós arise with lemon, ginger and turmeric, a combination that lands closer to a sour than a soft drink and has enough acid and heat to hold up against a plate of pasta.

The fourth line is Athletic Brewing's non-alcoholic golden ale at eight dollars, which is the sensible accompaniment to pizza and the item most likely to still be on the list whenever you visit; the two built drinks rotate with the seasonal cocktail card.

A few practicalities. The restaurant is closed on Mondays and serves from five until nine early in the week, until ten on Friday and Saturday. Happy hour runs in the first hour of service and is worth knowing about if the full prices look steep. The room is small and the pasta list is the reason most people come, so book at weekends. This is a licensed restaurant, not an alcohol-free space, and the wine list is long — but a non-drinker at this table has four printed choices at three price points rather than a bartender improvising, which is the distinction that matters.

The restaurant describes itself as a story steeped in fire, char and steak, and red sauce, parmesan and truffles — which is an accurate summary of a menu that runs wood-fired steaks alongside handmade pasta. That combination is also why the drinks list is worth having: an aperitivo-shaped drink before a plate of pasta is a specific thing a non-drinker usually has to give up in an Italian restaurant, and here it is printed on the card at thirteen dollars. The pizza and pasta are the reason most of the neighbourhood comes, and the bar seats are the easiest to get without a booking.
venues.pressQuote: Italian at heart and bold in its imagination, Cardellino offers diners a journey to Tuscany through America’s heartland, melding a midwest chophouse with a trattoria to create a comforting, yet elegant culinary experience.

venues.name: Casa Cacao
venues.description: Casa Cacao is Columbus' first kava and cacao bar, opened in 2024 by Ayala Wolak on East Hudson Street in Old North Columbus. No alcohol is served. The menu is built around two plant ingredients — kava, a root native to the Pacific Islands that is prepared as a drink for its relaxant effect, and ceremonial-grade cacao, ground to a paste and spiced. Alongside them sit a full espresso programme, loose teas, kombucha, hot chocolate and alcohol-free wine. Kava is a psychoactive botanical rather than an inert soft drink: Wolak has said each drink carries roughly a tablespoon and a half of kava powder, and concentrated shots are sold alongside the milder 12-ounce teas. The room occupies a long-dormant building that has been a theatre, a barbershop and a church, and it runs $5 kava on Thursday and Saturday evenings.
signatureDrinks: Bear's Elixir (cacao, orange oil, clove, cinnamon, coconut sugar)
Daisy's Limelight (double espresso, twist of lime)
venues.longDescription:
Casa Cacao opened on East Hudson Street in Old North Columbus in 2024, the work of owner Ayala Wolak, and is the first cafe in the city to build a menu around both kava and cacao. The building it occupies has had several lives — a theatre, a barbershop and a church — and had sat empty for years before the fit-out. Wolak told The Lantern that the opening "has been like a homecoming for me; not only back to Columbus, but into myself," and that she hoped guests would "feel like we care about them and leave with a sense of community." The cafe serves no alcohol at any hour, which makes it one of very few genuinely alcohol-free social rooms in Columbus rather than a bar with a zero-proof section bolted on.

The drinks divide into three families. Coffee runs to a full espresso list including Daisy's Limelight, a double shot cut with a twist of lime. Cacao is prepared as a paste rather than cocoa powder — more bitter, more concentrated, and carrying theobromine as its active compound — and appears in drinks such as the Bear's Elixir, built with orange oil, clove, cinnamon and coconut sugar. Kava is the third, and the one that most distinguishes the room: a root traditionally prepared in the Pacific Islands and served here as a spiced 12-ounce tea or as a concentrated shot. It is worth being plain that kava is psychoactive and mildly sedating, which is a different proposition from a mocktail; Wolak has put the dose at roughly a tablespoon and a half of powder per drink, with the tea noticeably weaker than the shot. Kombucha, hot chocolate, alcohol-free wine and a frothed oat-milk drink called The Fluffy round out the list, and the cafe runs $5 kava on Thursday and Saturday evenings from 6 to 8pm. Well-behaved leashed dogs are welcome. A few practical notes. Casa Cacao is a cafe rather than a bar, and it keeps cafe hours — from 8am daily, closing at 8pm most nights and 10pm on Fridays and Saturdays — so it works as a morning or afternoon room as readily as an evening one, which is unusual among alcohol-free venues. It is also, at the time of writing, effectively the only dedicated alcohol-free social space of its kind in Columbus, a city that has otherwise built its non-alcoholic offering inside licensed bars and restaurants. Anyone who has not had kava before should approach the shots with some care and ask staff about strength; the drink is legal and widely sold in the United States, but it is a sedating botanical and it interacts poorly with alcohol and with some medications, which is a conversation worth having rather than assuming.
venues.pressQuote: Casa Cacao is a family business with a lot of time, effort and love put into it. It's a cultivation of many things from around the world that we love and want to share with Columbus.

venues.name: Casadonna
venues.description: Casadonna is the coastal Italian restaurant on North Bayshore Drive at the southern edge of Edgewater, with a dining room and terrace facing Biscayne Bay. Its documented alcohol-free build is the Donna d'Oro, made with Almave Ámbar — a distilled blue agave spirit with no alcohol — balanced with pineapple and lime, which puts a genuine agave backbone under a drink that would otherwise be a fruit cooler. Secret Miami described the restaurant in December 2025 as an ideal destination for booze-free sips, and RESIDENT wrote that the drink channels coastal Italian ease while maintaining structure and depth. Dinner runs nightly from 5pm, with lunch on Saturday and brunch on Sunday.
signatureDrinks: Donna d'Oro (Almave Ámbar blue agave spirit, pineapple, lime)
venues.longDescription:
Casadonna occupies a bayfront site at 1737 N Bayshore Drive, on the Biscayne Bay waterfront at the southern end of Edgewater. The format is coastal Italian, the terrace runs along the bay, and service is split across a Saturday lunch, a Sunday brunch and dinner every night, closing at 10pm on weeknights and 11pm on Friday and Saturday.

The alcohol-free build documented at the restaurant is the Donna d'Oro. It is made with Almave Ámbar, the distilled blue agave spirit produced without alcohol, and balanced with pineapple and lime. The choice of base matters: Almave is made from cooked blue agave rather than flavoured water, so the drink carries a vegetal, faintly smoky weight that a straight fruit build does not, and it is the reason the same drink appears in two separate December 2025 Miami round-ups. Secret Miami listed Casadonna second in its survey of fifteen zero-proof rooms and called the pairing of coastal Italian cooking with sweeping waterfront views an ideal setting for booze-free drinking. RESIDENT, covering the same season, wrote that the Donna d'Oro channels coastal Italian ease while maintaining structure and depth, and that it is designed for lingering afternoons and long dinners. Almave is not currently carried in this catalogue's brand registry, so the entry names the spirit in the drink specification without attaching a brand tag. Note that some published listings give the address as 1717 N Bayshore Drive; Secret Miami records 1737, which is the number used here, and the restaurant occupies the first floor. For anyone planning an evening in Edgewater without drinking, Casadonna and Amara at Paraiso sit within a few blocks of each other on North Bayshore Drive, and both publish named alcohol-free builds. Bookings run through the restaurant's site and on (305) 475-2272; the venue posts as @casadonnamiami.
venues.pressQuote: Casadonna's coastal Italian menu and sweeping waterfront views make it an ideal destination for some booze-free sips!

venues.name: CASBAR Lounge
venues.description: CASBAR Lounge is the 24-hour cocktail lounge on the casino floor at SAHARA Las Vegas, at the quieter north end of the Strip, with live music every evening and a room built for sitting rather than passing through. Its non-alcoholic menu is unusually developed for a casino bar: rather than stripping the spirit out of a cocktail and serving what is left, the bar reaches for low- and no-ABV substitutes and rebuilds classics properly, working largely with Lyre's non-alcoholic spirits so that the juniper of a gin drink or the vanilla of a whiskey drink is still there. Documented builds include an N/A Old Fashioned made with Lyre's American Malt and an N/A Raspberry Mojito made with Lyre's White Cane Spirit. The Las Vegas Convention and Visitors Authority named it among seven must-try spirit-free stops in the city, and Best of Las Vegas awarded the lounge Bronze for Best Cocktail Bar in 2024. Because it never closes, it is one of the few genuinely round-the-clock spirit-free options in Las Vegas.
venues.address: 2535 S Las Vegas Blvd, Las Vegas, NV 89109
signatureDrinks: N/A Raspberry Mojito (Lyre's White Cane Spirit)
venues.longDescription:
CASBAR Lounge sits on the casino floor at SAHARA Las Vegas, at the north end of the Strip where the crowds thin out and the room rates drop, and it trades on being a lounge in the older sense of the word: a place with seating, live music every evening, and no expectation that you are moving on to somewhere else afterwards. It is open twenty-four hours a day, seven days a week. Best of Las Vegas awarded it Bronze for Best Cocktail Bar in 2024, which places it in genuine cocktail-bar territory rather than in the category of a bar that happens to be attached to a casino.

The non-alcoholic program is the reason it belongs in this directory, and it is better constructed than almost anything else of its kind on a casino floor. The bar's approach is to rebuild classic cocktails rather than subtract from them: instead of serving a gin drink without the gin, it works with low- and no-ABV substitutes, leaning heavily on Lyre's non-alcoholic spirits so that the botanical structure of the original drink survives. As one of its bartenders put it when explaining why simply omitting the spirit does not work, the guest otherwise misses the juniper in the gin, the vanilla of the whiskey and the agave of the tequila. Documented builds include an N/A Old Fashioned made with Lyre's American Malt and an N/A Raspberry Mojito made with Lyre's White Cane Spirit, and the wider non-alcoholic list has been described in coverage as extensive and thoughtful rather than perfunctory. The Las Vegas Convention and Visitors Authority's own guide named CASBAR among seven must-try spirit-free stops in the city, noting that it uses low or no ABV mixers to reimagine classic cocktails; the same guide describes the bar's party trick, a machine that prints an image of your choosing onto the foam of the finished drink, with the picture uploaded through the bar menu. The round-the-clock licence is the practical detail worth remembering: at four in the morning, on a street where the alternative is a soda from a slot-machine cocktail server, this is a room where someone not drinking can order a properly built drink and sit down to live music.
venues.pressQuote: CASBAR Lounge at SAHARA Las Vegas uses low or no ABV (alcohol by volume) mixers to reimagine classic cocktails as mocktails.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Visit Las Vegas, "Seven Must-Try Mocktails in Las Vegas"

venues.name: Cassis
venues.description: Cassis is a French brasserie on St. Petersburg's waterfront Beach Drive, and it's one of the only spots on that strip to give non-alcoholic drinks their own permanent menu section rather than a token mocktail. The list runs to a Codorniu Zero sparkling rosé from Spain, a Giesen Zero Chardonnay, a Hibiscus Breeze on hibiscus syrup and hibiscus ginger beer, and a Harvest Mojito built on Owen's mint cucumber — so a sober diner gets the same waterfront-patio experience as everyone else. A printed section rather than an off-menu favour is the distinction that matters here: it has to be stocked, trained on and kept through every menu redesign, which is why so few restaurants on this strip bother.

venues.longDescription:
Cassis sits on Beach Drive NE, the waterfront strip that is downtown St. Petersburg's main dining address, looking across to Straub Park and the marina. It is a French brasserie in the full sense — all-day service, a long menu, a patio that is the point for most of the year — and it occupies the kind of position where a restaurant can coast on the view rather than the drinks list.

It does not. Cassis is one of very few venues on that strip to give non-alcoholic drinks a permanent, named section of the menu instead of a token mocktail produced on request. The list includes a non-alcoholic sparkling Spanish rose, which matters more than it sounds: on a waterfront patio where the default order is a glass of wine, having a proper sparkling option in a proper glass is the difference between joining the table and being visibly exempted from it. On the June 2026 menu the built drinks are a Hibiscus Breeze — ginger syrup, hibiscus syrup, lime, mint and hibiscus ginger beer — and a Harvest Mojito made on Owen's mint cucumber with lime, muddled blueberries and mint, alongside a Corona Na by the bottle. One caution: the third drink in that mocktail section, the Ginger Haze, is made with 10mg THC and 10mg CBD and is sold 21+. It is not an alcohol-free option in the sense most people reading this page mean, and we do not count it as one.

I Love The Burg singled the restaurant out in January 2024 for exactly that permanence: the mocktail list gets its own entire section of the menu. A section is a commitment. It has to be printed, stocked, trained on and defended against the menu redesign, which is why so few restaurants bother and why the ones that do tend to keep doing it.

Two practical points. This is a full-service French brasserie with a substantial wine programme, so the alcohol-free list is a real part of the offering rather than its character. And Beach Drive is busy year-round — book, particularly if the patio is the reason you are going.
venues.pressQuote: The permanent mocktail list gets its own entire section on the menu, and even includes a non-alcoholic sparkling Spanish rose.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Bob Carskadon, I Love The Burg

venues.name: Cat Bite Club
venues.description: A hidden agave-and-rice-spirit speakeasy behind grey curtains at Monument Lifestyle on Duxton Road, Cat Bite Club (No. 44 on Asia's 50 Best Bars 2025) runs a genuine zero-proof program via its 'mirrored' menu: serves marked with a blue cat motif can be built alcohol-free on request. The standout is a non-alcoholic Puss in Boot, a guava milk punch with maple, lemon, lime and cinnamon that founding partner Jesse Vida (ex-Atlas) makes by running the full milk-washing and whey-straining process without any spirit, so the AF version keeps the silky texture of the tequila original. It's craft NA to order rather than a separate printed list, but the builds are executed to the same standard as the full-proof menu.
signatureDrinks: Zero-proof Puss in Boot - guava milk punch with maple, lemon, lime and cinnamon, milk-washed and whey-strained without any spirit (alcohol-free version of the tequila original)
venues.longDescription:
Cat Bite Club opened in June 2023 on Duxton Road in Tanjong Pagar, tucked behind heavy grey curtains inside the Monument Lifestyle store and cafe (look for the neon-red Cheshire-cat sign). It's the project of operating partners Gabriel Lowe and Jesse Vida, the latter formerly head bartender at Atlas, and it debuted to fast acclaim: winner of the Campari One To Watch Award 2024 and No. 44 on Asia's 50 Best Bars 2025.

The drinks concept is a playful collision of agave and rice spirits, spanning Mexico and Asia across more than 300 artisanal distillates, including what the bar bills as Singapore's largest agave collection at over 200 bottles. Signature full-proof serves include the Cat Bite Margarita, the Soju Sprint and, on the 2026 menu, builds like 'Get The MSG?' and 'Straight Outta Scallion'.

The non-alcoholic offering works through the bar's 'mirrored' menu: cocktails flagged with a blue cat motif can be prepared alcohol-free on request. The clearest example is the zero-proof Puss in Boot, a guava milk punch with maple and cinnamon that is normally tequila-based. To make it AF, Jesse Vida performs the milk-washing clarification without alcohol, adding guava, maple, lemon, lime and cinnamon, curdling with milk, then fine-straining the whey through cloth for a silky, delicate texture that mirrors the original.

The room is a low-lit, curtain-hidden speakeasy seating a small crowd; hours are daily from 5pm to midnight, and the bar is known for donating proceeds from its weekly milk punches to local cat charities.
venues.pressQuote: We do the milk washing process without alcohol. We add guava, maple, lemon, lime, cinnamon, followed by milk and let it curdle. The whey is slowly fine-strained through a cloth for a silky and delicate texture.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Jesse Vida, founding partner, Cat Bite Club

venues.name: Catalina Kitchen + Bar
venues.description: Catalina Kitchen + Bar is a coastal comfort food restaurant at 1942 E 7th Street in the Elizabeth on Seventh development, opened on 12 September 2023 as the first North Carolina restaurant from Chicago's Ditka Restaurant Group, named for its partner Mike Ditka. The 5,800-square-foot room has booths, high-tops, bar seating and a patio, with free parking in the Elizabeth on 7th garage. The kitchen runs a half-pound Ditka Burger at $18, seafood tagliatelle with bay scallops, lump crab and shrimp at $26, and a Sonoma chicken salad at $21, with happy hour weekdays from 3pm to 6pm and oysters at $2.50. Its printed "Zero Proof Cocktails" section holds four drinks at a flat $11: Almost Rita (Lyre's non-alcoholic blanco, cold-pressed lime, agave), No-Jito (Lyre's non-alcoholic white cane, mint, cold-pressed lime), Hibiscus Rose Fizz (hibiscus-infused water, rose, ginger beer) and Lavender Lemonade (lemonade, lavender-infused syrup, cold-pressed lemon, fizzy water). Best Day Brewing's non-alcoholic Kölsch is $6.
