venues.longDescription:
Colita is a Tex-Oaxacan restaurant from chef Daniel del Prado's DDP Restaurant Group — the team behind Martina and Bar La Grassa — open since October 2018 in a converted former gas station at 54th and Penn in the Armatage neighbourhood of southwest Minneapolis. It is named after del Prado's first dog. The kitchen runs Oaxacan-influenced barbecue, creative tacos and mole-driven dishes, and it is entirely gluten-free, which combined with the drinks list makes it an unusually easy restaurant to bring a group with different requirements to.

The drinks menu carries a dedicated Zero Proof section of four house-made non-alcoholic cocktails at $10 each, built with the same care as the alcoholic list: fruit-, herb- and tea-forward bases finished with carbonation. Rosas works rose against raspberry. Naranjitas combines citrus with lychee. The Horchata is a cinnamon coconut-milk build, which is the traditional partner for this food and considerably better than the version most restaurants pour from a carton. The 3leche Miele pairs honey with sarsaparilla — an old-fashioned root flavour that gives the list something bitter and adult at the end.

It is worth being straight about the scale of this programme relative to others in this directory. Four named drinks is a real, maintained list, not a token, and at a $10 price point they are properly made rather than marked up as a novelty. But it is a focused complement to a meal rather than a standalone bar menu — you would come here for the food and drink well alongside it, rather than come for the drinks themselves. For a neighbourhood restaurant in a residential corner of Minneapolis, that is exactly the right ambition, and it is more than most equivalent rooms manage. Dinner nightly, to 10pm on Friday and Saturday.

venues.name: Collective Arts Brewing (Toronto Taproom)
venues.description: Collective Arts Brewing's Toronto taproom occupies 777 Dundas St. West in Trinity-Bellwoods / Little Portugal, pairing a full-lineup taproom and retail store with a lower-level live music and event space. The brewery brews its own line of non-alcoholic beers - a 0.4% ABV Non-Alcoholic IPA hopped with Citra, Simcoe and Mosaic, a 0.4% ABV Hazy Pale Ale hopped with Mosaic and Citra, and an under-0.5% ABV Emerald Non-Alcoholic Stout - and stocks them in the on-site retail store alongside its full portfolio of beers, cocktails, spirits and glassware. blogTO has described it as "a popular Hamilton brewer now boasting a Toronto location."
signatureDrinks: Non-Alcoholic IPA — 0.4% ABV, brewed with Citra, Simcoe and Mosaic hops; citrus, tropical fruit and pine notes
Non-Alcoholic Hazy Pale Ale — 0.4% ABV, New England-style, brewed with Mosaic and Citra hops; citrusy tropical fruit and red berry notes
Emerald Non-Alcoholic Stout — under 0.5% ABV; rich chocolate, sweet caramel and hints of roast coffee, smooth finish
venues.longDescription:
Collective Arts Brewing's Toronto taproom is located at 777 Dundas St. West in the Trinity-Bellwoods / Little Portugal neighbourhood, combining a taproom, retail store and lower-level live music and event space under one roof. The taproom and retail store are open Tuesday through Thursday from 1pm to 10pm, Friday from 1pm to 11pm, Saturday from noon to 11pm, and Sunday through Monday from 1pm to 9pm, with a kitchen serving Mexican-inspired food on a separate schedule most days; the patio welcomes well-behaved leashed dogs, and the space has free wifi and plenty of outlets for working.

Alongside its full lineup of beers on tap, cocktails and spirits, Collective Arts brews its own line of non-alcoholic beers, sold in the on-site retail store next to the rest of its portfolio. The Non-Alcoholic IPA comes in at 0.4% ABV, brewed with Citra, Simcoe and Mosaic hops for citrus, tropical fruit and pine notes. The Non-Alcoholic Hazy Pale Ale is a New England-style beer, also 0.4% ABV, brewed with Mosaic and Citra hops for citrusy tropical fruit and red berry character. The Emerald Non-Alcoholic Stout comes in under 0.5% ABV, built around rich chocolate, sweet caramel and hints of roast coffee with a smooth finish.

blogTO has described Collective Arts as "a popular Hamilton brewer now boasting a Toronto location" - the brewery's roots are in Hamilton, Ontario, with the Dundas Street West taproom serving as its Toronto retail and tasting outpost.
venues.pressQuote: a popular Hamilton brewer now boasting a Toronto location

venues.name: Coltivare
venues.description: A garden-driven Italian restaurant in Houston's Heights neighborhood from chef Ryan Pera and Agricole Hospitality, Coltivare pairs its rustic, Gulf Coast-inflected Italian cooking with an award-winning "Zero Proof Cocktails" menu built on Houston-made Cut Above spirits, Lyre's, and Seedlip, plus non-alcoholic beer and wine.
venues.hours: Mon 5pm-10pm; Tue closed; Wed-Thu 5pm-10pm; Fri-Sat 5pm-11pm; Sun 5pm-9pm
venues.longDescription:
Coltivare is a garden-driven Italian restaurant in Houston's Heights neighborhood, opened in 2014 by award-winning chef Ryan Pera and partner Morgan Weber as the flagship of their Agricole Hospitality group, which also operates Eight Row Flint (Heights and East End) and EZ's Liquor Lounge. Known for rustic Italian cooking with a Gulf Coast perspective and produce from its own backyard garden, the no-reservations restaurant pairs its kitchen with a serious, long-running zero-proof program.

The dedicated "Zero Proof Cocktails" menu leans on Houston-made Cut Above zero-proof spirits alongside Lyre's and Seedlip, in named drinks such as the Not & Tonic (Cut Above zero-proof gin, elderflower tonic, grapefruit, lime, mint, green peppercorn), Et Tu, Brute? (Amaro Lucano Zero, Lyre's Italian Spirit, Topo Chico), and In the City (Seedlip 94, vanilla, cranberry, ginger), the last of which paired the restaurant with Sipple, a non-alcoholic bottle shop in Rice Village, for a past Dry January collaboration. As of the restaurant's January 2026 zero-proof lineup, the list also includes Il Rosmarino (cranberry, rosemary, black pepper), Silly Langtree (blood orange, ginger), Madame Pamplemousse (grapefruit, bay leaf), and Reset Spritz (raspberry, elderflower). Non-alcoholic beer and wine round out the list.

Coltivare was named "Best Mocktail List" in the Houston Press Best of Houston 2022 awards, recognized as an early adopter of zero-proof drinking in the city. The program has stayed active in the years since, with Coltivare's zero-proof menu featured in citywide Dry January roundups from both CultureMap Houston (January 2025) and Houston Press (January 2026), evidence of a sustained, multi-year commitment to the non-alcoholic list rather than a one-off seasonal gesture.
venues.pressQuote: One of the pioneers in embracing zero-proof cocktails, this Agricole Hospitality stunner puts out refreshing drinks for everyone, the sober, curious or just plain thirsty.

venues.name: Comfort Kitchen
venues.description: Comfort Kitchen is a restaurant and cafe in Upham's Corner, Dorchester, opened in January 2023 inside a restored 1912 comfort station on Columbia Road. The kitchen cooks what it calls global comfort food, tracing ingredients and techniques of the African diaspora from Asia to the Americas. Its drinks program is unusually deliberate about non-alcoholic service: the bar list is split into cocktails and a standing 'Free-Spirited Cocktails' section, and the rotating wine and beer selection includes N/A options. General manager and beverage director Kyisha Davenport built the program around the same pantry the kitchen uses, with Nepali timur pepper, West African suya spice and Middle Eastern sumac appearing in drinks on both sides of the menu. The cafe side pours coffee, espresso and tea.
signatureDrinks: Baobab Express (baobab, Nepali white tea, ginger, orange blossom water)
Chiya Punch (built on the spice blend used in the cafe's Nepali chiya)
venues.longDescription:
Comfort Kitchen opened in January 2023 in the Comfort Station at 611 Columbia Road, a 1912 municipal building in Upham's Corner that had sat unused for decades before the restaurant team restored it. The cooking is described by the house as global comfort food and traces the ingredients and routes of the African diaspora across Asia and the Americas; within a year it had drawn national attention alongside Moeca and Rubato as one of the Boston restaurants the rest of the country was watching. It runs dinner Wednesday through Sunday and brunch at weekends, with a full bar and a patio.

The drinks are where it earns a place in this directory. The bar menu is organised into cocktails and a standing 'Free-Spirited Cocktails' section, listed as its own category rather than appended at the bottom, and the rotating wine and beer list carries N/A options. Beverage director Kyisha Davenport told Edible Boston in November 2023 that she avoids the word mocktail entirely, and she builds the alcohol-free drinks from the same sourcing story as the food, using Nepali timur pepper, West African suya spice mix and Middle Eastern sumac. The two drinks Edible Boston documented were the Baobab Express, built on baobab and Nepali white tea with ginger and orange blossom water as a deliberate line drawn between the West African and South Asian diasporas, and a Chiya Punch using the spice blend behind the cafe's Nepali chiya. The menu rotates, so those specific drinks may not be pouring on a given night, but the section itself is permanent, priced in line with the cocktails, and staffed by people who treat it as a real order. Boston magazine reviewed the restaurant in May 2023 and the Globe reviewed it that December, and in September 2023 the Globe grouped it with Moeca and Rubato as the Boston restaurants drawing national attention. Dinner runs Wednesday through Sunday with a last seating at 9pm, and brunch is served Saturday and Sunday from 10am.
venues.pressQuote: I never really liked the word mocktail.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Kyisha Davenport, Comfort Kitchen general manager and beverage director

venues.name: Common Tiger
venues.description: Common Tiger is a hidden speakeasy in downtown Mission, Kansas, opened quietly in August 2024 by Abby Hans alongside her family. The bar is concealed behind a faux neighborhood corner store stocked with chips, cereal, and soaps; guests with the password are led past the shelves into a dim, tiger-themed lounge with red couches, music, and a small dance floor. The cocktail list rotates monthly around seasonal themes, and the kitchen turns out snacks and pizza. Its zero-proof side is small but genuine: bartenders build named mocktails such as the Starlight (a light pear-lemon soda) and the Filthy Chai (a spirit-free dirty chai), pour the dessert-style Pink Pony Club, and will spin up non-alcoholic versions of cocktails like the Bad Blood Mule on request. It sits near Sandhills Brewing and Urban Prairie Coffee in downtown Mission.
venues.longDescription:
Common Tiger is a speakeasy hidden behind a working corner shop at 5616 Johnson Drive in downtown Mission, Kansas, opened in August 2024 by Abby Hans with her parents Jason and Julie and her older brother Mason, in a space that had been the Beardé Salon until it closed in late 2022. The front half is not a facade for show — the Johnson County Post described an unassuming neighbourhood corner store stocking Zapp's chips, boxes of cereal, jars of almond butter, soaps and kitchen accessories, and you can shop it without ever going further. Getting into the back requires telling the cashier the password, which the bar circulates rather than hides completely. Behind the door the room turns dim and plush: dark red couches, low light and, as the Post put it, a lot of tiger decor. Opening hours started at 6pm to midnight on Friday and Saturday, and the family has expanded the operation since.

For a non-drinker the honest position is that this is a cocktail bar first, with zero-proof drinks made to order rather than a standing zero-proof list. The bar changes its cocktail menu monthly around seasonal ingredients and a theme, and the non-alcoholic options rotate with it — a Pink Pony Club has appeared as a mocktail built to drink like a milkshake, and the house Bad Blood Mule has been offered in a non-alcoholic version alongside the bourbon original. That monthly turnover is the important fact: any named list, including ours, is a snapshot rather than a menu, and the right move is to tell the bartender what you like and let them build something. The shop at the front also stocks non-alcoholic drinks you can take through to the lounge, which is a genuinely useful fallback. Given the password entry and the weekend-evening hours, this is a planned outing rather than somewhere to wander into — worth checking their current hours and how the password is being shared before you go.

venues.name: Commune
venues.description: Commune is a wine bar and hi-fi listening room in Avondale Estates, opened May 8, 2024 by Zopi Kristjanson and music producer/DJ Chris Devoe inside the Olive + Pine development. The wine list is curated by James Beard-nominated sommelier Steven Grubbs, formerly of Empire State South, who keeps an esoteric but approachably priced by-the-glass and bottle program. The space pairs that list with seasonal small plates and a nightly schedule of DJ sets and live performances spanning jazz, funk, Afrobeat, psych rock and post-punk. Alongside wine, cocktails, beer and tea, Commune maintains a standing N/A Drinks category for non-drinkers: a St. Agrestis Phony Negroni, an Oddbird Blanc de Blanc non-alcoholic sparkling chardonnay, an Aplos Ume Spritz, Athletic Upside Dawn and sparkling mineral water. The same list also carries an Afterdream Tropical THC Tonic, which is alcohol-free but psychoactive. The Atlanta Journal-Constitution reviewed the room favorably in August 2024, praising its creative, frequently changing food menu, well-trained staff and fair pricing.
venues.hours: Mon-Tue closed; Wed-Thu 6pm-11pm; Fri-Sat 6pm-12am; Sun closed
signatureDrinks: Oddbird Blanc de Blanc (non-alcoholic sparkling chardonnay) $12
Afterdream Tropical THC Tonic (alcohol-free but contains hemp-derived THC) $11
venues.longDescription:
Commune opened on 8 May 2024 at 6 Olive Street in Avondale Estates, inside the Olive + Pine development, from Zopi Kristjanson and the music producer and DJ Chris Devoe. It is a wine bar and a hi-fi listening room in equal measure, and the Atlanta Journal-Constitution's Henri Hollis caught what makes the room work: a listening bar in a windowless space carved out of a cinder block warehouse could have felt like eating inside a cheap subwoofer, and instead it feels like a midcentury sound engineer's living room.

The wine list is curated by Steven Grubbs, the James Beard-nominated sommelier formerly of Empire State South, and runs esoteric but sanely priced by the glass and the bottle. The kitchen, under executive chef Autumn Jade, changes almost daily; Hollis praised the staff as well-trained, knowledgeable guides through a menu that is efficiently descriptive rather than showy. Music runs nightly - DJ sets and live performances spanning jazz, funk, Afrobeat, Italian film soundtracks, bebop, psych rock and post-punk.

A listening room is a genuinely good format for not drinking, and it is worth saying why. The evening has a centre of gravity that is not the bar: people are there to hear something, conversation runs quieter, and nobody is tracking what is in your glass. That removes most of the social friction of being the sober person in the room, which is usually the actual obstacle rather than the drink itself.

Commune keeps a standing N/A Drinks category rather than improvising on request. As of August 2026 it runs to a St. Agrestis Phony Negroni, an Oddbird Blanc de Blanc - a de-alcoholised sparkling chardonnay - an Aplos Ume Spritz, Athletic Brewing's Upside Dawn golden ale and Marzia sparkling mineral water, with a separate tea list of blood orange hibiscus, a lion's mane and tulsi blend called Clarity, Dragonwell green tea and Earl Grey creme. One item on that same list needs flagging plainly: the Afterdream Tropical THC Tonic contains hemp-derived THC. It is alcohol-free, but it is not non-intoxicating, and anyone here because they are avoiding intoxication rather than alcohol specifically should order around it. It is a wine bar first and the list is short, so this is a place to go for the room and the records with a decent drink in hand, not a destination zero-proof programme. Open Tuesday to Saturday evenings.
venues.pressQuote: A listening bar in a windowless room carved out of a cinder block warehouse could be like eating inside a cheap subwoofer, but instead it feels like a midcentury sound engineer's living room.

venues.name: Community Beer Co.
venues.description: Community Beer Co. is a Dallas brewery, distillery, and taproom-restaurant founded by Kevin Carr in 2013, now housed in a sprawling former ExxonMobil campus near the Design District. Beyond its alcoholic lineup, Community brews its own non-alcoholic beer under the "Nada" label — making it one of relatively few breweries producing zero-proof beer in-house rather than reselling outside brands. The non-alcoholic range now runs to two beers: Nada IPA, hopped with Mosaic, Sabro and Simcoe, and Texas Free, a non-alcoholic lite beer, each roughly 25 calories, 5g carbs and under 0.5% ABV. A Nada Hazy IPA, Pilsner and Bock and a hop-infused "Hop'd Water" were previously part of the family but have been dropped from the published lineup as of August 2026. Note that the taproom also pours THC seltzers, listed on the same beverage menu, which readers avoiding intoxicants of any kind will want to know before ordering. Nada IPA earned a Bronze medal in the Non-Alcohol Beer category at the 2022 Great American Beer Festival. The Nada beers are poured and sold at the family- and dog-friendly taproom alongside food from the on-site kitchen.
signatureDrinks: Nada IPA (non-alcoholic IPA with Mosaic, Sabro and Simcoe hops, 25 calories)
Texas Free (non-alcoholic lite beer, 25 calories, 5g carbs)
venues.longDescription:
Community Beer Co. is a brewery, distillery and taproom-restaurant at 3110 Commonwealth Drive near the Design District, founded by Kevin Carr in 2013 and now occupying a sprawling former ExxonMobil campus. It matters to non-drinkers for a structural reason rather than a menu one: Community brews its own non-alcoholic beer in-house under the Nada label, which puts it in a small group of breweries producing zero-proof beer themselves rather than reselling somebody else's. The Dallas Observer reported in May 2024 that the brewery had collected six Great American Beer Festival awards, including one for its non-alcoholic beer, along with two World Beer Cup medals; Nada IPA took bronze in the non-alcohol category at the 2022 Great American Beer Festival.

The taproom's non-alcoholic beer section centres on Nada IPA, hopped with Mosaic, Sabro and Simcoe, and Texas Free, a non-alcoholic lite beer at roughly 25 calories and 5g of carbohydrate; the printed taproom menu has also carried Nada Hazy IPA, Nada Golden and Nada Wheat at around 30 calories each, poured from 12oz cans, though the published range rotates. Less well known is that the cocktail menu runs a separate block headed "Mocktails", explicitly marked as containing zero alcohol, with six named drinks — several of which use the brewery's own non-alcoholic beer as an ingredient. The Nada Shandy combines lemonade with Nada IPA and fresh-squeezed lime over ice, and the Nada Sunrise Shandy builds Nada Hazy IPA with cranberry juice, lemonade and lime. The Community Mock is hibiscus simple syrup, lime juice, Sprite and soda water; the Mock Mule is ginger beer, lime juice and soda water; and the list is rounded out by a Lavender Lemon and a Mocklada of pineapple juice, coconut cream, water and a lime wedge. One caveat worth knowing before you go: the taproom also pours THC seltzers from the same beverage menu, which readers avoiding intoxicants of any kind will want to be aware of when ordering. The taproom is open Wednesday to Sunday, closed Mondays and Tuesdays, and welcomes children and dogs.
venues.pressQuote: I'm completely sober.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Jamie Fulton, Community Beer Co. head brewer

venues.name: Compère Lapin
venues.description: Compère Lapin is the New Orleans flagship of James Beard Award-winning chef Nina Compton, opened in June 2015 inside The Old No. 77 Hotel & Chandlery in the Warehouse District. Born and raised in St Lucia and a Top Chef runner-up, Compton melds Caribbean cooking with French and Italian technique; she won Best Chef: South in 2018 and was a Food & Wine Best New Chef in 2017. The name means "Brother Rabbit", a trickster figure from her St Lucian childhood. The restaurant was the first in New Orleans to win a Tales of the Cocktail Spirited Award for Best American Hotel Bar, and it made OpenTable's Top 100 Hotel Restaurants in America for 2025. Its drinks list carries a "Non-Alc and Mocktails" section: a house Sorrel Tea ($8) of spiced hibiscus with ginger, lavender and lime; Silly Songs With Larry ($8) with cucumber, ginger, sesame, rice vinegar, chilli and soda; Athletic Brewing's Run Wild non-alcoholic IPA ($7); and a Unified Ferments jasmine green tea ($10 a glass, $40 a bottle). Dinner nightly from 5.30pm.
venues.longDescription:
Compère Lapin opened in June 2015 in the Old No. 77 Hotel & Chandlery in the Warehouse District and has been one of the city's most acclaimed restaurants since. Nina Compton grew up in St Lucia surrounded by the flavours of the islands, reached the final of Top Chef, was named a Food & Wine Best New Chef in 2017 and won the James Beard Award for Best Chef: South in 2018; she runs it with her husband and business partner Larry Miller. The name means Brother Rabbit — the trickster of St Lucian folk stories she grew up with. The cooking is Caribbean through French and Italian technique: curried goat with sweet potato gnocchi at $40, fried chicken with jerk honey and coconut grits at $32, semolina dumplings with shrimp in run down sauce at $34, and buttermilk biscuits with honey butter at $8. Dinner runs nightly from 5.30pm.

The bar's credentials are real — this was the first New Orleans restaurant to take a Tales of the Cocktail Spirited Award for Best American Hotel Bar — and the non-alcoholic section is built with that seriousness. It is headed Non-Alc and Mocktails, and it does something unusual that is worth spelling out: two of the drinks are written zero-proof first, with alcohol offered as a paid addition. The Sorrel Tea at $8 is spiced hibiscus with ginger, lavender and lime, and the menu notes you can make it boozy by adding rum for $8 more. Silly Songs With Larry, also $8, runs cucumber, ginger, sesame, rice vinegar, chilli and soda, with mezcal as the optional extra. That framing means the non-alcoholic version is the recipe rather than a subtraction from one, which is exactly backwards from how most restaurants build a mocktail — and sorrel, the spiced hibiscus drink served at Caribbean Christmas tables, belongs on this menu more than any imported bottle would. Alongside them sit Athletic Brewing's Run Wild non-alcoholic IPA at $7 and a Unified Ferments jasmine green tea at $10 a glass or $40 a bottle, poured like wine. The list rotates, so earlier drinks such as Tell Tale Heart and Garden Party have already been retired.
venues.pressQuote: Compère Lapin quickly became one of the city's hottest restaurants.

venues.name: Comstock Saloon
venues.description: Comstock Saloon is a North Beach bar on Columbus Avenue built in the style of a nineteenth-century San Francisco saloon, with a long mahogany bar, a classics-led cocktail list and a kitchen serving through the evening. Its non-alcoholic drinks sit in a dedicated section of the printed menu and are made to the same specifications as the full-proof list. Five are named: the Torino Spritz, with Martini & Rossi Floreale, non-alcoholic sparkling wine and seltzer; the No-No Nogroni, built on Lyre's gin, Giffard aperitif and a house kombucha standing in for vermouth; Sbagliato Sbagliato, the same kombucha vermouth with NA sparkling wine and Giffard aperitif; Spruce Goose, with Pathfinder, black tea, Giffard aperitif and lemon; and Freebird, with Ritual rum, Giffard aperitif, pineapple and lime.

venues.longDescription:
Comstock Saloon stands at the point where Columbus Avenue meets Pacific, on the edge of the old Barbary Coast, and is built to look and behave like a San Francisco saloon of the 1890s: pressed tin, a long bar with a foot rail, a mezzanine, and a cocktail list weighted towards martinis, Manhattans, sazeracs and other pre-Prohibition drinks made properly. The Infatuation's guide to the city's best cocktail bars describes it as the kind of old-school bar that feels like it has been around since people rushed to the city to pan for gold, and recommends it for solo drinking at the bar as much as for a date. The kitchen puts out saloon food — pickled eggs, oysters, a burger — through the evening.

The non-alcoholic drinks get their own heading on the menu and are built with the same bar-back ingredients as everything else, which is what separates a real programme from a list of sodas. Five are named. The Torino Spritz uses Martini & Rossi's Floreale de-alcoholised aperitivo with non-alcoholic sparkling wine and seltzer. The No-No Nogroni substitutes Lyre's zero-proof gin and Giffard's aperitif syrup and uses a house kombucha in place of sweet vermouth, a technique that gives the drink the acid and funk that most alcohol-free negronis lack. Sbagliato Sbagliato applies the same kombucha vermouth to a sparkling build. Spruce Goose is made with Pathfinder, the fermented and distilled hemp spirit, cut with black tea, Giffard aperitif and lemon. Freebird is the long, tropical option, built on Ritual's zero-proof rum with Giffard aperitif, pineapple and lime. The bar trades Tuesday to Saturday, opening at 4pm and at noon on Fridays, and closes at midnight; it is closed Sunday and Monday. Notably for a room this classics-focused, the alcohol-free drinks are not simply the house cocktails with the spirit removed — each one is a separate build with its own substitutions, which is the difference between a bar that has thought about the category and one that keeps a bottle of Seedlip behind the well for emergencies. Walk-ins are welcome and dinner reservations are taken.
venues.pressQuote: It’s the kind of old-school bar that feels like it's been around since people rushed to the city to pan for gold.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: The Infatuation, The 20 Best Cocktail Bars In SF

venues.name: Comune
venues.description: Comune is a plant-based — and very nearly vegan — restaurant on Parsons Avenue in Schumacher Place, working a spare Scandinavian dining room and a seasonal, locally sourced menu under executive chef Zachery Riddle. It was named among Columbus Monthly's best restaurants in the city for 2025. The bar runs a root-to-stem cocktail programme alongside natural wine and herbal digestifs, and marks its non-alcoholic options directly on the printed menu: cocktails available zero-proof carry a degree symbol, currently the Vermouth + Tonic at $8, the Alta Highball at $10 and the Comune Sour at $14. Beneath them sit house-made sodas at $6 — lemon and ginger, blueberry and cardamom shrub, or charred pineapple shrub — plus Casamara Club amaro soda and Good Liar, the non-alcoholic IPA brewed in Columbus.
signatureDrinks: House-made sodas: lemon + ginger, blueberry + cardamom shrub, charred pineapple shrub
venues.longDescription:
Comune occupies a corner site at 677 Parsons Avenue in Schumacher Place, on the eastern edge of German Village, and has spent several years as the most serious plant-based dining room in Columbus. The kitchen, led by executive chef Zachery Riddle, works an almost entirely vegan menu from seasonal and locally sourced produce, with breads and spreads and a crispy rice dish as the constants beneath ever-changing vegetable toppings. The room is spare and Scandinavian in feel, and Columbus Monthly included it among the city's best restaurants in 2025.

The drinks programme is where the restaurant earns its place in a zero-proof guide. Comune runs what it calls a root-to-stem cocktail list — the same waste-minimising logic as the kitchen, applied to the bar — alongside natural wines and herbal digestifs. Crucially, the non-alcoholic options are marked on the printed menu with a degree symbol against the cocktails that can be made zero-proof, which currently covers the Vermouth + Tonic at $8, the Alta Highball at $10 and the Comune Sour at $14. That is a meaningfully different arrangement from a bar that will make something up on request: the guest can read the list and choose, and the zero-proof price is printed rather than negotiated. Underneath the cocktails sit house-made sodas at $6, offered in lemon and ginger, blueberry and cardamom shrub, or charred pineapple shrub — shrubs being vinegar-based fruit syrups, which give the sodas an acidity that most restaurant soft drinks lack entirely. The list is finished with Casamara Club amaro soda at $5, Jarritos Mineragua and Vichy Catalan sparkling mineral water, and a can of Good Liar, the non-alcoholic Midwest IPA brewed in Columbus itself. Dinner only, Monday to Saturday. One further point worth making for anyone planning a night out: because the kitchen is plant-based and the bar prices its zero-proof drinks at $8 to $14, Comune is one of the few rooms in Columbus where a guest who is neither drinking nor eating animal products faces no compromise at all. Reservations are advisable, the room is small, and service is dinner only.
venues.pressQuote: Comune delivers an elegant and inventive plant-based — and nearly vegan — menu with creative cocktails and natural wines in a spare, Scandinavian dining room.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Columbus Monthly, Best Restaurants in Columbus 2025

venues.name: Con Alma
venues.description: Con Alma is a live-jazz supper club at 613 Penn Avenue in Downtown Pittsburgh's Cultural District, serving a Latin-inspired menu alongside a genuine zero-proof programme. It began on Ellsworth Avenue in Shadyside in 2019 and opened Downtown in 2021; the Shadyside original has since closed, so this is now the only location — worth knowing, because much of the press about Con Alma describes the other room. Esquire named it one of the 27 best bars in America in 2021. It is owned by executive chef Josh Ross, music curator John Shannon and beverage director Aimee Marshall. The non-alcoholic section carries two built cocktails — an N/A Painkiller with coconut cream, orange, pineapple and nutmeg, and an N/A Mojito ($10) — plus Eins-Zwei-Zero 0% sparkling Riesling ($12), a Bravas non-alcoholic golden ale ($6) and a rotating NA beer. Unusually, it also sells zero-proof spirits by the pour at $8–$9: Free Spirits gin, bourbon and tequila, Dr Zero Zero AmarNo and Pentire Coastal Spritz. Budget for a per-person music charge during live sets ($10 Thursday and Sunday, $15 Friday and Saturday, $5 in the bar).

venues.longDescription:
Con Alma is a live-jazz supper club at 613 Penn Avenue in Downtown's Cultural District. It began on Ellsworth Avenue in Shadyside in 2019, and the Downtown room opened in 2021 — the Shadyside original has since closed, so this is now the only location, which is worth knowing because much of the writing about Con Alma describes a different building. It has three owners with three jobs: Josh Ross, executive chef, thirty years in restaurants; John Shannon, a Pittsburgh native and Berklee graduate who curates the music; and Aimee Marshall, beverage director and general manager, who has been in the restaurant community since she was a teenager and listening to Pittsburgh jazz since she moved here at seventeen. Marshall describes the concept as the whole eat, drink, jazz experience — they came up with that and the name at the very beginning. Esquire named it one of the 27 best bars in America in 2021. The food is Latin-leaning and serious: bluefin tuna crudo and tamarind-glazed shrimp at $28, lechon at $38, lomo saltado at $34, a jerk platter at $36, jerk jackfruit roti at $24 for the vegetarians.

The non-alcoholic section is headed, in the restaurant's own slightly mistyped words, "non-alcholic drinks", and it is unusually well constructed for a music venue. Two are built cocktails: the N/A Painkiller, with coconut cream, orange, pineapple and nutmeg, and the N/A Mojito at $10 with fresh mint, lime, sugar and Topo Chico. Then there is a wine and beer line — Eins-Zwei-Zero 0% sparkling Riesling at $12, a Bravas non-alcoholic golden ale at $6, and a rotating non-alcoholic beer worth asking about. Most usefully, there is a shelf of zero-proof spirits sold on their own at $8 or $9: Free Spirits gin, bourbon and tequila, the bitter Dr Zero Zero AmarNo, and Pentire Coastal Spritz. That last group is what makes the room work for a non-drinker, because it means the bar can build you almost anything rather than pouring from a fixed list. One practical thing to budget for: a per-person music charge is added during live sets — $10 on Thursday and Sunday, $15 on Friday and Saturday, $5 in the bar and lounge.
venues.pressQuote: The whole eat, drink, jazz experience. We came up with that and the name in the beginning.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Aimee Marshall, owner and beverage director

venues.name: Connaught Bar
venues.description: The Connaught Bar in Mayfair, repeatedly ranked the world's best bar, gives its non-alcoholic drinking the same rigour as its celebrated martini trolley. The menu carries a dedicated 'Innocence' section, and the current Synergia list runs three from-scratch alcohol-free cocktails — one per chapter — built on a stocked range of non-alcoholic spirits and botanicals, such as The Chill Out with house chilli syrup and passion fruit.

venues.longDescription:
Opened in 2008 inside the Connaught hotel on Carlos Place in Mayfair, the Connaught Bar was conceived as a deliberate break from the stuffy, museum-like grand-hotel bar. The room is the work of the late David Collins and his studio: an Art Deco-inspired space of textured platinum silver-leaf walls, dark leather banquettes, marble floors and mirrored panels arranged around a cool grey bar, its 1920s cubist aesthetic softened by candlelight. Presiding over it since the beginning is Agostino "Ago" Perrone, the Connaught's director of mixology, who became one of the defining figures of modern hotel bartending. The bar has appeared in the World's 50 Best Bars ranking every year since 2010, was named the world's best bar in both 2020 and 2021, and held Europe's best-bar title in consecutive years.

Its signature ceremony is the martini trolley — a gleaming black-and-chrome cart wheeled tableside, from which a bartender builds your martini to order, letting you choose the gin, the degree of dilution and a spritz from a line-up of house-made aromatic bitters. The drinks list is presented as a themed, seasonally rotating "book" of chapters rather than a straight menu, mixing signature creations, reworked classics and rare vintage serves; prices run from the merely expensive to the famous £1,000-plus 1893 Sidecar.

Crucially for non-drinkers, the no-alcohol drinks are treated as first-class cocktails rather than an afterthought: recent chaptered menus have carried a dedicated zero-proof serve within each chapter, and the bar's Phaidon recipe book, "Cocktail Recipes and Iconic Creations", includes roughly a dozen alcohol-free builds among its 100 recipes. The house style leans on fermented and infused ingredients rather than off-the-shelf non-alcoholic spirits. The Glossy is poured a coppery red to echo the room's palette and layers red-berry kombucha, milk oolong tea, Amalfi lemon-leaf syrup and pink grapefruit juice; The Smooth Mover is a lighter, savoury-leaning blend of salted cacao coconut water, eucalyptus syrup and lime juice. Expect the same trolley-side theatre, glassware and garnish work given to the alcoholic list, at broadly comparable prices.
venues.pressQuote: What you're paying for, though, is a unique experience in one of the best bars in London – if not the world.

venues.name: Copper & Kings Rooftop Bar
venues.description: The rooftop bar and restaurant on the third floor of the Copper & Kings distillery in Butchertown looks out over downtown Louisville and the Ohio River, and keeps a named non-alcoholic list rather than a single token option. The Lavender Sky is a vanilla lavender lemonade; Movin' To The Country runs peach purée with pineapple, lime and ginger beer; and the Jazz Ensemble is a Topo Chico built to order with the flavours you choose, which makes it one of the few genuinely customisable alcohol-free drinks in the city. The distillery itself is ranked among Louisville's most-visited attractions, so the rooftop functions as a destination as much as a bar.
signatureDrinks: Movin' To The Country (peach purée, pineapple, lime, ginger beer)
Jazz Ensemble (Topo Chico with customisable flavours)
venues.longDescription:
Butchertown is the old meatpacking district east of downtown, now one of Louisville's better eating neighbourhoods, and Copper & Kings occupies a distillery building on East Washington Street in the middle of it. The distillery makes brandy and gin rather than bourbon, which already makes it an outlier in this city, and its rooftop — a bar and restaurant on the third floor with views across downtown and out to the Ohio River — is consistently ranked among Louisville's most-visited things to do.

For a non-drinker the rooftop is one of the more comfortable rooms in the guide, because the alcohol-free drinks are named on the menu and built rather than improvised. The Lavender Sky is a vanilla lavender lemonade, which sounds simple and lands aromatic. Movin' To The Country is the substantial one — peach purée with pineapple, lime and ginger beer, so it has the length and the bite that a tall alcoholic drink would. The Jazz Ensemble is the interesting structural choice: a Topo Chico built with flavours the guest picks, which means the non-alcoholic guest gets to make a decision rather than accept whatever the kitchen sends. Very few bars in any city extend that courtesy.

Practical considerations. This is a rooftop in a city with real winters and real summer humidity, so the experience varies sharply by season and rooftop hours are published separately from the rest of the building — check before travelling. The distillery below runs tours, which are worth knowing about in both directions: they are interesting, and they are tastings, so if a distillery tour is not something you want to be inside of, go straight up. Butchertown puts three other entries in this guide within a few hundred metres — Cultured Cheese Shop and Pizza Lupo are both walkable from the door.
venues.pressQuote: Lavender Sky: vanilla lavender lemonade. Movin' To The Country: peach puree, pineapple, lime, ginger beer. Jazz Ensemble: Topo Chico with customizable flavors.

venues.name: Copper Common
venues.description: A downtown craft cocktail bar and gastropub from chef Ryan Lowder, part of his CO Hospitality group alongside The Copper Onion. Opened in 2014 in the former Plum Alley space and rebooted as "Copper Common 2.0" in 2022, it was named Salt Lake magazine's 2025 Best Restaurant. Its bartenders treat alcohol-free orders with the same care as the acclaimed cocktail list: the signature move is "mocktail roulette," a bartender's-choice non-alcoholic cocktail they'll also tailor to your taste, backed by a low-ABV menu for those on the fence — making it a consistent pick among the city's best for alcohol-free drinking.
venues.address: 111 E Broadway Ste 190, Salt Lake City, UT 84111
venues.longDescription:
Copper Common is the more intimate sibling to chef Ryan Lowder's nearby Copper Onion, drawing on his New York City fine-dining background. Salt Lake magazine, which named it 2025 Best Restaurant, describes it as offering pours from a distinctively unique natural wine list backed by always inventive craft cocktails.

Local press repeatedly singles out its alcohol-free options: City Cast Salt Lake's mocktail roundup recommends the bartender's-choice "mocktail roulette" and notes the bar will tailor a non-alcoholic drink to your taste and keeps a low-ABV menu for those on the fence.
venues.pressQuote: Copper Common makes great drinks all around and the alcohol-free ones are no exception. I always go with the mocktail roulette which is bartender's choice, but if you ask nicely they'll make something tailored to your taste. They also offer a low-ABV menu if you're on the fence.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Terina Ria, City Cast Salt Lake
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: City Cast Salt Lake, "The Best Mocktails in Salt Lake," 2025

venues.name: Copra
venues.description: Copra is a coastal South Indian restaurant that opened in 2023 in San Francisco's Fillmore / Lower Pac Heights neighborhood, led by Michelin-starred chef Srijith "Sri" Gopinathan, drawing on the cuisines of Kerala and Tamil Nadu. Alongside a full cocktail and wine program, Copra runs a serious zero-proof menu that mirrors its cocktail list, building drinks from the same Southeast Asian-leaning pantry — coconut yogurt, makrut lime, star anise, lemongrass, and orange blossom — rather than treating non-alcoholic options as an afterthought. Several of the zero-proof cocktails are built on non-alcoholic spirits including Wilderton Lustre and Vibrante NA vermouth. Named pours include the Orange Ruby (lemongrass, Wilderton Lustre, Vibrante, orange blossom, tonic, makrut lime), the Salty City (coconut yogurt, cucumber, salt, black garlic, lemon), and the Tiger's Eye (cinnamon, star anise, lemon, Wilderton Lustre, bittersweet aperitivo). The room is a tropical, design-forward space.
venues.longDescription:
Copra is a coastal South Indian restaurant that opened in 2023 at 1700 Fillmore Street, on the edge of the Fillmore and Lower Pacific Heights, under Michelin-starred chef Srijith "Sri" Gopinathan. The cooking draws on Kerala and Tamil Nadu — coconut, curry leaf, tamarind, black pepper and seafood — and the dining room is a tropical, design-forward space that reads closer to a bar than a formal restaurant. It arrived in a crowded year on the Fillmore corridor and was singled out by The San Francisco Standard as "one of 2023's sexiest new arrivals on the scene." Service runs dinner nightly with weekend lunch, and the bar is a destination in its own right rather than a holding pen for the dining room.

Copra's non-alcoholic list is built rather than bought. Instead of stocking a few dealcoholized bottles and calling it a programme, the bar works from the same Southeast Asian-leaning pantry as the kitchen and the full cocktail menu — coconut yogurt, makrut lime, star anise, lemongrass, black garlic and orange blossom — using non-alcoholic spirits as a base rather than as the whole idea. Named zero-proof pours include the Orange Ruby (lemongrass, Wilderton Lustre, Vibrante non-alcoholic vermouth, orange blossom, tonic and makrut lime), the Salty City (coconut yogurt, cucumber, salt, black garlic and lemon) and the Tiger's Eye (cinnamon, star anise, lemon, Wilderton Lustre and a bittersweet aperitivo). The three cover distinct territory: one bright and floral, one savoury and saline, one bitter and warm-spiced, which is why they hold up across a full meal of assertive food rather than all reading as sweet. Writing in The San Francisco Standard on 31 December 2023, Astrid Kane placed Copra on the city's short list of serious alcohol-free destinations, reporting that "Copra also has a significant NA cocktail program, with three standouts designed to appeal to the widest range of palates." Because the zero-proof list mirrors the cocktail list course for course, a non-drinker can eat a full dinner here without ever being handed a soda.
venues.pressQuote: Copra also has a significant NA cocktail program, with three standouts designed to appeal to the widest range of palates.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Astrid Kane, The San Francisco Standard

venues.name: Coral Club
venues.description: Coral Club is a coastal- and tiki-inspired cocktail bar above a strip mall on Gallatin Avenue in East Nashville, opened in May 2024. It was founded by four hospitality veterans: brothers Aaron and Matthew Izaguirre (from the Florida Keys) and partners Brice Hoffman and Kristopher Esqueda, whose résumés include The Patterson House, The Catbird Seat, Saison, and Bastion. The space features a stone bar, a dimly lit lounge, and an open-air rooftop patio, with snacks like black truffle popcorn and tinned fish. The drink menu is organized into Standards, House, and a dedicated Zero-Proof section that co-owner Kristopher Esqueda says "doesn't feel like an afterthought." Confirmed zero-proof options include the Neo-Tropical (Giffard N/A Aperitivo, pineapple, ginger, lime soda), the Chaise Lounge (coconut water, cucumber, lime, soda), a St. Agrestis Phony Negroni, Sanbitter, and Corona 0%.
signatureDrinks: Neo-Tropical (Giffard N/A Aperitivo, pineapple, ginger, lime soda)
Chaise Lounge (coconut water, cucumber, lime, soda)
venues.longDescription:
Coral Club opened in May 2024 above a strip mall on Gallatin Avenue in East Nashville, and the unpromising address is part of the appeal — you climb the stairs into a coastal- and tiki-inspired room with a stone bar, a dim lounge and an open-air rooftop patio. It was founded by four hospitality veterans: brothers Aaron and Matthew Izaguirre, who grew up in the Florida Keys, with partners Brice Hoffman and Kristopher Esqueda, whose collective résumés run through The Patterson House, The Catbird Seat, Saison and Bastion. That is a serious set of kitchens and bars, and the drinks reflect it. Snacks run to black truffle popcorn and tinned fish.

The menu is organised into three sections — Standards, House, and a dedicated Zero-Proof list — and the structural point is that the spirit-free drinks sit as a named section of the same menu rather than on a separate card. Co-owner Kristopher Esqueda's own summary of the intent is the useful line: the zero-proof section "doesn't feel like an afterthought." The confirmed builds bear it out. The Neo-Tropical is built on Giffard's non-alcoholic aperitivo with pineapple, ginger and lime soda, giving a non-drinker access to the bitter-tropical register that tiki bars almost never offer without rum. The Chaise Lounge is lighter and more refreshing, combining coconut water, cucumber, lime and soda. Alongside those the bar stocks a St. Agrestis Phony Negroni, Sanbitter — the Italian non-alcoholic bitter aperitif that has been around far longer than the current category — and Corona 0%.

Open daily from 4pm to 1am, which is a genuine late schedule, and the rooftop makes it a legitimate destination rather than a fallback. For East Nashville, it is one of the strongest places to spend an evening without drinking.
venues.pressQuote: [The zero-proof section] doesn't feel like an afterthought.

venues.name: Cordelia
venues.description: Cordelia opened in 2022 at 2058 East Fourth Street, the downtown block that has carried Cleveland's restaurant reputation for two decades, from chef Vinnie Cimino and co-owner Andrew Watts. Cimino describes the cooking as Midwest melting pot meets modern grandma — a celebration of the region's farmers run through the immigrant home cooking the city was built on — and the recognition arrived fast: Cleveland Magazine named it Best New Restaurant in 2023, Cimino was a James Beard Award finalist, and Food & Wine made him a Best New Chef in 2025. Rather than keeping a token mocktail list, the bar rebuilds cocktails from the main menu using Lyre's and Seedlip and its own syrups, at the same prices as the originals.
signatureDrinks: 3 Dope Boyz In A Cadillac (Lyre's American Malt, Lyre's Amaretti, apple cider, ginger beer, lemon, candied ginger)
venues.longDescription:
Cordelia opened in 2022 at 2058 East Fourth Street, the downtown block that has carried Cleveland's restaurant reputation for two decades, from chef Vinnie Cimino and co-owner Andrew Watts. Cimino describes the cooking as Midwest melting pot meets modern grandma — a celebration of the region's farmers, run through the immigrant home cooking the city was built on — and the recognition arrived fast: Cleveland Magazine named it Best New Restaurant in 2023, Cimino was a James Beard Award finalist, and Food & Wine put him on its Best New Chefs list in 2025, calling the restaurant an unabashed homage to Cleveland. The pair have since announced a second restaurant in the former Alea space in Ohio City. The dining room does dinner Tuesday through Saturday, a Sunday brunch, and a "Bellie Up" tasting menu for anyone who wants the full run.

The bar programme is held to the kitchen's standard and treats zero-proof as a build rather than a substitution. Instead of keeping a short separate list, the team makes non-alcoholic versions of cocktails from the main menu, leaning on Lyre's and Seedlip alongside the house-made syrups and shrubs already in use behind the bar. The reference drink is the 3 Dope Boyz In A Cadillac at $17 — Lyre's American Malt and Lyre's Amaretti with apple cider, ginger beer and fresh lemon, finished with candied ginger — which reads as a long autumn whiskey drink rather than a spiced soda, and which Cleveland Magazine used as one of the city's benchmarks in its 2026 mocktail guide.

The pricing is the clearest signal of intent: at $17 the zero-proof drink sits level with the alcoholic list rather than being discounted into afterthought territory, and it is made with the same number of steps. Valet parking is validated at $14, which matters on East Fourth on an event night.
venues.pressQuote: Using Lyre's and Seedlip with house-made syrups, the bar team creates nonalcoholic versions, including the 3 Dope Boyz In A Cadillac.

venues.name: CORK, The Wine Shop at COOK
venues.description: CORK, The Wine Shop at COOK is a curated bottle shop on South 20th Street near Rittenhouse Square, opened in fall 2020 by restaurateur Audrey Claire Taichman in the space of her Audrey Claire COOK demonstration kitchen, whose cooking classes have been paused since. Alongside 120-plus hard-to-find wines, vermouths, ciders, and bottled cocktails, CORK has built one of the Philadelphia region's largest non-alcoholic selections, branding itself "Dry Bar Headquarters." Per a 2023 Philadelphia Inquirer feature, buyer Michelle Flisek said the store carries more than 100 varieties of zero-proof items, including Ritual Zero Proof spirits, Lyre's Aperitif Rosso, Spiritless tequila alternative, and canned Ghia apéritifs. The shop's own "Zero Proof Selections" guide also highlights Curious Elixir No. 4 and TÖST sparkling. Rounding out the inventory are mixers, bitters, snacks, and barware — a top regional source for NA bottles rather than a dedicated alcohol-free venue.
venues.longDescription:
CORK began in fall 2020, when Audrey Claire Taichman turned the space of her Audrey Claire COOK demonstration kitchen, on South 20th Street near Rittenhouse Square, into a bottle shop. COOK's cooking classes have been paused since, and CORK trades in the same room. Alongside more than a hundred and twenty hard-to-find wines, vermouths, ciders and bottled cocktails, it has assembled one of the Philadelphia region's largest non-alcoholic ranges and brands itself, without hedging, Dry Bar Headquarters.

A 2023 Philadelphia Inquirer feature put the figure at more than a hundred varieties of zero-proof stock, including Ritual Zero Proof spirits and Lyre's Aperitif Rosso. What matters as much as the number is where those bottles sit. This is a wine shop with a serious wine list, and the non-alcoholic range lives inside it rather than in a separate aisle — so choosing an alcohol-free bottle happens in the same conversation, with the same staff, as choosing a wine.

That conversation is the shop's actual product. The Inquirer quoted buyer Michelle Flisek's opening question to customers: what flavour profiles are you looking to enjoy? It is a small line and an unusually good one. Most non-alcoholic retail is organised around what a product replaces — the gin substitute, the wine alternative — which frames every purchase as a compromise against something better. Asking what someone wants to taste instead treats the category as a set of drinks in their own right, and it is a far more useful way to find something you will actually enjoy.

Open every day, eleven in the morning until eight at night.
venues.pressQuote: What flavor profiles are you looking to enjoy?
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Michelle Flisek, CORK buyer, in The Philadelphia Inquirer

venues.name: Corner Club
venues.description: Corner Club is an all-day cafe and neighborhood bar in Old Seminole Heights that runs one of Tampa's most developed zero-proof menus - a titled Mocktails section of five named builds plus an N/A Beverages fridge of non-alcoholic beer, wine and kombucha. Several builds use Lyre's non-alcoholic spirits, including Orange You Glad It's N/A (Lyre's Italian Orange, chamomile-ginger syrup, elderflower tonic, soda) and a Nahmaretto Sour (Lyre's Amaretto, lemon, sugar), alongside the spice-forward Jalapeno Business, an N/A Gria rebuilt on non-alcoholic wine, and a Bees Knees on non-alcoholic gin. Five named builds on real NA spirits plus a stocked fridge puts this well ahead of most neighbourhood bars anywhere in the country. One caveat worth stating plainly: the same N/A Beverages list carries a Recess CBD seltzer and an Aryloom CBD/THC drink, which are alcohol-free but not non-intoxicating.

venues.longDescription:
Corner Club occupies a former neighbourhood tavern on East Sligh Avenue in Old Seminole Heights, reopened under new ownership after a full renovation and now running as an all-day cafe and bar rather than the tavern it replaced. That shift in format is what produced one of the most developed zero-proof menus in Tampa: a room that opens for coffee and stays open for cocktails has to serve people across the whole day, including the many hours when drinking is not the point.

The alcohol-free list is a named section - Mocktails - rather than a footnote, and several builds run on Lyre's non-alcoholic spirits. Orange You Glad It's N/A pairs Lyre's Italian Orange with a chamomile-ginger syrup, elderflower tonic and soda; the Nahmaretto Sour is Lyre's Amaretto with lemon and sugar, shaken to the texture the name implies; the Bees Knees uses a non-alcoholic gin with lime and honey; and the N/A Gria rebuilds the bar's sangria on non-alcoholic wine with orange juice, grapefruit and cinnamon. Jalapeno Business is the outlier and the most interesting - a strawberry-jalapeno shrub with lemon, basil, spiced orange, ginger ale and soda, which is a genuinely savoury drink rather than a sweet one. Behind the cocktails sits an N/A Beverages fridge holding Lagunitas Hoppy Refresher, Lagunitas IPNA, kombucha and non-alcoholic wine by the glass.

Five named builds on real NA spirits, plus a stocked fridge, puts this well ahead of most neighbourhood bars anywhere, and it is the reason a venue in a residential pocket of Seminole Heights earns a place beside downtown cocktail rooms.

Practical notes: it functions as a cafe by day and a bar by evening, so the crowd and the volume change substantially depending on when you arrive. It is a licensed bar - the mocktail section is a real and unusually deep part of the menu, not the character of the room. The same N/A Beverages list also stocks a Recess CBD seltzer and an Aryloom CBD/THC drink; both are alcohol-free but psychoactive, so anyone avoiding intoxicants rather than alcohol specifically should order around them. Parking is on-street and the block is residential, so arrive expecting to walk a little.
venues.pressQuote: residents of Tampa's Old Seminole Heights neighborhood once again walked back through the doors on Monday
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Creative Loafing Tampa Bay, April 2021, on the reopening

venues.name: Cosmic Coffee + Cocktails
venues.description: Cosmic Coffee + Cocktails is a large South Austin garden bar and coffee house built around a landscaped outdoor space with food trucks, native planting and a pond, and it runs from 8am to late every day — which is what makes it genuinely useful to a non-drinker. The same counter that pulls espresso in the morning builds zero-proof cocktails at night, including a Zero-Proof Espresso Martini that bridges the two, and Liquid Sunshine, a pitaya-based energy elixir. Because coffee, kombucha and cocktails share one menu here, ordering something alcohol-free carries none of the social friction of a bar that treats it as a special request.
venues.longDescription:
Cosmic Coffee + Cocktails occupies a deep lot off Pickle Road in South Austin and is closer to a landscaped park than a bar: native plantings, a pond, shaded seating, resident food trucks, and a building that works as a coffee house by day and a bar by night. It opens at 8am seven days a week and runs to 10pm or midnight depending on the day, which gives it an unusually long useful window.

That all-day structure is the reason it belongs in an alcohol-free guide. Most bars force a non-drinker into a specific transaction: asking what can be made without alcohol, usually late in the evening, usually from a short list. At Cosmic the same counter serves espresso, kombucha, beer, cocktails and zero-proof drinks from one menu across the whole day, so the alcohol-free order is simply an order. For anyone in early sobriety, or a designated driver, or someone who just wants to sit outside for three hours without drinking, the absence of that friction matters more than the length of the mocktail list.

The zero-proof drinks themselves are properly built rather than sweetened. The Zero-Proof Espresso Martini is the natural signature for a venue that roasts and pulls its own coffee — it uses the espresso program as the drink's backbone, which is exactly how the alcoholic version works. Liquid Sunshine is a pitaya-based energy elixir, leaning on the functional-drinks side of the menu, and reads as bright and fruit-forward rather than dessert-sweet. Visit Austin's official zero-proof guide names both.

The garden is the draw in practice. It fills up on warm evenings, dogs are common, and the food trucks mean a group can settle in for a full evening without anyone needing to drink to justify staying. Because the site is outdoors and family-tolerant during daylight, it also solves the harder version of the problem — the sober afternoon, where most bar-shaped options simply do not exist.

One honest note on grading: this is a licensed venue with a full cocktail list, not an alcohol-free space, and the zero-proof menu is a section rather than the whole card. It earns a 4 on the strength of the named builds and the all-day structure, not because alcohol is absent. Anyone who needs a room with no alcohol in it at all is better served by Austin's dedicated venues — Sans Bar and Taano House are both listed in this guide.
venues.pressQuote: Cosmic Coffee & Cocktails: Zero-Proof Espresso Martini; Liquid Sunshine (pitaya energy elixir).

venues.name: Cosmic Roots
venues.description: Cosmic Roots is a fully alcohol-free kava and tea house tucked inside Ferndale's Pavilion Street Market food hall, the only non-food stall among the market's vendors. Owner Isabel Cali, a certified alchemical herbalist, pours traditional South Pacific kava garnished with pineapple alongside house-blended iced teas like Summa'love (hibiscus, yerba mate, rose hips) and Mint Marshmelli (marshmallow root, lemon balm, spearmint), plus a Mexi Mushie Mocha built on fermented cacao and medicinal mushrooms. There's no alcohol anywhere on the premises — just kava, cacao, chai, and loose-leaf herbal tea, mixed to order.
signatureDrinks: Kava (traditional South Pacific root, served with pineapple garnish)
Summa'love (hibiscus, yerba mate, rose hips, rose petals, lavender, butterfly pea)
Mint Marshmelli (marshmallow root, lemon balm, spearmint, lavender, butterfly pea)
Mexi Mushie Mocha (fermented cacao, medicinal mushroom blend, chili, Ceylon cinnamon)
venues.longDescription:
Cosmic Roots opened at the tail end of March 2026 as part of the grand opening of Pavilion Street Market, a food hall built inside the former Treat Dreams space at 22965 Woodward Avenue in Downtown Ferndale. Of the market's stalls — which also include a travel-inspired vegan kitchen, a dumpling concept, and a Venezuelan arepa bar — Cosmic Roots is the lone non-food vendor, built entirely around alcohol-free kava, tea, and cacao.

The anchor drink is kava, a root native to Fiji, Papua New Guinea, Samoa, Tonga, and Vanuatu, served here with a pineapple garnish. It reads like a slightly bitter, earthy tea, and brings on a tongue-tingling relaxation and mellow, giddy calm that lasts 40 minutes to an hour — with none of the intoxication of alcohol. Alongside it, Isabel Cali runs a rotating menu of house-blended herbal teas, including the hibiscus-and-yerba-mate Summa'love and the marshmallow-root Mint Marshmelli, plus Masala Chai, golden milk, and a Mexi Mushie Mocha made from fermented cacao and a medicinal mushroom blend with chili and Ceylon cinnamon. Chocolate truffles infused with medicinal mushrooms and scones round out the food side.

Cali is a certified alchemical herbalist trained at the School of Evolutionary Herbalism, with a background in yoga, somatic plant-medicine integration, and Peruvian shamanic lineage work. She first tried kava at 18 during a trip to Florida and came home telling herself Detroit needed a kava bar; after formal herbalism training, she sold herbal teas and kava at Detroit-area farmers markets before opening a permanent home for it at Pavilion Street Market. "Detroit needs a kava bar, we need spaces like this," she told MI Foodie Adventures in June 2026.

The space doubles as a small community hub, hosting pop-ups like tea-and-tarot readings and watercolor nights inside the market. In a neighborhood built around bars and breweries, Cosmic Roots is a genuine alcohol-free alternative — not a mocktail bolted onto a liquor list, but a bar built from the ground up without alcohol.
venues.pressQuote: Detroit needs a kava bar, we need spaces like this.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Isabel Cali, owner of Cosmic Roots

venues.name: Counter Culture
venues.description: Counter Culture is a plant-based restaurant and bar in South Tampa's Palma Ceia area, with a seasonal vegetarian menu and a small but real zero-proof program. Its two mocktails — the Sophia (Seedlip Spice, ginger beer, blueberry-rosemary shrub) and the Bikini Bottom (pineapple, passion fruit, lime, orgeat, ginger ale) — sit alongside a non-alcoholic German wheat beer. The menu rotates with the seasons, so the named drinks change.  A house-made shrub in a two-drink list is the tell: nobody makes one for a menu they are not taking seriously. Dinner from 4pm, brunch from 8am at weekends, which makes it one of South Tampa's more useful daytime rooms.
venues.address: 2909 W Bay to Bay Blvd, Tampa, FL 33629
signatureDrinks: Sophia (Seedlip Spice, ginger beer, blueberry-rosemary shrub)
Bikini Bottom (pineapple, passion fruit, lime, orgeat, ginger ale)
venues.longDescription:
Counter Culture is a plant-based restaurant and bar on West Bay to Bay Boulevard in the Palma Ceia area of South Tampa, running a seasonal vegetarian menu that changes as produce does. That rotation is worth knowing about in advance, because it applies to the drinks as well as the plates: the named mocktails move with the seasons, so the specific builds listed here are a snapshot rather than a fixture.

The zero-proof programme is small and genuine rather than large and decorative. Two named builds have anchored it — the Sophia, which sets Seedlip Spice against ginger beer and a house blueberry-rosemary shrub, and the Bikini Bottom, a tropical build of pineapple, passion fruit, lime, orgeat and ginger ale. A non-alcoholic German wheat beer sits alongside for anyone who would rather have a beer with dinner. A house-made shrub in a two-drink list is the tell: nobody makes a shrub for a menu they are not taking seriously, because it is work that has to be repeated every week.

The wider fit is straightforward. A restaurant whose entire kitchen is built around what people choose not to eat is, unsurprisingly, a comfortable room for someone choosing not to drink. The two decisions run on the same social logic, and the staff are unlikely to treat either as an inconvenience.

Practical notes: dinner runs from 4pm and brunch from 8am at weekends, which makes it one of the more useful daytime options in South Tampa. It is a licensed restaurant with a full bar, so the alcohol-free list is a section rather than the whole offering — and because the menu is seasonal, it is worth checking the current list rather than arriving set on a particular drink.  The room seats fewer than it looks from the street, so weekends are worth booking.
venues.pressQuote: One of the trendiest places in Tampa offers three tasty mocktails on their menu!
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: WiLD 94.1, 9 Tasty Mocktails in the Tampa Bay Area, January 2026

venues.name: The Coupe & Flute
venues.description: The Coupe & Flute is an art-deco "champagne tavern" at 3015 Beacon Ave S on Beacon Hill, opened in June 2022 by married couple Brooke St. Sauver and Curt Waller in a shuttered travel agency. Neither is a trained sommelier, which is rather the point — their aim was a down-to-earth, accessible room, and Waller has said it feels like a little piece of Europe landed in Seattle. It runs a genuinely carbonation-forward non-alcoholic list under its own "Zero Proof" heading: Scarlet Pimpernel ($16, Giffard aperitif, pomegranate molasses, pineapple), Garden Party ($15, infused tropical botanicals, lime, honey), We Got the Beet ($15, beet juice, Wilderton Citrus, orgeat, lime, soda), Bitter Patience ($15, a non-alcoholic Negroni on Giffard, Wilderton and Pathfinder), Mt. Kamigami ($14, matcha syrup, orange, lime, soda) and the Dirty Divino ($14, Grove non-alcoholic vermouth, olive brine, soda). Crucially for a champagne bar, it pours a de-alcoholised sparkling wine by the glass and bottle — Vinada N/A Chardonnay, $13 and $42. Fremont's non-alcoholic IPA is $8. Brunch at weekends; closed Mondays.

venues.longDescription:
The Coupe & Flute took over a shuttered travel agency on Beacon Hill in June 2022 and turned it into what its owners call a champagne tavern — an art-deco room lined with sparkling wine, run by Brooke St. Sauver and Curt Waller, a married couple, neither of whom is a trained sommelier. That last fact is deliberate rather than a gap. Waller's description of the intent is the best summary of the place: they are down to earth and very accessible, they wanted a space that felt like an extension of their home, and he likes to say it feels like a little piece of Europe landed in Seattle. There is something about champagne, he adds, that makes it feel like you are treating yourself. The kitchen is more ambitious than the word tavern suggests — deviled tea eggs at $10, Dungeness crab cakes at $28, kimchi arancini at $16, a French onion soup at $16, and caviar service running from $112 to $182 — plus weekend brunch with a braised duck benedict at $22.

The non-alcoholic list is the most carbonation-led in the city, which makes complete sense in a bar built on bubbles. It sits under its own Zero Proof heading and runs six or seven deep. Bitter Patience at $15 is a non-alcoholic Negroni assembled from three separate products — Giffard aperitif, Wilderton Citrus and Pathfinder — rather than one bottled shortcut, and it is the ambitious one. The Dirty Divino at $14 is the closest thing here to a dirty martini, built as a highball from Grove non-alcoholic vermouth with olive brine and soda. We Got the Beet at $15 puts beet juice and orgeat against Wilderton Citrus and lime. Mt. Kamigami at $14 is matcha syrup with orange, lime and soda. Scarlet Pimpernel and Garden Party round it out at $16 and $15. But the single most important item for a non-drinker in a champagne bar is the wine itself, and there is one: Vinada de-alcoholised Chardonnay, poured by the glass at $13 and by the bottle at $42 — which means you can share a bottle at the table like everyone else. Fremont's non-alcoholic IPA is $8. Names on this list rotate, so check the board.
venues.pressQuote: We call ourselves a champagne tavern. We're down to earth, very accessible… I like to say it feels like a little piece of Europe landed in Seattle.

venues.name: Coupes
venues.description: Coupes is a champagne bar at The Shops of Highland Park (on Oak Lawn Ave) that builds its craft mocktails on real zero-proof spirits rather than sugary stand-ins. Its named non-alcoholic cocktails include The Resolution, made with Martini & Rossi Floreal, cranberry, lime, ginger beer, and orgeat, and the Sparkling Conviction, made with blood orange, lemon, Lyre's Classico, and All the Bitter zero-proof aromatic bitters, alongside a spirit-free Aperol-style spritz. Because the whole room is built around bubbles, ordering a booze-free toast reads as native here rather than an afterthought. The zero-proof list was spotlighted by CultureMap and PaperCity for Dry January.
venues.hours: Mon closed; Tue-Thu 3pm-9pm; Fri-Sat 3pm-10pm; Sun closed
signatureDrinks: The Resolution — Martini & Rossi Floreal, cranberry, lime, ginger beer, orgeat
Sparkling Conviction — blood orange, lemon, Lyre's Classico, All the Bitter Zero-Proof Aromatic Bitters
Non-Alcoholic Aperol-Style Spritz — a zero-proof take on the classic spritz
venues.longDescription:
Coupes opened in early 2023 at The Shops of Highland Park, 4234 Oak Lawn Avenue, and was created by two champagne enthusiasts: Eric Chiappinelli, a law professor, and Amanda Hale, an attorney. Named for the coupe glass, the room is designed around bubbles, with a circular bar shaped like a coupe, custom mosaic tile, and lacquered Venetian plaster walls. The list runs to more than 100 labels of champagne and sparkling wine, with roughly 20 poured by the glass.

The non-alcoholic program leans on real zero-proof brands rather than syrup. The Resolution is built with Martini & Rossi Floreal, cranberry, lime, ginger beer, and orgeat, while the Sparkling Conviction pairs blood orange and lemon with Lyre's Classico and All the Bitter zero-proof aromatic bitters. The bar has also poured a non-alcoholic Aperol-style spritz as a spirit-free take on the classic. These builds were featured by CultureMap and PaperCity in their Dry January roundups, and reflect a bar that treats zero-proof drinks with the same care as its sparkling list.

Beyond the glass, Coupes offers small bites, caviar service, and brunch, and holds back a set of seats each evening for walk-in guests. It sits at the Oak Lawn edge of the Park Cities, minutes from Highland Park and Uptown.
venues.pressQuote: At The Shops of Highland Park, this popular new champagne bar has crafted a non-alcoholic Aperol Spritz for Dry January.

venues.name: The Cowfish Sushi Burger Bar
venues.description: A sushi-and-burger hybrid restaurant at Universal CityWalk known for its 'Burgushi' mashups, The Cowfish runs a small but genuinely crafted mocktail list built around fresh fruit, house syrups, and ginger beer.
signatureDrinks: Thyme After Time (thyme-infused simple syrup, lemon, muddled blueberries, Gosling's ginger beer)
Dragon Fruit Spritz (dragon fruit, lemongrass syrup, SanPellegrino Aranciata Rossa, lemon juice, Gosling's ginger beer)
Pineapple Princess (pineapple, yuzu, lemonade, SanPellegrino Aranciata)
venues.longDescription:
The Cowfish Sushi Burger Bar is a three-story, sushi-and-burger hybrid restaurant at Universal CityWalk that serves both gourmet burgers and made-to-order sushi - including its signature 'Burgushi' rolls that combine burger ingredients into sushi form. It sits at 6000 Universal Boulevard (Suite 700) in Orlando, along the entrance corridor between Universal Studios Florida and Islands of Adventure, with second- and third-floor dining rooms overlooking CityWalk.

The concept was founded in 2010 in Charlotte, North Carolina by Marcus Hall and Alan Springate, who combined two separate restaurant ideas - one sushi, one burgers - into a single menu. The Universal Orlando location, the brand's first inside a theme-park complex, officially opened at CityWalk in December 2014; a further location later opened at Universal Beijing Resort's CityWalk.

Its zero-proof drink list includes Thyme After Time (thyme-infused simple syrup, lemon, muddled blueberries, Gosling's ginger beer), inspired by then-general-manager Aaron Tang's grandmother's blueberry thyme tart recipe; the Dragon Fruit Spritz (dragon fruit, lemongrass syrup, SanPellegrino Aranciata Rossa, lemon juice, Gosling's ginger beer); and the Pineapple Princess (pineapple, yuzu, lemonade, SanPellegrino Aranciata). Tang told Universal's own Discover Universal blog that the team wanted 'something more elevated that is meant for grown-ups but does not have alcohol' - the mocktails are presented as a distinct section of the drink menu rather than an off-menu request, giving non-drinking guests a built-in reason to stop at CityWalk on the way in or out of the parks.

As with most CityWalk restaurants, closing time shifts seasonally with the complex's overall operating hours.
venues.pressQuote: This mocktail is inspired by Tang's very own grandmother's blueberry thyme tarts — yum!

venues.name: Craft Lounge
venues.description: Craft Lounge in Nampa keeps a Non-Alcoholic Old Fashioned and a Virgin Mule on its standing list. The Old Fashioned is the notable one, because it is the hardest classic to render without alcohol — the drink is essentially whiskey, sugar and bitters, so there is nowhere for a substitute to hide. A bar willing to put its name on one is making a real claim. With The Sick Stag a few minutes away, Craft Lounge gives the western end of the Treasure Valley a second option rather than a single point of failure. It keeps a sibling location in nearby Caldwell and serves from 3pm, closing at midnight on Friday and Saturday.
venues.longDescription:
Craft Lounge is on 11th Avenue South in Nampa, with a sibling location in nearby Caldwell, serving the western end of Idaho's Treasure Valley twenty-odd miles from downtown Boise.

Its two named alcohol-free drinks are a Non-Alcoholic Old Fashioned and a Virgin Mule, and the pairing is instructive because the two sit at opposite ends of difficulty. A Mule is easy: ginger beer and lime do nearly all the work and the vodka contributes almost nothing, so removing it costs very little. An Old Fashioned is the opposite and is arguably the hardest classic to attempt without alcohol. Strip it back and the drink is whiskey, sugar, bitters and ice — there is no citrus, no mixer, nothing to hide behind. Whatever stands in for the whiskey is fully exposed, which is why most bars will not attempt one.

Putting it on a printed menu is therefore a claim worth taking seriously, whether it is built on a non-alcoholic whiskey substitute or on tea, spice and bitters, which is the other common route. Either way somebody has spent time on it.

The practical value, as with The Sick Stag, is geographic. Nampa and Caldwell together hold well over a hundred and fifty thousand people, and the region's drinks writing barely acknowledges them. Two venues with named zero-proof options a few minutes apart mean a resident there has an actual choice on a given evening rather than one bar to hope is open. Hours are 3pm to 10pm through the week and to midnight on Friday and Saturday, closed Sundays. The Caldwell sibling extends the same offering a further ten minutes west, which is the closest thing the outer valley has to coverage.
venues.pressQuote: Craft Lounge is celebrated for its exceptional non-alcoholic menu
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: This Is Boise, The Boise Area's Best Non-Alcoholic Drinks and Mocktail Spots, January 2025

venues.name: Crafted Cocktail Bar
venues.description: Crafted Cocktail Bar is a small room on South Main in downtown Greenville trading on made-to-order drinks, and it surfaces consistently in searches for zero-proof cocktails in the city. It keeps early and short hours for a cocktail bar — 4pm to 9pm Monday through Thursday and to 10pm on Friday and Saturday, closed Sunday — which makes it an after-work stop rather than a late one, and a good first drink of an evening that continues elsewhere on the same block. This entry is graded conservatively: the alcohol-free offer is real but undocumented in detail.
venues.address: 116 A S Main St, Greenville, SC 29601
venues.longDescription:
Crafted is a narrow cocktail room on South Main in the middle of downtown Greenville, a few doors from the busier restaurants, working a made-to-order model rather than a long printed list.

This is the most conservatively graded entry in the Greenville guide and it is worth explaining why, because the reasoning applies to how the whole directory is built. Crafted appears reliably when you search for zero-proof cocktails in this city, and a bar of this type — small, bartender-led, built on technique — is very likely to make something good if asked. But likelihood is not evidence. There is no printed alcohol-free section this directory could read, no named build in the local coverage, and no non-alcoholic spirit confirmed on the back bar.

So it is listed at three, with no signature drinks, and with the recommendation to ask rather than to order. That is the honest position, and it is the same standard applied to a venue elsewhere in this session whose aggregator write-up promised sophisticated zero-proof pairings and turned out to mean soda and lime-ade.

What is genuinely useful about the room is its shape in an evening. It opens at 4pm and closes at 9pm Monday through Thursday, 10pm on Friday and Saturday — early by cocktail-bar standards. That makes it a first-drink venue rather than a destination, and it sits within two minutes' walk of UP on the Roof, Oak & Honey and STIR, all of which run later. For a non-drinker planning a night out, starting early somewhere small and moving on is often a more comfortable shape than committing to one loud room for four hours.

Closed Sunday.

venues.name: CrowBar
venues.description: CrowBar is the cocktail lounge and tasting room for Voliere Spirits, an all-women-owned distillery that opened in December 2025 in the former blacksmith shop of the historic Hamm's Brewery complex in Dayton's Bluff. Grete Bergland leads the drinks programme, and the zero-proof column is built with the same culinary approach as the rest of the list and priced at $8 — a flat rate across every non-alcoholic drink. The builds are savoury as often as sweet: one runs roasted strawberry and tomato with balsamic and champagne vinegar, caper, basil, aquafaba and prosciutto; another is charred citrus with baking spices, rosemary, lemon and soda water. House-made French and Italian sodas sit alongside.
venues.address: 704 Minnehaha Ave E, Saint Paul, MN 55106
venues.hours: Mon closed; Tue-Thu 5pm-11pm; Fri 4pm-11pm; Sat 2pm-12am; Sun closed
