Like...if I were wearing sweatpants today, I'd be sitting over there with the art freaks (roasted strawberry and tomato, balsamic and champagne vinegar, caper, basil, aquafaba, prosciutto)
I was half a virgin when I met him... (charred citrus, baking spices, rosemary, lemon, soda water)

venues.longDescription:
The Hamm's Brewery complex on Saint Paul's East Side has been slowly reoccupied over the past decade, and in December 2025 the former 11 Wells Spirits space — originally the brewery's blacksmith shop — became Voliere Spirits, an all-women-owned distillery making small-batch spirits on site, with CrowBar as its tasting room and cocktail lounge. Lead distiller Seth Reid, who had worked at 11 Wells, returned to run production. Grete Bergland runs the bar. Angie Littleton designed the room, and Mpls.St.Paul Magazine described the result in December 2025 as holding "a glorious wall of beer cans, twinkling trees sprouting up among leather couches; lampshades perched on mannequins; a 'confessional' booth with a rotary dial telephone." Food is currently ordered by QR code from neighbouring Saint Paul Brewing while CrowBar develops its own menu.

The non-alcoholic list is the reason it belongs on this site. Every zero-proof drink is $8 — flat, across the board — and the builds are as involved as anything on the alcoholic side. The most extreme is the one with the longest name, a savoury drink of roasted strawberry and tomato with balsamic and champagne vinegar, caper, basil, aquafaba and prosciutto, which is closer to a gazpacho than to a soft drink. Alongside it sit an orange, oat milk, vanilla and lemon build finished with frozen Greek yogurt balls; a charred-citrus drink with baking spices, rosemary, lemon and soda water; and a strawberry-lemon-rose slushie. Handcrafted French sodas with cream run to black cherry, raspberry, mango, grapefruit, lime and sour grape, with rotating Italian sodas a dollar cheaper. Mpls.St.Paul Magazine singled out Bergland's use of "a mocktail made with roasted red and golden beet shrub and Hungarian paprika," which gives a sense of the register. The bar is licensed and pours the distillery's own spirits, so this is not an alcohol-free venue — but the zero-proof column is genuinely part of the programme.
venues.pressQuote: a mocktail made with roasted red and golden beet shrub and Hungarian paprika

venues.name: Crumb & Spigot
venues.description: Crumb & Spigot is a gastropub and cocktail bar at 15322 Detroit Avenue in Lakewood, a few doors from Humble Wine Bar and the second room of a Chagrin Falls original. The format is wood-fired pizza with an unusually large share of the menu marked vegan and gluten-free — enough that it works as the default choice for a mixed group rather than as an accommodation bolted onto the end of the list. The bar built its non-alcoholic offering on purpose, the owners describing the aim as providing a different avenue versus just normal cocktails, and the drinks are constructed accordingly. The Sober Clover at $12 is a straight zero-proof reading of a clover club: grenadine, apple cider vinegar, citrus and egg white, shaken hard to a proper foam. Dinner six nights a week, closed Mondays, to 11pm on Fridays.
signatureDrinks: Sober Clover (grenadine, apple cider vinegar, citrus, egg white)
venues.longDescription:
Crumb & Spigot began on Chillicothe Road in Chagrin Falls and opened its Lakewood room at 15322 Detroit Avenue, a few doors from Humble Wine Bar on the same block. The format is a gastropub built around wood-fired pizza, with an unusually large share of the menu marked vegan and gluten-free — enough that it works as the default choice for a mixed group rather than as an accommodation bolted onto the end of the menu. The Lakewood room does dinner six nights a week, closing Mondays and running to 11pm on Fridays and Saturdays.

The non-alcoholic list exists because the ownership decided to build one, describing the aim as providing a different avenue versus just normal cocktails, and the drinks are constructed rather than poured. The Sober Clover, at $12, is the one Cleveland Magazine picked out in its 2026 mocktail guide: grenadine, apple cider vinegar, citrus and egg white, shaken hard so the egg white carries a proper foam and the vinegar supplies the acid bite that would normally come from gin. It is a straight zero-proof reading of a clover club and it works for the same reason the original does — texture and sourness carrying the drink rather than sugar. The rest of the zero-proof list rotates alongside the cocktail menu.

Because the brand operates in two places, the Lakewood and Chagrin Falls rooms keep separate phone numbers, hours and menus; Chagrin Falls is roughly twenty miles south-east and outside the Cleveland metro proper, so the Detroit Avenue address is the one listed here. Taken together with Humble, Sacred Waters and LBM, this stretch of Lakewood is the single strongest cluster for drinking well without alcohol in Greater Cleveland — four rooms, four different formats, all within a short walk.
venues.pressQuote: The Sober Clover ($12) is built from grenadine, apple cider vinegar, citrus and egg white.

venues.name: Crux Fermentation Project
venues.description: Crux brews the NØ MØ series in house — a genuine non-alcoholic line rather than a bought-in can, made with traditional brewing methods at under 0.5% ABV. The original NØ MØ IPA uses flaked oats, honey and crystal malts with Pacific Northwest Citra and Mosaic hops at about 30 calories, and the range has grown to include a hazy and a seasonal fresh hop release. The tasting room sits in a converted transmission shop with 28-plus taps, food carts, fire pits and a lawn facing the Cascades.
signatureDrinks: NØ MØ Non-Alcoholic IPA — under 0.5% ABV, ~30 calories; flaked oats, honey and crystal malts, Citra and Mosaic hops
NØ MØ Hazy IPA — non-alcoholic hazy
Fresh Hop NØ MØ — limited seasonal release
venues.longDescription:
Bend has more breweries per head than almost anywhere in America, and Crux is the one that took non-alcoholic beer seriously first. NØ MØ launched as a non-alcoholic IPA and has since grown into a series — which matters, because a brewery that makes one NA beer is running an experiment and a brewery that makes three is running a product line.

The beer itself is properly built rather than dealcoholised into blandness. It comes in under 0.5% ABV at roughly 30 calories, made using traditional brewing methods so the body and mouthfeel survive: flaked oats for texture, honey and crystal malts for backbone, and Citra and Mosaic hops grown in the Pacific Northwest for the citrus-and-tropical nose that makes it read as an IPA rather than as hop-flavoured water. The name is a nod to Crux's own Gimme Mo IPA, brewed with the same hop pair, and head brewer Cam O'Connor developed it through a long run of test batches rather than a single recipe. The line now includes a hazy version and, in autumn, a fresh hop release that uses just-harvested hops — a seasonal treatment almost never applied to non-alcoholic beer.

The tasting room is a converted AAMCO transmission shop near where Colorado Avenue, Industrial Way and Highway 97 meet, and it is one of the best rooms in Bend for a non-drinker precisely because nothing about the experience changes. There are more than 28 taps, a rotating cast of food carts, fire pits for the cold months and a wide lawn that looks straight at the Cascades at golden hour. You order at the same bar, sit in the same seat and watch the same sunset.

Cases of the NA releases are usually available to take away, which makes this a stocking-up stop as well as a drinking one — useful in a town where most people are heading out to a trail, a river or a mountain the next morning.
venues.pressQuote: their nømø series is packed with real hop character and zero compromise

venues.name: Cultured Cheese Shop
venues.description: Cultured is a locally, female-owned cheese and charcuterie bar in Butchertown, now operating inside the Copper & Kings building at the rooftop level after moving from its original East Main Street shop. It builds shared boards from farmstead cheeses and cured meats and serves them with a drinks list that includes named alcohol-free options — a Tart Cherry Old Fashioned, a Turmeric Ginger Mule and a Cucumber Aloe Margarita, built on mixers from the Louisville company Modica. It does not take reservations. Dine-in runs from 11am daily, to 6pm early in the week and 10pm Thursday through Saturday, with a separate to-go counter.
venues.longDescription:
Cultured began as a cheese and charcuterie bar at 1007 East Main Street in Butchertown and has since moved a few blocks east, into the Copper & Kings building at 1121 East Washington, where it now trades at rooftop level with views over the city. It is locally and female-owned, and the proposition is unchanged: farmstead cheeses, cured meats and shared boards, in a room designed for sitting for two hours rather than eating and leaving. It does not take reservations.

The drinks are the reason it is in this guide, and specifically the fact that the alcohol-free ones are named and built rather than improvised. The Tart Cherry Old Fashioned, the Turmeric Ginger Mule and the Cucumber Aloe Margarita all run on mixers from Modica, a Louisville company founded by JD Mitchell and Eric Wentworth — Wentworth came out of bartending and ownership at The Hub on Frankfort Avenue — whose mixes are built around superfoods, vitamins and electrolytes with up to 70% less sugar than conventional cocktail mixers. Roughly a third of Modica's customers use them for mocktails rather than cocktails, which is a rare case of a mixer company designing for both from the start. Pairing bitter, tart and vegetal alcohol-free drinks with a cheese board is also simply better than pairing a sweet mocktail with one.

One point of confusion worth flagging: aggregators still carry the original 1007 East Main listing, some marked MOVED and some not, so navigation apps may take you to an empty storefront. The correct address is 1121 East Washington Street, inside Copper & Kings. That co-location makes for an easy pairing — Copper & Kings' own rooftop bar keeps a separate named alcohol-free list including the Lavender Sky and Movin' To The Country — and puts two entries in this guide in one building, in a neighbourhood that already holds Pizza Lupo and Naïve.
venues.pressQuote: Tart Cherry Old Fashioned, Turmeric Ginger Mule and Cucumber Aloe Margarita, made with the Modica brand.

venues.name: Cultured South Fermentation Co.
venues.description: Cultured South Fermentation Co. is Georgia's first kombucha taproom, opened in May 2018 in the Lee + White warehouse district in the West End by Melanie Wade, who had been brewing Golda Kombucha since 2013. The taproom pours Golda on draught by the pint, flight, taste, growler and gelato float, and stocks water kefir and jun, the honey-fermented cousin of kombucha, alongside cold brew coffee and a cultured-foods counter of vegan cheeses, pickles and preserves. Readers should know the room is not fully alcohol-free: Cultured South also brews and serves Grandmother Hard Kombucha and kombucha cocktails, so the alcoholic and non-alcoholic taps sit on the same board and need to be asked about by name.
venues.longDescription:
Melanie Wade started selling Golda Kombucha in 2013 and spent five years working towards a room where people could drink it on draught. Cultured South opened on 20 May 2018 at 1038 White Street SW, a 1,200-square-foot unit in the Lee + White adaptive-reuse development in Atlanta's historic West End, on the BeltLine's Westside Trail. Atlanta Magazine covered the opening that April, reporting Wade's plan to start with six Golda flavours on tap — lavender lemon, peach ginger, strawberry mint, elderberry thyme, hibiscus blood orange and blackberry basil — and expand to ten lines rotating roughly twenty flavours. It was the first kombucha taproom in Georgia. Cultured South operates as the parent company for the fermentation side of the business and is the adopted home of Pure Abundance, the artisan vegan cheese line handmade and sold on site.

What you can drink there now spans the fermented spectrum: kombucha by the pint, flight, taste and growler, gelato floats built on it, water kefir, and jun — a lighter tea ferment made with honey instead of cane sugar. Apple Ginger Spice and a CBD Bluegrass kombucha are among the flavours the company currently promotes. Banjo cold brew coffee is on tap too, and the retail side sells local preserves, Doux South pickles, sourdough crackers and the Pure Abundance cheeses. The honest caveat, and the reason this is a four rather than a five: Cultured South is not an alcohol-free venue. It also brews Grandmother Hard Kombucha and mixes kombucha cocktails, and the hard and soft lines are poured from the same bar. Anyone avoiding alcohol should order by name and confirm, exactly as they would in a brewery taproom. With that said, the overwhelming majority of what is on offer is non-alcoholic, the room trades 11am to 7pm Tuesday through Sunday, and it is one of very few places on the Westside Trail where the default pour contains nothing.
venues.pressQuote: It's been my dream to have a taproom for kombucha.

venues.name: Cúrate Bar de Tapas
venues.description: Cúrate Bar de Tapas is a Spanish tapas restaurant at 13 Biltmore Avenue in downtown Asheville, founded in 2011 by chef Katie Button and Félix Meana. It won the James Beard Foundation's Outstanding Hospitality Award in 2022, Button has twice been a Best Chef in the Southeast finalist, and the restaurant was recommended in the 2025 Michelin Guide. The kitchen serves gildas, pan con tomate, croquetas, gazpacho, patatas bravas, tortilla española and pulpo a la gallega alongside a jamón counter and paella, with a Cúrate Experience prix fixe at $80. Its drinks list carries a dedicated "Sin Alcohol" section structured like the wine list rather than as an afterthought: a non-alcoholic gin and tonic on Dhos with Franklin & Sons tonic, a Solo Agrio built on Kentucky 74 non-alcoholic bourbon with Le Naturel Zero Zero red and lemon, St. Agrestis's Phony Negroni, and an N/A Sangría made with Le Naturel Zero Zero and an orange oleo. Le Naturel's Zero Zero blanco and tinto are poured as wine, with Estrella Galicia 0.0 and Sierra Nevada Trail Pass IPA on the beer list. Children of any age are welcome. No drink prices are published online.

venues.longDescription:
Cúrate opened in 2011 at 13 Biltmore Avenue in downtown Asheville, founded by chef Katie Button and Félix Meana, and it has since become one of the most decorated Spanish restaurants in the United States — winner of the James Beard Foundation's Outstanding Hospitality Award in 2022, a repeat Best Chef in the Southeast finalist for Button, and a Michelin Guide recommendation in 2025. WLOS marked its fifteenth year in March 2026 by calling it an Asheville staple. The format is straight Spanish tapas served properly: gildas, pan con tomate, croquetas, gazpacho, patatas bravas, tortilla española and pulpo a la gallega, alongside a jamón counter and paella, with a Cúrate Experience prix fixe at $80 a head. It serves from 11am daily and welcomes children of any age with highchairs and boosters on request — unusual for a restaurant of this standing and genuinely useful.

The non-alcoholic drinks have their own printed heading, "Sin Alcohol", and it is structured like the wine list rather than like a mocktail afterthought — cocktails, wine and beer, each with real products behind them. The built drinks run a non-alcoholic gin and tonic on Dhos with Franklin & Sons tonic and aromatics; a Solo Agrio combining Kentucky 74 non-alcoholic bourbon with Le Naturel Zero Zero red and lemon; St. Agrestis's Phony Negroni; and an N/A Sangría made with Le Naturel Zero Zero white or red, an orange oleo and citrus — a proper sangría build rather than juice, which matters at a Spanish table. Le Naturel's Zero Zero blanco and tinto are also poured straight as wine, and the beer list carries Estrella Galicia 0.0, Sierra Nevada Trail Pass IPA and an Untitled Art Juicy IPA. One item needs flagging: a Dram CBD Beauty Bubbles sits in that same section, with no dosage or warning printed beside it. Note the restaurant publishes no drink prices online.
venues.pressQuote: house sangrías and spirit-free options are always part of the offering

venues.name: Cure
venues.description: Cure is an Uptown New Orleans cocktail bar opened in 2009 by New Orleans native Neal Bodenheimer in a restored firehouse on a then-storm-damaged stretch of Freret Street — a move widely credited with sparking the corridor's revival. It won the James Beard Award for Outstanding Bar Program in 2018 and has held a place on North America's 50 Best Bars for three consecutive years. Its zero-proof drinks are printed as a section inside the bar's own "Cocktails We Love" card rather than on a separate menu. The current Zero Proof list runs four deep: Partly Cloudy ($12) with Undone Not Rum, coconut, lime and Q ginger beer; Round of Applause ($15) on The Pathfinder Bitter with Q tonic, lemon, strawberry and mint; Needlepoint Sour ($13) with verjus, grapefruit, ginger syrup, honey and egg white; and Second Opinion ($12) with chai tea, Giffard Apéritif Syrup, verjus and rose water. The list rotates, so earlier builds such as Gulfside, The Tide Is High and The Eureka are no longer served. The beer list also carries one non-alcoholic beer, Einbecker ($8). Open from 4pm Sunday to Thursday and 3pm Friday and Saturday.
venues.longDescription:
Cure opened in 2009 in a restored firehouse on Freret Street, at a point when that stretch of Uptown was still storm-damaged and largely empty, and it is credited with starting both the city's modern cocktail movement and the neighbourhood revival that followed it. It won the James Beard Award for Outstanding Bar Program in 2018, and Where Y'at noted that its excellence continues to shine as it secures a place on North America's 50 Best Bars for the third consecutive year — most recently at number 21. It opens at 4pm Sunday through Thursday and 3pm on Friday and Saturday, and takes dinner reservations for parties up to ten.

What matters here for a non-drinker is structural, and it is the thing most bars get wrong. Cure's zero-proof drinks are not on a separate card or a laminated afterthought — they are printed as a section headed Zero Proof on the same menu as Cocktails We Love, which is where the bar puts its own favourites. Four are on it now. Partly Cloudy is $12, a long drink of Undone Not Rum, coconut and lime topped with Q ginger beer, and is the easy one to drink for an evening. Round of Applause is the most expensive at $15 and the most cocktail-like, using The Pathfinder Bitter with Q tonic, lemon, strawberry and mint. Needlepoint Sour at $13 is a real sour with egg white, using verjus and grapefruit against ginger syrup and honey — a genuine texture that fruit and soda cannot fake. Second Opinion at $12 leans bitter and aromatic, with chai tea, Giffard Apéritif Syrup, verjus and rose water. Two of the four are built on verjus, the pressed juice of unripe grapes, which is the most useful acid in zero-proof bartending because it brings wine's tartness without wine's sugar. For a beer, the list carries one non-alcoholic option, Einbecker from Germany, at $8. The list rotates genuinely rather than nominally, so drinks documented here in past seasons — Gulfside, The Tide Is High, The Eureka — have already been retired. Expect the names to have moved on; expect the standard not to have.
venues.pressQuote: New Orleans' cocktail excellence continues to shine as Cure secures its position on North America's 50 Best Bars list for the third consecutive year.

venues.name: Cutler
venues.description: Cutler (formerly Cutler & Co) is Andrew McConnell's flagship Fitzroy fine diner on Gertrude Street, and it pairs its award-winning cellar with a genuinely deep non-alcoholic offering. Drinkers can choose alcohol-free beers from Upflow and Sobah, aromatic wine alternatives from Melbourne's NON, alcohol-free sparkling, red and white wine, plus alcohol-free spritzes, RTDs and house mocktails. The zero-proof list runs to close to twenty options and is treated with the same seriousness as the wine list, earning the restaurant a top 5/5 rating from non-alcoholic guide No & Low Life. The Grande Dame of Gertrude Street keeps close to twenty curated non-alcoholic options alongside the wine list, so the alcohol-free route through dinner is a real one.
signatureDrinks: Curated non-alcoholic list — close to twenty options poured alongside the wine list
venues.longDescription:
Cutler is the flagship restaurant of chef Andrew McConnell and partner Jo McGann, opened in 2009 as Cutler & Co in a converted metalworks factory on Gertrude Street in Fitzroy, Melbourne's first suburb. Part of the Trader House group, it recently dropped the "& Co" to become simply Cutler, but the ethos of refined, simple, hospitable dining is unchanged. It remains one of Melbourne's benchmark fine diners, serving spontaneous, seasonal modern-Australian cooking across a dining room and bar.

The non-alcoholic program is a real one, not an afterthought. Broadsheet describes it as "a fine diner with a stellar booze-free offering," pointing to alcohol-free beers from the likes of Upflow and Sobah, wine alternatives by NON, and a healthy list of alcohol-free cocktails. No & Low Life catalogues the full range as alcohol-free beer, alcohol-free sparkling, red and white wine, aromatic wine alternatives, alcohol-free spritzes and RTDs, and house mocktails, rating the venue 5 out of 5 for its no-and-low offering.

The room sits in the former factory space on the corner of Gertrude and Napier Streets, with a dining room, a bar and outdoor options. Cutler serves dinner Wednesday to Saturday from 5:30pm until late and opens for all-day Sunday dining from noon.

The scale of the alcohol-free list is what separates this from a fine-dining room that simply has something. Pub With No Booze, an Australian guide written specifically for non-drinkers, calls Cutler & Co the Grande Dame of Gertrude Street fine dining and notes that after nearly fifteen years as the flagship of Andrew McConnell's stable it has stayed at the front of what is new — and that it does not let alcohol-free drinkers down either, with a list of close to twenty well-curated options.

Twenty is a meaningful number. A restaurant can put three mocktails on a card and call it a programme; twenty options requires stock, storage, staff training and someone whose job it is to keep the list current. It also means a non-drinker at a long dinner can drink differently across four courses instead of ordering the same sweet thing twice and giving up. That is the practical difference between being catered for and being accommodated.
venues.pressQuote: You'll find beers from the likes of Upflow and Sobah, wine alternatives by Non and a healthy list of cocktails - all sans alcohol, all delicious.

venues.name: Cycene
venues.description: Cycene is a one-Michelin-star tasting-menu restaurant inside Shoreditch's Blue Mountain School, and its non-alcoholic pairing is built by a chef rather than the sommelier. Caitlin Jones and the kitchen make a bespoke flight of house-fermented kombuchas and drinks matched to each course - a double-fermented pear and celeriac kombucha with the opening snacks, a pumpkin, miyagawa and greengage-kernel drink alongside sea-urchin linguini, and honey-fermented milk with dessert. There is also a 'half-and-half' option that alternates glasses of fine wine with the homemade kombuchas, so non-drinkers get a genuine tasting experience rather than an afterthought.
signatureDrinks: Double-fermented pear and celeriac kombucha - made from pear and celeriac trimmings off the tasting menu, served with the opening snacks
Pumpkin, miyagawa and greengage-kernel drink - paired with linguini, sea urchin and bottarga
Honey-fermented milk and kombu infusion - served with the dark chocolate sabayon tart
venues.longDescription:
Cycene - Old English for 'kitchen' - opened in 2022 as the restaurant of Blue Mountain School, the multi-storey concept building on Chance Street in Shoreditch that also houses a gallery, boutique and studios. It won a Michelin star in March 2023 under founding chef Theo Clench; Clench left in August 2024, but the restaurant has retained its star and continues to serve a seasonal, British-produce-led tasting menu with subtle Asian influences. Time Out awarded it five stars in a November 2025 review, calling it 'by far the most magical' restaurant in east London.

The format is deliberately intimate and immersive, with only around sixteen covers per sitting. Guests begin with a drink and the first course in the ground-floor bar, move up to the kitchen for a snack, then are seated in the dining room for the balance of roughly nine courses (about £195, with a shorter £95 Saturday lunch). In the dining room a sommelier offers wines by the glass or bottle from Cycene's cellar. Dinner runs Wednesday to Saturday evenings, with an additional relaxed Saturday lunch service celebrating seasonal ingredients.

What sets Cycene apart for non-drinkers is that its non-alcoholic pairing is composed by a chef rather than the sommelier. Caitlin Jones and the kitchen build a bespoke flight of house-made kombuchas and fermented drinks matched course by course, drawing on trimmings from current dishes as well as preserved and fermented ingredients from past seasons. Documented pours include a double-fermented pear and celeriac kombucha made from tasting-menu waste and served with the opening snacks, a pumpkin, miyagawa and greengage-kernel drink poured alongside linguini with sea urchin and bottarga, and an intensely savoury honey-fermented milk and kombu infusion served with the dark chocolate sabayon tart. For those who don't want to commit fully, a 'half-and-half' option alternates glasses of fine wine with the homemade kombuchas. Jones has said that because the drinks sometimes echo the wines' profiles, 'the sommelier and I inspire each other,' and the team frames the non-alcoholic pairing as 'an authentic and genuine addition to each dish' rather than a concession to non-drinkers.
venues.pressQuote: Because the drinks I create sometimes echo the wines' profiles, the sommelier and I inspire each other.

venues.name: Da Cove Health Bar & Café
venues.description: Da Cove Health Bar & Café sits on Monsarrat Avenue between Waikīkī and Diamond Head, and is one of the very few Oʻahu businesses that keeps 'awa on a standing everyday menu rather than as an occasional special. It serves no alcohol. Kava comes as an ice-cold single at $6 for eight ounces or a double at $12 for sixteen, and the house 'awa coconut smoothie blends kava with coconut milk, maple syrup and banana. A chalkboard wall explains what kava is and what it does, which is unusual and useful — it is psychoactive. The rest of the menu runs açaí bowls, fruit smoothies and wild-caught ahi salads, wraps and sandwiches, and live music plays Tuesday through Thursday evenings.
signatureDrinks: 'Awa coconut smoothie (kava, coconut milk, maple syrup, banana — 16oz)
venues.longDescription:
Da Cove Health Bar & Café trades at 3045 Monsarrat Avenue, on the stretch running up from Kapahulu towards Diamond Head, and operated for years as Diamond Head Cove Health Bar before shortening the name. The daytime business is a health café — açaí bowls, fruit smoothies, wild-caught ahi salads, wraps and sandwiches — but what earns it a place in an alcohol-free guide is that it is one of the only venues on Oʻahu with 'awa written into a standing daily menu rather than served at a dedicated kava bar. That matters practically: it means a visitor can try kava in a bright, food-first room at two in the afternoon without walking into a nakamal, which is a lower step for someone unfamiliar with it.

The kava is sold plainly. An ice-cold single is $6 for eight ounces and a double $12 for sixteen, and the house 'awa coconut smoothie — kava blended with coconut milk, maple syrup and banana, $11 for sixteen ounces — is the version most first-timers order, because the coconut and banana carry the earthy, faintly bitter root flavour that puts people off a straight shell. A chalkboard wall in the café explains what kava is and what it is supposed to do, which is a rare piece of honesty in a category where a lot of venues let customers guess. The plain statement is worth repeating: kava contains no alcohol and Da Cove serves none, but it is psychoactive and mildly sedating, and it is not the same proposition as a mocktail. The café opens daily from 9am to 7pm, and runs live music on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday evenings from 8pm to 10pm, which extends it past café hours into something closer to a social room. Between the food, the hours and the fact that nothing on the premises contains alcohol, it functions as one of the more flexible alcohol-free options on this side of town.
venues.pressQuote: The former Diamond Head Cove Health Bar isn't focused solely on kava, but it does feature a chalkboard wall explaining the benefits of the drink and its active ingredients called kavalactones.

venues.name: Da Kine's Kava
venues.description: Da Kine's Kava is Durham's fully alcohol-free bar, open noon to midnight seven days a week in a unit on West Chapel Hill Street in the Burch Avenue neighbourhood. The house drink is kava — ground Noble Vanuatu root blended with water and served the traditional way, or mixed with juices on tap, still or sparkling — and there is a short mocktail list beside it, led by the Haleakala Sunrise on guava, pineapple, lime and coconut. Nothing on the menu contains alcohol, but read it before you order: kratom teas and hemp drinks carrying CBD and Delta-9 THC sit on the same page, clearly labelled. Discover Durham lists it on the city's official non-alcoholic page as an alcohol-free social space, and it is the only dedicated alcohol-free bar in Durham.
venues.address: 1114 W Chapel Hill St, Unit B, Durham, NC 27701
signatureDrinks: Traditional Kava ($6 / $10) — ground Noble Vanuatu kava root blended with pure water, served in a shell
DK Kava ($6 / $10) — the flagship on tap: juices and flavours mixed with kava extract, rotating seasonal flavour or a low-sugar Mai Tai
Sparkling Kava ($6 / $10) — carbonated juices and flavours with kava extract, rotating seasonal flavour
Grab The Bull ($15) — traditional kava, coconut milk, sweetener and a shot of kava extract
Haleakala Sunrise ($10) — guava, pineapple, lime and coconut with a strawberry drizzle, mixed with the base of your choice
venues.longDescription:
Da Kine's Kava is the only fully alcohol-free bar in Durham and one of a handful in the Raleigh-Durham metro. It sits in a unit on West Chapel Hill Street just west of downtown, in the Burch Avenue neighbourhood, and keeps hours that no coffee shop does — noon to midnight, seven days a week — which is the whole point. The bar exists so that there is somewhere to go at ten on a Friday night that is not a bar serving alcohol.

The house drink is kava, and it is worth being plain about what that is: kava is a root from the South Pacific, traditionally ground and steeped in water and served in a coconut shell, drunk for a calming, sociable effect. It is not alcohol and contains none, but it is psychoactive in its own mild way, and it is not for everyone — people on medication, pregnant, or with liver concerns should talk to a doctor first. If you are avoiding alcohol specifically, kava is a genuine alternative; if you are avoiding all mood-altering drinks, this is not the room for you, and the Triangle's cocktail bars below will serve you better.

The printed menu, read in September 2026, splits into kava bar classics, drinks on tap and mocktails. Traditional Kava is ground Noble Vanuatu root blended with water, six dollars for a shell and ten for the larger pour. The same kava extract goes into DK Kava, the flagship on tap, mixed with juices in a rotating seasonal flavour or a low-sugar Mai Tai, and into a sparkling version. Grab The Bull adds coconut milk and a second measure of kava, and the Haleakala Sunrise is the straightforward mocktail: guava, pineapple, lime and coconut with a strawberry drizzle, finished with whichever base you choose.

The rest of the list is where reading matters. Kratom — a plant in the coffee family with effects of its own, sold here as a house Indo tea and in drinks called Peaceful Warrior and Nitro Blast — and hemp drinks carrying CBD and Delta-9 THC share the same menu, each labelled, with the bar's own notes on dosage and the chance of a positive drug screen. None of it is alcohol, but a reader avoiding every intoxicant should stick to the traditional kava or the mocktail and say so. Federal rules on hemp-derived THC drinks change in November 2026, so expect that part of the list to move.

The room itself is set up as a lounge — low seating, conversation-height music, no television showing the game — and the crowd skews to students, recovery-community regulars and people who simply want a night out that ends clear-headed. Discover Durham lists it on the city's own non-alcoholic drinks page, which makes it one of the few Triangle venues whose alcohol-free credentials come from the tourism board rather than a blog.
venues.pressQuote: an alcohol-free social space offering alternative drink options

venues.name: Da Terra
venues.description: Da Terra is the two-Michelin-star restaurant of chef Rafael Cagali inside Bethnal Green's Town Hall Hotel, serving Brazilian-Italian tasting menus. Alongside its acclaimed wine list, head sommelier Maria Boumpa runs a dedicated non-alcoholic pairing built course by course from the kitchen's own produce. Pours are made in-house rather than pulled from a bottle list, and demand for the option has, per Club Oenologique, 'continued to soar.'
venues.address: 8 Patriot Square, London E2 9NF, United Kingdom
venues.hours: Mon-Tue closed; Wed 6pm-8pm; Thu-Sat 12pm-1:30pm & 6pm-8pm; Sun closed
signatureDrinks: Passion-fruit kombucha — house-made, paired with the moqueca (Brazilian fish stew)
Cherry, grape and umeboshi juice — paired with the pork feijoada and chimichurri
venues.longDescription:
Da Terra sits within the Grade II-listed Town Hall Hotel on Patriot Square in Bethnal Green, holding two Michelin stars and a place on La Liste's 2026 global ranking and The World's 50 Best Discovery. Chef-patron Rafael Cagali's cooking fuses his Brazilian roots with Italian technique across multi-course tasting menus, making it one of East London's most decorated dining rooms.

The non-alcoholic program is genuinely part of the fine-dining experience rather than an afterthought. Introduced roughly two years ago and overseen by head sommelier Maria Boumpa (IWSC UK Sommelier of the Year 2025), it is offered as a full pairing alongside the wine flights, with each drink built to match a specific course and often made from the kitchen's surplus ingredients.

House-made pours include a passion-fruit kombucha served with the moqueca (Brazilian fish stew) and a cherry, grape and umeboshi juice poured against the pork feijoada with chimichurri. Because the drinks are prepared in-house per course, the lineup shifts with the menu rather than following a fixed printed list.

According to Club Oenologique, requests for the non-alcoholic pairing 'have continued to soar,' with guests increasingly mixing wine and zero-proof pairings across a meal. The offering makes Da Terra a strong choice for someone who wants a marquee, alcohol-free tasting experience in a landmark London hotel setting.
venues.pressQuote: It's a challenge sometimes but it's fun.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Maria Boumpa, head sommelier, Da Terra

venues.name: Daisies
venues.description: Michelin Green Star–holding pasta restaurant in Logan Square with a dedicated 'Spirit Free Treats' menu built on the same zero-waste, fermentation-forward philosophy that drives the kitchen.

venues.longDescription:
Daisies earns its place among Chicago's most compelling destinations for non-alcoholic drinkers not by accident but by design. The Logan Square restaurant runs a dedicated 'Spirit Free Treats' section of its drink menu — a rare formal commitment at a full-service restaurant — rooted in the same zero-waste fermentation ethos that earned the kitchen its Michelin Green Star in 2023, 2024, and 2025. House-made kombucha flows from the tap in seasonally rotating flavors, and herb sodas are built from stems of parsley, basil, tarragon, and sage that would otherwise be composted.

The drink most cited by press and regulars alike is the Mushroom Sour — a non-alcoholic riff on the classic sour format made from a syrup fermented from portobello mushroom stems sourced directly out of the kitchen's prep scraps, shaken with egg white and lemon for a foamy, earthy-bright result. A Cranberry-Orange Shrub rounds out a menu that also includes fermented root beer. Beverage director Katherine Sturgill and bar manager Seth Marquez oversee a program that treats the zero-proof side with the same sourcing rigor as the wine list. Chef-owner Joe Frillman's brother Tim runs Frillman Farms in Michigan, which supplies the produce driving both the kitchen and the bar.

The 5,500-square-foot space on Milwaukee Avenue — a former honky-tonk the team took over in 2023 — is airy and unpretentious, filled with natural light, high ceilings, booths, and a comfortable bar. It runs the full day: counter-service café from 7am, lunch and weekend brunch without reservations, and a dinner service that requires booking in advance via Tock (a $10 per person deposit holds the reservation). A 25% service charge replaces tipping and is disclosed upfront. The room works equally well for solo laptop sessions in the morning and celebratory dinners at night — a rare combination in a neighborhood that already punches well above its weight on dining.
venues.pressQuote: The Logan Square eatery offers a range of booze-free bevs, from classics like root beer and iced tea to more novel drinks like a mushroom sour and cranberry-orange shrub.

venues.name: Danté Restaurant and Cocktail Bar
venues.description: Danté is a modern-Greek restaurant and cocktail bar on Northcote's High Street styled after 1930s Parisian glamour, where every cocktail on the list can be built alcohol-free. Non-drinkers are treated as VIPs: the bar swaps in AF spirits, liqueurs and sparkling so zero-proof guests get the same menu, and cocktail architect Jacob will build a bespoke NA drink on request. Named AF builds include the Chios Spritz with house-made AF mastiha and AF prosecco, and the theatrical Honey Ginger on Fire with smoked AF bourbon.
signatureDrinks: Blueberry Voir (AF) - house-made blueberry soda, lime juice, blue-pea butterfly tea syrup, egg white
Honey Ginger on Fire (AF) - smoked AF bourbon, honey syrup, ginger
Prince Pine (AF) - AF gin, pineapple juice, mint, lime, honey syrup, ginger syrup
Chios Spritz (AF) - house-made AF mastiha, AF prosecco, grapefruit juice, lemon juice, soda
venues.longDescription:
Danté sits in the middle of Northcote's buzzing High Street strip, fitted out in a dim, split-level Parisian-1930s aesthetic with an opulent, wall-lined cocktail bar. It trades as a modern-Greek restaurant and cocktail bar, and was named Luxury Cocktail Bar of the Year 2024 and Sustainable Restaurant of the Year (Melbourne) 2025. Co-owner Tas Pantotis frames the room around family food traditions and a sustainability ethos rather than pure spectacle.

The non-alcoholic program is unusually complete: rather than a token mocktail or two, every decadent cocktail on Danté's list is available in an alcohol-free version, with the spirit swapped for NA spirits, liqueurs and sparkling. Master cocktail architect Jacob will also invent something bespoke if none of the listed drinks appeal, so zero-proof guests get the full bar rather than a sidelined shortlist.

Popular alcohol-free builds documented by NoLo Life include the Blueberry Voir (house-made blueberry soda, lime juice, blue-pea butterfly tea syrup, egg white), Honey Ginger on Fire (smoked AF bourbon, honey syrup, ginger), Prince Pine (AF gin, pineapple juice, mint, lime, honey and ginger syrups) and the Chios Spritz (house-made AF mastiha, AF prosecco, grapefruit juice, lemon juice, soda). The house-made mastiha ties the zero-proof list back to the kitchen's Greek roots.

Danté is open Wednesday through Sunday for dinner plus a Sunday lunch service, and remains actively trading with strong recent reviews into 2026.
venues.pressQuote: Non-drinkers are catered for as VIPs, with every decadent cocktail listed being available in non-alcoholic form.

venues.name: Dante
venues.description: Caffe Dante is the Greenwich Village original at 79–81 MacDougal Street, named the World's Best Bar in 2019 and famous for its Negroni and Garibaldi programmes. Note that three separate Dante rooms share one website — this is the MacDougal Street original, not Dante West Village on Hudson Street or Dante Aperitivo on Bank Street. CORRECTION TO OUR EARLIER LISTING: we previously described a zero-proof menu called "Temperance" led by a signature "NOgroni". Neither appears anywhere on Dante's site or current menus, and we could not source either name; they have been removed. The real section is headed simply NON-ALCOHOLIC and runs five drinks: an Espresso Shakerato with orange juice and vanilla ($16), an NA Cosmojito with Dante cranberry, mint, lime and orange bitters ($14), a Dante Italian Spritz on Lyre's ($16), an NA Blood Orange Spritz with Seedlip Grove, raspberry and balsamic ($17), and a Forest Highball on Everleaf Forest with clementine and saffron ($15). It was shortlisted, not a winner, at NYC's Best Bars for NA 2025.
venues.longDescription:
Caffe Dante has been on MacDougal Street since 1915, and in 2019 it was named the World's Best Bar at the World's 50 Best Bars — a remarkable thing for a Greenwich Village café that started life serving espresso to the neighbourhood. It is best known for two drinks programmes: the Negroni, which it treats as a family of variations rather than a single recipe, and the Garibaldi, the deceptively simple Campari-and-orange-juice build whose whole quality rests on how the juice is aerated. One point of navigation before you go, because it trips people up: three separate Dante rooms share a single website. This is the MacDougal Street original. Dante West Village sits on Hudson Street at the corner of Perry, and Dante Aperitivo is on Bank Street, and their menus are not the same.

We owe a correction on the non-alcoholic side. Our earlier entry described a dedicated zero-proof menu called "Temperance" headed by a signature "NOgroni". Neither name appears anywhere on Dante's site or on any of its current menus, and we could not trace either to a real source — so both have been removed rather than repeated. What actually exists is good, and sits under a plain heading, NON-ALCOHOLIC. There are five. The Espresso Shakerato at $16 shakes fresh espresso with orange juice and vanilla, which sounds unlikely and is the one to order — the orange lifts the coffee the way a citrus twist lifts a martini. The NA Cosmojito at $14 uses the house cranberry with fresh mint, pressed lime and orange bitters. The Dante Italian Spritz at $16 is built on Lyre's Italian Spritz with non-alcoholic sparkling wine and San Pellegrino. The NA Blood Orange Spritz at $17 is the most constructed, layering Seedlip Grove with raspberry syrup, balsamic vinegar and Aranciata Rossa. And the Forest Highball at $15 runs Everleaf Forest with clementine, saffron, citrus and orange bitters. Dante was shortlisted, not a winner, at NYC's Best Bars for NA 2025.
venues.pressQuote: Dante takes cocktails seriously. Known for their Italian-leaning menu with contemporary takes on classics like spritzes and Negronis, it's also one of the few places where you'll find a take on a sort of zero-proof espresso martini, made with orange juice and vanilla.

venues.name: Dario
venues.description: Dario is an Italian restaurant with global influences that opened in Minneapolis's North Loop in early 2024, led by chef Joe Rolle and beverage director Stephen Rowe. Rowe spent nearly a decade as a founding team member of the acclaimed Marvel Bar, and at Dario he runs a dedicated spirit-free program built to stand alongside the full-proof cocktails rather than as an afterthought — the restaurant calls it "a groundbreaking spirit-free offering that mirrors the depth and creativity of the full-proof cocktails." The zero-proof list spans bitters-forward and botanical builds such as the New Age Outlaw (Dhos Blanco, Spritz del Conte, lime), No. 75 (ISH London Botanical, Oddbird Blanc de Blanc, lemon), Botanical & Tonic, and the Naw-groni. The kitchen also makes house sodas, pours an Athletic Brewing NA golden ale, and keeps a de-alcoholized wine list. Known for handmade pastas.

venues.longDescription:
Dario opened in the North Loop in early 2024, an Italian restaurant with global influences led by chef Joe Rolle and beverage director Stephen Rowe. Rowe's background is the thing to know: he spent close to a decade as a founding team member of Marvel Bar, which for years was the most serious cocktail room in Minneapolis and one of the most respected in the country. What he has built at Dario is a dedicated spirit-free programme designed to stand alongside the full-proof cocktails rather than beneath them — the restaurant describes it as "a groundbreaking spirit-free offering that mirrors the depth and creativity of the full-proof cocktails," and for once the marketing language is roughly accurate.

The zero-proof list is bitters-forward and botanical, which is exactly where most spirit-free menus refuse to go. The New Age Outlaw combines Dhos Blanco with Spritz del Conte and lime. No. 75 is built on ISH London Botanical with Oddbird Blanc de Blanc and lemon — a non-alcoholic reading of a French 75 that uses a dealcoholised sparkling wine rather than soda, which is the difference between the drink working and not. There is a straightforward Botanical & Tonic for anyone who wants something long and dry, and the Naw-groni covers the bitter aperitif register. Around those the kitchen makes its own sodas, the bar pours an Athletic Brewing non-alcoholic golden ale, and there is a dealcoholised wine list, so a non-drinker at a table ordering wine with handmade pasta has a genuine parallel rather than a substitute.

That combination — a named cocktail list, house sodas, NA beer and NA wine — is the full set, and relatively few restaurants at any price point assemble all four. Dinner nightly, to 10pm on Friday and Saturday.

venues.name: Dark Horse Bar & Eatery
venues.description: Dark Horse Bar & Eatery is a Lowertown, St. Paul neighborhood bar and restaurant that spent a decade serving the district before closing in February 2025 and reopening in July 2025 under new ownership. The relaunch is run by chef Shane Oporto in the kitchen and Sarah McDonough on the floor, backed by Eclective, the hospitality group behind Saint Paul Brewing and Can Can Wonderland. The reopened menu pairs elevated bar food — a signature burger, pizzas — with a cocktail list that gives equal attention to its non-alcoholic side. A dedicated "Zero Proof" menu section ($9 each) features house-made drinks: a Ginger Beer built on house ginger syrup, cayenne, and soda; a Squirt with house grapefruit cordial and soda; and a lightly fermented Tepache of pineapple, piloncillo, and cinnamon. Athletic Brewing non-alcoholic beers (Free Wave, Upside Dawn) are also stocked.
