venues.longDescription:
ECHO - Taste & Sound opened in March 2025 at 1301 South Main Street in the Arts District, a passion project from chef Natalie Young and entrepreneur Tom McAllister. Young has more than thirty years in kitchens, trained under Mark Miller and John Joho, and is best known in Las Vegas for the long-running Fremont East brunch restaurant EAT; her small plates here are meant, in the restaurant's phrase, to look like fine dining but taste like home. McAllister is a Las Vegas businessman with deep local roots including involvement in the World Series of Poker, and has committed himself to development in the Arts District. The room is mid-century modern — warm wood, acoustic panels, plants and vintage furnishings — and it is built around sound. There are two systems: a vintage analogue rig for warmth, and a world-class McIntosh setup for high-fidelity listening. Music director Rob Alahn and vinyl selector DJ Shoe program the records, moving the room from jazz through soul to unexpected global sounds over the course of a night.

Young is sober, and made an inclusive beverage program a priority from the day the place was conceived rather than adding one later; the bar talent was drawn from the storied and now-closed Downtown Cocktail Room. The menu splits its zero-proof drinks in two. A dedicated Non-Alcoholic Cocktails section mirrors spirited classics using zero-proof substitutes, including an N/A Old Fashioned (n/a bourbon, n/a amaro, simple syrup), Caught in the Rain (n/a rum, pineapple, mango, orange, coconut), Ring of Fire (n/a tequila, mango, orange juice, firewater bitters) and Take 5 (non-alcoholic amaro, cold brew, seasonal syrup). A separate Mocktails section holds original non-spirited creations built for their own sake rather than as substitutes — Cool Cat (cucumber syrup, lime, Sprite), Chef's Jam, and Bright Size Life (ube syrup, lemon, soda). The result is one of the few rooms in Las Vegas where the person not drinking and the person drinking are reading the same menu with the same expectations of it.
venues.pressQuote: The cocktail program is just as elevated as the menu, featuring some of the city's best drinks, plus thoughtful mocktails that pair perfectly with the food and the vibe.

venues.name: Echoes
venues.description: Echoes is a Montrose live-music and DJ bar on Richmond Avenue that runs until two in the morning six nights a week, and its non-alcoholic drinks are built as desserts and infusions rather than as watered-down cocktails. The lady marmalade combines espresso with chocolate syrup and crushed Oreos; never promised you a rose garden pairs rose tonic with hibiscus and lychee; dolce vita layers tamarind and melon syrups under mandarin and bergamot soda with heavy cream; and the tropical tango runs pineapple, lime and coconut into ginger beer. CultureMap Houston picked the bar out in its January 2026 round-up of the city's zero-proof drinking. The late licence is the real argument here — a two o'clock closing time means the non-alcoholic list is available at the hours a music bar actually fills up.
signatureDrinks: lady marmalade — espresso, chocolate syrup, crushed Oreos
never promised you a rose garden — rose tonic, hibiscus, lychee
dolce vita — tamarind syrup, melon syrup, mandarin and bergamot soda, heavy cream
tropical tango — pineapple, lime, coconut, ginger beer
venues.longDescription:
Echoes occupies a Richmond Avenue site in Montrose and trades as a live-music and DJ bar, open from four in the afternoon until two in the morning every night except Monday. That closing time is the single most relevant fact about it for anyone not drinking, because the problem with a music venue is rarely the music — it is that the last two hours of the night are structured entirely around rounds at the bar.

The non-alcoholic drinks here solve that in an unusual way: rather than imitating cocktails, they lean into being rich. The lady marmalade is espresso with chocolate syrup and crushed Oreos, which is frankly a dessert in a glass and none the worse for it. Dolce vita is the most constructed of the four, layering tamarind and melon syrups beneath a mandarin and bergamot soda and finishing with heavy cream — tamarind supplying a sour, slightly resinous depth that keeps the cream from flattening everything. Never promised you a rose garden works the opposite register, dry and floral, with rose tonic against hibiscus and lychee; hibiscus brings the tartness, and tonic water's quinine bitterness gives it the astringent finish a long drink needs. The tropical tango is the straightforward one, pineapple, lime and coconut lengthened with ginger beer.

CultureMap Houston listed the bar in its January 2026 survey of where to drink without alcohol in the city, which is how it came to our attention, and the drinks above are the ones that coverage names.

The case for a music bar as a night out without alcohol is a specific one. A room with a stage has a reason to be there that is not the drink in your hand: the evening has a shape imposed by the set times rather than by rounds, there is something to face other than the bar, and nobody counts what anyone is holding while a band is playing. Add a kitchen running until two in the morning and a drinks list with four builds that took real work, and Echoes becomes one of the more genuinely usable late rooms in Montrose for a non-drinker.

venues.name: The Edinburgh Castle Hotel
venues.description: Brunswick's longest-standing pub, opened in 1854, was one of a small group of Melbourne venues chosen to launch Heaps Normal's Original Draught on tap - Australia's first non-alcoholic draught beer. That means a genuine cold, poured AF beer at the bar rather than a can from the fridge: a crisp contemporary Aussie lager brewed with low-bitterness noble hops and toasted malt. It sits alongside the pub's extensive craft-beer list, gastropub food and a huge beer garden.
signatureDrinks: Heaps Normal Original Draught (on tap) - crisp, contemporary non-alcoholic Aussie lager, brewed with low-bitterness noble hops and toasted malt
venues.longDescription:
The Edinburgh Castle is Brunswick's oldest pub, opening in 1854 - the same year as the Eureka Stockade - originally as a watering hole for gold miners. Today it trades seven days a week from 681 Sydney Road, on the corner of Albion Street, with the #55 tram stopping right out front and Anstey station on the Upfield line a five-minute walk away. The room is a proper local: a huge beer garden, gastropub food, an extensive craft-beer list and free local live music with DJs from Thursday to Sunday.

Its non-alcoholic credentials come from being one of the select Melbourne pubs to put Heaps Normal's Original Draught on tap when the Australian NA brewer rolled out the country's first non-alcoholic draught beer nationally in early 2026. The Edinburgh Castle was named among the launch venues - alongside Beermash in Collingwood, The Old Bar in Fitzroy, Huzzah in Glen Iris and Brick Lane at the Queen Victoria Market - and hosted free rounds at the celebration on Friday 20 February 2026.

Original Draught is distinct from Heaps Normal's canned range: a crisp, contemporary Aussie lager brewed with low-bitterness noble hops and toasted malt for an amber hue, poured properly from the tap. As Heaps Normal co-founder Ben Holdstock put it, draught had 'long been the missing piece for non-alc beer,' and the Edinburgh Castle is one of the Brunswick locals where you can now order that pour by the schooner rather than settling for a can.
venues.pressQuote: For a long time, draught has been the missing piece for non-alc beer.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Ben Holdstock, Heaps Normal co-founder and Chief Product Officer

venues.name: Eem
venues.description: Eem is a Thai barbecue restaurant and cocktail bar in N Portland's Boise neighborhood, opened in February 2019 by chef Earl Ninsom (Langbaan), pitmaster Matt Vicedomini (Matt's BBQ), and bartender Eric Nelson. It was named Restaurant of the Year by both The Oregonian and Portland Monthly in 2019 and repeatedly wins Willamette Week's "Best Thai" reader poll, pairing Texas-style smoked meats with bold Thai flavors. The non-alcoholic program, inspired by co-owner Nelson's own sobriety, lives in a dedicated "Clear Headed" menu section of four named zero-proof drinks at $8 each — about half the price of the full cocktails — built with the same house shrubs, cordials, and NA spirits. Named pours include the cucumber-yuzu Approved by Chef, the hojicha and strawberry-guava Secret Serendipity, and the coconut-pineapple That's It, That's All. Heck N/A beer rounds out the list.
venues.longDescription:
Eem is a Thai barbecue restaurant and cocktail bar at 3808 N Williams Avenue in the Boise neighbourhood, and its name does double duty: the restaurant explains that eem translates to satiated in Thai and is also the initials of owners Earl, Eric and Matt. Those are chef Earl Ninsom, pitmaster Matt Vicedomini of Matt's BBQ, and bartender Eric Nelson, and the food is exactly the collision that suggests — Thai cooking drawn from the northern and southern regions, infused with Texas-style barbecue. The kitchen is direct about its scope: it focuses on curries and rice dishes, encourages family-style dining, and does not serve noodles. The Oregonian named it Restaurant of the Year in 2019, the New York Times has included it on a favourite-restaurants list, and Texas Monthly's barbecue editor Daniel Vaughn wrote that Eem served the best meal — not just the best barbecue meal — he ate that year. There is a year-round heated and enclosed patio alongside sidewalk seating in warmer months.

The non-alcoholic drinks sit in their own printed menu section headed "Clear Headed", and all four are $8 — roughly half what the full cocktails cost, which is unusual enough to be worth stating plainly. Approved by Chef is a cucumber yuzu shrub with ginger lime soda. Secret Serendipity builds hojicha tea with strawberry guava cordial, fresh lemon, orange blossom water, lemongrass and bitters. That's It, That's All runs coconut cream, pineapple soda, lime, cinnamon and grapefruit. The fourth is a Pathfinder N/A Negroni, described as notes of orange, herbaceous pine and mildly bitter — and the menu flags it 21+, a distinction worth noting for anyone avoiding hemp-derived ingredients. Heck non-alcoholic golden ale or IPA is $7, and the cooling classics list runs Thai tea with oat milk, coconut water, guava and mango nectars and a CBD seltzer. Travel Oregon, writing a non-drinker's guide to the city in November 2022, said Eem brings the funky vibes and fruity, alcohol-free cocktail options. Minors are welcome everywhere except the bar top; reservations are taken only for parties of six or more, and the waitlist must be joined in person.

venues.name: 80/20 Burger Bar
venues.description: 80/20 Burger Bar on 21st Street in Chelsea stocks both non-alcoholic wines and non-alcoholic beers, which is a more useful combination than it sounds — most bars manage one or neither, and NA wine in particular is the category venues skip because it is expensive and hard to store. It is also the late option in Norfolk's alcohol-free landscape, running to midnight midweek and 2am on Friday and Saturday. For anyone who wants a burger and a cold beer that happens to have no alcohol in it, rather than a project, this is the straightforward answer. It is a couple of minutes on foot from both Ceremony and Only You in Chelsea.
venues.longDescription:
80/20 Burger Bar sits on West 21st Street in Chelsea, the Norfolk neighbourhood that has quietly become the region's best few blocks for anyone not drinking — Ceremony's bottle shop and Only You are both within walking distance. The name refers to the beef ratio, and the room is what it sounds like: burgers, a bar, late hours.

Its alcohol-free offering is simple and worth respecting for that. It stocks non-alcoholic wine and non-alcoholic beer. No composed cocktails, no named list — just the two categories most bars fail to carry.

The wine is the notable half. Dealcoholised wine is the least-stocked category in the whole non-alcoholic market: it costs more than beer, takes fridge space, moves slowly, and most venues decide it is not worth the shelf. That means a non-drinker at dinner is routinely offered beer or a sweet mocktail when what the food actually calls for is wine. A burger bar that carries it has made a small, unglamorous decision in favour of a customer most places ignore.

The hours are the other reason it belongs here. It opens at 5pm and runs to midnight through the week and 2am on Friday and Saturday — later than anything else on this list. Sober nightlife thins out badly after eleven in most cities, and Hampton Roads is no exception; Ceremony closes at 7pm, Only You at midnight at best. Somewhere serving food and a decent alcohol-free drink at one in the morning is genuinely scarce, and it is not a bad place to end an evening. The kitchen runs as late as the bar, which is the other half of what makes a late venue actually usable.
venues.pressQuote: 80/20 Burger Bar: Non-alcoholic wines and beers.

venues.name: El Carlos Elegante
venues.description: El Carlos Elegante, Duro Hospitality's Michelin-recognized Mexico City-inspired restaurant in the Design District, gives non-drinkers a dedicated, printed 'Limonada Stand' section rather than a buried lone mocktail. The $9 zero-proof pours include Ace's Bell Pepper, Jamaica-Hibiscus, and a Pear Lemonade, made with the same scratch-kitchen sensibility as the masa program. CraveDFW singled out the Limonada Stand as 'a pear and hibiscus dream that doesn't skimp on complexity,' and the restaurant features the list for Dry January. It's a genuine named NA menu at an otherwise mezcal- and agave-forward restaurant.
signatureDrinks: Ace's Bell Pepper - non-alcoholic 'Limonada Stand' pour ($9)
venues.longDescription:
El Carlos Elegante is a Mexico City-inspired restaurant in the Dallas Design District from Duro Hospitality, the local group behind The Charles. The space is modeled after a Mexican hacienda with finishes, materials, and furniture sourced almost exclusively from Mexico, a front courtyard with an oversized fireplace and retractable roof, and a U-shaped bar. The kitchen runs an in-house masa program that nixtamalizes heirloom corn into scratch tortillas, teletas, and tostadas, alongside a wood-fired Argentinian-style grill, crudo and ceviche, and a global wine list. It has been recognized by the MICHELIN Guide as 'Recommended' for two consecutive years.

The beverage program leans heavily on mezcal and agave, but non-drinkers are served a dedicated, named 'Limonada Stand' section of zero-proof drinks priced at $9 each: Ace's Bell Pepper, Jamaica-Hibiscus, and Pear Lemonade. CraveDFW described the Limonada Stand as 'a pear and hibiscus dream that doesn't skimp on complexity,' and Dallas CultureMap featured the section in its Dry January mocktail roundup, confirming it as a real, printed part of the menu rather than an off-menu Shirley Temple.

El Carlos Elegante is open for dinner nightly at 1400 N Riverfront Blvd, from 5pm, closing at 10pm Sunday through Thursday and 11pm on Friday and Saturday. Reservations are available via OpenTable, and the restaurant is operated by Dallas-based Duro Hospitality.
venues.pressQuote: Even non-drinkers are treated to vibrant mocktails like the Limonada Stand, a pear and hibiscus dream that doesn't skimp on complexity.

venues.name: El Five
venues.description: El Five is a fifth-floor rooftop Mediterranean tapas restaurant in Denver's LoHi neighborhood, opened on May 3, 2017 by chef and restaurateur Justin Cucci as part of the employee-owned Edible Beats group. The dining room and open-air patio look across the downtown Denver skyline, and the menu draws on Spain, North Africa and the Middle East: paella, mezze, spreads, kebabs and croquettas. The current dinner menu carries a dedicated Zero-Proof Cocktails section rather than a token option. It runs the Faux Fashioned (Three Spirit Nightcap, spiced piloncillo, Turkish tobacco bitters), the Faux Negroni (Lyre's zero-proof spirit, verjus blanc, aperitif syrup, orange zest), the Scarlet Shrub (strawberry, pink peppercorn, champagne vinegar, soda) and a seasonal Faux Sangria, plus three of the bar's gin and tonics made zero-proof with Lyre's. Executive chef is Corey Ferguson. Dinner reservations are recommended, especially for the patio.

venues.longDescription:
El Five opened on May 3, 2017 on the fifth floor of 2930 Umatilla Street in Lower Highland, the fourth restaurant from Justin Cucci's Edible Beats group, which is local, independent and one hundred percent employee-owned. The draw is partly the room, an interior and open-air patio with an unobstructed view of the downtown Denver skyline, and partly the cooking, a small-plates menu that reads across the Mediterranean rather than settling in one country: Tunisian couscous, Turkish pizza, Galician empanada, Iberico kebabs, goat cheese croquettas with jamon serrano, and paella cooked to order and meant to be eaten from the caramelized socarrat at the pan's edge. Justin Cucci is chef and founder, Corey Ferguson is executive chef and Gabriel Sauer is chef de cuisine. Produce comes in part from a 320-square-foot hydroponic farm housed in an upcycled shipping container that supplies all Edible Beats restaurants year-round. Edible Beats runs as an ESOP, with gratuities shared across the whole hourly team, and adds a 6% Denver employee benefits surcharge to each check that goes to staff benefits rather than to the house.

The zero-proof programme is a labelled section of the dinner menu, not an off-menu accommodation. The Faux Fashioned ($15) is built on Three Spirit Nightcap with spiced piloncillo and Turkish tobacco bitters; the Faux Negroni ($12) uses a Lyre's zero-proof spirit with verjus blanc, aperitif syrup and orange zest; the Scarlet Shrub ($11) is a strawberry and pink peppercorn shrub finished with champagne vinegar and soda; and the Faux Sangria ($9) rotates on cranberry, pomegranate and seasonal fruit. A separate line offers any of the bar's gin and tonics zero-proof with Lyre's for $10, including Juniper Jones with lemon, rosemary and Mediterranean tonic, a Ford's build with grapefruit and mint, and a St. George build with cucumber and lime. A rotating Three Kings non-alcoholic beer is stocked at $9.50. Visit Denver's December 20, 2025 spirit-free guide highlighted the Faux Fashioned, and Westword's January 2026 round-up pointed readers specifically at the zero-proof gin and tonics. The zero-proof drinks also appear at happy hour, which runs 4pm to 5:30pm and pairs them with pintxos including harissa eggplant fries, confit chicken croquetta and bison meatball. Service runs to 9:30pm on weeknights and to 11pm on Friday and Saturday, and the patio is the reason to book ahead in warm months.
venues.pressQuote: Perched high above LoHi, El Five boasts spectacular views of the downtown Denver skyline...and a selection of spirit free cocktails that won't leave you wanting. Try the Faux Fashioned made with Three Spirit Nightcap, cherry, vanilla, Turkish tobacco bitters and spices.

venues.name: Electric Playhouse
venues.description: Electric Playhouse is an immersive projection-mapped venue on Albuquerque's west side — interactive games and light across whole rooms — with a full bar attached, and it names its mocktails the way it names everything else: Cocowatts, Nebula, Surge, Power Outage. It is explicitly family-friendly and all-ages, which makes it one of very few places in this directory where a group can include children, a designated driver and someone in recovery without any of them being an afterthought. (Electric Playhouse Albuquerque stopped trading on 2 August 2026 and is temporarily closed while its owner looks for a new operator to take over day-to-day running of the venue; no reopening date had been set as of September 2026 — check before you go.)
venues.longDescription:
Electric Playhouse is hard to categorise: a large space on Ouray Road on Albuquerque's west side where the floors and walls are projection-mapped into interactive games, with a restaurant and full bar inside it. It is the sort of venue that gets described as an experience rather than a bar, and for readers of this directory that is precisely the appeal.

The recurring difficulty of not drinking is that the default social activity is drinking, and the hours pass with nothing to do but hold a glass. A venue whose entire proposition is doing something removes that problem completely — the evening has a shape, everyone has something to occupy them, and nobody is tracking rounds. This directory has made the same argument for board-game cafés in Tulsa, an arcade bar in Burlington and a bowling alley in Omaha; Electric Playhouse is the largest-scale version of it.

The mocktails are named inside the house scheme rather than filed under a generic heading — Cocowatts, Nebula, Surge and Power Outage all sit in the same electrical-and-cosmic vocabulary as the rest of the venue. That is a small signal this directory weighs consistently: bars that name alcohol-free drinks the way they name everything else have integrated them rather than tolerated them.

The all-ages policy is the other reason it is here, and it is genuinely uncommon. Most rooms with a good alcohol-free list are 21-plus, which quietly excludes families and anyone bringing a younger sibling or a child. Visit Albuquerque lists Electric Playhouse among the city's mocktail destinations specifically as the family-friendly option.

Electric Playhouse Albuquerque stopped trading on 2 August 2026. The company said the venue would close temporarily while it looked for a new operator to license it and run it day to day, and it had not set a reopening date as of September 2026. Everything above describes the room as it traded; check the venue's own channels before making the trip.
venues.pressQuote: Electric Playhouse serves mocktails with names like Power Outage and Nebula.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Visit Albuquerque, Where To Find Mocktails in Albuquerque

venues.name: Electric Shuffle
venues.description: Electric Shuffle is Deep Ellum's high-tech shuffleboard bar, pairing competitive group gameplay with a documented non-alcoholic drink programme that goes well past soda-and-lime. The two longest-running mocktails are the Hibiscus No-Jito, a mojito riff on hibiscus ginger beer with lime and mint, and the Texas Sunset, which swaps tequila for pineapple, orange, lime grenadine and Topo Chico; a seasonal Poppi collaboration adds four more, including an Orange Creamsicle and a Strawberry Cucumber Smash. Athletic Brewing's Hazy IPA, IPA and Lite cover the beer list. Because there is full table service at the 17 shuffleboard tables, a non-drinker orders the same way as everyone else without leaving the game.
venues.longDescription:
In a neighborhood better known for live music and late-night bars, Electric Shuffle offers non-drinkers something genuinely rare on Deep Ellum's Elm Street: a full night out that doesn't require alcohol to feel complete. The venue's NA program runs beyond soda-and-lime territory, with dedicated mocktails that have appeared on the menu long enough to earn coverage in the Dallas Observer and CultureMap, plus a rotating Poppi-collab series documented on the official menu page. Sober guests can reserve a shuffleboard table, order drinks tableside, and participate in the same high-energy experience as everyone else — something that matters in a group-activity setting.

The two longest-running mocktails are the Hibiscus No-Jito — a mojito riff built on hibiscus ginger beer, simple syrup, lime, and mint — and the Texas Sunset, which swaps tequila for pineapple juice, orange juice, lime grenadine, and Topo Chico. The seasonal Poppi lineup adds four more zero-proof options: Vanilla Cherry Cola Float, Poppi Shirley, Orange Creamsicle, and Strawberry Cucumber Smash, each built around a specific Poppi flavor. Athletic Brewing's Hazy IPA, IPA, and Lite round out the NA beer options. No bar program director has been named publicly in press coverage, but the consistency of these offerings across multiple years of reviews suggests they're menu staples rather than one-off promotions.

Electric Shuffle occupies a large vintage brick building — a former warehouse — with 17 custom shuffleboard tables arranged in semi-private cove-style areas, a live DJ on weekends, and full table service so you never have to leave your game. Reservations are available for groups of four or more, making it a natural fit for birthday parties, work outings, and group date nights; walk-ins can grab bar or lounge seating. Parking is the main friction point: street spots are scarce on weekends, and the lot across the street at the Epic can run up to $30. Budget time for that, and the rest of the night runs smoothly.
venues.pressQuote: Electric Shuffle, the high-tech shuffleboard bar in Deep Ellum, has two mainstay mocktails on its menu.

venues.name: Elevate Kava Bar & Lounge
venues.description: Elevate runs 9am to 1am every day on North Orlando Avenue in Maitland, and calls itself a next-level social lounge and kava bar — a space for people of all walks of life to connect. The house drinks are named and built rather than generic: Mango Sunrise, Clear Skies, Passion and Berry Energetic. No alcohol is served. IMPORTANT for readers in recovery: the menu splits into kava for unwinding and what Elevate calls Mitra teas for daytime energy, and Mitra is Mitragyna speciosa — kratom. The naming is common across Florida and genuinely easy to miss. Kratom acts on opioid receptors, carries dependence and withdrawal risk, and is banned in several states; kava carries no comparable profile. Both are poured here, so order by name.
venues.address: 400 N Orlando Ave Unit 109A, Maitland, FL 32751
venues.longDescription:
Elevate runs 9am to 1am every day of the week from a unit on North Orlando Avenue in Maitland, and calls itself a next-level social lounge and kava bar — a space for people of all walks of life to connect and enjoy. It serves no alcohol.

What sets it apart from most of the Orlando field is that the drinks are properly built and properly named: Mango Sunrise, Clear Skies, Passion and Berry Energetic. That is a small thing with a large effect. A significant part of what people miss when they stop drinking is not the alcohol but the ritual of ordering something by name and being handed something that looks like it was made for you, and a menu of graded kava strengths does not supply that in the way a drinks list does.

Kava is the ground root of Piper methysticum, a shrub native to the South Pacific islands, prepared as a cold water infusion and drunk socially across Fiji, Vanuatu, Tonga and Samoa for roughly three thousand years. It contains no alcohol. It tastes earthy and bitter, numbs the lips and tongue on the first mouthful, and is mildly sedative rather than intoxicating in alcohol's sense. Kava exhibits reverse tolerance, so regular drinkers typically need less rather than more, and a first visit is best paced across an hour or two.

Maitland sits between Winter Park and Altamonte Springs on Orlando's northern edge, and a 1am close here puts a genuine late-night alcohol-free option within reach of a large stretch of the northern suburbs that otherwise has none.

The caution at this venue is the subtlest naming trap in the whole Florida kava scene, and it is the reason this entry spends a paragraph on it. Elevate splits its menu into kava for unwinding and what it calls Mitra teas for daytime energy — and Mitra is Mitragyna speciosa, which is kratom. Unlike "K-Tea" or a vein colour, "Mitra" is the plant's actual genus name, so the label is technically accurate while being almost completely opaque to anyone who does not already know the botany. A customer avoiding kratom could read that menu carefully, in good faith, and order it anyway.

The distinction is not academic. Kratom's principal alkaloids act on the opioid receptors; regular use produces tolerance and a genuine withdrawal syndrome, several US states ban it outright, and its concentrated 7-hydroxymitragynine derivatives are the subject of active federal scheduling. Kava carries no comparable dependence profile. Both are served here, from the same bar. Order by name, and if a drink is described as a Mitra tea, that is kratom.
venues.pressQuote: Elevate your day with our wide selections of Mitra Teas, or unwind for the night with a high-quality kava
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Elevate Kava Bar & Lounge, company statement

venues.name: Elevated Kava Lounge Downtown
venues.description: Elevated Kava Lounge's downtown room sits on College Street in the middle of Asheville's bar district and serves no alcohol at all, which is the point — it aims to provide the best kava and other alcohol alternatives in a cosy, artistic setting. The list runs kava, exotic and herbal teas, probiotic Buchi kombucha on tap, single-origin coffee and espresso from Brazilian-sourced beans roasted locally by Pisgah Coffee Roasters, tonics built from house mushroom tinctures, and Italian-style soda pops made from a large syrup selection. Free kava samples are offered to anyone curious. IMPORTANT for readers in recovery: this lounge serves kratom alongside kava. Kratom acts on opioid receptors, carries dependence risk, and concentrated 7-OH kratom products face federal scheduling — a materially different proposition from kava, and worth knowing before you walk in. A second Elevated room operates in West Asheville, and both host open-mic nights.
venues.longDescription:
Elevated Kava Lounge runs two Asheville rooms, and this is the downtown one, upstairs at 122 College Street in the thick of a bar district that has made the city a bachelorette-party destination. It serves nothing alcoholic. The stated aim is to provide the best kava and other alcohol alternatives in a cosy and inviting artistic setting, and the drinks list is broader than the name implies: kava, exotic and herbal tea concoctions, probiotic Buchi kombucha on tap, Brazilian-sourced single-origin coffee and espresso roasted locally by Pisgah Coffee Roasters, tonics built from the house mushroom tinctures, and custom Italian-style soda pops drawn from a large syrup selection, plus a cold case of canned and bottled options. Anyone unsure can ask for a free kava sample. The room programmes heavily around the arts — the long-running Sunday open mic at the West Asheville sister location is the flagship, with a poetry-specific open mic called Unpublished rotating between the two rooms monthly.

One thing has to be said plainly, because this directory is read by people in recovery and the distinction is not cosmetic: Elevated serves kratom as well as kava. The two are routinely sold side by side in American kava bars and are frequently spoken about in the same breath, but they are not equivalent. Kava is the ground root of a South Pacific shrub steeped in water, alcohol-free, sedating, drunk socially for roughly three thousand years and not known to produce physical dependence. Kratom is a Southeast Asian leaf whose alkaloids act on opioid receptors; it carries a real dependence and withdrawal risk, it is banned outright in several states, and concentrated 7-hydroxymitragynine products derived from it are the subject of active federal scheduling action. Plenty of people drink kava specifically because it is not that. If you are one of them, this is a room where you should order deliberately and ask what is in the cup — which the staff will tell you. For everyone else, it is one of the few genuinely late, genuinely alcohol-free places to sit in downtown Asheville, open to midnight Thursday through Saturday.

venues.name: ELEVEN Contemporary Kitchen
venues.description: ELEVEN is big Burrito Restaurant Group's flagship fine-dining restaurant, opened in 2004 as the group's eleventh — hence the name — in a rehabilitated warehouse on Smallman Street beside the old rail lines in the Strip District. Eli Wahl has been executive chef since 2016, only the third in its history, and Pittsburgh Magazine named it one of the city's 25 best restaurants for 2026. Wine and beverage director Rob Hirst builds the zero-proof list by taking a popular cocktail and re-creating it without alcohol, and it is printed as its own section headed "Zero Proof / NA Cocktails": the Cosmo-not ($12) on Seedlip Grove 42 and Dhos Orange with cranberry and lime; the Pink Flamingo ($12) on Dhos gin-free with strawberry-honey, lemon, cucumber and mint; Pimm's Pathfinder ($12), a faithful Pimm's Cup on Pathfinder amaro with cucumber and Fever-Tree ginger beer; and Sunrise Over Smallman ($14) on Ritual non-alcoholic tequila. Heineken 0.0 and Sam Adams Just the Haze cover the beer. The list rotates.
venues.longDescription:
ELEVEN opened in 2004 as big Burrito Restaurant Group's eleventh restaurant, which is where the name comes from, and it has been the group's flagship ever since. It sits in a rehabilitated warehouse alongside the old Pennsylvania rail lines on Smallman Street, an expansive room broken into pockets — a see-and-be-seen downstairs, moodier tables upstairs, and a seasonal patio over the street. Pittsburgh Magazine's verdict, putting it among the city's 25 best restaurants for 2026, was that Pittsburgh's dining scene owes it a great deal: for more than two decades this Strip District cornerstone has helped define what modern dining in the city can look like. Eli Wahl has run the kitchen since 2016, only the third executive chef in its history. Crab cake is $21, tuna tartare $19, ricotta cavatelli $28, black cod $42, prime strip steak $58.

The zero-proof list is the work of Rob Hirst, the wine and beverage director, a thirty-year veteran, and his method is worth quoting because it explains why these drinks land: he tries, for better or worse, to take a popular cocktail that he thinks would translate well without alcohol, and re-create it. His reading of why it matters is equally plain — the percentage of people drinking alcohol is down nationally, and people are being more conscious about health, about not drinking as much, and about not drinking and driving. The section is headed Zero Proof / NA Cocktails and runs four deep. The Cosmo-not at $12 rebuilds a Cosmopolitan on Seedlip Grove 42 and Dhos Orange with cranberry and lime. The Pink Flamingo, also $12, uses Dhos gin-free with strawberry-honey, lemon, cucumber, mint and lemon soda. Pimm's Pathfinder is the cleverest of them: Pathfinder amaro with cucumber, lemon and Fever-Tree ginger beer, which is a genuinely faithful Pimm's Cup, cucumber and all. Sunrise Over Smallman at $14 is the local one, built on Ritual non-alcoholic tequila with orange, peach, passionfruit, lime, grenadine and lemon soda. Heineken 0.0 and Sam Adams Just the Haze cover the beer. The list rotates annually or so, so expect the names to move on.
venues.pressQuote: I try to, for better, for worse, take a popular cocktail or cocktail that I think would translate well as an NA cocktail, and try to re-create it.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Rob Hirst, wine and beverage director

venues.name: Eli Tea Bar
venues.description: Eli Tea Bar is an explicitly alcohol-free "sober bar" in Andersonville, opened in November 2021 by founder Elias "Eli" Majid, who launched the original Eli Tea in Birmingham, Michigan in 2012 and attended Loyola University in Chicago. Occupying the former True North cafe space at 5507 N Clark St, it pours more than 100 loose-leaf teas, kombucha on tap, house bubble/boba tea (made with fresh milk, boiled tea, and tapioca pearls), chai, tea lattes, and tea-based mocktails such as the kombucha-nada. Majid describes the concept as sitting "between a wine bar and coffee shop," built to give LGBTQ+ and sober-curious Chicagoans a late-night place to gather without alcohol. Evenings bring open mics, book clubs, craft nights, trivia, drag bingo, and DJ sets. By late 2024 the shop was outpacing its sales goals and planning a line of canned non-alcoholic tonics.
venues.longDescription:
Eli Tea Bar opened at 5507 N Clark Street in December 2021, the second location of a Michigan tea company founded by Elias Majid, who studied at Loyola and had been waiting for the right moment to open in Chicago. It took over the former True North cafe space in Andersonville and fitted roughly two thousand square feet with a retail wall, cafe seating, a walk-up window and space for a small stage. The reception was immediate: our soft opening was not soft, Majid said a week in — it's been an insane embrace. His reading of why is the clearest argument for why this kind of room matters in a neighbourhood with a dense bar scene: the only late-night option is bars, he said, and the shop immediately had a rush of sober customers. It functions as an explicitly alcohol-free evening venue rather than a daytime cafe that happens to close late, and it programmes events — drag bingo sold out during its first month — that give people a reason to be there after dark.

The drinks are tea first and tea seriously. The shop carries more than a hundred loose-leaf options alongside its own in-house blends, with kombucha on tap and a bubble tea programme that is made properly rather than from powder: fresh milk, Indian-style boiled tea, tapioca pearls, sugar only if you ask for it, and oat or coconut milk versions for vegans, with no high-fructose corn syrup, preservatives or milk powders. Coffee and mocktails round out the list. Baked goods come from The Spoke & Bird in the South Loop. Two practical caveats. The shop does not publish an itemised drink list with prices online — its Chicago menu page runs through a mobile ordering widget rather than a readable menu — so the range is best browsed in person. And its Chicago page carries the Michigan flagship's address and phone number in the site footer, which is a template oversight rather than a relocation: the Chicago tea bar is on North Clark Street in Andersonville.
venues.pressQuote: We are proof of the concept that a sober space is needed. We have lots of programming. We have a diverse amount of customers — every age, every cultural background.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Elias Majid, Eli Tea Bar founder

The Harrison Street room in downtown Hollywood is where Elixir started, in February 2023, and it now anchors a four-site South Florida group. Two of the others already appear in this directory — the South Beach boutique on Meridian Avenue and the North Miami room on 123rd Street — and a fourth opened on the Hollywood Beach Broadwalk in December 2025. This original keeps the longest hours of the group by a margin: 10am to 3am, every day of the week, which makes it one of very few genuinely late alcohol-free rooms anywhere in downtown Hollywood.

The group sells itself as an organic mocktail bar and social workspace, and that dual framing is literal rather than decorative. Through the day the room functions as somewhere to work, with the power and connectivity that implies; through the evening and deep into the night it functions as a bar. Downtown Hollywood's Harrison Street strip is dense with conventional bars and restaurants, so a room on the same block trading to 3am without a liquor licence is a direct substitute rather than a consolation.

Kava is the foundation of the drinks list. It is the ground root of Piper methysticum, a South Pacific shrub, prepared as a water infusion and drunk socially across Fiji, Vanuatu, Tonga and Samoa for around three thousand years. It contains no alcohol, tastes earthy and bitter, numbs the lips and tongue at first sip, and is mildly sedative rather than intoxicating in alcohol's sense. Alongside it sits a genuine mocktail programme built on organic ingredients, which is presented as a headline rather than as an afterthought — the right way round for the audience this site serves.

One thing needs stating clearly rather than being left to a menu board, and it is the reason this entry carries a caution. Elixir's menu is built on two pillars, kava and what it markets as K-Tea, and K-Tea is kratom. The house framing describes it as a beverage from Indonesia and the Polynesian islands, a phrasing that folds two unrelated plants into a single tradition. They are not one tradition and they are not one risk profile. Kratom is the leaf of Mitragyna speciosa, a Southeast Asian tree, and its principal alkaloids act on the opioid receptors; regular use produces tolerance and a real withdrawal syndrome, several US states prohibit it outright, and its concentrated 7-hydroxymitragynine derivatives are the subject of live federal scheduling action. Kava has no equivalent dependence profile.

On a menu board the two sit inches apart and cost about the same, which is precisely why the distinction is easy to miss. If you have come to kava specifically to avoid substances that can take hold of you, order by name here, and ask.

Elixir Kava Bar's North Miami room at 2212 NE 123rd Street is the third of four sites in a group that started on Harrison Street in Hollywood in February 2023 and expanded quickly down into Miami-Dade. This directory already lists its South Beach boutique on Meridian Avenue; the Hollywood original and this room are both new here. It opens at 10am and closes at 1am seven days a week, which makes it the latest alcohol-free option on the 123rd–125th Street corridor by a comfortable margin.

The group's self-description — an organic mocktail bar and social workspace — is unusually literal about how the room gets used across a day. Through the afternoon it functions as a co-working space, with the power and WiFi that implies, and through the evening it turns into a bar. The mocktail programme is presented as the headline rather than as a concession, which is the right way round for the audience this directory serves, and the room is one of the few in North Miami where ordering something non-alcoholic at 11pm requires no explanation.

Geographically this belongs to the small northern cluster rather than to the Wynwood or South Beach scenes. Euphoria's North Miami branch is four blocks west on 125th Street, and Makana Kava Bar & Hawaiian Kitchen is on NW 7th Avenue. For anyone living in North Miami, North Miami Beach or Biscayne Park, this trio is the practical answer to an evening out, and Elixir is the one that stays open latest.

The disclosure matters more here than at most venues, because of how the menu is worded. Elixir's two pillars are kava and K-Tea, and K-Tea is kratom. The house framing describes it as a beverage from Indonesia and the Polynesian islands, a phrasing that blurs the two into one tradition. They are not one tradition and they are not one risk profile. Kava is the root of a South Pacific shrub, prepared as a cold water infusion, alcohol-free, mildly sedative, and drunk socially across Fiji, Vanuatu, Tonga and Samoa for roughly three millennia without an established pattern of physical dependence. Kratom is the leaf of a Southeast Asian tree, Mitragyna speciosa, whose alkaloids act on the opioid receptors; regular use produces tolerance and a genuine withdrawal syndrome, several US states ban it outright, and its concentrated 7-hydroxymitragynine derivatives are under active federal scheduling. If you are here because you want the social ritual of a bar without a substance that can take hold of you, kava is the order and kratom is not, and the two sit inches apart on this menu.

venues.longDescription:
Elixir Kava Boutique's South Beach room bills itself as Miami's first kava speakeasy, a fully alcohol-free lounge a short walk from the water at 418 Meridian Avenue. It is one of four Elixir locations across South Florida, which gives it something most independent kava bars lack — consistency of sourcing and preparation across sites.

The pours are freshly brewed kava and K-Tea, its kratom line, served in Red, Green and White strains plus a House Blend, alongside a roster of named mocktails: the Kavapolitan (kava, guava nectar, coconut milk, hibiscus syrup), Cinnamon Toast Krunch, The Thyme Machine, Blue Dream. Naming and building drinks rather than simply serving shells matters in South Beach specifically, where the surrounding competition is some of the most aggressive nightlife in the country and a plain cup of kava is a hard sell against it.

The room doubles as a social workspace, with WiFi, outdoor green-space seating and community events featuring live performances, and runs from early morning until 1am daily. There are no alcoholic drinks at all — the entire menu is non-alcoholic, which in South Beach makes it genuinely unusual rather than merely accommodating.

The caveat that belongs on every kava listing applies here and should not be softened: kava is psychoactive and sedating, with documented case reports of liver injury, and kratom acts on opioid receptors and carries real dependence and withdrawal risk. Everything served is free of alcohol. That is a narrower claim than nothing served having an effect, and for anyone whose reason for avoiding alcohol is recovery from a substance-use disorder, the difference is the whole question. South Beach is the hardest neighbourhood in Florida to spend an evening sober, which is precisely what makes a fully alcohol-free room a short walk from Ocean Drive worth knowing about. The speakeasy framing keeps it discreet rather than clinical, and the early-morning-to-1am span means it works as a workspace and as a night out on the same day.

One practical caution applies to every kava bar, here included. Kava is not alcohol, but it is psychoactive: it is a mild sedative and anxiolytic, and it interacts with alcohol, benzodiazepines and anything else that depresses the central nervous system. Some venues in this category also serve kratom, which is a different substance with a different and more contested risk profile, including physical dependence with regular use. If you are in recovery, treat that distinction as important rather than academic, ask staff directly what is in a drink before ordering, and check with a clinician if you take prescription medication. Staff at the established South Florida bars are generally straightforward about this if you ask.
venues.pressQuote: We pride ourselves on providing the most fresh Kava and K-Tea offerings you can find

The tiki-styled space — porch swings, couches, lanterns — is pet-friendly and hosts karaoke, live music, and game nights, building what Jepson calls a welcoming "tribe" of regulars who can gather whether or not they drink.

venues.longDescription:
Elixir Lounge Kava Bar is a fully alcohol-free tiki lounge and kava bar in Old Town Spring, the historic district on Houston's far-north edge. Founded by owner Chris Jepson, it opened on August 30, 2022, at 206 Main St. and celebrated its grand opening on September 3 with live music and hula dancers. It bills itself as the only N/A tiki-mocktail lounge, kava bar, and botanical-supplement shop in the Houston area.

The drink program centers on Polynesian kava and kratom, sourced from farms in Fiji, Vanuatu, and the Solomon Islands, served in traditional shells and bowls alongside zero-proof "virgin cocktails" like a Piña Colada (available straight or kava-infused) and a Mojo-jito. The tea side of the menu runs to iced cream teas, hot teas, and builds like the Lavender Lady (Earl Grey tea with vanilla and lavender syrups, whipped cream, and a honey drizzle), plus nitro cold brew, kombucha, artisan coffees, and herbal teas. Kava shells are poured in single and double sizes, with a Monday–Wednesday happy hour from 4–7pm.

Jepson brings real industry depth to the concept: before opening Elixir he worked as a kava and kratom supplier partnering with more than 65 kava bars nationally, visited over 150 kava establishments to study their operations and design, and has traveled to Indonesia 19 times to work directly with indigenous communities harvesting wild kratom leaves. Manager Cassandra Abercrombie frames the menu's two halves simply: kava is the calming side, kratom the energizing one.

The tiki-styled space — porch swings, couches, lanterns — is pet-friendly and hosts karaoke, drag bingo, live music, trivia, and game nights, building what Jepson calls a welcoming "tribe" of regulars who can gather whether or not they drink. At its 2022 debut the lounge's manager framed the goal as bringing "more night life, tourism and youth culture to Old Town Spring" — one of the district's first venues built entirely around zero-proof socializing.
venues.pressQuote: As more people seek alcohol-free social spaces, I saw a real need for a welcoming environment where anyone, regardless of whether they drink, can come together to unwind, connect and belong.

venues.name: Ellē
venues.description: Elle is a Mount Pleasant institution at 3221 Mt Pleasant Street NW that changes character through the day: a coffee shop and bakery in the morning, a counter-and-table lunch spot midday, and a full-service restaurant and bar at night. It opened in early 2018 in a former 1940s bakery, from founder and pastry chef Lizzy Evelyn with her husband Nick Pimentel, previously of Bad Saint and Room 11. The kitchen built its reputation on vegetable-forward cooking and acclaimed breads and pastries, earning a James Beard Best New Restaurant semifinalist nod in 2019 and the Michelin Bib Gourmand every year from 2021 through 2025. The bar pours alcohol-free cocktails including the Root Awakening, with watermelon shrub, Aperitivo Bianco NA, lemon, sumac and club soda, and a Pendennis Punch of black tea, pomegranate and bitters, alongside alcohol-free wines.
venues.address: 3221 Mt Pleasant St NW, Washington, DC 20010
signatureDrinks: Root Awakening (watermelon shrub, Aperitivo Bianco NA, lemon, sumac, club soda)
venues.longDescription:
Elle occupies a former 1940s bakery on Mt Pleasant Street, and it has kept the building's logic: bread and pastry in the morning, then a room that gradually becomes a restaurant. It opened in early 2018 from Lizzy Evelyn, founder and pastry chef, and her husband Nick Pimentel, who came from Bad Saint and Room 11 - two of the more serious rooms in the city at the time. The reputation was built on the baking and on vegetable-forward, inventive cooking rather than on a signature dish, and the recognition followed: a James Beard Best New Restaurant semifinalist nod in 2019, Bon Appetit naming it a Top 50 Best New Restaurant in America in 2018, and the Michelin Bib Gourmand every year from 2021 through 2025, alongside repeated placements on Washingtonian and Time Out best-of lists.

What makes it genuinely useful for someone not drinking is the shape of the day rather than only the drinks list. A room that serves good coffee at eight in the morning and a proper dinner at eight at night is a different proposition from a bar that opens at five, because it can be a morning, an afternoon or an evening without any of those requiring a decision about alcohol. On the drinks themselves, Resy's January 2025 roundup of DC bars with superb zero-proof cocktails noted that this popular cafe and restaurant offers unique non-alcoholic cocktails, wine and beer. The two named builds are the Root Awakening - watermelon shrub with Aperitivo Bianco NA, lemon, sumac and club soda, which uses the shrub's vinegar edge where a spritz would normally use bitterness - and the Pendennis Punch, made with black tea, pomegranate and bitters. Behind them sit low-ABV beers and alcohol-free wines including J&H Funkelwurtz sparkling.

Practical notes. Elle opens at 8am every day. Monday and Sunday it closes at 3pm, running as a bakery and lunch room only; Tuesday through Saturday it continues to 9pm with full dinner service. Mount Pleasant is a residential neighbourhood rather than a nightlife strip, which is part of the appeal - the room is quiet enough to talk in, and it is a short walk from Columbia Heights Metro.
venues.pressQuote: This popular café and restaurant offers unique non-alcoholic cocktails, wine, and beer
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Resy, 10 Washington, D.C. Bars With Superb Zero-Proof Cocktails, January 2025

venues.name: Elm & Good
venues.description: Elm & Good, the American tavern inside Deep Ellum's Kimpton Pittman Hotel, builds its zero-proof drinks on Seedlip rather than defaulting to soda-and-syrup. The bar pours a Gingiberi Fizz made with Seedlip Spice 42, ginger syrup, orange cordial, lemon, aquafaba and ginger beer, plus the Espresso Self, a spirit-free take on the espresso martini. These are shaken, aquafaba-foamed builds pulled from the same seasonal cocktail program the bar runs, not an afterthought Shirley Temple.
signatureDrinks: Gingiberi Fizz — Seedlip Spice 42, ginger syrup, orange cordial, lemon, aquafaba, ginger beer
Espresso Self — a zero-proof take on the espresso martini
venues.longDescription:
Elm & Good is the ground-floor restaurant and bar of the Kimpton Pittman Hotel, set inside the historic 1916 Knights of Pythias Temple on Elm Street in the heart of Deep Ellum. It opened in 2020 as a farm-to-table American tavern under founding chef Graham Dodds, with menus that spotlight Texas and Gulf Coast ingredients, sustainably ranched meats and produce from local farms. The kitchen is now led by executive chef JV Hernandez, and the room serves all-day brunch, a mid-afternoon Golden Hour and dinner daily.

The non-alcoholic angle here runs through the same seasonal cocktail list that drives the bar. Its headline zero-proof build is the Gingiberi Fizz — Seedlip Spice 42, ginger syrup, orange cordial, lemon, aquafaba and ginger beer — a properly shaken, egg-white-style foamed drink rather than a sweet mocktail. It sits alongside the Espresso Self, a spirit-free riff on the espresso martini, giving no-proof drinkers two considered options built on a real botanical distillate.

PaperCity Magazine featured Elm & Good in its Dallas Dry January mocktails guide, singling the tavern out for its zero-proof cocktail options. The bar is a comfortable fit for Deep Ellum visitors and hotel guests who want a genuine cocktail experience without the alcohol, in one of the neighborhood's most storied buildings.
venues.pressQuote: This upscale American tavern has a few great mocktail options.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: PaperCity Magazine, "The Best Mocktails in Dallas For a Dry — Or Damp — January"

venues.name: Elsewhere Cocktail Bar
venues.description: Elsewhere is an intimate craft cocktail bar tucked under South End's iconic Design Center water tower, co-founded by Wooden Robot Brewery CEO Josh Patton. The bar has prioritized an inclusive non-alcoholic program since day one, offering a rotating "For the Pilot" menu of thoughtfully crafted mocktails. Highlights include the "So Fun" — an NA margarita made with Ritual zero-proof tequila, pineapple, orange, lime, and jalapeño — alongside NA Guinness and Athletic Brewing on the menu.
venues.address: 101 W Worthington Ave, Suite 140, Charlotte, NC 28203
venues.hours: Mon closed; Tue-Wed 5pm-11pm; Thu 5pm-12am; Fri 4pm-2am; Sat 1pm-2am; Sun 4pm-10pm
venues.longDescription:
Elsewhere is an intimate craft cocktail bar tucked under the Design Center water tower in Charlotte's Historic South End, co-founded by Wooden Robot Brewery CEO Josh Patton. The location is a landmark — the water tower is one of the most recognisable objects in South End — and the bar itself is deliberately small in a district that has otherwise filled up with large, loud rooms.

What distinguishes it for this directory is that the non-alcoholic programme was not retrofitted. Elsewhere has prioritised an inclusive spirit-free list since it opened, running a rotating menu under the heading "For the Pilot" — the designated-driver framing done with some wit rather than apology. The headline build is the So Fun, a non-alcoholic margarita made with Ritual zero-proof tequila, pineapple, orange, lime and jalapeno, which puts real heat and acid into a category that too often defaults to sweetness. Alongside it sit the Moscow Midnight and the Greyhound Rescue, and the bar stocks non-alcoholic Guinness and Athletic Brewing for anyone who would rather have a beer. Guinness 0.0 is a particularly useful thing for a bar to carry, because it is one of very few non-alcoholic beers that looks completely unremarkable in the hand.

Queen City Nerve captured the register the bar is aiming for better than a description could: "These aren't beverages that will earn you a seat at the kid's table, but they also aren't going to cause you to dance on the table either." That is the whole proposition of a good spirit-free list in one sentence — adult, considered, and not a punishment. The bar runs late on weekends, to 2am on Friday and Saturday, which makes it a genuine night out rather than an early stop. Closed Mondays.
venues.pressQuote: These aren't beverages that will earn you a seat at the kid's table, but they also aren't going to cause you to dance on the table either.

venues.name: Emerald Eye
venues.description: Emerald Eye is an underground tropical cocktail bar beneath Larimer Square, opened in July 2023 by the hospitality group Pouring With Heart and modelled on the Caribbean of around 1955 — green tile, vintage-inspired lighting, botanical wall coverings and DJs playing Caribbean music at weekends. Its rum and agave programme is the main draw, but the menu carries a standing "NON ALCOHOLIC" heading with three house drinks at $12 apiece: an NA Piña Colada, an NA Margarita and an NA Negroni built on a non-alcoholic aperitif and non-alcoholic amaro. The bar opens at 4pm daily and runs to midnight on weeknights and 1am on Friday and Saturday, which makes it one of the later options downtown for a built alcohol-free drink.
signatureDrinks: NA Negroni (NA aperitif, grapefruit, NA amaro — $12)
NA Piña Colada (pineapple, passionfruit, lemon, coconut — $12)

naMenuItems.name: Heineken 0.0
naMenuItems.description: non-alcoholic

venues.longDescription:
Emerald Eye opened in July 2023 in the basement of 1403 Larimer Street, beneath the historic Larimer Square block, from Pouring With Heart — a hospitality organisation whose stated purpose is preserving existing bars and supporting the industry professionals who work in them. The concept is the Caribbean of around 1955, and the room commits to it: 303 Magazine described it on opening as "adorned with a dark tropical design from shining green tile, vintage-inspired lighting and botanical wall coverings", adding that "Emerald Eye brings a bit of mystery to the area". DJs play Caribbean sets at weekends, and the bar's own framing is a curated rum and agave programme with modern riffs on classic cocktails.

The non-alcoholic offering is modest by the standards of Denver's most committed zero-proof bars, but it is real, printed and consistent. The menu carries "NON ALCOHOLIC" as its own heading, with three house drinks at $12 each — a genuine price point rather than a soft-drink one, which reflects that these are built to order. The NA Piña Colada combines pineapple and passionfruit with lemon and coconut, keeping the tropical register of the rest of the list. The NA Margarita is drier and sharper, built from lime, agave, apple and ginger. The most interesting of the three is the NA Negroni, which uses a non-alcoholic aperitif and a non-alcoholic amaro with grapefruit — the bitter-aperitivo style is the hardest category to do without alcohol, and a bar that stocks two separate zero-proof bitter products to make one drink has made a deliberate choice rather than an improvised one. Red Bull and its sugar-free version are also listed for anyone who wants something else. Practically, Emerald Eye is useful because of its hours and location: 4pm to midnight Sunday through Thursday and 4pm to 1am on Friday and Saturday, in the middle of the downtown block most visitors end up on, in a room dark and busy enough that nobody is going to notice or ask what is in your glass.
venues.pressQuote: Adorned with a dark tropical design from shining green tile, vintage-inspired lighting and botanical wall coverings, Emerald Eye brings a bit of mystery to the area.

venues.name: Emerald Lounge
venues.description: Emerald Lounge is a small cocktail and wine bar on West 7th Street in Saint Paul, in the stretch between downtown and the Fort Road neighbourhoods. It keeps a named temperance menu alongside the full-strength list, carrying non-alcoholic beer and wine as well as house-built zero-proof cocktails. The two the city's visitor bureau singles out are the Crimson Breezeberry Shrub, made with raspberry, ginger, champagne vinegar and soda, and the Captain Jack Sparrow, built on milk-washed pineapple with coconut syrup, lime acid and mint — both using techniques, shrub acidity and milk-washing, that a bar reaches for when it wants a spirit-free drink to have structure rather than just sweetness.
venues.hours: Mon closed; Tue-Thu 5pm-10pm; Fri-Sat 5pm-11pm; Sun closed
signatureDrinks: Crimson Breezeberry Shrub (raspberry, ginger, champagne vinegar, soda)
Captain Jack Sparrow (milk-washed pineapple, coconut syrup, lime acid, mint)
venues.longDescription:
West 7th Street runs south-west out of downtown Saint Paul past the arena and the old brewery district, and its bar scene has historically been an honest one of neighbourhood taverns rather than cocktail rooms. Emerald Lounge opened into that stretch as a small, dark, intimate cocktail and wine bar with a seasonal food menu, and it is one of the few places on the corridor doing precise drink work. It runs evenings only, Tuesday through Saturday, closed Sunday and Monday, which keeps the room small and the bar attentive.

What earns it a place here is that the non-alcoholic drinks are given their own named menu section — the bar calls it a temperance menu, borrowing the nineteenth-century term — rather than being handled as an off-list request. That section carries non-alcoholic beer and wine by the bottle and glass alongside house-built zero-proof cocktails. Visit Saint Paul's guide to drinking without alcohol in the city names two of them. The Crimson Breezeberry Shrub is built on raspberry and ginger with champagne vinegar and soda: the vinegar is the working part, supplying the acid bite that would otherwise have to come from a spirit and keeping the drink from collapsing into fruit syrup. The Captain Jack Sparrow uses milk-washed pineapple with coconut syrup, lime acid and mint — milk-washing being the clarification technique that strips harshness and leaves a silky texture, and one that takes real bar time to execute. Both are the kind of build that signals a bar treating the zero-proof column as a craft problem rather than a compliance exercise. The bar is licensed and its full-strength cocktail and wine list remains the main programme, so this is not an alcohol-free venue; the temperance menu sits beside it. Note that the drink names above come from the city's visitor bureau rather than from a dated menu, so seasonal rotation is possible — worth confirming at the bar.

venues.name: Encina
venues.description: Encina is a farm-to-table New American restaurant in Oak Cliff's Bishop Arts District, operating since 2020, with a documented zero-proof cocktail menu built on Ritual Zero Proof spirits—priced at $10 each—alongside Athletic Brewing on the beer list.
venues.address: 614 W Davis St, Suite 100, Dallas, TX 75208
signatureDrinks: Cactus Jill (Ritual Zero Proof tequila, Giffard aperitif, lime, sweet peppers, dill)
Watermelon Rhapsody (watermelon cordial, cucumber, jalapeño, coconut water, sparkling water)
Peach Buck (Ritual Zero Proof whiskey, peach, apricot, chamomile, lemon, mint ginger beer)
