naMenuItems.description: ritual zero proof tequila, giffard aperitif, lime, sweet peppers, dill

naMenuItems.name: Athletic Brewing Upside Dawn
naMenuItems.description: non-alcoholic golden

venues.longDescription:
Encina sits in the former Bolsa space on W. Davis Street in Oak Cliff's Bishop Arts District, and for non-alcoholic drinkers it offers something more considered than the usual soda-or-nothing choice. The restaurant carries a dedicated set of zero-proof cocktails built on Ritual Zero Proof spirits, priced at $10, available at dinner and weekend brunch. The neighborhood itself draws a mix of regulars and destination diners, and the private lot makes it one of the easier parking situations in the area.

The zero-proof list still runs three cocktails, all at $10, reflecting the same seasonal, ingredient-forward thinking as the food menu. The Cactus Jill pairs Ritual Zero Proof Tequila with Giffard Aperitif, lime, sweet peppers, and dill—a savory-leaning riff on a margarita. The Watermelon Rhapsody is a spirit-free cooler of watermelon cordial, cucumber, jalapeño, coconut water, and sparkling water. The Peach Buck uses Ritual Zero Proof Whiskey with peach, apricot, chamomile, lemon, and mint ginger beer—a fruit-forward successor to the earlier Kentucky-Less Buck, which has rotated off the menu along with the Pineapple Nojito. The beverage program is overseen by co-owner Corey McCombs, who built the cocktail menu to mirror chef and co-owner Matt Balke's ethos of fresh, seasonal ingredients with only four or five components per drink. Athletic Brewing's Upside Dawn non-alcoholic golden ale also appears on the beer list.

Encina earned Dallas Observer's Best Brunch recognition in 2025, and Texas Monthly has listed it as a notable Dallas restaurant. The dress code is casual, reservations are recommended especially for weekend brunch, and the restaurant accepts OpenTable bookings. It's a strong pick for non-drinkers joining a group dinner or brunch—the zero-proof options are priced and presented on par with the cocktail list, not tucked away as an afterthought. The patio and private dining room make it work for larger gatherings too.
venues.pressQuote: Encina's zero proof cocktail menu is made with Ritual Zero Proof alcohol and are $10 each.

venues.name: Eno Vino Downtown
venues.description: Eno Vino Downtown is a wine bar and bistro on the eighth floor of the AC Hotel on North Webster Street, with views over the Capitol and Lake Monona, and it keeps a full mocktail menu rather than a token line. The named builds cover the ground a wine bar's customers actually ask for: a honey ginger lemon spritz, an apple cinnamon mule, a pal-no-ma and a strawberry nada-rita, plus Leitz Eins Zwei Zero non-alcoholic sparkling rosé by the glass — which matters in a room whose whole premise is wine. It opens at 4pm daily and runs to midnight, or 1am on Friday and Saturday.
signatureDrinks: Leitz Eins Zwei Zero non-alcoholic sparkling rosé
venues.longDescription:
Eno Vino sits eight floors up in the AC Hotel on North Webster Street, a block off the Capitol Square, and trades on the view as much as the list — the Capitol dome on one side, Lake Monona on the other, and a wraparound terrace that is one of the better places in Madison to be on a summer evening. It is a wine bar and bistro, with small plates built to go with the glass pours.

A wine bar is a structurally hard room for a non-drinker: the entire proposition is the bottle, and the usual alcohol-free option is a soda from the gun. Eno Vino runs a full mocktail menu instead, and the shape of it is telling. The honey ginger lemon spritz and the apple cinnamon mule are long, aromatic drinks that hold up over a meal the way a glass of wine would. The pal-no-ma and the strawberry nada-rita cover the tequila-shaped requests. Most usefully for this particular room, the bar pours Leitz Eins Zwei Zero non-alcoholic sparkling rosé by the glass — a de-alcoholised German wine rather than a grape soda, which means somebody not drinking can order wine, in a wine bar, and be handed wine. That single listing does more for the experience than four mocktails do.

Two practical notes. The hours are evening-only — 4pm daily, to midnight Sunday through Thursday and 1am on Friday and Saturday — so this is a night-out venue rather than a flexible one. And there is a second Eno Vino on Madison's west side with its own mocktail list, including a berries mojito, a blueberry basil crush and a passion spritz; the drinks named here are the downtown location's. Merchant, Lucille and Settle Down Tavern are all within a few minutes' walk around the Square.
venues.pressQuote: Eno Vino Downtown's mocktail menu includes a honey ginger lemon spritz, apple cinnamon mule, pal-no-ma, strawberry nada-rita and Leitz's Eins Zwei Zero NA sparkling rosé.

venues.name: Epiphany
venues.description: Epiphany opened at the end of 2022 on Highland Avenue in the Original Highlands, describing itself as a cocktail bar, brewery and spirits house built around bringing the farm-to-table idea into drinks. That premise is why its non-alcoholic drinks work: when the programme already runs on local produce, house syrups and infusions, removing the alcohol removes one ingredient rather than the whole structure. The alcohol-free list rotates seasonally. Verified builds include the Orange Turmeric Limeade, made with local honey from Happy Jack's Pumpkin Farm, orange blossom water and mint, and a seasonal Rose Ginger Lemonade. It is one of the city's most-cited zero-proof programmes.
signatureDrinks: Orange Turmeric Limeade (Happy Jack's Pumpkin Farm honey, orange blossom water, mint)

naMenuItems.name: Go Brewing: Suspended in a Sunbeam Pilsner
naMenuItems.description: german malt + hops, fresh, floral

naMenuItems.name: Sierra Nevada Trail Pass IPA
naMenuItems.description: amarillo + citra + mosaic hops, tangerine, grapefruit, pine, lush + aromatic

venues.longDescription:
The Original Highlands is the near end of Louisville's Highlands — closer to downtown than the Bardstown Road strip, quieter, more residential — and Epiphany opened there at the end of 2022 on Highland Avenue. It describes itself as a cocktail bar, brewery and spirits house, and its stated ambition is to bring farm-to-table thinking into the beverage world: sourcing produce locally, making its own syrups, cordials and infusions, and building drinks around what is actually growing rather than around a back bar.

That is the single best predictor of whether a bar's non-alcoholic drinks will be any good. A bar whose cocktails are spirit plus mixer has nothing left when the spirit goes; a bar whose cocktails are built from house components has most of the drink already made. Epiphany's liquor-free list rotates with the seasons for the same reason its cocktails do. The build most often cited is the Orange Turmeric Limeade — lime and turmeric sweetened with honey from Happy Jack's Pumpkin Farm, lifted with orange blossom water and mint, which is a savoury, aromatic drink rather than a sweet one, and name-checks the specific farm the honey comes from. A Rose Ginger Lemonade runs as a seasonal alternative. Because the list turns over, the sensible approach is to ask what is on rather than arrive expecting a specific glass.

GoToLouisville, the city's official visitor bureau, singled the bar out in its guide to where to drink alcohol-free in Louisville, which is a useful signal in a city whose zero-proof coverage is otherwise thin and quickly goes stale. Worth knowing: this is a full cocktail bar and spirits house, so alcohol is very much present — the appeal is the quality of the alternative, not a sober room. It is a short drive or a long walk from the Bardstown Road cluster where Seviche and LouVino sit, and about ten minutes from Butchertown.
venues.pressQuote: Epiphany has come out swinging with its non-alcoholic offerings, with liquor-free libations that rotate seasonally.

venues.name: Equipment Room
venues.description: Equipment Room is a hi-fi vinyl listening bar tucked under Hotel Magdalena on Music Lane just off South Congress, inspired by mid-century Tokyo kissa bars. The cocktail menu was developed by Austin mixologist Robert Björn Taylor (formerly of Péché, Otoko, and Emmer & Rye) and is split into an A-Side of classics and a B-Side of creative riffs. The audio system features custom Klipsch Heritage speakers and SIVGA headphones at select listening stations. Cocktails are $18; mocktails are available at $12. The space is intimate (reservations recommended via Resy), with food including caramel puffed cheese corn, tomato toast, and karaage.
signatureDrinks: The Pleasure Principle (NA: pathfinder, strawberry shrub, soda)
In Bloom (NA: pink peppercorn infused-ritual gin, grapefruit & rosemary infused-tonic syrup, el guapo bitters)

naMenuItems.name: The Pleasure Principle
naMenuItems.description: pathfinder, strawberry shrub, soda

naMenuItems.name: In Bloom
naMenuItems.description: pink peppercorn infused-ritual gin, grapefruit & rosemary infused-tonic syrup, el guapo bitters

venues.longDescription:
Equipment Room is a hi-fi vinyl listening bar underneath Hotel Magdalena on Music Lane, just off South Congress, and it is modelled on the mid-century Tokyo kissa — rooms built around a record collection and a sound system, where the music is the reason you are there and conversation is kept at a level that does not compete with it. The collection runs to around 1,200 records, played through custom Klipsch Heritage speakers, with SIVGA headphones at select listening stations for anyone who wants to disappear into a record entirely.

The cocktail menu was built by Robert Björn Taylor, previously of Péché, Otoko and Emmer & Rye, and is split into an A-Side of classics and a B-Side of original riffs. Cocktails are eighteen dollars; mocktails are twelve and available on request rather than as a separate named list. Food runs to caramel puffed cheese corn, tomato toast and karaage.

The format is the reason it belongs on this site. A listening bar solves the specific problem of not drinking better than almost any other kind of venue, because it supplies the thing alcohol is usually recruited to supply — a reason to be there, and a structure for the evening. The room runs at roughly 65 to 70 decibels: quiet enough to talk, loud enough that nobody expects constant talking. There is no round-buying, no bar to stand at, and no lull that a drink is needed to fill.

Bunkhouse, the group behind Hotel Magdalena, has form for rooms with this much specificity, and the intimacy is real — reservations through Resy are recommended rather than optional, because the space is small.

Open Monday to Thursday from 5pm to midnight, Friday from 5pm and Saturday from 2pm until 2am, closed Sunday. Ask the bartender what they can build zero-proof; the mocktails are made to the same standard as the A-Side, they just are not printed.

venues.name: Equitea Matcha Studio
venues.description: Equitea Matcha Studio is the first brick-and-mortar café from Equitea, the tea brand built by West Baltimore native Quentin Vennie, who grew the company on the West Coast before bringing it back home to Remington. The room is fully alcohol-free and built entirely around matcha — the studio describes itself as "an intimate matcha studio shaped by craft, sound, and sensory detail." The list runs to a lavender oat milk matcha sweetened with apple sugar, a yuzu matcha soda, a dirty iced matcha, and a matcha tonic made with lavender syrup. It is a daytime room, open Wednesday through Sunday and closed by late afternoon, rather than a nightlife stop.
signatureDrinks: Lavender oat milk matcha with apple sugar
venues.longDescription:
Equitea Matcha Studio opened at 311 W 28th Street in Remington in late December 2025, the first bricks-and-mortar home for a tea brand that Baltimore Magazine calls the city's first matcha house. It comes from Quentin Vennie, who grew up in West Baltimore and came to tea through his own health: he has written and spoken openly about years of anxiety, depression and prescription drug dependence, and about wellness practice as the thing that pulled him out of it. He is a certified yoga instructor and served as a vice president of the Yoga Alliance Foundation. He founded The Greenhouse Tea Co. with his wife Erin in 2020 and launched Equitea on Father's Day 2022; Gwyneth Paltrow found the brand on social media and became its first investor and a co-owner. The studio began as a pop-up on North Howard Street in February 2025 before taking the permanent space.

The room was designed by the artist and plantsman Hilton Carter, and it is built for staying rather than queueing — a listening station with vinyl, a lot of plants, and natural materials made by local artisans. The matcha is treated with the seriousness the format deserves: whisked into a paste for twenty to thirty seconds against water held at exactly 175 degrees Fahrenheit, which is the difference between a smooth bowl and a bitter one. The drinks run to iced matcha lattes with strawberry purée, hojicha lattes built on roasted green tea and oat milk, cold brew lattes, and matcha sodas, with drinks around the $6 mark. Everything here is alcohol-free by nature rather than by substitution, and there is nothing infused with anything else — no THC, CBD or functional additives anywhere on the menu, which is worth stating plainly in a state where that is no longer a safe assumption. Open Wednesday to Saturday from 9am to 4pm and Sundays 10am to 3pm.
venues.pressQuote: Being able to bring this business back to Baltimore and anchor ourselves back in this city — it's been an incredible thing

venues.name: Erst
venues.description: Erst is a Michelin Bib Gourmand natural-wine restaurant in Ancoats, serving modern Mediterranean sharing plates from an open kitchen. In January 2026 it launched the Soft Supper Club, an alcohol-free pairing series that treats zero-proof as a considered part of fine dining rather than an afterthought. The debut sequence matched a slow run of sharing plates with an aperitif, house-made sodas, palate cleansers and Eisberg's premium alcohol-free wines, developed with Manchester drinks start-up Fun Softs. It is a rare chance to eat a Michelin-recognised, tasting-style meal entirely without alcohol.
signatureDrinks: Eisberg Selection Blanc de Blancs - premium alcohol-free sparkling white poured as an opening aperitif
House-made sodas - served as palate cleansers between the sharing plates
Eisberg Grenache Rosé, Pinot Noir and Pinot Grigio - alcohol-free wines paired course by course through the meal
venues.longDescription:
Erst sits at 9 Murray Street in Ancoats, a neighbourhood natural-wine restaurant run by a group of friends who wanted to build somewhere they would choose to eat themselves. The Michelin Guide awarded it a Bib Gourmand in the 2026 edition, with inspectors calling it "inch perfect for 2026" and describing a place that "combines a natural wine bar with small plates and stripped-back industrial design." Expect an open kitchen, bright and punchy Mediterranean sharing plates, freshly charred flatbreads and keenly priced natural wines, many of which you can buy to take home.

The non-alcoholic angle is the Soft Supper Club, which launched at Erst on Sunday 25 January 2026 as the first in an intended ongoing series and is hosted by sobriety creator Karl Considine. Guests sit communally for a slow sequence of sharing plates, each matched to an alcohol-free pairing: an opening aperitif, house-made sodas, palate cleansers and Eisberg Selection premium alcohol-free wines (Blanc de Blancs, Grenache Rosé, Pinot Noir and Pinot Grigio), created in partnership with Manchester drinks start-up Fun Softs. The premise is that zero-proof choices can sit confidently within fine dining, not as a fallback but as a pairing in their own right.

That philosophy runs through the kitchen too. Co-founder Will Sutton has said the team believes every drinks option "should feel exciting, celebratory and aligned with our cooking" - a framing that puts the alcohol-free list on the same footing as Erst's celebrated natural-wine cellar. Because the Soft Supper Club runs as periodic events rather than an everyday printed menu, check Erst's channels for upcoming dates before planning an alcohol-free visit.
venues.pressQuote: We believe that all of our drinks options should feel exciting, celebratory and aligned with our cooking.

venues.name: Estereo
venues.description: Estereo is the Latin-American all-day bar from Heisler Hospitality on Milwaukee Avenue in Logan Square, known for one of Chicago's most serious agave spirits lists and, alongside it, a standing Non-Alcoholic section on the same printed menu. Two of its zero-proof pours are built in-house: a tepache of pineapple, black pepper, cloves, piloncillo and Rare Tea Cellar Mallorca melon tea, and an agua fresca of Seedling Farms tart cherries and mint. Two are mixed drinks - a Rosemary Spritz with rosemary syrup, lime and Martini and Rossi Floreale, and a Three Spirits Mule with ginger syrup, pina, lime and Three Spirits Nightcap. Athletic Brewing's Atletica NA copper ale and Lagunitas hop water complete the list, and the house coffee cocktail has a stated NA version.

venues.longDescription:
Estereo opened on Milwaukee Avenue in Logan Square as an all-day bar from Heisler Hospitality, the group behind Pub Royale, Sportsman's Club and Queen Mary Tavern, with drinks originally developed by Ben Fasman and Michael Rubel. The design is deliberately transporting - tiled floors, patterned detailing, a large triangular bar, roll-up garage doors on two sides for summer - and the soundtrack comes off a turntable. The bar's reputation rests on its agave program, a spirits list that runs to well over a hundred mezcals, destilados and sotols priced by the ounce and organized by producer, and on the Breezy, a house highball of yerba mate, falernum, lime and soda served in a branded plastic cup.

What makes it useful to non-drinkers is that the Non-Alcoholic heading sits inside that same menu, between the wine list and the agave spirits, with drinks that get the same treatment as everything else. Two are house preparations: a tepache built from pineapple, black pepper, cloves and piloncillo, lengthened with Rare Tea Cellar's Mallorca melon tea at $8, and an agua fresca of Seedling Farms tart cherries and mint at $7. Two are mixed: the Rosemary Spritz, made with rosemary syrup, lime and Martini and Rossi Floreale at $12, and the Three Spirits Mule of ginger syrup, pina, lime, simple syrup and Three Spirits Nightcap, also $12. Packaged options include Lagunitas hop water and Athletic Brewing's Atletica, a Mexican-style non-alcoholic copper ale, and the house coffee cocktail - 4 Letter Word cold brew with house horchata - is listed with an NA version at $10. The bar closes at 2am seven days a week, so the zero-proof list is available for the whole of a real night out. Estereo has a second location in Fulton Market carrying the same non-alcoholic heading at slightly different prices - tepache at $10, the Rosemary Spritz at $13, the Three Spirits Mule at $13 - and adding a St Agrestis Phony Negroni at $12 to that list. Empanadas from Cafe Tola are the food offer at that site; the Logan Square room serves a light snack menu in the morning and nothing after dark.
venues.pressQuote: Music from a turntable fills the air with bright Latin-American tunes.

venues.name: Eucalyptus Wellness Co. and Elixir Bar
venues.description: A natural-health store and plant-based elixir bar in Mount Pleasant's Houston Northcutt Boulevard shopping center, pouring herbal adaptogen drinks alongside smoothies, acai bowls, and toasts. The fully alcohol-free Elixir Bar builds its signature 20 oz tonics on superfoods, adaptogens, and Chinese herbs, with named blends like Brainstorm, Immune Delight, Energy Elixir, Beauty Burst, and Spirit. The shop also stocks CBD products, supplements, vitamins, and aromatherapy, and offers multi-day juice cleanses.
venues.address: 920 Houston Northcutt Blvd, Mount Pleasant, SC 29464
venues.longDescription:
Eucalyptus is a locally owned wellness store and elixir bar at 920 Houston Northcutt Blvd in Mount Pleasant. Its Elixir Bar serves herbal drinks the shop describes as "formulated with superfoods, adaptogens, and Chinese herbs to nourish every cell of your body" - $13, 20 oz blends such as Brainstorm (cacao, medicinal mushroom, ginkgo), Immune Delight (turmeric, ginger, astragalus, elderberry), Energy Elixir (ginseng, matcha, moringa, chlorophyll), and Spirit (passionflower, ashwagandha). The menu rounds out with smoothies, acai and blue bowls, avocado and salmon toasts, and 1-, 3-, and 5-day juice cleanses.

The concept is entirely alcohol-free: there is no beer, wine, or liquor on the menu, making it a botanical, daytime alternative to a conventional bar. The business is open Monday through Saturday and remains active in 2025-2026, with recent reviews across Yelp, Restaurantji, and Tripadvisor and a maintained website and Instagram presence.

venues.name: Eunice
venues.neighborhood: Upper Kirby / Greenway Plaza (Buffalo Speedway at Richmond)
venues.description: Eunice, chef-partner Drake Leonards' modern Cajun-Creole brasserie and raw bar in Greenway Plaza, keeps a standing "Mocktails" section on its regular menu alongside its full bar and raw bar. Both current drinks — the Strawberry Fizz and the Prickly Pear Ade — are built with fresh fruit and citrus over Topo Chico rather than poured from a bottle. The kitchen has also rotated in named zero-proof cocktails using Cut Above 0% proof spirits for past Dry January menus, showing the non-alcoholic list gets real seasonal attention rather than sitting as an afterthought.

venues.longDescription:
Chef-partner Drake Leonards, a Louisiana native who trained in New Orleans, at Manhattan's Michelin-starred Café Boulud, and for two years in Germany's Black Forest, opened Eunice in 2018 at 3737 Buffalo Speedway in Houston's Greenway Plaza — BRG Hospitality's first Houston restaurant, named after Leonards' hometown of Eunice, Louisiana. The modern Cajun-Creole brasserie and raw bar earned a Best New Restaurant nomination, a three-star review from Houston Chronicle critic Alison Cook, and a StarChefs Rising Star Chef honor for Leonards.

On the standing menu, Eunice runs a dedicated "Mocktails" section with two named, priced non-alcoholic drinks: the Strawberry Fizz (strawberry, lemon, Topo Chico) and the Prickly Pear Ade (prickly pear, lemon, lime, Topo Chico), each $8. The list rotates with the seasons — for Dry January 2025, Bayou Beat News reported Eunice serving the Cobbler's Cruise (Cut Above 0% proof gin, strawberry, orgeat) and the Undercover Chili (Cut Above 0% proof tequila, jalapeño, pineapple). Across rotations the restaurant has kept named, priced, alcohol-free options in circulation rather than treating it as a one-off gesture, even though the venue itself serves a full raw bar and cocktail program and is not alcohol-free.

The restaurant sits at the corner of Buffalo Speedway and Richmond Avenue on the edge of Upper Kirby. It's open daily for lunch and dinner and remains an active, frequently reviewed spot in 2026.
venues.pressQuote: Celebrate Dry January in style at Eunice, Houston's upscale Louisiana restaurant in Greenway Plaza. Known for its elevated seafood-forward menu, Eunice also caters to guests seeking non-alcoholic options with thoughtfully crafted mocktails.

venues.name: Euphorbia Kava & Coffee Bar
venues.description: Euphorbia is New Orleans' original kava bar, open on the Uptown end of Oak Street since 2014. It's a fully alcohol-free space built around kava, the calming Pacific-island root beverage, and has spent over a decade as a refuge for the city's sober and recovery communities. In August 2025, Big Easy Magazine publisher Scott Ploof acquired it and relaunched it as Euphorbia Kava & Coffee Bar, adding a late-night coffee program with local roaster Hey! Café and house kava/coffee mocktails. The signature pour is the Supermoon, espresso blended with kava for "energy and calm," alongside traditional pure-noble kava and canned kava seltzers (Leilo, Vanua Bliss). Regulars describe it as a community hub for artists and people in recovery; it also stocks THC/CBD products.
signatureDrinks: Crescent 9 and Cheech and Chong THC beverages
venues.longDescription:
Euphorbia has been on Oak Street since September 2014 and is New Orleans' original kava bar. Kava is prepared from the root of Piper methysticum, native to the South Pacific and used ceremonially and socially there for centuries, and the bar's best-selling product remains pure noble kava root served in its most traditional form — known for a calming, anti-anxiety effect without the loss of mental clarity that alcohol brings. Around it the bar builds kava-and-coffee drinks you will not find elsewhere in the city, the standout being the Supermoon, which blends espresso shots with kava. Food is raw, vegan and gluten-free with organically sourced ingredients, and pastries come from La Louisianne. It opens daily from noon to 11pm.

Two things have changed materially here and both matter. First, Louisiana banned kratom: Senate Bill 154 took effect on 1 August 2025, making sale and possession illegal, and kratom had accounted for roughly sixty per cent of Euphorbia's total sales. It is no longer available, which removes a substance many people arriving at a kava bar would otherwise encounter — a genuine improvement in clarity for anyone in recovery, and a serious commercial blow to the business that forced it to broaden what else it sells. Second, what it broadened into is hemp-derived cannabis: the bar stocks Hiatus beverages, which pair 5mg of THC with 125mg of CBD, alongside Crescent 9 and Cheech and Chong drinks and THC/CBD gummies. So kava and THC are both here and kratom is not. No dosage guidance or age policy is published on any page we could reach. One further note for readers weighing the coverage: the business changed hands on 1 August 2025, and the local outlet that has written most enthusiastically about it since is owned by the same person who now owns the bar.
venues.pressQuote: The staff and friends try kava: an intoxicating drink and infused food made from the kava root.

venues.name: Euphoria Kava Bar | North Miami
venues.description: The North Miami branch of Euphoria is the group's evening-only room: it opens at 4pm and runs to midnight, seven days a week, on the 125th Street corridor rather than on the beach. There is no alcohol. The programme mirrors the Ocean Drive original — traditional kava shells, juices and coffee — but the hours make the intent clearer, since this is a room that only exists after the working day ends. IMPORTANT for readers in recovery: as at the other Euphoria sites, kratom is sold alongside kava under the K-Tea name. Kratom's alkaloids act on opioid receptors and carry real dependence and withdrawal risk, and it is banned outright in several US states; kava, a South Pacific root, carries no comparable profile. The two sit next to each other on the same board, so ask which you are ordering.
venues.longDescription:
Euphoria's North Miami room sits at 855 NE 125th Street, on the main east-west commercial spine of North Miami rather than on Miami Beach, and it is the group's most straightforwardly bar-shaped site. It opens at 4pm and closes at midnight every day of the week. A venue that does not bother opening until late afternoon is not trying to be a cafe; it is trying to be the place you go in the evening, which is exactly the slot that is hardest to fill if you are not drinking. There is no alcohol served at any point.

North Miami matters here as a location. Miami's alcohol-free depth is concentrated heavily in Wynwood and on South Beach — this directory already lists Syndicate, SÜRENITEA and Kava Villa in Wynwood alone — and the northern half of Miami-Dade is comparatively bare. Between this room, the Elixir bar a few blocks east on 123rd Street, and Makana on NW 7th Avenue, the 125th Street corridor is quietly the second real cluster in the county, and it is the one that serves residents rather than visitors.

The drinks follow the Euphoria template established at the Ocean Drive original: traditional kava shells poured to order, fresh juices and smoothies, and coffee. The group's own web domain has lapsed to a parking page, so the current menu lives on its ordering platforms and its North Miami Instagram account rather than on a site of its own — worth knowing if you want to check prices before you go, and worth a phone call if you need something specific confirmed.

The same disclosure applies here as at every Euphoria room, and it is not a footnote. Kratom is served alongside kava, listed as K-Tea. These are two different plants with two different risk profiles, sold from the same bar at similar prices under similar names. Kava is the ground root of a South Pacific shrub, steeped in water and drunk socially; it contains no alcohol, is mildly sedative, and is not associated with physical dependence. Kratom is the leaf of a Southeast Asian tree whose alkaloids act on the opioid receptors, producing tolerance and a withdrawal syndrome in regular users; several states prohibit it outright, and concentrated 7-hydroxymitragynine products are the subject of live federal scheduling action. Anyone who has come to kava as a way out of a dependence should know which of the two is in the cup before drinking it, and staff will tell you if asked.

venues.name: Euphoria Kava Bar
venues.description: Euphoria is an alcohol-free kava and juice bar in a ground-floor unit on Ocean Drive, open 9am to 2am every day of the week — which is to say it is trading at the same hours as every drinks-led venue around it, on the single most alcohol-saturated street in Florida. That is its whole usefulness. The menu runs fresh juices and smoothies during the day and traditional kava shells, priced from around $8.99, into the night, alongside coffee. IMPORTANT for readers in recovery: the K-Tea listings that sit beside the kava, sold in regular and special versions, are kratom. Kratom acts on opioid receptors and carries genuine dependence and withdrawal risk; kava does not. Both are poured here, under names that look similar on a board, so ask before ordering.
venues.address: 448 Ocean Dr # Cu2, Miami Beach, FL 33139
venues.longDescription:
Euphoria Kava Bar occupies unit CU2 at 448 Ocean Drive, which places it in the middle of the South Beach strip — the stretch of sidewalk cafes, promoters and open-container drinking that is, for a lot of people who have stopped drinking, the least navigable few blocks in the state. A room on that street that opens at 9am and does not close until 2am, and that serves no alcohol at any point, is a genuinely useful piece of infrastructure rather than a novelty. You can sit on Ocean Drive at midnight and be handed something that is not a drink.

The business runs as a hybrid, and the two halves map roughly onto the two halves of the day. The juice side is a straightforward fresh juice and smoothie operation, and it is what the venue is categorised as on most listing sites. The kava side is the reason it appears in this directory: traditional kava shells poured to order, with the base shell priced around $8.99, plus a coffee programme. The room itself is small and planted heavily, with cosy seating and a lot of greenery, and the most consistent theme across its reviews is staff who will talk a first-timer through what kava is, what it tastes like — earthy, bitter, numbing on the lips — and how long to sit with it.

Euphoria is a small local group rather than a single site. There is a second room in North Miami at 855 NE 125th Street, also listed here, and a further Euphoria Juice & Kava Bar at 6942 Collins Avenue in mid-Beach. None of them serve alcohol.

The honest caveat has to be given its own space. Alongside the kava, Euphoria sells K-Tea in regular and special preparations, and K-Tea is kratom. The naming convention is standard across Florida kava bars and it is genuinely confusing on a menu board, where a kava shell and a K-Tea sit one line apart and cost about the same. They are not the same class of drink. Kava is a South Pacific root, infused in water, alcohol-free and mildly sedative, with no established pattern of physical dependence. Kratom is a Southeast Asian leaf whose principal alkaloids act on the opioid receptors; it produces tolerance and withdrawal in regular users, it is prohibited in several states, and its concentrated 7-OH derivatives are under active federal scheduling action. If your reason for looking up a kava bar is that you are avoiding intoxicants with dependence potential, that difference is the entire point, and it is worth one question at the counter.

venues.name: Eve Bar
venues.description: Eve Bar is the cocktail bar beneath Frog by Adam Handling in Covent Garden, built around cocktails, Champagne and caviar, with a glass-fronted drinks lab feeding both rooms and a near-total zero-waste philosophy. Its treatment of alcohol-free drinkers changed shape with the May 2026 menu: the earlier trio of purpose-built non-alcoholic cocktails (Strawberries and Cream, Gooseberry, Lemon) has been retired, and the current list instead marks selected serves as available alcohol-free with named zero-proof bases — the Peachy remade on Everleaf Mountain, the British Pop on Pentire Adrift, the Mirage Paloma on Pentire Seaward, and the house Gin Martini also offered alcohol-free. It remains a place where a non-drinker can order a composed, garnished cocktail rather than a soda, but the dedicated zero-proof builds are gone for now.

signatureDrinks: Peachy (alcohol-free with Everleaf Mountain: poached peach, thyme, London Essence white peach & jasmine soda)
British Pop (alcohol-free with Pentire Adrift: gooseberry, pineapple, woodruff)
Mirage Paloma (alcohol-free with Pentire Seaward: tomato, paprika, pink grapefruit, London Essence soda)
venues.longDescription:
Eve Bar is chef Adam Handling MBE's first venture into bars, opened in 2017 in the basement beneath his Michelin-starred restaurant Frog by Adam Handling on Southampton Street, in the heart of Covent Garden's Theatreland and directly opposite the Savoy. It takes its name and its mischievous motto — "Resist Everything Except Temptation" — from the Garden of Eden, and the mood matches: a small, low-lit underground den with luxe interiors, hung with rotating work by up-and-coming London artists and set apart from the bustle of the Piazza above. Cocktails, Champagne and caviar are the house's stock-in-trade, but the defining feature is a glass-fronted drinks lab where the team distils, clarifies, ferments and carbonates in view of the room.

Eve runs on a near-total zero-waste philosophy, working hand-in-glove with the Frog kitchen upstairs: surplus and byproducts — croissants, thyme sprigs, rhubarb pulp, biscuit trim, offcuts of chocolate — are rescued and redistilled into the bar's own syrups and liqueurs. Its earlier ingredient-led menus, "Evolve" and then "Adapt", centred each serve on a single seasonal British ingredient and kept three purpose-built non-alcoholic cocktails on the list at all times — the Strawberries and Cream, the Gooseberry (built on the bar's own Eve Lab non-alcoholic gooseberry "Chartreuse") and the Lemon. The May 2026 menu retired that format along with all three dedicated alcohol-free builds.

What replaced it is thinner but still deliberate. The current list is organised into Martinis, Signatures and Classics, and four serves are explicitly marked as available alcohol-free with named zero-proof bases: the Peachy (poached peach, thyme and London Essence white peach and jasmine soda) remade on Everleaf Mountain; the British Pop (gooseberry, pineapple, woodruff) on Pentire Adrift; the Mirage Paloma (tomato, paprika, pink grapefruit, London Essence soda) on Pentire Seaward; and the house Gin Martini, also offered alcohol-free. The zero-proof bases are named brands — Everleaf and Pentire — rather than Eve Lab distillates, and there is no longer a standing commitment to purpose-built non-alcoholic cocktails. A non-drinker still gets a composed, garnished drink built to the same spec as the full-proof version, but as of the May 2026 menu the alcohol-free offer is an adaptation of the cocktail list rather than a category of its own.

venues.name: Ever Andalo
venues.description: Ever Andalo is a Michelin Selected Italian restaurant at 3116 N Davidson Street in Charlotte's NoDa arts district, in the space that housed Crêpe Cellar for thirteen years. It shares a restaurant group — and mixologist Colleen Hughes, a 2025 Michelin Guide American South Exceptional Cocktails Award winner — with Supperland, and Queen City Nerve readers voted it Best NoDa Restaurant in 2024. The kitchen runs burrata with orange marmalade at $17, wagyu beef tartare at $26, Calabrian chilli pappardelle at $25 and a wagyu New York strip at $69. Its drinks list carries a "Spirit-Free Beverages" section of four cocktails: the Spirit-Free Bramble ($16, Amethyst botanical, Dr Zero Zero amaro, blackberry syrup, soda, basil), Bright & Spritzy ($16, verjus blanc, Amethyst grapefruit basil, simple syrup, soda), the Spirit-Free Spritz ($13, Lyre's Italian Spritz with non-alcoholic sparkling wine) and View from the Top ($12, lemon-anise syrup, grapefruit, lime, ginger beer). The list rotates seasonally, so older drink names circulating online are historical.

venues.longDescription:
Ever Andalo is an Italian restaurant at 3116 North Davidson Street in NoDa, two miles north-east of Uptown, in the space that was Crêpe Cellar for thirteen years before it closed. It is Michelin Selected, and it belongs to the same Charlotte restaurant group as Supperland — the two share a mixologist in Colleen Hughes, who holds a 2025 Michelin Guide American South Exceptional Cocktails Award, and the wine side is run by sommeliers Michael Klinger and Catherine Dawson. Queen City Nerve readers voted it the city's Best NoDa Restaurant in 2024 and runner-up for Best Italian. The cooking is northern Italian and generous rather than fussy: burrata with orange salt and orange marmalade at $17, wagyu beef tartare with Calabrian chilli and rosemary crackers at $26, a Calabrian chilli pappardelle with beef ragù and house ricotta at $25, pork milanese at $42, and a wagyu New York strip at $69. Dinner runs from 5pm, with weekend brunch from 10.30am.

The drinks list carries a section headed "Spirit-Free Beverages", and its four cocktails show the same hand as the alcoholic list rather than a simplified version of it. The Spirit-Free Bramble ($16) is the most complex, combining an Amethyst botanical with Dr Zero Zero amaro, blackberry syrup, soda and fresh basil — bitter and herbal, not a fruit drink. Bright & Spritzy ($16) uses verjus blanc with Amethyst grapefruit basil and soda, and verjus is the right call here: it brings acidity without the sugar that usually stands in for it. The Spirit-Free Spritz ($13) is the simplest and cheapest, pairing Lyre's Italian Spritz with non-alcoholic sparkling wine. View from the Top ($12) works a lemon-anise syrup with grapefruit, lime and ginger beer. The list does turn over — several drinks named in older coverage of this restaurant, including Get Up to Get Down and Ever Pink Collins, are no longer on the menu — so treat any list more than a season old as historical.
venues.pressQuote: Ever Andalo has an absolutely stellar lineup of mocktails that are perfect for dry January and beyond.

venues.name: F The Bar
venues.description: F The Bar is a craft cocktail and local-beer bar tucked inside Fergusons Downtown, the revitalized historic motel marketplace at 1028 E Fremont St in Downtown Las Vegas. Alongside its spirit-forward cocktails, it keeps a small standing mocktail menu of crafted zero-proof drinks: the Heatwave (watermelon soda, coconut syrup, lemon and lime juice, jalapeno, with a Tajin rim), The Earl of Fergusons (Earl Grey iced tea, green apple syrup, passion fruit, lime juice and fresh mint), and the Spring Fling, which is built on Lyre's non-alcoholic gin with dragon fruit syrup, orgeat and lemon juice. Guests can add a side of house shrub to any of these. The bar also runs a monthly hands-on mixology workshop series, and its January "Reset" edition centered specifically on clean, mocktail-style builds with the option to skip the spirit. It is open Thursday 2pm-10pm and Friday through Sunday 12pm-10pm.
venues.address: 1028 E Fremont St, Las Vegas, NV 89101
signatureDrinks: Heatwave (watermelon soda, coconut syrup, lemon, lime, jalapeno, Tajin rim)
The Earl of Fergusons (Earl Grey iced tea, green apple syrup, passion fruit, lime, fresh mint)
Spring Fling (Lyre's non-alcoholic gin, dragon fruit syrup, orgeat, lemon juice)
venues.longDescription:
F The Bar sits inside Fergusons Downtown at 1028 East Fremont Street, a 1940s motel that spent years abandoned before being redeveloped into a community marketplace east of the Fremont East entertainment district. The redevelopment kept the bones: the motel rooms survive, refurbished into freestanding boutiques, art studios and salons, the old parking lot is now a grassy lawn, and the front desk area became a bar. The complex is organised around Big Rig Jig, a forty-two-foot sculpture made from two 18-wheelers suspended in the air, and shares the site with Peyote and the Vegas Test Kitchen. F The Bar itself arrived in 2022 and is deliberately small — an eighty-person capacity room styled as greenhouse-meets-lounge, with more than fifty live plants distributed among banquettes, family-style highboys and a social bar.

The cocktail list is genuinely craft, running to builds like the Vegas Playground, The Clincher and Doctors Orders, and the non-alcoholic drinks are held to the same standard on a small standing mocktail section rather than being made up on request. The Heatwave combines watermelon soda, coconut syrup, lemon and lime juice and jalapeno with a Tajin rim; The Earl of Fergusons is built on Earl Grey iced tea with green apple syrup, passion fruit, lime juice and fresh mint; and the Spring Fling uses Lyre's non-alcoholic gin with dragon fruit syrup, orgeat and lemon juice. Any of the three can be ordered with a side of house shrub. The bar also runs a monthly hands-on mixology workshop, and the January edition, called Reset, was built specifically around clean mocktail-style drinks with the option to leave the spirit out entirely — the Las Vegas Review-Journal covered that class as one of the best drink deals in the city. Hours are limited and worth checking before travelling across town: Thursday 2pm to 10pm, and Friday through Sunday noon to 10pm.
venues.pressQuote: January's class centered around mocktails, featuring a welcome "Watermelon Wake-up" and build-your-own options called "Mint Condition" and "Rum Punchline."

venues.name: Fable All Day
venues.description: Fable All Day is a bright all-day café and natural-wine bar at 3309A Beacon Ave S on Beacon Hill, opening at 7am for specialty coffee, house-made dishes and pastries alongside a small natural wine and beer list. PLEASE READ BEFORE VISITING — THIS LISTING HAS CHANGED. As of August 2026 Fable is running what it calls a soft relaunch after a period of reduced service, and says on its own site that it is currently offering a limited menu and shortened hours, from 7am to 4pm, with expanded hours and menu to come. Its published menu page is currently empty, so nothing about the current food or drink offering can be verified from it, and its own social account gives closing time as 5pm rather than 4pm. We previously listed three St. Agrestis Phony Negroni variants, craft lattes and a toasted-sugar lemonade here. We can no longer confirm any of those are being served — the only trace of that description we could find leads back to our own earlier copy rather than to any independent source — so treat it as unconfirmed rather than current. The café is open daily; check before travelling.
venues.longDescription:
Fable All Day sits on Beacon Avenue South and does the thing its name promises: it opens at seven in the morning for specialty coffee, house-made dishes and pastries, and carries a small natural wine and beer list into the evening. The Infatuation's line about it is the most useful description of its register — slightly more energetic than a morning café, but not as raucous as a bar. That in-between quality is exactly what a lot of non-drinkers want and rarely find: somewhere you can sit for two hours at four in the afternoon without being the only person not holding a drink, and where the coffee is treated as seriously as the wine.

The honest position on this listing today is that we cannot tell you what is on the menu, and we would rather say so than repeat ourselves. As of August 2026 Fable states on its own site that it is in a soft relaunch, offering a limited menu and shortened hours from 7am to 4pm, with expanded hours and menu to come — language that follows a period of reduced service. Its menu page currently carries no items at all, only a placeholder line, so there is nothing on it to read. Its own social account lists closing at 5pm rather than 4pm, so even the hours conflict. And here is the part worth being especially plain about: our previous description of this café — three St. Agrestis Phony Negroni variants, craft lattes, a toasted-sugar lemonade — could not be traced to any independent source. When we went looking, the trail led back to this site's own earlier copy being reflected back through search results. That is not verification, and we have stopped presenting it as fact. Those drinks may well have been served, and may be served again once the full menu returns. But right now the café is doing a reduced service, publishes no list, and we have nothing solid to point you at. Go for the coffee and the room, both of which are real, and ask what the bar is pouring when you get there.
venues.pressQuote: Slightly more energetic than a morning café, but not as raucous as a bar.

venues.name: Fable Melbourne
venues.description: Fable is one of the tallest rooftop cocktail bars in the Melbourne CBD, perched on Level 13 of the Greek Community Building on Lonsdale Street. Alongside a mixologist-designed cocktail list, it runs three signature house mocktails built with the same care as its cocktails, including the Sancho Panza Vol 2 (watermelon syrup, lime, grapefruit, aquafaba, soda) and the Northstar (ginger, lime, mint, cucumber), plus an alcohol-free spiced-rum build. The zero-proof drinks pair with an entirely gluten-free Mediterranean share-plate menu. Time Out calls it Melbourne's highest rooftop bar and rates its three signature mocktails as original and painstakingly prepared, built on watermelon cordial, alcohol-free spiced rum, mint and fresh fruit.
signatureDrinks: Sancho Panza Vol 2 - watermelon syrup, lime, grapefruit, aquafaba, soda (A$15)
venues.longDescription:
Fable Melbourne opened in November 2021 on the 13th floor of the Greek Community Building at 168 Lonsdale Street, making it one of the highest rooftop bars in the CBD, with panoramic views taking in the Eureka Skydeck, the Arts Centre spire and the Bolte Bridge. Owned by Gehan Rajapakse, the room was reworked with an opened-up roof, heaters and a retractable awning so it trades year-round, seating around 70 or holding up to 100 for a standing cocktail event.

The kitchen, developed by chef Alex Xinis (formerly of the Press Club), runs a produce-driven Mediterranean menu of share plates - calamari with ouzo mayonnaise, lentil and eggplant moussaka, lamb shoulder with horiatiki and tzatziki - that is more than half gluten-free with vegan modifications available. The drinks program was designed by mixologist Alessandro Nardini (Nick & Nora's), and the same technique carries into the non-alcoholic list.

For non-drinkers, Fable pours three signature mocktails that Time Out Melbourne calls "original, balanced and painstakingly prepared," built with ingredients like watermelon cordial, alcohol-free spiced rum, mint and fresh fruit. The standouts are the Sancho Panza Vol 2 - watermelon syrup, lime, grapefruit, aquafaba and soda - and the Northstar, a lighter mix of ginger, lime, mint and cucumber, each around A$15.

Entry is via a small Fable sign at street level on Lonsdale Street, through glass automated doors and up the lift to the 13th floor. It is open Tuesday to Sunday from mid-afternoon (from 1pm on Saturdays), closed Mondays.

Height is the product here, and the drinks are built to match rather than to apologise. Time Out describes Fable as Melbourne's highest rooftop bar and rates the alcohol-free side alongside the view: three signature mocktails that the guide calls original, balanced and painstakingly prepared, drawing on watermelon cordial, alcohol-free spiced rum, mint and fresh fruit.

Three is a deliberate number rather than a thin one. A short, composed list that a bar can execute consistently at volume, forty-odd floors up, is worth more to a non-drinker than a long card of builds the staff have to look up. "Painstakingly prepared" is also the correct standard to hold a rooftop to, because altitude and a queue are exactly the conditions under which zero-proof drinks are usually reduced to juice and soda. Coming for the view costs a non-drinker nothing here, which is not true of most rooms with this kind of outlook.
venues.pressQuote: Melbourne's highest rooftop bar offers plenty of views - and great non-alcoholic options, too.

venues.name: FaceClock Zero-Proof Lounge & Gallery
venues.description: FaceClock Zero-Proof Lounge & Gallery is a fully alcohol-free spot near Philadelphia's Fishtown/Olde Kensington border, billed as the city's first zero-proof lounge. It was founded by Anastasia Farber, a former bartender who used her mixology background to build a place where people could socialize and "not be forced to have a drink in their hand." The roughly 1,100-square-foot space is part Adaptogen Bar, part rotating art gallery (works for sale), part small NA bottleshop, and part event venue hosting poetry slams, movie nights, and art parties. Drinks lean on natural ingredients and adaptogenic blends: the Elderberry Healer (Hatchet Granny, elderberry, lemon, soda, honey, black pepper), house Dandelion Root Tea, build-your-own Adaptogen Spritzes, and slow-simmered Eastern-European kompots. Its tagline: "Zero proof; full expression."

venues.longDescription:
FaceClock Zero-Proof Lounge & Gallery sits near the Fishtown and Olde Kensington border and bills itself as Philadelphia's first zero-proof lounge. It was founded by Anastasia Farber, a former bartender who used her mixology background to build somewhere people could socialise without being, in her words, forced to have a drink in their hand. That phrasing identifies the actual problem precisely: the difficulty of a night out sober is rarely thirst, it is the social expectation attached to holding a glass.

The roughly 1,100-square-foot space does four things at once. It is an adaptogen bar, mixing drinks built on functional botanicals rather than spirits. It is a rotating art gallery with the work for sale. It is a small non-alcoholic bottle shop, so a good drink can be taken home rather than only consumed on site. And it is an event venue, hosting poetry slams, film nights and art parties.

That last function is the one worth dwelling on. The hardest thing to replace when you stop drinking is not the alcohol but the calendar — the standing reason to leave the house and be among people on a Friday. A room that programmes poetry and films and parties is supplying that directly, rather than hoping people will invent their own reason to sit in it.

The drinks lean on natural ingredients and adaptogens: botanicals such as ashwagandha, reishi and lion's mane, traditionally used for their calming or focusing effects. It is worth being clear that these are herbal rather than intoxicating, and contain no alcohol — but anyone who prefers their drinks entirely free of functional additives should ask before ordering.

It is listed as open twenty-four hours, which is extraordinary for any venue in the city and unheard-of for an alcohol-free one. Worth confirming before a very late visit, but the intent is unambiguous: this is somewhere to go when everything else has shut.
venues.pressQuote: FaceClock fosters an artistic and cozy space boasting drinks that “elevate your senses with bold flavors, natural ingredients, and adaptogenic blends”
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Billy Penn (WHYY), Alcohol-free spaces to spend nights out in Philly, January 2026

venues.name: Fanboy
venues.description: Fanboy is an intimate, atmospheric cocktail bar on West Broad Street serving small plates alongside a rotating dinner menu, and local coverage consistently singles out the length of its non-alcoholic drink list rather than the existence of one. It is the late option among Richmond's alcohol-free-friendly venues: open until midnight midweek and 2am on Friday and Saturday, which puts it in a very small group in this city where someone not drinking can still be out at one in the morning with a properly made drink in front of them. With Point 5 closing at 6pm and SoBar running only two nights a week, that late licence is genuinely scarce here. Closed Mondays, and the room is small enough to fill early at weekends.
venues.longDescription:
Fanboy is a small, dark, deliberately atmospheric cocktail bar on West Broad Street, the sort of room built for a long conversation rather than a quick round. The kitchen turns out small plates against a rotating dinner menu, and the bar programme is the main event.

What earns it a place here is that Richmond's own food press describes it as having an extensive non-alcoholic drink list — the operative word being extensive. There is a meaningful difference between a bar that can make you something without alcohol and a bar with a list long enough to choose from, and only the second one gives a non-drinker the experience everybody else is having, which is deciding between options rather than accepting whatever arrives.

The hours are the other reason it matters, and in Richmond they are close to decisive. Fanboy runs to midnight Tuesday through Thursday and Sunday, and to 2am on Friday and Saturday. Sober nightlife tends to collapse after about 10pm in most American cities: the cafes shut, the dedicated alcohol-free venues keep early hours, and what remains is bars where the only thing on offer is soda. With SoBar running just two nights a week until midnight and Point 5 closing at 6pm, Fanboy is one of the very few Richmond rooms where a non-drinker can genuinely be out late.

A note on grading: the list is well regarded locally but individual drinks are not documented in the detail that would justify a higher rating, so a 3 is the honest call — a real programme rather than a headline one. It is closed Mondays, and the room is small enough that a weekend group should expect to wait. Arrive before nine if the group is more than four, or expect to stand.
venues.pressQuote: We've also embraced a new-wave style wine list as well as an alcohol-free drink menu featuring house-made shrubs and mocktails

venues.name: Federal Cafe & Bar
venues.description: Federal Cafe & Bar is a Kiwi- and Aussie-inspired brunch cafe that has anchored the Northern Quarter since 2014, now one of Manchester's most-followed coffee spots and a TripAdvisor Travelers' Choice 2025 winner. Its non-alcoholic drinking is genuinely developed rather than an afterthought, built around a proper matcha program — an iced matcha you can flavour with strawberry, blueberry or mango (£4.50), an oat-milk matcha latte and a Banana Bread Iced Matcha topped with banana bread cold foam (£5). Around it sit spiced chai and a 'dirty' chai spiked with an espresso shot, house batch and cold brew, hand-brewed single-origin filter coffee and fresh-pressed 'Fed' juices, so a non-drinker has a full all-day menu rather than a token soft drink.
signatureDrinks: Banana Bread Iced Matcha (iced matcha latte, banana bread cold foam)
Iced Matcha with strawberry, blueberry or mango
Dirty Chai Latte (spiced chai with an espresso shot)
Berry Boost (strawberry, blackcurrant, açai, beetroot, spinach, kale)
Raw Greens (kiwi, pear, kale, cucumber, apple)
venues.longDescription:
Federal Cafe & Bar opened on Nicholas Croft in the Northern Quarter in December 2014, started by three friends around a simple idea: recreate the relaxed, all-day neighbourhood cafes of Australia and New Zealand in central Manchester. It quickly became one of the city's defining brunch rooms — an Antipodean-style spot for gourmet coffee, big plates and homemade cakes that has since grown into a small local group with further sites on Deansgate and at Circle Square plus a coffee cart in Altrincham. It is one of the UK's most social-media-visible brunch destinations, with millions of TikTok views, and holds a TripAdvisor Travelers' Choice 2025 award; it trades walk-in only, so there is no booking, and queues are part of the experience.

What makes it worth a stop for non-drinkers is that the drinks list is treated as its own craft rather than a sideline to the food. The centrepiece is a genuinely developed matcha program: an Iced Matcha (£4.50) that can be built with strawberry, blueberry or mango, a Matcha Latte made with oat milk, and a Banana Bread Iced Matcha (£5) finished with a banana bread cold foam. The tea and chai side is just as considered — a Spiced Chai Latte, an Iced Chai and a 'Dirty' Chai Latte pulled with an espresso shot (£4.30) — alongside a serious coffee offer of house Batch Brew and Cold Brew, espresso-based drinks and single-origin specialty beans, with a rotating wall of loose-leaf teas served by the pot.

Beyond the hot drinks, the cold and pressed range is deliberately broad. Freshly squeezed orange juice sits next to two house 'Fed' juices — the Berry Boost of strawberry, blackcurrant, açai, beetroot, spinach and kale, and the Raw Greens of kiwi, pear, kale, cucumber and apple (both £4.50) — plus gut-friendly kombucha, Bundaberg ginger beer, Living Things craft sodas and the Aussie-diner staple Cold Milo. Set in a bright, plant-dressed corner room in the heart of the Northern Quarter and open from breakfast through to late afternoon daily, Federal is one of Manchester's easiest places to eat and drink well without alcohol.
venues.pressQuote: Federal goes above and beyond, though, with cold drinks including gut-loving Kombucha, ginger beer and the Aussie favourite Cold Milo.

venues.name: Félix Cocktails et Cuisine
venues.description: A Parisian-inspired cocktail bar and French restaurant on Upper King Street, recently named Best Cocktails in Charleston City Paper's Best of Charleston contest. The same seasonal craft extends to a small zero-proof list, including the Citron-Fraise (strawberry coulis, lemon, simple syrup), La Tahitienne (pineapple, lemon, hibiscus syrup, tonic), and La Fleur du Désert (Seedlip Notas de Agave, grapefruit, lime, jalapeño syrup). The bar is also known for building custom mocktails to taste on request.
venues.longDescription:
Félix Cocktails et Cuisine sits at 550 King Street in Charleston's Upper King district, a marble-and-gold French bistro-style bar serving craft cocktails and Parisian-inspired fare. It was named Best Cocktails in Charleston City Paper's annual Best of Charleston contest, and the same seasonal approach carries over to its zero-proof drinks.

The non-alcoholic list features three housemade options: the Citron-Fraise (fresh strawberry coulis, lemon juice, simple syrup), La Tahitienne (pineapple and lemon juice, hibiscus syrup, tonic), and La Fleur du Désert (Seedlip Notas de Agave, grapefruit and lime juice, jalapeño simple syrup). Beyond the printed mocktails, the bar team is known for crafting custom spirit-free drinks on request, which zero-proof guide The Zero Proof rated among the best mocktails in the city.
venues.pressQuote: Recently named Best Cocktails in Charleston City Paper's annual Best of Charleston contest, Félix Cocktails et Cuisine brings the same thoughtful craft and seasonal inspiration to its zero-proof offerings.

venues.name: Felix Trattoria
venues.description: Felix Trattoria is chef Evan Funke's acclaimed regional-Italian restaurant on Abbot Kinney Boulevard in Venice, opened in 2017 with restaurateur Janet Zuccarini. Known for handmade pasta produced daily in a glass-enclosed "pasta laboratorio," Felix is a Michelin Guide restaurant and a fixture of LA's dining scene. Its bar runs a genuine named non-alcoholic cocktail program built around imported and craft zero-proof bases — England's Pentire botanical aperitivo and Seattle's Pathfinder hemp-and-botanical amaro — plus house-made ginger beer. Lead bartender Henry Terhune frames the list around Italian aperitivo culture: drinks meant "to pique your appetite" before a carb-rich meal. Named zero-proof options include the Monte Rosa, Mare Nostrum, Zenzero, and the Coca-Felix, a Chinotto-style "bitter Coca-Cola" riff — composed, restaurant-quality options rather than an afterthought.
venues.longDescription:
Felix Trattoria is chef Evan Funke's regional Italian restaurant at 1023 Abbot Kinney Boulevard in Venice, run in partnership with Janet Zuccarini of Gusto 54. Funke trained under Alessandra Spisni at La Vecchia Scuola Bolognese in Bologna and describes himself as a custodian of Italian tradition and a master of old-world handmade pasta technique; Felix was, by the restaurant's own account, the first restaurant to feature a pasta laboratorio in the centre of the dining room, the glass-walled workshop where the day's pasta is made in view of the tables. He has been nominated twice for James Beard awards, his cookbook American Sfoglino won the 2020 IACP award for best cookbook, and he has been the official chef of the Vanity Fair Oscar party since 2022. He also operates Funke in Beverly Hills, Mother Wolf in Hollywood, Las Vegas and Miami, and Tre Dita in Chicago. Beyond the pasta, the kitchen is known for its round wood-fired focaccia.

The bar keeps a headed "senza alcol" section of six drinks, and its lead bartender, Henry Terhune, frames the list around Italian drinking custom rather than around abstinence: in Italian drinking culture, he told Resy in January 2026, you typically start with a cocktail to pique your appetite before eating a decadent, carb-filled meal. The drinks are built accordingly, as aperitivo rather than as soft drinks. Monte Rosa is a non-alcoholic amaro cocktail served on the rocks in a Collins glass, layered with house-made ginger beer and lime and garnished with basil. Mare Nostrum is a herbal spritz using Pentire, the English botanical aperitivo, with alyssum and rosemary. Zenzero is the simplest and most direct — freshly juiced ginger with farmers' market pomegranate juice, soda and lemon. Coca-Felix mixes tonic with Seattle's Pathfinder non-alcoholic amaro into something Terhune likens to Chinotto, the classic Italian soda, or as he puts it, something akin to a bitter Coca-Cola. Felix does not publish its menus online, so the list is best confirmed on the night. Dinner runs from 5pm daily, to 9pm on Sundays, 9.30pm midweek and 10pm on Friday and Saturday.
venues.pressQuote: In Italian drinking culture, you typically start with a cocktail to pique your appetite, before eating a decadent, carb-filled meal.

venues.name: Fellow Traveler
venues.description: Fellow Traveler is a fully vegan bar and cafe that opened in January 2022 at 3487 South Broadway in Englewood, just south of Denver, from a team including former Sputnik bartender Joe Phillips. It is celebrated for a deep collection of roughly forty amari and bitter liqueurs, but it also runs one of the inner metro's most developed zero-proof programs: a dedicated Zero Proof cocktail list alongside non-alcoholic beer and wine. Named alcohol-free pours include Nectar of the Gods (grapefruit, lemon, pickle brine, simple and soda), Billows & Thieves (grapefruit, lemon, cold brew, cardamom-cinnamon syrup), the N/agroni (Sanbitter, tart cherry, juniper syrup) and the N/alort, the house zero-proof answer to Malort, plus a Rosemary Peach Bellini, an Agua de Jamaica and a tart cherry, lemon and ginger health shot. 5280 flagged its "great nonalcoholic cocktail choices," and Westword named it Best You'd-Never-Know-It's-Vegan Restaurant in 2025.

venues.longDescription:
Fellow Traveler opened in January 2022 at 3487 South Broadway in Englewood, on the stretch of the Broadway corridor that runs south out of Denver proper, from a team that includes former Sputnik bartender Joe Phillips. Everything on the food menu is vegan, and the restaurant has built enough credibility on that front that Westword named it Best You'd-Never-Know-It's-Vegan Restaurant in 2025, while 5280's review of the place argued that the beverage programme outshone even the plant-based cooking. The bar's reputation among drinkers rests on a collection of roughly forty amari and bitter liqueurs, with an Amaro Wednesday discount, and on a house Malort. It is open from noon most days and from 10am at weekends, which makes it a daytime as well as an evening room.

For non-drinkers, the useful fact is that the zero-proof list is a printed section of the menu with its own named drinks, and that the same bitter, savoury sensibility runs through it. Nectar of the Gods combines grapefruit and lemon with pickle brine, simple syrup and soda. Billows & Thieves runs grapefruit and lemon against cold brew and a cardamom-cinnamon syrup. The N/agroni is built on Sanbitter with tart cherry and juniper syrup, and the N/alort exists, in the menu's own words, because they can: a zero-proof answer to the house Malort. Lighter options fill out the section, including a Rosemary Peach Bellini of peach nectar, lemon, soda and rosemary, an Agua de Jamaica of sweetened hibiscus tea, and Limone e Sale, a Sicilian lemon-and-salt serve. A health shot of tart cherry, lemon and ginger and a happy-hour watermelon and fresno chilli shot round it out, and non-alcoholic beer and wine are stocked alongside. Westword's January 2026 Dry January round-up pointed readers here for the Bellini, the grapefruit and pickle brine build, and the zero-proof Malort. Happy-hour versions of the same idea appear as a health mocktail of ginger, tart cherry and lemon and a watermelon and fresno chilli hot shot, so the alcohol-free list extends into the discounted hours rather than stopping at the door.
venues.pressQuote: great nonalcoholic cocktail choices

venues.name: Fermenteria
venues.description: Fermenteria on East Commerce Street builds its drinks around fermentation, which is the single most useful technique available to anyone making a serious alcohol-free drink — it produces acidity, funk and depth that no amount of fruit juice can imitate. The named zero-proof options are Butterfly Blossom, a pineapple coconut, and a strawberry lime tulsi built on holy basil. A venue whose whole identity is fermentation is naturally equipped for this category, since the process that makes kombucha interesting is the same one that makes wine interesting, minus the alcohol. Note the narrow window: it opens Thursday through Saturday only, from 4pm, and is closed the rest of the week.
venues.address: 2243 E Commerce St, San Antonio, TX 78203
venues.hours: Mon-Wed closed; Thu 4pm-10pm; Fri-Sat 4pm-12am; Sun closed
venues.longDescription:
Fermenteria sits on East Commerce Street on San Antonio's Eastside, and its name is also its method: the drinks programme is built on fermentation. For an alcohol-free guide that is close to the ideal starting point.

Here is why. The reason most non-alcoholic drinks disappoint is structural rather than a failure of imagination. Remove alcohol and you remove warmth, length and a particular kind of dryness, and what is usually left is fruit and sugar. Fermentation puts those qualities back by a different route — it generates acidity, tannin, faint funk and complexity, which is precisely what makes kombucha, kefir and tepache interesting to drink rather than merely sweet. A bar already fermenting for its main list has the technique and the cultures on hand, so its alcohol-free drinks are not a compromise built from a different toolkit.

The named options reflect that. Butterfly Blossom leans on butterfly pea flower, which is dramatic in colour and mildly earthy. The pineapple coconut is the tropical register. The strawberry lime tulsi is the most interesting — tulsi is holy basil, aromatic and slightly peppery, and it gives a fruit drink an adult, herbal finish that keeps it from reading as a soft drink.

The hours are the catch and they are strict: closed Monday through Wednesday and on Sunday, open Thursday from 4pm to 10pm and Friday and Saturday to midnight. It is a three-night-a-week venue. Within that window it is one of the more distinctive rooms in the city, and the Eastside location puts it slightly off the tourist path in a way that suits it. Anyone travelling from downtown should treat it as a deliberate trip rather than a stop, and check the day before setting out.
venues.pressQuote: Fermenteria: Butterfly Blossom, pineapple coconut, strawberry lime tulsi.

venues.name: The Fiction Kitchen
venues.description: The Fiction Kitchen is Raleigh's long-running vegetarian and vegan restaurant, now in Gateway Plaza on Crabtree Boulevard after leaving downtown. Its dinner menu carries a full "Zero Proof Cocktails" section — six named builds between $8 and $10 built around acid, bitterness and texture rather than sugar: verjus in the Sorta Sangria, a beet syrup against tonic in Let the Beet Build, a drinking vinegar in the Seasonal Shrub, cold brew and hickory syrup in Wake 'n Shake, and a house-made falernum in Spring Fling. Athletic's golden ale and Sierra Nevada's non-alcoholic IPA are on too. For a restaurant rather than a bar, it is one of the most developed non-alcoholic lists in the metro. Check the hours first: closed Monday and Tuesday, split lunch and dinner service on Friday and Saturday, lunch only on Sunday.
signatureDrinks: Sorta Sangria ($9) — verjus, mango purée, pineapple, orange juice, lime, ginger
Let the Beet Build ($8) — tonic water, beet juice syrup, lime, Remedy lemon-thyme bitters
Wake 'n Shake ($10) — cold brew, pineapple, hickory syrup, chocolate bitters
Seasonal Shrub ($9) — apple cider vinegar, carrot, thyme, ginger
Beetlejuice Beetlejuice ($9) — lemongrass, matcha, ginger beer, lemon, ube soy foam
Spring Fling ($9) — house falernum syrup, coconut water, lemon, pineapple (contains almonds)
venues.longDescription:
The Fiction Kitchen has been one of Raleigh's most-loved restaurants for over a decade, cooking entirely vegetarian and vegan, and it moved out of its downtown home to a larger space in Gateway Plaza on Crabtree Boulevard. The kitchen gets the attention, but the bar programme is the reason it belongs on this list: the menu carries a standing "Zero Proof Cocktails" heading with six named, priced builds, which is more than most dedicated cocktail bars in the Triangle offer.

The list is built the way a good zero-proof list should be — around acid, bitterness and texture rather than sugar. Sorta Sangria uses verjus, the pressed juice of unripe grapes, which gives the tartness wine would normally bring; it is thinned with mango, pineapple, orange and lime. Let the Beet Build is the sharpest thing on the menu, pairing a beet juice syrup with tonic, lime and lemon-thyme bitters. Seasonal Shrub is straightforwardly a drinking vinegar — apple cider vinegar with carrot, thyme and ginger — and it is the one to order if sweetness is the thing you dislike about non-alcoholic drinks.

The other three lean richer. Wake 'n Shake is a coffee build with cold brew, pineapple, hickory syrup and chocolate bitters. Beetlejuice Beetlejuice runs lemongrass and matcha over ginger beer with an ube soy foam on top, which is as much a texture exercise as a flavour one. Spring Fling uses a falernum made in house — the spiced almond-and-lime syrup from Caribbean drinking — with coconut water, lemon and pineapple; it contains almonds, which the menu flags.

Hours are worth checking before setting out, because the restaurant is closed Monday and Tuesday entirely and runs a split lunch and dinner service only on Friday and Saturday. Sunday is lunch only.
venues.pressQuote: The menu may all be vegetarian and vegan, but above all else, The Fiction Kitchen offers plain old good food

venues.name: Fifty West Brewing Company
venues.description: Fifty West Brewing Company is a destination brewery and burger bar strung along US Route 50 (Wooster Pike) on Cincinnati's east side, founded in 2012 in a former Prohibition-era roadhouse. For non-drinkers it is more than an afterthought: the house lineup includes a 0.0% ABV sparkling Hop Water brewed with pineapple and Citra hops (zero calories, gluten-free), a made-in-house root beer, hand-spun milkshakes and root beer floats, plus fountain drinks and rotating non-alcoholic options. It is a working brewery, so beer flows freely, but the zero-proof choices are genuinely house-produced rather than a token can in the cooler. The Wooster Pike taproom anchors a sprawling Route 50 campus with patios and sand volleyball, making it an easy stop whether or not you are drinking beer.
venues.longDescription:
Fifty West Brewing Company first opened in November 2012 inside a roughly 185-year-old building on US Route 50 heading west into Cincinnati, a spot tied to Prohibition-era bootlegger George Remus and once operated as a speakeasy known as Kelly's Roadhouse. Founders Whit Hesser, Blake Horsburgh (the brewmaster) and Bobby Slattery built the brand around the highway's east-west metaphor — "to the east, there's tradition and to the west, innovation" — and grew it from a single brewpub into a Route 50 campus of taprooms and outdoor recreation. The original full-service brewpub listing at 7668 Wooster Pike now shows as closed on third-party review sites; the brewery's own locations page lists the active taproom and burger bar at 7605 Wooster Pike.

For non-drinkers, Fifty West goes beyond the usual soda gun. The house lineup centers on a 0.0% ABV sparkling Hop Water brewed with pineapple and Citra hops — zero carbs, zero calories and gluten-free — alongside a made-in-house root beer, hand-spun milkshakes, root beer floats, fountain drinks and rotating non-alcoholic options. These are genuinely produced in-house rather than stocked from a distributor. Because it is a working brewery, the same bar pours sixteen drafts, house-made vodka seltzers, hard lemonades and THC seltzers, so this is an alcohol-serving room, not a sober space — but the zero-proof options are real and standing.

Practically, the Wooster Pike taproom runs Monday through Saturday 11am–11pm and Sunday 11am–9pm, with the kitchen closing about an hour before the bar. Expect Route 50 state-inspired burgers, fries and shakes, big patios and sand volleyball leagues in season, a family-friendly crowd and easy parking just west of Mariemont and Fairfax. It suits a group where some people want craft beer and others want a legitimately good non-alcoholic drink.
venues.pressQuote: Fifty West Brewing Company is poised to become one of the most influential microbreweries in Cincinnati, honoring the city's brewing past while laying a foundation for the area's revival as an important hub of beer innovation.

venues.name: Fig & Ash
venues.description: Fig & Ash is chef Cory Hughes' wood-fired contemporary American restaurant at 514 East Ohio Street in Deutschtown on the North Side, built out of two derelict late-19th-century buildings over three years, seven months and twenty-four days and opened in October 2020. Everything comes off a custom wood-fired grill made locally. Pittsburgh Magazine put it among the city's 25 best restaurants for 2026, describing it as serving comfort food with a thoughtful, elevated touch, and a reviewer characterised the room as comfortable and professionally done but not overly designed, full of houseplants and quirky art. There are three ways to sit: the dining room, a four-season covered patio, or the chef's counter. Its printed drinks list carries a section headed simply MOCKTAILS, holding two house builds at $10 each — the matcha-strawberry Match-A Made in Heaven (matcha, strawberry syrup, coconut milk, tonic) and the vegetal Celer-ous-ly, Noah? (celery juice, juniper, caraway, fennel, soda, mint). No non-alcoholic beer or wine brands are listed, and the pair rotates. Reservations via Resy; closed Sunday and Monday.
venues.hours: Mon closed; Tue-Thu 5pm-10pm; Fri-Sat 5pm-11pm; Sun closed
