venues.longDescription:
Free Spirit occupies a room inside Riverdale Hub, a century-old building at 1326 Gerrard Street East that was renovated into what Riverdale Hub calls East Toronto's 'greenest building,' running on geothermal heating with a green roof and solar panels. Riverdale Hub itself is a not-for-profit social enterprise combining a cafe, art gallery, coworking space and event venue in the Leslieville / Gerrard India Bazaar neighbourhood, and Free Spirit opened there on April 23, 2024 as a fully alcohol-free restaurant and bar — among the first of its kind in Toronto.

The bar runs on Riverdale Hub's social-enterprise model: staff are paid a living wage, guests are not required to tip, and proceeds from the restaurant go toward addressing barriers for equity-deserving groups in the community. As Riverdale Hub puts it, Free Spirit is meant to be 'an inclusive place where people taking a break from alcohol, or those who do not drink, can enjoy sophisticated, beautiful and delicious cocktail mixes.' Toronto outlet YourCityWithIN described it as a venue 'pioneering an alcohol-free restaurant and bar concept at Riverdale Hub.'

The menu lists ten named zero-proof cocktails built with real technique rather than simple juice blends: a Bloody Caesar with Clamato juice, Worcestershire sauce, Frank's hot sauce and a house-made seasoned rim; a Smoked Rosemary Old Fashioned on spirit-free HP Whiskey with bitters, orange and rosemary; a Cosmo made with Seedlip Garden 108, cranberry raspberry juice and lime juice, garnished with blood orange; and an Espresso Martini built on Seedlip Spice 94 with espresso, brown sugar, cocoa powder and espresso beans. Other builds include a Spicy Margarita, an Island Oasis made with spirit-free dark rum, coconut water, pineapple juice and house-made pineapple shrub, a Mule, a Mojito, an Apple & Rum with spiced spirit-free rum, apple juice, lemon juice, cardamom and coriander, and a grape-based Sangria paired with pineapple and cranberry raspberry juice.

Beyond the cocktail list, Free Spirit backs the bar with a zero-proof beer program that includes Guinness 0.0 and Heineken 0.0, giving the room both a full mixed-drink menu and a straightforward zero-proof beer option.
venues.pressQuote: Free Spirit is pioneering an alcohol-free restaurant and bar concept at Riverdale Hub.

venues.name: Free Spirited
venues.description: Free Spirited is a fully alcohol-free craft cocktail lounge and scratch kitchen in Alhambra, run by husband-and-wife Amber Pennington and Arleo De Guzman, and one of Southern California's first dedicated non-alcoholic bars. It opened in 2023 in a former Mexican restaurant. The current menu runs 26 cocktails across four sections — Health Conscious, Funky Flavors, Sweet Stuff and Caffeinated — and everything is $9, with tax and tip already included in the price, which is close to unheard of. A flight of up to four tasters is $5 each, and happy hour from 5 to 6 takes 20% off. The kitchen is entirely gluten-free and largely vegan. CORRECTION: we previously said the bar makes its own non-alcoholic spirits in-house. We could not source that anywhere and have removed it — what is true is that the drinks are built on unbranded house spirits named by character rather than brand (aloe herb, citrus rind, roasted grain, spiced molasses) plus its own FS bitters and vermouth. Open Wednesday to Sunday, 5–9pm, with free parking.

venues.longDescription:
Free Spirited is one of the few bars in this guide where the founders have said plainly why it exists, and it is not a market-opportunity story. Amber Pennington and her husband Arleo De Guzman opened it in Alhambra in 2023. Pennington's account: she nearly lost her life to a drunk driver and is disabled as a result, she lost her best friend to addiction, and it became her mission to create a nightlife spot that did not rely on alcohol. De Guzman's is equally direct — it took a DUI for him to realise how much he was risking and how many people he could have hurt, and he went sober for nine months afterwards to find himself again. The commercial spark came later, working a bar together and watching mocktail orders pile up: there was an actual demographic for this, so they did it. The room is warm rather than clinical, with plush booths and low lighting.

The menu is far bigger than most people expect. There are 26 cocktails, not the sixteen older write-ups mention, spread across Health Conscious, Funky Flavors, Sweet Stuff and Caffeinated — everything from a beet, turmeric and black pepper build called All My Best to a cucumber-and-rosewater Green Moissanite with a botanical ice cube, to a whole caffeinated section for people who want the evening to keep going. And everything is $9 with tax and tip already included, which in Los Angeles in 2026 is remarkable; a flight of up to four tasters is $5 each, and happy hour takes 20% off between five and six. The kitchen is entirely gluten-free and mostly vegan, running from $9 popcorn to a $26 black garlic pasta, with the same tax-and-tip-inclusive pricing. One correction to our earlier entry: we described the bar as distilling its own non-alcoholic spirits in-house. We could not find that claim on the venue's own site or in any independent report, and it appears to have originated with us, so it has been removed. What the menu actually shows is spirits named by character rather than brand — aloe herb, citrus rind, roasted grain, spiced molasses — alongside house-labelled FS bitters and vermouth. Distinctive either way, but we should not assert how they are made.
venues.pressQuote: The inspiration came when we were working at a bar together and a bunch of sober cocktails or mocktails were being ordered, and I was like, oh my God, there's an actual demographic for this.

venues.name: Free Spirits Beverage Company
venues.description: Free Spirits is Idaho's first alcohol-free bottle shop, and unusually it is also a manufacturer — the business began in 2018 as the bitters maker iOnE and became a full non-alcoholic beverage company in 2020, producing its own products in-house with no preservatives. The shelves carry its own shrub cocktail mixes, including the smoky Luke Peary and the sweet Cherry Chill, alongside national ranges like Ritual Zero Proof. It also runs the Temperance Trail, a Dry January passport of eight alcohol-free stops across Boise now in its third year, which makes this shop the organising centre of the city's sober scene rather than only its supplier.
signatureDrinks: Luke Peary - house smoky shrub cocktail mix
Cherry Chill - house sweet shrub cocktail mix
venues.longDescription:
Free Spirits Beverage Company on North Curtis Road is Idaho's first alcohol-free bottle shop, and it arrived at that from an unusual direction. It started in 2018 as iOnE, a bitters manufacturer, and expanded into a full non-alcoholic beverage company in 2020 — so it makes things as well as selling them, producing its own line in-house without preservatives.

That manufacturing side is what separates it from most alcohol-free retail. Alongside national ranges like Ritual Zero Proof, the shelves carry its own shrub-based cocktail mixes: the smoky Luke Peary, the sweeter Cherry Chill. Shrubs are drinking vinegars, and they exist precisely to solve the central problem of alcohol-free drinks — without alcohol a drink tends to fall flat and sweet, and vinegar restores the acidity and length. A shop that makes its own rather than reselling someone else's understands the category from the inside.

The more important thing it does is organise. Since 2024 Free Spirits has run the Temperance Trail, a Dry January initiative built around a printable passport of eight alcohol-free stops at businesses across downtown Boise, with tasting events, educational classes and a closing party. It is now in its third year and kicks off with a citywide alcohol-free cocktail mix-off. Very few American cities have anything comparable, and the effect is visible in this guide: Boise's bars carry properly built zero-proof drinks at a rate you would expect from a much larger city, because somebody has spent three years making it normal.

The practical catch is the hours, which are genuinely restrictive: open only Thursday and Friday, noon to 6pm. It sits on the Boise Bench rather than downtown, so it is a deliberate trip. Check the website before setting out, and note that the shop moved here from an earlier North Orchard Street address. If you can only make one alcohol-free stop in Boise, make it this one — and if the timing does not work, the Temperance Trail passport in January is the other way in. The shop also runs events through the year beyond Dry January, so the January trail is the peak of the calendar rather than the whole of it.
venues.pressQuote: Free Spirits Beverage Co. is Idaho's first alcohol-free bottle shop and manufacturing space

venues.name: Freemason Abbey Restaurant
venues.description: Freemason Abbey occupies a converted 1873 church in Norfolk's historic Freemason district — soaring ceilings, original woodwork, and a dining room that draws visitors as much for the building as the food. Its named alcohol-free drink is the Sparkly Blue Pearl, listed by Visit Norfolk among the city's mocktails worth ordering. The value here is situational: this is the room people book for an anniversary or a visiting family, exactly the kind of occasion where somebody at the table is pregnant, driving or simply not drinking, and having a proper named drink on the list keeps them part of the evening.
venues.longDescription:
Freemason Abbey is set inside a church built in 1873, in the historic Freemason district a few blocks from Norfolk's waterfront. The conversion kept the height, the arched windows and the timber, and the result is one of the most distinctive dining rooms in Hampton Roads — the sort of place locals take visiting relatives and book for anniversaries.

That context is the whole argument for its inclusion. A restaurant like this hosts occasions, and occasions are precisely when the non-drinking problem becomes socially visible: a table of ten raising glasses, one person holding a soda. Having a named drink on the list — here the Sparkly Blue Pearl, which Visit Norfolk picks out among the city's mocktails — means the person not drinking gets handed something that looks like it belongs in the toast rather than something that announces their abstinence to the table.

One named drink is a modest programme and the grade says so honestly. This is not a destination for the drink itself, and anyone who wants a genuinely composed zero-proof cocktail should be at Only You or Gershwin's instead. What Freemason Abbey offers is a beautiful room where being the non-drinker is uncomplicated, which for a particular kind of evening is the more useful thing.

The hours help too: 11am to 9pm Monday through Saturday and from 10am on Sunday, so it covers lunch, Sunday brunch and dinner rather than being an evening-only proposition. It is an easy walk from the Chrysler Museum and the waterfront, which makes it a natural anchor for an afternoon in downtown Norfolk. Book ahead at weekends; the room fills with exactly the occasion crowd described above.
venues.pressQuote: Freemason Abbey: "Sparkly Blue Pearl".

venues.name: Fremont Brewing
venues.description: Fremont Brewing's Urban Beer Garden at 1050 N 34th Street is one of Seattle's best-known taprooms and pours the deepest line of house-brewed non-alcoholic beer in the city. The brewery was founded in 2009 by Matt Lincecum and Sara Nelson (now Seattle City Council President); note that although its own site still describes it as family-owned, Seattle Hospitality Group — owner of Pike Brewing — acquired a controlling interest in April 2024. Five non-alcoholic beers are on the taplist, all printed at under 0.5% ABV: Non-Alcoholic IPA (Citra and Citra Cryo hops), Hazy IPA (Mosaic and Krush), Dark (chocolate and black malts, Chinook and Hallertau), Lite (Bohemian pilsner malt and Czech Saaz) and the alcohol-free Hoppy Spritz hop water. A Non-Alcoholic Orange Wit exists but is not currently pouring here. An NA flight of five is $15. The line is decorated: silvers at the 2026 North American Non-Alcoholic Cup for the IPA and the Lite, a 2026 World Beer Cup bronze and a 2025 Great American Beer Festival silver for the Dark. The beer garden is explicitly family- and dog-friendly, with covered heated seating and board games.
venues.longDescription:
Fremont Brewing's Urban Beer Garden is the rare taproom where a non-drinker has a genuine choice rather than a single token can. Five alcohol-free options are on the board, all brewed in-house, all printed at under 0.5% ABV, and — crucially — they span styles rather than repeating one. The Non-Alcoholic IPA runs Citra and Citra Cryo hops over 2-Row Pale and Carapils. The Hazy IPA uses Mosaic and Krush over wheat and rolled oats. The Dark is the one that surprises people, built on Crisp Brown, C-120, Munich, chocolate and black malts with Chinook and German Hallertau — a genuinely dark, roasty beer without alcohol, which is much harder to make than a pale one. The Lite is a Bohemian pilsner malt and Czech Saaz build for drinking all afternoon. And the Hoppy Spritz is not beer at all but hop water — carbonated water with Citra, Mosaic and Sabro — with no malt and no fermentation, so it is properly alcohol-free rather than merely low. You can order all five as a flight for $15, which is the single best way in Seattle to work out which non-alcoholic style you actually like. One caveat: a Non-Alcoholic Orange Wit exists on the brewery's website but is not on the current taplist here.

The judging backs it up. The line has taken silver at the 2026 North American Non-Alcoholic Cup for both the IPA and the Lite, bronze for the Hazy, and for the Dark a 2026 World Beer Cup bronze in Classic Non-Alcohol plus a 2025 Great American Beer Festival silver — that last one measured against the whole American brewing industry, not a specialist category. The beer garden itself is built for long stays and for people who are not there to drink: covered, heated outdoor seating, picnic tables inside and out, board games, free pretzels, a burger truck most afternoons, and an explicit welcome to children and dogs. It opens at 11am on weekdays and 10am at weekends. Two notes on the record. The brewery was founded in 2009 by Matt Lincecum and Sara Nelson, who is now president of Seattle City Council. And while its own pages still say family-owned, Seattle Hospitality Group — which owns Pike Brewing — took a controlling interest in April 2024.
venues.pressQuote: Fremont Brewing's new IPA is Seattle's first craft nonalcoholic beer.

venues.name: Fresko
venues.description: Fresko is a Mediterranean restaurant on Ingersoll Avenue with two documented alcohol-free drinks that sit at opposite ends of the register: a Blackberry Mocktail built on a spiced blackberry and rose simple syrup with lime juice and Fever Tree sparkling pink grapefruit, and a Chai Mocktail of chai tea, cola syrup and vanilla ice cream. The second is effectively a spiced float, and it is the rare alcohol-free drink designed to be a dessert rather than an aperitif — a category almost nobody caters for. Open 11am to 9pm through the week, later at weekends, and from 10am on Saturday and Sunday.

Chai Mocktail — chai tea, cola syrup, vanilla ice cream

venues.longDescription:
Fresko is a Mediterranean restaurant on Ingersoll Avenue, and it is in this guide for two drinks that between them cover a gap most venues never think about.

The Blackberry Mocktail is the conventional one and it is well built: a spiced blackberry and rose simple syrup, lime juice, and Fever Tree sparkling pink grapefruit. Rose and blackberry is a classic pairing, the spice keeps it from being merely floral, and the grapefruit tonic adds the bitterness that stops a berry drink turning into cordial.

The Chai Mocktail is the interesting one. Chai tea, cola syrup and vanilla ice cream is, functionally, a spiced float — and it is a dessert drink rather than an aperitif. That category barely exists in alcohol-free drinking, and its absence is a real gap. After a meal, everyone else at the table orders a digestif, an amaro, a dessert wine, a whisky. The non-drinker gets coffee or nothing, which is the second time in one evening that the ritual excludes them. A restaurant that has built something to occupy that slot has thought further ahead than almost anywhere else in this directory.

Both drinks were documented by Des Moines' tourism board in January 2026.

The hours are the other virtue: 11am to 9pm Monday through Thursday, to 10:30pm on Friday, and a weekend service from 10am — seven days a week with no closed day, in a city where the better cocktail rooms are shut on Sunday, Monday or both. It sits on the same Ingersoll stretch as The Bartender's Handshake and Eatery A, which makes that corridor the most reliable part of Des Moines for a non-drinker who has not planned ahead.

venues.name: Freya
venues.description: Freya is chef Doug Hewitt's tasting-menu restaurant in Detroit's New Center, where every menu comes with a choice of wine, cocktail, or non-alcoholic cocktail pairing built by beverage director Catherine Kurth. The non-alcoholic track is course-matched, not an afterthought — past pairings have included Rayula, a blend of castor and mango juices, turmeric honey, and lemon juice served alongside a roasted squab course, closing with a Black Raspberry Krydda Snaps made exclusively for the restaurant by Michigan's Norden Aquavit. Hewitt was a 2024 James Beard semifinalist for Best Chef: Great Lakes, and the kitchen treats the NA pairing with the same course-by-course intent as its alcohol counterparts.
signatureDrinks: Rayula (castor and mango juices, turmeric honey, lemon juice — paired with roasted squab)
Black Raspberry Krydda Snaps (made exclusively for Freya by Norden Aquavit)
venues.longDescription:
Freya opened in Detroit's New Center neighborhood at 2929 E. Grand Boulevard, from the team behind Chartreuse Kitchen and Cocktails. Chef Doug Hewitt runs a tasting-menu-only kitchen, changing roughly monthly, that "draws on the seasons and nods to Scandinavia," with parallel omnivorous, pescatarian, and vegan versions of the same multi-course format. The restaurant has been named one of the New York Times' "50 Most Exciting Restaurants in America" (2022) and Hour Detroit's Restaurant of the Year (2024), and Hewitt was a 2024 James Beard semifinalist for Best Chef: Great Lakes.

Every tasting menu is sold with a choice of three beverage pairings — wine, cocktail, or non-alcoholic — assembled by certified sommelier and beverage director Catherine Kurth. In Hour Detroit, Kurth said the non-alcoholic pairing "offers an opportunity for creativity, drawing upon a wide range of juices, teas, and nonalcoholic aperitifs for combinations that match the dishes," treating it as a full parallel program rather than a single substitute drink. Documented pairings have included Rayula — castor and mango juices, turmeric honey, and lemon juice, built to run alongside a roasted squab course — and a closing Black Raspberry Krydda Snaps made exclusively for Freya by Norden Aquavit, a Michigan-based producer.

New Center sits between Midtown and Boston-Edison, near the old Fisher and Cadillac Place buildings, and Freya operates as a reservations-first destination restaurant rather than a walk-in bar. Because the non-alcoholic pairing is built into the same tasting-menu structure as the wine and cocktail tracks, non-drinking guests get a full course-by-course beverage experience rather than a single mocktail added to the check.
venues.pressQuote: The nonalcoholic beverage pairing also offers an opportunity for creativity, drawing upon a wide range of juices, teas, and nonalcoholic aperitifs for combinations that match the dishes.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Catherine Kurth, Beverage Director at Freya

venues.name: The Friesian Gastro Pub
venues.description: The Friesian Gastro Pub is a neighbourhood restaurant and bar on the Michigan Street corridor at 720 Michigan Street NE, trading since 2018. Its menu changes weekly with globally-inspired dishes, it carries a deep run of vegetarian and vegan options, and it smokes its own bacon and makes its own carrot cake. For non-drinkers the notable thing is structural: the online drink menu carries a dedicated Non-Alcoholic Beverages section listed alongside Cocktails, Drafts, Wine, Cans, Liquor and Sake, rather than burying zero-proof options at the foot of another page. The builds are properly composed and priced from about $5 to $8, including the Cherry Apple Tonic, Matcha Millions and a blueberry-honey lemonade.
venues.address: 720 Michigan St NE, Grand Rapids, MI 49503

venues.longDescription:
The Friesian Gastro Pub opened on the Michigan Street corridor in 2018 and has settled into the role of a genuine neighbourhood room — casual enough for a quick plate, equipped for a date night or a long sit with friends. The kitchen updates its menu weekly with globally-inspired selections and keeps an unusually deep vegetarian and vegan roster for a gastropub, while still smoking its own bacon and baking its own carrot cake. It sits in Midtown, close to the Michigan Street medical corridor, which gives it a steady mixed trade of hospital staff, students and residents rather than a purely nightlife crowd.

The pub earns its place in an alcohol-free guide on the architecture of its drink list rather than on a single headline drink. Its published drink menu is split into Cocktails, Drafts, Wine, Cans, Liquor, Sake and Sparkling — and Non-Alcoholic Beverages, given equal billing as its own section rather than appended as a footnote. That distinction is the difference between a bar that will make you something and a bar that has already decided what it serves you. The builds themselves are composed drinks at composed-drink prices: the Cherry Apple Tonic combines Fruitbelt apple tonic with Luxardo maraschino cherry syrup and vanilla simple syrup, finished with a Luxardo cocktail cherry, at $8; Matcha Millions puts matcha green tea with coconut milk and strawberry puree in a glass rimmed with basil sugar, at $7; and a blueberry-and-honey build runs lavender syrup, lemon juice and lemonade at $5. Coffee, tea, juices, soft drinks and non-alcoholic beer fill out the rest. The pub trades 3pm to 10pm Monday through Thursday, 3pm to midnight Friday, noon to midnight Saturday and noon to 8pm Sunday. One practical note: two different phone numbers circulate for the venue in online directories and its own site does not settle the question, so book through the website or Tock rather than by phone.
venues.pressQuote: Coffee, tea, juices, soft drinks and N/A beers and cocktails are all available at this casual neighborhood pub.

venues.name: Frisco Kava Bar
venues.description: Frisco Kava Bar is a fully alcohol-free kava room on Preston Road serving what it calls 100% plant-based drinks. The menu runs to blended Kava-Ladas in mango, strawberry, piña colada, peach and mocha; a mocktail section including the Kava-Rita, Espresso Kavatini and The Frisco 75; plus flavoured kratom teas and raw kava. As with any kava room, the botanicals are psychoactive and some items are 21+ — alcohol-free, but not substance-free.

naMenuItems.name: Mango

venues.longDescription:
Frisco Kava Bar sits in a Preston Road retail strip and organises its menu more like a bar than most kava rooms bother to. The blended Kava-Ladas come in mango, strawberry, piña colada, peach and mocha; a separate mocktail section carries the Kava-Rita, the Espresso Kavatini and The Frisco 75 — names that borrow directly from the cocktail canon, which is precisely the point for someone who misses ordering a drink rather than a beverage.

Behind those sit the raw preparations: traditional kava served plain, and a range of flavoured kratom teas. The house describes the whole list as 100% plant-based, and no alcohol is served on the premises at any time.

The caution is the same one we attach to every kava and kratom venue in this directory, and it is not a formality. Kava is a relaxant; kratom is an opioid-receptor-active plant with real dependency potential, and the menu restricts parts of itself to 21 and over for that reason. This is an alcohol-free room, which for many people who have stopped drinking is exactly the environment they want — but it is not a substance-free one, and anyone whose recovery covers all mood-altering substances should know that before walking in.

venues.name: Front Street Cafe
venues.description: Front Street Cafe in Fishtown runs an all-day operation under the Market-Frankford El, and its menu carries a printed "Zero Proof" section — four drinks, every one built on an alcohol-free spirit rather than juice. The Zero Proof Louie is the simplest, honey and lime with Ritual gin. The Refresher runs Ritual gin into a house ginger syrup with cranberry, ginger ale and strawberries. The Buffalo is the most interesting build in the city's zero-proof canon, combining Ritual whiskey with pomegranate syrup and Seedlip Spice 94 — two different alcohol-free spirits layered in one glass, which almost nobody does. The Mocha Espresso Martini uses Ritual tequila with espresso, house chocolate sauce and peppermint syrup. Dinner runs to ten on Friday and Saturday.
signatureDrinks: Zero Proof Louie — honey, lime, Ritual gin
Zero Proof Refresher — Ritual gin, house ginger syrup, cranberry, ginger ale, strawberries
Zero Proof Buffalo — Ritual whiskey, pomegranate syrup, Seedlip Spice 94
Zero Proof Mocha Espresso Martini — Ritual tequila, espresso, house chocolate sauce, peppermint syrup
venues.longDescription:
Front Street Cafe sits on North Front Street in Fishtown, directly under the Market-Frankford El, and runs as an all-day room: coffee and breakfast from eight in the morning, a break in the afternoon, then dinner service into the evening. The building is large and plant-filled, with a garden, and the kitchen leans health-conscious without being humourless about it.

The drinks menu carries a printed "Zero Proof" heading, and what distinguishes this list from almost every other in Philadelphia is that all four drinks are spirit-based. Not fruit and soda with a garnish — actual alcohol-free spirits doing the structural work.

The Zero Proof Louie is the plainest: Ritual's gin alternative with honey and lime, which is a bee's knees without the gin. The Refresher takes the same base into a house ginger syrup with cranberry, ginger ale and fresh strawberries, and the double ginger — syrup and carbonated — gives it heat that carries.

The Buffalo is the drink worth travelling for, and it is genuinely unusual. It layers Ritual's whiskey alternative with pomegranate syrup and Seedlip Spice 94, which means two different alcohol-free spirits from two different producers in one glass. Almost no bar does this, because most treat a zero-proof bottle as a one-for-one swap and stop there. Spice 94 is built on allspice berry and cardamom with a long, bitter, bark-like finish, and layering it over a whiskey substitute produces the kind of depth that non-alcoholic drinks are usually accused of lacking.

The Mocha Espresso Martini rounds it out with Ritual tequila, espresso, house chocolate sauce and peppermint syrup — a dessert drink, and unashamed of it.

The practical note is the split service: the kitchen closes in the afternoon and reopens at five, running to ten on Friday and Saturday and nine the rest of the week, with the cafe side trading from eight in the morning. It is one of the few rooms in the city that works equally as a morning coffee and an evening out.

venues.name: Fullsteam Brewery at Boxyard RTP
venues.description: Fullsteam's taproom at Boxyard RTP, the shipping-container development in Research Triangle Park, is the brewery's trading location, and it pours Blank Check — a 0.5% ABV "prohibition pilsner" the brewery makes itself as the alcohol-free counterpart to its Paycheck lager. It is Craft Malt Certified, brewed with locally malted Cumberland corn, Epiphany pilsner malt and North Carolina two-row barley alongside Wakatu, Saphir and Magnum hops, at 26 IBU — enough bitterness to keep it dry rather than sweet. An NA beer brewed in-house rather than bought in is rare anywhere and unique in this metro. Note the location: the original Rigsbee Avenue brewery is not trading and the downtown site is under construction, so Boxyard, Tuesday to Saturday eleven to eight, is the one that will get you a beer. Cans go to go; call ahead for draught.
venues.address: 900 Park Offices Dr, Research Triangle Park, Durham, NC 27709
signatureDrinks: Blank Check — 0.5% ABV non-alcoholic prohibition pilsner, 26 IBU; Cumberland locally malted corn, Epiphany Modern Pilsner and aromatic malts, NC two-row barley; Wakatu, Saphir and Magnum hops
venues.longDescription:
Fullsteam has spent more than a decade building beers out of Southern agriculture — sweet potatoes, persimmons, locally malted grain — and Blank Check is that philosophy applied to non-alcoholic brewing. It is a 0.5% ABV pilsner the brewery calls a prohibition pilsner, made as the alcohol-free counterpart to Paycheck, its standard lager. Crucially it is brewed in house rather than contracted out or bought in, which almost no brewery of this size does.

The build is properly specified. The grain bill runs locally malted Cumberland corn, Epiphany Modern Pilsner malt, aromatic malt and North Carolina two-row barley; the hops are Wakatu, Saphir and Magnum; the yeast is an Apex Munich lager strain. It comes in at 26 IBU, which is enough bitterness to keep it dry rather than sweet — the failure mode of most non-alcoholic lagers. It carries Craft Malt Certification, meaning at least ten percent of the grain is regional, so the beer qualifies on the same local-sourcing terms as the rest of the range rather than being exempted for being alcohol-free.

The location matters here, and it has changed. Fullsteam's original Durham brewery is currently not trading, and the downtown site on the American Tobacco Campus is under construction with no announced opening. The taproom that is open is at Boxyard RTP, the shipping-container development in Research Triangle Park, Tuesday to Saturday from eleven until nine. If you have an older address for Fullsteam — Rigsbee Avenue or Blackwell Street — it will not get you a beer.

Blank Check is sold to go in twelve-ounce cans; if you are making a specific trip to drink it on site, it is worth calling ahead to confirm it is pouring on draught that day.
venues.pressQuote: The brewery's second location in Boxyard RTP will remain open

venues.name: Fura
venues.description: Fura is a future-food, low-carbon cocktail bar on Amoy Street whose printed 'Ugly Delicious' menu section runs five dedicated non-alcoholic drinks alongside five house-fermented low-alcohol 'wines'. The zero- and low-proof work is central to the concept: imperfect surplus fruit and vegetables (in partnership with local vendor Fresh Veggies) are fermented in-house into fruit wines and kombucha rather than thrown away. Run by ex-Noma head forager Christina Rasmussen and ex-Operation Dagger bartender Sasha Wijidessa, it won the Ketel One Sustainable Bar Award at Asia's 50 Best Bars 2024.
venues.longDescription:
Fura opened in 2023 on the second storey of a shophouse at 74A Amoy Street, in the Telok Ayer precinct of Singapore's CBD, as a self-described 'future food' bar built around a low carbon footprint. It is the project of Christina Rasmussen, formerly head forager at Copenhagen's Noma, and Sasha Wijidessa, who previously ran the bar at Singapore's Operation Dagger before working with Lars Williams at Empirical Spirits. The 40-seat room includes a rooftop herb garden, and the fit-out leans into the ethos, with coasters made from oyster shells, lime-washed walls and reclaimed lighting.

In 2024, Fura won the Ketel One Sustainable Bar Award at Asia's 50 Best Bars, recognising its waste-reduction approach to drinks. The core menu, 'Journal of Future Food', explores ingredients such as invasive species and plant-based alternatives, but a large share of the drinks list is deliberately low- or no-alcohol and flavour-first.

The non-alcoholic anchor is the 'Ugly Delicious' section, which pairs five house-fermented low-alcohol 'wines' with five dedicated non-alcoholic drinks. In partnership with local vendor Fresh Veggies, the team takes less-than-perfect surplus produce (fruits such as pumpkin, pineapple, strawberry and blackberry) that would otherwise be discarded and ferments it in-house into fruit wines and kombucha, alongside components like lacto-fermented local tomato and micro-garden botanicals from the bar's own herb garden.

Fura remained open through 2025, with co-owner Christina Rasmussen quoted in November 2025 press on the pressures facing Singapore's bar scene. For non-drinkers it is one of the city's most substantive stops, offering a genuinely built-out zero-proof and low-ABV program rather than an afterthought.
venues.pressQuote: We want to make sustainable dining more approachable by using ingredients that have a low carbon footprint

venues.name: Gai Noi
venues.description: Gai Noi is chef Ann Ahmed's acclaimed Lao restaurant, opened in May 2023 in the former 4 Bells space on Harmon Place, overlooking Loring Park in downtown Minneapolis. Ahmed — also behind Lat 14 and Khâluna, and a James Beard Best Chef: Midwest nominee — draws on the Xieng Khouang region of Laos her family is from; the name references khao gai noi, a short-grain sticky rice. In 2023 Gai Noi became the only Minnesota restaurant named to the New York Times' list of the 50 best restaurants in America. Its drinks menu includes a dedicated "Zero-Proof Cocktails" section of five named, fruit-forward house creations: the Guava Mule, Star Boi (star fruit elixir, citrus oil), Dole Whip (pineapple and coconut cream), Pineapple Butterfly, and Lemongrass Palmer. The restaurant spans a ground-floor bar, upper dining rooms, and a rooftop patio.
venues.longDescription:
Gai Noi is chef Ann Ahmed's Lao restaurant, opened in May 2023 in the former 4 Bells space on Harmon Place overlooking Loring Park in downtown Minneapolis. Ahmed — also behind Lat 14 and Khâluna, and a James Beard Best Chef: Midwest nominee — draws on the Xieng Khouang region of Laos that her family comes from, and the name references khao gai noi, a prized short-grain sticky rice. In 2023 Gai Noi became the only Minnesota restaurant named to the New York Times list of the fifty best restaurants in America, which is about as strong a national signal as a Twin Cities restaurant has received in years. The building spans a ground-floor bar, upper dining rooms and a rooftop patio, and it serves from late morning to 10pm every day.

The drinks menu carries a dedicated Zero-Proof Cocktails section of five named house creations, and they are unapologetically fruit-forward rather than attempting to imitate spirits — a legitimate and, given the food, a smarter choice. Lao cooking runs to chilli heat, fish sauce, lime and herbs, and a sweet, cold, acidic drink is genuinely the right partner for it, in the way a beer is. The Guava Mule brings ginger bite; Star Boi is built on a star fruit elixir with citrus oil; the Dole Whip works pineapple against coconut cream; the Pineapple Butterfly uses butterfly pea flower for its colour shift; and the Lemongrass Palmer is a Lao reading of an Arnold Palmer. Five named builds is a real list rather than a gesture, and together with sister restaurant Khâluna — whose zero-proof menu runs longer than its cocktail list — it means Ann Ahmed is quietly responsible for two of the best non-alcoholic drinking rooms in Minnesota.

venues.name: Gaia's Kava Root
venues.description: Gaia's Kava Root is a family-owned, 100% alcohol-free kava bar that opened in October 2024 on Central Avenue near the University of New Mexico, and describes itself as a sanctuary — "a living room for the curious, the creative, the healers, and the ones who needed something different." Kava shells run from $6 to $20 alongside kava shots, and the bar also serves kanna, the mood-lifting South African botanical, which is an unusual thing to find on a menu in the United States. A long herbal tea list covers strawberry, pineapple, cherry, watermelon, lavender, mango and lemon-lime, and the specialty mocktails contain no alcohol at all. It keeps late hours, running past midnight most nights and to 4am on Friday and Saturday. Both kava and kanna are psychoactive botanicals rather than inert soft drinks, and the bar restricts kava to adults 18 and over.

venues.longDescription:
Gaia's Kava Root opened in October 2024 on Central Avenue, the old Route 66 corridor running past the University of New Mexico, and it is family-owned — co-founder Jonjon is the name attached to it publicly. The stated intent is unusually explicit for a bar of any kind: the room is meant to be a sanctuary, described in its own words as "a living room for the curious, the creative, the healers, and the ones who needed something different." In practice that means a space built for staying rather than turning over, on a street where the alternatives after midnight are student bars. It is 100% alcohol-free, and it keeps genuinely late hours — past midnight through the week, and to 4am on Friday and Saturday nights, which is later than most licensed venues in the city manage.

The drinks list is broader than a straight kava bar's. Kava is the anchor, served by the shell from around $6 up to $20 depending on size, with shots for anyone who wants it fast. Alongside it the bar pours kanna — Sceletium tortuosum, a mood-lifting succulent from South Africa traditionally chewed or brewed — which is genuinely uncommon on an American drinks menu and gives the room a second thing to be known for. A long herbal tea list runs strawberry, pineapple, cherry, watermelon, lavender, mango and lemon-lime, and the specialty mocktails are built to be ordered on their own merits rather than as consolation, with zero alcohol in any of them. Sodas, energy drinks and water fill out the rest, with prices from about $2. One point deserves stating plainly for readers in recovery: both kava and kanna are psychoactive botanicals, not inert soft drinks. Neither contains alcohol, and neither is a stimulant in the way coffee is, but both act on mood and both are intoxicants in the broad sense. Gaia's draws the line where most kava bars do, restricting kava to adults 18 and over.
venues.pressQuote: We are a family-owned kava bar founded on the belief that you deserve a space to relax, be yourself, and feel something good — no alcohol required

venues.name: Garden Party
venues.description: Garden Party is a combined plant shop and bar on South Madison Street in downtown Spokane, a room full of greenery where the drinks list runs to wine, wine cocktails, champagne cocktails, a couple of local taps from YaYa and Lumberbeard — and an entire mocktail menu of its own. Its most useful feature for a non-drinker is structural rather than liquid: the door is not carded, only the order is, so under-21s and anyone who would rather not be assessed on the way in can sit in the room like everybody else. Small bites rotate, with a grilled cheese made on bread from the bakery next door. Thursday to Saturday, 4pm to 11pm.
venues.longDescription:
Garden Party opened at 107 South Madison in downtown Spokane as two businesses in one room: a plant shop you can buy from and a bar you can sit in, with the stock doubling as the decor. The drinks list is unusual in shape — wine and wine cocktails, champagne and champagne cocktails, a couple of beers on tap from Spokane-area brewers YaYa Brewing and Lumberbeard Brewing, and a full mocktail menu running alongside all of it rather than tucked underneath.

The detail that matters most here is not on the menu at all. Garden Party does not check ID at the door; it checks at the point of order. That single operational choice makes the room genuinely all-ages, and it solves a problem that comes up constantly for people who do not drink — being carded, sorted and implicitly asked to justify yourself before you have even sat down. A teenager, a pregnant friend, someone in recovery and someone ordering a glass of wine can all occupy the same table here on the same terms.

The botanical setting is not incidental to the drinks either. A bar whose stock-in-trade is plants has a natural pantry to work from, and the mocktails lean on that rather than on bottled mixers. Food is a rotating small-bites list — a grilled cheese made with bread from Twenty-Seventh Heaven, the scratch bake shop next door, plus a charcuterie board and flower spring rolls.

The hours are the main constraint and they are tight: Thursday, Friday and Saturday only, 4pm to 11pm, closed the other four days. This is a weekend room, and on a summer Saturday it fills. Worth checking the shop's Instagram before travelling, since a plant business keeps different rhythms from a bar and the schedule has moved before.
venues.pressQuote: We sell fancy cocktails and plants at the same time. (It's) a good place to hang out, do work, sit and have a drink.

venues.name: Gates & Brovi
venues.description: Gates & Brovi is a neighbourhood American restaurant and bar on Monroe Street in Dudgeon-Monroe, the walkable stretch of shops and kitchens west of the UW campus, and it keeps a straightforward non-alcoholic list that covers what people actually order: an NA paloma, an NA margarita, an NA gin and tonic and a virgin bloody mary — the last of which is close to a civic requirement in Wisconsin. There is nothing avant-garde here, and that is the appeal; it is a well-run neighbourhood room where asking for a drink without alcohol produces a properly made one rather than a conversation. Weekend service starts at 9am.
venues.longDescription:
Monroe Street runs south-west from the University of Wisconsin campus through Dudgeon-Monroe, and is one of the few Madison neighbourhoods outside the isthmus with a proper commercial street — bakeries, a wine shop, a handful of restaurants, all walkable from the houses around them. Gates & Brovi sits at 3502, doing American cooking with a full bar, and functions as the neighbourhood's dining room.

Its non-alcoholic list is the least fashionable in this guide and one of the more useful. There is no smoked tea, no adaptogen and no drink with a paragraph-long name. There is an NA paloma, an NA margarita, an NA gin and tonic and a virgin bloody mary, all recorded in BRAVA Magazine's survey of Madison mocktails. Those four cover the overwhelming majority of what someone who has stopped drinking actually wants to order in a restaurant: the drink they used to have. The bloody mary deserves particular note in Wisconsin, where the garnish arms race is a genuine regional tradition and where a virgin version is a completely normal order rather than an apologetic one — which is exactly the social ease a non-drinker is looking for.

Practically, the weekend hours are the draw: 9am on both Saturday and Sunday, which makes it a brunch option in a guide heavy with evening venues, running through to 10pm on Saturday. Weekdays it is dinner only, from 4pm. The location puts it away from the Capitol Square cluster and on the same side of town as Leopold's Books Bar Caffe in Greenbush, about ten minutes east along Regent Street, and Hilldale with Cafe Hollander a similar distance north — so a west-side day without drinking is easy enough to assemble around it.
venues.pressQuote: Specific drinks at Gates & Brovi include NA paloma, NA margarita, NA gin and tonic, and virgin bloody mary.

venues.name: Gather Coffee & Kava Bar
venues.description: Gather Coffee & Kava Bar is a fully alcohol-free kava bar and third-wave coffee house on Ray Street in North Park, San Diego, open from 2pm until late every night of the week. It runs two programs side by side: espresso and cold brew pulled from locally roasted Mostra Coffee beans, and noble kava sourced from sustainably grown crops in Vanuatu, the Solomon Islands, Fiji and Hawaii. Kava is a psychoactive root drink from the South Pacific, prepared as a water infusion and drunk socially in place of alcohol — it contains no alcohol, but it is mildly sedative in its own right, which matters if your recovery rules out intoxicants generally rather than alcohol specifically. Gather serves kava only, with no kratom on the menu, which is a meaningful distinction in a category where the two are often poured side by side. Newcomers are directed to the kava flight, which samples across preparations, and staff are widely described as walking first-timers through the whole experience. The room is dog-friendly, stocked with board games, and drinks can be taken to go.
venues.longDescription:
Gather Coffee & Kava Bar occupies a Ray Street storefront in North Park, in the space that previously housed Mystic Water Kava Bar, and it is one of only a handful of places in San Diego where the entire menu is alcohol-free by design rather than by omission. The operating hours tell you what it is: doors at 2pm daily, running to 11pm at the start of the week, midnight on Wednesday and Thursday, and 1am on Friday and Saturday. That is a bar's schedule, not a cafe's, and the room is set up to match — dog-friendly, stocked with board games, comfortable enough to sit in for the couple of hours that kava actually asks of you. Two programs run in parallel: third-wave coffee pulled from beans roasted locally by Mostra Coffee, and noble kava sourced from sustainably grown crops in Vanuatu, the Solomon Islands, Fiji and Hawaii.

Kava deserves describing plainly, because the people most likely to seek out a bar like this are the people who most need to know what they are ordering. It is a psychoactive drink made from the ground root and stump of a South Pacific shrub, infused in water and drunk socially. It contains no alcohol whatsoever, and the bar's own framing is that it amplifies sociability and reduces everyday stress without most of alcohol's downsides — but it is mildly sedative and mildly intoxicating on its own terms, a distinction that matters if your recovery rules out intoxicants generally rather than alcohol specifically. Importantly, Gather is kava-only: no kratom is served, which separates it from a large share of American kava bars where the two sit on the same menu. The house guidance is to treat the visit as leisurely — one to two servings every twenty minutes across at least an hour — because kava exhibits reverse tolerance, meaning regular drinkers typically need less rather than more to feel it. Newcomers are pointed at the kava flight, and the staff's willingness to talk first-timers through what kava tastes like and how it feels is the single most consistent theme in the venue's reviews. In its own words: "We are an easy-going crew and we love newcomers!"

venues.name: GB's Bottle Shop & Tasting Bar
venues.description: A craft beer, wine, and mead retailer and taproom in Orlando's Ivanhoe Village with one of the city's deepest non-alcoholic beer selections. Alongside its full-strength inventory it stocks roughly two dozen rotating NA beers from Athletic Brewing, Best Day Brewing, Gruvi, and others - both to-go and on the tasting bar.
signatureDrinks: Athletic Brewing Upside Dawn (NA golden ale)
Best Day Brewing West Coast IPA (NA)
Untitled Art Mango Dragonfruit Fruited Sour (NA)
venues.longDescription:
A sister operation to Gnarly Barley, GB's at 531 Virginia Dr in Ivanhoe Village is first and foremost a bottle shop and growler-fill counter, paired with an on-site tasting bar pouring around 20 rotating draft lines alongside an extensive retail shelf of beer, wine, and mead.

GB's isn't an alcohol-free venue - it's a full bottle shop and bar - but its non-alcoholic beer program is unusually deep for Orlando, with roughly two dozen rotating NA options including Athletic Brewing's Upside Dawn, Best Day Brewing's Electro-Lime, Kolsch, and West Coast IPA, Gruvi's Juicy Dayz IPA, Deschutes' Black Butte Non-Alcoholic porter, and Untitled Art's Mango Dragonfruit fruited sour, giving NA drinkers real choice rather than a single token tap.

GB's opened in late 2016 as Gnarly Barley's second Orlando location, its arrival on Virginia Drive marked that August by a mural from local artists Alex Ray and Nicole Ami Ray reimagining a classical creation scene with beer in place of the divine spark. It now anchors a stretch of Virginia Drive - alongside neighbors like Thirsty Topher and The Matador - regarded as one of Orlando's best bar crawls.

The retail shop opens at noon daily; the bar opens 4pm Monday-Tuesday and noon the rest of the week (until 1am Friday-Saturday), making it a regular stop on Ivanhoe Village's Virginia Drive bar strip.
venues.pressQuote: GB's serves up a serious crash course on craft beer for the discerning drinker.

venues.name: Gemini Room
venues.description: Gemini Room is a women- and LGBTQIA+-owned, 1970s-inspired all-day café and bar at 1101 East Pike Street in Capitol Hill's Chophouse Row, opened in mid-December 2022 as the debut project of Tanner Mclaughlin and Jackie Proctor in partnership with Burgess/Hall. By day it does locally roasted espresso, coffee and tea lattes, breakfast staples and seasonal bowls and sandwiches; after dark it becomes, in the Infatuation's words, a party that can only really be described as groovy, with mod lounge furniture and 1970s glassware. Its mocktail list is one of the longest in Seattle — nine drinks under a "Mocktails" heading — and most are $8. The full list: a bottled St. Agrestis Phony Negroni ($12), Clear Sky Sour ($13, Pathfinder Hemp and Root, lemon, simple syrup, soda), Sparkling Citrus Soda, Ginger Basil Grapefruit Soda, Fancy Shirley (Toschi cherry syrup, lemon-lime soda), Ube Orange Cream Soda, Everyone Loves a Rickey (coconut cream, lime, soda), a Crodino Spritz and a Pathfinder Espresso Tonic. A separate non-alcoholic section adds Athletic Brewing, kombucha and Casamara Club botanical sodas. Open from 9am; closed Mondays.

venues.longDescription:
Gemini Room opened in mid-December 2022 in Chophouse Row on Capitol Hill, the debut project of Tanner Mclaughlin and Jackie Proctor in partnership with Burgess/Hall, and it is women- and LGBTQIA+-owned. Its own account of the day-to-night shift is precise: locally roasted espresso, coffee and tea lattes, grab-and-go breakfast staples and seasonal bowls, salads and sandwiches by day; and after dark, shareable bites, house-infused drinks, herbaceous elements, fresh juices, and glassware that will transport you back to '73. The Infatuation put it more bluntly — by day a sleepy espresso bar serving a decent breakfast sandwich, by night a party that can only really be described as groovy, all mod lounge furniture and 1970s vibes. Happy-hour bites run $5 apiece: sweet and spicy chicken bites, pink pickled deviled eggs, fries with aioli, fried ravioli. It opens at 9am Tuesday through Sunday and closes on Mondays.

What makes it genuinely useful is the length and the pricing of the alcohol-free list. There are nine drinks under a heading that simply says Mocktails, and six of them are $8 — which in a Capitol Hill bar in 2026 means a non-drinker can settle in for an evening without paying cocktail prices for sugar. The two that cost more are the ones doing the most work: a bottled St. Agrestis Phony Negroni at $12, and the Clear Sky Sour at $13, built on Pathfinder Hemp and Root with lemon, simple syrup and soda. A word on that name, because it matters to some readers: Pathfinder Hemp & Root is a 0.0% ABV spirit distilled from hemp *seed*, and the maker states plainly that it contains no THC and no CBD — the hemp is the botanical base, doing the job gin's juniper does, not an infusion. The rest of the list is playful and well made: a Fancy Shirley on Toschi cherry syrup, an Ube Orange Cream Soda that uses ube sweetened condensed milk, Everyone Loves a Rickey with coconut cream and lime, a Crodino Spritz, and a Pathfinder Espresso Tonic for the afternoon. A separate non-alcoholic section adds Athletic Brewing's Upside Dawn, two Cultureshock kombuchas and Casamara Club's botanical sodas.
venues.pressQuote: By day, Gemini Room is a sleepy espresso bar that serves a decent breakfast sandwich. By night, however, it's a party that can really only be described as "groovy."

venues.name: Gershwin's
venues.description: Gershwin's is a Granby Street cocktail bar in downtown Norfolk whose alcohol-free drinks are built on non-alcoholic spirits and finished with the same techniques as its full menu. The Bohemian combines alcohol-free gin with elderflower syrup, grapefruit juice, egg white and bitters — a proper sour, foam and all — while the Grand Illumination pours non-alcoholic whiskey smoked over cherry wood with orange peel and bitters. Smoking a zero-proof drink tableside is the clearest possible signal that a bar considers the alcohol-free order worth its time, since the theatre is the point and none of it depends on the alcohol.
signatureDrinks: Bohemian - alcohol-free gin, elderflower syrup, grapefruit juice, egg white, bitters
Grand Illumination - non-alcoholic whiskey, cherry wood smoked, orange peel, bitters
venues.longDescription:
Gershwin's sits on Granby Street, the spine of downtown Norfolk's restaurant and nightlife district, and works a classic cocktail-bar register. Its two documented alcohol-free drinks, both named by Visit Norfolk, are unusually revealing about how the bar thinks.

The Bohemian is a sour in full: alcohol-free gin, elderflower syrup, grapefruit juice, egg white and bitters. The egg white is the detail that matters. Foam requires a hard shake and adds a couple of minutes to the build, and most bars quietly skip it on a non-alcoholic order because they assume nobody will notice. Including it means the drink arrives with the texture and the presentation the alcoholic version would have — which, for someone who is not drinking, is most of the experience.

The Grand Illumination goes further. Non-alcoholic whiskey, smoked over cherry wood, finished with orange peel and bitters: this is the smoked-old-fashioned treatment, theatre included. Smoking a drink is pure performance — it occupies the bartender, it fills the room with cherry wood, and every part of it works identically whether or not there is alcohol underneath. A bar that will do this for a zero-proof order has decided the non-drinking customer gets the show too, and that is rarer than any ingredient on the list.

Both drinks lean on non-alcoholic base spirits rather than juice, which is the other marker of a serious programme — it means someone specified, bought and stocked products that only exist to serve people who are not drinking.

Hours are straightforward: closed Mondays, otherwise from 5pm, to 11pm midweek and midnight on Friday and Saturday. It is walkable from most of downtown Norfolk and sits a short ride from the Chelsea cluster. For a night out where one person is not drinking, the Granby Street stretch plus Chelsea covers almost everything the region has.
venues.pressQuote: Gershwins: "Bohemian" (alcohol-free gin, elderflower syrup, grapefruit juice, egg white, bitters); "Grand Illumination" (non-alcoholic whiskey, cherry wood smoked, orange peel, bitters).

venues.name: Gibson
venues.description: Gibson is a second-floor speakeasy on Bukit Pasoh Road from the Jigger & Pony Group, a longtime fixture of Asia's 50 Best Bars, whose menu carries a genuinely considered non-alcoholic section illustrated with watercolour sketches of its key ingredients. The anchor is the Urban Farmer No.4 (S$18), a zero-proof build around locally grown cranberry hibiscus from urban-farming collective Edible Garden City, with tangy, citrusy notes. Gibson also pours a non-alcoholic Bloody Mary (S$18) and alcohol-free variations of its signature cocktails, so a non-drinker is treated to the same care as the spirit-forward list.
signatureDrinks: Urban Farmer No.4 (S$18) - non-alcoholic build around locally grown cranberry hibiscus from Edible Garden City; tangy and citrusy, autumn-hued
Non-alcoholic Bloody Mary (S$18) - zero-proof version of the classic
venues.longDescription:
Tucked up a staircase on the second floor of a Bukit Pasoh shophouse in Outram, Gibson is one of the Jigger & Pony Group's most enduring bars, a compact, low-lit room named for the dry martini garnished with a pickled onion. It has been a mainstay of Asia's 50 Best Bars, appearing across the 2016-2020 editions, peaking at No.14 in 2017 and holding the No.25 spot in 2020, and it is known for reimagining classic cocktails through Asian and locally sourced ingredients.

Under principal bartender Gregory Camillo, Gibson's rotating menus (recent editions include Chimera and the tenth-anniversary Timeless) devote a real, printed section to non-alcoholic drinks rather than treating them as an afterthought. Time Out Singapore singled the bar out in its guide to the city's best non-alcoholic drinks, noting the zero-proof list is illustrated with watercolour sketches of its ingredients so non-drinkers don't feel they are missing the full experience.

The headline pour is the Urban Farmer No.4 (S$18), part of a running collaboration with Edible Garden City, a Singapore agriculture collective that grows food in under-utilised urban spaces. This iteration is built around their locally grown cranberry hibiscus, giving the drink its autumn-hued colour and an unexpectedly tangy, citrusy palate. Alongside it, Gibson offers an alcohol-free Bloody Mary and zero-proof takes on its signature serves, making the NA offering a genuine parallel to the alcoholic menu rather than a token gesture.
venues.pressQuote: Its non-alcoholic section is just as well thought out - complete with watercolour sketches of key ingredients so you don't feel like you're missing out on the full experience.

venues.name: Gift Horse
venues.description: Gift Horse is a raw bar on Westminster Street from chef Benjamin Sukle, built entirely on Rhode Island shellfish — its oyster programme runs through every growing region in the state. The bar makes non-alcoholic drinks with a local streak, including one built on Del's, the frozen lemonade that is a Rhode Island institution, and an orange shrub. Playful room, seriously sourced.
venues.longDescription:
Gift Horse takes its name from the saying about not looking one in the mouth, which tells you most of what you need to know about the tone of the place. It is a raw bar on Westminster Street in downtown Providence, chef Benjamin Sukle's second room on the block after Oberlin, and it is centred on local shellfish, seafood and whatever came off New England boats that morning. The oyster programme is the point of pride: oysters drawn from every growing region in Rhode Island, so you can taste the difference between one salt pond and the next across a single tray.

The drinks follow the same instinct toward local specificity. The non-alcoholic build the bar is known for is made with Del's — the frozen lemonade sold from roadside stands across Rhode Island since the 1940s, and about as close to a state emblem as a drink can get — combined with lemon, lime and a citrus cordial. Ordering it is a small piece of local literacy. Alongside it sits an orange shrub, a drinking vinegar that cuts through the brine of a dozen oysters better than anything sweet would.

Two built drinks rather than a full printed section puts this at a three, but the pairing logic is genuinely good: shellfish wants acid, and both of these deliver it. For a non-drinker eating raw seafood, that is a more useful offer than a long list of sweet mocktails would be.

We have not published prices or confirmed current names here — Gift Horse does not publish a drinks menu online, and the list moves with the kitchen. The restaurant sits two doors from Oberlin under the same ownership, and both take reservations through the same system.
venues.pressQuote: Gift Horse is anchored by its bar because that's where the oysters are
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Rhode Island Monthly, dining review, October 2023

venues.name: Gigantic
venues.description: Gigantic is a jewel-box cocktail bar on Easthampton's Cottage Street, opened in 2018 by Ned King in a small room with a pressed-tin ceiling, painted portraits and stained-glass lamps. The cocktail list is organised by year of origin, from 1937 to the present, and the house mocktails get the same treatment as the spirited drinks — the Dream Defender is a zero-proof rebuild of the Zombie on lemon, lime, passionfruit, pineapple, pineapple syrup and mint. It is a full bar serving alcohol, so this is a good zero-proof list inside an ordinary bar rather than an alcohol-free room. No kitchen — eat first.
signatureDrinks: Dream Defender (zero-proof Zombie — lemon, lime, passionfruit, pineapple, pineapple syrup, mint)
venues.longDescription:
Gigantic occupies a small storefront on Cottage Street, the block that carries most of Easthampton's evening life, and it has been there since 2018. The Daily Hampshire Gazette once described it as a glam museum, a punk-rock saloon and a Tinder-date destination at once, which is a fair summary of a room with a pressed-tin ceiling, painted portraits on the walls, stained-glass lamps and about as many seats as a large living room. Owner Ned King lights forty-five candles before service and builds the playlists himself; the attention shows in the way the place feels rather than in anything on a sign.

The drinks list is arranged historically, running from 1937 to the present, which makes it a cocktail-history exercise as much as a menu, and includes a run of tropical and tiki builds. The relevant part for anyone not drinking is that the non-alcoholic drinks are treated as cocktails rather than as an afterthought. The Dream Defender is the one to know: a zero-proof reconstruction of the Zombie, built on lemon, lime, passionfruit, pineapple, pineapple syrup and mint, and served with the same care as the rum version it descends from. Reviewers who order the mocktails tend to mention them unprompted, which is not the usual pattern.

Two practical things. Gigantic is a full bar and most of the room will be drinking alcohol, so it is a place to get a genuinely good zero-proof drink rather than a place to avoid alcohol entirely — a different proposition from Dry Humor a few streets away, and worth knowing which you want before you go. And there is no kitchen, so eat first or plan to move on; Cottage Street has options within a few doors either way.

Hours are evening-only and it is closed Mondays. The room is small enough that a busy Friday fills it, and the bar posts closures to Instagram when weather or staffing intervenes, so a look at the feed before setting out is worth the ten seconds.
venues.pressQuote: It's a place people can come and feel a little bit special.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Ned King, Gigantic owner, to the Daily Hampshire Gazette

venues.name: Gigglewaters
venues.description: Gigglewaters is a 1920s speakeasy-styled restaurant and bar in downtown Safety Harbor with a single-screen classic-movie theater in back — order a drink and catch an old film. Its award-winning bar treats mocktails with the same care as its cocktails; the Fyre Fest (blood orange, grapefruit, pineapple, honey, fresh basil, sugar rim) leads a spirit-free list that locals rank among the area's best. Opened in 2018 by Richie and Rachel Fine Wilson.  The screening room is the real differentiator for a non-drinker: an evening with a structure other than drinking is a far easier three hours to spend without a glass.
signatureDrinks: Fyre Fest (blood orange, grapefruit, pineapple, honey, fresh basil, sugar rim)
venues.longDescription:
Gigglewaters sits on Main Street in Safety Harbor, a small waterfront town on the western shore of Old Tampa Bay, and combines a restaurant and bar with a screening room — a Prohibition-themed room whose name is period slang for alcohol, which is a piece of irony worth enjoying given why it appears in this directory. The cinema is the differentiator: a venue where the evening has a structure other than drinking is a materially easier place to spend three hours without a drink.

That structural point is most of the case for it. A great deal of sober socialising fails not on the quality of the alternatives but on the shapelessness of the evening — three hours in a bar with nothing to do but hold something. A film gives the time a spine, and it means the drink is an accompaniment rather than the entire activity.

The bar carries named non-alcoholic builds alongside the full cocktail list, and the Prohibition framing gives the alcohol-free side a coherence most themed bars never manage: a room decorated around the era when nobody was legally drinking is well placed to make a virtue of a menu where nobody has to.

Practical notes: Safety Harbor is a drive from Tampa or St. Petersburg and the town is small, so this is a destination evening rather than a stop. Screening times govern the room, so check what is playing and book if the film matters — seats are limited and the schedule is the constraint rather than the table. It is a licensed bar and restaurant; the zero-proof options are a genuine part of the list rather than the character of the venue.  Safety Harbor is small enough that the cinema schedule effectively governs the evening, so check what is playing before setting out.
venues.pressQuote: Gigglewaters, nestled in the quaint town of Safety Harbor, offers an immersive experience that transports patrons to the bygone era of Prohibition

venues.name: Gilt Bar
venues.description: Gilt Bar is the River North restaurant and bar that launched Brendan Sodikoff's Hogsalt group in 2010, a dark, brass-and-leather room that describes itself as dedicated to the pleasures of drinking in restaurants and eating in bars, with a concealed speakeasy called The Library beneath it. Its cocktail menu carries a Spirit-Free heading whose drinks are priced at $14.95, within three dollars of the full-proof list. The Citrus Ritual is built on Ritual's tequila alternative with blood orange, lime, mint and club soda; the Seedlip Sour pairs Seedlip Grove 42 with cranberry; and a St. Agrestis Phony Negroni is poured from the bottle. Resy singled the program out in its guide to Chicago's non-alcoholic cocktails.

naMenuItems.description: ritual tequila alternative, blood orange, lime, mint, club soda

naMenuItems.name: Seedlip Sour
naMenuItems.description: seedlip grove 42, cranberry

venues.longDescription:
Gilt Bar opened on West Kinzie Street in River North in 2010 and became the founding room of Hogsalt, the group that went on to build Maude's Liquor Bar, Au Cheval and Bavette's. The premise it states for itself - dedicated to the pleasures of drinking in restaurants and eating in bars - explains the format: a full kitchen sending ricotta toast, bone marrow and steak into a low-lit dining room, a long bar working through classic cocktails, and a hidden lounge called The Library downstairs that nods to the neighborhood's speakeasy history. The room has been a River North fixture long enough that its non-alcoholic list has been through several iterations.

The current menu keeps a Spirit-Free heading immediately after the cocktails, with drinks at $14.95 against $17.95 for the full-proof list - close enough that ordering from it does not feel like ordering down. The Citrus Ritual is the most fully constructed of them, using Ritual Zero Proof's tequila alternative with blood orange, lime, mint and club soda for a long, sharp drink that works alongside the kitchen's richer plates. The Seedlip Sour is shorter and drier, built on Seedlip Grove 42 with cranberry. A St. Agrestis Phony Negroni rounds out the section from the bottle. Resy's guide to the city's non-alcoholic cocktails picked the bar out specifically for the fact that its booze-free drinks read as festive rather than dutiful, noting that the list ran to five drinks at the time of writing. Service starts at 4pm daily and runs to 10:30pm on weeknights and 11pm at weekends, and the spirit-free list is available at the bar as well as at table. The Library, the concealed bar beneath the restaurant, references the speakeasy culture that ran through this part of River North during Prohibition, and it is part of the same operation rather than a separate venue. Gilt Bar was the first room Hogsalt opened, and the group has since grown into one of the larger independent restaurant companies in the city, which is part of why the spirit-free list here is stocked with branded non-alcoholic spirits rather than improvised from juice.
venues.pressQuote: While the bar is lined with traditional liquor, the menu here has five booze-free drinks that are just as festive and celebratory as the rest.

venues.name: Gin Gin's
venues.description: Gin Gin's is a neighbourhood cocktail bar and kitchen at 345 Summer Avenue NW, just off the Bridge Street run on the West Side, trading under the line "There's always time for a good time." It keeps three crafted spirit-free cocktails on the standing menu alongside the canned St. Agrestis Phony Negroni, an Italian-style non-alcoholic amaro build that is one of the few pre-made zero-proof products bitter enough to satisfy a negroni drinker. The bar is open Monday through Saturday and closed Sunday, with late finishes on Friday and Saturday. It sits within a couple of minutes' walk of Drip Drop Cocktail Room and The Knickerbocker.
venues.address: 345 Summer Ave NW, Grand Rapids, MI 49504
signatureDrinks: St. Agrestis Phony Negroni (canned non-alcoholic negroni)
venues.longDescription:
Gin Gin's occupies 345 Summer Avenue NW, a block off the main Bridge Street strip on the West Side, and trades as a neighbourhood cocktail bar and kitchen rather than a destination cocktail room. Its own tagline — "There's always time for a good time" — sets the register, and the venue turns up regularly on local date-night lists. Hours run Monday through Thursday 4pm to 11pm, Friday 4pm to 11:30pm and Saturday 3pm to 11:30pm, closed Sunday.

The zero-proof offer is modest in size and specific in kind. Three crafted spirit-free cocktails sit on the standing menu — made by the bar, rotating, and not individually named in the sources available, so they are not listed here as signature drinks. The documented item is the canned St. Agrestis Phony Negroni, which is worth explaining because it fills a gap most non-alcoholic lists cannot. Zero-proof drinks skew sweet and fruit-forward, because sugar and acid are the easiest things to build with once the spirit is gone; genuine bitterness is much harder, and it is exactly what a negroni drinker is looking for. The Phony Negroni, made by the Brooklyn amaro producer St. Agrestis, is built on bitter orange and gentian and lands close enough to the original to work as a substitute rather than a consolation. Stocking it is a small decision that tells you something about the bar's intent, in the same way that Buffalo Traders buying Little Saints does. For a guest who does not drink, Gin Gin's is best understood as one stop on a West Side circuit rather than a whole evening: it is a few minutes from Drip Drop Cocktail Room on Bridge Street, which has the deeper named list, and from The Knickerbocker, which brews its own alcohol-free beer.
venues.pressQuote: Three crafted spirit-free cocktails, plus the canned St. Agrestis Phony Negroni.

venues.name: Ginger's
venues.description: Ginger's is a subterranean speakeasy-style cocktail lounge beneath a historic East Quarter building downtown, named Dallas Observer's Best Cocktail Bar in 2025, with a dedicated N/A section built around Three Spirit's botanical spirits. The Zen Level pairs Three Spirit Livener with lemongrass green tea syrup, lemon and yuzu; the Zenicillin riffs on a penicillin template with Three Spirit Nightcap, ginger syrup and lemon; and the Ginger Collins runs Nightcap into a house gin-eric syrup, lemon and soda. All three were $14 as of January 2025. The lounge is walk-ins only with no reservation system and seats roughly 50, so weekends fill early. Open 6pm to midnight daily.

venues.longDescription:
For non-drinkers navigating Dallas's nightlife, Ginger's is one of the few upscale cocktail lounges in the East Quarter that treats zero-proof options as a genuine part of the program rather than an afterthought. The bar's menu includes a dedicated N/A section — confirmed in both PaperCity (January 2024) and CultureMap (January 2025) — built around Three Spirit's botanical spirits, alongside the full range of classics. The setting itself is subterranean: a 1,200-square-foot room beneath a building that dates to Dallas's early Auto Row era, entered via a dramatic staircase and outfitted by local firm JonesBaker with leather U-shaped booths and a marble-topped walnut bar.

The three documented NA cocktails all lean on Three Spirit's functional botanical spirits: the Zen Level pairs Three Spirit Livener with lemongrass green tea syrup, lemon juice, and yuzu for a bright, aromatic pour; the Zenicillin riffs on a classic penicillin template with Three Spirit Nightcap, ginger syrup, and lemon; and the Ginger Collins uses Three Spirit Nightcap with a house gin-eric syrup, lemon, and soda for something effervescent and herbal. All three were priced at $14 as of January 2025. The bar program was originally created by Sean Kenyon, an award-winning mixologist and Tales of the Cocktail 2014 American Bartender of the Year; current menu development is led by Bar Lead Eric Simmons, who introduced the 2025 cocktail and dessert menus.

Ginger's operates without a reservation system for the lounge — walk-ins only, first-come on the booths — which means arriving early on weekends matters if you want a seat. The room fits roughly 50 people comfortably before it tips toward crowded. Valet is available on-site. The venue maintains a dress code (call ahead for current guidelines), but the Dallas Observer notes it leans toward 'come as you are' rather than strict enforcement. It earned Dallas Observer's Best Cocktail Bar award in 2025, making it a credible destination for anyone who wants a genuinely polished night out in Downtown Dallas, with or without alcohol.
venues.pressQuote: Ginger's Downtown cocktail lounge connected to Sushi | Bar has three mocktails: Zen Level with Three Spirit Livener, lemongrass green tea syrup, lemon juice, & yuzu; Zenicillin with Three Spirit Nightcap, ginger syrup, & lemon; and Ginger Collins with Three Spirit Nightcap, Gin-eric syrup, lemon, & soda.

venues.name: Gipsy Hill Brewing Co. Taproom
venues.description: The Gipsy Hill Brewing Co. Taproom occupies a Hamilton Road industrial unit in West Norwood, directly opposite the working brewhouse, pouring up to a dozen keg lines backed by fridges of cans and rotating low- and no-alcohol options. Its non-alcoholic anchor is brewed in-house: HepcAF, a 0.5% alcohol-free IPA built from the recipe for Hepcat, the brewery's best-selling IPA, using the same Citra, Mosaic, Ekuanot and Mouteka hops. That makes for a genuinely hop-forward zero-proof pint poured by the people who brew it, alongside the full-strength core range, guest cask and wine. Local street-food vendors rotate through the yard and Yard Sale Pizza delivers on-site.

venues.longDescription:
Gipsy Hill Brewing Co. began brewing in July 2014, founded by Sam McMeekin and Charlie Shaw, who had met behind the bar at Borough Market's craft-beer institution The Rake. It grew into one of the larger independent breweries in South London, became employee-owned in 2021, and in 2024 was acquired by Sunrise Alliance Beverages; the West Norwood site has continued to brew and to run its taproom throughout. The taproom sits in Unit 5 of the Hamilton Road industrial estate, a short walk from both West Norwood and Gipsy Hill stations, directly across the yard from the brewhouse that supplies it.

The room itself is a straightforward one-room brewery tap: a long bar with up to a dozen keg lines, two handpumps for real ale and cider, three large fridges of cans for drinking in or taking away, and rows of wooden barrels where beer ages in view of drinkers. There is bench seating inside and an outdoor yard, with rotating local street-food traders and free Yard Sale Pizza delivery every day the taproom is open.

For non-drinkers the draw is that the alcohol-free option is brewed on the premises rather than bought in. HepcAF, launched in January 2023, is a 0.5% ABV alcohol-free IPA developed from the base recipe of Hepcat — Gipsy Hill's flagship IPA — with adjustments to the fermentable sugars and yeast, then dry-hopped with the same Citra, Mosaic, Ekuanot and Mouteka blend. The result pours a hazy amber with a tropical, citrus-forward nose and real hop bitterness, and it is a fixture in the taproom's fridges. Beyond HepcAF the bar keeps a rotating selection of low- and no-alcohol beers from Gipsy Hill and guest breweries, so a non-drinker can work through several genuine options in a session rather than defaulting to a soft drink.

venues.name: Goat & Rabbit
venues.description: Goat & Rabbit is a cozy cocktail bar that opened in November 2020 on Kansas City's 39th Street, in the Volker neighborhood. Brothers Jugal and Atit Patel named it after the Pendergast-era "Goats" and "Rabbits" — rival political factions who eventually joined forces — a nod to the bar's come-as-you-are philosophy. The room is known for its emerald-green seating, warm wood, and big windows. Its non-alcoholic program is treated with the same rigor as the full bar: a dedicated, seasonal zero-proof section using house syrups and cordials alongside dedicated NA spirits like Bare Zero Proof gin, Undone spiced "rum," and Pathfinder Hemp & Root. Current named zero-proof cocktails include the Chaiball (Undone N/A spiced "rum," chai, vanilla, soda), Petal Talk (charred-cinnamon hibiscus tea, guava, agave, lychee meringue), Night of the Roxberry (raspberry coulis, mint, lemon, soda), and the Smedley Gaze. The venue is 21+.
