venues.longDescription:
Goat & Rabbit opened in November 2020 at 1804 W 39th Street in Volker, in the space that had been Nomad's Coffee, from brothers Jugal and Atit Patel — who also part-own Dodson's Bar & Commons in Waldo. The name is local history rather than whimsy: the nicknames Goats and Rabbits date to the era of Kansas City's rival political machines, the Rabbit boss Joe Shannon and the Goat boss Tom Pendergast. Jugal Patel set the brief plainly at opening: elevated without being over the top, a staple bar for people who work and play in the 39th Street and Volker areas. It is 21 and over, opens at 4pm midweek and 9am at weekends for brunch, and runs happy hour Monday to Friday from 4pm and all evening on Sundays. Food is minimal — a pub snack mix at $5 — so this is a drinking room rather than a dining one.

The non-alcoholic list is unusually long for a neighbourhood bar, printed under its own heading and running seven drinks. The Pitch, naming it in Best of KC 2025, put the point well: even the mocktails are crafted with the same care, making Goat & Rabbit a spot where non-drinkers aren't left out of the fun. Smedley Gaze ($10) is the most savoury, building Bare Zero Proof gin with fresh cucumber and tomato juice, Thai basil syrup and a Thai chilli tincture. Chaiball ($10) uses Undone's non-alcoholic spiced rum with a local chai concentrate and soda. Petal Talk ($12) layers hibiscus tea steeped with charred cinnamon sticks under a lychee meringue. Dirty Fernot & Coke ($12) is the cleverest of them, using Pathfinder's hemp-and-root spirit with Coke and a plant-based vanilla foam. Night of the Roxberry and Leaves of Three, Let It Be are $10 each. Athletic's Run Wild IPA and a Fritz Müller non-alcoholic sparkling cover beer and wine. One drink needs flagging: Flying Kites ($13) is built on a Climbing Kites sparkling water containing 10mg of THC, so anyone avoiding intoxicants entirely should order around it.
venues.pressQuote: The bar gives its non-alcoholic cocktails the same respect and attention to detail as their alcoholic counterparts.

venues.name: Gold Point
venues.description: Gold Point is a whiskey-forward neighbourhood bar on Larimer Street in Five Points, known locally as an industry hangout where bartenders drink after their shifts, with a patio and no pretension. Despite the reputation, it keeps a standing "Non-Alcoholic" heading on its own drink menu alongside cocktails, cans and bottles, wine and combos. The three house zero-proof drinks are built on non-alcoholic spirits rather than juice, and priced at $11 to $12: a fruity non-alcoholic French 75 made with Ritual gin, a Phony Negroni, and a tropical bitter spritz built on The Pathfinder hemp spirit. The bar also stocks Athletic Brewing's Atletica Mexican-style lager and Three Spirit Spark by the can. It opens at 4pm on weekdays, 2pm at weekends, and trades to 2am daily.

venues.longDescription:
Gold Point sits at 3126 Larimer Street in Five Points, on the stretch of Larimer that the RiNo art district has grown around, and has built its reputation on a long whiskey list and a determinedly unfussy room — an industry bar where bartenders end up after their own shifts, with a patio and, as one listing puts it, zero pretense. That reputation makes the non-alcoholic section on its menu more notable rather than less: this is not a wellness-positioned venue trying to capture the sober-curious market, it is a whiskey bar that decided the people not drinking should get a properly built drink.

The menu carries "Non-Alcoholic" as a standing heading alongside cocktails, cans and bottles, wine and combos. The house drinks use non-alcoholic spirits as the base rather than treating the category as flavoured soda. "Sugar, Spice, and F@#$ ICE!" is described on the menu as a fruity non-alcoholic French 75, built from Ritual non-alcoholic gin with strawberry, rosemary and Three Spirits Spark, at $12. "Whoa, Mama!" is a tropical bitter spritz combining The Pathfinder hemp spirit with Thai and Szechuan spiced pineapple and pineapple cream soda, also $12. A Phony Negroni at $11 is described with characteristic brevity as "Just like a regular Negroni, but hold the booze." By the can the bar keeps Athletic Brewing's Atletica, a non-alcoholic Mexican-style lager, at $5.75, and Three Spirits Spark, a non-alcoholic sparkling rosé, at $10. The list rotates: Westword's January 2026 round-up of non-alcoholic options in Denver caught a different pair on the board, describing "Situationship, a bittersweet blend of Pathfinder, apple soda and Chinese five spice; as well as Ghosted, a spicy and umami-forward drink featuring chai, miso and a woodsy elixir from Three Spirit." The bar opens at 4pm Monday to Friday and 2pm at weekends, and runs to 2am every night.
venues.pressQuote: Situationship, a bittersweet blend of Pathfinder, apple soda and Chinese five spice; as well as Ghosted, a spicy and umami-forward drink featuring chai, miso and a woodsy elixir from Three Spirit.

venues.name: Golden Kava Lounge
venues.description: Golden Kava Lounge describes itself as having the vibe of a coffee shop mixed with a nightclub, and that is a fair account of a room that serves kava teas, hosts live music, game nights and themed events, and stays open into the small hours without a drop of alcohol on the premises. It sits on South Golden Road at the western edge of the metro, and its influence on the Colorado scene is larger than its size suggests: the five founders of Denver Café & Kava, now open on East Colfax, met each other here as customers before opening their own room in the city. The list runs kava, exotic teas and specialty products.
venues.longDescription:
Golden Kava Lounge sits at 16399 South Golden Road, on the far western edge of the Denver metro where Golden meets the foothills, and its own description of itself is the most economical summary anyone has written of what a good kava bar actually is: the vibe of a coffee shop mixed with a nightclub. It serves kava teas, it hosts events, it stays open into the small hours, and it has never served alcohol.

Its significance to the Colorado scene is out of proportion to its size. The five people who founded Denver Café & Kava — Kevin Bloom, Elizabeth Leung, Cam Webbe, Jayden MacDonald and Jack Kestian — met one another here, as customers, and went on to open the city's own version on East Colfax in early 2026. That is the clearest evidence available that this room does the thing it sets out to do. A venue that turns its regulars into friends, and then into business partners who build another one, is functioning as a third place in the full sense rather than as a retail outlet with seating.

The programming runs to live music, game nights and themed gatherings, and the drinks are kava alongside a curated range of exotic teas and specialty products. Kava is the ground root of a South Pacific shrub, prepared as a water infusion; it contains no alcohol, tastes earthy and bitter, numbs the lips and tongue on the first mouthful, and is mildly sedative — which is why it works as a social drink rather than merely as a substitute for one. It has been drunk communally across Fiji, Vanuatu, Tonga and Samoa for around three thousand years.

One practical note. Published hours for this venue disagree across sources: some listings show it as open 24 hours, while the lounge's own listings describe an 8am to 4am day, seven days a week. Either way it is among the latest-trading alcohol-free rooms in Colorado, but if you are planning an overnight visit it is worth checking on (720) 663-7996 first. The lounge's active presence is on Instagram rather than a conventional website, which is where events are announced.

venues.name: The Golden Pineapple
venues.description: The Golden Pineapple is a bartender-owned corner bar in one of West Asheville's oldest buildings, opened by master mixologist Katey Ryder. Per Explore Asheville, its team makes its own alcohol-free spirits using herbs, aromatics, and an immersion circulator, which anchor a dedicated "No Grav" section of the cocktail menu — the Casamara Cosmo, the Cutecumber, and the NoGroni — alongside botanical sodas and a non-alcoholic beer list. It is a full bar, but one that treats the no-proof list with the same house-made care (its own orgeat and tepache) as the rest.
venues.longDescription:
The Golden Pineapple is a cocktail bar and restaurant at 503 Haywood Road in West Asheville, owned by Katey Ryder, occupying a historic building on the strip that has previously housed a recording studio, a pharmacy and a deli. It is a genuinely local room — Mountain Xpress featured it in a piece on the animals that belong to Asheville businesses, noting that the menu features items named after Marty, the bar's resident dog, which tells you as much about the tone as any description of the décor would. It sits on the same block as The Whale, which makes that stretch of Haywood Road good for a non-drinker moving between places in one evening. The bar closes Tuesdays and Wednesdays and opens at 5pm the rest of the week, with the kitchen shutting half an hour before the bar.

The defining fact about the drinks here is that the menu changes weekly — the bar says so on its own homepage and tells you to check back for the current list. That is unusual and it cuts both ways for a non-drinker. It means the zero-proof options are being rewritten as often as the cocktails, rather than sitting untouched for years as they do at most bars, and the names that have appeared on the list reflect real technique: a Casamara Cosmo built on the Italian amaro-style soft drink, a cucumber-led Cutecumber, a NoGroni and an Espresso Phony Negroni. It also means no printed list can be relied on in advance, including this one. Compounding that, the bar publishes its menus as images rather than text, so they cannot be read online at all — not by search engines, not by screen readers, and not by anyone checking their phone before they arrive. The practical approach is to treat the names above as evidence of the house style, tell the bartender what you like, and ask what is on that week.
venues.pressQuote: The master mixologists at the helm make their own alcohol-free spirits using herbs, aromatics and an immersion circulator. The finished product serves as the foundation for a dedicated section of their cocktail menu called No Grav.

venues.name: Golden Ratio
venues.description: Golden Ratio is a Clinton Hill cocktail bar from Redwood Hospitality where every drink on the menu has both a spirited and a non-alcoholic version, built around house-made distillates and hydrosols crafted from foraged and upcycled ingredients.
venues.longDescription:
Golden Ratio opened November 26, 2025 in Clinton Hill, Brooklyn, from Redwood Hospitality, the team behind Place des Fêtes, Cafe Mado, and Laurel Bakery. Its defining concept is that the menu is split evenly between roughly 16 spirited cocktails and 16 non-alcoholic ones, with every drink orderable with or without alcohol and both versions getting equal attention. Rather than de-boozing classics, the zero-proof drinks are treated as parallel expressions of the same featured seasonal ingredient (the drinks carry ingredient names like Purple Shiso, Pine, Fir, Bergamot, and Mandarin), so the NA side is a genuine counterpart rather than an afterthought. Beverage director and Redwood partner Piper Kristensen builds proprietary, house-made non-alcoholic water distillates and hydrosols using a rotary evaporator, capturing volatile flavors from greenmarket produce, foraged elements, and byproducts from the group's own kitchens, such as leftover bread from Laurel Bakery and citrus peels from Place des Fêtes, forming a near-zero-waste closed loop. The room is warm and minimal with repurposed furniture, soft amber light, and multiple seating zones; the bar runs largely on walk-ins with limited Resy bookings.

The printed menu sets the two halves side by side in four columns each, sorted by mood rather than by base spirit. On the non-alcoholic side those columns run bright, spritz, complex and savory: an Apple of grape skins and cider and a Sorrento Lemon in the first; Bergamot with blueberry and coriander, Fir with needles and grapefruit, Guava with prickly pear, Mandarin with juice and tonic, and Pineapple Guava with chrysanthemum and pineappleweed in the spritz column; Green Almond with cucumber and lime and Sapodilla with burnt honey and soba cha under complex; and Purple Shiso with bread and lime, Pine with pine nut, lactose and lemon, and Licorice Root with coconut and citrus under savory. Most sit at $16, with the Pine at $8. Athletic Brewing's Atletica is listed by the glass for anyone who wants a beer instead. Because the list is rebuilt around whatever the farms, foragers and preservation projects are yielding, the specific names rotate several times a year and the bar states plainly that the published menu reflects a recent rather than a fixed offering; the four-column structure and the parallel spirited and zero-proof halves are the constants. The kitchen keeps the same discipline, running bar snacks, seasonal vegetable plates, larger dishes and desserts that change on the same cycle, and it closes at 9:30pm nightly even when the bar keeps going.
venues.pressQuote: Every drink can be ordered with or without alcohol and both versions get equal attention.

venues.name: Good News Bar
venues.description: Good News Bar is San Diego's first dedicated 100% alcohol-free bar, opened in Hillcrest in mid-July 2025 with an integrated non-alcoholic bottle shop. The concept was created by married former bartenders Kaylee and Crystal Clark, who left drinking behind in recovery; since August 2025 the bar has been operated by its majority owner, Ality Richardson. It is named after Mac Miller's song "Good News" and frames itself around raising awareness of addiction and mental health. The house line is coffee by day, cocktails by night, community always: mornings bring coffee, tea, functional cocktails and freshly baked pastries, while evenings run "functional" cocktails built around adaptogens, nootropics, nervines, kava and hemp-derived CBD alongside "free-spirited" builds that reimagine classics with non-alcoholic spirits, plus apéritifs, dealcoholized wines, NA beers and cider. Signature zero-proof drinks include The Merry Go Round, The Woods, Deborah Downer and Goosebumpz. Trivia, live music and DJ nights fill the calendar.
venues.longDescription:
Good News Bar opened on Park Boulevard in Hillcrest in mid-July 2025 — soft-launching over Pride weekend — as San Diego's first dedicated alcohol-free bar, in a city whose drinking culture had until then offered non-drinkers a choice between a coffee shop and staying home. The concept came from Kaylee and Crystal Clark, a married pair of former bartenders who stopped drinking themselves and wanted somewhere that worked as a bar rather than as a substitute for one; the bar has been operated by its majority owner, Ality Richardson, since August 2025. The name is taken from Mac Miller's song "Good News," and the bar is explicit that it exists partly to raise awareness around addiction and mental health rather than simply to sell drinks — a framing that Hillcrest, long the centre of San Diego's LGBTQ+ nightlife, has taken to.

The operating model is the interesting part: coffee by day, cocktails by night, with a non-alcoholic bottle shop built into the room so you can drink there or take something home. Mornings run coffee, tea and freshly baked pastries alongside functional cocktails. Evenings split the list in two. The "functional" drinks are built around adaptogens, nootropics, nervines, kava and hemp-derived CBD, and are mostly 0.0% ABV. The "free-spirited" cocktails reimagine classics using non-alcoholic spirits and sit under 0.5% ABV, joined by apéritifs, dealcoholized wines, non-alcoholic beers and cider. The named house builds — The Merry Go Round, The Woods, Deborah Downer and Goosebumpz — are the ones regulars order, and the bar stocks Best Day Brewing, Three Spirit and Curious Elixirs among others. Trivia nights, live music and DJ sets fill the week, which is the part that matters most: a bar for people who do not drink only works if there is a reason to turn up on a Tuesday. It runs Tuesday to Sunday, to midnight on Friday and Saturday.
venues.pressQuote: Unlike conventional bars that relegate mocktails to the bottom of a menu, Good News places non-alcoholic offerings at the forefront

venues.name: Goodale Station
venues.description: Goodale Station is the twelfth-floor rooftop bar and restaurant of the Canopy by Hilton Columbus Downtown Short North, on Nationwide Boulevard between downtown and the Short North. The room is glass-enclosed with outdoor terraces on either side, which keeps it usable year-round rather than seasonally. Its alcohol-free drinks are treated as part of the regular list and, according to local coverage, sell like it: the Don't Carrot All and the Berry Manilow are described as bestsellers of the season rather than as accommodations. Alongside the named AF cocktails the bar keeps a rotating range of shrubs — vinegar-based drinks built from fruit, herbs and sugar, sweet and sharp at once — which change through the year. Brunch runs at weekends from 11am and the bar stays open to 1am on Fridays and Saturdays.

venues.longDescription:
Goodale Station sits on the twelfth floor of the Canopy by Hilton Columbus Downtown Short North at 77 East Nationwide Boulevard, on the strip between the convention district and the southern end of the Short North. The room is glass-enclosed with terraces opening off either side, giving it a long view over the Columbus skyline and — unlike most rooftop bars in a city with real winters — a year-round season. It serves brunch at weekends from 11am, dinner nightly, and runs to 1am on Fridays and Saturdays.

The non-alcoholic list is small but distinctive, and the local framing of it is unusually direct: rather than describing the AF drinks as an option for guests who need one, coverage of the bar reports that the Don't Carrot All and the Berry Manilow are among the bestsellers of the season outright. That is a different claim from most zero-proof menus in the city, and it is consistent with how the bar presents them — as named drinks on the list with the puns intact, not as a separate concession. Behind the two named builds, the more interesting part of the offering is the shrub programme. Shrubs are drinking vinegars: fruit, herbs and sugar macerated with vinegar into a syrup that is then lengthened, producing something simultaneously sweet and sharp, with an acidity that gives a non-alcoholic drink the backbone it usually lacks. Goodale Station rotates them through the year rather than keeping a fixed roster, which means the AF options change with the season in the same way the cocktail list does. Guests should note the bar is inside a hotel and the ground-floor entrance routes through the lobby lifts. For planning purposes the room works better as an early-evening or brunch destination than a late one: the kitchen closes at 10pm even on nights when the bar runs to 1am, and the weekend brunch service from 11am is when the terraces are at their best. Being inside a hotel, it also tends to be quieter midweek than the street-level bars in the Short North a few blocks north.
venues.pressQuote: Like a good pun or clever name? Goodale Station's AF drinks like the Don't Carrot All and Berry Manilow are bestsellers of the season.

venues.name: Goodkind
venues.description: Goodkind is a cocktail-forward restaurant and corner tavern in Milwaukee's Bay View neighborhood, run by chef Paul Zerkel and bar director Katie Rose. Known for seasonal Americana cooking and a serious drinks program — it was a 2022 James Beard Award semifinalist for Outstanding Bar Program — the bar also maintains a rotating slate of zero-proof cocktails. The spirit-free lineup ranges from NA aperitifs and tonics to sweet-and-savory builds, anchored by the NA-mericano and a house-brewed Szechuan ginger beer.
signatureDrinks: NA-mericano (Ritual zero-proof aperitif, raspberry, Fluere Botanicale, lemon, tonic)
venues.longDescription:
Opened in 2014 in a converted corner building on S. Wentworth Avenue, Goodkind pairs chef and co-owner Paul Zerkel's seasonal Americana cooking with a cocktail program overseen by co-owner Katie Rose. The bar's reputation reaches well beyond Bay View: in 2022 Goodkind was named a James Beard Award semifinalist for Outstanding Bar Program, and it continues to appear on OnMilwaukee's rotating roundup of the city's essential restaurants.

That same craft carries into the venue's alcohol-free drinks. Goodkind builds a rotating, seasonal slate of zero-proof cocktails that runs from spirit-free aperitifs and NA tonics to more elaborate sweet-and-savory drinks. Its signature non-alcoholic pour, the NA-mericano, combines Ritual's zero-proof aperitif with raspberry, Fluere Botanicale, lemon and tonic, while a house-brewed Szechuan ginger beer gives non-drinkers a spicy, made-in-house option alongside the cocktail list.

Milwaukee outlets — including OnMilwaukee's guide to the city's best zero-proof cocktails and Visit Milwaukee's NA-cocktail directory — consistently cite Goodkind as a go-to for guests who want to skip alcohol without sacrificing craft. The kitchen and bar serve evenings, Friday through Tuesday from 5 p.m. (closed Wednesday and Thursday), with reservations available through Tock.

venues.name: Goodwins
venues.description: Goodwins is a Lower Greenville all-day restaurant whose current menu carries a section printed as NO ABV — a heading that leaves no ambiguity, on a stretch of Greenville Avenue where the competition is mostly bars. Both builds use Ritual Zero Proof spirits: the Mocking Marg pairs its tequila alternative with lime and agave, and the Ginger Peach Sour runs the gin alternative into peach, lime, ginger and rose water. Athletic Brewing and Crazy Mountain non-alcoholic beers sit on the same menu. Two drinks is a short list, and it lives inside a menu PDF rather than a drinks page, so it is easy to miss — but both are properly built on non-alcoholic distillates.
signatureDrinks: Mocking Marg (Ritual tequila alternative, lime, agave)
Ginger Peach Sour (Ritual gin alternative, peach, lime, ginger, rose water)
venues.longDescription:
Goodwins occupies a stretch of Greenville Avenue where the competition is mostly bars, and it runs as an all-day restaurant with lunch and dinner services either side of an afternoon break. Its non-alcoholic drinks are printed under a heading that leaves no ambiguity — NO ABV — on the dinner menu revised in late April 2026. That matters more than it sounds on this particular street, where a non-drinker's realistic options are otherwise a soda at a bar built for drinking.

There are two, and both are built on Ritual Zero Proof, the Chicago distillate range that has become the default working spirit for American bars taking the category seriously. The Mocking Marg keeps it clean: the tequila alternative with lime and agave, which is the drink most people want first when they stop drinking, and the one that most exposes a bar that is not trying. The Ginger Peach Sour is the more elaborate build, running the gin alternative into peach liqueur syrup, lime, ginger and a rose water finish — the rose water in particular is the kind of flourish that only appears when someone has actually tasted the drink and decided it needed a top note. Non-alcoholic beer comes from Athletic Brewing and Crazy Mountain's lime lager, which widens the list considerably for anyone who would rather drink beer than a mixed drink.

We would rather be straight about the scale: two mixed drinks is a short list, and it sits inside a menu PDF rather than on a drinks page of its own, so it is easy to miss when browsing and worth naming at the table. What makes it worth the entry is that both are made with real non-alcoholic spirits rather than juice and soda — an ordinary neighbourhood restaurant doing the thing properly rather than gesturing at it, which is a more useful signal for the rest of the street than another cocktail bar's showpiece list. The all-day format is the practical upside: with lunch and dinner either side of an afternoon break, this works as a daytime meeting as readily as an evening one, and a daytime table is the easier place to be the person not drinking on a street built almost entirely around the opposite.

venues.name: Grace by Nia
venues.description: Grace by Nia is a supper club on the third floor of 60 Seaport Boulevard in Boston's Seaport, opened in May 2023 by restaurateur Nia Grace, who also runs Darryl's Corner Bar & Kitchen in the South End. It spans more than 5,000 square feet of dining room and stage, programming live jazz and soul most nights it is open, and the kitchen runs a Southern menu — chargrilled oysters, fried catfish, bourbon peach ribs, country fried chicken with carrot cake waffles, lobster mac and cheese. The drinks list carries a named alcohol-free section headed Free Spirit, built on zero-proof tequila and bourbon rather than juice, priced at $14 for the spirit-based builds. It opens Friday through Sunday only.
signatureDrinks: Pretty in Pink (Clean Co. alcohol-free tequila, coconut cream, lemon, Red Bull Red Edition, Caliwater cactus water)
Prohibition (Free Spirits bourbon, alcohol-free bitters, habanero pepper maple, oversized ice)
Peach Sweet Tea Lemonade (peach, lemon, sweet tea)
venues.longDescription:
Grace by Nia opened in May 2023 in the Seaport as the second venue from Nia Grace, whose Darryl's Corner Bar & Kitchen in the South End is one of the longest-running Black-owned restaurants in the city. The Seaport room runs to more than 5,000 square feet across restaurant and live entertainment space on the third floor of 60 Seaport Boulevard, with a stage that programmes jazz, soul and other live acts as a core part of the offer rather than as background. Boston Magazine reviewed it in September 2023 as bringing supper-club glamour to the Seaport, and the business was financed through Eastern Bank, which announced the deal in May 2023. Grace has since extended the brand to Foxwoods. The kitchen's Southern menu covers chargrilled oysters, fried catfish bites, bourbon peach ribs, country fried chicken with carrot cake waffles and lobster mac and cheese, with a weekend brunch running brown butter beignets, piri piri shrimp with grits, red velvet pancakes and cajun home fries.

The alcohol-free drinks are printed under their own heading, Free Spirit, and are built on zero-proof spirits rather than being sweet juice mixes, which is what allows them to hold up in a room this loud. Pretty in Pink is $14 and combines Clean Co. alcohol-free tequila with coconut cream, lemon, Red Bull Red Edition and Caliwater cactus water. Prohibition is also $14, built on Free Spirits bourbon with alcohol-free bitters and a habanero pepper maple, served over an oversized rock — the one drink on the list with real heat and bitterness in it. Peach Sweet Tea Lemonade at $8 is the simplest option, made from peach, lemon and sweet tea. Caliwater cactus water is sold on its own at $6 in ginger lime or pineapple, and Heineken 0.0 is stocked at $8 among the bottles and cans. Meet Boston's January 2026 zero-proof guide judged the drinks bold and expressive. The venue currently trades Friday and Saturday evenings and Sunday for brunch and dinner.
venues.pressQuote: Grace by Nia delivers zero-proof drinks with bold, expressive flavors that match the energy of the space.

venues.name: Gracias Madre
venues.description: Gracias Madre is a vegan Mexican restaurant at 8905 Melrose Avenue in West Hollywood, opened in January 2014 in a former antique emporium — whitewashed brick, high ceilings with exposed beams, and a patio under mature olive trees with built-in heaters. CORRECTION: we previously described a spirit-free section called "On the Wagon" and a Michelada Sin Cerveza. Neither appears on the current menu. The section is now headed "zero/low proof" and holds four drinks at $16.50: the Rosemary Love (ginger and rosemary elixir, poured tableside) and Como No (Ritual apéritif, lemon, pineapple, jalapeño, guajillo, agave, foam), both printed 0 ABV; plus the Raspberry Orchard Shrub and No Sabo, both built on Green Apple NOOT. NOTE ON THOSE TWO: the menu defines NOOT as a functional blend of botanicals, herbs and nootropics containing under 1% alcohol, which cannot be served to anyone under 21 — so they are low-proof and age-restricted, not alcohol-free. Separately, eight standard cocktails can be made non-alcoholic with Cut Above NA tequila or mezcal at no extra charge. Aguas frescas and horchata are $6.50, seasonal kefir soda $8.50, and a rotating NA lager $10.50.
signatureDrinks: Any of eight cocktails made NA with Cut Above, no upcharge

naMenuItems.name: Non-Alcoholic Lager
naMenuItems.description: rancho west 0% 16oz

venues.longDescription:
Gracias Madre opened on Melrose Avenue in January 2014, the West Hollywood expression of a concept that began in San Francisco in 2009 from the founders of Café Gratitude. The room is a converted antique emporium, whitewashed brick and high ceilings with exposed beams and a great deal of natural light, and the open plan runs straight out onto a patio with an outdoor bar, heaters for cool evenings and the shade of mature olive trees. The cooking is entirely vegan Mexican, and the bar has always been the draw as much as the kitchen.

Our previous entry needs two corrections. The spirit-free section is no longer called "On the Wagon" — the current menu heads it zero/low proof — and the Michelada Sin Cerveza we listed does not appear on it; the only michelada now printed is the standard one with Mexican lager. What is there is four drinks at $16.50, and the distinction between them matters. Rosemary Love, a ginger and rosemary elixir shaken and poured tableside, and Como No, built on Ritual apéritif with lemon, pineapple, jalapeño, guajillo chilli, agave and foam, are both printed 0 ABV and are the genuinely alcohol-free choices. The Raspberry Orchard Shrub and No Sabo are built on something called Green Apple NOOT, and the menu is admirably clear about what that is: a functional blend of natural botanicals, herbs and nootropics containing less than 1% alcohol, which by the restaurant's own rule cannot be served to anyone under 21. They are low-proof and age-restricted rather than alcohol-free, and the section's honest name — zero slash low proof — is doing quiet work that a skim-reader would miss. The better news is what sits outside that section: eight of the standard cocktails, including the Purista Margarita and the Turmeric Mule, can be made non-alcoholic with Cut Above's NA tequila or mezcal at no additional charge, which effectively doubles the list. House drinks are cheap and good — aguas frescas and horchata at $6.50, a seasonal kefir soda at $8.50 — and a rotating non-alcoholic lager is $10.50. Note also that a CBD cocktail programme covered in the press a decade ago is long retired; nothing on the current menu is infused.

venues.name: Grand Concourse
venues.description: Grand Concourse is a large seafood restaurant in the former Pittsburgh & Lake Erie Railroad Station at Station Square, a Beaux-Arts terminal listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1974 and converted to a restaurant in 1978; it is known for its stained-glass vaulted ceiling, marble columns and riverfront views, and is now part of the Landry's group. Its drinks list splits the non-alcoholic offering across two separate sections, which is worth knowing before you order. "Free Spirited" holds two built cocktails at $13 on Clean Co non-alcoholic spirits — the Desert Rose (Clean Co tequila alternative, desert pear, sweet and sour, wild hibiscus salt) and Lavender & Bubbles (Clean Co gin alternative, lavender, lemon, honey, chamomile tea and Fre alcohol-free sparkling brut). "No Alcohol, No Problem" holds five simpler mixed drinks at $6 to $6.50 with refills at $2.50: Cucumber & Honey, Blood Orange & Sage, the Faux-Jito, the Peach Palmer and the Black Cherry Palmer. Business casual attire is recommended, and valet parking runs from 4pm.
venues.address: 100 W. Station Square Dr., Pittsburgh, PA 15219
signatureDrinks: Lavender & Bubbles ($13, Clean Co gin alternative)

venues.longDescription:
Grand Concourse occupies the former Pittsburgh & Lake Erie Railroad Station at Station Square, a Beaux-Arts terminal that was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1974 and became a restaurant in 1978. It is one of the genuinely grand rooms in the city — a stained-glass vaulted ceiling, marble columns, and windows onto the Monongahela — and it now belongs to the Landry's group, which is worth knowing because it means chain-scale consistency rather than a chef's personality. The cooking is classic seafood house: raw oysters at $21 the half dozen, a crab cake at $25, roast lobster tail at $52, prime rib from $40, filet mignon from $44, and a chilled seafood tower at $89 or $169 depending on how many of you there are. Business casual is recommended, valet parking starts at 4pm, and happy hour runs weekdays from 3.30 to 6.30 in the bar, lounge and patio only.

The non-alcoholic drinks are split across two headings, and understanding the split is the whole trick to ordering well here. "Free Spirited" — subtitled, in the restaurant's own words, for adults that prefer little to no alcohol — carries two properly built cocktails at $13 on Clean Co non-alcoholic spirits: the Desert Rose, a tequila-alternative drink with desert pear, sweet and sour and a wild hibiscus salt rim, and Lavender & Bubbles, a gin-alternative build with lavender, lemon, honey, chamomile tea and Fre alcohol-free sparkling brut. Those are the ones to order if you want a drink that behaves like a cocktail. "No Alcohol, No Problem" is the other section, and it is priced completely differently — five mixed drinks at $6 to $6.50, with refills at $2.50, which is the single most useful line on the menu for a non-drinker sitting through a long dinner in a room where everyone else is on a second bottle. Those are Cucumber & Honey, Blood Orange & Sage, the Faux-Jito, the Peach Palmer and the Black Cherry Palmer. One warning: an older cocktail page is still live on the restaurant's own website showing these drinks with $0 prices and outdated ingredients. Trust the priced menu.

venues.name: Grassroots Kava House
venues.description: Grassroots Kava House is a fully alcohol-free kava bar in St. Petersburg's Edge District, founded in 2017 by a former bank executive who found kava helped with stress. It pours premium Vanuatu kava and kratom tea alongside locally roasted coffee, nitro cold brew, botanical teas, house sodas, and kombucha, in a dog-friendly gathering spot stocked with board games and Wi-Fi. (It serves kratom in addition to kava.)  Open from 7am on weekdays and 8am at weekends, running to midnight nightly, with a real coffee programme alongside the kava so a group with mixed intentions can share a table rather than everyone opting into the same unfamiliar drink.
venues.longDescription:
Grassroots Kava House opened in St. Petersburg's Edge District in 2017, founded by a former bank executive who came to kava as a way of managing stress and built a business out of it. That origin shows in how the room is set up: it is a working third place rather than a themed one — dog-friendly, stocked with board games, Wi-Fi throughout, open from 7am on weekdays and 8am at weekends, running to midnight every night.

The drinks list spans further than kava alone. Premium Vanuatu kava and kratom tea sit alongside locally roasted coffee, nitro cold brew, botanical teas, house-made sodas and kombucha, which means the room works for someone who wants nothing psychoactive at all as readily as for someone who does. That breadth matters more than it might appear: a venue that serves only kava is asking every visitor to opt into an unfamiliar substance, whereas one with a real coffee programme lets a group with mixed intentions sit at the same table.

The Edge District position puts it within walking distance of downtown St. Petersburg without being in the middle of the bar strip, which suits the format — people come here to stay for two hours, not to pass through between rounds.

The caveat is explicit in the venue's own description and belongs here too: Grassroots serves kratom alongside kava. Kava is psychoactive and mildly sedating with documented case reports of liver injury; kratom acts on opioid receptors and carries real dependence and withdrawal risk. Everything poured is free of alcohol, and none of it is inert. For a designated driver this is an easy recommendation; for someone in recovery it is a decision to make with the full picture.  The Edge District position puts it inside walking distance of downtown without sitting in the middle of the bar strip.
venues.pressQuote: Second Place: Grassroots Kava House
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Creative Loafing Tampa Bay, Best of the Bay 2020 readers' pick, Best Kava Bar
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Creative Loafing Tampa Bay, Best of the Bay 2020

venues.name: Gravity Bound Brewing Co.
venues.description: Gravity Bound Brewing is a downtown Albuquerque brewery on Central Avenue that keeps hop water on — carbonated water infused with hops, no alcohol, no sugar and no calories. Hop water is the most underrated answer in this whole category: it delivers the bitterness and the pine-and-citrus aroma that make an IPA worth drinking, without the alcohol or the sweetness that makes most non-alcoholic options tiring across an evening. In a brewery taproom, where the alternative is usually a soda gun, having it on tap changes what a non-drinker can do with a whole evening out.
signatureDrinks: Hop water — carbonated water infused with hops, non-alcoholic

naMenuItems.name: Love Is Metaphysical
naMenuItems.description: palo santo wood and locally grown mint

venues.longDescription:
Gravity Bound Brewing sits on Central Avenue in downtown Albuquerque, and it is in this guide for one item on the board: hop water.

Hop water deserves a proper explanation, because it is the most quietly useful thing in alcohol-free drinking and most people have never been offered one. It is carbonated water run through hops — the same hops that give an IPA its aroma and bitterness — with no alcohol, no sugar, no malt and effectively no calories. What that produces is a drink that smells like beer and tastes bitter and resinous, with none of the sweetness that makes most non-alcoholic beers heavy going after two.

That last point is the one that matters over an evening. Sweetness is what defeats the average mocktail: the first is refreshing, the third is exhausting. Bitterness is the opposite — it resets the palate and invites another. Hop water is the only widely available alcohol-free drink built entirely around bitterness, which is why it works in a brewery, over three or four hours, in a way that a fruit-based mocktail does not.

This directory has now recorded breweries making their own hop water in Bend and pouring it in Albuquerque, and it is a strong signal in both places: it means the brewery has thought about the person at the table who is not drinking rather than assuming they will have a soda.

Graded three honestly. One documented alcohol-free option, no non-alcoholic beer line of the brewery's own confirmed, no printed zero-proof section.

The hours are good: 4pm to 9pm Monday, 3pm to 10pm Tuesday through Thursday, 2pm to 11pm Friday, noon to 11pm Saturday and noon to 9pm Sunday. Seven days, no closed day, and a downtown location within reach of the Old Town cluster.
venues.pressQuote: We debuted a hop water [carbonated water steeped with hops] during Dry January this year
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Chris Frigon, co-owner, quoted in New Mexico Magazine
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: New Mexico Magazine, Albuquerque's nonalcoholic bars, June 2024

venues.name: The Great Dane Pub & Brewing Co. — Downtown
venues.description: The Great Dane's downtown brewpub occupies the 1850s Fess Hotel building on East Doty Street, a block off the Capitol Square, and is the original of a five-pub Wisconsin group that has been brewing in Madison since 1994. It is in this guide because the bar keeps Ritual Zero Proof behind it and builds real drinks with it rather than pouring soda — the dark cherry margarita and the nada-paloma both use Ritual's non-alcoholic tequila alternative, and a very cherry mockarita runs on its agave spirit. For a brewpub in a beer state to stock a non-alcoholic tequila is a more deliberate choice than it first appears.
signatureDrinks: Dark cherry margarita (Ritual Zero Proof non-alcoholic tequila alternative)
Nada-paloma (Ritual Zero Proof non-alcoholic tequila alternative)
Very cherry mockarita (Ritual Zero Proof agave spirit alternative)
venues.longDescription:
The Great Dane opened in 1994 in the old Fess Hotel on East Doty Street, a nineteenth-century building a block off the Capitol Square, and grew into a five-pub group that is close to a Wisconsin institution. The downtown original is a brewpub in the full sense — beer brewed on site, a long menu, a beer garden, pool tables downstairs — and it is exactly the kind of place a non-drinker in this state ends up in whether they chose it or not, because it is where everyone goes after work.

So it matters more than it might elsewhere that the bar stocks Ritual Zero Proof and uses it properly. Ritual makes distilled non-alcoholic alternatives to specific spirits rather than generic botanical waters, and the Great Dane builds three drinks on its tequila and agave expressions: a dark cherry margarita, a nada-paloma and a very cherry mockarita, all recorded by BRAVA Magazine's survey of Madison mocktails. The significance is that these are shaken, soured, salted drinks with a spirit base doing the structural work — not fruit juice with a lime wedge. A brewpub whose own product is beer has no commercial reason to buy in a non-alcoholic tequila; doing it anyway is a choice about hospitality.

The practical case is the hours and the room. It opens at 11am on weekdays and 10am at weekends and runs to 11pm most nights and 1am on Friday and Saturday, so it covers lunch, dinner and late. It is large enough to absorb a group without a reservation, which the smaller Capitol Square cocktail bars in this guide are not. And it is thirty seconds from Lucille on King Street and two minutes from Merchant and Settle Down Tavern on Pinckney — the whole downtown cluster is walkable. Be clear that this is a working brewery pub and beer is the point of it; the alcohol-free drinks are good, but the room is not a quiet one.
venues.pressQuote: Great Dane Pub & Brewing serves a dark cherry margarita and a nada-paloma using Ritual Zero Proof NA tequila.

venues.name: Great Lakes Distillery & Tasting Room
venues.description: Wisconsin's original craft distillery doubles as a genuinely sober-friendly stop in Walker's Point. Founder Guy Rehorst distills SANS Junipre, a house-made non-alcoholic botanical spirit (juniper, ginseng, cardamom, chili, coriander; under 0.5% ABV) that anchors a standing low- and no-alcohol cocktail list. Zero-proof pours like the A Dry Splash sit alongside Lakefront non-alcoholic beers, so non-drinkers and designated drivers get a real menu rather than a lone soda. The adjoining Fox Den walk-up window slings smash burgers to round out the visit.
signatureDrinks: A Dry Splash (SANS Junipre N/A spirit, cranberry juice, TopNote Classic tonic)

naMenuItems.name: Sans Junipre
naMenuItems.description: non-alcoholic botanical spirit less than 0.5% abv | 0 calories | 0 sugar | junipre is made with a select blend of natural botanical extracts using various distillation techniques. made with natural flavors including juniper, basil, ginseng, orange zest, chili pepper, cardamom, coriander and more.

venues.longDescription:
Great Lakes Distillery is Wisconsin's first distillery since Prohibition, opened by founder Guy Rehorst in 2004 and now the anchor of the Walker's Point tasting room at 616 W Virginia St. The room pours the distillery's own craft spirits and cocktails, but it earns its place in a sober directory because Rehorst also makes his own non-alcoholic spirit in-house: SANS Junipre, a botanical zero-proof spirit built on juniper, ginseng, orange zest, cardamom, chili pepper and coriander at under 0.5% ABV, with zero calories and zero sugar. It was designed as a one-to-one replacement for gin and other spirits, which lets the bar mix genuine cocktails rather than sugary stand-ins.

The tasting room keeps a standing "low- and no-alcohol cocktails" section on its current menu. The fully non-alcoholic A Dry Splash pairs SANS Junipre with cranberry juice and TopNote Classic tonic, while the low-ABV Crantini rounds it out with Good Land cranberry liqueur; assorted Lakefront non-alcoholic beers are also on hand for beer drinkers who are skipping the alcohol. Milwaukee Magazine featured the program in its Milwaukee mocktail roundup, noting the herbaceous house spirit can take the one-to-one place of any spirit in a cocktail. Because the venue still serves full-strength alcohol, it is a hybrid rather than a fully dry bar, but the non-alcoholic offering is substantial and, crucially, non-intoxicating.

Practically, the tasting room runs Monday through Thursday from noon to 9pm, Friday until midnight, Saturday 11am to midnight, and Sunday 11am to 7pm, and it remains active in 2026 per its posted hours, recent Yelp activity, and current first-hand visit write-ups. The Fox Den window inside the room serves beef, chicken and vegan smash burgers plus shareable "foxy bites," and the distillery layers in tours and evening social programming, making it an easy group destination whether or not everyone is drinking.
venues.pressQuote: While the herbaceous profile works well as a non-alcoholic substitute for gin, it can take the one-to-one place for any spirit used in a cocktail.

venues.name: Greenhouse
venues.description: Greenhouse is a fully non-alcoholic hi-fi "listening bar" that operates inside Tampa Heights' Elevation Coffee Roasters — billed as Tampa's first booze-free music spot. Launched in July 2025, it runs as a sober "third space" on curated vinyl nights (typically Friday evenings), serving craft zero-proof cocktails built on Ritual, Seedlip, and Curious Elixirs alongside non-alcoholic beer and wine, while a high-fidelity analog system plays new and old funk and soul. The room is designed so the main activity is listening, not drinking.  Sessions are event-based rather than continuous, so check the schedule before travelling; the same address trades as a coffee roaster by day.
venues.longDescription:
Greenhouse runs inside Elevation Coffee Roasters on North Franklin Street in Tampa Heights, and is billed as the city's first booze-free music venue. It launched in July 2025 as a hi-fi listening bar — a format borrowed from 1950s Japanese jazz kissa, where the sound system is the reason people come and conversation is kept low enough not to compete with it. Co-founder Nolan Hammer has described the idea as growing from a shared love of music through high-fidelity audio and the nostalgia of those Japanese rooms.

The format solves something specific. Most alcohol-free venues have to answer the question of what people are supposed to do instead of drinking, and most answer it weakly — board games, a quiz, nothing. A listening bar answers it structurally: the activity is the record, played through an analogue system on curated vinyl nights, generally Friday evenings, running new and old funk and soul. Nobody needs a drink in hand to justify being there, which is the whole difficulty of sober socialising resolved by the room's design rather than by willpower.

The drinks are built rather than poured. Craft zero-proof cocktails run on Ritual Zero Proof, Seedlip and Curious Elixirs, with non-alcoholic beer and wine alongside, and the plan has been a set of staple mocktails each week supplemented by specials and seasonal builds. By day the same address is a working coffee roaster, so the space earns its rent across the whole week rather than on Friday nights alone.

Practical notes: check the schedule before travelling, because the listening-bar sessions are event-based rather than continuous, and the daytime operation is a coffee shop rather than a bar. Everything served in the Greenhouse programme is alcohol-free — this is one of the few venues in the region where that is true of the entire offering rather than a section of it.
venues.pressQuote: The intimate, underground feel with fully-immersive sound dominates the ambiance, creating a space where the main activity is listening to what's being played rather than the sole hum of chatter.

venues.name: Grey Ghost Detroit
venues.description: Grey Ghost's printed drink menu carries a dedicated Mocktails section with six named non-alcoholic cocktails, from the Faygo-riffing House Rock & Rye (house-made cherry, vanilla, and cinnamon syrups over soda) to the tropical I Insist (coconut milk tea, cold brew coffee, pineapple, hot honey). The Brush Park steakhouse also pours Athletic Brewing's Free Wave for guests wanting a non-alcoholic beer. Detroit Free Press singled out the House Rock & Rye as delivering the city's nostalgic soda flavor "without the questionable ingredients."
signatureDrinks: Back on Earth (earl grey, grapefruit, honey, pineapple, demerara, lemon, lavender cream)
House Rock & Rye (house-made cherry, vanilla, cinnamon syrups, soda)
Spa Water (cucumber, mint, honeydew, lime, soda)
I Insist (royal coconut milk tea, cold brew coffee, pineapple, hot honey)
Cola de Jamaica (orange, Coca-Cola, hibiscus honey, lime)
venues.longDescription:
Grey Ghost opened in July 2016 on Watson Street in Brush Park, in the former Ye Olde Butcher Shoppe building near Woodward Avenue. Chefs John Vermiglio and Josef "Joe" Giacomino met working under chef Matthias Merges at Charlie Trotter's in Chicago before returning to Detroit to build a meat-driven restaurant and bar named for a Prohibition-era Detroit rum runner. The restaurant, part of Vermiglio's Four Man Ladder Hospitality group (which also runs Second Best across the street), marked its 10th anniversary in July 2026 with a throwback menu and an anniversary dinner held July 28.

The drink list has a standalone Mocktails section of six house-made non-alcoholic cocktails: Rule No. 1 (orange, blueberry, Calpico, lime), Back on Earth (earl grey, grapefruit, honey, pineapple, demerara, lemon, lavender cream), House Rock & Rye (house-made cherry, vanilla, cinnamon syrups, soda), Spa Water (cucumber, mint, honeydew, lime, soda), I Insist (royal coconut milk tea, cold brew coffee, pineapple, hot honey), and Cola de Jamaica (orange, Coca-Cola, hibiscus honey, lime). Guests who want a non-alcoholic beer instead can order Athletic Brewing's Free Wave (0.4% ABV, brewed in Connecticut), which is also listed on the printed menu.

Detroit Free Press picked out the House Rock & Rye in a 2024 metro-Detroit mocktail roundup, describing it as delivering the sweet-and-spicy flavor and crisp texture of Detroit's own Faygo Rock & Rye "without the questionable ingredients" — evidence the bar treats its non-alcoholic list as a real extension of its cocktail program rather than an afterthought.

Grey Ghost sits between Brush Park and Midtown, a short walk from Comerica Park and the Fox Theatre. It's open nightly: Sunday–Thursday 4pm–11pm, Friday–Saturday 4pm–midnight.
venues.pressQuote: The blend of house-made cherry, vanilla and cinnamon syrups suspended in soda water offers the sweet and spicy flavor and crisp texture of Detroit's famous Faygo Rock & Rye without the questionable ingredients.

venues.name: Grey Tiger
venues.description: Grey Tiger is a cocktail bar and bottle shop on Bloor Street West in Toronto's Bloordale neighbourhood, described by blogTO's Amy Carlberg as "an artist-run cocktail bar for new romantics." Its printed menu carries a dedicated "Path of Temperance" section of four full-price, zero-proof cocktails made with the same technique — vermouths, shrubs, bitters and acids — as the rest of the list. The attached bottle shop stocks a dedicated non-alcoholic collection, including bottles from Gruvi.

venues.longDescription:
Grey Tiger is a cocktail bar and bottle shop at 1190 Bloor St W in Toronto's Bloordale neighbourhood, described by blogTO's Amy Carlberg as "an artist-run cocktail bar for new romantics." Alongside the bar, Grey Tiger runs the School of Hard Drinks, offering beginner and intermediate cocktail classes for individuals and groups, and takes part in neighbourhood events such as the Big on Bloor Street Festival.

The bar's printed menu carries a dedicated "Path of Temperance" section of four full-price ($15), zero-proof cocktails, built with the same technique-forward approach as the rest of the list rather than as an afterthought: the Crown Spritz (white vermouth, red bitter, soda, grapefruit acid), The Finest Timeline (black rice aperitif, chili lime cucumber shrub, ginger beer, mint bitters), Sky Reset (concord grape vermouth, rosemary, lime acid, bitter soda) and Love in the Shadows (juniper sumac tonic, blueberry bitter, tartaric acid, kalamata olive brine).

Grey Tiger also operates an online and in-store bottle shop, which carries a dedicated non-alcoholic collection alongside its cocktail spirits, liqueurs, natural wine, craft beer and cider — including bottles from Gruvi.

venues.name: Ground Level Lounge
venues.description: Ground Level Lounge, trading in full as Ground Level Lounge & Hawaii's Luxury Hookah, is a hookah lounge and kava bar on Makaloa Street in Ala Moana, a few minutes from Waikīkī. It serves no alcohol, and its hours are the reason it matters: 9am to 1am Sunday through Thursday and 9am to 2am on Friday and Saturday, which makes it one of the only rooms in Honolulu where somebody who does not drink can still be out at closing time. What it is should be stated plainly rather than discovered on arrival — hookah and tobacco are the main draw, and the kava it pours is psychoactive. This is a night out without alcohol, not a guaranteed sober space.
venues.longDescription:
Ground Level Lounge sits at 1538 Makaloa Street in the Ala Moana district, minutes from both Ala Moana Center and the western edge of Waikīkī, and trades in full as Ground Level Lounge & Hawaii's Luxury Hookah. The format is a hookah lounge that also operates as a kava bar, and no alcohol is served on the premises. Its practical value in a guide like this comes down to opening hours. Honolulu's fully alcohol-free venues are overwhelmingly daytime businesses — cafés, juice bars and kava rooms that close by seven or eight in the evening — which leaves a real gap for anyone who wants to be out late without drinking. Ground Level runs 9am to 1am Sunday through Thursday and 9am to 2am on Friday and Saturday, matching the closing time of the bars around it.

The caveats need stating up front rather than left for a visitor to work out, because this site's readers include people in recovery and the two things on offer here are not neutral. Hookah is the primary business, which means tobacco smoke in an enclosed room for the whole visit — a material consideration for anyone with respiratory issues, and for many people simply not what they are looking for in an evening out. The kava, meanwhile, is psychoactive and mildly sedating, in the same category as the 'awa poured at 'Awa Hou and Fiji Kava. Neither is alcohol, and for a great many people who have stopped drinking that is exactly the point — but describing the venue as a sober bar would overstate it. The honest description is the one this guide applies to the kava lounges of Davie, Florida: a genuine alcohol-free room, open late, on terms you should understand before you go. Taken on those terms it fills a slot in Honolulu that almost nothing else does.

venues.name: Group Therapy Pub & Playground
venues.description: Group Therapy Pub & Playground sits on Falls Street in Greenville's West End, near Falls Park, and it is an activity bar as much as a drinking one — games and a playground alongside the pub. Its alcohol-free entry is the Not Your Grandpa's Old Fashioned, built on Spiritless bourbon, which puts it among the small number of Greenville rooms stocking an actual non-alcoholic spirit rather than improvising with juice. Open 11am to 10pm through the week and to 1am on Friday and Saturday, seven days with no closed day, which makes it the most reliably available room in this guide after the kava bar.
venues.address: 320 Falls St Ste G, Greenville, SC 29601
signatureDrinks: Not Your Grandpa's Old Fashioned — Spiritless bourbon
venues.longDescription:
An old fashioned is the drink non-drinkers miss most, and it is the one that is hardest to fake. It is essentially neat spirit with sugar and bitters — there is nowhere to hide, no juice or soda to carry the flavour, nothing to do but taste like whiskey. Group Therapy's answer is to use a real product: Spiritless bourbon, a distilled non-alcoholic whiskey alternative, in a build it calls Not Your Grandpa's Old Fashioned.

That is a meaningful investment for a neighbourhood pub. A bottle of Spiritless sits on the back bar earning its keep only from customers who are not drinking, which is exactly why so few bars buy one. Stocking it is the clearest signal in this category that a room has thought about the problem rather than improvised around it.

The venue itself is on Falls Street in the West End, near Falls Park on the Reedy, and it is built as a pub with a playground and games rather than a straight drinking room. That format does the same work here as the board-game cafés and bowling alleys elsewhere in this directory: it gives an evening a structure that is not the round, which is the single most useful thing for someone who is not drinking, and it makes the venue workable for families as well as for groups.

The hours are the other argument. Eleven in the morning to ten at night Sunday through Thursday, and to 1am on Friday and Saturday — seven days a week with no closed day, in a city where most of the good cocktail rooms are dark on Sunday and Monday.

GVLtoday, Greenville's daily newsletter, named the drink in its round-up of thirty-plus craft mocktails across the city, which is the sourcing behind this entry.
venues.pressQuote: Group Therapy Pub & Playground offers the Not Your Grandpa's Old Fashioned, made with Spiritless bourbon.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: GVLtoday, Sip on 30+ craft mocktails in Greenville

venues.name: Gufo
venues.description: Gufo is a modern Italian restaurant, bar and cafe at 660 Cambridge Street in East Cambridge, opened on July 28, 2023 as Coda Restaurant Group's first venue outside Boston, joining its siblings The Salty Pig, SRV and Baleia. The name is Italian for owl. It runs weekday lunch, weekend brunch and dinner around handmade pasta, pizza and antipasti, with an all-season patio and a bocce court attached. The drinks list prints a standing section headed Zero or Low Proof, holding four house-built non-alcoholic cocktails between $9 and $11 plus a Lucano non-alcoholic amaro served neat or as a spritz, and a further Low Proof Beer + Wine block covering non-alcoholic hazy IPA, lager and three German non-alcoholic wines.

venues.longDescription:
Gufo opened on July 28, 2023 at 660 Cambridge Street in East Cambridge, the fourth concept from Coda Restaurant Group and its first outside Boston proper. The group began with CODA in 2008, added The Salty Pig in 2012 and SRV in 2016, and followed Gufo with Baleia in the South End in 2024, so the Italian technique and the drinks-list conventions are shared across the family. Gufo — Italian for owl — is pitched as a restaurant, bar, cafe and community meeting place rather than a dinner-only room, and trades accordingly: weekday lunch from 11am, weekend brunch, and dinner service from 5pm. The food is handmade pasta, pizza and what the kitchen calls comforting-yet-inventive antipasti, and the site includes an all-season patio and a bocce court. Boston Magazine, in its guide to Boston's best mocktails, recommended pairing dinner entrees like the squid ink bucatini and swordfish Milanese with the Garden Party and the Non-Baldi, and noted the drinks fit the relaxed feel of the patio.

The non-alcoholic offering is printed as a named section, Zero or Low Proof, and is priced well below the cocktail list, which makes it genuinely usable across a whole meal. Non-Baldi is $9, a red-bitter aperitivo build using Stappi Red Bitter with orange. Garden Party is $9 and the most-photographed of them, a mix of green tea, basil, lemon and pineapple. Snap Back, also $9, is the savoury one, made from snap pea, salted lime and soda. Trade Route at $11 uses Lucano non-alcoholic amaro with grapefruit, sumac and agave and is flagged at under 0.5% ABV. The amaro is also sold on its own at $8, with the option to lengthen it into a spritz with orange. A second block headed Low Proof Beer + Wine carries the non-alcoholic hazy IPA from Notch, which brews it a few miles away in Brighton and Salem, at $9, Al's non-alcoholic lager at $9, Delirium's Delirio at $15, and three German non-alcoholic wines: Wolffer "Spring in a Bottle" at $14, Wander & Found "Cuvee Blanc" at $13 and Odd Bird "GSM" at $14.
venues.pressQuote: Pair fun dinner entrées like the squid ink bucatini and swordfish Milanese with equally lively mocktails: the Garden Party, a refreshing mix of green tea, basil, lemon, and pineapple, or the Non-Baldi, a classic red bitter with orange.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Boston Magazine, "Here's Where to Drink Creative Mocktails around Boston", updated January 2026

venues.name: Gunther & Co.
venues.description: Gunther & Co. is a modern American restaurant in the historic Gunther Boiler Building at 3650 Toone Street in Brewers Hill, open since May 2016 under executive chef and co-owner Jerry Trice — a Culinary Institute of America graduate who pioneered ChefDriven, the first restaurant-style food truck in Washington DC, named the city's best by both Washingtonian and The Washington Post in 2012. Almost everything is made in house, including the ice cream, burger buns and brunch biscuits. Its printed "Zero Proof Cocktails" section runs three house-built drinks: the Amalfi Spritz ($12, house-made zero-proof Amalfi aperitif, Lyre's NA sparkling wine, soda, orange), Spa Water ($9, house cantaloupe-pandan shrub, coconut water, lemon, soda) and Rose of Althea ($6, house hibiscus shrub, lime, soda). Five non-alcoholic beers follow — Go Brewing, Ceria, Athletic, New Trail and Estrella Galicia 0.0 — plus Fever-Tree and Q Drinks sodas at $5. Parking is free and the list rotates seasonally.

venues.longDescription:
Gunther & Co. has occupied the historic Gunther Boiler Building at 3650 Toone Street in Brewers Hill since May 2016 — a decade of modern American cooking with global influences in a room built inside a former brewery's plant. Executive chef and co-owner Jerry Trice is a Culinary Institute of America graduate whose route here was unusual: he pioneered ChefDriven, the first restaurant-style food truck in Washington DC, which both Washingtonian and The Washington Post named the city's top food truck in 2012, and before that led kitchens at Yin Yankee in Annapolis and Bethesda and Sam's on the Waterfront. His standard is stated plainly — pretty much everything is made in house, including the ice cream, the burger buns and the brunch biscuits. The menu runs a butter-poached Maine lobster roll at $48, wood-oven roasted oysters with Thai chilli butter at $15, a dry-aged burger at $18 and hanger steak frites at $39. Parking is free, which in this part of Baltimore is worth noting.

The zero-proof section is short, cheap and made from scratch, which is a better combination than long and bought-in. The Amalfi Spritz ($12) is built on a house-made zero-proof Amalfi aperitif with Lyre's non-alcoholic sparkling wine, soda and orange. Spa Water ($9) uses a house cantaloupe-pandan shrub with coconut water, lemon and soda. Rose of Althea, at just $6, is a house hibiscus shrub with lime and soda — the cheapest properly built drink on any menu in this guide, and the shrub base means it has real acidity rather than sweetness. Behind them sits an unusually good non-alcoholic beer list of five: Go Brewing's New School Sour, Ceria's Grainwave Belgian wit, Athletic's Upside Dawn, New Trail's Broken Heels hazy IPA and Estrella Galicia 0.0, plus Fever-Tree and Q Drinks sodas at $5. The Baltimore Banner's line about the programme is the one worth quoting: style and substance combine in zero-proof creations that would make Chappell Roan drool. Note the list rotates seasonally.
venues.pressQuote: At Gunther & Co. in Brewers Hill, style and substance combine in zero-proof creations that would make Chappell Roan drool.

venues.name: Hai Hai
venues.description: Hai Hai is chef and co-owner Christina Nguyen's Southeast Asian street-food restaurant in Northeast Minneapolis, opened in 2017 with business partner Birk Grudem in the former 22nd Avenue Station dive bar (the name nods to "twenty-two" in Vietnamese). In 2024 Nguyen won the James Beard Award for Best Chef: Midwest, becoming the first Vietnamese woman to take a Beard cooking medal; the restaurant was earlier named among the best new restaurants in the country by Eater, Thrillist, and Esquire. Alongside its tropical craft cocktails, Hai Hai keeps a small, named spirit-free trio whose names are Vietnamese numerals — Mot, Hai, and Ba (one, two, three). The drinks lean on house-made cordials and shrubs built from the kitchen's bright pantry of lychee, jackfruit, guava, grapefruit, rhubarb, strawberry, and ginger. Reservations via Resy; walk-ins welcome.
venues.longDescription:
Hai Hai is chef and co-owner Christina Nguyen's Southeast Asian street-food restaurant in Northeast Minneapolis, opened in 2017 with business partner Birk Grudem in the former 22nd Avenue Station dive bar — the name nods to "twenty-two" in Vietnamese. In 2024 Nguyen won the James Beard Award for Best Chef: Midwest, becoming the first Vietnamese woman to take a Beard cooking medal, and the restaurant had already been named among the best new restaurants in the country by Eater, Thrillist and Esquire.

The bar is known for tropical craft cocktails, and the spirit-free offering follows the same pantry rather than departing from it. The zero-proof trio is named for Vietnamese numerals — Mot, Hai and Ba, meaning one, two and three — and the drinks are built on house-made cordials and shrubs drawn from the kitchen's own ingredients: lychee, jackfruit, guava, grapefruit, rhubarb, strawberry and ginger. That last point is the thing worth understanding about why these work. A shrub is a vinegar-based syrup, and vinegar is one of the few ways to get genuine sharpness and length into a drink without alcohol; a kitchen already making cordials and shrubs for its cocktails can produce non-alcoholic drinks with real structure at almost no extra cost. It is why restaurant bars with strong pantries tend to beat dedicated cocktail bars at zero-proof.

Three named builds is a focused list rather than an exhaustive one, and it is honest to say so — this is not a venue with a dozen spirit-free options. But they are made rather than opened, they change with the fruit, and they are designed to stand up to food that runs hot, sour and herbaceous. Reservations go through Resy, walk-ins are welcome, and the restaurant serves Tuesday through Sunday, closed Mondays.
venues.pressQuote: Nguyen's menu reads like a street-smitten ode to Southeast Asia, a pop song that can brighten up even the murkiest of days
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Esquire, Best New Restaurants in America, November 2018

venues.name: HaiSous Vietnamese Kitchen
venues.description: HaiSous is the Vietnamese restaurant chef Thai Dang and co-owner Danielle Dang opened in Pilsen, a room built around charcoal-grilled skewers, caramelized fish-sauce wings and family-style tasting menus. Its beverage list keeps a named Alcohol-Free Spritz at $10 in four rotating flavors - blood orange and citrus, prickly pear and mint, blueberry Thai basil, and mango lime - alongside a non-alcoholic section stocking Fever Tree ginger beer and the usual soft pours. It is a modest program rather than a full zero-proof cocktail list, but it is named, priced and permanent rather than improvised. Be aware that the same non-alcoholic section carries two Marz Community Brewing products that contain cannabinoids: a 10mg THC Kush Party and a cherry basil CBD.

naMenuItems.name: Alcohol-Free Spritz
naMenuItems.description: choose your flavor! blood orange & citrus prickly pear & mint blueberry thai basil mango lime

venues.longDescription:
Thai Dang and Danielle Dang came out of Embeya to open HaiSous on Carpenter Street in Pilsen, with a stated intention of preserving heritage through food rather than fusing it - a distinction Time Out picked up on when it reviewed the restaurant, calling the result stunning and noting how rarely authentic Vietnamese cooking of this kind appeared south of Montrose Avenue. The menu is organized into salads listed as for fun, drinking food, house specialties, vegetarian dishes and pickled things, with crispy wings in caramelized fish sauce and an octopus salad with eggplant confit among the signatures, and family-style tasting menus for tables that want to be guided.

The drinks program is smaller than the food, but the non-alcoholic part of it is named and fixed rather than left to the server's discretion. An Alcohol-Free Spritz is listed at $10 with four flavors to choose from - blood orange and citrus, prickly pear and mint, blueberry Thai basil, and mango lime - which gives a non-drinker a real choice at the point of ordering instead of a single default. The rest of the non-alcoholic block covers Fever Tree ginger beer at $5, Coke, Diet Coke, Sprite and ginger ale at $4, and sparkling water. Two items in that same block come from Marz Community Brewing in Bridgeport and contain cannabinoids: a Kush Party at 10mg THC for $14 and a cherry basil CBD at $10. They are clearly labeled on the restaurant's own menu, but they sit under the same heading as the alcohol-free spritzes, so anyone in recovery or otherwise avoiding psychoactive drinks should read the line rather than the heading. Strength here is a genuine three - a real, named, permanent offering, not a destination zero-proof bar. Time Out also noted that guests can order one of the tasting menus served family-style, which is the setting where a named, priced alcohol-free option matters most, because the whole table commits to a format together and a non-drinker who has to improvise ends up outside it. The restaurant runs Wednesday through Sunday, with a Sunday daytime service from 10am.
venues.pressQuote: Embeya vets Thai and Danielle Dang bring authentic Vietnamese flavors to Pilsen—and the results are stunning.

venues.name: Hale Pele
venues.description: Hale Pele is a renowned Northeast Portland tiki bar with a robust spirit-free section built on fresh-squeezed juices, house syrups, and NA spirits like Wilderton. Non-alcoholic options include tiki-style drinks such as the Jumanji and the Saturn Return, plus alcohol-free versions of its tiki classics.

naMenuItems.description: a tantalizing tribute to raffles' hotel and ngiam tong boon, the reputed developer of the singapore sling. fresh citrus, pineapple juice and pomegranate blend beautifully with herbacious non-alcoholic gin and amaro to create a refreshing experience with just the right amount of bite.
