venues.longDescription:
Harley & Rose sits on the Barkly Street strip in West Footscray, about twenty minutes west of the Melbourne CBD, and it is the sort of place a neighbourhood keeps to itself: a wood-fired oven turning out puffy pizzas with pipis, parsley, lemon and cream, nduja-stuffed fried olives, a wood-fired lasagne, a front courtyard, and enough children on a Friday night that nobody minds yours. Time Out named it Best Casual Restaurant in 2018. The wine programme, run by former Cumulus beverage manager Mark Williamson, is the reason the drinks list is better than the format suggests.

That care extends to the drinks with nothing in them, which is rarer in a suburban pizzeria than in a CBD cocktail bar. The list prints MOCKTAILS as a heading with three house builds beneath it, all made in-house rather than poured from a bottle. The Lemon Leaf Sour uses a house-made lemon leaf cordial with lemongrass. The Pine-Lime Splice sets apricot and pineapple against lime and falernum, which keeps it from collapsing into sweetness. And the non-alcoholic mulled wine, on a house-made spiced syrup, is a genuine winter drink - the kind of thing most venues only make with wine in it.

A separate ZERO PROOF block covers the bottles, and it is a properly considered four rather than a token one: Heaps Normal lager in 333ml cans from Canberra, Heaps Normal 'High Hopes' prosecco, a zero-alcohol Squealing Pig sauvignon blanc from Marlborough, and Altina 'Pepperberry' shiraz, one of the better Australian de-alcoholised reds and made with native pepperberry. Because there is a bottle shop attached, anything you like can go home with you. Practically: it opens evenings only, Tuesday to Saturday, closes Sunday and Monday, and Friday is the loud night. Come earlier midweek if you want to actually taste the drinks.
venues.pressQuote: Footscray's diner churns out pipi pizzas and has an impressive front courtyard.

venues.name: Harold's Haunt
venues.description: Harold's Haunt is a queer-owned, witch-themed "they bar" on Grant Avenue in Millvale, opened in October 2022 by the people behind the attached Maude's Paperwing Gallery, and it is intentional about sober inclusion — its own site says there are always mocktails on the menu for its sober friends, served as house-made "Fauxtions" alongside the full bar. Food is vegan-friendly, supplied by Lemon Tree PGH, and orders are marked at the table with tarot cards; past dishes have included the Hobbit Pizza and Calcifer's Coals. There is a patio out back for when the front gets loud. Note that the bar does not publish a current drinks list online, so the Fauxtions rotate and are best asked about in person; the ones documented in press have been fruit-and-soda builds rather than non-alcoholic-spirit cocktails. The venue is candid that it is not fully accessible: there is a step at both the front and back doors, a steep slope in the back hallway, and small bathrooms without handles.
venues.hours: Mon closed; Tue 5pm-11pm; Wed-Thu 5pm-12am; Fri-Sat 5pm-1am; Sun 4pm-10pm
venues.longDescription:
Harold's Haunt opened on 13 October 2022 on Grant Avenue in Millvale, attached to Maude's Paperwing Gallery, and is run by what it calls Millvale's own queer witches. The theming is thorough and unironic — a themed bar with comfy community vibes, in its own words, with food orders marked at the table by tarot cards and dishes named the Hobbit Pizza and Calcifer's Coals. But the theme is not really the point. Co-owner Athena Flint has described what the room is actually for: truly, she said, the number of trans individuals she knows who have come dressed as they wished they could for the first time in public, here, is just amazing. Her other line is the one that explains the atmosphere — it is not party city; you come here and you are cosy and comfortable. Food is vegan-friendly and comes from Lemon Tree PGH, there is a patio out back for when the front room gets loud, and there is a resident bar dog.

For a non-drinker the offer is genuine but informal. The bar's own standing commitment is that there are always mocktails on the menu for its sober friends, served under the house name Fauxtions, and the specialty shots have alcohol-free versions too — which matters more than it sounds, because a shot is the most socially loaded drink in any bar and being able to take part in a round is the whole thing. What we cannot give you is a current list. Harold's does not publish its drinks online, and the Fauxtions documented in press over the years — a cranberry, rosemary and bubbles build with a gummy frog dropped in, a strawberry-soda and blood-orange one, a mint frother — read as playful fruit-and-soda drinks rather than non-alcoholic-spirit cocktails, and none can be confirmed as still being poured. Ask at the bar. Two practical notes worth having in advance: the bar is honest on its own site that it is not fully accessible, with a step at both doors, a steep slope in the back hallway and small bathrooms without handles; and there is no car park, though Millvale has plenty of street parking and the meters stop being checked after 6pm.
venues.pressQuote: Truly, the number of trans individuals that I know who have come dressed as they wished they could for the first time in public, here, is just amazing.

venues.name: Harrar Coffee & Roastery
venues.description: Harrar Coffee & Roastery is a fully alcohol-free, family-owned Ethiopian coffee house and roastery at 2904 Georgia Avenue NW, on the Park View stretch north of Howard University. It roasts daily rather than in batches held in storage, and sells only as much as it needs so that what reaches the cup is fresh. The range is almost entirely Ethiopian single-origin, named by region and roast: Ethiopia Harrar in medium and dark, Yirgacheffe in medium and dark, Sidama in medium and dark, Limu in medium and dark, plus named lots including Sidama Sibune, Yirgacheffe Yirhama and Harrar Haruva, and decaf Sidama and Limu. The room is set up for sitting - meeting a friend, reading, working. No alcohol is served.
signatureDrinks: Ethiopia Harrar, medium or dark roast
Ethiopia Yirgacheffe, medium or dark roast
Ethiopia Sidama, medium or dark roast
Ethiopia Limu, medium or dark roast
venues.longDescription:
Harrar sits on Georgia Avenue NW just north of Howard University, on the Park View stretch that runs up towards Petworth, and it is both a coffee house and a working roastery. It is family-owned, and its stated vision when it opened was narrow in a useful way: deliver outstanding coffee to the immediate community, and become a fixture for neighbourhood regulars and local businesses rather than a destination. Its own description of the room is worth repeating because it explains the format - a place to escape the daily stresses of life, to meet a friend for coffee and conversation, or to get comfortable with a book.

The roasting practice is the part that distinguishes it. Harrar roasts daily rather than producing large batches that then sit, and it deliberately roasts only as much as it needs, so what goes into the grinder is days old rather than months. It extends the same advice to customers buying beans: do not buy more than a month's worth, because the cup at home should taste like the cup in the shop. The range is almost entirely Ethiopian and it is organised by region and roast rather than by blend name, which makes it easy to drink your way across the country's growing areas. Ethiopia Harrar, which gives the business its name, comes in medium and dark and carries the full-bodied, mocha-ish character the eastern highlands are known for. Yirgacheffe, in medium and dark, is the floral and citrus-bright one. Sidama runs in medium, dark and a medium decaf, and Limu in medium and dark. On top of the regional roasts sit named single lots - Sidama Sibune, Yirgacheffe Yirhama, Harrar Haruva - and a three-ounce Ethiopian Collection for anyone who wants to compare several at once. A small number of non-Ethiopian coffees, including a Colombia Supremo, round out the shelf.

No alcohol is served. The practical constraint is the clock: the shop closes at 2pm on weekdays and 3pm at weekends, which makes this firmly a morning and lunchtime venue rather than an afternoon or evening one. Georgia Avenue-Petworth Metro is the closest station, a walk up the hill, and the Howard University campus is immediately south.
venues.pressQuote: Harrar Coffee & Roastery is a local, family-owned business offering a variety of high-quality coffee at competitive price.

venues.name: Hash Vegan Eatery
venues.description: Hash is San Antonio's only fully spirit-free cocktail bar — a completely alcohol-free room on South Flores serving a full zero-proof drinks list alongside an all-vegan kitchen. Nothing behind the bar contains alcohol, which puts it in a different category from every other venue in this guide: there is no negotiating, no scanning a short mocktail section, no being the only person at the table drinking something different. Optional CBD and Delta-8 upgrades are offered on the drinks, which is worth knowing in advance if you are avoiding all intoxicants rather than alcohol specifically. Hours are unusual — closed Wednesday and Thursday, and it shuts at 7pm.
venues.address: 5007 S Flores St, San Antonio, TX 78214
venues.hours: Mon 11am-7pm; Tue 11am-5pm; Wed-Thu closed; Fri 11am-7pm; Sat 11am-6:30pm; Sun 11am-7pm
venues.longDescription:
Hash sits on South Flores Street, south of downtown San Antonio, and it is the only venue in the city where the entire bar is alcohol-free. CultureMap calls it San Antonio's only 100 percent spirit-free cocktail bar, and that single fact makes it the anchor of this guide.

The distinction is bigger than it sounds. Every other venue here is a licensed bar or restaurant with a good zero-proof section — which is genuinely useful, but it still means walking into a room built around alcohol and ordering the exception. At Hash there is no exception, because there is no alcohol. For someone in early recovery, for whom a wall of bottles is not neutral scenery, that changes the calculation entirely. It also removes the small social friction that a non-drinker in a bar absorbs all evening without ever quite naming.

The kitchen is fully vegan, which pairs naturally: this is a room designed around what people want to put in their bodies, and the drinks follow the same logic rather than imitating cocktails for the sake of it.

One thing to understand before going. The drinks can be upgraded with CBD or Delta-8, the latter being a psychoactive hemp derivative. That is a choice, not a default, but it means the room is not a guaranteed intoxicant-free space in the way the alcohol-free framing might suggest. Anyone whose sobriety covers all substances should order accordingly and can simply decline the upgrade.

The hours are the main practical obstacle and they are genuinely odd for a bar: 11am to 7pm, closed Wednesday and Thursday. This is effectively a daytime and early-evening venue, so treat it as lunch, an afternoon or an early drink rather than a night out. It is south of the centre and not walkable from downtown, so plan transport — but for anyone who wants a room with no alcohol in it at all, it is the only address in San Antonio that qualifies. That scarcity is worth stating plainly: a city of 1.5 million people has exactly one fully alcohol-free bar, and it closes at seven and shuts two days a week. The demand is clearly there — what is missing is somewhere open at nine on a Saturday, and until that exists Hash carries the whole load on its own.
venues.pressQuote: San Antonio's only 100 percent spirit-free cocktail bar.

venues.name: Hawksmoor Manchester
venues.description: Hawksmoor Manchester is the acclaimed British steak-and-seafood group's Deansgate restaurant, set in a landmark former bank a short walk from Spinningfields. Alongside its charcoal-grilled, dry-aged native-breed beef and grand banking-hall dining room, it keeps a genuine, named alcohol-free cocktail list — the 'Lo & No Alc' section, part of the group's wider 'Temperates' philosophy of what to drink when you're not drinking. Zero-proof builds run from Steady Pete's Ginger Brew (Tanqueray 0.0 and Lucky Saint IPA) and a Non-Alc Cherry Negroni with Lyre's Amaretti to the Afterburner, made with Botivo and Almave non-alcoholic agave spirit. Homemade sodas and a grown-up Shirley Temple riff round out a list built with the same care as the full bar.
venues.longDescription:
Hawksmoor is the British steak-and-seafood group founded in London in 2006 by Will Beckett and Huw Gott, and the Manchester restaurant — its first outside the capital — opened in 2015 inside a landmark former bank on Deansgate, a short walk from Spinningfields. The grand old banking hall gave the team an unusually handsome shell to work with, all soaring ceilings, marble and dark wood, restored into a warm, low-lit dining room with a substantial bar. It has become one of the city's benchmark occasion restaurants, known for native-breed beef dry-aged in-house and grilled over charcoal, day-boat seafood and a much-loved Sunday roast.

Drinks matter as much as the food here, and Hawksmoor treats non-drinkers seriously rather than as an afterthought. The group's wider ethos is captured in its 'Temperates' idea — what to drink when you're not drinking — and the Manchester bar carries a named 'Lo & No Alc' section on its cocktail list, built on proper alcohol-free spirits rather than sugary mixers. Steady Pete's Ginger Brew combines Tanqueray 0.0 with lemon, ginger and Lucky Saint IPA; the Non-Alc Cherry Negroni is built from Tanqueray 0.0, Lyre's Amaretti and sour cherry; and the Afterburner mixes Botivo and Almave non-alcoholic agave spirit with jalapeño, lime and pineapple. Lighter, lower-sugar options include the Shirley T — sparkling ginger tea with lemongrass and pomegranate, a grown-up take on a Shirley Temple — and a tangy homemade Pineapple Soda, with alcohol-free beer poured alongside.

The list changes with the seasons but the intent is constant, and it has drawn local praise. Rounding up the city's best alcohol-free drinking in January 2026, Manchester's Finest singled out Hawksmoor's 'concise but perfectly-formed alcohol-free menu', from a stivo spritz to a booze-free sangria. For a high-end steakhouse to give its zero-proof drinks their own billing on the cocktail list, made with the same technique as the full programme, is exactly the kind of considered NA offering that earns Hawksmoor Manchester a place here — somewhere a designated driver, a pregnant guest or anyone simply off the sauce can order something proper to sit beside the steak.
venues.pressQuote: Their concise but perfectly-formed alcohol-free menu contains a stivo spritz, a grown-up take on a Shirley Temple, and even a booze-free sangria.

venues.name: Haywire
venues.description: Haywire's La Cantera location, in the shopping and hotel district on San Antonio's far north side, keeps three named zero-proof drinks on the menu: The Lady Bird, a Mojito Refresher and Hibiscus Haze. The Texas-hill-country concept runs consistent alcohol-free options across its locations — the same group appears in this guide in Dallas — which is worth knowing, because a chain that standardises its non-alcoholic list is one you can order from confidently without researching each branch first. Useful for anyone staying out by the resorts rather than downtown. It is roughly twenty minutes north of the centre, near the Rim and the La Cantera hotels, and keeps broad family-friendly hours.
venues.address: 15900 La Cantera Pkwy Suite 11200, San Antonio, TX 78256
venues.longDescription:
Haywire at La Cantera sits in the retail and resort district at the far northern edge of San Antonio, close to the Rim and the big hotels, about twenty minutes from downtown without traffic. The concept is Texas hill country — a large, comfortable room built for groups and families.

Its three named zero-proof drinks are The Lady Bird, a Mojito Refresher and Hibiscus Haze. None is complicated, and the grade reflects a solid rather than an inventive programme, but there is a specific reason this listing earns its place beyond the drinks themselves.

Haywire is a group, and it runs comparable alcohol-free options across its locations — the same brand appears in this guide's Dallas coverage. For a non-drinker that consistency has real practical value. Most of the work of not drinking in an unfamiliar city is research: checking menus in advance, guessing whether somewhere will have anything, arriving prepared to be disappointed. A chain that reliably prints named zero-proof drinks removes that work. You can walk in without checking. That is worth something even when the individual drinks are less interesting than what an independent bar might build.

The hours are broad and family-friendly — 11am to 10pm through the week, later on Friday and Saturday, from 10am at weekends. The La Cantera location specifically serves visitors staying at the northern resorts rather than downtown, a group otherwise poorly served by this guide, since almost everything else worth ordering in San Antonio is clustered downtown, in Southtown or around the Pearl. If you are staying at La Cantera without a car, this is realistically your one good option, and it is a perfectly decent one.
venues.pressQuote: Haywire: The Lady Bird, Mojito Refresher, Hibiscus Haze.

venues.name: Haywire – Legacy West
venues.description: A Texas farm-to-fork flagship in Plano's Legacy West district, Haywire pairs its award-winning whiskey and wine program with a documented three-drink mocktail menu built on local ingredients like prickly pear, Lady Bird Tonic, and fresh herbs.
venues.longDescription:
Haywire's Legacy West outpost is one of the few full-scale Texas steakhouses in the Dallas metro that treats its non-alcoholic program as a genuine part of the bar menu rather than an afterthought. Spread across three floors — a ground-floor whiskey lounge, a main dining room, and a rooftop patio — the restaurant's Marfa-inspired atmosphere works equally well for sober-curious guests who want the full upscale experience. The mocktail list is available year-round, not just during Dry January, and the $8 price point is honest for the craft involved.

The three signature zero-proof drinks each draw on specifically Texan flavor profiles. The Hibiscus Haze blends hibiscus, prickly pear, and lemon, sweetened with simple syrup and finished with Lady Bird Tonic for a floral, vivid pour. The Lady Bird Tonic cocktail layers grapefruit, pineapple, cranberry, and guava over Lady Bird Grapefruit Soda — a drink named deliberately after Texas's own Lady Bird Johnson. The Mojito Refresher builds lemon, pineapple, cucumber, and mint with agave and ginger ale for a clean, cooling finish. The bartending team at Haywire — part of Front Burner Restaurants' group portfolio — created the menu with the stated intent of matching the complexity of the restaurant's alcoholic cocktail program.

Haywire Legacy West is a good fit for business dinners, date nights, and groups that include non-drinkers, since the mocktails integrate naturally into the full menu rather than arriving on a separate laminated card. Reservations are strongly recommended on weekends; OpenTable is the easiest booking route. Dress is smart-casual — the rooftop skews younger and louder, while the second-floor dining room is quieter. Valet parking is available on Winthrop St., and three free parking garages are within the Legacy West development. The companion Uptown Dallas location at 1920 McKinney Ave also carries the same mocktail program.
venues.pressQuote: Haywire is offering a bold take on Dry January with a free-spirited mocktail menu that delivers full flavor without the proof.

venues.name: Haywire – Uptown Dallas
venues.description: Haywire is a Texas farm-to-fork restaurant in Dallas's Uptown neighborhood offering an unapologetically Lone Star dining experience — and a dedicated three-drink mocktail menu built from local ingredients that holds its own alongside their acclaimed cocktail program.
venues.longDescription:
Haywire sits on McKinney Avenue in the heart of Uptown Dallas and stands out as one of the few full-service Texas steakhouses in the neighborhood to offer a dedicated, named mocktail menu rather than an afterthought soda list. The restaurant explicitly frames its three zero-proof drinks as year-round offerings — not just Dry January specials — making it a reliable option for non-drinkers at a table where everyone else is ordering from an extensive whiskey and wine program.

The signature Hibiscus Haze combines hibiscus, prickly pear, and lemon, finished with Lady Bird Tonic for a floral, slightly tart pour that photographs as well as it tastes. The Lady Bird Tonic mocktail layers grapefruit, pineapple, cranberry, and guava with Lady Bird Grapefruit Soda — a Texas-made mixer — for something tropical and bright. The Mojito Refresher swaps rum for a clean combination of lemon, pineapple, cucumber, mint, agave, and ginger ale. All three are priced at $8. According to OpenTable, the Uptown location is managed by General Manager James O'Neal, and the bar team has publicly described these drinks as built with the same attention to craft as Haywire's alcoholic cocktails.

The Uptown location occupies the former Water Grill space and spreads across an indoor dining room, a whiskey lounge, and an outdoor patio with a fireplace and a retractable roof — the patio also features a vintage Haywire Shasta trailer available for private use or walk-ins. The vibe is Texas-chic: elevated but not stuffy, busy on weekends, with a crowd that skews professional and date-night. Reservations are strongly recommended for dinner and weekend brunch; valet is available. The space works well for groups, corporate dinners, and anyone who wants a genuinely Texas dining experience without feeling sidelined at the bar.
venues.pressQuote: Haywire Texas-centric restaurant has three non-alcoholic drinks: Hibiscus Haze, with hibiscus, prickly pear, & lemon; Lady Bird Tonic with grapefruit, pineapple, cranberry, guava, & Lady Bird grapefruit soda; and Mojito Refresher with lemon, pineapple, cucumber, mint, agave, & ginger ale.

venues.name: Haywood Famous
venues.description: Haywood Famous closed its West Asheville shop in late summer 2026 because the building is set to be demolished for the I-26 Connector. The owner is looking for a new location and hopes to reopen in West Asheville in 2027, so there is nowhere to visit for now — check before you go. For two years it was a 100% alcohol-free Cuban-coffee cafe and art space, founded by Eva Rodriguez-Cué to offer a "sober nightlife" alternative — a comfortable place for alcohol-free evening socializing when other cafes had closed. It pulled Cuban coffee drinks (Cubano, cafecito, café con leche, cortadito, and the shareable colada) with Cuban pastries, and doubled as a community hub for art and music.
venues.longDescription:
Haywood Famous is closed for now. The shop at 508 Haywood Road shut in late summer 2026 because the North Carolina Department of Transportation is acquiring the building for the I-26 Connector: owner Eva Rodriguez-Cué was given 90 days to leave, and the building is set to be demolished. The shop's own site reads "Goodbye for now" and says a relocation is under way, and she told Mountain Xpress she hopes to reopen somewhere in West Asheville in 2027. No new address or date had been announced as of early October 2026, so there is nowhere to visit yet. What follows describes the shop as it ran for its two years on Haywood Road.

Haywood Famous was a Cuban coffee shop at 508 Haywood Road in West Asheville, opened on 1 August 2024 by Eva Rodriguez-Cué, a first-generation Cuban American who was twenty-three when she launched it. She had left UNC Asheville during the pandemic and built her own hospitality apprenticeship instead, working front and back of house across restaurants and coffee shops before opening her own. The room was designed as a 1960s and 70s gathering space, furnished with vintage pieces, and built around late-night games of dominoes and morning pastelitos. The venue stated its position without hedging: it was proud to be a sober community, and it was fully alcohol-free.

What made it unusual was not that it served no alcohol — plenty of cafés do — but that it deliberately operated as nightlife. Rodriguez-Cué's reasoning is the clearest articulation of why this category exists that anyone has given in Asheville: her generation, she told Mountain Xpress, is statistically the most sober and the most socially isolated, and she wanted a gathering place for people to get off their phones, off social media, and be with each other. The hours were built for it. Haywood Famous opened at 8am for coffee and then reopened in the evening from 7pm to 10pm on Thursday, Friday and Saturday, so there was somewhere in West Asheville to go at nine at night that was not a bar. The drinks were Cuban coffee done properly — cortaditos, cafecito, café con leche, the Cubano and the colada, which is the shared, sugar-whipped espresso poured into thimble cups and meant to be passed around a table. A rose chai latte covered the non-coffee side.
venues.pressQuote: My generation is statistically the most sober and the most socially isolated. I wanted to create a gathering place for people to get off their phones, get off social [media] and be with each other.

venues.name: Hearth '61
venues.description: The New American restaurant at Mountain Shadows Resort in Paradise Valley, with hearth-fired cooking and a dining room angled at Camelback Mountain — and an unusually generous non-alcoholic list for a resort. The spirit-free options are built on named NA spirits rather than juice, leaning on Seedlip and the Cornish botanical brand Pentire: the Blueberry Basil Bliss (Seedlip Garden 108, lemon, blueberry, basil), the Pink Petal (Pentire, grapefruit, hibiscus) and the Berry-Berry-Berry Delightful. Reaching past Seedlip to a second, less common NA spirit is the signal here — it indicates someone chose the range rather than ordering the default bottle.
venues.address: 5445 E Lincoln Dr, Paradise Valley, AZ 85253
venues.longDescription:
Hearth '61 is the flagship restaurant of Mountain Shadows, a mid-century resort in Paradise Valley that was rebuilt and reopened after decades of dereliction, and the room is designed around the view: floor-to-ceiling glass angled at Camelback Mountain, with the golf course in the middle distance. The kitchen cooks over an open hearth, which gives the menu its name and most of its character.

Resort restaurants are the hardest category in which to find a serious non-alcoholic drink. The economics push toward a house margarita and a soda gun, and the guest is assumed to be on holiday and therefore drinking. Hearth '61 does not follow that script. Its spirit-free list is built on named non-alcoholic spirits and reaches past the obvious one — alongside Seedlip Garden 108 it pours Pentire, a Cornish botanical distillate made with rock samphire and sea kelp that almost never appears on American menus. The Blueberry Basil Bliss works the Seedlip with lemon, blueberry and basil; the Pink Petal sets Pentire against grapefruit and hibiscus; the Berry-Berry-Berry Delightful is the sweeter of the three.

Stocking a second, less common NA spirit is the detail worth noticing, because it is not an accident. Seedlip is the bottle a bar buys when it wants to be able to say it has one; adding Pentire means someone tasted the category and made a choice about range. For a guest at the resort who is not drinking, that is the difference between three variations on the same base and an actual list. Practical notes: this is a resort restaurant with resort prices and a full bar, it is a drive from central Phoenix, and the view seats are worth requesting when booking. Sunset is the hour to aim for, when the light comes off the mountain face and the room earns the glass it was built behind.

venues.name: Hecate
venues.description: Hecate is an underground cocktail bar in Back Bay, reached through a door off Public Alley 443 and sitting below its sibling Greek restaurant Krasi. It opened in April 2022 from the Krasi team, with Demetri Tsolakis among the co-owners alongside Stefanos Ougrinis, Tasha Breshinsky and Kayla Padilla, and takes its name and its occult styling from the Greek goddess of witchcraft and crossroads. Drinks arrive via a leather-bound book of spells, each cocktail tied to a piece of folklore, and the alcohol-free builds sit within that same framework under a dedicated Zero Proof list. They are not simplified: the spirit-free drinks use clarified milk, aquafaba, saline, bittering roots and house cordials, and are constructed with the same number of steps as the full-proof menu.
venues.longDescription:
Hecate opened on April 7, 2022 in the Back Bay, tucked below Krasi, the Greek wine-focused restaurant its team already ran, and entered through a discreet door in Public Alley 443 rather than off the street. The bar is named for Hecate, the Greek goddess associated with witchcraft, night and crossroads, and the whole room commits to that: low light, occult iconography, and a menu bound as a book of spells in which every drink is attached to a piece of folklore. Boston.com covered the opening on April 1, 2022, describing it as a place where you enter the realm of spirits, and Boston Magazine ran a first-look the same day. Boston Magazine has since returned to it in its running guide to the city's best mocktails, noting that the book of spells also holds unconventional spirit-free options and that the room's atmosphere is the draw whether you are drinking alcohol or not.

The zero-proof list is short and built to the same specification as the alcoholic one. Copal Oro pairs the copal oro base with clarified milk, a technique borrowed straight from milk-punch practice. Theta Range is the most involved drink on the list, layering chicory, beetroot, fig, hibiscus and pomegranate over copal oro and clarified milk with lemon, aquafaba, saline and club soda. Eighth Tower runs herbal and bitter, using devil's claw, yarrow and mugwort with DRAM black bitters, lemon, aquafaba, saline and soda. Secret Chiefs is the simplest and driest of the four, built on juniper, cinchona bark and a lime peel demerara, and reads as a tonic-adjacent aperitif. The aquafaba and clarified-milk techniques matter here, because they are what give the alcohol-free drinks the weight and texture that non-alcoholic cocktails most often lack. Hecate trades Tuesday through Saturday from 5pm to 1am and is closed Sunday and Monday.
venues.pressQuote: At Hecate, you enter the realm of spirits.

venues.name: Heck's Cafe
venues.description: Heck's Cafe has been serving burgers and American bistro food from a pre-Civil-War building on Bridge Avenue in Ohio City since 1974, which makes it one of the neighbourhood's longest-running restaurants and the original of three locations. The dining room runs back into a glass conservatory. Several mocktails sit on the standing printed menu rather than being made on request, led by a pomegranate-ginger spritz at $10 built on non-alcoholic sparkling wine and a Passion Fruit Picante. It opens at 11am six days a week, which few of the city's zero-proof programmes do.
venues.longDescription:
Heck's Cafe opened on Bridge Avenue in Ohio City in 1974, in a brick building that predates the Civil War, and has spent fifty years as the neighbourhood's burger institution — long enough to have been there through Ohio City's decline and the whole of its revival. The dining room runs back into a glass conservatory, and the menu holds a consistent American bistro line: burgers ground in house, steak frites, salads, and a long Sunday brunch. The group describes its founding mission as sharing a passion for food and has kept the same values around fresh ingredients, community and sustainability since the early seventies. The Ohio City room is the original; locations in Avon and Beachwood followed, each with its own phone number and hours, so it is worth checking you are calling the right one.

The non-alcoholic offering is modest by the standards of the dedicated rooms on this list, but it is genuinely on the printed menu rather than made on request, which is the distinction that matters when you are ordering for a table. The pomegranate-ginger spritz at $10 is the one Cleveland Magazine singled out in its 2026 mocktail roundup — sweet, tart and spicy, built on non-alcoholic sparkling wine so it drinks like an aperitif rather than a soda, and holding its own next to the wine-by-the-glass list. A Passion Fruit Picante and one or two further mocktails sit alongside it.

The practical argument for Heck's is the clock. It opens at 11am six days a week and 10:30am on Sundays, where most of Cleveland's serious zero-proof programmes do not unlock their doors until 4pm. If you want a properly built non-alcoholic drink in the middle of a Tuesday afternoon in Ohio City, this is close to the only option.
venues.pressQuote: The pomegranate-ginger spritz ($10) is a sweet, tart and spicy blend built with sparkling nonalcoholic wine.

venues.name: Hello, Marjorie
venues.description: Hello, Marjorie occupies the former Register & Tribune building on Locust Street in downtown Des Moines, styled as a mid-century living room, and it runs the most serious alcohol-free programme in the city — a rotating spirit-free list built on real non-alcoholic liquor rather than juice. The Amaretto Stone Sour uses N/A amaretto and N/A rum with orange, lemon, cinnamon and orgeat; the G&T is Seedlip Spice 94 against a house tonic with spiced pear, clarified lime and soda water. Clarifying a lime is a technique most bars will not do for a drink with alcohol in it, let alone one without.
signatureDrinks: Amaretto Stone Sour — N/A amaretto, N/A rum, orange, lemon, cinnamon, orgeat
G&T — Seedlip Spice 94, house tonic, spiced pear, clarified lime, soda water
venues.longDescription:
Hello, Marjorie is in the old Register & Tribune building on Locust Street, and the room is done as a stylish living room from several decades ago — low light, deep seating, the kind of place designed to keep you for three hours. Its alcohol-free list is the best in Des Moines, and the reason is technique rather than stock.

Look at the G&T specification: Seedlip Spice 94, a house-made tonic, spiced pear, clarified lime and soda water. Two of those five components are labour. A house tonic means making cinchona syrup rather than opening a bottle. Clarified lime means running citrus juice through a milk or agar clarification to strip the cloudiness and soften the acid while keeping the aroma — a process that takes hours and that most bars will not undertake for their alcoholic cocktails, let alone a drink for someone not drinking. Seedlip Spice 94 is the allspice-and-cardamom expression, which is the right one to pair with pear.

The Amaretto Stone Sour is the other documented build and it goes the opposite direction: N/A amaretto and N/A rum together with orange, lemon, cinnamon and orgeat, which is a rich, nutty, almost dessert-adjacent drink. Between the two, the bar covers both ends of what a non-drinker might want on a given night, which very few venues in this directory manage.

The list rotates, which is why only these two are recorded — Des Moines' tourism board documented them in January 2026 and the rest of the menu will have turned over since. The rotation is itself the signal: a static pair of mocktails is a decision made once, a rotating list is a decision made every season.

Open 4pm to midnight Monday through Thursday and 4pm to 1am on Friday and Saturday. Closed Sunday. It sits a couple of blocks from In Confidence and Revival House, which makes downtown Des Moines walkable for an evening built this way.

A caution that belongs in this city guide somewhere visible, and this is the entry to carry it. Des Moines' own tourism board published its round-up of the best mocktails in the metro on 5 January 2026, and two of the venues it recommends are permanently closed as of August 2026: Louie's Wine Dive and 503 Cocktail Lab. That is less a criticism of the guide than a measure of how fast this category moves — seven months was long enough for a fifth of a city's recommended list to disappear. Check before travelling, here and everywhere.
venues.pressQuote: G&T: Seedlip Spice 94, house tonic, spiced pear, clarified lime, soda water

venues.name: Henrietta Lane
venues.description: Henrietta Lane is a neighborhood cocktail and snack bar on King Street East in Corktown, in what its owners call "one of Toronto's oldest communities," open until 2am seven nights a week with an attached bottle shop. It was founded by two friends with a shared passion for coffee, food and bartending, and the kitchen runs on "quality ingredients & recipes made with care." The menu sets aside a dedicated "Teetotaller" section for zero-proof drinks, among them the Chai Blossom — a house chai concentrate mixed with soda and lime juice, garnished with star anise and a twist of citrus — and pours Partake non-alcoholic beer.
venues.address: 394 King St E, Toronto, ON M5A 1K9, Canada
signatureDrinks: Chai Blossom ($5) — house chai concentrate mixed with soda and lime juice, garnished with star anise and a twist of citrus
venues.longDescription:
Henrietta Lane sits at 394 King St E in Corktown, open Sunday through Thursday from 4pm to 2am and Friday and Saturday from 2pm to 2am, with its attached bottle shop open until 11pm. It was founded by two friends bound by a shared passion for coffee, food and bartending, and the venue describes its mission as bringing "small town service & love" to one of Toronto's oldest communities. It operates as a neighborhood cocktail and snack bar with a patio.

The kitchen leans on "quality ingredients & recipes made with care," turning out snack boards and rotating specials — including a vegan smoked mushroom sandwich — alongside a seasonal cocktail menu and house-made touches like a mocha liqueur and a Furikake-Ranch Chex mix.

The non-alcoholic program has real texture for a cocktail bar: the menu carves out a dedicated "Teetotaller" section for zero-proof drinks, including the Chai Blossom ($5) — a house chai concentrate mixed with soda and lime juice, garnished with star anise and a twist of citrus. Partake non-alcoholic beer is also poured. Some Good Clean Fun singled the bar out in its roundup of Toronto's best mocktails, writing that "the three mocktails on the menu at Henrietta Lane are unique and creative... The owners put as much importance on their placebo cocktails as their full-proof options."
venues.pressQuote: "The three mocktails on the menu at Henrietta Lane are unique and creative... The owners put as much importance on their placebo cocktails as their full-proof options."

venues.name: Herb & Sea
venues.description: Herb & Sea is a modern seafood restaurant in downtown Encinitas, steps from Moonlight State Beach, opened in November 2019 as the coastal sister to Brian Malarkey's Herb & Wood (both run by Puffer Malarkey Collective). The kitchen focuses on wood-fired cooking and sustainably sourced local fish, and that seasonal approach carries into a rotating beverage program with a dedicated "Spirit Free" section. Current named zero-proof drinks include "Luke, I Did It Again" (hibiscus tea, strawberry, vanilla, lemon, soda) and a Pentire N/A cocktail offered as a spritz, dirty martini, or rosemary and tonic, plus Kollo single-origin iced tea; NA beer options include Athletic Brewing's Run Wild IPA. A lively beach-town spot where non-drinkers get composed builds rather than an afterthought.

venues.longDescription:
Herb & Sea is a modern seafood restaurant in downtown Encinitas, a few steps from Moonlight State Beach, opened in November 2019 as the coastal sister to Brian Malarkey's Herb & Wood in San Diego proper — both run by the Puffer Malarkey Collective. The kitchen is built around wood-fired cooking and sustainably sourced local fish, and the room has the loud, full, beach-town energy that a restaurant on that stretch of Encinitas either has or fails without. It serves dinner Tuesday through Sunday.

The seasonal approach in the kitchen carries into the bar, which runs a rotating beverage programme with a dedicated Spirit Free section rather than a fixed pair of afterthoughts. The current named zero-proof builds include "Luke, I Did It Again," which works hibiscus tea against strawberry, vanilla and lemon with soda, and a Pentire non-alcoholic cocktail offered three ways — as a spritz, as a dirty martini, or simply with rosemary and tonic. Pentire is a Cornish botanical distillate built on coastal plants, which is a deliberate and rather good match for a seafood restaurant on the Pacific; offering it in a dirty martini format in particular gives a non-drinker access to the savoury, saline end of the drinks spectrum that spirit-free lists almost always skip in favour of fruit. Kollo single-origin iced tea sits alongside for anyone wanting something simpler, and the beer list carries Athletic Brewing's Run Wild IPA for a non-alcoholic option that arrives in a proper glass. The practical result is that a table splitting a whole wood-fired fish can order across the whole meal without anyone defaulting to a soda — which, at a restaurant of this price and this noise level, is the difference between a non-drinker being part of the evening and being a guest at it.
venues.pressQuote: Since opening in November 2019, just before the pandemic, Herb & Sea has established itself as one of the most sought-after reservations in town

venues.name: Herb & Wood
venues.description: Herb & Wood is a wood-fired Mediterranean restaurant in Little Italy, opened in April 2016 by Top Chef alum Brian Malarkey and partner Christopher Puffer (Puffer Malarkey Collective, also home to Herb & Sea). The kitchen centers on a custom wood-fired hearth turning out housemade pastas, flame-kissed proteins, and seasonal vegetables, and the bar keeps a standing "Spirit-Free" section with four named zero-proof drinks so non-drinkers get composed builds rather than soda or juice. Current options include the Lemon & Herbs (lemon, roasted lemon-thyme syrup, grenadine, soda), the Kauai Chickens (cinnamon pineapple, spiced grapefruit cordial, lime, egg white, mineral water), a non-alcoholic Sbagliato (alcohol-removed sparkling wine and aperitivo), and Malarkey in Paris (smoke tea, bergamot, spearmint, carbonated). It marked its 10th anniversary in March 2026.

venues.longDescription:
Herb & Wood is a wood-fired Mediterranean restaurant on Kettner Boulevard in Little Italy, opened in April 2016 by Top Chef alum Brian Malarkey and partner Christopher Puffer under the Puffer Malarkey Collective, which also runs Herb & Sea up the coast in Encinitas. It marked its tenth anniversary in March 2026 — a long run in a neighbourhood that turns over as fast as Little Italy has. The kitchen is organised around a custom wood-fired hearth producing housemade pastas, flame-cooked proteins and seasonal vegetables, in a room that has stayed one of the more reliably full dining destinations in central San Diego.

The bar keeps a standing Spirit-Free section of four named drinks, which is the difference between a restaurant that can make a non-drinker something and one that has already decided what. Lemon & Herbs works lemon against a roasted lemon-thyme syrup with grenadine and soda. The Kauai Chickens is the most technically involved of the four, combining cinnamon pineapple and a spiced grapefruit cordial with lime, egg white and mineral water — egg white being the ingredient that gives a zero-proof drink the weight and foam that alcohol otherwise provides, and one most kitchens will not bother with. There is a non-alcoholic Sbagliato built from alcohol-removed sparkling wine and aperitivo, which covers the bitter aperitif register properly, and Malarkey in Paris pairs smoke tea with bergamot and spearmint, carbonated. Four composed drinks across sweet, savoury, bitter and smoky is a genuinely complete list rather than a gesture — enough that a non-drinker can order differently across three courses. Dinner nightly. Little Italy is among the densest restaurant districts in the county and one of the harder places to eat without drinking, since almost every room on Kettner is built around a wine list. Ten years in, Herb & Wood remains one of the few there with a printed spirit-free section.
venues.pressQuote: Wood-fired dishes are the cornerstone of this upscale, trendy restaurant established by celebrity chef Brian Malarkey to showcase California and Mediterranean flavors

venues.name: Herban Flow
venues.description: Herban Flow is billed as Florida's first non-alcoholic and functional bottle shop, and its downtown St. Petersburg storefront (a second location to the original near Tyrone) carries one of the area's deepest spirit-free selections — non-alcoholic beer, wine, and zero-proof spirits (gin, whiskey, rum, mezcal) plus pre-made mocktails and canned mimosas. The shop also sells THC, CBD, kava, and mushroom functional drinks, so it's alcohol-free but not necessarily substance-free; for stocking up on NA, it's the standout in town.  The sampling bar is the useful part: zero-proof spirits are expensive and wildly variable in quality, and tasting before committing is how people avoid writing off the whole category on one bad bottle.
venues.address: 501 Dr. M.L.K. Jr. St N, Unit 103, St. Petersburg, FL 33701
venues.longDescription:
Herban Flow is billed as Florida's first non-alcoholic and functional bottle shop, and now runs a downtown St. Petersburg storefront alongside the original near Tyrone. Its stock is the deepest spirit-free selection in the region: non-alcoholic beer and wine, zero-proof gin, whiskey, rum and mezcal, pre-made mocktails and canned mimosas — the range a person needs to actually keep a house stocked rather than to make one drink for a dinner party.

That distinction is what a bottle shop contributes that a bar cannot. Most non-drinking happens at home, not out, and the practical obstacle is supply — a supermarket carries one alcohol-free lager and nothing else, so the alternative to a glass of wine on a Tuesday is a soft drink. A shop with four categories of zero-proof spirit changes what is possible in a kitchen, not just on a night out. I Love The Burg noted the sampling bar and the scale of the selection when surveying the region's non-alcoholic options.

The sampling bar is worth calling out on its own. Alcohol-free spirits are expensive, unfamiliar and wildly variable in quality, and buying a bottle blind is how people conclude the whole category is bad. Being able to taste before committing is the single most useful service in the sector.

One honest caveat, which the shop's own range makes necessary. Alongside the non-alcoholic drinks it sells THC, CBD, kava and mushroom functional beverages. Everything is alcohol-free; not everything is inert. For anyone whose reason for avoiding alcohol is recovery from a substance-use disorder, that distinction is worth knowing before browsing rather than at the till.  Two locations now trade — the original near Tyrone and the downtown St. Petersburg storefront — and the downtown site is the one with the sampling bar and the fuller range. Staff are used to explaining the category to newcomers, which is worth more than it sounds when facing a wall of unfamiliar bottles for the first time — the difference between leaving with something you will drink and leaving with an expensive bottle that sits unopened. For anyone building a home bar without alcohol, this is the single most useful address in Tampa Bay, and the reason it earns a listing alongside rooms you can actually sit in.
venues.pressQuote: Herban Flow is focused on establishing itself as a reliable and informative source for non-alcoholic beverages and wellness products.

venues.name: Herbst Eatery & Farm Stand
venues.description: Herbst Eatery & Farm Stand is a farm-sourced restaurant and market on Raymond Avenue in Saint Anthony Park, opened in 2023 by Angie and Jorg Pierach and supplied by a co-op of young Driftless-area farmers. Its drinks list is structured unusually and to the benefit of anyone not drinking: cocktails are organised first by flavour profile — mineral, bitter, funky, earthy, plus a seasonal slot — and then by potency, with a full-proof, a low-proof and a no-proof version of each. The no-proof builds are not the alcoholic drink minus the alcohol; they are separate recipes engineered to land on the same flavour, so the earthy no-proof reaches for sparkling green and lapsang teas where the full-proof uses mezcal.

venues.longDescription:
Herbst opened in 2023 on Raymond Avenue in Saint Anthony Park, in the industrial-edged stretch of Saint Paul between the university's agricultural campus and the Green Line. It is owned by Angie and Jorg Pierach and it sources through a co-operative of young farmers from the Driftless region, running as a restaurant at the front and a farm stand alongside it. Jason DeRusha, reviewing it for Minnesota Monthly in May 2023, described the drinks list as organised "by flavor profile (mineral, bitter, funky, earthy) and potency (low-proof, full proof and no proof)" — a grid rather than a list, and one of the few in the Twin Cities where a zero-proof drink occupies structurally the same square as its full-strength sibling instead of sitting in an appendix at the bottom of the page.

That structure matters more than it sounds. Within each of the flavour categories the three versions are not the same recipe stepped down; they are three different builds aimed at the same sensory target. In the earthy column, the full-proof runs tequila and mezcal with sumac; the low-proof drops the tequila and adds gentian and dry vermouth; the no-proof keeps the sumac and brings in sparkling green and lapsang souchong teas to carry the smoke and tannin that the mezcal was supplying. The effect is that ordering the no-proof is a lateral move rather than a downgrade, and it removes the usual problem of a spirit-free list that reads as three fruit juices. A rotating seasonal profile joins the four fixed ones. The restaurant is licensed and does pour full-strength drinks — this is not an alcohol-free room — but the no-proof column is a permanent, designed part of the menu rather than a concession. Service runs evenings Monday to Saturday with a Sunday midday seating, and the room is small enough that booking ahead is sensible.
venues.pressQuote: Cocktails are organized by flavor profile (mineral, bitter, funky, earthy) and potency (low-proof, full proof and no proof).

venues.name: Here Kitty Kitty Vice Den
venues.description: Here Kitty Kitty Vice Den is a hidden cocktail bar inside Famous Foods Street Eats, the Singapore-style hawker-hall food court at Resorts World Las Vegas. Entry is the point: the bar sits behind the shelves of a small gift-and-sundries stall, and guests check in with a hostess who moves a bookshelf to let them through. Drinks are the only thing served, and the mixology program takes Prohibition-era construction and runs it through a Singaporean lens, which extends to the zero-proof options listed alongside the cocktails rather than hidden behind a request. The Las Vegas Convention and Visitors Authority singled out the Invisible Ink, built from cold brew, orange, raspberry and CALPICO soda, among seven must-try spirit-free drinks in the city. The room runs High Fidelity Fridays, a weekly all-vinyl music series with DJs playing analog-based sets, and opens nightly at 6pm, to midnight Sunday through Thursday and to 1am on Friday and Saturday.
venues.address: 3000 S Las Vegas Blvd, Las Vegas, NV 89109
signatureDrinks: Invisible Ink (cold brew, orange, raspberry, CALPICO soda)
venues.longDescription:
Here Kitty Kitty Vice Den is a hidden bar tucked inside Famous Foods Street Eats, the Singapore-style hawker hall at Resorts World Las Vegas, and finding it is deliberately part of the experience. The entrance sits behind the shelves of a small gift-and-sundries stall on the food-hall floor; guests check in with a hostess, who moves a bookshelf aside to let them through into a small, dark, Tokyo-inflected room. Drinks are the only thing served here — there is no food menu, which is unusual for a bar of this kind and is possible precisely because it sits in the middle of a food hall, so anything you want to eat is thirty seconds away. The mixology program takes Prohibition-era cocktail construction and filters it through a Singaporean sensibility, producing drinks like a Jerry Thomas Brandy Punch built with hibiscus and grenadine alongside house creations. On Fridays the room runs High Fidelity Fridays, a weekly all-vinyl series with DJs playing analog-based sets, and there is a disco bathroom hidden in plain sight for anyone who goes looking.

For a bar with no food and a concealed entrance, the handling of non-drinkers is better than it needs to be: zero-proof options are listed on the menu alongside the cocktails rather than left to be negotiated with a bartender, which is the difference between a bar that will accommodate you and a bar that expected you. The Las Vegas Convention and Visitors Authority's own guide to the city's must-try spirit-free drinks singles out the Invisible Ink, built from cold brew, orange, raspberry and CALPICO soda — the Japanese cultured-milk soft drink — which is a genuinely distinctive build rather than a juice with a garnish on it. Reservations are worth making, since the room is small and the entrance ritual depends on a hostess expecting you. It opens nightly at 6pm, running to midnight Sunday through Thursday and to 1am on Friday and Saturday, and the dress code is casual.
venues.pressQuote: Here Kitty Kitty Vice Den bills itself as a “vice den,” but it’s up to you if that vice is alcohol.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Visit Las Vegas, "Seven Must-Try Mocktails in Las Vegas"

venues.name: Here Nor There
venues.description: Here Nor There is a reservation-only speakeasy in downtown Austin, located at 612 Brazos Street near the historic Driskill Hotel. Opened in June 2018, the bar seats only 55 guests in an intimate basement space accessed by a code-locked alley gate, with reservations made through a dedicated mobile app. The cocktail program is led by experienced mixologists with a globally-influenced, theatrical approach — guests are greeted with complimentary prosecco by a taxidermy bear before being escorted to their table. Cocktails are spirits-forward and priced between $30–50; upscale mocktails are available for guests who prefer alcohol-free options, though the bar's primary focus is craft cocktails.
venues.longDescription:
Here Nor There is a reservation-only speakeasy at 612 Brazos Street, in a basement beneath an alleyway beside the historic Driskill Hotel. It opened in June 2018 and seats just 55. Getting in is part of the design: reservations go through a dedicated app, which releases a code shortly before your booking to open the alley gate. The Infatuation's Nicolai McCrary noted it sounds like a lot of effort, and that it stops feeling that way the moment you are through the door and greeted by a life-sized stuffed bear holding a tray of champagne with old-school hip hop on the speakers.

The cocktails are expensive — thirty to fifty dollars — and technically serious, with liquid nitrogen-cooled olives, clarified punches and hand-stamped ice, all of which McCrary read as part of the show rather than as affectation. The menus are high-concept and rotate.

For a non-drinker the honest assessment is that this is a craft cocktail bar first. Upscale mocktails are available and made to the same standard as everything else, but they are not a named, published programme the way they are at the Roosevelt Room or Parley — you are asking the bar to build you something rather than reading a list. Given the technique on display that is usually a good trade, but it is worth knowing before you book a table at these prices.

What the format does offer a non-drinker is unusual and underrated. The evening is a seated, ticketed, hour-and-a-half experience with a hard start time, in a room of 55 people. Nobody is buying rounds, nobody is at a bar, and the pace is set by the venue rather than by whoever is drinking fastest. That structure removes most of the social machinery that makes a normal night out difficult when you are not drinking, which can matter more than what is in the glass. Open from 5pm nightly.
venues.pressQuote: The cocktails are pricey, but with liquid nitrogen-cooled olives, clarified punches, and hand-stamped ice at play, it all feels like part of the show.

venues.name: Herman's Coffee
venues.description: Herman's Coffee is a coffee roastery, café, and specialty market in Philadelphia's Pennsport neighborhood, opened by owner Mat Falco in 2017 inside a former auto-mechanic's shop. Beginning in 2020 — after discovering the non-alcoholic aperitif Ghia — Falco built what the Philadelphia Inquirer calls one of the region's largest zero-proof selections: over 200 non-alcoholic wines, spirits, and beers, plus 50–75 mixers and syrups and more than 100 bitters, much of it sold to take home. By day, the café pours house-made non-alcoholic creations such as the Blood Orange Espresso Tonic, Lavender Lemonade Spritz, and the "Don't Call Me Shirley Temple." On Friday and Saturday nights, Herman's After Dark switches to candlelit table service with a menu of cocktails and wines "with and without alcohol," plus light bites and rotating food pop-ups.
venues.longDescription:
Herman's Coffee is a roastery, café and specialty market in Pennsport, opened by Mat Falco in 2017 inside a former auto-mechanic's shop. Its significance to anyone not drinking is a matter of scale: beginning in 2020, after Falco discovered the non-alcoholic aperitif Ghia, he built what the Philadelphia Inquirer describes as one of the region's largest zero-proof selections — over two hundred non-alcoholic wines, spirits and beers, fifty to seventy-five mixers and syrups, and more than a hundred bitters, most of it available to take home.

That bitters count is the striking number. More than a hundred varieties is a serious collection by any bar's standard, and bitters are the component that most often quietly disqualifies a drink for someone avoiding alcohol entirely, since the conventional product is 35–45% ABV. A shop stocking non-alcoholic bitters at that depth is solving a problem most people do not know they have until they read a label.

By day the café pours its own house-made non-alcoholic creations — the Blood Orange Espresso Tonic among them, which is the espresso-and-tonic combination that sounds implausible and works: the quinine bitterness and carbonation lift the coffee's acidity into something startlingly refreshing. A Lavender Lemonade Spritz sits at the softer end.

The combination of café, roastery and market is what makes it useful in practice. Someone new to not drinking can taste something on site, ask what it is, and then buy a bottle of it to have at home — which is the gap between curiosity and actually changing what you drink. Very few venues close that loop.

The hours are generous and slightly irregular: six in the morning to eleven at night on Monday, Thursday and Friday, six to six on Tuesday and Wednesday, and seven to eleven at weekends. Note the early Tuesday and Wednesday close before planning an evening.

venues.name: HEX Superette
venues.description: HEX Superette is the market, cafe, and bar from Shane and Meaghan Carpenter, whose HEX Ferments has been making kraut, kimchi, and kombucha since 2013 — production still runs out of the back of the same Govans building. The Kitchen & Bar menu keeps a dedicated NA Cocktails section: the Teetotally Tiki builds Ghia apéritif over HEX's own smoky pineapple kombucha with warm spices and lime, the Dandy Tonic pours house tonic with dandelion, chicory root, and lemon, and the Spicy Melissa mixes umami ginger syrup, lime, ginger, and tonic. Six house kombuchas — butterfly lime, ginger, lazy days, smoky pineapple, turmeric tonic, and a rotating seasonal — pour by the glass, and the farm sodas are built from house seasonal fruit concentrates and shrubs. The attached market stocks Ghia spritzes alongside Parch's Desert Margarita and Prickly Paloma to take home.

naMenuItems.name: Owl Spoon Hibiscus Mojito Water Kefir
Dram Cardamom & Black Tea Sparkling Water

venues.longDescription:
HEX Superette at 5718 York Road in Govans is three businesses sharing one address: a small grocery at the front, a fermentation production facility at the back, and a tasting-room bar in between. It comes from Shane and Meaghan Carpenter, who have been making kraut, kimchi and kombucha as HEX Ferments since 2013 and built the superette around that work rather than beside it. Baltimore Magazine called the result one of the most unique drink menus in the city. The food follows the same logic — approachable rather than technical, as Meaghan Carpenter put it: they are not using tweezers or foams, it is very approachable food that is extremely nutrient-dense.

The reason a non-drinker should care is fermentation, and specifically what it does to a drink's texture. Shane Carpenter's explanation is the clearest argument for kombucha as a cocktail base rather than a health drink: its natural carbonation is a by-product of the ferment, and that produces a much bigger, more acidic bubble than force-carbonating a liquid ever will. That acidity and structure is exactly what non-alcoholic drinks usually lack, and it is made on the premises. The bar list runs house-made sodas and kombucha-built mocktails — the Teetotally Tiki, a Dandy Tonic, a Spicy Melissa, a non-alcoholic oxymel spritz and a farm soda have all featured — alongside wines and a few beers. Two things to be clear about. HEX Superette is not an alcohol-free venue: it serves full-strength cocktails, wine and beer as well, so this is a strong non-alcoholic programme inside a working bar rather than a dry room. And the business is midway through moving its website to a new address, with several menu pages currently returning errors, so the current list is best confirmed in person.
venues.pressQuote: In addition to the mixed drinks, there are mocktails, wines, housemade sodas, and a few beers available

venues.longDescription:
Hey Love is an award-winning tropical cocktail lounge and restaurant set inside the Jupiter NEXT hotel at 920 East Burnside Street, in Portland's Buckman neighborhood. It opened in October 2018, the project of co-owners Aaron Hall and Nicholas Musso (also behind the longtime Portland bar Dig A Pony) together with a bartending team drawing on years at Portland institutions like Dig A Pony and Rum Club. The plant-filled, jungle-inspired room — full of ferns, vintage lanterns and local art — bills itself as "a top-notch cocktail lounge, a community meeting hall, a hidden garden, and a house party, all wrapped into one." In 2023 it was named Best U.S. Hotel Bar at Tales of the Cocktail's Spirited Awards, and it has been a repeat winner in Willamette Week's Best Cocktail Bar category.

Hey Love runs a serious, clearly labeled non-alcoholic program under the menu heading "Clear Eyes, Full Hearts, No Proof," built with the same care as its full-proof tiki list. Zero-proof options lean on dedicated NA spirits and brands rather than simple juice mixes: the Midnight Mass combines Pathfinder Amaro, Giffard NA Aperitif, cold brew and orange oil; the Rose City Swizzle pairs Pathfinder Amaro with pineapple, lemon, orgeat and mint; and the Phony Negroni serves St. Agrestis's non-alcoholic Negroni over the rocks. The list also includes the Sassy Tami (ginger tamarind-sarsaparilla lemonade), a de-alcoholized Noughty Sparkling Rosé, and two builds on the house Bloody mix — the N/A Bloody Miriam and the N/A Bargain Beach, made with non-alcoholic Corona and a Tajín salt rim.
venues.pressQuote: Hey Love's extensive no-proof menu has flavors to hit every craving, including phony espresso Negronis, a michelada with NA Corona, "de-alcoholized" tempranillo sparkling rosé, and a house-made bloody mary punched up with savory mushroom bouillon.

venues.name: Heyma Yemeni Coffee & Brunch
venues.description: Heyma Yemeni Coffee & Brunch is an alcohol-free Yemeni coffeehouse and all-day kitchen on Ninth Street in western SoMa, the San Francisco sibling of the Heyma cafe that opened on University Avenue in Berkeley in October 2023. It keeps the longest hours of any Yemeni room in the city, running 7am to 11:30pm most nights and to midnight on Friday and Saturday, and describes itself simply as open early and staying late. The drinks are traditional and spice-driven: the Heyma Latte built with cardamom and cinnamon, Aden tea cooked with cardamom, ginger and cream, and Mufawaar, the cream-topped spiced coffee that anchors most Yemeni menus. A full brunch kitchen runs alongside the coffee bar.
signatureDrinks: Heyma Latte (spiced with cardamom and cinnamon)
Mufawaar (spiced coffee with cardamom, ginger and cream)
venues.longDescription:
Heyma opened its Berkeley cafe on University Avenue near San Pablo in October 2023, one of the arrivals The Oaklandside identified that year as a new wave of Yemeni coffee shops bringing added spice and late hours to the region's cafe scene. The San Francisco outpost sits at 248 Ninth Street in western South of Market, a stretch better known for nightclubs and late-night food than for anywhere to sit without a drink in hand. Heyma serves no alcohol, and its trading hours make it one of the strongest alcohol-free evening options in the city: 7am to 11:30pm Sunday through Thursday and 7am to midnight on Friday and Saturday, which is later than most licensed bars in the surrounding blocks stop serving food.

The drinks are the traditional Yemeni set, built on whole spices rather than syrup pumps. The Heyma Latte is richly spiced with cardamom and cinnamon. Aden tea — the Yemeni black tea usually written adeni — is cooked with cardamom, ginger and cream until it is closer to a small dessert than a cup of tea. Mufawaar, the third of the house staples, is the spiced coffee finished with cream that gives most Yemeni menus their signature. Beyond those, the counter runs a conventional espresso programme with the pistachio and chocolate variations the category has made popular, and there is a kitchen: the venue trades as Heyma Yemeni Coffee & Brunch and puts out a full brunch menu through the day, which means an evening visit can be a meal rather than only a drink. The room is set up for staying, with communal seating and a steady late crowd, and its position beside the Ninth Street corridor gives people leaving nearby venues somewhere alcohol-free to end the night. That combination — a spiced drinks list built on cardamom, ginger and cinnamon, a kitchen running through the day, and a midnight close on weekends — is the pattern The Oaklandside identified when it wrote about the category's arrival in the Bay Area, and Heyma's San Francisco room is one of the clearest examples of it in the city.

venues.name: HG Sply Co.
venues.description: HG Sply Co. is a farm-to-table rooftop restaurant on Lower Greenville with a dedicated mocktail menu, skyline views and a health-conscious ethos that makes it one of Dallas's more inclusive rooms for non-drinkers. The #BeetBetter is the standout, combining beet, strawberry, lime, turbinado and Topo Chico into something genuinely complex; the Pina Colorita — coconut water, orange juice, pineapple and lime — is the lighter option; and the HG Mule swaps spirits for agave, lime and Buddha's Brew ginger kombucha, giving it a fermented bite most virgin mules lack. The 9,000-square-foot rooftop is partly covered and fitted with misters and firepits, so it works across seasons.
venues.longDescription:
HG Sply Co. sits at the heart of Lower Greenville — one of East Dallas's most walkable and socially mixed stretches — and it is one of the few full-service restaurants in the city that treats its mocktail programme as a genuine part of the drinks menu rather than an afterthought. The 9,000-square-foot rooftop, partly covered and outfitted with misters, firepits and greenery, makes it an unusually comfortable place to spend an evening without alcohol across every season, which matters more than it sounds in a city where the alternative is often a dark bar built entirely around drinking.

The #BeetBetter is the standout non-alcoholic drink: beet, strawberry, lime, turbinado and Topo Chico, a combination that is genuinely complex and drinks like something from a proper bar programme rather than a compromise. The Pina Colorita — coconut water, orange juice, pineapple and lime — is a lighter option, and the HG Mule mocktail swaps spirits for agave, lime and Buddha's Brew ginger kombucha, giving it a fermented bite that most virgin mules lack; the kombucha is the detail worth noting, because fermentation supplies exactly the sourness and depth that a spirit would otherwise carry. Dallasites101 records the menu running to at least three distinct mocktails, and staff are reported to improvise custom zero-proof builds on request.

HG Sply Co. is casual in dress and vibe — cornhole on the rooftop, big screens for game days, and a crowd that skews toward young professionals and neighbourhood regulars. It takes reservations via OpenTable, offers validated parking behind the building, and runs a Monday to Friday happy hour from 3pm to 6pm that includes half-price apps and cocktails. It works equally well for a weeknight dinner, when the rooftop is quieter and there is more table space, or a weekend brunch when it fills early. If parking is a concern, rideshare or the nearby valet on Greenville Avenue is the better call on Friday and Saturday nights.
venues.pressQuote: The Lower Greenville spot also has a mango refresher and the Guava Dawg for Dry January participants.

venues.name: Hi Stranger
venues.description: Hi Stranger is a cocktail bar at 27 Neil Road, a short walk from Maxwell MRT, that opened in July 2026 and describes itself as a modular bar where each menu becomes a new universe. Its first signature list, A World Aglow, is themed on volcanologists, with drinks such as The Crater and The Krafft Negroni. The printed menu marks every drink with a strength rating, and two are marked NO% instead: The Lemongrass Fizz, built on non-alcoholic spirits with lemongrass syrup, lime and soda, and The Berry Basil Smash, with non-alcoholic spirits, strawberry, raspberry, lemon and basil. Both sit on the same page as the classics rather than on a separate card for non-drinkers. It trades Tuesday to Saturday from 6pm.

The Berry Basil Smash (NO%: non-alcoholic spirits, strawberry, raspberry, lemon juice, basil, syrup)
