venues.longDescription:
Hi Stranger opened on Neil Road in July 2026, in the row of shophouses between Maxwell and Duxton Hill. The idea, in the bar's own words, is a playground where stories roam free: a modular bar whose menu is rebuilt around a new theme each time, never fixed and never finished. The first edition, Signature Menu #01 - A World Aglow, takes its cue from a documentary about volcanologists, and the drinks follow the theme by name. The Crater is a rum and coffee liqueur build with chocolate bitters, The Krafft Negroni layers Campari, sweet vermouth, gin and mezcal, and The Smoky Sour puts Islay whisky against lemon and egg white. Alongside the signatures runs a long classics section arranged by family: martinis and friends, Negroni and friends, Manhattan and friends, daiquiris, sours and old fashioneds, with a Ramos gin fizz made only when the sign at the bar is switched on. Happy hour runs from 6pm to 8pm every night it is open, and each cocktail ordered in that window comes with a complimentary wagyu tartare.

What earns it a listing here is how the zero-proof drinks are presented. Every drink on the menu carries a strength rating made of plus signs, and two carry the marker NO% instead. The Lemongrass Fizz (S$20) is built on non-alcoholic spirits with lemongrass syrup, lime juice and soda water, and reads as fresh, fizzy and herbaceous on the menu's own flavour tags. The Berry Basil Smash (S$22) uses non-alcoholic spirits with strawberry, raspberry, lemon juice, basil and syrup, and is the drink Honeycombers singled out in its August 2026 round-up of new bars, noting that it can be had with a zero-proof spirit. That is a short list, two drinks, and the bar does not claim more than that, but both are priced and built like the rest of the menu rather than treated as an afterthought, and a Coca-Cola Zero sits on the soft drinks line for anyone who wants nothing mixed at all. The room is small and reservations are taken online, with a 10 per cent service charge on top of the printed prices. Hours are Tuesday to Saturday from 6pm until about 11.30pm, closed Sunday and Monday, and the bar is reached from Maxwell MRT exit 3.
venues.pressQuote: the Berry Basil Smash ($22) is my recommendation – and you can have it with a zero-proof spirit!

venues.name: Hi-Wire Brewing (Biltmore Village)
venues.description: Hi-Wire Brewing's Biltmore Village taproom is a 27,000-square-foot production brewery and taproom at 2A Huntsman Pl, Asheville, opened in summer 2015, with vibrant indoor and outdoor murals, a large sun-shaded patio and free parking. Guajiro Cuban Comfort Food is permanently parked on site, and outside food is welcome. The taproom is pet- and family-friendly, open from 11am at weekends and 3pm on Mondays. IMPORTANT for anyone avoiding intoxicants: the taproom lists its non-alcoholic and THC options together, and alongside N/A beer, local High Noon nitro cold brew and local soda it sells Hi-Wire's own Hi-Jinks THC-infused sparkling water, produced in 2mg and 5mg doses in Original and Clementine. The N/A beer itself is not named on the venue's page. Note that the Hi-Wire facility destroyed by Helene flooding was the separate River Arts District site at 284 Lyman St, which reopened in May 2025 — not this Biltmore Village taproom.
signatureDrinks: Non-alcoholic beer (brand not named on the taproom menu — ask what is pouring)
venues.longDescription:
Hi-Wire Brewing's Biltmore Village site at 2A Huntsman Place is the company's 27,000-square-foot production brewery, opened in summer 2015 with a taproom attached. It is built for spending time in rather than passing through: vibrant murals inside and out, a large sun-shaded patio, free parking, and Guajiro Cuban Comfort Food permanently parked on site serving Cuban sandwiches and lechón asada, with outside food welcome too. It is pet-friendly and family-friendly, opening at 11am at weekends and from mid-afternoon on Mondays. Hi-Wire is a serious brewery by any measure — a World Beer Cup bronze in 2026 for its 10W-40 coconut candy bar stout, silvers in 2023, 2024 and 2025, and Great American Beer Festival golds in 2016, 2019 and 2021.

Two things need stating plainly. First, the geography: Helene destroyed a Hi-Wire facility in late September 2024, but that was the company's separate River Arts District site at 284 Lyman Street, which was submerged and took nearly eight months to reopen, celebrating its return on 24 May 2025. Co-founder Adam Charnack described it then as incredibly gratifying and, more than anything, great to feel somewhat normal again. That flood damage does not belong to this Biltmore Village taproom, which carries no closure notice. Second, and more important for readers here: this taproom lists its non-alcoholic and THC options together in a single sentence. Alongside non-alcoholic beer, a local nitro cold brew and local soda, it sells Hi-Wire's own Hi-Jinks THC-infused sparkling water, made in 2mg and 5mg doses in Original and Clementine flavours. That is alcohol-free but psychoactive, and the brewery's own page does not separate the two categories. If you are avoiding alcohol only, this is a comfortable room with plenty to do; if you are avoiding intoxicants generally, order by name and check what you are handed. The non-alcoholic beer is not named on the taproom's page, so ask what is pouring.

venues.name: Hi-Wire Brewing Charlotte
venues.description: Hi-Wire Brewing's South End Charlotte taproom is an 8,700-square-foot family-friendly space featuring two full bars, arcade games, and a 2,000-square-foot beer garden. The venue explicitly lists N/A beer, mocktails, kombucha, and soda alongside its 20-plus draft beer taps, making it one of the more inclusive craft taprooms in the neighborhood. The Noble Cider Bar within the taproom adds further variety with gluten-free cider and mead options.
venues.address: 340 W Tremont Ave, STE 140, Charlotte, NC 28203
venues.longDescription:
Hi-Wire Brewing's Charlotte taproom opened in July 2022 at 340 W Tremont Avenue in South End, directly across the street from Pins Mechanical, and Queen City Nerve readers voted it the city's Best New Brewery in 2024. The Asheville brewery built something closer to an entertainment venue than a tasting room here: 8,700 square feet with seating for more than three hundred, two full bars, 360 degrees of vibrant indoor murals, a large sun-shaded patio, and arcade games, ping pong, foosball and shuffleboard through the space. There is no kitchen — the taproom points guests to nearby options including Benny Ferrovia's pizza and The Dumpling Lady, and outside food is welcome while outside drinks are not. It is pet-friendly and family-friendly until 8pm, after which it becomes 18 and over. Parking is limited and free immediately in front, with towing enforced elsewhere in the apartment lot.

The non-alcoholic offering is stated on the taproom's own page and is broader than most breweries manage: non-alcoholic beer, mocktails, kombucha and soda, so a non-drinker has a choice of formats rather than a single can. What Hi-Wire does not do is publish the specific items — no names, ABVs or prices appear anywhere online, and the taproom's live tap list does not log its non-alcoholic pours, so what is actually available on a given evening has to be asked about at the bar. One thing does need stating plainly, because it sits in the same sentence as the non-alcoholic list on the brewery's own site: Hi-Wire also serves Hi-Jinks, its THC-infused sparkling water. That is alcohol-free but psychoactive, and it is offered alongside the mocktails rather than separately from them. For anyone avoiding alcohol only, this is a genuinely comfortable room with plenty to do and no pressure to drink; for anyone avoiding intoxicants generally, order by name and check what you are being handed.
venues.pressQuote: Best New Brewery (Last Two Years) — Winner: Hi-Wire Brewing Charlotte

venues.name: Hidden Gem
venues.description: Hidden Gem is St. Louis's disco dive bar: roughly 300 disco balls, a blush-pink glitter-flecked bar, karaoke and trivia nights, and weekend dance parties in Midtown, from Golden Gems founders (and sisters) Amanda Helman and Susan Logsdon. The drink menu was built to be inclusive from day one, and a dedicated Spirit Free section runs year-round — the Nah-Hito, a choose-your-own-flavor Spirit Free Moscow Mule running from strawberry to lavender to jalapeño, and The Apple's Cider — alongside WellBeing Golden Wheat from St. Louis's own alcohol-free brewery and Mighty Kind CBD seltzer. Every January the 21-plus bar goes further with an exclusive Dry January menu.
venues.hours: Mon closed; Tue-Thu 4pm-12:30am; Fri-Sat 4pm-1am; Sun closed
venues.longDescription:
Hidden Gem opened December 20, 2023, at 3118 Locust Street in Midtown — the first bar from sisters Amanda Helman and Susan Logsdon, founders of the St. Louis accessories brand Golden Gems. They call it a disco dive bar, and the label is literal: roughly 300 disco balls, hung one by one by the owners themselves, shimmer over the two-story room, anchored by a 60-foot blush-pink resin bar embedded with glitter and a second-level lounge styled like a 1970s living room. Three months in, Feast Magazine declared the place a certified hit in Midtown.

Zero-proof drinks were part of the plan before the doors opened. When the bar debuted, bar manager Tiffany Kaltenbach told St. Louis Magazine that spirit-free options were among the most common requests from future guests: "We wanted the drink menu to also be inclusive." That intent holds on the current menu, which carries a dedicated Spirit Free section year-round: the Nah-Hito (sparkling water, citrus-mint simple, lime juice), a build-your-own Spirit Free Moscow Mule in flavors from strawberry and raspberry to jalapeño, lavender, and hibiscus, and The Apple's Cider (apple-cinnamon simple, lemon, club soda). Alcohol-free beer includes WellBeing Golden Wheat from St. Louis's own dedicated NA brewery, plus Mighty Kind CBD seltzer. Each January the bar goes further with an exclusive Dry January menu — 2025's brought playful builds like Clear Eyes, Full Hearts and the hibiscus-cayenne Desert Rose.

St. Louis Magazine's guide to nonalcoholic cocktails in the city recommends the Nah-Hito and sums up the appeal: a pink bar, quilted stools, an indoor marquee, and zero-proof cocktails for dancing the night away. Expect programming most nights — karaoke, trivia, drag, and weekend dance parties — in a 21-plus room where ordering spirit-free is entirely normal. As the owners put it to Feast, "You can get a really great craft cocktail here or you can get a Stag. There are also great non-alcoholic options."
venues.pressQuote: Pink bar, cozy quilted bar stools, an indoor marquee, and zero-proof cocktails are great when you want to dance the night away on a glittering dance floor.

venues.name: HiFi at The Finn
venues.description: HiFi at The Finn is a Tokyo-inspired vinyl listening lounge on the mezzanine of The Finn, a chef-driven food hall inside the historic Jones on Main building in Downtown Houston. Built around a curated turntable system with rotating DJ sets Wednesday through Saturday, the room is kept deliberately quieter than the food hall below so the music stays audible. It opened in 2025, and its bar food now comes from sister concept Nyam Nyam Korean BBQ. The most recent published list of its zero-proof cocktails is from Dry January 2026, when several were built on Cut Above alcohol-free spirits — Tang, Tang, Taaang with Cut Above tequila, lime oleo, agave and house-made tangerine soda, and No Speed Limit, which layered Pathfinder Hemp & Root with Cut Above whiskey, black cherry and coffee. The bar does not publish its current drinks list, so ask what is on.
venues.hours: Mon-Tue closed; Wed 4pm-9pm; Thu-Fri 4pm-12am; Sat 6pm-12am; Sun closed
venues.longDescription:
HiFi at The Finn is a vinyl listening lounge and craft cocktail bar on the mezzanine of The Finn, a chef-driven food hall inside the historic Jones on Main building at 712 Main Street in Downtown Houston. It is modelled on Japan's kissa and listening-bar tradition, built around a record collection and a curated turntable system, with rotating DJ sets from Wednesday to Saturday. The room is kept deliberately quieter than the food hall below so the music remains audible. It soft-opened on 1 May 2025 and held its grand opening on 27 June 2025.

The bar food is now curated by The Finn's sister concept Nyam Nyam Korean BBQ. When HiFi opened, the menu was Filipino-inspired small plates from James Beard Award-winning chef Tom Cunanan.

The most recent published list of its zero-proof cocktails is from Dry January 2026, when several were built on Cut Above's alcohol-free spirits. Tang, Tang, Taaang paired Cut Above tequila with lime oleo, agave and a house-made tangerine soda — oleo being oleo-saccharum, the aromatic oil drawn out of citrus peel by steeping it in sugar, a labour-intensive punch-house technique almost never applied to a non-alcoholic drink. No Speed Limit layered Pathfinder Hemp & Root with Cut Above whiskey, black cherry and coffee; Pathfinder is a fermented hemp-and-root distillate with a bitter, woody character. Kiwi No. 0 kept it simple with fresh kiwi, citrus and crushed ice, and Pine the Time Away ran pineapple, ginger, agave and lime with No Sec liqueur. The bar does not publish its current drinks list online, so treat these as examples and ask what is on.

The listening-bar format is the strongest argument here. The music is the reason to be in the room, volume sits where conversation is possible but not compulsory, and there is no bar to stand at — which removes the unstructured time that makes a night out sober hard work. Open Wednesday to Saturday, to midnight Thursday through Saturday.
venues.pressQuote: HiFi at The Finn's Dry January lineup swaps booze for bold flavors, with zero-proof cocktails that keep the edge.

venues.name: High & Dry
venues.description: High & Dry is a fully alcohol-free coffee-and-cocktail bar that opened in 2024 in Bushwick, on the Bed-Stuy border at 899 Broadway, tucked beneath the elevated J/M/Z tracks near Myrtle Avenue. It was opened by a team that includes Tobly McSmith (a young-adult novelist for HarperCollins), Garret Peterson (a former Coney Island paramedic), Breandan Carroll, and Daniel Stettner (a graphic designer who handles branding), several of whom have worked across other NYC sober spaces. The name is a play on its concept: the caffeine drinks get you "high," and the no-alcohol policy keeps it "dry." Open daily from noon to midnight, it pitches itself as a "third space" for creatives, remote workers, and night owls who want bar-style socializing without booze. The menu runs to spirit-free cocktails, coffee and espresso, matcha, tea, and rotating kombucha on tap, with most drinks priced under $8.
venues.longDescription:
High & Dry opened in 2024 at 899 Broadway in Bushwick, on the Bed-Stuy border, tucked beneath the elevated J/M/Z tracks near Myrtle Avenue — a location that is pure Brooklyn in a way a polished Manhattan sober bar could never be. It is fully alcohol-free, and the name is the concept: the caffeine drinks get you high, the no-alcohol policy keeps it dry. The founding team is an unusual mix that says something about who builds these places — Tobly McSmith, a young-adult novelist for HarperCollins; Garret Peterson, a former Coney Island paramedic; Breandan Carroll; and Daniel Stettner, a graphic designer who handles the branding — several of whom have worked across other New York sober spaces.

It runs from midday to midnight every day of the week, which is the detail that makes it work. A bar that closes at 6pm is a café; one open until midnight is somewhere you can actually spend an evening. The pitch is a third space for creatives, remote workers and night owls who want bar-style socialising without alcohol, and the format serves all three across a single day. The menu spans spirit-free cocktails, coffee and espresso, matcha, tea and rotating kombucha on tap, with most drinks priced under $8 — genuinely important, because a great many alcohol-free bars price their drinks at cocktail rates and quietly exclude the people most likely to need them. Named builds include a New York Egg Cream, a Butterfly Pea Lemonade and a Laura Palmer.

Co-owner Garret Peterson's description of what happens when people walk in is the best short account of why rooms like this matter: "People come in, and they're shocked that people are in here having fun without alcohol, and it makes me very happy to see that." The surprise is the point — most people have simply never seen it.
venues.pressQuote: People come in, and they're shocked that people are in here having fun without alcohol, and it makes me very happy to see that.

venues.name: High Bank Distillery Co.
venues.description: High Bank Distillery Co. is a working distillery with a full pub attached, established in 2017 on Goodale Boulevard in Grandview Yard. It takes its name from the high bank above the fork of the Scioto and Olentangy rivers, and produces bourbon, rye, gin, vodka and apple brandy on site alongside a modern American kitchen serving lunch, dinner, brunch and late night. Unusually for a distillery pub, it keeps non-alcoholic cocktails on the menu year-round rather than only through Dry January: local coverage currently names a non-alcoholic mule, the blackberry-purée Berry Burlesque, a Cinnamon Apple and Wings Over Ohio, with earlier menus carrying a Beachside Coffee of cold brew, honey syrup, blood orange and citrus and a cranberry-vanilla Lost Jewel. The list rotates seasonally.

venues.longDescription:
High Bank Distillery Co. was established in 2017 at 1051 Goodale Boulevard, in the Grandview Yard development just west of the Olentangy. The name refers to the high bank above the fork where the Olentangy meets the Scioto — a Columbus geographical reference rather than a whiskey one. It is a genuine production site: bourbon, straight bourbon, bottled-in-bond, uncut and unfiltered expressions, rye, a bourbon-barrel four-peel gin, vodka and an apple brandy are all distilled on the premises, alongside limited releases and a nocino. Attached to the still house is a full distillery pub with free off-street parking, serving lunch, dinner, weekend brunch and late-night food.

For a distillery — a category where the whole business model points towards drinking the product — the non-alcoholic list is more considered than it needs to be, and it runs all year rather than appearing for January. Local coverage of the current menu names four: a non-alcoholic mule built seasonally, most recently on apple cider syrup and ginger beer; the Berry Burlesque, which uses a blackberry purée as its base; a Cinnamon Apple; and Wings Over Ohio. Earlier iterations of the same list carried a Beachside Coffee — cold brew with honey syrup, blood orange purée and fresh citrus — and the Lost Jewel, a cranberry-vanilla drink finished with mint and citrus. The rotation is the point: the zero-proof drinks change with the seasons in step with the cocktail list rather than sitting static at the bottom of the menu. Worth knowing that Sunday service ends at 3pm, and that the address, while carrying a Columbus postal designation, sits inside the Grandview Yard district rather than downtown. The pub itself is a large, casual room built for volume rather than intimacy, which makes it one of the easier bookings in the metro for a mixed group where some people are drinking and some are not. Brunch runs at weekends, the kitchen serves late, and parking is free and off-street — small logistical points, but the kind that decide where a group actually ends up. The distillery also runs tours and a bottle shop on site for anyone visiting for the production side.
venues.pressQuote: Another establishment with year-round mocktails is High Bank Distillery, including their non-alcoholic mule, Berry Burlesque, Cinnamon Apple, and Wings Over Ohio.

venues.name: High Climate Tea Company
venues.description: High Climate Tea Company is a downtown single-origin Chinese and Taiwanese loose-leaf tea shop and lounge whose signature is the tea "flight" — a roughly 30-minute guided tasting at a tea bar, with a tea "bartender" walking you through each tea and its heritage, plus a back lounge for shared pots. It is a calm, alcohol-free social third space built around the ritual of tea rather than a grab-and-go counter — a quiet counterpoint to Asheville's busier bar scene.
venues.address: 12 S Lexington Ave, Ste 1, Asheville, NC 28801
venues.longDescription:
High Climate Tea Company is a Chinese loose-leaf tea shop and tea bar at 12 S Lexington Avenue in downtown Asheville, and it is a specialist operation rather than a café with a tea list. The owner's route into it explains the depth: formerly an English teacher, their life changed when they began training under Uncle Gee and Ming Duong at Vital Tea Leaf in San Francisco's Chinatown, and they now travel to China every year with them to source directly. The retail side runs to more than two hundred distinct teas and wares, priced from a few dollars up to $579 for an aged puerh cake — a 2013 Lao Man'e — with a 2008 Lao Ban Zhang at $459 and a Phoenix cake at $85. That is a serious cellar for a shop this size, and it is the sort of range you normally have to buy online and hope.

The part that matters for a non-drinker is that you can sit and drink here rather than only buy. The shop runs a tea bar offering Gung Fu Cha — thirty-minute guided tastings at the counter, brewed in the traditional Chinese style of many short infusions from a small pot, which is a genuinely different experience from a mug of tea and closer in attention to a tasting flight. The service list is priced simply: Bai Mu Dan white tea at $8, described as producing a buttery-textured liquid with the fragrance of a fresh-baked fruit danish; Silver Needle at $8, from young Anhui buds with an aroma of white peach; a Jasmine Silver Needle at $10; a Jasmine Pearl at $8; Dragonwell at $8; and a Jade Spring green tea from Jiangsu at $6 to $10 across three grades. Nothing here is alcoholic and nothing is infused with anything else. Two caveats: the shop opens 12pm to 6pm Thursday through Monday only, and its food service has at points been suspended, so confirm before travelling for anything beyond tea.

venues.name: High Praise Rooftop Bar
venues.description: High Praise is the rooftop bar at the InterContinental San Antonio Riverwalk, and its menu has a Zero Proof Cocktails section — Mediodia, Autumn in Paradise and Currently Vibing, each made with Ritual Zero Proof spirit — plus Heineken 0.0 and Athletic Run Wild IPA in cans. It is a weekend-only room, opening Friday evening and running through Sunday afternoon, which makes it a specific rather than a general recommendation. But it adds a second downtown rooftop with something properly made for a non-drinker, and given how many visitors to San Antonio stay within a few blocks of here, that redundancy is genuinely useful. Between this and The Moon's Daughters at the Thompson, a non-drinker downtown has an actual choice of rooftops rather than one option to hope is open.
venues.address: 111 E Pecan St, San Antonio, TX 78205

venues.longDescription:
High Praise sits on the roof of the InterContinental San Antonio Riverwalk on East Pecan Street, in the middle of the downtown hotel district. Its menu has a Zero Proof Cocktails section of three drinks, each made with Ritual Zero Proof spirit: Mediodia (the tequila alternative with cinnamon syrup, grapefruit and lime), Autumn in Paradise (the rum alternative with apple spice syrup, ginger beer and lime) and Currently Vibing (the whiskey alternative with pineapple, lemon and vanilla). Heineken 0.0 and Athletic Run Wild IPA come in cans.

The value here is redundancy, which sounds like faint praise and is not. San Antonio's downtown hotel corridor holds an enormous share of the city's visitors, and a large proportion of any group staying there will include somebody who is not drinking — pregnant, driving, in recovery, on antibiotics, or simply not in the mood. One rooftop with named zero-proof drinks is luck. Two, within walking distance of each other, starts to be a scene. Between High Praise and The Moon's Daughters at the Thompson, a non-drinker downtown has an actual choice of rooftops rather than a single option to hope is open.

Mediodia means midday, which suits Sunday, the one day the room opens at noon.

The schedule is the significant limitation and needs stating plainly: closed Monday through Thursday. It opens Friday and Saturday from 5pm to 10pm and Sunday from noon to 6pm, and it is 21 and over after 7pm. This is a weekend venue, and a midweek visitor will find it shut. Anyone downtown on a Tuesday should head for The Moon's Daughters, which serves from 7am daily, or Double Standard a few streets away. Within its window, though, the view over the river and the named drinks make it a straightforward recommendation. Sunday afternoon is the time to catch it in daylight, when the room opens at noon.
venues.pressQuote: With both indoor and outdoor options, enjoy an evening in the Alamo City from up above before enjoying a zero-proof cocktail like the Lime in Coconut or Mediodia.

venues.name: High Stakes Rooftop
venues.description: High Stakes is a rooftop bar and grill on the top of the Tempo by Hilton at the NuLu end of East Jefferson Street, with sweeping views over downtown Louisville and a bar carrying more than a hundred bourbons. Its non-alcoholic drinks are the product of a deliberate partnership rather than an afterthought: the bar works with Elixir Kombucha to build a named alcohol-free list, including Treat for Max with caramel butter syrup, Fire & Ice on a lemon ginger tea syrup, and the Collius with pineapple Szechuan syrup — three genuinely unusual flavour directions. It opens at 4pm Tuesday to Saturday and closes Sunday and Monday.
venues.hours: Mon closed; Tue-Thu 4pm-10pm; Fri-Sat 4pm-11pm; Sun closed
signatureDrinks: Treat for Max (caramel butter syrup, Elixir Kombucha)
Fire & Ice (lemon ginger tea syrup, Elixir Kombucha)
venues.longDescription:
The Tempo by Hilton on East Jefferson Street opened at the NuLu end of downtown and put High Stakes on its roof: an American grill with a hundred-plus bourbon list and a view across the Louisville skyline. Like every rooftop it trades partly on the view, and like every bourbon-forward Louisville bar it could easily have left non-drinkers with a lemonade.

What it did instead is worth noting as a model. Rather than buying a bottle of non-alcoholic spirit and calling the problem solved, the bar partnered with Elixir Kombucha and built a named list around fermented kombucha bases and house syrups. That produces drinks that taste like nothing else on the menu rather than like diminished versions of the cocktails: Treat for Max runs a caramel butter syrup, which is a dessert-adjacent direction almost no alcohol-free menu attempts; Fire & Ice is built on a lemon ginger tea syrup, so the heat is aromatic rather than spirituous; and the Collius uses a pineapple Szechuan syrup, where the Szechuan pepper supplies the tingling numbness that alcohol would otherwise contribute. Kombucha has trace alcohol from fermentation — typically under 0.5% ABV, the same threshold as non-alcoholic beer — which is worth knowing if your abstinence is strict.

Practically, the hours are tighter than the address suggests: Tuesday through Saturday from 4pm, closing at 10pm midweek and 11pm on Friday and Saturday, dark on Sunday and Monday. It is two blocks from bar Vetti on East Market, which has the city's best-constructed zero-proof negroni, so NuLu supports a full evening without a drink in it. Being a hotel rooftop, it also takes solo guests at the bar more comfortably than a destination restaurant would.
venues.pressQuote: High Stakes Rooftop Grill has partnered with Elixir Kombucha to create an array of non-alcoholic drinks including Treat for Max with caramel butter syrup, Fire & Ice with lemon ginger tea syrup, and Collius with pineapple Szechuan syrup.

venues.name: Higher Ground
venues.description: Higher Ground is a farm-driven modern British bistro on the fringe of Manchester's Chinatown, run by three friends — chef Joseph Otway, wine and drinks lead Daniel Craig Martin and general manager Richard Cossins — who met working at Dan Barber's Blue Hill at Stone Barns in New York. It opened permanently in February 2023 in Faulkner House on New York Street after an earlier pop-up, and around 90% of its produce comes from Cinderwood Market Garden, the team's own regenerative farm in Cheshire, feeding a daily-changing menu of seasonal vegetables, whole-animal butchery, hand-rolled pasta and fish cooked over coal. It holds a Bib Gourmand in the 2026 Michelin Guide — named Michelin's first-ever Bib of the Month for Great Britain and Ireland — and placed 36th in the 2025 National Restaurant Awards. Alongside a natural-wine list of small low-intervention European growers, the team pours a no- and low-alcohol selection reviewers have singled out as exceptional.

venues.hours: Mon-Tue closed; Wed 5pm-10pm; Thu 12:30pm-1:30pm & 5pm-10pm; Fri-Sat 12:30pm-2pm & 5:30pm-11:30pm; Sun closed
venues.longDescription:
Higher Ground is run by a trio of friends — chef Joseph Otway, wine and drinks lead Daniel Craig Martin, and general manager Richard Cossins — who met working at Dan Barber's Blue Hill at Stone Barns in New York. It opened permanently in February 2023 in Faulkner House on New York Street, on the fringe of Manchester's Chinatown, after an earlier pop-up. Around 90% of the produce comes from Cinderwood Market Garden, the team's own regenerative farm in Cheshire, feeding a daily-changing menu built on seasonal vegetables, whole-animal butchery, hand-rolled pasta and fish cooked over coal.

The restaurant carries serious critical weight. It holds a Bib Gourmand in the 2026 Michelin Guide — Michelin named it the first-ever 'Bib of the Month' for Great Britain & Ireland — and it has appeared in the National Restaurant Awards for several years running, placing at number 36 in the 2025 top 100. That pedigree makes its attention to non-drinkers notable rather than incidental.

Drinks are treated with the same curiosity as the food. The wine list spotlights low-intervention, small-scale winemakers from across Europe, and running alongside it is a considered no- and low-alcohol offering that reviewers have described as exceptional, with some genuinely unusual choices — a deliberate counterpart to the wine program rather than an afterthought. Because the drinks list, like the menu, moves with what is available, the specific no-and-low pours change regularly.

The room itself is compact and unfussy: an open kitchen, house music, and a low, humming buzz, seating a small number of covers across à la carte and shared-menu formats. It reads as one of the most quietly ambitious dining rooms in the city, and one where an alcohol-free guest is looked after with real intent.
venues.pressQuote: The modern British menu is understated but original, perfectly matching the low, humming buzz that makes diners feel like they're in the heart of Manchester's happening restaurant action.

venues.name: Hillman Beer
venues.description: Hillman Beer is a family-owned brewpub that opened in April 2017 at 25 Sweeten Creek Road near Biltmore Village, run by brothers Brad and Greig Hillman with Greig's wife Brandi. Brad picked up homebrewing in 2006 while living in Brooklyn, and the first beer out of the garage was a Dunkelweizen they named Dingaudamnit — which tells you the register the place operates in. His brief was a brewpub with a comfortable environment and a cool vibe, and the beer has backed the ambition up with Great American Beer Festival medals in three consecutive years within the brewery's first three. The taproom keeps the non-drinker in mind: Athletic Brewing non-alcoholic beer on hand, plus locally made Devil's Foot craft sodas — an Asheville mocktail-base staple — kombucha and soda. A relaxed, food-forward brewery where the alcohol-free options are genuine craft rather than the usual cola-or-water default.
venues.longDescription:
Hillman Beer opened in April 2017 at 25 Sweeten Creek Road near Biltmore Village, a family brewery run by brothers Brad and Greig Hillman with Greig's wife Brandi. Brad picked up homebrewing in 2006 while living in Brooklyn, and the first beer out of the garage was a Dunkelweizen they named Dingaudamnit — which tells you the register the place operates in. His brief was modest and has held: a brewpub with a nice comfortable environment, a cool atmosphere and a cool vibe, in a city where, as he put it, people have proven that they love beer and going to breweries. The results back the ambition — Great American Beer Festival medals in three consecutive years within the brewery's first three, a bronze in 2017 for Four Fat Baby, silver for its ESB in 2018 and gold for that same ESB in 2019. The taproom has a shaded area at the back beside Sweeten Creek and generous seating out front, a kitchen that closes at 9pm, and a leashed-dogs-welcome policy inside the brewery. A second location opened in Old Fort in July 2020.

Two things are worth knowing. On Helene: Hillman's own account is that its Asheville site sits in an area that did not experience the same level of flood impact as the neighbourhoods closer to the French Broad river corridor, and both its locations came through open and serving. That is a meaningful distinction in a city where a mile in either direction determined whether a business survived. On the non-alcoholic side, the brewery is explicit about the principle — it states that non-alcoholic options are available so that designated drivers and sober-curious guests never feel like an afterthought — but it does not publish what those options are. No non-alcoholic item appears on its live tap list, and no brand, style or price is named anywhere. The intent is clearly stated; the specifics have to be asked for at the bar.
venues.pressQuote: Athletic Brewery non-alcoholic beer, Devils Foot, kombucha and soda.

venues.name: Hillside Farmacy
venues.description: Hillside Farmacy is a family-owned New American bistro in East Austin, housed inside a Texas Historical Landmark building that was originally a 1950s pharmacy. The restaurant honors the building's history with a 'Soda Fountain' menu of house-made syrups and herbal blends — Visit Austin describes them as 'craft elixirs' rather than standard soft drinks, and the venue's own framing invites guests to order any of them 'with or without a splash of booze.' Beyond the soda fountain, the menu is farm-to-table New American: proteins from Texas ranchers and the Gulf Coast, Texas wildflower honey, microgreens from Joe's, mushrooms from Hi-Fi, locally roasted Proud Mary and Fara coffee, and Evergreen Chai brewed in East Austin. The space is family-friendly with three dining rooms and dog-friendly heated and cooled outdoor patios. The cocktail and wine programs lean into Texas distilleries (Still Austin Whiskey appears in their signature Old Fashioned) and approachable wines.
venues.longDescription:
Hillside Farmacy is a family-owned New American bistro at 1209 East 11th Street, in a Texas Historical Landmark building that spent its earlier life as a 1950s pharmacy. The restaurant leans into that history rather than decorating with it, and the result is the most literal soda fountain in the city: a menu section of house-made syrups and herbal blends that Visit Austin described as craft elixirs rather than standard soft drinks.

The house framing is the detail that makes this venue genuinely useful. Any drink on the fountain menu can be ordered with or without a splash of booze — which quietly removes the whole social transaction of asking for a mocktail. Nobody has to specify a category, order off a separate list or explain themselves; two people order the same drink and one of them has alcohol in it. That is a small piece of menu design doing more for a non-drinker at a table than most dedicated zero-proof lists manage.

The Country Doctor is the signature, served hot or cold, built on ginger, fresh apple and cinnamon — a drink that works in a Texas August over ice and in January warmed through, which is more range than most cocktails have.

The kitchen is farm-to-table in a way that is specific rather than decorative: proteins from Texas ranchers and the Gulf Coast, Texas wildflower honey, microgreens from Joe's, mushrooms from Hi-Fi, locally roasted Proud Mary and Fara coffee, and Evergreen Chai brewed in East Austin. The same sourcing runs through the fountain syrups.

There are three dining rooms and heated and cooled outdoor patios, both dog-friendly, and the room is genuinely family-friendly — which, combined with the all-day trade and the soda fountain, makes it one of the easier places in Austin to bring a group with mixed drinking habits and have nobody's evening be about it.
venues.pressQuote: Located in a beautifully restored 1950s pharmacy, Hillside Farmacy offers a nostalgic and sophisticated take on non-alcoholic refreshments. Their 'Soda Fountain' menu features house-made syrups and herbal blends that feel more like craft elixirs than standard soft drinks.

venues.name: Hinterland
venues.description: Hinterland is Manchester's only permanent, purpose-built fully alcohol-free bar and vegan café, tucked into the basement of the Manchester Buddhist Centre in the Northern Quarter. Opened in June 2024 as a registered community interest company, it was founded by Stephen Jeffreys — drawing on his own recovery — with friends from the Buddhist Centre. The menu runs to eight alcohol-free cocktails alongside no- and low-alcohol beers, wines, ciders, kombucha and speciality teas, with vegan food from the Wholesome Junkies pop-up kitchen. Expect live music, spoken word and sober socials in a calm, dark-green room.

venues.longDescription:
Hinterland opened its doors on 18 June 2024 as Manchester's first and only permanent, purpose-built alcohol-free bar and café — a not-for-profit community interest company rather than a commercial venture. It was founded by Stephen Jeffreys, who after years of alcohol addiction and several years sober wanted a social space that did not revolve around drinking ("Going through recovery was an isolating experience for me, as nearly every social activity would be centred around drinking"), together with friends from the Manchester Buddhist Centre including Hatthaka Sanghadhara. The bar occupies the basement beneath the Buddhist Centre on Turner Street, in the heart of the Northern Quarter.

The space is a calm, low-lit retreat done out in rich dark greens and warm wood tones — deliberately unlike the noisy high-street bar scene, yet still recognisably a bar. It is dog-friendly, takes no reservations, and doubles as an event space: the weekly programme runs from live music and spoken word to guest poets, workshops and sober socials, welcoming anyone sober, sober-curious or simply after a night out without alcohol.

Because Hinterland is entirely alcohol-free, everything behind the bar is zero-proof. The cocktail list runs to eight house drinks, among them the NoGroni — an alcohol-free take on the 1919 Negroni, short and bittersweet — and The Accountant Martini, built on Lyre's White Cane with passion fruit, lime and a hint of vanilla. Beyond cocktails there is a proper bank of no- and low-alcohol beers, wines and ciders, plus kombucha, speciality teas, coffee and hot chocolate. Food comes from the Wholesome Junkies vegan pop-up kitchen — burgers, loaded fries, tots, ramen, crunchy mushroom 'chicken' and corn ribs — making it a genuine all-day café as well as an evening bar.
venues.pressQuote: Manchester's only permanent and purpose-built alcohol-free bar and cafe

venues.name: HK Brewing Collective
venues.description: A women-owned, queer-owned kombucha brewery and taproom in the Ballpark/Granary district that doubles as one of the metro's strongest zero-proof cocktail programs — winner of City Weekly's "Best Zero-Proof Cocktails" in 2024 and 2025. The taproom opened in spring 2023 inside a converted former auto-repair shop, the project of founder Hannah Hendrickson, who began brewing Han's Kombucha while at the University of Utah, and co-owner Kate Lubing. Non-alcoholic Han's Kombucha is fermented on-site, poured in a build-your-own flight, and forms the base of many crafted zero-proof cocktails on the taproom's "Free Your Spirits" list, such as the Persephone and the HK Spritz. As Lubing puts it, whether a guest is sober-curious, fully sober, a cocktail lover or a beer drinker, the space is built so everyone feels equally considered.

venues.longDescription:
Han's Kombucha — the house booch poured throughout the taproom — has been voted Utah's Best Kombucha three years running, and the draft list rotates through staples like Ginger Hibiscus, Grapefruit Rosemary, Pineapple Cactus Nectar, Raspberry Rose and White Peach Champagne, plus a taproom-only Brewer's Pick. The 5,300-square-foot space, decorated in a warm modern-southwestern style with a dog-friendly patio, also hosts yoga, co-working and local-artist events, making it a genuine community hub rather than just a bar.

The non-alcoholic program is a deliberate centerpiece: City Cast Salt Lake's mocktail guide singles the taproom out, noting that many of the NA drinks include the house-made kombucha — and that you can order a whole kombucha flight.

The zero-proof cocktails run under their own heading, "Free Your Spirits", with a line on the menu confirming that every drink in the section is non-alcoholic. Eight builds sit there: the HK Spritz of N/A gin, honey, pineapple and red apple rhubarb kombucha at $11; the Persephone of N/A bourbon, pomegranate, honey and ginger hibiscus kombucha and the Talk to the Peach of N/A Aperol, peach, lemon, pomegranate and white peach champagne kombucha, both $12; the Bloody Maria of N/A tequila, lemon, green onion, tomato and soda and the Razzle Dazzle of clementine, raspberry and Woody’s N/A prosecco, both $14; the Dirty Earl of cold brew, Earl Grey, lavender and oat milk at $6; a $3 Holy Trinity shooter of ginger, lemon and pineapple; and a bartender’s-choice FAFO Roulette at $13. That is a longer non-alcoholic list than most cocktail bars carry, and it is priced at or below the alcoholic equivalents rather than at a premium.

Han’s Kombucha itself pours at $6 for a 16oz draft or $10 for a flight, and there are further non-alcoholic options beyond the house brand: a rotating Athletic Brewing beer and a rotating Original Sin cider at $6, and Woody’s N/A sparkling prosecco by the glass at $10. Cans and growlers of Han’s are available to take home. The taproom does serve full spirits, beer and wine alongside all of this, so it is a mixed room rather than a dry one, but a non-drinker can order across the whole evening without falling back on soda.
venues.pressQuote: I've always enjoyed the NA drinks here because a lot of them include the yummy house made kombucha. You can even go crazy and do a whole kombucha flight.

venues.name: Hojoko
venues.description: Hojoko is the Japanese tavern at the Verb Hotel in the Fenway, opened by Tim and Nancy Cushman of o ya as a louder, later counterpart to their tasting-menu restaurant. Maki, ramen, robata skewers and a vinyl lounge share the room with a drinks list that is best known for scorpion bowls, and the bar keeps a printed section called DRY/DAMP for drinks with no alcohol in them. All four are $13 and shadow a classic: Blush and Bashful is a grapefruit spritz of grapefruit and lime juice, simple syrup and fresh mint; Coco Crush Colada uses coconut cream, pineapple juice and a house-made pineapple shrub; Citrus and Salt is a margarita build of lime, lemon and orange with an optional Tajin rim and muddled jalapeno; and the Golden Nojito layers mint syrup and the same pineapple shrub.

venues.longDescription:
Hojoko occupies the ground floor of the Verb Hotel at 1271 Boylston Street, a mid-century motor inn reborn as a rock-and-roll hotel a short walk from Fenway Park. It comes from Tim and Nancy Cushman, whose o ya is one of the most decorated restaurants in the city, and it was designed as the opposite of that room: loud, late, covered in music memorabilia, with a vinyl lounge and a menu that runs creative maki alongside ramen, robata skewers and a bacon-wrapped, jalapeno-stuffed hot dog. It is open until midnight six nights a week, which in the Fenway makes it a genuine late option rather than a dinner-only one.

The drinks list is famous for its large-format tiki bowls, but the bar also prints a DRY/DAMP section for guests who want the same care with no alcohol. Each of the four costs $13 and is built as a shadow of a specific classic rather than as sweetened juice. Blush and Bashful is the grapefruit spritz, made with grapefruit juice, lime juice, simple syrup and fresh mint. Coco Crush Colada stands in for the pina colada, using coconut cream, pineapple juice and a pineapple shrub syrup the bar makes in house. Citrus and Salt is the classic margarita rebuilt from lime, lemon and orange juice with simple syrup, and the kitchen will do a spicy version with a Tajin rim and muddled jalapeno on request. The Golden Nojito is the pineapple mojito, layering mint simple syrup, the house pineapple shrub, fresh mint, pineapple juice and lime juice. Time Out has given the restaurant a five-star review, and the house shrubs on the zero-proof side are the same ones used behind the full-proof list. Time Out's five-star review describes a drink list that runs to twenty sakes, frozen tiki classics and large-format pours served from the tank; the DRY/DAMP block sits on the same menu as those rather than on a card you have to ask for.

venues.name: Holey Moley Golf Club
venues.description: Holey Moley Golf Club is an indoor mini-golf bar on East Fourth Street, built around elaborately themed holes with a full bar attached — an activity venue where the drinking is optional scenery rather than the point of the evening. Its zero-proof options are named menu items rather than off-list requests: Pink Lightning, and a frozen Mock O'Colada that puts a non-drinker in the same territory as everyone else holding a frozen drink. Visit Austin's official zero-proof guide names both. It opens from midday most days, runs to midnight on Fridays and Saturdays, and sits in the middle of the East Fourth bar strip, so it slots easily into a night out with a mixed group.
venues.longDescription:
Holey Moley Golf Club is an indoor mini-golf course wrapped around a bar, on East Fourth Street in the middle of one of Austin's densest going-out strips. The holes are heavily themed and deliberately absurd, and the format means an evening here has a structure that does not depend on drinking — you are moving, playing and competing, and the glass is incidental.

For a non-drinker that is the core value, and it is the same argument as any good activity bar: the hardest part of a sober night out is usually not the absence of alcohol but the absence of anything else to do. A venue that supplies the something-else removes the problem rather than compensating for it.

The drinks are a step above the category's usual standard in one specific way: the zero-proof options are printed, named items rather than something you have to negotiate. Pink Lightning and the frozen Mock O'Colada both appear on Visit Austin's official zero-proof guide. The Mock O'Colada is the more interesting of the two in practice — frozen drinks are strongly social objects, and holding the same frozen glass as the rest of a group is a small thing that materially changes how a night feels when you are the one not drinking.

The grade here is honest rather than generous: two named drinks is a real commitment but a modest one, and the builds are not documented in the detail that a dedicated cocktail bar's are. Treat it as a reliable, genuinely fun option for a group rather than a destination for the drink itself. It opens from midday most days and runs to midnight on Fridays and Saturdays, and booking a tee time ahead is wise at weekends, when the East Fourth strip fills up and walk-in waits get long.
venues.pressQuote: Holey Moley Golf Club (Mini-golf): Pink Lightning; Mock O'Colada (frozen).

venues.name: Holy Ghost
venues.description: Holy Ghost is a Southeast Portland cocktail bar whose dedicated zero-proof program — built on Ritual non-alcoholic spirits plus house syrups and fresh juice — won Best Bar for Mocktails in Willamette Week's 2024 Best of Portland readers' poll. Named non-alcoholic drinks include the No Worries Fizz and the Nada Margarita.

venues.longDescription:
Holy Ghost is a neighborhood cocktail bar in southeast Portland's Creston-Kenilworth neighborhood, at the corner of SE 28th Avenue and Gladstone Street in the former Pub at the End of the Universe space. It opened in November 2021 after roughly four years of planning, run by Ezra Caraeff as part of the Three on a Match bar group (which also operates Old Gold and Paydirt). The room is anchored by a roughly 30-foot marble bar top, neon signage, and a mural by local artist Kyler Martz, and the drink program is known for a deep agave focus — a 400-plus-bottle collection of tequilas and mezcals — alongside a labor-intensive cocktail list.

Just as central to Holy Ghost's identity is its dedicated zero-proof program, which won Best Bar for Mocktails in Willamette Week's Best of Portland readers' poll in 2024 (and was again recognized in 2025). The alcohol-free menu is built largely on Ritual non-alcoholic spirits, with Pathfinder also used. The current list runs five named spirit-free drinks: the No Worries Fizz (a Ramos gin fizz riff with Ritual N/A gin, citrus, orange blossom, cream and egg white, served tall and taking a stated fifteen minutes to prepare), the Nada Margarita (Ritual N/A tequila, Ritual N/A apéritif, sugar and lime with a choice of salt), Ten Million Fireflies (Pathfinder, Ritual N/A apéritif, lemon, blueberry syrup and soda), Hear No Evil (Ritual N/A tequila, coconut corn syrup, cilantro, jalapeño and lime), and Temporary Prosperity (Ritual N/A gin, Ritual N/A apéritif, pineapple, cinnamon syrup, egg white and lemon); earlier builds Wounded Path and Wistful Disposition have rotated off. The spirit-free cocktails are priced from $12 to $14, in the same range as much of the full-proof list, and a rotating non-alcoholic beer and Underwood non-alcoholic rosé round out the alcohol-free options for anyone who wants a bottle or a glass of something simpler than a built cocktail.
venues.pressQuote: We really care about non-alcoholic drinks and want them to be more than just pity lemonade, as my wife used to call the drinks she was offered at bars when she was pregnant.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Ezra Caraeff, Holy Ghost owner (Willamette Week)

venues.name: Homeboy Bar
venues.description: Homeboy opened in 2018 on Islington's Essex Road as the debut bar from Dublin-born Aaron Wall, who had already run award-winning bars in Paris, Dublin and London. Its Modern Irish Hospitality concept — presented under Wall's tongue-in-cheek MIH Records banner, with the drinks list laid out as a vinyl set list of Disc 01 The Intro, Disc 02 The Crescendo and Disc 03 The Finish — pairs Irish comfort food and a hip-hop and R'n'B soundtrack with a genuinely serious cocktail programme. The room is snug and low-lit, all dark wood, deep leather banquettes and a black-and-white chequered bar, with live Irish music on Thursdays and Sundays and DJs at weekends. It is a World's 50 Best Discovery bar and a fixture on the Top 50 Cocktail Bars list, with a second room in Battersea. Its menu is organised into three pillars — Irish whiskey, Contemporary and Classics — and carries two dedicated non-alcoholic cocktails made with the same technique-led approach as the rest of the list.
signatureDrinks: Pure Dove (non-alcoholic) — Crossip Fresh, lime, San Pellegrino grapefruit soda
Floradorable (non-alcoholic) — Crossip Pure, fresh raspberry, lime, ginger cordial, Franklin & Sons ginger ale
venues.longDescription:
Homeboy opened in 2018 on Islington's Essex Road as the debut bar from Dublin-born Aaron Wall, who had already run award-winning bars in Paris, Dublin and London. Its "Modern Irish Hospitality" concept — presented under Wall's tongue-in-cheek MIH Records banner, with the drinks list laid out as a vinyl "set list" of Disc 01 The Intro, Disc 02 The Crescendo and Disc 03 The Finish — pairs Irish comfort food and a hip-hop and R'n'B soundtrack with a genuinely serious cocktail programme. The room is snug and low-lit, all dark wood, deep leather banquettes and a black-and-white chequered bar, with live Irish music on Thursdays and Sundays and DJs on Fridays and Saturdays. It is a World's 50 Best Discovery bar, a fixture on the Top 50 Cocktail Bars list and a Tales of the Cocktail Spirited Awards regional honoree, with a second Homeboy in Battersea.

The main list is Irish-whiskey-led, drawing on the likes of Busker, Teeling, Redbreast, Roe & Co and Bushmills through house drinks such as the Wogan, the Taoiseach, the Blackthorn No.2 and the Modern Irish Pornstar, alongside a trio of stripped-back "Mineral Martinis" and the frozen Irish coffees the bar is known for. The non-alcoholic drinks are treated with the same care rather than as an afterthought: the menu carries a dedicated Non-Alcoholic Cocktails section built around the British zero-proof spirit Crossip and the bar's own house cordials and infusions.

Two house alcohol-free cocktails anchor that section, both £7.50. The Pure Dove is a floral grapefruit-and-lime long drink of Crossip Fresh, fresh lime and San Pellegrino grapefruit soda; the Floradorable is a zero-proof riff on the classic Floradora, layering Crossip Pure with fresh raspberry, lime, ginger cordial and Franklin & Sons ginger ale. Beyond the printed pair, the bar invites guests to talk to the team and have a bespoke non-alcoholic drink built to taste from the "many non-alc potions, cordials, and infusions we make", and both Pure Dove and Floradorable are also offered as the alcohol-free choice on the bottomless weekend brunch (Saturdays and Sundays, 1pm–5pm).
venues.pressQuote: A refreshingly unpretentious Irish cocktail bar that feels more like Dublin than Essex Road

venues.name: HomeMakers Bar
venues.description: HomeMakers Bar is a "slightly retro, mostly modern" Over-the-Rhine cocktail bar whose zero-proof program is the deepest of any Cincinnati cocktail bar. The standing menu carries six house no-proof cocktails, each $10 and built like their full-proof counterparts: The Echo (Seedlip Garden, cucumber, rye syrup, lemon, salt, egg white), the Katz Nap (a mezcal-alternative with tepache and grapefruit), the Boatbuilder, the Toy Gun (a non-alcoholic French 75 with Seedlip Spice and NA sparkling wine), and The Harvey. Co-owner Julia Petiprin, who also built Sundry and Vice and Fifty Fifty Gin Club, champions mocktails with the same texture and balance as spirited drinks. An attached bottle shop lets you take the sober vibe home, stocking Seedlip Spice, Athletic Brewing's Free Wave, non-alcoholic sparkling Riesling, and Fever-Tree mixers.
venues.hours: Mon closed; Tue-Thu 4pm-12am; Fri 4pm-2am; Sat 1pm-2am; Sun 1pm-8pm
venues.longDescription:
HomeMakers Bar opened in Over-the-Rhine in 2019, the project of co-owners Julia Petiprin and Catherine Manabat. The room leans into a "slightly retro, mostly modern" aesthetic — colorful, kitschy, and built as a warm "home away from home" that honors makers of all sorts. Petiprin is one of Cincinnati's most prominent bar operators, also behind Sundry and Vice, Fifty Fifty Gin Club, and the design consultancy House of Departure; her fingerprints on the drink program are a big reason HomeMakers turns up in nearly every local non-alcoholic roundup.

The no-proof menu is a standing fixture, not a seasonal afterthought: six alcohol-free cocktails, each priced at $10 and made with a non-alcoholic spirit alongside house syrups, fresh juice and proper garnish. The Echo layers Seedlip Garden with cucumber, rye syrup, lemon, salt and egg white; the Katz Nap uses a mezcal alternative with tepache, grapefruit and lime; the Boatbuilder folds sage, raspberry, cinnamon, honey and fee foam over a mezcal-alternative base; and the Toy Gun rebuilds a French 75 with Seedlip Spice, lemon and non-alcoholic sparkling wine. Petiprin has said she enjoys the challenge of creating mocktails with the same texture, balance and complexity as a full cocktail. The attached bottle shop extends the program to takeaway, carrying Seedlip Spice, Athletic Brewing's Free Wave Hazy IPA, non-alcoholic sparkling Riesling, and Fever-Tree tonic and ginger ale.

HomeMakers sits at 39 E 13th St, in the heart of OTR's bar district. It's closed Mondays and opens at 4 p.m. Tuesday through Friday (Friday until 2 a.m.), with weekend hours starting at 1 p.m. Saturday (until 2 a.m.) and Sunday (until 8 p.m.). Expect a lively, design-forward space that suits both a full night out and a sober-curious drop-in — this is a full-service cocktail bar, so the zero-proof list sits alongside a spirited menu rather than replacing it. Call ahead at 513-394-7559 to confirm the current no-proof lineup, which rotates.
venues.pressQuote: With six different options, HomeMakers Bar in Over-the-Rhine is a great place for a fun mocktail for all tastes.

venues.name: Honey Elixir Bar
venues.description: Honey Elixir Bar is a wellness-forward elixir lounge tucked into the art-covered alley behind Denver Central Market in RiNo, opened in 2019 by Jocasta Hanson. The bar's animating principle is 'rejuvenation over depletion' — by day, the menu runs cacao, jun (a fermented honey tea similar to kombucha but built on honey instead of sugar), kefirs, smoothies, matcha, and chai; by night, it shifts into apothecary cocktails and a full lineup of NA potions, all made with organic herbs, botanicals, raw honey in place of sugar, and adaptogens including lion's mane, chaga, reishi, mucuna pruriens, and Shatavari. The NA potions are unlike anything else in Denver: drinks like the Radiant Roots (turmeric, ginger, house-made jasmine rice milk, oat milk, honey, vanilla) and the Love Spell (hibiscus, blueberry, star anise, shatavari, damiana, rose, violette) come garnished with actual crystals — citrine, rose quartz, rainbow lemurian — and flowers including gardenia, pink yarrow, linden, and cherry blossom. The space is a retro velvet-forward lounge that doubles as a rotating gallery for Denver artists, with a retail section for local makers. Music event nights run every other Friday; regular service is 18+, music nights are 21+. Featured in Westword's January 2026 NA roundup and 5280 Magazine's restaurant guide.

venues.longDescription:
Honey Elixir Bar opened in 2019 in the art-covered alley behind Denver Central Market on Walnut Street in RiNo, founded by Jocasta Hanson around a stated operating principle of rejuvenation over depletion. The room is a velvet-heavy retro lounge that doubles as a rotating gallery for Denver artists, with a small retail section given over to local makers; standard service is 18+, and the music events that run every other Friday are 21+. The daytime menu is built on cacao, jun, kefirs, smoothies, matcha and chai. Jun is the house signature: a fermented tea closer to kombucha than to sweetened iced tea, but built on raw honey instead of cane sugar and cultured on green tea. After dark the bar shifts into what it calls potions, an apothecary list assembled from organic herbs, botanicals, raw honey in place of refined sugar, and adaptogens including lion's mane, chaga, reishi, mucuna pruriens and shatavari. Drinks come garnished with actual crystals, among them citrine, rose quartz and rainbow lemurian, and with edible flowers such as gardenia, pink yarrow, linden and cherry blossom.

The alcohol-free potions are the main event rather than a side list, and they carry the same construction and pricing as everything else on the menu. Radiant Roots ($12) blends turmeric, ginger, house-made jasmine rice milk, oat milk, honey and vanilla; Love Spell ($13) layers hibiscus, blueberry, star anise, shatavari, damiana, rose and violette; Cooling Embers ($16) starts from organic cherry-apple juice, chamomile and lemon balm and is layered with fennel, saffron, black cohosh and ashwagandha root; Chocolit ($16) is a cacao drink built with reishi, lion's mane, chaga, mucuna pruriens, honey, sea salt and MCT oil, with orange, rose or peppermint available as a dollar add-on. Rose of Venus ($14) uses a non-alcoholic gin and NOVA non-alcoholic rose alongside hibiscus simple syrup, ginger honey and lime. A rotating Honey Cream Soda ($12) and ceremonial-grade Peruvian cacao round out the list. Westword named the bar in its January 1, 2026 round-up of local non-alcoholic options, singling out the jun and the Radiant Roots. A Press Seltzer ($9) and ceremonial-grade Peruvian cacao in micro and macro pours ($12 and $15) sit alongside them, and the cacao and Chocolit both take orange, rose or peppermint add-ons for a dollar. The bar is closed Mondays and runs to midnight Tuesday through Saturday, which puts it among the few genuinely late alcohol-free rooms in the neighbourhood.
venues.pressQuote: Tuck into the art-covered alley behind Denver Central Market to sample potions galore. Many from Honey Elixir Bar star a range of feel-good superfoods like raw cacao, functional fungi and medicinal herbs. Sample its jun, a fermented drink made from green tea and honey, or the Radiant Roots mocktail featuring turmeric, ginger and housemade jasmine rice milk.

venues.name: Honey Road
venues.description: Honey Road is a women-owned Eastern Mediterranean mezze restaurant on the Church Street Marketplace, repeatedly recognised by the James Beard Foundation and generally regarded as the best restaurant in Burlington. Its drinks list carries a distinct N/A Beverage section alongside the cocktails, and the bar is set up to offer low-alcohol or spirit-free counterparts to the drinks it is known for — a barberry caipirinha, a turmeric-and-ginger gin build — rather than only what is printed. Hotel Vermont's own guide to drinking in the city singles it out for having several non-alcoholic options. Dinner runs 4pm to 9pm, seven days a week.
venues.longDescription:
Honey Road opened on the Church Street Marketplace and has spent the years since collecting James Beard recognition and a reputation that reaches well outside Vermont. It is a women-owned-and-operated mezze restaurant — Eastern Mediterranean small plates, wood fire, a lot of dishes on a small table — and it is the reservation most visitors to Burlington try to get first.

The bar is built with the same specificity as the kitchen. The cocktail list runs to things like a barberry caipirinha and a turmeric-and-ginger gin drink, flavours drawn from the same pantry as the food, and the menu carries an N/A Beverage section as a standing part of the list. Just as usefully, the staff are set up to suggest low-alcohol or spirit-free counterparts to the printed cocktails, which for a restaurant with this much flavour-led bartending is a more valuable offer than a fixed pair of mocktails would be — the interesting ingredients are the syrups, brines and infusions, and those do not need the spirit to work.

Hotel Vermont's guide to drinking in Burlington, which is written by people who send guests out to other bars all night, lists Honey Road among the places with several non-alcoholic options. That is a peer recommendation rather than a marketing claim.

This entry is graded three rather than four, and the reason is documentation rather than doubt: the N/A section exists, but the restaurant does not publish its drink list online in a form that could be read for this guide, so no signature drinks are recorded and the strength of the section could not be measured. Ask at the bar — this is a room where asking gets a good answer.

Dinner is served 4pm to 9pm every day of the week, and walk-in seats at the bar are usually the realistic way in.

venues.name: HoneyBee Sage Express
venues.description: HoneyBee Sage Express is a compact, fully alcohol-free café inside the historic Marshall Building in Milwaukee's Historic Third Ward — the second outpost of Angela Mallett's HoneyBee Sage wellness brand. The roughly 500-square-foot "Express" space opened in autumn 2025 and pours brewed herbal teas alongside alcohol-free craft cocktails built from spirit alternatives, teas, bitters, and juice. Grab-and-go sandwiches, soups, salads, and packaged wellness goods round out the menu. Because no alcohol is served, every drink on the list is zero-proof. (The Third Ward café appeared to be temporarily closed in early October 2026, with no announcement from the business; the original café on King Drive was open. Check before you go.)
venues.address: 207 E. Buffalo St., Suite 104, Milwaukee, WI 53202
venues.longDescription:
HoneyBee Sage Express is the second location of HoneyBee Sage Wellness & Apothecary, the fully alcohol-free herbal beverage café founded by Angela Mallett, whose original "hive" has anchored Milwaukee's Bronzeville neighborhood on Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Drive for years. Opened in autumn 2025 inside the historic Marshall Building at 207 E. Buffalo St. in the Historic Third Ward, the roughly 500-square-foot "Express" model strips the apothecary services back to a focused, grab-and-go concept centered entirely on quick-service tea and food. Mallett has described the outpost as a way to test the brand's scalability and explore future franchising while keeping it fully owned in-house.

The through-line is that nothing here contains alcohol. The menu pairs brewed herbal teas with alcohol-free craft cocktails made from spirit alternatives, teas, bitters, and juices — the signature Warm Ember Glow among them — plus the Fit 4 You Lavender Lemonade, Mosi Chi chai, Soul Brew Kombucha, mushroom coffee, and grab-and-go sandwiches, soups, and salads. Packaged teas, tea accessories, and honey are available to take home. A cheerful yellow palette and a handful of small tables give the tight footprint an intimate, welcoming feel. Hours run Tuesday through Saturday, 9 a.m. to 4 p.m.

The location has drawn quick local attention: Milwaukee Magazine named HoneyBee Sage a Dry January must-try in January 2026, noting that "the community wellness space serves creative NA cocktails," and Radio Milwaukee's dining coverage highlighted the new Third Ward home's "cheerful yellow theme and craft mocktails." For visitors seeking a genuinely zero-proof daytime stop in the Third Ward, HoneyBee Sage Express offers a wellness-minded, entirely alcohol-free alternative to the neighborhood's bar scene.

One caution: the Third Ward café appeared to be temporarily closed in early October 2026, with no announcement from the business. The original café on King Drive was open at the time, so check before you travel.
venues.pressQuote: With a second location opened in autumn, the community wellness space serves creative NA cocktails.

venues.name: HoneyBee Sage Wellness & Apothecary Cafe
venues.description: HoneyBee Sage Wellness & Apothecary Cafe is Milwaukee's first fully alcohol-free bar, a Bronzeville hybrid of herbal apothecary, tea cafe, and zero-proof craft cocktail lounge founded by herbalist Angela Mallett in 2018. Nothing on the menu contains alcohol; hand-crafted "AF cocktails" are built from fresh fruit, natural sweeteners, and alcohol-free spirits under the house motto "Elevation without intoxication." The Cream City-brick space doubles as a working apothecary stocking 200-plus herbs, medicinal teas, and clean body products. It is the Bronzeville flagship, distinct from the newer Third Ward location.
venues.address: 1819 N. Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Dr., Milwaukee, WI 53212
venues.longDescription:
Opened in 2018 on North Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. Drive, HoneyBee Sage Wellness & Apothecary Cafe is widely credited as Milwaukee's first alcohol-free cocktail bar. Owner Angela Mallett, a licensed massage therapist, doula, and herbalist, built the concept around the idea of a bar experience without the alcohol, lining the cozy room with Milwaukee's iconic Cream City brick and honeycomb-inspired decor. The venture carries personal weight: Mallett has said the shop is "part of my dad's legacy," noting he died of alcohol-related organ failure about four months after she opened the first HoneyBee Sage, which is why she "did not want to introduce alcohol into a space where we offer healing alternatives and medicine."

The program is entirely non-alcoholic. Hand-crafted zero-proof cocktails are made from fresh fruit, natural sweeteners such as honey, maple, and agave, and alcohol-free spirits, alongside herbal and traditional teas, kombucha, and bakery items. Signature pours include "A Little Bit of Love," a mocktail associated with Milwaukee Bucks player Bobby Portis, a Wisconsin "New" Fashioned, and Moonwater. Beyond the beverage bar, the space operates as a full apothecary carrying more than 200 herbs, medicinal herbal teas, clean body products, and metaphysical healing tools, hosting community wellness events under the motto "Elevation without intoxication."

The cafe has become a recognized anchor of Milwaukee's sober and sober-curious scene, featured by FOX6, Spectrum News 1, OnMilwaukee, and Visit Milwaukee's mocktail guides. It maintains a 4.9-star Yelp rating and remains actively operating in 2026 with posted daily hours. A second, newer HoneyBee Sage location has since opened in the Historic Third Ward, with the King Drive site serving as the original Bronzeville flagship.
venues.pressQuote: HoneyBee Sage is the sober and sober-curious headquarters for all your mocktail dreams.

venues.name: Honeysuckle Rose
venues.description: A reservation-only chef's tasting restaurant on Charleston's West Side, opened in the former Purlieu space on Fishburne Street and run by chef-owner Ryan Jones and co-proprietor Kelleanne Jones. The eight-course prix-fixe experience runs $250 per person and pairs each course with either wine or a "zero beve" non-alcoholic program built with the same intention as the wine list. For non-drinkers the kitchen serves artisanal mocktails individually designed to complement all eight dishes, using herbs, spices, and fresh seasonal-fruit juices.
venues.hours: Mon closed; Tue-Thu 6pm-9pm; Fri-Sat 7pm-10pm; Sun closed
venues.longDescription:
Honeysuckle Rose is an immersive eight-course tasting concept on Charleston's West Side, at 237 Fishburne Street in the former Purlieu space. Chef-owner Ryan Jones and co-proprietor Kelleanne Jones run a single nightly seating Wednesday through Saturday at $250 per person, with the beverage pairing curated by director of beverage and hospitality Shane Meszaros. Guests choose between a wine pairing and a non-alcoholic "zero beve" pairing for each course.

The zero-proof program is a deliberate parallel to the wine list rather than an afterthought: artisanal mocktails are individually designed to complement each of the eight dishes, built with herbs, spices, and fresh juices from seasonal fruits. The team reports unexpectedly high demand for the alcohol-free pairing, and recent diner reviews (through late 2025 into 2026) describe the experience and service as a standout, confirming the restaurant is actively operating.
venues.pressQuote: We never expected the high level of interest in non-alcoholic pairings. We thought there would be one or two requests per week, but it's sometimes nine per night.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Chef-owner Ryan Jones, in Charleston Living Magazine

venues.name: Hop City Craft Beer & Wine
venues.description: Hop City Craft Beer & Wine is the Krog District (formerly Krog Street Market) outpost of the Atlanta beer-and-wine retailer founded by Kraig Torres in 2009. The location pairs a curated bottle shop with an adjacent full-service bar pouring dozens of rotating draft selections. For non-drinkers, the appeal is two-fold: the shop keeps a deep, dedicated non-alcoholic section, and the bar runs a dedicated N/A draft line that rotates between Untitled Art and Athletic Brewing. The retail NA shelf is one of the broadest in the city, spanning Athletic Brewing (Free Wave, Run Wild, Upside Dawn), Untitled Art, Guinness 0.0, Lagunitas Hoppy Refresher, Brooklyn Special Effects, Best Day, Ghia, and St. Agrestis Phony Negroni, with Sober Carpenter sold by the single. Sitting directly on the Eastside BeltLine trail, it's a practical NA stop whether you want a pour or a six-pack to go.

venues.longDescription:
Hop City Craft Beer & Wine was founded by Kraig Torres in 2009, and the Krog District shop at 99 Krog Street pairs a bottle shop with a full bar pouring dozens of rotating drafts. There are now four locations — Krog District and West End in Atlanta, plus Fayetteville and Birmingham, Alabama — and the Krog room sits directly on the Eastside BeltLine trail, which is the practical detail: it is a stop you can walk or cycle to mid-route.

For a non-drinker it works two ways at once, and that combination is rare. The bar runs a dedicated non-alcoholic draft line, rotating between Untitled Art and Athletic Brewing, so you can order a pour and sit at the bar rather than buying a can and leaving. Getting NA beer on draft at all is uncommon — it needs a line, a keg and the turnover to justify both — and it changes the experience from carrying a bottle around to being served like everyone else.

The retail shelf is one of the broadest in the city. Athletic Brewing across Free Wave, Run Wild and Upside Dawn; Untitled Art; Guinness 0.0; Lagunitas Hoppy Refresher; Brooklyn Special Effects; Best Day; Ghia; and St. Agrestis Phony Negroni, with Sober Carpenter sold as singles so you can try one without committing to a four-pack. It also stocks Halfway Crooks' Brevet Pils, the non-alcoholic German-style pilsner brewed a couple of miles away in Summerhill — worth knowing if you want to drink locally made NA beer rather than shipped-in national brands.

The Krog bottle shop runs Monday to Saturday from 10am to 9pm and Sunday from 12:30pm to 7pm, with the bar keeping slightly different hours. Single-can pricing on much of the NA range makes it a genuinely low-risk place to work out what you actually like.

venues.name: Hop Shop
venues.description: Hop Shop is an independent, owner-run craft beer store in the basement of Bukit Timah Plaza, a short walk from Beauty World MRT, with an online shop and same-day island-wide delivery alongside the counter. Its range runs to imports from the United States, Belgium, the United Kingdom, Australia and New Zealand, and it keeps a dedicated Non Alcoholic section: the Heaps Normal line from Australia in four styles, Deschutes Fresh Squeezed non-alcoholic IPA, Garage Project's Tiny But Mighty hazy IPA, Huyghe's alcohol-free Delirio blond ale, Collective Arts Botany adaptogenic elixirs and Living Things natural sodas. Cans are sold singly, so a non-drinker can build a mixed six-pack rather than commit to a case. It opens daily, until 8pm from Monday to Saturday.
