venues.longDescription:
Bukit Timah Plaza is an older neighbourhood mall on Jalan Anak Bukit, and Hop Shop occupies unit B1-15 in its basement, one floor down from the street. It is a small, owner-run bottle shop rather than a bar, with no taps and no seating, but it holds one of the deeper craft beer ranges on the island: the shelves are organised by style, from hazy IPAs and sours to Trappist ales and barrel-aged stouts, and by country, with the United States, Belgium, the United Kingdom, Australia, New Zealand and Japan all represented alongside Singapore's own brewers. A parallel online store mirrors the shelves, with free delivery above S$125 and same-day delivery on orders placed before 6pm from Monday to Saturday, and online orders can be collected in store the same day. Reviews consistently mention the staff recommendations as the reason to come in person, and there is a discount for six bottles or more.

For this guide the relevant shelf is the Non Alcoholic category, which the shop filters into non-alcoholic beers and sodas. In September 2026 it listed the Heaps Normal range from Australia, Quiet XPA, Half Day Hazy, Another Lager and Third IPA, in 375ml cans at S$24.90 for four; Deschutes Fresh Squeezed non-alcoholic IPA from Oregon at S$7.10 a can; Garage Project's Tiny But Mighty No Regrets hazy IPA from New Zealand at S$6.60; and Huyghe's Delirio alcohol-free blond ale from Belgium, at 0.3% ABV, for S$10.50. Beyond beer there were Collective Arts Botany adaptogenic elixirs at 0.0% in lemon, ginger and chamomile and in blueberry, mango and acai, and Living Things prebiotic sodas in rhubarb and apple and in raspberry. Stock rotates and individual lines sell out, so check the website before making the trip for one specific can. The shop is open Monday to Saturday from 11am to 8pm and on Sundays and public holidays from 11am to 5pm, and it answers stock questions on WhatsApp.

venues.name: Hosmer Bar
venues.description: Hosmer Bar, in Bend's Waypoint Hotel on 3rd Street, puts zero-proof drinks at the front of the offer rather than the back. It makes non-alcoholic versions of the classics — negroni, bloody mary, sours — pours Crux's NØ MØ non-alcoholic beer and Fre alcohol-removed wines, and will substitute non-alcoholic spirits into other drinks on request. Closed Tuesdays; Sunday opens at 10am.
venues.longDescription:
Hosmer Bar is the bar of the Waypoint Hotel on 3rd Street in midtown Bend, named for Hosmer Lake up in the Cascade Lakes — the one where the fishing is fly-only and the water is clear enough to see the bottom. The bar was reworked with inclusivity as an explicit goal, and in practice that means the non-alcoholic offer is structural rather than decorative.

It works on three levels at once, which is unusual. First, the cocktails: the bar makes zero-proof versions of the classics rather than inventing sweet alternatives — a negroni, a bloody mary, sours. Those are the drinks people actually miss, and rendering a negroni without alcohol is a real test of a bar's willingness to stock proper non-alcoholic bitters and aperitifs. Second, the beer: Crux's NØ MØ is on, so the local non-alcoholic IPA is available in a hotel bar rather than only at the brewery. Third, the wine: Fre alcohol-removed wines are poured by the glass, which is the thing most bars skip entirely and the thing that most often strands a non-drinking guest at a dinner.

On top of that, the bar will substitute non-alcoholic spirits into other drinks on request, so the list is not a hard boundary. Between the four routes, a non-drinker at Hosmer has roughly the same range of choices as anyone else at the bar — which is the actual definition of an inclusive drinks programme, and rarer than it should be.

One practical note: the bar is closed on Tuesdays, and Sunday is the outlier in the other direction, opening at ten in the morning. We have not published drink names or prices, as the bar does not publish a menu online — the Facebook page is its main presence.
venues.pressQuote: brings zero-proof drinks to the forefront in a reimagined, inclusive hotel bar experience

venues.name: Hotel Neptune Bar
venues.description: The European-style cocktail bar inside Hotel Neptune — the downtown boutique hotel that traded as The Dean until its June 2026 rebrand — sits behind a curtain off the lobby. It is a weekend room now: the hotel publishes the bar as open Friday and Saturday from 5pm, and some listings add a Thursday, so check before a midweek trip. Its non-alcoholic builds include a Paloma made with an agave alternative and a zero-proof Cosmopolitan. The same building holds a karaoke den and a lobby coffee shop, both keeping longer hours than the bar.
venues.longDescription:
This is the cocktail bar at 122 Fountain Street in Downcity Providence, tucked behind a curtain off the lobby of a 52-room boutique hotel. A name note first, because it will save you confusion: the hotel opened as The Dean, ran under that name for eleven years, and rebranded to Neptune — an Ash hotel — on 2 June 2026. The bar traded for years as The Dean Bar and much of the local coverage still calls it that. The hotel's own site has moved to the Neptune naming. Same room, same curtain, same address.

The bar is done in a European style — dark, compact, built for conversation rather than volume. Its hours have narrowed sharply since we first listed it, and the correction is worth stating plainly: we previously recorded a full week here, running to 1am midweek and 2am at weekends. The hotel now publishes this room as open Friday and Saturday only, 5pm to close, and some listings add a Thursday with a midnight close. Those late weekday hours we had belong to Boombox, the karaoke den downstairs, which is the room in this building that genuinely runs to 2am. Treat the bar as a weekend room and ring ahead for a midweek visit.

Two non-alcoholic builds are documented in current Providence coverage. One is a Paloma made with grapefruit and an agave alternative in place of tequila, which keeps the drink's dry, slightly bitter character rather than sweetening it. The other is a zero-proof Cosmopolitan. Both are recognisable classics rendered without spirit rather than invented mocktails, which suits a bar whose main list runs to European classics.

The wider building is worth knowing about: alongside this bar, Neptune houses a coffee shop in its lobby library, a full-service restaurant, and Boombox, a karaoke den with private singing rooms and its own bar. A new restaurant and bar concept has been announced for the hotel, so expect the ground floor to keep changing. We have not published drink prices or a full list, as the bar does not publish a menu online.

venues.name: House of Found Objects
venues.description: House of Found Objects is a downtown Birmingham cocktail bar on 2nd Avenue North whose zero-proof drinks are treated as creations in their own right rather than as subtractions — built from fresh fruit and botanicals, with the complexity and structure the bar puts into its alcoholic list. Bham Now's January 2026 guide to non-alcoholic drinking in the city leads with it. The room keeps late hours, opening at 4pm Tuesday through Saturday and running to midnight midweek and 2am on Friday and Saturday, which makes it one of the few places in the city where a non-drinker can genuinely stay out.
venues.longDescription:
House of Found Objects takes its name literally — the room on 2nd Avenue North downtown is assembled from salvage and oddments, and the drinks follow the same logic of building something considered out of parts that were not obviously meant to go together.

For a non-drinker the relevant question about a bar like this is whether the creativity extends past the spirits, and here it does. Bham Now's January 2026 survey of non-alcoholic drinking in the city led with this room, describing the zero-proof drinks as vibrant creations thoughtfully crafted with fresh fruit, botanicals and bold flavours. The word doing the work in that sentence is botanicals: fresh fruit alone gives you a juice, and it is the botanical side — herbs, aromatics, bitter and floral elements — that gives an alcohol-free drink the length and complexity that makes it worth sitting with.

The practical value is the hours. The bar opens at 4pm from Tuesday to Saturday and runs to midnight midweek, 2am on Friday and Saturday. Late closing is disproportionately important in this category, because the small hours are exactly when a non-drinker's options normally vanish and the choice narrows to going home or holding a soda. Two in the morning on a Friday with a properly made drink in your hand is a materially different experience.

This entry records no signature drinks. The bar's zero-proof list rotates and is not published in a form that could be read for this guide, so naming a specific build would be wrong within a season — the durable fact is the standing commitment, which Birmingham's own paper has documented.

Closed Sunday and Monday. It sits a few minutes' walk from Pink Lantern, Paper Doll and Neon Moon, in the downtown cluster where this city's alcohol-free drinking is concentrated.
venues.pressQuote: Discover vibrant, zero-proof creations at House of Found Objects. Each mocktail is thoughtfully crafted with fresh fruit, botanicals and bold flavors

venues.name: House of Mana Kava
venues.description: An alcohol-free 'third space' in Orlando's SoDo district that pairs a traditional kava bar with a gamer-friendly social lounge - pool tables, arcade cabinets, and a packed weekly calendar of tournaments, open mics, and trivia. Guests order kava shells, botanical teas, boba, cold brew, and CBD drinks instead of cocktails. (Alcohol-free, though its kava and CBD drinks aren't substance-free.)

venues.longDescription:
Branded 'Your First Place for the Third Space,' House of Mana at 4401 S Orange Ave in SoDo runs a fantasy- and gaming-themed menu: kava shells sold single, double, or triple; a 'Leaf Compendium' of botanical teas; 'Elixirs of the Realm' kava mocktails and 'Pixel Potions' botanical tea mocktails; extract-seltzer shots from 'The Quickdraw Bar'; cold brew coffee flights from 'The Alchemist's Still'; and a run of canned kava/kratom-extract beverages. By day it's a coworking and study space with wifi and workstations; by evening it shifts into a lounge with a stage, pool tables, and arcade machines.

As with any kava bar, it's worth noting House of Mana is alcohol-free but not substance-free - its kava, extract shots, and CBD drinks are mood-altering botanicals rather than plain caffeine or herbal tea, so it markets itself as a 'sanctuary free of spirits,' not a fully substance-free space.

The lounge runs a dense recurring events schedule: Monday all-you-can-drink kava, biweekly D&D nights, fighting-game and pool tournaments, and community board-game nights, plus monthly Magic: The Gathering, trivia, movie nights, open-mic music, bingo, paint-and-sip, a Sunday book club, a first-Wednesday 'Mana Mixer' networking night, a third-Wednesday industry speaker series, a last-Wednesday philosophy club, and an end-of-month 'Level Up' celebration. It's open daily from 8am to 2am.
venues.pressQuote: Orlando's fantasy-forged kava social lounge in SoDo, near Downtown and moments from Winter Park

venues.name: Howl at the Moon
venues.description: Howl at the Moon is the duelling-piano bar on the River Walk, and it carries named non-alcoholic drinks — Mother of Dragons and Purple Rain — alongside non-alcoholic beer and wine. The format is the argument for including it: a piano bar is an entertainment venue where the show is the reason you are there, so the evening does not depend on what is in your glass. That, plus a 2am licence seven nights a week, makes it a viable late option in the most tourist-heavy part of the city. It opens at 7pm most nights and 6pm at weekends, running to 2am every single night of the week.
venues.address: 111 W Crockett St #201, San Antonio, TX 78205
venues.longDescription:
Howl at the Moon on West Crockett Street is a duelling-piano bar on the River Walk — a chain format, loud, tourist-heavy, and built entirely around the performance. Two pianists trade songs and take requests; the room sings along.

That format is exactly why it is worth listing. The recurring difficulty of a sober night out is not the absence of a good drink but the absence of anything else happening. In a quiet cocktail bar, the drink is the event, and being the person without one is conspicuous for three hours. In a room where two people are playing Bohemian Rhapsody at volume and everyone is shouting the words, nobody has the attention to spare for what is in your hand. Entertainment venues do more for non-drinkers than most dedicated mocktail menus, and they are systematically underrated for it.

The drinks are straightforward — Mother of Dragons and Purple Rain, both named on Visit San Antonio's list — and the bar also stocks non-alcoholic beer and wine, which covers the guest who wants something familiar rather than a construction. It is a chain offering, and the grade says so honestly.

The hours are the other advantage: 7pm to 2am every night, from 6pm on Friday and Saturday. This is a genuine late-night venue in the middle of the River Walk, where a very large share of San Antonio's visitors are staying. For anyone who wants to be out until one in the morning without drinking — a group where one person is driving, say, or a visitor in recovery who still wants a night out — it is one of the few honest answers in the tourist core. It is also loud enough that nobody will ask what you are drinking, which for some people is the entire point.
venues.pressQuote: Howl at the Moon: Mother of Dragons, Purple Rain, plus non-alcoholic beer and wine options.

venues.name: Hula's Modern Tiki
venues.description: A hip, retro tiki restaurant and bar in Old Town Scottsdale, Hula's serves playful tropical mocktails in vintage tiki mugs, complete with umbrellas and fruity garnishes. Named zero-proof builds include the Captain's Colada (coconut cream, allspice falernum syrup, pineapple juice), the Castaway Cooler (a fruity ginger beer build) and the Hula Juice, which layers passion fruit syrup with pineapple, orange and cranberry. Tiki is a format that works unusually well without alcohol — the sweetness, spice and presentation carry the drink rather than the rum — and Hula's leans into that rather than treating the non-alcoholic list as an obligation. Multiple Valley locations, with the Old Town room the most central.

venues.longDescription:
Hula's Modern Tiki has been a Valley fixture long enough to have shed any irony about the format: mid-century tiki done straight, in a room of rattan, warm light and vintage mugs, with a kitchen turning out Hawaiian-leaning plates rather than tiki as pure theatre. The Old Town Scottsdale site is the most central of its several Valley locations, sitting a block off the main strip in a neighbourhood where most of the alternatives are loud and late.

Tiki happens to be the drink category that survives best without alcohol, and Hula's exploits that. A rum-forward tropical build gets its structure from acid, spice, syrup and dilution as much as from the spirit, so removing the rum leaves more behind than it does in, say, a martini. The Captain's Colada is coconut cream, allspice falernum syrup and pineapple juice; the Castaway Cooler is a fruity ginger beer build with a genuine bite to it; the Hula Juice layers passion fruit syrup with pineapple, orange and cranberry. All of it arrives in the same carved mugs and with the same umbrellas and fruit as the rum drinks, which sounds trivial and is not — a great deal of the tiki experience is presentation, and being handed a plain glass while everyone else gets a ceramic idol is precisely how non-drinkers get quietly excluded.

DiningOut Phoenix summed up the appeal in May 2026: these are drinks that transport you to an island paradise, without the need for rum or tequila. Worth knowing: this is a full bar and restaurant with a substantial rum list, not an alcohol-free venue, and the format is food-led, so it works better as dinner than as a place to nurse a single drink. Happy hour is the cheapest way to test the zero-proof list before committing to a table.
venues.pressQuote: transport you to an island paradise, without the need for rum or tequila

venues.name: Huli Huli Tiki Lounge
venues.description: The second Huli Huli Tiki Lounge opened on 20 May 2026 in the long-vacant Jury Room space at 22 East Mound Street, downtown — a room with a bar lineage running back to the nineteenth century, now fitted out as a tiki lounge by owner Dustin Sun. The drinks programme follows the Powell original, which means the alcohol-free side is unusually deep for a new opening: house cocktails including the Honolulu Mule, the Blue Hawaiian and the Baby Aspirin are all served in alcohol-free versions built to order rather than swapped for a soft drink. Because tiki drinks are constructed from fruit, spice, syrup and dilution, the zero-proof versions read as complete rather than hollowed out. The downtown room keeps shorter hours than Powell, opening Wednesday to Saturday evenings only.
venues.hours: Mon-Tue closed; Wed-Thu 4:30pm-10:30pm; Fri-Sat 4:30pm-11:30pm; Sun closed
venues.longDescription:
The downtown Huli Huli opened on 20 May 2026 at 22 East Mound Street, taking over the Jury Room — a space that had been a bar in one form or another since 1831 and had sat empty for years before the tiki fit-out. It is the second location for owner Dustin Sun, following the Powell original, and the announcement drew more attention than most Columbus openings precisely because of what was being replaced: a room that traded on being the city's oldest continuously licensed bar site becoming a tropical lounge was, to put it mildly, discussed.

For a non-drinking guest the practical point is that the downtown room inherits the Powell drinks programme, which was already one of the more serious alcohol-free offerings in the metro. The house cocktails are available zero-proof to order — the Honolulu Mule, the Blue Hawaiian and the Baby Aspirin are the three that local coverage consistently names — and they are built rather than substituted. This matters more in tiki than in most categories: a daiquiri or a mai tai without rum is a genuinely different drink, but a Blue Hawaii or a mule is largely a structure of fruit, citrus, syrup, spice and crushed ice, so the zero-proof version arrives at the table looking and reading like the full-proof one. The Baby Aspirin — pineapple, orange and cream of coconut in a coconut cup — is served identically either way. The downtown room runs a tighter schedule than Powell, opening Wednesday through Saturday evenings only, and does not publish a separate phone line; reservations and enquiries route through the same site as the Powell bar. Note that this is a distinct venue from the Powell lounge, not a relocation. The location is a genuine convenience for anyone staying downtown: it sits a short walk from the Brewery District and German Village, which puts it within the same evening as Law Bird and Cobra for anyone building an alcohol-free crawl on the south side of the centre. Being new, the room is also less pressed than the Powell original at weekends.
venues.pressQuote: Feeling like a tropical getaway? Huli Huli Tiki Lounge has alcohol-free versions of their Honolulu Mule, Blue Hawaiian, and Baby Aspirin.

venues.name: Huli Huli Tiki Lounge
venues.description: Huli Huli Tiki Lounge is the original of Dustin Sun's two Columbus-area tiki bars, occupying a former antique shop in downtown Powell, north of the city. Tiki is a format that translates unusually well to zero-proof drinking — the classics are built on fruit, syrup, spice and dilution as much as on rum — and Huli Huli leans into that rather than treating it as a compromise. Alcohol-free versions of the house drinks are made to order, including the Honolulu Mule and a zero-proof Blue Hawaii sold as the Untrod Beach, and there are non-alcoholic builds designed as such: the Baby Aspirin, a blend of pineapple, orange and cream of coconut served in a coconut cup, and the Seafoam Sipper of cream soda, pandan and mint. The room keeps early hours by bar standards, opening at 1pm on Saturdays and Sundays.
venues.hours: Mon closed; Tue-Thu 4:30pm-9:30pm; Fri 4:30pm-11pm; Sat 1pm-11pm; Sun 1pm-8pm
signatureDrinks: Baby Aspirin (pineapple, orange, cream of coconut, served in a coconut cup)
venues.longDescription:
Huli Huli Tiki Lounge opened in a former antique shop on West Olentangy Street in downtown Powell, the Delaware County suburb at the northern edge of the Columbus metro, and is the first of two rooms run by owner Dustin Sun. The bar takes its name and its philosophy from Hawaiian rather than generic Polynesian-pop tiki, and the house framing is the aloha spirit — the site quotes the definition at length — which in practice means a room built for lingering rather than for volume drinking.

Tiki is a better fit for non-alcoholic drinking than most bar formats, because the architecture of the classics is fruit, syrup, spice, citrus and crushed ice, with the rum providing weight rather than the whole idea. Huli Huli works that to its advantage in two directions. First, the house cocktails are available in alcohol-free versions built to order: the Honolulu Mule, the Blue Hawaii — which the bar serves zero-proof under the name Untrod Beach — and others across the list. Second, there are drinks conceived as non-alcoholic from the start. The Baby Aspirin blends pineapple, orange and cream of coconut and arrives in a coconut cup, which sounds like a garnish decision but matters: the presentation is identical to the full-proof service, so nobody at the table is visibly the one not drinking. The Seafoam Sipper pairs cream soda with pandan and mint, pandan being a South-East Asian leaf with a grassy, vanilla-adjacent flavour that gives the drink something to do beyond sweetness. CityScene named the bar in its December 2025 alcohol-free roundup on the strength of that menu. The room opens at 1pm on Saturdays and Sundays and closes Mondays. Powell itself is a small historic downtown roughly twenty minutes north of central Columbus, and the bar is one of the few destinations in the northern suburbs with a developed alcohol-free list, which makes it worth the drive for anyone based on that side of the metro rather than only for tiki enthusiasts. Food is tropical bar snacks rather than a full kitchen.
venues.pressQuote: Located in a former antique shop, Huli Huli brings the tiki spirit to downtown Powell through fruity drinks and tropical bites.

venues.name: Humble Wine Bar
venues.description: Humble Wine Bar is a neighbourhood wine bar on Detroit Avenue in Lakewood serving stone-oven Neapolitan-style pizza and curated small plates alongside a by-the-glass list. A wine bar is the hardest format in which to drink well without alcohol, which is what makes its standing commitment to keeping several non-alcoholic options worth noting. The house benchmark is the Phony Negroni at $10 — Seedlip Spice for the botanical backbone, DHOS Bittersweet for the amaro bitterness, aperitivo rosso for the vermouth weight — stirred and served in the same glass as the original.

venues.longDescription:
Humble Wine Bar sits on the Detroit Avenue strip in downtown Lakewood, a few doors from Crumb & Spigot and around the corner from Sacred Waters, on what has quietly become the densest run of alcohol-free-friendly rooms on Cleveland's west side. The bar describes itself as a chic but approachable gathering spot and the format is straightforward: a curated by-the-glass list leaning on small producers, stone-oven-fired Neapolitan-style pizzas, and a short menu of small plates, open from 4pm Monday through Saturday. Nick and Geoff run it, and the room doubles as a private-event space during daytime hours through the week.

A wine bar is the hardest room in which to drink well without alcohol — the entire proposition is the bottle list, and the usual fallback is sparkling water with a wedge of something. That is what makes Humble's standing commitment to carrying several non-alcoholic options genuinely useful rather than decorative. The house benchmark is the Phony Negroni at $10: Seedlip Spice for the botanical backbone, DHOS Bittersweet for the amaro-like bitterness, and an aperitivo rosso for the red-vermouth weight, stirred and served in the same glass as the real thing. It is a build that lives or dies on whether the bitterness holds up without gin behind it, and Cleveland Magazine's 2026 mocktail roundup picked it out as one of the region's better zero-proof aperitivi.

The rest of the non-alcoholic list rotates alongside the wine, so a non-drinking guest at a table ordering bottles has an actual choice through a meal rather than one drink and then nothing. The pizza, cooked in the stone oven behind the bar, is what most people come back for, and the kitchen runs to 10pm on weeknights and 11pm at weekends.
venues.pressQuote: The Phony Negroni ($10) is built with Seedlip Spice, DHOS Bittersweet and Apertivo Rosso.

venues.name: Portland Hunt & Alpine Club
venues.description: Portland Hunt & Alpine Club is the Scandinavian-leaning Market Street bar that did more than any other room to build Portland's cocktail reputation, and its non-alcoholic drinks are held to the same standard as the rest. The Paper King is the one to order: Thai tea syrup, pineapple and lemon lengthened with Stappi, the Italian red bitter soda. That last ingredient is the tell — Stappi exists to supply genuine bitterness, and reaching for it rather than another fruit juice is what separates a bar thinking about balance from one thinking about sweetness. The bar opens from 3pm midweek and 2pm at weekends, and is closed Mondays; it is a couple of minutes from Via Vecchia and Andy's.
venues.hours: Mon closed; Tue-Thu 3pm-10pm; Fri 3pm-12am; Sat 2pm-12am; Sun 2pm-10pm
signatureDrinks: Paper King - Thai tea syrup, pineapple, lemon, Stappi red bitter soda
venues.longDescription:
Portland Hunt & Alpine Club opened on Market Street in the Old Port and became, fairly quickly, the bar that people cite when they argue Portland punches above its size for drinking. The aesthetic is Scandinavian — pale wood, clean lines, a snack menu heavy on smoked fish and rye — and the cocktail programme has been nationally recognised for years.

What matters here is that the non-alcoholic drinks were not left out of that seriousness. The Paper King combines Thai tea syrup with pineapple and lemon, then lengthens it with Stappi, the Italian red bitter soda. Thai tea brings tannin and a slightly astringent, spiced sweetness; pineapple and lemon handle the fruit and acid; and Stappi does the job that has no substitute — actual bitterness.

That choice is the whole signal. Bitterness is what makes a drink taste designed for an adult palate, and it is the single hardest quality to achieve without alcohol, since most bitter elements in a bar arrive dissolved in spirit. A bar that stocks a bitter soda specifically so its zero-proof drinks can have a spine has thought about the problem properly rather than reaching for another juice. It is notable that Arcadia, across town, arrived at the same solution independently — Stappi has quietly become the marker of a Portland bar that takes this seriously.

Hours are generous by Portland standards: from 3pm Tuesday through Friday, from 2pm at weekends, running to midnight on Friday and Saturday, closed Mondays. It sits within a couple of minutes' walk of Via Vecchia and Andy's Old Port Pub, which makes the Old Port the most practical neighbourhood in the city for an evening where not everyone is drinking.
venues.pressQuote: Rightfully, Hunt and Alpine is now the Portland institution it has always deserved to be
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Thrillist, The Best Cocktail Bars in the Country

venues.name: Husk
venues.description: Husk Nashville is an acclaimed Southern restaurant that opened on 23 May 2013 in a restored 1880s home in the Rutledge Hill section of downtown's SoBro, following chef Sean Brock's Charleston original of 2010. Brock's involvement is now historical rather than current — he is not listed on the restaurant's own site, and the kitchen has passed through seven executive chefs, most recently in August 2026 when Bryan O'Kelly was promoted after Ben Norton left for Los Angeles. The cooking remains hyper-regional and ingredient-driven Southern. Its bar keeps a dedicated "Spirit-Free" section that is deeper than most restaurants of its standing manage: the Faux-Spresso ($14, Pathfinder, Crema Coffee, cardamom, salted whip), Free Spirit ($10, Lyre's Apéritif, pomegranate-rosemary shrub, soda), and two house-made drinks at $7 — a Husk Lemonade cut with shiso, jalapeño and sea salt, and the T & T, a thyme-honey shrub with tonic and lemon. Southern sodas, Sierra Nevada's Trail Pass NA IPA and a Leitz non-alcoholic sparkling rosé complete it.
signatureDrinks: Free Spirit (Lyre's Apéritif, pomegranate-rosemary shrub, soda) $10
Faux-Spresso (Pathfinder, Crema Coffee, cardamom, salted whip) $14
venues.longDescription:
Husk Nashville opened on 23 May 2013 at 37 Rutledge Street, in a refurbished 1880s house in the quiet Rutledge Hill pocket near downtown that was once the home of a nineteenth-century Nashville mayor. It arrived as the second Husk, following chef Sean Brock's Charleston original, and built its reputation on hyper-regional Southern cooking sourced from named farms. Brock's involvement is now historical rather than current — he is not listed anywhere on the restaurant's own site — and the kitchen has passed through seven executive chefs, most recently in August 2026 when Ben Norton left for Los Angeles and Bryan O'Kelly, previously his colleague, was promoted into the role. The current supper menu runs Alabama shrimp with sungold tomato and hoja santa, Murder Point oysters with kimchi and cucumber, pimento cheese with benne seed wafers, Benton's country ham with peach and tarragon, shrimp and grits with green gumbo and okra, and a dry-aged Bear Creek ribeye, with buttermilk cheddar biscuits alongside. A carriage house behind the restaurant, The Stables at Husk, handles private dining.

The drinks book carries a properly built section headed "Spirit-Free", and its range is wider than most Southern restaurants of this standing manage. Faux-Spresso ($14) is the most ambitious, combining Pathfinder with coffee from local roaster Crema, cardamom and a salted whip, and it is priced level with the cocktails rather than beneath them. Free Spirit ($10) uses Lyre's Apéritif with a pomegranate-rosemary shrub and soda. Two house-made drinks anchor the cheaper end at $7 each: the Husk Lemonade, cut with shiso, jalapeño and sea salt rather than served plain, and the T & T, a thyme-honey shrub with tonic and lemon. Casamara's Alta amaro-style soft drink is $8. Below those the list leans into Southern soda properly — Devil's Foot ginger beer, Abita root beer, Cheerwine, Mexican Coke and Sprite — which suits the cooking better than an imported tonic would. Non-alcoholic beer is Sierra Nevada's Trail Pass IPA at $9, and the wine list carries its own non-alcoholic heading with Leitz sparkling rosé from the Mosel at $15 a glass. Dinner runs from 5pm nightly with weekend brunch from 10am; reservations are through Resy.
venues.pressQuote: It's the mark of a great restaurant that it can maintain consistency of food and service in the face of major personnel changes, and Husk hasn't received enough credit for navigating the difficult dining conditions of Nashville while experiencing changes in leadership.

venues.name: Husk Savannah
venues.description: Husk Savannah is the Georgia outpost of the Southern restaurant group founded by chef Sean Brock in Charleston, occupying a restored early-twentieth-century building on Oglethorpe Avenue in the Historic District. Its beverage list is one of the most seriously constructed alcohol-free programmes in the city: the printed cocktail menu carries a section headed SPIRIT-FREE, positioned alongside the house cocktails rather than buried after the sodas, with four builds priced $12 to $14. They are made with named non-alcoholic spirits — Lyre's coffee and rum expressions, ISH Caribbean spice, Seedlip Grove, Giffard's alcohol-free ginger — plus a South African sparkling Pinotage rosé sold by the glass and Athletic Brewing's Upside Dawn on the beer list.
signatureDrinks: NA Espresso Martini — Lyre's NA coffee and rum spirits, vanilla, coffee, NA bitters
In the Clear — ISH NA Caribbean spice spirit, Seedlip Grove, coconut, lime
Spark Plug — ginger, grapefruit, Giffard ginger NA spirit, NA bitters, Misty Cliffs sparkling NA chardonnay
Lautus sparkling Pinotage non-alcoholic rosé, South Africa
venues.longDescription:
Husk began in Charleston in 2010 under chef Sean Brock, built on a rule that has since been copied across the South: if an ingredient is not grown or raised in the South, it does not come through the kitchen door. The Savannah restaurant applies the same logic on Oglethorpe Avenue, a block off Bull Street in the Historic District, and its bar has quietly become one of the more rigorous alcohol-free programmes in coastal Georgia.

What makes it rigorous is structural. The cocktail menu prints SPIRIT-FREE as a named section directly under HUSK COCKTAILS — not an afterthought at the foot of the page — and the drinks in it are priced and constructed like the alcoholic ones. The NA Espresso Martini is built on Lyre's non-alcoholic coffee and rum spirits with vanilla and coffee, finished with alcohol-free bitters. In the Clear runs ISH Caribbean spice spirit against Seedlip Grove with coconut and lime. Spark Plug is the most technical of the four: ginger and grapefruit, Giffard's alcohol-free ginger spirit, non-alcoholic bitters, lengthened with Misty Cliffs sparkling non-alcoholic chardonnay. A South African Lautus sparkling Pinotage rosé is listed as a glass pour in its own right, and Athletic Brewing's Upside Dawn golden ale sits on the beer list with its ABV printed alongside every other beer.

The menu is dated on its face — the copy checked for this listing was marked April 25, 2026 — which is a useful signal in a city where drink lists move fast. It also shows how fast: the mocktails Savannah's own tourism guide credits to Husk, the Amethyst Twilight and the Negroni Bambino, are both gone from the current sheet. The programme survived the rotation; the specific drinks did not.

Dinner runs 5pm to 10pm daily, with brunch added Saturday and Sunday from 10am, and a weekday happy hour from 5pm.

For a non-drinker the practical advantage of eating here is that the wine and whiskey lists are the reason most people book, and the spirit-free drinks are constructed to sit alongside a menu built for them rather than to fill a gap. The Lautus rosé in particular is poured as a wine rather than as a substitute for one, which means a table can share a bottle course without one person opting out of the meal. That is a small thing to engineer and a rare one to find in a restaurant of this level anywhere in coastal Georgia.

venues.name: Hvala
venues.description: Hvala is a Japanese teahouse whose flagship now occupies a large ground-floor space in Odeon Towers near City Hall, with tatami-style floor seating, communal tables and a retail counter selling leaf, powder and ware. It is entirely alcohol-free and unusually rigorous about sourcing: the house produces its own matcha and hojicha powders directly from plantations in Uji, Kyoto, and whisks each bowl to order in front of the guest rather than pulling it from a batch. More than thirty matcha and hojicha items run across drinks, desserts and food, including a matcha kaya toast served with soft-boiled eggs. It is a daytime room rather than an evening one.
venues.address: 333 North Bridge Road, #01-11 Odeon Towers, Singapore 188720
signatureDrinks: Ceremonial-grade matcha, whisked to order from house-produced Uji powder
Hojicha, from the house's own roasted-leaf powder
venues.longDescription:
Hvala has been one of Singapore's more serious Japanese tea operations for several years, and it recently consolidated around a new flagship at Odeon Towers on North Bridge Road, a short walk from City Hall. The move is worth flagging because the old CHIJMES flagship has closed, and a number of published guides still send people there. The Odeon room is considerably larger, with high ceilings, a mix of conventional tables and tatami-style floor seating, and a dedicated retail section selling tea leaves, matcha powder and brewing accessories.

The sourcing is what separates Hvala from the broader matcha boom. Rather than buying finished powder from a distributor, the house sources and produces its own matcha and hojicha lines directly from family plantations in Uji, Kyoto — the region most closely associated with high-grade Japanese green tea. Bowls are whisked to order in front of the guest, which matters more than it sounds: matcha degrades quickly once prepared, and batching it is the single most common shortcut in the category. Across drinks, desserts and food there are more than thirty matcha and hojicha items, so the leaf runs through the whole menu rather than appearing only in a latte.

The food has grown alongside the tea. The flagship serves proper mains — cold salmon sashimi udon, chazuke — and a matcha kaya toast in which brioche is layered with butter and the house matcha-infused kaya and served with soft-boiled eggs, a neat Singaporean-Japanese hybrid. For a non-drinker this is a daytime and early-evening room rather than a night out: it closes at 8:30pm most days and 9:30pm on Saturdays. Within those hours it is the most rigorous cup of matcha in the city.

One practical note for anyone working from a guidebook or an older blog post: Hvala operates several outlets, and the addresses in circulation are unreliable. The CHIJMES site has closed. There is a refreshed flagship at 111 Somerset, which has become known for a robotic matcha-whisking arm, and a retail counter at Takashimaya in Ngee Ann City. The Odeon Towers room described here is the fullest expression of the tea house format, with the seating and the retail range to match.
venues.pressQuote: Hvala sources and produces its own line of matcha and hojicha powders directly from tea plantations in Kyoto!

venues.name: Hyacinth
venues.description: Hyacinth is a 40-seat Italian and Mediterranean kitchen on Grand Avenue in St. Paul's Summit Hill, opened in August 2018 by chef Rikki Giambruno (formerly of Brooklyn's Franny's) and named for the street he grew up on in Victoria, Minnesota. Since 2023 it has been led by chef-owner Abraham Gessesse, a founding member of the team. The intimate room is known for house-made pasta and a frequently changing, ingredient-driven menu, and it ranks among the Twin Cities' most acclaimed restaurants, drawing top Star Tribune reviews and James Beard recognition. Its beverage list carries a dedicated non-alcoholic section that treats zero-proof drinking seriously: spirit-free cocktails alongside a house-made lychee soda, NA beer, and an NA sparkling wine. Recent named pours include the Spiritless Spritz, Final Say, and the seasonal Flightless Paper Plane. The NA list rotates with the kitchen, so specific drinks vary by visit.
venues.longDescription:
Hyacinth is a forty-seat Italian and Mediterranean kitchen on Grand Avenue in St. Paul's Summit Hill, opened in August 2018 by chef Rikki Giambruno — formerly of Brooklyn's Franny's — and named for the street he grew up on in Victoria, Minnesota. Since 2023 it has been led by chef-owner Abraham Gessesse, a founding member of the original team. The room is small, the pasta is made in house, the menu changes often around whatever is good, and it sits consistently among the most acclaimed restaurants in the Twin Cities, drawing top Star Tribune reviews and James Beard recognition.

For a restaurant of that size, the beverage list is notably generous to people who are not drinking. It carries a dedicated non-alcoholic section that runs spirit-free cocktails alongside a house-made lychee soda, non-alcoholic beer and a non-alcoholic sparkling wine — the last of which matters disproportionately at a forty-seat restaurant where tables are often marking something. Recent named pours include the Spiritless Spritz, the Final Say, and the seasonal Flightless Paper Plane, the last a zero-proof reading of the Paper Plane cocktail. Visit Saint Paul recommended precisely that drink, noting it "tastes like a cocktail: tart, bitter, and herbaceous without being too sweet," which is the exact combination that separates a considered spirit-free build from a glass of juice.

One practical note: the non-alcoholic list rotates alongside the kitchen's frequently changing menu, so the specific drinks named here will vary by visit. That is a feature rather than a warning — a rotating zero-proof list is a maintained one, and it means the bar is thinking about these drinks seasonally in the same way it thinks about the food. Dinner Tuesday through Sunday, closed Mondays. Grand Avenue is the densest restaurant strip in St. Paul, and between Hyacinth and Bar + Cart a few doors down, that single street now holds two of the better non-alcoholic drinks lists in the metro — which makes it the obvious place to start an evening that does not involve drinking.
venues.pressQuote: Try the "Flightless Paper Plane" which tastes like a cocktail: tart, bitter, and herbaceous without being too sweet.

venues.name: Idle Beer Hall & Brewery
venues.description: Idle Beer Hall & Brewery on Brooklyn Avenue is a working brewery that also keeps four named mocktails on its list — a Southside, a Spanish gin and tonic, a beachside fizz and a French twist. A brewery bothering to build proper cocktails for people who are not drinking beer is genuinely unusual, and the choices are telling: a Southside and a Spanish G&T are both dry, herbal, bitter-leaning drinks rather than sweet ones. It also runs late, to midnight midweek and 2am on Friday and Saturday, which makes it a workable end to an evening. It sits on Brooklyn Avenue near the Pearl, next door to Tony's Siesta, which keeps similarly late hours.
venues.longDescription:
Idle Beer Hall & Brewery is on Brooklyn Avenue in River North, a short walk from the Pearl, and it brews on site. Breweries are a specific problem for non-drinkers: the room exists to sell beer, the staff are enthusiasts about beer, and the alcohol-free provision is typically one imported can in a fridge, if that.

Idle does something better. It keeps four named mocktails on the list, and the selection shows someone thought about balance rather than reaching for juice. A Southside is a mint, lime and citrus drink, sharp and herbal. A Spanish gin and tonic is defined by botanicals and quinine bitterness, served long over ice — arguably the single easiest classic to render convincingly without alcohol, because so much of its character comes from the tonic and the garnish rather than the gin. A beachside fizz and a French twist round out the range.

What those choices have in common is dryness. None of them is a sugar delivery system, which is a meaningful signal from a venue that could easily have printed three fruit sodas and called it a menu.

The hours make it one of the more useful addresses in this guide: open from noon every day, to midnight through the week and 2am on Friday and Saturday. Combined with Double Standard and The Moon's Daughters, it means San Antonio has a genuine late-night option for someone not drinking, which is more than most cities of its size manage. Its position near the Pearl and Isidore makes it a natural second or third stop on an evening. The brewing operation also means the beer-drinkers in the group are properly served, which is what makes it work as a compromise venue rather than a concession. Nobody in the group is settling, which is the difference between a venue that tolerates a non-drinker and one that has actually thought about mixed company.
venues.pressQuote: Idle Beer Hall & Brewery: Southside mocktail, Spanish gin and tonic, beachside fizz, French twist.

venues.name: ilili
venues.description: ilili is the Washington outpost of the Manhattan Lebanese institution, opened on 7 October 2021 at 100 District Square SW at The Wharf on the Southwest waterfront. It is led by executive chef, CEO and owner Philippe Massoud, and the menu is an ode to his Lebanese heritage, served mezza-style with an emphasis on Mediterranean seafood. The dining room is built to evoke a Beirut courtyard: custom daisy-tile floors, hand-painted wallpaper, reclaimed barn wood, citrus trees, hanging plants and a water fountain. Its non-alcoholic programme centres on spirit-free bottled drinks created by beverage director Rachid Hdouche, who builds them around Levantine flavours - the Karkadih, a hibiscus and rosehip cordial, and a Levantine Lemonade with mint and fresh lemon juice. Lunch, weekend brunch and dinner nightly.
venues.hours: Lunch: Wed-Fri 11:30am-2:30pm; Brunch: Sat-Sun 11am-2:30pm; Dinner: Sun-Thu 5-10pm, Fri-Sat 5-10:30pm
signatureDrinks: Levantine Lemonade (mint and fresh lemon juice)
venues.longDescription:
ilili began in Manhattan, where it became one of the city's best-known Lebanese restaurants, and the Washington branch opened on 7 October 2021 at The Wharf, the redeveloped stretch of the Southwest waterfront. It is led by Philippe Massoud, who is executive chef, CEO and owner rather than a name on the door, and the menu is explicitly an ode to the tables and flavours of his Lebanese heritage: mezza-style small plates built for sharing, with a pronounced emphasis on Mediterranean seafood. The room is one of the more considered in the neighbourhood, designed to evoke a Beirut courtyard with custom daisy-tile floors, hand-painted wallpaper, reclaimed barn wood, citrus trees, hanging plants and a water fountain, and it is large enough that it works for a group without feeling like a hall.

The non-alcoholic programme is unusual in form as well as content. Rather than building spirit-free drinks to order, beverage director Rachid Hdouche makes them as bottled drinks, which lets him get Levantine flavours to sit properly rather than relying on a shake to hold them together. Washingtonian, listing ilili among DC-area restaurants with great non-alcoholic cocktails, described exactly that - Hdouche capturing Levantine flavours in the spirit-free bottled drinks at the Manhattan institution's roomy Wharf outpost. The two named pours are the Karkadih, a hibiscus and rosehip cordial that runs tart and floral rather than sweet, and the Levantine Lemonade, made with mint and fresh lemon juice, which is the simpler and more refreshing of the pair and pairs naturally with the mezza.

A few practical points. The restaurant keeps unusually wide hours for a place of its ambition: lunch Wednesday through Friday from 11.30am, brunch on both weekend days from 11am, and dinner every night, to 10pm Sunday through Thursday and 10.30pm on Friday and Saturday. That breadth matters for anyone not drinking, because it means the spirit-free list is available across brunch and lunch as well as dinner. The Wharf setting puts it on the water with a long promenade outside, and it is a short walk from the Waterfront Metro station.
venues.pressQuote: Beverage director Rachid Hdouche captures Levantine flavors in the spirit-free bottled drinks at the Manhattan Lebanese institution's roomy Wharf outpost, including the Karkadih, a hibiscus and rosehip cordial, and the Levantine Lemonade with mint and fresh lemon juice.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Washingtonian, "13 DC-Area Bars and Restaurants With Great Non-Alcoholic Cocktails" (2024)

venues.name: In Confidence
venues.description: In Confidence is the speakeasy inside the Hotel Fort Des Moines, and it stocks the Lyre's range properly — a Zero Proof Mint Julep built on Lyre's bourbon alternative with simple syrup and mint, and a gin and tonic on Lyre's London dry with Fever Tree tonic. Both are straight substitutions into classics, which is exactly what a lot of non-drinkers actually want: not an invented fruit drink, but the thing they used to order, made properly. A julep in particular is almost all spirit, so making a convincing one without alcohol requires the bar to have bought a real product rather than improvised.
signatureDrinks: Zero Proof Mint Julep — Lyre's bourbon alternative, simple syrup, mint
Gin & Tonic — Lyre's London dry spirit, Fever Tree tonic
venues.longDescription:
The Hotel Fort Des Moines is a restored 1919 property downtown, and In Confidence is the speakeasy beneath it — a small, dark room behind an unmarked entrance, open only Thursday through Saturday.

Its alcohol-free approach is the one this directory finds most consistently underrated: straight substitution into classics using real products, rather than inventing something new. The Zero Proof Mint Julep is Lyre's bourbon alternative with simple syrup and mint. The gin and tonic is Lyre's London dry with Fever Tree tonic. Neither is clever. Both are correct.

The julep is the one that proves the bar is serious. A mint julep is essentially bourbon, sugar, mint and crushed ice — there is no juice, no soda, nothing to carry flavour except the spirit itself. It is one of the hardest drinks in the canon to make without alcohol, and it is completely impossible to fake. A bar putting one on the menu has bought a bottle of Lyre's bourbon and decided it works.

That matters for a specific reason. A large share of people who stop drinking do not want an invented alcohol-free cocktail with dragon fruit in it; they want the drink they always ordered, in the glass it always came in, without the alcohol. Being able to order a julep in a speakeasy and have it arrive looking exactly like everyone else's is a different experience from being handed something new and fruit-forward.

Des Moines' tourism board documented both drinks in January 2026.

The hours are the constraint and they are tight: 5pm to 1am Thursday, Friday and Saturday only, closed Sunday through Wednesday. This is a weekend room. Booking is sensible, as the space is small.
venues.pressQuote: Zero Proof Mint Julep (Lyre's bourbon, simple syrup, mint)

venues.name: In Good Spirits
venues.description: In Good Spirits is a dedicated non-alcoholic bottle shop and community space in Chicago's West Town, opened on July 15, 2023 by couple Adriana Gaspar and Hector Diaz. The two ran sober pop-ups around the city before securing a permanent storefront; both came to the alcohol-free life through personal experience — Gaspar stopped drinking after losing her father to COVID-19, and Diaz cut back following a kidney cancer diagnosis. The shelves carry zero-proof beer, wine, spirits, aperitifs, functional and hemp drinks, and RTDs to take away, with local delivery and online pick-up ordering. This is a shop rather than a bar — drinks are sold to go, not poured to sit with. Beyond retail it works as a third space, and the events calendar is the reason to plan a visit: sober supper clubs with local restaurants, zero-proof cocktail workshops, 'POUring' brand tastings with producers such as Copenhagen Sparkling Tea Co. and Kolonne Null, book swaps, artist showcases, sound meditations, and Lotería nights. It is Chicago's longest-running non-alcoholic shop.
venues.longDescription:
In Good Spirits opened on 15 July 2023 at 858 N Ashland Avenue in West Town, and it is now the longest-running dedicated non-alcoholic shop in Chicago. It is owned by Adriana Gaspar and Hector Diaz, who came to it from inside the drinks industry — Diaz worked in beverage alcohol for nearly a decade, and Gaspar spent her career at marketing agencies representing major alcohol brands — and from personal reckonings that they have been open about. Gaspar stopped drinking after her father died of COVID-19 in late 2020; Diaz cut back after a kidney cancer diagnosis and surgery. They spent 2022 running sober pop-ups around the city before taking the Ashland storefront, which was designed by Points of Sail with furniture built by Rainbolt Productions, and the result is a shop that reads as a room to spend time in rather than a shelf of substitutes.

The range covers the full category rather than a corner of it — non-alcoholic beer, still and sparkling wine, zero-proof spirits, aperitifs and functional drinks — and the important structural detail is that you are not limited to taking it away. Anything on the shelf can be opened and drunk in the shop's community space, and the owners run a rotating menu of handmade cocktails alongside it, which makes this function as a bar as much as a bottle shop. That community-space framing is the stated point: the shop describes itself as a third space where connection can happen without alcohol present, and it programmes events accordingly. The Chicago Sun-Times, reporting on the city's sober-curious drinkers at the end of 2024, found business here rising year on year with holiday sales outpacing the previous season. Two practical notes. Opening hours are Wednesday through Sunday, closed Monday and Tuesday, and the shop occasionally posts adjusted hours that are worth checking before travelling. And alongside the strictly non-alcoholic stock the range includes hemp and functional products, so anyone avoiding all psychoactives will want to read labels or ask rather than assume everything on the shelf is inert.
venues.pressQuote: Today, the event space and retail store is the longest-running non-alcoholic store in the city.

venues.name: Incloud
venues.description: Incloud is a fully alcohol-free Chinese teahouse on Prinsep Street, and the only venue of its kind in Singapore built around a floating stream: a channel of running water set into the communal table that carries cups of tea to guests. It trades as an elegant tea-set room by day, with pastries and full gongfu service, and shifts into something much closer to a bar at night. The hours are what make it genuinely useful to a non-drinker — it runs until 3am from Sunday to Friday and until 4am on Saturdays, which is later than most licensed bars in the city, making it one of the very few late-night social venues in Singapore where alcohol is not part of the equation.
venues.longDescription:
Incloud opened on Prinsep Street as Singapore's first teahouse with a floating river — a shallow channel of moving water built into the communal table, along which cups and small dishes are floated to guests. The gimmick is genuinely charming, and it has made the room a fixture of local food media, but the reason it belongs in an alcohol-free guide is more practical than aesthetic: this is a fully alcohol-free venue that stays open past the point at which most of Singapore's bars have closed.

The tea programme is a real one. The room serves Chinese-style teas in proper gongfu format alongside elegant tea sets with pastries, and it is set up for the slow, repeated-infusion drinking that makes tea a social activity rather than a single-cup transaction. During the day the atmosphere is closer to a refined cafe, and it draws a crowd that comes for the interiors as much as the leaf. The shift happens in the evening, when the lighting drops and the room takes on a bar-like character — the same table, the same stream, a different mood.

That late licence is the crucial detail. Incloud runs to 3am Sunday through Friday and to 4am on Saturday. For anyone in Singapore who is not drinking, the usual problem is not finding a good non-alcoholic drink at 8pm; it is finding anywhere to sit with friends at 1am that is not built around a bar. Incloud answers that directly, and it does so without kava, kratom or any of the psychoactive alternatives that fill the same niche in American cities — this is tea, served late, in a room designed for lingering. Reservations are taken by phone and WhatsApp, and are worth making at weekends.

venues.name: Indígena by Owamni
venues.description: Indígena by Owamni is the new Guthrie Theater home of chef Sean Sherman's James Beard Award-winning Indigenous restaurant, which closed its original Water Works space in May 2026 and reopened along the Mississippi riverfront in spring 2026. Operated through Sherman's nonprofit NĀTIFS (North American Traditional Indigenous Food Systems), it serves decolonized, pre-colonial cuisine that excludes wheat, dairy, cane sugar, and other colonial imports. The bar is a defining feature: built originally by Anishinaabe/Ojibwe bar manager Kareen Teague, it pioneered an entirely spirit-free Indigenous cocktail menu using foraged Minnesota ingredients — wild rice, corn, currants, teas, and birch, maple, or honey in place of cane sugar. The expanded Guthrie program keeps cocktails and mocktails sourced from BIPOC producers, plus Indigenous teas and Indigenous-owned Copper Cup coffee. Documented zero-proof pours include the Amikomin (black currant, juniper, sumac, birch) and Oginii-Waabigwan (rosehip, strawberry, lavender, agave, rosewater).
venues.longDescription:
Indígena by Owamni is the Guthrie Theater home of chef Sean Sherman's James Beard Award-winning Indigenous restaurant, which closed its original Water Works space in May 2026 and reopened on the Mississippi riverfront in spring 2026. It operates through Sherman's nonprofit NĀTIFS — North American Traditional Indigenous Food Systems — and serves decolonised, pre-colonial cuisine, which in practice means the kitchen excludes wheat, dairy, cane sugar, beef, pork, chicken and other ingredients brought by European colonisation. That constraint is the restaurant's entire intellectual proposition, and it produces food that tastes like almost nothing else in American dining.

The bar is not an afterthought to that idea but an extension of it, and it is the reason this restaurant belongs near the top of any list of spirit-free drinking in the United States. Built originally by Anishinaabe and Ojibwe bar manager Kareen Teague, it pioneered an entirely spirit-free Indigenous cocktail menu drawn from foraged Minnesota ingredients — wild rice, corn, currants, teas, and birch, maple or honey standing in for cane sugar. The logic is elegant: distilled spirits are themselves a colonial import, so a decolonised bar is necessarily a non-alcoholic one, and the zero-proof menu here exists for reasons of history rather than wellness. Documented pours include the Amikomin, built on black currant with juniper, sumac and birch, and the Oginii-Waabigwan, which works rosehip and strawberry against lavender, agave and rosewater. A third, Nimaammaa, sits alongside them. The expanded Guthrie programme keeps both cocktails and spirit-free drinks sourced from BIPOC producers, and pours Indigenous teas and Indigenous-owned Copper Cup coffee. Teague's own summary is the clearest statement of why it works: "To have a non-alcoholic menu, especially in the larger context of Indigenous food and culture, just feels right." For a non-drinker, this is one of very few restaurants anywhere where the absence of alcohol is the point of the room rather than a concession within it.
venues.pressQuote: To have a non-alcoholic menu, especially in the larger context of Indigenous food and culture, just feels right.

venues.name: The Inferno Room
venues.description: The Inferno Room is a tiki bar on Virginia Avenue in Fountain Square, opened on 11 September 2018 by longtime tiki collector Ed Rudisell with his wife Sasatorn Rudisell and partner Chris Coy, in a building that once held a Marion County courthouse. It holds what the bar describes as one of the largest collections of Papua New Guinea art outside a museum, split across the Kahuna Lounge and the Luau Room. The non-alcoholic drinks are printed as their own MOCKTAILS section of the cocktail menu at $10 each — the Coocoonut Grove, The Way to Eden and Veiled Virtues — built to the same tropical, layered spec as the rum drinks rather than reduced to fruit juice.
venues.hours: Mon closed; Tue-Thu 4pm-11pm; Fri 4pm-1am; Sat 2pm-1am; Sun 4pm-11pm
signatureDrinks: Coocoonut Grove (coconut, pineapple, cinnamon, walnut bitters, lemon)
The Way to Eden (passion fruit, orgeat, pineapple, kiwi, prickly pear, lemon)
Veiled Virtues (strawberry, cinnamon, coconut, pineapple, lemon, orange juice)
