venues.longDescription:
Ed Rudisell had been collecting Polynesian and Papua New Guinean art for years before he turned it into a bar. The Inferno Room opened on 11 September 2018 at 902 Virginia Avenue in Fountain Square — a building that previously housed a Marion County courthouse — with Rudisell, his wife Sasatorn Rudisell and partner Chris Coy behind it. What they built is a serious tiki room rather than a themed one: the drink list pays close attention to mid-century Polynesian restaurant menus, the rum selection is deep, and the collection on the walls is, by the bar's own account, among the largest holdings of Papua New Guinea native art outside a museum. The space divides into the Kahuna Lounge and the Luau Room, and the bar runs its own annual Infernohana event.

Tiki is a difficult category to drink in without alcohol, because the classics are built on overproof rum and the usual alcohol-free substitute is a glass of pineapple juice. The Inferno Room prints a MOCKTAILS heading on its cocktail menu and puts three drinks under it at $10 each, all constructed rather than poured. The Coocoonut Grove runs coconut and pineapple against cinnamon, lemon and walnut bitters, so it lands bitter and spiced rather than sweet. The Way to Eden is the most complex of them — passion fruit, orgeat, pineapple, kiwi, prickly pear and lemon. Veiled Virtues sits between the two, on strawberry, cinnamon, coconut, pineapple, lemon and orange juice. Local Dry January coverage has also listed a fourth, The Deceiver, which rotates on and off. Hours run to 11pm midweek and 1am on Friday and Saturday, and the room sits three blocks from Nine Lives on Shelby Street, which makes for one of the better alcohol-free evenings available in Indianapolis. Two things to plan around. The Inferno Room is small and does not take the whole neighbourhood at once, so weekend evenings run on a wait; going early on a Tuesday or Wednesday is the way to actually look at the art and talk to the bartender about what is in the glass. And the room is unmistakably a rum bar — the shelves, the smell and the conversation are all about overproof Jamaican rum and Swedish punsch, so if you are avoiding alcohol in a way that makes being surrounded by it difficult, this is a harder room than a café. If it works for you, though, it is the most ambitious alcohol-free drink in the city, and the only place in Indianapolis building non-alcoholic drinks around orgeat, prickly pear and walnut bitters rather than juice and soda.
venues.pressQuote: The Inferno Room in Fountain Square offers four mocktail options — the Coocoonut Grove, The Deceiver, The Way to Eden, and Veiled Virtues — each for $10.

venues.name: INI Studio
venues.description: INI Studio is a fully alcohol-free, all-white specialty cafe on Queensberry Street in Carlton, built around silky ceremonial matcha and manual-brew coffee. It is a daytime third-space rather than a bar: the drinks list runs to a matcha latte (A$5.50), an iced matcha (A$7.50) that reviewers rate among the best in Melbourne, and a hojicha latte (A$5.50), alongside pour-over coffee, seasonal Korean binsu shaved ice, waffles and tiramisu. There is a second, equally minimalist location on Smith Street in Collingwood. Every drink on the menu is non-alcoholic.
signatureDrinks: Matcha latte — whisked ceremonial matcha with milk (around A$5.50)
Iced matcha — cold matcha over ice, rated among Melbourne's best (around A$7.50)
Hojicha latte — roasted green tea latte (around A$5.50)
Filter / pour-over coffee — manual-brew specialty coffee
venues.longDescription:
INI Studio opened its original Carlton cafe on Queensberry Street in 2021, a beautifully minimal room dedicated to specialty coffee and the craft of manual brewing. Started by barista Kiyong Jung, it has since grown to a second, equally all-white site at 62 Smith Street in Collingwood, both trading on the same tranquil, pared-back aesthetic.

The drink of note here is matcha: INI whisks a silky, frothy matcha that regulars and Melbourne food writers single out, poured hot as a matcha latte (around A$5.50) or over ice (around A$7.50). Beyond matcha the counter runs a hojicha latte (around A$5.50), carefully made pour-over and espresso coffee, and sweets including a cult tiramiu and seasonal Korean binsu shaved ice. There is no bar and no alcohol anywhere on the menu, making it a genuinely alcohol-free social space by design rather than by afterthought.

The room is the draw as much as the cup: an all-white, modern, minimalist interior that reads calm and gallery-like, a quiet place to sit and sip. It keeps daytime cafe hours (roughly 7am to 4pm on weekdays, shorter on weekends), so it works as a morning or afternoon third-space rather than an evening venue. Time Out's Melbourne matcha guide named it a genuine hot spot, and it has become a fixture of the city's matcha scene.
venues.pressQuote: With two iconic locations and likely more to come, Ini Studios has become quite the hot spot in Melbourne if you're after a relaxing, aesthetically pleasing spot for your morning matcha run.

venues.name: Inside Passage
venues.description: Inside Passage is an immersive undersea-themed cocktail bar on Pike Street on Capitol Hill, entered through a passage inside Rumba, opened on 25 June 2021 by Travis Rosenthal's Pike Street Hospitality Group. The room is the point: aged ship-hull walls, float and pufferfish lights, and Kiki, an octopus with tentacles up to eighteen feet wrapped across the ceiling in a perpetual state of mid-slither — bar staff spent a spring at home crafting the fake suckers. Drinks arrive with enough theatre that Seattle Met named the phenomenon "the fajita effect": a bartender walks a drink carefully through the tight room and every table pauses to watch. It maintains a dedicated non-alcoholic menu headed "Spirit Free Libations". IMPORTANT: that menu is published through a system we cannot read — the site renders its drink lists entirely in the browser with no readable version underneath — so we cannot list the current spirit-free drinks, their ingredients or their prices, and we could not complete our usual check for infused ingredients. Ask at the bar. It is 21+, seats parties of six or fewer, takes reservations up to six weeks ahead, and adds a 20% service charge.
venues.longDescription:
Inside Passage opened on 25 June 2021 in a former Stussy shop on Pike Street, reached through a passage inside Rumba, and it is the most committed piece of set design in Seattle drinking. Travis Rosenthal's Pike Street Hospitality Group is behind it, with interiors by Notch Gonzalez. The walls are aged wooden ship hull with light leaking through the plank cracks; the ceiling carries float lamps and pufferfish lights and Kiki, an octopus whose tentacles run up to eighteen feet, described by Seattle Met as suspended overhead in a perpetual state of mid-slither. Some of the city's best bartenders spent a spring at home making her fake suckers. The drinks are served with matching theatre — Seattle Met coined "the fajita effect" for it: a bartender walks a drink carefully through the tight interior, and every table pauses, hushed, to take in the spectacle. Manager Jen Akin's framing of how the bar arrived at its concept is characteristically unromantic: they had done a lot of learning in the last year.

The bar keeps a dedicated non-alcoholic menu, and it is headed Spirit Free Libations — we can confirm the section exists and what it is called. What we cannot give you is what is on it, and it would be wrong to pretend otherwise. Inside Passage publishes all of its menus through a system that assembles them in the browser, with no readable version underneath, so the drinks, their ingredients and their prices cannot be checked from outside. That also means we could not complete the check we run on every venue for cannabis, kava or other infused ingredients hiding under a zero-proof heading — not because we found something, but because we could not see the list at all. For a bar this theatrical the spirit-free drinks are very likely to be worth ordering, and every account of the room suggests the staff take them seriously. Just ask at the bar rather than planning around a name. Practical notes that do check out: it is 21-and-over with a physical ID required, seats parties of six or fewer because the room is small, takes reservations up to six weeks ahead with a $20-per-person no-show charge, and adds a 20% service charge retained by the house.

venues.name: Insomnia ISG Kava Bar and Lounge
venues.description: Insomnia ISG is a Temple Terrace kava lounge that describes itself plainly as a sober bar, open from noon to midnight through the week and to 11pm on Sunday, in a family-friendly room rather than a nightlife one. It serves no alcohol. The list runs kava, botanical teas, loose-leaf tea and coffee, and the venue sits close enough to the University of South Florida to function as a late study room as well as a social one. Two things to know before going: hookah is served, so the room is not smoke-free, and the hours posted on its own site differ slightly from other listings, so call ahead on (813) 570-8137 if you are arriving near closing.
venues.longDescription:
Insomnia ISG describes itself, plainly and without qualification, as a sober bar. That phrasing is rarer than it should be in this category — most kava rooms sell themselves on wellness or on botanicals, and relatively few name the thing their customers are actually looking for. It trades from noon to midnight through the week and to 11pm on Sunday, from a unit on North 56th Street in Temple Terrace, and it serves no alcohol.

The room is presented as family-friendly rather than as nightlife, which shapes who uses it. Temple Terrace sits immediately east of the University of South Florida, and the venue works as a late study room as much as a social one — the drinks list runs kava, botanical teas, loose-leaf tea and coffee, which covers both a working afternoon and an evening out.

Kava is the ground root of Piper methysticum, a shrub native to the South Pacific islands, prepared as a cold water infusion and drunk socially across Fiji, Vanuatu, Tonga and Samoa for roughly three thousand years. It contains no alcohol. It tastes earthy and bitter, numbs the lips and tongue on the first mouthful, and is mildly sedative rather than intoxicating in the way alcohol is. Because kava exhibits reverse tolerance, regular drinkers typically need less rather than more to feel it, so a first visit is best taken slowly across an hour or two — advice worth emphasising near a university campus, where the instinct may be to treat a shell like a shot.

Two practical notes before visiting, both of which are reasons to arrive informed rather than reasons to stay away.

First, hookah is served here, and the room is therefore not smoke-free. For a lot of people managing recovery — particularly anyone with a respiratory condition, or anyone who has given up tobacco alongside alcohol — that matters as much as the drinks question does, and it is not something the venue's sober-bar framing tells you.

Second, the hours posted on the venue's own site differ slightly from other listings, so if you are arriving near closing it is worth a call on (813) 570-8137 first. Small independent rooms update one listing and forget the other, and a wasted trip across town is a bad way to find that out.

For the USF area — a large student population, a lot of people not drinking, and very little else open late without a bar attached — this is a genuinely useful room.

venues.name: Ishizuka
venues.description: Ishizuka is a two-hatted, 16-seat basement kaiseki counter down a Bourke Street laneway, where a Kaga-style seasonal degustation is matched course-by-course to drinks. Alongside its award-winning wine list, the kitchen runs a genuine non-alcoholic beverage pairing (from A$90 per person) built from house juices, teas and infusions timed to each of the courses. It's a real zero-proof pairing at a fine-dining level rather than a token soft-drink option, which makes the A$315 tasting menu fully drinkable without alcohol. The kaiseki menu offers non-alcoholic matches from $90 per person, printed on the same menu as the $250 wine matches rather than arranged on request.
venues.address: Basement B01/139 Bourke Street, Melbourne VIC 3000
signatureDrinks: Non-alcoholic matches — the kitchen's alcohol-free pairing, from $90 per person
venues.longDescription:
Ishizuka sits below a Bourke Street laneway in the Melbourne CBD, its entrance next to sister restaurant Oden. Only 16 seats wrap the counter inside a room designed by Russell & George as a light, airy cocoon crowned by a huge white dome evoking a Japanese lantern. The restaurant serves a single seasonal Kaga kaiseki degustation and holds two hats in the Age Good Food Guide 2026.

The kitchen was founded by chef Tomotaka Ishizuka, who previously ran Koko at Crown and cooked at Kisume; the current seasonal menu is led by executive chef Katsuji Yoshino. The multi-course kaiseki is priced at A$315 per person and changes with what the market brings — as the chef has put it, the sashimi fish is chosen day to day based on what the fishmonger delivers.

Drinks are treated as seriously as the food. Ishizuka took Three Glasses at Australia's Wine List of the Year Awards 2024, and its beverage pairings run in parallel: a wine match from A$250 and a dedicated non-alcoholic pairing from A$90 per person, poured course-by-course from house juices, teas and infusions rather than off-the-shelf substitutes. That course-timed zero-proof pairing lets a non-drinking guest follow the same progression as the table without compromise.

Dinner runs Wednesday to Sunday from 5:30pm, and with just 16 seats booking ahead is essential. Find it on Instagram at @ishizuka_australia.

The pairing is printed, and the price is the proof. Ishizuka's own menu lists wine matches from an additional $250 per person and non-alcoholic matches from $90 per person — two lines in the same place on the same card. A restaurant that prints an alcohol-free price has committed to producing it on a quiet Tuesday as well as a full Saturday, and it removes the small social tax of having to ask the waiter what might be possible.

Kaiseki is also unusually well suited to the format. The menu moves through many small, precisely seasoned courses in a fixed order, which is exactly the structure a drinks flight is built to track, and Japanese cooking already has a deep non-alcoholic pantry to draw on — cold-brewed and hot teas, roasted grains, dashi-adjacent savoury infusions and fruit vinegars. The room itself is a quiet basement dining room seating a small number of guests, so booking well ahead is essential and the pairing is best requested when you reserve.
venues.pressQuote: My fishmonger will always get the best fish for me, so I'll change the fish for the sashimi course based on what he brings me.

venues.name: Isidore
venues.description: Isidore is the fine-dining anchor of the Pullman Market development, and its zero-proof drinks are built on the two non-alcoholic spirits that actually work rather than on syrup. The Maravilla Margarita is modified with Almave blanco, the agave-based non-alcoholic distillate developed with Lewis Hamilton, and the Labrador Spritz uses Tenneyson Black Ginger, a bitter non-alcoholic aperitif that supplies the quality most zero-proof drinks lack. Choosing those two products over a house cordial is the whole signal: they are expensive, they exist only to serve non-drinkers, and stocking them is a deliberate decision. Dinner only, Tuesday to Sunday from 5pm, inside the Pullman Market development just north of downtown.
signatureDrinks: Maravilla Margarita (modified) - Almave blanco non-alcoholic agave
Labrador Spritz - Tenneyson non-alcoholic black ginger aperitif
venues.longDescription:
Isidore is the flagship restaurant inside Pullman Market, the food hall and market development that reworked a stretch of San Antonio's near-downtown, and it operates at the top end of the city's dining. Its non-alcoholic drinks are worth attention for one specific reason: the products behind them.

The Maravilla Margarita is rebuilt with Almave blanco. Almave is a non-alcoholic agave distillate made from blue agave rather than assembled from botanical extracts, and it is one of very few zero-proof spirits that survives being the base of a margarita — the drink is so spirit-forward that a weak substitute simply collapses into limeade. The Labrador Spritz uses Tenneyson Black Ginger, a non-alcoholic aperitif built around bitterness and ginger heat.

Both choices point the same way. These are expensive, specialist products with exactly one use: serving people who are not drinking. A restaurant that stocks them has spent money on a customer most kitchens accommodate with soda water and a lime. It also means the drinks can be genuinely dry and bitter rather than sweet, which is the single most common failure in the category.

That Tenneyson turns up again at Double Standard, across downtown, is worth noting — San Antonio's better bars have converged on the same short list of NA products that actually perform, which is a sign of a scene talking to itself rather than each venue improvising alone.

Isidore serves dinner only, 5pm to 10pm, closed Mondays. Pullman Market itself is worth arriving early for, and the surrounding development puts several other options within a short walk, including Idle Beer Hall and Tony's Siesta on Brooklyn Avenue. For a visitor prepared to spend properly on dinner, it is the strongest argument in the city that a zero-proof pairing can be as considered as a wine list. The kitchen changes with the seasons, so the specific drinks will move; what should persist is the willingness to build around real non-alcoholic spirits rather than fruit juice, which is the part that took investment.
venues.pressQuote: Isidore: Modified Maravilla Margarita (with Almave blanco), Labrador Spritz (with Tenneyson non-alcoholic black ginger aperitif).

venues.name: Jackworth Ginger Beer
venues.description: Jackworth is Pennsylvania's first modern ginger beer brewery, at 6615 Hamilton Avenue on the edge of Larimer, opened to the public in May 2024 by Jackworth Smith — that is his real name — who grew up in his father's East End restaurant, was tending bar at seventeen, and first brewed these recipes at home on a half-barrel system in 2013. It brews naturally fermented ginger beer in both alcoholic versions (a 5% ABV Original and a Sorrel) and a canned zero-proof line printed at 0.0%: Classic (organic Peruvian ginger, lime, water, cane sugar), Spicy (the same with habanero), Honey Lavender and Dry. Because the base is genuinely brewed rather than mixed from syrup, the alcohol-free version keeps the bite and body most zero-proof substitutes lack. The bar builds zero-proof cocktails on it too — a Texas Remedy, a Blood in the River and a Peaches for CJ have all featured — though the bar menu cannot be read online, so treat those names as indicative. The room is salvage-built: a bar of old fencing, bank marble and gold-leaf mansion windows.
venues.longDescription:
Jackworth is a ginger beer brewery at 6615 Hamilton Avenue in Larimer, and the founder's name really is Jackworth Smith. He grew up in his father's restaurant and bar in the East End, started washing dishes at six and was tending bar at seventeen, and in 2013 used century-old recipes and his own fermentation knowledge to make the first batches at home on a half-barrel system. The brewery opened to the public on 9 May 2024. Pittsburgh Magazine catalogued the room better than any summary could: the bar is made from an old fence, marble salvaged from a bank and gold-leaf windows from a gutted mansion, and the fittings run to a desanctified holy water font, a Joe Camel dartboard and the original Dunning's Grille sign on a distressed wall. The drink tokens are poker chips reading "Hey, hun! Good for one." The magazine's description of the aesthetic — somewhere between industrially elegant and gothically yinzer — is exactly right. It opens at 5pm most nights, 4pm on Friday and noon at weekends.

The reason it belongs on an alcohol-free list is structural rather than incidental. Ginger beer is fermented, and fermentation is where the alcohol comes from, so Jackworth brews the same product two ways: an Original and a Sorrel at 5% ABV, and a canned zero-proof line printed at 0.0%. That line runs Classic (organic Peruvian ginger, lime, water, cane sugar), Spicy (the same with habanero), Honey Lavender and Dry. Because the base is genuinely brewed rather than mixed from syrup, the alcohol-free version has the bite and body that make ginger beer worth drinking, which is not true of most zero-proof substitutes. The bar also builds zero-proof cocktails on it — a Texas Remedy, a Blood in the River and a Peaches for CJ have all been on the list — though the bar menu is published in a format that cannot be read online, so treat the names as indicative and ask when you arrive. One curiosity worth flagging so nobody is caught out: Jackworth makes an Orange Kush in collaboration with Wiz Khalifa's Khalifa Kush brand, which sounds infused and is not. Its own label says no THC, no CBD — the cannabis strain supplies terpenes for flavour only.
venues.pressQuote: The bar, for instance, is made from an old fence, marble salvaged from a bank and goldleaf windows from a gutted mansion.

venues.name: Jagger Suite
venues.description: Jagger Suite is a tenth-floor rooftop bar above the Moxy Atlanta Downtown at 329 Marietta Street, opened in early March 2026 by The Restaurant People. The room is styled on Studio 54 — mirrored surfaces, a twelve-foot disco unicorn, sightlines to Mercedes-Benz Stadium — and it trades until 2am, which makes it one of the later options downtown. The non-alcoholic drinks are grouped under a menu heading of their own, Free-Spirited, rather than buried in the list. Rooftop Retreat pairs Ritual's tequila alternative with pineapple, basil and coconut water; Flashback uses a whiskey alternative with ginger and lemon; and Off the Record is built on zero-proof gin with vanilla, pomegranate and citrus. All three are served with the same garnish and glassware as the full-proof list.
venues.address: 329 Marietta St NW, 10th Floor, Atlanta, GA 30313
signatureDrinks: Rooftop Retreat (Ritual tequila alternative, pineapple, basil, coconut water)
Off the Record (zero-proof gin, vanilla, pomegranate, citrus)

naMenuItems.name: Flashback
naMenuItems.description: sharp | lively | reviving ritual whiskey alternative, giffard ginger, lemon. *substitute bulleit bourbon +5

venues.longDescription:
The Restaurant People took the tenth floor of the Moxy Atlanta Downtown at 329 Marietta Street NW and opened Jagger Suite there in early March 2026, aiming squarely at the big-night market: a rooftop lounge with a Studio 54 reference running through the design, a twelve-foot disco unicorn as the room's centrepiece, and a terrace looking across the western edge of downtown towards Mercedes-Benz Stadium. It runs a golden-hour menu of elevated bites early and turns into a late room after ten, trading to 2am Wednesday through Saturday. The cocktail programme includes a dedicated espresso martini list, which tells you the register the bar is working in.

The non-alcoholic drinks are not an afterthought on the board. They are collected under their own heading — Free-Spirited — and there are three of them. Rooftop Retreat uses Ritual Zero Proof's tequila alternative with pineapple, basil and coconut water, a long tropical drink that holds up against the room's noise. Flashback runs a whiskey alternative with ginger and lemon, essentially a non-alcoholic Penicillin structure without the smoke. Off the Record closes the set with a zero-proof gin base, vanilla, pomegranate and citrus. DiningOut's 2026 zero-proof survey noted that all three provide the same energy as the alcoholic cocktails and are best enjoyed under the disco unicorn — which, at a bar built around spectacle, is the whole point: the drink has to look like everyone else's. For anyone in recovery who still wants a rooftop and a DJ rather than a quiet corner, Jagger Suite is one of the few downtown rooms where the alcohol-free order does not mark you out. It sits at a four rather than a five because it is a fully licensed bar with a substantial spirits programme; the zero-proof section is real, named and permanent, but it is a section.
venues.pressQuote: Perched above the Moxy Downtown with Mercedes-Benz Stadium glittering in the distance, Jagger Suite is loud, glamorous, and built for a big night.

venues.name: Jalsah Yemeni Coffee
venues.description: Jalsah is a fully alcohol-free Yemeni coffeehouse on South Broadway in Downtown Los Angeles, open until 9pm on Friday, Saturday and Sunday. It serves eleven Yemeni signature drinks alongside a full espresso bar: hot Adeni, black tea with milk, cardamom and warm spices; Mufawaar, a rich spiced coffee; Qishr, the cascara-style brew made from coffee husk; Baydani, a Yemeni white drink with toasted sesame and ginger; and Jebani. Beans are single-origin from terraced farms in the Yemeni highlands, sourced direct and roasted in small batches. The room is built for staying - free Wi-Fi, plenty of seating, no rush - and the shop's own line for it is to come in for one cup and stay for three. No alcohol is served at any hour.
signatureDrinks: Hot Adeni - black tea with milk, cardamom and warm spices
Hot Mufawaar - rich, aromatic spiced coffee
Hot Qishr - cascara-style drink with Yemeni spice balance
Hot Baydani - Yemeni white drink with toasted sesame and ginger
venues.longDescription:
Jalsah sits on South Broadway at Tenth, in the South Park end of Downtown Los Angeles, and it is a Yemeni coffeehouse in the full sense rather than a cafe that happens to sell Yemeni coffee. The name is the Arabic word for a sitting - a gathering, the act of staying somewhere with people - and the shop builds everything around that. Its three stated principles are the origin, the method and the room: beans grown on terraced mountain farms in the Yemeni highlands and sourced direct, every cup made to order with no shortcuts, and a space with free Wi-Fi, plenty of seating and no pressure to leave. Yemen is where coffee was first cultivated and brewed before it went out through the port of Mokha, and the shop leans on that history without being precious about it.

The drinks list runs to eleven Yemeni signature preparations plus a full espresso bar, and the traditional half is the reason to come. Hot Adeni is black tea with milk, cardamom and warm spices - the Aden-style chai that anchors most Yemeni menus. Mufawaar is the spiced coffee, rich and aromatic, and there is an Adeni Mufawaar that crosses the two. Qishr is brewed from the coffee husk rather than the bean, cascara-style, balanced with Yemeni spice. Baydani is the white drink, made with toasted sesame and ginger. Jebani rounds out the traditional set. Against those sit the modern lattes the shop is equally known for - the Jalsah Signature, the Jalsah Spices, pistachio, coconut, Dubai chocolate and tiramisu - plus iced builds, a slow bar, teas and juices, and fresh pastries including a honeycomb and a smoked salmon bagel.

Nothing on the menu contains alcohol. The hours are what make it useful for an evening rather than a morning: 7am to 8pm Monday through Thursday, 7am to 9pm on Friday and Saturday, and 8am to 9pm on Sunday. That matters in this particular part of Downtown, which is dense with bars serving the Crypto.com Arena and LA Live crowd and thin on anywhere to sit for two hours without drinking. Two practical notes: the in-store board carries the full lineup, which is longer than the website's sample, and the room genuinely is built for working, so it fills with laptops on weekday afternoons.
venues.pressQuote: Come in for one cup. Stay for three.

venues.name: Japp's Since 1879
venues.description: Japp's Since 1879 is a historical-cocktail bar in Over-the-Rhine, opened in 2010 by celebrated Cincinnati bartender Molly Wellmann inside a 19th-century building that started as John G. Japp's hair-and-wig shop. Its specialty is drinks from the 1700s through the 1950s, made with housemade simple syrups, fresh herbs, berries, juices and floral waters, and that same craft carries over to what Wellmann calls "nonnys." Non-alcoholic selections sit right on the regular menu, usually two rotating house zero-proof cocktails built on CleanCo non-alcoholic gin: past pours include the Beehive Jive (chai, honey, pineapple, lemon, orange-blossom water), while the current menu lists Jade without the Fade and Pomade & Pomelo. NA beers (Sam Adams Just the Haze, Budweiser 0.0) round out the list. TV-free and intentionally old-school.
signatureDrinks: Jade without the Fade (CleanCo NA gin, ancho reyes, toasted-sesame syrup, lime, pineapple, saline)
Pomade & Pomelo (pomegranate, lemon, lime, simple syrup)

naMenuItems.name: Jade Without the Fade
naMenuItems.description: cleanco non-alcoholic gin, ancho reyes, toasted sesame simple syrup, lime juice, pineapple juice, and saline. *contains sesame

naMenuItems.name: Pomade & Pomelo
naMenuItems.description: pomegranate juice, lemon juice, lime juice, and simple syrup.

venues.longDescription:
The story of Japp's stretches back to 1879, when John G. Japp opened a hair-and-wig shop at 1134 Main Street in what is now Over-the-Rhine. In 2010, local celebrity bartender Molly Wellmann reopened the space as a cocktail bar devoted to historical drinks, keeping the building's 19th-century details intact and deliberately leaving out televisions to encourage old-school appreciation for classic concoctions. The menu specializes in cocktails from the 1700s through the 1950s, and if you don't arrive with an order in mind the bartenders will happily build something around your preferred spirit.

Wellmann has long championed alcohol-free drinking here. "I have so many customers that come in that love to drink but don't want to drink alcohol," she told CityBeat, and the bar answers with what she calls "nonnys" — non-alcoholic cocktails made with the same care as the rest of the list. All drinks at Japp's, boozy or not, are crafted with housemade simple syrups, fresh herbs, berries, juices and floral waters. The zero-proof selections live right on the regular menu, typically two rotating house cocktails built on CleanCo non-alcoholic gin. A recent standout, the Beehive Jive, layered CleanCo gin with chai, honey, pineapple, lemon juice and orange-blossom water for a creamy, honeyed sip; the current menu lists the Jade without the Fade (CleanCo NA gin, ancho reyes, toasted-sesame syrup, lime, pineapple, saline) and the lighter Pomade & Pomelo (pomegranate, lemon, lime, simple syrup). Non-alcoholic beers — Sam Adams Just the Haze and Budweiser 0.0 — round things out.

Japp's is small and unpretentious, tucked into OTR's Main Street entertainment strip. It's open Tuesday through Sunday from 4 p.m. — until midnight early week and Sunday, and until 2:30 a.m. Thursday through Saturday — and closed Mondays. Because the nonny cocktails rotate, the exact two on offer vary by visit, so it's worth asking the bartender for the current zero-proof options; they're glad to recommend one. Note that the bar adds a small operational surcharge to checks (removable on request) and an automatic 20% gratuity on open tabs at close.
venues.pressQuote: I have so many customers that come in that love to drink but don't want to drink alcohol.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Molly Wellmann, owner, quoted by Kara Driscoll in CityBeat

venues.name: Jasher's Organic Tea House
venues.description: Jasher's Organic Tea House is a fully alcohol-free tea house tucked inside Joyce Skylight Court in Bay View, pouring more than 20 organic loose-leaf teas in a living-room-style cafe. Owners Jack and Rumi DeDecker serve ceremonial matcha, pour-over coffee and a masala chai built from Rumi's childhood recipe, alongside fresh popcorn and local baked goods. Nothing on the menu contains alcohol — the entire board is zero-proof by design.
venues.address: 2680 S. Kinnickinnic Ave., Ste. 4, Milwaukee, WI 53207 (inside Joyce Skylight Court)
venues.hours: Mon closed; Tue-Fri 4pm-9pm; Sat 9am-5pm; Sun closed
venues.longDescription:
Opened quietly in late November 2025 and named for the owners' young son, Jasher, this Bay View tea house occupies Suite 4 of Joyce Skylight Court at 2680 S. Kinnickinnic Ave. Jack and Rumi DeDecker built the room to feel like a living room rather than a transactional coffee counter, with cozy couches, gentle background music and a shelf full of board games.

The draw is the tea itself: an all-organic lineup of nearly two dozen loose-leaf teas, from Jade Cloud green and Silver Needles white to fermented Pu'er Tuo Cha, plus herbal infusions like Turmeric Ginger Tonic and Vanilla Rooibos. Ceremonial matcha, pour-over coffee and hot cocoa round out the board, and the standout is a traditional masala chai made with black Assam tea, fresh ginger, whole spices and jaggery from Rumi's childhood recipe. Snacks run to fresh coconut-oil popcorn and baked goods from local Rise and Shine Bakery.

Because nothing on the menu contains alcohol, Jasher's is a genuine zero-proof destination, a place to linger over a hot or iced cup without a single intoxicating option in the room. The DeDeckers marked the milestone with a three-day grand opening June 11-13, 2026, featuring tea tastings, live music and giveaways. Hours are Tuesday through Friday, 4 to 9 p.m., and Saturday, 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.
venues.pressQuote: Cozy couches, gentle background music and a shelf full of board games give the cafe the feel of a living room.

venues.name: Lightbox Cafe
venues.description: Lightbox Cafe is an all-vegan, fully alcohol-free cafe and lounge in Queen Village billed as the Philadelphia region's first kava bar, home to the Jaya Kava kava program. Note that it now trades daytime hours only, closing at 5pm and shut Sunday and Monday, so it works as an afternoon alternative rather than an evening one. It was founded by Jennifer Hombach - a sustainability activist and yoga teacher who first built Jaya Kava as a pop-up - together with Gabriel Vazquez, a former operations manager at Philadelphia Brewing Co. The two opened the South 4th Street location in 2021. The concept is deliberate: an alcohol-free alternative to the neighborhood bar, serving certified Pacific-Island kava straight in coconut shells or mixed into "kavatails," alongside kratom teas, herbal elixirs, cacao drinks, and superfood smoothies. Named pours include House Kava Kava, Mylky Kava, Cacao Kava, the Kava Mule, Kava Colada, Passion Fruit Kava and the Hibiscus Kava Spritz. The plant-based food menu spans bowls, toasts, wraps, and vegan desserts.

Kava Colada (kava blended with frozen pineapple, fresh lime juice, coconut cream, agave) $13

Hibiscus Kava Spritz (kava shaken with hibiscus, lime, muddled mint, palo santo bitters, lavender lemonade, club soda) $12
venues.longDescription:
Lightbox Cafe on South 4th Street in Queen Village is the home of the Jaya Kava programme, and it is billed as the Philadelphia region's first kava bar. It is entirely vegan and entirely alcohol-free. It was founded by Jennifer Hombach — a sustainability activist and yoga teacher who first ran Jaya Kava as a pop-up — with Gabriel Vazquez, formerly an operations manager at Philadelphia Brewing Co., and the two opened the permanent room in 2021.

Hombach's own framing of the concept, given to the Philadelphia Inquirer, is that a kava bar is an alternative to bars, and a friendlier and more social one. The room was built to that brief: certified Pacific Island kava served traditionally in coconut shells or mixed into what the bar calls kavatails, alongside kratom teas, herbal elixirs, cacao drinks and superfood smoothies. Named pours include House Kava Kava, the Mylky Kava brewed with oat mylk and dates, a Cacao Kava, the Kava Mule, a Kava Colada, a Passion Fruit Kava and a Hibiscus Kava Spritz. A Golden Chai Kava was listed here previously and is no longer on the menu as of August 2026. The food is plant-based throughout — bowls, toasts, wraps and vegan desserts.

An important practical correction, because it changes what this venue is useful for: Lightbox now trades daytime hours only, opening at ten in the morning and closing at five, shut on Sunday and Monday. Earlier coverage described kava service beginning at five in the evening, so the evening trade appears to have been discontinued. It is now an afternoon room rather than a night-out one, which is why it is graded as a strong daytime destination rather than as a bar substitute. Check before making a late trip.

On kava and kratom, the same caution applies here as anywhere. Neither contains alcohol; both are psychoactive. Kava is calming and mildly sedative; kratom is stimulant at low doses, sedative at higher ones, and carries a real dependence risk. Anyone pregnant, on medication, managing liver health or in recovery should consult a doctor first.
venues.pressQuote: A kava bar is an alternative to bars. It's more friendly and social.

venues.name: Jerry's Bar
venues.description: Jerry's Bar is a Northern Liberties corner bar in a former general store, and its menu carries a printed "Mocktails" heading with four house builds between $8 and $9. The NA Toasted Coconut Espresso Martini is the most technically ambitious — cold brew with a toasted coconut simple syrup and coconut purée, shaken to the foam an espresso martini lives or dies by. Lady Lavender runs citrus with lavender simple and club soda; Sunflower Fizz uses a blackberry sunflower simple with pomegranate and lemon; and Hibiscus Breeze pairs hibiscus tea and grapefruit with a spicy lavender syrup. Athletic Brewing's non-alcoholic beer is $8. The Philadelphia Inquirer covered the bar as part of the city's first large-scale Dry January bar crawl in January 2026.
signatureDrinks: NA Toasted Coconut Espresso Martini ($9) — cold brew, toasted coconut simple, coconut purée
Lady Lavender ($8) — citrus, lavender simple, club soda
Sunflower Fizz ($8) — blackberry sunflower simple, pomegranate, lemon, club soda
Hibiscus Breeze ($9) — hibiscus tea, grapefruit, spicy lavender simple, club soda

naMenuItems.name: Toasted Coconut Espresso Martini
naMenuItems.description: cold brew, toasted coconut simple, coconut puree

venues.longDescription:
Jerry's Bar occupies a corner building on West Laurel Street in Northern Liberties that spent decades as a general store, and the room still reads that way — tin ceiling, long wooden bar, the feel of a neighbourhood fixture rather than a designed concept. It keeps proper bar hours, to midnight on Friday and Saturday, and opens at nine in the morning at weekends for brunch.

The drinks list carries a printed "Mocktails" heading and four house builds beneath it, which puts it ahead of most corner bars in the city. The NA Toasted Coconut Espresso Martini is the one that shows the bar is trying: an espresso martini is defined by its foam, the dense pale head that comes from hard-shaking fresh espresso, and removing the vodka makes that head harder to build, not easier. Using cold brew with a toasted coconut simple syrup and coconut purée gives the shake enough fat and sugar to hold the texture, which is a real piece of bar thinking rather than a substitution.

The other three run lighter and all finish on club soda. Lady Lavender is citrus with a lavender simple; Sunflower Fizz uses a blackberry sunflower syrup with pomegranate and lemon; Hibiscus Breeze pairs hibiscus tea and grapefruit with a spicy lavender syrup, and hibiscus is the smart choice there because its natural tartness does what an acid would otherwise have to. Athletic Brewing covers the beer drinker at eight dollars.

The Philadelphia Inquirer covered Jerry's in January 2026 as part of the city's first large-scale Dry January bar crawl — a useful signal, because a bar that signs up for that is committing to serve those drinks well on the busiest possible night for people ordering them.

For a non-drinker the appeal is the format. This is a neighbourhood bar with a full kitchen and weekend brunch, not a cocktail destination, which means the social pressure is lower and the visit can be an hour or four. Four named drinks under a printed heading is exactly enough to get through an evening without repeating yourself.
venues.pressQuote: Jerry's is the kind of spot with a lot of regulars, $8 wine, and plenty of $5 happy hour deals
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Philadelphia Magazine, Where to Eat in Northern Liberties, December 2024

venues.name: Jethro's Cocktail Lounge
venues.description: Jethro's Cocktail Lounge is a retro, midcentury-modern room on the Montrose side of the Montrose/Midtown line, opened in April 2024 by hospitality partners Russell Malixi, Wade McElroy and Andrew Corbett — the team behind Ma'am Sir LA, Horse Thief BBQ and the Arroyo Club in Los Angeles. Dark woods, geometric shapes and black booths pair with a walk-up bar and an airy patio, and the compact menu runs about ten signature cocktails alongside smashburgers and fries. Its zero-proof program is small but genuinely built on real non-alcoholic spirits rather than juice: four named mocktails at $10, including the Watermelon Fresca with Cut Above zero-proof agave, watermelon and lime, and the Botanical Crown with Empress 1908 0.0, honey and Topo Chico. Peach Blossom and 9 Out of 10 round out the list.
signatureDrinks: Watermelon Fresca (Cut Above zero-proof agave, watermelon, lime)
venues.longDescription:
Jethro's Cocktail Lounge opened April 30, 2024 in a roughly 2,200-square-foot space at 95 Tuam St, on the Montrose side of the Montrose/Midtown line. It's the project of hospitality partners Russell Malixi (a Houston native and University of Texas alumnus), Wade McElroy (a fellow Texan and UT alumnus), and Andrew Corbett (a California native); the trio also run Ma'am Sir LA, Horse Thief BBQ, and the newly opened Arroyo Club in Los Angeles. "Texas was calling me home, and Montrose seemed like the perfect place to launch Jethro's," Malixi told Houston Food Finder at opening. "The welcoming vibe reminded me a little of LA, but the bustling nightlife scene and neighborhood feel is really what sealed the deal."

The lounge pairs dark woods, geometric shapes, and sleek black booths with contemporary decor, plus a walk-up bar and an airy patio. The compact menu runs about ten signature cocktails alongside a handful of house classics and a short beer and wine-by-the-glass list, paired with a smashburger, a plant-based burger, and fries.

Alongside the full bar, Jethro's runs a small but genuine zero-proof program built on real non-alcoholic spirits: four named house mocktails priced at $10, including the Watermelon Fresca (Cut Above zero-proof agave, watermelon, lime), the Botanical Crown (Empress 1908 0.0, honey, Topo Chico), the Peach Blossom (peach purée, lemon), and 9 Out of 10 (strawberry purée, orgeat, lime).
venues.pressQuote: Texas was calling me home, and Montrose seemed like the perfect place to launch Jethro's. The welcoming vibe reminded me a little of LA, but the bustling nightlife scene and neighborhood feel is really what sealed the deal.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Russell Malixi, co-owner of Jethro's Cocktail Lounge

venues.name: Jewel of the South
venues.description: Jewel of the South is a French Quarter cocktail bar and restaurant set in a renovated 1830s Creole cottage on St. Louis Street, with a courtyard and parlour rooms. It opened in 2019, co-founded by acclaimed bartender Chris Hannah (a French 75 Bar veteran) and Nick Detrich; Hannah remains beverage director. The bar ranked No. 6 on North America's 50 Best Bars 2026 — its fourth straight top-10 finish — and appeared on The World's 50 Best Bars 2025. Its cocktail menu carries a dedicated "Spirit-Free Sips" section with four named zero-proof drinks: the Floreal And Tonic (Martini & Rossi Floreale, tonic, lime), the Faux-Groni (Lyre's Dry London, Martini & Rossi Vibrante, Bols Fluère bitter), the Blueberry Sling (Mockly Blueberry, rose, mint, soda), and the Tangerine Daisy (Mockly Tangerine, basil, lemon).
venues.address: 1026 St Louis St, New Orleans, LA 70112

venues.longDescription:
Jewel of the South won the James Beard Foundation's Outstanding Bar award in 2024 — the national one, not a regional nod — and beverage director and partner Chris Hannah's reaction on the night was simply that it was the highlight of his entire career. He had already spent years making the French 75 Bar one of the best-known cocktail rooms in America before opening this with Nick Detrich and John Stubbs in March 2019, in a renovated 1830s Creole cottage on St Louis Street with a courtyard and parlour rooms. The restaurant calls itself a classic New Orleans tavern reimagined, and the kitchen backs that up: crawfish bread at $19, red beans at $23, shrimp and grits at $23, blackened fish at $49, and caviar service running from $110 to $220 for anyone marking an occasion.

The spirit-free drinks get their own printed section, Spirit-Free Sips, and it is one of the better-built lists in the city precisely because it does not lean on a single supplier. Four drinks, three of them $11 and one $13, against full cocktails at considerably more. The Floreal And Tonic is Martini and Rossi's Floreale non-alcoholic aperitif with tonic and lime — a straightforward long drink with real bitterness. The Faux-Groni at $13 is the ambitious one, layering Lyre's Dry London Spirit, Martini and Rossi Vibrante and Bols Fluère non-alcoholic bitter to rebuild a Negroni's three-part structure with three separate non-alcoholic products rather than one bottled shortcut, which is why it costs more and why it tastes closer to the original. The Blueberry Sling and the Tangerine Daisy are built on Mockly, with rose, mint and soda for the first and basil and lemon for the second, and both are lighter and fruit-led. It is a list assembled the way a bartender assembles a back bar — by what each bottle does — rather than by what one distributor happened to sell.
venues.pressQuote: Amazing. It's the highlight of my entire career. It's fantastic.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Chris Hannah, on Jewel of the South winning Outstanding Bar

venues.name: JIA Asian Street Kitchen
venues.description: JIA's zero-proof lineup matches the playful, flavour-packed cooking — three named builds rather than the single token mocktail most restaurants manage. The ube lavender sparkler runs fizzy and floral, the passionfruit mango iced tea arrives topped with whipped cream and diced mango, and the tiki panda mixes fruit and fizz. On Bend's south side in River Rim.
signatureDrinks: Ube lavender sparkler — fizzy and floral
Passionfruit mango iced tea — topped with whipped cream and diced mango
venues.longDescription:
JIA Asian Street Kitchen sits on the south side of Bend in the River Rim area, cooking street food across a range of Asian traditions, and it has one of the more genuinely fun zero-proof lists in Central Oregon. Three named builds is more than most restaurants attempt, and the range across them is what makes it work rather than the count.

The ube lavender sparkler leans floral and fizzy, built on ube — the purple yam that runs through Filipino desserts, earthy and vanilla-adjacent rather than simply sweet — with lavender and carbonation to keep it light. The passionfruit mango iced tea goes maximalist in the other direction, arriving topped with whipped cream and diced mango, which puts it closer to a dessert than a drink and makes it the obvious order for anyone who has spent the evening watching other people have pudding. The tiki panda plays it for whimsy, mixing fruit and fizz in the tiki register.

What is notable is that none of the three is a subtraction. They are not cocktails with the spirit left out; they are drinks designed around ingredients the kitchen already works with, which is why they hold up next to the food rather than getting lost against it. For a family eating here, that also means the non-alcoholic list is genuinely appealing to everyone at the table rather than being the children's option by another name.

The restaurant is out in the newer south-side development rather than downtown, so it is a drive from the centre, and it keeps restaurant rather than bar hours — last orders around half past eight most nights, nine on Friday and Saturday.
venues.pressQuote: the zero-proof lineup matches the food's playful, flavor-packed vibe

venues.name: Jigger & Pony
venues.description: Jigger & Pony, Singapore's most decorated modern classic cocktail bar, builds its non-alcoholic drinks into the same rotating 'menuzine' as everything else rather than relegating them to a separate mocktail page. The 2026 edition, BLOOM, gives them a titled chapter - Free Spirited - holding three builds at S$22 against S$28 for the spirited list: Pear & Hops, which sets Seedlip Spice against pear, hops, lemon and Fever-Tree Indian Tonic; Osmanthus & Tea, a classic-style sour using Lyre's Agave Blanco, osmanthus, orchid white tea, lemon and egg white; and Bitter Orange & Raspberry, an aperitivo answer built on Monin Bitter, raspberry, NON 1 and lemon. Each is printed at under 0.5% ABV, and the bar notes that spirited versions can be made on request.
venues.address: 165 Tanjong Pagar Road, Amara Singapore, Singapore 088539
signatureDrinks: Pear & Hops (Seedlip Spice, pear, hops, lemon, Fever-Tree Indian Tonic) S$22
Osmanthus & Tea (Lyre's Agave Blanco, osmanthus, orchid white tea, lemon, egg white) S$22
Bitter Orange & Raspberry (Monin Bitter, raspberry, NON 1, lemon) S$22
venues.longDescription:
Jigger & Pony first opened on Amoy Street in 2012 and moved to its current home inside Amara Singapore on Tanjong Pagar Road in 2018, where the sleek, low-lit room helped the concept grow into a Lion City institution. It is one of the most awarded bars in Asia: No. 9 on The World's 50 Best Bars 2025 (No. 5 in 2024) and No. 3 on Asia's 50 Best Bars 2025, with creative director Uno Jang taking the Altos Bartenders' Bartender Award at the 2025 World's 50 Best ceremony. The bar's signature device is the 'menuzine' - a magazine-style menu, reissued roughly annually, that tells the story of the bar, its bartenders and its community around the drinks. The 2026 edition is titled BLOOM and runs past sixty pages, organised into chapters named Hope, Growth, Beauty, Just Be, Free Spirited and Punch Bowls.

Free Spirited is the non-alcoholic chapter, and its placement is the point: it sits inside the same book as the spirited list, is priced at S$22 against S$28 for the rest, and carries the same tasting notes and photography. BLOOM holds three builds. Pear & Hops combines Seedlip Spice, pear, hops and lemon with Fever-Tree Indian Tonic, described by the bar as fruity and citrusy on the first sip before it deepens into lightly bitter notes from the tonic and the hops. Osmanthus & Tea is a classic-style sour on Lyre's Agave Blanco with osmanthus, orchid white tea, lemon and egg white, pitched as floral with a gentle citrus lift. Bitter Orange & Raspberry uses Monin Bitter, raspberry, NON 1 and lemon, leaning on NON's salted raspberry and chamomile for an aperitivo profile. All three are printed at under 0.5% ABV, and the menu states that alcoholic versions can be made on request. Earlier menuzines carried a Sea Breeze of sage, samphire and grapefruit with a green-salt rim, and a Coffee & Cacao pitched as a no-ABV answer to the Negroni; neither appears in BLOOM, which is the expected consequence of a menu rewritten wholesale each year. The list is deliberately small, but each drink is dialled in with the same culinary technique as the rest of the bar's celebrated programme.
venues.pressQuote: The craft philosophy here is simple - extract natural flavours from fresh fruit and intense botanicals using sophisticated culinary techniques. Albeit a small list, they are all mighty stellar.

venues.name: Jock Lindsey's Hangar Bar
venues.description: An Indiana Jones-themed adventurer's bar on the waterfront at Disney Springs' The Landing, Jock Lindsey's serves four named non-alcoholic 'libations' alongside its cocktail list, plus pub snacks in a vintage cargo-plane hangar setting.
venues.address: 1486 E Buena Vista Dr, Lake Buena Vista, FL 32830
venues.hours: Mon 11:30am-11pm; Tue 1pm-11pm; Wed-Thu 11:30am-11pm; Fri 11:30am-11:30pm; Sat 11am-11:30pm; Sun 11am-11pm
signatureDrinks: Poisonless Dart (soda water, mint, simple syrup, fresh lime juice)
venues.longDescription:
Jock Lindsey's Hangar Bar opened at Disney Springs (then Downtown Disney) on September 22, 2015, themed as the cluttered hangar of Indiana Jones' fictional pilot Jock Lindsey, filled with cargo crates, vintage aviation gear, and props from the Indiana Jones films. It sits on the waterfront in The Landing neighborhood of Disney Springs at Walt Disney World Resort in Lake Buena Vista, with indoor and outdoor seating overlooking the water.

Alongside its cocktail menu, the bar lists non-alcoholic 'libations': the Antidote (Sprite, maraschino cherry juice), the Diving Bell (Simply Lemonade, watermelon), the Poisonless Dart (soda water, mint, simple syrup, fresh lime juice - essentially a virgin mojito), and Teddy's Tea (green tea, mint, tangerine).

The drinks are simple, soda-fountain-style builds rather than spirit-based mocktails, making the bar an easy stop for non-drinkers traveling with a group that wants the Indiana Jones theming and live entertainment without needing a dedicated craft mocktail program. A 2016 TouringPlans review of the bar from a non-drinker's perspective noted it included 'at least one special non-alcoholic drink on each page of its drink menu,' suggesting the roster is a deliberate, longstanding feature rather than an afterthought.
venues.pressQuote: The selection of non-alcoholic drinks, plus the establishment's fantastic theming and easy atmosphere, make this new addition to Disney Springs a must-do for this teetotaler and for families and fans of Indiana Jones.

venues.name: John's Marketplace
venues.description: John's Marketplace is a bottle shop and taproom on SE Powell Boulevard in Creston-Kenilworth, opened in July 2020 as the eastside store of a long-running Portland beverage retailer. Non-alcoholic drinks are a standing category rather than a token shelf: "Non-Alc" sits in the shop's top-level navigation alongside beer, wine and cider, the range reaches past NA beer into non-alcoholic spirits, wine and mixers, and the Powell store hosted a free 20-vendor Dry January "Booze-Free Fest" in January 2025. It is an alcohol-forward bottle shop with a serious non-alcoholic selection, not an alcohol-free venue.
venues.longDescription:
John's Marketplace opened its Powell Boulevard store on July 3, 2020, the eastside location of a Portland bottle-shop business that has been trading for more than two decades. It works as both retailer and bar: an indoor bar area, indoor and outdoor seating, an outdoor draft window facing the adjacent "The Original" food cart pod, and shelves that Untappd files under beer store, beer garden, wine shop and beer bar. It is one of two remaining locations — the other is Multnomah Village at 3535 SW Multnomah Blvd — after the company closed its Beaverton store on December 31, 2025.

The non-alcoholic side is a deliberate, standing program rather than a shelf of leftovers, though it is run at company level rather than built specifically for this store. "Non-Alc" is one of the top-level categories in the shop's own navigation, alongside beer, wine and cider, with its own landing page; owner Paul Petros told a March 2026 trade interview that non-alcoholic drinks had been moved into prime refrigerated shelf space ahead of hard seltzer, and that "NA is permanent. It's here to stay." Travel Oregon describes the selection as covering non-alcoholic spirits, beer, wine and mixers. Programming at this address goes back years: a free Dry January "Booze-Free Fest" with roughly 20 vendors on January 4, 2025, and non-alcoholic producer tastings on site since at least January 2023. Two things are worth knowing before a trip: this is an alcohol-forward bottle shop and beer bar that happens to carry a strong non-alcoholic range, not an alcohol-free space; and because the business runs no online catalogue, the exact size of that range and the specific brands in stock on any given day are not documented anywhere — call ahead if you are after something particular.
venues.pressQuote: NA is permanent. It's here to stay.

venues.name: Joia Beach
venues.description: Joia Beach is a restaurant and beach club on Watson Island, the strip of land in Biscayne Bay between downtown Miami and South Beach, with what RESIDENT calls a European-inspired setting, on the sand facing the city skyline. Its documented alcohol-free build is the Joia Lemonade, which combines Seedlip Garden with citrus, pineapple, a rosemary agave and activated charcoal — a striking, near-black drink that reads herbal rather than sweet. RESIDENT described it in December 2025 as clean and intentional and as a zero-proof option designed for daylight hours and slow afternoons by the water. The club opens at 11:30am and runs to 11pm on Friday and Saturday. It is closed on Tuesdays.
venues.hours: Mon 11:30am-8pm; Tue closed; Wed-Thu 11:30am-8pm; Fri-Sat 11:30am-11pm; Sun 11:30am-10pm
signatureDrinks: Joia Lemonade (Seedlip Garden, citrus, pineapple, rosemary agave, activated charcoal)
venues.longDescription:
Joia Beach sits at 1111 Parrot Jungle Trail on Watson Island, the man-made island in Biscayne Bay that the MacArthur Causeway crosses between downtown Miami and South Beach. The setting is the point: a beach club and dining room on the sand, facing back across the water at the downtown skyline. Service starts at 11:30am and finishes at 8pm on Monday, Wednesday and Thursday, 10pm on Sunday and 11pm on Friday and Saturday; the venue is closed on Tuesdays, which is worth checking before making the drive out.

The alcohol-free drink documented at the club is the Joia Lemonade, and it is one of the more distinctive builds on this list. Seedlip Garden — the pea-and-hay expression from the London non-alcoholic distiller — is combined with citrus, pineapple and a rosemary agave, then coloured and softened with activated charcoal, which turns the glass almost black and cuts some of the sweetness the pineapple would otherwise carry. RESIDENT covered the drink in its December 2025 Miami round-up, wrote that it reads clean and intentional, and noted that the European-inspired setting reinforces the appeal, describing it as a zero-proof option designed for daylight hours and slow afternoons by the water. That is a fair reading of the venue: this is a daytime and early-evening destination rather than a late-night bar, and the drinks list is built for the sun. Only one named alcohol-free build is published, which is why the programme is graded as real but modest. Two practical points. Watson Island is reached only by the MacArthur Causeway, so the venue is a drive or a rideshare rather than a walk from anywhere, and there is no realistic way to combine it with a second stop on foot. Second, the venue is closed on Tuesdays and shuts at 8pm on Monday, Wednesday and Thursday, so the Friday and Saturday evenings are the only late windows; call ahead on (305) 400-7280. The venue posts as @joiabeach and @joiabeachmiami.
venues.pressQuote: It is a zero-proof option designed for daylight hours and slow afternoons by the water.

venues.name: Juju Kitchen & Cocktails
venues.description: Juju keeps spirit-free cocktails on the menu year-round rather than as a January special, and the builds are properly savoury. Endless Summer is made with homemade tepache — the Mexican fermented pineapple drink — plus pineapple, lime, serrano chilli syrup, orgeat and soda; Falling Up combines ginger, apple, lemon, harvest syrup and tonic. The tepache is the detail that matters: a bar fermenting its own base gets acidity and funk that no juice can supply, and adding serrano heat pushes the drink further from sweetness in the direction of an actual cocktail. Open Tuesday to Saturday from 4pm, a short walk from most of downtown and from Dive Bar on K Street.
signatureDrinks: Endless Summer - homemade tepache, pineapple, lime, serrano chili syrup, orgeat, soda
Falling Up - ginger, apple, lemon, harvest syrup, tonic
venues.longDescription:
Juju Kitchen & Cocktails sits on L Street in downtown Sacramento, and its spirit-free drinks are on the menu all year rather than appearing each January and vanishing in February — which is the distinction that matters most to anyone who has actually stopped drinking rather than paused.

Endless Summer is the drink to examine. It is built on house-made tepache, the lightly fermented Mexican pineapple-rind drink, then extended with pineapple, lime, serrano chilli syrup, orgeat and soda. Two things about that spec are unusual. First, the tepache: fermenting your own base is real kitchen labour, and it delivers acidity, a faint funk and body that no fruit juice can imitate — the same reason fermentation keeps recurring as the best technique in alcohol-free bartending. Second, the serrano. Chilli heat occupies the palate in a way that reads as intensity, which is precisely what a drink loses when the alcohol comes out.

Falling Up works the autumnal register instead — ginger, apple, lemon, harvest syrup and tonic — with the tonic's quinine supplying bitterness and the ginger supplying bite. Between the two, a non-drinker can have something hot and savoury or something spiced and dry, rather than two variations on sweet.

The hours are the limitation: Tuesday to Saturday, 4pm to 10pm, closed Sunday and Monday. It is a short walk from most of downtown Sacramento and from Dive Bar on K Street, which makes a two-stop evening straightforward for a group where not everyone is drinking.

One practical note on ordering here. Because the spirit-free drinks sit on the main menu rather than a separate card, there is none of the small awkwardness that comes with asking whether anything non-alcoholic is available and watching a bartender think about it. You order by name, like everyone else at the table, and what arrives is a proper drink in proper glassware. That sounds trivial and is not: the most common complaint from people who have stopped drinking is not about the liquid but about being visibly the exception, and a menu that treats zero-proof as ordinary removes the moment entirely.
venues.pressQuote: Juju Kitchen & Cocktails, year-round: Endless Summer (homemade tepache, pineapple, lime, serrano chili syrup, orgeat, soda) and Falling Up (ginger, apple, lemon, harvest syrup, tonic).

venues.name: Jukebox
venues.description: Jukebox is a bar and restaurant in a corner building at West 29th and Church in Hingetown, where the record-driven music programming is the identity. Its non-alcoholic offering is unusually broad for a neighbourhood bar: five non-alcoholic beers and ciders including Athletic Brewing's Cerveza Atletica at $5 and BrewDog's Hazy AF at $5.50 — cheaper than the full-strength taps — Surely brut sparkling wine by the glass at $11, and a house mocktail list led by the creamy Harry Nilsson at $9. It opens at 11:30am at weekends.

venues.longDescription:
Jukebox occupies a corner storefront at West 29th and Church in Hingetown, and functions as the neighbourhood bar of that small Ohio City pocket. The name is literal — the music programming is the identity, and the kitchen runs a short menu of sandwiches and bar food until 10pm — but the reason it belongs on a non-alcoholic list is that the drinks board treats not drinking as a real category with real choices rather than as a gap to be plugged with cola.

Cleveland Magazine's 2026 mocktail roundup counted five non-alcoholic beers and ciders in the fridge, priced from $5, including Athletic Brewing's Cerveza Atletica at $5 and BrewDog's Hazy AF IPA at $5.50 — genuinely cheaper than the full-strength taps, which is rarer than it should be and quietly the most respectful thing a bar can do for a non-drinker. Surely's non-alcoholic brut sparkling wine is poured by the glass at $11, so a table with something to celebrate can actually toast rather than mime it. On the mixed-drink side the house list is led by the Harry Nilsson at $9, a creamy build named for the singer in keeping with the record-shop framing, alongside two or three rotating mocktails.

The hours are the other argument. Jukebox opens at 11:30am on Saturdays and Sundays and runs to 2am on Friday and Saturday nights, which makes it one of very few places in the neighbourhood where an alcohol-free drinker can turn up at either end of the day and find something built for them. Jukebox and Amba, two of Cleveland's better non-alcoholic options, sit within a single Hingetown block.
venues.pressQuote: Jukebox pours Athletic Brewing's Cerveza Atletica and BrewDog's Hazy AF IPA alongside Surely Brut sparkling wine and the creamy house mocktail Harry Nilsson.

venues.name: Juliet Italian Kitchen
venues.description: Juliet Italian Kitchen sits on Barton Springs Road with one of the more pleasant patios in central Austin, and it keeps named non-alcoholic drinks on the printed list rather than improvising them. The two Visit Austin singles out are seasonal and built on real preparations: New Year, New Me! uses a house blueberry basil shrub — a vinegar-based syrup that gives a drink genuine acidity and length — and the Resolution Refresher runs alongside it. A shrub is a meaningful signal: it takes days to make and exists specifically to give a non-alcoholic drink the structure that alcohol usually provides.
signatureDrinks: New Year, New Me! - blueberry basil shrub
venues.longDescription:
Juliet Italian Kitchen occupies a corner of Barton Springs Road, the strip that runs between Zilker Park and downtown, and it trades heavily on its patio — string lights, olive trees, a room that works as easily for a long lunch as for dinner. The cooking is straightforward Italian-American, and the bar supports it rather than competing with it.

The reason it belongs in an alcohol-free guide comes down to one technical detail. The house non-alcoholic drink Visit Austin names, New Year, New Me!, is built on a blueberry basil shrub. A shrub is a drinking vinegar — fruit, sugar and vinegar left to macerate for days — and it exists precisely to solve the problem non-alcoholic drinks have: without alcohol, a drink tends to fall flat and sweet, because alcohol is what normally supplies bite and length. A shrub restores both. Any bar making one has decided the alcohol-free side of the menu is worth real prep time, and that is a much stronger signal than the number of mocktails listed.

The Resolution Refresher runs alongside it, and the naming of both suggests the pair were introduced as a Dry January offering. That is worth knowing: seasonal drinks can rotate out, so it is worth asking what the current alcohol-free options are rather than arriving expecting these two specifically.

The grade is a considered 3 — the drinks are named and properly made, but this is a restaurant bar with a short alcohol-free selection rather than a parallel program. What it offers a non-drinker is a genuinely nice room, an easy patio, all-day trading from 11am, and a kitchen substantial enough that nobody at the table is there only to drink. For a group splitting between drinkers and non-drinkers over a long dinner, that combination matters more than the length of the alcohol-free list.
venues.pressQuote: Juliet Italian Kitchen (Barton Springs area): New Year, New Me! (blueberry basil shrub); Resolution Refresher.

venues.name: Jūn
venues.description: Jūn is a James Beard Award-winning New Asian American restaurant in Houston's Heights, opened in February 2023 by chef-owners Evelyn Garcia — a Top Chef Season 19 finalist — and Henry Lu, a veteran of New York kitchens including Pearl & Ash and Llama Inn. The 57-seat, open-kitchen room draws on the pair's first-generation Salvadoran, Mexican and Southeast Asian upbringings, with wok cooking and fermentation at its core; they won the James Beard Award for Best Chef: Texas in June 2026. The kitchen keeps a dedicated five-drink "Zero Proof" section that mirrors that cross-cultural cooking rather than defaulting to fruit juice: the Oye Morro built on Salvadoran horchata with pineapple, coconut and lime; a savory N/A Michelada with Topo Chico, fish sauce, hoisin, chili and lime; a Suero; a Tamarind Arnold Palmer; and Miles Away with passionfruit and vanilla.

venues.longDescription:
Jūn opened February 7, 2023 at 420 E 20th St. in the Heights (in the former Steel City Pops/Central City Co-op space), founded by chefs Evelyn Garcia and Henry Lu. Garcia, a Top Chef Season 19 finalist, previously cooked at Jean-Georges' Spice Market and Kin Shop in New York and ran the Kin stand at Politan Row in Houston; Lu built his career in New York kitchens including Pearl & Ash and Brooklyn's Llama Inn before moving to Houston to open Jūn with Garcia. The two describe the 57-seat, open-kitchen restaurant as 'New Asian American,' drawing on their first-generation, cross-cultural upbringings across Salvadoran, Mexican, and Southeast Asian influences and a shared love of wok cooking and fermentation.

Jūn was a James Beard Award semifinalist for Best New Restaurant in its debut year, and in June 2026 Garcia and Lu won the James Beard Award for Best Chef: Texas at the ceremony in Chicago, with Garcia telling the room, 'Houston, I love you so so much... It is a city of dreams and hopes.' The restaurant has also drawn coverage from Texas Monthly and CultureMap Houston. In March 2026, Jūn added a full liquor license, layering new cocktails (Pink Lady, Post/Shift, a Carajillo) atop the wine- and sake-based low-ABV program Garcia and Lu had run since opening.

That expansion hasn't touched the kitchen's non-alcoholic side: Jūn's dedicated 'Zero Proof' menu remains intact, mirroring the restaurant's cross-cultural cooking with five house-built drinks — the Oye Morro (Salvadoran horchata, pineapple, coconut, lime), the savory N/A Michelada (Topo Chico, fish sauce, hoisin, chili, lime), Suero (Topo Chico, lime, black salt), a Tamarind Arnold Palmer (tamarind Jarritos, cold brew oolong tea, lemon), and Miles Away (passionfruit, vanilla, Topo Chico). CultureMap Houston has repeatedly spotlighted the program in its Dry January coverage, calling out the Oye Morro and N/A Michelada by name.
venues.pressQuote: Try the 'oye morro,' a creation of Salvadoran horchata, coconut milk, lime, and pineapple gomme syrup, or the 'n/a michelada,' a Topo Chico elixir infused with fish sauce, hoisin, chili, and lime.

venues.name: Juniper
venues.description: Juniper is Greenville's first gin-centric bar, on the roof above Paloma at 315 South Main with one of the best views downtown, and it prints its alcohol-free drinks under a Zero Proof heading at the same $10 as the rest of the list. The builds are properly constructed rather than sweetened: a Juice Bomb of watermelon shrub, black sesame seed syrup, lemon, grapefruit and grapefruit soda; a Root For Me on blackberry sauce, ginger and lime cordial; a Kiwi Crush with kiwi cordial, pineapple, agave and club soda. A gin bar taking the zero-proof side seriously is a good sign — gin is the hardest category to replace convincingly.
signatureDrinks: Juice Bomb — watermelon shrub, black sesame seed syrup, lemon, grapefruit, grapefruit soda
Root For Me — blackberry sauce, ginger, lime cordial
Kiwi Crush — kiwi cordial, pineapple, agave, club soda
