venues.longDescription:
Liliana is a contemporary Italian restaurant on Queen Street West in Toronto's Beaconsfield Village (West Queen West), run by chef Marvin Palomo. The kitchen turns out housemade pastas — agnolotti, pappardelle, troffie — alongside refined antipasti such as stracciatella, tuna crudo and beef carpaccio, and secondi built around ocean trout, tiger shrimp and prime striploin, with ingredients sourced in part from Martin Family Farms. The restaurant opened in late September 2025 and is designed as an intimate room for shared, celebratory dining.

The name comes from Palomo's own mentor in Italy: "Liliana was named after my chef I worked for in Italy, who mentored me at a young age. She taught me more about just cooking, but also about the care and compassion that goes towards true hospitality," he has said of the restaurant. Toronto food blog Shanea Savours called it "a warm, inspired, and very welcome addition to the Toronto dining scene" after visiting in late November 2025.

Liliana treats its non-alcoholic list as a genuine standalone cocktail menu rather than an afterthought, with four named, priced drinks. The Willow ($15) is a non-alcoholic Italian aperitif with grapefruit and bubbles; the Daisy ($16) combines gentian, a non-alcoholic orange liqueur, pineapple, lime and cucumber; and the Iris ($16) pairs a black cherry sherry shrub with sparkling tea. Alongside the cocktails, the restaurant also pours Copenhagen "Blå" sparkling tea — jasmine, white tea and darjeeling — priced at $15 and $30.

Liliana is open Wednesday through Sunday, 5:00 to 11:00 p.m., and closed Monday and Tuesday.
venues.pressQuote: A warm, inspired, and very welcome addition to the Toronto dining scene.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Shanea Savours, Toronto food blog, November 2025

venues.name: Lilo
venues.description: Lilo is an intimate 22-seat chef's-counter tasting-menu restaurant tucked behind Wildland in Carlsbad Village, opened in April 2025 by chef Eric Bost and restaurateur John Resnick and awarded a Michelin star within weeks of opening. The seafood-leaning, coastally driven menu runs roughly twelve courses, and Lilo treats zero-proof seriously: alongside its wine, Champagne, and hybrid pairings, it offers a full dedicated non-alcoholic beverage pairing (about $110), composed in tandem by beverage director Andrew Cordero and wine director Savannah Riedler to match each plate. Zero-proof creations like the Okinawa Spritz — built around tea tannin, saline, and citrus bitters — are designed to elevate the food rather than merely accompany it, making it one of North County's most serious non-alcoholic pairings.
venues.longDescription:
Lilo is a twenty-two-seat chef's-counter tasting-menu restaurant tucked behind Wildland in Carlsbad Village, opened in April 2025 by chef Eric Bost and restaurateur John Resnick and awarded a Michelin star within weeks of opening — an unusually fast recognition even by the standards of a well-connected opening. The menu runs to roughly twelve courses, seafood-leaning and coastally driven, served at a counter where the cooking happens in front of you.

The reason it belongs in this directory is that Lilo offers a full dedicated non-alcoholic beverage pairing, at around $110, sitting alongside its wine, Champagne and hybrid pairings rather than beneath them. That price point is the tell. A zero-proof pairing costing within range of a wine pairing is a restaurant saying, in the only language that matters commercially, that the non-alcoholic programme took comparable work and deserves comparable respect — and it removes the quiet indignity of being the person at a tasting counter handed sparkling water for twelve courses while everyone else is poured something considered. The pairing is composed in tandem by beverage director Andrew Cordero and wine director Savannah Riedler, matched plate by plate rather than assembled as a generic sequence, and builds like the Okinawa Spritz — constructed around tea tannin, saline and citrus bitters — show the technique involved. Tannin and salt are precisely what non-alcoholic drinks usually lack and precisely what makes a drink work against food; using tea for structure and salinity for length is the same problem-solving a sommelier does, applied without alcohol. For a non-drinker in North County who wants a genuine occasion meal rather than a good dinner with a compromise attached, this is the most serious option in the region. Tuesday to Saturday, evenings only, and the room seats twenty-two — book well ahead.

venues.name: Lincoln Social Rooftop
venues.description: Lincoln Social Rooftop is a Cameron Mitchell bar on the ninth floor of 711 North High Street in the Short North, with a retractable roof, a fire pit and skyline views. It is a 21-and-over room. The cocktail menu is organised into four bands — Bold & Boozy, Easy Drinking, Sessions: Low ABV and Classics — and one of them, headed Spiritless, is entirely non-alcoholic. That list runs eight deep and is built rather than poured: a Mean & Green of serrano, celery, agave, cilantro and lime; No Secrets, which combines Töst sparkling tea with Giffard aperitif and lemon; an Espresso & Tonic; and a Blueberry Iced Tea infused with earl grey. Alongside them sit Mionetto alcohol-removed sparkling by glass or bottle, Best Day Brewing's Electro Lime and Good Liar's Midwest IPA, the non-alcoholic beer brewed in Columbus.

venues.longDescription:
Lincoln Social Rooftop occupies the ninth floor at 711 North High Street, at the northern end of the Short North, and is one of Cameron Mitchell Restaurants' bar-led rooms rather than a dining concept. The space has a retractable roof and a fire pit, which is what keeps it viable through an Ohio winter, and it is restricted to guests 21 and over. The kitchen closes an hour before the bar, and the room runs late on Fridays and Saturdays.

The drinks list is unusually well structured for a rooftop. It is banded by intent rather than by spirit: Bold & Boozy at the top end, Easy Drinking beneath it, a genuine Sessions: Low ABV section for guests who want one drink rather than none, a Classics list, and — set out with the same weight as the others — a section headed Spiritless. That section carries eight entries and reads like a cocktail list rather than a soft-drink afterthought. Mean & Green is a savoury build of serrano pepper, celery, agave, cilantro and lime juice at $12. No Secrets, at $15, layers Töst sparkling tea with Giffard aperitif and lemon, and is priced within a few dollars of the low-ABV cocktails. Espresso & Tonic pairs espresso concentrate with cherry and orange over a Fever-Tree topper, and a Blueberry Iced Tea uses a blueberry earl grey infusion with lemon. Behind the built drinks sit bottles: Töst sparkling tea on its own, Mionetto alcohol-removed sparkling wine at $13 a glass or $52 a bottle, and two non-alcoholic beers — Best Day Brewing's Electro Lime out of Northern California and Good Liar's Midwest IPA, which is brewed in Columbus itself. The presence of a full-bottle sparkling option and a local NA beer, rather than a single token can, is what puts this above most hotel and rooftop lists in the city.
venues.pressQuote: At Lincoln Social, for a non-alcoholic option, try a zero-proof 'bartender roulette' for variety or stick with classics like cold brew or sparkling water.

venues.name: Lion Brewery Co Taproom
venues.description: Lion Brewery Co Taproom is the flagship brewpub of a Singapore beer company that revived the name of a London brewery founded on the Thames in 1836 and demolished in 1949. A group of friends brought the brand back in Singapore in 2018 and opened this taproom in a heritage shophouse on Club Street in 2021, with an in-house brewery and 25 taps that include traditional English hand-pumps. Its beer menu carries Free Hit XPA, the brewery's own non-alcoholic extra pale ale at 0.5% ABV, brewed hop-forward with tropical fruit and citrus and poured on draught here at S$8.50 for 355ml. That is the only alcohol-free tap, so this is a listing for beer drinkers who want a proper NA pint, not a dry venue.

venues.longDescription:
The name is older than the company. Lion Brewery was founded in London in 1836 on the banks of the Thames and spent a century shipping India Pale Ale and other ales to trading posts across the globe, including Asia, before the site was demolished in 1949. In 2018 a group of friends with a passion for brewing revived it in Singapore, the Lion City, and in 2021 the company opened its flagship taproom and brewpub in a heritage building at 36 Club Street. Time Out's 2024 review counts 25 taps, including English hand-pumps, alongside pool tables, live sport on large screens and a speakeasy hidden behind a false refrigerator. The core range is a German-style Island Lager, Straits Pale Ale, The Boss IPA and a nitro stout, with monthly Brewlab seasonals such as a chilli padi pilsner and a rosella lager. One house tradition should be stated plainly for readers who avoid drinking culture: Pressure Hour, in which a gong signals a free-flow beer window for the room.

The reason it appears in this guide is a single tap. Free Hit XPA is the brewery's own non-alcoholic extra pale ale, and the brewery has written about why it took the challenge on: hop-forward styles carry citrus, pine and tropical fruit that cover the absence of alcohol, and the bitterness balances leftover sweetness. The beer menu lists it at 0.5% ABV and 25 IBU with gentle bitterness, a blend of tropical fruits and a citrus aroma, at S$8.50 for a 355ml pour and S$11 for 473ml; the brewery markets it as its 0% edition, so ask the bar if the distinction matters to you. As of mid-2025 it was available only on draught, at this brewpub and a handful of other venues, which makes Club Street the reliable place to find it. There is no wider zero-proof list beyond the usual soft drinks, and the gastropub kitchen runs a weekend roast. Hours published by the taproom are Monday to Thursday 3pm to 11pm, Friday and Saturday 11.30am to 1am and Sunday 11.30am to 11pm, with happy hour on selected pints until 7pm.

venues.name: Lioness
venues.description: Lioness is a small, loud Italian wine bar and restaurant at 7009 Greenwood Ave N in Phinney Ridge, opened at the turn of 2024 by chef Renée Erickson's Sea Creatures group. It has eight indoor tables and a bar too tight to seat anyone — customers stand at it, as drinkers do in Rome or Barcelona — with candles flickering in Chianti bottles and custom-painted plates Erickson chose herself. The food is small-plate Italian: burrata, smoked black cod mousse, brothy clams, bouncy cavatelli and a much-discussed $18 meatball. Its non-alcoholic programme is well regarded locally — the Infatuation describes people mingling over bergamot-infused spritzes and frothy zero-proof garibaldis, and Seattle's own alcohol-free bottle shop rates the bar's spirit-free work as top shelf, crediting bartender Hudson with about three seasonal non-alcoholic cocktails at a time. PLEASE NOTE: Lioness's website sits behind a security check we cannot get past, so we could not read the current drinks list — the named zero-proof cocktails and their prices need confirming in person. A clarification on awards: Erickson won a James Beard Award in 2016, but for an earlier restaurant, not for Lioness.
venues.longDescription:
Lioness is tiny and knows it. Eight indoor tables, each one full from the minute the doors open, and a bar area too tight for stools, so drinkers stand at it the way they would in Rome or Barcelona. Seattle Met's description catches the register precisely: candles flicker in Chianti bottles, and Renée Erickson picked out the custom-painted plates that hold the oysters, the smoked cod mousse, and a meatball so compelling it needs no spaghetti. It opened at the turn of 2024 in Phinney Ridge as part of Erickson's Sea Creatures group, with James Ingles as general manager. The food is loud, salty, Italian small plates — burrata, brothy clams, bouncy cavatelli, and that $18 meatball, which is over-spiced in the way an over-spiced meatball should be.

For a non-drinker the appeal is that the bar has a genuine reputation here rather than a token gesture. The Infatuation's account of the room has people mingling and sipping bergamot-infused spritzes and frothy zero-proof garibaldis alongside the martinis, which is the right comparison — a garibaldi is orange juice and Campari, and the frothiness comes from hard-shaken juice, so a zero-proof one is a genuine drink rather than a substitution. Cheeky & Dry, Seattle's own alcohol-free bottle shop and about as expert a local judge as exists, rates the bar's spirit-free programme top shelf and credits bartender Hudson with never once failing to deliver a craveable non-alcoholic cocktail, keeping around three seasonal ones at a time. What we cannot do is name them. Lioness's website sits behind a security challenge that will not let us read the menu, so the current drinks and their prices have to be confirmed in the room. Two smaller notes. Because there are eight tables and no bar seating, arriving early or standing is the plan. And on awards: Renée Erickson won the James Beard Award for Best Chef: Northwest in 2016, but that was for The Whale Wins, seven years before Lioness existed — it is her award, not this restaurant's.
venues.pressQuote: Candles flicker in Chianti bottles; Erickson picked out the custom-painted plates that hold oysters, smoked cod mousse, and a meatball so compelling it needs no spaghetti.

venues.name: Lions Den
venues.description: Lions Den is the bar at Le Méridien Dallas in the historic Stoneleigh, opened in 2026 under chef Michael White, and its menu carries a printed Zero Proof section that treats non-alcoholic drinking as an aperitivo tradition rather than a lemonade problem. Giusto E Sbagliato is the ambitious one — Lyre's American Malt with Roots Rosso, a cocoa-infused Giffard aperitif syrup and Crodino, the Italian bitter aperitivo. The Prickly Hibiscus Spritz is built on Ghia with hibiscus, prickly pear, lemon and club soda, alongside a third build called La Bombola. The bar runs breakfast, lunch and dinner services daily, so the list is available from 6:30am.

venues.longDescription:
The Stoneleigh has been an Uptown landmark since the 1920s, and its bar reopened in 2026 as Lions Den under chef Michael White, with an Italian-leaning menu to match. The drinks list carries a section printed as Zero Proof, and it is one of the few in Dallas that treats non-alcoholic drinking as an aperitivo tradition rather than a lemonade problem — a distinction that decides whether a zero-proof list tastes of fruit or of something closer to a drink.

Giusto E Sbagliato is the drink that demonstrates the point. It layers Lyre's American Malt with Roots Rosso, a cocoa-infused Giffard aperitif syrup and Crodino — the bittersweet Italian aperitivo that has been non-alcoholic since long before the category had a name, and which remains the most useful bottle on any zero-proof back bar. The result is the bitter, structured, slightly medicinal profile that is hardest to reproduce without alcohol, and it is priced at the top of the list accordingly. The Prickly Hibiscus Spritz is the easier drink of the set, running Ghia's botanical aperitif into hibiscus, prickly pear, lemon and soda, and La Bombola completes the section.

The format is the practical advantage here. This is a hotel bar attached to a restaurant running three services a day — breakfast from 6:30am, lunch from 11:30am and dinner from 5pm, to 10pm most nights and 11pm on Friday and Saturday — so the zero-proof list is available at hours when a cocktail bar would still be shut. That makes it a genuine option for a morning meeting or an early evening drink, not only for a night out. One thing to keep an eye on: the hotel is in the middle of rebranding to Marriott's Autograph Collection, so the bar's name and menu are more likely than most to shift over the next year.

venues.name: Listen Bar
venues.description: IMPORTANT — LISTEN BAR APPEARS TO BE DORMANT. It is a pioneering alcohol-free bar that has always run as a roving pop-up rather than a fixed venue, founded by Lorelei Bandrovschi after a friend dared her to spend a month without drinking, and first opened in October 2018 as a five-day proof-of-concept in an empty South Williamsburg bar space. Staffed by musician bartenders, it became one of the original templates for the modern non-alcoholic bar and drew national press. As of August 2026, however, we can find no confirmed activity dated later than January 2025: the newest entry on its own events page is the Good AF Awards 2025, and no 2026 edition or event appears anywhere. Its website and Instagram both remain live and are written in the present tense, which is not the same as being open. Documented signature drinks have included Actual Sunshine, created by Eamon Rockey, and Dollar Slice, by Aaron Polsky, alongside Athletic Brewing beer and Pilot Kombucha on tap. Check before planning around it.
venues.longDescription:
Listen Bar began because a friend dared Lorelei Bandrovschi to spend a month without drinking. She found there was nowhere she wanted to go, and in October 2018 opened Listen Bar as a five-day proof-of-concept in an empty bar space in South Williamsburg. It was staffed by musician bartenders — that was the point, not a gimmick. Bandrovschi's ambition was to create a new revenue stream for independent musicians, something like an in-person Patreon where you are not buying merch but sharing a one-on-one experience, because she believed the next revolution in music is experience, and not just arena shows but intimacy. It never took a permanent lease, running instead as a roving pop-up across New York venues, and it became one of the original templates for the modern alcohol-free bar, collecting a run of national press along the way and hosting its own Good AF Awards for non-alcoholic drinks. Documented signature drinks include Actual Sunshine, a recipe by Eamon Rockey, and Dollar Slice, by Aaron Polsky, with Athletic Brewing beer and Pilot Kombucha on tap alongside bottled Curious Elixirs and Club Mate.

We have to tell you plainly that it appears to be dormant. As of August 2026 we can find no confirmed Listen Bar activity dated later than January 2025. The newest item on the bar's own events page is the Good AF Awards 2025, which took place that January; everything below it is older, and no 2026 edition appears there or anywhere else we could search. The most recent substantial interview with Bandrovschi we could find dates from September 2024. That is roughly nineteen months of silence. What has not changed is the website, which is live, well-maintained and written entirely in the present tense, and an Instagram account with thousands of followers still standing. Neither is evidence of activity — a maintained site is exactly what a paused project looks like from outside, and we have been caught by that before in both directions. So: this entry stays, because a pop-up that has gone quiet is not a pop-up that has closed, and Listen Bar has revived for Dry January more than once. But do not plan an evening around it without checking first.
venues.pressQuote: Though not exactly a brick-and-mortar space, Listen Bar earns its place for helping kickstart the New York sober bar scene.

venues.name: Little Coyote
venues.description: Little Coyote is a smoked-barbecue restaurant in St. Elmo, at the foot of Lookout Mountain, from the team behind Main Street Meats and Easy Bistro — a MICHELIN Guide listing and one of the more serious kitchens in Chattanooga. Its bar offers zero-proof versions of the two drinks a barbecue room actually needs, a margarita and a paloma, both built rather than poured from a mix. In a format where the default alternative is sweet tea, having a proper sour and a proper citrus highball available without alcohol is more useful than a long mocktail list would be. Dinner from 4pm daily, with weekend lunch from 11:30am.
venues.longDescription:
St. Elmo sits at the foot of Lookout Mountain, at the far end of Chattanooga's streetcar suburb, and Little Coyote is its barbecue restaurant — smoked meat and sides from the group behind Main Street Meats and Easy Bistro, with a MICHELIN Guide listing to its name. It opened in November 2023 and has been busy since.

The alcohol-free offer here is narrow and well chosen, which this directory rates more highly than a long list of poorly executed drinks. Barbecue asks for two things at the bar: something sour and cold to cut the fat, and something long and citric to drink across a whole meal. Little Coyote makes both without alcohol — a zero-proof margarita and a zero-proof paloma, built to order rather than poured from a sweet-and-sour mix. Anyone who has sat through a barbecue dinner with a glass of sweet tea will recognise how much difference that makes.

NOOGAtoday singled the restaurant out on exactly this basis in its guide to drinking without alcohol in Chattanooga, noting that there is more here than the smoked barbecue.

The grade of three rather than four is deliberate and reflects scale. Two well-made drinks are two well-made drinks; there is no printed zero-proof section and no non-alcoholic spirit programme behind it. What there is, is a kitchen and bar of genuine quality that has not treated the non-drinking diner as an afterthought — and in a destination restaurant, being able to order something good is often the whole requirement.

Hours run 4pm to 8:30pm Monday through Thursday, to 9pm on Friday, with weekend service starting at 11:30am. Worth booking; the room is small and St. Elmo fills up at weekends when the mountain is busy.
venues.pressQuote: This St. Elmo restaurant has more than just delicious smoked BBQ — try its zero-proof margarita or paloma.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: NOOGAtoday, Local mocktails + non-alcoholic drinks in Chattanooga

venues.name: Little Jumbo
venues.description: Little Jumbo is a craft cocktail bar at 241 Broadway Street in Asheville's Five Points, opened on 7 November 2017 in the old Jenkins grocery by co-owners Chall Gray and Jay Sanders, with Leisa Payne in the kitchen. The room keeps the building's bones — tin ceilings, green leather — and USA Today named it Bar of the Year in 2025, with Garden & Gun placing it among the best of the South. Its non-alcoholic list is one of the longest in the city: a printed "Spirit-Free Sippers" section of seven drinks at $9–$10, roughly half the price of the full cocktails, and built across three different non-alcoholic spirit houses rather than one. Rita's Day Off ($10) uses Ritual NA tequila with basil, lime, orange, lemon and agave; Mint to Refresh You ($9) uses Ritual NA rum; the Cos-No-Politan ($9) and Drømme Roll Please ($10) are built on Drømme; Shoots Then Leaves ($9) pairs Seedlip Garden 108 with spicy ginger ale and celery bitters; and the Berry-Nice Gimlet ($10) layers an Amethyst blueberry-ginger-mint with two bitters and orange flower water. The list rotates seasonally.

venues.longDescription:
Little Jumbo opened on 7 November 2017 at 241 Broadway Street in Five Points, in the old Jenkins grocery, and co-owner Chall Gray's approach to the fit-out explains why the room works: they tried to let the room dictate what would work best, because the building has so much character and they wanted to let the bones of it show. What emerged is a warmly lit refuge with tin ceilings, green leather and, as the bar puts it, a thousand recipes behind the counter. Gray runs it with Jay Sanders, with Leisa Payne in the kitchen. In 2025 USA Today named it Bar of the Year, and Garden & Gun has placed it among the best of the South — remarkable recognition for a neighbourhood bar in a city with a great many of them. It opens at 4pm every day and there is free parking in the Five Points lot.

The non-alcoholic list is one of the longest in Asheville, printed under its own heading, "Spirit-Free Sippers", and running seven drinks between $9 and $10 — roughly half what the full cocktails cost. What lifts it above most is the range of bases: three different non-alcoholic spirit houses appear rather than one. Rita's Day Off ($10) uses Ritual's non-alcoholic tequila with basil, lime, orange, lemon and agave. Mint to Refresh You ($9) uses Ritual's rum with lime, mint and soda. Two drinks are built on Drømme — the Cos-No-Politan ($9) on Drømme Awake with cranberry and Regan's orange bitters, and Drømme Roll Please ($10) on Drømme Calm with grapefruit and Mediterranean tonic. Shoots Then Leaves ($9) works Seedlip Garden 108 against a spicy ginger ale and Scrappy's celery bitters, which is the savoury option. The Berry-Nice Gimlet ($10) is the most layered, combining an Amethyst blueberry-ginger-mint with lime, two kinds of bitters and orange flower water. The list rotates, so treat any older set of names as historical.
venues.pressQuote: This intimate North Asheville bar was well ahead of the NA boom, with mocktails — or as co-owner Chall Gray prefers, spirit-free cocktails — on the menu since it opened in 2017.

venues.name: Little Mercies
venues.description: Little Mercies is a small, multi-award-winning neighbourhood cocktail bar on Broadway Parade in Crouch End, open since 2018. It was founded by Alan Sherwood with brothers Max and Noel Venning — the team behind the acclaimed Three Sheets in Dalston and Soho — and carries the same low-waste, precision-led ethos, having been named Sustainable Bar of the Year by the UK's Top 50 Cocktail Bars three times, in 2022, 2023 and 2025. The space is compact and unshowy, with bare brick walls, accents of midnight blue, banquettes and a handful of bar stools, and it fills with a bustling neighbourhood crowd; a kitchen turns out playful seasonal small plates, so it works equally as a date-night spot and a drop-in local. It carries a genuine dedicated low- and no-alcohol cocktail selection alongside its main list, built with the same house-made ingredients Three Sheets is known for.

venues.longDescription:
Little Mercies is a small, multi-award-winning neighbourhood cocktail bar on Broadway Parade in Crouch End (N8), open since 2018. It was founded by Alan Sherwood together with brothers Max and Noel Venning — the team behind the acclaimed Three Sheets in Dalston and Soho — and it carries the same low-waste, precision-led ethos: Little Mercies has been named Sustainable Bar of the Year by the UK's Top 50 Cocktail Bars three times (2022, 2023 and 2025). It runs alongside a kitchen turning out playful seasonal small plates, so the room works equally as a date-night spot and a drop-in local.

The space is compact and unshowy — bare brick walls, accents of midnight blue, banquettes and a handful of bar stools — and fills with a bustling neighbourhood crowd, particularly on Friday and Saturday nights. Prices are deliberately gentle for London: house cocktails land around £11, there's a 30%-off happy hour from 6pm to 7pm every day, and even "mini" drinks (such as a £6 lychee martini) for anyone easing in slowly.

Crucially, the bar treats its non-alcoholic drinks as a proper third section of the menu — house cocktails, classics and non-alcoholic — rather than an afterthought. The centrepiece is a house-made alcohol-free "gin", built by the bartenders as a sugar syrup engineered to do the job of gin without the booze: juniper and coriander seed oils, lemon, lemongrass and a few highly concentrated bitter infusions, with sugar and citric acid added for stability. That base anchors the low-and-no offering, turning up in a non-alcoholic gin and tonic and a non-alcoholic negroni built from Campari sugar, bitters, the boozeless gin and orange. The list is short, seasonal and keenly priced, and — as with everything here — made in-house rather than poured from a bottle, which is what sets it apart from most bars' token mocktail.
venues.pressQuote: The gin is actually an in-house alcohol-free 'gin,' which the bartenders created with a sugar syrup that did the job of gin without the booze, combining juniper and coriander seed oils, with some lemon, lemongrass, and a few highly concentrated bitter infusions while sugar and citric acid provide stability.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: London Living, London's Best Mocktails For Sober October

venues.name: Little Palm
venues.description: Little Palm is the breezy, tropical-themed poolside bar and restaurant inside the Ryder Hotel on Meeting Street in downtown Charleston, run by the Makeready hospitality group. Alongside its cocktail program it pours tropical mocktails built on fresh fruit and juices, including "The Shallow End" (strawberries, lime, and seltzer) and "The School Night," which pairs a non-alcoholic dry riesling with citrus cordial and mulled hibiscus.
venues.longDescription:
Set on the pool deck of the Ryder Hotel at 237 Meeting Street, Little Palm leans into a pastel, coastal-leisure aesthetic and serves from breakfast through late night. It is best known as a cocktail and swim-club destination, but its bartenders also turn out a handful of named zero-proof drinks made with fresh produce rather than sodas.

Documented mocktails include "The Shallow End," a seltzer-based build with fresh strawberries and lime, and "The School Night," which uses a non-alcoholic dry riesling with citrus cordial and mulled hibiscus. The venue remains active in 2025-2026 with current Yelp and Tripadvisor reviews and an active Instagram presence, and was a nominee for Best Rooftop Bar in the Charleston City Paper Best of Charleston awards.
venues.pressQuote: Little Palm is the trendy pool bar at the Ryder Hotel. They have tropical themed mocktails with fresh fruit and juices.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Leisurely Linds, "9 Best Mocktail Bars in Charleston"
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Leisurely Linds, Best Mocktail Bars in Charleston

venues.name: Little Rituals
venues.description: A fourth-floor cocktail bar above the Residence Inn/Courtyard in downtown Phoenix, Little Rituals was a James Beard Award semifinalist for Outstanding Bar Program in both 2024 and 2025 — and it treats its alcohol-free drinks with the same seriousness as the spirited list, with roughly 40 percent of the menu available without alcohol. Syrups, infusions and foams are all made in house, which is what separates these from sweetened juice. Named non-alcoholic builds include the N/A Paloma (spirit-free blanco tequila, seasonal grapefruit soda, key lime, sea salt), an N/A White Grapefruit and Koji Paloma, and the blackberry-lemon Big City Nights.

venues.longDescription:
Little Rituals sits on the fourth floor of a downtown Phoenix hotel block, above the shared lobby of a Residence Inn and Courtyard — an address that undersells it considerably. It has been a James Beard Award semifinalist for Outstanding Bar Program in consecutive years, 2024 and 2025, which puts it in national company, and the room is built for drinking rather than for hotel traffic: a proper bar, a terrace, and a team that treats the menu as a piece of work.

Roughly 40 percent of that menu can be made without alcohol, and the figure is meaningful because of how the bar is set up. Syrups, infusions and foams are produced in house and used across both sides of the list, so an alcohol-free order draws on the same larder as everything else instead of being assembled from what is open. The N/A Paloma is the signature — spirit-free blanco tequila, seasonal grapefruit soda, key lime and a touch of sea salt — and it is joined by an N/A White Grapefruit and Koji Paloma, which brings a fermented, savoury note that almost never appears in zero-proof drinks, and the blackberry-lemon Big City Nights. DiningOut Phoenix listed the bar among the metro's best for a mocktail in May 2026.

It keeps late hours by local standards, running to midnight Sunday and Tuesday through Thursday and to 1am on Friday and Saturday, closing Mondays. The fourth-floor position means a view over downtown, which is a real part of the appeal on a spring evening. As with every bar on this list at this level, it is a licensed cocktail room — the alcohol-free menu is a large, deliberate section of the offering rather than the whole of it, and the room fills with an after-work drinking crowd from about seven.
venues.pressQuote: Many of the drink components, including syrups, infusions, and foams, are made in-house

venues.name: Little Sparrow
venues.description: Little Sparrow is Ford Fry's French bistro in the Westside Provisions District, opened in October 2023 in the former JCT Kitchen & Bar space and named for Edith Piaf. It is recommended in the Michelin Guide and was named one of Esquire's best new restaurants in America in 2024. The bar keeps three non-alcoholic cocktails on the standing menu rather than improvising them on request. No Regrets is the most ambitious of the three, described on the menu itself as peaty and complex, reminiscent of a fine Speyside malt; Triple Crown builds Wilfred's bitter orange aperitif into a ginger-forward highball; and Rose-Colored Glasses is a blood orange fizz. Steak frites, oysters and classic bistro cooking fill the plates.
signatureDrinks: No Regrets (peaty and complex, reminiscent of a fine Speyside malt — 0% ABV)
Triple Crown (Wilfred's bitter orange aperitif, ginger highball)
venues.longDescription:
Ford Fry took the former JCT Kitchen & Bar space at 1198 Howell Mill Road — a room he had run for well over a decade — and reopened it in October 2023 as Little Sparrow, a Parisian-style bistro named after Edith Piaf, whose nickname it was. The neighbouring bar Marcel is named for the boxer Marcel Cerdan, Piaf's lover, so the pair read as a set. The kitchen deals in the classics done properly rather than reinvention: frites, fats, shellfish, steak. It has been recommended in the Michelin Guide and Esquire named it one of the best new restaurants in America in December 2024. The dining room seats through dinner Monday to Saturday with weekend brunch service added on Saturday and Sunday mornings.

What earns Little Sparrow a place here is that the non-alcoholic cocktails are printed on the standing menu with the same descriptive care as the full-proof list. There are three. No Regrets is the one that gets written about: the menu itself calls it peaty and complex, reminiscent of a fine Speyside malt, which is an unusual register for a zero-proof drink and a claim the bar is willing to put in print. Triple Crown is built on Wilfred's bitter orange aperitif and finished as a ginger-forward highball, giving it the bitterness and length that a juice-based drink cannot reach. Rose-Colored Glasses is the lightest of the three, a blood orange fizz meant to sit alongside the raw bar. DiningOut singled the programme out in its April 2026 survey of Atlanta zero-proof bars, updated that June. Three drinks is a modest list by the standards of a dedicated alcohol-free bar, but they are house-built, kept on permanently and served in a room where the rest of the table is drinking wine — which is the situation most sober diners actually face.
venues.pressQuote: Ford Fry's Michelin-recommended French bistro on Howell Mill has three N/A cocktails, and the most interesting one is No Regrets.

venues.name: Little Walter's
venues.description: Little Walter's is a 32-seat modern Polish restaurant and bar in East Kensington, opened in June 2024 by chef-owner Michael Brenfleck as a tribute to his late grandfather, Walter Bubick. The kitchen emphasizes scratch cooking and regional sourcing — house-made sourdough rye, pierogi ruskie, kielbasa, and rotisserie pork over bigos. In 2024 it was the only Philadelphia restaurant named to The New York Times' "Restaurant List: 50 Favorite Places in America Right Now," and it won a Philadelphia Magazine Best of Philly award. The bar runs a dedicated zero-proof section on its menu titled "bezalkoholowe" (Polish for "non-alcoholic"), priced at $7, alongside the cocktail, wine, and beer lists. Named NA drinks include the Mleczarz (whey, apple shrub, dill), Sadownik (tart cherry, orange, cardamom), Zielarz (rosemary honey, herbal tea, bitters), and Feniks, plus a non-alcoholic beer.

venues.longDescription:
Little Walter's is a thirty-two-seat modern Polish restaurant and bar in East Kensington, opened in June 2024 by chef-owner Michael Brenfleck as a tribute to his late grandfather, Walter Bubick. The kitchen cooks from scratch and sources regionally — house-made sourdough rye, pierogi ruskie, kielbasa, rotisserie pork over bigos. In 2024 it was the only Philadelphia restaurant named to The New York Times' Restaurant List of fifty favourite places in America, and it has taken a Philadelphia Magazine Best of Philly award.

The bar carries a dedicated zero-proof section printed under the heading "bezalkoholowe" — Polish for non-alcoholic — and the choice to name it in Polish rather than in English is a small thing that says a lot. It is not a separate menu for a separate kind of customer; it sits inside the restaurant's own language alongside everything else.

The four named drinks follow the same convention. Mleczarz means dairyman, Sadownik means orchardist, Zielarz means herbalist and Feniks means phoenix — trades and archetypes rather than cocktail puns, which places them in the same rural Polish register as the food. Naming a zero-proof drink after a herbalist rather than calling it a "virgin" something is a deliberate refusal of the apologetic framing the category usually gets.

The pairing logic is sound too. Polish cooking runs to sour, fermented and fatty flavours — rye, soured cabbage, cured pork, dill, vinegar — and that palate is better served by acidity and herbal bitterness than by anything sweet. It is also a cuisine with a deep non-alcoholic drinking tradition of its own in kompot and fermented rye drinks, so building alcohol-free options here is a continuation rather than an invention.

A thirty-two-seat room means booking ahead. Open Tuesday to Thursday from four to nine, Friday to ten, Saturday from five to ten and Sunday afternoons; closed Mondays.
venues.pressQuote: Little Walter's just dropped a whole menu of zero-proof cocktails dubbed "bezalkoholowe" (which translates to "non-alcoholic" in Polish), so picking just one drink this Dry January is tricky.

venues.name: Lobby Bar at The Hotel Chelsea
venues.description: The Lobby Bar occupies the ground floor of the Hotel Chelsea, the most storied building in American bohemia, restored and reopened as a bar that is genuinely worth visiting rather than a lobby with a counter. It was shortlisted at the inaugural NYC's Best Bars for NA Awards. Its practical advantage over almost everything else in this guide is time: 11am to 2am, every single day, so it works for a mid-afternoon meeting and a late night from the same room. Alcohol is served. Spirited Away, New York's deepest non-alcoholic bottle shop, is a five-minute walk away on Eighth Avenue, which makes this a natural pairing for an afternoon.
venues.longDescription:
The Lobby Bar sits on the ground floor of the Hotel Chelsea on West 23rd Street — the building that housed Dylan Thomas, Leonard Cohen, Patti Smith, Janis Joplin and a century of others, and which reopened after a long and contested restoration. The bar is not an afterthought to that history; it is one of the reasons people now come to the building at all, and it was shortlisted at the inaugural NYC's Best Bars for NA Awards, judged in 2025 and reported by Time Out.

The single most useful thing about it for this guide's readers is the clock. It opens at 11am and closes at 2am, seven days a week, with no gap. Very little in New York of this quality is continuously available across fifteen hours, and the significance for someone not drinking is larger than it looks: the hardest moments are rarely 9pm on a Saturday, when everyone is out and plans exist. They are the unplanned afternoon, the hour to kill before a dinner, the point late in an evening when everyone else is a few drinks in and the options narrow to bars. A room that is open, good and comfortable at all of those hours is unusually valuable.

The honest framing: this is a full cocktail bar in a hotel and it serves alcohol. It is listed for the quality of what it will make a non-drinker, evidenced by an external NA shortlist, not as an alcohol-free space.

Chelsea is a strong neighbourhood to build an evening in for anyone using this guide. Spirited Away — America's first booze-free bottle shop and the deepest non-alcoholic selection in the city — is about a five-minute walk north on Eighth Avenue and closes at 8pm, so a tasting there before a drink here is an easy sequence. NoMad's Portrait Bar is a short walk east. For a visitor staying in Midtown or Chelsea and not drinking, this trio is close to the most efficient introduction to the city's zero-proof scene that exists.
venues.pressQuote: A broader shortlist highlighted bars with strong NA options citywide, including Sugar Monk, Lobby Bar at Hotel Chelsea, Dante, Pearl's Social & Billy Club, Dynaco, Saint Eve's, Pitts and more.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Time Out New York, NYC's Best Bars for NA Awards 2025

venues.name: L'Oca d'Oro
venues.description: L'Oca d'Oro is an Italian-inspired neighborhood restaurant in Austin's Mueller district, opened in 2016 by chef/owner Fiore Tedesco and co-owner Adam Orman after a pop-up series that began in 2013. Tedesco, a 2017 StarChefs Austin–San Antonio Rising Star, builds a seasonal, locally sourced menu of housemade pasta and Italian fare, with a stated emphasis on sourcing and staff compensation. The bar program carries a genuine, menu-listed "No / Very Low ABV" section rather than an afterthought. Zero-proof options include the School Night Spritz (strawberry cordial, fresh basil and mint, lime, bubbles) and the Dry County O.F. (dark-roast yaupon tea, yerba-orange cordial, and house orange and aromatic bitters). A Ritual Zero Proof gin alternative can be paired with housemade Italian sodas (limonata, orange cream, basil-lime, tangerine-rosemary). Non-alcoholic also includes Lost Pines Yaupon iced tea and Rambler sparkling water. Bar and patio service runs Tuesday through Sunday from 4pm.
venues.longDescription:
L'Oca d'Oro is an Italian-inspired neighbourhood restaurant in the Mueller district, opened in June 2016 by chef Fiore Tedesco and co-owner Adam Orman after three years of pop-ups and supper clubs. Tedesco came up through Roberta's and Gramercy Tavern in New York and was named a StarChefs Rising Star for Austin–San Antonio in 2017. The Austin Chronicle's Brandon Watson reviewed it that September with a line that still fits the place: luxury isn't preening, but when you find it, it's hard to notice anything else.

The restaurant is as well known for how it operates as for what it cooks — sustainable, local sourcing and a stated commitment to staff compensation, in a business where neither is standard. The Austin American-Statesman named it the city's best restaurant in 2022.

The bar carries a menu-listed No / Very Low ABV section rather than an improvised one. The School Night Spritz is strawberry cordial with fresh basil and mint, lime and bubbles. The Dry County O.F. is the more interesting build: dark-roast yaupon tea with a yerba-orange cordial and house orange and aromatic bitters, working as a zero-proof Old Fashioned.

Yaupon is worth knowing about. It is a holly native to Texas and the American Southeast, and the only caffeinated plant indigenous to North America — dark-roasted it gives tannin, body and a woody bitterness that stands in for barrel-aged spirit remarkably well. Using a local plant to solve the hardest problem in zero-proof drinks, rather than importing a bottled substitute, is exactly the sourcing philosophy the kitchen runs on, applied to the bar.

A Ritual Zero Proof gin alternative can be paired with house Italian sodas — limonata, orange cream, basil-lime, tangerine-rosemary — and there is Lost Pines yaupon iced tea and Rambler sparkling water. Bar and patio service runs Tuesday to Sunday from 4pm.
venues.pressQuote: Luxury isn't preening, but when you find it, it's hard to notice anything else.

venues.name: Local Jones
venues.description: Local Jones is the all-American bistro and neighbourhood bar inside Halcyon, a hotel in Cherry Creek, serving breakfast, lunch and dinner from 7:30am daily. Its zero-proof drinks are treated as part of the cocktail list rather than as a soft-drink afterthought: Visit Denver names the Snowcap, built from vanilla mint chai tea with lemon, honey, pomegranate and egg white, and the spicier Prickle My Fancy, describing both as the perfect people-watching sippers. The egg-white build on the Snowcap is the tell — it is shaken and finished like a sour rather than poured. The room's Cherry Creek North setting, all-day hours and hotel setting make it one of the more practical options in the neighbourhood for a mixed group meeting early or late.
signatureDrinks: Snowcap (zero-proof: vanilla mint chai tea, lemon, honey, pomegranate, egg white)
venues.longDescription:
Local Jones occupies the ground floor of Halcyon at 249 Columbine Street, in the middle of Cherry Creek North's grid of boutiques and galleries. It describes itself as an all-American bistro and neighbourhood bar — warm and inviting, where good food, good drinks and good company come together from morning to night — and it backs that up with hours that few Denver restaurants keep, opening at 7:30am seven days a week and running to 10pm on weeknights and 11pm on Friday and Saturday. That span is the practical reason it appears here: it is one of the few places in the neighbourhood where a non-drinker can meet someone for a properly made drink at 8am or 8pm.

The zero-proof drinks are positioned as cocktails rather than as juice, and the construction shows it. The Snowcap, as Visit Denver's December 2025 alcohol-free guide describes it, is "a mix of vanilla mint chai tea, lemon, honey, pomegranate and egg white" — a tea-based sour, shaken with egg white for foam and body, with the chai supplying the tannin and spice that would otherwise come from a spirit. Its companion on the list, Prickle My Fancy, runs in the opposite direction, described by the same guide as spicy; the pair are characterised there as "the perfect people-watching sippers", which is a fair read of what the room is for, given the sidewalk seating and the Cherry Creek foot traffic. Beyond the two named drinks, the kitchen's all-day format means the beverage list also covers a full coffee service in the morning and the hotel bar's stock in the evening. Local Jones is a modest rather than a landmark non-alcoholic programme — two named house drinks rather than a rotating section — but they are genuinely built, they appear on the same menu as everything else, and the venue's hours make it usable in a way that a 5pm-opening cocktail bar is not.
venues.pressQuote: At Local Jones inside Halcyon, a hotel in Cherry Creek, the zero-proof Snowcap — a mix of vanilla mint chai tea, lemon, honey, pomegranate and egg white — and spicy Prickle My Fancy are the perfect people-watching sippers.

venues.name: Lolita's
venues.description: Lolita's is a Carytown Mexican restaurant with an unusually deep bench of alcohol-free drinks for a place whose reputation rests on margaritas. There are five mocktail flavours on the standing list, including mango, hibiscus and corazón, alongside buzz-free margaritas and a range of aguas frescas — the traditional Mexican fruit waters that were alcohol-free long before anyone marketed them as such. That combination matters in practice: the aguas frescas mean a non-drinker can order something that belongs on the table rather than something invented to fill a gap, and the zero-proof margaritas cover the social ritual everyone else is participating in.
signatureDrinks: Five mocktail flavours including mango, hibiscus and corazón

naMenuItems.name: Handcrafted Mocktails
naMenuItems.description: choose between: mango | hibiscus | passion fruit | guava | corazón

naMenuItems.name: Non-Alcoholic Margarita

venues.longDescription:
Lolita's occupies a prominent spot on West Cary Street in Carytown, and like most Mexican restaurants in an American city its bar identity is built around the margarita. What makes it worth listing in an alcohol-free guide is that it has not treated that as a reason to neglect the people who are not drinking one.

The standing list carries five mocktail flavours — mango, hibiscus and corazón among them — which is a genuine menu section rather than a token line, and buzz-free margaritas sit alongside them. The hibiscus in particular is a sensible choice: agua de jamaica has real tartness and depth, and it holds its own against the salt, chilli and lime that dominate the food in a way that most sweet mocktails cannot.

The aguas frescas deserve their own mention, and they are the reason a non-drinker often has an easier evening in a Mexican restaurant than in a cocktail bar. These are traditional fruit waters — horchata, jamaica, tamarindo and their relatives — that have always been part of the cuisine and were never conceived as substitutes for anything. Ordering one is not a statement or an accommodation; it is simply what a lot of people at the table are drinking anyway. That absence of social friction is worth more than a long zero-proof list at a venue where the alcohol-free order marks you out.

The restaurant keeps generous hours, to 11:30pm on Friday and Saturday, and sits within a few minutes' walk of Point 5, Richmond's non-alcoholic bottle shop. The two together make the easiest afternoon-into-evening a non-drinker can assemble in Richmond without needing a car.
venues.pressQuote: Lolita's is a restaurant inspired by the women, who through generations instilled in us the love of Mexican culture and food

venues.name: Long Road Distillers
venues.description: Long Road Distillers became the first craft distillery in Grand Rapids when it opened on the West Side in May 2015, and its cocktail bar and kitchen at 537 Leonard Street NW remain its home. The house principle is "take no shortcuts": Long Road does not buy in finished spirit, but mills locally sourced grain, ferments and distils on site. In 2025 it extended that to alcohol-free drinking with Uncharted, its own zero-proof canned cocktail line — a Chinotto, a Lavender Lemonade, a Lemongrass Mule and a Red Amaro Spritz — which is poured in the taproom alongside a non-alcohol list running past twenty selections. The kitchen serves farm-fresh food sourced from the same regional growers.
