venues.longDescription:
Long Road Distillers opened in May 2015 as the first craft distillery in Grand Rapids, on Leonard Street NW on the city's West Side, and it is unusually literal about its process claims. The founding decision was to take no shortcuts, which in practice means the distillery does not source spirit and rebottle it: it sources ingredients, milling locally grown grain, fermenting and distilling every batch on site. Relationships with regional farmers underpin both the spirits and the kitchen, which runs a farm-fresh menu rather than standard bar food. The Leonard Street site has a full cocktail bar and event space, and the company has since added locations in Grand Haven and a third venue, Less Traveled.

What makes the taproom relevant to non-alcoholic drinking is that Long Road applied the same in-house production logic to zero-proof. In 2025 it launched Uncharted, its own line of canned zero-proof cocktails, rather than stocking a third-party mixer: the range covers a Chinotto, a Lavender Lemonade, a Lemongrass Mule and a Red Amaro Spritz, all bitter- or citrus-forward builds aimed at adult palates rather than the sweetened sodas that usually fill this slot. Those sit inside a broader non-alcohol list that runs past twenty selections, so a guest who does not drink is choosing from a menu rather than accepting whatever is available. This matters more at a distillery than almost anywhere else, because a distillery taproom is a room where the entire proposition is the alcohol — a serious zero-proof list is a deliberate decision by the people who make the spirits, not a concession. The bar trades Tuesday and Wednesday 4pm to 10pm, Thursday and Friday 4pm to 11pm and Saturday noon to 11pm, and is closed Sunday and Monday. Reservations are taken for the Grand Rapids room.

venues.name: Loro
venues.description: Loro is the Asian smokehouse from Austin chefs Tyson Cole and Aaron Franklin, and its East Dallas room on Haskell Avenue runs a printed Zero Proof section. The Strawberry Thai Basil Margarita is built on Ritual's tequila alternative; the canned St. Agrestis Phony Negroni gives the list a genuine bitter aperitivo option, which few restaurants stock and which matters a great deal against fatty smoked meat. A Spicy Cucumber, a Ginger Cooler and a frozen pink lemonade fill out the mixed drinks, with Best Day Brewing's Kölsch and Sapporo Zero on the non-alcoholic beer list. Note that press crediting this menu with Athletic Brewing and a kombucha Singapore Sling was describing the Addison location.
signatureDrinks: Strawberry Thai Basil Margarita (Ritual tequila alternative)
venues.longDescription:
Loro began as a collaboration between Tyson Cole of Uchi and pitmaster Aaron Franklin, and the East Dallas location on Haskell Avenue brings that Asian smokehouse format — smoked meats, chili-heavy sides, frozen drinks — to a big indoor-outdoor room. Its drink menu carries a section printed as Zero Proof, and the composition is smarter than most, because it has been built around what the food actually needs rather than around what is easy to pour.

The Strawberry Thai Basil Margarita is the house build, made with Ritual's tequila alternative against strawberry and Thai basil, which lines up with the kitchen's flavours rather than sitting apart from them. The more interesting listing is the St. Agrestis Phony Negroni, a canned non-alcoholic negroni from Brooklyn that delivers real bitterness — the flavour that zero-proof menus most often fail to provide, and the one that does the most work at a restaurant serving fatty smoked brisket and pork. Bitterness cuts richness; sweetness compounds it, which is why so many mocktail pairings collapse halfway through a barbecue meal. A Spicy Cucumber, a Ginger Cooler and a frozen pink lemonade cover the lighter end, and the beer list carries Best Day Brewing's Kölsch alongside Sapporo's zero-alcohol lager.

The frozen drinks deserve a word of their own, because Loro is a restaurant where the frozen cocktail is part of the identity, and a frozen pink lemonade means a non-drinker is not left out of the one order the table makes together. One correction worth recording, because it circulates widely: press coverage crediting this menu with Athletic Brewing and a K-Tonic kombucha Singapore Sling was describing Loro's Addison location, not East Dallas. The list above is what the Haskell Avenue room actually pours, and the two menus are not interchangeable.

venues.name: Loro Houston
venues.description: Loro Houston is an Asian smokehouse and bar in The Heights, a collaboration between James Beard Award winners Tyson Cole (chef of Uchi) and pitmaster Aaron Franklin (Franklin Barbecue), set inside a converted 1940s brick church. Beyond the post-oak-smoked Southeast Asian menu, Loro runs a genuinely deep Zero Proof cocktail program alongside non-alcoholic beer and craft soda/kombucha options.
signatureDrinks: Strawberry Thai Basil Margarita (Ritual tequila alternative, lime, Thai basil)
K-Tonic Kombucha Singapore Sling (cherry, baking spice, black tea)
venues.longDescription:
Loro Houston is an Asian smokehouse and bar in The Heights, a collaboration between James Beard Award winners Tyson Cole (chef and founder of Uchi) and pitmaster Aaron Franklin (Franklin Barbecue), operated under Hai Hospitality. This Heights location — Loro's third overall after Austin and Dallas — officially opened February 23, 2022, inside the converted former W 11th Church of God, a 1940s brick sanctuary reimagined as a soaring dining room with an umbrella-dotted patio.

The renovation, led by Hai's director of design Ellen Saathoff, added skylights and an east-facing glass wall in place of the old church entrance, plus acoustic ceiling panels and white-oak finishes to tame the sanctuary's echo. Saathoff called it "a really special project to all of us because we got to use this amazing existing building." The kitchen runs on two large rotisserie-style smokers from J&R Manufacturing, sized up from the Austin and Dallas locations to handle a to-go business that now makes up roughly 20-30% of sales.

The food pairs Southeast Asian flavors with post-oak-smoked meats and fish, from brisket sandwiches topped with Thai papaya salad to oak-smoked salmon in cucumber-yuzu broth.

For non-drinkers, Loro maintains a dedicated Zero Proof menu section rather than a token offering. House mocktails include the Strawberry Thai Basil Margarita (Ritual tequila alternative, lime, Thai basil), Spicy Cucumber (lime, yuzu, spicy agave), Ginger Cooler (yuzu, ginger beer), Frozen Pink Lemonade (lemon, strawberry), K-Tonic Kombucha Singapore Sling (cherry, baking spice, black tea), Grapefruit Fizz (grapefruit, yuzu honey), Jasmine Honey (jasmine tea, yuzu) and Cherry Spritz (cherry, lemon, basil) — the latter four singled out in Houston Press's January 2026 Dry January mocktail guide. Packaged non-alcoholic options add Best Day Brewing Kölsch, Sapporo Zero and St. Agrestis Phony Negroni, alongside a deep soft-drink list: a K-Tonic x Loro collaboration kombucha on draft, handmade yuzu soda, coconut matcha limeade, Vietnamese coffee, Thai tea, and soda-fountain floats like the Lonestar Float (Dr. Pepper, vanilla cream, passionfruit).
venues.pressQuote: Loro's zero-proof cocktails include the K-Tonic Kombucha Singapore Sling with cherry, baking spice and black tea, and a Strawberry Thai Margarita made with a Ritual tequila alternative, lime and Thai basil.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Houston Press, "Houston's Dry January Mocktail Guide: Zero-Proof, Full Flavor" (Jan. 1, 2026)

venues.name: Loro
venues.description: Loro is the Asian smokehouse on South Lamar from Tyson Cole of Uchi and pitmaster Aaron Franklin — a genuine Austin institution, and the original of the concept that has since spread to Dallas and Houston. Its bar program is built for the food, which is smoky, spicy and sweet, and the non-alcoholic side reflects that: the Spicy Cucumber pairs yuzu with ghost agave, giving a drink with real heat and citrus acidity rather than a sweet fallback. Visit Austin's official zero-proof guide names it. The room is casual counter-service with a large patio, so it works for a group at any hour of the day.
venues.longDescription:
Loro on South Lamar is the original location of the Asian smokehouse concept created by Tyson Cole, the chef behind Uchi, and Aaron Franklin, whose barbecue needs no introduction in Texas. The pairing produced something genuinely Austin: Central Texas smoke technique applied to Southeast Asian flavours, served counter-service in a big room with an even bigger patio. The concept has since expanded to Dallas and Houston, but this is where it started.

The food is loud in the best sense — smoked meats cut with chilli, herbs, citrus and sugar — and that has consequences for the drinks. A beverage here has to survive heat and fat, which is exactly the problem a weak non-alcoholic drink fails at. The Spicy Cucumber is built for the job: yuzu supplies sharp citrus acidity, and ghost agave brings genuine heat, so the drink cuts through the smoke instead of drowning under it. Visit Austin's official zero-proof guide names it as the house alcohol-free option.

One named drink is a modest program, and the grade reflects that honestly — this is not a bar with a parallel zero-proof list. What makes it worth listing anyway is the combination of the drink actually being designed rather than defaulted, and the setting being unusually easy for a non-drinker: counter service means no bar-side negotiation, the patio is large and casual, and the venue trades all day from 11am rather than being an evening drinking room.

The South Lamar location is the flagship and stays busy through the evening; the patio absorbs most of it, and counter service keeps the queue moving faster than the crowd suggests. Note that the Dallas Loro listed elsewhere in this guide is the same concept under the same group, with its own separate drinks list, so the alcohol-free options are not guaranteed to match between the two cities.
venues.pressQuote: Loro (South Austin): Spicy Cucumber (yuzu, ghost agave).

venues.name: Los Fuegos by Francis Mallmann
venues.description: Los Fuegos is the Argentine grill restaurant that Francis Mallmann runs inside Faena Miami Beach on Collins Avenue in Mid-Beach, cooking over open fire, the method Mallmann is known for. The bar's documented alcohol-free build is the Hibiscus Bloom, which blends passionfruit with hibiscus tea and a honey-lavender element — tart and floral rather than sugary, and closer in shape to an infusion than to a fruit punch. RESIDENT wrote in December 2025 that the zero-proof offering feels as intentional as the open-fire cooking. The restaurant serves breakfast and lunch from 7am to 4pm every day and dinner from 6:30pm, running to 11pm on Friday and Saturday.
venues.longDescription:
Los Fuegos by Francis Mallmann occupies the ground floor of Faena Miami Beach at 3201 Collins Avenue, in the Faena District of Mid-Beach. Mallmann is the Argentine chef known for cooking over open flame, and the restaurant is built around that method. The room keeps long hours for a hotel restaurant, serving breakfast and lunch continuously from 7am to 4pm every day and dinner from 6:30pm, closing at 10:30pm on weeknights and 11pm on Friday and Saturday.

The alcohol-free build documented at the restaurant is the Hibiscus Bloom, which blends passionfruit with hibiscus tea and a honey-lavender element. It is a tart, floral drink rather than a sweet one — hibiscus supplies acidity and colour, and the lavender keeps the honey from dominating — and it is built to sit against smoke and char rather than to be drunk on its own. RESIDENT covered the restaurant at the head of its December 2025 Miami round-up and wrote that at Los Fuegos the zero-proof offering feels as intentional as the open-fire cooking, describing the drink as composed and refreshing and as aligning with Mallmann's elemental approach to flavour. Only one named alcohol-free drink is published, so the programme is graded as real but modest; readers should expect a hotel bar of this size to also carry non-alcoholic beer and soft options that are not listed publicly. The restaurant posts as @losfuegosfaena and can be reached on (786) 655-5600. One further note on geography: Aguasal by José Andrés, already carried in this catalogue, sits further south along Collins Avenue inside Andaz Miami Beach, so a guest planning a Beach evening without drinking has two documented options on the same road. The venue's Instagram account, @losfuegosfaena, describes the restaurant as a contemporary asado experience by Francis Mallmann, open daily for breakfast, lunch and dinner at Faena Miami Beach, which matches the trading hours recorded here.
venues.pressQuote: The Hibiscus Bloom blends passionfruit, honey-lavender, and hibiscus tea into a composed, refreshing mocktail that aligns seamlessly with Francis Mallmann’s elemental approach to flavor.

venues.name: Lost Cultures Tea Bar
venues.description: Lost Cultures Tea Bar is a fully non-alcoholic bar in Albuquerque's Sawmill District where owner Ryan Brown builds cocktails out of tea rather than out of spirit substitutes. The Ancient Fashioned is pu'erh tea with sugar, orange bitters and wood smoke; the Smokey Rose runs lapsang souchong against grapefruit, lemon, rose simple syrup and foaming bitters; the paloma is built on chamomile with lime, agave and grapefruit soda. Kombucha is poured alongside. Brown does not use the word mocktail for any of it, and the room is a genuine bar rather than a tea shop with a late licence — Friday and Saturday it runs to 10pm.
venues.address: 1761 Bellamah Ave NW Suite C, Albuquerque, NM 87104
signatureDrinks: Ancient Fashioned — pu'erh tea, sugar, orange bitters, wood smoke
Smokey Rose — lapsang souchong tea, grapefruit, lemon, rose simple syrup, foaming bitters
Paloma — chamomile tea, lime juice, agave syrup, grapefruit soda

naMenuItems.name: Untitled Art
naMenuItems.description: juicy ipa, oktoberfest, chocolate stout alcohol removed

venues.longDescription:
Most alcohol-free bars solve the problem by buying a non-alcoholic spirit and building the familiar cocktails with it. Lost Cultures, in Albuquerque's Sawmill District, solves it a different and more interesting way: it builds drinks out of tea.

The logic is sound. What tea offers that juice cannot is tannin, bitterness and smoke — the structural qualities that make a spirit-based drink worth sipping slowly rather than draining. Owner Ryan Brown's Ancient Fashioned uses pu'erh, a fermented tea with genuine earthy depth, with sugar, orange bitters and wood smoke, and it occupies the same place at a table that a real old fashioned does. The Smokey Rose is built on lapsang souchong, which is smoked over pine, against grapefruit, lemon, rose syrup and foaming bitters — the foam giving it the texture a sour would have from egg white. Even the paloma is a tea drink, chamomile with lime, agave and grapefruit soda.

Brown is precise about the language, telling New Mexico Magazine that he does not really use the word mocktail. That refusal recurs across this directory — Burlington's The 126 insists on Temperance Cocktails, Greenville's Bar Margaret heads its section Don't Call Them Mocktails — and it is consistently a marker of the rooms doing the best work. The word frames the drink as an imitation, and the people who care most about the category will not accept that framing.

The line that explains why this venue leads the guide is his, too: at least twice a week, someone comes in and thanks him for providing a completely non-alcoholic space. That is the whole argument for a dedicated room over a good mocktail list, made by the person hearing it.

Hours are Wednesday and Thursday 3pm to 9pm, Friday and Saturday 11am to 10pm, Sunday 11am to 9pm, closed Monday and Tuesday. Kombucha is served alongside the tea drinks.

There is a structural reason tea works where fruit juice does not, and it is worth spelling out for anyone trying to order well elsewhere. Alcohol contributes three things to a drink: aroma, weight and a faint astringent bite. Juice replaces none of them and adds sugar instead, which is why most mocktails are pleasant for one glass and tiring by the second. Tea supplies tannin for the bite, brewed body for the weight, and — in a smoked or fermented leaf like lapsang or pu'erh — genuine aroma. It is the closest thing the non-alcoholic world has to a base spirit, and Lost Cultures is the only venue in this directory built entirely on that insight.
venues.pressQuote: At least twice a week someone will come in and thank me for providing a completely nonalcoholic space.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Ryan Brown, owner, Lost Cultures Tea Bar

venues.name: Lost Whale
venues.description: Lost Whale is a sustainability-minded craft cocktail bar in Milwaukee's Bay View, open since 2018 in the former Boone & Crockett space on Kinnickinnic Avenue. Alongside an acclaimed full-proof program, it keeps a standing "spiritless" section of four to five zero-proof cocktails built on Ritual Zero-Proof and Lyre's, plus non-alcoholic beer. The snug, midcentury-modern room pairs seasonal cocktail themes with a documented green ethos — composting, biodegradable straws, and cross-utilized produce. Because it also serves alcohol, it is a hybrid rather than a fully alcohol-free bar.
venues.longDescription:
Lost Whale opened in June 2018 in Bay View's former Boone & Crockett space at 2151 S. Kinnickinnic Ave., the work of Milwaukee hospitality veterans Tripper Duval and Daniel Beres. Named for Lake Michigan folklore and perched near the Kinnickinnic River, the bar built a national reputation — features in Forbes and Imbibe and a spot on the Tales of the Cocktail Foundation's Top 30 New Cocktail Bars in America — while staying rooted in neighborhood warmth and a genuine sustainability program of composting, biodegradable straws, cross-utilized produce, and waterway-focused community work.

Non-drinkers are treated as first-class guests here. Lost Whale carries a dedicated "spiritless" section on its menu, and per OnMilwaukee you'll "always find at least four or five great options, all of which are just as delicious as their full-proof offerings." The zero-proof builds lean on Ritual Zero-Proof (both the rum and the aperitif) and Lyre's — think a Hemingway-ish Daiquiri made with Ritual Zero-Proof Rum, grapefruit-lime, Demerara and bitters, or a zero-proof Carrot Top built on Lyre's Agave Blanco, Cane and Orange Sec. Non-alcoholic beer is always on hand, and the list rotates alongside the bar's seasonal, often theme-driven cocktail menus.

Practically, the bar runs Monday through Thursday 4pm to midnight, Friday and Saturday 4pm to 2am, and Sunday noon to 10pm, with a daily 4–6pm happy hour and a rotating food truck on site. Visit Milwaukee singles it out for "expertly crafted mocktails," making Lost Whale one of Bay View's most reliable rooms for a serious zero-proof cocktail without giving up the craft-bar setting.
venues.pressQuote: Serving a wide array of deliciously designed beverages and mocktails, including zero-proof rum, whiskey and more, Lost Whale concocts flavorful drinks that taste like the real thing.

venues.name: Lotus Brew Coffee
venues.description: Lotus Brew Coffee is a queer-, immigrant- and furry-owned coffee shop and dry bar at 211 Diamond Avenue SE in East Hills. It serves no alcohol. Alongside a full coffee and tea program it runs what its own site calls a Queer Dry Bar, with a non-alcoholic cocktail list, a weekday happy hour from 4pm to 6pm, and a standing schedule of events, mixers and meets billed as an alt non-alcoholic queer night space. The shop moved here from 781 College Avenue NE, where it operated inside the Communitea Wellness building, into a room roughly twice the size. It keeps a lending library, and its logo was designed by Alix, a local trans non-binary artist, with all profits from logo merchandise going to them.
venues.address: 211 Diamond Ave SE, Grand Rapids, MI 49506
venues.longDescription:
Lotus Brew Coffee began inside Communitea Wellness on College Avenue NE and has since moved to 211 Diamond Avenue SE, a building about twice the size, in the East Hills neighbourhood. The relocation is the important detail for anyone navigating by an older listing: the College Avenue address is no longer current. The shop is queer, immigrant and furry owned, and functions as a community hub as much as a cafe — there is a lending library, a published set of public resources, and a rolling calendar of weekly events, mixers and meets. Its logo was drawn by Alix, a local trans non-binary artist, and the shop passes 100 percent of the profits from logo merchandise back to them. A sign behind the counter reads "This coffee kills fascists."

What makes it relevant here is that Lotus Brew is not a coffee shop that happens to have a couple of mocktails. Its own site advertises a Queer Dry Bar as a distinct part of the business, running an alt non-alcoholic queer night space with a weekday happy hour from 4pm to 6pm, and its online ordering menu carries a dedicated Non Alcoholic Cocktails category alongside the espresso and tea lists. Nothing on the premises contains alcohol, which puts it in a small group of Grand Rapids venues where a sober guest is not making a substitution. The drinks lean bright and sweet rather than bitter-and-botanical — the Mango Mule is the one most often named in local coverage. One caution on planning a visit: the location-and-hours block on the shop's own website is an unedited template still showing a placeholder San Francisco address and phone number, so the opening times published there should not be relied on. Confirm current hours with the shop directly on (616) 419-8613.
venues.pressQuote: Serving a variety of coffees, teas and mocktails – such as a Mango Mule.

venues.name: LouElla Wine, Beer & Beverage
venues.description: LouElla is a bottle shop, bar and neighbourhood hangout on West Geer Street in Old North Durham, with Saturday tastings and a bar you can drink at rather than only buy from, and its non-alcoholic range runs to roughly sixty products — far beyond the token shelf most wine shops keep. The selection spans non-alcoholic beer from Burial and Untitled Art, de-alcoholised wine from Leitz, St. Agrestis' bottled Phony Negroni, Eric Bordelet's sparkling pear Perlant from Normandy and a deep bank of tonics and social seltzers from CANN, Crescent 9, High Rise and Resident Culture. It sells alcohol too, and carries Delta-9 and THC products alongside the non-alcoholic range, so read labels. Discover Durham lists it for non-alcoholic products made locally and beyond. Closed Monday; open to nine or ten the rest of the week.
venues.address: 316 W Geer St Suite A, Durham, NC 27701
venues.longDescription:
LouElla describes itself as equal parts wine shop, bar and community hangout, and it sits on West Geer Street in Old North Durham with Saturday tastings and a bar you can drink at rather than only buy from. It sells alcohol — this is not an alcohol-free shop — but its non-alcoholic range is substantial enough to make it a destination in its own right rather than a place that happens to stock a few cans.

The collection runs to around sixty non-alcoholic products, and the breadth is what distinguishes it. On beer there is Burial, the Asheville brewery whose Chaosmachine NA IPA is one of the better American examples, and Untitled Art's non-alcoholic variety pack. On wine there is Leitz's Eine Zwei Zero range from the Rheingau. On cocktails there is St. Agrestis' Phony Negroni, the bottled bittersweet aperitif that has become the default good answer for people who want something adult. There is Eric Bordelet's Perlant, a sparkling pear juice from a Normandy cidermaker, which is the kind of thing that only turns up in shops where somebody is actually choosing the list. Around that sit tonics and social seltzers — CANN, Crescent 9, High Rise, Resident Culture, Happy Bird — and a range of Five Flowers lemonades and mixers.

The products come from Austria, France, Germany, Spain, the USA and South America, with the largest single group American. For anyone building a home bar without alcohol, or looking for something to bring to a dinner that is not sparkling water, this is the best-stocked room in the metro.

Two practical notes. The shop also carries Delta-9 and THC products alongside the non-alcoholic range, so read labels carefully if you are avoiding those. And the web address has moved: louellawine.com now redirects to louelladurham.com.
venues.pressQuote: non-alcoholic products made locally and beyond

venues.name: Louie's Cocktail Lounge
venues.description: Louie's Cocktail Lounge in Rancho Cordova stocks three non-alcoholic beers — Heineken 0.0, Michelob Ultra 0.0 and Corona Cero — alongside Shirley Temples, virgin margaritas and virgin piña coladas. The drinks are unpretentious, but the hours are extraordinary: 6am to 2am, every day, twenty hours a day. For shift workers, early risers and anyone whose day does not run on a standard schedule, a room that is open and has three cold non-alcoholic beers at seven in the morning is a genuinely different kind of useful. It is in Rancho Cordova, about fifteen minutes east of downtown. Three different NA beers on one back bar also suggests real demand rather than a token gesture, since neighbourhood lounges do not carry redundant stock for appearances.
venues.address: 3030 Mather Field Rd, Rancho Cordova, CA 95670
venues.longDescription:
Louie's Cocktail Lounge sits on Mather Field Road in Rancho Cordova, a suburb east of Sacramento near the former air force base. It is a neighbourhood lounge rather than a cocktail destination, and its alcohol-free offering is straightforward: three non-alcoholic beers — Heineken 0.0, Michelob Ultra 0.0 and Corona Cero — plus Shirley Temples, virgin margaritas and virgin piña coladas.

The drinks are ordinary and this listing does not pretend otherwise. What is not ordinary is the schedule: 6am to 2am, seven days a week. Twenty hours a day, every day.

That deserves attention because of who it serves. Almost everything written about alcohol-free drinking assumes a particular customer — someone choosing between cocktail bars on a Friday evening. It does not describe the nurse coming off a night shift, the construction crew finishing at seven in the morning, the person whose social hours simply are not the same as everyone else's. Those people also stop drinking, and when they do, the entire published landscape of thoughtful mocktail menus is closed.

A lounge open at six in the morning with three cold non-alcoholic beers in the fridge is not competing with Kupros or Juju. It is covering hours that nothing else in this guide touches, for people the category tends to overlook entirely. Stocking three different NA beers rather than one also suggests actual demand rather than a token gesture.

Rancho Cordova is about fifteen minutes east of downtown, well outside the Midtown cluster, which extends the geographic reach of this guide further still.

It is also worth noting what three NA beers on one back bar implies. Stocking a single Heineken 0.0 is what a distributor pushes; stocking Heineken, Michelob Ultra Zero and Corona Cero side by side means somebody looked at what was selling and reordered. Neighbourhood bars do not carry redundant stock for image. The likeliest explanation is that a reliable number of regulars are drinking them, which says something about how far the shift away from alcohol has travelled outside the places that write about it.
venues.pressQuote: Louie's Cocktail Lounge: Heineken 0.0, Michelob Ultra 0.0, Corona Cero, Shirley Temples, virgin margaritas, virgin piña coladas.

venues.name: Lounge Here
venues.description: Lounge Here is a retro '70s cocktail lounge in East Dallas near White Rock Lake, opened by musicians Julie Doyle and Tim DeLaughter (The Polyphonic Spree, Tripping Daisy) beside their Good Records shop. Its zero-proof options go past a token soda: a named mocktail like Memaw's Apple Pie (apple cider, cinnamon syrup, lemon, ginger ale) sits alongside canned Athletic non-alcoholic beer and HOP WTR, a functional sparkling water dosed with ashwagandha and L-Theanine in Blood Orange and Mango. The bar builds its alcohol-free drinks with the same care as the full cocktail list, so non-drinking guests aren't stuck with a Shirley Temple.
signatureDrinks: Memaw's Apple Pie (apple cider, cinnamon syrup, lemon, ginger ale)
Paisley Daisy (Ritual Zero Proof tequila alternative, lime juice, agave, orange juice)
venues.longDescription:
Lounge Here occupies a strip on Garland Road in the Casa Linda / White Rock stretch of East Dallas, next door to the beloved Good Records store. It was opened by Julie Doyle and Tim DeLaughter — the husband-and-wife team behind Tripping Daisy and The Polyphonic Spree — and leans hard into a retro, Marfa-tinged '70s airport-lounge look: plush banquettes, moody lighting, and a large photo mural by Rainer Judd. The kitchen turns out Southern-inspired shareable plates (deviled eggs, pimento cheese, shrimp and grits) alongside the drinks program.

For non-drinkers, the lounge stocks a real set of alcohol-free options rather than a lone soft drink. It pours canned Athletic non-alcoholic beer and carries HOP WTR — a sparkling water pitched as an IPA-style sip without alcohol, spiked with the adaptogens ashwagandha and L-Theanine and offered in Blood Orange and Mango. On the cocktail side, the bar makes named zero-proof builds; the recurring favorite is Memaw's Apple Pie, a blend of apple cider, cinnamon syrup, lemon, and ginger ale, and a Paisley Daisy built on a Ritual Zero Proof tequila alternative with lime, agave, and orange juice.

Day to day it works as a neighborhood happy-hour and dinner spot — happy hour runs late afternoon, with a Sunday brunch — and its cocktail-lounge identity means the NA drinks are shaken and built to order rather than pulled from a fountain. That makes it a workable option for sober and sober-curious guests who want an actual crafted drink in a stylish room, though the alcohol-free list is a handful of items rather than a full dedicated menu.
venues.pressQuote: Athletic non-alcoholic beer and HOP WTR, a sparkling water that has a similar taste of an IPA without alcohol

venues.name: Love Kava Bar
venues.description: Love Kava is an alcohol-free social bar in Doral, open until 1am every night and from 6pm on Sundays, and it is the only venue of its kind in a part of Miami-Dade otherwise served by chain restaurants and airport-corridor hotel bars. The layout does a lot of work: an indoor lounge, an outdoor area, a hidden speakeasy room and a ping-pong table, with Sunday tardeo sessions running live DJs. IMPORTANT for readers in recovery: alongside kava, the bar sells kratom and stocks hemp products including vapes. Kratom acts on opioid receptors and carries dependence and withdrawal risk that kava does not, so if the reason you are looking for a kava bar is that you are avoiding substances with a hold, this room requires you to order specifically.
venues.longDescription:
Love Kava sits at 7700 NW 56th Street in Doral, which is worth stating plainly because Doral is not a neighbourhood this directory has been able to serve well. It is a city of about 80,000 people west of Miami International Airport, dense with corporate offices and new residential towers, and its evening options run heavily to chain restaurants and hotel bars. Love Kava is, as far as we can establish, the only dedicated alcohol-free social room in it. It opens at 11am Monday through Saturday and at 6pm on Sunday, and closes at 1am every night.

The room is laid out to be occupied rather than passed through. There is an indoor lounge and an outdoor section, a ping-pong table, and a speakeasy area tucked behind the main space. The Sunday programme is the distinctive one — tardeo sessions with live DJs, an afternoon-into-evening dance format borrowed from Latin American nightlife, which in a city as Venezuelan and Colombian as Doral is a much better fit than a quiz night would be. It is one of the few places in Miami-Dade where you can dance, at night, to a DJ, without a bar being the centre of the room.

The kava programme is the core of the menu and the reason the venue is categorised here as a kava bar rather than as a lounge. Kava is a South Pacific root, ground and infused in water, alcohol-free, earthy and numbing to the lips, and mildly sedative — a genuine social drink rather than a soft drink, and the basis of the alcohol-free bar scene across most of Florida.

Two caveats belong in the open rather than at the bottom of a page. Love Kava serves kratom alongside kava, and it stocks hemp products including vapes. Neither is unusual for a Florida kava bar, and neither is alcohol, but neither is neutral for the audience this site is written for. Kratom is the leaf of Mitragyna speciosa; its alkaloids act on opioid receptors, regular use produces tolerance and a withdrawal syndrome, several states ban it, and concentrated 7-OH kratom products are under federal scheduling action. Kava has no comparable dependence profile. If you are avoiding alcohol specifically, none of this need trouble you. If you are avoiding intoxicants and dependence-forming substances generally — which is a large share of the people who search for rooms like this — then the honest position is that Love Kava has a menu you need to navigate rather than one you can order from blindly. Staff will tell you what is in a drink if you ask.

venues.name: Low Tide Kava Bar
venues.description: Low Tide Kava Bar is a traditional South-Pacific-style kava bar on Gulfport's Beach Boulevard, built as a calm, alcohol-free alternative to a night out. It serves kava and kratom tea along with kombucha on tap and soft drinks, drawing a regular neighborhood crowd with live music and trivia from morning into the early-morning hours. (It serves kratom alongside kava.)  It shares Gulfport's short main street with Sober Bar, the fully zero-proof room that opened in 2026 — two alcohol-free venues within a few hundred metres, which makes this small waterfront town the densest pocket of sober nightlife anywhere in Tampa Bay.
venues.longDescription:
Low Tide Kava Bar sits on Beach Boulevard in Gulfport, the small waterfront town southwest of St. Petersburg whose main street runs a few blocks and ends at the bay. It is built as a traditional South-Pacific-style kava bar rather than as a cocktail room that happens not to serve alcohol — the format is the nakamal, the drink is the point, and the room is arranged for sitting and talking rather than for standing and ordering.

What makes it work as a venue rather than merely a kava shop is the programming. It draws a regular neighbourhood crowd with live music and trivia nights, running from the morning into the early hours, which gives the week a shape. Kava and kratom tea are the core, with kombucha on tap and soft drinks for anyone who wants nothing psychoactive — a useful option in a room where the default order is unfamiliar to most first-time visitors.

Gulfport is worth understanding as context. It is a small arts-leaning town with a disproportionate number of bars for its size, and Low Tide shares its main street with Sober Bar, the fully zero-proof room that opened in 2026. Two alcohol-free venues within a few hundred metres, in a town of this scale, is genuinely unusual and makes Gulfport the densest pocket of sober nightlife in Tampa Bay.

The standard caution applies. Low Tide serves kratom alongside kava; kava is psychoactive and sedating with documented case reports of liver injury, and kratom acts on opioid receptors with dependence and withdrawal risk. Nothing served contains alcohol, and that is not the same as nothing served having an effect.  For a designated driver or someone taking a night off, it is an easy recommendation; for someone in recovery, the distinction deserves real weight before walking in.
venues.pressQuote: the Loves discovered the laid-back kava house in Gulfport, Low Tide Lounge

venues.name: Loyal Legion
venues.description: Loyal Legion is an all-Oregon beer hall in the Central Eastside known for 99 taps of local craft beer. Beyond beer it keeps a genuine non-alcoholic program: its published taplist lists multiple dedicated NA pours including Best Day Brewing's American Light lager and Kölsch, Bitburger NA pilsner, Crux NO MO NA IPAs, and Lazy Days hop water.
signatureDrinks: Best Day American Light N/A Lager
Crux NO MO West Coast IPA
Lazy Days Hop Gossip hop water
venues.longDescription:
Loyal Legion is a Portland beer hall that opened in 2015 in the historic P.P.A.A. building at SE 6th & Alder, created by Kurt Huffman and his ChefStable restaurant group. It is named after a vintage "Loyal Legion of Loggers and Lumbermen" sign Huffman discovered in 2008, now hung over the room's central bar. The hall is built around a roughly 99-tap lineup devoted almost exclusively to Oregon beer and cider, alongside a large whiskey selection, sausages and burgers; ChefStable has since expanded the concept to Beaverton and the Portland airport.

Loyal Legion also maintains a notably deep non-alcoholic draft and can program, which it spotlights each Dry January with curated craft NA pours and tasting events featuring NA producers. Verified non-alcoholic offerings have included Best Day Brewing American Light N/A Lager and N/A Kölsch, HECK Brewing "Gentle Persuasion" Golden Ale, Bitburger N/A Pilsner, Crux NO MO West Coast and Hazy IPAs, plus Lazy Days "Hop Gossip" hop water. As a beer-hall venue, the NA selection is poured at the same central bar as the main tap list.
venues.pressQuote: This sprawling beer hall boasts almost 100 Oregon beers and ciders on tap daily, with draft lines and kegs meticulously cared for and maintained.

venues.name: Lucille
venues.description: Lucille is a wood-fired pizza restaurant and bar on King Street just off the Capitol Square, and one of the downtown rooms Madison's guides name repeatedly for non-alcoholic drinking. Its zero-proof builds are seasonal and properly constructed rather than sweetened — the Honeycrisp and Tart Cherry Mule leans on apple and sour cherry against ginger, and the Pineapple Mint No-Jito is the house mojito without the rum. The kitchen runs late for Madison, to 11pm most nights and 1am on Friday and Saturday, which matters in a downtown where a lot of the better zero-proof lists sit in restaurants that stop serving at nine.
venues.longDescription:
King Street is the short diagonal running off the Capitol Square towards Lake Monona, and it is one of the densest restaurant blocks in Madison. Lucille sits at the top of it at number 101, doing wood-fired pizza and a full bar across two floors, and it functions as the unfussy end of the downtown drinking scene — a place you can walk into on a Tuesday without a reservation and still get a properly made drink.

The non-alcoholic list is short and seasonal rather than long and static, which is the right trade for a room this size. The Honeycrisp and Tart Cherry Mule is the autumn build — apple and sour cherry set against ginger, so it lands tart and spiced rather than sweet, and the mule format gives it the length and the copper-mug ritual that makes a non-alcoholic drink feel like a drink rather than a consolation. The Pineapple Mint No-Jito is the summer counterpart, muddled to order. Both appear in Madison Eats Food Tours' guide to the city's must-try non-alcoholic drinks, and City Cast Madison independently names the No-Jito.

The hours are the practical argument for putting Lucille in a downtown plan. It opens at 11am Thursday through Sunday and runs to 11pm most nights and 1am on Friday and Saturday, which is later than Merchant, Heritage Tavern or Eno Vino manage. For a group that wants to eat and then keep going, that removes the usual problem of the evening ending early because the good zero-proof room shuts. Merchant and Settle Down Tavern are both a two-minute walk away on Pinckney Street, and the Great Dane's downtown brewpub is around the corner on Doty.
venues.pressQuote: Lucille's non-alcoholic options include the Honeycrisp and Tart Cherry Mule and the Pineapple Mint Nojito.

venues.name: Lucky Belly
venues.description: Lucky Belly is a ramen and Asian-fusion restaurant and bar on North Hotel Street in Chinatown, and one of the venues that anchored the district's revival. Its non-alcoholic drinks are unusually well constructed for a restaurant of its size. The Chinatown Swizzle is built on galangal, kaffir lime and lemongrass with drinking vinegar and coconut water — a savoury, aromatic drink that owes nothing to the fruit-and-soda template. The Liliko'i Fizz combines passionfruit purée with spiced almond syrup, fresh mint and club soda, and a hibiscus lemonade sits alongside them. All are priced around $5, well below the cost of a cocktail.

signatureDrinks: Chinatown Swizzle (galangal, kaffir lime, lemongrass, drinking vinegar, coconut water)
Liliko'i Fizz (liliko'i purée, spiced almond syrup, fresh mint, club soda)
venues.longDescription:
Lucky Belly has traded at 50 North Hotel Street since the early 2010s and was one of the restaurants that turned Chinatown from a district people avoided after dark into the centre of Honolulu's independent food scene. The kitchen is built around ramen and Asian fusion, the room is small and dark, and the bar has always been taken more seriously than a noodle house strictly requires.

That shows in the non-alcoholic list, which is more interesting than most dedicated cocktail bars manage. The Chinatown Swizzle is the standout and the one worth ordering: galangal, kaffir lime and lemongrass — the aromatic base of a great deal of South-East Asian cooking — combined with drinking vinegar and coconut water. Drinking vinegar is the same principle as the shrub used up at SKY Waikīkī, and it does the same job of supplying sharpness, but here it is set against savoury, resinous aromatics rather than fruit, which produces something genuinely unlike a soft drink. Galangal in particular is sharper and more medicinal than ginger, and it gives the drink a bitterness that has nothing to do with sugar. The Liliko'i Fizz works the sweeter side, with passionfruit purée against spiced almond syrup, fresh mint and club soda, and a hibiscus lemonade covers the simplest case. The pricing is the other thing worth noting: these have historically run around $5, roughly a third of what a cocktail costs, which is the opposite of the usual hotel-bar practice of charging cocktail prices for a drink with the expensive ingredient removed. Chinatown puts the restaurant within a couple of blocks of both Senia and The Pig & The Lady, and a short walk from Yours Truly on Bishop Street, which makes the downtown grid the densest concentration of decent non-alcoholic drinking in the city.
venues.pressQuote: We were happy to discover that one of our favorite spots for comfort food during a stressful workweek also serves two Island-inspired mocktails.

venues.name: Lucky Star
venues.description: Lucky Star is a Taiwanese cafe and cocktail bar in the lobby of the Star Metals complex on Howell Mill Road in West Midtown, opened in December 2024 by chef Jason Liang and John Chen of Michelin-starred Brush. It runs as a coffee shop and bakery by day and flips to a cocktail bar at night, with a kitchen serving Taiwanese food throughout. The bar is recommended in the Michelin Guide and is built around laboratory technique — clarification, precision dilution — applied identically whether or not there is alcohol in the glass. Named spirit-free drinks include Bee's Ginger on a non-alcoholic gin base with honey, lemon and ginger; Tomato + Tonic, which pairs clarified tomato with Fever-Tree; and Aztec January, layering passionfruit and lemon over a house-made mole syrup.
venues.address: 1055 Howell Mill Rd Suite 110, Atlanta, GA 30318

Aztec January (passionfruit, lemon, house-made mole syrup)
venues.longDescription:
Lucky Star opened on 6 December 2024 in the lobby of the Star Metals office complex at 1055 Howell Mill Road, from chef Jason Liang and John Chen — the partners behind Brush, the Michelin-starred sushi counter in Buckhead, as well as Momonoki and Momo Cafe in Midtown. It was, for Liang, a reconnection with his Taiwanese roots after years of working in Japanese cooking. The format changes across the day: coffee, pastries and Taiwanese breakfast and lunch dishes from mid-morning, then a break, then a reopening at four or five as a cocktail bar with an à la carte menu and a cocktail omakase option. Co-beverage directors Kirk Gibson and Nik Soukavona run the drinks programme, which leans hard on laboratory method — centrifuge clarification, controlled dilution, house cordials and syrups built from scratch.

The reason it belongs on a non-alcoholic guide is that the method does not change when the alcohol comes out. DiningOut put it plainly in 2026: the techniques do not change based on what is in the glass. Three spirit-free drinks are named on the menu. Bee's Ginger sits on a non-alcoholic gin base with honey, lemon and fresh ginger, a straightforward sour given backbone by the botanical base. Tomato + Tonic is the technical showpiece — tomato clarified until it is water-clear, then lengthened with Fever-Tree tonic, so the drink reads savoury and dry rather than like a juice. Aztec January layers passionfruit and lemon over a house-made mole syrup, using chilli and chocolate bitterness to do the work that alcohol would otherwise do. The drinks are designed to be paired with the kitchen's food rather than drunk in isolation, which is the tell of a programme that treats zero-proof as part of the meal. The bar trades Wednesday through Saturday into the late evening and closes Monday and Tuesday.
venues.pressQuote: The techniques at Lucky Star don't change based on what's in the glass. The team behind this Michelin-recommended Taiwanese bar builds spirit-free cocktails with the same scientific precision.

venues.name: Lulu Bar
venues.description: Lulu Bar is the Toronto outpost of Concorde Group's Pacific-inspired restaurant and bar, set inside The Well development in the Entertainment District. Opened in 2024, it pairs a chef-driven menu spanning Hawaii, California and British Columbia with a genuine list of alcohol-free cocktails, beer and wine rather than a token mocktail. Its signature zero-proof pour is the Hawaiian Honeycreeper, a jungle-bird riff built on Lumette LumRum non-alcoholic spirit with a sparkling bitter aperitivo, roasted pineapple, honey and lime.

venues.longDescription:
Lulu Bar is the Toronto location of Concorde Group's Pacific-inspired restaurant and bar concept, occupying a corner of The Well — the mixed-use development at 427 Wellington St W that anchors Toronto's Entertainment District. It opened in 2024 as a "welcoming, airy space" built around a chef-driven menu the venue describes as drawing flavours "from Asia to Hawaii, California to British Columbia," turning out what its own site calls "light and fresh fare that is heavy of flavour."

Lulu's non-alcoholic program goes well beyond a token mocktail on request. The venue's own promotion advertises a dedicated alcohol-free drink menu built around a Zero Proof Coconut Cooler, and independent Toronto coverage treats the list as one of the city's more serious no/low programs: NOW Toronto named Lulu Bar as having the "most extensive zero proof menu" in its roundup of Toronto's best alcohol-free bars, calling out a coconut cooler, a zero-proof "whiskey" sour and a non-alcoholic wine, while Destination Toronto, the city's official tourism board, separately praises its "outstanding list" of alcohol-free options.

The best-documented pour is the Hawaiian Honeycreeper, a zero-proof spin on the jungle bird built on Lumette LumRum — a 0% ABV distilled spirit standing in for the rum — shaken with a sparkling bitter "aperitivo," a splash of lime, roasted pineapple and honey. Toronto Life singled it out by name in a review of the menu, writing that it delivers "all the beachy bliss without the buzz (or the jet lag)." It's available daily during the "Honolulu Happy Hour" (3–6pm) alongside Lulu's broader alcohol-free cocktail, beer and wine list.
venues.pressQuote: The Hawaiian Honeycreeper is a spin on the jungle bird with alcohol-free rum and a zero-proof sparkling "aperitivo," delivering all the beachy bliss without the buzz (or the jet lag).

venues.name: Luma Restaurant
venues.neighborhood: Entertainment District (TIFF Bell Lightbox, King West)
venues.description: Luma Restaurant is a contemporary restaurant on the second floor of TIFF Bell Lightbox in Toronto's Entertainment District, part of the Oliver & Bonacini hospitality group. Alongside its full bar, it runs a genuine, named "Spirit-Free" menu of non-alcoholic cocktails and non-alcoholic beer, served during regular dining hours and spotlighted in the restaurant's "Magic Hour" happy hour. The spirit-free lineup runs to six drinks, from the herbal Rosemary Mist to the tropical, jalapeno-spiked Dante's Detox. Oliver & Bonacini's own editorial has singled out Luma's Magic Hour for its "glowing lineup of booze-free beverages."

venues.longDescription:
Luma occupies the second floor of TIFF Bell Lightbox in Reitman Square at 350 King St W, overlooking King Street West in Toronto's Entertainment District. Part of the Oliver & Bonacini restaurant group, the space pairs a dining room finished in rich woods, leather and stone with a lounge of plush sofas and eye-catching artwork, set behind floor-to-ceiling windows. Chef de Cuisine John Lynch, Michelin-trained with kitchen experience in the U.K., leads a globally inspired, locally sourced menu built on fresh fish and seafood, quality meats and seasonal vegetables.

The bar carries a genuine, named "Spirit-Free" section alongside its cocktail, wine and beer lists. Drinks include the Rosemary Mist (grapefruit and lemon juice, rosemary syrup, club soda, dehydrated lemon, $8), the LUMA-NADE (lemongrass, lavender syrup, lemon juice, q water, $6), Flower Power (hibiscus rose tea syrup, orange blossom water, lime juice, club soda, $10), Robin (blackberry syrup, lime juice, ginger beer, club soda, $11), The Great Gentleman Ginger Beer ($5) and Dante's Detox (jalapeno wheels, pineapple juice, lime juice, Old Thyme Jamaican ginger beer), plus three non-alcoholic beers.

The non-alcoholic drinks also anchor Luma's "Magic Hour" happy hour, which runs Tuesday to Saturday from 4-5:30pm and again from 8pm to close, alongside discounted cocktails ($7-$9), 16oz house beer ($6) and 5oz wine pours ($9). Oliver & Bonacini's own editorial has spotlighted the program directly, writing that Luma's Magic Hour "delivers a glowing lineup of booze-free beverages" - a rare instance of an O&B property naming its non-alcoholic offering in its own press.
venues.pressQuote: Offering one of the best happy hours in the city, Luma's Magic Hour delivers a glowing lineup of booze-free beverages.

venues.name: Lunarium
venues.description: Lunarium is a late-night tea and coffee lounge on North Monroe Street, opened in 2021 by Dorian Karahalios and Aimee Clark in a former boutique, and it does something almost nothing else in Spokane does: it keeps bar hours. The room runs from 3pm to midnight Wednesday through Saturday, serving slow-bar coffee, tea by the pot, house craft sodas, scratch-made baked goods and a dinner menu of toasts and grilled cheese, with a stage for live events. Its published drinks list carries no alcohol on it at all — which after the closures of Patera and The Wet Whistle makes it the most substantial late-evening room in the city for someone who is not drinking.
venues.address: 1925 N Monroe St Suite A, Spokane, WA 99205
venues.longDescription:
The problem with being a non-drinker in most cities is not the drinks, it is the hours. Cafés shut at three in the afternoon and bars open at four, so the part of the evening when everyone else is out is exactly the part with nowhere to go. Lunarium is Spokane's answer to that, and it is almost the only one left.

Dorian Karahalios and Aimee Clark opened it in 2021 in the former Atomic Threads Boutique on North Monroe Street, in the North Monroe District, and built it as a late-night lounge rather than a daytime café that stays open a bit longer. It runs 3pm to midnight from Wednesday to Saturday and 3pm to 9pm on Sunday. The offer is slow-bar coffee — including Vietnamese coffee — tea by the pot, house-made craft sodas and jam, scratch-baked pastries and cookies, and a real dinner menu built on gourmet grilled cheese, avocado toast and savoury scones. There is a stage for live events and a conference room, so the space is used for readings, music and work as much as for sitting.

The framing on its own site is a fair summary of the room: come read a book, write a book or sketch up a storm once the day is done. That is a description of a third place, and third places that operate at 10pm without a liquor licence are genuinely rare.

A note on how this entry is graded and worded. Lunarium does not describe itself as an alcohol-free venue, and this directory does not put that label on a business that has not claimed it. What is verifiable is that its published drinks list is entirely non-alcoholic — coffee, tea and craft sodas — and that it keeps evening hours no café in the city matches. After Patera Temperance Lounge closed, this is the closest Spokane has to a room where the whole menu works for a non-drinker.

Closed Monday and Tuesday.

One practical caution about the North Monroe District: it is a driving neighbourhood rather than a walking one, roughly two miles north of downtown along Monroe Street, so this is not a stop you fold into an evening on Main Avenue. Treat it as the destination. The reward is a room where nobody is drinking around you at eleven o'clock at night, which in Spokane is now close to unique, and where the kitchen is still sending out food when most of the city's cafes have been dark for eight hours.
venues.pressQuote: Come read a book, write a book or sketch up a storm once the day is done.

venues.name: Luna's Kava Root
venues.description: Luna's Kava Root is a fully alcohol-free kava bar on Gold Avenue in downtown Albuquerque that stays open until 2am seven nights a week — the detail that makes it useful, since it means someone not drinking has somewhere to be at the hour when the rest of downtown is at its loudest. It has been described as a sober bar with a buzz: tropical drinks, after-hours service and lounge seating in a cosy, modern room with steady music and deliberately low-key energy. The menu is organised the way a bar's is rather than a cafe's, running kava by the shell and by the growler, exotic teas served as tiki-style builds, on tap, as shots and as mocktails, hot and iced coffee, and a snack counter of grab-and-go items and desserts. Live music and events run through the week, and reviewers consistently single out staff who will explain kava to a first-timer rather than just pour it.
venues.address: 400 Gold Ave SW Ste 105, Albuquerque, NM 87102
venues.longDescription:
Luna's Kava Root occupies a suite on Gold Avenue in the middle of downtown Albuquerque, and the single most important thing about it is the closing time: 2am, every night of the week, with nothing alcoholic served at any point. Downtown bar districts are the hardest environment in any city for somebody who has stopped drinking, because the alternative to the bar is usually going home, and a room that keeps genuine late-night hours without a liquor licence is a rare and specific kind of useful. The space has been described as a sober bar with a buzz, and that framing is fair — cosy but modern, plenty of seating, music kept at a level people can talk over, and an atmosphere pitched deliberately away from the hectic energy of the venues around it. Live music and events run through the week.

The menu is built like a bar list rather than a cafe board. Kava comes by the shell or by the growler to take away. The exotic tea programme is the unusually deep part, split across tiki-style builds, teas on tap, tea shots and full mocktails, so a group can order four genuinely different things without anyone defaulting to a soda. Hot and iced coffee runs alongside, and a snack counter covers grab-and-go food and desserts for a long sitting. Reviewers return repeatedly to the same point — that the staff will walk a newcomer through what kava is, how it tastes and how much to start with — which is the behaviour that distinguishes a kava bar people come back to from one they try once. Kava is a psychoactive root drink from the South Pacific, prepared by steeping the ground root in water. It has no alcohol in it, but it is a genuine relaxant with an intoxicating quality of its own, which is worth being clear about if what you are avoiding is intoxication rather than alcohol specifically.

venues.name: Lutèce
venues.description: Lutece is a snug Michelin Guide-listed French neo-bistro at 1522 Wisconsin Avenue NW in Georgetown, opened in February 2020 in the former Cafe Bonaparte space. It is led by chef-partner Matt Conroy, a Food & Wine Best New Chef who earned a Michelin star at Brooklyn's Oxomoco, with pastry chef Isabel Coss, as part of The Popal Group. The non-alcoholic programme is one of the most developed in the city: bar manager Megan Coyle curates a roster of zero-proof cocktails available at the bar or with the tasting menu, plus a $55 Sans Alcool pairing built on non-alcoholic wines including Jorg Geiger Mirabellengold sparkling and Oddbird Blanc de Blancs Chardonnay. Named drinks include the Defanged Chupacabra and Indulgence in Moderation. Dinner only, seven nights.
venues.longDescription:
Lutece opened in February 2020 at 1522 Wisconsin Avenue NW, in the Georgetown space that used to hold Cafe Bonaparte, and it is small - a snug room built for a neighbourhood rather than an occasion, even though it has become an occasion restaurant. It is part of The Popal Group, the family business behind Lapis in Adams Morgan and Pascual on Capitol Hill, and it is led by chef-partner Matt Conroy, a Food & Wine Best New Chef who won a Michelin star at Oxomoco in Brooklyn, alongside pastry chef Isabel Coss. The cooking is modern seasonal French, poured against a natural-wine list, and the recognition has been broad: a place on the New York Times list of the most exciting restaurants in America, a top ranking in Washingtonian's 100 Very Best Restaurants, and a listing in the Michelin Guide. The Infatuation's Thomas Rose has written that it spins the rigid recipes and thousand-year-old techniques that define French cooking into a menu full of genuine surprises.

The reason it matters here is the depth of the non-alcoholic programme, which goes well past a couple of house sodas. Bar manager Megan Coyle curates a roster of zero-proof cocktails that can be ordered at the bar a la carte or taken through the tasting experience, and the restaurant offers a full Sans Alcool pairing at $55 - a genuine parallel to the wine pairing rather than a discount version of it. That pairing is built on serious non-alcoholic bottles: Jorg Geiger's Mirabellengold sparkling, made from mirabelle plums rather than dealcoholised wine, and Oddbird's Blanc de Blancs Chardonnay. Named zero-proof cocktails on the list have included the Defanged Chupacabra, built on agave syrup, grapefruit and picante spices, and Indulgence in Moderation, made with non-alcoholic vermouth, honey and almond.

Practical notes worth having. Lutece is dinner-only, from 5pm, seven nights a week, closing at 9pm Sunday to Thursday and 10pm on Friday and Saturday. The room is genuinely small, so reservations matter, and the bar is the place to sit if you want the zero-proof list a la carte rather than as a pairing. It sits on the upper Wisconsin Avenue stretch of Georgetown, a walk up from the waterfront.
venues.pressQuote: Lutèce spins the rigid recipes and thousand-year-old techniques that define French cooking into a menu full of genuine surprises

venues.longDescription:
Luxe Bar and Bistro is a casual bar and bistro at 1430 Central Ave in downtown Summerville, pouring craft beer, wine and cocktails alongside coffee and a bistro-style food menu of paninis, charcuterie boards and pub pretzels. It is a relaxed, family- and dog-friendly spot built around a large oak-shaded patio with cornhole, ping pong and regular live music.

Non-alcoholic drinks are a real menu category here rather than an afterthought: the drink list breaks out a dedicated "Mocktails" section of about a dozen named zero-proof drinks (Mock Mule, Con Cosmo, Mama Margarita, Non Island Iced Tea, Crimson Lemonade, Mo Mojito, Juice on the Beach and more), plus an expanded "Sunday Mocktails" list. Friday happy hour from 4-6 PM takes $1.50 off house liquor, wines, beers and mocktails, confirming mocktails as a standing, discounted category.

venues.name: Lyaness
venues.description: Lyaness is the South Bank flagship of Ryan Chetiyawardana, the bartender who trades as Mr Lyan and whom The Telegraph dubbed the world's most awarded bartender. It opened on 29 March 2019 inside Sea Containers London, taking over the Thames-side room that had housed his previous bar, Dandelyan — a venue he closed at its peak, months after it was crowned World's Best Bar at the 2018 World's 50 Best Bars. Lyaness earned the same standing of its own, named World's Best Cocktail Bar at the 2022 Spirited Awards, and remains a fixture on the global best-bars lists. The list is built around a handful of house "ingredients" reinvented each year. Five of its fifteen cocktails are offered in full alcohol-free versions made with the same technique as the originals, and the zero-proof Three Spirit Livener — grass amazake, gentian and pine — is a signature non-alcoholic serve.
venues.address: Sea Containers, 20 Upper Ground, London SE1 9PD
venues.longDescription:
Lyaness is the South Bank flagship of Ryan Chetiyawardana, the bartender who trades as Mr Lyan and whom The Telegraph dubbed "the world's most awarded bartender". It opened on 29 March 2019 inside Sea Containers London, taking over the Thames-side room that had housed his previous bar, Dandelyan — a venue he closed at its peak, months after it was crowned World's Best Bar at the 2018 World's 50 Best Bars. Lyaness went on to earn the same standing of its own, named World's Best Cocktail Bar at the 2022 Spirited Awards, and it remains a fixture on the global best-bars lists.

The room, designed by Jacu Strauss of Lore Design, trades Dandelyan's pinks for a palette of electric baby blue set against the site's existing green-marble bar, with picture windows framing the Thames and St Paul's across the water. The drinks list is deliberately unlike a standard cocktail menu: every drink is built around one of the bar's own house-made "core" ingredients — cryogenically produced vinegars, unusual ferments, cordials and tinctures drawn from everything from figs and parsnips to cornflakes — and the team will steer you by flavour rather than by spirit. The current list, Collaboration 2.0, runs to eleven new drinks alongside a set of revisited classics.

Crucially for non-drinkers, Lyaness rebuilds much of that same list without alcohol. Many of the signature cocktails are offered in a "boozeless" version, priced at £11, that keeps the drink's full flavour architecture and house-made ingredients while dropping the base spirit — so the zero-proof list is the real menu remade rather than a token afterthought. Confirmed boozeless builds include the Lobster Frappé, a creamy-yet-fresh drink centred on "immortal coconut" (coconut repeatedly reinfused into itself, then toasted and caramelised) with cucumber and a whisper of anise; the Pink Belly Gimlet, a savoury-leaning riff on carrot, honey and lemon; the Cherry Cannon Punch, built on straw-currant, pine and sakura tea with a lightly sparkling finish; and the Martini-style Lunar Tuxedo, which plays on raspberry. As the review site Hot Dinners put it, "if you're not on the sauce for whatever reason, then this is the bar for you".
venues.pressQuote: If you're not on the sauce for whatever reason, then this is the bar for you with many of the new cocktails coming in no-alcohol versions too, so you won't miss out on any of the fun.

venues.name: Lyla Lila
venues.description: Lyla Lila is a Southern European restaurant in Midtown Atlanta, on the ground floor of the Lilli Midtown tower. It opened December 6, 2019, from chef Craig Richards (formerly of St. Cecilia) and restaurateur Billy Streck; the name combines the founders' daughters' names. The kitchen turns out seasonal southern Italian and Spanish small plates, pasta, and seafood. For non-drinkers, the bar keeps a standing spirit-free cocktail list of roughly six rotating drinks (around $8–9) alongside the full bar. Current named zero-proof options include Cigarettes & Coffee (espresso, grapefruit, yuzu, tonic), Rings of Saturn (spiced oolong, orange, lime, pineapple, almond), and Tahitian Hut (grapefruit, lemon, vanilla, onda), plus Casamara Club builds. The restaurant has earned recognition in the MICHELIN Guide.

venues.longDescription:
Lyla Lila opened on 6 December 2019 on the ground floor of the Lilli Midtown tower at 693 Peachtree Street, from chef Craig Richards — previously of St. Cecilia — and restaurateur Billy Streck. The name is a combination of the founders' daughters' names. The kitchen cooks southern European: seasonal Italian and Spanish small plates, house pasta and seafood, with menus that change with what is available rather than on a fixed cycle. The restaurant is recognised in the MICHELIN Guide.

The bar keeps a standing spirit-free list of roughly six rotating drinks, priced around eight or nine dollars — and both halves of that sentence matter. A standing list means a non-drinker is reading from a menu rather than negotiating with a bartender, and the rotation means it gets the same seasonal attention as the food. The pricing is worth noting too: many restaurants charge cocktail prices for zero-proof drinks, and this one does not.

The drinks themselves are built on tea, bitterness and acid rather than on sweetness. Cigarettes & Coffee works espresso against grapefruit, yuzu and tonic. Rings of Saturn is spiced oolong with orange, lime, pineapple and almond. Tahitian Hut combines grapefruit, lemon and vanilla with Casamara Club Onda, an Italian-style amaro soda, and Casamara's low-sugar sodas appear across the list. Atlanta Magazine, covering the zero-proof scene in March 2022, singled out a Lyla Lila build of ginger, sherry vinegar, orange and lime oleo — sherry vinegar in a mocktail being a reasonable summary of the bar's whole approach.

Vinegar, over-steeped tea and tonic all do the job alcohol usually does: they add astringency and length, so the drink finishes dry instead of cloying. That is the difference between a zero-proof list a restaurant is proud of and one it tolerates. Open daily from 5pm.

venues.name: M.Bird
venues.description: M.Bird is a stylish rooftop bar and restaurant atop the Armature Works food hall in Tampa Heights, with skyline-and-river views over the Hillsborough. Its cocktail menu carries a dedicated "Mocktails" section of four named zero-proof drinks, led by the Seedlip-based Raging Bull (lemon, honey, watermelon, watermelon Red Bull), alongside Josie's Vacation, Berried Alive, and Like a Virgin — an easy spirit-free choice for a rooftop night.  Having four named builds printed on the menu matters at a busy rooftop bar: it means ordering from the same list as everyone else rather than negotiating with a bartender mid-rush. Armature Works is where a great many Tampa evenings start.

venues.longDescription:
M.Bird sits on the roof of Armature Works, the restored 1910 streetcar barn in Tampa Heights that now houses a food hall and event space on the bank of the Hillsborough River. The bar occupies the top floor with skyline and river views, which makes it one of the more in-demand rooftop rooms in the city and a default choice for a group looking for a view rather than a specific drink.

Rooftop bars are usually poor ground for non-drinkers. The economics favour volume, the menu leans on frozen and sweet, and the alcohol-free option is whatever the soda gun produces. M.Bird instead prints a "Mocktails" section with four named builds, led by the Raging Bull — Seedlip with lemon, honey, watermelon and watermelon Red Bull, which is exactly the sort of high-energy rooftop drink the room actually calls for rather than a polite botanical spritz. Josie's Vacation, Berried Alive and Like a Virgin fill out the list.

The useful thing here is context rather than craft. Armature Works is where a great many Tampa evenings begin, and a group heading to the roof will not be choosing the venue based on its zero-proof credentials. Having four named drinks on the printed menu means the person not drinking is ordering from the same list as everyone else instead of negotiating with a bartender during a rush — which, in a busy rooftop bar on a Saturday, is the difference between being served and being managed.

Practical notes: expect queues at peak, the rooftop is weather-dependent, and the food hall downstairs is the fallback if the lift line is long. It is a full bar with a substantial cocktail list; the mocktail section is a real part of the menu rather than the character of the venue.
venues.pressQuote: This deco-inspired rooftop restaurant offers unmatched panoramic views of the downtown skyline and Hillsborough River

venues.name: Machine Cocktail Bar
venues.description: Machine Cocktail Bar opened in May 2025 on West Institute Place in River North and treats every drink on its menu as a piece of stagecraft, with the zero-proof ones given exactly the same production values as the spirit-forward list. Breakfast in Bed is built on Seedlip Spice with French toast syrup, pineapple juice, lime juice and a splash of soda at $15; Judgement Free Zone combines watermelon, mango, passion fruit, habanero and lime juice at $13; and Pretty Peas - honeysuckle, sugar snap peas, lime juice and soda - arrives hanging inside a glass globe. The bar keeps late hours on Friday and Saturday, running to 2am, and Block Club Chicago made it a stop on its Dry January sober drink crawl.
