venues.longDescription:
Machine Cocktail Bar opened in May 2025 at 213 W Institute Place, a short block off Wells Street on the northern edge of River North, and built its reputation on presentation. Drinks arrive in custom vessels, under cages that have to be broken with a hammer, or with their own dispensers; the bar's own description of the Bee's Pajamas, for instance, has it landing with a honeycomb dispenser attached. That approach is applied without discrimination to the alcohol-free list, which is the reason the bar reads differently to most cocktail rooms with a token mocktail: a non-drinker at Machine gets the same theater as the table next to them.

The zero-proof menu runs to three drinks. Breakfast in Bed is the most substantial, a $15 build on Seedlip Spice with French toast syrup, pineapple juice, lime juice and a splash of soda that lands sweet and warm rather than thin. Judgement Free Zone, at $13, is fruit-driven and hot - watermelon, mango and passion fruit cut with habanero and lime juice. Pretty Peas is the one the press has fixed on: honeysuckle, sugar snap peas, lime juice and soda, delicate and floral, served hanging in a glass globe that Block Club Chicago compared to an air plant. Block Club named the bar as the third stop on its January 2026 sober drink crawl through Albany Park and River North, noting that the room makes a production of spirit-free and spirit-forward drinks alike. The bar is open Wednesday and Thursday until midnight and Friday and Saturday until 2am, and is closed Sunday through Tuesday. The bar posts its zero-proof drinks on its own channels alongside the full-proof ones rather than treating them as an afterthought, and Pretty Peas in particular has been used as the front of house image for the whole menu. For a directory like this one the useful signal is the ratio: three of the drinks on a seasonal menu are alcohol-free and each is given a distinct serve, which is a materially different proposition from a bar that will shake a citrus-and-soda on request.
venues.pressQuote: The three offerings on Machine’s zero-proof menu include Pretty Peas, made with honeysuckle, sugar snap peas, lime juice and soda.

venues.name: Mad Hatter Kava | Ahwatukee
venues.description: The Ahwatukee room is part of a four-site Arizona group that calls itself a 100% alcohol alternative bar, and it runs 8am to 11pm through the week and to midnight on Friday and Saturday, with bar counters, lounge seating and live music. The drinks are properly built and properly named — Queen of Hearts, Mercury, Kava Colada, The Hatter, Topsy Turvey, Kavachata and Roses Are Pink, plus non-alcoholic takes on a margarita and a piña colada. IMPORTANT for readers in recovery: the group's own description is a wide selection of kava, kratom and botanical blends. Kratom acts on opioid receptors and carries dependence and withdrawal risk that kava does not, so check what is in a given build before ordering.
venues.longDescription:
The Ahwatukee room on South 48th Street is one of four Arizona sites in the Mad Hatter group, alongside Gilbert, Chandler and Mesa, and the group describes itself without hedging as a 100% alcohol alternative bar aiming at a positive, uplifting environment. It runs 8am to 11pm from Sunday through Thursday and 8am to midnight on Friday and Saturday, and the rooms are fitted with proper bar counters and lounge seating, with live music programmed through the week.

What distinguishes Mad Hatter from most of the category is that the drinks are genuinely built and genuinely named. The list runs to Queen of Hearts, Mercury, Kava Colada, The Hatter, Topsy Turvey, Kavachata and Roses Are Pink, plus non-alcoholic versions of a margarita and a piña colada. That matters more than it might sound. A large part of what people miss when they stop drinking is not ethanol but the ritual of ordering something with a name, receiving it in a proper glass, and holding it — and a menu of numbered kava strengths does not deliver that in the way a drinks list does.

Kava itself is the ground root of Piper methysticum, a shrub native to the South Pacific islands, prepared as a cold water infusion and drunk socially across Fiji, Vanuatu, Tonga and Samoa for around three thousand years. It contains no alcohol. The taste is earthy and bitter and it numbs the lips and tongue on the first mouthful; the effect is mildly sedative and sociable rather than intoxicating in the way alcohol is. Kava also shows reverse tolerance, so regular drinkers usually need less rather than more, and a first visit is best paced across an hour or two rather than rushed.

Ahwatukee sits in the far south of Phoenix, cut off from the rest of the city by South Mountain, and its evening options are thin. A room here trading to midnight without a liquor licence is a genuine local amenity rather than a destination, which is the more useful thing for the people who live there.

One disclosure belongs in the open. The group's own description of its menu is a wide selection of kava, kratom and botanical blends, so kratom is served here alongside the kava. Kratom is the leaf of a Southeast Asian tree whose principal alkaloids act on the opioid receptors; regular use produces tolerance and a real withdrawal syndrome, several US states prohibit it outright, and its concentrated 7-hydroxymitragynine derivatives face active federal scheduling. Kava has no comparable dependence profile. Because the named house drinks do not always make their base obvious, the sensible move here is to ask which of the two a given build is made with before you order it.
venues.pressQuote: a Phoenix institution—and one of the most popular kava bars in Arizona, hands down

venues.name: Mad Hatter Kava Bar | Mesa
venues.description: The Mesa branch of Mad Hatter bills itself simply as an alcohol-free social lounge offering a night out without the hangover, and it keeps its own site and its own hours — 9am to 10pm through the week, 11pm on Friday and Saturday, 8pm on Sunday. The menu covers premium kava, botanical teas and handcrafted non-alcoholic drinks, with two house builds named on the front page: Topsy Turvey, made with passion fruit, vanilla and lime, and the KavaColoda, built on pineapple, coconut and lime. For the East Valley — Mesa, Tempe and Chandler — this is one of a very small number of rooms that are alcohol-free by design rather than by omission, and it is the only Mad Hatter site with an independent web presence.
venues.longDescription:
The Mesa branch of Mad Hatter is the only site in the group to keep its own website and its own identity, and the framing it uses there is the clearest in the category: an alcohol-free social lounge offering a night out without the hangover. It runs 9am to 10pm from Monday through Thursday, 9am to 11pm on Friday and Saturday, and 9am to 8pm on Sunday, from a unit on West Broadway Road.

The menu is described as premium kava, botanical teas and handcrafted non-alcoholic drinks, and two house builds are named with their components spelled out — Topsy Turvey, made with passion fruit, vanilla and lime, and the KavaColoda, built on pineapple, coconut and lime. Publishing the ingredients rather than just the names is a small thing that signals a room comfortable being asked what is in the glass.

Kava is the ground root of Piper methysticum, a shrub native to the South Pacific, prepared as a cold water infusion and drunk socially across Fiji, Vanuatu, Tonga and Samoa for roughly three thousand years. It contains no alcohol whatsoever. It tastes earthy and bitter and numbs the lips and tongue on the first mouthful; the effect is mildly sedative and sociable rather than intoxicating in the way alcohol is. Because kava exhibits reverse tolerance, regular drinkers typically need less rather than more to feel it, so a first visit is best taken slowly across an hour or two rather than treated like a round of shots.

The East Valley — Mesa, Tempe, Chandler and Gilbert — holds well over a million people and has very few rooms that are alcohol-free by design rather than by omission. Lighthouse Kava Bar in Tempe and this Mad Hatter site are effectively the anchors, with the group's own Gilbert and Chandler rooms extending the same format further out. For anyone in Mesa who has stopped drinking, this is the practical answer to an evening out, and its 11pm weekend close puts it in genuine nightlife territory rather than cafe hours.

One point of difference from its sibling rooms is worth recording accurately. The Ahwatukee site and the group's shared marketing describe a wide selection of kava, kratom and botanical blends, but the Mesa location's own website makes no mention of kratom at all and presents kava as the focus alongside botanical teas. That may reflect a genuinely different menu or simply a different web page, and this directory is not going to assert which. If you are avoiding kratom — a Southeast Asian leaf whose alkaloids act on the opioid receptors, carrying dependence and withdrawal risk that kava does not — treat this as a room where the question is worth asking at the counter rather than one where the answer is already published.

venues.name: Mad Hatters Ethnobotanical Tea Bar
venues.description: Mad Hatters is an Alice-in-Wonderland-themed kava and ethnobotanical tea bar in north St. Petersburg, open since 2014 as a sober place to gather late — it looks like a bar, but nothing is made with alcohol. The menu spans kava, kratom, loose-leaf herbal teas, nitro coffee, kombucha, and boba, with a hookah lounge on site. Open until 2–3am, it's one of the city's longest-running kava rooms. (It serves kratom alongside kava.)  Running to 3am from Thursday to Saturday, it competes with bars on their own hours rather than offering a daytime alternative to them. A hookah lounge on site means tobacco smoke is part of the environment.
venues.longDescription:
Mad Hatters has been open in north St. Petersburg since 2014, which makes it one of the longest-running kava rooms in a city that has more of them than anywhere else in the country. It is themed on Alice in Wonderland and commits to the conceit properly, and the effect is the important part: it looks like a bar, is laid out like a bar, and keeps bar hours — open until 2am most nights and 3am from Thursday to Saturday — while nothing in the building is made with alcohol.

That combination is rarer than it sounds and is the reason the venue matters. Most alcohol-free rooms close when cafes close, which leaves the hardest hours of the week uncovered: eleven at night on a Friday, when everyone else is still out. A room that runs to 3am is competing with bars on their own ground rather than offering a daytime alternative to them.

The menu is broad — kava, kratom, loose-leaf herbal teas, nitro coffee, kombucha and boba — with a hookah lounge on site, and the ethnobotanical framing is closer to a tea house than to a cocktail bar. Nobody here is pretending a drink is something it is not, which some people prefer to a mocktail shaped like a negroni.

The caveats need stating plainly and there are two. Mad Hatters serves kratom alongside kava: kava is psychoactive and sedating with documented liver-injury case reports, and kratom acts on opioid receptors with dependence and withdrawal risk. And the on-site hookah means tobacco smoke is part of the environment. Everything poured is alcohol-free. That is a narrower claim than substance-free, and anyone in recovery should weigh both points before going.  For a designated driver or anyone wanting somewhere genuinely open late without alcohol, it remains one of the most reliable rooms in the city.
venues.pressQuote: After two years, the liquor-slinging Loves are calling it quits on serving alcohol, whipping up a new brand of legal high, kava

venues.name: MadTree Brewing – Oakley Taproom
venues.description: MadTree Brewing's flagship Oakley taproom on Madison Road was one of Cincinnati's first craft breweries to brew its own non-alcoholic beer — the draft-only "Leave No Trace" pale ale, released in 2021. Today the brewery-restaurant keeps a genuine zero-proof lineup alongside its 30-plus taps: guest non-alcoholic beers including Lagunitas Hazy IPNA and Athletic Brewing's Upside Dawn Golden Ale, plus two house-made mocktails mixed to order — The Garden Variety and the Watermelon Limeade. It's a full kitchen with weekend brunch, a big patio and event spaces, so a non-drinker can settle in for a whole evening rather than nurse a soda. One honest caveat: the taproom also pours Floral's THC-infused beverages, so it's alcohol-free-friendly but not entirely substance-free.
signatureDrinks: Athletic Upside Dawn Golden Ale (NA beer)
venues.longDescription:
MadTree Brewing, founded in Cincinnati in 2013, runs its flagship brewery and restaurant at 3301 Madison Road in Oakley, just off Oakley Square and near Rookwood Commons. Built on a reputation for hop-forward IPAs and a rotating craft lineup poured across more than 30 taps, MadTree also folds sustainability into its brand — it donates 1% of sales to environmental nonprofits, the same "leave no trace" ethos that would later name its non-alcoholic beer.

In December 2021 MadTree became one of the region's first craft breweries to make its own alcohol-removed beer, releasing "Leave No Trace," a 0.5%-ABV dry-hopped pale ale, as a taproom-only draft. As MadTree told CityBeat when the beer launched, "It has to be appealing and taste good. If we are going to do this, we want to do this right." That release read more as a landmark experiment than a permanent fixture — it no longer appears on the regular menu — but the taproom kept a standing non-alcoholic program in its place. As of early 2025, CityBeat reported MadTree pours guest NA beers including Lagunitas Hazy IPNA and Athletic Brewing's Upside Dawn Golden Ale, and the bar mixes two house mocktails to order: The Garden Variety and the Watermelon Limeade. Earlier menus also featured house-made ginger ale, bottled craft root beer and an "Empty Threats" mocktail with blood-orange cordial, lime juice and non-alcoholic grapefruit bitters.

The Oakley taproom is open Monday–Thursday 11am–11pm, Friday 11am to midnight, Saturday 10am to midnight and Sunday 10am–11pm, with weekend brunch, a full food menu, a large patio and private event spaces, and is easy to reach from I-71. It makes a comfortable pick for a designated driver or a sober night out with a group. One caveat for the strictly alcohol-free crowd: alongside the mocktails and NA beers, the taproom also stocks Floral's THC-infused beverages, so ask the bartender if you want a zero-buzz drink — the house mocktails and the guest NA beers are your safe bets.
venues.pressQuote: MadTree may be best known for their IPAs, but the local brewery also offers plenty of non-alcoholic options as well, like the Hazy IPNA and Upside Dawn Golden.

venues.name: Mahina & Sun's
venues.description: Mahina & Sun's is the restaurant and bar of the Surfjack Hotel & Swim Club on Lewers Street in Waikīkī, run by Kānaka Maoli executive chef Erik Leong. It keeps four named non-alcoholic drinks on the list. Mr Brightside is built on a turmeric shrub with lemonade and fresh mint; Limonata is a creamy Brazilian limeade; Tropic Thunder pairs kalamansi with lilikoʻi; and The Pretender is a zero-proof reading of a penicillin, carrying the smoke of the original. That last one is the most technically ambitious non-alcoholic drink documented in Honolulu — smoke and peat are the hardest things to reproduce without whisky.

venues.longDescription:
Mahina & Sun's occupies the ground floor of the Surfjack Hotel & Swim Club at 412 Lewers Street, a block back from Kalākaua Avenue in Waikīkī. The Surfjack is a mid-century motel reworked as a design hotel, and the restaurant reflects that: open to the courtyard and the pool, live music several nights a week, and a kitchen led by executive chef Erik Leong, who is Kānaka Maoli and cooks Hawaiian-inspired food from island producers. Service runs a lunch and lanai menu with happy hour from noon to 5.30pm and dinner from 5.30pm to 10pm, and it takes walk-ins.

The non-alcoholic list is the most interesting in Waikīkī and one of the two or three best in the city. Four drinks sit on it, and each solves a different problem. Mr Brightside is built on a turmeric shrub — vinegar-based, earthy and bitter — cut with lemonade and fresh mint, which gives it the sharpness and the slightly medicinal edge that a zero-proof drink usually lacks entirely. Limonata is the simplest, a creamy Brazilian limeade, and works as the crowd-pleaser. Tropic Thunder pairs kalamansi, the small sour citrus used across the Philippines and increasingly grown in Hawaiʻi, with lilikoʻi, doubling down on acidity rather than sugar. The one worth going for is The Pretender, a non-alcoholic twist on a penicillin. The penicillin is a modern classic built on blended Scotch, honey, lemon and ginger with a peated Islay float, and its defining characteristic is smoke — which is precisely the hardest thing to reproduce without whisky, because smoke in a cocktail normally arrives dissolved in alcohol. Attempting it at all signals a bar taking the format seriously rather than sweetening juice, and it is the closest thing Honolulu has to the kind of zero-proof cocktail programme that cities on the mainland now take for granted. For a visitor staying in Waikīkī who wants one proper drink and does not want alcohol, this is the booking.

venues.name: Maison Selby
venues.neighborhood: St. James Town (bordering Cabbagetown / South Rosedale)
venues.description: Maison Selby is a French bistro, café and cocktail bar from Toronto's Oliver & Bonacini restaurant group, set inside the 136-year-old Gooderham mansion at Bloor and Sherbourne in St. James Town. Built in 1883 for one of Toronto's wealthiest families - the Gooderhams of Gooderham & Worts, the distillery that later became the Distillery District - the building now holds multiple dining rooms, a patio, and the basement Bar Sous Sol. The official menu carries a dedicated "Zero-proof Cocktails" section with five priced, non-alcoholic drinks, including a Raspberry Pepper Mojito and sangrias built on Grüvi sangria and alcohol-free Chardonnay.

venues.longDescription:
Maison Selby takes its name from the corner of Selby Street and Sherbourne Street, where the building it occupies has stood since 1883. It was built as a mansion for the Gooderham family - the Gooderhams of Gooderham & Worts, the distillery whose old works became Toronto's Distillery District - and has passed through several uses over its history before Oliver & Bonacini, the Toronto hospitality group behind Canoe and Auberge du Pommier, opened it in 2019 as Maison Selby: a French bistro, café and cocktail bar.

The restaurant occupies the historic mansion's rooms, including the private L'Orangerie dining room and a street-side patio. Service runs across lunch on weekdays, dinner nightly, weekend brunch, and daily takeout, with a basement bar, Bar Sous Sol, open Thursday through Saturday evenings for drinks.

The official menu lists a dedicated "Zero-proof Cocktails" section with five non-alcoholic drinks. The Fraîcheur d'Été mixes strawberry juice, lemon juice and cucumber ($10); the Pineapple Mule pairs pineapple and lime with Fever-Tree ginger beer ($10); and the Raspberry Pepper Mojito combines raspberry juice, raspberry pepper syrup, lime juice, mint and soda water ($10). Two sangrias round out the list: a Red Sangria made with Grüvi sangria, raspberry and hibiscus ($14), and a White Sangria built on JP. Chenet alcohol-free Chardonnay and white cranberry ($14).
venues.pressQuote: "Maison Selby (592 Sherbourne, at Selby...) has lived several lives in its 150-year existence, but as of this spring, it's a French restaurant from Oliver and Bonacini, the people behind Canoe, Auberge du Pommier and a host of other local hot spots. The building, known as the Gooderham mansion... has reflected the changing face of Bloor and Sherbourne throughout its history, starting its life as a mansion built in 1883 by one of the city's richest families: the Gooderhams, of Gooderham and Worts, the distillery that later became the Distillery District."

venues.name: Makana Kava Bar & Hawaiian Kitchen
venues.description: Makana Kava Bar & Hawaiian Kitchen opened in North Miami in 2024 and is a rarer thing than it sounds: a kava bar with a real kitchen behind it. Nothing alcoholic is served — the house line is premium kava, botanical mocktails and daily good vibes, with no alcohol. The food is Hawaiian and substantial, running chicken katsu tenders, loco moco fries, huli huli sliders, poke bowls and empanadas, which makes this one of the few venues in the category where a group can eat a full meal rather than drink around a bag of chips. Doors open at noon and it runs to 2am every night of the week. Kava is a South Pacific root drink prepared by steeping the ground root in water: it contains no alcohol, but it is genuinely relaxing and mildly intoxicating in its own right, a distinction worth understanding if you are avoiding intoxicants rather than avoiding alcohol.

venues.longDescription:
Makana Kava Bar & Hawaiian Kitchen opened in North Miami in 2024, and the second half of its name is what makes it worth a specific trip. Most kava bars are drinks-only rooms where the food, if it exists, is a basket of chips and a couple of empanadas — which quietly limits how long a group can stay and how easily a kava bar substitutes for a night at a restaurant bar. Makana runs an actual Hawaiian kitchen: chicken katsu tenders, loco moco fries, huli huli sliders, poke bowls and empanadas, served alongside the drinks rather than as an afterthought to them. Combined with hours that run from noon to 2am seven nights a week, that turns the room into somewhere you can arrive hungry at nine and still be there at one, which is precisely the pattern that a licensed bar normally owns.

The drinks are premium kava and botanical mocktails, and the house framing is refreshingly plain — premium kava, botanical mocktails, daily good vibes, and no alcohol. Miami already has one of the densest kava scenes in the United States, and the competition for a new room here is genuinely stiff, so pairing the kava with a kitchen is a sensible way to be distinct rather than merely additional. For anyone in recovery reading this, the honest description of the anchor drink: kava is made from the ground root of a South Pacific shrub, steeped in water and strained, and has been drunk socially across the Pacific for roughly three thousand years. It contains no alcohol at all, and it is not a stimulant. It is, however, a genuine relaxant with an intoxicating quality of its own, and it is served to adults. If what you are avoiding is alcohol specifically, kava is a straightforward substitute; if what you are avoiding is intoxication in general, it is worth knowing what you are ordering before you order it.

venues.name: Mana
venues.description: Mana is Simon Martin's one-Michelin-star restaurant in Ancoats — the chef, a Noma alumnus, brought Manchester its first star in over 40 years and retained it in the 2026 Michelin Guide. The 30-cover room looks onto an open kitchen where fermentation and fire drive a hyper-seasonal tasting menu. For non-drinkers there is a full non-alcoholic drinks pairing served course-by-course alongside the wine flight — paid for and pre-booked when you reserve — backed by a genuinely deep alcohol-free list of house ferments, juices and six or seven zero-proof cocktails. It is one of the most serious non-alcoholic pairings in the city.

signatureDrinks: Non-alcoholic drinks pairing (paid; pre-book at booking)
Six to seven non-alcoholic cocktails on the drinks list
venues.longDescription:
Mana opened in Ancoats in 2018 and, in 2019, won Manchester its first Michelin star in more than four decades — a landmark for a city whose fine-dining scene had long been overlooked. It is the project of chef-patron Simon Martin, whose reputation is inextricably linked to his time working closely with René Redzepi at Noma in Copenhagen, including the restaurant's Mexico pop-up. Martin has held the star every year since, retaining it in the 2026 Michelin Guide, where Mana remained one of only a handful of starred restaurants in the region. The name is set in lower case, but the ambition is anything but modest.

The restaurant occupies Sawmill Court on Blossom Street, a soaring, pared-back room of neutral tones and statement lighting — reviewers have singled out its cruciform, almost ceremonial light fittings. It seats just 30, with well-spaced tables arranged so that every seat looks onto the open kitchen. Fermentation and fire are the twin pillars of the cooking: a hyper-seasonal tasting menu that shifts roughly with the seasons, leaning on British produce, plenty of seafood and Asian technique, with obsessive kitchen craft (one juice is famously reduced from 400 litres down to a single concentrated litre). Recent menus have run from a reduced lunch around £70 per head to a condensed dinner near £110 and a full "complete" menu around £175, with a sommelier-led wine flight alongside.

Crucially for non-drinkers, Mana treats the alcohol-free option as a proper pairing rather than an afterthought. A dedicated non-alcoholic drinks flight runs course-by-course beside the wine flight, but it must be selected and paid for when you book — pre-booking is required, so it cannot be added on the night. The programme reflects the kitchen's Noma-rooted fermentation focus: house-made kombuchas, cordials, cold-pressed juices and infusions built to match the food, with reviewers noting serves such as a thick, almost soup-like whisked green tea among the paired drinks. Beyond the flight, the standing drinks list carries a still-generous alcohol-free selection, including six or seven non-alcoholic cocktails, so even walk-up glasses are given real thought.
venues.pressQuote: Fermentation and fire are the pillars of the preparation at Mana, with a menu constantly shifting with the seasons.

venues.name: Mango Mango Dessert
venues.description: Mango Mango Dessert on Cherry Street keeps the most consistent late hours of any alcohol-free room in Chinatown: noon until eleven at night, seven days a week, with no shorter weeknight schedule. The house style is Hong Kong dessert-shop cooking, where the drinks and the desserts are the same thing — the Special Mango Juice with sago and pomelo topped with mango ice cream is the signature, and there are coconut and strawberry versions of the same build. The more adventurous end runs to coconut juice with durian and black rice, and a lychee jasmine rose drink. Sago and pomelo are the traditional Cantonese pairing, and the pomelo's slight bitterness is what keeps these from being merely sweet.
signatureDrinks: Special Mango Juice Sago & Pomelo with Mango Ice Cream
Strawberry Mango Juice Sago & Lychee Jelly
Coconut Juice with Durian and Black Rice
Snow White Mango Juice with Red Beans
venues.longDescription:
Mango Mango Dessert trades on Cherry Street in Chinatown and keeps the steadiest late hours of anything alcohol-free in the neighbourhood: midday to eleven at night, every day of the week, with no weeknight reduction. That consistency is worth more than a later closing time that only applies on Saturdays, because it means the place is a reliable answer on a Tuesday.

The format is the Hong Kong dessert house, in which the line between a drink and a pudding is deliberately not drawn. The signature is the mango juice with sago and pomelo, topped with mango ice cream. Every element of that is doing a job: sago are small tapioca pearls that give the drink body, pomelo is the large citrus whose flesh separates into firm juice-filled threads, and its faint bitterness is exactly what stops the mango from being cloying. This combination — mango, sago, pomelo — is a Cantonese classic dating to the 1980s, and the version here is the standard one done properly. Coconut and strawberry variants follow the same structure, the strawberry swapping in lychee jelly.

The more interesting orders sit further down. Coconut juice with durian and black rice is the one that divides a table; durian's savoury, sulphurous depth against sweet coconut and nutty black glutinous rice is a genuinely complex thing to drink, and it is not a beginner's order. The lychee jasmine rose drink is the opposite, floral and light. Snow White mango juice with red beans splits the difference.

For an evening without alcohol, a dessert house at ten at night does something a bar cannot. The order takes time, it arrives as a spectacle, and it gives a group a shared reason to still be sitting there. That is the same social function a round of drinks performs, achieved by other means, which is the whole argument of this directory in miniature.

On alcohol, there is none on the menu and no licence — recorded as evidence rather than as a venue statement. Nothing psychoactive is served beyond tea and coffee.

venues.name: Manhattan
venues.description: Manhattan is the grand hotel cocktail bar on Level 2 of the Conrad Singapore Orchard (the former Regent Singapore), a former World's Best Bar in Asia that runs a genuine printed zero-proof section called 'Off Broadway' — four non-alcoholic creations, one for each chapter of its 'Seasons of Manhattan' menu. Head bartender Zana Mohlmann builds the Autumn Groove Fizz by dosing tonic with a lemon-mushroom oleo saccharum, and the Blooming Daisy on Lyre's non-alcoholic agave spirit with bee pollen and rose lychee milk tea. The same house-craft techniques behind the bar's barrel-aged cocktails carry into the zero-proof drinks, so alcohol-free guests get a genuine seat in one of Asia's most decorated rooms.
venues.address: Conrad Singapore Orchard, 1 Cuscaden Road, Level 2, Singapore 249715
signatureDrinks: Autumn Groove Fizz — tonic dosed with lemon-mushroom oleo saccharum (non-alcoholic)
Blooming Daisy — Lyre's non-alcoholic agave spirit, bee pollen, rose lychee milk tea (non-alcoholic)
venues.longDescription:
Manhattan opened as an homage to New York's golden age of cocktails and quickly became one of the region's most awarded bars, ranking No. 33 on The World's 50 Best Bars in 2022, No. 21 on Asia's 50 Best Bars in 2023, and taking the title of Best Bar in Asia. It sits on the second floor of the Conrad Singapore Orchard — the 1980s Cuscaden Road landmark that operated as Regent Singapore until it was rebranded under Hilton's Conrad flag in 2023 — with olive-leather banquettes, a raised marble bar, and the world's first in-hotel rickhouse where barrel-aged Manhattans and solera-aged Negronis rest in oak.

The non-alcoholic program lives in a dedicated menu section titled 'Off Broadway,' offering four zero-proof tipples so teetotal guests can also enjoy the show. For the current 'Seasons of Manhattan' menu — a desk-calendar of 31 cocktails spanning Spring, Summer, Autumn and Winter in New York City — each seasonal chapter carries its own alcohol-free creation inspired by the pillars of that chapter.

Bon Appetit singled out two of head bartender Zana Mohlmann's builds: the Autumn Groove Fizz, which doses tonic with a lemon-mushroom oleo saccharum, and the Blooming Daisy, which echoes spring's first blossoms with Lyre's non-alcoholic agave spirit, bee pollen and rose lychee milk tea. The drinks apply the same oleo, ferment and house-syrup techniques that define the alcoholic list, rather than treating no-proof as an afterthought.

Manhattan trades in the evenings Monday through Saturday and all day Sunday, and remains fully open as of 2025–2026 following the hotel's rebrand and the May 2025 launch of the Seasons of Manhattan menu.
venues.pressQuote: From the Seasons of Manhattan menu, head bartender Zana Mohlmann doses tonic with lemon-mushroom oleo saccharum in the Autumn Groove Fizz and echoes spring's first blossoms with Lyre's non-alc agave spirit, bee pollen, and rose lychee milk tea in the Blooming Daisy.

venues.name: Maple & Ash
venues.description: The Scottsdale outpost of the Chicago steakhouse, sitting on Camelback Road with a bar and lounge that runs a daily Tower Hour from 4pm. Its non-alcoholic drinks are built from real alcohol-free spirits rather than juice — the Lavender & Luxury pairs CleanCo non-alcoholic gin with lychee, honey and a foam, and the Like a Virgin is a spiced take on a margarita. DiningOut Phoenix named it among the metro bars worth going to for a mocktail in May 2026. A steakhouse rather than a bar, so expect to be eating; the zero-proof drinks sit alongside a large wine and spirits programme.
venues.longDescription:
Maple & Ash arrived in Scottsdale from Chicago as a wood-fired steakhouse with a bar programme large enough to stand on its own, taking a corner of the Camelback Corridor shopping district. The kitchen cooks over live fire and the dining room leans loud, dark and expensive — closer to a night out than a dinner reservation. The bar and lounge run a daily Tower Hour from 4pm to 6pm, which is the practical way into the room without committing to a full steakhouse bill, and Sunday adds a brunch service from 10:30am.

The non-alcoholic drinks are made the way the rest of the bar works: from real alcohol-free spirits rather than fruit juice. The Lavender & Luxury is built on CleanCo non-alcoholic gin with lychee, honey and a foam — a drink with actual texture, which is what usually separates a considered zero-proof list from a sweet one. The Like a Virgin is a spiced, margarita-shaped build. DiningOut Phoenix listed the venue in its May 2026 round-up of metro bars worth visiting specifically for a mocktail.

One point of accuracy belongs on the record. That article describes the zero-proof drinks as sitting under a menu section called "No F@cking Alcohol Please", which would be entirely consistent with the restaurant's house voice — its chef's tasting menu is called "I Don't Give a F*@k" — but the section name does not appear anywhere on the restaurant's own website. It is therefore not stated here as fact. What is verifiable is that the drinks exist, that they are built on a named non-alcoholic spirit, and that a third-party guide singled them out. Two practical notes: this is a steakhouse with a strong bar rather than an alcohol-free venue, and the format assumes a table and a substantial spend, so it is a poor fit for a quick drink and a good one for an occasion where you happen not to be drinking.
venues.pressQuote: The extensive cocktail menu has a dedicated section for sober guests

venues.name: Maple House
venues.description: An all-day cafe and bar in downtown Chandler, in the southeast of the Phoenix metro, built so that the alcohol-free options are the point rather than an afterthought. Maple House pours espresso and coffee from 7am and moves into a full slate of zero-proof cocktails — including a Seedlip-based Nojito — as the evening comes on, in a comfortable, living-room-style room that stays open to 11pm on Friday and Saturday. Phoenix New Times named it Best Non-Alcoholic Drink Options in its 2024 Best of Phoenix awards, which for a suburban cafe competing against downtown cocktail bars is a genuine result.

venues.longDescription:
Maple House occupies a corner of downtown Chandler and solves a problem most of the Phoenix metro does not: where to go in the evening, socially, without the evening being organised around alcohol. It opens at 7am as a coffee house — espresso, filter, the usual pastry case — and rather than closing when the cafes close, it carries on into the night with a full zero-proof cocktail list, running to 9pm most nights and 11pm on Friday and Saturday. The room is deliberately domestic: soft seating, low tables, the feel of a large living room rather than a bar.

That all-day structure is the whole proposition. A cafe that shuts at four leaves non-drinkers with nowhere to go at eight; a bar that opens at eight offers them a soda. Maple House covers the entire span with the same quality of drink, which is why it functions as a genuine alternative rather than a compromise. The cocktail side is built on real non-alcoholic spirits — the Nojito is a Seedlip build — and sits on the menu as the main event rather than in a corner of it.

Phoenix New Times gave it Best Non-Alcoholic Drink Options in the 2024 Best of Phoenix awards. That is worth pausing on: the category was won not by one of the downtown cocktail rooms with a James Beard nomination but by a suburban cafe twenty-five miles southeast, which says something about how seriously the place takes it. The location is the main caveat — Chandler is a drive from central Phoenix, and this is a neighbourhood venue rather than a destination for visitors staying downtown. The light-rail line does not reach Chandler, so plan on driving or a rideshare — which, given the entire premise of the place, at least nobody at your table will mind doing.
venues.pressQuote: that bar experience without everything that comes with it
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Maple House operations director, to Phoenix New Times

venues.name: Mar | Muntanya
venues.description: A 6th-floor rooftop Northern Spanish restaurant atop the downtown Hyatt Regency, serving Basque- and Catalan-inspired tapas, wild game and a suckling-pig experience under executive chef Tyson Peterson, with sweeping skyline and Wasatch Mountain views. The name pairs "mar" (sea) and "muntanya" (mountain). Opened in October 2022, it leans into Spain's gin-and-tonic culture with four specialty G&Ts, and keeps non-drinkers in mind during cocktail hour with a non-alcoholic sangria and a rotating $8 mocktail.

venues.longDescription:
Mar | Muntanya debuted in October 2022 as the rooftop dining centerpiece of the Hyatt Regency Salt Lake City, on West Temple near the convention center and Salt Palace. Executive chef Tyson Peterson — known in Utah for Spanish-themed concepts — builds the menu around the Basque and Catalan regions, from campfire elk loin to shareable tapas.

The beverage program centers on Spanish gin-and-tonic service with house-made tonics, and its cocktail-hour menu (Wed–Sat, 2:30–5pm) keeps non-drinkers in mind: an $8 non-alcoholic sangria built on cranberry, citrus and seasonal fruit sits alongside the wine-based sangrias, plus a rotating $8 mocktail.
venues.pressQuote: A classic gin and tonic are one of the signatures of Spain, and so Mar | Muntanya went all out with a list of four specialty G&Ts.

venues.name: Marcelino's Boutique Bar
venues.description: Marcelino's is a Mediterranean cocktail bar in downtown Providence with one of the deepest non-alcoholic lists in Rhode Island — a full mocktail section built almost entirely on the Lyre's range rather than on juice. The bar makes its own infusions, syrups and dehydrated garnishes from scratch, and the same kitchen work goes into the alcohol-free drinks as the rest of the menu. Sister rooms operate in Boston and the Seaport.

venues.longDescription:
Marcelino's Boutique Bar sits on West Exchange Street in downtown Providence, part of a small Mediterranean group with rooms in Boston and the Seaport. It is a craft cocktail bar first — the bartenders make their own infused spirits, house syrups and dehydrated citrus and fruit garnishes rather than buying them in — and the reason it belongs on this list is that the non-alcoholic drinks are made inside that same process rather than beside it.

The mocktail section is unusually deep for a Rhode Island bar, and unusually consistent in its approach: it is built almost entirely on the Lyre's range of non-alcoholic spirits rather than on fruit juice. That matters because Lyre's products are engineered to carry the bitterness, heat and aromatic length that a spirit provides, so the resulting drinks have structure rather than just flavour. The list runs across the categories — a rum-style build with mint, lime and ginger beer; a gin-style one with strawberry, berry tea, milk and citrus; a bittersweet aperitif build combining a rosso aperitif with an Italian bitter, ginger and tonic; and a coffee build using a non-alcoholic dark cane and coffee liqueur with fresh espresso. There is also a batched non-alcoholic negroni infused with strawberries, dried citrus and thyme, which is the sort of thing that only exists where somebody has decided the alcohol-free list deserves prep time.

We have not published the individual drink names and prices here, and that is deliberate. Marcelino's publishes its menus only as PDFs that do not render as text, so while the shape and ingredients of the programme are well documented across Rhode Island coverage, we could not confirm the current list against the bar's own live menu. The programme is real; the specific names may have moved. Ask at the bar, and note the group runs separate menus in Boston and the Seaport, so a list you have seen elsewhere may not be the Providence one.
venues.pressQuote: the latest craft cocktail bar to open in Providence

venues.name: Marcella's
venues.description: Marcella's is Cameron Mitchell Restaurants' Italian dining room on North High Street in the Short North, across the street from The Guild House and Soul at The Joseph, and it prints its zero-proof drinks on the same beverage list as the cocktails. There are two built non-alcoholic cocktails: Strawberry Fields, made with Seedlip Citrus, strawberry and a lemon foam, and a Citrus Spritz of Lyre's Italian Orange lengthened with alcohol-removed sparkling wine — an alcohol-free reading of the Aperol spritz that is otherwise unavoidable on an Italian menu. A rotating Athletic Brewing non-alcoholic beer sits alongside them. The coffee list is genuinely part of the drinks offering rather than an afterthought, including Il Finto Espresso with vanilla and honey and an affogato of vanilla gelato drowned in hot espresso.

venues.longDescription:
Marcella's sits at 615 North High Street in the Short North, one of two Columbus locations for the Cameron Mitchell Italian concept — the other is on Polaris Parkway to the north. The Short North room runs dinner daily from 4pm with a happy hour in the bar and cocktail lounge on weekday evenings, and works a broad Italian menu of pizza, pasta and small plates aimed at groups rather than at a tasting-menu occasion. Its position matters for anyone planning an alcohol-free evening: it is directly across High Street from The Guild House and Soul at The Joseph, which means three restaurants with printed zero-proof sections stand within about a hundred metres of each other, the densest such cluster in the city.

The zero-proof drinks are printed on the same beverage list as the cocktails, wine and beer. There are two built cocktails. Strawberry Fields uses Seedlip Citrus as its base with strawberry and a lemon foam, the foam doing the work that egg white or aquafaba does in a full-proof sour by giving the drink texture rather than only flavour. The Citrus Spritz is the more useful of the two on an Italian list: Lyre's Italian Orange, the zero-proof amaro-style aperitif, lengthened with alcohol-removed sparkling wine, which lets a non-drinking guest order the spritz that everyone else at the table is drinking rather than something structurally different. A rotating Athletic Brewing non-alcoholic beer covers the beer side. Beyond the cocktails, the coffee list is unusually developed and functions as a genuine after-dinner option — Il Finto Espresso built with vanilla and honey, a caffè caramello layered with sweet cream and whipped cream, and an affogato of vanilla gelato drowned in hot espresso. Because it is a large room built for groups rather than a tasting-menu restaurant, it is also the most practical of the three Short North zero-proof lists for a party of mixed preferences — the sort of booking where one person is not drinking, one is driving, and nobody wants that to shape where everyone else eats. Note that the Polaris Parkway location north of the city runs its own menus, and the drinks listed here are the Short North list.

venues.name: Marcy's
venues.description: Marcy's is a modern seafood bistro on Duxton Road with an intimate bar counter that stays open late. Alongside craft spirits and cocktails, the bar pours a small run of made-to-order mocktails, singled out by Honeycombers as booze-free ways to close a meal: a virgin mojito, a virgin Pimm's, and the fruity house Island in the Sun. It is a genuine, if compact, non-alcoholic option rather than a full zero-proof menu.
signatureDrinks: Island in the Sun (a fruity non-alcoholic drink)
venues.longDescription:
Marcy's opened at 39-40 Duxton Road in early 2021 as a modern seafood bistro, tucking an intimate bar counter against an eclectic Victorian-style interior with an edgy, low-lit dining room beyond. The kitchen takes familiar seafood ideas and reworks them, drawing on Latin American and Coastal Italian cooking with techniques borrowed from Peruvian, Japanese, Mexican, Chinese and Italian traditions, on a menu that shifts with the seasons.

The bar is the venue's late-night heart, open past the kitchen with craft spirits, cocktails and atypical small plates. For non-drinkers, the team mixes a short set of mocktails to order: a virgin mojito, a virgin Pimm's, and Island in the Sun, a fruity house build that Honeycombers recommends as a way to end the meal. There is no printed zero-proof list, so the offering is best understood as a few real NA builds from a capable bar rather than a dedicated program.

Marcy's has drawn steady coverage from Singapore food media since opening and continues to trade at Duxton Road into 2026, with recent reviews and guides confirming it remains open. No Michelin or Asia's 50 Best accolade is on record for the venue.
venues.pressQuote: This seafood bistro has our hearts with its fresh and indulgent plates.

venues.name: Marguerite
venues.description: Marguerite is a one-Michelin-star restaurant set inside the Flower Dome conservatory at Gardens by the Bay, led by chef-owner Michael Wilson. Its temperance beverage pairing (around S$88) is a genuine, dish-by-dish non-alcoholic flight built to mirror wine rather than a list of mocktails: clarified juices and house-fermented jun teas. Standouts include a gala apple and verjuice juice aged on oak chips to echo a lighter chardonnay, and a jackfruit jun tea fermented from green tea and honey. Every pour is house-made, with no commercial zero-proof brands.

Jackfruit jun tea — green tea and honey fermented for two weeks, then infused with fresh jackfruit slices (paired with New Caledonian prawn tagliolini)
venues.longDescription:
Marguerite occupies a glass-walled dining room within the Flower Dome conservatory at Gardens by the Bay (unit 01-09), an unusual fine-dining setting ringed by the cooled flower gardens. It is helmed by chef-owner Michael Wilson and has held one Michelin star in the MICHELIN Guide Singapore from 2022 through 2025.

The non-alcoholic offering is a full 'temperance' beverage pairing, priced around S$88, conceived as the zero-proof counterpart to the wine pairing rather than an afterthought. Wilson develops each pour by first studying the flavour profile of the wine that would traditionally match a dish, then finding a fruit to echo it. As he puts it: 'We research the predominant flavour profiles of a wine that we think would pair well with a particular dish and find a corresponding fruit that would match before developing a temperance beverage around this.'

The drinks lean on clarified juices and house-fermented jun teas. A gala apple and verjuice juice is clarified and infused with oak chips so it drinks like a lighter chardonnay alongside a fish course, while a jackfruit jun tea — green tea and honey fermented for two weeks, then steeped with fresh jackfruit slices for another week — brings a robust, effervescent profile to a New Caledonian prawn tagliolini. The programme is entirely house-made, with no reliance on off-the-shelf non-alcoholic labels.
venues.pressQuote: We research the predominant flavour profiles of a wine that we think would pair well with a particular dish and find a corresponding fruit that would match before developing a temperance beverage around this.

venues.name: The Marigold Club
venues.description: The Marigold Club is a Goodnight Hospitality room in Montrose, listed in the Michelin Guide, styled after a British members' club and serving a menu that runs from martinis to a full dinner service. Its alcohol-free drinks are built on Seedlip: the Secret Garden pairs Seedlip Garden 108 — the herbaceous pea-and-hay expression — with an olive, making a genuinely savoury drink rather than a sweet one, and the Chelsea Bloom runs Seedlip Grove 42's citrus character against cranberry and lime. Houston Press named both in its January 2026 zero-proof guide. A savoury alcohol-free option is unusual and worth seeking out, because the martini-adjacent register is the hardest one for a non-drinker to find anywhere.
signatureDrinks: Chelsea Bloom — Seedlip Grove 42, cranberry, lime

venues.longDescription:
The Marigold Club sits on Kuester Street in Montrose, part of the Goodnight Hospitality group, and it is listed in the Michelin Guide. The conceit is a British members' club — dark rooms, a martini programme, a proper dinner menu — and it is played straight rather than as pastiche.

The alcohol-free drinks are built on Seedlip, and the more interesting of the two is the Secret Garden, which is essentially Seedlip Garden 108 served with an olive. Garden 108 is the herbaceous expression of the range, built on pea, hay, spearmint, rosemary and thyme, and it is deliberately vegetal rather than sweet. Put an olive in it and what you have is a savoury drink in a stemmed glass — a martini's structural cousin, brine and botanicals and nothing sugary anywhere near it. That is a genuinely rare thing. The overwhelming majority of non-alcoholic drinks anywhere are built on fruit and sugar, which means the person who orders a dry martini has almost nowhere to go when they stop drinking. This is one of the few answers to that in Houston.

The Chelsea Bloom is the more conventional counterpart, using Seedlip Grove 42 — the citrus expression, built on blood orange, ginger and lemongrass — against cranberry and lime. It is tart rather than sweet, and it does the job the club soda-and-lime would otherwise do, but with a bitter, aromatic backbone.

Houston Press named both drinks in its Dry January 2026 guide. Seedlip sits at the premium end of the non-alcoholic spirits market in this city, and the bars that reach for it — this one, and a handful of others — are generally the ones taking the category most seriously.

On timing: the club is closed Mondays, opens for dinner only from Tuesday to Thursday, and adds a late-morning to mid-afternoon service on Friday, Saturday and Sunday, running to eleven at the weekend. It is a booking rather than a walk-in, and it is the sort of room where an evening is built around sitting at a table for three hours — which is, on the whole, the format that works best when you are not drinking.

venues.name: Marigold
venues.description: Marigold is Minnesota's first dedicated non-alcoholic bottle shop, opened by hair stylist and Honeycomb Salon owner Erin Flavin in late 2022 on Nicollet Avenue in the Kingfield neighborhood of South Minneapolis. Born out of Flavin's own 2020 sobriety journey and conversations with salon clients, the shop is entirely alcohol-free, stocking NA spirits and aperitifs, de-alcoholized wine and sparkling teas, NA beer, bitters, mixers, ready-to-drink cocktails, adaptogenic and functional beverages, plus a THC/CBD section. The curated shelves carry brands including Three Spirit, Ghia, Kin Euphorics, Aplos, and Untitled Art N/A, alongside local THC and CBD producers. As of 2026 it is the Twin Cities' last standing NA bottle shop after the closure of its St. Paul outpost and a Northeast Minneapolis competitor — a status that makes it both a community anchor and, by the owner's own account, a week-by-week labor of love.
