venues.longDescription:
Marigold was Minnesota's first dedicated non-alcoholic bottle shop, opened in late 2022 on Nicollet Avenue in the Kingfield neighbourhood of South Minneapolis by Erin Flavin, a hair stylist and the owner of Honeycomb Salon. The origin is unusually specific: Flavin got sober in 2020, and the idea grew out of the conversations she was having in her salon chair — which is, if you think about it, one of the few remaining settings where people talk honestly about their drinking to someone who is not a doctor. The shop is entirely alcohol-free, and the range is broad enough to serve both a curious first-timer and somebody restocking: non-alcoholic spirits and aperitifs, dealcoholized wine and sparkling teas, NA beer, bitters and mixers, ready-to-drink cocktails, adaptogenic and functional drinks, plus a THC and CBD section. Three Spirit, Ghia, Kin Euphorics, Aplos and Untitled Art N/A sit on the shelves alongside local THC and CBD producers.

What makes the shop worth writing about at length in 2026 is its position. It is now the last standing non-alcoholic bottle shop in the Twin Cities, after its own St. Paul outpost closed and a Northeast Minneapolis competitor did too — and by Flavin's own account the business is a week-by-week labour of love rather than a comfortable one. That is a useful corrective to the market-size reports about this category booming: the drinks sell, but a shop selling only them, in a cold-weather city, is a hard business. It is also the reason the place functions as a community anchor rather than just a retailer. Flavin's framing of who the shop is for is the best articulation of the inclusive position anyone in this category has offered: "That's what's so nice about this place: It's for everybody. I don't want anybody to feel like they can't come in here because they still drink." That sentence is why the shop works, and it is worth quoting to anyone who assumes non-alcoholic retail is only for people in recovery. Open seven days, later on Thursday through Saturday.
venues.pressQuote: That's what's so nice about this place: It's for everybody. I don't want anybody to feel like they can't come in here because they still drink.

venues.name: Marion
venues.description: Marion is Andrew McConnell's celebrated Gertrude Street wine bar, sitting alongside his two-hat Cutler & Co in the heart of Fitzroy. Serious as its wine list is, the bar keeps a genuine low-and-no section for anyone off the vinos: an Italian Orange Spritz built on verjus and tonic, a Spritz Veneziano, and a sparkling salted raspberry-and-cranberry drink. Verjus runs through the kitchen too (used over vinegar in dressings), so the non-alcoholic pours read as considered rather than afterthoughts. Time Out singles out the Italian Orange Spritz with verjus and tonic, a Spritz Veneziano and a sparkling salted raspberry and cranberry build as the zero-proof picks.
signatureDrinks: Italian Orange Spritz - verjus and tonic
venues.longDescription:
Marion opened on Gertrude Street in 2015 as Andrew McConnell's fourth venue on the strip, spanning two shopfronts next door to his two-hat restaurant Cutler & Co. The room keeps the bones of the site's past life as a metal-plating factory - white-washed brick, an untouched original floor, black leather, dark wood and ceiling-high wine racks around a small curved bar, with an open kitchen anchoring the left-hand side. In 2025 it celebrated ten years and was inducted into Broadsheet's Ten-Year Club, cementing it as one of the venues that helped set the template for Melbourne's wine-bar boom.

The draw is one of the most comprehensive wine lists in the neighbourhood, running deep on orange wines and less-familiar varietals like gruner veltliner, chenin blanc and gamay, alongside a daily-changing menu of oysters, bay scallops and charcuterie from McConnell's own butcher, Meatsmith.

For guests skipping alcohol, Marion holds a real low-and-no section rather than a lone token option. Time Out Melbourne highlights an Italian Orange Spritz made with verjus and tonic, a Spritz Veneziano, and a sparkling salted raspberry-and-cranberry drink - builds that lean on the same verjus-forward, ingredient-led thinking the kitchen applies everywhere else.

It is a moody, grown-up room built for lingering, and the non-alcoholic pours are treated with the same care as the wine, which makes it a rare zero-proof-friendly stop among Fitzroy's serious drinking dens.

A wine bar is the hardest room in which to not drink, which is what makes this one worth naming. Time Out's guide to drinking in Melbourne without alcohol puts it directly: Marion may be Andrew McConnell's wine bar, but if you are off the wine there are still plenty of low- and zero-alcohol options, and it names three — an Italian Orange Spritz built with verjus and tonic, a Spritz Veneziano, and a sparkling salted raspberry and cranberry drink.

Verjus is the detail worth noticing. Pressed from unripe grapes, it carries the acidity and grip that make wine work at the table without any alcohol, and it is the ingredient a wine bar reaches for when it is taking the problem seriously rather than reaching for cordial. Served long in the same glassware, in the same moody room, it reads as a drink rather than as an abstention — which is the whole job on a table where everyone else has a glass of something.
venues.pressQuote: Marion might be Andrew McConnell's wine bar, but if you're off the vinos there's still plenty low and zero-alcoholic options you can drink.

venues.name: Marisi
venues.description: Marisi is an Italian restaurant on Wall Street in the village of La Jolla with a Spirit Free section printed on both its dinner and brunch cards. Three builds use real alcohol-free product rather than juice: a Rossini on strawberry, grapefruit and non-alcoholic sparkling wine, an Aperitivo Spritz on a non-alcoholic aperitivo with verjus blanc and champagne acid, and an espresso martini made with the restaurant's own espresso blend and a non-alcoholic amaro. Three drinks is a short list rather than a deep one, but each is built around acidity and bitterness rather than sugar — verjus and champagne acid in the spritz, a non-alcoholic amaro in the espresso martini — which is what separates a considered zero-proof drink from a soft one. Dinner runs nightly from five, until ten on Friday and Saturday, with lunch added on Saturday and Sunday from eleven until two, and the spirit-free section is printed on that card as well.
signatureDrinks: Rossini — strawberry, grapefruit, non-alcoholic sparkling wine
Aperitivo Spritz — non-alcoholic aperitivo, verjus blanc, champagne acid
Espresso Martini — Marisi's espresso blend, non-alcoholic amaro, demerara sugar
venues.longDescription:
Marisi trades on Wall Street in the village of La Jolla, a short walk from the cove, and cooks Italian food from an open kitchen with pasta made in house. It says it sources from responsible farmers, ranchers and fishermen, and the room is one of the more polished dining spaces in the neighbourhood.

The drinks card carries a Spirit Free heading on both the dinner and the weekend lunch menus, and the three drinks under it are built rather than bought. The Rossini is the Italian classic — usually strawberry purée and prosecco — rebuilt with strawberry, grapefruit and non-alcoholic sparkling wine, which keeps the shape of the original without the alcohol. The Aperitivo Spritz uses a non-alcoholic aperitivo with verjus blanc and champagne acid; verjus, the pressed juice of unripe grapes, is what supplies the sharpness that wine would otherwise bring, and champagne acid does the same job for the finish. The third is an espresso martini made with the restaurant's own espresso blend, a non-alcoholic amaro and demerara sugar, which is a harder drink to get right without alcohol than most menus admit.

Those three are the whole section, so this is a short list rather than a deep one — but it is a considered short list, printed at both services, using ingredients chosen for acidity and bitterness rather than sweetness. For a non-drinker at an Italian table, the aperitivo spritz in particular does the thing an aperitivo is supposed to do.

Hours are worth checking before setting out. Dinner runs from five every night, until nine early in the week, ten on Friday and Saturday. Lunch is served on Saturday and Sunday from eleven until two, and the spirit-free section appears on that card as well. Reservations are advisable: the village is busy in summer and the dining room is not large. This is a licensed restaurant with a full wine programme, not an alcohol-free room.

The weekend lunch is the service worth planning around if the drinks are the draw. The kitchen puts out custard-soaked brioche with whipped vanilla mascarpone and strawberries, soft eggs with pomodoro and charred sourdough, and a bacon and egg sandwich on pain au lait, and the spirit-free drinks read better against that food than against a heavy dinner. The restaurant states that it sources from responsible farmers, ranchers and fishermen and that everything is cooked with intention, and the pasta is made on site. La Jolla parking is metered and tight at weekends, so allow time or use one of the structures a few streets back from the cove.
venues.pressQuote: We proudly source our ingredients from the most responsible farmers, ranchers and fishermen. Everything is cooked with love, intention and grace.

venues.name: Martina
venues.description: Martina is the Linden Hills restaurant that launched Daniel del Prado as a Twin Cities restaurateur, an Argentinian-Italian room on Upton Avenue with a bar programme that has been taken seriously since Marco Zappia set it up in 2018. Its non-alcoholic cocktails are listed on the same menu as the full-strength ones at $12 and rotate with the seasons: a Tropical on passion fruit, mango and lime with carbonation; an Apollo built on a non-alcoholic berry amaro with masala chai and lime; and a Lemongrass with ginger, galangal and lemon verbena. ISH sparkling rose and Gruvi's Juicy Dayz non-alcoholic IPA round out the zero-proof options.
signatureDrinks: Apollo (non-alcoholic berry amaro, masala chai, lime)

naMenuItems.name: Apollo
naMenuItems.description: non-alcoholic berry amaro, masala chai, lime

naMenuItems.name: Lemongrass
naMenuItems.description: ginger, galangal, lemon verbena, carbonation

venues.longDescription:
Martina opened in 2018 on Upton Avenue South and gave Linden Hills its first cocktail bar, in a neighbourhood that until then had run on ice cream and bakeries. It was Daniel del Prado's first restaurant of his own and the beginning of a group that now includes Rosalia next door, Porzana in the North Loop and several others. The food blends Argentinian and Italian cooking; the bar was built by Marco Zappia, previously of Lawless Distilling and Grand Cafe, on a technical premise that turns out to matter for non-drinkers: Zappia designed the drinks around roughly fifty percent dilution from non-alcoholic ingredients, against the thirty percent typical of a cocktail bar, which means the house style was never dependent on spirit alone to carry a drink.

That shows in the zero-proof column, which sits inside the cocktail menu at $12 rather than in a separate section, and which rotates with what is in season. The current three run in different directions. Tropical is the most straightforward — passion fruit, mango and lime under carbonation. Apollo is the most interesting: it uses a non-alcoholic berry amaro against masala chai and lime, borrowing the bitterness and spice that a real amaro would bring and then rebuilding the length with tea. Lemongrass works ginger, galangal and lemon verbena into a carbonated build that reads as Southeast Asian rather than Italian, which is where the tourism board's description of the list leaning "toward the tropics and Southeast Asia" comes from. Beyond the house drinks, Martina pours ISH sparkling rose by the glass and stocks Gruvi's Juicy Dayz non-alcoholic IPA at $6. The restaurant is licensed and its wine and cocktail programme is the main event — this is not an alcohol-free room — but the spirit-free drinks are made with the same attention and are priced within a dollar of their alcoholic equivalents. Dinner runs nightly, with weekend brunch.
venues.pressQuote: Blending Argentine and Italian flavors on plates coming out of the kitchen, this upscale Linden Hills destination leans toward the tropics and Southeast Asia on its mocktail menu.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Meet Minneapolis, Best Mocktails in Minneapolis

venues.name: Matcha Mate
venues.description: Matcha Mate is a fully alcohol-free matcha cafe and tasting room at 100 Langridge Street, Collingwood, opened as a standalone shop at the end of 2025 by Belle Vy and Chian Ting — who first ran it as a pop-up inside their CBD dessert shop Nimbo in 2023. Guests are walked through seven first-harvest Japanese matcha blends and two roasted hojicha varieties the way a wine bar guides you through bottles, from the creamy, malty house blend Hikari to the bright, floral single-cultivar Osu, all hand-whisked to order. Zero alcohol by design, it's a genuine daytime social spot built entirely around tea.
signatureDrinks: Usucha — ceremonial thin-whisked matcha, hand-prepared from a single blend such as Osu or Hikari
Iced matcha latte with optional matcha ice-cream, matcha cream, matcha pudding or house-made dango
venues.longDescription:
Matcha Mate started life in 2023 as a matcha pop-up tucked inside Nimbo, the CBD dessert shop run by Belle Vy and Chian Ting. At the end of 2025 the pair opened this permanent standalone location — branded "Matcha Mate 100" for its street number — at 100 Langridge Street in Collingwood, turning the side project into a dedicated shop that is part cafe, part tasting room.

The draw is depth: seven first-harvest matcha blends and two roasted hojicha varieties, each with its own character. The house signature Hikari leans creamy, malty and umami-rich; Osu, a single-cultivar Okumidori from Kyoto, reads bright and floral; the range runs on through Nanako, Maru, Asa, Kaki and Minami. Loose-leaf tins sell retail from around A$25 for the darker hojicha up to A$52 for the top Uji blend Asa. Everything in the cup is hand-whisked to order — classic tea, ceremonial usucha, hot and iced lattes, plus seasonal builds like strawberry matcha and an apple-crumble matcha, with optional toppings of matcha ice-cream, matcha cream, matcha pudding or house-made dango.

Desserts carry the same obsession: a matcha parfait layered with pudding, red bean, dango, yuzu jelly, rice puffs and matcha ice-cream; hana konyaku, a warabi mochi dressed with edible flowers, kuromitsu and kinako; and baked goods carried over from Nimbo including matcha Basque cheesecake and matcha white-chocolate cookies.

Open Monday to Saturday during daytime hours only, Matcha Mate is entirely alcohol-free — a place to sit, taste and compare rather than a bar, and a natural fit for anyone looking for a considered, social alternative to a drink.

venues.name: Matilda Midnight
venues.description: Matilda Midnight is a downtown Chattanooga cocktail lounge on East 10th Street whose drinks are named after tarot cards, a conceit that runs through the alcohol-free options as well as the spirited ones. The house mocktail is the Abundance — coconut water, house cream, pineapple, lime, lavender syrup and soda — a rich, layered build that uses a made-in-house cream rather than a bought mixer, which is the difference between a drink and a soft drink. The room is dark, late and deliberately atmospheric, opening at 5pm Wednesday through Sunday and running to midnight, and closed Monday and Tuesday.
signatureDrinks: Abundance — coconut water, house cream, pineapple, lime, lavender syrup, soda
venues.longDescription:
Matilda Midnight sits on East 10th Street in downtown Chattanooga and builds its whole identity on tarot: the cocktails are named for the cards, the room is dark and candlelit, and the experience is pitched somewhere between a cocktail lounge and a séance. It is exactly the kind of bar where a non-drinker usually ends up holding a glass of soda while everyone else gets the theatre.

That is not what happens here. The Abundance is a mocktail with a card of its own, and it is built rather than poured — coconut water, a house-made cream, pineapple, lime, lavender syrup and soda. The house cream is the technical detail that matters: making your own means the alcohol-free drink has body and texture, which is the single hardest thing to replicate without a spirit and the thing most mocktails fail at. Lavender and lime give it aromatics; the coconut water keeps it from turning cloying.

Chattanooga's daily newsletter NOOGAtoday named the Abundance in its guide to drinking without alcohol in the city, which is how it came to this directory's attention, and the bar's inclusion of it in the tarot naming scheme rather than in a separate mocktail annex is the reason it grades where it does.

This entry records one signature drink rather than a list, and that is honest: Matilda Midnight's alcohol-free offer is a well-made single build with more available on request, not a printed zero-proof section on the scale of The Rosecomb's. What it offers instead is atmosphere — a late, dark, unusual room where the drink in your hand belongs to the concept.

Doors at 5pm Wednesday through Sunday, midnight close (11pm on Wednesday), closed Monday and Tuesday. It is a short walk from the Chattanooga Choo Choo and the Southside bars.

One structural note that reaches beyond this bar. Chattanooga is unusual among metros of its size in having three fully alcohol-free rooms rather than one, and the effect on a themed venue like this is indirect but real: when a city's non-drinkers already have somewhere to go, licensed bars stop treating them as an edge case worth a single bottled option and start writing them into the concept instead. The Abundance getting its own tarot card, rather than its own annex at the back of the menu, is what that shift looks like in practice.
venues.pressQuote: Order the Abundance mocktail, made with coconut water, house cream, pineapple, lime, lavender syrup + soda.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: NOOGAtoday, Local mocktails + non-alcoholic drinks in Chattanooga

venues.name: Mattie's at Green Pastures
venues.description: Mattie's at Green Pastures is a historic American restaurant set in an 1895 Victorian home in Austin's Bouldin Creek neighborhood. The property is a Texas Recorded Historic Landmark on the National Register of Historic Places — originally opened as a restaurant in 1946, it was notable for serving customers of all races 18 years before Austin restaurants were desegregated by law. Renovated and reopened in 2017 as Mattie's, named after the property's matriarch, the menu features pan-Southern farm-fresh fare under sprawling live oaks with resident peacocks roaming the grounds. The cocktail program leans Southern (John Henry's Julep with Still Austin bourbon is a signature), and the Back Porch Tea — a blend of spearmint and eucalyptus tea with wildflower honey, lemon, and fresh mint — is explicitly available in a non-alcoholic preparation.
venues.address: 811 W Live Oak St, Austin, TX 78704
signatureDrinks: The Back Porch Tea (available NA: spearmint and eucalyptus tea with wildflower honey, lemon, fresh mint)
venues.longDescription:
Mattie's at Green Pastures sits in an 1895 Victorian house in Bouldin Creek, a Texas Recorded Historic Landmark on the National Register of Historic Places, on grounds shaded by live oaks and patrolled by resident peacocks. It first opened as a restaurant in 1946, and the most important fact about it is not architectural: it served customers of all races eighteen years before Austin's restaurants were desegregated by law. It was renovated and reopened as Mattie's in 2017, named for the property's matriarch.

The Infatuation's Raphael Brion put the place's role well — people from across Austin have come here for Easter brunches, wedding receptions and close encounters with the peacocks who roam the grounds. Those are the occasions that fill the building, and they are worth naming, because they are precisely the occasions where not drinking is most conspicuous. A wedding reception, an Easter brunch and a milestone birthday are all events where a glass gets raised and someone notices what is in yours.

The kitchen cooks pan-Southern farm-fresh food, and the bar leans the same way — the John Henry's Julep with Still Austin bourbon is the house signature. For non-drinkers the standing option is the Back Porch Tea, explicitly available in a non-alcoholic preparation: spearmint and eucalyptus tea with wildflower honey, lemon and fresh mint.

That a single drink can be ordered either way is the useful part. Eucalyptus and spearmint give it a cooling, almost medicinal length that holds up against rich Southern food, and honey supplies the body that alcohol would otherwise provide. On a wraparound porch in August it is the right drink whether or not there is bourbon in it, which means the choice stops being a statement.

Open Wednesday to Friday evenings, with lunch and dinner on Saturday and lunch on Sunday.
venues.pressQuote: people from across Austin have come here for Easter brunches, wedding receptions, and close encounters with the peacocks who roam the grounds

venues.name: Maui Brewing Co. Waikīkī
venues.description: Maui Brewing Co.'s Waikīkī brewpub sits inside the Outrigger Waikiki Beachcomber Hotel on Kalākaua Avenue and bills itself as the largest bar in Waikīkī, with thirty-six taps running Maui Brewing year-round beers, limited releases and guest pours from other independent brewers. Its documented non-alcoholic build is the Orange Crush — orange juice, mint, lemon-lime soda and simple syrup. Happy hour runs Monday to Friday from 3.30pm and there is a late-night happy hour from 9.30pm most nights, which along with the 11pm close makes it one of the more flexible rooms on the strip for a group that is only partly drinking.
signatureDrinks: Orange Crush (orange juice, mint, lemon-lime soda, simple syrup)
venues.longDescription:
Maui Brewing Co. operates its Waikīkī brewpub at 2300 Kalākaua Avenue, on the ground floor of the Outrigger Waikiki Beachcomber Hotel and a few steps from the beach. The room is large — the business describes it as the biggest bar in Waikīkī — and it pours thirty-six taps covering Maui Brewing's year-round range, its limited releases, and guest beers from other independent breweries. It opens daily from 11am to 11pm, with happy hour Monday to Friday from 3.30pm to 4.30pm and a late-night happy hour from 9.30pm to 10.30pm on most nights.

This is a brewpub rather than a zero-proof destination, and the entry sits at a three for that reason. The documented non-alcoholic build is the Orange Crush, made with orange juice, mint, lemon-lime soda and simple syrup — a straightforward, sweet, refreshing drink rather than a technical one, and the sort of thing a bar makes when it wants to offer something better than a can without building a programme. Anyone hoping for the kind of thing Maui Brewing's mainland counterparts increasingly do — brewing a genuine non-alcoholic beer in house, as New Holland does with its Zylch IPA — will not find it here; no such product is published for this location. What the venue does offer is scale and hours. A group of eight where two people are not drinking is a hard booking in Waikīkī, and a room this size with a long trading day, food service throughout and a drink on the list that is not a soft drink from the gun handles that situation better than a smaller, more precious bar would. It is a practical inclusion rather than an aspirational one, and the honest framing is that the beer is the reason the room exists.
venues.pressQuote: The Orange Crush is a glass of sunshine—its orange juice, mint, lemon-lime soda and simple syrup making lunch taste more like brunch with a mimosa mocktail.

venues.name: Mauro Colagreco at Raffles London at The OWO
venues.description: Mauro Colagreco at Raffles London at The OWO is the one-Michelin-star (2025) flagship of three-Michelin-star chef Mauro Colagreco, set inside the restored Old War Office on Whitehall. Its non-alcoholic offering is a genuine, kitchen-led programme rather than an afterthought: a dedicated multi-course Temperance Pairing (about £80 for five courses, £105 for seven) of sparkling teas, water kefirs and from-scratch mocktails built to mirror the tasting menu's 70-plus British fruits and vegetables. Serves include The Smokey Carrot, the English Garden No-Tini with Seedlip Garden 108 and Everleaf Marine, and the 'Dandy Smoke' zero-alcohol homage to Islay whisky.
venues.address: Raffles London at The OWO, Whitehall, London SW1A 2BX
venues.hours: Lunch: Thu–Sat 12pm–2pm; Dinner: Tue–Sat 6pm–10pm; closed Sun–Mon
signatureDrinks: The Smokey Carrot — carrot and sea buckthorn
English Garden No-Tini — Seedlip Garden 108, Everleaf Marine and celeriac leaf oil
Dandy Smoke — a zero-alcohol homage to Islay whisky with wood-smoked Lapsang tea, sea buckthorn and carrot trimmings
venues.longDescription:
Mauro Colagreco at Raffles London at The OWO is the signature restaurant of Argentine-Italian chef Mauro Colagreco, whose Mirazur on the French Riviera holds three Michelin stars and was named the World's Best Restaurant in 2019. Opened in late 2023 inside the meticulously restored Old War Office (The OWO) on Whitehall — a landmark Edwardian building turned Raffles hotel — the restaurant won its first Michelin star in the 2025 guide. The cooking is hyper-seasonal and vegetable-forward, built around more than 70 varieties of fruit and vegetables grown across the British Isles, a celebration of British land-and-sea terroir.

What makes the non-alcoholic offering real is that it is designed by the drinks team as a full parallel to the wine pairing. Under Vincenzo Arnese, Raffles London's director of wine, the restaurant runs a dedicated multi-course Temperance Pairing — roughly £80 alongside the five-course menu and £105 alongside the seven-course menu — of sparkling teas, water kefirs and bespoke mocktails, each conceived to echo a specific dish rather than to fill a glass. Arnese has said he approaches the soft serves 'as if they are a dish' themselves, developing them directly with the kitchen chefs, and reports that about 15 percent of guests now choose the soft-drink pairing, a share that keeps rising.

The serves are drawn from the English countryside and the menu's produce. The Smokey Carrot leans on carrot and sea buckthorn; the English Garden No-Tini is built from Seedlip Garden 108, the non-alcoholic aperitif Everleaf Marine and celeriac leaf oil; and the 'Dandy Smoke', a zero-alcohol homage to Islay single malt, uses wood-smoked Lapsang tea leaves, sea buckthorn and carrot trimmings, poured to accompany sea bass sashimi. A Quince Pet Nat and other house sparkling teas and kefirs round out a list that treats abstaining guests to the same craft and progression as the cellar.

This is a formal fine-dining room inside a five-star hotel rather than a bar, so the non-alcoholic experience comes as part of a tasting menu with reservations essential; there is a smart dress code and a minimum age of 12. For anyone seeking a marquee, occasion-level meal in central London without alcohol, it is one of the city's most credible destinations — a Michelin-starred kitchen where the zero-proof pairing is engineered, course by course, to stand shoulder to shoulder with the wine.
venues.pressQuote: About 15% of our guests choose the soft-drink pairing option but that's increasing by the week.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Vincenzo Arnese, director of wine, Raffles London

venues.name: Max's South Seas Hideaway
venues.description: Max's South Seas Hideaway is a two-storey tiki bar and restaurant at 58 Ionia Avenue SW, and the most ambitious tiki project built in the Midwest in decades. It is a joint venture between Mark Sellers, who founded HopCat; Martin Cate, the James Beard award-winning author and owner of San Francisco's Smuggler's Cove, who designed the cocktail program; and Gecko, a Hawaii-based tiki and Polynesian artist. The two floors hold one of the largest collections of new and vintage tiki art and memorabilia anywhere. The bar keeps a standing Zero Proof menu of eight island-style mocktails — among them the Ginger Zing, Coconut Mojito, Island Passion, Pomegranate Punch, Orange Creamsicle and both a Pom and a standard Virgin Pina Colada — and also pours locally made Brix Sodas.
venues.address: 58 Ionia Ave SW, Grand Rapids, MI 49503
venues.longDescription:
Max's South Seas Hideaway occupies two floors at 58 Ionia Avenue SW in downtown Grand Rapids and was described on opening as the most ambitious tiki bar to open in the Midwest in decades. It is a passion project for three owners with unusually specific credentials: Mark Sellers, the founder of the HopCat beer-bar chain; Martin Cate, the James Beard award-winning author and owner of Smuggler's Cove in San Francisco, generally regarded as the most serious tiki bar in the United States, who built the cocktail program here; and Gecko, a renowned Hawaii-based tiki and Polynesian artist. A team of tradespeople and artists working with local contractors spent months on the build. The result houses one of the largest collections of new and vintage tiki art and memorabilia in the country, spread across two levels designed to read as perpetual twilight, with island-inspired food alongside the drinks.

Tiki is a useful format for non-alcoholic drinking and this bar treats it that way. Rum-forward tropical cocktails are carried by fruit, spice, citrus and texture as much as by spirit, which means a zero-proof version is a genuine drink rather than a diminished one — and Max's keeps a standing Zero Proof section of eight island-themed mocktails rather than improvising on request. The named builds run to the Ginger Zing, the Coconut Mojito, Island Passion, Pomegranate Punch, Cinnamon Splash, Orange Creamsicle, the Pom Pina Colada and a Virgin Pina Colada; earlier menus carried drinks named 5 Spice Makes It Nice, Call Me in the Morning and Mahalo Mint, and the list rotates. Guests who want something simpler can order Brix Sodas, which are made locally with cane sugar and which Experience Grand Rapids singles out. The bar trades 4pm to 10pm Monday through Thursday, 4pm to 11pm Friday, 2pm to 11pm Saturday and 2pm to 10pm Sunday, and takes reservations.
venues.pressQuote: Max's is also a great place to enjoy Brix Sodas.

venues.name: Maya Moon Cacao Lounge
venues.description: Maya Moon Cacao Lounge is an alcohol-free ceremonial-cacao concept that opened in May 2025 inside GOODONYA, the long-running organic eatery on South Coast Highway 101 in Encinitas. A North County outpost of Maya Moon Collective — founded by Kathryn Rogers, whose Normal Heights café bills itself as Southern California's first ceremonial-cacao café — its draw is a rotating set of signature herbal cacao blends, drinking-cacao tasting flights, adaptogenic drinks, handcrafted truffles, and house honey marshmallows, a genuine zero-proof, ritual-forward experience. Note that the host GOODONYA also serves natural wine, prosecco, and local beer alongside an alcohol-free "social tonic" menu, so the dry experience here is the cacao program rather than the whole building.
venues.longDescription:
Maya Moon Cacao Lounge is the North County outpost of Maya Moon Collective, opened in May 2025 inside GOODONYA, the long-running organic eatery on South Coast Highway 101 in Encinitas. The parent business — founder Kathryn Rogers's Normal Heights café, which bills itself as Southern California's first ceremonial-cacao café — built its reputation on treating cacao the way a coffee bar treats coffee or a wine bar treats wine: as something with origin, preparation method and tasting notes worth taking seriously, rather than as hot chocolate. This location brings that to a beach town whose social life otherwise runs on surf, coffee and natural wine.

The draw is a rotating set of signature herbal cacao blends, drinking-cacao tasting flights, adaptogenic drinks, handcrafted truffles and house honey marshmallows. The flight format is the thing worth travelling for, because it turns a drink into an experience with a beginning and an end — the closest structural equivalent a non-drinker gets to a wine flight, and a genuinely ritual-forward alternative to a bar. Ceremonial cacao is unprocessed cacao paste prepared as a drink, mildly stimulating through theobromine rather than intoxicating, and it contains no alcohol.

One honest caveat belongs on this listing, and it is the reason this venue is graded lower than the Normal Heights room. The host business, GOODONYA, also serves natural wine, prosecco and local beer alongside its own alcohol-free social tonic menu. So the dry experience here is the cacao programme, not the whole building — which is fine if you are comfortable sitting somewhere that serves alcohol to other tables, and worth knowing in advance if you are not. For anyone who specifically wants a room where nothing alcoholic is poured at all, the Normal Heights café and its Moon Flower evening lounge are the ones to choose.

venues.name: Mayawell
venues.description: Mayawell is a bar in the Pepper Place district of Birmingham, east of downtown near the Saturday market, and its contribution to this guide is the Chef's Kiss — a mocktail Bham Now picked out by name in its January 2026 round-up of the city's non-alcoholic drinking, on the strength of how it looks as much as how it tastes. Presentation is not a trivial consideration in this category: a drink that arrives looking like everyone else's is the difference between being included in a round and being visibly opted out of one. Open Tuesday to Saturday from 4pm, with a 2pm Saturday start, closed Sunday and Monday.
venues.longDescription:
Pepper Place is the converted industrial district east of downtown Birmingham, best known for its Saturday farmers' market, and Mayawell is one of the bars that has grown up around it on 4th Avenue South.

Its entry in this guide rests on a single named drink, the Chef's Kiss, which Bham Now picked out in its January 2026 survey of where to drink without alcohol in the city — and picked out specifically for being pretty. That is worth taking more seriously than it sounds. The most common complaint from people who do not drink is not that the alternatives taste bad; it is that they arrive in a different kind of glass, without garnish, looking like something handed to a child. A mocktail that is plated and presented like the cocktails is doing social work as well as sensory work, and bars that understand this tend to understand the rest of it too.

The grading here is three rather than four, and the reason is documentation rather than doubt. One named drink is one named drink: there is no printed zero-proof section visible, no non-alcoholic spirits programme this directory could verify, and the ingredients of the Chef's Kiss are not published. What is verified is that Birmingham's own daily recommended it by name six months ago and that the bar is trading normally.

The hours are worth planning around, because Mayawell keeps a bar schedule rather than a restaurant one: 4pm to 11:30pm Tuesday through Thursday, 4pm to 12:30am on Friday, a 2pm start on Saturday, and closed Sunday and Monday. It is roughly a mile east of the downtown cluster, walkable in good weather and a short drive otherwise, and it sits close to Noble Pursuits in Lakeview — the two make a sensible pairing for an evening.
venues.pressQuote: A pretty mocktail with a name like Chef's Kiss? Count me in.

venues.name: Mazajj Organic Coffee
venues.description: Mazajj Organic Coffee is a Yemeni coffeehouse on Richmond Avenue in Greater Uptown, and it keeps later hours than almost any bar in Houston: midnight Sunday through Thursday and one in the morning on Friday and Saturday. The drinks are the traditional Yemeni repertoire rather than a Western cafe list — Adeni chai, black tea brewed with cardamom, cinnamon and milk; qishr, made from spiced coffee husks rather than the bean; and a spiced sweet latte built on double espresso with cardamom and cinnamon. Texas Monthly covered the venue as part of the Yemeni coffeehouse wave that has spread across Texas since 2024. No alcohol is served or licensed at the address, and the room is built for sitting rather than for takeaway, which is the entire point of the format.
signatureDrinks: Adeni chai — Yemeni black tea brewed with cardamom, cinnamon and milk
Qishr — hot infusion of spiced coffee husks rather than the coffee bean
Spiced Sweet Latte — double espresso, milk, cardamom, cinnamon, syrup
venues.longDescription:
Mazajj Organic Coffee sits on Richmond Avenue in Greater Uptown, and the single most useful fact about it is the closing time. It trades until midnight from Sunday to Thursday and until one in the morning on Friday and Saturday — later than most licensed bars in the same postcode, and with no last call, because there is nothing to call last orders on. For anyone who wants somewhere to be at eleven at night that is not a bar, that is a rarer thing in Houston than it should be.

The drinks list is the traditional Yemeni one rather than a Western cafe menu with a token tea. Adeni chai is black tea brewed with cardamom, cinnamon and milk, the everyday drink of Aden and the thing most regulars order. Qishr is the more interesting proposition: an infusion made from the dried husk of the coffee cherry rather than the bean itself, spiced and served hot, tasting closer to a spiced fruit tea than to coffee. It is a genuinely old preparation — husk coffee predates bean coffee as a Yemeni drink — and it is nearly impossible to find outside a Yemeni house. Alongside those sit a spiced sweet latte built on double espresso with cardamom and cinnamon, a pistachio latte, a pistachio matcha and a red velvet latte.

Texas Monthly covered Mazajj as part of the Yemeni coffeehouse wave that has spread across Texas since 2024, and its framing is worth repeating: these rooms draw a mixed crowd precisely because they are alcohol-free and open late. The magazine described the appeal as no loud music and no alcohol, just espresso machines, cinnamon and cardamom, and the hum of conversation.

On alcohol, the position is unambiguous but worth stating precisely: Mazajj does not serve any, and the Texas alcoholic beverage licence register returns no permit for the trade name anywhere in the state, nor any permit at this address. That is evidence-based rather than a claim the venue makes in those words. It serves caffeine only — no kava, no kratom, nothing psychoactive beyond coffee and tea.
venues.pressQuote: Some of the most popular late-night spots in Texas right now have no loud music and no alcohol—just the whir of espresso machines, the smells of cinnamon and cardamom, the clinking of ceramic and glass cups, and the peaceful hum of meaningful conversation.

venues.name: MDRD
venues.description: MDRD is a modern Spanish restaurant on the 27th floor of the Tower wing at the Amway Grand Plaza, 187 Monroe Avenue NW, with panoramic views over the Grand River and the city. It holds a AAA Four Diamond rating and serves expressive entrees, shareables and desserts in the Madrid idiom the name points at. For non-drinkers the relevant point is that the mixing team builds a mocktail list alongside the cocktails rather than treating zero-proof as a request to be handled — Experience Grand Rapids describes the non-alcoholic selection as every bit as impressive as the rest of the menu. The named build most often cited is the Elote, a fruity, iced and bright drink finished with a mint garnish. Non-alcoholic beers are also stocked.
venues.address: 187 Monroe Ave NW, Grand Rapids, MI 49503
venues.hours: Mon closed; Tue-Thu 4:30pm-10pm; Fri-Sat 4:30pm-11pm; Sun closed

naMenuItems.description: pilsner (non-alcoholic)

naMenuItems.name: Bero
naMenuItems.description: hazy ipa, noon wheat, golden pilsner, double tasty ipa (non-alcoholic)

venues.longDescription:
MDRD occupies the 27th floor of the Tower wing at the Amway Grand Plaza on Monroe Avenue NW, which makes it the highest dining room in Grand Rapids and gives it panoramic views across the Grand River and the western half of the city. The name is the airport code shorthand for Madrid, and the cooking is modern Spanish: expressive entrees, a run of shareables built for the middle of the table, and desserts, held to a AAA Four Diamond standard. It is the city's default special-occasion room, and a weekend brunch service extends the same menu logic into the daytime with a Spanish brunch format.

That context is what makes its non-alcoholic list worth recording. A hotel fine-dining room at this price point is precisely where a guest who does not drink is most exposed: the wine pairing is the spine of the meal, the bar list is the house's showcase, and the fallback is usually sparkling water for three hours while everyone else is served something considered. MDRD does not run it that way. Its mixing team builds a mocktail selection as a standing part of the menu, and Experience Grand Rapids records that the talented mixologists here have also created a selection of nonalcoholic mocktails that are every bit as impressive as the rest of the menu. The best-documented of these is the Elote — fruity, iced and bright, finished with a mint garnish, and named after the Mexican street-corn preparation whose sweet-savoury profile it borrows. Non-alcoholic beers are also stocked for guests who want something simpler with the food. Dinner runs Tuesday through Thursday 4:30pm to 10pm and Friday and Saturday 4:30pm to 11pm; the restaurant is closed Sunday and Monday, and reservations are effectively required. For an anniversary or a business dinner where one person at the table is not drinking, it is the strongest option in the city.
venues.pressQuote: The talented mixologists here have also created a selection of nonalcoholic mocktails that are every bit as impressive as the rest of the menu.

venues.name: Mean Mule Distilling Co.
venues.description: Mean Mule Distilling Co. is a woman-owned agave-spirits distillery and tasting room in Kansas City's Crossroads Arts District, founded by Jeff Evans (CEO) and Meg Evans (COO) with master distiller Tyler Gloe. The company began distilling in 2016 from 100% organic blue Weber agave and opened its Crossroads distillery and tasting room at 1733 Locust St in April 2019. Its core lineup is American Agave Spirit in Silver, Gold, and Heritage expressions; the flagship Silver earned a gold medal at the San Francisco World Spirits Competition. Beyond spirit flights and craft cocktails, the tasting room keeps a small dedicated mocktail list of roughly five house-built zero-proof drinks. Named examples include Pickle's Punch (house red-pepper syrup, cactus brine, ginger beer, lime) and the Kleopatra, built on Ghia's non-alcoholic aperitif with an almond-and-ube syrup.
venues.hours: Mon closed; Tue-Thu 4pm-10pm; Fri 2pm-12am; Sat 12pm-12am; Sun 1pm-8pm
signatureDrinks: Pickle's Punch (house red pepper syrup, cactus brine, ginger beer, lime)
Kleopatra (Ghia non-alcoholic spirit, almond and ube syrup)
venues.longDescription:
Mean Mule Distilling Co. is an agave-spirits distillery and tasting room at 1733 Locust Street in the Crossroads, and it began the way the best small distilleries do — Jeff and Meg Evans spent a summer break teaching themselves to distil in their garage, using a still they had built themselves. The brand launched around 2016 and the public distillery and tasting room opened on 12 April 2019, with Jeff as chief executive and head distiller, Meg as chief operating officer and Patrick Little handling brand and marketing. The distillery describes itself as family-operated and woman-owned. It makes agave spirit in Missouri rather than importing it, which is unusual enough on its own, and the tasting room is built around cocktails made with what is distilled on site. Beverage director Amy Connor now runs the drinks programme, and The Pitch was still covering new seasonal cocktails there in spring 2026.

A distillery tasting room is not an obvious entry in a non-alcoholic guide, which is exactly why this one is worth knowing about: Mean Mule keeps five custom-made mocktails alongside the agave list, built with the same house ingredients rather than poured from bottles. KCUR picked out two when mapping the city's zero-proof options. Pickle's Punch leads with the punch of the distillery's own house-made red pepper syrup, mixed with cactus brine, ginger beer and lime — savoury and briny, and about as far from a sweet mocktail as a drink gets. Kleopatra is the aperitif of the pair, built on Ghia's non-alcoholic spirit with a syrup made from almonds and ube. Both are made in house by the same team making the cocktails, which is the distinction that matters in a room like this. Two honest caveats. The tasting room's website does not publish its menu in readable form, so the current mocktail list cannot be checked in advance and the two drinks above were documented in 2023 rather than this season. And the venue's own award claims carry no named awarding body, so treat those as marketing rather than verified recognition.
venues.pressQuote: Although they're primarily known as a distillery, Mean Mule's tasting room features five custom-made mocktails.

venues.name: Mélange by Cali Sober
venues.description: Mélange by Cali Sober opened on 14 November 2025 above Bamboula's at 516 Frenchmen Street in the Marigny, from Monica Olano — known online as Cali Sober Mom and founder of the Cali Sober Market in Metairie — and it bills itself as the first non-alcoholic, functional and THC beverage bar on Frenchmen Street. READ THIS BEFORE VISITING: the venue is alcohol-free but explicitly not substance-free. Alongside house-crafted non-alcoholic cocktails it serves kava, functional-mushroom drinks and hemp-derived THC beverages that it describes as legal under the 2018 Hemp Bill and Louisiana regulations. The important mechanic is that THC is served in individual vials so guests add their own dose to a drink rather than being served a fixed-strength cocktail — so the same named drink can be entirely inert or not, depending on what you add. Named drinks include the Mélange Old Fashioned, a Vesper Martini and the Cali Sober Love Potion, and the menu explains for each whether it is built to give an energy buzz, a calming effect, or a THC buzz. It has a balcony over the live music room. Open Thursday to Sunday evenings.
venues.longDescription:
Mélange by Cali Sober opened on 14 November 2025 in the room above Bamboula's at 516 Frenchmen Street, with its own balcony looking down over one of the busiest live-music strips in America — which is exactly the point. Frenchmen Street is where New Orleans goes to drink, and until this opened there was nowhere on it to spend an evening without alcohol. It comes from Monica Olano, a New Orleanian and mother of three who built a national following as Cali Sober Mom and opened the Cali Sober Market in Metairie the year before. Press has described it as the first non-alcoholic, functional and THC beverage bar on the street. There are small plates, including boudin balls, and the room runs Thursday through Sunday evenings.

The name is doing precise work, and it deserves unpacking rather than glossing. "California sober" means abstaining from alcohol while continuing to use cannabis, and Mélange is built on that definition: it is alcohol-free but explicitly not substance-free. Alongside genuinely non-alcoholic cocktails it serves kava, functional-mushroom drinks and hemp-derived THC beverages that it describes as compliant with the 2018 Farm Bill and Louisiana regulations. The mechanic that matters most is how the THC is served: in individual vials, so the guest adds their own dose rather than receiving a fixed-strength drink. That means a named drink here is not inherently infused — the Mélange Old Fashioned, the Vesper Martini and the Cali Sober Love Potion are functional or non-alcoholic builds, and the menu explains for each whether it is designed to give an energy buzz, a calming effect, or a THC buzz. For someone avoiding alcohol who wants cannabis, this is close to an ideal room. For someone avoiding both, it is entirely usable — but order without the vial and say so clearly, because the default assumption here runs the other way.
venues.pressQuote: We want to help people find their best alternative for the night and give them a little reprieve from the alcohol-fueled nightlife.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Monica Olano, Mélange by Cali Sober owner

venues.name: Melrose Umbrella Co.
venues.description: Melrose Umbrella Co. is a post-Prohibition-themed craft cocktail bar at 7465 Melrose Avenue in the Fairfax District, open since 2013 from owners Zach Patterson and Austin Melrose. The room is built from salvage: an 1890s fireplace facing an arched ceiling covered in New York City subway tile, and a massive 1920s wooden apothecary cabinet shipped from the East Coast and retrofitted as the back bar, with a string-lit heated patio behind. Its non-alcoholic offering is a genuine nine-item menu across two printed sections. Under "Non-Alcoholic Cocktails" sit five at $15: Not Even Smashed (Ritual zero-proof whiskey, blackberry, mint, lemon, elderflower tonic), the Pa-No-Ma (Ritual zero-proof tequila, prickly pear, green apple, ruby red grapefruit), the Keto Pepino (Ritual zero-proof gin, cucumber, lime, monkfruit, celery salt), The Valet (Pathfinder, Pentire Coastal Spritz, Seedlip Garden 108, orange), and a canned Piña Margarita or Negroni. Under "Non-Alcoholic Beers, Bubbles & Beyond" sit four cans at $7, including Athletic's Run Wild IPA and Deschutes' organic Kernza Golden. Open from noon, closed Mondays; reservations via Resy.
venues.longDescription:
Melrose Umbrella Co. has been on Melrose Avenue since 2013, and Time Out's four-star summary is the fair one: a dimly lit watering hole that has kept the good times coming with a fleet of reasonably priced cocktails. Owners Zach Patterson and Austin Melrose set out to build something nostalgic while the craft cocktail revival was still finding its feet, and the room is assembled from genuine salvage rather than reproduction — an 1890s fireplace facing an arched ceiling tiled in New York City subway tile, and a massive 1920s wooden apothecary cabinet shipped across the country and retrofitted into the back bar. Behind it there is a string-lit heated patio with a fireplace and couches. It opens at noon and runs to midnight, later at weekends, and takes reservations through Resy.

The non-alcoholic list is a real nine-item menu split across two printed sections, which is more than most cocktail bars of this vintage manage. Five drinks sit under Non-Alcoholic Cocktails at $15 each, and they lean on Ritual's zero-proof range for three of them: Not Even Smashed is a whiskey-alternative build with blackberry, mint, lemon and elderflower tonic; the Pa-No-Ma is a tequila-alternative paloma with prickly pear, green apple reduction and ruby red grapefruit; the Keto Pepino is a gin-alternative cucumber drink sweetened with monkfruit and finished with celery salt, which is the one to order if you want something savoury. The Valet is the most ambitious, layering Pathfinder with Pentire's Coastal Spritz aperitif and Seedlip Garden 108. The fifth is a canned Piña Margarita or Negroni from I'm Good. The second section, Non-Alcoholic Beers, Bubbles & Beyond, holds four cans at $7 — Athletic Brewing's Run Wild IPA, Deschutes' organic Kernza Golden, and two organic canned cocktails. One note on the menu's own wording: the section subhead promises drinks "pumped full of functional flavors & radical adaptogens", but no adaptogen is named in any of the five ingredient lists, so read that as marketing rather than a disclosed infusion. The Valet's Pathfinder is distilled from hemp seed and its maker states it contains no THC or CBD.
venues.pressQuote: Since 2013, this dimly lit Melrose Avenue watering hole has kept the good times coming with a fleet of reasonably priced cocktails.

venues.name: Merchant & Trade
venues.description: Merchant & Trade is a 19th-floor rooftop bar and lounge atop the Kimpton Tryon Park Hotel in Uptown Charlotte, offering panoramic skyline views across four distinct zones — indoor bar, outdoor terrace, private terrace, and the lawn. The venue maintains a serious zero-proof cocktail program with rotating seasonal mocktails crafted with the same care as their alcoholic offerings, using ingredients like Seedlip Spice 94, Ritual Zero Proof spirits, and locally brewed Lenny Boy Ginger Kombucha. Named drinks include the Endless Vacation, Bobcat Territory, The Gold Line, and the Faux & Falcon, reflecting both local Charlotte culture and a genuine commitment to spirit-free options.
venues.longDescription:
Merchant & Trade is the rooftop bar and lounge on the nineteenth floor of the Kimpton Tryon Park Hotel in Uptown Charlotte, with panoramic views across the skyline. It is unusually large for a rooftop, spread across four distinct zones — an indoor bar, an outdoor terrace, a private terrace and a lawn — which means it works for a quiet drink and for a group occasion equally well.

The zero-proof programme is more serious than a hotel rooftop needs it to be, and that is the reason it earns a listing rather than a mention. The bar runs rotating seasonal spirit-free cocktails built with the same process as the alcoholic list, using real non-alcoholic products rather than juice: Seedlip Spice 94, Ritual Zero Proof spirits, and locally brewed Lenny Boy Ginger Kombucha, which is a genuinely good local sourcing decision rather than a generic mixer. The named drinks lean into Charlotte references — Bobcat Territory nods to the city's NBA team, The Gold Line to the streetcar — alongside the Endless Vacation, Madame Blackberry and the Faux & Falcon. Naming a spirit-free drink after a local landmark rather than calling it "virgin" anything is a small thing that signals how the bar thinks about the category.

Scoop Charlotte, covering the city's mocktail options, noted the bar offers "quite a few mocktails to sip on while you look out at the Charlotte skyline," and that the options change with the season — expect juices and flavours that fit the time of year. A rotating list is a maintained one, which also means the specific drinks named here will vary by visit. Open nightly from 4:30pm, to midnight on Friday and Saturday. Uptown Charlotte empties out considerably after the business day, so a rooftop with four separate zones and a real spirit-free list is one of the few places in the district that works equally well for an after-work group and a weekend evening.
venues.pressQuote: Merchant & Trade offers "quite a few mocktails to sip on while you look out at the Charlotte skyline," featuring sophisticated zero-proof cocktails — the mocktail options change with the season, but you can expect juices and flavors that fit the time of year.

venues.name: Merchant
venues.description: Merchant has been the reference craft cocktail bar on Madison's Capitol Square for years, and is one of the handful of downtown rooms local coverage consistently names when the question is where to drink well without alcohol. Its zero-proof menu is built rather than substituted — the No Regrets works a non-alcoholic "gin-ish" spirit against rosemary and lime, which is a dry, herbaceous drink rather than a sweet one. The bar sits on South Pinckney Street a few doors from Settle Down Tavern and around the corner from Lucille and Eno Vino, which makes it the natural anchor of an alcohol-free evening on the Square. Closed Mondays; weekend brunch from 9am.
venues.hours: Mon closed; Tue-Thu 4pm-9pm; Fri 4pm-12am; Sat 9am-12am; Sun 9am-9pm
venues.longDescription:
Merchant opened on South Pinckney Street off the Capitol Square and spent the following years as the bar other Madison bartenders cite — a serious cocktail room with a kitchen, in a city that did not have many when it started. It is on the short list every local publication reaches for when writing about drinking well in Madison, and it turns up on the short list for drinking well without alcohol too, which is a different and rarer distinction.

The drink to know is the No Regrets, built on a non-alcoholic gin alternative — City Cast Madison records it on the menu as "gin-ish" — with rosemary and lime. That is a deliberately austere construction. There is no fruit purée and no syrup doing the heavy lifting; the juniper-forward base carries the aromatics, the rosemary extends them, and the lime supplies acid, so the drink finishes dry. It is the sort of thing a bar makes when it has thought about what a non-drinker actually misses, which is usually bitterness and length rather than sweetness. The bar's broader habit of house syrups and fresh juice is what makes it possible.

For planning, the geography here is the real argument. The Capitol Square holds four entries in this guide within about five minutes' walk of each other: Merchant on Pinckney, Settle Down Tavern a few doors along the same street, Lucille on King Street and Eno Vino on North Webster, with Nitro Beverage Lounge and the Great Dane's downtown brewpub a little further out. That density is unusual — most cities in this registry have their zero-proof depth scattered — and it makes an evening downtown genuinely plannable. Merchant is closed on Mondays and serves brunch from 9am on Saturday and Sunday.
venues.pressQuote: Merchant's "No Regrets" features "gin-ish," rosemary and lime.

venues.name: Mercury
venues.description: Mercury is a downtown Omaha cocktail bar on South 16th Street, and local drinks coverage credits it with the most extensive dedicated mocktail list in the city — dedicated being the operative word, meaning a standing section written as its own thing rather than a couple of substitutions offered on request. It is open 4pm to midnight seven days a week with no closed night, which combined with the depth of the list makes it the single most reliable place in Omaha to turn up without a plan and order well without alcohol. The room is a stylish mid-century lounge, intimate rather than loud.

naMenuItems.name: Clausthaler n/a
naMenuItems.description: n/a beer, frankfort, de 0.5%

venues.longDescription:
Of all the bars in this city guide, Mercury is the one to go to if you want the widest choice. Omaha's local drinks writing credits it with the most extensive dedicated mocktail list in the city, and the important word in that description is dedicated.

The distinction this directory draws repeatedly is between a bar that will make you something without alcohol and a bar that has written a list of alcohol-free drinks. The first is a service; the second is a menu. A menu means the drinks have been costed, tested and trained on, that the components are stocked for them specifically, and — most importantly for the person ordering — that you get to choose rather than to describe what you like and accept what arrives. Choosing is most of what a bar offers anyone.

Mercury's hours reinforce it: 4pm to midnight, seven days a week, no closed night and no shortened Sunday. Across this batch of cities the venues that turned out to matter most were rarely the ones with the cleverest single drink; they were the ones that were reliably open. A bar that is dark on Sunday and Monday cannot be anybody's default.

This entry deliberately records no signature drinks. The list is extensive, which is the point, but it is not published in a form that could be read for this guide, and this directory does not print a drink name it has not seen on a current menu. Ask for the mocktail list by name — it exists, and it is longer than what you will be shown elsewhere in the city.

South 16th Street puts Mercury a short walk from Wicked Rabbit, Cumbia and Anna's Place, in the downtown cluster where most of Omaha's alcohol-free drinking now happens.
venues.pressQuote: Mercury is a stylish mid-century lounge with an intimate atmosphere perfect for relaxing or socializing.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Hurrdat ONE, 10 Best Zero-Proof & Nonalcoholic Bars in Omaha, Nov 18, 2025

venues.name: Merriman's Honolulu
venues.description: Merriman's Honolulu is the Ward Village restaurant of chef Peter Merriman, one of the twelve founders of Hawaii Regional Cuisine — the 1991 movement that pushed the state's restaurants towards local farms and away from imported convention. The kitchen sources accordingly. Its documented zero-proof drink is the Maikaʻi Zero Proof Mai Tai, finished with a honey liliko\'i foam, which is a more considered piece of construction than the name suggests: the foam supplies the weight and texture that a mai tai normally gets from rum, and the passionfruit brings acidity. It sits in the same group as Monkeypod Kitchen in Waikīkī.

Zero-Proof Mai Taipog (passion-orange-guava juice, house-made macadamia nut orgeat, lime, honey lilikoʻi foam)
