venues.longDescription:
Merriman's Honolulu trades from Suite 170 at 1108 Auahi Street in Ward Village, the master-planned stretch of Kakaʻako running down towards Ala Moana. It is the Honolulu room of Peter Merriman, who opened his first restaurant in Waimea on Hawaiʻi Island in 1988 and was one of the twelve chefs who founded Hawaii Regional Cuisine in 1991 — the movement that established local sourcing as the default expectation for serious cooking in the islands rather than a novelty. The group now includes Monkeypod Kitchen, which appears separately in this guide at the OUTRIGGER Reef in Waikīkī.

The zero-proof drink the restaurant is documented for is the Maikaʻi Zero Proof Mai Tai, and the interesting part is the honey liliko'i foam it is finished with. The mai tai is the drink Hawaiʻi sells more of than any other, and it is also one of the harder cocktails to build without alcohol, because what rum contributes is not just flavour but weight — a viscosity and warmth that fruit juice alone cannot replace, which is why most virgin mai tais taste thin. A foam is a direct answer to that problem: it adds body and a slow mouthfeel at the top of the glass, and using honey rather than syrup gives it a rounder sweetness, while liliko'i — passionfruit — supplies the sharp acidity that stops the whole thing collapsing into sugar. Whether the drink is currently listed should be checked when booking, since the published reference for it is a few years old and restaurant lists at this level rotate. What does not change is the context: this is a special-occasion room from one of the most significant chefs in the state, in a district dense with other options, and a table here that includes someone not drinking is not going to be handed a glass of pineapple juice.
venues.pressQuote: This drink is simply the restaurant's mai tai without the rum, which makes it veer toward the sweet side, but it's still delightful, with a honey liliko'i foam.

venues.name: The Merryweather
venues.description: The Merryweather is a neighbourhood bar on the corner of Lydia Street in Schnitzelburg, one of Louisville's older working-class German neighbourhoods on the south side. Its non-alcoholic programme is unusually committed for a corner bar: the standing Sober Ghia Spritz is built on Ghia, the gentian-and-yuzu Mediterranean aperitif, and each January the bar prints a full alcohol-free menu of its own — the Dry Tai, the Nada Colada, the Mock-Scow Mule and the Not Toddy, which cover the tiki, tropical, ginger and hot-drink positions between them. That is a bar treating Dry January as a menu-writing exercise rather than a marketing line, and it is why the venue keeps appearing in Louisville's zero-proof coverage.
venues.longDescription:
Schnitzelburg is the pocket of south Louisville settled by German immigrants in the nineteenth century, still known for the Dainty Contest and for corner bars that have been corner bars for a century. The Merryweather, at 1101 Lydia Street, is the modern version of that — a neighbourhood bar with a kitchen, not a destination cocktail room — and it is precisely because of that positioning that its non-alcoholic list is worth writing about. Serious zero-proof programmes usually appear in expensive cocktail bars where the bartender has time and a budget for components. Finding one in a neighbourhood bar is rarer and, for most people most evenings, more useful.

The standing option is the Sober Ghia Spritz, built on Ghia — the Mediterranean-style non-alcoholic aperitif made from gentian root, yuzu, elderflower and rosemary, which drinks genuinely bitter rather than sweet and has become the default backbone for spritz-shaped drinks without alcohol. Each January the bar goes further and prints a whole alcohol-free menu. The 2026 list ran to a Dry Tai, a Nada Colada, a Mock-Scow Mule and a Not Toddy: a tiki build, a frozen tropical, a ginger-and-lime long drink and a hot spiced drink, which between them cover most of what someone actually wants to order across a month of not drinking. The names are jokes; the drinks are not.

Two things to know before you go. The Dry January menu is seasonal by design, so outside January the reliable order is the Ghia spritz and whatever the bar is building that week — worth asking rather than assuming the full list is up. And this is a bar in the ordinary sense: alcohol is served, the room is loud at weekends, and it is a neighbourhood local rather than a sober space. Schnitzelburg sits south of Germantown, about ten minutes from downtown, and Canary Club and The Breeze in Shelby Park are the nearest other entries in this guide.
venues.pressQuote: With a special January menu including a "Dry Tai," "Nada Colada," "Mock-Scow Mule" and "Not Toddy" available.

venues.name: Mesmer Kava
venues.description: Mesmer Kava is Vermont's first kava bar, opened in May 2025 by Gwen and Roderick Russell in Suite 109 of the Karma Bird House on Maple Street, a block from the Burlington waterfront. It serves traditionally prepared kava from the ground root of the South Pacific plant, plus kava drinks built with pineapple and ginger, herbal teas and kava-infused hot chocolate. Nothing on the menu contains alcohol, and it keeps genuine evening hours — 3pm to 8pm Wednesday through Saturday, from 4:30pm on Tuesday — which makes it the only room in the state offering a sit-down evening out with no alcohol in the building. Kava is mildly psychoactive, which the owners state plainly.
venues.hours: Mon closed; Tue 4:30pm-8pm; Wed-Sat 3pm-8pm; Sun closed
venues.longDescription:
Vermont did not have a kava bar until the middle of May 2025, when Gwen and Roderick Russell opened Mesmer Kava in the Karma Bird House on Maple Street, near the corner of Battery Street and a short walk from the Lake Champlain waterfront. It is the only fully alcohol-free evening venue in a city whose social life otherwise runs almost entirely through breweries, cider houses and cocktail bars — and that scarcity is the point of the listing as much as the drink is.

Kava is made from the ground root of a South Pacific plant, prepared traditionally here and served alongside kava drinks flavoured with pineapple and ginger. The Russells have added herbal teas and a kava-infused hot chocolate to the list since opening. The room is small, the pace is slow, and it is built for conversation rather than turnover: this is somewhere you sit for two hours, not somewhere you stop for one round.

Roderick Russell has been unusually careful about how he describes the effect, telling Seven Days that kava can help smooth the rough edges of your life and that it is mood-altering, not mind-altering. That distinction matters to a substantial part of this site's readership, and it is worth restating plainly: kava is mildly psychoactive. For someone in recovery this is a night out without alcohol rather than a substance-free room, and the difference is theirs to weigh.

The practical detail that makes it work is the hours. Mesmer is open 3pm to 8pm Wednesday through Saturday and from 4:30pm on Tuesday — an evening operation, not a daytime café that happens to lack a licence. Burlington's cafés close mid-afternoon and its bars open at four or five; Mesmer is the one address that covers the early evening without alcohol. Closed Sunday and Monday.

The location helps more than it looks like it should. The Karma Bird House is a converted brick building on Maple Street that houses design studios, non-profits and small creative businesses, so the bar sits inside a working community rather than on a bar strip — the people at the next table are as likely to be finishing a workday as starting a night out. That changes the texture of the room considerably, and it is the reason Mesmer functions as a third place rather than as a novelty stop. For a city where the default invitation is a brewery, having somewhere to say yes to is the whole point.
venues.pressQuote: It can help smooth the rough edges of your life. It's mood-altering, not mind-altering.

venues.name: Meta
venues.description: Meta is chef Sun Kim's two-Michelin-starred contemporary Korean restaurant on Mohamed Sultan Road, near Robertson Quay. Its tasting menus are offered with a full non-alcoholic pairing at S$120++, a house-made zero-proof flight built to run course-by-course alongside the S$280++ wine pairing rather than as an afterthought. The NA program mirrors the kitchen's Korean-rooted, seasonally driven cooking, giving diners a genuine no-alcohol route through the full degustation. Chef Sun Kim told The Korea Times he does not believe in perfection so much as the process of getting closer to it, and the drinks flight is treated with that same seriousness.
venues.longDescription:
Meta was opened in November 2015 on Keong Saik Road by chef Sun Kim, who was born in Busan and raised in Seoul, cooking first in his mother's gamja-tang eatery before training under Tetsuya Wakuda in Sydney and at Waku Ghin in Singapore. The restaurant relocated to 9 Mohamed Sultan Road, in the Robertson Quay / River Valley precinct, in 2023. Its cooking is a contemporary interpretation of Korean flavours, blending traditional heritage with global influence and modern technique across a seasonal tasting-menu format.

Meta holds two Michelin stars, with its second awarded in the 2024 guide, and has featured on Asia's 50 Best Restaurants since 2021; it also received the American Express One To Watch award in 2021. The tasting menus run at S$248++ for the Friday-and-Saturday lunch and S$288++ to S$328++ at dinner (six- or eight-course).

For drinkers skipping alcohol, Meta lists a dedicated Non-Alcoholic Pairing at S$120++ as a printed alternative to its S$280++ beverage pairing. It is a full-length, house-composed zero-proof flight designed to track the tasting menu course by course, giving the no-alcohol pairing the same status as the wine list rather than reducing it to a soft drink. Specific pours change with the menu and season.

The room sits on Mohamed Sultan Road, a short walk from the Singapore River at Robertson Quay. Service is dinner Monday to Saturday from 6pm, with additional lunch seatings on Friday and Saturday; the restaurant is closed on Sundays.

Sun Kim has been careful in interviews not to let the cooking be filed away too neatly. Speaking to The Korea Times in January 2026, he resisted the label itself — the moment a chef decides their cooking is "Korean," he argued, the range gets smaller — and described his working method as a process of getting closer to something rather than arriving at it. That is worth knowing before booking, because it explains a menu that reads Korean in memory and technique without being a survey of Korean classics.

For a non-drinking guest the relevant detail is structural. Meta prints its non-alcoholic pairing on the menu at S$120++ next to the S$280++ wine flight, which puts the two in the same column rather than burying the alcohol-free option in a conversation with the sommelier. That distinction matters more than it sounds: a printed price is a commitment the restaurant has to honour on a quiet Tuesday as well as a full Saturday, and it removes the small social cost of having to ask.

The pours are house-composed and change with the tasting menu, so there is no fixed list to publish and no commercial zero-proof brand to point at. Service is dinner Monday to Saturday from 6pm with additional Friday and Saturday lunch seatings, and the restaurant is closed Sundays. Reservations are essential.
venues.pressQuote: I don’t believe in perfection. I believe in the process of getting closer to it.

venues.name: Meteor
venues.description: Meteor is a cocktail bar in the Hawthorne neighbourhood of North Minneapolis, opened by Elliot Manthey and Robb Jones in a former dive on North 2nd Street and since recognised well beyond the city — a 2024 James Beard Award semifinalist for Outstanding Bar, and listed by the World's 50 Best Discovery guide. Its reputation rests on a seasonal cocktail programme built across mezcal, aquavit and other less-obvious spirits, and the same bar team applies that thinking to drinks with nothing in them: the standing non-alcoholic reference point is a wild rice horchata, a Minnesota reworking of the drink, alongside rotating seasonal zero-proof builds. Hot dogs are the food.
venues.hours: Mon 4pm-12am; Tue closed; Wed-Fri 4pm-2am; Sat 12pm-2am; Sun 12pm-12am
venues.longDescription:
Meteor occupies a stretch of North 2nd Street in Hawthorne that had held a dive bar for decades, and co-owners Elliot Manthey and Robb Jones kept the bones of the room while rebuilding what came across the bar. The result has been one of the more improbable success stories in Twin Cities drinking: a neighbourhood bar in North Minneapolis, serving hot dogs, that was named a 2024 James Beard Award semifinalist in the Outstanding Bar category, carries an Excellent rating from the Pinnacle Guide, and appears in the World's 50 Best Discovery listing. The stated intention was a bar that would serve top-tier drinks to anyone who walked in regardless of background, and the room reflects it — this is not a reservations-and-velvet-rope cocktail bar.

For a non-drinker the relevant fact is what that bar team does with the constraint. The seasonal cocktail list runs through spirits most bars leave alone — mezcal, aquavit — and rotates several times a year, and the non-alcoholic drinks rotate with it rather than sitting frozen at the bottom of the page. Explore Minnesota's guide to non-alcoholic drinking in the state singles Meteor out for its zero-proof work and names a wild rice horchata: horchata rebuilt on manoomin, the wild rice that grows in Minnesota's shallow lakes and carries a nutty, toasted character that rice horchata does not, which makes it a genuinely regional non-alcoholic drink rather than a borrowed one. Beyond that named build, the list carries seasonal zero-proof specials and low-ABV drinks. This is a licensed bar with a full spirits programme and it is graded accordingly — a real but modest non-alcoholic offering rather than a designed parallel menu — but it is the only entry on this page in North Minneapolis, and the hours are the widest here: 2am on Wednesday through Saturday, midnight otherwise, closed Tuesday.
venues.pressQuote: Meteor Bar is home to a nationally renowned cocktail program led by expert bartenders who are passionate about their craft.

venues.name: metrobar
venues.description: metrobar is an 11,000-square-foot indoor-outdoor bar built around a redesigned WMATA Metro railcar, which serves as the central bar structure, with a platform-style lounge and a cocktail garden beside the Rhode Island Ave-Brentwood station in Edgewood. The concept is to connect the District's eight wards through craft cocktails spotlighting local DMV spirits, breweries and wineries, with food from rotating truck partners. It was voted Best Bar in DC by Washington City Paper readers in 2024 and was a 2025 Rammys Best Bar finalist. Non-alcoholic drinks are on the everyday menu alongside the cocktails, beer, cider and wine, and each January the bar runs a full Dry January menu of hot and cold spirit-free libations billed as District-made cocktails without the hangover. Ordering is by QR-code Toast tab at the table.
venues.address: 640 Rhode Island Ave NE, Washington, DC 20002
venues.hours: Mon-Tue closed; Wed 5pm-11pm; Thu 5pm-12am; Fri 4pm-1am; Sat 12pm-1am; Sun 12pm-11pm
venues.longDescription:
metrobar is built around a decommissioned WMATA Metro railcar. The car was redesigned to serve as the bar structure itself, with a platform-style lounge alongside it and an 11,000-square-foot indoor-outdoor cocktail garden around that, on a site immediately beside the Rhode Island Ave-Brentwood station in Edgewood. The transit theme is not only decorative: the stated concept is to connect the District's eight wards, and the drinks list is built to spotlight local DMV spirits, breweries and wineries rather than national brands. Food comes from rotating truck partners rather than a fixed kitchen, which changes what is available week to week. It was voted Best Bar in DC by Washington City Paper readers in 2024 and was named a 2025 Rammys Best Bar finalist, and Washingtonian covered the opening with the observation that a 5000-series train is one of the main attractions.

For anyone not drinking, the honest position is that this is a bar with non-alcoholic options rather than a bar with a developed zero-proof programme, and the offer is strongly seasonal. Non-alcoholic drinks sit on the everyday menu alongside the cocktails, beer, cider and wine, but the most substantial expression of it arrives each January, when the bar runs a full Dry January menu of hot and cold spirit-free libations, billed as District-made cocktails without the hangover. That seasonal list is genuinely worth planning around; outside it, expect a shorter standing selection rather than named house builds, and it is worth checking what is on before making the trip specifically for the drinks.

What the venue offers year-round is the setting, and for a group that is not all drinking it is a strong one - large, outdoors, walk-in, and structured around space rather than around a bar rail. Practical notes: it is closed Monday and Tuesday, opens at 5pm Wednesday and Thursday, 4pm on Friday and noon at weekends, and runs to 11pm midweek and 1am on Friday and Saturday. Ordering is handled through QR-code Toast tabs at each table rather than at a bar, which suits a large outdoor space. The Rhode Island Ave Metro station is directly adjacent.
venues.pressQuote: A 5000-series train is one of the main attractions at Metro-themed cocktail garden Metrobar

venues.name: Miami Kava & Coffee
venues.description: Miami Kava & Coffee is a fully alcohol-free kava lounge in Little River, billed as the City of Miami's first kava bar. The business started in 2015 in a small Wynwood house under the names House of Roots and later Roots Miami Kava, before expanding across Miami and settling its flagship room at 393 NE 59th St; in 2025 it marked its tenth anniversary. Everything served is plant-based and zero-proof: fresh-brewed traditional kava, herbal teas, house-brewed yerba mate, specialty coffee, and pressed ginger shots. The drink menu carries playful named pours such as the Cheech, Mr. T, Icey Tea, and the Fruity Rooty kava shot. Long a hub for Miami's creative community, the venue hosts open mics, live music, and local art showcases, functioning as a gathering space for artists and the sober-curious alike.
venues.longDescription:
Miami Kava & Coffee is billed as the City of Miami's first kava bar, and its history supports the claim. It began in 2015 in a small Wynwood house trading as House of Roots, later Roots Miami Kava, before expanding across the city and settling its flagship room at 393 NE 59th Street in Little River. In 2025 it marked its tenth anniversary — a long run in a category where most venues are younger than the trend that produced them.

Everything served is plant-based and zero-proof: fresh-brewed traditional kava, herbal teas, house-brewed yerba mate, specialty coffee and pressed ginger shots. The named pours have the loose humour of a room that grew out of a house rather than a business plan — the Cheech, Mr. T, Icey Tea, the Fruity Rooty kava shot.

What it has become is a hub for Miami's creative community, hosting open mics, live music and local art showcases. That matters more than the drinks list for the audience this directory serves: a venue that started as somebody's house and became an arts space has a social gravity a newly opened wellness lounge has to spend years building. For an artist, a musician or anyone sober-curious in Little River, it functions as the default room rather than the alternative one.

The caveat that belongs on every kava listing applies here and should not be softened: kava is psychoactive and sedating, with documented case reports of liver injury, and kratom acts on opioid receptors and carries real dependence and withdrawal risk. Everything served is free of alcohol. That is a narrower claim than nothing served having an effect, and for anyone whose reason for avoiding alcohol is recovery from a substance-use disorder, the difference is the whole question.
venues.pressQuote: Even during a pandemic, the Kava bar and vegan eatery seems to be making headway with exciting shows that turn newcomers into regulars overnight
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Caplin News (FIU), April 2021, on the venue's earlier Roots Miami Kava room

venues.name: Michael’s Genuine Food & Drink
venues.description: Michael's Genuine Food & Drink is chef Michael Schwartz's flagship neighborhood restaurant in Miami's Design District, open since 2007. A James Beard Award winner (Best Chef: South, 2010), Schwartz built the room around fresh, local, wood-fired cooking, and it carries a 2026 MICHELIN Guide Bib Gourmand. Its bar runs one of Miami's more developed zero-proof offerings: the Greater Miami CVB describes it as "one of the city's most robust zero-proof programs," built on house-made sodas, seasonal juice blends, and named non-alcoholic cocktails. Two confirmed spirit-free pours are the No-Proof Bulletproof, made with Lyre's American Malt, cherry-rosemary syrup and lemon, and Find Your Path, with Pathfinder hemp-derived non-alcoholic spirit, mint, citrus, and soda. The NA list sits inside a full-service bar rather than a dedicated alcohol-free venue, making it a comfortable fit for non-drinkers.
venues.longDescription:
Michael's Genuine Food & Drink has anchored the Miami Design District since 2007, and is the flagship of chef Michael Schwartz, who won the James Beard Award for Best Chef: South in 2010. The cooking is fresh, local and wood-fired, and the restaurant carries a Bib Gourmand in the 2026 MICHELIN Guide — a long run of relevance in a city whose restaurant scene turns over quickly.

The bar has been making house sodas and considered non-alcoholic drinks for years rather than adding them recently, which is the difference between a programme and a response to a trend. The Greater Miami Convention & Visitors Bureau describes it as one of the city's most robust zero-proof programmes, built on house-made sodas, seasonal juice blends and named alcohol-free cocktails.

Two confirmed pours show the range. The No-Proof Bulletproof is built on Lyre's American Malt with cherry-rosemary syrup and lemon — a whiskey-shaped drink rather than a fruit one, which is the harder thing to do without alcohol. Find Your Path uses Pathfinder, the hemp-derived non-alcoholic spirit, with mint, citrus and soda.

House-made sodas deserve particular note. They are the least glamorous item on any bar list and among the most useful to a non-drinker: a made soda is a drink somebody built, served in a proper glass, at a price that signals it counts. It is the difference between being served and being accommodated.

The list sits inside a full-service bar rather than a dedicated alcohol-free venue, which makes it an easy room for a mixed table — a neighbourhood restaurant where the person not drinking has a genuine choice rather than a concession. The Design District location makes it an easy lunch as well as a dinner, and the bar is comfortable to sit at alone.
venues.pressQuote: One of the city's most robust zero-proof programs.

venues.name: Middle Park Hotel
venues.description: This heritage bayside gastropub near Albert Park keeps a genuine booze-free option going behind the bar. Alongside alcohol-free beer and wine, Middle Park Hotel pours a zero-proof Espresso Martini built on cold-drip coffee, vanilla and Lyre's organic cane and coffee spirits, earning it a spot on Broadsheet's roundup of Melbourne's best non-alcoholic bars.
signatureDrinks: Espresso Martini - cold-drip coffee, vanilla and Lyre's organic cane and coffee spirits
venues.longDescription:
The Middle Park Hotel is a heritage corner pub on Canterbury Road in the bayside suburb of Middle Park, a short stroll from Albert Park Lake and Port Phillip Bay. Run by Australian Venue Co, it spreads across multiple bars and dining rooms plus a beer garden and boutique accommodation, trading as a relaxed gastropub built around classic Australian pub cooking and fresh seafood.

Broadsheet names it among Melbourne's best non-alcoholic bars, noting that "aside from the booze-free beer and wine, there's always a cocktail (or two) behind the bar at this gastropub." The house recommendation is a zero-proof Espresso Martini mixing cold-drip coffee, vanilla and Lyre's organic cane and coffee spirits - a proper build rather than a token soda, backed by a rotating selection of alcohol-free beer, wine, sparkling and spritzes.

Open seven days for lunch and dinner, the hotel suits a long table over a dozen oysters or a fireside cocktail as easily as a spot in the sun in the beer garden, making it an easy place for a non-drinker to order something considered rather than settle for a lemonade.
venues.pressQuote: Aside from the booze-free beer and wine, there's always a cocktail (or two) behind the bar at this gastropub. We recommend the Espresso Martini, mixing cold-drip coffee, vanilla and Lyre's organic cane and coffee spirits.

venues.name: Midnight Cowboy
venues.description: Midnight Cowboy is one of Austin's oldest and most well-known speakeasies, opened in 2012 in a 313 E 6th Street building that previously housed a brothel masquerading as a massage parlor — Midnight Cowboy Modeling Oriental Massage — and the venue embraces that history rather than hiding it. Entry is by reservation only: guests receive a code name from a Prohibition-era bartender (e.g. Harry Craddock), then push the corresponding button at the unmarked door, ring the bell, and are escorted to one of nine intimate booths for a one-to-two-hour cocktail experience. Drinks are crafted tableside via a bar cart with theatrical presentation, and recent menus have followed themed concepts (a tarot-inspired menu, for example) that span stirred classics, martinis, sours, tiki variations, and zero-proof creations. ATX Today's January 2026 Austin mocktails roundup specifically highlights Midnight Cowboy's zero-proof program, which uses alcohol-free gin and whiskey to build full cocktail experiences rather than juice-based mocktails. Cocktails are $14–$16, with discounts for ordering multiples of the same drink. Located in the heart of 6th Street nightlife, Midnight Cowboy is the quiet, intentional exception on an otherwise raucous block.
venues.longDescription:
Midnight Cowboy is among Austin's oldest and best-known speakeasies, opened in 2012 at 313 East 6th Street in a building that previously housed a brothel operating as a massage parlour under the name Midnight Cowboy Modeling Oriental Massage. The bar kept the name and the neon, which is the more honest choice than scrubbing it.

Entry is by reservation only and deliberately theatrical. Guests are given a code name drawn from a Prohibition-era bartender — Harry Craddock, for instance — then press the corresponding button at an unmarked door, ring the bell, and are escorted to one of nine booths for a session of an hour or two. Drinks are built tableside from a bar cart. Menus follow themed concepts, one recent list organised around tarot, spanning stirred classics, martinis, sours, tiki and zero-proof builds. Cocktails run fourteen to sixteen dollars, with a discount for ordering multiples of the same drink.

The zero-proof drinks use alcohol-free gin and whiskey to construct full cocktails rather than juice-based mocktails, which in a room where the drink is assembled in front of you is the only approach that would work — a bar cart has nowhere to hide.

The booth format is the real argument for coming here as a non-drinker. There is no bar to stand at, no rounds, a fixed seating time and a table of your own on a block that is otherwise the loudest in Texas. Midnight Cowboy is the quiet, intentional exception on 6th Street, and that structure does more for an evening without alcohol than any single drink can.

One caveat worth stating: the published zero-proof selections are not a fixed named list and rotate with the themed menus, so at least one third-party menu listing shows no non-alcoholic section at all. Mention when booking that you want zero-proof drinks and the bar can plan the session around it. Open Tuesday to Saturday evenings.
venues.pressQuote: This Downtown speakeasy offers a zero-proof menu in a moody setting, with alcohol-free gin and whiskey drinks.

venues.name: Midnight Morning
venues.description: Midnight Morning is an all-day cafe, bar and restaurant at 14 Birch Street in Roslindale Village, opened in 2023 by owner Virginia Schubert in the space that had long housed Birch Street Bistro. Schubert worked in design before moving into hospitality, and the business is certified with the City of Boston as a Minority Business Enterprise, Woman Business Enterprise and Small Local Business Enterprise. The kitchen, led by executive chef Rory Lee, runs a made-from-scratch seasonal menu across breakfast, lunch, dinner and weekend brunch. The bar keeps a standing Zero Proof section of four cocktails at $10, all built on non-alcoholic spirits rather than juice: Remember Me with AMASS Riverine, Bad Decisions with Everleaf Forest, Threat Level Midnight with Zero Zero Amaro and cold brew, and the Arbore'rum with Ritual Proof Rum. Two non-alcoholic beers are poured alongside them.
signatureDrinks: Remember Me (AMASS Riverine, lemon, honey, aquafaba) $10
Bad Decisions (Everleaf Forest, lime, lemongrass, orange blossom) $10
Threat Level Midnight (Zero Zero Amaro, cold brew, condensed milk) $10
Arbore'rum (Ritual Proof Rum, lime, pomegranate, rose, ginger beer) $10
Kit 'On Your Mark' non-alcoholic American blonde, gluten removed $8
venues.longDescription:
Midnight Morning opened in 2023 at 14 Birch Street in Roslindale Village, taking over the premises of the longtime Birch Street Bistro. Its owner, Virginia Schubert, came to the business from a career in design and built it around a single format problem: that Roslindale had few places that could carry a customer from morning coffee through to a late drink without changing venue. The name states the ambition. The restaurant is certified in the City of Boston's Supplier Diversity Program as a Minority Business Enterprise, Woman Business Enterprise and Small Local Business Enterprise, and the kitchen is run by executive chef Rory Lee on a globally inflected, made-from-scratch menu that turns over with the seasons. The Boston Globe profiled it on October 12, 2023, describing the house cocktail list — the margarita-adjacent Captain Crunch made with corn liqueur, and the Honey Oats, a daiquiri topped with oat milk foam — and recording that there are also several zero-proof offerings.

The day starts as a cafe and the coffee programme is not an afterthought. The printed cafe menu runs drip, decaf drip, cafe au lait, iced coffee, cold brew and iced decaf; a rotating pour-over selection that has recently included Banda Rebelde and E.A. Decaf Popayan; a full espresso bar of americanos, lattes, cappuccinos, cortados and flat whites; and matcha, chai and Rishi teas. House favourites listed at the top of the board include a grapefruit and orange blossom espresso tonic, a dark chocolate mocha latte and a sparkling matcha lemonade — all alcohol-free drinks built with the same care as a cocktail. Behind that sits a house-made syrup and sweetener range covering vanilla bean, dark chocolate, dulce de leche, real maple, honey syrup and cold foam. In the evening that same care goes into a standing Zero Proof section on the printed drink menu, four cocktails priced at $10 alongside the alcoholic house list rather than tucked beneath it: Remember Me, built on AMASS Riverine with lemon, honey and aquafaba; Bad Decisions, on Everleaf Forest with lime, lemongrass and orange blossom; Threat Level Midnight, which pulls the cafe and the bar together with Zero Zero Amaro, cold brew and condensed milk; and the Arbore'rum, on Ritual Proof Rum with lime, pomegranate, rose and ginger beer. Two non-alcoholic beers are poured as well, Lagunitas IPNA and Kit's gluten-removed On Your Mark blonde, both at $8. Food runs from a breakfast menu served until 4pm through lunch sandwiches and salads to a dinner list of pastas and larger plates. The restaurant opens at 8am on weekdays and 10am at weekends, and runs to 12:30am on Fridays.
venues.pressQuote: There are also several zero-proof offerings.

venues.name: Mijo Modern Mexican
venues.description: Mijo Modern Mexican is a coastal Mexican restaurant inside Durango Casino & Resort in the southwest Las Vegas valley, serving a progressive menu of prime meats, whole fish, and elevated street-food favorites across multiple dining rooms and a greenery-framed patio. While the bar is known for an extensive tequila and mezcal program, its cocktail menu carries a dedicated "Zero Proof" section of crafted mocktails priced at $13. The standout is the Watermelon Cooler, which uses Almave Blanco non-alcoholic tequila with watermelon, lime, and soda, alongside options like Pinky's Up (hibiscus, passion fruit, pineapple, soda) and Nice Mangos (mango, lime, agave, ginger beer). The restaurant was highlighted in Las Vegas Weekly's January 2026 Dry January guide for these alcohol-free offerings. Weekend brunch runs Saturday and Sunday from 10am to 3pm.
venues.address: 6915 S Durango Dr, Las Vegas, NV 89148

Pinky's Up (hibiscus, passion fruit, pineapple, soda)
Nice Mangos (mango, lime, agave, ginger beer)

venues.longDescription:
Mijo Modern Mexican opened on 5 December 2023 as part of the debut of Durango Casino & Resort, Station Casinos' property in the far southwest Las Vegas valley, and it was one of the first restaurants at Durango to draw serious attention on its own terms. It comes from the Las Vegas-born Clique Hospitality, with Donald Thompson II heading the kitchen after years with Clique at Hearthstone. The cooking is coastal Mexican and wood-grill-driven: whole fresh fish, prime meats, ceviches, house-made tortillas and elevated street-food dishes, served across several dining rooms and a patio framed in greenery. The bar's reputation rests on an extensive tequila and mezcal list, which is precisely what makes the other half of the program notable.

Rather than leaving non-drinkers to the soda gun in an agave-focused room, Mijo runs a dedicated Zero Proof section of crafted mocktails at $13. The standout is the Watermelon Cooler, built on Almave Blanco — the non-alcoholic blue agave distillate co-created by Lewis Hamilton — with watermelon, lime and soda, which puts a genuine agave-flavoured drink in front of someone who cannot or does not drink tequila. Alongside it sit Pinky's Up (hibiscus, passion fruit, pineapple and soda) and Nice Mangos (mango, lime, agave and ginger beer). Las Vegas Weekly featured the restaurant in its January 2026 Dry January guide on the strength of those offerings, calling it a sun-drenched escape without the plane ticket and the crown jewel of the southwest. Because Durango sits about twenty minutes off the Strip and serves a largely local clientele, Mijo functions as a genuine neighbourhood option for an alcohol-free night out rather than a tourist stop, with dinner nightly and brunch service at the weekend.
venues.pressQuote: For a sun-drenched escape without the plane ticket, head to Mijo Modern Mexican at Durango, the crown jewel of the southwest.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Las Vegas Weekly, Dry January guide

venues.name: Mikkeller Brewpub London
venues.description: Mikkeller Brewpub London is the Danish cult brewery's two-floor Exmouth Market brewpub, opened in 2019 in collaboration with pop singer Rick Astley and built around an on-site 7.5-hectolitre brewery that feeds 20 ever-changing taps. Roughly half the taps pour beer brewed on the premises, and the line-up always keeps at least one non-alcoholic beer on draught, including Mikkeller's own alcohol-free IPA that reviewers say drinks like the full-strength original rather than a compromise. Because Mikkeller is one of the most respected names in low- and no-alcohol brewing, the NA pour here is a genuine draught option beside the food, not a token soft drink.
venues.longDescription:
Mikkeller Brewpub London opened on Exmouth Market in Clerkenwell in October 2019, a year after the Danish brewery's first London bar in Shoreditch, and was launched in collaboration with the singer Rick Astley, whose partnership with founder Mikkel Borg Bjergsø had already produced beers such as their Astley's Amber Ale. It began as a pop-up pouring from 20 taps before the on-site brewery and restaurant came fully online, with fresh beer eventually flowing directly from the tanks and a kitchen inspired by Mikkeller's Copenhagen venues. Mikkeller is one of the most influential names in modern craft brewing, a "gypsy"-turned-bricks-and-mortar operation with an international bar network, which makes this one of the more pedigreed brewpubs in the city.

The venue occupies two floors and about 264 square metres, with a raw, industrial feel softened by the brand's signature quirks; as its creative director put it, "this is not a restaurant with a brewery, it is a brewery with a restaurant." The compact 7.5-hectolitre brewhouse sits on site and normally supplies around half of the 20 draught lines, with the remainder split between other Mikkeller beers and rotating guests, so the tap list changes constantly and the room carries the smell of malt and hops. It sits in the middle of Exmouth Market's pedestrianised run of restaurants and stalls, a short walk from Farringdon and Angel.

Crucially for non-drinkers, the brewpub keeps at least one non-alcoholic beer on draught at all times, so there is always a real zero- or low-alcohol pour to have alongside the food rather than a fridge afterthought. The standout is an alcohol-free IPA that reviewers single out as tasting like a proper IPA with no sense of compromise. That credibility is backed by Mikkeller's own extensive non-alcoholic range, brewed at around 0.3% ABV and led by its widely stocked flagship Drink'in the Sun, a bright, citrus- and pine-forward wheat ale, so the alcohol-free beer here comes from a brewer that treats NA as a serious category in its own right.

venues.name: Miku Toronto
venues.description: Miku Toronto is an Aburi-style Japanese sushi restaurant on the Harbourfront, occupying more than 7,000 square feet inside WaterPark Place on Bay Street with a raw bar, sushi bar, and large patio. It opened in 2015 as ABURI Restaurants' first East Coast location, following the group's expansion from Japan to Vancouver. Alongside its wine and sake program, Miku carries what Foodism.ca calls "a substantial section of zero-proof drinks," including non-alcoholic wine, non-alcoholic beer, and named mocktails such as the yuzu-elderflower-lavender Tōji Fizz.
venues.address: 10 Bay St #105, Toronto, ON M5J 2R8, Canada (WaterPark Place)
signatureDrinks: Tōji Fizz — yuzu, elderflower, and lavender (described by Foodism as "a floral lemonade")
venues.longDescription:
Miku Toronto occupies a large, contemporary space inside WaterPark Place on Bay Street, at the edge of the city's Harbourfront near Queen's Quay in the Southern Financial District. The restaurant spans more than 7,000 square feet and is built around a raw bar, a dedicated sushi bar, and a large patio, matching its billing as "Toronto's First & Finest Home of Aburi Sushi."

It opened in 2015 as the first East Coast location for ABURI Restaurants, the Japanese hospitality group that developed its flame-seared aburi sushi technique in Japan before expanding to Vancouver and then Toronto. The kitchen pairs that searing technique with contemporary Japanese cooking across several formats — an omakase-style sushi bar, seasonal tasting menus, and kaiseki-style multi-course dining — under the restaurant's "Ningenmi" philosophy of finding joy in life by bringing joy to others.

Alongside its wine, sake, and cocktail program, Miku runs a genuine zero-proof section rather than a token mocktail or two. Foodism.ca, surveying Toronto's best non-alcoholic drink menus, singled out Miku for carrying "a substantial section of zero-proof drinks," including non-alcoholic wine from Oddbird and non-alcoholic beer from Asahi and Bellwoods alongside named mocktails. The standout, per Foodism, is the Tōji Fizz — yuzu, elderflower, and lavender — a drink the outlet described as "a floral lemonade."
venues.pressQuote: They also have a substantial section of zero-proof drinks. Find non-alcoholic wine (Oddbird), non-alcoholic beer (Asahi and Bellwoods) and mocktails on the list. My favourite drink on the menu is the Tōji Fizz, a yuzu, elderflower and lavender concoction that drinks like a floral lemonade.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Foodism.ca — 9 of the best mocktail and non-alcoholic drink menus in Toronto

venues.name: Mint Coffeehouse
venues.description: Mint Coffeehouse is a Middle Eastern-influenced cafe on Lawrenceville Highway in Tucker, opened on 15 August 2024 by the husband-and-wife team Ahmad and Marianna Alzoukani as the bricks-and-mortar home of their existing catering and mobile espresso business. Ahmad is Syrian, and the decor and part of the menu reflect that: Syrian-inspired fittings, and manaeesh flatbread with cheese and vegetables sold next to the toasts and pastries. Coffee is a Colombian blend used for both espresso and drip. The house drinks are the Mint Mocha Latte and an in-house chai latte, with matcha, cold brew and fruit smoothies alongside. No alcohol is served. Hours are daytime only, which is why this is a strong daytime alternative rather than a going-out room.
venues.longDescription:
Ahmad and Marianna Alzoukani ran a catering and mobile-espresso company before they took the lease at 3926 Lawrenceville Highway, and Mint Coffeehouse — نعنع on the sign — opened as a full-service cafe on 15 August 2024. 285 South folded it into its March 2025 survey of the Middle Eastern cafes reshaping metro Atlanta's coffee scene, noting that the pair had brought the shop to Tucker alongside fellow newcomer Mokhaport. Ahmad's Syrian heritage is written into the room: the decor is Syrian-inspired, and the food menu carries manaeesh, the flatbread baked with cheese and vegetables, next to the toasts, quick bites and pastries a conventional American cafe would stock. Catering and the mobile espresso cart still run out of the same business, serving the wider Atlanta area.

The drinks are straightforward and honestly priced rather than elaborate. A Colombian blend is used for both the espresso and the drip coffee. The Mint Mocha Latte is the house special the owners point first-timers towards, and the chai latte is made in-house rather than poured from a concentrate — a small distinction that matters in a category where most cafes do the opposite. Matcha, cold brew and fruit smoothies including a strawberry-banana fill out the board, and oat milk is stocked. There is no alcohol on the premises and no licence. What keeps Mint at a four rather than a five on our scale is simply the clock: it trades 7:30am to 6pm on weekdays, 8am to 5pm on Saturday and closes on Sunday, so it functions as a daytime third place — a good one, in a suburb short of independent options — rather than as an evening destination the way the later-trading Yemeni coffeehouses elsewhere in the metro do. For anyone in east DeKalb looking for a substantial, alcohol-free room to meet in during the day, it is among the best available.
venues.pressQuote: In August, Syrian founders Ahmad and Marianna Alzoukani brought Mint Coffeehouse to Tucker—where it joined fellow newcomer Mokhaport.

venues.name: Mint Mark
venues.description: Mint Mark is a near-east-side restaurant and bar that moved from its small Winnebago Street room to a larger space on East Washington Avenue, and it runs one of the zero-proof menus Madison's food press names first. The drinks carry the same off-kilter humour as the rest of the operation — "What Is This, A Titleist?" and "Narrow Straits" are both standing alcohol-free builds. The venue runs three distinct services under one roof: coffee on weekday mornings from 7am, dinner from 5pm, and a bar that stays open to 2am Monday through Saturday, which makes it usable at almost any hour a non-drinker might want a room to be in.
venues.longDescription:
Mint Mark built its reputation in a small room on Winnebago Street on Madison's near east side, doing a short, precise menu of shared plates with a bar programme that took itself seriously without being solemn, and has since moved to a larger space at 1874 East Washington Avenue in Emerson East. The move is worth knowing because older listings and several guides still point at the Winnebago address.

The zero-proof drinks are among the most consistently cited in Madison. "What Is This, A Titleist?" and "Narrow Straits" both sit on the standing menu, and the names tell you something real about the programme: they are written in the same voice as the cocktails, which in practice is the clearest signal that the alcohol-free drinks were developed alongside the rest of the list rather than appended to it. City Cast Madison names both in its guide to the city's best non-alcoholic cocktails, and the venue appears in Visit Madison's own round-up of high-end kitchens running zero-proof menus, alongside Merchant and Heritage Tavern.

The structure of the day is the practical selling point. Mint Mark runs coffee service on weekday mornings from 7am to 2pm, dinner from 5pm, and keeps the bar open until 2am Monday through Saturday. Very few venues anywhere in this registry cover that span, and for a non-drinker it means one room can be the morning coffee, the dinner and the late drink — which removes the awkward part of a night out, where everyone else moves on to a bar and you decide whether to follow. It sits about a mile north-east of the Capitol along East Washington, an easy walk or a short bus ride from the Square, with Public Parking on East Johnson roughly halfway between.
venues.pressQuote: Mint Mark's zero-proof cocktails include "What Is This, A Titleist?" and "Narrow Straits."

venues.name: Minus Moonshine
venues.description: The second Minus Moonshine bottle shop, on the corner of Driggs Avenue and Eckford Street in Greenpoint, Brooklyn. Like the original Prospect Heights store it is entirely alcohol-free: NA beer, wine, spirits, aperitifs, ready-to-drink cocktails, mixers and bitters, from a stock list the shop has been building since 2021 that includes Ghia, Seedlip, Kin Euphorics and Curious Elixirs. Minus Moonshine is Queer, Trans-Nonbinary, Indigenous and Autistic owned, and founder Aqxyl Storms has run both shops on a "drink what you love" premise — zero-proof versions of the drinks people actually miss, rather than substitutes framed as compromises. Open seven days a week, with same-day local delivery on orders placed online before 5pm.

naMenuItems.name: Kiki Light Wash — alcohol-removed, lightly sparkling, chillable red, 750 ml
Kin Euphorics — Lightwave, grounding calm 4 pack
Curious Elixirs — No. 2 - Spicy Pineapple Ginger
Curious Elixirs — No. 4 - Blood Orange Spritz

venues.longDescription:
The second Minus Moonshine sits on the corner of Driggs Avenue and Eckford Street in Greenpoint, and it extends to north Brooklyn the model the original built in Prospect Heights from 2021: a shop that looks and works like a neighbourhood bottle shop, where every single bottle is alcohol-free.

Greenpoint is a well-chosen second address. It is the densest concentration of alcohol-free venues anywhere in New York — Soft Bar, the fully alcohol-free cafe and cocktail bar on Banker Street, is minutes away, and Rule of Thirds and the wider Greenpoint bar strip sit around it. Someone spending an evening in the neighbourhood without drinking has, unusually, a genuine choice of rooms and a shop to take something home from afterwards. That density is what a functioning alcohol-free scene actually looks like, and it exists in very few places.

The stock list is the one founder Aqxyl Storms has been building since 2021: non-alcoholic beer, wine, spirits, aperitifs, ready-to-drink cocktails, mixers and bitters, taking in Ghia, Seedlip, Kin Euphorics and Curious Elixirs among many others. The premise is the same as the original's — "drink what you love", meaning zero-proof versions of the drinks people genuinely miss, sold as drinks rather than as health products or as consolation.

Minus Moonshine is Queer, Trans-Nonbinary, Indigenous and Autistic owned. The shop opens seven days a week and offers same-day local delivery on orders placed online before 5pm, which is a practical detail worth knowing if you are hosting: the most common reason people end up serving nothing but soda to non-drinking guests is that they left the decision too late to find anything better.

For visitors, the useful framing is that this shop and its Prospect Heights sibling are not competing with each other but covering two different halves of Brooklyn — north and central — with Spirited Away covering Manhattan. Together they are the reason New York's non-alcoholic retail is the deepest in the country.

venues.name: Minus Moonshine
venues.description: Minus Moonshine is a fully alcohol-free bottle shop in Prospect Heights, Brooklyn, opened in 2021 by founder Aqxyl Storms — making it one of New York City's earliest dedicated zero-proof package shops. From the street it reads like a neighborhood liquor store, but every bottle is non-alcoholic: NA beer, wine, spirits, aperitifs, mixers, bitters, and adaptogenic "potions." Inventory spans well-known zero-proof names including Ghia, Seedlip, Kin Euphorics, and Curious Elixirs, alongside NA wines and CBD/adaptogen spritzers. The shop is Queer, Trans-Nonbinary, Indigenous and Autistic owned, and is built around the idea of "drink what you love" — non-alcoholic whiskey, wine and aperitivo for sober and sober-curious customers, rather than substitutes framed as compromises. A second Brooklyn shop is open in Greenpoint, at 257 Driggs Ave.

Kin Euphorics — Lightwave, Grounding Calm 4 Pack
Curious Elixirs — No. 2 - Spicy Pineapple Ginger
Curious Elixirs — No. 4 - Blood Orange Spritz

venues.longDescription:
Minus Moonshine opened on Sterling Place in Prospect Heights in 2021, which makes it one of the earliest dedicated zero-proof package shops in New York City and, alongside Spirited Away in Chelsea, one of the two anchors of non-alcoholic retail in the five boroughs. Founder Aqxyl Storms built it to read like a neighbourhood liquor store from the street — shelves, bottles, the ordinary furniture of a place that sells drink — with the single difference that nothing in it contains meaningful alcohol.

That design choice is the whole argument. A great deal of non-alcoholic retail presents itself as wellness: pale packaging, adaptogen language, the visual grammar of a supplement shop. Minus Moonshine deliberately does not. The shop's own premise is "drink what you love" — non-alcoholic whiskey, wine and aperitivo for people who miss those specific things, rather than substitutes framed as a compromise or a health decision. For a lot of people who have stopped drinking, being sold a wellness product is its own small indignity; being sold a good bottle is not.

The range covers NA beer, wine, spirits, aperitifs, mixers, bitters and the shop's adaptogenic "potions", with the category's established names — Ghia, Seedlip, Kin Euphorics, Curious Elixirs — alongside non-alcoholic wines and CBD and adaptogen spritzers. It is a genuinely browsable selection rather than a token shelf, which matters because the category's prices are high enough that a blind purchase can put someone off the whole idea.

The shop is Queer, Trans-Nonbinary, Indigenous and Autistic owned, and its ownership is not incidental to how it operates: sobriety and sober-curiosity cut across communities that conventional bar culture has often served badly, and a shop run from inside those communities reads differently to the people in them.

A second Minus Moonshine trades in Greenpoint at 257 Driggs Avenue, also listed in this guide. Between the two of them and Spirited Away, a New Yorker can now buy good non-alcoholic drink in person, from someone who can answer questions about it, in three different parts of the city — which was true of nowhere in America a decade ago.

venues.name: Mirador
venues.description: Mirador, the penthouse restaurant atop the former Forty Five Ten department store in Downtown Dallas, refreshed its menu for 2026 with a wellness-minded direction that includes three spirit-free mocktails built like the kitchen's cocktails. The lineup leads with the Main Squeeze (passion fruit, coconut, orgeat and citrus finished with a splash of Topo Chico), the Citrus Sparkler (berry cordial, citrus and mint over mineral water), and the Smoked Milk Tea, which layers Fujian Province smoked lapsang souchong with creamy coconut milk, rosemary honey, strawberry and lime. These are composed, ingredient-driven builds served alongside the lunch and afternoon-tea service, not afterthought sodas.

signatureDrinks: Main Squeeze — passion fruit, coconut, orgeat and citrus, finished with a splash of Topo Chico
Citrus Sparkler — berry cordial, citrus and mint, topped with mineral water
Smoked Milk Tea — Fujian Province smoked lapsang souchong, creamy coconut milk, rosemary honey, strawberry and lime
venues.longDescription:
Mirador occupies the top-floor penthouse of the building that housed luxury retailer Forty Five Ten at 1608 Elm Street, in Downtown Dallas' Main Street District. The restaurant closed during the pandemic and reopened in December 2023, repositioning away from dinner service toward brunch, lunch and a signature afternoon tea in its lofty, light-filled dining room.

For 2026, Mirador leaned into wellness with a health-conscious menu refresh — crudo, a farro bowl, lobster Cobb salad and chicken paillard — anchored by a trio of refreshing spirit-free mocktails. DiningOut's Dry January guide singled out the Main Squeeze (passion fruit, coconut, orgeat and citrus, finished with a splash of Topo Chico), the Citrus Sparkler (a bright blend of berry cordial, citrus and mint kept fizzy with mineral water), and the standout Smoked Milk Tea, which layers Fujian Province smoked lapsang souchong with creamy coconut milk, rosemary honey, strawberry and lime.

Mirador is open Tuesday through Saturday for lunch and afternoon tea and closed Sundays and Mondays; a sister location, Café Mirador, opened in Fort Worth's Cultural District in March 2026.
venues.pressQuote: Power lunch with one of three refreshing spirit-free mocktails such as the Main Squeeze, a mix of passion fruit, coconut, orgeat, and citrus, finished with a splash of Topo Chico.

venues.name: Mírate
venues.description: IMPORTANT CORRECTION — WE HAVE REMOVED THIS VENUE'S LISTED DRINKS. Mírate is an award-winning multi-level Oaxaca-inspired restaurant and mezcalería in Los Feliz from co-owner Matthew Egan and chef Joshua Gil, opened in late November 2022, ranked No.12 in North America's 50 Best Bars in 2025 and No.28 in 2026. We previously listed its Tepache and Nitro Pulque as non-alcoholic drinks. That was wrong. They sit in a section called "Bebidas Ancestral" — ancestral beverages — which appears between the cocktail list and the Mexican wine list as another alcoholic category, alongside Pasita, a Mexican rum-raisin liqueur. Nothing on the menu describes them as non-alcoholic or prints an ABV. Pulque is traditionally 4–7% ABV, roughly beer strength; tepache varies with ferment length. Beverage director Max Reis says he takes pride in offering them "in their authentic format" so guests can taste "the ingredient in its pure form", and the same tepache and pulque are used inside the bar's alcoholic cocktails. We found no dedicated alcohol-free section here. Ask the bar directly rather than ordering from Bebidas Ancestral expecting zero proof.
venues.address: 1712 N Vermont Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90027
venues.longDescription:
Mírate opened in late November 2022 in Los Feliz, the second project from co-owner Matthew Egan and chef Joshua Gil after Beverly Hills' Mírame, and it is a genuinely spectacular room. Egan's description of the effect is accurate: people's jaws drop when they round the corner of the bar and see what is hidden behind the storefront. The space runs to 7,500 square feet across several levels — a quieter, darker agave bar upstairs, the livelier Bar Mírate downstairs, and a mezzanine dining deck with a roof that opens, built around a tree in a planted atrium. Its bar programme is one of the most decorated in the country: it debuted on North America's 50 Best Bars in 2024, climbed thirty-four places to No.12 in 2025 — taking Best Bar in West USA and the Highest Climber award — and sits at No.28 in 2026. Beverage director Max Reis sets the tone at the top of the agave list: no additives, no celebrities, no bullshit.

We owe readers a correction, and it is the reason this entry has been downgraded. We previously listed Mírate's Tepache and Nitro Pulque as its non-alcoholic drinks. They are not presented that way, and the evidence points the other direction. They sit in a section headed Bebidas Ancestral — ancestral beverages — printed between the classic cocktails and the Mexican wines, as one more alcoholic category; the third item beside them is Pasita, a rum-raisin liqueur from Puebla. No part of the menu calls them non-alcoholic, and no ABV is printed. Pulque, fermented from agave sap, is traditionally somewhere around 4–7% ABV, which is beer strength; tepache's alcohol depends entirely on how long it has fermented and can be anywhere from negligible to several per cent. Reis has said he takes immense pride in offering them in their authentic format, so that someone who enjoys them in a cocktail can then taste the ingredient in its pure form — and the bar does exactly that, pouring both into fully alcoholic drinks elsewhere on the list. North America's 50 Best Bars describes the same items plainly as pre-Hispanic fermented beverages. So we have removed them. We could not find a dedicated alcohol-free section at Mírate at all. A bar this good will almost certainly build you something excellent without alcohol — but ask, rather than ordering from Bebidas Ancestral and assuming.
venues.pressQuote: This labyrinth of a Mexican restaurant in Los Feliz looks like a luxurious, multi-story treehouse built for a billionaire evading the IRS in the jungle.

venues.name: Miru
venues.description: Miru is the Japanese restaurant on the eleventh floor of the St. Regis Chicago in Lakeshore East, looking out over the mouth of the Chicago River toward Navy Pier and Lake Michigan, and it runs one of the deepest hotel-restaurant zero-proof lists in the city. A Spirit Free heading on the cocktail menu holds six drinks at $14-$16: Setting Sun with fresh yuzu, Valencia orange, lychee and soda; Sunny Day with lemon, passionfruit, rice cordial and ginger beer; an N/A Rita of agave, fresh lime and sea salt; a Phony Negroni Bianco; an N/Aperol Spritz built on Lyre's Italian Orange and Lyre's sparkling; and a Coffee Cloud of Metropolis cold brew, demerara and vanilla. A separate zero-proof wine list carries Prima Pave and Oddbird by the glass and bottle.

venues.longDescription:
Miru occupies the eleventh floor of the St. Regis Chicago, the Jeanne Gang tower at 401 E Wacker Drive where the Chicago River meets Lake Michigan, and the room is designed around the view: rich wood, floor-to-ceiling glass and a summer terrace that faces Navy Pier. The kitchen works through nigiri, sashimi and maki, a robata section of smoked pork belly and charred octopus skewers, and larger plates such as white miso black cod, with desserts by pastry chef Juan Gutierrez. Service runs from 7am breakfast through a 2pm-5pm lounge menu into dinner, which means the bar list is available across the whole day.

That bar list is where the restaurant earns its place here. A Spirit Free section sits directly beneath the seasonal and classic cocktails and runs to six drinks rather than the usual one or two. Setting Sun combines fresh yuzu, Valencia orange, lychee and soda at $14; Sunny Day pairs lemon and passionfruit with a rice cordial and ginger beer, also $14; the N/A Rita strips a margarita back to agave, fresh lime and sea salt at $14; the Coffee Cloud uses Metropolis cold brew with demerara and vanilla at $14. Two are built on bottled non-alcoholic products - a $16 Phony Negroni Bianco using St. Agrestis's white expression, and an N/Aperol Spritz at $14 made with Lyre's Italian Orange and Lyre's sparkling. Beyond the cocktails, a zero-proof wine list carries Prima Pave brut blanc de blancs, brut rose and brut rose dolce in 200ml at $18 each, plus Oddbird's Presence gewurztraminer blend and GSM by the glass at $14 and bottle at $56, and the daytime menu adds cold-pressed juices. A non-drinker at a celebration table here has as many decisions to make as anyone else. Breakfast runs from 7am, a lounge menu covers 2pm to 5pm and dinner starts at 5pm, so the Spirit Free list can be ordered at almost any point in the day rather than only at dinner service. In summer the terrace is first come, first served and faces the Navy Pier fireworks on Wednesday and Saturday evenings.
venues.pressQuote: On the 11th floor of the St. Regis Chicago, Miru pairs breathtaking views with upscale Japanese cuisine.

venues.name: Miss Angeline's
venues.description: Miss Angeline's on Denton's downtown square runs the deepest non-alcoholic cocktail list in the metroplex: a printed Non-Alcoholic Drinks section with eight named mocktails, nearly all built on Lyre's non-alcoholic spirits. The range covers a MockaRita, a French 86, a PiNO Colada, an EspressotiNO and a NOgroni — meaning a non-drinker can order across the whole cocktail canon rather than picking from two. Six taps and cans back it up, including Guinness Zero and four Athletic Brewing beers. Open daily until 2am.

French 86 (Lyre's gin alternative, raspberry, lemon, soda)
EspressotiNO (Lyre's coffee liqueur alternative, cold brew, cream)
NOgroni (Lyre's gin alternative, Italian orange, aperitif rosso)

venues.longDescription:
Denton's downtown square is a college-town drinking district, and Miss Angeline's has quietly built the most complete non-alcoholic cocktail programme anywhere in the metroplex. The menu carries a printed Non-Alcoholic Drinks section split into Mocktails and Beers & Seltzers, and the mocktail half runs to eight named builds — four times what a typical Dallas zero-proof list offers.

Almost all of them are built on Lyre's, the Australian non-alcoholic spirit range that produces analogues across the whole back bar, and the list uses that breadth deliberately. There is a MockaRita on the agave spirit, a French 86 on the gin, a PiNO Colada on the rum, an AmarettNO Sour, an EspressotiNO on the coffee liqueur, and a NOgroni built with Italian orange and an aperitif rosso. A Cranberry Spritz uses Clean Co.'s vodka alternative. The practical effect is that a non-drinker at this bar chooses a drink the way everyone else does — by mood and style, not by whichever single mocktail exists.

The Dallas Observer noted the commitment behind it, counting six taps given over to non-alcoholic alternatives. Those include Guinness Zero and four Athletic Brewing beers alongside root beer and kombucha. It is a full bar serving alcohol, and the same menu block also lists THC seltzers, which are non-alcoholic but intoxicating and worth knowing about. Doors are open every day until 2am.
venues.pressQuote: Six [taps] fulfilling a commitment to offering nonalcoholic alternatives

venues.name: Mita's
venues.description: Mita's is James Beard-nominated chef Jose Salazar's Spanish and Latin American tapas restaurant in downtown Cincinnati's 84.51° building at Fifth and Race. Its drinks list carries a dedicated "No Alcoholicas" section built on Ritual's zero-proof tequila alternative: the Sacrificio pairs it with guava, hibiscus, and lime, while the Paloma Picante adds grapefruit, jalapeño, ginger, agave, lime, and soda for a spicy, citrus-forward pour (both $12.50). Beyond the house mocktails, the kitchen stocks Best Day Brewing non-alcoholic beer in lime cerveza or West Coast IPA, plus Leitz Eins-Zwei-Zero non-alcoholic sparkling wine, alongside Jarritos and Mexican fountain sodas. It's a genuine sit-down alcohol-free option inside one of the city's most ambitious tapas rooms, named for Salazar's Colombian grandmother.
