venues.longDescription:
Mita's opened in 2015 as the second restaurant from James Beard-nominated chef Jose Salazar, following his flagship Salazar in Over-the-Rhine. He named it for his Colombian grandmother, Martha Mejia de Toro — his "Mita" — recalling summers in Medellín watching her grind white masa into the arepas and empanadas that now anchor the menu. The 130-seat dining room sits in the 84.51° building at Fifth and Race, and pays homage to the traditional and modern food of Spain and Latin America: tapas, ceviches, cured hams, cheeses, and a Valencian-style paella for two. Cincinnati Magazine reviewed it warmly and later ranked it among the city's best restaurants.

The non-alcoholic offering lives in a clearly labeled "No Alcoholicas" section of the cocktail-and-beer list. Two house mocktails are built on Ritual Zero Proof's tequila alternative: the Sacrificio (guava, hibiscus, lime) and the Paloma Picante (grapefruit, jalapeño, ginger, agave nectar, lime, soda), each $12.50. The kitchen also pours Best Day Brewing non-alcoholic beer in lime cerveza or West Coast IPA ($7) and Leitz Eins-Zwei-Zero non-alcoholic sparkling wine ($13), plus Jarritos, Mexican fountain sodas, Deeper Roots coffee, and Churchill's Fine Teas for zero-proof drinkers.

Mita's serves dinner Monday through Thursday 5–10pm and Friday and Saturday 4–10pm, with reservations available through OpenTable and a comfortable bar and lounge for walk-ins. It suits a date night or celebration where one person wants a full, flavor-driven tapas dinner without alcohol and still a real drink in hand. Note this is a restaurant bar rather than an alcohol-free venue, and the "No Alcoholicas" list is a short, curated section — two mocktails plus NA beer and sparkling — that can shift as the seasonal cocktail menu changes.
venues.pressQuote: Deftly executed comfort food ripe with the flavors of the Spanish diaspora.

venues.name: Mitch e Amaro
venues.description: Mitch e Amaro is a cocktail-supply shop, specialty bottle store and bar opened in February 2019 by brothers Josh and Ben Edwards on Armour Road in North Kansas City, in the former Le Monde Bakery space. The centrepiece bar is an integral part of the store, separating the retail at the front from the lounge at the back, so it functions equally as a shop and as a place to sit and drink. Its printed "Non-Alcoholic" menu is priced flat at $10 — the same as many of its alcoholic cocktails — and is built almost entirely on Seedlip: Garden 108, Spice 94 and Grove 42 are each available with soda, tonic or Fever-Tree ginger beer, alongside built drinks including the Pen-No-Cillin (Spice 94, lemon, honey ginger syrup), the Garden Sour, the Rabarbar-Oh-No! Highball and Unbuzzed, made with cold brew from local roaster Colony. One item, Smoke & Spice, carries the bar's own printed note that its Bittermens habanero shrub contains a trace amount of alcohol. Retail shelves stock Bare Zero-Proof, Kin Euphorics and Ritual Zero-Proof.
venues.address: 306 Armour Rd, North Kansas City, MO 64116
signatureDrinks: Pen-No-Cillin (Seedlip Spice 94, lemon, honey ginger syrup) $10
Garden Sour (Seedlip Garden 108, lemon, simple syrup) $10
Rabarbar-Oh-No! Highball (Seedlip Grove 42, Fee Bros rhubarb bitters, lemon, simple, club soda) $10
Unbuzzed (Seedlip Spice 94, Colony cold brew, Fee Bros rhubarb bitters, simple syrup) $10
Spice & Ginger (Seedlip Spice 94, Fever-Tree ginger ale) $10
venues.longDescription:
Mitch e Amaro opened in February 2019 at 306 Armour Road in North Kansas City, in the former Le Monde Bakery, from brothers Josh and Ben Edwards. It is genuinely two businesses in one room: the centrepiece bar is an integral part of the store in both form and function, separating the retail at the front from the lounge at the back, so you can buy a bottle, buy a book about bottles, or sit down and have someone else make the drink. Josh is a career bartender who started the day after he turned 21 and has worked everything from big nightclubs to corporate restaurants; Ben describes himself as a software nerd and cocktail enthusiast who got into this because he ran out of room at home for bottles. Their stated goal, as Josh put it to The Pitch, is to make it accessible. The shop is named after Mitch, a rescued pitbull and aggressive cuddler who likes to eat big ice cubes. Doors open at 11am daily, running to 11pm on Friday and Saturday.

The bar keeps a printed section headed "Non-Alcoholic", and every drink on it is $10 — the same price whether or not there is alcohol in the glass. The programme is built almost entirely on Seedlip, with all three expressions available: Garden 108, Spice 94 and Grove 42 can each be had simply with soda, tonic or Fever-Tree ginger beer. Beyond those, the built drinks are proper cocktail constructions. Pen-No-Cillin uses Spice 94 with lemon and a honey ginger syrup. Garden Sour is Garden 108 with lemon and simple syrup. The Rabarbar-Oh-No! Highball works Grove 42 with rhubarb bitters into a long drink, and Unbuzzed combines Spice 94 with cold brew from local roaster Colony. One drink carries a caveat the bar prints itself rather than hiding: Smoke & Spice uses a Bittermens Hellfire habanero shrub, and the menu notes plainly that the shrub contains a trace amount of alcohol. The retail shelves also stock Bare Zero-Proof, Kin Euphorics and Ritual Zero-Proof to take home.
venues.pressQuote: It's been interesting how it's developed from an option for a small group of people to something that's more ingrained in the culture of bars.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Josh Edwards, Mitch e Amaro co-owner

venues.name: Mitsi
venues.description: Mitsi is a cocktail bar and sushi counter on Naud Street, in the pocket between Chinatown and Mission Junction, opened in April 2026 by Ben Lovett of Mumford and Sons through his hospitality company TVG and sitting next door to the Pacific Electric concert venue. It seats about 110 across indoor and outdoor space, with a working sushi counter built into one end of a long bar, and a food menu by chef Jon Kim. It is licensed, and the drink menu carries a named Spirit Free section: the Phony Negroni from St. Agrestis in New York, a Longan Osmanthus Flower sparkling tea from S.C Lab in Taiwan, and a Tieguanyin Apple sparkling tea from the same producer. Open Thursday to Saturday only, 6pm to 1am, with the kitchen running to 11pm.
signatureDrinks: Phony Negroni - St. Agrestis, New York
Longan Osmanthus Flower Sparkling Tea - S.C Lab, FOMO, Taiwan
Tieguanyin Apple Sparkling Tea - S.C Lab, ETHER, Taiwan
venues.longDescription:
Mitsi opened on 17 April 2026 on Naud Street, in the industrial pocket where Chinatown meets Mission Junction, and it was built by Ben Lovett of Mumford and Sons through TVG, the hospitality company he runs alongside a string of music venues. It sits next door to Pacific Electric, a small concert room, and that adjacency explains the design brief. The Infatuation, reviewing it in May 2026, put the look somewhere between Soho House and a converted church and described the whole thing as deliberately designed for grown-up pre-gaming - stylish digs with surprisingly creative drinks and premium snacks, rather than a destination restaurant. There are around 110 seats across indoor and outdoor space, and a working sushi counter built into one end of the long bar, with a menu from chef Jon Kim.

The cocktail programme is the headline and it is genuinely inventive - an Old Fashioned with rye, Amontillado sherry, miso honey and overproof rum; a tomato-water fifty-fifty martini; a palo-santo-smoked Negroni. Alcohol is served throughout. What earns the listing here is that the drink menu carries its own named Spirit Free section rather than folding non-alcoholic options into the soft drinks. The three current entries are curated bottles rather than house builds, and they are well chosen. The Phony Negroni is St. Agrestis's bottled non-alcoholic negroni out of Brooklyn, which is one of the few pre-made drinks in the category with enough bitterness to sit next to a real one. The other two come from S.C Lab in Taiwan, a producer that ferments and carbonates tea rather than sweetening it: a Longan Osmanthus Flower sparkling tea under the FOMO label, floral and honeyed, and a Tieguanyin Apple sparkling tea under ETHER, built on the roasted oolong.

Practical notes worth having. Mitsi opens three nights a week only - Thursday, Friday and Saturday, 6pm to 1am - and is closed Sunday through Wednesday, so it is easy to get wrong. The kitchen stops at 11pm even though the bar runs two hours later. Prices are not published for the spirit-free list on the online menu, and the handrolls are, in The Infatuation's phrasing, enjoyable if expensive. Parking on Naud Street is street-only and the block is quiet and industrial, which is part of the appeal and worth knowing after dark.
venues.pressQuote: somewhere between Soho House and a converted church

venues.name: Mixtli
venues.description: Mixtli is San Antonio's most ambitious restaurant — a tasting-menu room in Southtown exploring regional Mexican cooking with real scholarship, and one of the most decorated kitchens in Texas. It offers multiple zero-proof options alongside its pairings, which matters disproportionately at this kind of venue: a long tasting menu is precisely the format where a non-drinker is most exposed, sitting through fifteen courses while everyone else receives a matched pour. The individual drinks are not publicly documented, so ask when booking rather than on the night. Dinner only, Tuesday to Saturday from 5:30pm; the room is small and reservations are essential.
venues.address: 812 S Alamo St Ste 103, San Antonio, TX 78210
venues.longDescription:
Mixtli began in a converted rail car and has since moved to South Alamo Street in Southtown, where it serves a tasting menu built on deep research into regional Mexican cooking — the menu rotates by region and period, and the kitchen treats the food as scholarship as much as hospitality. It is among the most acclaimed restaurants in Texas.

The reason it belongs in this guide is a structural one about tasting menus. A long, fixed sequence of courses is the single most difficult format for a non-drinker. There is no ordering, no browsing, no pace of your own; the meal arrives as it arrives, and at each course everyone else receives a matched pour while you are handed water. Over two or three hours, that accumulates. A restaurant that offers a genuine zero-proof accompaniment converts the evening from one you are sitting through into one you are participating in.

Mixtli offers multiple zero-proof options, per CultureMap. What they are is not publicly documented, and this listing does not invent them — the grade is a 3 for that reason, reflecting a real but undescribed programme rather than a headline one. Given the kitchen's approach, agua fresca traditions and Mexican fermented drinks would be the natural direction, but that is inference rather than fact.

The practical advice is to ask at the point of booking rather than on arrival. Tasting-menu kitchens plan pairings in advance, and a restaurant of this seriousness is far more likely to build you something considered given notice than improvise on the night. Dinner only, Tuesday through Saturday from 5:30pm; reservations are essential and the room is small. Given the price and the format, the twenty seconds it takes to ask about zero-proof options when booking is the highest-return question in this guide.
venues.pressQuote: Mixtli offers multiple zero-proof options.

venues.name: Mnemonic Coffee
venues.description: Mnemonic Coffee is a queer, women-owned café in Bankers Hill, opened in July 2023 by longtime specialty-coffee pros Gia Giambalvo and Sarah Girdzius and built intentionally as both a coffee and zero-proof drink space. Alongside oat-milk lattes, cold brew, and pour-overs, the team builds creative coffee sodas and mocktails for people who want the communal feel of a café without alcohol — or without downing multiple cups of caffeine. Named non-alcoholic drinks include the Maple St. (maple syrup, long pepper, cinnamon, apple foam, Topo Chico), the Soy Libre (Coke, simple syrup, soy sauce, lime, cinnamon), the cardamom-and-jasmine Ocean Eyes, and the orange-cream-soda-like Zephyr. The 1970s-inspired space keeps daytime hours, Tuesday through Sunday, with pastries from Relic Bageri.
venues.longDescription:
Mnemonic Coffee is a queer, women-owned café in Bankers Hill, a short walk from Balboa Park, opened in July 2023 by Gia Giambalvo and Sarah Girdzius — both longtime specialty-coffee professionals who built the place from the outset as a coffee shop and a zero-proof drinks bar at the same time rather than adding the second thing later. The room is 1970s-inspired, it keeps daytime hours from Tuesday through Sunday, and the pastry case comes from Relic Bageri. The coffee side is what you would expect from operators with that background: oat-milk lattes, cold brew and pour-overs done properly.

The reason it belongs here is the other half of the menu. The team builds creative coffee sodas and non-alcoholic cocktails for people who want the communal feel of a café without alcohol — and, just as importantly, without drinking four cups of coffee to justify staying. That second point is an underrated problem: cafés are the default alcohol-free meeting place, and caffeine is a real ceiling on how long anyone can use them. The named builds are genuinely inventive rather than sweet-by-default. The Maple St. layers maple syrup with long pepper and cinnamon under an apple foam, lengthened with Topo Chico. The Soy Libre is the boldest thing on the list, combining Coke and simple syrup with soy sauce, lime and cinnamon — a savoury-saline build that reads strange and works. The Ocean Eyes pairs cardamom with jasmine, and the Zephyr lands somewhere close to an orange cream soda. San Diego Magazine singled the programme out for offering "a zero-proof menu in addition to their lattes, for folks who want to enjoy the communal feel of a café without downing multiple cups of caffeine," which is a fair summary of exactly the gap it fills.
venues.pressQuote: A zero-proof menu in addition to their lattes, for folks who want to enjoy the communal feel of a café without downing multiple cups of caffeine.

venues.name: MO Bar
venues.description: MO Bar, the flagship cocktail bar of Mandarin Oriental, Singapore, treats its non-alcoholic drinks as first-class pours rather than afterthoughts. The kitchen-driven bar team makes its own kombuchas and ferments, and the current Vol. 7 'Modern Localism' menu is built so drinks can be ordered either way: mocktails such as The Artis (fermented banana tibicos, pandan and coconut salt) are served alcohol-free by default with the choice to add vodka, while cocktails like B.T.B (Bean to Bar) come in a non-alcoholic variation. An earlier menu produced The Formosan (S$16), a coconut-cream Irish-coffee alternative served hot or cold.
venues.address: 5 Raffles Avenue, Level 3, Mandarin Oriental, Singapore 039797
signatureDrinks: The Artis - fermented banana tibicos, pandan and coconut salt (served non-alcoholic; vodka optional)
B.T.B (Bean to Bar) - cacao nib kombucha, wolfberry and chocolate, available non-alcoholic
The Formosan (S$16) - a non-alcoholic Irish-coffee alternative topped with clouds of coconut cream, served hot or cold
venues.longDescription:
MO Bar sits on Level 3 of Mandarin Oriental, Singapore at 5 Raffles Avenue, with wraparound windows looking out over Marina Bay. The bar reopened in 2023 following a full renovation of the hotel, and remains one of the city's benchmark hotel bars, drawing on Asia's ports and the Pacific for its themed, volume-by-volume cocktail programme.

It is a genuine world-class operation: MO Bar climbed to No. 8 on Asia's 50 Best Bars in 2022 (winning that year's Nikka Highest Climber Award), appeared at No. 57 on The World's 50 Best Bars 2022, and took the Michter's Art of Hospitality Award in 2021. The team works with modern kit including sonic infusers and water baths, and makes its own kombuchas and ferments in house.

The non-alcoholic offering is woven through the menu rather than tucked into a separate list. On the current Vol. 7 'Modern Localism' menu (launched March 2026), drinks are designed to flex both ways: The Artis, a collaboration with Hans Tan Studio built on fermented banana tibicos, pandan and coconut salt, is poured alcohol-free by default with vodka as an optional add, while the dessert-leaning B.T.B (Bean to Bar), made with cacao nib kombucha and chocolate, is available in a non-alcoholic version. Earlier menus produced named zero-proof serves such as The Formosan (S$16), an indulgent coconut-cream take on an Irish coffee served hot or cold.

MO Bar opens Sunday to Thursday from 5pm to midnight and Friday to Saturday from 5pm to 1am; reservations run through the hotel on +65 6885 3500. It is an 18-and-over room.

venues.name: Mockery Zero Proof
venues.description: Mockery Zero Proof is Detroit's first dedicated zero-proof bottle shop, stocking non-alcoholic spirits, wines, and beers out of a storefront on the Livernois–McNichols corridor in Bagley. Founder Karlyta Williams — trained as a zero-proof bartender over three years and previously ran a mobile NA bar — also books Private Pours, one-hour closed-door sessions where guests choose a guided non-alcoholic wine flight or a custom zero-proof cocktail mixed to their own flavor and mood. It soft-opened in November 2024 with a grand opening timed to Dry January 2025, and keeps a running calendar of sober social events, including a February 2026 Galentine's zero-proof gathering.
venues.hours: Mon-Tue closed; Wed 12pm-5pm; Thu-Sat 2pm-7pm; Sun closed
signatureDrinks: Guided Zero-Proof Wine Flight (Private Pours tasting, narrated by founder Karlyta Williams)
Custom Zero-Proof Cocktail Experience (Private Pours, one bespoke mocktail built to each guest's flavor and mood)
venues.longDescription:
Karlyta Williams, a lifelong Detroiter, built Mockery Zero Proof out of a personal reckoning with drinking during the pandemic. She started mixing non-alcoholic drinks for herself and friends, spent three years training as a zero-proof bartender, and ran a mobile NA bar business before opening the brick-and-mortar shop at 7400 W. McNichols — soft-opening November 30, 2024, with a grand opening on January 2, 2025, deliberately timed to Dry January.

The shop is a retail bottle shop first: non-alcoholic spirits, wines, and beers sold to go, alongside glassware and other sober-social goods. Beyond the shelf, Williams runs Private Pours, a bookable one-hour closed-door experience for private groups — guests pick either a Guided Zero-Proof Wine Flight, a seated tasting she narrates herself, or a Custom Zero-Proof Cocktail Experience, where each guest gets one bespoke mocktail built around their own flavor preferences and mood, with additional drinks available to purchase separately. It's positioned for birthdays, girlfriend get-togethers, baby showers, and team events, and the shop has hosted themed gatherings like a February 2026 Galentine's zero-proof social.

Mockery sits in Bagley, on Detroit's northwest side within the Livernois–McNichols (Live6) corridor. Per a Voyage Michigan interview, the location has personal resonance for Williams — it echoes her great-grandparents' old neighborhood market in Southwest Detroit, a full-circle moment for a business she describes as being about connection and belonging as much as beverages. The shop's stated belief is that "celebration doesn't require alcohol to be meaningful," framing the space around presence rather than escape — a theme Williams returns to in the shop's January blog post reframing Dry January as a mindful reset rather than restriction.
venues.pressQuote: I'm not trying to remind you of what you've done. I'm trying to offer you something different.

venues.name: Mockingbird
venues.description: Mockingbird is Park Slope's first fully alcohol-free cocktail bar, serving thoughtfully crafted zero-proof cocktails alongside coffee, matcha, weekend brunch, and elevated bar bites at 213 7th Ave in Brooklyn.
venues.longDescription: Mockingbird is an entirely alcohol-free, zero-proof cocktail bar in Brooklyn's Park Slope, opened January 16, 2025 by friends and co-owners Evan Clark and Coulton Vento after roughly two years of planning. The LGBTQ+-owned, mid-century modern space (seating about 30) works as an all-day neighborhood kitchen and beverage lounge: by day it pours creative coffee and matcha and serves weekend brunch with comfort food, and in the evening it turns to thoughtfully crafted non-alcoholic cocktails plus supper specials and elevated bar food such as truffle popcorn, charcuterie boards, and flatbreads. Its drink list spans original zero-proof cocktails alongside non-alcoholic beers and wines, with an emphasis on minority- and women-owned producers. Signature pours include The Herbalist (house-made gentian aperitif, Roots Divino Bianco, verjus, basil, lemon, CO2), The Nightshift (Three Spirit Nightcap, lapsang souchong, ginger, lemon, honey), and the Perennial Tonic, and one house cocktail is finished in a whipped-cream dispenser for a lavender-colored, marshmallow-thick texture. Widely described as Park Slope's very first zero-proof bar, Mockingbird gives non-alcoholic drinks the same care and complexity as their spirited counterparts.
venues.pressQuote: "Perfect for a first date or quick catch-up with a friend, Mockingbird is a casual neighborhood cocktail bar that just happens to be booze-free."

venues.name: Modern World
venues.description: A fully non-alcoholic bottle shop on the Avenue in Hampden, opened by Laurie Hefner, a Minneapolis native who came up in hospitality and natural wine and was partly inspired by a friend's shop back home. Everything on the shelves is spirit-free at no more than 0.5 percent ABV, spanning canned NA cocktails, zero-proof spirits like Aplós, hop waters such as Hoplark Hopsour, and NA beers including La Trappe Nillis 0.0. The stock runs well past drinks into tinned fish and conservas from Espinaler, Gueyu Mar and Jose Gourmet, plus Torres chips, glassware and pantry goods, which makes it as much a dinner-party shop as a bottle shop. It is retail only, with no bar or on-site cocktail service, but Hefner has been explicit that she built it as a third space where not drinking isn't othered.
venues.longDescription:
Modern World is a dedicated non-alcoholic bottle shop at 1006 W 36th Street, on the Avenue in Hampden, opened in early 2024 by Laurie Hefner — a Minneapolis native who came up through hospitality and natural wine before deciding Baltimore needed somewhere to buy this category properly. Her framing of who it is for is deliberately wide, and worth repeating because it explains the shop's tone: she built it for everybody to explore fun things to enjoy themselves and share with other people, rather than as a resource aimed only at people who have stopped drinking. Baltimore Magazine has described it since as a bright non-alcoholic bottle shop, and it has become the reference point for the category in the city.

Everything on the shelves is 0.5% ABV or less. The range covers zero-proof spirits, hop waters and non-alcoholic beers, with canned cocktails from St. Agrestis and kombucha-style bottles from Unified Ferments among the products that move fastest — Unified in particular is a producer more often found in restaurant cellars than on retail shelves, and its presence is a fair signal of how the buying is done here. Around the drinks sit tinned fish, potato chips and glassware, which makes it a shop you can put a whole evening together in rather than just a bottle run. Two practical notes. It is retail: no source, including the shop's own site, describes any seating or on-site tasting, so plan to take what you buy elsewhere. And the shop still trades on a raw Shopify subdomain rather than its own web address, and posts holiday changes to Google and Instagram rather than the site, so check those before a special trip. Open seven days: 1pm to 6:30pm on Monday and Tuesday, 11am to 7:30pm Wednesday through Saturday, and 11am to 6pm on Sunday.
venues.pressQuote: One of the main reasons I wanted this place to exist was so that people could feel comfortable and enjoy themselves. The idea of a third space.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Laurie Hefner, founder of Modern World

venues.name: Moku Kitchen
venues.description: Moku Kitchen is the anchor restaurant at SALT at Our Kakaʻako, the warehouse redevelopment that became the district's main food and drink block. It trades daily from 11am to 11pm, a longer day than most of Kakaʻako manages, and the kitchen works a farm-to-table brief with Hawaiian growers. Its current non-alcoholic build is the Mahana Sands, made with agave, lemon juice, pineapple juice, cucumber juice and soda water — mahana meaning warmth in Hawaiian, and the name taken from a green and a beach on Hawaiʻi Island. The cucumber juice is what makes it work, cutting the pineapple so the drink finishes dry rather than sweet. An earlier fixture, the So Figgin' Awesome, paired cinnamon, fig and vanilla in soda.
venues.address: 660 Ala Moana Blvd, Ste 145, Honolulu, HI 96813
signatureDrinks: Mahana Sands (agave, lemon juice, pineapple juice, cucumber juice, soda water)
So Figgin' Awesome (cinnamon, fig and vanilla in soda)
venues.longDescription:
Moku Kitchen occupies Suite 145 at 660 Ala Moana Boulevard, inside SALT at Our Kakaʻako — the block of converted warehouses that became the centre of gravity for independent food and drink in the district. The restaurant works a farm-to-table brief with Hawaiian producers, runs live music, and keeps notably long hours for the area, 11am to 11pm every day, which makes it one of the more dependable places to end up in Kakaʻako when other kitchens have closed.

The non-alcoholic offer is narrower than the venues higher up this guide, which is why it sits at a three rather than a four, but the one drink that is consistently documented is worth knowing about because it does something nothing else in Honolulu does. The So Figgin' Awesome combines cinnamon, fig and vanilla in soda — a warm, autumnal, dessert-leaning profile in a city where the non-alcoholic default is overwhelmingly tropical fruit. Pineapple, passionfruit, lychee and hibiscus dominate almost every list in this guide, for good reason, since they are local and they carry acidity. But that consistency means a visitor working through Honolulu's zero-proof drinks encounters a lot of the same register, and a fig-and-cinnamon build is a genuine change of direction. It also happens to be one of the cheaper composed non-alcoholic drinks in the city. Beyond it, the bar keeps a standard soft list rather than a developed zero-proof programme, so this is a venue to visit for the room, the hours and the food, with one good drink rather than a menu of them. Its position at SALT puts it a few minutes from Aloha Beer Company on Queen Street and a short distance from Merriman's at Ward Village.
venues.pressQuote: Mahana means warmth/warm weather in Hawaiian. The mocktail is named after a green and beach on the Big Island.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Moku Kitchen, via Aloha State Daily

venues.name: Monarch
venues.description: Monarch is a wood-fired modern Italian restaurant on the 49th floor of The National building in downtown Dallas, created by two-Michelin-star chef Danny Grant, with a rotating seasonal zero-proof cocktail menu alongside its full bar.
venues.longDescription:
For non-alcoholic drinkers, few settings in Dallas are as striking as Monarch's 49th-floor perch inside The National building in the heart of downtown. The floor-to-ceiling windows frame a panoramic skyline that's hard to replicate at street level, and the kitchen's serious Italian cooking means you're not just there for the views. Crucially, Monarch treats its zero-proof program with the same craft attention as its full bar, rotating the mocktail menu seasonally so there is always something new—and priced accessibly at $10—for guests who aren't drinking alcohol.

Three drinks have earned press attention across multiple outlets. The Smoked Old Fashioned uses Lyre's Amaretti and Lyre's Highland Malt with black walnut bitters for a spirit-forward, smoky sip that mirrors the complexity of its boozy counterpart. The Icy Road is more delicate: verjus blanc, lychee water, and violet syrup poured over rosemary and hibiscus ice in a format that makes the ice itself part of the flavor. Seasonal offerings like Grapefruit Goddess and Purple Reign round out the rotating card. Wine director Nicole Nowlin oversees the broader beverage program, which is known for its deep cellar and thoughtful pairings.

Monarch sits firmly in the special-occasion tier—business casual dress is required, and a meal for two can easily run well over $200 before drinks. Reservations are strongly recommended; window booths require a per-person deposit applied to the final bill. That said, the bar and lounge area allows walk-in seating and offers happy hour Monday through Friday and Sunday, making it a viable option for guests who want the views and a craft zero-proof cocktail without committing to a full dinner. It's a strong pick for non-drinkers attending a celebration with a mixed crowd—you'll have something genuinely interesting to sip.
venues.pressQuote: Monarch embraces a philosophy of flavor and balance in its alcohol-free concoctions, which change seasonally.

venues.name: Monday Morning
venues.description: Monday Morning is a fully alcohol-free bottle shop and tasting bar in Ocean Beach, the second San Diego location from founder Zane Curtis, opened January 2, 2026 at 4967 Newport Ave inside the OB Business Center — on the one-year anniversary of the original Pacific Beach store. It stocks more than 500 zero-proof products: non-alcoholic beer, dealcoholized wine, spirit alternatives, ready-to-drink mocktails, and functional drinks across 50-plus brands including Athletic, Bravus, Partake, Seedlip, and Ritual. A tasting bar lets customers try anything before buying, and because the OB space is compact, the team opens the windows to serve the boardwalk. It's a genuine alcohol-free retail-and-tasting destination steps from the beach.
venues.longDescription:
The Ocean Beach Monday Morning opened on 2 January 2026 at 4967 Newport Avenue, inside the OB Business Center — deliberately timed to the one-year anniversary of the Pacific Beach original. It is the second fully alcohol-free bottle shop and tasting bar from founder Zane Curtis, who started the business after getting sober and finding San Diego had nowhere to buy good non-alcoholic drinks, and whose own account of it runs: "I joke that my drinking problem materialized into sobriety for San Diego." Newport Avenue is Ocean Beach's main strip and one of the more determinedly countercultural streets in the county, which makes it a natural second home for a shop like this.

The stock mirrors the original: north of 500 zero-proof products across more than fifty brands, spanning non-alcoholic beer, dealcoholized wine, spirit alternatives, ready-to-drink cocktails and functional drinks built on adaptogens and nootropics, with Athletic, Bravus, Partake, Seedlip and Ritual all represented. A tasting bar lets customers try before buying, which matters more in this category than almost any other — non-alcoholic spirits and dealcoholized wines differ enormously between brands, and a single bad bottle at $30 is enough to convince somebody the whole category is not for them. The Ocean Beach space is noticeably more compact than Pacific Beach, and the team works around it by opening the windows and serving out toward the boardwalk, which suits a beach neighbourhood where most of the day happens outdoors. One practical note worth checking before you travel: this location currently keeps weekday-only hours, Monday to Friday, and is closed at the weekend — the reverse of what a beach-adjacent shop would normally do, and the opposite of the Pacific Beach store's schedule. For a first visit, the tasting bar is the whole reason to come in person rather than order online: an hour there will tell you more about which non-alcoholic spirits and dealcoholised wines are worth your money than any amount of reading, and the staff have tasted everything on the shelves.
venues.pressQuote: I joke that my drinking problem materialized into sobriety for San Diego.

venues.name: Monday Morning
venues.description: Monday Morning is San Diego's first exclusively non-alcoholic bottle shop and tasting room, opened in Pacific Beach in late 2024 by founder Zane Curtis after he embraced a sober lifestyle. The shop stocks more than 500 zero-proof products — non-alcoholic beer (IPAs, lagers, stouts, sours, wheat), dealcoholized wine, spirit alternatives (gin, whiskey, tequila, rum), ready-to-drink mocktails, and functional drinks with adaptogens and nootropics — across 50-plus brands including Athletic, Bravus, Partake, Seedlip, and Ritual. A tasting bar lets customers sample anything before buying, with staff guiding selections. Curtis's business also handles NA distribution, custom recipes, staff training, and events, and in January 2026 it opened a second location in Ocean Beach.
venues.longDescription:
Monday Morning on Garnet Avenue was San Diego's first exclusively non-alcoholic bottle shop and tasting room, opened in Pacific Beach in late 2024 by founder Zane Curtis after he stopped drinking and found the city had nowhere to buy anything decent that was not alcohol. His own summary of how the business came about is the best line anyone in this category has given: "I joke that my drinking problem materialized into sobriety for San Diego." Pacific Beach is a pointed place to have put it — the most relentlessly drink-forward neighbourhood in the county, where Garnet Avenue is essentially a corridor of bars — and opening an alcohol-free shop in the middle of it was a statement as much as a business decision.

The range is what makes it a destination rather than a novelty: more than 500 zero-proof products across upwards of fifty brands. Non-alcoholic beer covers IPAs, lagers, stouts, sours and wheat beers; there is dealcoholized wine, a full set of spirit alternatives across gin, whiskey, tequila and rum, ready-to-drink cocktails, and functional drinks built on adaptogens and nootropics. Athletic, Bravus, Partake, Seedlip and Ritual are all stocked. Crucially there is a tasting bar, so anything can be sampled before it is bought, with staff walking customers through the choice — which addresses the single biggest problem with this category, that non-alcoholic products vary wildly in quality and cost enough that a bad guess puts people off for a year. Beyond retail, Curtis's business also runs non-alcoholic distribution, custom recipe development, staff training for other venues and events, which is why its influence around San Diego runs wider than one shop. In January 2026 it opened a second location in Ocean Beach, on the first anniversary of this one.
venues.pressQuote: I joke that my drinking problem materialized into sobriety for San Diego.

venues.name: Monkeypod Kitchen by Merriman
venues.description: Monkeypod Kitchen by Merriman opened in 2024 inside the OUTRIGGER Reef Waikiki Beach Resort as the centrepiece of an $85 million rebuild of the property. It comes from chef Peter Merriman, one of the founders of Hawaii Regional Cuisine, through his Handcrafted Restaurants group. The mocktail list is a full menu section rather than an afterthought: the Virgin Monkeypod Mai Tai, the Blind Tiger built on hibiscus and lavender soda, and the Green Fevah. Opening daily from 7am to 11pm with happy hours at both 3.30pm and 9pm, it is the most reliably available option in Waikīkī for a table where not everybody is drinking.
venues.longDescription:
Monkeypod Kitchen by Merriman opened in 2024 at 2169 Kalia Road, inside the OUTRIGGER Reef Waikiki Beach Resort, as the anchor restaurant of an $85 million transformation of the hotel. It belongs to chef Peter Merriman's Handcrafted Restaurants group — Merriman is one of the twelve chefs who founded Hawaii Regional Cuisine in 1991, the movement that pushed Hawaiʻi's restaurants towards local sourcing and away from imported convention — and the Monkeypod format applies that thinking at a more casual price point than his flagship rooms.

The non-alcoholic offer is worth taking seriously in context. Waikīkī is the hardest district in the state to drink nothing in: it is dense with resort bars whose entire business model is the mai tai, and the standard accommodation for a non-drinker is a fruit juice at cocktail prices. Monkeypod runs mocktails as a designated section of its menu with named, specified builds. The Virgin Monkeypod Mai Tai is the important one, because the mai tai is the drink Waikīkī sells more than any other, and a zero-proof version means somebody at the table can order what everyone else is ordering by name — the social equivalence that matters more to most people than novelty does. The Blind Tiger, built on hibiscus and lavender soda, is the more interesting drink on its own terms, floral and dry where the format usually defaults to sweet. The Green Fevah completes the trio. Hours are unusually generous for a restaurant of this type, 7am to 11pm daily, with happy hour from 3.30pm to 5pm and a late-night happy hour from 9pm to 11pm, which means the room works for breakfast, an afternoon drink, dinner or a nightcap. For a group split between drinkers and non-drinkers staying anywhere near the beach, it is the single most practical booking in this guide.
venues.pressQuote: It's a casual, open-air restaurant with chill vibes—you feel like you're on vacation when you're dining here.

venues.longDescription:
Monkey's Tail is a Lindale Park cantina and cocktail bar operated by Barrel of Monkeys Hospitality, the Houston group led by Jessie Gonzales. Houston Press dates the bar's opening to 2018 and describes a laid-back room strung with Spanish-language neon signs flashing sentiments like "good vibes" and "shut up and drink" — a funky, irreverent dive-bar tone it has held onto even as its drink programs drew citywide recognition. In the Houston Press Best of Houston 2025 awards it took two titles: Best Mocktail List, and Best Bar in the Heights.

The zero-proof program is branded "Free-Spirited" on the beverage list, under the header "Drink Without the Cruda," and it is priced and printed alongside the full-proof cocktails rather than tucked away. Seven drinks run on it: the Tropi-Carajillo (espresso/cold-brew blend, fresh pineapple, baking spices, saline, gomme syrup), the Penichill'n (Lyre's Highland Malt, salted honey, ginger, grapefruit, lemon, spritzed smoky tea), the Picka-Piña (fresh pineapple, chamoy, Giffard grenadine, lime, dill pickle brine, Tajín), the Viva Maracuyá (passion fruit and mango, tiki spices, lime, salt, club soda), a Lyre's G&T (non-alcoholic gin and tonic served over ice with lime), the Chango House Soda (housemade guava-and-cinnamon soda in a cold mug), and Jessie's Topo (Topo Chico, lime, Tajín and salt). Non-alcoholic beer from Best Day Brewing rounds out the list. Click2Houston's January 2026 Dry January guide summed the program up as "a stacked list of non-alcoholic cocktails that drink like the real thing."

Beyond the drinks, Monkey's Tail is known for Mexican-American comfort food — tacos, chips and queso, and the Chango Burger — plus a Steak Night every Monday, crawfish Thursday through Sunday in season, and a happy hour that runs from open until 7 p.m. Monday through Friday. The centerpiece is a large dog-friendly patio with picnic tables and umbrellas, decked out with TVs and oversized fans. The whole family is welcome before 8 p.m., with under-21 guests admitted only alongside a parent or guardian.
venues.pressQuote: Monkey's Tail also crushes it when it comes to zero-proof sipping. The booze-free lineup is anything but boring...
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Houston Press, "Best Of Houston 2025: Best Mocktail List"

venues.name: Moon Flower
venues.description: Moon Flower is a fully alcohol-free cocktail lounge that takes over Maya Moon Collective — a cacao café and organic chocolate shop on Adams Avenue in Normal Heights — Thursday through Sunday evenings. The zero-proof program is run by co-owner Grace Mestecky alongside Maya Moon founder Kathryn Rogers, who launched the collective's booze-free menu in 2023; the evening lounge format took shape in 2024. The rotating, seasonal menu leans on functional and adaptogenic ingredients, local produce, and herbs, building booze-free riffs on classic cocktails. Signature pours include Smoke and Mirrors (NA whiskey, black cardamom, orange bitters, burned honey, lapsang souchong), Spiritual Rest (Dromme, Everleaf, lemon, honey, ginger, turmeric), and Hi Barbie! (NA gin, NA bubbly, prickly pear, strawberry, yuzu, lime, kanna).
venues.longDescription:
Moon Flower is a fully alcohol-free cocktail lounge that exists by taking over another business after dark: Thursday through Sunday evenings it occupies Maya Moon Collective, the ceremonial-cacao café and organic chocolate shop on Adams Avenue in Normal Heights. The zero-proof programme is run by co-owner Grace Mestecky alongside Maya Moon founder Kathryn Rogers, who launched the collective's booze-free menu in 2023; the evening lounge format took shape the following year. Sharing a room this way is a smart answer to the hardest economics in this category — an alcohol-free bar carries a bar's costs without a bar's margins — and it means the space arrives already furnished with the warmth of a café rather than the fluorescence of a juice counter.

The menu rotates seasonally and leans on functional and adaptogenic ingredients, local produce and herbs, building spirit-free riffs on classic cocktails rather than sweet inventions. Smoke and Mirrors is the clearest demonstration: non-alcoholic whiskey with black cardamom, orange bitters, burned honey and lapsang souchong, a drink constructed entirely around smoke and bitterness, which are precisely the registers that bad zero-proof menus avoid. Spiritual Rest combines Dromme and Everleaf with lemon, honey, ginger and turmeric. Hi Barbie! is the showpiece, built on non-alcoholic gin and non-alcoholic bubbly with prickly pear, strawberry, yuzu, lime and kanna. Mestecky has described the reception plainly: "People don't always understand the concept. But when they see the thought and intention behind the drink, it sells them pretty fast." That is the whole argument for this kind of room in one sentence — the barrier is not demand, it is that most people have never been handed a good example. The Thursday-to-Sunday evening format is worth planning around — outside those nights the address is Maya Moon Collective operating as a cacao café, which is a good thing in its own right but an entirely different experience from the cocktail lounge described here.
venues.pressQuote: People don't always understand the concept. But when they see the thought and intention behind the drink, it sells them pretty fast.

venues.name: Moon Rabbit
venues.description: Moon Rabbit is chef-owner Kevin Tien's modern Vietnamese restaurant at 927 F Street NW in Penn Quarter, reborn there in 2024 in the former Co.Co. Sala space after its original run inside the Wharf's InterContinental hotel closed in 2023. The intimate room of roughly 50 seats pairs Tien's cooking, threaded with his Louisiana roots, with a bar led by director Thi Nguyen, who won the 2024 Michelin Guide Washington DC Exceptional Cocktails Award. The Spirit Free list is given equal billing and equal pricing at $13: The Life of A Showgirl, with nectarine, verjus blanc and jasmine-lemongrass soda; Sai Gon Fruit Cart, on Lyre's white cane spirit with lacto-fermented pineapple and shrimp salt; Tho Ngoc | Jade, with soursop and osmanthus; and Ho Xuan Huong | The Poet. A zero-proof Beaujolais is poured by the glass.

venues.longDescription:
Moon Rabbit had two lives. The first was inside the InterContinental at the Wharf, where chef Kevin Tien built a reputation for modern Vietnamese cooking before the hotel closed the restaurant in 2023. The second began in 2024 at 927 F Street NW in Penn Quarter, in the room that used to hold Co.Co. Sala - roughly fifty seats, considerably more intimate, and entirely Tien's. The cooking is Vietnamese threaded with his Louisiana upbringing, and the recognition has followed the move: a place in the Michelin Guide, a spot on the North America's 50 Best Restaurants 2026 list, and a continuing Washingtonian 100 Very Best Restaurants pick.

The bar is led by Thi Nguyen, who won the 2024 Michelin Guide Washington, D.C. Exceptional Cocktails Award, and the structural point about her list is that the Spirit Free section is priced at $13 against alcoholic cocktails at $19 to $22 but built with the same number of moving parts. Sai Gon Fruit Cart is the most involved: Lyre's white cane spirit with lacto-fermented pineapple, lime, clarified coconut milk, soda and shrimp salt - the shrimp salt being the detail that makes it read as a drink from this kitchen rather than a tropical cooler. Tho Ngoc, or Jade, runs soursop, osmanthus and lemon under a vegan foam. Ho Xuan Huong, The Poet, named for the eighteenth-century Vietnamese poet and credited on the menu to Amanda Deviana, is built from chrysanthemum rice milk, red bean, sesame and ginger syrup, and is the closest thing on the list to a dessert. The Life of A Showgirl is the lightest, with nectarine, verjus blanc and jasmine-lemongrass soda. Beyond the cocktails the wine list carries a zero-proof Beaujolais, Domaine des Grottes Antilope, at $14 the glass and $52 the bottle, which is a real bottle on a serious list rather than a token.

Practical notes. Dinner runs Monday through Saturday, 4.30pm to 9.30pm, closed Sunday. The room is small and reservations are effectively required. The drinks list rotates - the Dynas-Tea and Purple Shiso Spritz that appeared on earlier versions are no longer served - so ask what is current rather than arriving set on a specific drink.
venues.pressQuote: Bar Manager Thi Nguyen, who recently received a Michelin award for exceptional cocktails, incorporates many Vietnamese ingredients from the kitchen into her drinks
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Washingtonian, Where to Drink Great Nonalcoholic Cocktails, December 2024

venues.name: Moona Moono
venues.description: Moona Moono is a coffee, matcha and boba shop at Hennepin and 31st in Uptown that doubles as a retail space for Asian and Asian-American goods — K-beauty, stationery, ceramics, blind boxes. It is one of the few rooms in the neighbourhood that a sober restaurant critic has flagged as a place to spend an evening: it keeps cans of Ghia, the non-alcoholic aperitif, alongside a salted yuzu soda and a full matcha and espresso list, and it programmes the space with mahjong nights, silent book clubs, lo-fi craft nights and body-doubling sessions rather than relying on drinks alone to fill seats. A short list of Japanese beers is also stocked.
venues.longDescription:
Uptown's Hennepin Avenue has lost a lot of its old bar strip over the past decade, and Moona Moono opened into that gap at the corner of Hennepin and 31st with a hybrid format: a coffee, matcha and boba counter at the front, and a retail floor of Asian and Asian-American goods behind it — Korean skincare, stationery, ceramics, kids' books and toys, blind boxes. The shop celebrates Asian and Asian American culture explicitly, and the room is light and glassy rather than dark. It is graded here as a modest non-alcoholic offering rather than a strong one for two honest reasons: it closes at 6pm most days, and it stocks a small number of Japanese beers, so it is not an alcohol-free space.

What earns it the entry is that the non-alcoholic side is deliberate rather than incidental. The shop keeps cans of Ghia — the botanical non-alcoholic aperitif built on gentian, yuzu, elderflower and fig — priced at $7, which puts a genuine bitter aperitif in a room where the alternative would be a soft drink. A salted yuzu soda sits alongside it, and the tea programme runs matcha lattes, black tea and flavour builds including a yuzu strawberry. The other half of the argument is programming: mahjong nights, silent book clubs, lo-fi craft nights and body-doubling sessions for people who want company while they work. A sober restaurant critic writing for Beyond Beurre Blanc in January 2026 put it on a list of the nine best places to go drinking in the Twin Cities without drinking, on exactly that basis — "for folks who really just don't want to be in a bar, this is the spot!" That is the use case: an evening out of the house, in a room with a social structure to it, where nothing on the table has to contain alcohol. Thursday is the one late night, running to 8pm.
venues.pressQuote: For folks who really just don't want to be in a bar, this is the spot!

venues.name: The Moon's Daughters
venues.description: The Moon's Daughters is the rooftop bar at the Thompson Hotel, twenty floors above the River Walk with the best view in downtown San Antonio, and it keeps named zero-proof drinks on the list — Pluto's Revenge and Feeling Prickly, the latter built on the prickly pear that turns up across the city's better alcohol-free menus. Rooftop bars are usually the worst rooms for a non-drinker, because the whole proposition is a cocktail and a view at sunset. Having something properly made here means the person not drinking gets the view on the same terms as everyone else. It also serves from 7am daily and runs to 2am at weekends, an unusually long window for a hotel rooftop.

venues.longDescription:
The Moon's Daughters occupies the rooftop of the Thompson Hotel on Lexington Avenue, twenty floors up, with the widest view of downtown San Antonio and the river below. The design leans celestial and the room is built for sunset.

Rooftop bars are, as a category, the hardest places to be the person not drinking. The entire experience is constructed around holding a cocktail while the light changes; there is no food to focus on, no game to play, nothing else to do with your hands. When the only alcohol-free option is a soda, the gap between your evening and everybody else's is at its most visible.

That is why the two named drinks matter more here than the same two would in a restaurant. Pluto's Revenge and Feeling Prickly are on the menu as drinks, with names, in the same list as everything else — so ordering one is a choice rather than an admission. Feeling Prickly uses prickly pear, which recurs across San Antonio's better zero-proof menus and belongs to the landscape rather than being imported for colour; it is tart, intensely magenta and looks exactly as good as anything with tequila in it, which on a rooftop is not a trivial consideration.

The hours are remarkable and worth knowing: 7am to midnight most days, to 2am on Friday and Saturday. A rooftop serving from seven in the morning means coffee with the view is an option too, and the 2am close makes it one of the few places in the city where a non-drinker can still be out very late with something decent. Being in the Thompson puts it within a short walk of the Pearl and most of downtown. It is the single best view a non-drinker can get in this city with a proper drink in hand, which is not a small thing on a hot evening.
venues.pressQuote: The Moon's Daughters: Pluto's Revenge, "Feeling Prickly".

venues.name: More or Less
venues.description: More or Less is a fully non-alcoholic bottle shop at 434 Leonard Street NW on the West Side of Grand Rapids, and Michigan's original dedicated non-alcoholic retail store. It was founded by Chad Clark and Neil DeMeester, who both stopped drinking in recent years and opened the shop at the turn of 2023 under the name Alt City NA Bottles and Beer before rebranding. The shelves carry more than 450 alcohol alternatives: canned craft mocktails, zero-proof spirits, botanical seltzers, gourmet sodas, adaptogenic drinks, CBD seltzers and non-alcoholic wines. Between six and ten bottles are kept open on a rotating basis so customers can taste before committing to a full bottle, which is the shop's main answer to a category where a bad guess is expensive.
venues.address: 434 Leonard St NW, Grand Rapids, MI 49504
venues.longDescription:
More or Less sits at 434 Leonard Street NW, about a five-minute drive from downtown Grand Rapids, and is the state's first shop built entirely around drinks with no alcohol in them. Chad Clark and Neil DeMeester met by chance at Clark's original business and went into partnership on it; both had quit drinking and both had developed an interest in what the non-alcoholic category was starting to produce. They opened at the turn of 2023 as Alt City NA Bottles and Beer, and later rebranded to More or Less — a piece of wordplay about the industry, and a nod to how many people walk through the door who still drink and are simply looking for something to alternate with. The pair describe the business as a passion project and the buying as deliberately selective, blending what they characterise as Clark's creative instincts with DeMeester's more analytical approach.

The inventory runs past 450 items and spans most of what the category now offers: non-alcoholic beer, zero-proof spirits, canned craft mocktails, botanical and CBD seltzers, adaptogenic drinks, gourmet sodas, and non-alcoholic wines. Because the category is young and unfamiliar — and because a 750ml bottle of zero-proof spirit costs about what a real one does — the shop keeps a rotating selection of roughly six to ten bottles open for guests to taste in store before buying, which is unusual for a retailer and is the closest thing the business has to a bar program. Trading hours are Tuesday through Saturday, noon to 7pm, closed Sunday and Monday. It is the only venue in this guide that is a shop rather than a place to sit and drink, and it functions as the supply line for much of the rest of the city's alcohol-free drinking.
venues.pressQuote: This Leonard Street retail shop, just a five-minute drive from downtown GR, carries 450+ non-alcoholic alternatives.

venues.name: Mother Cocktail Bar
venues.description: Mother Cocktail Bar is a full-service cocktail bar and restaurant on Queen Street West in Toronto's West Queen West neighborhood, built around rotating, thematically-driven menus and fermentation-forward technique. Its current menu, "The 5th Horizon," carries a dedicated Signature Non-Alcoholic section with three named, house-made zero-proof cocktails — Tomato Soup, Fading Silhouette and Tonka Brew — each priced at $17. The bar was ranked No. 48 on Canada's 100 Best Bars 2026 list and No. 22 on North America's 50 Best Bars 2026.
