venues.longDescription:
Mother Cocktail Bar occupies 874 Queen St W in Toronto's West Queen West neighborhood, part of the strip's eclectic corridor of dining and nightlife on the city's west end. It was founded by a group its own site describes as "likeminded people with a common goal – elevate the Canadian cocktail scene," built around sourcing quality natural ingredients, using fermentation techniques to develop them, and pairing the bar program with a kitchen turning out small bites, mains and desserts inspired by cuisines around the world.

The bar runs on rotating, thematically-driven menus rather than a static list. Its current program, "The 5th Horizon," is the bar's fourth full menu iteration, drawing on ideas of global horizons to explore change, transformation and hope for the future across both the cocktail list and the food menu. Mother has been recognized for that approach with a No. 48 ranking on Canada's 100 Best Bars 2026 list and a No. 22 spot on North America's 50 Best Bars 2026.

Non-alcoholic drinkers aren't an afterthought here: the menu carries a dedicated Signature Non-Alcoholic section with three named, house-made zero-proof cocktails, each priced at $17 alongside the bar's alcoholic offerings. The Tomato Soup is a savoury, lacto-fermented tomato drink with fresh oregano and basil and a silky coconut milk finish; the Fading Silhouette pairs plum and black cardamom with kombucha fizz, warmed by amaretto; and the Tonka Brew is a clean, bitter highball built on tonic and savoury citrus, finished with a gentle spice. Forbes Travel Guide singled the bar out for sticking "to its innovative approach to cocktails and unique flavor profiles with its 0% ABV cocktail list."
venues.pressQuote: Over on Queen West, Mother Cocktail Bar sticks to its innovative approach to cocktails and unique flavor profiles with its 0% ABV cocktail list.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Forbes Travel Guide, "Where To Find Innovative Mocktails In Toronto"

venues.name: Mother's House
venues.description: Mother's House is a woman-owned tattoo studio, coffee lounge, and mocktail bar tucked into Oak Lawn in Dallas, founded by tattoo artist Brieana Jones, who spent years sketching in coffee shops before building a space that married her two loves. The result is a fully alcohol-free venue: every guest is met by a non-alcoholic beverage and coffee lounge serving espresso-based drinks, teas, and mocktails, with seating in a whimsical striped-ceiling lounge or a green checkered patio. The studio runs six artists and is widely noted as a safe, judgment-free, LGBTQ+-welcoming space. Walk-ins are welcome Wednesday through Saturday. Because the venue pours zero alcohol by design, the coffee-and-mocktail bar is genuinely sober-first rather than a token NA list bolted onto an alcohol program.
venues.longDescription:
Mother's House is a woman-owned tattoo studio at 2512 Oak Lawn Avenue that doubles as a coffee lounge and non-alcoholic bar, founded by tattoo artist Brieana Jones. The Dallas Observer, naming it among the city's best tattoo shops in May 2024, noted that the studio also offers a coffee and non-alcoholic beverage bar, and described Jones as an artist whose work falls somewhere between American traditional and neo-traditional. The premise is straightforward and unusually well executed: tattoo appointments involve a great deal of waiting, for the client and for whoever came with them, and Mother's House treats that waiting time as the point rather than an inconvenience. The studio's own description of the space is that it is the best waiting room ever, and the seating is split between a striped-ceiling lounge and a green checkered patio.

For anyone looking for somewhere to sit in Dallas that serves nothing alcoholic at all, this is a genuinely alcohol-free venue rather than a bar with a zero-proof section — every guest is met with a non-alcoholic drink, and the counter runs espresso-based coffee, teas and mocktails. The studio works with several resident artists and is consistently described as a judgment-free, LGBTQ+-welcoming room, which is part of why it functions as a hangout for people who are not being tattooed that day. Walk-ins are taken Wednesday through Saturday, 10am to 7pm, while Sunday through Tuesday is appointment-only, so anyone coming for the coffee and mocktails rather than for ink should plan around the walk-in days — this is a tattoo studio with a bar in it, not a cafe that happens to tattoo, and the rhythm of the room follows the appointment book. One further caveat worth setting expectations on: Mother's House does not publish a current drinks list online, so the specific mocktails rotate and are best asked about in person. What is verified here is the format, the fully alcohol-free policy and the coffee programme, rather than a fixed menu of named drinks — which makes it a dependable place to sit without a drink in hand, and an unpredictable one if you have arrived hoping for something specific.
venues.pressQuote: Their mocktails all have adaptogens like ashwagandha and l-theanine, which help relax you

venues.name: Mothership
venues.description: Mothership is a sci-fi tiki cocktail bar and fully plant-based restaurant in South Park, opened in August 2022 by the team behind the vegan restaurant Kindred. The immersive, crash-landed-spaceship interior won an Orchid Award, and while the rum-forward tiki list is the headline, the bar also runs a genuine, fully built-out zero-proof program: its menu carries a dedicated "Beverages" section where every drink is labeled zero-proof. Named alcohol-free options include the X-Ray (white cane NA spirit, lime, Szechuan peppercorn, spearmint, peppermint oil), Tracking Device (coconut water, coconut cream, lime, hibiscus), Baby Bird (Italian bitter NA spirit, blood orange, caramelized pineapple, lime, soda), and Mindchiller. Mothership ranked among Yelp's 2023 Top 25 mocktail spots in the U.S.
venues.longDescription:
Mothership is a science-fiction tiki bar and fully plant-based restaurant on 30th Street in South Park, opened in August 2022 by the team behind the vegan restaurant Kindred. The interior is the thing people describe first — an immersive crash-landed spaceship that won an Orchid Award, San Diego's long-running architecture and design prize — and the rum-forward tiki list is the headline draw. What earns the bar a place in this directory is that the zero-proof drinks are not an afterthought bolted onto that: the menu carries a dedicated beverages section in which every drink is labelled zero-proof, built with the same construction logic as the spirited list rather than assembled from juice on request.

The named alcohol-free builds show the work. The X-Ray combines a white cane non-alcoholic spirit with lime, Szechuan peppercorn, spearmint and peppermint oil — a drink with genuine tingle and heat rather than sweetness. The Tracking Device works coconut water and coconut cream against lime and hibiscus. Baby Bird is built on an Italian bitter non-alcoholic spirit with blood orange, caramelised pineapple, lime and soda, which gives a non-drinker access to the bitter-aperitif register that zero-proof menus most often lack. A fourth, the Mindchiller, rounds out the section. Yelp ranked Mothership among its 2023 top twenty-five mocktail spots in the United States. The bar's beverage director, David Kinsey, has described the standard he applies plainly: "For a good alcohol-free drink, I approach it the same way I would a cocktail. It needs to be balanced, have a good nose, solid presentation, and unfold on the palate." That, combined with an entirely plant-based kitchen, makes it one of the few rooms in San Diego where a guest who neither drinks nor eats animal products has the full menu open to them rather than a corner of it.
venues.pressQuote: For a good alcohol-free drink, I approach it the same way I would a cocktail. It needs to be balanced, have a good nose, solid presentation, and unfold on the palate.

venues.name: MOTW Coffee and Pastries
venues.description: MOTW Coffee and Pastries is the Georgia branch of a specialty coffee and Arabic pastry chain that grew out of Muslims of the World, the storytelling platform Sajjad Shah started on Instagram. The Alpharetta shop sits on McGinnis Ferry Road and is fully alcohol-free, trading to 11pm Sunday through Thursday and to 1am on Friday and Saturday. That late close is what makes it useful as a going-out room rather than a morning stop, and it is one of the few in the far north metro. The counter pairs an espresso programme with Arabic pastries and desserts, and the company frames the cafe as an extension of its community and philanthropic work rather than as a straight retail concept. The Atlanta-area franchise is run by local owner Mudassir.
venues.longDescription:
MOTW stands for Muslims of the World, the Instagram project Sajjad Shah began during a period of heightened anti-Muslim sentiment in the United States as a way of publishing ordinary people's stories. The coffee shops came later and are described by the company as a physical extension of that platform — "a space where stories, culture, and philanthropy converge over a cup of coffee", in the words of its own about page. The chain has since spread across Indiana, Illinois, Connecticut, Massachusetts, Texas, Wisconsin, New York, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island and California; the Alpharetta shop on McGinnis Ferry Road is its only Georgia location, run by local franchise owner Mudassir, and it opened with Pakistani-American ownership behind it.

What lands it on a non-alcoholic guide is a combination of format and clock. MOTW serves specialty coffee and Arabic pastries, has no bar and no licence, and trades to 11pm Sunday through Thursday and 1am on Friday and Saturday. In a stretch of far-north metro Atlanta where the evening options are chain restaurants and bars, that gives sober and sober-curious drinkers a room with a genuine late-night atmosphere. The interior is laid out as a lounge — soft seating, long tables, room for a group to sit for two or three hours — and the trade after 9pm is social rather than transactional. The counter runs a conventional espresso bar alongside desserts and Arabic baked goods. We have deliberately not listed named signature drinks here: MOTW publishes its drinks menu only as a downloadable PDF that we could not read reliably, and rather than guess at names we have left the field empty. Everything else — hours, address, format, ownership and the total absence of alcohol — is confirmed from the company's own site. The Alpharetta branch sits on McGinnis Ferry Road near the Forsyth County line, a stretch of the metro whose growing South Asian and Muslim population has driven much of the demand for late-opening rooms that serve no alcohol, and MOTW is one of a small handful in that corridor. Alongside coffee, the counter carries the Arabic pastry range the brand is known for, and the philanthropic strand of the business — a share of proceeds directed back through the Muslims of the World platform — remains part of how the company presents itself.

venues.name: MOTW Coffee & Pastries
venues.description: MOTW Coffee & Pastries is an alcohol-free cafe on Willard Street in Quincy, the Boston-area location of a chain that grew out of Muslims of the World, the Instagram storytelling project Sajjad Shah founded in 2014. The Quincy store runs to 9pm on weeknights and to midnight on Fridays and Saturdays, and its roughly 1,700 square feet are split between table seating and a lounge area of sofas meant for long stays. The menu is globally sourced rather than American-cafe generic: Yemeni chai and Egyptian teas sit beside date cardamom, Spanish and pistachio lattes, matcha drinks and fruit refreshers. Food is Arabic pastry and light bites, including baklava, milk cakes, date cookies, muffins and halal savory empanadas. It is Muslim-owned and halal; no alcohol is sold or served.
venues.longDescription:
MOTW stands for Muslims of the World, the Instagram page Sajjad Shah started in 2014 during a period of heightened anti-Muslim sentiment in the United States. The account collected first-person stories and grew into a community of more than 670,000 followers; in 2021 Shah and his wife Fatimah opened the first MOTW cafe as a physical version of the same idea. The chain has since spread across several states, and the Javid family brought it to Quincy at 279 Willard Street, announced by What Now Boston in January 2026 and now trading. The room was designed for lingering rather than turnover, with conventional table seating on one side and a sofa lounge on the other, and the late Friday and Saturday closing time makes it one of the few places in the southern part of the metro where a group can sit together at eleven at night without a bar involved.

The drinks list reads like the diaspora the brand documents. Yemeni chai and Egyptian teas anchor the traditional side; the specialty lattes run to date cardamom, Spanish and pistachio; matcha drinks and fruit refreshers cover the cold end. The pastry counter is Arabic-leaning, with baklava, milk cakes, date cookies and muffins, plus halal savory empanadas for anyone treating it as dinner. Everything on the menu is non-alcoholic, and the cafe is halal, which makes it a straightforward answer for readers who want an evening out with no alcohol anywhere in the room rather than a bar with a zero-proof section. Quincy sits at the end of the Red Line and draws from Braintree, Milton and Dorchester as well as its own large South Shore population, so the store functions as a regional late-night gathering point rather than a neighborhood coffee stop. What Now Boston reported the Quincy project in January 2026, when the store was still waiting on its certificate of occupancy; it is now trading, with published closing times of 9pm on weeknights and midnight on Friday and Saturday.
venues.pressQuote: Spanning just under 1,700 square feet, the space will feature both table seating and a lounge-style area with sofas, encouraging guests to stay awhile.

venues.name: Mountain Madre
venues.description: Mountain Madre is a Mexican kitchen and agave bar at 13 W Walnut Street in downtown Asheville, from owners Danny and Paige Scully, who built it to bring families and friends together. The kitchen runs empanadas at $14, chorizo-stuffed avocado at $18, downtown street tacos at $15, smoked brisket tacos at $17, enchiladas at $21 and carne asada at $34, with a proper kids' menu. It reopened with limited hours after Hurricane Helene. Its non-alcoholic drinks sit in a clearly separate section headed "0% ABV Cocktails", all built on Seedlip: the Prickly Pear ($13, Seedlip Notas de Agave, fresh lime, agave), Spicy Fuego ($15, Seedlip Garden 108, habanero pineapple syrup, lime) and Spiced Violet ($16, Seedlip Spice 94, blackberry syrup, lime). IMPORTANT: the bar's Blackberry Smoke and Spice of Life are full-strength margaritas built on mezcal and tequila and appear only in the alcoholic Margaritas section — order from the 0% ABV list by name.
signatureDrinks: Prickly Pear (Seedlip Notas de Agave, fresh lime, agave) $13
Spicy Fuego (Seedlip Garden 108, habanero pineapple syrup, lime) $15
Spiced Violet (Seedlip Spice 94, blackberry syrup, lime) $16
venues.longDescription:
Mountain Madre is a Mexican kitchen and agave bar at 13 W Walnut Street in downtown Asheville, owned by Danny and Paige Scully, who describe the intention behind it simply as bringing families and friends together. The kitchen backs that up with a genuinely family-shaped menu — empanadas at $14, chorizo-stuffed avocado at $18, a guacamole flight at $16, downtown street tacos at $15, smoked brisket tacos at $17, enchiladas at $21 and carne asada at $34, alongside a real children's menu rather than a token one. It serves from 11am Tuesday through Saturday and from noon on Sundays. Like most of downtown, it was closed by Hurricane Helene in late September 2024 and came back on reduced hours before returning to a full schedule.

The non-alcoholic drinks are worth being precise about, because the menu contains a trap for the unwary. The zero-proof drinks live in their own clearly headed section called "0% ABV Cocktails", and all three are built on Seedlip rather than on juice: the Prickly Pear ($13) with Seedlip Notas de Agave, fresh lime and agave; the Spicy Fuego ($15) with Seedlip Garden 108, a habanero pineapple syrup and lime; and the Spiced Violet ($16) with Seedlip Spice 94, blackberry syrup and lime. Those are the drinks to order. Two other drinks — a Blackberry Smoke and a Spice of Life — have circulated online, including previously on this page, as though they were the non-alcoholic options. They are not. Both appear only in the Margaritas section of the bar's own menu and both are full-strength: the Blackberry Smoke is built on Mezcal Union at $16, and the Spice of Life on Astral Blanco tequila at $15. If you are avoiding alcohol, ask for one of the three by name from the 0% ABV list rather than describing a flavour.

venues.name: Mr West Bar & Bottle Shop
venues.description: A two-level Footscray institution that pairs a proper walk-in bottle shop downstairs with a bar upstairs, both taking non-alcoholic drinks seriously. The bottle shop stocks a genuine zero-proof range across beer, wine and spirits alongside the natural wine and wild-fermented beer it's known for, so you can walk in and buy alcohol-free by the bottle. Confirmed non-alcoholic stock has included Garage Project's Tiny non-alc Stout and IPA and Dr Lo non-alcoholic sparkling, plus house-made non-alcoholic options poured in the bar. NoLo Life rates its no/low range a 4 out of 5. A Footscray bar with a full bottle shop downstairs, run by two operators who track new alcohol-free releases closely enough to have supplied a national non-alcoholic guide with its first NA beer.
venues.hours: Mon closed; Tue-Thu 1pm-11pm; Fri 1pm-1am; Sat 12pm-1am; Sun 12pm-10pm
venues.longDescription:
Mr West opened on Footscray's bustling Nicholson Street Mall in 2017 and quickly became a cornerstone of Melbourne's inner west. It's a two-storey operation: a bottle shop and casual bar rolled into one, deliberately down to earth and, in Broadsheet's words, "nerdy and obsessive about drinks." Local students and families take the picnic tables out front, there are comfy booth seats inside, and an upstairs courtyard that catches the good afternoon sun.

The main draw is a set of 24 taps pouring beer, cider, wine and cocktails, backed by a shop floor deep in natural wine, wild-fermented and Belgian-style beer, and obscure mezcal. Crucially for a non-drinker, that same obsessive curation extends to the zero-proof shelf: the bottle shop carries a real alcohol-free range spanning AF beer, AF red, white and sparkling wine, and adult non-alcoholic spirits, so this is a genuine suburban bottle shop where you can walk in and buy zero-proof to take home.

Specific non-alcoholic stock has included Garage Project's Tiny non-alc Stout and non-alc IPA and Dr Lo non-alcoholic sparkling, while the bar upstairs mixes house-made non-alcoholic drinks alongside its cocktail list. NoLo Life, the Australian no/low directory, lists Mr West with a GOOD range of AF and LA drinks and a NoLo rating of 4.

Food stays casual and BYO-friendly, with cheese boards, charcuterie and ploughman's platters, and staff happy for you to bring in banh mi, Indian or African food from the surrounding streets. It's the kind of unpretentious neighbourhood room where ordering an alcohol-free beer or a house NA drink raises no eyebrows.

The bar-plus-bottle-shop format is the reason this one works so well for non-drinkers. Pub With No Booze describes Mr West as the bar everyone in Footscray wishes were their local, run by Caleb and Josh — two operators it calls passionate hospitality young guns, always looking out for exciting new products — and notes, as an aside that says more than the rest, that Mr West sold the guide its own first non-alcoholic beer. With a comprehensive bottle shop downstairs, the guide reckons all your non-alcoholic needs are covered.

That structure matters practically. A venue with retail underneath turns over stock far faster than a bar alone, which means the alcohol-free range is current rather than a dusty shelf of whatever was bought in two years ago, and it means you can drink something in the room and then take it home. For anyone building a non-alcoholic repertoire rather than getting through a single evening, that is a more useful thing than another cocktail list.
venues.pressQuote: Melbourne is full of great liquor stores, but few are as nerdy and obsessive about drinks as this two-storey bar and bottle shop in bustling Nicholson Street Mall.

venues.name: M'tucci's Bar Roma
venues.description: M'tucci's Bar Roma is the Nob Hill room of a local Italian restaurant group, on Central Avenue, and its alcohol-free drinks are built on house shrubs — pineapple rosemary and blueberry raspberry among them. Shrubs are the most useful thing a restaurant can make for a non-drinker: fruit preserved in vinegar and sugar, they bring sharp acidity and a savoury edge that no juice can, and they hold up across a meal instead of cloying. Italian dining is also where the aperitivo ritual lives, so a bar making its own shrubs can give a non-drinker something to do at the start of dinner. Open 11am daily, to 10pm and 11pm at weekends.
venues.longDescription:
M'tucci's is a local Italian group with several rooms across Albuquerque, and Bar Roma is its Nob Hill outpost on Central Avenue — the old Route 66 strip that is still the city's best stretch for walking between places.

The reason it earns a place here is a technique rather than a drink: the bar makes its own shrubs, and the mocktails are built on them, with pineapple-rosemary and blueberry-raspberry both documented by Visit Albuquerque. A shrub is fruit preserved in sugar and vinegar, and it is the single most useful component in alcohol-free bartending. It delivers acidity with far more depth than citrus alone, it carries a savoury, almost fermented edge, and crucially it stops a drink from becoming sweet — which is the failure mode that makes most mocktails undrinkable by the second half of the glass.

They are also, almost always, made in-house. Nobody stocks a bought shrub, so a bar listing one is telling you it prepares its own drink components, which is the same signal this directory reads at Clio in Omaha and Wild Sage in Spokane.

The Italian setting adds something specific. The aperitivo — a bitter drink before dinner, with something to eat — is one of the few drinking rituals that translates cleanly without alcohol, because bitterness rather than strength is the point of it. A rosemary-and-pineapple shrub with soda does that job properly. For a non-drinker at an Italian table, having a genuine start to the meal rather than waiting for the food is most of the experience.

Open 11am to 10pm Monday through Thursday, to 11pm Friday and Saturday, and to 9pm on Sunday — seven days, all day, with no closed evening.
venues.pressQuote: M'tucci's Bar Roma makes shrub mocktails featuring pineapple rosemary and blueberry raspberry.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Visit Albuquerque, Where To Find Mocktails in Albuquerque

venues.name: Muchacho
venues.description: Muchacho keeps a printed zero-proof cocktail section on its bar menu built with real non-alcoholic spirits, not a token juice pour. The Mock-a-Rita swaps hibiscus-infused Lyre's Agave into the house margarita, and the No-Fashioned is built on Lyre's American Malt with chicha morada and orange. Rounding out the list are the No-Groni Sbagliato (non-alcoholic gin, Italian rosso, rose water, non-alcoholic prosecco) and the herbal Serene-Tea (pear, green tea, grenadine, lemon). Dallas's DiningOut named the lineup among the city's best zero-proof cocktails for Dry January.
signatureDrinks: No-Groni Sbagliato — non-alcoholic gin, Italian rosso, rose water, non-alcoholic prosecco
No-Fashioned — Lyre's American Malt, chicha morada, orange
Mock-a-Rita — hibiscus-infused Lyre's Agave, lime, agave
Serene-Tea — pear, green tea, grenadine, lemon
venues.longDescription:
Muchacho is an elevated Tex-Mex restaurant from five-time James Beard Award-nominated chef Omar Flores, who opened the original in Dallas's Preston Center in 2019 inside the Plaza at Preston Center on Villanova Street. Flores — an Abacus alum who also launched Driftwood, Casa Rubia and Whistle Britches — runs a from-scratch kitchen with an on-site smoker for brisket and smoked meats alongside regional Mexican dishes. The concept has since expanded to Southlake (2021) and Frisco (2026).

While margaritas anchor the bar, Muchacho carries a genuine spirit-free cocktail section built on real non-alcoholic spirits rather than sodas and syrups. The Mock-a-Rita reworks the house margarita with hibiscus-infused Lyre's Agave, lime and agave; the No-Fashioned uses Lyre's American Malt with chicha morada and orange; the No-Groni Sbagliato layers non-alcoholic gin, Italian rosso, rose water and non-alcoholic prosecco; and the Serene-Tea blends pear, green tea, grenadine and lemon. These are priced and served as full cocktails (roughly $15-$17), not afterthoughts.

DiningOut spotlighted the program in its Dry January roundup of Dallas's best zero-proof cocktails, calling Muchacho "the Dallas Tex-Mex staple" and noting the Mock-a-Rita lets everyone in on the chips-queso-and-margarita ritual.
venues.pressQuote: The Dallas Tex-Mex staple uses hibiscus-infused Lyre's Tequila Alternative with lime and agave for a sober-friendly indulgence. The zero-proof menu also includes a No-Fashioned, No-Groni Sbagliato, and Serene-Tea, an invigorating blend of pear, green tea, grenadine, and lemon.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: DiningOut, "Dry January, Dallas-Style: Where to Find the City's Best Zero-Proof Cocktails"

venues.name: Muddy Water Kava
venues.description: Muddy Water runs 8am to 2am every day of the week in north St. Petersburg, one of the longest trading days in a county that calls itself the unofficial kava capital of the United States. Kava is the primary focus, and the coffee and tea alongside it are locally roasted, organic and treated as a programme in their own right rather than as filler. The staff are the selling point: the venue's own framing is that they will walk you through a wide array of botanicals — damiana, rhodiola, yerba mate, kanna, matcha. IMPORTANT for readers in recovery: kratom is among those botanicals. It acts on opioid receptors and carries dependence and withdrawal risk that kava does not, so say what you are avoiding and they will steer you.
venues.longDescription:
Muddy Water runs 8am to 2am every day of the week in north St. Petersburg — an eighteen-hour trading day, in the county that calls itself the unofficial kava capital of the United States. Pinellas County genuinely earns that description: dozens of kava bars operate across it, and this directory already lists Grassroots, Bula Kafe, Speakeasy Central and Mad Hatters Ethnobotanical in St. Petersburg alone, with Low Tide and The Muddy Root down in Gulfport.

What distinguishes Muddy Water within that crowded field is the seriousness of the non-kava programme. The coffee and tea are locally roasted, organic and treated as a discipline in their own right rather than as something to offer people who do not want kava — the venue's own framing is consciously crafted, and it shows in a menu that would stand up in a specialist coffee bar. For a room open from 8am, that matters: it means the first half of the day is not an afterthought.

Kava is the ground root of Piper methysticum, a shrub native to the South Pacific islands, prepared as a cold water infusion and drunk socially across Fiji, Vanuatu, Tonga and Samoa for roughly three thousand years. It contains no alcohol. It tastes earthy and bitter, numbs the lips and tongue on the first mouthful, and is mildly sedative rather than intoxicating in the way alcohol is. Kava exhibits reverse tolerance, so regular drinkers typically need less rather than more to feel it, and a first visit rewards a slow pace across an hour or two.

The staff are the venue's stated selling point, and the claim is specific enough to be checkable: they are described as knowledgeable across a wide array of botanical products, and the list the bar itself gives runs damiana, rhodiola, yerba mate, kanna, matcha — and kratom. That breadth is genuinely useful if you know what you are looking for and genuinely hazardous if you do not.

Which is the caution. Kratom is among those botanicals, sold from the same bar as everything else. It is the leaf of Mitragyna speciosa, a Southeast Asian tree, and its principal alkaloids act on the opioid receptors; regular use produces tolerance and a real withdrawal syndrome, several US states ban it outright, and its concentrated 7-hydroxymitragynine derivatives face active federal scheduling. Kava carries no comparable dependence profile, and neither do damiana, rhodiola, yerba mate or matcha. The good news is that this is a room where the staff will actually engage with the question: say what you are avoiding and why, and they will steer you through the list. That is a better position than most kava bars offer, and it is worth using.
venues.pressQuote: Beyond the unique effects of kava, we pride ourselves on fostering a sense of community within our walls

venues.name: Multnomah Whiskey Library
venues.description: Multnomah Whiskey Library is a spirits library at 1124 SW Alder Street in downtown Portland, famous for one of the deepest whisky collections in the country — and, less famously, it keeps a real non-alcoholic list. CORRECTION TO OUR EARLIER LISTING: older versions of its beverage menu carried nothing alcohol-free; the current menu, updated in April 2026, has a printed "Mocktails" section of six drinks. Love at Midnight ($10) is coconut cream, pineapple, lime, orange and demerara; Jungle Flower ($12) pairs pineapple with Ghia apéritif, lime and house falernum; Out of the Woods ($15) is the ambitious one, built on Everleaf Forest apéritif with non-alcoholic sparkling wine and lemon; and three bottled St. Agrestis Phony Negronis — original, white and espresso — are $12 each. Best Day Electro Lime and Athletic Run Wild are $7. IMPORTANT ON ACCESS: the formal Library room is member-nominated and reservation-led, but the ground-floor Green Room takes walk-ins every day with no membership and no reservation — its general manager says plainly that they want walk-ins. All spaces are 21+.

venues.longDescription:
Multnomah Whiskey Library is exactly what its name promises — a downtown Portland room lined floor to ceiling with spirits, where drinks are brought to the table from rolling carts — and it is not the sort of place a non-drinker would think to try. Two things make it worth reconsidering. The first is access. The Library proper works on a membership model with a waiting list and nominations, which puts most people off entirely, but that is only half the building: the ground-floor Green Room takes walk-ins with no membership and no reservation at all. General manager Lani Sickman has put it as directly as anyone could — they take walk-ins every day, they want walk-ins, they love to see them. All spaces are 21 and over.

The second is that the non-alcoholic list is real, and this is a correction to our earlier entry. An older version of the beverage menu carried nothing alcohol-free, and anyone checking would reasonably have concluded a whisky library has nothing for them. The menu was rewritten in April 2026 and now has a printed Mocktails section running six deep. Love at Midnight at $10 is the tropical one — coconut cream, pineapple, lime, orange and demerara. Jungle Flower at $12 puts pineapple and lime against Ghia, the botanical apéritif, with a house falernum. Out of the Woods at $15 is the drink to order if you want something with the weight of an actual cocktail: Everleaf Forest apéritif lengthened with non-alcoholic sparkling wine and lemon, which gives it both bitterness and length. And there are three bottled St. Agrestis Phony Negronis at $12 apiece — the original, the white and the espresso — which is unusual; most bars stock one. Below that sits a soft-drink section done with the same care as everywhere else in the building: Mexican Coca-Cola and Sprite, Fever-Tree tonic and ginger beer, Topo Chico, Steven Smith teas and Proud Mary coffee, both Portland roasters. Non-alcoholic Best Day Electro Lime and Athletic Run Wild are $7 on the beer list.
venues.pressQuote: There's no need to become a member — or even make a paid reservation — to get the experience. "We take walk-ins every day," says Lani Sickman, general manager. "We want walk-ins. We love to see them."

venues.name: Muni Muni Tea Shop
venues.description: Muni Muni Tea Shop is a fully alcohol-free tea and matcha bar on Church Street in downtown Nashville, a few blocks north of the Broadway strip. Everything is brewed or whisked to order rather than poured from a batch, and the menu is unusually specific about it: ceremonial-grade matcha, first-flush roasted hojicha, assam and jasmine green teas brewed per cup. The signature builds include a Strawberry Matcha Latte with milk cap and strawberry inclusions, a Coconut Matcha Latte with house virgin coquito and toasted coconut, a Hojicha Cheese Einspanner, and Cafe Cha, which layers earl grey and blue mountain coffee over coffee jelly. Bubble tea and tapioca options run alongside. No alcohol is served, and it stays open to 7pm on Friday, Saturday and Sunday.
signatureDrinks: Strawberry Matcha Latte - ceremonial grade matcha, whole milk, milk cap and strawberry inclusions $7.25
Coconut Matcha Latte - matcha, whole milk, house virgin coquito, milk cap, cinnamon and toasted coconut $7.95
Hojicha Cheese Einspanner - first flush roasted green tea, whole milk, cheese cap $7.25
Cafe Cha - earl grey black tea and blue mountain coffee with coffee jelly and milk cap $7.70
Muni Muni Milk Tea - earl grey black tea, brewed to order $6.20
Lychee Dragon Fruit Tea - lychee, dragon fruit, assam or jasmine green tea $6.70
Ube Matcha Latte - matcha, whole milk, house-made ube milk blend, milk or cheese cap $7.95
venues.longDescription:
Muni Muni sits in a ground-floor suite on Church Street, three blocks up from the Broadway honky-tonks and squarely inside the downtown core, which is what makes it worth knowing about: this stretch of Nashville is overwhelmingly given over to drinking, and there is very little in it that is open in the evening and serves nothing alcoholic. Muni Muni does. The Nashville Downtown Partnership, the business-district organisation that keeps the official downtown directory, lists it as the local downtown tea shop for bubble milk tea, matcha and boba.

The menu rewards reading rather than pointing. Matcha is ceremonial grade and whisked per order, and the flavoured versions are built rather than syruped: the Strawberry Matcha Latte comes with a milk cap and actual strawberry inclusions; the Coconut Matcha Latte uses a house virgin coquito with cinnamon and toasted shredded coconut on top; the Banana Nut Toffee version uses banana milk, a salted banana cream cap and almond toffee bits; there is an Ube Matcha Latte with a house-made ube milk blend. The tea side is brewed to order too - the Muni Muni Milk Tea on earl grey, a roasted oolong milk tea, a mango milk tea on jasmine green, a Lychee Dragon Fruit fruit tea. Two drinks stand out as the ones to order if you want to see what the shop can do: the Hojicha Cheese Einspanner, a first-flush roasted green tea under a generous cheese cap, low in caffeine and built for the end of a day; and Cafe Cha, which layers earl grey and blue mountain coffee over coffee jelly with a milk cap. Tiger sugar milk with tapioca pearls and a bruleed cheese cap covers the classic bubble-tea end.

Nothing on the list contains alcohol. Sizes are 16oz for the matcha builds and 22oz for the teas, and most drinks land between $6 and $8. Hours are 11am to 6pm early in the week, 11am to 7pm on Friday and 10am to 7pm at weekends, so this is an afternoon and early-evening stop rather than a late one - useful before a show at Bridgestone or the Ryman, both a short walk away.
venues.pressQuote: Your local, downtown Nashville tea shop for bubble milk tea, matcha, and boba!

venues.name: Muskellounge & Sporting Club
venues.description: Muskellounge & Sporting Club is a cocktail bar on Monona Drive in the Lake Edge neighbourhood, themed around Wisconsin's fishing and sporting-club tradition, and its non-alcoholic list leans on ready-to-drink bitters rather than sugar. It pours St. Agrestis's Phony Negroni — the Brooklyn producer's non-alcoholic negroni in a bottle, which is genuinely bitter and carbonated — alongside the Amaro Falso, its zero-proof amaro. Serving two bittersweet Italian styles rather than two sweet ones is an unusual and welcome choice. The bar keeps late hours for the east side, to midnight midweek and 1am on Friday and Saturday.
signatureDrinks: St. Agrestis Phony Negroni (non-alcoholic negroni, bitter and carbonated)
venues.longDescription:
The muskellunge is Wisconsin's state fish, a large and famously difficult predator that generations of anglers have failed to catch, and Muskellounge & Sporting Club builds its whole identity on that tradition — the sporting club being a genuine Upper Midwest institution, part bar and part fishing society. It sits on Monona Drive in Lake Edge, on the east side between Lake Monona and the Beltline, well outside the downtown cluster.

The non-alcoholic choice made here is a specific and intelligent one. Rather than building mocktails from scratch, the bar stocks St. Agrestis — the Brooklyn producer whose Phony Negroni is the most successful bottled non-alcoholic cocktail in the American market — and its companion Amaro Falso. What distinguishes both is bitterness. The Phony Negroni is genuinely bitter and lightly carbonated, built to be poured cold over ice with an orange twist, and it drinks like an apéritif rather than a soft drink; the Amaro Falso does the digestif end of the same idea. For a non-drinker, the thing most often missing from a bar's alcohol-free offer is bitterness — sugar is easy, bitterness is not — and a bar that solves it by stocking the right bottle rather than pretending to build it from scratch has made the honest call.

It is worth being plain that this is a full cocktail bar with a Wisconsin bar's atmosphere, not a quiet room, and the hours reflect it: 3pm to midnight Monday through Thursday, to 1am on Friday and Saturday, opening at 1pm Saturday and noon Sunday. It is about ten minutes' drive east of the Capitol and does not connect on foot to anything else in this guide, so treat it as its own destination — which, for a bittersweet drink in a room full of taxidermy and vintage lures, it comfortably is.
venues.pressQuote: Muskellounge and Sporting Club serves St. Agrestis's Phony Negroni and Amaro Falso.

venues.name: Myriel
venues.description: Myriel is chef-owner Karyn Tomlinson's tasting-menu restaurant on South Cleveland Avenue in Macalester-Groveland; Tomlinson won the James Beard Award for Best Chef: Midwest in June 2025. The kitchen cooks a Midwestern menu from what the season gives it, and the beverage side runs a full non-alcoholic pairing against the tasting menu rather than offering a single spirit-free drink as an alternative. The pairing's anchor is a dry sparkling tea, deliberately oversteeped so that the tannin gives it the body and drying finish of a wine and resets the palate between courses. Two sweeter non-alcoholic options run alongside it. Bar seats are held for walk-ins.
venues.address: 470 S Cleveland Ave, Saint Paul, MN 55105
signatureDrinks: Dry sparkling tea (oversteeped, served as a non-alcoholic tasting-menu pairing)
venues.longDescription:
Myriel sits on South Cleveland Avenue in Macalester-Groveland, in the residential middle of Saint Paul rather than in any of its restaurant districts, and it works as a tasting-menu room with a short a la carte alternative and a handful of bar seats kept back for walk-ins between 4:45pm and 9:30pm. Karyn Tomlinson is the chef-owner. In June 2025 she won the James Beard Award for Best Chef: Midwest, beating Shigeyuki Furukawa of Kado No Mise and Diane Moua of Diane's Place, and accepted it wearing a coral dress her grandmother had worn in 1941; the cooking that got her there is rooted in Midwestern produce, preserving and dairy rather than in imported luxury.

For a non-drinker the relevant fact is that Myriel runs a genuine non-alcoholic pairing against the tasting menu, course by course, rather than treating spirit-free as a substitution to be handled on request. The drink at the centre of it is a dry sparkling tea, brewed deliberately past the point where most kitchens would stop: the extra steeping pulls more tannin, which gives the liquid weight in the mouth and a drying finish, and the effect is that it functions structurally the way a dry white wine functions in a pairing — it clears the palate between courses instead of coating it. A sober restaurant critic writing for Beyond Beurre Blanc in January 2026 called it their favourite non-alcoholic cocktail in the Twin Cities, noting that it is "slightly oversteeped, giving it body and the mouthfeel of a good wine." Two sweeter non-alcoholic options sit alongside it for anyone who wants something less austere. The restaurant is licensed and pours wine, so this is not an alcohol-free room; what distinguishes it is that the non-alcoholic side has been designed as a parallel pairing rather than an accommodation. Service runs Wednesday to Saturday only, and reservations are strongly advised for the dining room.
venues.pressQuote: The dry sparkling tea is slightly oversteeped, giving it body and the mouthfeel of a good wine.

venues.name: Naïve Kitchen + Bar
venues.description: Naïve occupies a corner building on East Washington Street in Butchertown and has been one of Louisville's more health-conscious restaurants since it opened, winning LEO Weekly's Readers Choice for Best Butchertown Restaurant and building a reputation on vegetable-forward cooking and an eco-minded operation. Its earlier menu carried a genuinely developed alcohol-free list — a Grapefruit Thyme Spritz, a ginger turmeric mule using the Louisville-made Modica mixers, and an apricot tarragon shrub soda — and Louisville's visitor bureau listed it among the city's best mocktail stops on that basis. The kitchen has since relaunched with a Latin-leaning menu, so ask what the current alcohol-free builds are.
venues.longDescription:
Naïve opened in Butchertown as a deliberately health-forward restaurant — vegetable-centric, seasonal, eco-conscious down to the fit-out — and won LEO Weekly's Readers Choice award for Best Butchertown Restaurant. That positioning made it a natural fit for a non-alcoholic guide, and its drinks list backed it up: a Grapefruit Thyme Spritz, an apricot tarragon shrub soda, and a ginger turmeric mule built on Modica, the Louisville-founded mixer company started by JD Mitchell and Eric Wentworth, whose superfood-based cocktail mixes are used for mocktails by roughly a third of their buyers. GoToLouisville, the city's official visitor bureau, listed Naïve among the best places in town to drink alcohol-free.

The restaurant has since relaunched. It now describes itself as globally inspired and locally executed, with bold seasonal flavours and a Latin soul, trading from the same corner at 1001 East Washington Street with a new menu. We have verified that it is open and trading — the address, phone and hours here come from the restaurant's own site — but we have not been able to verify which alcohol-free drinks survived the change, so the named builds above are recorded as its documented past programme rather than as a current menu. Ask at the bar.

One note for anyone checking this venue elsewhere: Yelp currently carries a CLOSED flag on the old Naïve listing, which reflects the end of the previous concept rather than the end of the business. The restaurant is open, Thursday through Monday, from 11am, with the kitchen running to 9pm on Sunday and Monday and 10pm Thursday through Saturday, and it is closed Tuesday and Wednesday. Butchertown puts Copper & Kings' rooftop, Pizza Lupo and the relocated Cultured cheese and charcuterie bar all within a short walk.
venues.pressQuote: Naive is a West Coast-inspired, vegetable-forward eatery that prizes healthy lifestyles. Its alcohol-free offerings include a Grapefruit Thyme Spritz, Modica's Ginger Turmeric Mule, and an Apricot Tarragon Shrub Soda.

venues.name: Nalu Kava Tea Lounge
venues.description: Nalu is a fully alcohol-free tea lounge hidden on the second floor above Cherry Sprout Produce in Humboldt, reached by an alley behind the Red Fox. Owner Holland Mulder opened it after deciding she no longer wanted to spend evenings in bars, and the menu is built around hand-prepared kava, thick drinking chocolate, mushroom tonics such as chaga and lion's mane, superfood lattes, kombucha and fire cider. The indoor room is full of plants, books and oracle decks; above it sits a rooftop patio and greenhouse. Kava is alcohol-free but psychoactive and mildly sedating — worth knowing before a first visit.
venues.longDescription:
Nalu occupies the second floor of the building at 722 N Sumner Street that Cherry Sprout Produce has anchored since 2007, tucked in beside the Red Fox on a corner that has been a Humboldt neighbourhood institution for years. Getting in requires knowing it is there: the entrance is off the alley behind the bar, up a flight of stairs, with no street frontage to speak of. Owner Holland Mulder has been candid that this is deliberate — as she told Willamette Week when the lounge opened, only the daring and persistent find the place.

She built it for a specific reason. Mulder reached a point where she no longer wanted her evenings to happen in bars, and what she wanted instead — somewhere open late, social, with something interesting in the cup and no alcohol anywhere — did not exist in her part of North Portland. So the menu is kava prepared by hand from real root, drinking chocolate made properly and thickly, mushroom tonics built on chaga and lion's mane, superfood lattes, kombucha and fire cider. Nothing on it is alcoholic.

The room does a lot of the work. Indoors it is small and warm, filled with plants, stacks of books and oracle decks, and it suits both a solo evening with something to read and a table of three or four talking quietly. Upstairs again is the part regulars send people for: a rooftop patio with a greenhouse, which in a city that spends half the year under cloud is a genuinely different proposition from a covered smoking shelter. Hours are short and specific — five to eleven, closed Tuesdays and Wednesdays — so it rewards checking Instagram before setting out.

The honest caveat is the same one that applies to every kava room. Kava contains no alcohol, but it is psychoactive: mildly sedating, slow to come on, and not something to mix with alcohol or with sedating prescriptions. Some of the mushroom and adaptogen drinks here are functional rather than intoxicating, and the drinking chocolate is simply drinking chocolate, so there is plenty on the menu for someone avoiding mood-altering substances entirely — but it is worth asking which is which rather than assuming.
venues.pressQuote: I reached a place where I just didn't want to go to the bar anymore.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Holland Mulder, Nalu owner, to Willamette Week

venues.name: Namak
venues.description: Namak is an Eastern Mediterranean and Persian restaurant at 1813 Columbia Road NW in the heart of Adams Morgan, opened in 2024 by longtime friends and established restaurateurs John Cidre and Saied Azali. The kitchen turns out creative takes on Persian, Greek, Turkish and North African cooking - sesame-crusted feta, walnut-marinated tenderloin kebabs, braised lamb shoulder in a harissa-scented jus - inside a room of cosy alcoves and Moroccan tile work. Its non-alcoholic list is unusually serious for a restaurant, and Resy singled it out as a menu where the zero-proof drinks take centre stage. The Zero Proof section of its current menu runs from the N/Amaro Namakia, a house-made lapsang souchong amaro-style liqueur, and Sekahnjebin, built on mint, cucumber, rose, honey and vinegar, to Şalgam, the traditional spicy fermented black carrot juice, plus house-made sodas in ginger-lemongrass, spiced mango-passionfruit and blackberry-long hot pepper.
venues.longDescription:
Namak opened in 2024 at 1813 Columbia Road NW, in the middle of Adams Morgan, from two established DC restaurateurs and longtime friends, John Cidre and Saied Azali. The cooking is Eastern Mediterranean and Persian and it ranges widely - sesame-crusted feta, walnut-marinated tenderloin kebabs, braised lamb shoulder in a harissa-scented jus, drawing on Persian, Greek, Turkish and North African traditions rather than settling in one. The room is built in cosy alcoves with Moroccan tile work, which makes a restaurant of its size feel like several smaller ones, and it stays busy through service. Washingtonian placed it at number 98 on its 100 Very Best Restaurants 2026 list, published in January 2026.

The non-alcoholic list is the reason it is here, and Resy's January 2025 roundup of DC bars with superb zero-proof cocktails put it plainly: at Namak the non-alcoholic menu takes centre stage with a diverse range of flavours, including drinks from the Eastern Mediterranean. That last part is what separates it from a restaurant that simply keeps a mocktail on hand. The beverage menu the restaurant publishes now carries a Zero Proof section of its own, and it mixes one house invention with two drinks that are not cocktail riffs at all but traditional pours from the region the kitchen cooks from. The invention is the N/Amaro Namakia at $18, a house-made amaro-style liqueur built on lapsang souchong, the smoked black tea. Sekahnjebin, at $12, is the traditional Persian mint-and-vinegar cooler, made here with mint, cucumber, rose, honey and vinegar. Şalgam, at $6, is listed as traditional spicy fermented black carrot juice, and it is the more challenging of the two - sour, salty and an acquired taste that rewards ordering alongside kebab rather than on its own. House-made sodas at $10 come in ginger-lemongrass, spiced mango-passionfruit and blackberry-long hot pepper.

Practical notes. Namak is closed on Monday, serves dinner Tuesday through Saturday from 5pm - to 9pm midweek and 10pm on Friday and Saturday - and adds a Sunday brunch from 11am to 3pm before an early Sunday dinner service. Adams Morgan gets loud at weekends, and this is one of the calmer rooms on that stretch. It sits a few doors from The Green Zone and Lapis, which makes the block unusually good for a night out without drinking.
venues.pressQuote: Namak's non-alcoholic menu takes center stage with a diverse range of flavors, including drinks from the Eastern Mediterranean
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Resy, 10 Washington, D.C. Bars With Superb Zero-Proof Cocktails, January 2025

venues.name: Namaste & Midtown
venues.description: Namaste & Midtown is a fully alcohol-free kava and healing lounge on Kansas City's 39th Street corridor, in the Volker/Midtown area. It reopened in August 2025 from the former Midtown Kava, reframed by owners Moon Brown (a community organizer and anti-violence advocate), Alan Wayne (a Kansas City rapper behind the "Namaste & Shit" brand), and Andrew Beck. Local press describes it as a Black- and queer-owned sober bar built as a sanctuary for Black, queer, trans, and sober communities. The drink program is entirely zero-proof: house "Sacred Sips" plus carried-over staples like kombucha, traditional kava, and THC- and CBD-infused herbal teas. Named pours include Blue Moon (kava, coconut, CBD, microdose THC), Glitch in the Matrix (kava, ube coconut cream, vanilla matcha), and Astral Grounds (cold brew, functional mushrooms, cacao, eucalyptus honey, kava). The space also hosts "Tiny Shell Sessions" spotlighting Black and queer artists.
venues.longDescription:
Namaste & Midtown is an alcohol-free kava and healing lounge at 1415 W 39th Street on Kansas City's 39th Street corridor, which reopened on 1 August 2025 in the space that had been Midtown Kava. It comes from three owners with unusually varied backgrounds: Moon Brown, a community leader and abolitionist with nearly two decades of anti-violence work behind her, who previously ran a metaphysical boutique in Belize; Alan Wayne, a Kansas City rapper who brings the energy of his Namaste & Shit clothing line to the room; and Andrew Beck, whose background is in construction and project management. Startland News covered the reopening under the headline "Sacred sips", describing an alcohol-free bar creating a healing space where every drink is medicine. Brown's own framing of why the format works is the most useful line written about kava bars in this city: kava, she said, lets people with anxiety be in a bar without alcohol.

The drinks are built on traditional kava, and the lounge kept the staples of its predecessor — kombucha, traditional kava preparations and herbal teas — while adding its own. Blue Moon combines house kava with creamy coconut, 10mg of CBD and a microdose of THC. Glitch in the Matrix pairs kava with ube coconut cream and vanilla matcha. Astral Grounds is the most caffeinated, layering cold brew coffee with functional mushrooms, cacao and eucalyptus honey over traditional kava. Two things need stating plainly. First, several drinks here contain THC and CBD, and the herbal teas carried over from Midtown Kava are THC-infused — so while nothing on the menu contains alcohol, this is not a venue for anyone avoiding psychoactive substances generally, and kava itself is psychoactive in its own right. Second, the lounge maintains no website we can find, and its only surviving social presence is under the former Midtown Kava name, so hours and the current drink list are best confirmed by calling ahead or asking in person.
venues.pressQuote: Kava lets people with anxiety be in a bar without alcohol.

venues.name: Nari
venues.description: Nari is a one-Michelin-star contemporary Thai restaurant inside Hotel Kabuki in San Francisco's Japantown, from chef/owner Pim Techamuanvivit of Kin Khao. The name "Nari," a Thai word for "women," honors generations of Thai women who shaped the country's cuisine, and the kitchen filters traditional Thai cooking through California ingredients. The bar runs a small, deliberately edited "zero-proof cocktails" list that sits alongside the full cocktail and wine programs — five spirit-free drinks at $16 each, built on non-alcoholic spirits like Seedlip Grove and Pentire. Current named pours include the Unakarn (Seedlip Grove, shiso, lemongrass, tonic), the Suwan (Seedlip Grove, pomegranate, lime), the Nohra (Pentire Adrift, mint, lime, shiso), the Illa (Pentire, passionfruit, lemon, orgeat), and the dairy-forward Kusuma (mango-lassi, pandan, pineapple). It's a fine-dining destination, so reservations are recommended well in advance.

venues.longDescription:
Nari is a contemporary Thai restaurant inside Hotel Kabuki at 1625 Post Street in Japantown, from chef and owner Pim Techamuanvivit, who also runs Kin Khao in San Francisco and has held the kitchen at Bangkok's Nahm. The name is a Thai word for "women," chosen to honour the generations of Thai women who shaped the country's cooking, and the kitchen filters heritage recipes through California produce — brick-red bumbai curry with crisp fried eggplant and flaky roti, grilled Monterey squid in chilli-lime dressing with pork jowl. Dishes arrive family style with a degree of refinement, and the restaurant holds a Michelin star. Service is dinner only, from 5:30pm, and the room books out well in advance.

The bar runs a small, deliberately edited zero-proof list that sits on the same menu as the cocktails and wine rather than on a separate card — five spirit-free drinks at $16 each, priced with the cocktails. They are built on distilled non-alcoholic spirits rather than juice: the Unakarn (Seedlip Grove, shiso, lemongrass and tonic), the Suwan (Seedlip Grove, pomegranate and lime), the Nohra (Pentire Adrift, mint, lime and shiso), the Illa (Pentire, passionfruit, lemon and orgeat) and the dairy-forward Kusuma (mango lassi, pandan and pineapple). The editing is the point. Five drinks that each pair to a different part of a Thai menu — herbal, sour, sweet-sharp, and one lassi-style pour built to sit against chilli heat — is more useful across a shared table than a longer list of variations on the same sweet profile. Shiso and lemongrass recur because they bridge the drinks to the food rather than competing with it. For a non-drinker, Nari is one of the few Michelin-starred rooms in the city where the alcohol-free option is a considered part of the beverage programme rather than an improvisation requested at the table.

venues.name: Narrative
venues.description: Narrative is the signature restaurant of The Jacquard, an Autograph Collection hotel in Cherry Creek North with a rooftop pool and bar. It runs a seasonal mocktail list alongside its cocktails, changed with the menu rather than held static: Visit Denver names Bitter Passion, built on passion fruit and ginger, and Herb Heaven, made with lemon, mint and cucumber. The restaurant opens at 6:30am on weekdays and 7am at weekends and serves through to 11pm, covering breakfast, lunch, dinner and late drinks in a neighbourhood where most kitchens close earlier. The rooftop gives the same drinks a second setting in summer. It is a modest but genuine zero-proof offering in a part of Denver that the city's existing non-alcoholic coverage has largely missed.

venues.longDescription:
Narrative is the signature restaurant of The Jacquard, an Autograph Collection hotel at 222 Milwaukee Street in Cherry Creek North, and takes its name from the idea that everything on the menu should have a story attached to it. The hotel is known locally for its rooftop pool and bar, which gives the restaurant a second, seasonal room with a view over the neighbourhood, and Narrative itself has been covered by Eater Denver and is a regular fixture on Cherry Creek North's dining lists. The kitchen opens at 6:30am on weekdays and 7am at weekends and serves until 11pm, which is a longer day than almost any other restaurant in the district keeps.

The non-alcoholic list is described by Visit Denver's December 2025 guide as seasonal, which is the key detail — the drinks change with the menu rather than sitting on the board indefinitely. Two that the guide names are Bitter Passion, built on passion fruit and ginger, and Herb Heaven, made with lemon, mint and cucumber. The naming convention gives away the intent: one is structured around a bitter-and-sharp axis, the other around fresh herbs and cucumber, which are the two most reliable ways to build an alcohol-free drink that does not simply taste sweet. Neither is a landmark programme of the kind that Lady Jane or Peach Crease Club run on the other side of the city, and Narrative is listed here at a modest strength for that reason. What it offers instead is coverage: Cherry Creek is one of Denver's busiest dining districts and has been substantially absent from the city's non-alcoholic mapping, and Narrative, alongside Forget Me Not a few blocks west and Local Jones on Columbine, gives a visitor staying in that part of town three separate rooms where a considered zero-proof drink is on the printed menu. The rooftop is the differentiator in summer, when the same drinks arrive somewhere with a view rather than in a hotel dining room.
venues.pressQuote: Inside the Jacquard Hotel & Rooftop, you'll find the hotel's signature restaurant, Narrative, and some exciting seasonal mocktails like Bitter Passion with passion fruit and ginger, and Herb Heaven with lemon, mint and cucumber.

venues.name: Native
venues.description: Native, Vijay Mudaliar's pioneering sustainability-led cocktail bar on Amoy Street, runs a full non-alcoholic menu with as many drinks as its alcohol list, all built without refined sugar using hydrosols, edible oils and in-house ferments. Zero-proof anchors include the Sereh Telang (butterfly pea, lemongrass, calamansi) and a house Thai-style ginger beer (galangal, lemongrass, kaffir lime leaf, chili), each around S$12. The team leans on its fermentation lab -- kombuchas, misos, meads and a koji-aged 'pineapple shoyu' from fruit waste -- to give the no-alcohol builds real depth. Native ranked No. 45 on Asia's 50 Best Bars 2025 and No. 84 on The World's 50 Best Bars 2025.
signatureDrinks: Sereh Telang (butterfly pea, lemongrass, calamansi) - S$12
Thai Style Ginger Beer (galangal, lemongrass, kaffir lime leaf, chili) - S$12
venues.longDescription:
Founded in December 2016 by Vijay Mudaliar (formerly of Operation Dagger), Native occupies a converted shophouse at 52A Amoy Street in the CBD's Telok Ayer / Tanjong Pagar quarter. The multi-floor concept pairs a ground-floor restaurant exploring locality through food with a cocktail bar of regional spirits and experimental drinks and an in-house fermentation lab, all guided by a sustainability-led philosophy built on local and regional ingredients.

Native has been a fixture on the world stage since it was named Highest Climber on The World's 50 Best Bars in 2018, jumping 34 places. In 2025 it ranked No. 45 on Asia's 50 Best Bars and No. 84 on The World's 50 Best Bars, cementing its reputation as one of Southeast Asia's most influential drinks destinations.

The zero-proof offering is a genuine anchor rather than an afterthought. As founder Vijay Mudaliar puts it, the bar keeps a non-alcoholic menu that equals the number of cocktails, none of it using refined sugar and drawing instead on hydrosols, edible oils and the team's ferments. Signatures include the Sereh Telang, a butterfly-pea build with lemongrass and calamansi, and a house Thai-style ginger beer of galangal, lemongrass, kaffir lime leaf and chili, each around S$12.

Fermentation underpins the whole program: the lab turns out kombuchas, misos, meads and a two-month koji-aged 'pineapple shoyu' made from fruit waste, letting the kitchen and bar lengthen and deepen local flavours that Singapore, with few alcohol producers of its own, would otherwise struggle to source. It is one of the clearest examples anywhere of a top-ranked cocktail bar treating no- and low-alcohol drinking with the same rigour as its spirits list.
venues.pressQuote: We also have a non-alcoholic menu that equals the number of cocktails. None of it uses refined sugars and we use techniques such as hydrosols, edible oils and ferments.

venues.name: Nativo
venues.description: Nativo is a modern Mexican cantina on York Boulevard in Highland Park, owned by Gabriel Paredes and Corrissa Hernandez, who also run Xelas in Boyle Heights. It is a licensed bar built around agave, rum and cerveza artesanal, and it carries one of the deepest standing zero-proof lists in Los Angeles: a titled Zero Proof Cocktails section with six named builds, all made with zero percent alcohol. The list runs a Margarita Mocktail on Ritual Zero tequila with orange cordial, lime, agave and housemade Tajin salt; a Zero Proof Pina Colada; a Paloma Mocktail; a Zero Proof Mojito; a Zero Proof Whiskey Sour with egg whites; and a Zero Proof Penicillin finished with a smoky botanical mist spray. Open to 2am on Friday and Saturday.
venues.hours: Mon closed; Tue-Thu 5pm-12am; Fri-Sat 5pm-2am; Sun closed
signatureDrinks: Zero Proof Margarita - Ritual Zero tequila, orange cordial, lime, agave, kosher or housemade Tajin salt $11
Zero Proof Pina Colada - Ritual Zero Proof rum alternative, pineapple, lime, coconut cream $14
Zero Proof Paloma - Ritual Zero Proof tequila alternative, grapefruit juice, lime, soda, kosher salt $10
Zero Proof Mojito - Ritual Zero Proof rum alternative, lime, sugar, mint, soda $10
Zero Proof Whiskey Sour - Ritual Zero Proof whisky alternative, lemon, sugar, egg whites $15
Zero Proof Penicillin - Ritual Zero Proof whisky, lemon, ginger, honey, smoky botanical mist spray $11
venues.longDescription:
Nativo opened on York Boulevard in 2020, and L.A. TACO covered it as a concept nine years in the making: a Latin-owned modern cantina with an emphasis on agave, rum and cerveza artesanal, with a Mexican food menu drawn from owner Gabriel Paredes' family roots in Northeast LA and, further back, in Guadalajara. Paredes runs it with his wife Corrissa Hernandez; it was their third business together, after Craft Beer Cellar in Eagle Rock and alongside Xelas in Boyle Heights. The room is a proper neighbourhood bar rather than a restaurant with a bar attached, walk-ins only, open late.

The reason it belongs in this directory is the zero-proof section, which is unusually serious for a cantina. It sits on the same cocktail menu as everything else under a heading that states the case without hedging - Zero Proof Cocktails, made with zero percent alcohol - and it runs to six drinks rather than the customary one or two. Five of them are built on Ritual Zero Proof's spirit alternatives, which means they are constructed the way the alcoholic versions are rather than being sweetened juice. The Margarita Mocktail uses Ritual Zero tequila with orange cordial, lime, agave and a choice of kosher or housemade Tajin salt, at $11. The Zero Proof Pina Colada is Ritual's rum alternative with pineapple, lime and coconut cream at $14. The Paloma Mocktail is the tequila alternative with grapefruit juice, lime, soda and kosher salt at $10, and the Zero Proof Mojito is the rum alternative with lime, sugar, mint and soda, also $10. The two that show the most intent are at the whisky end: a Zero Proof Whiskey Sour, shaken with egg whites at $15, and a Zero Proof Penicillin with lemon, ginger and honey, finished with a smoky botanical mist spray at $11 - a direct mirror of the alcoholic Penicillin on the list above it, which uses an Islay mist.

Practical notes. Nativo is closed Monday and Sunday, runs 5pm to midnight Tuesday through Thursday and 5pm to 2am on Friday and Saturday, and does not take reservations for the bar. Happy hour is Monday to Friday 5-7pm and all day Thursday, but the zero-proof list is priced off the standing menu rather than discounted.
venues.pressQuote: a Latin-owned modern cantina with an emphasis on agave, rum, and cerveza artesanal

venues.name: Nautilus Pier 4
venues.description: Nautilus Pier 4 is the Boston outpost of the Nantucket restaurant The Nautilus, on the water at Pier 4 Boulevard in the Seaport. It serves modern Asian-inflected seafood and small plates with a raw bar, dinner nightly and lunch at weekends. Its drinks list prints a non-alcoholic section under the heading Don't Mock It 'Til You Try It, subtitled N/A bevies for the sober curious, with three named drinks at $13 and cold brew on draft at $7. G+G is guava, grapefruit, citrus and soda; Pineapple Express is pineapple, a house-made ginger soda and lime; and Thai Herb Swing is watermelon, Thai herbs, lime and soda. The cold brew is roasted locally at Atomic Coffee. The builds are citrus- and fruit-forward and designed to sit next to seafood.
venues.hours: Mon-Wed 5pm-9:30pm; Thu-Fri 5pm-10pm; Sat 12pm-2:45pm and 5pm-10pm; Sun 12pm-2:45pm and 5pm-9pm
signatureDrinks: Pineapple Express (pineapple, house ginger soda, lime)
Thai Herb Swing (watermelon, Thai herbs, lime, soda)
Cold Brew on Draft (locally roasted at Atomic Coffee)
venues.longDescription:
Nautilus Pier 4 opened in spring 2021 as the mainland version of The Nautilus, the Nantucket restaurant known for Asian-influenced seafood and a bar that takes itself seriously without being solemn. The Boston room sits at 300 Pier 4 Boulevard, right on the water in the Seaport, and runs dinner every night with an additional weekend lunch service. The food is raw bar, crudo, dumplings and shared plates; the drinks list is organised into house sections with names like Nauti Standards and O.G. Nauti Creations, and includes porrons, the Basque glass pitchers poured directly into the mouth, for tables that want a spectacle.

The non-alcoholic block has its own heading, Don't Mock It 'Til You Try It, with the subtitle N/A bevies for the sober curious, and it sits on the same page as the beer and seltzer rather than being hidden at the back. There are three named drinks, all $13, which is a dollar or two under the house cocktails. G+G is guava, grapefruit, citrus and soda. Pineapple Express is pineapple with a ginger soda the bar makes in house, plus lime. Thai Herb Swing is watermelon, Thai herbs, lime and soda, and is the one that reads most clearly as a designed drink rather than a spritz. Cold brew on draft, roasted locally at Atomic Coffee, is listed at $7 in the same block, which is a sensible thing to have on a menu at a restaurant whose last seating is at 10pm. Meet Boston included the restaurant in its January 2026 zero-proof guide, and Boston.com had already picked out the G+G in its January 2024 round-up of where to order non-alcoholic drinks in the city. Boston magazine published a first look at the Pier 4 menu in March 2021, the week the restaurant opened. Weekend lunch runs from noon with a last seating at 2.45pm and dinner starts at 5pm every day, so the alcohol-free block is available across both services.
venues.pressQuote: Nautilus Pier 4 focuses on refreshing, coastal-inspired zero-proof drinks.

venues.name: Navy Strength
venues.description: Navy Strength is a tropical cocktail bar at 2505 2nd Avenue in Belltown (entrance on Wall Street), opened on 30 March 2017 by Anu Apte and Chris Elford, whose Canoe Ventures group also runs Rob Roy and Vinnie's Wine Shop. It won Best New American Cocktail Bar at the 2018 Spirited Awards at Tales of the Cocktail. "Tiki bar" undersells it — the drinks list travels, taking on a new set of international flavours every six months, the first of which was India, in a nod to Apte's heritage. It keeps three named non-alcoholic drinks on the menu at all times under a heading that simply reads "Mocktails", each $12: the Sober Saturn (bright, zesty, passion fruit), the Mint Sour (light and easy-drinking) and the Pom Pom (fruity and bubbly). The bar prints tasting notes rather than ingredients for these, so ask what is in them if it matters. Food runs from a $19 nacho platter to $7 sliders and $4.50 Pacific Northwest oysters. The bar is 21+, open Wednesday to Saturday. During its October 2026 Halloween pop-up, Nightmare on Wall Street, the regular list is swapped for a horror-film cocktail menu on which three drinks — Lamia's Curse, Pearl's Swizzle and Mister Babadook — can be made as mocktails; the standing three come back with the regular menu.
venues.hours: Mon-Tue closed; Wed 5pm-11pm; Thu-Sat 5pm-12am; Sun closed
