venues.longDescription:
Navy Strength opened on 30 March 2017 in Belltown, from Anu Apte and Chris Elford, and Seattle Met's line on opening night still holds: tiki bar is a woefully incomplete descriptor for it. The conceit is that the drinks list travels — it embraces a new set of international flavours every six months, and the first destination was India, chosen in homage to Apte's heritage. It took Best New American Cocktail Bar at the 2018 Spirited Awards at Tales of the Cocktail, which is the industry's own verdict rather than a listicle's. The food is generous bar cooking: a $19 nachos platter built to share, sliders at $7 apiece including a teriyaki-glazed spam musubi, Pacific Northwest oysters at $4.50 with a tepache mignonette, and a $28 charcuterie board borrowed from sister shop Vinnie's. It opens Wednesday to Saturday from 5pm, until 11pm on Wednesday and midnight from Thursday to Saturday, and it is 21-and-over.

For a non-drinker the important fact is structural rather than lyrical: Navy Strength always keeps non-alcoholic drinks on the menu, printed under their own heading, rather than treating them as a request. There are three, all $12, and they rotate as the travel list rotates: the Sober Saturn, the Mint Sour and the Pom Pom. The bar describes them the way it describes its cocktails — the Sober Saturn as bright, zesty and passion fruit; the Mint Sour as easy-drinking, light and yummy; the Pom Pom as fruity, refreshing, bubbly and chuggable. That last word is doing more work than it looks like, because chuggable is exactly what a non-drinker needs in a room where everyone else is on a second round. One honest limitation: unlike Rob Roy up the road, Navy Strength prints only those tasting notes and no ingredients, so if you need to know what is actually in a drink — for an allergy, or because you want to avoid a particular non-alcoholic spirit — you will have to ask at the bar. There is also a Mindful Boilermaker at $12, a non-alcoholic IPA with a shot of Pathfinder amaro, but it is billed at 0.5% ABV rather than zero.

One seasonal note: through October 2026 the bar runs its Halloween pop-up, Nightmare on Wall Street, and the regular menu is replaced by a horror-film cocktail list. Three of those cocktails — Lamia's Curse, Pearl's Swizzle and Mister Babadook — are marked as available as mocktails, so there is still a zero-proof order to be had, but the Sober Saturn, Mint Sour and Pom Pom are off the page until the regular menu returns.
venues.pressQuote: So it's no surprise "tiki bar" is a woefully incomplete descriptor of Navy Strength.

venues.name: neat.
venues.description: neat. is a whiskey and cocktail bar on Pico Boulevard in West Los Angeles, known for a deep rare-spirits list and guided whiskey tastings, and it keeps a standing non-alcoholic section on the same printed drink menu. That section runs five items: Wishful Sinful, built on Pathfinder non-alcoholic spirit with yuzu, lemon and ginger; Eyes Wide Shut, an espresso build with cucumber tonic and orange; Alter Ego, with elderflower, cucumber, mint and lemon; a non-alcoholic Negroni; and Weihenstephaner's alcohol-free lager. Prices run $8 to $12, in line with the rest of the room rather than marked down. The bar is open until 2am Thursday through Saturday, with happy hour every day from 5 to 7pm.
venues.address: 11780 W Pico Blvd, Los Angeles, CA 90064
signatureDrinks: Wishful Sinful - Pathfinder n/a spirit, yuzu, lemon, ginger $10
Eyes Wide Shut - espresso, cucumber tonic, orange $8
Alter Ego - elderflower, cucumber, mint, lemon $10
venues.longDescription:
neat. sits on Pico Boulevard in West Los Angeles, between Westwood and Sawtelle, and its stated purpose is a bar born to remind us of what it means to get back to basics. In practice that means an unusually deep spirits collection - bourbon, Japanese whisky, mezcal and rare bottles that mostly do not appear on other LA back bars - plus guided whiskey and spirits tastings run in the room. It is, in other words, a bar for people who care what is in the glass, which is exactly the sort of place where a non-alcoholic list is either an afterthought or genuinely good.

Here it is the latter, and it is printed on the same drink menu as everything else rather than produced on request. Five items sit under the non-alcoholic heading. Wishful Sinful, at $10, is built on Pathfinder - a distilled hemp-and-root non-alcoholic spirit with real bitterness to it - with yuzu, lemon and ginger. Eyes Wide Shut is the cheapest thing on the list at $8 and the most interesting: espresso, cucumber tonic and orange, which is a genuinely odd combination and works. Alter Ego, $10, runs elderflower, cucumber, mint and lemon. There is an N/A Negroni at $12, which is the drink that most often exposes a weak non-alcoholic programme because the bitterness has nowhere to hide. And for anyone who wants a beer rather than a cocktail, Weihenstephaner's alcohol-free lager is $8 - the alcohol-free version from the world's oldest brewery, and a better pour than most NA taps in the city.

What is worth noting is the pricing. The non-alcoholic drinks run $8 to $12 against house cocktails and rare pours considerably above that, so they are not discounted to the level of a soft drink and not padded to the level of the full-strength list. That is the correct treatment and still not the common one. Practical notes: neat. is closed on Monday, opens at 5pm every other day, runs to midnight on Tuesday, Wednesday and Sunday and to 2am Thursday through Saturday, and has a daily happy hour from 5 to 7pm. There is metered and side-street parking; the room is small enough that a weekend visit after 9pm usually means standing.
venues.pressQuote: a bar born to remind us of what it means to get back to basics

venues.name: Neon Moon
venues.description: Neon Moon is a late bar on 2nd Avenue North in downtown Birmingham, and it opens when most places are winding down — 8pm midweek, 6pm at weekends, running to 2am every night it trades. Its non-alcoholic list is genuinely deep rather than nominal, with enough drink creations that Bham Now described it as a room where you will not feel like you are missing out on anything, and its frozen Kentucky coffee is the one the paper singled out. A late bar that has done this work is unusually valuable, because midnight onwards is where alcohol-free options normally disappear.
venues.longDescription:
Neon Moon does not open until 8pm from Tuesday to Thursday. That tells you what kind of room it is: a proper late bar on 2nd Avenue North in downtown Birmingham, trading to 2am every night it is open, with a 6pm start at weekends.

Bars like this are usually the worst possible place to be sober. The later the hour, the narrower the options, and by midnight most rooms have nothing to offer but a soda gun. Neon Moon has gone the other way. Bham Now's January 2026 guide to non-alcoholic drinking in Birmingham described it as having so many non-alcoholic creations that you will not feel like you are missing out on anything — which is a strong claim from a publication that had seven other venues to compare it against, and it is the specific thing this directory looks for.

The named recommendation is a frozen Kentucky coffee, made without alcohol. Frozen drinks are an underrated answer to the alcohol-free problem: the texture does a lot of the work that alcohol's weight would otherwise do, and a coffee base brings bitterness, which is the quality most mocktails lack and the reason so many of them cloy by the second half of the glass.

This entry records the one named drink and no others. The wider list is not published in a readable form, so this guide does not enumerate it — but the breadth is documented by the city's own paper, which is the basis for the grade.

Closed Sunday and Monday. Neon Moon sits within a couple of blocks of Pink Lantern, Paper Doll, House of Found Objects and Wooden City, making the 2nd Avenue North stretch the single best place in Alabama to spend an evening out without drinking.
venues.pressQuote: They have so many non-alcoholic drink creations available, you won't feel like you're missing out on anything. The frozen Kentucky coffee is one of my favorite drinks ever.

venues.name: Neon Pigeon
venues.description: Neon Pigeon is a Tokyo-inspired 'third culture' izakaya on Carpenter Street whose drinks list is deliberately split into full-proof, half-proof and zero-proof cocktails built with the same craft — the alcohol-free builds are listed alongside the rest rather than buried at the back of the menu. The best-selling zero-proof No Kaze pours Lyre's London Dry (alcohol-free gin) with London Essence blood-orange-and-elderflower tonic, a house Thai-basil cordial and a dashi-and-seaweed saline, garnished with Japanese cucumber, shiso and celery. The floral Lady Hinata (S$14) layers zero-proof gin with lavender, cucumber and shishito peppers, and there's a non-alcoholic Amaretti Sour built on Lyre's Amaretti and zero-proof Prosecco.
signatureDrinks: No Kaze (zero-proof) — Lyre's London Dry alcohol-free gin, London Essence blood-orange & elderflower tonic, house Thai-basil cordial, dashi-and-seaweed saline; garnished with Japanese cucumber, shiso and celery
Lady Hinata (zero-proof, S$14) — zero-proof gin, lavender, cucumber and shishito peppers
Amaretti Sour (zero-proof) — Lyre's Amaretti and zero-proof Prosecco, a non-alcoholic take on the sour
venues.longDescription:
Neon Pigeon is a modern Japanese izakaya that bills itself as 'The Original Third Culture Izakaya.' After years on Keong Saik Road it relocated to a larger space at 36 Carpenter Street in the Boat Quay conservation area near Clarke Quay, where the room is split into a casual bar, a raw bar with counter seats and a main dining area, all wrapped in raw concrete, dim light and graffiti by local street artist Zero. It carries a spot on The World's 50 Best Discovery list. The kitchen is led by executive chef Sean Mell, formerly of Nobu, and the bar by manager Mario la Pietra, previously of the award-winning Luggage Room bar in Mayfair, London.

The non-alcoholic program is a genuine anchor rather than an afterthought. The drinks menu is intentionally organised into full-proof, half-proof and zero-proof cocktails that, in the venue's own words, vary only in the amount of alcohol they contain and not in the effort it takes to craft them — the zero-proof builds are listed and mixed alongside the rest of the list. The flagship alcohol-free drink is the No Kaze, made with Lyre's London Dry, London Essence blood-orange and elderflower tonic, a house-made Thai-basil cordial and a dashi-and-seaweed saline, served in a large wine glass with Japanese cucumber, shiso and a celery stick.

Beyond No Kaze, the zero-proof section includes the Lady Hinata (S$14), a floral gin-cooler twist crafted with zero-proof gin, lavender, cucumber and shishito peppers, and a non-alcoholic Amaretti Sour that reworks the amaretto/whisky sour with Lyre's Amaretti and zero-proof Prosecco. Half-proof options offer roughly half the alcohol of a standard cocktail for guests pacing themselves. Neon Pigeon opens daily from the early evening for izakaya sharing plates — charcoal kushiyaki, sashimi and reimagined classics — making it a rare Singapore restaurant where a full alcohol-free evening is treated with the same seriousness as the spirit list.
venues.pressQuote: Going sober? You'd still soak up all that fun with the slick selection of zero-proof cocktails.

venues.name: Nepantla Cafe
venues.description: All-vegan Mexican food trailer and cafe in Detroit's Mexicantown where the entire menu — food and drinks — is alcohol-free by design, built around named mocktails, elixirs, and horchata drinks.
venues.hours: Thu–Sun 4–8:30pm (food trailer/pop-up; schedule varies by week)
signatureDrinks: Rocky's Road Brew (coffee drink named for Coronado's original coffee truck)
venues.longDescription:
Rocky Coronado, a Texas-born chef who relocated to Detroit in 2017, opened Nepantla Cafe as an all-vegan Mexican food trailer rooted in Indigenous, pre-Columbian culinary traditions — plant-forward dishes like banana-blossom fish tacos, mock-duck fries, and Armadillo Eggs rather than meat-and-dairy standards. Coronado previously ran Rocky's Road Brew, a Southwest Detroit coffee truck, before launching Nepantla; the work earned Coronado a 2024 James Beard Award emerging-chef semifinalist nod.

The drink menu is alcohol-free because Coronado is: six years sober at the time of Nepantla's founding, Coronado has said, "I'm six years sober, so I want to create a safe space for sober adults at night. We will have vegan mocktails and elixirs." That shows up as a full non-alcoholic drink list built alongside the food — horchata and Horchata Latte, a Turmeric, Ginger, Pineapple Lemonade, Lavender Latte, Matcha Lemonade, the smoothie Sangre de Copil, and Rocky's Road Brew, a coffee drink named for Coronado's earlier truck — with nothing on the menu to abstain from.

Nepantla runs out of Southwest Detroit's Mexicantown, based at 5410 W. Vernor Highway with a rotating pop-up schedule around the city (Taco Tuesdays at Kelly's Bar in Hamtramck, Wednesdays at the Dequindre Cut, Saturday mornings at Eastern Market), alongside plans for a permanent brick-and-mortar buildout at the Vernor address. Check the cafe's Instagram for the current week's locations and hours, since both shift regularly as a trailer/pop-up operation.
venues.pressQuote: I'm six years sober, so I want to create a safe space for sober adults at night. We will have vegan mocktails and elixirs.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Rocky Coronado, founder and chef of Nepantla Cafe

venues.name: Nest at Nurture
venues.description: Nest is the cafe inside Nurture, a wellness campus on Federal Boulevard in West Highland that also houses fitness studios and care providers. It opened in May 2020 under co-founder Kelly Campbell with culinary director Elizabeth Woodard, and its beverage programme is built around cold-pressed juice, adaptogenic drinks and coffee rather than around a bar. Named juices include the Jasper, a watermelon-lime-jalapeño-cilantro blend, and the Onyx, made with lavender, raw honey, lemon and ginger with activated charcoal; the coffee menu extends to adaptogenic mushrooms and oils such as palo santo, and there is an iced mushroom coffee served with oat or A2 whole milk. Westword lists it among Denver's non-alcoholic options for its mocktails. It is a daytime venue, closing at 4pm.
signatureDrinks: Onyx (lavender, raw honey, lemon, ginger with activated charcoal)
Iced Mushroom Coffee (with oat milk or Origin A2 whole milk)
venues.longDescription:
Nest is the counter-service cafe at the centre of Nurture, the wellness campus at 2949 Federal Boulevard that Denver's official neighbourhood boundaries place in West Highland. Nurture combines fitness studios, treatment rooms and care providers under one roof, and Nest opened within it in May 2020 under co-founder Kelly Campbell, with Elizabeth Woodard as culinary director. The kitchen's stated mission is nourishing bodies and minds from the inside out, turning organic ingredients into everyday meals, and the menu reflects that: smoothies, salads, tartines, dosas and other counter-service food alongside a beverage programme that is considerably more developed than the room's size suggests.

The drinks are where Nest earns a place in Denver's non-alcoholic map. The organic cold-pressed juices are named rather than described by ingredient list — the Jasper is a watermelon, lime, jalapeño and cilantro blend that carries real heat, and the Onyx pairs lavender and raw honey with lemon and ginger, finished with activated charcoal. The coffee menu extends well past espresso into adaptogenic territory, using mushroom extracts and aromatic oils including palo santo, and an iced mushroom coffee is served with oat milk or Origin A2 whole milk. There is a further tier of house drinks built for their functional ingredients rather than for flavour alone — the Root to Rise and the Superfood Steamer among them — and Westword's January 2026 round-up of local non-alcoholic options describes the cafe as offering "nourishing fare, smoothies, cold-pressed juices, adaptogenic concoctions, coffee beverages and a range of tasty mocktails". The honest caveat is hours: Nest closes at 4pm on weekdays and 3pm at weekends, so it fails the going-out test that separates a genuine evening alternative from a daytime cafe. It is listed here as a solid daytime option in a neighbourhood — West Highland, just north of Sloan's Lake — where Denver's non-alcoholic coverage is otherwise thin, rather than as a substitute for a night out. Nurture is a licensed campus and the cafe has served alcohol, so this is not an alcohol-free venue.
venues.pressQuote: In addition to fitness classes and care providers, Nurture houses a cafe with nourishing fare, smoothies, cold-pressed juices, adaptogenic concoctions, coffee beverages and a range of tasty mocktails.

venues.name: Nevada Brew Works
venues.description: Nevada Brew Works is a family-friendly craft brewery and brewpub in the heart of the Las Vegas Arts District, with an industrial taproom where the brewing tanks are in full view and a spacious outdoor beer garden strung with lights. Beyond its house-brewed beers and brick-oven pizza, burgers and pub fare, the taproom markets itself as "accessible for any kind of drinker," keeping rotating non-alcoholic beers on hand along with mocktails, cider and wine, plus simple zero-proof staples like lemonade and Arnold Palmers. It draws a mixed crowd of locals, families and visitors for casual hangouts, date nights and weekend afternoons. The brewery has grown beyond its original Arts District home, adding a second location at Boca Park in Summerlin. Non-drinkers can comfortably join a group here, though the non-alcoholic program is accommodating rather than a dedicated, named zero-proof menu.
venues.address: 1327 S Main St Ste 160, Las Vegas, NV 89104
venues.longDescription:
Nevada Brew Works is a family-friendly craft brewery and brewpub in the Las Vegas Arts District, with an industrial taproom where the brewing tanks are in full view and a large outdoor beer garden strung with lights. Its brewers trained at the Siebel Institute of Technology in Chicago, and the house line is that everything starts with the beer; the kitchen backs it with brick-oven pizza, burgers and pub food. It draws a genuinely mixed crowd — locals, families, visitors wandering up from Main Street — for casual afternoons and low-key nights out, and it has since expanded beyond the original Arts District taproom with a second, larger location at Boca Park in Summerlin, at 820 South Rampart Boulevard, which added a full bar and a dog-friendly patio with heat lamps and misters.

The non-alcoholic side deserves an honest description rather than a generous one. Nevada Brew Works markets itself as accessible for any kind of drinker, and in practice that means rotating non-alcoholic beers kept in stock alongside mocktails, cider and wine, plus straightforward zero-proof staples like lemonade and Arnold Palmers. What it does not have is a named, printed zero-proof menu of the sort that Palate, ECHO or the Golden Tiki run — the accommodation is real but it is accommodation, not a program, and the specific non-alcoholic beers on hand rotate rather than being a fixed list worth travelling for. That distinction matters for how you use the place. As a brewery where a non-drinking member of a group can sit down, order something decent and not feel like an inconvenience for a whole afternoon, it works well and the beer garden makes it comfortable. As a destination chosen specifically for its alcohol-free drinks, there are better-suited rooms in this city, several of them within a few blocks in the same Arts District.

venues.name: Never Say Dive
venues.description: Never Say Dive sits on Broadview Road in Old Brooklyn, the largely residential south-west Cleveland neighbourhood that has slowly been gaining bars worth crossing town for, and the name is the joke: it looks like a dive and is emphatically not one. The kitchen runs rotating seasonal dishes and hands the room over to guest cooks regularly — a Cold Noodle Monday Vietnamese pop-up is the standing example — and the bar takes reservations through Resy, which tells you how the place actually operates behind the shopfront. Its non-alcoholic drink comes off the same station as the cocktails: a house strawberry tonic at $9 built from strawberry syrup with cinchona bark, fennel seed and basil, so it carries genuine quinine bitterness rather than sweetness with soda over it. Four non-alcoholic beers sit in the fridge alongside.
signatureDrinks: Strawberry tonic (strawberry syrup, cinchona bark, fennel seed, basil)
venues.longDescription:
Never Say Dive sits on Broadview Road in Old Brooklyn, the largely residential south-west Cleveland neighbourhood that has slowly been gaining bars worth crossing town for, and the name is the joke: it looks like a dive and is emphatically not one. The kitchen runs rotating seasonal dishes and hands the room over to guest cooks regularly — the Cold Noodle Monday Vietnamese pop-up is the standing example — and the bar takes reservations through Resy and orders through Toast, which tells you how the place actually operates behind the shopfront.

The non-alcoholic drink is made the same way as the cocktails, which is the whole point of listing it. The house strawberry tonic, $9 in Cleveland Magazine's 2026 mocktail guide, is built from strawberry syrup with cinchona bark, fennel seed and basil — cinchona being the natural source of quinine, so the drink carries real tonic bitterness rather than sugar with soda splashed over it. The fennel and basil push it herbal and slightly savoury, and the result sits much closer to an aperitivo than to a strawberry soda, which is the reason it survives a whole evening. Four non-alcoholic beers are kept in the fridge for anyone who would rather hold a can, and the bar rotates what it stocks.

The practical case for Never Say Dive is that it is a genuine neighbourhood bar — open from 5pm, later at weekends, no dress code, no reservation needed for two people at the bar — that happens to make one very good zero-proof drink properly rather than treating the request as a nuisance. For a non-drinker looking for an ordinary night out rather than a destination, that combination is harder to find in Cleveland than a dedicated alcohol-free room is.
venues.pressQuote: The strawberry tonic ($9) is built from strawberry syrup, cinchona bark, fennel seed and basil, alongside four nonalcoholic beers.

venues.name: New Holland Brewing – The Knickerbocker
venues.description: The Knickerbocker is New Holland Brewing's Grand Rapids brewpub, on the Bridge Street strip at 417 Bridge Street NW. It is a large room by brewpub standards — three separate bars, a wood-fired oven, indoor and outdoor beer gardens and several private dining spaces. Its relevance to non-alcoholic drinking is that New Holland brews its own alcohol-free beer rather than stocking somebody else's: Zylch IPA is a 0.00% ABV IPA made with ingredients that let it carry real malt and hops. The brewery also produces Aquanut, a non-alcoholic sparkling water, and the bars mix a selection of zero-proof cocktails. In a city that has called itself Beer City USA since 2012, this is the brewery that answers the question of what a non-drinker orders.
venues.address: 417 Bridge St NW, Grand Rapids, MI 49504
signatureDrinks: Zylch IPA (0.00% ABV non-alcoholic IPA, brewed in house)

naMenuItems.name: No Pain
naMenuItems.description: pineapple juice, orange juice, coconut puree

venues.longDescription:
New Holland Brewing opened The Knickerbocker on a busy stretch of Bridge Street NW as its Grand Rapids outpost, and it is built at scale: three separate bars, a wood-fired oven, an indoor and outdoor beer garden and a series of dining spaces that take private events. Grand Rapids has traded on the Beer City USA name since 2012 and was named America's Best Beer City by USA Today in 2022, 2023, 2024 and 2025, with a Beer City Ale Trail linking more than 35 craft breweries. That reputation is a problem for anyone not drinking, because the default social venue in this city is a taproom, and most taprooms treat non-alcoholic beer as a canned afterthought bought in from elsewhere.

The Knickerbocker is the exception worth knowing about, because New Holland makes its own. Zylch IPA is brewed at 0.00% ABV using newer process ingredients that allow genuine malt and hop character rather than the thin, worty profile that dogged early alcohol-free beer; it is served on the same footing as the rest of the range. The brewery also produces Aquanut, a non-alcoholic sparkling water, which covers the guest who wants something with no sweetness at all. Beyond the two house products, the bars mix a selection of zero-proof cocktails rather than pointing at the soda gun, so a table can order across the whole group without anyone being handed a glass of cola. The food is substantial — wood-fired pizza anchors it — and the beer garden makes the venue usable in summer for groups mixing drinkers and non-drinkers, which is the practical test most breweries fail. It is the only venue in this guide where the non-alcoholic beer on tap was brewed in the building.
venues.pressQuote: They also produce a zero-alcohol near beer (Zylch IPA) and non-alcoholic sparkling water (Aquanut), and offer a selection of expertly mixed zero-proof cocktails.

venues.name: New Mexico Ferments
venues.description: New Mexico Ferments is a local kombucha producer in Albuquerque with kombucha on tap, and it is the second working ferment house in this city guide alongside UrbanMama505. For a non-drinker the value is takeaway rather than an evening out: growler fills and bottles mean the drink you would order in a bar is available at home, which is where most people who have stopped drinking need the alternatives most. Albuquerque having two independent kombucha brewers pouring on tap is a genuinely unusual local asset for a metro this size. Hours are not published reliably for a producer this small, so check before travelling.
venues.longDescription:
New Mexico Ferments brews kombucha in Albuquerque and pours it on tap, and it appears in New Mexico Magazine's survey of where to drink without alcohol in the city alongside UrbanMama505.

Two independent kombucha producers with taps in one metro is a real local characteristic, and it says something about Albuquerque that is worth recording. Kombucha is a serious drink when it is made properly — sour, tannic, lightly effervescent, closer to a natural wine or a gueuze than to a soft drink — and a city that supports two brewers of it has an alcohol-free culture with actual production behind it rather than just menu additions at licensed bars. That is the same pattern this directory found in Burlington, where the strength came from producers rather than rooms.

The practical use of this listing is different from the rest of the guide. This is a producer and a fill station, not an evening out. What it solves is the harder half of not drinking: the Tuesday at home, the dinner party you are hosting, the fridge that needs to contain something other than sparkling water. Being able to fill a growler with something genuinely good is worth more to most people over a year than any single night out.

This entry is graded three and carries no hours, because a small producer's public hours move and this directory does not publish a time it cannot verify — check before travelling. It is recorded as a bottle shop rather than a bar for the same reason: the value here is what you carry away.

One technical note repeated from the UrbanMama505 entry: kombucha is a live ferment and contains trace alcohol, typically under 0.5%, which is comparable to a non-alcoholic beer. Immaterial for most readers, worth knowing for anyone abstaining completely.
venues.pressQuote: New Mexico Ferments has refreshing kombuchas on tap in Albuquerque and Santa Fe
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: John Clary Davies, New Mexico Magazine

venues.name: Night Hawk
venues.description: Night Hawk is a small, consistently full cocktail bar hidden behind Five Oars Coffee Roasters on Tanjong Pagar Road, named for Edward Hopper's 1942 painting Nighthawks and fitted out to match. It is run by veteran bartender Peter Chua and ranked 77th on Asia's 50 Best Bars in 2025. Its commitment to non-drinkers shows in the pricing rather than in marketing: non-alcoholic drinks are a standing line on the menu at S$22++ against S$25++ for the spirited ones, so a zero-proof order is a normal transaction at a normal price. Bartenders will also build non-alcoholic versions of menu drinks or work to a guest's palate. Walk-in only — the bar takes no reservations.
signatureDrinks: Mynahs (NA: n.a. rum, n.a. coffee liqueur, coffee, hot coconut foam)

naMenuItems.name: Mynahs
naMenuItems.description: n.a. rum, n.a. coffee liqueur, coffee, hot coconut foam

venues.longDescription:
Night Hawk is reached through Five Oars Coffee Roasters on Tanjong Pagar Road — you walk through the coffee shop to find it — and the room beyond is small, dim and almost always busy. The name and the fit-out both nod to Edward Hopper's Nighthawks, the 1942 painting of a late-night diner counter, and the design leans into that timeless, slightly cinematic register rather than chasing a trend. It is run by Peter Chua, a bartender with a long track record in Singapore, and it placed 77th on Asia's 50 Best Bars in 2025.

What makes it worth a non-drinker's time is structural rather than promotional. Night Hawk prices its non-alcoholic drinks as a standing menu line at S$22++, set against S$25++ for the alcoholic ones. That single fact does more than a page of mocktails would: it establishes that a zero-proof order is an ordinary transaction at close to full price, made with the same ingredients and the same labour, rather than a favour or a discount item. Bars that treat non-alcoholic drinks as an afterthought almost never price them this way.

Beyond the fixed list, the bartenders are comfortable producing non-alcoholic versions of drinks from the main menu and will build to a guest's preferences if you describe what you like. That kind of dealer's-choice flexibility is arguably more valuable than a printed list, because it means the ceiling on what you can drink is set by the bartender's skill rather than by a short section on a card. Two practical notes: the bar does not take reservations and is walk-in only, which is unusual in Singapore and means arriving early on weekend nights, and the room is genuinely tiny, so a large group will struggle.

venues.name: Nightjar
venues.description: Nightjar opened in 2011 on City Road at the northern edge of Shoreditch and was among the bars that defined London's modern cocktail revival. It was founded by Edmund Weil and Rosie Stimpson, a jazz, swing and blues singer, who set out to build a room that would do justice to the music as much as the drinks — Weil has said the idea came from the style and the music angle before the drinks, rooted in a love of art deco design and the pre-Prohibition era. venues.longDescription:
Nightjar opened in 2011 on City Road, at the northern edge of Shoreditch, and was among the bars that defined London's modern cocktail revival. It was founded by Edmund Weil and Rosie Stimpson, a jazz, swing and blues singer, who set out to build a room that would do justice to the music as much as the drinks — Weil has said the idea "came from the style and the music angle before the drinks," rooted in a love of art deco design and the pre-Prohibition era. The bar took Difford's Guide's Best New Bar award in its opening year and went on to a remarkable run on The World's 50 Best Bars list, placing third in 2012 and second in 2013 and remaining a fixture through much of the decade. It also holds one of the UK's largest absinthe collections and a cellar of vintage spirits dating back to the 19th century.

The venue is a low-lit basement speakeasy marked only by the nightjar symbol on its door, a couple of minutes' walk from Old Street station. Inside it is all exposed brick, dark wood and closely packed tables, with live jazz, blues and swing every night from 9pm — a cover charge is added to the bill and goes directly to the musicians. The cocktail list is divided by historical era, with pre-Prohibition, Prohibition and post-war sections sitting alongside signature and non-alcoholic drinks, and every drink arrives elaborately, sometimes theatrically, garnished. Nightjar runs a 21-and-over policy, a smart-casual dress code and a minimum spend of £15 per person, per hour.

Crucially for non-drinkers, the zero-proof cocktails form their own section on the main menu and are built with the same care as the vintage-spirit list rather than defaulting to a soft drink. They lean on named non-alcoholic spirits — Lyre's and Seedlip — layered with house syrups and unusual ingredients. The Libre combines Lyre's Dark Cane Spirit with Zooz energy drink, fresh lime juice, black cardamom caramel and orange blossom soda; Heal Me Up pairs Seedlip Garden 108 with blood orange, plant-based vitamin D extract and elderflower cordial; the Midori mixes Seedlip Garden 108 with aloe vera soda and jasmine blossom; and Passion de Coco builds Seedlip Grove 42 with coconut orgeat, coconut water and lemongrass. The result is a genuine alcohol-free offering inside one of the world's most decorated cocktail bars, well suited to anyone who wants the full Nightjar experience — the room, the garnishes and the jazz — without the alcohol.
venues.pressQuote: This low-lit London speakeasy has become world famous for its lavish – and spectacularly garnished – drinks, as well as for its late-night live jazz, blues and swing.

venues.name: Nightshade
venues.description: Nightshade is a nightlife venue at 32 Banks Ave #105 in Asheville's South Slope, open Thursday to Saturday evenings, with DJs, live shows and a BASSBOSS sound system, partnered with Plant Bar for plant-based food. It serves genuine zero-proof cocktails — a Matcha Blossom ($12) with matcha, pineapple, sakura and Roots Divino, a Lemon Pop Drop ($11), a Butterfly Gin & Tonic ($12), a zero-proof Old Fashioned ($11) and a Spring No-Jito ($9) — plus a Mertails line crafted by The Nohm. READ THIS BEFORE VISITING: Nightshade markets itself as "entirely alcohol-free", and that is true of alcohol only. It also runs a menu section headed "Catch a Buzz" of cannabinoid drinks on draft at $7, dosed from CBD-only up to Cosmic at 15mg THC ("potent"), Yerba Mate at 25mg THC, and Elevation at 50mg THC ("very potent"), with $3 add-on shots including HHC, delta-9, kanna, blue lotus and kava. The only warning printed on the menu concerns caffeine and pregnancy. Anyone avoiding intoxicants should order strictly from the signature or classic cocktail sections and say so clearly.
venues.hours: Mon-Wed closed; Thu-Fri 5pm-11pm; Sat 5pm-1am; Sun closed

Lemon Pop Drop (lemon, rosehip, walnut-fig bitters, toasted poppy seed) $11
Spring No-Jito (mint, cucumber, Let's Root herbal syrup, choice of NA spirit) $9
venues.longDescription:
Nightshade opened in Asheville's South Slope at 32 Banks Avenue, and it describes itself as redefining nightlife in the city — a space where the energy is high, the vibes are welcoming and the experience is entirely alcohol-free. On its own terms that is accurate and the room delivers on it: a proper nightlife venue rather than a café that stays open late, built around curated music, DJs and live shows on a BASSBOSS sound system, open Thursday and Friday from 5pm to 11pm and Saturdays until 1am. Food comes from a partnership with Plant Bar, so the kitchen is plant-based. The zero-proof cocktails are genuinely made: a Matcha Blossom ($12) infusing matcha with pineapple, sakura and Roots Divino; a Lemon Pop Drop ($11) built on lemon, rosehip, walnut-fig bitters and toasted poppy seed; a Butterfly Gin & Tonic ($12); a zero-proof Old Fashioned ($11); and a Spring No-Jito ($9) with mint, cucumber and a choice of non-alcoholic spirit. A separate Mertails range is crafted by The Nohm.

What has to be said plainly is that alcohol-free is not the same as substance-free, and at Nightshade the gap between those two things is unusually wide. Alongside those cocktails the menu carries a section headed "Catch a Buzz" — seven cannabinoid drinks on draft at $7, dosed and labelled by the venue itself: Uplift and Mellow are CBD and CBG blends, Bliss is 5mg THC, Green Man 10mg, Cosmic 15mg and marked potent, a Yerba Mate at 25mg THC with 100mg of caffeine, and Elevation at 50mg THC, marked very potent. Fifty milligrams is a substantial dose by any measure. A shots list adds $3 and $4 pours of HHC, delta-9, kanna honey, blue lotus and kava extract, and there is a separate kava section with bowls from $8. The only warning printed anywhere on the menu says that items marked with notes may contain caffeine or are not recommended during pregnancy. If cannabis is what you want, this is a well-run room built for it. If you are in recovery, subject to drug testing, or simply want a drink that does nothing, order from the signature or classic cocktail sections by name and say clearly that you want nothing infused.
venues.pressQuote: Asheville's zero-proof nightlife destination in South Slope

venues.name: NIL Bottle Shop
venues.description: NIL Bottle Shop is Greater Cincinnati's first exclusively non-alcoholic retail store, a curated zero-proof bottle shop tucked inside the Painted Tree Boutiques marketplace on Montgomery Road in Symmes Township. Founder Brady Mescher launched parent company NIL Distributing in late 2024 after noticing that regional liquor distributors were ignoring the fast-growing zero-proof category, then opened the booth in December, timed to Dry January. The self-serve, unstaffed stall stocks alcohol-free wines, craft NA spirits, ready-to-drink mocktails and mixers, including Mescher's favorite, the Spiritless Espresso Martini, with informative QR-code signage in place of a bartender. Everything on the shelf is booze-free, making it a genuine destination for the sober and sober-curious rather than a token NA shelf inside a liquor store.
venues.longDescription:
NIL Bottle Shop is the retail arm of NIL Distributing, a zero-proof beverage company founded by Brady Mescher and his wife in November 2024. As Cincinnati Magazine reported, the couple identified a market gap: non-alcoholic options were expanding rapidly in other cities while regional liquor distributors largely neglected zero-proof products. "We knew the void had to be filled," Mescher told the magazine. A month after launching the distribution business, they opened the bottle shop in December 2024 — deliberately timed to catch the annual Dry January wave — inside the Painted Tree Boutiques marketplace at 11315 Montgomery Road in Symmes Township.

The shop is 100 percent alcohol-free. Its handpicked shelves carry non-alcoholic wines, craft NA spirits, ready-to-drink mocktails and mixers, chosen, in Mescher's words, for "flavor, quality, or experience." Cincinnati Magazine singled out the Spiritless Espresso Martini as one of Mescher's favorites among the drinks on offer. Because the concept is retail rather than a bar, there is no bartender: the booth is unstaffed, restocked regularly, and each product is paired with an informative sign and QR code so shoppers can read tasting notes and details before they buy. Mescher frames the mission around inclusion — "Providing options that mimic full proof alternatives gives people a feeling of inclusion" — and the magazine noted the shop's first-month sales exceeded the founders' goals.

Practically, NIL is a vendor stall rather than a standalone storefront, so it keeps the Painted Tree Boutiques marketplace's hours — generally Monday through Saturday 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. and Sunday 11 a.m. to 6 p.m. — and you check out through the marketplace, not a dedicated register. It suits anyone doing Dry January, pregnant or in recovery, or simply curious to take home a bottle of alcohol-free spirit or wine without driving to a big-city bottle shop. For questions or wholesale inquiries, NIL Distributing lists (859) 240-7207 and posts new arrivals on Instagram at @th3_nilshop.
venues.pressQuote: Enter the NIL Bottle Shop, Cincinnati's first exclusively nonalcoholic retail store.

venues.name: Nine Lives Cafe & Cat Lounge
venues.description: Nine Lives is a fully alcohol-free café and cat lounge on Shelby Street in Fountain Square, and was the first cat café in Indiana when it opened in 2017. Kelley Niiyama and her husband Hidetaka took it over in March 2020 and have run it since, pairing an espresso bar with a separate lounge of adoptable cats placed through IndyAdopts, the nonprofit they founded in 2021. The drinks list is short and made properly: the house Café Meow is a honey and cinnamon latte, the chai is a standing favourite, and every drink comes in a 12oz "kitten" or 16oz "cat". Pastries come from the vegan bakery Sea Salt & Cinnamon. Lounge sessions are best reserved; the room is all-ages until 1pm, 13+ until 5pm and 18+ after.
venues.hours: Mon-Tue 8am-4pm; Wed closed; Thu 8am-4pm; Fri-Sat 8am-7pm; Sun 8am-5pm
venues.longDescription:
Nine Lives opened on Shelby Street in Fountain Square in 2017, founded by owners who had travelled in Asia and come home wanting Indiana to have a cat café. It was the first in the state. Kelley Niiyama — a former classical musician who had worked at the café for about a year — bought it with her husband Hidetaka in March 2020, eight days before COVID-19 forced the doors shut, which is not the start anyone would choose. They kept it. Six years on it is one of the more durable independent rooms in Fountain Square, and the cat side has been formalised into IndyAdopts, the nonprofit the Niiyamas founded in 2021 to handle adoptions and, alongside them, to promote Japanese culture. The café's own count puts it at more than 1,600 cats rehomed.

The café half is the reason it belongs in an alcohol-free guide rather than only a pet one. Nothing on the menu contains alcohol, the espresso program is taken seriously, and the drinks are named and sized with some wit — a 12oz is a "kitten", a 16oz is a "cat", and the house Café Meow is a honey and cinnamon latte that regulars order by name. The chai and the matcha hold up, and the food is local: pastries from the vegan bakery Sea Salt & Cinnamon, with gluten-free options. The cat lounge is separate from the café floor and works on reservations, with walk-ins taken when there is room; the age policy steps up through the day, all ages before 1pm, 13 and over until 5pm, and 18-plus in the evening. Friday and Saturday it stays open until 7pm, which makes it one of the few genuinely alcohol-free evening rooms in the city since Memento Zero Proof closed. Two practical points. The café side can be used without booking the lounge — you can come in, order a Café Meow and sit, and plenty of people do, particularly students from the University of Indianapolis, who have written about using it as a place to decompress during exams. And Fountain Square is the single best neighbourhood in the city for an alcohol-free evening: The Inferno Room, with the metro's most developed zero-proof tiki list, is three blocks away on Virginia Avenue, and Harmony Tea Shoppe is on the same stretch. Closed Wednesdays, which catches people out.
venues.pressQuote: When an adoption happens, you see these people's faces light up. They're getting this cat, and it's the most amazing and wonderful thing.

venues.name: 9 Mile Brewing Co.
venues.description: 9 Mile Brewing Company is Bloomington's first brewery, located in a James Avenue South business park near the Mall of America in the southern Twin Cities metro. Beyond standard craft beer, the brewery has earned regional attention for actually brewing its own non-alcoholic sours in house, using its "house sour grist" — a rotating program that has included a Non-Alcoholic Peach Passionfruit Sour (peach and passion fruit, finished with Sabro hops) and a summer orange-mango release. Explore Minnesota featured the brewery for these NA sours, noting they retain a thick body and mouthfeel often lost in non-alcoholic beer. The current taproom NA lineup also carries Athletic Brewing non-alcoholic beers, J's Kombucha, and Northern Craft Soda, while a scratch kitchen, Creekside Kitchen, opened in March 2025. Because the in-house NA sours rotate seasonally, it's worth confirming the day's zero-proof options on arrival.
venues.address: 9555 James Ave S, Suite 290, Bloomington, MN 55431
venues.longDescription:
9 Mile Brewing Company is Bloomington's first brewery, in a James Avenue South business park near the Mall of America in the southern Twin Cities metro. A scratch kitchen, Creekside Kitchen, opened on site in March 2025. What sets it apart from the dozens of other taprooms in this metro is that it actually brews its own non-alcoholic beer in house, rather than stocking someone else's — and it does so in a style almost nobody attempts.

The programme is built on the brewery's house sour grist, producing rotating non-alcoholic sours: releases have included a Non-Alcoholic Peach Passionfruit Sour finished with Sabro hops, and a summer orange-mango version. Sours are a genuinely clever choice for non-alcoholic brewing, and the reason is technical. The great weakness of NA beer is thinness — remove the alcohol and you remove much of the body, which is why so many non-alcoholic IPAs taste hollow. A sour leans on acidity and fruit for its structure rather than on alcoholic weight, so the format survives dealcoholisation far better than most. Explore Minnesota featured the brewery specifically for these sours, noting that they retain a thick body and mouthfeel usually lost in non-alcoholic beer. Alongside the house pours the taproom carries Athletic Brewing non-alcoholic beers, J's Kombucha and Northern Craft Soda.

One practical caveat: because the in-house NA sours are a rotating seasonal programme rather than a fixed year-round product, the specific release will vary and there may be periods when none is pouring. It is worth confirming the day's zero-proof options when you arrive rather than travelling across the metro for a particular can. Open daily, from late morning at weekends. Bloomington is not somewhere most Twin Cities drinkers travel for a taproom, so the pull here is specifically the in-house sours — if you are making the trip for those, calling ahead is the difference between a good evening and a wasted one.

venues.name: Nite Owl
venues.description: Nite Owl is a cocktail bar in Omaha's Blackstone district, west of downtown, and its alcohol-free drinks are among the most interesting in the city. The Phony Negroni is exactly what the name promises — a bitter, red, stirred aperitif build rather than something sweet — and the switchel is a genuine piece of drinks history: a vinegar-and-ginger farm drink that predates soft drinks entirely and has the acidity and length that most mocktails lack. Open Tuesday through Sunday from 5pm, to midnight midweek and 1am on Friday and Saturday, closed Monday. Blackstone is a short drive west of the Old Market and has its own run of bars and restaurants.
venues.longDescription:
Blackstone is the Farnam Street district west of downtown Omaha that has become the city's most concentrated food and drink strip, and Nite Owl is its late cocktail bar. Two drinks on its alcohol-free list are worth the trip on their own.

The Phony Negroni is the more obvious of them and the more useful. A negroni is bitter, red, stirred and served short — the archetypal aperitif — and it is the single hardest classic to replace without alcohol, because the bitterness that defines it normally comes from a fortified amaro. Building a convincing one requires either a proper non-alcoholic bitter aperitif or a lot of work with tea, gentian and citrus peel. That a bar bothers to make it, and names it honestly rather than dressing it up, is a reliable signal about the rest of the list.

The switchel is the more unusual. It is a colonial-era American farm drink of water, vinegar, ginger and a sweetener — molasses, honey or maple — that field workers drank in the heat long before soft drinks existed. It has real acidity, genuine ginger heat and no pretension to being a substitute for anything, which makes it one of the best possible answers to the question of what to drink for three hours in a bar. Its revival on cocktail menus is one of the more sensible things to happen to this category.

Omaha's local drinks coverage names both, which is the evidence behind this listing.

Nite Owl opens at 5pm Tuesday through Sunday and runs to midnight, 1am on Friday and Saturday, closed Monday. Blackstone is a short drive or a long walk from downtown; the strip around it means an evening here does not have to be a single stop either.
venues.pressQuote: Nestled in Omaha's Blackstone District, Nite Owl serves up a vibrant late-night scene with plenty of personality.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Hurrdat ONE, 10 Best Zero-Proof & Nonalcoholic Bars in Omaha, Nov 18, 2025

venues.name: Nitro Beverage Lounge
venues.description: Nitro Beverage Lounge is a coffee bar and craft cocktail lounge on West Washington Avenue near the Capitol, and it puts more technique into its non-alcoholic drinks than anywhere else in Madison. The bartenders build mocktails the way they build cocktails, reaching for lapsang souchong to get smoke into The Woodsman rather than adding sugar. The standing list runs to the Rose Spritz on rose essence, lemon and soda; the Arbol Bloom, which sets pomegranate and hibiscus against chilli de árbol and lime; and I'd Rather Be On The Beach, a pistachio creme, banana, lemon, honey, coconut milk and banana leaf build that is closer to a dessert than a soft drink.
venues.hours: Mon closed; Tue-Thu 4pm-11pm; Fri 12pm-12am; Sat 10am-12am; Sun 12pm-8pm
signatureDrinks: Arbol Bloom (pomegranate, hibiscus, chilli de árbol, lime)
I'd Rather Be On The Beach (pistachio creme, banana, lemon, honey, coconut milk, banana leaf)
venues.longDescription:
Nitro Beverage Lounge sits on West Washington Avenue a few blocks off the Capitol Square, and runs as a coffee bar through the day and a craft cocktail lounge into the evening — a format that is becoming common and that happens to be ideal for non-drinkers, because a room already geared to making espresso drinks properly has the equipment, the syrups and the staff patience that a good alcohol-free drink actually requires.

The evidence is in the technique. BRAVA Magazine's survey of Madison mocktails singled the bar out for using lapsang souchong — the pine-smoked Chinese black tea — to put smoke into The Woodsman, which is the sort of move a bartender reaches for when they are trying to replace what a peated whisky would have contributed rather than trying to make something sweet. The rest of the list holds that standard. The Rose Spritz is restrained: rose essence, lemon, soda. The Arbol Bloom sets pomegranate and hibiscus against chilli de árbol and lime, so the heat and the tartness carry it. I'd Rather Be On The Beach is the maximalist one, layering pistachio creme, banana, lemon, honey and coconut milk and finishing it with banana leaf.

Practically, the hours make it one of the more flexible entries here: it opens at 10am on Saturday and noon on Friday and Sunday, runs to midnight on Friday and Saturday, and closes Mondays. That means it works as a morning coffee, an afternoon working session and a Saturday night out, which very few venues in this guide can claim. It is also walkable from the Capitol Square cluster — Merchant, Settle Down Tavern, Lucille and Eno Vino are all within about ten minutes on foot — so it slots easily into a downtown evening built around not drinking.
venues.pressQuote: Bartenders use techniques like lapsang tea in The Woodsman mocktail to impart smoky flavors.

venues.name: No. 119
venues.description: An upscale, whiskey-forward cocktail bar on the second floor above the Grand Hall of the restored 1908 Union Pacific Depot, opened in late 2024 with the Asher Adams (Marriott Autograph Collection) hotel at The Gateway downtown. Named after the historic Union Pacific No. 119 steam locomotive, it pairs original stained glass and terrazzo floors with skyline views. The hotel's food and beverage director has said the bar carries roughly as many non-alcoholic options as traditional cocktails, anchoring a serious zero-proof program built on NA spirits like Seedlip Garden 108.
venues.address: 2 S 400 W, Salt Lake City, UT 84101
venues.hours: Mon closed; Tue-Thu 5pm-12am; Fri-Sat 5pm-1am; Sun closed
signatureDrinks: Garden Boxcar (Seedlip Garden 108, Peychaud's bitters, mint, sparkling water)
venues.longDescription:
The Asher Adams was developed by Hatteras Sky inside and around the landmark Union Pacific Depot, with No. 119 designed to evoke a speakeasy with upscale, big-city polish. The room is whiskey-led but built to please every palate, which is where the zero-proof list comes in.

The flagship non-alcoholic pour, the Garden Boxcar, uses Seedlip Garden 108 — a distilled botanical zero-alcohol spirit — lengthened with sparkling water and finished with Peychaud's bitters and mint, mirroring the bar's classic-cocktail sensibility without the alcohol.

venues.name: No Hard Feelings
venues.description: No Hard Feelings is a late-night cocktail bar on Broad Street in downtown Chattanooga, open until 1am most nights and 2am from Thursday to Sunday — the latest hours of any venue in this guide. It stocks Seedlip Garden 108, the pea-and-hay non-alcoholic spirit, and uses it properly rather than as a novelty: the house Blackberry Basil Gimlet is built alcohol-free on Seedlip with blackberry syrup and lemon, so the alcohol-free version of the drink is the same drink rather than a different, lesser one. For anyone who wants to be out past midnight in Chattanooga without drinking, this is the address.
signatureDrinks: Blackberry Basil Gimlet (non-alcoholic) — Seedlip Garden 108, blackberry syrup, lemon
venues.longDescription:
The single most useful thing a bar can do for a non-drinker is stay open late. Sobriety does not come with an early bedtime, and the hours between midnight and two are when a city's alcohol-free options collapse to nothing. No Hard Feelings, on Broad Street in downtown Chattanooga, runs to 1am Monday through Wednesday and 2am from Thursday through Sunday — later than anything else in this guide.

It also keeps a real non-alcoholic spirit behind the bar. Seedlip Garden 108 is the herbaceous expression of the range, built on peas and hay with spearmint, rosemary and thyme, and it is the one that actually works in a gimlet because the vegetal, green character does the job juniper would. The bar's Blackberry Basil Gimlet is offered built on it with blackberry syrup and lemon, which means the alcohol-free order is the same cocktail off the same menu rather than a separate, sadder drink brought out afterwards.

That structural point is worth spelling out because it is the difference between accommodation and inclusion. A bar that hands a non-drinker a different menu has marked them out; a bar that builds the house cocktail without the gin has not. NOOGAtoday flagged this specific substitution in its guide to non-alcoholic drinking in the city.

The room itself is a proper late bar — dark, loud enough, and busier after eleven than before it — which is either the appeal or the warning depending on what you are looking for. If you want a quiet drink, come at five; if you want to still be out when everyone else is, this is the only realistic option in the metro.

Weekend opening moves an hour earlier, to 4pm on Saturday and Sunday.
venues.pressQuote: The Blackberry Basil Gimlet can be made non-alcoholic with Seedlip Garden 108 (NA spirit), blackberry syrup + lemon.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: NOOGAtoday, Local mocktails + non-alcoholic drinks in Chattanooga

venues.longDescription: No More Cafe is a fully alcohol-free cocktail bar and all-day cafe at 352 E 13th Street in Manhattan's East Village, opened in 2024 by founder Rodrigo Nogueira. Every drink on the menu is zero-proof: chef-crafted non-alcoholic cocktails built from scratch with real ingredients and house-made syrups, alongside specialty coffee, loose-leaf tea, kava, functional shots, and botanical beverages. Conceived by Nogueira as a place to enjoy great conversation, food, and proper drinks without alcohol, the space doubles as a daytime "third place" with Wi-Fi and outlets and stays open until midnight daily. It hosts live music (its Thursday Sessions series), private events, and brand activations. No More also produces a line of bottled non-alcoholic cocktails — including Island Echo, Agave Phantom, and Amber Dream — available at the cafe and shipped nationwide. Time Out grouped No More Cafe among the city's fully alcohol-free venues ("The Sobers") in its 2025 NA bar awards coverage, and Lonely Planet featured it among its favorite bars around the world.

venues.name: No Vacancy
venues.description: No Vacancy is a cocktail bar on Toronto's Ossington Strip, ranked No. 14 on Canada's 100 Best Bars list for 2026 and No. 82 on the 50 Best Bars North America list for 2026. Its cocktail program, credited to bartender Liam McKinnon, runs alongside a deep Japanese whisky and highball list, but the menu carries a dedicated "Zero Proof Cocktails" section for non-drinkers. The two named builds are Love and Passion, made with Roots Divino 0 Proof, yuzu, orange and lemon-lime soda, and N/A, an amaretto sour built on Noa Amaretto 0% with lemon, lime, sugar and egg whites. The alcohol-free lineup extends further with canned Maison Perrier Chic mocktails and Asahi Super Dry 0.0 non-alcoholic beer.

venues.longDescription:
No Vacancy is a cocktail bar at 74 Ossington Ave in Toronto's Ossington Strip. It has built a reputation as one of the city's more decorated cocktail rooms, currently ranked No. 14 on Canada's 100 Best Bars for 2026 and No. 82 on the 50 Best Bars North America list for 2026. The drinks program leans heavily on Japanese whisky — pours and highballs from Nikka, Suntory's Hakushu and Yamazaki, Hibiki Harmony, Toki and more fill a full page of the menu — alongside a cocktail list credited to bartender Liam McKinnon and an extensive by-the-glass and Bourgogne-heavy wine list.

For non-drinkers, the June 2026 drink menu carries a standalone "Zero Proof Cocktails" section with two named, priced builds: Love and Passion ($16), made with Roots Divino 0 Proof, yuzu, orange and lemon-lime soda, and N/A ($16), an amaretto-sour-style drink built on Noa Amaretto 0% with lemon, lime, sugar and egg whites. The alcohol-free options continue beyond the cocktail list — a "Zero Proof Maison Perrier" section pours plain Perrier by the bottle as well as the canned Maison Perrier Chic Mojito and Chic Peach Spritzer mocktails, and the beer list includes Asahi Super Dry 0.0, a non-alcoholic lager from Osaka, alongside the bar's regular beer cans and bottles.

No Vacancy is open Tuesday, Wednesday and Sunday from 6pm to 1am, and Thursday through Saturday from 6pm to 2am; it's closed Monday. Reservations run through Resy, and private events are booked separately through the Good Night Cocktail Club events team.
venues.pressQuote: They don't spare any effort when it comes to their zero-proof offerings though. In addition to canned Perrier Chic mocktails (IYKYK), there's non-alcoholic wine, beer and sparkling iced tea. Available by the glass or bottle, French Bloom Le Blanc Alcohol-Free French Sparkling is actually a great bubbly option, not just "good for a non-alc wine." And their list of non-alcoholic craft cocktails even includes a milk punch!

venues.name: Noble Pursuits
venues.description: Noble Pursuits is Alabama's first bar dedicated to traditional kava, opened in Birmingham's Lakeview district in August 2026, and it serves no alcohol at all. The room pours kava prepared in the traditional way alongside house-made speciality botanical drinks, and it keeps hours no other alcohol-free venue in the state comes close to — 11am to 10pm, seven days a week, with no closed day. For a city whose social life runs through Lakeview's bars, having a room on the same streets that opens at eleven in the morning and is still serving at ten at night changes what a night out can look like for someone who does not drink.
venues.longDescription:
Alabama did not have a kava bar until August 2026. Noble Pursuits opened in Birmingham's Lakeview district as the state's first bar specialising in traditionally prepared kava, alongside a list of house-made speciality botanical drinks, and it is fully alcohol-free — a first for a state whose relationship with alcohol regulation has always been complicated and whose social infrastructure has never included a room like this.

The significance for this directory is straightforward. Every other venue in this city guide is a licensed bar or restaurant that makes good drinks for people who are not drinking; Noble Pursuits is a bar whose entire purpose is that. The difference matters most at the point where a group has to choose where to go. When the alcohol-free option is a good mocktail at a bar, the non-drinker is still a guest in someone else's room; when it is a bar of its own, they can be the one making the suggestion.

The hours are the second reason it leads this list, and they are remarkable for the category. Eleven in the morning to ten at night, every day of the week, with no closed day — while several of Birmingham's better licensed programmes do not open before four and shut on Sunday and Monday. That is a room you can actually build a habit around rather than a Friday-night novelty.

Lakeview is the right address for it too. It is one of Birmingham's densest bar districts, so Noble Pursuits sits among the venues it is an alternative to rather than off in a quiet corner — which is precisely where an alcohol-free bar needs to be if it is going to be part of a night rather than a substitute for one.

The usual plain note applies: kava is mildly psychoactive, and this is a night out without alcohol rather than a substance-free room. The bar opened on 8 August 2026 and was verified operational two days later; details will firm up as it settles in.

One further reason this opening matters beyond Birmingham. Alabama has no dedicated alcohol-free bar anywhere else in the state, and the nearest comparable rooms are in Nashville and Atlanta, both roughly three hours away. Until August 2026 the honest answer to "where can I go out in Alabama without alcohol" was a coffee shop that closed at four. That is the gap this room fills, and it is why it leads this guide despite being the newest venue in it.

venues.name: Noble Rot
venues.description: Noble Rot is the original, cult wine bar and restaurant on Bloomsbury's Lamb's Conduit Street, born from the acclaimed wine magazine of the same name and celebrated for one of the best by-the-glass lists in London. For no- and low-alcohol drinkers it goes beyond a token soft drink: its adjoining Shrine to the Vine shop stocks genuine de-alcoholised 0% ABV wines from France's Domaine des Grottes, so you can drink a real dealcoholised Gamay or Malvasia rather than a mocktail. It is the rare serious wine destination where the zero-proof option is actual wine.
signatureDrinks: Des Grottes 'L'Antidote' (0% ABV) - de-alcoholised Gamay from Beaujolais, £17.50
Des Grottes 'Antilope' (0% ABV) - de-alcoholised Malvasia from Beaujolais, £17.50

venues.longDescription:
Opened in 2015, Noble Rot Lamb's Conduit is the flagship of the Noble Rot group, an atmospheric Bloomsbury townhouse of rough-lacquered dark wood, candlelight and walls papered with covers of the founders' Noble Rot wine magazine. It is listed in the Michelin Guide and has won a string of the industry's top wine-list honours, including the Wine List Award at the 2019 World Restaurant Awards and Wine List of the Year at the National Restaurant Awards in 2016, 2017 and 2018.

The kitchen serves unfussy, French-leaning cooking overseen with input from Stephen Harris of the Michelin-starred The Sportsman in Whitstable, but the reason to come is the vast, meticulously curated wine list, ranging from undervalued glasses to hard-to-find bottles from the world's leading growers.

The non-alcoholic angle is a natural extension of that wine obsession. Through its Shrine to the Vine shop, Noble Rot carries dealcoholised 0% ABV wines from Domaine des Grottes in Beaujolais: 'L'Antidote', a de-alcoholised Gamay, and 'Antilope', a de-alcoholised Malvasia, each £17.50. For a room this devoted to what's in the glass, offering proper 0% wine rather than a fizzy substitute makes it a genuine destination for no-alcohol drinkers.

venues.name: Nobody's Darling
venues.description: Nobody's Darling is a Black- and queer-owned cocktail bar in Andersonville, opened in late May 2021 by Renauda Riddle and Angela Barnes, who met volunteering at the Center on Halsted. Named after the Alice Walker poem "Be Nobody's Darling," it is one of the few nightlife spaces in Chicago centered on queer women and the city's second Black-owned LGBTQ bar alongside Jeffery Pub. It was a 2022 James Beard Award finalist for Outstanding Bar Program and is featured on The World's 50 Best Discovery list. Beyond its cocktails inspired by iconic women of color, the bar runs a serious zero-proof program: a dedicated "Lower and No Alcohol" menu section with roughly ten seasonal non-alcoholic drinks built on spirits like DHŌS spiritless gin and aperitivo. Co-owner Renauda Riddle has said the team plays with its non-alcoholic beverages as much as its alcoholic ones.
venues.hours: Mon-Tue closed; Wed-Thu 5pm-11pm; Fri 4pm-12am; Sat 2pm-12am; Sun 2pm-11pm
signatureDrinks: Mai No Tai (Ritual NA rum, DHOS orange liqueur, orgeat, lime) $12
Say Less (DHOS tequila, DHOS orange liqueur, agave, hibiscus grenadine, lime) $12
venues.longDescription:
Nobody's Darling opened in late May 2021 at 1744 W Balmoral Avenue in Andersonville, a Black- and queer-owned cocktail bar from Renauda Riddle and Angela Barnes, who met a decade earlier volunteering at the Center on Halsted. Riddle had been organising pop-up events and parties for queer women; Barnes is a business attorney. The two had been regulars at Joie De Vine, the lesbian-owned neighbourhood wine bar, and had even discussed buying it before it closed for the pandemic and never reopened — so this room exists partly to replace what the city lost. Its name comes from the Alice Walker poem "Be Nobody's Darling", an ode to outsiders, and the interior leans glamorous, with chandeliers salvaged from the shuttered downtown restaurant Lawry's. Barnes has described imagining a laid-back, Sunday-morning, Nina Simone-styled lounge, while Riddle wanted a classy, sexy room where great cocktails arrive on demand. It was a James Beard finalist for Outstanding Bar Program in 2022, and has drawn national coverage from the Washington Post and NBC News for its place in Chicago's lesbian bar history. The bar is accessible, has street parking, and takes booth reservations against a minimum spend.

It is worth being precise about the non-alcoholic offering, because this is a full-proof cocktail bar with a small zero-proof corner rather than a sober-forward room. The summer 2026 menu carries a section headed "Low and No Alcohol" at $12, and only two of its four drinks are actually alcohol-free: Mai No Tai, built on Ritual non-alcoholic rum with DHOS orange liqueur, orgeat and lime, and Say Less, using DHOS tequila and orange liqueur with agave, hibiscus grenadine and lime. Both are properly made and priced below the $14–15 full cocktails. The other two in that section are labelled low-ABV and do contain alcohol. Non-alcoholic beer is Sam Adams Just The Haze and Athletic's Upside Dawn at $8. One caution that matters more than the drink count: the menu groups THC and CBD seltzers under its non-alcoholic heading, and one house cocktail is both 16% ABV and THC-dosed, so read the line rather than the section header before ordering.
venues.pressQuote: We play with our non-alcoholic beverages probably as much as we play with our alcoholic beverages.

venues.name: Nobu Dallas
venues.description: Nobu Dallas, the Uptown outpost of Nobu Matsuhisa's global Japanese empire inside Hotel Crescent Court, backs its non-alcoholic offering with real product rather than a token Shirley Temple. The printed menu carries Asahi 0.0% non-alcoholic rice lager alongside an extensive whole-leaf Ikaati tea program with several caffeine-free options, and the bar has built serious spirit-free cocktails on genuine NA spirits: the Sansho Verde on Seedlip Garden 108 and the Oaxacan Punch on Seedlip Spice 94. Nobu's corporate beverage team has also developed a green-tea "tea cocktail" pairing program aimed at sober-curious fine-dining guests, positioning tea as a wine-like alternative alongside the omakase.
signatureDrinks: Sansho Verde - Seedlip Garden 108 (non-alcoholic spirit), cucumber juice, agave, yuzu juice, and ground sansho peppercorns
Oaxacan Punch - Seedlip Spice 94 (non-alcoholic spirit), passionfruit puree, lime juice, cucumber slices, shichimi, ginger beer, and Lapsang Souchong tea-infused agave syrup
venues.longDescription:
Nobu Dallas opened in 2005 inside Hotel Crescent Court in Uptown and celebrated its 20th anniversary in 2025. Part of chef Nobu Matsuhisa and Robert De Niro's worldwide Nobu empire, the Dallas location pairs the group's signature contemporary Japanese cooking (Black Cod Miso, Rock Shrimp Tempura, omakase at the sushi bar) with a Rockwell Group-designed dining room and a cocktail lounge where guests can watch the sushi chefs at work.

The bar's non-alcoholic program goes well beyond a soft drink. The current beverage menu lists Asahi 0.0% Non-Alcoholic Rice Lager and a deep Ikaati whole-leaf tea selection, including caffeine-free Sobacha, Soothe, and Lemongrass Ginger. For Dry January, the bar has featured two named spirit-free cocktails built on real NA spirits: the Sansho Verde (Seedlip Garden 108, cucumber juice, agave, yuzu juice, and ground sansho peppercorns) and the Oaxacan Punch (Seedlip Spice 94, passionfruit puree, lime juice, cucumber slices, shichimi, ginger beer, and Lapsang Souchong tea-infused agave syrup) that leans smoky to mimic mezcal.

The emphasis on serious zero-proof drinks reflects a wider Nobu strategy: the group worked with a Japanese green-tea expert to build alcohol-free "tea cocktail" pairings for its tasting menus, treating premium teas as a wine-caliber alternative for the roughly 30 percent of fine-dining guests now foregoing alcohol.
venues.pressQuote: This favorite Dallas sushi spot has two mocktails this Dry January. The Sansho Verde is a non-alcoholic spirit Seedlip Garden 108, cucumber juice, agave, yuzu juice, and ground sansho peppercorns mixture.

venues.name: Nocturne Jazz & Supper Club
venues.description: Nocturne Jazz & Supper Club is a modern jazz and supper club opened in 2015 by Nicole and Scott Mattson, set inside a restored early 20th-century warehouse in Denver's RiNo Arts District. The two-level art deco space — designed for the acoustics of its raw steel and tall wood ceilings, with a mezzanine overlooking the stage — features live jazz nightly Wednesday through Sunday, including an Artist-in-Residency programming where artists explore a single musical icon, genre, or original work across a four-to-eight-week run. The dinner program is built as 'Dinner and a Show' — a three-course seasonal menu paired with the evening's music — and Nocturne is the only venue in Colorado to feature jazz programming exclusively. The non-alcoholic offering is just as intentional as the live music: the seasonally-rotating 'Ain't Misbehavin'' menu is a curated collection of four original NA cocktails, available à la carte at the bar or paired with the dinner menu. Current and recent named selections include the Violet Suede (Lyre's N/A gin, verjus, aquafaba, blueberry pink peppercorn syrup), Crimson & Clover (Lyre's London Dry N/A gin, spiced cranberry syrup, soda), Cha Cha Chai (chai-infused Seedlip 94, rosemary, coconut water, cranberry, lemon, orange), and Golden Harmony (Lyre's White Cane Spirit, Seedlip Garden 108, tamarind, verjus, orange, spice whipped honey). A Billie Holiday mural by Denver street artist Detour marks the entrance. A per-guest artist fee is added to checks to support the performing musicians.
signatureDrinks: Violet Suede (NA: Lyre's N/A gin, verjus, aquafaba, blueberry pink peppercorn syrup)
Crimson & Clover (NA: Lyre's London Dry N/A gin, spiced cranberry syrup, soda)
Cha Cha Chai (NA: chai-infused Seedlip 94, rosemary, coconut water, cranberry, lemon, orange)
Golden Harmony (NA: Lyre's White Cane Spirit, Seedlip Garden 108, tamarind, verjus, orange, spice whipped honey)
venues.longDescription:
For non-drinkers in Denver, Nocturne is one of the few upscale venues where the zero-proof experience is genuinely considered rather than an afterthought. The 'Ain't Misbehavin'' menu — named with a nod to the jazz standard — is a seasonally rotating program of original spirit-free cocktails, designed to pair course-by-course with the kitchen's three-course supper. Guests in the Five Points neighborhood can also order from it à la carte at reserved bar seats, meaning a full evening here doesn't require a full dinner commitment.

The current menu leans on Lyre's and Seedlip as its base spirits, assembled into drinks that hold up conceptually against the cocktail list proper. 'Violet Suede' combines Lyre's N/A gin with verjus, aquafaba, and a blueberry pink peppercorn syrup for a velvety, lightly tart pour. 'Cha Cha Chai' uses chai-infused Seedlip 94 with rosemary, coconut water, cranberry, lemon, and orange — aromatic and bright. 'Golden Harmony' layers Lyre's White Cane Spirit with Seedlip Garden 108, tamarind, verjus, orange, and spice-whipped honey for something richer and more complex. Co-owners Scott and Nicole Mattson built this program with the same philosophy they apply to everything at Nocturne: cuisine, cocktails, service, and music should all be executed at the same level.

Nocturne operates Wednesday through Sunday in an acoustically designed, bi-level converted warehouse that blends industrial RiNo bones with 1920s art-deco details. Reservations are strongly recommended and are often pre-ticketed through the venue's website; walk-ins are accepted when space allows, with a per-person music charge added to the check. The dress code is smart-casual to dressed-up — the crowd takes the experience seriously, and the room rewards it. Guests 14 and older are welcome when accompanied by a parent; no one under 14 is admitted. It's a strong choice for date nights, anniversaries, or any occasion where you want the full arc of an evening — food, drink, and live music — without having to compromise on the drinks side of the equation.
venues.pressQuote: Order non-alcoholic beverages à la carte or pair them with Nocturne's three-course dinner and a show menu. The jazz bar currently has four seasonal specials, including Violet Suede made with zero-proof gin, verjus, aquafaba and blueberry pink peppercorn syrup. It's a velvety, sweet sip that's perfect for date night.

venues.name: Noko
venues.description: Noko is an Asian-inspired, wood-fired restaurant that opened in East Nashville in March 2023, founded by owner Jon Murray, managing partner Wilson Brannock, and executive chef and partner Dung "Junior" Vo (a 2025 James Beard semifinalist). It earned Eater Nashville's Best New Restaurant (2023), spots on OpenTable's Top 100 Restaurants in America (2023 and 2024), and recognition from the New York Times. Alongside its cocktail and sake program, Noko keeps a small but genuine named Zero-Proof section on its own menu. House-made options include the Phony Negroni (Tasmanian pepper berry, cinnamon, juniper, orange essence), The Hero (lychee, hibiscus, yuzu, soda), and Guava Girlies (Seedlip Garden 108, guava, basil, yuzu, serrano), with non-alcoholic wine (Vinada Chardonnay) and an Untitled Art NA IPA rounding out the zero-proof choices.

Guava Girlies (Seedlip Garden 108, guava, basil, yuzu, serrano) $7
