venues.longDescription:
Noko is an Asian-inspired, wood-fired restaurant at 701 Porter Road in East Nashville, opened in 2023 in the space that had been Pomodoro East. It was founded by Jon Murray, who came to restaurants from the music business as an artist manager, with executive chef and partner Dung "Junior" Vo — a 2025 James Beard semi-finalist — and managing partner Wilson Brannock, the three having previously worked together on projects for Charleston's Indigo Road Hospitality Group. Murray set the tone early and it still holds: this is not a white-tablecloth place, he said before opening, and they were keeping the neighbourhood feel. The room seats 82 in a Japanese farmhouse register built around maple, and the cooking runs from salmon carpaccio with ponzu and pickled wasabi and bluefin tuna crudo with truffle mustard soy through lobster bao buns, Korean hot wings with gochujang barbecue and yuzu ranch, wagyu brisket, a smoked half chicken, and A5 wagyu teppanyaki sold by the ounce. It has been named to OpenTable's Top 100 Restaurants in America and took Eater Nashville's Best New Restaurant award.

The drinks list carries a section headed "Zero-Proof", and its most striking feature is the price: at $6 and $7, the built non-alcoholic cocktails cost roughly a third of what the restaurant's full cocktails do, which is unusual anywhere and almost unheard of in a room serving a $145 tomahawk. The Hero ($6) is the lightest, combining lychee, hibiscus, yuzu and soda. The house Phony Negroni ($7) is the one the Nashville Scene singled out when it reviewed the restaurant in October 2024 — three zero-proof cocktails, the critic wrote, including a house-made Phony Negroni that had me at Tasmanian pepper berry, bring the party to non-imbibers — and it is built from that pepper berry with cinnamon, juniper and orange essence rather than from a bought-in bottle. Guava Girlies ($7) uses Seedlip Garden 108 with guava, basil, yuzu and serrano. Since that review the list has grown to four with the addition of Kisumé, a non-alcoholic sparkling rosé poured by the glass at $11, tasting of crisp apple, melon and citrus. Noko serves Tuesday to Sunday, closed Mondays, with about fifty parking spaces in the shared Shops at Porter East lot.
venues.pressQuote: Three zero-proof cocktails — including a house-made Phony Negroni that had me at Tasmanian pepper berry — bring the party to non-imbibers.

venues.name: Nola's Creole and Cocktails
venues.description: Nola's is a Creole restaurant and cocktail bar on Cherry Street in Tulsa, and it runs the most technically serious alcohol-free drink in the city. The Haley's Comet is built on Abstinence Cape Citrus and Lyre's Italian Orange Bitter — two named non-alcoholic spirits rather than a syrup — with raspberry, fresh lime juice and Recess blood orange adaptogen sparkling water. That is a spirit-led, bitter, layered build, and it is the sort of drink that only exists when a bar has actually invested in stocking the category. Open from 11am seven days a week, to 10pm early in the week and 11pm from Thursday, with a 10am weekend start.
signatureDrinks: Haley's Comet — Abstinence Cape Citrus, Lyre's Italian Orange Bitter, raspberry, fresh lime, Recess blood orange sparkling water
venues.longDescription:
Cherry Street is the stretch of East 15th that functions as one of Tulsa's two main restaurant districts, and Nola's is its Creole room — gumbo, po' boys, a bar that takes cocktails seriously, and the single best-constructed alcohol-free drink in the city.

The Haley's Comet is worth reading component by component, because the specification tells you how much thought went into it. Abstinence is a South African non-alcoholic spirits house, and Cape Citrus is its bright, orange-forward expression. Lyre's Italian Orange Bitter is the alcohol-free answer to Campari or Aperol — genuinely bitter, which is the quality most mocktails lack entirely. Together those two do the work a spirit and an amaro would do in a cocktail. Raspberry and fresh lime supply fruit and acid, and Recess blood orange adaptogen sparkling water lengthens it.

What that adds up to is a bitter, aromatic, spirit-led drink rather than a fruit cup, and it requires the bar to have bought and stocked two separate non-alcoholic spirits that will only ever be used for this category. That is the investment signal this directory weighs most heavily: a house syrup is cheap and reusable, but a bottle of Lyre's on the back bar exists only for people who are not drinking.

Tulsa Remote picked the drink out in its January 2025 ranking of the city's mocktails, which is the corroboration this listing rests on alongside the menu itself.

The hours are unusually good for a bar-forward restaurant: 11am every day of the week, to 10pm Monday through Wednesday, 11pm Thursday through Saturday, and 10am opening at weekends for brunch. Seven days, no closed evening, in a district you can walk.

One more thing that makes Nola's the right first stop in this city. Creole and Cajun cooking is heavily spiced and rich, and it is one of the cuisines where a good alcohol-free drink genuinely improves the meal rather than merely accompanying it — the bitterness in the Lyre's and the acid from the lime do the same job a cold beer or a highball would against a plate of gumbo or blackened fish. Readers who have given up on ordering anything but water with a big dinner should try this pairing specifically.
venues.pressQuote: Haley's Comet: Abstinence Cape Citrus, Lyre's Italian Orange Bitter, raspberry, fresh lime juice, Recess Blood Orange Adaptogen Sparkling Water

venues.name: Nolia Kitchen
venues.description: Nolia Kitchen is chef-owner Jeffery Harris's Black-owned Over-the-Rhine restaurant, a refined-casual homage to his New Orleans upbringing and the food of the Ninth Ward, Texas and the Carolinas. Harris, who holds multiple James Beard nominations, earned Nolia the No. 4 slot on Cincinnati Magazine's 2026 Best Restaurants list. The bar backs its cocktails with a genuine zero-proof lineup: two $12 mocktails (the N/ATINI, built on Feragaia non-alcoholic spirit and green-tomato brine, and the N/AGRIA of dealcoholized rosé, strawberry and yuzu), a pair of Plus & Minus non-alcoholic wines from Australia by the glass or bottle, and Best Day Brewing's Electro-Lime and Hazy IPA NA beers. The kitchen overhauls its menu each season, so the exact pours rotate over the year.
venues.hours: Mon closed; Tue-Thu 5pm-9pm; Fri-Sat 5pm-10pm; Sun closed
signatureDrinks: N/ATINI (Feragaia zero-proof spirit, green tomato brine)
Plus & Minus Blanc de Blancs (NA sparkling)
venues.longDescription:
Nolia Kitchen opened in Over-the-Rhine in 2022 as chef and owner Jeffery Harris's tribute to his native New Orleans. The kitchen draws on Harris's upbringing in the Ninth Ward along with influences from across the South — Texas, the Carolinas, the Gulf. CityBeat described a menu "stacked with dishes like delectable smoked chicken slathered in Alabama white sauce, cider-stewed collard greens, redfish court-bouillon." The room is refined-casual: exposed wood, bare brick and muted greens wrapped around an open kitchen. Harris, a multiple James Beard nominee, has become one of the city's most decorated chefs, and Cincinnati Magazine ranked Nolia the No. 4 restaurant in its 2026 Best Restaurants issue.

The non-alcoholic program is a real, dedicated part of the bar menu rather than an afterthought. Two $12 mocktails anchor it: the N/ATINI, a spirit-forward pour built on Feragaia zero-proof spirit and green-tomato brine, and the N/AGRIA, a bright mix of dealcoholized rosé, strawberry and yuzu. Non-drinkers can also order from a short NA wine list by the glass or bottle — Plus & Minus Blanc de Blancs and Plus & Minus Rosé, both from Australia ($15/$50) — or reach for a can of Best Day Brewing's Electro-Lime or Hazy IPA ($8). It's a thoughtful spread that lets a sober guest move through cocktail, wine and beer courses alongside the rest of the table.

Nolia sits at 1405 Clay Street, a short walk from Findlay Market, and serves dinner Tuesday through Thursday 5–9pm and Friday–Saturday 5–10pm, closed Sunday and Monday; reservations are the norm for this open-kitchen, special-occasion spot. One caveat worth knowing: the menu changes seasonally with a complete overhaul each cycle, so the specific mocktails, NA wines and beers above may rotate. The zero-proof section itself is a fixture, but call ahead at (513) 384-3597 if you're coming for a particular pour.
venues.pressQuote: The plating is elegant and thoughtful without extravagance.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Cincinnati Magazine, "Best Restaurants No. 4: Nolia Kitchen"

venues.name: NØLO
venues.description: NØLO is Western North Carolina's dedicated non-alcoholic bottle shop — "adult beverages, without the booze" — curating NA beer, wine, spirits, functional drinks, RTD cocktails, and mixers, with in-store tastings and pop-ups for the sober and sober-curious. After losing its original storefront to Hurricane Helene, it is rebuilding a physical presence inside Atomic Furnishing on Broadway under owners Jen & Jason while continuing tastings and online sales, so it is worth confirming in-store hours before a special trip.
signatureDrinks: Amethyst Botanical Spirit, lemon cucumber serrano $30.99
Dr. Zero Zero AmarNo non-alcoholic amaro $43.95

naMenuItems.name: De Soi Purple Lune Non-Alcoholic Apéritif (4 pack)

venues.longDescription:
NØLO is, by its own account, the Southeast's first and North Carolina's only dedicated non-alcoholic bottle shop. It was founded in Asheville in 2021 to create more diversity of choice and inclusion in how people socialise, and changed hands in 2024, when Jen and Jason took it over. What happened next is the reason this listing reads differently from most. In the owners' own words: they had only just started having a blast getting out into the shop and the community to host tastings and pop-ups and help customers find their new non-alcoholic favourites, when Hurricane Helene decided to change their direction. The shop was destroyed. For roughly two months NØLO had no home, shifting to online sales with local pickup while Blue Ridge Hiking Company in Asheville and Claywood in Hendersonville opened their doors so customers could still collect orders — a detail the owners went out of their way to thank publicly. On 1 December 2024 it reopened at 178 Broadway Street, inside the new location of Atomic Furnishing.

The range is a genuine specialist's selection rather than a shelf of the obvious brands, organised into beer, spirits, wines and proxies, ready-to-drink, mixers and functionals. Stock runs from an Amethyst botanical spirit in lemon cucumber serrano at $30.99 and Dr. Zero Zero's AmarNo non-alcoholic amaro at $43.95 through to Free Spirits' Kentucky Mule at $16 for four cans — which is the useful spread, since the category now spans everything from a cheap can to a bottle you would open for a dinner party. Two practical notes. This is retail rather than a bar: the shop hosts tastings and pop-ups as organised events, but there is no standing counter to drink at, so plan to take what you buy home. And because it sits inside a furniture showroom rather than behind its own shopfront, it is worth knowing what you are looking for before you arrive.
venues.pressQuote: Western North Carolina's Non-Alcoholic Bottle Shop

venues.name: NOMAD Melbourne
venues.description: NOMAD is the Melbourne outpost of the Sydney Mediterranean restaurant, built into the lower ground floor of the Adelphi Hotel on Flinders Lane around a wood-fired oven. Its bar menu prints NON-ALCOHOLIC COCKTAILS as its own heading, and the four drinks under it are built rather than poured: a fresh yuzu lemonade on Ito-Farm juice and cane sugar; a Melon Cooler with non-alcoholic gin, honeydew, cucumber, verjus and tonic; a Picante of grapefruit, chilli, holy basil, rose and guindilla brine; and Herb Garden on Lyre's Italian Orange with lemon myrtle verjus, honey, rosemary, chamomile and vanilla. A WINE, BEER & SPIRIT ALTERNATIVES block follows, running NON #1, Heaps Normal lager, honey kombucha and both Four Pillars Bandwagon zero-proof gins.

venues.longDescription:
Rebecca and Al Yazbek brought NOMAD south from Sydney and put it under the Adelphi Hotel on Flinders Lane: a hundred seats on the lower ground floor, dark and low-ceilinged, with a wood-fired oven dominating the room and house-made cheese and charcuterie - duck mortadella, trout basturma - as the kitchen's signature. The cooking draws on Spain, Morocco and the Levant through Australian produce, and the wine list is a long, deliberately Australian document that runs to thirty pages.

The reason it is listed here sits on the back page of the separate bar menu, under a heading printed twice for emphasis: NON-ALC. Four cocktails follow, and none of them is a compromise. The fresh yuzu lemonade is Ito-Farm yuzu juice with cane sugar and soda, which is a real ingredient decision rather than a cordial. The Melon Cooler runs non-alcoholic gin with honeydew, cucumber, verjus and tonic. Picante is the interesting one - grapefruit, chilli, holy basil, rose and guindilla brine, so it lands savoury and hot rather than sweet, which is exactly what is usually missing from an alcohol-free list. Herb Garden is built on Lyre's Italian Orange with lemon myrtle verjus, honey, rosemary, chamomile and vanilla.

Beneath them, WINE, BEER & SPIRIT ALTERNATIVES covers the rest of an evening: NON #1 salted raspberry and chamomile, Heaps Normal 'Another' lager, Beesbucha banana honey kombucha, a Yumbo lemon iced tea soda, and both Four Pillars Bandwagon Dry gin and Bloody Bandwagon shiraz gin poured by the measure. The menu carries an allergen warning covering nuts, dairy, sesame and eggs, and states that no modifications are made to house cocktails - worth knowing before you ask. Lunch runs to 2.15pm and dinner from 5pm daily; a ten per cent surcharge applies on Sundays. It is a booking, not a walk-in bar, and the four non-alcoholic cocktails are the strongest reason for a non-drinker to take the reservation.
venues.pressQuote: Sydney's much-loved Mediterranean restaurant Nomad has landed on Flinders Lane with its first Melbourne outpost, celebrating local produce and wine.

venues.description: NON HQ is the Cheltenham headquarters of NON, the Melbourne alcohol-free 'wine alternative' brand founded by Aaron Trotman in 2019 - and the world's first non-alcoholic cellar door. Everything poured is 0.0%: the chef-crafted NON range (NON1 Salted Raspberry & Chamomile through the darker NON7 Stewed Cherry & Coffee), built from real ingredients with culinary techniques rather than de-alcoholised wine. It's a booking-only tasting experience rather than a walk-in bar - intimate first-Friday tours (A$50pp, max ten guests) that walk you through how the liquids are made and finish with a guided tasting paired with cheese and charcuterie.

venues.longDescription:
NON is a Melbourne-made range of chef-crafted, fully alcohol-free 'wine alternatives' founded by Aaron Trotman in 2019, made from real ingredients using culinary techniques in a purpose-built facility rather than by de-alcoholising wine. In 2023 the brand opened NON HQ at 79 Taunton Drive, Cheltenham - billed as the world's first non-alcoholic cellar door, a lab-style tasting room where the whole point is that nothing on offer contains any alcohol.

The experience runs as intimate guided tours on the first Friday of every month, 9am to 4pm, with eight one-hour sessions capped at ten guests each (group discounts for parties of eight or more). For A$50 per person you meet the makers - the chefs, food scientists, bartenders and winemakers behind NON - do a flavour workshop in the NON kitchen, go behind the scenes of production, and finish with a guided tasting of the range paired with cheese and charcuterie. Every guest leaves with a complimentary bottle of NON to take home (RRP A$30).

The range poured spans NON1 Salted Raspberry & Chamomile, NON2 Caramelised Pear & Kombu, NON3 Toasted Cinnamon & Yuzu, NON5 Lemon Marmalade & Hibiscus and NON7 Stewed Cherry & Coffee, each designed around food. Reviewers have described the room as feeling like a modern art gallery and showroom crossed with a distillery, with interiors by Weekdays Design and Jardan.

Honest note: NON HQ is a booking-only tasting and tour experience, not a walk-in bar - you can't drop in for a drink on a random evening. Sessions are limited and reserved ahead via hello@non.world, so it reads more as a destination cellar-door outing for the alcohol-free curious than a regular night-out venue.
venues.pressQuote: I literally jumped off a cliff and built a plane on the way down. And I still am.

venues.longDescription:
North Italia's Sand Lake Road location serves the group's handmade pasta and wood-fired pizza in the Restaurant Row dining corridor of Dr. Phillips, near the Universal-and-convention tourist zone, with lunch, happy hour, dinner, and weekend brunch service. The restaurant occupies The Rialto plaza on Restaurant Row and was reviewed as a brand-new arrival by longtime Orlando restaurant critic Scott Joseph in December 2021.

The zero-proof section of the drink menu lists six named options: Just Peachy (white peach, raspberry, lemon, ginger beer), 00 Spritz (Mionetto non-alcoholic aperitivo, crushed lemon, bubbles), La Spezia (Pentire non-alcoholic spirit, blood orange, honey, lemon), Pina No-Lada (coconut, pineapple, fresh lime, bubbles), Faux Me Twice (non-alcoholic sauvignon blanc, strawberry, pineapple, smashed citrus), and Phony Negroni (St. Agrestis non-alcoholic amaro spirit).

The bar also pours non-alcoholic prosecco (Zonin Cuvée Zero), a non-alcoholic sauvignon blanc (Miguel Torres Serena N/A), and Athletic Brewing's N/A Golden Ale among the beers, giving the corridor's many visiting non-drinkers a full spirit-free menu — cocktails, wine, and beer — rather than a single token option.

The program has drawn outside recognition beyond the restaurant's own marketing: Visit Orlando, the region's official tourism board, named North Italia among its 'Marvelous Orlando Mocktail Spots for Sober Sipping,' specifically calling out the six-drink zero-proof lineup as standing apart from a typical chain wine-and-beer list.
venues.pressQuote: They have six unique options to suit all palates, from the sweet Pina No-Lada (coconut, pineapple, lime, berries) to options crafted with nonalcoholic wine and spirits.

venues.name: North Main Kava Bar
venues.description: North Main is a woman-owned and LGBTQ+-owned kava bar in downtown Lowell, west of Charlotte in Gaston County, and by its own account the only kava bar for seventy-five miles. It is closed on Monday and otherwise opens at 1pm, running to 10pm through the week and 9pm on Sunday. The room is a pet-friendly coffeehouse in format — well-behaved leashed dogs are welcome inside or at the outdoor tables — and the drinks are kava and kratom mocktails alongside coffee. IMPORTANT for readers in recovery: kratom is half of that pairing and the bar is open about it. Kratom acts on opioid receptors and carries dependence and withdrawal risk that kava does not, so order by name.
venues.longDescription:
North Main Kava Bar occupies 118 North Main Street in Lowell, a small mill town in Gaston County about twenty miles west of uptown Charlotte, and its own description of its position is the most useful fact about it: it is the only kava bar for seventy-five miles. That is a real statement about coverage. The Charlotte metro, for all its size, has almost nothing in the dedicated alcohol-free category, and what exists is concentrated in the city itself. For anyone in Gastonia, Belmont, Mount Holly or Lowell, this is the local option and there is no second one.

The bar is woman-owned and LGBTQ+-owned, which in a small Southern mill town is part of what the room is — it has been written about locally as a place building community as much as serving drinks. The format is a coffeehouse rather than a nightlife venue: it opens at 1pm, closes at 10pm from Tuesday through Saturday and at 9pm on Sunday, and is shut on Mondays. It is pet-friendly in a properly worked-out way, with well-behaved leashed dogs welcome inside as well as at the outdoor tables.

The drinks are built as mocktails rather than served as plain shells, which suits an audience that is largely new to the category. Kava is the ground root of Piper methysticum, a South Pacific shrub, infused in water and drunk socially for roughly three thousand years across Fiji, Vanuatu, Tonga and Samoa. It contains no alcohol, tastes earthy and bitter, numbs the lips and tongue at first sip, and is mildly sedative rather than intoxicating in alcohol's sense. Coffee is also served.

The honest caveat is one the bar itself makes no attempt to hide, and it belongs here rather than in a footnote. North Main serves kratom alongside kava, and markets the two together — its own framing is that kava is a good alternative to alcohol while kratom gives an energy lift without the crash or jitters of coffee. That is a fair description of why people drink it, but it is not the whole picture, and the people most likely to consult this directory need the rest. Kratom is the leaf of a Southeast Asian tree, Mitragyna speciosa, and its principal alkaloids act on the opioid receptors. Regular use produces tolerance and a genuine withdrawal syndrome, several US states ban it outright, and concentrated 7-hydroxymitragynine products derived from it are the subject of active federal scheduling action. Kava carries no comparable dependence profile. Both are poured here, so if you have come to kava specifically to avoid substances that can take hold, order by name and ask.

venues.name: Notch Brewing (Brighton Biergarten)
venues.description: Notch Brewing's Brighton site is a 2,000 sq ft biergarten and taproom at 525 Western Avenue, in the restored Charles River Speedway headquarters, opened in July 2021 as the brewery's second location after its Salem home. Notch was founded by Chris Lohring in 2010 as the first US brewery to build itself entirely around session beer, and every beer it makes sits at or below 4.5% ABV. That discipline extends to a permanent non-alcoholic range: three Notch-brewed 0.5% ABV beers — a craft pils, a New England-style IPA and a blonde ale — are available at all times at both taprooms, alongside sparkling hop water. The biergarten seats around 250 at communal tables and runs year-round, heated in winter and shaded in summer.

venues.longDescription:
Chris Lohring founded Notch in 2010 as a contract-brewed brand with a single organising idea: that the US craft market had almost no well-made low-strength beer, and that every Notch beer would therefore be 4.5% ABV or lower. The brewery took over its own Salem premises in 2016, and in October 2019 Boston Magazine reported plans for a second brewery, taproom and beer garden in Brighton. That site opened in July 2021 at the Charles River Speedway, a restored former horse-racing administration complex at the corner of Western Avenue and Soldiers Field Road that has since become an open-air market of small food and retail tenants. The Brighton biergarten runs to roughly 2,000 square feet with seating for about 250 people at communal tables, operates year-round with heaters through the winter and umbrellas through the summer, and pours in the Central European measures the brewery favours — quarter, half and full litre.

The reason Notch matters to non-drinkers is that its non-alcoholic beers are brewed in-house rather than bought in, and are treated as a permanent part of the range rather than a seasonal experiment. Three are kept on at all times across both taprooms: a non-alcoholic craft pils, a non-alcoholic New England-style IPA and a non-alcoholic blonde ale, each at 0.5% ABV. Northshore Magazine covered the launch of the pair that started the programme, and Lohring's explanation of why a pilsner is the hardest style to get right without alcohol — that pilsner is very delicate beer, so any variable affecting flavour shows up immediately — is a fair summary of the technical problem. Sparkling hop water and mineral water round out the alcohol-free options. The alcoholic taps alongside run to Hefe Weisse, Dunkel Weizen, German Afternoons Pils, Salem Lager, Kolsch, Dunkel Bier, radlers, The Mule corn lager, Punto Pils and a New England pale ale. The biergarten opens at 3pm on weekdays and noon at weekends.
venues.pressQuote: Pilsner is very delicate beer. So, if there are any variables that would impact the flavor, they are going to show right away in a pilsner.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Chris Lohring, founder of Notch Brewing

venues.name: Nothing's Left Brewing Co.
venues.description: Nothing's Left is a Tulsa brewery that produces its own non-alcoholic line, MoodBrü, and serves MoodBrü mocktails in the taproom — including a paloma, with watermelon and blackberry-lime-mint variations. One thing to know before ordering: MoodBrü drinks are terpene-infused and are sold on their intended effects, described as watermelon to unwind and blackberry lime mint for uplift. They contain no alcohol, but they are not simply flavoured soda either, and readers avoiding functional or hemp-derived ingredients should ask. The taproom is closed Monday, opens at 3pm midweek and noon on Saturday.
venues.hours: Tue-Thu 3pm-9pm; Fri 1pm-11pm; Sat 12pm-11pm; Sun 1pm-7pm; Mon closed
venues.longDescription:
A brewery that makes its own non-alcoholic line is a strong signal, because it means the alcohol-free option was engineered rather than bought in. Nothing's Left, in Tulsa's Kendall-Whittier neighbourhood, produces MoodBrü and serves it in the taproom, including as mocktails — a paloma among them, with watermelon and blackberry-lime-mint variations.

This listing comes with a caveat that readers of this directory are entitled to have stated plainly rather than buried, and it is the reason the venue is graded three rather than four. MoodBrü drinks are terpene-infused, and they are marketed on their intended effects: the watermelon expression to unwind, the blackberry lime mint for uplift. Terpenes are the aromatic compounds found in hops, citrus peel and cannabis, and drinks built around them sit in the functional category alongside adaptogens and nootropics rather than in the straightforwardly non-alcoholic one.

What that means practically: these contain no alcohol, and for most readers they are an interesting local product from a brewery doing something genuinely unusual. For readers in recovery who avoid anything sold on a mood effect, and for anyone steering clear of hemp-derived ingredients, they are worth asking about first. This directory's position is that the disclosure belongs on the page, not in the small print — the same approach taken with the kava venues elsewhere in this guide and with the hemp drinks in Bend.

The taproom itself is a straightforward Tulsa brewery room. Closed Monday; 3pm to 9pm Tuesday through Thursday; 1pm to 11pm Friday; noon to 11pm Saturday; 1pm to 7pm Sunday.

For anyone who wants an alcohol-free beer with nothing functional attached, Cabin Boys a few blocks away keeps Big Drop's Pine Trail Pale on.

Credit where it is due, though: a brewery choosing to develop its own alcohol-free line rather than buying one in is doing something most of the industry still will not, and MoodBrü has given Tulsa a locally made zero-proof product that did not exist before. The disclosure above is about helping readers order accurately, not about discouraging them — for most people this is simply an interesting drink from a small brewery.
venues.pressQuote: MoodBrü Mocktails: terpene-infused, with varieties offering watermelon to unwind and blackberry lime mint for uplift

venues.name: NRG Haus
venues.description: NRG Haus is a fully alcohol-free social wellness club in Toronto's Liberty Village, pairing a sauna-and-cold-plunge contrast therapy circuit with a zero-proof mocktail lounge built around a vapour fireplace. It opened on February 20, 2026, founded by Ivan Ho, with Will Edwards as director of operations, on the premise — as Ho has put it — of "community recovery without the need of alcohol being at the centre of it." No alcohol is served anywhere on the premises; instead the bar pours three named functional mocktails, Up Regulate, Down Regulate and Moderate, formulated respectively for energy, calm and rehydration.

signatureDrinks: Up Regulate — contains B-12, described as an uplifting/energizing functional beverage (per NOW Toronto)
Down Regulate — contains L-theanine and ashwagandha, calming/sleep-support functional beverage (per NOW Toronto)
Moderate — rehydration and balance focused functional beverage (per NOW Toronto)
venues.longDescription:
NRG Haus is a social wellness club in Liberty Village at 171 East Liberty Street, built around contrast therapy rather than a conventional bar or gym. The facility runs a spacious sauna room alongside a cold-plunge room with four tubs set to different temperatures and LED visuals for guided breathwork, plus showers and multiple lounge areas; it operates as a barefoot facility with towel service, and robes and sandals are available. It was founded by Ivan Ho, with Will Edwards as director of operations, and opened on February 20, 2026 — the name stands for Nourish, Recharge, Gather.

The concept is explicitly built around sobriety: as Ho told NOW Toronto, "NRG Haus, which stands for Nourish, Recharge, Gather, is a next generation social wellness club that's built on community recovery without the need of alcohol being at the centre of it." Director of operations Will Edwards has pointed to the broader generational shift away from drinking — noting alcohol consumption has fallen by roughly 90% globally — as part of the thinking behind a social space with no alcohol at all; IV therapy with vitamin injections is offered alongside the contrast-therapy sessions to round out the recovery focus.

True to that premise, no alcohol is served anywhere on site. The mocktail bar instead pours a small menu of named functional beverages: Up Regulate, dosed with B-12 for an energizing lift; Down Regulate, built on L-theanine and ashwagandha for a calming, sleep-supportive evening pour; and Moderate, a rehydration- and balance-focused option. Drinks are served in the lounge areas around the vapour fireplace, where the format is built for conversation rather than a traditional bar crowd.

Access runs on a pay-per-visit and membership model: a single 90-minute contrast-therapy session costs $45, a two-week unlimited introductory pass is $99, and Founding Club memberships offer locked-in pricing. The club also runs weekend "Haus Parties" — $49, 120-minute themed events running Friday through Sunday, with DJs, alcohol-free drinks and dancing. NRG Haus has drawn coverage from Toronto Life, blogTO, NOW Toronto, Toronto Guardian, Streets of Toronto and SWAGGER Magazine, and holds a 4.8-star rating across more than 500 ClassPass reviews.
venues.pressQuote: NRG Haus, which stands for Nourish, Recharge, Gather, is a next generation social wellness club that's built on community recovery without the need of alcohol being at the centre of it.

venues.name: Nubian Markets
venues.description: Nubian Markets is a halal butchery, African grocery and cafe on Washington Street in Roxbury's Nubian Square, opened in May 2023 by chef Ismail Samad and Yusuf Yassin. The cafe side, Nuba Cafe, serves made-to-order food drawn from across the African diaspora, including the Butcher's Burger built on halal ground beef from the in-house butchery with berbere citrus mayo and tomato jam in a house pita, plus lamb couscous, jerk chicken, chickpea peanut stew and bunny chow. The coffee bar is the reason to sit down: Yassin's chai latte has a following, and a vanilla orange blossom latte runs alongside standard espresso drinks. Because the business is halal and built to serve Greater Boston's Muslim communities, no alcohol is sold or served anywhere in the store.
venues.longDescription:
Nubian Markets opened in May 2023 at 2565 Washington Street, in a Nubian Square that had spent years without a full-service grocery. Chef Ismail Samad and Yusuf Yassin built it as three businesses under one roof: a halal butchery sourcing from regional halal farms, a grocery stocked for the North, West, East and Central African cooking of the surrounding neighborhoods, and Nuba Cafe, a counter-service restaurant and coffee bar. The project has been covered as a food-access story as much as a restaurant one, by Edible Boston in September 2023 and the Bay State Banner the same month, and Samad has been consistent in framing it as neighborhood infrastructure rather than a destination.

For a reader who is not drinking, the useful fact is structural: the entire business is halal, so there is no alcohol on the shelves or behind the counter, and the cafe keeps evening hours to 8pm six days a week. The coffee bar runs a full espresso program with a chai latte that has become the thing regulars order by name, plus a vanilla orange blossom latte that leans on the same aromatic pantry the kitchen uses. Food from the cafe covers the diaspora deliberately, from the Butcher's Burger with halal ground beef, cheddar, berbere citrus mayo, tomato jam, shaved onion and lettuce in a house-made golden pita, to lamb couscous, ginger beef with injera, jerk chicken, chickpea peanut stew and chicken bunny chow served in a hollowed bread bowl. It works as an early-evening meeting place rather than a late-night one, and it is one of very few options in Roxbury where the no-alcohol answer is the building's default rather than a special request. The market has also been covered as a public-health story rather than a restaurant one, by Boston Medical Center's Health City and by the Conservation Law Foundation, both writing about what a full-line grocery does for a neighborhood that had gone without one.
venues.pressQuote: We are speaking to as many people as we can, welcoming people to our home, welcoming people to our neighborhood.

venues.name: Nur House Cafe
venues.description: Nur House Cafe is a Somali family-run cafe that opened on 25 March 2026 in a downtown Minneapolis storefront that had been a Starbucks, a few blocks from the Commons and U.S. Bank Stadium. It is fully alcohol-free and runs into the evening, to 8pm most nights and 9pm on Friday and Saturday. The drinks lean on Somali and other global coffee and tea traditions and rotate seasonally; the baking is done in house by one of the owners, a self-taught baker, and covers chocolate pistachio scones, tahini banana bread, brown butter cinnamon rolls and an Egyptian croissant bread pudding served with cardamom creme anglaise.
venues.longDescription:
Nur House Cafe opened on 25 March 2026 at 515 South 4th Street, taking over a downtown storefront that had been a Starbucks. Nur means light; the cafe is run by a Somali family, one of whom left a job teaching high-school English to open it, working with her brothers. Downtown Minneapolis has no shortage of coffee, but it has had almost nothing that reflects the city's East African population, and that is the stated reason the family opened here. Speaking to Racket in July 2026, Fadumo Ali said "the need has been long overdue. We haven't really felt represented within a lot of the coffee shop scene." The location does specific work: it sits within walking distance of the Commons and U.S. Bank Stadium, so it catches the crowds that fill and empty that end of downtown on event nights — exactly the moments when the surrounding options are bars.

The programme is coffee and tea led, drawing on Somali and other global traditions and rotating with the seasons rather than holding a fixed signature list, which is why this entry names no individual drinks: what was on the board in one month was not what was on it in the next, and this site does not publish drink names it has not seen. What is consistent is the baking, all of it done on site by a self-taught baker: chocolate pistachio scones, tahini banana bread, brown butter cinnamon rolls, and an Egyptian croissant bread pudding finished with cardamom creme anglaise. There is no alcohol on the premises and no bar. The hours run early — 6:30am on weekdays, catching commuters — and hold into the evening, closing at 8pm most nights and 9pm on Friday and Saturday, with the family noting that they extend further in summer when the Commons park across the way is busy. It is graded here as a strong non-alcoholic room rather than a late-night destination: it is entirely alcohol-free, but it closes before most people's evening does.
venues.pressQuote: The need has been long overdue. We haven't really felt represented within a lot of the coffee shop scene.

venues.name: O-Ku
venues.description: O-Ku is an upscale sushi and Japanese restaurant at Atherton Mill in Charlotte's South End, sourcing premium fish from markets in Norway, Scotland, Hawaii, and New Zealand. The restaurant features a dedicated "Spirit Free" section on its drinks menu with five Asian-inspired mocktails — including a Cherry-Yuzu Soda and Matcha Limeade — all priced at $8. The lively, stylish dining room makes it a natural fit for sober diners who want a thoughtful zero-proof experience alongside exceptional sushi.

venues.longDescription:
O-Ku is an upscale sushi restaurant at 2000 South Boulevard, Suite 510, in the Atherton Mill development in South End, part of a group founded by Steve Palmer with Kimball Brienza as managing partner, Vonda Freeman running wine and Whitney Hicks on pastry. It sources premium fish from markets in Norway, Scotland, Hawaii and New Zealand, and the raw list shows it — yellowtail carpaccio at $18, otoro tartare at $28, a lobster temaki at $26, and an omakase at $175 a head with an optional wine and sake pairing at $50. Queen City Nerve readers made it runner-up for both Best Sushi and Best Japanese Cuisine in 2024, and the restaurant has collected a Charlotte BOB award and a Top 100 Restaurants listing. Service runs from 5pm nightly, to 11pm on Friday and Saturday, with happy hour on Mondays and Wednesdays from 4pm for dine-in guests.

The zero-proof list is one of the most reasonably priced in the city for a restaurant at this level: a section headed "Zero-Proof" holding five drinks, every one of them $8, against cocktails that run several times that. They are built as sushi accompaniments rather than as cocktail substitutes, which is the right instinct — nothing here fights delicate raw fish. Cherry-Yuzu Soda combines Amarena cherry with yuzu and ginger. Matcha Limeade pairs matcha with a house limeade, bitter and sharp at once. Imagine Dragon works tonic with lychee purée and dragonfruit powder. Des-Tea-Nation is the most aromatic, layering orange blossom tea with honey, ginger and soda, and Daydream is the richest, using coconut cream with pineapple, orange and lime. For anyone who would rather drink beer with sushi, an Asahi Zero at 0.0% and a Best Day non-alcoholic Kölsch are $5 each. The whole zero-proof offering, drinks and beer together, is cheaper than a single cocktail.

venues.description: Oak & Honey is a locally sourced restaurant and bar on East Washington Street in downtown Greenville, named in the city's mocktail coverage among the rooms worth going to for an alcohol-free drink. Its relevance for a non-drinker is the sourcing: a kitchen built on local produce keeps a pantry of fresh fruit, herbs and house syrups, and those are precisely the components an alcohol-free build needs when there is no spirit to carry it. Open 3pm to 11pm Tuesday through Thursday and to midnight on Friday and Saturday, closed Sunday and Monday.

venues.longDescription:
Oak & Honey trades on local sourcing — the name is the pitch — from a room on East Washington Street a block off Main in downtown Greenville. It appears in this guide because Greenville's mocktail coverage lists it among the places to drink without alcohol, and because of a general principle this directory has found reliable across sixty-odd cities.

The principle is that farm-to-table kitchens make better alcohol-free drinks than dedicated cocktail bars sometimes do, and the reason is the pantry rather than the bartending. A restaurant built on local produce already has ripe fruit, fresh herbs, house syrups and infusions in daily use for the food. Those are exactly the ingredients that have to do the work in a drink with no spirit in it — the spirit is the easiest component to leave out when everything else is made in-house and actually tastes of something.

That is why the recommendation here is to ask rather than to order from a list. This entry is graded three and records no signature drinks, honestly: there is no printed zero-proof section this directory could verify and no named build published in a readable form. What is documented is that the room is recommended locally for this, and what is inferable is that a kitchen of this type can deliver if asked.

The hours are a real constraint and worth planning around: 3pm to 11pm Tuesday through Thursday, 3pm to midnight on Friday and Saturday, and closed both Sunday and Monday. In a city where several of the better rooms take the same two days off, that makes the start of the week thin — The Kava Konnection, Group Therapy and UP on the Roof are the Sunday and Monday answers.

It is a short walk from UP on the Roof, Crafted and STIR.
venues.pressQuote: Greenville is embracing the mocktail trend, offering residents and visitors a range of innovative, alcohol-free drinks with flavors like lavender, ginger, and blood orange.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Here Greenville, Discover The Best Mocktails In Greenville

venues.name: OAK Long Bar + Kitchen
venues.description: OAK Long Bar + Kitchen is the bar and restaurant inside the Fairmont Copley Plaza on St James Avenue, facing Copley Square, and it is open from 7am to midnight every day, which makes it one of the few full bars in Back Bay a person can walk into at any hour. Its drinks menu carries a section headed Spirit Free with three named builds. Honey Badger is lemon, grapefruit, honey and ginger beer at $15; Super Fresh is white cranberry, lemon and soda at $14; and Raspberry Fields is built on Lyre's Italian Spritz with raspberry, basil, agave and lemon at $15. The offering is modest rather than extensive, but it is named, printed and priced alongside the cocktails.
signatureDrinks: Honey Badger (lemon, grapefruit, honey, ginger beer)
Raspberry Fields (Lyre's Italian Spritz, raspberry, basil, agave, lemon)
venues.longDescription:
OAK Long Bar + Kitchen sits inside the Fairmont Copley Plaza at 138 St James Avenue, a hotel bar in the grand sense, with a long marble counter running down one side of a room that opens onto Copley Square. It serves breakfast from 7am, lunch, dinner and a late bar every night to midnight, with last call for drinks at 11.45pm, and it is a common meeting point for people who work in the surrounding towers and stay in the hotel. That mix, plus the hours, is why it belongs in a directory like this: the situation it answers is the after-work drink in Back Bay where one person at the table is not drinking.

The non-alcoholic offering is honest rather than ambitious. The drinks list, published in its current form in May 2026, carries a section headed Spirit Free between the craft cocktails and the draft beer, with three drinks on it. Honey Badger is lemon, grapefruit, honey and ginger beer at $15. Super Fresh is white cranberry, lemon and soda at $14. Raspberry Fields is the one built on a non-alcoholic spirit, using Lyre's Italian Spritz with raspberry, basil, agave and lemon at $15. Two of the three are essentially high-quality long drinks rather than cocktail analogues, which is why this is graded as a real but modest programme rather than a serious one, but the section is printed, the drinks are named, and they are priced within a couple of dollars of the alcoholic list rather than being dumped at soda prices or, worse, left off the menu entirely. The draft list also leans local, with Aeronaut, Dorchester Brewing and Mighty Squirrel among the taps. Anyone wanting a deeper zero-proof list in the same neighborhood should look at Rochambeau on Boylston Street or Cafe Sauvage at the Massachusetts Avenue end, both of which build on non-alcoholic spirits across a longer menu. OAK's value is the hours and the position on Copley Square rather than the depth of the list.

venues.name: Oasis Botanical Lounge
venues.description: Oasis Botanical Lounge is an alcohol-free daytime lounge in the centre of Carr Mill Mall on North Greensboro Street in downtown Carrboro, open ten to seven Monday to Saturday and from noon on Sunday. It began as a coffee shop and now describes itself as a haven for botanical wellness: micronized kava prepared in juice or milk, functional mushroom drinks built on Sporeganix powders from Winston-Salem, Rishi organic teas and Pure Intentions Peruvian coffee, with comfortable seating, workspaces and weekly drumming, stretching and monthly Kirtan music events. It also prepares kratom drinks and sells delta-THC and CBD products, all labelled, so read before you order. No alcohol is served. It closes at seven, so treat it as an afternoon room rather than a night out.
venues.address: 200 N Greensboro St A-5, Carrboro, NC 27510
signatureDrinks: Micronized Kava — powdered kava prepared in a juice or milk of your choice
Functional Mushroom drink — Sporeganix mushroom extract powders, up to three kinds, in juice or chocolate almond milk
Rishi organic hot teas — Earl Grey, Peach Blossom White, Masala Chai, Jasmine Green and more
Pure Intentions Peruvian coffee — organic, direct trade, roasted in Charlotte
venues.longDescription:
Oasis sits in the middle of Carr Mill Mall, the converted textile mill on North Greensboro Street that is the commercial centre of downtown Carrboro, and it is the second alcohol-free room in a town whose social life otherwise runs on bars. Where Krave a few blocks away keeps bar hours, Oasis keeps café hours — ten in the morning until seven, from noon on Sunday — and that is the right way to think about it: a place to sit with a drink in the afternoon, work, or meet someone, with no alcohol on the premises.

The founders are Alicia Roskind Dearing and James Dearing, carrying on the work of her father Robert Roskind, an author whose books and free music events in Jamaica, Guatemala and the Havasupai reservation are the source of the One Love message the room is built around. The lounge began as a coffee shop — the coffee is still Pure Intentions, an organic direct-trade Peruvian roast from Charlotte, and the hot teas are Rishi organics from Earl Grey to Masala Chai and Jasmine Green — and has grown into what it calls a haven for botanical wellness.

Kava is the drink to know about. Oasis serves it micronized, a finely ground powder that is prepared in one of the house juices or milks rather than steeped and strained, and it also sells the powder to take home. Beside it are functional mushroom drinks built on Sporeganix extract powders from Winston-Salem — reishi, lion's mane, chaga and five others, up to three in one drink in juice or chocolate almond milk — and cold teas and fermented drinks. Kava contains no alcohol but is mildly psychoactive; anyone pregnant, on medication or managing liver health should ask a doctor first.

Two things need saying plainly. The lounge also prepares kratom, a plant in the coffee family with effects of its own, in four strains, and it sells delta-THC and CBD products under its own wellness line. All of it is labelled, none of it is alcohol, and a reader avoiding every intoxicant should order the coffee, the tea or a mushroom drink and say so. Weekly stretching and drumming sessions and a monthly Kirtan music evening are the events that give the room its character, and the shop ships its products for anyone not in the neighbourhood.

venues.name: Oberlin
venues.description: Oberlin is chef Benjamin Sukle's Westminster Street restaurant, built around raw fish, pasta and New England produce, and its bar keeps non-alcoholic drinks made from house cordials rather than from bottled mixers. The two standing builds run citrus-forward and herbal respectively — a house citrus cordial and a garden julep. Small room, seasonal list.
venues.longDescription:
Oberlin sits on Westminster Street in downtown Providence, the first of chef Benjamin Sukle's restaurants and still the one that defines his cooking for most people — raw fish handled with precision, hand-made pasta, and vegetables from growers he has worked with for years. The room is narrow and busy and the menu changes with what is landing and growing.

The bar follows the kitchen's logic, which is what earns the restaurant a place here. Its non-alcoholic drinks are built from cordials and infusions made in house rather than assembled from bottled mixers, so they carry the same seasonal character as the plates. Two builds are documented in current Providence coverage: a house citrus cordial, served light and zesty, and a garden julep that runs herbal and deliberately calming rather than sweet. Between them they cover the two things a non-drinker usually wants — something sharp with food, and something long and aromatic to sit with.

This is a restaurant rather than a bar, and the alcohol-free offering is correspondingly compact: two considered drinks rather than a full printed section, which is why we grade it a three rather than a four. What it has over most restaurants at that level is that the drinks are actually made, not poured. If you are eating here and not drinking, you will get something built for the meal rather than a glass of soda.

Oberlin shares its ownership and its block with Gift Horse, the raw bar a couple of doors down at 272 Westminster, so the two can be treated as a pair on the same evening. We have not published prices or exact current names, as the list moves seasonally and we could not read the restaurant's live drinks menu directly.

venues.name: Ocean Beach Cafe
venues.description: Ocean Beach Cafe is an all-day cafe, fully alcohol-free bar and non-alcoholic bottle shop at 734 La Playa Street in the Outer Richmond, one block from Ocean Beach. It was opened by career bartender Joshua James, who bills it as San Francisco's first non-alcoholic bar, and it serves scratch-made food and Four Barrel coffee alongside craft zero-proof cocktails, chai and kava. The retail side stocks one of the largest selections of non-alcoholic beer, wine and spirits in the country. The cafe also runs Temperance Tastings, alcohol-free mixology classes, a private lounge called Temperance and a membership programme, Club AF. The San Francisco Standard has called it the granddaddy of the city's alcohol-free nightlife, and it is the anchor of non-alcoholic drinking in San Francisco.

venues.longDescription:
Ocean Beach Cafe sits one block from the sand at 734 La Playa Street in the Outer Richmond, and it is the venue most responsible for there being an alcohol-free scene in San Francisco at all. It was founded by Joshua James, a career bartender who took a year off drinking and then built the business he could not find, and it bills itself as the city's first non-alcoholic bar. The cafe operates on three levels at once: an all-day room serving scratch-made food and Four Barrel coffee; a fully alcohol-free bar; and a bottle shop stocking one of the largest retail selections of non-alcoholic beer, wine and spirits in the country. Writing in The San Francisco Standard in December 2023, Astrid Kane called it "the granddaddy of San Francisco's alcohol-free nightlife," noting that it is "where to stock up on supplies to build out a nonalcoholic home bar cart while sitting down for 'Temperance Tastings' and NA mixology classes."

The cocktail list is built rather than assembled from bottles: named pours run $16 and include the Destroyer of Bad Vibes (Melati Classics, The Pathfinder, honey, citrus, All The Bitter orange and cinnamon), the mezcal-inspired Good Buzz Daisy, the Needle In The Groove, the Nuevo Compañero and the Ghia Spritz. The New Pear-Adigm and the booze-free French 75, both listed here previously, are no longer on the card as of August 2026. James also runs a private lounge called Temperance, hourlong Temperance Tastings, mixology classes and an alcohol-free membership programme, Club AF, which together make the venue a community hub rather than only a bar — a distinction that matters for readers who want somewhere to go rather than only something to drink. One thing to know before visiting: alongside coffee, chai and zero-proof cocktails, Ocean Beach Cafe serves kava, a root beverage traditional to the South Pacific. Kava contains no alcohol but it is mildly psychoactive and sedating, and readers in recovery may want to make a deliberate choice about it rather than encounter it unannounced. Hours run daytime rather than late — roughly 8am to 5 or 6pm — so this is a morning-through-afternoon destination, with evening events booked separately. The SF Standard has also described it simply as "mocktail central in San Francisco."
venues.pressQuote: Ocean Beach Cafe is mocktail central in San Francisco.

venues.name: Octopi Brewing
venues.description: Octopi Brewing in Waunakee, fifteen minutes north of Madison, is where Untitled Art is brewed — one of the largest and most inventive non-alcoholic beer lines in the United States, and the single biggest reason the Madison metro matters on a national alcohol-free map. Isaac Showaki founded Octopi and launched Untitled Art with Levi Funk of Funk Factory Geuzeria in December 2016; the non-alcoholic range is fully fermented and then stripped of ethanol by reverse osmosis, which preserves the hop oils and malt character that boiling-off destroys. The taproom pours the line on site, including the mango dragonfruit sour and the west coast IPA that Visit Madison singles out.
signatureDrinks: Untitled Art Non-Alcoholic Mango Dragonfruit Sour
Untitled Art Non-Alcoholic West Coast IPA
Untitled Art non-alcoholic range on draft and in cans
venues.longDescription:
Most cities in this registry have non-alcoholic beer poured in them. The Madison metro makes it, at scale, and that is genuinely unusual. Octopi Brewing sits on Uniek Drive in Waunakee, about fifteen minutes north of the city, and is the contract and production brewery behind Untitled Art — the label Isaac Showaki launched with Levi Funk of Funk Factory Geuzeria in December 2016, and which has become one of the most widely distributed and most adventurous non-alcoholic beer ranges in the country.

The production method is the part worth understanding, because it explains why these beers taste like beer. Untitled Art brews and ferments the beer completely, the normal way, and only then removes the ethanol using reverse osmosis membrane filtration. That is a physical separation carried out cold, so the hop oils, the malt character and the fermentation-derived esters developed during brewing survive the process. The cheaper alternative — arresting fermentation before alcohol forms, or boiling the alcohol off — leaves you with something closer to sweet wort or to cooked beer, which is why so much non-alcoholic beer disappoints. The range is also unusually ambitious in style: fruited sours, pastry stouts, hazy and west coast IPAs, rather than the lager-and-nothing-else roster most producers stop at.

The taproom pours the line on site, which makes the drive worth it for anyone who has only encountered Untitled Art in a four-pack. Visit Madison, the city's official visitor bureau, names the mango dragonfruit sour and the west coast IPA specifically. Be clear that this is a working brewery taproom and the majority of what is poured contains alcohol — Octopi brews under many labels, including seltzers and contract beers — so it is not a sober room, it is a room where the non-alcoholic option is made on the premises to the same standard as everything else. Check hours before driving up; the taproom schedule is narrower than the brewery's.
venues.pressQuote: Octopi Brewing in Waunakee pours Untitled Art's line of NA beers, featuring flavors like mango dragonfruit sour and west coast IPA.

venues.name: Oddball
venues.description: A creative Alphabet City cocktail bar, opened November 2025, where non-alcoholic drinks are built in-house with the same rigor as the spirited menu rather than treated as an afterthought. The zero-proof builds favor unusual, savory and offbeat ingredients over the standard fruity mocktail.
venues.longDescription: Oddball opened in November 2025 at 188 Avenue B in the East Village (Alphabet City), in a roughly 1,100-square-foot former jazz bar redesigned into a retro-futurist space that blends 1970s cosmic nostalgia with diner Americana. The bar is led by beverage director Logan Rodriguez alongside partners LaTeisha Moore and Philip Reichenberger, and its debut menu pairs high-contrast ingredients into surprising combinations across drinks such as the Far Side (a margarita with fig-leaf tequila, cilantro, dill, pineapple and tomatillo brine) and the Infinite Loop (sesame and hazelnut gin, guava, whey brandy and white aperitif). Non-alcoholic drinks are a deliberate part of the program rather than a tacked-on list, made in-house with the same conceptual clarity and technical attention as the spirited cocktails. In January 2026, Time Out New York named Oddball among the city's best non-alcoholic bar programs, praising it as a newcomer that "stood out for its punchy, in-house-made NA drinks and cozy, slightly sci-fi bar vibe." The bar is open Wednesday through Saturday from 5 p.m. to 1 a.m. and takes reservations via Resy while still welcoming walk-ins.
venues.pressQuote: Newcomer Oddball, which was barely weeks old at the time of judging, stood out for its punchy, in-house-made NA drinks and cozy, slightly sci-fi bar vibe.

venues.name: Oddstory Brewing Co.
venues.description: Oddstory Brewing Co. runs a taproom on Martin Luther King Boulevard in downtown Chattanooga, and its attached Greenhouse space is the most comprehensively stocked alcohol-free fridge in the city: non-alcoholic beer, mocktails, sparkling "wine", kombucha and cider, all available side by side rather than as a single token option. That breadth is the point — a brewery that carries five different categories of alcohol-free drink has thought about the fact that non-drinkers have preferences too, rather than assuming one NA lager covers everybody. Open from 4pm on weekdays and noon at weekends, running to 10pm.
venues.address: 336 E M L King Blvd, Chattanooga, TN 37403
venues.longDescription:
Breweries are usually the hardest rooms in a city for a non-drinker, because the entire proposition is the beer and the alternative is a soda from a gun. Oddstory has done something about that. Its taproom on East Martin Luther King Boulevard, and the attached Greenhouse space, carry alcohol-free beer, mocktails, sparkling non-alcoholic "wine", kombucha and cider — five distinct categories, stocked together.

That breadth is a more meaningful signal than any single product would be. One non-alcoholic lager on the board is a box-ticking exercise; it assumes every non-drinker wants the same thing and that what they want is a slightly worse version of what everyone else is having. Carrying an NA sparkling wine as well as an NA beer as well as kombucha means someone has thought about the group that turns up — the pregnant friend, the designated driver, the person in recovery and the person who simply does not like beer all want different drinks, and Oddstory can serve all four without anybody having to ask for something off-menu.

The brewery itself is a Chattanooga fixture, with a second location on Central Avenue, and the taproom works the way good taprooms do: long tables, a rotating board, no table service, a room that is as comfortable at four in the afternoon as at nine. It is a short walk from the Southside bars and from 330 Main, which makes an evening combining a taproom and a fully alcohol-free bar entirely practical on foot.

This entry records no signature drinks, because the alcohol-free stock is a rotating retail selection rather than a fixed menu — naming a specific can would be wrong within a season. NOOGAtoday's guide to non-alcoholic drinking in the city documents the categories, which is the durable fact.

Weekdays from 4pm to 10pm; weekends open at noon, closing 10pm Saturday and 9pm Sunday.
venues.pressQuote: Grab a non-alcoholic beer, mocktail, sparkling "wine," kombucha, or cider.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: NOOGAtoday, Local mocktails + non-alcoholic drinks in Chattanooga

venues.name: Off Elm
venues.description: Webster Groves finally has a destination cocktail bar, and it takes zero-proof drinkers seriously. Opened in November 2024 by Matt and Jess Longueville — the couple behind cocktail-catering company STL Barkeep and The Vandy — Off Elm is a walk-in-only, mid-century-modern room on Big Bend Boulevard. The printed menu carries a dedicated Non Alcoholic section: Blood For The Blood God layers zero-proof rum with blood orange, lime, orgeat, and bitters, while the Crimson Gimlet pairs zero-proof gin with red wine syrup and lime. Gruvi NA lager and Best Day NA kölsch anchor the beer list, and the menu promises most classic cocktails can be made non-alcoholic.
venues.address: 8709 Big Bend Blvd., Webster Groves, MO 63119
venues.longDescription:
Off Elm opened on November 29, 2024, at 8709 Big Bend Boulevard in Webster Groves, the second brick-and-mortar project from Matt and Jess Longueville after The Vandy in Forest Park Southeast. The couple built their reputation with STL Barkeep, their St. Louis cocktail-catering company, and brought beverage director Patrick Gioia aboard for this neighborhood bar. Designed by Brian Leenig with mid-century modern lines, the room seats 16 at the bar, 20 at low-top tables, and 16 more at communal tables. There are no reservations: Off Elm is walk-in only, managing busy nights through an online waitlist, and the bar asks guests to text rather than call for the fastest reply.

The zero-proof program is written directly into the menu rather than hidden behind a bartender's shrug. The current menu's Non Alcoholic section leads with Blood For The Blood God — zero-proof rum, blood orange, lime, orgeat, and bitters — and the Crimson Gimlet, which pairs zero-proof gin with red wine syrup and lime, both priced at $12 right alongside their spirited siblings. The beer list backs them up with Gruvi NA lager and Best Day NA kölsch at $6, and sober guests can also opt for Mighty Kind CBD seltzers in Cherry Blossom or Heady Lemon, or Liquid Death sodas. Best of all is the printed pledge at the bottom of the section: most classic cocktails can be made non-alcoholic — just ask a server or bartender.

Off Elm drew immediate attention from the St. Louis food press. Sauce Magazine's first look praised how the bar "blends sophistication with approachability, offering guests a cozy yet refined space to unwind," while Feast Magazine described it as blending sophisticated cocktails and casual elegance, and St. Louis Magazine flagged the opening as a new cocktail destination for Webster Groves. Expect a deep whiskey selection with separate whiskey and spirits lists, a snack menu of bagel-crust pies and boards, and happy hour from 4 to 6 p.m. Tuesday through Thursday. Doors open at 4 p.m. Tuesday through Sunday and close at 11 p.m. Tuesday to Thursday, midnight on Friday and Saturday and 10 p.m. on Sunday, with last call 15 minutes before close.
venues.pressQuote: Off Elm blends sophistication with approachability, offering guests a cozy yet refined space to unwind.

venues.name: Offtrack
venues.description: Offtrack is a music-centric bar and restaurant at 34 North Canal Road, near Boat Quay, that placed No.16 on Asia's 50 Best Bars in 2026. The room is built around listening: an acoustically treated space, a carefully assembled sound system and a wall of vinyl from Singapore and the wider region. The cocktail list is an equal split of classics and contemporary builds, and the bar states plainly that the menu also offers an inclusive non-alcoholic selection of mocktails and non-alcoholic beers. A visitor in 2025 recorded a Passionfruit Jamu Soda at S$16 from that list. The kitchen serves a pan-Asian menu, with a late-night snack menu on Fridays and Saturdays, and it trades until midnight on weekdays and 1am at weekends.
signatureDrinks: Passionfruit Jamu Soda (from the non-alcoholic list; S$16 when recorded in Aug 2025)
venues.longDescription:
Offtrack has been trading on North Canal Road since early 2022 and describes itself as a third space for the creative community, a bar and restaurant that draws on great social spaces around the world. The distinguishing feature is sound. The room was acoustically treated and fitted with a carefully assembled system, and the music programme is curated to surface records from Singapore and the region that most guests will not have heard, some of which hang on the walls as part of a vinyl display. Time Out described it in 2024 as a groovy watering hole serving pan-Asian grub and a tight selection of classic cocktails, with a side of carefully curated tunes, and the wider bar industry has agreed: it entered Asia's 50 Best Bars at No.25 in 2024 and stood at No.16 on the 2026 list. The pan-Asian kitchen leans on South East Asian flavours with a contemporary twist, and a separate late-night snack menu runs on Friday and Saturday nights.

The drinks list is anchored by craft spirits, natural wines and seasonal beers, with the cocktail menu now split evenly between classics and contemporary drinks. For non-drinkers the relevant line is the bar's own: the menu also offers an inclusive non-alcoholic selection of mocktails and non-alcoholic beers. The list rotates and the bar does not publish it online, so the only named drink on record here is a Passionfruit Jamu Soda, at S$16, ordered by a Girl Eat World reviewer in August 2025 who had chosen not to drink that night; jamu is the Indonesian herbal tonic tradition, so expect roots and spice rather than a fruit cordial. Two practical notes from the same visit: the bar keeps a one-drink-per-person policy, so the non-alcoholic list is not optional for anyone at the table, and the zero-proof prices sit close to the cocktail prices. Hours are Monday to Thursday 6pm to midnight and Friday and Saturday 5pm to 1am, closed Sunday; reservations for groups of eight to ten, or for tables after 10pm, are taken by phone or text message.
venues.pressQuote: Offtrack is a groovy watering hole serving up Pan-Asian grub and a tight selection of classic cocktails, with a side of carefully curated tunes.

venues.name: Old City Kava Company
venues.description: Old City Kava Company is a fully alcohol-free kava and kratom lounge that opened in December 2025 at 40 S. 2nd Street in Philadelphia's historic Old City. Founded by Luca Kobza and Adam Lagner, the 1,900-square-foot space is built as a bar alternative for the sober-curious, with roughly 60 seats across a bar, two-tops, and jewel-toned couches, a small board-game collection, and rotating contemporary art for sale. The drink program centers on 16-plus kava-, kratom-, and botanical-tea-based mocktails, including the Lemongrass Paloma, the Old City Red Eye (kava, kratom, ReAnimator cold brew, oat milk, agave, vanilla), the Old Citywide, the Cucumber Basil Cooler, and Maple Masala. By day it doubles as a coworking cafe serving ReAnimator coffee, Random Tea Room teas, and Funky Fresh kombucha; it stays open until midnight on weekdays and 2 a.m. on weekends.
venues.longDescription:
Old City Kava Company opened in December 2025 at 40 South 2nd Street, in the middle of one of Philadelphia's densest drinking neighbourhoods, and it is fully alcohol-free. Founded by Luca Kobza and Adam Lagner, the 1,900-square-foot room seats around sixty across a proper bar, two-tops and jewel-toned couches, with a small board-game collection and rotating contemporary art for sale on the walls. A customer quoted in the Philadelphia Inquirer described the effect exactly: it feels like a bar without really being a bar.

The hours are what make it work. Ten in the morning until midnight Sunday through Thursday, and until two in the morning on Friday and Saturday — the same closing time as the licensed bars around it. An alcohol-free venue that shuts at nine is not an alternative to a night out; one that runs to two genuinely is.

The drink list is sixteen-plus builds on kava, kratom and botanical teas. The Lemongrass Paloma pairs kava with lemongrass and guava. The Old City Red Eye is the most elaborate, layering kava and kratom with ReAnimator cold brew, oat milk creamer, agave and vanilla syrup. There is an Old Citywide — a nod to Philadelphia's ubiquitous shot-and-beer special — and a Cucumber Basil Cooler for anyone who wants something lighter.

One thing must be stated plainly, because our readers include people in recovery. Kava and kratom contain no alcohol, but both are psychoactive. Kava is a Pacific Island root that produces a mild, calming, sociable effect. Kratom is a Southeast Asian leaf whose effects are stimulant at low doses and sedative at higher ones, and which carries a genuine dependence risk — it is the more serious of the two, and it is not a neutral substitute for a drink. Anyone on medication, pregnant, managing liver health, or in recovery from substance dependence should speak to a doctor before drinking either. For people avoiding alcohol specifically, this is one of the best rooms in the city; for people avoiding everything, the zero-proof cocktail bars are the better route.
venues.pressQuote: It feels like a bar without really being a bar. I like that vibe.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Carissa Kilbury, customer, in The Philadelphia Inquirer

venues.name: On Swann
venues.description: On Swann is a New American restaurant and bar in Hyde Park Village, open since 2016 with a leafy patio and a brunch-to-dinner crowd. Its bartenders build named spirit-free cocktails to order — the Sober Mule (CleanCo Clean G, strawberry-watermelon agave, Giffard orgeat, lemon, ginger beer) and Not Another Spicy Margarita (habanero- and jalapeño-infused Seedlip Notas de Agave, agave, lime) — treating zero-proof drinks with the same care as the full cocktail list.  It is a neighbourhood restaurant rather than a sober venue, which is exactly why it works for the common case — a table of six where one person is not drinking and nobody wants to pick the venue around that.
signatureDrinks: Sober Mule (CleanCo Clean G, strawberry-watermelon agave, Giffard orgeat, lemon, ginger beer)
Not Another Spicy Margarita (jalapeño-infused Seedlip Notas de Agave, agave, lime)
venues.longDescription:
On Swann occupies a corner of Hyde Park Village, the low-rise shopping and dining district in one of Tampa's oldest neighbourhoods, and has been open since 2016. It runs as a New American restaurant and bar with a leafy patio that carries most of the trade — brunch through dinner, a crowd that skews local and regular rather than destination.

Its non-alcoholic drinks are built to order rather than pre-mixed, and they are built on named alcohol-free spirits, which is the distinction that separates a real programme from a courtesy. The Sober Mule uses CleanCo Clean G with a strawberry-watermelon agave, Giffard orgeat, lemon and ginger beer — a drink with enough acid and length to work through a meal rather than collapsing into sweetness after the first sip. Not Another Spicy Margarita is built on Seedlip Notas de Agave infused with habanero and jalapeno, with agave and lime, and the name is doing something useful: it acknowledges that the spicy margarita is the most over-served drink in America and then makes a good one without alcohol anyway.

The useful thing about On Swann for a non-drinker is its ordinariness. It is not a sober venue and does not market itself to that audience; it is a neighbourhood restaurant that happens to take the category seriously, which means it works for the situation most people actually face — a table of six where one person is not drinking and nobody wants to choose the venue around that fact.

Practical notes: it serves lunch and dinner with a gap in the afternoon, adds brunch at weekends from 11am to 2pm, and the patio is the seat worth asking for. Full bar, full wine list — the spirit-free builds are a genuine part of the menu rather than its character.
venues.pressQuote: a destination for Contemporary American cuisine that features a seasonal menu with local flair

venues.name: One Trick Pony
venues.description: One Trick Pony is a Club Street hybrid — a coworking cafe by day that turns into a restaurant and cocktail bar by night — whose 'No-Low & Full ABV' programme is billed as Singapore's first to build the drink around a fully zero-proof base you can optionally spike, rather than treating the non-alcoholic version as an afterthought. The signature list runs alcohol-free by default, with drinks like the Golden Glow and Popcorn Paloma, and cocktails start from S$20. The drinks direction comes from Vijay Mudaliar, founder of Native, one of Asia's 50 Best Bars. The Honeycombers describes the signature list as a fully zero-proof line-up that you can choose to have spiked, which is the inversion that makes this bar worth the trip.
venues.longDescription:
Opened in mid-2026 at 98 Club Street (#03-01), on the corner of Club Street and Ann Siang Road, One Trick Pony is a flexible "third space" that merges coworking, cafe dining, cocktails and community events under one roof. Freelancers and creatives work the room by day from 9am, and come evening it shifts into a dining-and-drinking destination serving sharing plates, bar snacks, beer, cocktails and non-alcoholic drinks.

What sets it apart for zero-proof drinkers is its 'No-Low & Full ABV' cocktail programme, promoted as the first of its kind in Singapore: the signature drinks are conceived as fully alcohol-free builds first, with the option to spike any of them with liquor if you want the boozy version. That makes the non-alcoholic cocktail the base of the drink rather than a stripped-down substitute, and the zero-proof lineup is extensive, headlined by drinks such as the Golden Glow and Popcorn Paloma, with cocktails starting from S$20.

The cocktail direction is led by Vijay Mudaliar, the founder of Native — the acclaimed Singapore bar known for foraged and locally sourced ingredients that has ranked among Asia's 50 Best Bars and been recognised on the World's 50 Best Bars list. His involvement brings a serious, ingredient-driven pedigree to a low-and-no programme in a city better known for high-ABV cocktail culture.

The bar operates Monday to Saturday, from 5pm (4pm on Saturdays) until late, and is closed on Sundays; the coworking space runs weekdays from 9am. Reservations and contact are handled via onetrickpony.sg and Instagram @onetrickpony.sg.

It is worth being precise about why the ordering matters, because plenty of bars claim something similar. At most places the cocktail is designed with alcohol and the alcohol-free version is what survives its removal — thinner, sweeter, and usually shorter. Here the drink is built to work at zero proof and the spirit is the optional addition. The Honeycombers, covering the opening, described the signature menu as a fully zero-proof line-up that you can choose to have spiked if you want the boozy kick. That is the same sentence in the opposite order, and it changes what a non-drinker is handed.

The practical effect is that a mixed table orders from one list. Nobody reads a separate section, nobody waits while a bartender improvises, and the price is the same conversation for everyone. For a group where one person is not drinking — the designated driver, the pregnant friend, the person in recovery, the colleague with an early start — that is the difference between being accommodated and simply being served.

The daytime identity is genuinely separate. From 9am on weekdays the room works as a coworking space for freelancers and creatives, with workshops, vinyl nights, pop-ups and chef collaborations running through the calendar, and it shifts into a restaurant and bar from 5pm (4pm on Saturdays). It is closed Sundays. That dual life is why the drinks list leans the way it does: a room full of people working through the afternoon needs something good to drink that will not end the working day.
venues.pressQuote: Its signature drinks menu features a fully zero-proof line-up created for anyone looking for an alcohol-free sip. Of course, you can always choose to have it spiked with liquor if you’re looking for that boozy kick.

venues.name: One Twenty Three Tavern
venues.description: One Twenty Three Tavern takes its name from its address at 123 Ionia Avenue SW, on the downtown block that also holds Big Mini Putt Club and Max's South Seas Hideaway. It is a straightforward American tavern with a full kitchen, open daily from 11am to 11pm, which makes it one of the more reliably available options in the centre of the city. Its approach to zero-proof drinking is to rebuild the classics rather than invent new ones: the bar makes non-alcoholic versions of the Margarita, the Gin and Soda and the Tom Collins, all three of which were named in the Downtown Grand Rapids guide to the city centre's best non-alcoholic drinks in October 2025.
venues.address: 123 Ionia Ave SW, Grand Rapids, MI 49503
