venues.longDescription:
One Twenty Three Tavern is named for its street number and sits at 123 Ionia Avenue SW, part of the run of downtown venues on Ionia that includes Big Mini Putt Club at number 70 and Max's South Seas Hideaway at number 58. It is a New American tavern with a full kitchen and a broad menu, and its most useful feature for planning purposes is its opening hours: 11am to 11pm every day of the week, without the Sunday or Monday closures that make several of the better zero-proof rooms in this guide unavailable for half the week.

Its non-alcoholic approach is the opposite of Cafe Jazzy Rose's. Where Jazzy Rose builds new drinks out of adaptogens and botanicals, One Twenty Three rebuilds the standards: a non-alcoholic Margarita, a non-alcoholic Gin and Soda and a non-alcoholic Tom Collins, all three named in the Downtown Grand Rapids alliance's October 2025 round-up of the best non-alcoholic drinks downtown. There is an argument for each approach, and the classics route has a specific advantage worth naming — a guest can order a Tom Collins in the same words everyone else at the table is using, and receive something that looks and reads like what the rest of them are drinking. For a lot of people, particularly early in not drinking, that anonymity matters more than novelty does, and a tavern that will build the three most-ordered long drinks without alcohol covers most of what anyone is likely to want. Combined with the daily 11am to 11pm hours and a full food menu, it is a practical default rather than a destination: the place to suggest when the group has not decided, when it is a Sunday, or when somebody needs to eat.
venues.pressQuote: Nonalcoholic versions of the Margarita, Gin & Soda and Tom Collins.

venues.name: Only You
venues.description: Only You occupies the upper floors above The Veil Brewing Co in Norfolk's Chelsea district, and its zero-proof drinks are composed rather than improvised — three named builds that Visit Norfolk's own guide lists alongside the alcoholic menu. The No Coquito uses Lyre's non-alcoholic rum with coconut milk, coconut cream, cinnamon demerara and vanilla; the Ginger Sorrel Sour layers hibiscus tea with ginger-thyme syrup and lemon; and the Free Spirit pairs a honey-miso-yuzu syrup with calamansi and soda. That last one in particular is a savoury, fermented-edge drink of the sort most bars never attempt without alcohol. It sits directly above The Veil Brewing Co, a short walk from Ceremony, which makes Chelsea an easy pairing.
venues.address: 2314 Colonial Ave, 2nd and 3rd Floor, Norfolk, VA 23517
venues.hours: Mon-Tue closed; Wed 5pm-11pm; Thu-Sat 5pm-12am; Sun closed
signatureDrinks: No Coquito - Lyre's N/A rum, coconut milk, coconut cream, cinnamon demerara, vanilla
Ginger Sorrel Sour - hibiscus tea, ginger-thyme syrup, lemon
Free Spirit - honey miso yuzu syrup, calamansi, soda
venues.longDescription:
Only You sits on the second and third floors above The Veil Brewing Co on Colonial Avenue, in the Chelsea district that has become Norfolk's most interesting corner for drinking. It is a cocktail bar in the modern register — small, dark, ingredient-driven — and its non-alcoholic list is properly part of the programme rather than an appendix.

Three drinks are documented by Visit Norfolk, the city's official destination organisation, and the specs are worth reading because they show real construction. The No Coquito builds on Lyre's non-alcoholic rum with coconut milk, coconut cream, cinnamon demerara and vanilla — a genuine attempt at the Puerto Rican Christmas drink rather than a sweet approximation, and one where the NA rum has actual work to do. The Ginger Sorrel Sour uses hibiscus tea as its base with ginger-thyme syrup and lemon, which is a smart choice: hibiscus brings sharp acidity and tannin, the two things most alcohol-free drinks lack.

The Free Spirit is the one that signals a serious bar. Honey, miso, yuzu and calamansi with soda is a savoury, fermented, citrus-driven drink — miso in particular is an ingredient almost no bar reaches for on the non-alcoholic side, because it demands balance rather than sweetness to work. A bar willing to put that on the menu is thinking about what a drink should do, not just how to remove the alcohol from one.

Practically, this is an evening venue with a narrow window: closed Sunday through Tuesday, open from 5pm Wednesday to Saturday, running to midnight at the end of the week. Being above a brewery makes it a natural second stop, and it is a short walk from Ceremony's Baldwin Avenue shop — the two together make Chelsea the best few blocks in Hampton Roads for someone who is not drinking. Buy a bottle in the afternoon, drink something properly made in the evening, all within a few hundred metres. Given how much of Hampton Roads requires a car and a bridge crossing, a walkable pairing like that is worth planning an evening around rather than treating as a coincidence.
venues.pressQuote: Only You: Ginger Sorrel Sour (Hibiscus Tea, Ginger-Thyme Syrup, Lemon); No Coquito (Lyre's N/A Rum, Coconut Milk, Coconut Cream, Cinnamon Demerara, Vanilla); Free Spirit (Honey Miso Yuzu Syrup, Calamansi, Soda).

venues.name: Ooh De Lally
venues.description: Ooh De Lally is a neighbourhood restaurant and bar in Dundee, the walkable Underwood Avenue district north-west of downtown Omaha, and it is the only venue in this guide serving both lunch and dinner every day of the week — 11am to 2pm and then 4pm to 9pm, with a 10am Sunday start. It is listed among the city's spirit-free options in Omaha's curated drinks guide. For a non-drinker the value is coverage rather than complexity: this is the address for a Tuesday lunch or an early Sunday, when the downtown bars are all still locked. Dundee is about three miles north-west of the Old Market, so treat it as its own trip.

venues.longDescription:
Dundee is Omaha's most walkable inner suburb, a short stretch of Underwood Avenue north-west of downtown with independent shops and restaurants along it, and Ooh De Lally is one of its neighbourhood rooms.

It earns its place in this guide on coverage rather than on any single drink, and that is a deliberate editorial choice. A city guide made only of downtown cocktail bars that open at five is not much use to most people most of the time. Somebody who does not drink still eats lunch on a Tuesday, still takes a family out on a Sunday morning, and still wants somewhere within walking distance of home rather than a trip into the Old Market. Ooh De Lally is the entry that answers those.

The hours are the substance of it: 11am to 2pm and 4pm to 9pm Monday through Thursday, to 10pm on Friday and Saturday, and a 10am start on Sunday. Split service, seven days, lunch and dinner both — a pattern no other venue in this guide matches.

The alcohol-free offer is documented by Omaha's curated local drinks guide as part of the city's spirit-free options, and the grade of three is honest about what that means: attested, real, but with no published list and no named build that could be verified for this entry, so none is recorded. In a neighbourhood restaurant that is generally the shape of it — a bartender who will make something decent, without a printed programme behind it.

Dundee is roughly three miles from downtown, so this is a stop in its own right rather than part of an Old Market evening. It pairs naturally with Nite Owl in Blackstone, which is between the two.

A general note for readers using this guide outside a city centre. The venues that end up mattering most to people who have stopped drinking are usually not the destination bars with the cleverest lists; they are the ordinary local rooms that are open when you need them and comfortable to sit in alone. Those places rarely get written up, which is why a curated local guide naming one is worth more than it looks — somebody with local knowledge decided this was where a non-drinker would be looked after.

venues.name: Oquirrh
venues.description: An acclaimed farm-to-table New American restaurant in downtown Salt Lake City, opened in February 2019 by chef Andrew Fuller and his wife Angie (Angelena) Fuller. Named Salt Lake magazine's Best Restaurant of 2025 and a repeat James Beard Award semifinalist for Best Chef: Mountain, it is one of the city's most decorated kitchens. Oquirrh was an early local restaurant to take non-alcoholic drinking seriously — it keeps a stock of NA spirits, including non-alcoholic whiskey, so the bar can build a zero-proof version of essentially any cocktail on its menu, with the same care given to the wine and whisky list.
venues.address: 368 E 100 S, Salt Lake City, UT 84111
venues.longDescription:
Co-owners Andrew and Angie Fuller met working at The Copper Onion and opened Oquirrh — named for the mountain range west of the city, two blocks east of the Eccles Theater — as their long-planned dream restaurant in 2019. The kitchen is built around seasonal, locally sourced ingredients and a frequently changing, precision-driven New American menu.

The Salt Lake Tribune highlighted Oquirrh in its October 2021 "Mocktails find their moment" feature, photographing co-owner Angelena Fuller mixing a no-alcohol cocktail. Rather than a fixed list of named zero-proof drinks, the program works by stocking non-alcoholic spirits and ingredients so the bar can build a faithful alcohol-free version of nearly any cocktail to order.
venues.pressQuote: He's stripping phenomenal raw ingredients down to their elemental potential, building them back up in unexpected and whimsical ways.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Salt Lake magazine, 2025 Best Restaurant feature on chef Andrew Fuller

venues.name: Orangily
venues.description: Orangily is a dedicated non-alcoholic bottle shop on East Main Street in Carmel, opened in the summer of 2022 by sisters Andrea Simpson and Kristin Patrick under its original name, Loren's Alcohol-Free Beverages. It was the first shop of its kind in the Indianapolis metro and remains the anchor of the region's alcohol-free retail scene. The shelves run to alcohol-removed red, white, rosé and sparkling wine, non-alcoholic beer, zero-proof cocktail spirits, ready-to-drink mocktails, bitters, mixers, syrups and kava drinks, with most of the range low-sugar, gluten-free and vegan. There is a small bar and lounge area at the back, and the staff pour generous samples rather than sell blind. The business took the Orangily name in 2025.
venues.address: 5790 E Main St Suite 150, Carmel, IN 46033
venues.longDescription:
Orangily began life as Loren's Alcohol-Free Beverages, opened in the summer of 2022 in Carmel by sisters Andrea Simpson and Kristin Patrick. Both were in their forties when they started it, and both had arrived at the same conclusion independently — that alcohol had stopped agreeing with them and that Indiana had nowhere to buy a decent alternative. At the time the nearest comparable shop was Generation NA in Lafayette, an hour up I-65. The Carmel store opened on East Main Street with a deliberately retail-first layout: shelves organised by category rather than by novelty, and a small tasting bar at the back so that customers could try a de-alcoholised Sauvignon Blanc or a zero-proof agave spirit before committing to a bottle.

The range now covers alcohol-removed red, white, rosé and sparkling wine, non-alcoholic beer, functional and cocktail spirits, ready-to-drink mocktails, kava drinks, bitters, mixers and syrups, with most of the catalogue low-sugar, gluten-free and vegan. The sisters rebranded the business to Orangily in 2025 to widen the framing beyond recovery — Kristin Patrick told Indianapolis Monthly that the customer base splits between people who want an alternative for one evening and people who have stopped drinking entirely, and the old name spoke mainly to the second group. A second Orangily opened in South Broad Ripple in March 2025. The Carmel shop also runs personalised delivery across the north side by text or email, which matters in a metro where the alcohol-free options are otherwise scattered across three counties. Practically, this is the shop to start at if you are new to the category and live north of the city. The staff will talk through which de-alcoholised wines actually resemble wine and which are closer to grape soda, which zero-proof spirits hold up in a spirit-forward build and which need a long mixer to work at all — the kind of triage that saves an expensive mistake. Hours are short and irregular by bar standards, opening at 10am on Monday, midday most other days and 11am on Friday, and closing at 6pm or 7pm, so it is an errand rather than an evening. Note also that the shop sells kava alongside the alcohol-free drinks; kava contains no alcohol but is psychoactive, and it is shelved separately from the wine and beer.
venues.pressQuote: Like many of our clientele, we just found that we weren't bouncing back like we used to.

venues.name: Orangily
venues.description: Orangily's second shop opened in March 2025 on East 54th Street in the SoBro stretch of Meridian-Kessler, next door to United State of Indiana and across from Breadworks. It is the only dedicated non-alcoholic bottle shop inside Marion County — the original Orangily and every other alcohol-free retailer in the metro sits out in Hamilton County. Sisters Andrea Simpson and Kristin Patrick stock alcohol-removed wine, non-alcoholic beer, zero-proof spirits, ready-to-drink mocktails, kava drinks, mixers, bitters and syrups, and keep bottles open for tasting so nobody buys unseen. Afternoon and weekend hours are built around the neighbourhood rather than around a bar crowd, and personalised delivery is available by text.
venues.address: 1051 E 54th St Suite A, Indianapolis, IN 46220
venues.longDescription:
For three years the Indianapolis metro's only alcohol-free bottle shop was in Carmel, which meant a twenty-minute drive up Keystone for anyone living inside the old city. That changed in March 2025, when sisters Andrea Simpson and Kristin Patrick opened a second Orangily at 1051 East 54th Street, in the South Broad Ripple pocket of Meridian-Kessler that everyone here calls SoBro. The storefront faces 54th, sits beside United State of Indiana and looks across at Breadworks, and it is — as of August 2026 — the only shop of its kind inside Marion County.

The stock mirrors the Carmel store: alcohol-removed red, white, rosé and sparkling wine, non-alcoholic beer, zero-proof cocktail spirits, functional and adaptogenic drinks, kava, ready-to-drink mocktails, bitters, mixers and syrups, most of it low-sugar, gluten-free and vegan. What distinguishes both shops is that the sisters keep bottles open and pour samples freely — the category is expensive enough that a bad blind purchase can put someone off non-alcoholic wine for good, and the staff are explicit about which de-alcoholised wines taste like wine and which do not. The business opened in 2022 as Loren's Alcohol-Free Beverages and took the Orangily name in 2025; Patrick has been clear that the rename was about the breadth of the customer base rather than a change of direction. The hours run afternoons and weekends rather than bar hours, and the sisters will deliver across the north side by text or email. Given that Indianapolis lost its only fully alcohol-free bar when Memento Zero Proof closed in 2024, the two Orangily shops now carry most of the weight of the metro's alcohol-free retail. That gives the SoBro store a role beyond retail. It is the one place inside the city where the whole category is physically in front of you at once — the alcohol-removed wines next to the functional drinks next to the zero-proof amari — and where somebody will explain the difference between a spirit distilled without alcohol and a wine that had its alcohol taken out afterwards. For anyone building a home bar rather than going out, that is more useful than another bar with three mocktails on the menu. The 54th Street stretch is walkable: Gallery Pastry Shop is a few blocks west on College Avenue, and Broad Ripple proper, with Union Jack Pub and Cholita, is a mile north up the Monon Trail.
venues.pressQuote: Some people are just looking for alternatives to a cocktail one night; others are giving it up completely.

venues.name: Orapax Restaurant and Bar
venues.description: Orapax is a long-running neighbourhood restaurant and bar in Ghent, the kind of unpretentious room that has fed a Norfolk neighbourhood for decades, and its named alcohol-free drink is the Sparkling Lavender Lemonade — Perrier, fresh lemon juice, lavender syrup, fresh rosemary and blackberries. What earns it a listing is the specification: fresh juice and fresh rosemary rather than a mix, in a venue whose reputation rests on Greek-inflected comfort food rather than its bar. It also keeps genuinely useful hours, open from 11am to 10pm most days, which makes it a rare all-day option. Most of the region's better alcohol-free drinking hides behind 5pm bar openings, so an all-day kitchen matters.
signatureDrinks: Sparkling Lavender Lemonade - Perrier, fresh lemon juice, lavender syrup, fresh rosemary, blackberries
venues.longDescription:
Orapax has been a fixture on Redgate Avenue in Ghent for decades — a neighbourhood restaurant and bar known for Greek-inflected comfort cooking rather than for a drinks programme. That context is what makes its alcohol-free drink worth noting.

The Sparkling Lavender Lemonade is specified as Perrier, fresh lemon juice, lavender syrup, fresh rosemary and blackberries. Read that again as a working bartender would: fresh lemon juice rather than a sour mix, and fresh rosemary rather than an extract. Those two choices cost time and money on every single serve, and they are the first things a kitchen cuts when a drink is not taken seriously. A neighbourhood restaurant that squeezes lemons for its non-alcoholic option is telling you something about how the whole place is run.

The build itself is sound. Lavender and rosemary together are aromatic and slightly resinous, blackberry adds depth and colour, and the Perrier keeps it dry rather than syrupy. It is a drink that survives a full meal, which is more than can be said for most sweet mocktails poured alongside heavy food.

The hours are the practical advantage and the reason Orapax appears here rather than a flashier room: 11am to 10pm Monday through Friday, from noon on Saturday and 2pm on Sunday. Hampton Roads' better alcohol-free options skew heavily to evening bars with narrow windows — Only You opens at 5pm four days a week, Gershwin's at 5pm, Press 626 closes two days — so an all-day neighbourhood restaurant fills a real gap for anyone who wants lunch, an afternoon, or an early dinner without a drink. It is also a room where nobody will look twice at what you ordered, which after a certain number of explanations is worth as much as the drink.
venues.pressQuote: Orapax: "Sparkling Lavender Lemonade" (Perrier sparkling water, fresh lemon juice, lavender syrup, fresh rosemary, blackberries).

venues.name: Oren
venues.description: Oren is a Brookside restaurant in Tulsa with one of the longest-running commitments to zero-proof drinking in the city — it was serving a Seedlip Spice 94 build called The Seven Sisters back when almost no bar in Oklahoma stocked a non-alcoholic spirit at all. The current entry is the Maiden Manhattan: cold brew coffee, cranberry, lemon, demerara and Angostura bitters, a stirred, dark, genuinely bitter drink built to sit beside food rather than to refresh. Dinner runs Wednesday to Sunday from 5pm, with weekend brunch from 10am, and the kitchen is among the more ambitious in the metro.
venues.address: 3509 S Peoria Ave Suite 161, Tulsa, OK 74105
signatureDrinks: Maiden Manhattan — cold brew coffee, cranberry, lemon, demerara, Angostura bitters
venues.longDescription:
Oren, on South Peoria in Brookside, has been paying attention to this category longer than anywhere else in Tulsa. When the local drinks writing first made the case for zero-proof cocktails in the city, Oren was already pouring The Seven Sisters, built on Seedlip Spice 94 — at a point when a non-alcoholic distilled spirit on an Oklahoma back bar was close to unheard of.

The drink the restaurant is known for now is the Maiden Manhattan, and it is an unusually grown-up piece of work. Cold brew coffee provides the dark, roasted backbone that whiskey would otherwise give; cranberry supplies tannic astringency; lemon and demerara balance it; and Angostura bitters finish it the way they would finish the original. It is stirred rather than shaken in character — dense, bitter and slow — which is exactly what a manhattan drinker misses when they stop drinking, and almost the opposite of what most mocktail menus offer.

That naming is doing something too. Calling it a Maiden Manhattan rather than inventing a fruit-themed name places it as a version of a classic, which is how someone ordering it wants to think about it.

Tulsa Remote named the drink in its January 2025 ranking of the city's best mocktails; the earlier Seedlip build is documented in local drinks coverage from 2020, which is what establishes the length of the commitment rather than the currency of that specific drink.

The restaurant keeps restaurant hours and they are tight: closed Monday and Tuesday entirely, dinner from 5pm Wednesday through Friday, and weekend service that adds brunch from 10am. Sunday evening service is short, 5:30pm to 7:30pm. Book ahead.

A note on the wider point Oren illustrates. The venues in this directory that do the best alcohol-free work are rarely the ones that set out to serve non-drinkers; they are the ones with the deepest technique, which then applies that technique to the problem. A kitchen that already makes its own demerara syrup and keeps good cold brew has most of a Maiden Manhattan on hand before anyone asks for it. That is why restaurants with serious bar programmes keep outperforming venues that advertise mocktails.
venues.pressQuote: Maiden Manhattan: Cold brew coffee, cranberry, lemon, demerara, Angostura bitters

venues.name: Origin Bar
venues.description: Origin Bar is the flagship cocktail lounge at Shangri-La Singapore, where Director of Beverage Adam Bursik treats no- and low-ABV drinks as 'a permanent shift' rather than a trend, weaving them throughout the list instead of quarantining them in a separate section. The bar designs each drink around flavour and experience first, not alcohol level, so lighter builds like the Bubble Club - distilled guava lychee, umeshu, vitamin C cordial and water - sit alongside its full-strength cocktails as fully developed offerings. Bursik favours year-round moderation and 'discovery, not restriction' over strict abstinence.
venues.address: Shangri-La Singapore, Tower Wing, Lobby Level, 22 Orange Grove Road, Singapore 258350
signatureDrinks: Bubble Club - distilled guava lychee, umeshu, vitamin C cordial and water (low-ABV; dry, aromatic and complex)
venues.longDescription:
Origin Bar is the signature cocktail bar of the Shangri-La Singapore, tucked into the Tower Wing lobby at 22 Orange Grove Road in the Orchard/Tanglin district. It was ranked No. 32 on Asia's 50 Best Bars 2024, and its programme is led by Director of Beverage Adam Bursik, a Slovakia-raised bartender who has steered the room through successive concept-driven menus drawing on Singapore's tropical produce, neighbourhoods and rituals.

What makes the no/low angle real here is that it is a design principle rather than a token afterthought. Bursik describes low- and no-alcohol cocktails as 'a permanent shift,' and says the team builds 'our menu around flavour and experience first, not alcohol level.' Rather than a separate zero-proof chapter, lighter and alcohol-free options are integrated across the list - a lower-intervention approach that suits guests practising what Bursik calls mindful drinking, or 'discovery, not restriction.'

The emblematic lighter pour is the Bubble Club, a dry, aromatic and complex build of distilled guava lychee, umeshu, vitamin C cordial and water. Because it leans on house distillates and a splash of umeshu, it reads as a genuinely low-ABV cocktail rather than a sugary mocktail - the through-line of Origin's philosophy that a drink's interest should not depend on its proof.

The setting is a polished five-star hotel lounge with a smart-casual dress code, open nightly from 5:30pm to 1:00am. Menus rotate on a concept basis (recent editions include an 18-drink 'Point of View' collection), so the exact no/low pours change - but the commitment to weaving lighter options throughout is a standing feature of the programme.
venues.pressQuote: We design our menu around flavour and experience first, not alcohol level.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Adam Bursik, Director of Beverage, Origin Bar

venues.name: The Original Nite Cap
venues.description: The Original Nite Cap is an intimate second-floor speakeasy above Pulcinella! in New Orleans' Seventh Ward, revived in 2024 by burlesque performer Bella Blue, her husband Andrew Principe, and partner JD Solomon. It takes its name from a mid-century Nite Cap whose original signage was found during renovation. With roughly 14 bar seats plus tables, it hosts burlesque, drag, comedy, and live music alongside a craft cocktail and Italian wine program. Its zero-proof list is fully built out with named drinks rather than afterthoughts: the Corset Strings (Lyre's NA dark cane, chai cordial, lemon, soda, NA bitters), the Stage Kitten (NA gin, hibiscus cordial, lime, NA bubbles), the Show Stopper (cold brew, coffee demerara, NA gin, foam), and Dazzle 'Em (NA rum, lime, ginger syrup, ginger beer).
venues.address: 1300 St Bernard Ave, New Orleans, LA 70116
venues.longDescription:
The Original Nite Cap is a second-floor speakeasy above Pulcinella! at 1300 St Bernard Avenue in the Seventh Ward, and it is a revival rather than a theme. The first Nite Cap was run in the 1960s by Big Chief Alfred Doucette and closed in the 1980s; the original signage turned up during renovation and the name came back with it. It reopened in 2024 under burlesque performer Bella Blue, her husband Andrew Principe and partner JD Solomon, with Shea Vidrine in the kitchen, and it runs dinner-and-show packages Thursday to Saturday. The food is Italian-leaning cabaret fare — a spiced house nut mix at $8, house giardiniera at $7, fried stuffed olives at $16, smoked Gulf fish dip at $16, the Nite Cap burger at $18 with Calabrian chilli aioli and olive salad, tiramisu at $12.

The zero-proof drinks sit on the Showgirl Sips card under a heading that says exactly that: ZERO PROOF. Four of them, $12 or $13, against a room where the main event is a burlesque show — which matters, because a burlesque audience sits for a couple of hours holding a drink, and holding a soda for two hours is a different experience from holding a cocktail. Show Stopper is $13 and coffee-based, using Lyre's Coffee Original with cold brew, coffee demerara and a foam, which is the one to order if you want to stay sharp through a late show. Dazzle 'Em is $13 on Almave non-alcoholic blanco with Lyre's triple sec, basil simple syrup and lime. Stage Kitten at $12 is a non-alcoholic gin with hibiscus cordial, lime and soda. Corset Strings at $12 uses Lyre's dark cane spirit with a chai tea cordial, soda and non-alcoholic aromatic bitters. The bar card adds Athletic non-alcoholic beer at $6 and a bottled Phony Negroni at $10. One practical note: the venue has no website of its own — everything lives on the production company's site under an originalnitecap page, so search for that rather than the bar's name alone.
venues.pressQuote: Mocktails move the industry forward in a way that keeps us together.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Fox Monroe, Original Nite Cap operations manager

venues.name: Oriole
venues.description: Oriole is chef Noah Sandoval's two-Michelin-starred tasting-menu restaurant in the West Loop, reached through an unmarked back-alley door and a freight elevator, and it is one of the few rooms at that level in Chicago to publish a spirit-free pairing as a first-class option. The restaurant lists three pairings against its $325 tasting menu - spirit free, standard and reserve - with wine director Emily Rosenfeld curating the wine flights and bar director Maddie Balintona building the spirit-free one from creative non-alcoholic beverages made to complement the menu course by course. Cocktails in the dining room are created by Balintona; the wine list, curated by Rosenfeld, is old-world in emphasis with a focus on white wines. Service runs Tuesday to Saturday evenings only.
venues.longDescription:
Oriole sits behind an all-but-unmarked door in a back alley off West Walnut Street in the West Loop; guests are collected there, put into a freight elevator with a drink in hand, and delivered into a dining room that seats a single service a night. Chef Noah Sandoval's cooking is deliberately minimalist in construction and maximalist in sourcing - Hokkaido uni with tiger prawn, morita chilli and maple, Maine lobster with almond milk and geranium custard - and the restaurant has held two MICHELIN stars for years. The tasting menu is $325.

What sets it apart for a non-drinker is that the restaurant offers three pairings and names them equally: spirit free, standard and reserve. Wine director Emily Rosenfeld curates the standard flight to match the courses and a reserve flight built from older vintages, esteemed producers and rarer bottles. Bar director Maddie Balintona builds the spirit-free pairing, which the restaurant describes as featuring creative, non-alcoholic beverages made to perfectly complement the menu. Balintona also creates the cocktails served in the dining room, so the same person is responsible for both the alcoholic and the alcohol-free drinks - the arrangement that tends to produce serious zero-proof programmes rather than juice substitutions. The wine list itself is old-world inspired with a focus on white wines, and there is a $50-per-bottle corkage policy with a two-bottle limit for guests bringing something of their own. Because the pairing changes with the menu, the restaurant does not publish the individual spirit-free drinks in advance; the commitment that is published is structural, and at this level of dining that structure - a non-alcoholic flight offered by name at the point of booking rather than requested as a favour - is the thing that matters. Service is Tuesday to Saturday from 5pm, closed Sunday and Monday.
venues.pressQuote: Upon arrival, guests are escorted into a freight elevator and given a drink before the door opens to reveal the dining room.

venues.name: Osaka Miami
venues.description: Osaka Miami is the Brickell Bay Drive outpost of the Nikkei restaurant group, cooking the Japanese-Peruvian hybrid cuisine the brand built in Lima. Its non-alcoholic list runs to four named builds and is made from the kitchen's own infusions and cordials rather than from bottled substitutes: the Coco Bang combines coconut miso, genmaicha tea, kumquat and orange blossom; the Yuzu Tea pairs a sencha infusion with pineapple and yuzu foam; the OSK Fresh brings tangerine cordial, rosemary and soda; and the Blossom Lemonade blends sakura tea, watermelon cordial and lime. The room serves lunch Tuesday through Friday and Sunday, dinner nightly, and runs to midnight Thursday through Saturday. Secret Miami named it first among fifteen Miami zero-proof rooms in December 2025.

venues.longDescription:
Osaka Miami sits at 1300 Brickell Bay Drive, on the waterfront edge of Brickell, and is the Miami location of the Osaka Nikkei group that made its name in Lima. Nikkei cooking is the century-old Japanese-Peruvian hybrid that came out of Japanese immigration to Peru, and the restaurant applies the same logic behind the bar: Japanese tea and citrus meeting Peruvian produce and technique. Service is split, with lunch from 1pm to 3pm Tuesday through Friday, a Sunday midday service until 4pm, and dinner every night, running to midnight Thursday through Saturday.

The alcohol-free list is the reason the restaurant belongs in this catalogue, and it is unusually specific for a Brickell dining room. The Coco Bang is a savoury-sweet build of coconut miso, genmaicha tea, kumquat and a lift of orange blossom. The Yuzu Tea pairs a sencha infusion with pineapple and a yuzu foam. The OSK Fresh is the driest of the four, working tangerine cordial and rosemary over soda. The Blossom Lemonade blends sakura tea with watermelon cordial and lime. All four are made in-house from teas, cordials and infusions the kitchen already runs, rather than from off-the-shelf non-alcoholic spirits, which is why no brand is attached to this entry. Secret Miami placed Osaka at the top of its December 2025 round-up of fifteen Miami rooms serving zero-proof drinks and described the list as blending Japanese-inspired flavours with tropical flair. An older Miami New Times survey from January 2024 recorded a different four-drink line-up at the same restaurant — The Only Tonic, Chicha Jamaica, Osaka Fresh and Barley & Honey — which suggests the menu is refreshed periodically and that a caller should confirm the current list. The room sits on the waterfront edge of Brickell Bay Drive, a short distance from Rosa Sky on SW 8th Street and ADRIFT Mare on Brickell Avenue, both already carried in this catalogue, which makes the neighbourhood one of the denser clusters of documented alcohol-free drinking in Miami. Osaka takes bookings on (786) 627-4800 and posts as @osakanikkei.miami.
venues.pressQuote: This Nikkei gem has you covered with multiple zero-proof offerings blending Japanese-inspired flavors and tropical flair.

venues.name: Osito's Tap
venues.description: Osito's Tap is a speakeasy-inspired bar in the heart of Little Village, entered through Moreno's Liquors, the Moreno family's three-generation shop on South Ridgeway Avenue, and run by Mike Moreno Jr. The bar brings a modern Latinx sensibility to a room that draws on the neighborhood's early-1900s Bohemian tavern history, and its program is built around education in tequila and mezcal. Choose Chicago, the city's official tourism body, lists it among the Chicago bars with the best mocktails, describing a non-alcoholic list that leans on classic Mexican flavors and ingredients; Block Club Chicago has separately documented zero-proof drinks made with carrot juice, grapefruit juice, apricot cinnamon syrup and ginger beer. The kitchen serves botanas and entrees until late.
venues.longDescription:
Osito's Tap is reached through Moreno's Liquors on South Ridgeway Avenue, the bottle shop the Moreno family has run in Little Village across three generations, and is operated by Mike Moreno Jr. The bar describes itself as a speakeasy-inspired room highlighting craft spirits, beer and cocktails with a modern Latinx flair, drawing on the Bohemian tavern culture that filled this part of the West Side in the early 1900s. Its reputation rests on agave: the program is explicitly educational about tequila and mezcal, and the bar keeps a separate spirits menu alongside the cocktail, michelada and draft lists. Food runs to botanas, entrees and desserts from a kitchen that stays open until 10 or 11pm depending on the night.

The non-alcoholic side of the program is documented by two independent Chicago sources rather than by a published menu, because the bar posts its drinks as images rather than text. Choose Chicago, the city's official destination marketing organization, includes Osito's Tap in its guide to Chicago bars with great mocktails and describes a list that shakes up drinks incorporating classic Mexican flavors and ingredients - the same agave-adjacent vocabulary the rest of the bar works in. Block Club Chicago, listing the bar in its Dry January round-up, described non-alcoholic cocktails made with carrot juice, grapefruit juice, apricot cinnamon syrup and ginger beer. Because the drink names are not published anywhere we could verify, none are listed above; ask at the bar rather than arriving with a specific order in mind. The value of the entry is geographic as much as anything - Little Village is one of the largest Mexican-American neighbourhoods in the United States and had no zero-proof listing in this directory before now, and Osito's is open until midnight midweek and 1am at weekends. The Illinois state tourism site lists the bar as well, and Osito's own site sets out separate cocktail, michelada, wine and draft menus alongside a dedicated spirits list, with the kitchen running botanas, entrees and desserts on its own shorter hours. Anyone visiting for the non-alcoholic drinks specifically should expect them to be made to order rather than picked off a printed list.
venues.pressQuote: This popular Little Village bar and restaurant shakes up mocktails that incorporate classic Mexican flavors and ingredients.

venues.name: Other Half Brewing
venues.description: Other Half Brewing's Philadelphia taproom on Canal Street prints an "NA Beverages" section directly on its live draft list, which is rarer among breweries than it should be. The anchor is All In, Other Half's own non-alcoholic hazy IPA at under 0.5% ABV — hopped with Citra, Simcoe and Centennial, giving notes of peach candy, ripe grapefruit and mango. That it is brewed in-house rather than bought in matters: this is a brewery known nationally for hop-forward beer applying that expertise to a beer with the alcohol taken out. Alongside it the taproom pours St. Agrestis Phony White Negroni and Phony Mezcal Negroni. The room runs to eleven on Friday and Saturday.
signatureDrinks: All In (0.5% ABV) — Other Half's own non-alcoholic hazy IPA, hopped with Citra, Simcoe and Centennial: peach candy, ripe grapefruit, mango
St. Agrestis Phony White Negroni — alcohol-free bottled aperitif
St. Agrestis Phony Mezcal Negroni — alcohol-free bottled aperitif
venues.longDescription:
Other Half Brewing built its reputation in Brooklyn on hazy, aggressively hopped IPAs, and its Philadelphia taproom on Canal Street in Fishtown pours the same range. What earns it a place in this directory is a heading on the live draft list: "NA Beverages", printed alongside the IPAs, lagers and stouts rather than tucked into a footnote.

The anchor is All In, and the important fact about it is that Other Half brews it themselves. Most breweries that offer a non-alcoholic option buy in someone else's — usually Athletic — which is a perfectly good answer but tells you nothing about whether the brewery cares. Brewing your own means committing equipment, tank time and recipe development to it. All In is a hazy IPA under 0.5% ABV, hopped with Citra, Simcoe and Centennial, and the taproom's own description promises peach candy, ripe grapefruit and mango. Those are three of the most-used hops in modern American IPA, and the flavours listed are exactly what you would expect from a full-strength beer in the same style, which is the point the brewery is making.

Alcohol is doing more work in a beer than most drinkers realise — it carries aroma, adds body, and provides the faint sweetness that balances hop bitterness. Removing it and still landing a beer that reads as a hazy IPA is a genuine technical achievement, and it is why a brewery-made non-alcoholic beer usually beats a contract-brewed one.

Alongside the beer, the taproom stocks St. Agrestis's Phony White Negroni and Phony Mezcal Negroni — bottled, alcohol-free, properly bitter aperitifs from a Brooklyn producer, which cover anyone who does not want a beer at all.

The hours make it a real evening venue: four in the afternoon to ten midweek, opening at noon on Friday and eleven at weekends and running to eleven at night. A taproom is a good format for a mixed group, since ordering by the glass at a counter means nobody is buying rounds and nobody is counting.
venues.pressQuote: Other Half Brewing Company, a Brooklyn-based craft beer brewer and distributor, is slated to move into the space where Goose Island Brewery formerly operated at 1002 Canal St. in Fishtown

venues.name: Othership Adelaide
venues.description: Othership Adelaide is an entirely alcohol-free sauna, ice bath and social club in Toronto's Fashion District, just off King Street West. Toronto Life has singled it out as a deliberate booze-free alternative to the King West bar scene, noting its late hours are meant to give the neighbourhood's nightlife crowd somewhere else to gather. The tea lounge serves Clover Botanicals Adaptogenic Tea, built around valerian root and ashwagandha — complimentary to guests in the space, or available to buy on its own for $13.
venues.address: 425 Adelaide St W, Toronto, ON M5V 3C1, Canada
signatureDrinks: Clover Botanicals Adaptogenic Tea — valerian root and ashwagandha (complimentary in the space; $13 to purchase)
venues.longDescription:
Othership Adelaide is an entirely alcohol-free sauna, ice bath and social club at 425 Adelaide St W in Toronto's Fashion District, just off King Street West. The circuit centers on what the venue calls Toronto's largest performance sauna, built from Western Red Cedar and heated to an average of 75–85°C, paired with eight individual cold-plunge ice baths kept between 0°C and 4°C. Non-gendered changing stalls and lockers, showers with body wash provided, and a shared social commons round out the space, which Othership describes as designed "to soothe the senses, from cedar-infused air to warm ambient lighting."

The club is booze-free by design rather than as an afterthought — no alcohol is served or permitted on site. Toronto Life featured Othership as a purpose-built answer to the King West bar scene, writing that it is "entirely booze free, and its late hours are intended to give King Street's nightlife revellers an alternative space to congregate." In practice that means staying open past 11pm most nights of the week — later than many of the bars just down the block.

Guests wind down in the tea lounge with Clover Botanicals Adaptogenic Tea, a blend built around valerian root and ashwagandha. It's complimentary to anyone using the space, and also sold on its own for $13, giving Othership a specific, ingredient-documented non-alcoholic pour rather than a generic herbal-tea afterthought.
venues.pressQuote: Othership is entirely booze free, and its late hours are intended to give King Street's nightlife revellers an alternative space to congregate.

venues.longDescription:
Otto's High Dive opened in Orlando's Milk District on December 6, 2022, founded by Giovanni Fernandez, Justin Levaughn, Sean Pagan, and Chris Munro. The concept traces back to Fernandez's grandfather Otto, who ran a neighborhood bar in Manzanillo, Cuba, during the 1950s height of the country's cocktail renaissance -- the inspiration behind a Cuban-Floridian rum program built around cantinero (bar director) Justin Levaughn: Cuba Libre on tap, daiquiris by the pitcher, and a build-your-own Ti Punch kit made with a choice of Rhum JM Volcanique or Clement Canne Bleue.

The bar earned a Michelin Bib Gourmand in 2023 for its food menu of oysters, chicken mojo, and short rib ropa vieja, a rating it has retained every year since, and USA Today named it one of the '10 Best New Restaurants in the US' in January 2024. That same year, Levaughn personally received the Michelin Guide Florida award for Exceptional Cocktails. As of the bar's spring 2026 printed menu, the kitchen is led by head chef Justice Placeres.

That same craft extends to the bar's seven-drink Mocktails section, priced at $12 each (the same as the cocktails and daiquiris) and printed right alongside them on the current menu: Coqui (pandan leaf, Granny Smith apple, citrus, coconut, pineapple), Coco Loso (coconut milk, maduro cordial, pineapple, coconut balsamic, cinnamon), Pajarito (red tea, orange blossom, rose hip, verjus, coconut balsamic), Sans Hattan (orange blossom tea, angostura, tobacco), Gold Doubloon (Florida tea, lúcuma, verjus, glycerin, lactic acid), Y Que Fue (passionfruit, red miso, aloe, mango sangrita, coconut), and Agua de Pipa (fresh coconut water).

'Otto's mocktails don't compromise. They seduce,' one write-up of the bar's program noted, and the zero-proof drinks are built with the same lacto-fermented, verjus-driven techniques as the rum cocktails around them rather than treated as an afterthought.
venues.pressQuote: Otto's mocktails don't compromise. They seduce.

venues.name: Outta the Blue
venues.description: Outta the Blue is a beach- and tiki-themed cafe and bar in Leawood's Park Place development, opened in June 2021 as a concept from the Made in KC group with co-owner Keith Bradley. The room commits hard to the theme, down to two live Great King palm trees imported from San Diego, and runs as a genuine all-day venue from 7am daily. Its non-alcoholic offering comes from two directions. A printed Mocktails menu holds tiki classics made without spirits — a Blue Hawaiian and a Painkiller on lime, coconut cream and pineapple juice, a blended Piña Colada, a Strawberry Daiquiri on strawberry purée and turbinado, and a Mojito. Separately, the cafe side lists non-alcoholic Signature Drinks including the Rising Tide coconut caramel latte, the Golden Hour honey orgeat latte and the Beach Break hibiscus lemonade, all $5 during a cafe happy hour Monday to Thursday, 2pm to 5pm. Note that Outta the Blue is not an alcohol-free venue: it also runs a full bar with spirits, a natural-leaning wine list and local beer.

venues.longDescription:
Outta the Blue is a beach cafe in the Park Place development in Leawood, Kansas, opened in June 2021 as a concept from the Made in KC group. Co-owner Keith Bradley set out to make it feel like somewhere else entirely — when you walk in, he said at opening, you don't feel like you're in Kansas City at all — and the room commits, down to two live Great King palm trees imported from San Diego. It runs as a genuine all-day venue rather than a bar with daytime hours, opening at 7am every day and closing at 10pm midweek, 11pm on Friday and Saturday and 6pm on Sundays. Mornings are coffee, breakfast biscuits at $9, quiches at $7, burritos at $9 and pastries; the counter also does cold-pressed juices and grab-and-go salads and sandwiches.

The non-alcoholic side is unusually broad because it comes at the drinker from two directions. There is a printed Mocktails menu of tiki and tropical classics made without spirits — a Blue Hawaiian and a Painkiller both built on lime, coconut cream and pineapple juice with blue curaçao syrup, a blended Piña Colada, a Strawberry Daiquiri on strawberry purée and turbinado, and a Mojito with mint and club soda. Separately there is a list of non-alcoholic Signature Drinks from the cafe side that are worth as much attention: Rising Tide is a coconut caramel latte, Golden Hour a honey orgeat latte, Beach Break a hibiscus lemonade, Matcha Mist a strawberry matcha, and White Cap a salted caramel and white mocha latte. Those signature drinks drop to $5 during a cafe happy hour, Monday to Thursday from 2pm to 5pm. One thing to be clear about: Outta the Blue is not an alcohol-free venue. It runs a full bar with spirits, a wine list leaning natural and organic, and local beers, and holds a separate bar happy hour from 4pm. The zero-proof menu is real and properly made — but you will be ordering it in a room where most people are drinking.
venues.pressQuote: As part of their beach-forward cocktail menu, Outta the Blue offers seven different N/A plays on classic tropical and tiki drinks like a mojito, daiquiri, painkiller, blue Hawaiian and a Pina Colada.

venues.name: Overlook Lounge
venues.description: Overlook Lounge, Aperitifs & Spirits is an opulent European-glamour cocktail lounge inside Wynn Las Vegas, set in an anchor space overlooking the resort's Lake of Dreams waterfall and lush atrium (in the former Parasol Up location, redesigned by Wynn's Todd-Avery Lenahan with jewel tones, crystal chandeliers and vintage European furnishings). The drink program comes from Wynn master mixologist Mariena Mercer Boarini, a 2026 James Beard Award semifinalist (and finalist) for Outstanding Professional in Cocktail Service. The menu is built around five spritzes, five reinterpreted classics, and a standing trio of named zero-proof mocktails, with every drink named for iconic figures from fashion, film, history and mythology. The three alcohol-free options are the Ava (a zero-proof Italian orange spritz), the Ruby (a sparkling pomegranate and Pompelmo spritz), and the Wilde (an exotic sparkling yuzu lemonade), so non-drinkers get crafted, on-menu choices rather than an afterthought. The lounge is open daily, seats first-come, first-served (no reservations), and requires upscale resort attire.

venues.longDescription:
Overlook Lounge debuted at Wynn Las Vegas as a reimagining of the resort's former Parasol Up bar, transformed by Wynn Design & Development president and chief creative officer Todd-Avery Lenahan into a jewel-toned, "equal parts opulent and cozy" room evoking an upscale socialite's living room. Perched above the Lake of Dreams, it pairs crystal chandeliers and vintage European furnishings with sweeping views of the resort atrium.

The cocktail list is the work of Wynn master mixologist Mariena Mercer Boarini, named a 2026 James Beard Award semifinalist and finalist for Outstanding Professional in Cocktail Service, who has shaped more than 30 cocktail programs across Wynn and Encore. The Overlook menu centers on five aperitif-driven spritzes and five reworked classics, plus three deliberately crafted alcohol-free mocktails: the Ava (zero-proof Italian orange spritz), the Ruby (sparkling pomegranate and Pompelmo spritz), and the Wilde (exotic sparkling yuzu lemonade). The dedicated, named zero-proof options make it a comfortable stop for sober and sober-curious guests looking for something more elevated than a soda water on the Strip.
venues.pressQuote: The trio of zero-proof options includes the Ava, an Italian orange spritz; the Ruby, a sparkling pomegranate and Pompelmo spritz; and the Wilde, an exotic sparkling yuzu lemonade.

venues.name: Pacific Cocktail Haven (PCH)
venues.description: Pacific Cocktail Haven, known as PCH, is a cocktail bar at 550 Sutter Street in Union Square, opened in 2016 by bartender Kevin Diedrich and rebuilt at its current address in March 2022 after a fire destroyed the original room. The menu is broken out by base spirit and carries a standing non-alcoholic section, and bartenders will build a spirit-free version of nearly anything else on the list. Named zero-proof pours include Raisin da Roof (Lyre's non-alcoholic gin and dry aperitif, raisin, orange, apple cider vinegar), Karl the POG (Seedlip Spice, house passionfruit-orange-guava, orgeat, citrus, ginger beer) and Cactus Makes Perfect (nopales water, jicama, sakura). PCH has won Best American Cocktail Bar at the Tales of the Cocktail Spirited Awards and reached No. 16 on North America's 50 Best Bars in 2025.

venues.longDescription:
Pacific Cocktail Haven, universally shortened to PCH, opened in 2016 under bartender Kevin Diedrich and has become one of the most decorated bars in the United States. Its drinks lean on Asian-Pacific ingredients that reflect Diedrich's Filipino heritage, and the room draws a mix of industry regulars and Union Square visitors. In February 2021 a fire destroyed the original space; the bar reopened in March 2022 at 550 Sutter Street, a few doors from where it started. It has won Best American Cocktail Bar at the Tales of the Cocktail Spirited Awards, appears regularly on North America's 50 Best Bars, and climbed to No. 16 on that list in 2025. It opens at 5pm Monday to Saturday and is closed Sundays.

The menu is organised by base spirit, with non-alcoholic drinks given their own standing section rather than a line at the bottom, and the bar will build a spirit-free version of nearly anything else on the list on request — which in a room this decorated is the more valuable offer, because it means a non-drinker is not restricted to three choices. Named zero-proof pours currently include Raisin da Roof, built on Lyre's non-alcoholic gin and Lyre's dry aperitif with raisin, orange and apple cider vinegar; Karl the POG, which combines Seedlip Spice with the bar's house passionfruit-orange-guava blend, orgeat, citrus and ginger beer; and Cactus Makes Perfect, made with nopales water, jicama and sakura. The vinegar in the first and the ginger beer in the second are doing the same job — supplying the bite and length that alcohol normally provides — and they are the reason these read as cocktails rather than as juice. The Infatuation, in its guide to drinking in San Francisco without alcohol, singled the bar out: "Pacific Cocktail Haven dedicates a portion of their menu to non-alcoholic options, including a N/A gin-based concoction with raisins, orange, and apple cider vinegar."
venues.pressQuote: Pacific Cocktail Haven dedicates a portion of their menu to non-alcoholic options, including a N/A gin-based concoction with raisins, orange, and apple cider vinegar.

venues.name: Pacific Rootz Kava Lounge
venues.description: A Polynesian-owned kava lounge in Orlando's MetroWest neighborhood, billed as the city's first true kava bar. Tongan and Fijian kava is served the traditional way - by the shell or the gallon - in a room decorated with island art and set to reggae, with a free pool table and regular open-mic nights. (Alcohol-free; kava is a traditional, mildly psychoactive Pacific Island beverage.)
venues.address: 6996 Piazza Grande Ave Ste 103, Orlando, FL 32835
signatureDrinks: Big Kahuna (specialty kava cup; a customer-favorite per reviews)
venues.longDescription:
Owned and operated by native Pacific Islanders, Pacific Rootz calls itself Orlando's '1st and ONLY true Kava Bar.' At 6996 Piazza Grande Ave in MetroWest, the lounge leans into an authentic island-retreat feel - original Pacific-island art and history on the walls, poly reggae on the speakers, and traditional Tongan and Fijian kava prepared and served the customary way, by the shell or by the gallon. Regulars also single out the 'Big Kahuna,' a specialty cup that has built its own following alongside the shell-and-gallon traditionalists.

Happy hour runs 6-8pm with buy-one-get-one cups, there's a free pool table, and the room fills up after 8pm most nights; the lounge also hosts open-mic nights for the neighborhood's creative crowd.

As with any kava bar, Pacific Rootz is alcohol-free by design but not substance-free - alongside its Tongan and Fijian kava, the lounge also pours kratom drinks (a single blend of all three strains), another traditional, mildly psychoactive botanical distinct from a strictly caffeine-only sober space. It's open evenings, Monday-Friday 6pm-2am and weekends 7pm-2am.

venues.name: Pacific Standard
venues.description: Pacific Standard is the ground-floor cocktail bar of the KEX Portland hotel in the Central Eastside, opened in October 2022 by acclaimed bartender Jeffrey Morgenthaler (formerly of Clyde Common) and partner Benjamin Amberg. The menu is built around radical transparency: the ABV of every drink is printed on the menu, running from 0% all the way to a 39% House Old Fashioned, so guests can make informed choices. A dedicated "Alcohol-Free Cocktails" section anchors the non-alcoholic program, alongside a "Low-Proof Cocktails on Draft" list and zero-proof beverages including kombucha, Leitz "Eins Zwei Zero" wine, and BERO non-alcoholic beer. The bar pours its own house-made non-alcoholic spirit and uses Wilderton Lustre in zero-proof cocktails like the Tiger Balm (pineapple, lime) and the Wandering Path (grapefruit, lemon, egg white). Food spans oysters, steak frites, and Morgenthaler's famed chocolate chip cookies.
venues.address: 100 NE Martin Luther King Jr Blvd, Portland, OR 97232
signatureDrinks: Tiger Balm (NA: housemade non-alcoholic spirit, Wilderton Lustre, pineapple, lime — 0% ABV)
Wandering Path (NA: Pathfinder non-alcoholic hemp spirit, grapefruit, lemon, egg white — 0% ABV)
venues.longDescription:
Pacific Standard is the ground-floor bar of the KEX hotel at 100 NE Martin Luther King Jr Boulevard in the Central Eastside, opened by Jeffrey Morgenthaler and Benjamin Amberg, both previously of Clyde Common. The bar describes itself as a modern West Coast drinking and dining hall that celebrates the hotel bar by aiming to be a living room for the city — a destination for international travellers, but also a haunt for local regulars. Travel Oregon has described Morgenthaler as one of Portland's most renowned mixologists and among the earliest involved in the craft-cocktail movement in the early 2000s. The kitchen is bar food taken seriously: oysters on the half shell, deviled eggs with chives and paprika, a drive-thru burger with American cheese and dijonnaise, a fried chicken sandwich with Oaxaca cheese and tomatillo sauce, steelhead trout with shaved fennel and celeriac purée, and the bartender's cookies with chocolate chunks and sea salt.

What makes Pacific Standard genuinely useful to anyone managing their drinking is a menu-design decision rather than a single drink: the alcohol by volume of every cocktail is printed beside it, running from 0% up to a 39% house old fashioned. Willamette Week noted the practice when the bar relaunched its list in July 2022, describing myriad low- and no-alcohol options with the alcohol by volume for all of them printed on the menu. That means zero-proof drinks are not quarantined in a separate section but sit in the main cocktail grid, marked 0% ABV. Tiger Balm combines the bar's own house-made non-alcoholic spirit with Wilderton Lustre, pineapple and lime over pebble ice. Wandering Path is built on Pathfinder non-alcoholic spirit with grapefruit, lemon and egg whites, served up. Between those and full strength sits a genuine low-ABV ladder — a fun-sized mandarin orange gimlet at 9.5%, an all-day bloody mary at 9%, a pine-Aperol spritz at 10.6% — which makes the room equally legible whether you are moderating or not drinking at all. Kombucha, Leitz Eins Zwei Zero wine and BERO non-alcoholic beer round out the list. The bar is open daily from 3pm to midnight, with happy hour from 3 to 6pm and again from 10pm.
venues.pressQuote: Low-proof and alcohol-free cocktails are featured prominently on our menu, and the ABV of every drink is listed so that our guests have all of the necessary information to make informed choices.

venues.name: Pagu
venues.description: Pagu is chef-owner Tracy Chang's Spanish-Japanese tapas restaurant at 310 Massachusetts Avenue in Central Square, Cambridge, a Michelin Bib Gourmand holder that draws on Chang's training across Japanese, Spanish and Taiwanese cooking. The kitchen is entirely nut-free and works hard around gluten-free, dairy-free and vegan requests. The drinks list prints a non-alcoholic section on the same page as the cocktails, built mostly from tea, fruit and vinegar rather than zero-proof spirits: an oolong-based mojito, a guava and hibiscus cooler, and a pomegranate build with chocolate bitters and rose water, all between $5 and $10. Pagu also bottles its own rotating sparkling tea and pours Athletic Brewing's non-alcoholic IPA, plus single-origin teas and Gracenote coffee.
signatureDrinks: G & H (guava, lime, hibiscus, club soda)
Pomo Rojo (pomegranate, chocolate bitters, lemon, hibiscus, rose water, soda)
venues.longDescription:
Pagu is the Central Square restaurant of Tracy Chang, a Lexington native who cooked in Japan and Spain before opening in Cambridge, and who has since become one of the more publicly civic figures in Boston food — Pagu's menus carry a standing appeal for Project Restore Us, the grocery-delivery initiative Chang runs for food-insecure families. The restaurant holds a Michelin Bib Gourmand and describes itself as values-driven and playful rather than fine dining; the food is tapas-style and shared, moving between Japanese, Spanish and Taiwanese registers on a single menu — squid ink bao, guchi's midnight ramen, green crab laksa, duck paella, jamon iberico, patatas bravas. The entire kitchen is nut-free, which is rare at this level, and the menu is annotated throughout for gluten-free and vegetarian diners. Boston Magazine has covered the bar's alcohol-free work in its guide to creative mocktails around Boston, and Meet Boston's January 2026 zero-proof guide noted that at Pagu, zero-proof and low-ABV drinks reflect the restaurant's adventurous approach to flavour.

The non-alcoholic block sits on the same page as the cocktails and is built from the same larder as the kitchen, which is why it reads as a chef's list rather than a bartender's afterthought. The Oolong-jito is $10 and combines mint and ginger with oolong tea in place of rum; G & H is $8, mixing guava, lime and hibiscus with club soda; Pomo Rojo is $9 and layers pomegranate, chocolate bitters, lemon, hibiscus and rose water over soda; and a house cranberry lemonade runs $5. Beyond the cocktails, Pagu bottles its own sparkling tea in rotating selections at $12 for a 187ml and $42 for a 750ml, and carries the Ama pet-nat teas from Sri Lanka and East Africa at $75 a bottle for the table. Athletic Brewing's Run Wild non-alcoholic IPA is $8. The tea and coffee list is a genuine part of the offer, covering Taiwanese oolong and black tea, Chinese chrysanthemum, Boston-made buckwheat tea and a Gracenote coffee americano.
venues.pressQuote: The Bara No Bara from Pagu combines tart blood orange and pomegranate with rice vinegar and cacao rose water.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Boston Magazine, "Here's Where to Drink Creative Mocktails around Boston"

venues.name: Palate Las Vegas
venues.description: Palate Las Vegas is a modern Americana kitchen-and-bar in the heart of the Arts District, led by Chef Sterling Buckley with managing partners Rudy Aguas and Marisa Martino of Bar-Kada Hospitality, where "the food is art and the cocktails are art." Its bar program includes a standing, clearly labeled "FREE SPIRITED" section of five crafted zero-proof cocktails: Kiss From a Rose (Empress N/A indigo gin, hibiscus, elderflower, lime, lemonade, rose), Pineapple Express (pineapple-jalapeño-infused N/A mezcal, lime, agave, pineapple, smoked), Whiskey '0' Sour (zero-proof whiskey, lemon, demerara), Zero Plane (zero-proof whiskey, Lyre's Orange Aperitif, Lucano N/A amaro, lemon), and Valerie (Empress N/A indigo gin, lemon, ginger). Non-alcoholic beer is also stocked, with Athletic Brewing's Atletica and Free Wave on the list. The venue gives back through its drink menu: for every free-spirit cocktail sold, $1 is donated to the Vegas Stronger foundation. It serves dinner Wednesday through Sunday plus weekend brunch in a space that doubles as a showcase for local Las Vegas artists.

venues.longDescription:
Palate opened in spring 2024 at 1301 South Main Street, inside the Colorado building in the Las Vegas Arts District, and describes itself as minority-owned, woman-owned and locally owned. It is led by managing partners Rudy Aguas and Marisa Martino of Bar-Kada Hospitality, with Sterling Buckley as executive chef. Buckley grew up in Los Angeles, moved to Las Vegas in 2000, and has cooked at the Stratosphere, Le Cordon Bleu Las Vegas, La Cave at the Wynn, Gordon Ramsay Steak, Honey Salt and Momofuku; his cooking fuses Southern food with Latin American, Pan-Asian and European influences across dishes like the Duck Dynasty charcuterie board and an American Wagyu flank steak. Martino brings three decades in food and beverage, graduated with honours from UNLV's William F. Harrah College of Hospitality and sits on the board of the Epicurean Charitable Foundation; Aguas spent more than twenty years across Wynn and Encore and the Venetian-Palazzo. The restaurant was created, in its own words, to pay homage to the Arts District, and it does so literally: local artists' work hangs throughout the room, live music runs Thursday through Saturday, and the team partners with neighbourhood trades, vendors and suppliers.

The house line is that the food is art and the cocktails are art, and the zero-proof drinks are held to that same standard rather than parked at the bottom of the menu. A standing section titled FREE SPIRITED carries five crafted non-alcoholic cocktails: Kiss From a Rose (Empress N/A indigo gin, hibiscus, elderflower, lime, lemonade, rose), Pineapple Express (pineapple-jalapeno-infused N/A mezcal, lime, agave, pineapple, smoked), Whiskey '0' Sour (zero-proof whiskey, lemon, demerara), Zero Plane (zero-proof whiskey, Lyre's Orange Aperitif, Lucano N/A amaro, lemon), and Valerie (Empress N/A indigo gin, lemon, ginger). Non-alcoholic beer is stocked alongside them, including Athletic Brewing's Atletica and Free Wave. The program also gives back through the glass: for every free-spirit cocktail sold, one dollar is donated to the Vegas Stronger foundation, which works on addiction recovery and homelessness in the city. Dinner runs Wednesday through Sunday, with brunch at the weekend.
venues.pressQuote: Peruse Palate's wine, beer or cocktail lists, all of which have respectable depth, breadth and, in the case of the mixed drinks, ambition.

venues.name: Palio
venues.description: Palio is a Tuscan restaurant at 545 Michigan Street NE, named for the Palio, the bareback horse race run twice each summer through the Piazza del Campo in Siena. The kitchen turns out large pizzas from an industrial gas-fired stone oven alongside bolognese, carbonara, lasagna and reinvented classics, using herbs cut from the restaurant's own in-house herb garden. Its non-alcoholic list is the deepest of any restaurant in this guide by count: seven named drinks, each titled after an Italian figure — Buble, Di Nero, Rossellini, Sinatra, Bellucci, Alighieri and Michaelangelo — which puts the zero-proof menu on the same naming footing as a cocktail list rather than labelling them generically as mocktails.
venues.address: 545 Michigan St NE, Ste 102, Grand Rapids, MI 49503
venues.longDescription:
Palio takes its name from the Palio di Siena, the bareback horse race run twice each summer around the Piazza del Campo, and the restaurant sits at 545 Michigan Street NE in Midtown, a short distance along the same corridor as The Friesian. The kitchen is built around an industrial gas-fired stone pizza oven producing large pizzas, and the rest of the menu runs through bolognese, carbonara, lasagna and a set of reinvented Italian classics. The detail that anchors the cooking is the in-house herb garden: herbs are cut fresh for service rather than bought dried, which is a small operational commitment that shows up across both the plates and the drinks.

The non-alcoholic list is the reason Palio appears here, and it is unusual on two counts. The first is simple depth — seven named zero-proof drinks is more than any other restaurant in this guide carries, and more than most cocktail bars manage. The second is the naming. Rather than filing them under a generic mocktail heading, Palio titles each after an Italian cultural figure: Buble, Di Nero, Rossellini, Sinatra, Bellucci, Alighieri and Michaelangelo, running from Dante through Michelangelo to Monica Bellucci and Robert De Niro. That choice does real work. A drink called Alighieri sits on the page as an equal of the wine list; a drink called "mocktail no. 3" does not, and a guest ordering it out loud in front of a table is making a different kind of announcement. It is the same principle that Pacific Standard applies by printing ABV on every drink — the menu design decides whether a non-drinker is choosing or conceding. Palio trades Monday through Saturday, 4pm to 10pm, and takes reservations through Resy; the fresh-herb garden means the specific builds shift with what is cut that week.

venues.name: Palm&Pine
venues.description: Palm&Pine is a French Quarter restaurant at 308 North Rampart Street, opened in 2019 by chef/owners and partners Amarys Koenig Herndon and Jordan Herndon, who were James Beard Best Chef: South semifinalists in both 2023 and 2024 and named Rising Star Chefs in 2022. The kitchen draws on Louisiana, the broader South and what they call "South of That" — the Caribbean and Mexico. Its non-alcoholic list has its own name, the Kitten Club, and appears as a titled section on both the dinner and brunch drinks menus. At dinner it runs the Rosella Refresher ($13) on Pathfinder non-alcoholic spirit with hibiscus, lemon and Mineragua; St. Buena Vida non-alcoholic sparkling chardonnay ($17 a glass, $56 a bottle); Parleaux sparkling hop water ($6); and Untitled Art American Gold non-alcoholic beer ($8). At brunch it swaps in a Holy Margarita! on Almave non-alcoholic agave spirit ($15) and a non-alcoholic michelada ($7). Closed Tuesdays and Wednesdays. A 20% gratuity is added to all checks.

venues.hours: Mon 5:30pm-9pm; Tue-Wed closed; Thu 5:30pm-9pm; Fri-Sat 5:30pm-10pm; Sun 10:30am-2pm
signatureDrinks: St. Buena Vida NA sparkling chardonnay ($17)
venues.longDescription:
Palm&Pine sits at 308 North Rampart Street on the edge of the French Quarter, in what was a white box before Amarys Koenig Herndon, Jordan Herndon and a third partner turned it into the room it is now. The two chefs met as sous chefs at Bayona and Ralph on the Park and spent years popping up together before opening here in 2019; they were James Beard Best Chef: South semifinalists in both 2023 and 2024 and Rising Star Chefs in 2022. The cooking runs from Louisiana through the wider South and into what they call South of That — the Caribbean and Mexico. There is a kitchen counter where you can talk to them while they cook. Dinner Thursday through Monday, brunch on Sunday, closed Tuesday and Wednesday, and a 20% gratuity is added to every check for the servers, hosts and bartenders.

The non-alcoholic list is named, which tells you how it is treated. It is the Kitten Club, and it appears as its own titled section on both the dinner and brunch drinks menus rather than as a line at the bottom. At dinner it runs four deep: the Rosella Refresher at $13, built on Pathfinder non-alcoholic spirit with hibiscus, lemon and Mineragua sparkling mineral water; St. Buena Vida non-alcoholic sparkling chardonnay at $17 a glass or $56 a bottle, which is the detail worth noticing, because a bottle price means the restaurant expects a table to share one over dinner the way any other table shares wine; Parleaux sparkling hop water at $6 from a local brewery; and Untitled Art American Gold non-alcoholic beer at $8. Brunch swaps in a Holy Margarita! on Almave non-alcoholic agave spirit at $15 and a non-alcoholic michelada at $7. The list rotates with the seasons, so names change — earlier Kitten Club drinks including the Heartfruit Tonic are no longer served — but the section itself is permanent.
venues.pressQuote: Palm&Pine, located in the French Quarter, will be serving a non-alcoholic menu called Kitten Club during this Dry January.

venues.name: Palm House
venues.description: Palm House is a tropical bar and restaurant at 2032 Union Street in Cow Hollow, set in a historic 1854 dairy farmhouse behind what the venue describes as San Francisco's second-oldest palm tree, and trading under the Palm House name since 2014. The Caribbean- and Hawaiian-leaning kitchen and tiki-influenced bar pair vacation-style food with a standing non-alcoholic list printed on the main menu rather than hidden behind a request. The "Free Spirited" section runs the Virgin Islands (passion fruit, prickly pear, pineapple gomme), the Piñita Colada (coconut water, coconut puree, pineapple gomme, lime), the Hibiscus Mate (hibiscus tea, yerba mate, lemon, simple syrup) and an N/A Michelada built on non-alcoholic lager, priced $8 to $10. Rationale Brewing non-alcoholic lager is poured, and drag brunch, trivia and DJ nights are regular fixtures.
