venues.longDescription:
Palm House occupies a historic 1854 dairy farmhouse at 2032 Union Street in Cow Hollow, set back from the street behind what the venue describes as San Francisco's second-oldest palm tree — the feature the bar takes its name from. It has traded under the Palm House name since 2014, serving Caribbean- and Hawaiian-leaning food in a room and patio styled as a permanent holiday: rattan, greenery and warm light rather than the darker register of a dedicated tiki bar. It is closed Mondays, opens at noon Tuesday through Friday and runs to 2am on Friday and Saturday nights, with weekend service starting at 10:30am. Drag brunch, trivia and DJ nights give it a genuine going-out identity rather than a purely restaurant one.

For non-drinkers the useful detail is that the alcohol-free drinks are printed on the main menu under their own heading, "Free Spirited," and priced at $8 to $10 — meaningfully cheaper than the cocktails rather than charged at parity. The list runs the Virgin Islands (passion fruit, prickly pear and pineapple gomme), the Piñita Colada (coconut water, coconut puree, pineapple gomme and lime), the Hibiscus Mate (hibiscus tea, yerba mate, lemon and simple syrup) and an N/A Michelada built on spiced bloody mary mix and non-alcoholic lager. The gomme syrup shared across the first two is the detail worth noting: it gives the drinks a texture and body that fruit juice alone does not, which is the usual failure point for tropical alcohol-free drinks. Rationale Brewing non-alcoholic lager is poured by the glass, and the bar also keeps freshly squeezed orange and grapefruit juice, drip coffee, cold brew and lattes, so the venue works across a whole day rather than only at night. The frozen house slushies and the punch bowls are alcoholic and are not offered in zero-proof versions.

venues.name: Palomar
venues.description: Palomar is an acclaimed Cuban cocktail bar and restaurant owned by award-winning bartender Ricky Gomez, who won the inaugural Diageo World Class U.S. Bartender of the Year competition in 2012 and whose résumé includes New Orleans' Commander's Palace and Cure as well as Portland's Teardrop Lounge. He opened Palomar in 2018 in Southeast Portland, where it quickly drew acclaim for its 1960s-Havana atmosphere and a daiquiri-focused programme rooted in Cuban and New Orleans cocktail traditions, before the bar moved to Northwest 23rd Avenue in 2025. It is a three-time Tales of the Cocktail finalist for Best U.S. Restaurant Bar. Its current menu carries a dedicated "NO PROOF" section of signature non-alcoholic drinks — a Pathfinder daiquiri plus zero-proof Mojito, Moscow Mule, Spritz and Piña Colada — alongside non-alcoholic beer and wine.
venues.longDescription:
Palomar is a Cuban cocktail bar and restaurant in Northwest Portland, owned by award-winning bartender Ricky Gomez, who won the inaugural Diageo World Class U.S. Bartender of the Year competition in 2012 and whose résumé includes New Orleans' Commander's Palace and Cure as well as Portland's Teardrop Lounge. Gomez opened Palomar in 2018 in Southeast Portland, where it quickly drew acclaim for its '60s-Havana atmosphere and a daiquiri-focused program rooted in Cuban and New Orleans cocktail traditions; in March 2025 it relocated to 1422 NW 23rd Avenue. The Oregonian and Eater Portland both named it Bar of the Year in 2018, and it has been a Tales of the Cocktail Spirited Awards finalist for Best U.S. Restaurant Bar in 2023 and 2024.

The bar is built around blended daiquiris and house infusions such as its house pineapple gin, and its current menu carries a dedicated "NO PROOF" section of signature non-alcoholic drinks — including a Pathfinder daiquiri and zero-proof takes on the Mojito, Moscow Mule, Spritz and Piña Colada — alongside non-alcoholic beer and wine. The relocated venue welcomes minors and runs a daily happy hour.
venues.pressQuote: Acclaimed Cuban restaurant and cocktail bar Palomar has completed its move across the river and is open for business on Northwest 23rd Avenue.

venues.name: Paper Doll
venues.description: Paper Doll is a downtown Birmingham cocktail bar on 1st Avenue North built around bespoke service: the bar's reputation is for making the right drink once you describe what you are in the mood for, rather than handing over a fixed list. That approach extends to the non-alcoholic side, where the Cream Cycle is the drink Bham Now named in its January 2026 city guide. Open Tuesday to Saturday from 5pm, to 10pm midweek and 1am on Friday and Saturday, and closed Sunday and Monday.
venues.longDescription:
Paper Doll, on 1st Avenue North in downtown Birmingham, works on the dealer's-choice model: rather than handing over a card, the bartenders ask what you feel like and build to it. Bham Now's summary of the room is that it is known for creating the perfect drink when you tell them whatever you are in the mood for.

That model normally gets a sceptical reading in this directory. "We'll make you something without alcohol" is the standard deflection from bars with no programme at all, and it puts the burden of negotiation on the person who is already the odd one out. Paper Doll clears the bar because the improvisation is the house style for every customer, not a fallback reserved for non-drinkers — and because there is a specific documented alcohol-free build, the Cream Cycle, which Birmingham's own paper named in its January 2026 round-up of the city's non-alcoholic drinking.

The distinction is worth stating plainly, since it recurs across this directory: a bar that improvises for everyone is including you; a bar that improvises only for you is accommodating you. The first is a good sign, the second usually is not.

The grade of three reflects scale honestly. One named non-alcoholic drink, no printed zero-proof section, no non-alcoholic spirits programme documented. What a reader gets is a good cocktail bar where describing what you like will produce something made with care.

Hours run 5pm to 10pm Tuesday through Thursday and 5pm to 1am on Friday and Saturday, closed Sunday and Monday. It sits in the middle of the downtown cluster, a minute from Neon Moon and Pink Lantern, which makes it easy to fold into a longer evening rather than treating as a destination on its own.
venues.pressQuote: Paper Doll is known for creating the perfect drink when you tell them whatever you're in the mood for

venues.name: Papi Steak
venues.description: Papi Steak is a South Beach steakhouse on 1st Street in the South of Fifth district, which RESIDENT describes as a high-energy setting. Its documented alcohol-free build, the Elixir De Alma, is properly constructed: lychee, cucumber and lime with Almave Blue Agave Spirit — a distilled non-alcoholic agave — and a dash of spicy bitters, which gives the drink both an agave base and a genuine peppery finish. RESIDENT described it in December 2025 as structured and refreshing and as a zero-proof option that still fits the restaurant's high-energy atmosphere. Dinner runs nightly from 6pm, to 11:30pm on Thursday and 11pm on Friday and Saturday.
signatureDrinks: Elixir De Alma (Almave Blue Agave Spirit, lychee, cucumber, lime, spicy bitters)
venues.longDescription:
Papi Steak trades at 736 1st Street in South Beach, in the South of Fifth pocket a few blocks back from Ocean Drive, in what RESIDENT describes as a high-energy setting. It opens for dinner only, from 6pm every night, closing at 10pm early in the week, 11:30pm on Thursday and 11pm on Friday and Saturday.

The reason the restaurant belongs in an alcohol-free catalogue is the Elixir De Alma, which is a properly built drink rather than a token juice. It combines lychee, cucumber and lime with Almave Blue Agave Spirit — the distilled non-alcoholic agave spirit made from cooked blue agave, not a flavoured syrup — and finishes with spicy bitters. The result has an agave backbone, a cooling cucumber middle and a peppery finish, which is exactly the profile a guest ordering off a steakhouse list is likely to want. RESIDENT documented the drink in its December 2025 Miami round-up and wrote that the result is structured and refreshing, and that it offers a zero-proof option that still aligns with the restaurant's high-energy atmosphere. Almave is not currently carried in this catalogue's brand registry, so the spirit is named in the drink specification without a brand tag. Only one named alcohol-free build is published for the venue, so the programme is graded as real but modest; the restaurant can be reached on (305) 800-7274 and posts as @papisteak. Two practical notes for a first visit. The drink specification comes from RESIDENT's December 2025 survey, because the restaurant's own site does not publish a beverage list. And because the restaurant opens at 6pm and no earlier, there is no daytime option here; South of Fifth's alternatives for an alcohol-free drink before dinner are limited, and the nearest documented options in this catalogue are on Collins Avenue further north.
venues.pressQuote: The result is structured and refreshing, offering a zero-proof option that still aligns with the restaurant’s high-energy atmosphere.

venues.name: Paradisaea
venues.description: Paradisaea is a French-modern California restaurant in La Jolla's Bird Rock neighborhood, opened in September 2022 by husband-and-wife owners Eric and Zoe Kleinbub inside the landmark "Piano Building" on La Jolla Boulevard, and Michelin Guide recommended since 2023. Its cocktail program is presented as an illustrated "field guide" to the bird species behind the restaurant's name and includes a dedicated non-alcoholic section. Zero-proof options include The Woods (non-alcoholic distilled agave spirit, marionberry, pomegranate, orange bitters), the Ghia-based Ostrich, and a Seedlip-and-Blue-Majik Takahe, with spirit-free builds also drawing on Ritual. The bar room features lounge seating, board games, and a small retail space selling bottled and canned drinks — a polished, design-forward spot where the NA list gets the same illustration and care as the cocktails.
venues.address: 5680 La Jolla Blvd, San Diego, CA 92037
venues.longDescription:
Paradisaea is a French-modern California restaurant in the Bird Rock stretch of La Jolla, opened in September 2022 by husband-and-wife owners Eric and Zoe Kleinbub inside the landmark Piano Building on La Jolla Boulevard, and Michelin Guide recommended since 2023. The name comes from the genus of birds-of-paradise, and the conceit runs right through the room and onto the drinks list, which is presented as an illustrated field guide to the species behind it.

That presentation is the detail worth noting, because the non-alcoholic drinks sit inside the same field guide with the same illustrations and the same care rather than being relegated to a line of text at the bottom. The zero-proof section is genuinely built: The Woods combines a non-alcoholic distilled agave spirit with marionberry, pomegranate and orange bitters; the Ostrich is built on Ghia, the bitter Californian aperitif; and the Takahe pairs Seedlip with blue majik, the spirulina extract that gives it a startling colour. Ritual appears across other spirit-free builds. Beyond the dining room there is a bar room with lounge seating and board games, plus a small retail space selling bottled and canned drinks to take away — which quietly makes this one of the few high-end restaurants in the county where a non-drinker can also buy something to bring home. The combination of a Michelin recommendation, a design-forward room and a zero-proof list that has been illustrated rather than tolerated makes Paradisaea a straightforward recommendation for an occasion dinner where somebody at the table is not drinking. Tuesday to Sunday, evenings, closed Mondays. The bar room is the part worth knowing about if you are not eating: it takes walk-ins, the board games encourage staying, and the retail shelf means an evening there can end with something to take home. For a non-drinker, having all three in a Michelin-recommended room is close to unheard of in San Diego.
venues.pressQuote: Contemporary California cuisine in a tropical, Instagram-worthy dining room

venues.name: Paradiso
venues.description: Paradiso is a Southern European-inspired restaurant and cocktail bar set within a shaded garden courtyard in Bishop Arts, and it runs a documented mocktail programme of five zero-proof cocktails built from house-made syrups, fresh-pressed juices and botanical tinctures. The Silent Dove — grapefruit, soda, lime and simple syrup — is the closest thing to a house paloma without the tequila. Flight of the Bees layers honey, lemon and ginger beer, and the bolder On the Road Again uses a spirit-free American malt base with cold-pressed ginger syrup, lemon and maraschino cherry for something closer to a proper sour. The all-day format runs brunch through dinner seven days a week.

venues.longDescription:
Tucked along North Bishop Avenue in Dallas's Bishop Arts District, Paradiso is one of the few full-service restaurants in the city where non-drinkers aren't an afterthought. The bar program treats its zero-proof section with the same seasonal intentionality applied to the craft cocktail list — house-made syrups, freshly squeezed juices, and botanical tinctures are standard-issue here, not a workaround. The setting helps: a shaded garden courtyard with vines trailing from gold-lit fixtures and a sprawling plant-lined patio creates an environment where what's in the glass matters less than the conversation around it.

The mocktail roster has enough range to reward repeat visits. The Silent Dove — grapefruit juice, soda, lime, and simple syrup — is the closest thing to a house paloma without the tequila, clean and easy to pair with the mezze carts that circulate the dining room. Flight of the Bees layers honey, lemon, and ginger beer into something that drinks more like a considered cocktail than a placeholder. The bolder pick is On the Road Again, which leans on an American malt spirit-free whiskey base alongside cold-pressed ginger syrup, lemon, and maraschino cherry for something closer to a proper sour. The restaurant is a concept from Exxir Hospitality, the group behind neighboring Bar Eden, with Jeremy Hargrove serving as COO and Nick Hurry as executive chef.

Paradiso skews lively, especially on weekend evenings — the music gets loud and the crowd tends toward date-night and celebration groups, so it is not the place for a quiet catch-up. Reservations are strongly advised for Friday and Saturday dinners; multiple reviewers note the room fills quickly and walk-ins face waits. Dress code is smart casual. Valet parking is available, as street and lot parking in Bishop Arts can be competitive. The all-day format (brunch through dinner, seven days a week) makes it one of the more flexible options in the neighborhood for anyone wanting zero-proof drinks at any hour.
venues.pressQuote: Paradiso creates its mocktails with freshly squeezed juices and house-made syrups.

venues.name: Parley
venues.description: Parley opened in December 2025 on East Cesar Chavez Street in East Austin, founded by Terance Robson and Jack 'Slim' Hogan — both originally from Ireland and previously of Bar Hacienda, Bar Fino, and Here Nor There. The concept is a love letter to the Irish neighborhood pub Robson and Hogan grew up around, reimagined for East Austin with Asian and Korean influences through a kitchen collaboration with next-door Oseyo. The cocktail program is accessibly priced ($10–16) and ambitious, with drinks built around ingredients like spent coffee, snap pea, eucalyptus, vanilla gelato, mascarpone tequila, and blue corn salt. Visit Austin's official tourism blog highlights Parley's non-alcoholic offerings as 'composed cocktails rather than placeholders,' calling out the Penichillin' (pear, honey, ginger, lemon — an NA play on the classic Penicillin) and the earthy Beetrooter (beet, apple, carrot, orange, cinnamon). The bar opens at 11am daily for coffee and light bites and runs until 2am with a late-night menu available on request.
venues.address: 1628 E Cesar Chavez St, Austin, TX 78702
signatureDrinks: The Beetrooter (beet, apple, carrot, orange, cinnamon)
venues.longDescription:
Parley opened in December 2025 on East Cesar Chavez Street, founded by Terance Robson and Jack Hogan — known as Slim — both originally from Ireland and both previously at Bar Hacienda, Bar Fino and Here Nor There. The concept is the Irish neighbourhood pub they grew up around, rebuilt for East Austin, with Asian and Korean influences arriving through a kitchen collaboration with Oseyo next door.

The cocktail list is ambitious and deliberately affordable at ten to sixteen dollars, working with ingredients like spent coffee, snap pea, eucalyptus, vanilla gelato, mascarpone-washed tequila and blue corn salt. That same imagination carries into the non-alcoholic drinks, which is the part worth flagging: Visit Austin's assessment is that Parley treats NA drinks as composed cocktails rather than placeholders, and the phrasing is exact.

The Penichillin' is the clearest evidence. It is a zero-proof reading of the Penicillin, a modern classic built on blended Scotch, honey, ginger and lemon with a smoky Islay float — a drink that on paper should be impossible without whisky, because smoke and peat are the whole point of it. Rebuilding it around pear, honey, ginger and lemon means going after the drink's structure rather than imitating its base spirit, which is the harder and more interesting approach. The Beetrooter runs beet, apple, carrot, orange and cinnamon: earthy, vegetal and savoury, in a category that usually defaults to sweet.

The opening hours matter as much as the menu. Parley runs from 11am daily through to 2am, serving coffee and light bites early and keeping a late-night menu available on request after midnight. That span makes it usable as a morning coffee, an afternoon working spot and a genuine late-night option on a street where the alternatives close around a bar — and being able to stay somewhere until closing time without drinking is the practical test most venues fail.
venues.pressQuote: Newly opened in late 2025, Parley treats NA drinks as 'composed cocktails' rather than placeholders. Try the balanced Penichillin' (pear, honey, ginger, and lemon) or The Beetrooter, an earthy blend of beet, carrot, and cinnamon.

venues.name: Parlour
venues.description: Parlour is a craft cocktail and burger bar in Minneapolis's North Loop, opened in 2013 below sister restaurant Borough by the local restaurant group Jester Concepts. Originally conceived as a waiting room for the upstairs dining room, it became a destination in its own right, known for the cult-favorite Parlour Burger and a serious classics-forward cocktail program built on fresh-squeezed juice, house-made syrups, and bitters. The bar maintains a dedicated "Non-Alcoholic Cocktails" section rather than a single token mocktail, using NA spirits alongside the same botanical and bitter techniques as its full bar. Named zero-proof builds include the NA Parlour Old Fashioned (NA bourbon, NA spiced spirit, piloncillo, bitters), a Phony Negroni, a Gin & Apricot Sour (thyme, lemon, apricot jam, egg white), and a Perfect Matcha made with an NA botanical spirit. It sits among the North Loop's marquee craft-cocktail venues.

Phony Negroni (bitters, juniper, citrus and floral notes)

Cilantro Mojito (cilantro, ginger, lime, soda water)
venues.longDescription:
Parlour opened in 2013 in the North Loop, below its sister restaurant Borough, from the local group Jester Concepts. It was originally conceived as somewhere for people to wait for a table upstairs, and it long ago outgrew that role to become a destination in its own right — known for the cult-favourite Parlour Burger and for a classics-forward cocktail programme built on fresh-squeezed juice, house-made syrups and bitters. It is one of the North Loop's marquee cocktail rooms, open to 1am on Fridays and Saturdays.

The useful thing for a non-drinker is that Parlour keeps a dedicated Non-Alcoholic Cocktails section rather than a single token option, and applies the same botanical and bitter techniques there that it uses on the full bar. The NA Parlour Old Fashioned is built on a non-alcoholic bourbon and a non-alcoholic spiced spirit with piloncillo — the unrefined Mexican cane sugar — and bitters, which is a considerably more serious attempt at that drink than the usual sweetened substitute. There is a Phony Negroni carrying the juniper, citrus and floral notes the original needs, and a Gin & Apricot Sour built on non-alcoholic gin with honey, thyme, lemon, apricot jam and egg white. The Perfect Matcha combines a non-alcoholic botanical spirit with matcha cold brew, coconut purée and lemon, and a Cilantro Mojito rounds the list out with cilantro, ginger, lime and soda.

What that range means in practice is that the spirit-free list covers the four registers a real bar needs — spirituous and sweet, bitter, sour with texture, and long and refreshing. A guest who is not drinking can order across a whole evening at a bar known for its burgers and its classics without ever repeating themselves or ordering a soda, which at a venue of this profile is the entire point.
venues.pressQuote: The metro's haute-burger-famous Parlour opened its newest location beside Shiki

venues.name: Partenope Ristorante
venues.description: Partenope is a downtown Dallas Neapolitan restaurant and pizzeria whose bar builds genuine spirit-free versions of the Italian classics rather than defaulting to sodas. Its zero-proof set runs $9 and leans on house-made components — a house-made bitter non-alcoholic liquor and a house-made non-alcoholic sweet vermouth — alongside named brands like Ritual Zero Proof gin and Lyre's. The NA Negroni in particular is built almost entirely from those house-made NA aperitivo elements, which is what pushes these past off-the-shelf mocktails.
signatureDrinks: NA Negroni — house-made bitter non-alcoholic liquor, house-made non-alcoholic sweet vermouth, and Ritual Zero Proof gin
NA French 75 — Ritual Zero Proof gin, lemon juice
NA Dirty Tonic — Lyre's non-alcoholic sparkling, house-made lemon paste, tonic water, and green olives
venues.longDescription:
Partenope Ristorante is a Neapolitan restaurant and pizzeria in downtown Dallas's Main Street District, at 1903 Main St directly across from Main Street Garden Park. It specializes in true Vera Pizza Napoletana and has become one of the city's most decorated Italian rooms — appearing on the 50 Top Pizza USA list for six consecutive years, landing at No. 18 in 2026 and earning a Made in Italy special award.

For non-drinkers, the appeal is a serious spirit-free take on Italian aperitivo culture rather than a token soda. As documented by CultureMap Dallas, the bar offers a $9 set of three named zero-proof cocktails: an NA Negroni built from house-made bitter non-alcoholic liquor, house-made non-alcoholic sweet vermouth, and Ritual Zero Proof gin; an NA French 75 with Ritual Zero Proof gin and lemon juice; and an NA Dirty Tonic using Lyre's non-alcoholic sparkling with house-made lemon paste, tonic water, and green olives. The reliance on house-made NA bitter liquor and NA sweet vermouth — the two components that actually define a Negroni — is what makes the program feel like craft substitution instead of sweetened filler.

The restaurant is open daily for lunch and dinner (Sun–Thu 11am–10pm, Fri–Sat 11am–10:30pm) and takes reservations via Resy. It's a strong downtown pick for a non-drinker joining a table for wood-fired Neapolitan pizza who still wants a proper, alcohol-free aperitivo in hand.
venues.pressQuote: This Italian pizzeria features an NA Negroni with house-made bitter non-alcoholic liquor, house-made non-alcoholic sweet vermouth, and Ritual zero-proof gin; NA French 75 with Ritual zero-proof gin, lemon juice; and Lyre's non-alcoholic sparkling Dirty Tonic with house-made lemon paste, tonic water and green olives. Drinks are $9.

venues.name: Pascual
venues.description: Pascual is a wood-fired modern Mexican restaurant at 732 Maryland Avenue NE on Capitol Hill, just off Barracks Row, opened in February 2024 by chefs Isabel Coss and Matt Conroy. The kitchen centres on fire, masa and heritage ingredients, with tortillas made in house and a seasonal, locally sourced menu that drew national attention fast: one of Eater's Best New Restaurants in America in 2024, top of the Best New Restaurant lists from the Washington Post and Eater DC, a place in the Michelin Guide, and 2025 James Beard semifinalist nods for both chefs. The non-alcoholic side is genuine rather than an afterthought, built on rotating aguas frescas and named zero-proof cocktails including the Temperate Margarita, made with NA tequila and orange liqueur, and the Nada Colada, a pina colada riff with a hint of mango.
venues.longDescription:
Pascual opened in February 2024 at 732 Maryland Avenue NE, a block off Barracks Row on Capitol Hill, from chefs Isabel Coss and Matt Conroy - the same pair behind Lutece in Georgetown, though this is a very different room. The cooking is modern Mexican built around fire: a wood-fired open kitchen, masa ground and pressed in house into tortillas, and heritage ingredients treated as the point rather than the garnish. The reception was immediate. In 2024 it was named one of Eater's Best New Restaurants in America and topped Best New Restaurant lists from both the Washington Post and Eater DC; it is included in the Michelin Guide; and in 2025 Coss and Conroy were James Beard Award semifinalists for Best Chef: Mid-Atlantic.

The bar is small and mezcal-leaning, and it extends the same care to the drinks without alcohol in them. The foundation is rotating aguas frescas, which is the right base for a kitchen working with this fruit, and above them sit named zero-proof cocktails. Washingtonian highlighted two during Dry January: the Temperate Margarita, built with non-alcoholic tequila and orange liqueur so it keeps the structure of a margarita rather than becoming limeade, and the Nada Colada, a pina colada riff lifted with a hint of mango. Next door the restaurant runs Volcan, a panaderia-style window serving Mexican pastries, cafe de olla and aguas frescas, which is worth knowing about independently - it means there is somewhere on this block for a good non-alcoholic drink during the day without a reservation.

Practical notes. Pascual is closed Monday and Tuesday. Dinner runs Wednesday and Thursday 5pm to 9pm, Friday and Saturday 5pm to 9.30pm, and Sunday adds a brunch service from 11am to 2pm before dinner from 5pm to 9pm. The dining room is intimate and heavily reservation-driven, so this is not a walk-in proposition at weekends; the Volcan window is the fallback. Eastern Market and Union Station are both walkable, and Barracks Row itself has enough going on to build an evening around.
venues.pressQuote: Try the "Temperate Margarita" with NA tequila and orange liqueur or the "Nada Colada," a pina colada riff with a hint of mango.

venues.name: Passage Kava Lounge
venues.description: Passage Kava Lounge is a fully alcohol-free, 21+ kava and botanical lounge in Madison, tucked in the EastSide Bowl plaza on Gallatin Pike S. Owned by Ryan and Warren Holding, it opened in 2024 and bills itself as the only Nashville-area bar dealing in zero alcohol. The Victorian-inspired room pours traditional kava (including a communal Bula ceremony), botanical teas, coffee, kratom, kombucha, and mocktails, with house kava drinks like Royal Cinnamon, Velvet Shortcake, and Berry Chocolate. Owner Ryan Holding describes it as "a mix of a coffee shop and bar, but without the bar fights," emphasizing connection over intoxication. The lounge programs nightly events: live music on Mondays and Tuesdays, trivia Wednesdays, and karaoke Thursdays. In its first months open, it placed second for Best New Business in the Nashville Scene's Best of Nashville 2024 awards.
signatureDrinks: Royal Cinnamon kava creation (warm, spiced, like Cinnamon Crunch milk) $12
Velvet Shortcake kava creation (vanilla and strawberry) $12
Majestic Bloom mocktail (crisp botanicals, bubbles, edible hibiscus) $14
Golden Hour mocktail (sweet, sharp, brightened with spice) $11
venues.longDescription:
Passage Kava Lounge sits at 1504B Gallatin Pike South in Madison, north-east of central Nashville, and describes itself in exactly six words on its own site: a 21+ non-alcoholic bar in Nashville. It is the work of Ryan Holding, who had managed a 24-hour kava bar in Florida before opening his own. Seeing the power of a safe, relaxed space there, he has said, convinced him there was a better way to do it — and the room he chose to do it in was an old Kmart garden centre, four bare walls when he took it on. What he built inside is deliberately unlike a bar: Victorian-influenced, with dark wood wainscoting, deep green walls, leather lounge chairs and a chandelier, arranged for sitting and talking rather than standing and drinking. The lounge has been open since around September 2024, though the plan dates to 2021, and it placed second for Best New Business in the Nashville Scene's Best of Nashville reader awards in 2024.

The centre of the drinks list is traditional kava, made from imported South Pacific root — the powder is steeped in water and strained through cheesecloth, and the result is genuinely bitter, with a numbing tingle in the mouth that first-timers should expect rather than be surprised by. Around that sit house kava drinks priced roughly $5 to $12, including Royal Cinnamon, Velvet Shortcake and Berry Chocolate, alongside mocktails, artisanal kombucha, teas and coffee, with charcuterie boards if you are staying a while. Holding's framing of the place is the clearest description of what it is for: for a lot of people, he has said, going out drinking is more about being social — and elsewhere he has called it almost a mix of a coffee shop and a bar, but without the bar fights. The lounge programmes most nights of the week with live music, trivia and karaoke, which is what makes it function as a genuine evening out rather than a daytime cafe. Note the 21+ door policy, and that kava is psychoactive in its own right, which some people avoiding alcohol will want to weigh.
venues.pressQuote: It's almost like a mix of a coffee shop and bar, but without the bar fights.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Ryan Holding, Passage Kava Lounge owner

venues.name: Paydirt
venues.description: Paydirt is a craft cocktail bar tucked inside the Zipper, Kevin Cavenaugh's micro-restaurant development on NE Sandy Boulevard in Portland's Kerns neighborhood. The bar leans into a warm, vaguely Western-saloon aesthetic and is known for a serious cocktail program — and an equally deliberate non-alcoholic one. Paydirt keeps a standing menu of five named zero-proof cocktails built on Ritual and Pathfinder non-alcoholic spirits, including Fool's Gold (Ritual NA whiskey, lime, guava, toasted almond bitters), Lone Buck (Ritual NA whiskey, pandan, lime, ginger beer), Moondance (Ritual NA tequila, honeydew, lemon, orange bitters, Tajín, soda), and Comeback Kid (Pathfinder NA spirit, lime, passionfruit, agave, orange bitters, soda). The NA menu rotates seasonally and is priced $12–$14, on par with the bar's full-proof list.

venues.longDescription:
Paydirt describes itself, with no elaboration, as a dedicated drinking establishment. It sits at 2724 NE Pacific Street inside the Zipper, the micro-restaurant building in the Kerns neighbourhood, and it is a sibling to The Old Gold across town — Willamette Week identified it in October 2015 as coming from the owners of Old Gold, including former Portland Mercury music editor Ezra Caraeff, and both bars still publish the same single-barrel programme in the same words, flying longtime staff to Kentucky each year to hand-select bourbon sold only at their own bars. Willamette Week's review captured the setting exactly: the Zipper sits snugly between I-84, Sandy Boulevard, a barbed-wired parking lot and a Pepsi warehouse, and on the outdoor patio there is a fire pit and freeway noise. There is no kitchen — food comes from the Zipper's other tenants — and the bar's booking policy is characteristically blunt, asking guests not to phone but to email instead.

The non-alcoholic list is a full menu section headed "Non-Alcoholic Drinks", and unusually every one of the five is built on a non-alcoholic spirit rather than juice and soda, which puts them at the same complexity as the bar's full-strength list and at broadly the same price. Fool's Gold ($13) is Ritual non-alcoholic whiskey with lime, guava and toasted almond bitters on the rocks. Lone Buck ($12) uses the same Ritual whiskey with pandan, lime and ginger beer, served tall. Moondance ($13) is Ritual non-alcoholic tequila with honeydew, lemon, orange bitters, Tajín and soda. The two Pathfinder drinks are Lane Change ($14), with lemon, strawberry, basil and ginger beer, and Comeback Kid ($14), with lime, passionfruit, agave, orange bitters and soda. There is no non-alcoholic beer on the list, so the zero-proof offering here is entirely a cocktail programme. Paydirt opens at noon on Saturdays and Sundays and at 3pm the rest of the week, running to 1am on Friday and Saturday, with happy hour all day Monday and from 3 to 5pm Tuesday through Friday.

venues.name: The Peach Crease Club
venues.description: The Peach Crease Club is a mid-century-inspired vinyl listening bar in Denver's RiNo district, across the plaza from Mission Ballroom, opened November 28, 2025 by husband-and-wife bartenders Alex Jump and Stuart Jensen. The culinary-driven cocktail list names drinks after the dishes they reference, and — crucially for non-drinkers — the menu prints the alcohol-by-volume of every drink and marks those that can be built non-alcoholic, with a full Non Alc page carrying four cocktails of their own: Green Curry (non-alcoholic rum, curry spices, palm sugar, rice, coconut, MSG, soda), Peanuts & Cola (The Pathfinder, Three Spirit Nitecap, peanuts, cola), Borscht (non-alcoholic vodka, beets, yogurt, dill, lime, horseradish cream) and Hazelnut & Peaches (non-alcoholic white wine and French aperitif, peaches, sweet potato, dukkah). Non-alcoholic beer, wine and Casamara Club sodas are listed alongside. It earned a 2026 Tales of the Cocktail Spirited Awards nomination for Best New US Cocktail Bar.

venues.longDescription:
The Peach Crease Club opened on November 28, 2025 at 4180 Wynkoop Street, across the plaza from the 4,000-capacity Mission Ballroom, from husband-and-wife bartenders Alex Jump and Stuart Jensen. The name and the concept came from their own house: they had called their home bar the Peach Crease Club through the pandemic, when they were hosting dinner parties, and the bar is furnished with their art, furniture and record collection. Jump spent half a decade at Death & Co Denver and was named Best US Bar Mentor at the 2024 Spirited Awards; Jensen co-owns Curio and Roger's Liquid Oasis. Music is a structural pillar rather than a background: Jensen spent two and a half years assembling an audio system with seven main speakers that can play vinyl, digital or reel-to-reel tape. The room seats about seventy-five, the food is Danish-style smorrebrod, tinned seafood and caviar service, and the drinks list changes roughly three times a year. It drew a 2026 Tales of the Cocktail Spirited Awards nomination for Best New US Cocktail Bar.

The menu is the part that matters most for anyone not drinking. Every cocktail is printed with its alcohol-by-volume, from a 0.0% build up to a 26.8% Fattoush, and drinks that can be made without alcohol are marked, so nobody has to ask. Beyond the convertible builds, there is a dedicated Non Alc cocktail page with four drinks of its own. Peanuts & Cola ($16) is nitrogen-infused and built on The Pathfinder and Three Spirit Nitecap with peanuts and cola, a riff on the Southern habit of dropping peanuts into a Coca-Cola that Jump grew up with in Tennessee. Borscht ($18) uses non-alcoholic vodka with beets, yogurt, dill, lime and horseradish cream at a measured 0.0%. Green Curry ($18) runs non-alcoholic rum with curry spices, palm sugar, rice, coconut, MSG and soda. Hazelnut & Peaches ($15) is built on non-alcoholic white wine and a French aperitif with peaches, sweet potato and dukkah. The non-alcoholic beer, wine and soda list is equally worked through: Guinness Draught 0, Untitled Art pilsner and West Coast IPA, Good Twin sparkling glera, Oddbird white, Leitz Eins Zwei Zero pinot noir, and Casamara Club leisure sodas.
venues.pressQuote: Meanwhile, the nutty, bittersweet Peanuts & Cola, a zero-proof, nitrogen-infused creation, will have Southerners smiling.

venues.name: Pearl's Social & Billy Club
venues.description: Pearl's Social & Billy Club has been a Bushwick mainstay since June 2011, and it marks fifteen years in the community in 2026. Its own framing is the reason it is here: in New York City our bars are our living rooms, and whether you are on or off the wagon you will find something that hits just right. That is backed by a genuinely dedicated "Zero Proof" menu — a separate printed card, not a footnote — carrying six named cocktails: the Dark & Stormless (Three Spirit Nightcap, fresh ginger, ginger beer, lime), a Booze Free G&T (non-alcoholic gin, Roots Divino Blanco, house lemon, rosemary and thyme tonic) that donates $1 to local charities, the Kala Khama (Three Spirit Livener, passionfruit, lemon), the Sherita non-alcoholic passionfruit margarita, the Bucatini, and a St. Agrestis Phony Negroni. Rarest of all, Athletic IPA is poured ON DRAFT at $8 — almost no New York bar does this. Fourteen non-alcoholic spirits are stocked behind the bar. Open from 2pm, to 4am Thursday through Sunday.
venues.longDescription:
Pearl's Social & Billy Club opened on St Nicholas Avenue in Bushwick in June 2011 and marks fifteen years in the community in 2026, which in that neighbourhood makes it an institution. Its own description of what a bar is for is the best sentence any venue in this guide has written about itself: in New York City, our bars are our living rooms — that is exactly how Pearl's was built, a place for everyone, and whether you are on or off the wagon you will find something that hits just right. It is a dive-adjacent local rather than a cocktail destination, open from 2pm and running to 4am from Thursday through the weekend.

The phrase would be marketing at most bars. Here it is backed by a separate, printed Zero Proof menu — a dedicated card, produced in May 2026, not a line at the bottom of the cocktail list. Six named drinks sit on it. The Dark & Stormless rebuilds a Dark and Stormy on Three Spirit Nightcap with fresh ginger, ginger beer and lime. The Booze Free G&T pairs non-alcoholic gin with Roots Divino Blanco and a house-made lemon, rosemary and thyme tonic, and donates a dollar from every one to local charities. Kala Khama runs Three Spirit Livener with passionfruit and lemon; the Sherita is a non-alcoholic passionfruit margarita; the Bucatini uses non-alcoholic Corona with a Lapos aperitif and lemon; and there is a bottled St. Agrestis Phony Negroni. The genuinely rare thing, though, is on the tap list: Athletic IPA on draft at $8. Almost no bar in New York pours non-alcoholic beer from a tap rather than handing over a can, and the difference matters more than it sounds — you get a pint glass, a head on it, and the same ritual as everyone else at the bar. Budweiser Zero, non-alcoholic Corona, Guinness 0, Asahi Dry Zero and Athletic Cerveza fill out the fridge from $5 to $9, and fourteen non-alcoholic spirits sit on the back bar, from Lyre's and Seedlip through Roots Divino, Gnista, Pathfinder and both Three Spirit expressions. One small caveat: the bar's two current PDFs disagree by a dollar on the price of Budweiser Zero.
venues.pressQuote: A broader shortlist highlighted bars with strong NA options citywide, including Sugar Monk, Lobby Bar at Hotel Chelsea, Dante, Pearl's Social & Billy Club, Dynaco, Saint Eve's, Pitts and more.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Time Out New York, NYC's Best Bars for NA Awards 2025

venues.name: Peregrin
venues.description: Peregrin is the rooftop bar on top of the Perry Lane Hotel, an all-weather open-air lounge with a year-round pool, tropical planting and long views over the Historic District. Its drinks list carries a section headed simply MOCKTAILS, four drinks at a flat $12, and every one is built on a named non-alcoholic spirit rather than juice and syrup: Seedlip Garden and Grove, Lyre's alcohol-free brut and aperitivo, Giffard's non-alcoholic elderflower. The beer list adds Athletic Brewing golden ale and IPA at $8. It is open from 11am to 11pm daily, to midnight on Friday and Saturday, which makes it one of the few good zero-proof lists in Savannah available in daylight.
