venues.longDescription:
Planter's House opened in 2013 at the corner of Chouteau and Mississippi in Lafayette Square, the brick-and-mortar home of husband-and-wife bartending team Ted and Jamie Kilgore, who run the bar and restaurant with partner Ted Charak. It has become one of St. Louis' most decorated drinking destinations: in 2019, Planter's House was named a James Beard Award semifinalist for Outstanding Bar Program, a national category. The back bar stocks more than 350 spirits, including 39 Planter's House-exclusive bourbons, ryes and rums, and house originals like the In A Pickle, Industry Sour and Purgatory have become modern St. Louis classics.

The cocktail list includes a dedicated Spirit Free Cocktails section — six zero-proof drinks at $10 apiece, built from a deep bench of NA modifiers. Current selections include Not a Pickle (cucumber-dill Feragaia free spirit, NA elderflower, ginger, orgeat and lime — a name that echoes the house's famous In A Pickle), Bell Tolls (Dhos NA tequila, yellow bell pepper citrate and lemon), Mace of Spades (Feragaia, Giffard NA Spritz, cherry syrup, lime and grapefruit-mace cordial), Rosalita, Pony Club and Under The Grapefruit Moon, which tops Dhos NA gin and Giffard NA Spritz with Nozeco alcohol-free sparkling rosé. The bar also keeps NA orange and aromatic bitters on hand, and St. Louis Magazine's 2025 non-alcoholic guide highlighted a spirit-free NA Negroni as well — a sign the zero-proof list rotates right alongside the leaded menu.

That guide called Planter's House a 'St. Louis institution' where 'knowledgeable bartenders mix exquisite versions of the classics as well as creative drinks unique to the restaurant,' adding that the bar 'also makes mocktails with equal skill and finesse.' Expect a seasonal food menu alongside the drinks — the kitchen runs until 9pm on weeknights and 10pm on Friday and Saturday — with reservations available through Tock. The room opens at 4pm Tuesday through Sunday and holds a 4.6-star rating across more than 80 Tripadvisor reviews, whether you're drinking with alcohol or without.
venues.pressQuote: Planter's House also makes mocktails with equal skill and finesse.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Emily Adams & Mike Miller, St. Louis Magazine

venues.name: Platypus
venues.description: Platypus is the eclectic Grove cocktail bar that Food & Wine named one of the 10 best bars in the country in 2026 — and co-owner Meredith Barry is one of St. Louis's most vocal champions of zero-proof drinking. The chalkboard list of roughly five cocktails rotates constantly, and the NA builds get the same culinary treatment as the boozy ones: recent menus have featured the Flibbertygibbety, with zero-proof tequila, star anise, bitter lemon, and a coffee reduction, and the frozen Jelly of The Month Club made with Ritual rum alternative. Kombucha and NA seltzers round things out amid pinball, live music, karaoke, and comedy nights.
venues.hours: Mon 5pm-1:30am; Tue closed; Wed-Fri 5pm-1:30am; Sat 4pm-1:30am; Sun closed
venues.longDescription:
Platypus opened in late 2021 at the west entrance of The Grove, taking over the former U.R.B. space — Urban Chestnut Brewing Co.'s onetime experimental kitchen — at 4501 Manchester Avenue. Co-owners Meredith Barry and Tony Saputo are both veterans of the St. Louis bar scene: Barry ran the beverage programs at the Angad Arts Hotel's Grand Tavern and ART Bar rooftop, while Saputo worked behind the bars at Wheelhouse, Start Bar, and The Midwestern Meat + Drink. The shotgun-style space unfolds in three connected rooms — a main bar, a pinball-and-booth lounge, and a back-room stage — and the drink list is a chalkboard of roughly five cocktails that changes constantly, a format Feast Magazine reported was designed to encourage staff creativity.

Zero-proof drinking is baked into the bar's DNA. Barry, who has made zero-proof cocktails a personal specialty, told St. Louis Public Radio's St. Louis on the Air that an NA drink should be 'not just a mix of pineapple and cranberry and orange juice, but something that's more elevated,' and STL Barkeep beverage director Patrick Gioia told St. Louis Magazine that 'Platypus and Meredith Barry, in particular, have been a huge piece of the zero-proof cocktail scene.' St. Louis Magazine's guide to nonalcoholic cocktails highlighted the Flibbertygibbety — BARE zero-proof tequila with Sobreo star anise, bitter lemon, coffee reduction, and lemon — and the frozen Jelly of The Month Club, blending spiced blackberry tea, Ritual rum alternative, hibiscus, rooibos, elderberry, currant, and lemon, with Confluence kombucha and NA seltzers rounding out the fridge. Because the board turns over constantly, ask what's zero-proof tonight rather than hunting for a specific drink.

The accolades have stacked up. In Liquor.com's Best of 2023 awards, a national panel of roughly five dozen bartenders named Platypus the country's Best Underrated Bar, and in April 2026 KSDK reported that Food & Wine had named it to a list of the 10 best bars in the entire country, alongside spots from New York, Chicago, and Los Angeles — citing live music, comedy nights, karaoke, monthly queer mixers, and local artwork that feed 'the raucous feel of a neighborhood living room.' Expect exactly that: pinball, DJs, an inclusive crowd, and doors open until 1:30 a.m. every night of the week.
venues.pressQuote: The constantly updated drink menu at this bar in The Grove means every trip is sure to be unique.

venues.name: Pleasant House Pub
venues.description: Pleasant House Pub is the Pilsen all-day pub built around British royal pies - steak and ale, kale and mushroom, chicken balti - in the former Nightwood space on South Halsted Street, open from 10am for coffee and pastry and switching to full-service dinner in the evening. Its drinks list carries a clearly marked NA block with four options: an NA Aperitif Spritz built from a Giffard non-alcoholic aperitif with soda, tonic water and an orange twist at $9; a Proxies Bubbly Red wine alternative with blackberry, raspberry and black tea notes at $11; a Saint Viviana sparkling chardonnay at $13; and a Cann blood orange cardamom at $12, which contains 2mg THC and 4mg CBD per 8oz can and should be avoided by anyone steering clear of cannabinoids.
signatureDrinks: NA Aperitif Spritz (Giffard NA aperitif, soda and tonic water, orange twist)
Proxies Bubbly Red (blackberry, raspberry and black tea notes; wine alternative)

naMenuItems.name: NA - Aperitif Spritz
naMenuItems.description: giffard na aperitif with a spritz of soda and tonic water, orange twist

venues.longDescription:
Pleasant House consolidated its Chicago operation and its Three Oaks, Michigan location into the former Nightwood space on South Halsted Street in Pilsen and turned it into an all-day pub. Time Out described the result as a room where people sit over laptops with their pastries during the day and couples take coffee dates over snacks, with the menu switching to full-service dinner in the evening. The cooking is British: hand-raised royal pies including a savoury steak and ale and a vegetarian kale and mushroom, bubble and squeak on the side, a jar of pickled beets, carrots and gherkins to start, and seasonal fruit trifle to finish.

The drinks list reflects a pub that expects daytime customers as well as evening ones, and the non-alcoholic options are labeled as such rather than left to inference. The NA Aperitif Spritz is the only built drink of the four, made with a Giffard non-alcoholic aperitif lengthened with soda and tonic water and finished with an orange twist at $9 - a genuine bitter aperitivo shape rather than a sweet substitute. Two are wine alternatives: Proxies Bubbly Red at $11, described on the menu as a bright, juicy lambrusco-style pour with blackberry, raspberry and black tea notes and designed specifically to be drunk with wood-fired pizza or a charcuterie board, and a Saint Viviana sparkling chardonnay at $13 with green apple, citrus, honey and brioche notes, sold in cans so it travels. The fourth listed NA item is a Cann blood orange cardamom at $12; it is a tonic rather than an alcoholic drink but it contains 2mg of THC and 4mg of CBD per 8oz can, which the menu states, and it should be avoided by anyone in recovery from any substance or simply not wanting a psychoactive. The pub also pours coffee all day, which is what makes it usable from 10am.
venues.pressQuote: It’s open all day, meaning you’ll find people hunched over tables with computers by their pastries, and couples on coffee dates chatting over snacks.

venues.name: Plot Twist
venues.description: Plot Twist is a woman-owned, all-day coffee and cocktail bar that opened in April 2026 in Plaza Midwood, designed as a true "third space" where guests can move from morning coffee to evening drinks. The beverage program treats mocktails as a first-class option alongside cocktails: every drink is built from a shared base of eight house-made syrups — including ube coconut, brown sugar cardamom, chai, and Thai tea — and can be prepared as a coffee, cocktail, mocktail, or THC-infused drink. Guests who don't drink alcohol can experience the full flavor-forward menu without compromise.
venues.hours: Mon closed; Tue-Thu 7am-10pm; Fri 7am-11pm; Sat 8am-11pm; Sun 8am-9pm
venues.longDescription:
Plot Twist opened in April 2026 at 1518 Lyon Court in Plaza Midwood, and it was built from the start as a third space — somewhere that works at seven in the morning and at ten at night without changing what it is. Co-founder and general manager Nikki Velazquez runs it with Sarah Woods, and the project was deliberately woman-led throughout: not only the leadership team but the designer, the architect and the artists involved. That intent shows in how the day is structured. The doors open at 7am Tuesday through Friday and 8am at weekends, closing at 10pm midweek and 11pm on Friday and Saturday, with Mondays off. There is no point in the day when the room switches from being a cafe to being a bar; the counter simply serves whatever you want at whatever hour you arrive.

What makes it useful to a non-drinker is that the same kitchen work goes into the drinks whether or not they contain alcohol. The bar builds around eight house-made syrups, and those syrups run across the whole range — into the coffee, into the cocktails, into the mocktails and into the dirty sodas, which means a zero-proof order is made from the same components as everything else rather than from a separate shelf of mixers. Dirty sodas are worth calling out as a format, since they are common in Utah and Idaho and still rare in the Southeast: a flavoured soda built with cream and syrup, sweet and substantial, and entirely alcohol-free by nature rather than by substitution. Two honest caveats. Plot Twist does not publish a menu on its website, so the specific drinks rotate and cannot be checked in advance — worth asking what syrups are on when you order. And because it opened recently, the coverage of it is still thin, so the range described here is the shape of the programme rather than a fixed list.
venues.pressQuote: Plot Twist should feel like you're going to your big sister's house.

venues.name: Plume
venues.description: Plume is an Art Deco-inspired cocktail bar in Houston's Heights that treats its non-alcoholic list as a real menu section rather than an afterthought. The current menu carries three built mocktails using genuine zero-proof spirits — Seedlip, Giffard NA Apéritif, and Ritual Zero Proof Whiskey — and CultureMap Houston's Dry January coverage has separately profiled four more named $10 mocktails from the bar's rotating list. It's a full bar first, not an alcohol-free venue, but non-drinking guests get composed drinks rather than a soda-and-lime substitute.
signatureDrinks: Guava Glam Spritz (Seedlip Grove 42, guava, Giffard NA Apéritif, lemon, topped with grapefruit soda)
Tropic Daydream (Seedlip 42, Giffard NA Apéritif, mango, passion fruit, pineapple, topped with Angostura art)
Matcha Mochi Sip (Ritual Zero Proof Whiskey, coconut matcha, honey, egg white)
Naked in Paradise ($10, citrus, coconut cream)
venues.longDescription:
Plume opened July 26, 2024 at 1100 W 23rd St in the Urban Office–West Heights development, the debut project of Golden Ratio Hospitality Group — co-owners Ted Baker (previously of Bobcat Teddy's and Penny Whistle Pub) alongside Dan Braun and James Fitch of Braun Enterprises. Interior designer Bradford Collier of B.W. Collier Interior Design built out the Modern Deco, Hollywood-glam space — the bar's name references an ornamental arrangement of feathers, and the room carries peacock motifs, teal-and-gold finishes, and a climate-controlled patio. It sits in the Shady Acres pocket of the Heights, positioned by its owners as a more intimate, seated alternative to the sports-bar patios along nearby 20th Street.

Plume's own live menu carries a dedicated non-alcoholic cocktail section built on real zero-proof spirits: the Guava Glam Spritz (Seedlip Grove 42, guava, Giffard NA Apéritif, lemon, topped with grapefruit soda), the Tropic Daydream (Seedlip 42, Giffard NA Apéritif, mango, passion fruit, pineapple, topped with Angostura art), and the Matcha Mochi Sip (Ritual Zero Proof Whiskey, coconut matcha, honey, egg white). CultureMap Houston's Dry January coverage separately documented four additional $10 mocktails — the chai-infused cold brew After Glow, the citrus-and-coconut-cream Naked in Paradise, plus Raspberry Dreams and Matcha Palmer — indicating the zero-proof list rotates rather than holding to one fixed set of names.

Alongside the drink program, Plume runs a tapas-style small-bites menu — meatballs in chipotle ragout, bacon-wrapped dates stuffed with stilton, deviled eggs on avocado toast — plus weekly programming that includes Tuesday–Friday happy hour, a Wednesday birria-and-palomas special, a Thursday oyster night, and a Sunday DJ brunch.
venues.pressQuote: Luxuriate in Plume's intimate atmosphere while sipping on the "after glow" ($10), a chai-infused cold brew, or the "naked in paradise" ($10) with citrus and coconut cream. The sweet "raspberry dreams" ($10) and the earthy "matcha Palmer" ($10) round out the mocktail menu.

venues.name: Point 5
venues.description: Point 5 is Richmond's dedicated non-alcoholic bottle shop, on West Cary Street in Carytown, and as of 2026 it is the last one standing in the city — the Fan's Ceremony has closed its Richmond location and moved to Norfolk. Owner Jody Sidle stocks more than 100 brands across zero-proof spirits, non-alcoholic beer and wine, functional drinks, ready-to-drink mocktails and botanical elixirs, which makes it the one place in Richmond where the whole category sits on a shelf to be compared. It is a shop rather than a bar, but it runs tastings, education classes and community events for alcohol-free living, so it functions as the scene's meeting point too.

naMenuItems.name: Le Spritz - Ghia Sumac + Chili (4 Pack)

venues.longDescription:
Point 5 sits on West Cary Street in Carytown, Richmond's most walkable shopping strip, and it was the first dedicated non-alcoholic bottle shop the city had. In 2026 it is also the only one: Ceremony, the Fan district shop that local guides still pair it with, has closed its Richmond location and relocated to Norfolk. That leaves Point 5 carrying the whole retail side of Richmond's alcohol-free scene by itself.

The range is the reason it matters. Owner Jody Sidle stocks north of 100 brands, spanning zero-proof spirits, non-alcoholic beers and wines, functional and adaptogenic drinks, ready-to-drink mocktails and botanical elixirs. That breadth changes what is possible for a non-drinker in a way a supermarket aisle cannot: you can compare three non-alcoholic gins side by side, find out whether a dealcoholised red is worth the money before buying a case, and ask someone who has tasted all of it. For anyone building a home bar without alcohol — which is where most sober drinking actually happens — a shop like this is more useful than any number of bars with a token mocktail.

It also functions as the closest thing Richmond has to a community hub for alcohol-free living. The shop hosts tastings, education classes and events, which gives people a reason to be in the room together rather than simply buying a bottle and leaving. In a city that has just lost both its dedicated alcohol-free bar and its second bottle shop, that social function is doing real work.

There is a wider point buried in Point 5's survival. Dedicated alcohol-free retail is a genuinely difficult business: the margins are thin, the category is young, and the customer base is still forming. Richmond has now lost two alcohol-free businesses in quick succession while this one has held on, which says something about both the fragility of the sector and the value of the shops that make it through. If you care about there being somewhere in your city to buy this stuff in five years, the shops that exist now are the ones worth using.

Practical notes: it is closed Mondays and Tuesdays, opens 11am Wednesday to Saturday and noon on Sunday, and closes early — 6pm at the latest, 5pm on Sundays. Plan it as a daytime stop rather than an evening one, and pair it with the rest of Carytown while you are there; Lolita's is a short walk away.
venues.pressQuote: Carytown's Point 5 offers a rare and refreshing perspective

venues.name: Point Easy
venues.description: Point Easy is a chef-driven New American restaurant in Denver's Whittier neighborhood, opened on June 29, 2022 in the former Whittier Pub space at the corner of East 28th Avenue and Williams Street. The owners are Andy Bruch and brothers Dan and Dennis "Denn" Phelps, alumni of the Kitchen Restaurant Group in Boulder who had developed the concept years before the pandemic delayed it; Denn Phelps, who wrote the opening menu, died unexpectedly on July 22, 2022, weeks after the doors opened, and the team has run the restaurant in his memory since. The kitchen is now led by executive chef Reuben Tomlins, with Richard Long as general manager. The menu is seasonal and farm-driven with a house-made pasta program, and the wine list favours biodynamic and small-producer bottles. The bar keeps a headed 0% ABV section of six drinks on its own published menu, from a fermented pineapple tepache and a Colorado-made non-alcoholic crabapple cider to cocktails built on Dr Zero Zero amaro, Citadel non-alcoholic gin and Giffard elderflower non-alcoholic liqueur, and the bar's Get Fed service will build a drink to a guest's stated preferences.

AmericaNA (Dr Zero Zero amaro, Strongwater aperitif) $9
Ouiser Boudreaux (Citadel non-alcoholic gin, amarena cherries, ginger, rosemary) $10
West of Thomaston (Giffard elderflower non-alcoholic liqueur, lemon, honey) $10
venues.longDescription:
Point Easy opened on June 29, 2022 at 2000 East 28th Avenue in Whittier, taking over a corner that had been the Whittier Pub until 2020 and, for more than thirty years before that, M&D's Cafe. The owners are Andy Bruch and the brothers Dan and Dennis "Denn" Phelps, who had worked together at the Kitchen Restaurant Group in Boulder and had been planning a neighbourhood restaurant of their own since before the pandemic. The conversion turned a dark pub into a bright room with a long bar seating roughly twenty and tables spilling onto a patio. Denn Phelps, who built the opening menu and told Westword during the first week that he has good ideas and silly ideas, died unexpectedly on July 22, 2022 at 37; the restaurant has carried on under Bruch and Dan Phelps, with Reuben Tomlins now executive chef, Marianella Giannini as sous chef and Richard Long as general manager.

The food is seasonal and local-leaning, anchored by a house-made pasta programme, and the wine list runs to biodynamic and smaller-producer bottles chosen by an in-house sommelier. The bar's defining service is Get Fed, in which a guest describes what they like and the bartender builds something to match, and that same posture governs the spirit-free drinks: the restaurant describes them on its own site as spirit-free options that are actually worth ordering, and they are listed with the cocktails rather than in a separate box. The restaurant's own published menu carries a headed 0% ABV section of six drinks, which as of August 2026 runs: a pineapple tepache and soda, fermented and fizzy, at $8; the Haykin Family Cider 'Dolgo Crabapple', a non-alcoholic sparkling cider made in Aurora, at $9; the Pink Gold Peach with grapefruit, lime, non-alcoholic peach bitters and citrus oil at $9; the AmericaNA, built on Dr Zero Zero amaro and the Colorado-made Strongwater aperitif, at $9; the Ouiser Boudreaux with Citadel non-alcoholic gin, amarena cherries, ginger and rosemary at $10; and West of Thomaston, on Giffard elderflower non-alcoholic liqueur with lemon and honey, at $10. A rotating non-alcoholic brew is $5. Because the list turns with the seasons the specific names rotate, but the section itself is standing, and a non-drinker gets the same bartender's-choice treatment as anyone else. The room is small, about twenty seats at the bar plus tables and a patio, and it runs Tuesday through Saturday from 5pm to 9pm only, so it fills. Westword's first-look review picked out a morel mushroom agnolotti at $18 as the dish that set the tone, and 5280 has since written it up as the neighbourhood restaurant of your dreams.
venues.pressQuote: Point Easy strives to serve seasonal, local, and interesting food. That goal carries over into its NA offerings like the 'Pink Gold Peach' (grapefruit, lime, peach bitters (n/a), citrus oil), 'AmericaNA' (Dr. Zero Zero Amaro, Strongwater aperitif), and more.

venues.name: Poka Lola Social Club
venues.description: Poka Lola Social Club is a cocktail bar inside The Maven Hotel at Dairy Block in Denver's LoDo (Lower Downtown) neighborhood, with a concept that blends art-deco elegance and Midwestern soda-shop nostalgia inspired by turn-of-the-century American soda fountain culture. Beverage manager Lexi Parker runs a seasonal cocktail program built around fresh produce — recent menus have featured ingredients like ube, lychee, snap peas, turmeric, and pink peppercorn-infused spirits. The bar maintains a dedicated non-alcoholic cocktail menu on its own website, which turns over with the seasons: the current list runs Water Your Garden (La Borosa non-alcoholic agave spirit, Giffard NA aperitif, herbes de Provence, lemon), Sandy Cheeks (house coconut cream, pineapple, lime), Walking on Sunshine (strawberry, honey, mint, lemon), and Rootin' Tootin' (sarsaparilla, molasses, wintergreen, star anise). The venue features live music, an alley bar that opens for warm-weather seating, and a 'Dealer's Choice' option where the bar crew creates a custom cocktail based on the guest's preferences.

venues.longDescription:
Poka Lola Social Club sits inside The Maven Hotel at Dairy Block, the alley-and-arcade redevelopment between Wazee and Blake in Denver's Lower Downtown. The concept crosses art-deco cocktail-bar polish with turn-of-the-century American soda fountain nostalgia, which shows up in the room's tile, brass and counter seating and in the way the drinks are written. Live music runs on a regular schedule, an alley bar opens for warm-weather seating onto the Dairy Block passage, and the bar offers a Dealer's Choice service where guests hand the bartender a set of preferences and get a custom build back. Beverage manager Lexi Parker runs the programme seasonally, and past menus have leaned on produce that is unusual for a hotel bar: ube, lychee, snap peas, turmeric and pink peppercorn-infused bases among them. The Maven is a boutique hotel, and the bar functions as its ground-floor public room as well as a destination in its own right; service runs to 10pm early in the week and to midnight on Friday and Saturday.

What distinguishes the bar for non-drinkers is that the non-alcoholic list is a fixed section of the published menu with its own drinks, not a set of substitutions. Four are current, all built in-house. Water Your Garden ($12) combines La Borosa non-alcoholic agave spirit and Giffard non-alcoholic aperitif with herbes de Provence and lemon, an unusually savoury opener. Sandy Cheeks ($12) is the tropical option, house coconut cream with pineapple and lime. Walking on Sunshine ($12) runs strawberry, honey, mint and lemon. Rootin' Tootin' ($7) is the bar's own root beer, made from sarsaparilla, molasses, wintergreen and star anise, and priced closer to a soda than a cocktail. A separate N/A Classics line covers ginger beer, tonic and the standard sodas. Visit Denver's December 20, 2025 spirit-free guide grouped the bar under Downtown and noted the seasonally changing options; Westword's January 1, 2026 Dry January round-up covered a rotating January set including a Wrinkle in Thyme with white peach, thyme, cinnamon and white balsamic vinegar, and a Main Squeeze with orange, pineapple, vanilla and cream, alongside a half-price mocktail event. Prices are worth noting because they are unusually low for a downtown hotel bar: the built non-alcoholic cocktails are $12 against a spirited list that runs considerably higher, and the root beer is $7.
venues.pressQuote: You'll find a handful of seasonally changing mocktail options, all made with just as much thought and care as the rest of the drink menu.

venues.name: Polite Provisions
venues.description: Polite Provisions is a craft cocktail bar that opened in 2013 from San Diego hospitality group CH Projects, set in a 1920s apothecary-style room with a long marble bar near the North Park–Normal Heights border. After a closure tied to a liquor-license suspension, it reopened in early 2025 with a reworked menu organized into five sections — including a dedicated "Sans Alcohol" list — under beverage director Alicia Perry. The zero-proof options lean into the bar's housemade-soda and soda-fountain heritage: Daisy's Soda Pop (apple spice, pomegranate, lime, soda) and Gabe's Painless Killer (passionfruit, coconut, pineapple, lime), plus brand-built drinks like a Cinnamon Cherry Cola on Pentire and a Cacao Strawberry on Feragaia, some served as ice cream floats. It carries James Beard and Tales of the Cocktail recognition.
venues.longDescription:
Polite Provisions opened in 2013 from the San Diego hospitality group CH Projects, in a 1920s apothecary-style room with a long marble bar near the North Park and Normal Heights border, and it has carried James Beard and Tales of the Cocktail recognition for most of the time since. After a closure tied to a liquor-licence suspension it reopened in early 2025 with a reworked menu organised into five sections, one of them a dedicated Sans Alcohol list, under beverage director Alicia Perry — who framed the return as bringing back "our new cocktail menu, inclusive of 30 new offerings and a variety of non-spirited options." That a bar of this stature rebuilt its list with a standing zero-proof section rather than a token pair of drinks is the useful signal here.

The zero-proof builds lean directly into the room's soda-fountain heritage, which is the smartest thing about them: an apothecary bar with a housemade-soda tradition already has the technique for good non-alcoholic drinks, and does not need to fake body with sugar. Daisy's Soda Pop combines apple spice, pomegranate and lime with soda; Gabe's Painless Killer works passionfruit, coconut, pineapple and lime into a tiki register. Alongside those sit brand-built drinks — a Cinnamon Cherry Cola on Pentire, and a Cacao Strawberry on Feragaia, the Scottish non-alcoholic botanical spirit — and some of the list is served as ice cream floats, which is both a genuine period detail and a format almost nobody else offers a non-drinking adult. Hours run to 2am seven nights a week, so this functions as a proper late bar rather than an early-evening stop, and a non-drinker can stay for the whole night with something in hand that was made rather than opened. For a bar that has held national recognition for over a decade, that is a meaningful signal about where the category now sits.
venues.pressQuote: We are excited to welcome the neighborhood back to experience our new cocktail menu, inclusive of 30 new offerings and a variety of non-spirited options.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Alicia Perry, Polite Provisions beverage director

venues.name: Polly Bar
venues.description: Polly is one of Melbourne's oldest surviving cocktail bars, a plush, Art Deco-styled room on Brunswick Street in the heart of Fitzroy. Its non-alcoholic offering isn't an afterthought: the menu carries a dedicated printed mocktail section, built with the same attention to flavour that goes into its cocktails, spanning bright-and-fresh through creamy-and-indulgent. Named zero-proof drinks include Summer In Fitzroy, Teas Me, Sassy Lassie and Milk Bar. Polly keeps a dedicated mocktail menu printed below the cocktail list, built with the same attention to flavour the bar gives its cocktails, and running from bright and fresh through to creamy and indulgent.
venues.hours: Mon-Tue closed; Wed-Thu 5pm-12am; Fri 5pm-3am; Sat 2pm-3am; Sun 5pm-12am
venues.longDescription:
Polly opened on Brunswick Street over 25 years ago and is reputed to be the oldest still-surviving cocktail bar in Melbourne — one of the city's first. The room takes its cues from 1920s Paris boudoirs: plush velvety interiors, low lighting, and an atrium out back. The bar team carries decades of combined cocktail experience, and the drinks list runs to more than 20 craft cocktails alongside absinthe, whisky and spirits tastings.

The non-alcoholic program sits as its own printed section on the menu, below the cocktail list. Polly describes its mocktails as "expertly created, with the same attention to flavours that goes into all our cocktail creations," ranging from bright and fresh to creamy and indulgent. The four named house builds are Summer In Fitzroy, Teas Me, Sassy Lassie and Milk Bar — a proper zero-proof list rather than a single token option, which is what makes Polly worth a non-drinker's visit.

Beyond the standing menu, the bartenders will also mix mocktails to taste, and the venue runs cocktail classes, whisky and absinthe tastings, and a high tea with a twist. Open Wednesday through Sunday from 5pm (2pm Saturdays), it's a late-night Fitzroy institution that treats the alcohol-free crowd as more than a compromise.

The bar is explicit about how it treats the alcohol-free list, which is unusual enough to be worth quoting from its own menu: for guests who want to indulge in a non-alcoholic way, Polly says it has a range of mocktails created with the same attention to flavours that goes into all of its cocktail creations, running from bright and fresh through to creamy and indulgent. The mocktails sit below the cocktails on the same menu rather than on a separate card.

That placement is the tell. A bar that prints its zero-proof drinks at the foot of the main list has to keep them current every time the cocktail menu changes; a bar that keeps them on a separate sheet usually does not. Polly is an ornate, low-lit Fitzroy cocktail room on Brunswick Street that trades late — Wednesday and Thursday from 5pm, Friday from 5pm until 3am, Saturday from 2pm until 3am and Sunday from 5pm — which makes it one of the more useful late options for someone who wants the night out without the drinking.

venues.name: Pomona Cafe & Wine Bar
venues.description: Pomona Cafe & Wine Bar opened in July 2026 in East Boston's Maverick Square, an all-day room that pours single-origin Colombian drip and espresso in the morning and turns into a small wine bar at night. It is open 8am to midnight every day of the week, which is unusual for the neighborhood. The drinks list carries a named Mocktails section with three builds: Hugo Libre, a spritz of elderflower, fresh mint, lime juice, non-alcoholic sparkling wine and soda at $15; Corsa, made with non-alcoholic tequila, strawberry, grapefruit, lime, aperitivo and soda water at $14; and Roselle, a raspberry, hibiscus and lemon build at $13. Separate non-alcoholic wine and beer sections list a dealcoholised Loire rose, a German zero sparkling brut and Zero Gravity's Green State Lager Zero.

venues.longDescription:
Pomona Cafe & Wine Bar opened at 18 Meridian Street in Maverick Square in July 2026, and Boston magazine covered it a month later under the headline 'East Boston's New Wine Bar Runs on Colombian Coffee.' The room was hand-built by contractor Elkin Villegas, who was hired as general contractor for the project and ended up its owner mid-build when expansion plans shifted; the East Boston location is loosely affiliated with a Pomona in Swampscott but operates under separate ownership. The name comes from the Roman goddess of orchards and abundance, and the format matches: single-origin Colombian drip and espresso through the day, small plates and clams casino at night, and a room that stays open from 8am to midnight seven days a week.

For a directory reader, the useful part is that the alcohol-free side of the list is built out rather than implied. A Mocktails section names three drinks: Hugo Libre, a spritz of elderflower, fresh mint, lime juice, non-alcoholic sparkling wine and soda at $15; Corsa, a crisp, citrus-forward build of non-alcoholic tequila with strawberry, grapefruit, lime, aperitivo and soda water at $14; and Roselle, a raspberry, hibiscus and lemon drink with botanicals at $13, all priced at or just under the alcoholic cocktails. Beyond the mocktails there are separate Non-Alcoholic Wines and Non-Alcoholic Beer sections, listing a Chavin Zero Rose made from dealcoholised Cinsault, Syrah and Grenache from the Loire Valley, a Dr. Fischer Steinbock Zero sparkling brut, and Zero Gravity's Green State Lager Zero from Vermont. East Boston has very little of this, and a cafe with a real coffee programme, a printed zero-proof list and a midnight close covers most of the reasons someone would want a room in that neighborhood. The room is a short walk from the Maverick stop on the Blue Line, which makes it one of the easier alcohol-free-friendly evening options in the metro to reach from downtown without a car.
venues.pressQuote: East Boston has a new all-day gathering space: Pomona Cafe & Wine Bar opened last month in Maverick Square.

venues.name: Pop's Blue Moon
venues.description: Pop's Blue Moon calls itself "A Mindful Bar," and it has receipts: this century-old tavern on The Hill — built with lumber salvaged from the 1904 World's Fair — pours one of St. Louis' deepest non-alcoholic lineups alongside its regular bar. Owner Joshua Grigaitis launched booze-free New Moon N/A Saturdays back in November 2018, and by 2022 Feast Magazine reported that non-alcoholic options accounted for about 30 percent of sales, from Athletic Brewing and WellBeing beers to some ten varieties of Lyre's zero-proof spirits and his own Cheerz NA seltzers. One honest heads-up: alcohol-free here isn't always substance-free — the bar also serves CBD, CBG and delta-8 THC-infused drinks. Live music keeps the tiny room loud most nights.
signatureDrinks: Cheerz Crème de la Crème seltzer
venues.longDescription:
The building at 5249 Pattison Avenue was framed with lumber salvaged from the 1904 World's Fair, and it has anchored The Hill ever since — three generations of the Gianella family ran the tavern through Prohibition and two World Wars before Terry Grigaitis and his 21-year-old son Josh bought the bar for $100,000 in 1999 and renamed it Pop's Blue Moon. The Riverfront Times has gone as far as calling it St. Louis' oldest continuous bar. Under Josh Grigaitis — a bar-industry lifer who also ran the Cherokee Street nightclub 2720 — the little tavern grew into one of the city's most beloved live-music rooms.

Grigaitis' own decision to step back from drinking reshaped the bar. In November 2018 he launched New Moon N/A Saturday, a fully booze-free bar night with live music that ran weekly and drew coverage from St. Louis Magazine, Feast and the Riverfront Times (call ahead for the current schedule). The non-alcoholic stock is an everyday feature, though: more than 30 NA canned drinks, Athletic Brewing and WellBeing beers, around ten varieties of Lyre's zero-proof spirits, and Grigaitis' own Cheerz NA seltzers in flavors like orange jasmine and purple rose. By October 2022, Feast reported that 30 percent of the bar's sales came from its NA offerings. One honest caveat: Pop's is alcohol-free-friendly, not substance-free — it also pours CBD, CBG and delta-8 THC-infused drinks and has served as a tasting room for local cannabis-beverage brand Mighty Kind.

Sauce Magazine put it plainly, placing Pop's at the forefront of the NA bar movement, and the bar's Instagram bio now reads simply "A Mindful Bar." Expect a genuine dive in the best sense — a tiny, century-old room hung with Italian-American memorabilia, a vinyl record jukebox, and bands packed close to the crowd — where asking for a beer gets you a follow-up question: with alcohol, or without? Doors open Tuesday through Saturday evenings; check the shows calendar before you go.
venues.pressQuote: With over 30 non-alcoholic canned cocktails and a large variety of spirit-free liquors and booze-free beers available, Pop's Blue Moon is at the forefront of the NA bar movement.

venues.name: Port Street Beer House
venues.description: Port Street Beer House is the Northern Quarter's benchmark craft-beer bar, open since 2011 and a cornerstone of Manchester's independent beer scene. Alongside its 18 keg lines, seven cask pumps and hundreds of rotating cans, it keeps a genuinely deep alcohol-free bank rather than a token 0% option — modern, crafty zero-per-cent beers on tap and in the fridge from brewers such as Hawkshead, Jever and Schneider Weisse. It is widely cited as the best place in the city to actually drink a range of good AF beer rather than settle for whatever is left over. Run by the Common & Co group, it treats a well-poured 0.0% with the same seriousness as its cask and keg.
venues.longDescription:
Port Street Beer House opened in 2011 on a quiet side street in the Northern Quarter, launched by Jonny and Charlotte Heyes and the team behind Common bar. It arrived as one of the first venues in Manchester to bring together the full breadth of modern beer — cask, keg and a deep bottle-and-can list — under one roof, and quickly became a cornerstone of the city's craft-beer revival. The same team went on to found the Independent Manchester Beer Convention (Indy Man Beer Con) at Victoria Baths, and the bar now sits within the Common & Co hospitality group alongside The Beagle and The Pilcrow. Two decades of Manchester beer culture run through the place, and it is routinely named among the best beer bars in the country.

The bar itself is small and characterful: a traditional, wood-lined ground-floor room built around the main bar and its bank of taps, a larger and quieter first-floor space upstairs, and a semi-hidden yard at the back that stands in for a beer garden. Behind the bar are 18 keg lines and seven cask hand-pulls, plus fridges and shelves carrying hundreds of rotating bottles and cans from the world's best breweries — anything from a crisp pilsner to a Caribbean chocolate cake stout — as well as a specialist spirits list. Witty branding, genuinely knowledgeable bar staff and a mixed, all-week crowd have made it one of the Northern Quarter's most-loved drinking holes.

Crucially, that same curatorial approach extends to alcohol-free drinking. Rather than the single token 0% lager most pubs keep, Port Street runs a rotating selection of modern, crafty alcohol-free beers on tap and in cans, drawing on brewers such as Hawkshead, Jever — whose Jever Fun is a crisp 0.0% North German pilsner — and Bavaria's Schneider Weisse, known for its alcohol-free wheat beer. Manchester's Finest singles the bar out as the best place to try a proper range rather than the token one many pubs offer, and the local drinks press repeatedly points to it as the city-centre spot for genuinely good AF beer. For anyone who wants the full craft-beer-bar experience — the taps, the room, the specialist knowledge — without the alcohol, it is Manchester's benchmark.
venues.pressQuote: There's always a solid selection of modern, crafty 0% beers on tap and in cans, from breweries like Hawkshead, Jever and Schneider Weisse.

venues.name: Porzana
venues.description: Porzana is Daniel del Prado's Argentinian wood-fire steakhouse in the North Loop, occupying the former Bachelor Farmer space on North 1st Street. It keeps one of the deepest standing spirit-free lists in the city: six non-alcoholic drinks, five of them at $13, listed on the same cocktail menu as the full-strength ones rather than tucked away. The house builds are the Sanguino, with blood orange, white chocolate, rhubarb, elderflower, lime and sparkling tea, and the Serrata, with blackberry, hibiscus, beet, Greek yogurt and lemon. A tarragon and verde tea drink called T&T, two Copenhagen sparkling teas and a dealcoholised sparkling rose complete the section.

venues.longDescription:
Porzana took the North Loop corner at 200 North 1st Street that the Bachelor Farmer had made famous, and reopened it as an Argentinian wood-fire steakhouse under Daniel del Prado, the chef behind Martina, Rosalia and a string of other Twin Cities rooms. The kitchen runs prime Argentinian cuts and A5 wagyu over live fire, with handmade pasta, crudo and a raw bar; the sweetcorn agnolotto became the dish the city argued about after it opened. It is a steakhouse in the full sense, which usually implies a wine-first drinks programme and a token spirit-free line at the bottom of the page. That is not what happens here.

The non-alcoholic section on Porzana's own cocktail menu carries six entries, all but one priced at $13 — the same order of magnitude as the full-strength cocktails, which is the clearest signal a bar can send about how seriously it takes the category. The two house builds are the most involved. The Sanguino layers blood orange, white chocolate, rhubarb, elderflower and lime over sparkling tea, using the tea to supply the tannin and length that a spirit would normally carry. The Serrata goes the other way, into savoury and sour: blackberry, hibiscus, beet, Greek yogurt and lemon, with the yogurt giving weight and the beet doing the earthy work. T&T is built on tarragon, verde tea, cacao and lime zest lengthened with tonic. Beyond the house drinks, the list carries two Copenhagen sparkling teas — the Lysegron with lemongrass, earl grey, green apple and citrus, and the Bla with jasmine, black tea, green tea and citrus — and a $16 pour of Woody's dealcoholised sparkling rose for anyone who wants something to toast with. Dinner runs nightly, with weekend brunch on Saturday and Sunday mornings. One practical note for a non-drinker booking here: the spirit-free drinks live inside the cocktail menu rather than on a separate card, so there is no need to ask for a different list at the table. Reservations are effectively necessary at dinner; the bar takes a smaller number of walk-ins, and the full non-alcoholic list is available there as well as in the dining room.
venues.pressQuote: This modern Argentinian steak house from Chef Daniel del Prado serves everything from decadent pastas to tuna crudo and the star of the show: wood-fired wagyu steaks.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Meet Minneapolis, Best Mocktails in Minneapolis

venues.name: Post Haste
venues.description: Post Haste is a farm-to-glass cocktail bar and restaurant that opened in June 2023 at 2519 Frankford Ave in Philadelphia's East Kensington neighborhood, led by beverage director Fred Beebe and director of operations Gabe Guerrero. Its defining conceit is hyper-regional sourcing: every spirit, beer, wine, herb, and mixer comes from east of the Mississippi River. That same craft extends to a dedicated "Free Spirit" zero-proof section, where the bar builds non-alcoholic cocktails with as much intent as the full-proof list. Current spirit-free pours include the Tea El See (Charleston black tea, condensed oat milk, allspice, cardamom, pandan, and Ritual non-alcoholic aperitivo), the Holy Negroni, and Peachy Keen. Post Haste was named to Esquire's Best Bars in America 2024, one of two Philadelphia bars on that year's list. NA cocktails run $12–$14.
venues.longDescription:
Post Haste opened in June 2023 at 2519 Frankford Avenue in East Kensington, led by beverage director Fred Beebe and director of operations Gabe Guerrero, and its organising idea is hyper-regional sourcing: every spirit, beer, wine, herb and mixer comes from east of the Mississippi River. That constraint is the whole personality of the bar, and it is a demanding one — it rules out agave from Mexico, most citrus, and the great majority of the imported bottles a cocktail list normally leans on.

What makes the bar relevant here is that the same discipline extends to a dedicated zero-proof section headed "Free Spirit", built with the same intent as the full-proof list rather than as a concession bolted on at the end. A bar working under a sourcing constraint has already had to become good at building flavour from what is available rather than from what is conventional, and that skill transfers directly to making a drink without alcohol — both problems are the same problem, which is how to construct depth when the obvious ingredient is off the table.

The Tea El See is the clearest expression of it: Charleston black tea with condensed oat milk, allspice and cardamom. Tea supplies tannin, which is the astringency that gives a drink structure and stops it reading as sweet — the same compound that makes red wine feel dry. Condensed oat milk brings body and sweetness in one ingredient, and allspice and cardamom provide the warm aromatic top notes that would otherwise come from a barrel-aged spirit. It is a drink built the way a bartender builds, from tannin, fat, sugar and aromatics, rather than assembled from juices.

The farm-to-glass framing means the list moves with what is growing, so the specific pours rotate. Open Wednesday to Saturday from five in the evening until midnight, and Sunday until ten; closed Monday and Tuesday.
venues.pressQuote: Each and every libation is made only with ingredients from the East Coast

venues.name: Post Office Place
venues.description: Opened in June 2018 by Takashi and Tamara Gibo — the team behind the acclaimed Takashi sushi next door — Post Office Place is an intimate craft cocktail bar that shares an entrance with the restaurant on Market Street. Known for a deep Japanese whisky list and a James Beard Foundation Outstanding Bar Program semifinalist nod in 2023, it also keeps one of the most thorough printed non-alcoholic menus in Salt Lake City. The dedicated NA menu itemizes a bottled St. Agrestis Phony Negroni, Athletic NA beers, Gruvi Sparkling Rosé, and build-your-own zero-proof cocktails on Spiritless (Kentucky 74, Jalisco 55), Dhōs Gin, and Monday Zero whisky — plus a bespoke "Bartender Roulette" the team crafts to order. In 2026 the bar was named Salt Lake magazine's Best Restaurant alongside its Takashi omakase collaboration.

venues.longDescription:
Post Office Place launched on June 19, 2018, in part to give Takashi diners a place to enjoy a pre-dinner drink while waiting for a table, since Utah liquor law only allows cocktails once seated. It quickly earned national attention: in January 2023 the James Beard Foundation named it a semifinalist for Outstanding Bar Program, a list of the best bars in the United States.

In 2025 it deepened its partnership with chef Takashi Gibo's flagship, launching a weekly omakase serving monthly-changing dishes per seating. That collaboration earned the pairing Salt Lake magazine's Best Restaurant of 2026 honor.
venues.pressQuote: Between a bed of noodles knotted by hand, to salted cherry blossoms and habanero kosho delicately balanced on top of nigiri, each bite is carefully assembled.

venues.name: Postino WineCafe
venues.description: Postino WineCafe is a regional wine-bar chain founded in Phoenix's Arcadia neighborhood in 2001 by Craig and Kris DeMarco (Upward Projects), known for its approachable wine list, bruschetta boards, and "Board + Bottle" deals. The South Lamar location — Postino's Austin South Lamar outpost — opened November 9, 2024, near the Saxon Pub. In January 2025, Postino introduced a five-drink zero-proof cocktail menu across all its locations, its first dedicated non-alcoholic cocktail program: the Glow-Up (cucumber, mint, lime, ginger beer), the Espresso Flirtini (spiced cane, hazelnut, espresso), the Mockingbird (pineapple, Italian orange, toasted almond bitters), the Unfashioned (honey, bitters, amaro), and the Naked Ranch Water (lime and soda). The full-service wine bar pairs these with its small-plates menu, 12-plus bruschetta varieties, and an extensive wine and beer list.
venues.address: 1301 S Lamar Blvd, Ste 102, Austin, TX 78704
venues.longDescription:
Postino WineCafe is a regional chain founded in Phoenix's Arcadia neighbourhood in 2001 by Craig and Kris DeMarco under Upward Projects, built on an approachable wine list, bruschetta boards and Board + Bottle deals. The South Lamar location opened on 9 November 2024, near the Saxon Pub.

In January 2025 Postino added a five-drink zero-proof cocktail menu across every location — its first dedicated non-alcoholic programme. A chain rolling out a zero-proof list company-wide is a different kind of signal from an independent bar doing it: it means the demand has been measured rather than guessed, and it means the drinks are standardised, so what you get in Austin is what the group signed off on rather than whatever the bartender improvises.

The five are the Glow-Up (cucumber, mint, lime, ginger beer), the Espresso Flirtini (spiced cane, hazelnut, espresso), the Mockingbird (pineapple, Italian orange, toasted almond bitters), the Unfashioned (honey, bitters, amaro) and the Naked Ranch Water (lime and soda). Two of those deserve attention. The Mockingbird and the Unfashioned both use bitters, and the Unfashioned uses amaro — bitterness being the quality that most reliably makes a drink read as adult rather than as a soft drink, and the one most zero-proof menus skip.

A wine bar is a particular kind of challenge for a non-drinker, because wine is the entire premise and there is no equivalent of ordering a beer instead. Having five named, properly built drinks on the menu means you order from the same list as everyone else rather than negotiating, and the small-plates and bruschetta format means the evening is about the table rather than the bottle.

Open from 11am on weekdays and 10am at weekends, to 11pm or midnight. One practical note: the zero-proof list is the same at every Postino, so if it works for you here it will work at any of them — which for a chain is the whole point, and is worth knowing if you travel.

venues.name: Posto
venues.description: Posto is chef Joe Cassinelli's Neapolitan pizzeria and enoteca, which moved from Davis Square to a larger room at Assembly Row in Somerville in November 2024 after thirteen years on Elm Street. Wood-fired pizza, house pasta and grilled meats sit alongside a long wine list and, notably, a printed 'Zero Proof - Alcohol Free' section of eight drinks. Six are built on non-alcoholic spirits at $15, matching the cocktail price: an N/A-perol Spritz on non-alcoholic Mionetto aperitivo and N/A sparkling wine, an Espress-No Martini on Fluere spiced cane with dark roast espresso and cream, a No-Groni and a Faux Mule on non-alcoholic Amsterdam Damrak, a No-jito, and a Tilden Spritz. Two simpler spritzes are $8.

venues.longDescription:
Posto opened on Elm Street in Davis Square in 2009 and became one of Somerville's fixtures before chef and owner Joe Cassinelli moved the restaurant to Assembly Row in November 2024, closing the Davis Square room after thirteen years and taking over the much larger former Frank space at 400 Assembly Row. The new site combines a full-service dining room with a takeout market and cafe, and the cooking remains what it was: wood-fired Neapolitan-inspired pizza, hand-made pasta, grilled meat and fish, and a deep glass list. A second Posto operates in the South End.

What makes the Assembly Row room worth a listing here is a drinks menu that carries a section headed 'Zero Proof - Alcohol Free' and treats it as a peer of the cocktail list rather than a concession. Six of the eight drinks are $15, the same as the house cocktails, and are built on genuine non-alcoholic spirits: the N/A-perol Spritz on non-alcoholic Mionetto aperitivo with N/A sparkling wine, the Espress-No Martini on Fluere non-alcoholic spiced cane with dark roast espresso and cream, the No-Groni on non-alcoholic Amsterdam Damrak with non-alcoholic bitters and bubbles, the No-jito on Fluere spiced cane with lime, mint syrup and bubbles, the Faux Mule on Damrak with rosemary syrup, lime and ginger beer, and a Tilden Spritz using the Lacewing base with cucumber, basil, lychee, juniper, a non-alcoholic Szechuan pepper extract, lime and bubbles. Two lighter builds, a Blood Orange Spritz and a Raspberry Spritz, are $8. Meet Boston listed Posto in its January 2026 guide to zero-proof drinks in the city. Cassinelli's group also runs a second Posto in the South End and Posto Mobile, a wood-fired pizza truck. The Assembly Row room serves weekday lunch from 11:30am and weekend brunch from 10am, with dinner to 10pm on weeknights and 11pm on Friday and Saturday, and the zero-proof section is available across all of those services.
venues.pressQuote: Posto's zero-proof beverages favor balance and restraint, often built from fresh juices, house infusions, and subtle herbal elements.

venues.name: Potluck Teahouse
venues.description: Potluck Teahouse is a fully alcohol-free teahouse and working pottery studio on Gallatin Pike in Inglewood, East Nashville, and it describes itself as the city's only pottery studio-teahouse. The tea list is a curated selection rather than a house blend: single-origin and blended leaf from High Garden, the original East Nashville teahouse whose signature blends Potluck deliberately carries on; from Tea for Tea, blended locally in Nashville; and from Spirit Tea in Chicago. Pours run to Rose Garden Grey, Sun Drenched, Bee's Knees, Garden Party Green, Kodama Sencha and Lapsang Souchong, all $4.50. The room doubles as a gallery for local pottery and goods, and the studio runs public workshops - wheel throwing, handbuilding, matcha-set classes with a tasting. No alcohol is served.

signatureDrinks: Rose Garden Grey - earl grey with orange peel, rose and lavender buds $4.50
Sun Drenched - Dooars estate assam, lemon verbena, spearmint, dried oranges $4.50
Bee's Knees - green earl grey, jasmine green tea, lemon verbena, rose petals, dried oranges and lavender $4.50
Garden Party Green - organic earl grey green, jasmine green, rose petals and honeysuckle blossoms $4.50
Black Current Earl Grey - blackcurrant and bergamot with cornflower petals $4.50
Kodama Sencha - Japan, toasted nori, sesame and honeydew $4.50
Lapsang Souchong - smoke-dried black tea, smoke and pine $4.50
venues.longDescription:
Potluck opened on the Inglewood stretch of Gallatin Pike with a question rather than a business plan: how to strengthen the connection between Nashville artists and the people who live around them. The answer was to put a working pottery studio and a teahouse in the same room. One half is a quiet space for tea, with shelves of art, pottery and goods from local makers for sale; the other is a studio where members work and where the public can watch the making happen through the glass. The studio runs workshops for anyone - intro to wheel throwing, morning mugs, ceramic wind chimes, and a handbuilding class where you make a matcha set and then taste matcha with it. For a city with very few evening options that are not bars, a teahouse you can also make something in is a genuinely different proposition.

The tea itself is bought in rather than blended in house, and the sourcing is the point. The largest section is High Garden, the East Nashville teahouse whose blends a generation of the neighbourhood grew up on; Potluck says plainly that it wanted to honour the original East Nashville teahouse and carries its signature blends for that reason. Tea for Tea, blended locally in Nashville, supplies black, green and herbal blends. Spirit Tea, out of Chicago, supplies the single-origin leaf for anyone who wants to drink something more particular. Everything on the leaf list is $4.50.

Worth ordering: Rose Garden Grey, an earl grey lifted with orange peel, rose and lavender buds; Sun Drenched, a Dooars estate assam with lemon verbena, spearmint and dried oranges, which the menu says is best iced; Bee's Knees, a green earl grey with jasmine, lemon verbena, rose petals, dried oranges and lavender, also best iced; and Lapsang Souchong for anyone who wants smoke and pine. On the single-origin side there is Kodama Sencha from Japan, with toasted nori and honeydew notes, and Morning Mist from China. No alcohol is served. The shop is closed on Mondays and shuts at 6pm the rest of the week, 4pm on Sunday, so plan it as an afternoon.
venues.pressQuote: Our teahouse offers a quiet, cozy space to enjoy thoughtfully sourced teas

venues.name: Prazbar
venues.description: CHECK BEFORE YOU TRAVEL — this listing has changed. Prāzbar is a faith-based, fully non-alcoholic wine project founded by Quenjana Adams, which began as pop-ups in Bronzeville and West Town in late 2021 and opened a permanent shop, "2048", at 2048 W Chicago Ave in September 2023, named for its address. As of September 2026 we still cannot confirm that shop is still trading: every one of its own web properties is dead (2048chi.com no longer resolves, prazbar.org and both of its Square storefronts return 404), prazbar.com forwards to a ticket page for a one-off fashion event at a different venue, and no opening hours have been publishable since 2023. What is definitely active is the brand. Adams posts regularly, and in June 2026 announced that Prāzbar is building a permanent music venue for faith-genre live music in Chicago — writing that the team has spent several years producing live faith and music events in the city and that "today, we are building that home." Treat Prāzbar for now as an alcohol-free events producer with a venue in development. The wines it pours are all between 0% and 0.5% ABV.
venues.longDescription:
Quenjana Adams started Prāzbar in late 2021, after years of thinking about how best to serve non-drinkers in her faith community. It ran first as wine pop-ups and tastings around Chicago — Bronzeville, then West Town — for about eighteen months. Then, walking past an empty storefront at 2048 West Chicago Avenue near where she lived, she approached the owner about taking it over. The space came with a huge "2048" sign already in the front window, which is why the shop opened under that name rather than hers in September 2023. Her reason for doing it at all is the best short statement of the case we have found: she had not seen a wine bar, or a wine shop, that was exclusive to non-alcoholic wine, and she likes to stand out, so she said let's do this. Everything poured is between 0% and 0.5% ABV. She has also described the position she occupies with unusual honesty — that she finds herself on a very thin line between being part of the sober movement and simply being a safe space for people who do not drink.

What we cannot tell you is whether the shop is open today, and it would be dishonest to imply otherwise. Three separate web properties belonging to it are dead: 2048chi.com no longer resolves at all, and both Square storefronts return 404. The prazbar.com domain now forwards visitors to a ticketing page for a single fashion event at an unrelated venue. No hours have been publishable since the 2023 opening notice. Against that, the brand itself is plainly alive — Adams was posting in July 2026, and in June 2026 she announced that Prāzbar is building a permanent music venue in Chicago dedicated to faith-genre live music, writing that after several years of producing live faith and music events in the city, that music and the people who love it deserve a permanent home, and that today they are building it. Read together, the most likely picture is a project that has moved from retail into events while it develops a room of its own. If you are travelling for the wine shop, contact them first. If you are looking for alcohol-free nights out with a faith community in Chicago, follow the newsletter — that is where the next thing will be announced.
venues.pressQuote: I hadn't seen a wine bar, or a wine shop, that was exclusive to non-alc wine. And I like to stand out.

venues.name: Press 626 Wine Bar
venues.description: Press 626 is a wine bar and cafe in a converted Ghent house, and its non-alcoholic offering is a set of Garden Lemonade Spritzers built in three variations — lavender rosemary, chamomile orange, and pomegranate sage. Herb-and-flower pairings like those are a deliberate choice rather than a default: they give a soft drink aromatic complexity and a dry finish, which is exactly what is missing when you take wine off the table. In a venue where the entire proposition is wine, having a considered alternative on the printed list is the difference between a guest being catered for and being tolerated.
venues.hours: Mon closed; Tue-Wed 11am-10pm; Thu-Sat 11am-11pm; Sun closed
venues.longDescription:
Press 626 occupies a converted house on West Olney Road in Ghent, Norfolk's most walkable neighbourhood, and trades as a wine bar and cafe with a garden. Wine bars are among the hardest rooms for a non-drinker, because unlike a cocktail bar there is no technique to fall back on — the entire menu is one product, and removing it leaves very little.

Press 626's answer is a set of Garden Lemonade Spritzers in three variations: lavender rosemary, chamomile orange, and pomegranate sage. The pairings are the interesting part. Each combines a floral or herbal element with a fruit, which is how you build aromatic complexity into a drink without alcohol — lavender and rosemary in particular are strongly perfumed and slightly bitter, so they push a lemonade away from sweetness and toward something that finishes dry. That is precisely the quality wine provides and sugar destroys.

Three variations also constitutes a choice rather than a token. A single house mocktail tells a non-drinker they were an afterthought; three options in a named format tells them somebody sat down and worked on it, which in a wine bar is a more meaningful gesture than it would be in a cocktail room.

The garden is the other draw, and it makes this an easy afternoon rather than an evening-only stop — the bar opens at 11am. Hours are limited at the ends of the week: closed Sunday and Monday, to 10pm on Tuesday and Wednesday, 11pm Thursday through Saturday. It sits within a short walk of Ghent's main strip and a few minutes from Ceremony in Chelsea. For an afternoon rather than an evening, the garden here is among the most pleasant places in Norfolk to sit without a drink in hand.
venues.pressQuote: Press 626: "Garden Lemonade Spritzers" with lavender rosemary, chamomile orange, or pomegranate sage.

venues.name: Prima Dopo
venues.description: A Fells Point "cucina and cocktail house" on Thames Street serving contemporary Italian small plates, artisan pizza and house-made pasta until 2 a.m. on weekends. Its main menu boxes out a dedicated Mocktails section beside the cocktail list, built on real non-alcoholic spirits rather than juice: My Cousin Dill combines Seedlip Grove 42 with cucumber puree, lemon, agave, dill and soda, and Le Moxie mixes Seedlip Spice 94 with strawberry puree, lemon, agave, rosemary and ginger ale. The third pour, Cafe Kinda Dopo, is a cold brew with brown sugar simple syrup and oat milk — a zero-proof mirror of the bar's Casamigos-spiked Cafe Dopo. All three are $12, in line with the house cocktails.
signatureDrinks: My Cousin Dill (Seedlip Grove 42, cucumber purée, lemon, agave, dill, soda) $12
Le Moxie (Seedlip Spice 94, strawberry purée, lemon, agave, rosemary, ginger ale) $12
Cafe Kinda Dopo (cold brew, brown sugar simple syrup, oat milk) $12
venues.longDescription:
Prima Dopo opened in January 2023 at 1724 Thames Street in Fells Point, from restaurateur Dominic Lascola, in a building with a working past — dating to the 1800s, the property was once a barn that stabled horses and later garaged cars, and it sits between Thames Street Oyster House and The Daily Grind on one of Baltimore's most walked waterfront blocks. It calls itself a cucina and cocktail house, and the hours back that up: it serves until midnight early in the week and until 2am on Thursday, Friday and Saturday, which makes it one of the few kitchens in the city still cooking properly late. The menu runs crab toast with garlic herb butter at $18, meatballs with lemon whipped ricotta and pistachio at $18, a spicy salami pizza with hot honey at $26, spaghetti carbonara at $28 and a table-side chicken parm at $32.

The non-alcoholic drinks sit under a printed "Mocktails" heading and all three are $12 — the same as the low end of the cocktail list rather than priced as soft drinks. Two are built on Seedlip and one is not, which gives the list more range than three drinks usually manages. My Cousin Dill uses Seedlip Grove 42, the citrus expression, with cucumber purée, lemon, agave, dill and soda; The Baltimore Banner picked it out as a refreshing take when it surveyed the city's mocktails, and it is the one to order with something rich. Le Moxie works Seedlip Spice 94 against strawberry purée with lemon, agave, rosemary and ginger ale — warmer and more aromatic. Cafe Kinda Dopo is the after-dinner option, a cold brew built with brown sugar simple syrup and oat milk, and it is genuinely vegan rather than incidentally so. The menu is current as of August 2026. Note the restaurant adds a 3% fee to card payments, removed if you pay cash, and a 20% gratuity to parties of eight or more.
venues.pressQuote: This buzzy Fells Point cocktail house has some solid NA options. Check out the My Cousin Dill, a green-colored libation featuring Seedlip, lemon, dill, and cooling cucumber puree.

venues.name: Prime 131
venues.description: Prime 131 is Berg Hospitality's live-fire steakhouse, sushi bar, and Korean-BBQ concept in Houston's Lazybrook/Timbergrove neighborhood, named Best Steakhouse in Houston Press's 2024 Best of Houston awards and one of CultureMap's 12 best new restaurants of 2024. Its bar carries four signature zero-proof mocktails priced around $10-$12, on par with many of the restaurant's alcoholic cocktails rather than as an afterthought; confirmed builds include the Strawberry Rose Refresher and the Kosnopolitan. It remains a full-bar restaurant first, so this is a solid named NA list, not an alcohol-free destination.
venues.hours: Mon closed; Tue-Thu 4pm-10pm; Fri-Sat 4pm-11pm; Sun closed
venues.longDescription:
Prime 131 opened in 2024 in Houston's Lazybrook/Timbergrove neighbourhood as a Berg Hospitality Group concept. The live-fire steakhouse and sushi bar puts a wood-burning grill in the middle of the dining room, with a shareable menu spanning prime and wagyu steaks, Japanese sushi and Korean-barbecue tabletop grilling. Recognition came quickly: CultureMap Houston named it one of the city's twelve best new restaurants of 2024, and Houston Press awarded it Best Steakhouse in its 2024 Best of Houston awards, describing a room that evokes the high-energy late-nineties dining scene of New York's Meatpacking District, with an open kitchen showing four wood-fire grills and stadium seating.

For guests skipping alcohol, the bar carries four signature mocktails at roughly $10 to $12 — the same tier as many of the restaurant's classic cocktails. Two are confirmed by name, the Strawberry Rose Refresher and the Kosnopolitan, both of which surface in Houston Dry January round-ups.

The detail worth knowing is that this list is shared across Berg Hospitality's restaurants, appearing identically at sister venue Turner's Cut. That sounds like a corporate shortcut and is in fact an advantage for a non-drinker. A zero-proof menu built by one enthusiastic bartender disappears when that bartender leaves; a list documented and trained across a restaurant group is one where the recipes exist on paper, the ingredients are ordered centrally, and any bartender on shift can make the drink correctly. Consistency is the thing most often missing from non-alcoholic drinks — the same order arriving differently on different nights — and a group programme is the most reliable fix for it.

Prime 131 is not an alcohol-free venue; it runs a full bar and wine list alongside these drinks. But the mocktails are a standing part of the beverage programme rather than a Dry-January-only gesture, which is the distinction that matters when you are booking a table in June.

As of mid-2026 it keeps dinner-only hours, four in the afternoon onward Tuesday through Saturday and to eleven at weekends, closed Sunday and Monday — reflecting a reservation-driven, special-occasion format.
venues.pressQuote: The showstopping live-fire steakhouse evokes the high-energy vibes of the late '90s dining scene of NYC's Meatpacking District, with an open kitchen showcasing its four wood-fire grills, bumping music and main dining room with stadium seating so everyone can catch the show.

venues.name: Proof on Main
venues.description: Proof on Main is the restaurant and bar of the 21c Museum Hotel on West Main Street, open since 2006 and a fixture of Louisville dining, with a bar holding more than 75 Kentucky bourbons. Its non-alcoholic programme is among the deepest in the city and is built on stock rather than improvisation: the bar carries the full Lyre's range plus Spiritless Kentucky 74 and Jalisco 55, the Louisville-made non-alcoholic bourbon and tequila, and NKD LDY de-alcoholised gin, and it makes its own ginger ale and tonic water in house. Effectively anything on the cocktail list can be built alcohol-free, and the bar also understands half-measures for anyone reducing rather than stopping.
signatureDrinks: Any cocktail on the list built alcohol-free with Lyre's, Kentucky 74 or Jalisco 55
venues.longDescription:
21c Museum Hotel put a contemporary art museum inside a hotel on West Main Street in 2006 and changed how downtown Louisville worked; Proof on Main is its restaurant, and two decades on it remains one of the city's defining dining rooms. The cooking is Southern and Appalachian with a farm-to-table backbone — Cody Stone, part of the original 2005 sous chef team, returned as executive chef after running the kitchen at Decca in NuLu — and the bar holds more than seventy-five Kentucky bourbons.

What makes it the most capable non-alcoholic bar in Louisville is inventory. Most bars that advertise zero-proof drinks own one bottle; Proof on Main carries the entire Lyre's range, which covers the gin, whiskey, amaretto, orange and aperitif positions, plus Spiritless Kentucky 74 and Jalisco 55 — the non-alcoholic bourbon and tequila made here in Louisville — and NKD LDY de-alcoholised gin. With that behind the bar, the claim that anything on the cocktail list can be made without alcohol is a statement about stock rather than a promise to improvise something. The bar also makes its own ginger ale and tonic water, which is the detail that separates a good non-alcoholic drink from a decent one: the mixer is usually where these drinks fall apart. And it will build 'halfsies' — part non-alcoholic spirit, part alcoholic — which is a genuinely useful option for people moderating rather than abstaining, and one very few bars offer without making it awkward.

Practically: this is a hotel restaurant on Museum Row, so it runs consistent hours across the day and takes solo diners at the bar without fuss, which is not true of most of the destination rooms in this guide. It sits six blocks west of Barrel Bar & Grill on Whiskey Row, the other downtown entry pouring Kentucky 74, so the two make an obvious pair for anyone wanting to drink the Louisville non-alcoholic story rather than read about it. One caveat on sourcing: the claim that anything on the list can be built alcohol-free comes from The Zero Proof's Louisville city guide rather than from a printed menu, and that guide has proved stale elsewhere in this city — it still lists Nostalgic Cocktail House, which closed in July 2024. The bottles it describes are consistent with multiple sources and with the bar's own positioning, but the sensible approach is to say what you would normally order and let the bartender build it, rather than arriving expecting a printed zero-proof section.
venues.pressQuote: Everything on their list can be made non-alcoholic, and they carry the entire line of Lyre's to do that.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: The Zero Proof, Louisville city guide

venues.name: Proper Bar at Proper Eats (Aria)
venues.description: Proper Bar is the central full-service bar inside Proper Eats Food Hall, the 24,000-square-foot, chef-driven food hall on the Promenade Level of ARIA Resort & Casino, operated by Clique Hospitality. Alongside its beer, wine, and cocktail list, the bar has run a crafted non-alcoholic agave program built around Almave, the zero-proof blue-agave "tequila" co-created by Formula 1 champion Lewis Hamilton, including the Golden Hour Margarita (Almave Blanco, fresh lime, prickly pear syrup, agave nectar), the Blanco Paloma (Almave Blanco, fresh grapefruit and lime, Squirt), and the Ámbar Carajillo (Almave Ámbar, cold brew, agave nectar, aromatic bitters). These crafted zero-proof drinks were highlighted as a Dry January feature rather than a permanent year-round menu. Standing non-alcoholic choices at the bar include Fever-Tree sodas, fresh-pressed juices, Perrier, and Red Bull, and the surrounding food hall offers coffee, donuts, and other vendors for non-drinkers. The food hall is open daily from 7:00 AM, making the bar an accessible Strip option for an alcohol-free order.
venues.address: 3730 S. Las Vegas Blvd, Las Vegas, NV 89158

Blanco Paloma (Almave Blanco, fresh grapefruit & lime juice, Squirt)
Ámbar Carajillo (Almave Ámbar, cold brew coffee, agave nectar, aromatic bitters)
venues.longDescription:
Proper Bar is the central full-service bar of Proper Eats Food Hall, the 24,000-square-foot food hall that Clique Hospitality opened in the winter of 2022 in the space ARIA's buffet used to occupy, on the resort's second-level promenade. The room was designed by the Italian designer Munge, and the roster was curated by Clique founder Andy Masi together with culinary director Jason McLeod and Oliver Wharton of A Perfect Bite. It launched with twelve dining concepts, several of them making their first appearance outside their home cities: Seoul Bird's first location outside London, Wexler's Deli's first outside Los Angeles, San Diego's Temaki Bar, New York's breakfast-focused Egghead, and Steve Aoki's Pizzaoki. The bar sits in the middle of all of it, and because the hall opens at 7am daily it is one of the earliest places on the Strip to get a properly made drink of any kind.

Its non-alcoholic work has been built around Almave, the zero-proof blue-agave distillate co-created by the Formula 1 champion Lewis Hamilton, in three crafted builds: the Golden Hour Margarita (Almave Blanco, fresh lime, prickly pear syrup, agave nectar), the Blanco Paloma (Almave Blanco, fresh grapefruit and lime, Squirt), and the Ambar Carajillo (Almave Ambar, cold brew coffee, agave nectar, aromatic bitters). One honest caveat belongs on that list: those drinks were promoted as a Dry January feature rather than as a permanent year-round menu, so it is worth asking at the bar rather than assuming they are pouring in July. What is always available is a reliable set of standing non-alcoholic choices — Fever-Tree sodas, fresh-pressed juices, Perrier and Red Bull — and the surrounding hall covers the rest, with coffee, donuts and a dozen kitchens that make it an easy place to spend an evening without ordering alcohol at all.

venues.name: Providence Oyster Bar
venues.description: Providence Oyster Bar sits on Atwells Avenue in the middle of Federal Hill, the city's Italian quarter, doing raw bar and seafood. Its non-alcoholic list runs to a blood orange nojito and an alcohol-free Italian spritz — two builds that suit both the shellfish and the neighbourhood. Named on the Providence tourism board's own mocktail guide.

venues.longDescription:
Atwells Avenue is the spine of Federal Hill, Providence's historic Italian neighbourhood, marked at its entrance by the bronze pinecone hanging over the arch at DePasquale Square. Providence Oyster Bar sits in the middle of it, which makes it an unusual thing — a serious raw bar in a district built on red sauce — and it has held that position for years on the strength of its shellfish.

For a non-drinker the room offers two documented builds, and both are chosen well for the setting. The blood orange nojito takes the mojito's mint-and-lime frame and swaps in blood orange, which gives it enough bitterness to work against oysters rather than fighting them. The Italian spritz is the alcohol-free rendering of the drink the neighbourhood runs on — the bittersweet orange aperitif style that every table on Atwells drinks in summer — and having it available without alcohol on this particular street is a genuinely useful thing.

Two constructed drinks rather than a printed section puts this at a three. What lifts it above the many Providence restaurants with a single token mocktail is that both builds are recognisably part of a drinking culture rather than sweetened juice, and that they are designed to sit alongside food.

Both drinks are named on Go Providence's own mocktail guide, published by the city's tourism board in August 2026. We have not published prices or a fuller list, as the restaurant does not publish its drinks menu online. Federal Hill is dense with parking difficulty on weekend evenings; the municipal lots off Atwells are the sane option.

venues.name: Public Parking
venues.description: Public Parking opened on East Johnson Street in October 2024 and became nationally noticed almost immediately: Bon Appétit put it on its 2025 list of the Best New Bars in the US, and it was a James Beard Best New Bar semifinalist in 2026. The house style is long, absurd drink names, elaborate garnishes, irreverent glassware and cocktails served in nitro-chilled glass. The non-alcoholic drinks get the same treatment rather than a separate lesser one — the standing zero-proof build, "I'm Just a Baby . . . I Can Pay You In Blocks", runs smoked tea against lemon, ginger and bubbles. Open daily from 4pm to 2am.
