venues.longDescription:
Queen & Rook is a board game cafe on South Street, and it has quietly assembled one of the longest non-alcoholic drinks lists in Philadelphia. The menu carries a printed heading — "Zero Proof Cocktails & Beer" — with eight drinks beneath it, all flat-priced at eight dollars. That is a section, not a gesture.

The builds are properly constructed and the names are, predictably, deep-cut fantasy references. Princess Rosalina uses butterfly pea tea, which is the deep blue flower infusion that turns violet when acid hits it, with lychee, lime and soda — so the drink changes colour in front of you as the lime goes in. Galadriel is the savoury outlier and the most interesting thing on the list: pineapple and lychee cut with jalapeño, tajín and cilantro, which is a margarita's flavour architecture with no tequila anywhere near it. Two drinks use house shrubs — Abraxos gets Iron Teeth with blackberry, mint and lemon, and Smaug's Scales with strawberry and basil — and a shrub is a drinking vinegar, which supplies the sharp acidity that makes a non-alcoholic drink taste finished rather than sugary. Turning Violet is a blueberry-cardamom sparkling lemonade. The Butterbeer, at ten dollars, is non-alcoholic and available vegan or dairy.

The bottled side is unusually well chosen for a cafe: Guinness 0 on draught, Best Day's hazy and Kölsch, and St. Agrestis Phony Negroni. There are also eight house loose-leaf teas by the cup or pot, with names in the same register — Brew Tang Forever, Invasion of the Red Pandas, Psycho Kitty.

The format is the real argument. A board game cafe is one of the few evening venues where the activity, not the drink, is the reason everyone is at the table — you are playing something for two hours, the glass is incidental, and nobody is counting rounds. Add a genuine eight-drink zero-proof list and it becomes one of the strongest nights out in the city for a group where some people drink and some do not. It is licensed, so this is not an alcohol-free room; it is a room where not drinking costs you nothing. Open to midnight Friday and Saturday, from five in the evening on weekdays.
venues.pressQuote: Queen & Rook is a Philadelphia board-game favorite that serves more than your typical brewsky
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Billy Penn (WHYY), Alcohol-free spaces to spend nights out in Philly, January 2026

venues.name: Queen Yemeni Coffee
venues.description: Queen Yemeni Coffee is an alcohol-free Yemeni coffeehouse that opened in May 2026 in the ground floor of the historic Bridgeview Bank building at Lawrence Avenue and Broadway in Uptown, taking over a space that had been a Starbucks. It is the second location of a small operation that started in suburban Libertyville, and it is run as a late-night room: doors open at 5am and stay open until midnight on weeknights and 1am on Friday and Saturday. The name, logo and wall mural all reference the Queen of Sheba, ruler of Yemen and Ethiopia, and the beans are sourced from Yemen. The menu covers traditional milk and cardamom-spiced coffees at $5-$6, spiced signature lattes, teas, smoothies, breakfast plates and a dessert case. No alcohol is served.
signatureDrinks: Queen Spice Latte (cinnamon, cardamom and warm Arabian spices over steamed milk)
Pistachio Latte (roasted pistachio cream folded into espresso)
Turmeric Latte (turmeric, ginger and cardamom; caffeine-free)
Biscoff Latte (espresso with caramelized Biscoff, topped with cookie crumble)
venues.longDescription:
Queen Yemeni Coffee took over the former Starbucks at the corner of Lawrence Avenue and Broadway in Uptown, in the ground floor of the landmark Bridgeview Bank building, and opened there on 20 May 2026 as the second location of a business that began in suburban Libertyville. Manager and co-owner Abdullah Monssar told Block Club Chicago that the cafe's name, logo and the mural painted on its wall are all drawn from the Queen of Sheba, the ruler of Yemen and Ethiopia, the two countries where coffee is generally held to have originated. The beans come from Yemen, which was brewing coffee as early as the 12th century, and Monssar framed the offer plainly as an alternative to the American chains: an opportunity, he said, to taste coffee as it came from the place that first made it.

The drinks list is built on that heritage and then extends into the sweet, social-media-facing lattes that have made Yemeni coffeehouses a national category. Traditional milk and cardamom-spiced coffees run $5-$6. The signature side of the menu includes the Queen Spice Latte, made with cinnamon, cardamom and warm Arabian spices over steamed milk; a Pistachio Latte built on roasted pistachio cream; a caffeine-free Turmeric Latte of turmeric, ginger and cardamom; and a Biscoff Latte finished with golden cookie crumble. Teas, smoothies, breakfast items and a dessert case of Dubai chocolate cheesecake, pistachio cheesecake, house tiramisu and chocolate pecan cake round out the offer. Nothing served contains alcohol, and the hours make it a genuine night-out option rather than a daytime coffee stop: the room opens at 5am and does not close until midnight on weeknights, 1am on Friday and Saturday. The corner it occupies, Lawrence Avenue and Broadway, is one of Uptown's busiest crossings, and the arrival of a room that trades from before dawn until after midnight and serves no alcohol changes what is available there once the bars along Broadway have filled. Block Club Chicago reported the planned opening date as 20 May, with hours still being settled at the time of writing; the schedule the cafe now keeps is the one listed above.
venues.pressQuote: Ethiopia and Yemen are the first people who started the coffee business. People here are missing a lot of the original taste of coffee.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Abdullah Monssar, Queen Yemeni Coffee manager and co-owner

venues.name: R House Wynwood
venues.description: R House Wynwood is a restaurant, art gallery, and drag-entertainment venue opened in 2012 by chef Rocco Carulli and co-owner Owen Bale, widely credited as one of Wynwood's pioneer restaurants. Best known for its bottomless drag brunches and Latin-inspired menu, it expanded into zero-proof drinking with a dedicated alcohol-free cocktail program rolled out in September 2024. The standing zero-proof menu features house-built craft cocktails using non-alcoholic spirits, including the No-Groni (Bare Gin, Martini & Rossi Vibrante and Floreale), the Pathfinder Old Fashioned (Pathfinder Hemp & Root, brown sugar, aromatic bitters, orange peel), a Blanco Margarita made with Almave Blanco, and a Smoky Mango Margarita built on Little Saints St. Ember. The program also offers bottomless zero-proof mimosa and mocktail brunch packages aimed at sober, sober-curious, pregnant, under-21, and designated-driver guests. R House has been featured on The View and Good Morning America.
venues.hours: Mon-Tue closed; Wed-Thu 4pm-10pm; Fri 4pm-12am; Sat 11:30am-12am; Sun 11:30am-6pm

naMenuItems.name: No-Groni
naMenuItems.description: bare gin, martini & rossi vibrante, martini & rossi floreale

venues.longDescription:
R House opened in Wynwood in 2012 under chef Rocco Carulli and co-owner Owen Bale, early enough to be counted among the neighbourhood's pioneer restaurants, and combines a Latin-inspired menu with an art gallery and drag entertainment. Its bottomless drag brunches are what it is known for nationally — it has appeared on The View and Good Morning America.

That context makes its zero-proof programme unusually significant. A bottomless brunch is, structurally, the most alcohol-dependent format in hospitality: the entire proposition is unlimited drinks for a fixed price, and a non-drinker attending is both paying for nothing and visibly outside the event. In September 2024 the restaurant rolled out a standing alcohol-free cocktail menu and, critically, bottomless zero-proof mimosa and mocktail brunch packages — aimed explicitly at sober, sober-curious, pregnant, under-21 and designated-driver guests.

That is a genuinely rare piece of design. It means a table of six can book the same experience at the same price with some of them not drinking, rather than one person opting out of the format entirely.

The drinks are built on real products: the No-Groni uses Bare Gin with Martini & Rossi Vibrante and Floreale; the Pathfinder Old Fashioned works Pathfinder Hemp & Root with brown sugar, aromatic bitters and orange peel; a Blanco Margarita uses Almave Blanco, and a Smoky Mango Margarita is built on Little Saints St. Ember. Four different alcohol-free base spirits across four drinks is a stocked bar rather than a token bottle.

It is a full-service restaurant and entertainment venue with a busy bar. The zero-proof offering is a parallel programme, and at brunch it is close to a parallel event. If you are attending a drag brunch as the designated driver, book the zero-proof package explicitly rather than assuming it can be arranged on the day.
venues.pressQuote: ...zero-alcohol spirits and zero-proof cocktails that allow guests to be part of the R House party without being just your average overpriced juice on ice.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Rocco Carulli, R House chef & co-owner

venues.name: Radhaus
venues.description: Radhaus is an Alpine beer hall and restaurant in Building A at Fort Mason Center, with waterfront views across the bay and a menu of German and Austrian cooking — schnitzel, currywurst, pretzels — served alongside imported bier. Its current menu, updated in March 2026, carries a short N/A Cocktails section holding two built drinks at $13: Die Zitronenbeere, made with Abstinence Lemon, raspberry wine and soda, and Little Blossom, combining citrus, spice, ginger, bier nectar and apple cider vinegar. Alcohol-free beer is treated as a proper category rather than an afterthought, with Weihenstephaner's N/A Weissbier poured by the half litre and an N/A Radler by the third. The restaurant is dog-friendly and opens from noon most days.
signatureDrinks: Die Zitronenbeere (Abstinence Lemon, raspberry wine, soda)
Little Blossom (citrus, spice, ginger, bier nectar, apple cider vinegar)
venues.longDescription:
Radhaus occupies Building A at Fort Mason Center for Arts and Culture, on the Marina waterfront between Aquatic Park and the Marina Green, and is run as an Alpine beer hall: long communal tables, a wall of taps pouring German and Austrian bier, and a kitchen turning out schnitzel, currywurst, sausages, pretzels and rotisserie chicken. The building's windows face the bay, the terrace takes dogs, and the restaurant opens from noon most days, which makes it one of the few places in the city where a long afternoon is the intended use rather than an accident.

The alcohol-free drinking is better than the format suggests. The menu published on the restaurant's own site, marked as updated on 30 March 2026, carries a distinct N/A Cocktails heading with two house builds at $13 each. Die Zitronenbeere is made with Abstinence Lemon — one of the South African de-alcoholised botanical spirits — with raspberry wine and soda. Little Blossom is drier and more savoury, built from citrus, spice, ginger, a bier nectar and apple cider vinegar, which gives it the acidity that a beer-hall menu otherwise lacks. More usefully for a room whose whole identity is beer, the bottle list treats alcohol-free bier as a real category rather than a token: Weihenstephaner's N/A Weissbier is poured in half-litre bottles at $9, and an N/A Radler is available by the third of a litre at the same price, both listed among the imported bottles rather than hidden in a soft-drinks column. The Infatuation's guide to drinking without alcohol in San Francisco recommends the venue for exactly this combination of imported N/A beer and the ABV-less drinks list, though the specific drinks it names have since rotated off the card — the current pair are Die Zitronenbeere and Little Blossom. The kitchen list is unusually accommodating alongside them, running from oysters and pickled deviled eggs through to the full Alpine plates, so an alcohol-free visit here is a proper dinner rather than a stop for one drink.
venues.pressQuote: try a pint of N/A imported beer or something from their list of ABV-less drinks that include spins on negroni and margarita.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: The Infatuation, Where To Drink When You’re Not Drinking

venues.name: Radio Bar
venues.description: Radio Bar is a neighbourhood cocktail bar on Northwest Boulevard in Spokane's Audubon-Downriver district, a cosy room with a fireplace and a retro sound system, well outside the downtown bar cluster. Its drinks list balances classics with the bartenders' own creations, and carries a handful of non-alcoholic cocktails on a rotating seasonal basis alongside a range of alcohol-free beers — the seasonal rotation being the point, since the list changes with the produce rather than sitting static. Imported wine, bottled and canned beer, cider and seltzer fill out the rest. Open Tuesday to Saturday from 4pm, plus Sunday afternoons, closed Monday.
venues.longDescription:
Radio Bar sits on Northwest Boulevard in Audubon-Downriver, a residential district north-west of the Spokane River and a long way from the downtown bar strip. It is a neighbourhood bar in the good sense: a fireplace, a retro sound system, a room that fills with people who walked there.

The drinks list is split between classic cocktails and the bartenders' own creations, and the alcohol-free options sit on it as a rotating seasonal set rather than a permanent fixture. That rotation is the reason this entry records no signature drinks — a named drink would be wrong within a season — but it is also the reason the bar is worth listing at all. A seasonal non-alcoholic list means someone is rebuilding it every few months with whatever is good, which is a materially different commitment from printing two mocktails once and leaving them there for three years. Alongside them the bar keeps a variety of alcohol-free beers, plus an imported wine list and bottled and canned beer, cider and seltzer.

The Inlander, covering the bar's opening, described its beverage list as running to craft cocktails plus a handful of non-alcoholic ones, which is an honest description of the scale: this is not a dedicated programme on the level of Zola's, and it is graded three here accordingly. What it is, is a good bar in a residential neighbourhood where a non-drinker can turn up on a Tuesday and be looked after.

The hours are worth noting because they include something unusual for Spokane: a Sunday afternoon service from noon to 8pm, when most of the rooms in this guide are dark. Tuesday to Thursday runs 4pm to 11pm, Friday and Saturday to midnight, and the bar is closed on Monday.
venues.pressQuote: a handful of nonalcoholic cocktails
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: The Inlander, on Radio Bar’s drinks list

venues.name: Ramadan's Egyptian Coffee House
venues.description: Ramadan's Egyptian Coffee House is an alcohol-free late-night cafe in Marcy Holmes, a block from Dinkytown and the University of Minnesota campus. It soft-opened on 4 June 2026 under owner Ramadan Hussein, with his cousin Ali Mohammed helping run it, and it does not open until 1pm — the schedule of an evening room, running to midnight on weeknights and 1am on Friday and Saturday. The drinks list is genuinely Egyptian rather than Egyptian-themed: sahlab, sobia, carob, tamarind and hibiscus sit alongside Shaay Koshary, Shaay Fatla and Shaay Bilaban teas, Turkish coffee and a saffron or cardamom Arabic coffee served from a dallah.
venues.longDescription:
Ramadan's opened on 4th Street SE in Marcy Holmes, next to Maxwell's and a short walk from Dinkytown, with a soft opening on 4 June 2026. It is named for its owner, Ramadan Hussein; his cousin Ali Mohammed has been helping get the room running. The premise is stated plainly in the opening hours: the doors do not open until 1pm and they stay open until midnight Sunday through Thursday and 1am on Friday and Saturday. Mohammed told Racket in July 2026 that "within the Marcy Holmes and Dinkytown neighborhood, unless it's a bar, there's no late night spot" — a gap that matters in a district built around a campus with a large Muslim student population and a large population of students who simply do not drink. The room is decorated with woven lights, camel-and-pyramid artwork and shelves of decorative pharaohs, and it functions as a study space as much as a social one.

The menu is unusually deep for a cafe. The Egyptian section alone carries sahlab, the thickened milk drink dusted with cinnamon and nuts; sobia, the sweetened coconut-and-rice drink associated with Ramadan; carob; tamarind; hibiscus; ginger; and fenugreek. The tea collection lists Shaay Koshary at extra strength, Shaay Fatla, Shaay Bilaban with milk, Somali tea, karak, mint and green. Turkish coffee comes plain, medium or sweet, and Arabic coffee is served from a dallah with saffron or cardamom. Against that traditional spine sits a full modern espresso bar — honey cardamom, pistachio, Biscoff, Spanish and brown sugar cinnamon lattes — a run of iced matcha lattes in strawberry, mango, lavender, raspberry and ube, and a specialty list including the Dubai Mocha, Pistachio Pearl, Golden Mocha, Desert Bloom and Spiced Nectar. Smoothies and freshly pressed sugarcane juice round it out. No alcohol is served. The doors do not open until 1pm on weekdays, so this is not a morning coffee stop and does not try to be — the trade is almost entirely afternoon and evening, and the room turns over slowly enough that a group can hold a table for hours. On Saturday and Sunday it opens at 8am instead, which gives the neighbourhood a weekend daytime option as well as a late one.
venues.pressQuote: Within the Marcy Holmes and Dinkytown neighborhood, unless it's a bar, there's no late night spot.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Ali Mohammed, Ramadan's Egyptian Coffee House

venues.name: Rare Bird Rooftop
venues.description: Rare Bird is the rooftop bar and lounge atop the Noelle Hotel in downtown Nashville, perched on the building's 13th floor with views over the skyline and the Cumberland River. It opened to the public in March 2018, built around a "draft cocktails and uncaged spirits" concept in a colorful, design-forward setting. The bar is walk-in only and runs a daily "Golden Hour" happy-hour menu on weekdays. Alongside its full cocktail program, Rare Bird keeps a small headed zero-proof section it calls Hatchlings, both drinks at $13: The Perch, built on Seedlip Garden with orgeat and lime, and the Blushing Canary, with strawberry, passionfruit, lemon and Topo Chico. The list turns over — the Lemon Julip, N/Aperol Spritz and Daiquiri-Ish that anchored it in 2025 are gone — so treat it as two well-made drinks rather than a menu. It's a scenic, tourist-popular rooftop where a sober guest can still order something composed.
signatureDrinks: Blushing Canary (strawberry, passionfruit, lemon, Topo Chico) $13
venues.longDescription:
Rare Bird is the rooftop bar and lounge on the thirteenth floor of the Noelle Hotel in downtown Nashville, with views across the skyline and out to the Cumberland River. It opened to the public in March 2018 around a concept it describes as draft cocktails and uncaged spirits, in a colourful, design-forward room that has made it one of the more photographed rooftops in the city. It is walk-in only — no reservations — and runs a daily Golden Hour happy-hour menu on weekdays.

The zero-proof list is small and it changes. On the spring 2026 menu it sits under its own heading, Hatchlings, and holds two drinks at $13. The Perch is built on Seedlip Garden — the herbal, pea-and-hay expression of the original non-alcoholic distillate — with orgeat and lime, which gives it the nutty body a spirit-free sour otherwise lacks. The Blushing Canary is the fruit-forward one: strawberry and passionfruit with lemon, lengthened with Topo Chico. Both are made with the same care as the cocktail list above them, and the Seedlip base is the signal — using a real non-alcoholic spirit costs a bar money it does not have to spend, and a hotel rooftop choosing to do so rather than defaulting to fruit purée is the point. Earlier versions of the list ran three drinks — a Lemon Julip on Seedlip Grove 42, an N/Aperol Spritz on Ritual's non-alcoholic gin with Giffard aperitif, and a Daiquiri-Ish — and all three have been replaced, so anyone who read about them should expect the current pair instead. There is no non-alcoholic beer on the bottle list.

The practical value is situational and worth naming plainly: a rooftop with a skyline view is one of the standard things visitors to Nashville want to do, and it is exactly the sort of place where a non-drinker usually ends up holding a soda while everyone else has a cocktail in a nice glass. Two composed spirit-free builds solves that, at a venue people were going to anyway. Open daily, to midnight on Friday and Saturday. Because the bar is walk-in only, it is also one of the easier rooftops in the city to reach without planning — worth knowing on a night when a group decides late that it wants a view.
venues.pressQuote: Overlooking historic Printers Alley, the space was designed by Nashville-based D|AAD, led by Nick Dryden. It features two limestone fireplaces supplementing the bar area.

venues.name: Rare Society
venues.description: Rare Society is the retro steakhouse in chef Brad Wise's group, on Park Boulevard in University Heights, and its cocktail card carries a Spirit Free section of four. Three are built drinks: Fountain of Youth on a salted raspberry and chamomile sparkling with grapefruit and soda, Fool's Gold on a non-alcoholic Italian aperitif with lemon and a miso-ginger syrup served over a large cube, and Staycation on a white cane spirit alternative with pineapple, lime, orgeat, cranberry and mint. Best Day Brewing's non-alcoholic kölsch is eight dollars. What distinguishes the section is that it sits on the cocktail card among the classics rather than at the back with the sodas, and that three of its four entries are made to order rather than opened. Dinner runs nightly from five, until nine early in the week and ten on Friday and Saturday, in a room built to look like a mid-century Las Vegas steakhouse.
signatureDrinks: Fountain of Youth ($14) — salted raspberry and chamomile sparkling, grapefruit, soda
Fool's Gold ($15) — non-alcoholic Italian aperitif, lemon, miso ginger, big cube
Staycation ($14) — white cane spirit alternative, pineapple, lime, orgeat, cranberry, mint
venues.longDescription:
Rare Society trades on Park Boulevard at the edge of University Heights and is chef Brad Wise's homage to the mid-century Las Vegas steakhouse — red leather, wood-fired dry-aged beef, martinis on a cart. It has since grown into a small chain with rooms in Solana Beach, Santa Barbara and further afield; this is the original San Diego location.

What makes it usable for a non-drinker is that the Spirit Free heading sits on the cocktail card among the classics rather than at the back with the sodas, and three of its four entries are built drinks rather than bottles poured out. Fountain of Youth, at fourteen dollars, uses a salted raspberry and chamomile sparkling with grapefruit and soda — tart and low in sugar, which is unusual in this category. Fool's Gold at fifteen is the one to order if you miss the bitterness of a proper aperitivo: a non-alcoholic Italian aperitif with lemon and a miso-ginger syrup, served over a single large cube, with enough salt and umami to stand next to a steak. Staycation at fourteen is the tiki-leaning option, built on a white cane spirit alternative with pineapple, lime, orgeat, cranberry and mint.

The fourth line is Best Day Brewing's kölsch at eight dollars, from the Californian non-alcoholic brewery whose beers turn up across this city's better lists.

The room is a steakhouse first and the wine and whiskey lists are long, so this is a venue for a mixed table rather than a destination for people who do not drink. Service runs from five every night, until nine early in the week and ten on Friday and Saturday. The group prints the same spirit-free section across its locations, so what is pouring here should also be available at the Solana Beach room, and the built drinks rotate with the seasonal card while the Best Day line tends to stay.

A note on which room you are booking. Rare Society now has locations in Solana Beach, Santa Barbara, San Clemente, Las Vegas and Washington state as well as this one, and the group's website presents them together, so a search can easily land you on the wrong city's page or phone number. This listing is the University Heights room on Park Boulevard. The wood-fired grill is the centre of the kitchen, the beef is dry-aged in house, and the vegetables cooked over the same fire are the part regulars talk about. Book ahead at weekends; the dining room fills early and the bar is small.
venues.pressQuote: Sink your teeth into Rare Society from Trust Restaurant Group, Chef + Restaurateur Brad Wise’s west coast-based restaurant concept that pays homage to retro steakhouses.

venues.name: Raven Records
venues.description: Raven Records is a heavy-metal record store, metal-themed coffee shop and fully alcohol-free bar in Camden Town, billed as the world's first heavy-metal alcohol-free bar. Everything on offer is 0.0%: Heineken 0.0 on draught alongside Guinness 0.0, Stella 0.0 and craft NA beer from Brulo, plus seven alcohol-free whiskies and AF gin, vodka, tequila and botanical spirits used in the bar's alcohol-free cocktails. Founded by owners Ben and Chloe, it was conceived as a socialising space that doesn't revolve around alcohol.
venues.hours: Mon 12pm-6pm; Tue closed; Wed 12pm-6pm; Thu 12pm-8pm; Fri-Sat 12pm-9pm; Sun 12pm-6pm
signatureDrinks: Alcohol-free whisky (seven varieties behind the bar)
venues.longDescription:
Raven Records opened at 24 Camden Road in late 2023, about 100 metres from Camden Town station, and pitches itself as the world's first heavy-metal alcohol-free bar. The venue is three things at once: a vinyl, CD, book and band-merch record store, a metal-themed coffee shop pouring ultra-dark roasts from Black Coffee Worship and occult teas from Black Prism Tea, and a fully 0.0% bar. A basement space (complete with an illuminated upside-down cross) hosts DJ sets, signings and events.

The bar is genuinely alcohol-free from top to bottom. On draught there's Heineken 0.0 alongside Guinness 0.0, Stella 0.0 and a full range of 0.0% beers and ciders, including beer from independent craft NA brewer Brulo. The back bar carries seven different alcohol-free whiskies plus AF gin, vodka and tequila and a range of botanical and mood-enhancing spirits, which the team builds into alcohol-free cocktails. The fridge rounds it out with Liquid Death and functional drinks from Trip, Goodrays and Peak.

The project is personal for co-owner Ben Dean, who has spoken openly about being in recovery and runs a secular twelve-step program; his co-owner Chloe DJs. Together they set out to make a space where metal fans can socialise without alcohol at the centre of it. Raven Records is open Thursday to Monday, 12pm to 8pm.
venues.pressQuote: This should be a place where people can socialise without having to lubricate themselves with alcohol.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Ben Dean, co-owner of Raven Records

venues.name: R&D
venues.description: R&D is a craft cocktail bar in Philadelphia's Fishtown neighborhood, opened in October 2018 in the former Root Restaurant & Wine Bar space at 1206 Frankford Avenue. It's run by Defined Hospitality, the group behind Suraya, Pizzeria Beddia, Condesa, and Kalaya; the cocktail program was built by Aaron Deary and is curated by bar manager Resa Mueller. R&D has won Best of Philly for Best Cocktail Bar. Beyond its acclaimed full bar, R&D maintains a permanent zero-proof presence on its menu, and bartenders also build custom non-alcoholic drinks on request. Mueller refreshes the zero-proof cocktails every few months, leaning on tiki-style builds with fresh juices, coconut, house-made syrups, small-batch sodas, and tannic teas. Named NA drinks have included the Virgin Piña Colada and a negroni-inspired build, plus NA beers from Athletic Brewing and Guinness 0.
venues.longDescription:
R&D opened in October 2018 at 1206 Frankford Avenue in Fishtown, in the space that previously held Root Restaurant & Wine Bar. It is run by Defined Hospitality — the group behind Suraya, Pizzeria Beddia, Condesa and Kalaya — with a cocktail programme originally built by Aaron Deary and now curated by bar manager Resa Mueller. It has won Philadelphia Magazine's Best of Philly for Best Cocktail Bar, which is the relevant context for what follows: this is a serious cocktail room, not a venue that specialises in non-alcoholic drinks.

Which is exactly why its zero-proof provision counts. R&D keeps a permanent spirit-free presence on the printed menu rather than a seasonal one, and Mueller refreshes those drinks alongside the rest of the list. Bartenders will also build custom non-alcoholic drinks on request — an offer that is only meaningful at a bar with the depth of house syrups, cordials and technique to improvise from, which this one has.

The named builds tell you the approach. The N/A Negroni and the N/A Penicillin both take famously spirit-defined classics and rebuild them: a Negroni is equal parts gin, vermouth and bitter aperitivo, so a zero-proof version has to find bitterness from somewhere else entirely; a Penicillin is a scotch drink built on honey, lemon and fresh ginger, where the ginger's heat can carry a version without the whisky. The N/A Spritz and a Virgin Piña Colada round out the list at the more refreshing end.

Mueller's own observation to the press is the most useful summary of why this matters: the industry has moved beyond the point ten years ago when walking into any bar meant a choice between orange, pineapple and cranberry juice. A Best of Philly cocktail bar keeping a standing zero-proof section is the proof of that shift.

Open from five in the evening, to midnight on Thursday and one in the morning on Friday and Saturday. Closed Sundays.
venues.pressQuote: We've moved beyond 10 years ago when you'd walk into any bar and the only things they'd have are orange juice, pineapple juice, and cranberry juice on the [soda] gun.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Resa Mueller, R&D bartender & cocktail curator

venues.name: Realm of the 52 Remedies
venues.description: Realm of the 52 Remedies is a hidden cocktail bar in the Convoy District, themed on an ancient Chinese medical text and reached through an apothecary front. Its signature cocktails are twenty dollars, and every one of them is printed with the same line: available spirit free at fifteen. That makes the whole seasonal list — drinks such as the Sunomono, the Je Ju and Softly Spoken — orderable without alcohol, rather than a separate short section. The bar does not publish a separate ingredient list for those versions, so what arrives is its own rebuild of the drink without the spirit, at a five-dollar discount — worth asking which of the current list the bartenders think survives the swap best. The bar trades nightly from five, to midnight in the week and half past one on Friday and Saturday, and the room is small enough that a reservation is the safer plan.
signatureDrinks: Sunomono, spirit free ($15) — the house old fashioned, offered without its whisky
Je Ju, spirit free ($15) — mandarin, ginger, cinnamon and lemon, offered without its spirits
Softly Spoken, spirit free ($15) — mango, lime, orange and Chinese five spice, offered without its rum
venues.longDescription:
Realm of the 52 Remedies sits on Convoy Street in Kearny Mesa, the centre of San Diego's Asian food scene, and is entered through what presents itself as an apothecary. The name comes from the Wushi'er Bingfang, a Chinese medical text from around 215 BCE recovered from the Mawangdui tombs, which lists more than 250 elixirs and treatments; the bar describes itself as paying tribute to traditional methods of building health and longevity, and the drinks are presented as remedies.

The thing that matters for a non-drinker is structural rather than decorative. Each signature cocktail on the seasonal list is printed at twenty dollars with a line underneath reading that it is available spirit free at fifteen. That is not a short mocktail section bolted to the end of the menu — it is an offer to rebuild the bar's actual cocktails without the alcohol, across the list. On the spring and summer cards that has included the Sunomono, the bar's take on an old fashioned built around matsutake shoyu, shiso and plum vinegar, sesame and cucumber; the Je Ju, inspired by the mandarins of the Korean island, with ginger, cinnamon, mandarin and lemon; and Softly Spoken, built on mango, lime, orange and Chinese five spice and described by the bar as its most tropical drink.

Be clear about what the spirit-free versions are: the bar does not publish a separate ingredient list for them, so what arrives is the kitchen's rebuild of that drink without its spirit, at a five-dollar discount. Ask at the bar which of the current list they think works best without alcohol — the flavour-led drinks built on vinegar, tea and fruit lose less than the whisky-forward ones.

The room is small, dark and reservation-friendly, and the theming is committed. Hours run from five every night, until midnight Sunday through Thursday and half past one on Friday and Saturday. The list is seasonal and changes several times a year, so the named drinks above are examples of the form rather than fixtures.

The theming is unusually complete for a bar that could have coasted on a hidden door. The original manuscript the bar is named for sits in the Hunan Provincial Museum in Changsha, and the menu presents drinks the way the text presents treatments — tonics, tinctures, serums, potions and elixirs, each with a written intention and a garnish chosen to match. For a non-drinker this turns out to matter more than it sounds: a bar that has already decided its drinks are about botanicals, bitterness and infusion rather than about alcohol is a bar where removing the spirit costs the drink less than it would elsewhere. Convoy Street is a fifteen-minute drive from downtown and parking is straightforward, which is not true of most of this city's better cocktail bars.
venues.pressQuote: This space pays tribute to traditional methods of building health and longevity—physical, as well as mental and emotional.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Realm of the 52 Remedies, company statement
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Realm of the 52 Remedies, bar website

venues.name: 48 Record Bar
venues.description: 48 Record Bar is a vinyl listening room and cocktail bar that opened in December 2023 on the second floor above Sassafras Bar in Old City, Philadelphia. It was founded by Donal McCoy, owner of Sassafras and the former Tin Angel music venue, with Joey Sweeney. Inspired by Tokyo's audiophile "kissa" bars, the roughly 45-seat room pairs a high-fidelity vinyl sound system with a menu of about 16 cocktails, plus beer and wine. The bar carries a small but genuine named zero-proof lineup alongside its full cocktail list, including the Polyester Dinosaur (pineapple, turmeric-honey syrup, ginger, tajín rim) and a Coconut Matcha Mojito (cream of coconut, lime, matcha), with seasonal additions like a Moroccan mint tea mocktail and a "hot mocklate" with pistachio orgeat. There are no reservations; the room hosts listening parties and vinyl events.
venues.longDescription:
48 Record Bar opened in December 2023 on the second floor above Sassafras Bar in Old City, founded by Donal McCoy — who owns Sassafras and formerly ran the Tin Angel music venue — with Joey Sweeney. It takes its cue from Tokyo's audiophile kissa bars: a room of roughly forty-five seats built around a high-fidelity vinyl system and a collection, with about sixteen cocktails alongside beer and wine.

The listening-bar format is one of the best answers there is to the problem of a night out without alcohol, and the reason is structural rather than about the drinks. In a kissa the music is the reason you are in the room. Volume sits at a level where conversation is possible but not constant, which removes the obligation to keep talking that makes sober socialising tiring. There is a thing to attend to that is not the glass in your hand, no bar to stand at, and no rhythm of rounds — the record side sets the pace instead.

The zero-proof lineup is small but genuinely named rather than improvised. The Polyester Dinosaur combines pineapple with a turmeric-honey syrup and ginger over a tajín rim, which is a properly savoury build: turmeric is earthy and slightly bitter, ginger brings heat, and tajín — the Mexican chilli-lime-salt blend — puts salt and acid on the lip of the glass, so every sip starts sharp. A Coconut Matcha Mojito runs creamier, with matcha's vegetal astringency doing the work that would otherwise fall to the rum.

The hours are the other argument. Five in the evening until two in the morning, Tuesday through Sunday, with a four o'clock Saturday opening. A room that runs to two, where the entertainment is a record collection rather than a bar, is about as good as this gets. Closed Mondays.
venues.pressQuote: 48 Record Bar is a listening room and cocktail bar right above Sassafras in Old City
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Billy Penn (WHYY), Alcohol-free spaces to spend nights out in Philly, January 2026

venues.name: Red Feather Lounge
venues.description: Red Feather Lounge on the 8th Street pedestrian block builds its alcohol-free drinks with the same technique as its cocktails, which shows most clearly in Well Orange You Sophisticated — orange vanilla syrup, lime and egg white foam. The foam is the detail worth noticing: it requires a hard shake and adds real time to the build, and it is the first thing most bars quietly drop from a zero-proof order. There is also I Know a Tiki When I See One, a pineapple, almond orgeat, cinnamon and lime build, and Dorothy, made with lavender soda and dry secco. It sits on the pedestrianised 8th Street block and runs to 1:30am on Friday and Saturday, later than almost anything else in this guide.
signatureDrinks: Well Orange You Sophisticated - orange vanilla syrup, lime, egg white foam
I Know a Tiki When I See One - pineapple juice, almond orgeat, cinnamon, lime, soda

naMenuItems.name: State of Mind
naMenuItems.description: pineapple jalapeno mint shrub, coconut water

naMenuItems.name: Punch Drunk Love
naMenuItems.description: strawberry basil milk punch, gruvi gruvi dry secco

venues.longDescription:
Red Feather Lounge sits on the pedestrianised stretch of 8th Street in downtown Boise, the block that carries most of the city's outdoor drinking in summer. It has been part of Boise's cocktail scene for years, and it treats its alcohol-free list as part of the same programme rather than an appendix.

The evidence is in Well Orange You Sophisticated: orange vanilla syrup, lime, and egg white foam. That last component is the tell. A foam means a dry shake and then a wet shake — a genuinely more laborious build — and it is the single most common thing dropped when a bartender assumes the non-drinker will not notice. Including it means the drink arrives with the same texture and the same crown of foam as the sours everyone else is holding, which is most of the experience.

I Know a Tiki When I See One takes the other approach, building depth through orgeat, cinnamon and pineapple. Tiki is a natural fit for zero-proof work because the style already depends on layered syrups, spices and citrus rather than on the spirit alone, so removing the rum costs less than removing gin from a martini. Dorothy is the lightest of the three, lavender soda with dry secco.

The hours are among the best in this guide: from 4pm through the week and 11am at weekends, running to 1:30am on Friday and Saturday. Boise's alcohol-free options otherwise skew early — Free Spirits shuts at 6pm two days a week — so a downtown bar serving properly built zero-proof drinks past one in the morning matters. It is a few minutes' walk from Art Haus, Thick as Thieves and Bar Please!, which makes the 8th Street area easy to work through in an evening. For a visitor with one night in Boise and no interest in drinking, that block is the single most efficient thing to plan around. The Saturday and Sunday 11am opening also makes it one of very few places in the city where a considered alcohol-free drink is available before the evening, which is otherwise Boise's weakest hour.
venues.pressQuote: Red Feather Lounge serves non-alcoholic beverages crafted with the same care as their signature cocktails
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: This Is Boise, The Boise Area's Best Non-Alcoholic Drinks and Mocktail Spots, January 2025

venues.name: Red Rabbit
venues.description: Red Rabbit is an "uncomplicated, authentic Italian" restaurant — pizza, pasta, and oysters — owned by Luke Shimp, the restaurateur behind the Red Cow burger group. The original Red Rabbit opened in 2016 in Minneapolis's North Loop; this Summit Hill location debuted in October 2018 at 788 Grand Ave in the former Wild Onion space, and in 2023 the concept was named one of FSR Magazine's Top 50 Independent Restaurants. Beyond the food, Red Rabbit keeps a genuine "Spirit Free" section in its beverage book, so non-drinkers get more than soda. Named zero-proof options include a Spirit-Free Old Fashioned (Spiritless 74 NA bourbon, demerara, NA bitters), a Spirit-Free Martini (Abstinence NA gin), the Ginger Spritz, the canned Lagunitas Hoppy Refresher, and a bottled St. Agrestis Phony Negroni. Visit Saint Paul singles out the Grand Avenue location for its "sizable selection of liquor-free beverages."

venues.longDescription:
Red Rabbit is an uncomplicated Italian restaurant — pizza, pasta and oysters — from Luke Shimp, the restaurateur behind the Red Cow burger group. The original opened in 2016 in the Minneapolis North Loop; this Summit Hill location arrived in October 2018 at 788 Grand Avenue, in the former Wild Onion space, and in 2023 the concept was named to FSR Magazine's Top 50 Independent Restaurants.

The spirit-free section in its beverage book is one of the deepest attached to any restaurant in the Twin Cities, and unusually it is priced honestly — the simple builds cost $7 rather than being charged at cocktail rates for a glass of juice. At the top end sit proper spirit conversions: a Spirit-Free Old Fashioned built on Spiritless 74 non-alcoholic bourbon with demerara and non-alcoholic bitters, and a Spirit Free Martini using Abstinence non-alcoholic gin with a lemon twist. A martini is the hardest drink on any list to render without alcohol, because there is nothing to hide behind, and a restaurant offering one is making a statement about how seriously it takes the category. Below those the list runs a Ginger Spritz of non-alcoholic gin with ginger beer, honey and lemon; an Abstinence Spritz with non-alcoholic aperitivo and soda; a Lavender Revolution of lavender, lime and tonic; a Granata Pop combining non-alcoholic aperitif with cherry cola, grapefruit, lime and soda; and a Limore built on saffron, lemon and soda. A 400ml bottled St. Agrestis Phony Negroni and canned Lagunitas Hoppy Refresher complete it.

Eight named options spanning spirituous, bitter, floral and long is a genuine bar list rather than a courtesy, and Visit Saint Paul singles out this Grand Avenue location specifically for its "sizable selection of liquor-free beverages." Open Tuesday through Sunday, with weekend brunch.

venues.name: Redemption Bar
venues.description: Redemption Bar is country artist Ashley McBryde's NA-forward bar, opened in August 2025 on the fifth floor of Eric Church's Chief's on Lower Broadway in downtown Nashville. Inspired by McBryde's own path to sobriety (she is nearly four years sober), the bar centers an 18-drink zero-proof cocktail menu "composed like a setlist," with each drink named after lyrics that carried her forward — including Flickerin' Flames of Hell, Martini McBryde, Gospel Night, and The Devil I Know. The bar takes its name from McBryde's song "Redemption." Alcohol is also served, since "everyone is welcome." Beyond the drinks, the space features an intimate troubadour-style stage built for solo or duo singer-songwriter sets. Billed by the venue as "Broadway's first NA-focused bar," it offers a sober-friendly alternative on a famously alcohol-soaked strip, with a full food menu alongside the zero-proof and alcoholic lists.
venues.longDescription:
Redemption Bar opened in August 2025 on the fifth floor of Eric Church's Chief's on Lower Broadway, and it is country artist Ashley McBryde's bar. The context matters: Lower Broadway is one of the most relentlessly alcohol-soaked streets in the United States, a strip of honky-tonks where the entire economy runs on drinking, and putting a non-alcohol-forward bar in the middle of it is a genuinely unusual act. McBryde is nearly four years sober, and the bar grew directly out of that. It takes its name from her song "Redemption," and her own reaction to the idea is the most quotable thing any founder in this directory has said: "I couldn't believe that was an option. I thought I would end up owning a tattoo parlor or a coffee shop."

The zero-proof menu runs to eighteen drinks and is composed, in the bar's phrase, like a setlist — each one named after lyrics that carried her through, including Flickerin' Flames of Hell, Martini McBryde, Gospel Night and The Devil I Know. Eighteen named non-alcoholic drinks is one of the largest such lists anywhere in this directory, and it means a non-drinker on Broadway can go somewhere with a real menu rather than nursing a soda in a honky-tonk. Alcohol is also served, on the explicit principle that everyone is welcome, which is the right call for a room meant to be somewhere a sober person can bring their drinking friends rather than a separate space they retreat to.

Beyond the drinks there is an intimate troubadour-style stage built for solo and duo singer-songwriter sets — the format Nashville actually runs on, and a reason to stay for the night. The venue bills itself as Broadway's first NA-focused bar, and there is a full food menu alongside both lists. Open daily, to 3am on Friday and Saturday.
venues.pressQuote: I couldn't believe that was an option. I thought I would end up owning a tattoo parlor or a coffee shop.

venues.name: Redstraw Tea Bar
venues.description: Redstraw Tea Bar is a fully alcohol-free tea lounge in Carrollton whose 'Tea Artists' hand-craft a menu of cocktail-inspired specialty teas built from fresh seasonal juices and loose-leaf tea. The named list reads like a mocktail card - Peach Bellini (peach black tea with lychee and mango), Grapefruit Punch (jade tea with fresh grapefruit juice), and a run of alcohol-free 'mojitos' (mango-lime, watermelon-rose, matcha-mint). It stays open until 11pm on Friday and Saturday, making it a genuine booze-free option for a late evening out, with everything made fresh to order and no alcohol on the premises.

venues.longDescription:
Redstraw Tea Bar is the Carrollton outpost of the Redstraw tea-bar concept, a fully alcohol-free spot at 1012 MacArthur Drive that builds its identity around handcrafted, cocktail-inspired teas rather than boba-shop sweetness alone. The staff are billed as 'Tea Artists' who make each drink to order from fresh fruit, seasonal juices, organic herbs, and loose-leaf tea, and the shop advertises a custom service where a Tea Artist will 'create the custom tea of your dreams.'

The specialty-tea menu is explicitly modeled on cocktails without the alcohol. Named builds include the Peach Bellini (peach black tea with lychee and mango), the Grapefruit Punch (a special-blend jade tea mixed with fresh grapefruit juice), the French Daisy (jasmine green tea with fresh lemon, colored naturally with butterfly pea), and a run of alcohol-free mojitos - Mango Mojito (jasmine green tea with mango and lime), Watermelon Rose Mojito, Organic Matcha Mojito, and Green Mojito (mint and key lime). A build-your-own 'Custom Tea' option lets guests design their own zero-proof drink alongside milk teas and coffee.

With weekend hours running until 11pm, Redstraw functions as a late-night, zero-proof alternative to a bar - a place to meet friends over a 'cocktail' that happens to be tea. It is entirely non-alcoholic, uses organic milks (soy, almond, oat) and organic cane sugar or honey, and is available for delivery across DoorDash, Uber Eats, and Grubhub.

venues.name: Repeal 33
venues.description: Repeal 33 is a bar and restaurant on Martin Luther King Jr Boulevard, named for the amendment that ended Prohibition and built around an inventive cocktail programme run by beverage director Jim McCourt. Its non-alcoholic drinks are treated as part of that programme rather than as a fallback: Savannah's tourism board singles the room out specifically for them, describing four distinct builds that include one on a non-alcoholic botanical distillate with lemon and basil and another on an alcohol-free aperitif syrup with orange and soda. The kitchen runs dinner from 4pm every day, with weekend brunch from 11am on Saturday and Sunday.

venues.longDescription:
Repeal 33 takes its name from the Twenty-first Amendment, which repealed Prohibition in 1933, and sits on Martin Luther King Jr Boulevard on the western edge of the Historic District. The bar describes its list as a continuing exploration of inventive cocktails under beverage director Jim McCourt, and the alcohol-free drinks are folded into that exploration rather than parked at the end of it.

What that looks like in practice, according to Visit Savannah's zero-proof guide, is four separate builds that each take a different route to the same problem. Kiss From a Rose works on lemon, almond and rose water — floral and nutty, no spirit substitute involved. Best In Show is the crowd-pleaser, a strawberry shrub with fresh orange juice and lemon-lime soda. Two Tears is the technical one, built on a non-alcoholic botanical distillate with lemon and basil, which is the closest the list comes to a gin sour. Dry S.O.B. runs an alcohol-free aperitif syrup with orange and soda, an Americano in structure if not in alcohol.

Those four names are recorded here as evidence of the programme, not as a current order list, and this entry deliberately publishes no signature drinks for that reason. Three other Savannah venues in this guide have replaced every zero-proof drink the same tourism article credits them with, so the honest position is that Repeal 33 demonstrably runs a real alcohol-free list and the specific names should be checked on arrival.

The room trades from 4pm Monday through Friday, opening at 11am on Saturday and Sunday for brunch, and runs to 11pm or midnight depending on the night.
venues.pressQuote: The ease, charm and elegant allure of Repeal 33's non-alcoholic drinks are worth speaking easy.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Visit Savannah, Where to Find Incredible Mocktails in Savannah

venues.name: Reposado Bar & Lounge
venues.description: Reposado Bar & Lounge is a tequila- and mezcal-focused bar and lounge on Ossington Avenue in Toronto's Ossington strip, open since 2007 and voted one of Canada's Top 50 Bars in 2024. Alongside live jazz on Fridays and funk on Saturdays, it runs a dedicated "Non-Alcoholic" menu page listing seven named zero-proof drinks with prices, from a $1 Spicy Sangrita Shot to $6 zero-proof takes on its blood orange margarita, Dark 'n Stormy and pineapple fizz. Heineken 0.0 and Guinness 0.0 round out the alcohol-free list.

venues.longDescription:
Reposado Bar & Lounge has been pouring on Ossington Avenue — the strip of Toronto nightlife known simply as "Ossington" — since 2007, and was voted one of Canada's Top 50 Bars in 2024. The bar and lounge builds its list around tequila and mezcal, including flights, and keeps a weekly live-music program running behind it: Jazz Night on Fridays and Funk Night on Saturdays.

According to Secret Toronto's roundup of the city's best mocktail spots, the kitchen turns out tacos and empanadas to go with the tequila and mezcal menu — food built to pair with drinks whether or not those drinks contain alcohol.

Non-drinkers get their own page on the bar's website, headed simply "Non-Alcoholic." It lists seven items with prices: a $1 Spicy Sangrita Shot and a $3.50 soda, bottled Heineken 0.0/Corona Cero ($6) and Guinness 0.0 ($8), and three $6 zero-proof house cocktails — an N/A Blood Orange "Marg," an N/A Black & Stormy and an N/A Pineapple Fizz — each built as a zero-proof take on one of Reposado's tequila classics, though the bar hasn't published ingredient breakdowns for them. Secret Toronto's own writeup singles out the blood orange marg and the non-alcoholic black & stormy by name as standouts for anyone skipping the alcohol.
venues.pressQuote: Specializing in top-shelf tequilas and mezcal, Reposado Bar & Lounge on Ossington has a number of zero-proof takes on their classics as well to pair with their delectable tacos and empanadas. From their blood orange "marg" to their non-alcoholic black & stormy, you'll get to enjoy all of the flavour sans booze.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Secret Toronto, "10 Great Spots To Find A Delicious Mocktail In Toronto"

venues.name: Republic
venues.description: Republic is the 1960s-inspired cocktail bar and lounge inside The Ritz-Carlton, Millenia Singapore, and one of the city's most awarded hotel bars. Alongside its acclaimed cocktail list, the team keeps a genuine no-and-low selection: a curated run of fine bubbles, natural-wine alternatives and zero-proof distillates. Time Out Singapore singles out Muri 'Passing Clouds' (about S$25) as a standout champagne alternative - floral, honeyed and pleasantly dry - making Republic a rare high-end Singapore bar where a non-drinker can order with the same care as everyone else.
venues.address: The Ritz-Carlton, Millenia Singapore, 7 Raffles Avenue, Singapore 039799
signatureDrinks: Muri 'Passing Clouds' - a zero-proof sparkling champagne alternative with a bouquet of flowers, honey and ripe fruit, vinous funk and a dry, faintly tannic finish (about S$25)
venues.longDescription:
Republic opened in 2021 as part of a major refurbishment of The Ritz-Carlton, Millenia Singapore, conceived as a multi-dimensional lounge-and-bar that evokes an elegant private residence. Set in the Marina Centre precinct at 7 Raffles Avenue, the bar leans into the cultural energy of the 1960s, with vintage posters, vinyl records and period music lining a room built for slow, considered drinking. Its cocktail program is released in numbered 'Volumes' - the current Volume Three, 'Breakthrough,' collects 16 drinks that pay tribute to the trailblazers and cultural shifts of the decade.

Republic ranks among Singapore's most decorated hotel bars. It placed No. 12 on Asia's 50 Best Bars in 2022 and No. 16 in 2023, and continues to appear on Tatler and Travel + Leisure best-of lists. (Note: Republic was not on the 2025 Asia's 50 Best Bars 51-100 list - the No. 60 slot that year went to Origin Bar, a different Singapore venue.)

The reason Republic earns a place in a non-alcoholic directory is the seriousness of its no-and-low offering. Rather than a single token mocktail, the bar keeps what Time Out Singapore calls 'a painstakingly curated list of fine bubbles, natural wine alternatives and zero-proof distillates.' The headline pour is Muri 'Passing Clouds' (about S$25), a Danish zero-proof sparkling made to stand in for champagne - all flowers, honey and ripe fruit up front, with a vinous funk and a dry, faintly tannic finish.

Practically, Republic is open daily from noon (until midnight Sunday to Thursday, 1am on Friday and Saturday, with an earlier close on Sunday), and its lounge doubles as an afternoon-tea room. For a visiting non-drinker, it is one of the safest bets in Marina Bay for a genuinely composed alcohol-free drink in a luxury-hotel setting - tempered by the fact that the zero-proof list is a curated shelf rather than a large printed named menu, so it is worth asking the bartender what is pouring on the night.
venues.pressQuote: A painstakingly curated list of fine bubbles, natural wine alternatives and zero-proof distillates.

venues.name: Reserve Wines
venues.description: Reserve Wines is an independent Manchester wine merchant whose Altrincham outpost sits inside the Market House at the town's celebrated food hall, pouring by the glass and selling by the bottle to drink in or take away. Founded in 2003 by drinks expert Kate Goodman, it carries a genuinely curated low- and no-alcohol range alongside its 200-plus wines. The alcohol-free shelf spans zero-proof red, white, sparkling and rosé plus artisan spirits from Lyre's, Three Spirit, Almave and Botivo, with De Bortoli's 'The Very Cautious One' and Vallformosa's Catalan 0% sparkling anchoring the wine end of the shelf, so the sober drinker gets the same considered treatment as everyone else at the bar.

venues.longDescription:
Reserve Wines was set up in 2003 by Kate Goodman, a straight-talking drinks expert and sometime BBC Food & Drink contributor, on a mission to make wine 'fun and accessible for everyone'. The West Didsbury shop on Burton Road remains the mothership, but the group has since spread across Greater Manchester with smaller branches including this one inside Altrincham Market. It occupies the Market House — the covered bar building beside the main food hall — a couple of minutes from Altrincham's tram and rail interchange, and manager Kallum and his team run relaxed tastings around the wine barrels as well as larger seated masterclasses with local names such as Honest Crust and Chorlton Cheesemongers.

The set-up is a hybrid: part bottle shop, part bar. More than 200 bottles line the walls to buy and carry out, while a changing list of seasonal wines by the glass and flight, eco-friendly keg wines, spritzes and cocktails is poured to drink in among the market's buzz. It stays open late for a wine shop — until 10pm Tuesday to Saturday — which makes it as much an evening spot as a daytime errand.

For non-drinkers the draw is the alcohol-free shelf, which Manchester Confidential singled out as 'a comprehensive alcohol-free wine selection that covers all your favourites taking in Riesling, Shiraz and Pinot Gris'. Expect zero-proof wine right across the board — De Bortoli's 'The Very Cautious One' Shiraz 0.0% and Vallformosa's Catalan 0% sparkling among them — plus white and rosé alternatives, and a proper run of artisan no-alcohol spirits and aperitifs. Lyre's Italian Orange and Italian Spritz stand in for an Aperol-style spritz, Three Spirit's botanical Livener, Nightcap and Social Elixir cover the functional end, and Almave's agave distillates and Botivo's bittersweet aperitif make long serves with tonic or soda. Pentire's Adrift, listed here previously, is no longer in the range as of August 2026. Staff are happy to open something or build an alcohol-free spritz to drink in, so it works equally well as a bottle-shop run or a low-key sober night out.
venues.pressQuote: a comprehensive alcohol-free wine selection that covers all your favourites taking in Riesling, Shiraz and Pinot Gris

venues.name: The Restaurant at 1900
venues.description: The Restaurant at 1900 opened in April 2018 inside the 1900 Building in Mission Woods, Kansas, a modernist structure built in 1967 for H.D. Lee Jeans and since restored and expanded by the architecture firm RMTA. Chef Linda Duerr leads the kitchen, and the restaurant was a James Beard semifinalist for Best Chef: Midwest in 2025 and for Outstanding Hospitality in 2023. Its beverage director is Doug Frost, one of only four people in the world to hold both the Master of Wine and Master Sommelier titles simultaneously, and the zero-proof list reflects that palate. The menu carries a section headed "Spirit Free Beverages": Verano ($12), a savoury build of tomato water, tomatillo, poblano, celery, white wine vinegar and onion; Agua de Jamaica ($9) with hibiscus, lemon, lime, ginger and canela; a Good Twin non-alcoholic sparkling from Villorba, Italy at $12; and Boulevard Space Camper NA, Heineken 0.0 and Clausthaler at $7 each.

venues.longDescription:
The Restaurant at 1900 opened in April 2018 inside the 1900 Building in Mission Woods, a small Kansas enclave on the edge of the metro, in a modernist structure originally built in 1967 for H.D. Lee Jeans and since restored and expanded by the architecture firm RMTA. The site has form: the Green Parrot Restaurant stood here from the 1920s until the late 1950s, known for home cooking. The kitchen is led by chef Linda Duerr, previously of The River Club, and the restaurant was a James Beard semifinalist for Best Chef: Midwest in 2025 and for Outstanding Hospitality in 2023. Dinner is serious and priced accordingly — chilled cucumber soup with lemon agrumato and toasted walnuts at $18, crispy potatoes with amur kaluga caviar and crème fraîche at $39, a rack of lamb with confit artichokes and potatoes gratinée at $52, and an American wagyu strip at $76.

The reason a non-drinker should care about this room more than most is the person running the drinks. Beverage director Doug Frost is one of only four people in the world to hold both the Master of Wine and Master Sommelier titles simultaneously, and the zero-proof list reflects that palate rather than being handed to whoever was free. The menu carries a section headed "Spirit Free Beverages", and the drinks are savoury and structured rather than sweet. Verano ($12) is the one to order: tomato water with tomatillo, poblano, celery, white wine vinegar and onion, which drinks closer to a clarified bloody mary than to a mocktail. Agua de Jamaica ($9) is the lighter option, hibiscus with lemon, lime, ginger and canela. Beyond the built drinks there is genuine non-alcoholic wine and beer — a Good Twin sparkling from Villorba in Italy at $12 a glass, Boulevard's Space Camper NA at $7, and Heineken 0.0 and Clausthaler at $7. One note: the restaurant shows two different sets of opening hours on its own site, so confirm when booking through their reservation link.
venues.pressQuote: We loved the idea of having something classic and non-boozy, like old fashioned egg cream, on the menu.

venues.name: Restaurant Born
venues.description: Chef Zor Tan's contemporary fine-dining room inside the restored Jinrikisha Station runs a genuine, full-length non-alcoholic beverage pairing (S$138 per person) that stands beside its wine flight rather than behind it. The zero-proof programme is built from in-house ferments and cold-pressed juices alongside teas sourced from China, Korea and Taiwan, echoing the same ingredients used on the plate. Named pours include the Celery & Shiso sparkling soda, the naturally fermented Jerusalem Artichoke 'Fly', a Milk Oolong from Anxi in Fujian and a Woojeon green tea from Jeju Island.
