venues.longDescription:
Restaurant Born occupies Jinrikisha Station, the restored 1903 heritage landmark at 1 Neil Road on the edge of Chinatown and Tanjong Pagar, and serves as the contemporary fine-dining restaurant of chef Zor Tan. The kitchen bridges Western technique with Chinese and East Asian flavour, and its degustation is designed to be followed course by course with either a wine or a non-alcoholic pairing.

The non-alcoholic programme costs S$138 per person and is treated as a full flight rather than an afterthought. It is composed of house-made ferments and cold-pressed juices alongside a curated run of teas from China, Korea and Taiwan, with seasonal selections drawn from Western and Chinese flavour combinations and from the same ingredients that appear in the dishes themselves.

Specific pours make the depth clear. A Celery & Shiso sparkling soda -- celery, shiso leaves, lemon zest and Himalayan pink salt -- works as a palate cleanser, while the Jerusalem Artichoke 'Fly' is a house ferment of Jerusalem artichoke with sugar and water, pasteurised and poured to shadow Tan's Jerusalem artichoke dish with lily bulbs and caviar. The tea side runs to a Milk Oolong from Anxi in Fujian and a Woojeon green tea from Jeju Island in Korea, among others.

For non-drinkers this is one of Singapore's most serious restaurant-level zero-proof pairings: bespoke, ingredient-led and priced as a genuine counterpart to the wine list, in a plush heritage dining room a short walk from Outram Park and Tanjong Pagar.
venues.pressQuote: The non-alcoholic beverage programme ($138 per person) at Chef Zor Tan's contemporary restaurant includes in-house ferments and juices along with teas from China, Korea and Taiwan.

venues.name: Restaurant Labyrinth
venues.description: One-Michelin-star Mod-Sin restaurant from chef LG Han where the Singapore-heritage tasting menu comes with a genuine non-alcoholic pairing option run course by course. The kitchen's zero-proof anchor is a house sparkling tea pairing that reviewers describe as floral, refreshing and not too sweet, offered as a full alternative to the wine flight rather than an afterthought. The room sits inside Esplanade Mall rather than a hotel or a shophouse, which undersells it: the cooking is a serious, narrative-led reading of Singaporean food, and the tea flight is built to track it course by course.
signatureDrinks: Non-Alcoholic Sparkling Tea Pairing - a floral, restrained house sparkling tea poured course by course as a full alternative to the wine flight
venues.longDescription:
Restaurant Labyrinth is chef LG Han's one-Michelin-star ode to Singapore, a 'Mod-Sin' tasting-menu restaurant tucked inside Esplanade Mall at 8 Raffles Avenue in Marina Centre. The kitchen reworks hawker and heritage dishes, from chilli crab to rojak, into a fine-dining narrative, and the room has carried a Michelin star while appearing on Asia's 50 Best and World's 50 Best Restaurants lists across recent years, with chef Zee Chan supporting daily service.

For non-drinkers, the draw is a proper beverage alternative rather than a token mocktail. Alongside the wine pairing, Labyrinth serves a non-alcoholic pairing built around a house sparkling tea that guests describe as floral, refreshing and restrained, poured course by course to track the menu. Diners on TripAdvisor have called the tea pairing 'arguably the better show' next to the wine and 'an excellent non-alcoholic pairing.'

Because the pairing follows the tasting menu, it is best arranged when booking; the restaurant runs Wednesday to Sunday with lunch on weekends, closed Mondays and Tuesdays. The non-alcoholic flight leans on the kitchen's own teas and infusions rather than commercial zero-proof spirit brands, which is exactly why it reads as a real, considered program.

The setting is the first thing most reviewers have to get past. FACT Magazines put it plainly in its review, calling the mall an unlikely home for a Michelin-starred tasting menu before conceding that Labyrinth makes its case within minutes. What follows is a menu of hawker and childhood references rebuilt with restraint rather than novelty. The closing stretch is the clearest illustration: a pink guava palate cleanser sharpened with sour plum salt, drawn from the chef's own after-school snack, and a kaya "toast" that sets house-made pandan-coconut jam against a teh tarik meringue.

That matters for anyone drinking alcohol-free, because it explains why the tea flight is not a compromise. This is food built on sweetness, sourness, palm sugar, pandan and chilli — flavours that wine frequently fights rather than flatters. A sparkling tea poured course by course has an easier job than a wine list here, and the kitchen composes it knowing that. Ask for the non-alcoholic pairing when you book rather than on arrival, since it is prepared alongside the menu rather than poured from bottles behind the bar.
venues.pressQuote: A mall is not the obvious setting for a MICHELIN-starred tasting menu, but Labyrinth makes its case in minutes, pairing black-box calm with a smart, Singapore-first story that tastes far more serious than its playful packaging suggests.

venues.name: Restaurant Olivia
venues.description: Restaurant Olivia is a pasta-focused Italian restaurant in Denver's Wash Park / South Gaylord neighborhood, opened in January 2020 by chef-proprietor Ty Michael Leon, beverage director and proprietor Austin James Carson and hospitality director and proprietor Heather Morrison. Its handmade pasta and beverage program have earned a place in the Michelin Guide Colorado, a James Beard nomination for Outstanding Hospitality and a 2025 Michelin Service Award. The non-alcoholic offering is a genuine part of the beverage list rather than an afterthought, though it currently runs through bottles and glasses rather than built cocktails: Codorniu Cava "Zero" is poured alcohol-free by the glass, Casa Emma's Zeero Bianco and Zeero Sangiovese carry the non-alcoholic wine section, and three Copenhagen Sparkling Teas are listed by the bottle. Seasonal zero-proof cocktails, including a clarified milk punch, appear on the menu at intervals through the year.
signatureDrinks: Codorniu Cava "Zero" (alcohol-free sparkling, by the glass)
Copenhagen Sparkling Tea "Bla" (green + white tea, by the bottle)
Casa Emma Zeero Bianco (non-alcoholic Tuscan white)
Casa Emma Zeero Sangiovese (non-alcoholic Tuscan red)
venues.longDescription:
Restaurant Olivia opened in January 2020 at 290 South Downing Street, on the South Gaylord side of Washington Park, as the second project from chef-proprietor Ty Michael Leon, beverage director and proprietor Austin James Carson, and hospitality director and proprietor Heather Morrison, for whose daughter the restaurant is named. It is a pasta restaurant first, with everything rolled and cut in house, and the run of recognition it has collected since is unusual for a room of its size: entries in the Michelin Guide Colorado in 2024 and 2025, a James Beard nomination for Outstanding Hospitality, and a 2025 Michelin Service Award. The beverage side is staffed accordingly, with a wine director and three sommeliers under Carson, and the wine list runs deep into Barolo, Barbaresco and northern Italian nebbiolo before broadening out to France and the United States.

The non-alcoholic offering is built into that list rather than kept on a separate card, and at present it runs through bottles and glasses rather than built cocktails. Codorniu Cava "Zero" is poured alcohol-free by the glass at $12, sitting in the same Bubbles line as the Franciacorta and the Bollinger. The Unique Beverages page carries a Non-Alcoholic Sparkling section of three Copenhagen Sparkling Teas at $76 for 750ml: the green-and-white-tea "Bla", the oolong-and-hibiscus rose "Lyserod", and the citrus-and-green-tea "Lysegron". A Non-Alcoholic Wine section follows with Casa Emma's Zeero Bianco and Zeero Sangiovese from Tuscany at $59 each, which means a table not drinking can be poured through a pasta menu from a wine list rather than from a soda gun. Seasonal zero-proof cocktails appear at intervals: Westword's January 1, 2026 round-up described a zero-proof milk punch with a spiced, vibrant flavour and velvety texture, noting it was on for that month only, which is the pattern to expect here. The restaurant serves Tuesday through Saturday from 5pm to 9pm and adds a 20% service charge split equitably among staff. Carson's team runs to a wine director, Scott Thomas, and three sommeliers, which is the reason the non-alcoholic bottles are chosen and described with the same care as the Barolo.
venues.pressQuote: Mocktails at Olivia are as purposeful as its spirited selection — and everything else, for that matter.

venues.name: Retreat Gastropub
venues.description: A Central West End fixture since 2015, Retreat Gastropub pairs elevated pub fare with one of St. Louis's most respected cocktail programs — and the current menu gives the zero-proof side its own dedicated Non-Alcoholic section. Alongside Giffard-based builds like the Nah-Perol Spritz and the tiki-leaning Jungle Birdie, you'll find a coffee-forward Cold Fashioned, the savory pineapple-and-bell-pepper Hush Pupper, a house shrub and soda, Athletic Brewing and Best Day NA beers, Gruvi's alcohol-free Dry Secco, and a Mighty Kind CBD seltzer. Now owned by longtime staffers Jennifer Anderson and Sydney Caldwell, Retreat serves dinner six nights a week plus a popular Sunday brunch.
venues.address: 2 N. Sarah St., St. Louis, MO 63108
venues.hours: Mon, Wed-Thu 4-9pm; Fri-Sat 4-10pm; Sun 11am-9pm; closed Tue
venues.longDescription:
Retreat Gastropub opened in October 2015 in the 6 North building at the corner of Sarah and Laclede, on the Central West End's edge near the Cortex innovation district. Founder Travis Howard and bar manager Tim Wiggins built it into one of St. Louis's defining modern gastropubs before going on to open Yellowbelly; the pair later passed the keys to Jennifer Anderson and Sydney Caldwell, longtime Retreat staffers — and a couple whose relationship began at the restaurant. Feast Magazine profiled the new owners in 2024 as they put their own mark on a spot known for elevated pub fare and an exceptional cocktail program.

The zero-proof program is not a Dry January stunt — it is a permanent, dedicated Non-Alcoholic section on the current cocktail menu. Six alcohol-free builds lead it: the Zero Gravity (tang cordial, almond, N/A aperitif, lime, mint, soda), the savory Hush Pupper (pineapple, yellow bell pepper, lemon, sparkling water), the Nah-Perol Spritz (Giffard non-alcoholic apertivo with alcohol-free bubbles and an orange twist), the tiki-style Jungle Birdie (pineapple, Giffard N/A apertivo, lime, sugar), the Cold Fashioned (cold brew coffee, simple syrup, bitters, orange twist), and a house shrub and soda. The list rounds out with Athletic Brewing's Free Wave hazy IPA, Best Day Brewing's N/A kolsch, Gruvi's alcohol-free Dry Secco by the bottle, and a Mighty Kind CBD seltzer — beer, bubbles, seltzer, and cocktails all covered without a drop of alcohol.

St. Louis Magazine put Retreat on its guide to the city's best nonalcoholic cocktails, writing that the beverage menu at this Central West End gastropub can hold its own with the best in town and singling out the Jungle Birdie. Reservations run through Resy, and the room does double duty: a serious bar up front, full dinner service every night except Tuesday, and a popular Sunday brunch where the Cold Fashioned stands in for the espresso martini. Expect burgers and elevated pub plates alongside the drinks — and a staff comfortable steering zero-proof drinkers through a real menu rather than an afterthought.
venues.pressQuote: In addition to the nearly two dozen boozy cocktails available at the bar, Retreat's mocktail menu covers all the bases.

venues.name: Retrograde
venues.description: Retrograde is a retro-futuristic cocktail lounge hidden behind the freezer door of Sweet Action Ice Cream on East 19th Avenue in Denver's Uptown. Guests flip a light switch by the door to signal staff, then enter a dim room styled with mid-century furniture, cosmic detailing and cult films projected on the walls. The cocktail list is named after B-movies, and the non-alcoholic list follows the same conceit: the current board, titled "Invasion of the Pod People", carries four built non-alcoholic cocktails rather than a single bartender's-choice option. They are Forbidden Texture (apple custard, toasted sugar, aromatic bitters, aqua faba), Low Orbit (apple, orange, marshmallow), The Thing on the Rocks (American oak tea, pear core, aromatic bitters) and The Day the Juice Stood Still (clarified orange juice, cold pear, lemon, sobacha, soda water). Retrograde is 21+, first-come first-served with no reservations, and caps parties at five.
signatureDrinks: Forbidden Texture (NA: apple custard, toasted sugar, aromatic bitters, aqua faba)
The Thing on the Rocks (NA: American oak tea, pear core, aromatic bitters)
The Day the Juice Stood Still (NA: clarified orange juice, cold pear, lemon, sobacha, soda water)
venues.longDescription:
Retrograde is entered through the walk-in freezer door at the back of Sweet Action Ice Cream at 530 East 19th Avenue in Uptown. There is no sign and no reservation system: guests walk past the ice cream counter, flip a light switch beside the freezer door and wait for a member of staff to open it. Behind it is a small, dim lounge furnished in mid-century pieces with cosmic detailing, cult and B-movie films projected on the walls, and a soundtrack to match. The bar is 21+, first-come first-served, and caps parties at five, which means a wait is normal on weekend nights. The full-proof menu is organised as a set of film-titled drinks, among them Bubba Ho-tep, Robo Vampire, Operazione Luna, Werewolf Bitches from Outer Space, The Apple, Moon Ghost, Tale of an Onion Witch and Up from the Depths, and the room was named in Westword's Best of Denver 2026 awards.

The bar keeps a standing N/A Cocktails section on its own site, and it is a genuine parallel menu rather than a substitution list. The current board is presented as a mock film poster titled "Invasion of the Pod People" and carries four built drinks. Forbidden Texture is the most technical of them: apple custard, toasted sugar, aromatic bitters and aqua faba, shaken for a foam that reads like a sour. Low Orbit is the lightest, apple, orange and marshmallow. The Thing on the Rocks, subtitled "It Opens Up", is a stirred, spirit-forward analogue built from American oak tea, pear core and aromatic bitters, and is the one to order if the point of the evening is to drink something that behaves like whiskey. The Day the Juice Stood Still is the long drink, clarified orange juice with cold pear, lemon, sobacha and soda water. Bartenders will also build off-menu on request. An earlier bartender's-choice item called A Virgin Among the Living Dead, cited in Do303's Denver non-alcoholic guide, has been replaced by this four-drink board. The bar opens at 6pm Sunday through Thursday and 5pm on Fridays and Saturdays, running to 1am every night, and cocktails start around $17; the non-alcoholic board is priced into the same list rather than discounted, which is consistent with how much work goes into it.
venues.pressQuote: Behind an unassuming freezer door in a Denver ice cream shop, Retrograde serves libations in a discreet, retro-futuristic cocktail lounge. Guests looking for the vibes without the booze can order 'A Virgin Among the Living Dead,' a bartender's choice of zero-proof spirits, seasonal syrups, and juices.

venues.name: Revival House
venues.description: Revival House is a neon-lit tiki bar in downtown Des Moines and it carries three alcohol-free builds, the deepest single list in the city. The Cyclone runs orange juice, passion purée, lime, demerara and grenadine; the Blue Hawaiian is built on pea flower tea with pineapple, coconut and lime; and the Double Tea Old Fashioned uses double-steeped Earl Grey with demerara, orange and Angostura. That last one is the interesting build — double-steeping tea concentrates its tannin, which is what stands in for the grip of whiskey in an old fashioned. Local coverage notes the booze-free versions come with a smaller bill too.
signatureDrinks: Cyclone — orange juice, passion purée, lime, demerara, grenadine
Blue Hawaiian — pea flower tea, pineapple, coconut, lime
Double Tea Old Fashioned — double-steeped Earl Grey, demerara, orange, Angostura
venues.longDescription:
Revival House is Des Moines' tiki bar — neon, thatch, a room built as an escape from an Iowa winter — and it carries three alcohol-free drinks, more than anywhere else in the city.

Two of them are what you would expect from the format, and that is a compliment. Tiki is the most forgiving cocktail style for anyone not drinking, because the drinks are assemblies of fresh juice, house syrups, spice and heavy garnish with the rum as one component among many. The Cyclone works orange juice and passion purée against lime, demerara and grenadine. The Blue Hawaiian gets its colour from butterfly pea flower tea rather than curaçao, with pineapple, coconut and lime.

The third is the one worth going for. The Double Tea Old Fashioned is built on double-steeped Earl Grey with demerara, orange and Angostura, and the technique is doing something specific. Steeping tea twice as strong concentrates its tannin, and tannin is the closest available substitute for the astringent grip that whiskey gives an old fashioned. Bergamot in the Earl Grey handles the citrus oil that an orange twist would provide. It is a genuinely well-reasoned drink rather than a sweet one wearing the name.

One small practical note that local coverage flags and that this directory rarely gets to report: the alcohol-free versions here cost less. Most bars charge the same for a mocktail as for a cocktail — defensible, given the labour, but a persistent irritation for people who drink alcohol-free every time they go out. Revival House passing on the saving is worth knowing.

Open 4pm to 10pm Wednesday, Thursday and Sunday, and 4pm to 1am on Friday and Saturday. Closed Monday and Tuesday.
venues.pressQuote: Double Tea Old Fashioned (steeped Earl Grey, demerara, orange, angostura)

venues.name: Revival at the Sawyer
venues.description: Revival, the bar at the Kimpton Sawyer hotel in Downtown Commons, runs a dedicated Sober Sundays menu — Italian Stallion, Little Rizz, Fleur de Lis and the Vezenkov Sour, the last a nod to the Kings player, which tells you the room knows exactly which crowd walks over from the arena. A named recurring alcohol-free menu is a stronger commitment than a permanent line or two, because it creates an occasion rather than an accommodation: there is a night when not drinking is the point rather than the exception. It sits inside the Kimpton Sawyer beside the Golden 1 Center, and serves to midnight Thursday through Saturday.
venues.longDescription:
Revival is the bar at the Kimpton Sawyer, the hotel embedded in Downtown Commons beside the Golden 1 Center, and its alcohol-free offering takes an unusual form: a recurring named menu called Sober Sundays, with four drinks of its own — Italian Stallion, Little Rizz, Fleur de Lis and the Vezenkov Sour.

That structure is worth thinking about. A permanent mocktail or two on the main list is useful but passive; it waits for a non-drinker to find it. A named night does something different — it advertises, it recurs, and it gives people a reason to turn up specifically. For anyone who has stopped drinking, the loss is rarely the alcohol itself; it is the occasion, the standing plan, the thing in the diary. A bar that creates one is addressing the actual problem.

The Vezenkov Sour is named for Sasha Vezenkov of the Sacramento Kings, which locates the whole exercise precisely: this is a hotel bar fifty yards from the arena, and its Sunday crowd includes people heading to or from a game. Sport and drinking are heavily bundled in American culture, and a good zero-proof drink named after a player is a small, effective way of unbundling them.

The hours run 4pm to 10pm early in the week and to midnight Thursday through Saturday. Being inside a Kimpton means it is comfortable for a non-drinker in the way hotel bars often are — nobody is tracking rounds, and there is no pressure to keep pace. Worth confirming that Sober Sundays is still running when you plan, since named menus rotate more than permanent ones.

The location does something else useful. Downtown Commons is a compact district, and Revival sits within a few minutes' walk of Dive Bar, Darling Aviary and Juju — four venues with documented alcohol-free drinks inside a small radius. For a visitor staying downtown, or a group forming a plan on the night, that density is the thing that makes not drinking easy rather than effortful. Sacramento is not a large city by American standards, and its centre being walkable turns a handful of good venues into something closer to a scene.
venues.pressQuote: Revival at the Sawyer: Sober Sundays menu includes Italian Stallion, Little Rizz, Fleur de Lis, and Vezenkov Sour.

venues.name: Rhinegeist Brewery
venues.description: Rhinegeist occupies the historic 1895 Christian Moerlein bottling plant in Over-the-Rhine, a soaring brick hall that has anchored Cincinnati's craft-beer revival since 2013. In fall 2025 the brewery brought its beer heritage to the sober-curious with Ghost, a dedicated non-alcoholic line brewed on Sustainable Beverage Technologies' BrewVo nested-fermentation process rather than dealcoholized after the fact. Ghost Pils, an NA German pilsner, took a bronze medal in the Non-Alcoholic Beer category at the 2025 Great American Beer Festival and a silver at the 2026 Craft Beer and Brewing NANA Cup; Ghost Haze pours as a full-flavored NA hazy IPA and is a year-round release in cans and on draft. Both sit at or below 0.5% ABV and sell in 12oz six-packs for taproom pickup and shipping. A West Coast-style Ghost Hops was announced for early 2026 but has not appeared on the brewery's beer list, so the Ghost line stands at two beers. The cavernous taproom pairs cornhole, ping-pong, and rooftop views with a genuinely award-winning zero-proof pour.
signatureDrinks: Ghost Pils (non-alcoholic German pilsner; 2025 GABF bronze, 2026 Craft Beer & Brewing NANA Cup silver)
Ghost Haze (non-alcoholic hazy IPA, year-round, cans and draft)
venues.longDescription:
Founded in 2013 by Bob Bonder and Bryant Goulding, Rhinegeist ("ghost of the Rhine") took over the cavernous former Christian Moerlein bottling plant, an 1895 brick landmark on Elm Street in the heart of Over-the-Rhine's historic Brewery District. The taproom quickly became a cornerstone of Cincinnati's craft-beer renaissance and one of the region's largest independent brewers, known for its soaring industrial hall, cornhole and ping-pong, and a popular rooftop bar overlooking the neighborhood.

The brewery had explored non-alcoholic beer for years but held back until it could match its own quality bar, lacking both pasteurizing equipment and space. The breakthrough came through a partnership with Sustainable Beverage Technologies and its patented BrewVo process, a nested-fermentation method that repeatedly strips alcohol from partially brewed beer while adding fresh wort for additional fermentation. The result launched in August 2025 as Ghost, a dedicated NA sub-brand. Ghost Pils is a non-alcoholic German pilsner with smooth, bready malts and a light, crisp finish that won a bronze medal in the Non-Alcoholic Beer category at the 2025 Great American Beer Festival and a silver medal at the 2026 Craft Beer and Brewing Magazine NANA Cup; Ghost Haze is a full-flavored NA hazy IPA with stone-fruit notes, brewed year-round for cans and draft. Both are at or below 0.5% ABV, sold in 12oz six-packs, and distributed across nine states (Ohio, Kentucky, Indiana, West Virginia, Illinois, Pennsylvania, Michigan, Tennessee and Wisconsin). A West Coast-style Ghost Hops IPA was announced for early 2026 but has not appeared on the brewery's beer list as of August 2026, and the Ghost line remains two beers.

The taproom sits at 1910 Elm St and is open Monday–Thursday 3–10pm, Friday–Saturday noon–midnight and Sunday noon–9pm; reach it at (513) 381-1367 or @rhinegeist on Instagram. It suits groups, game nights and anyone wanting a lively brewery atmosphere without missing out. Note that this is a full working brewery whose core business is alcoholic beer, so the Ghost NA beers are most reliably found in cans and six-packs for pickup; call ahead if you specifically want them on draft.
venues.pressQuote: It's awesome to see a win for this category here in Cincinnati!

venues.name: Rhody Roots
venues.description: Rhody Roots on Main Street in Warren keeps a real bank of non-alcoholic spirits and non-alcoholic beers behind the bar — not a token can in the fridge — and will build any cocktail on its list without alcohol. Stocking finished NA spirits and NA beer alongside a make-anything-zero-proof policy puts it among the best-equipped rooms in the state for a non-drinker, twenty minutes down the bay from Providence.
venues.longDescription:
Warren is a small town on the east side of Narragansett Bay, about twenty minutes from Providence, and Rhody Roots sits on its Main Street. It is worth the drive for anyone not drinking, because it solves the two problems that make most bars difficult in a single stroke.

The first is stock. Rhody Roots keeps a genuine selection of non-alcoholic spirits and non-alcoholic beers behind the bar, rather than the single dusty bottle of alcohol-free lager that passes for provision in most places. That means the raw material for a proper drink exists on the premises — which sounds obvious, and is the thing most venues get wrong.

The second is willingness, backed by capability. Any cocktail on the list can be made without alcohol. Because the bar holds real non-alcoholic spirits, that is a substitution rather than a subtraction: the drink keeps its structure. A handful of the house cocktails are specifically flagged as working well in their zero-proof form, and the bartenders will steer you toward those if you ask.

We have not published named drinks here. The list rotates and we were unable to read Rhody Roots' current menu directly, so while the programme is well documented in Rhode Island coverage, the specific names would be a guess. The stocking policy and the make-anything-zero-proof offer are the durable facts, and they are what make this a destination rather than a fallback. Warren also sits on the East Bay Bike Path, which makes it a natural stop on a ride rather than a special trip.
venues.pressQuote: boasts a good selection of non-alcoholic spirits and beers and can turn any of their cocktails into a mocktail

venues.name: Rich Table
venues.description: Rich Table is a Hayes Valley fine-dining mainstay opened in 2012 by married chefs Evan and Sarah Rich, both alumni of acclaimed kitchens, who built a name on market-driven California cooking. Now in its 13th year, it ranked #3 on the San Francisco Chronicle's 2025 Top 100 Bay Area Restaurants and anchors a growing family that includes RT Rotisserie and, as of January 2026, RT Bistro. Its drink program treats non-alcoholic guests as first-class: the current list carries dedicated "Non-Alcoholic Refreshers" and "Non-Alcoholic Milk Wash" sections of house cocktails built on NA spirits and house ingredients, alongside a non-alcoholic beer from nearby Best Day Brewing of Sausalito. Named zero-proof pours — like The Remedy (NA agave spirit, pineapple, carrot, ginger, lemon, bitters), the Strawberry Fauxgroni, and Pod Culture — rotate with the seasons, mirroring the same farm-driven philosophy as the food.
venues.longDescription:
Rich Table opened in 2012 at 199 Gough Street in Hayes Valley, run by married chefs Evan and Sarah Rich, who met in a New York kitchen and moved west before going out on their own. The cooking is market-driven California food summarised by the line printed on the restaurant's own menu — "Go to the market, see what's good and cook it" — executed with more technique than that suggests. More than a decade on, the restaurant placed No. 3 on the San Francisco Chronicle's 2025 Top 100 Bay Area Restaurants and anchors a small family of businesses including RT Rotisserie and, from January 2026, RT Bistro. Service runs nightly from 5pm. Surveying the city's best non-alcoholic drinking in December 2023, The San Francisco Standard's Astrid Kane wrote that "chefs Sarah and Evan Rich have been stalwarts of Hayes Valley's impressive food scene for well over a decade, serving elegant, rarefied comfort food."

The beverage list treats non-drinking guests as a standing category rather than a special case. The current menu carries dedicated "Non-Alcoholic Refreshers" and "Non-Alcoholic Milk Wash" sections — the second is the unusual one, since milk-washing is a clarification technique normally reserved for spirits and applying it to a zero-proof build is a deliberate piece of kitchen labour rather than a substitution. Named pours rotate with the seasons in step with the food: The Remedy (non-alcoholic agave spirit, pineapple, carrot, ginger, lemon and bitters), the Strawberry Fauxgroni and Pod Culture have all appeared on the current list, while earlier menus ran the Quince-Essential, made with white peppercorn, pine-smoked tea, cardamom, quince and half-and-half, and the Pear Necessities, built from verjus, pear, ginger, applesauce and maple foam. Best Day Brewing's non-alcoholic beer, brewed across the bridge in Sausalito, covers the beer slot. Because the zero-proof drinks turn over on the same seasonal cycle as the tasting menu, the specific names change but the sections do not.
venues.pressQuote: Chefs Sarah and Evan Rich have been stalwarts of Hayes Valley's impressive food scene for well over a decade, serving elegant, rarefied comfort food.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Astrid Kane, The San Francisco Standard

venues.name: Rigo
venues.description: Rigo is a Spanish-Italian restaurant on Kapahulu Avenue, serving tapas, wood-fired pizzas, house-made pastas and grill plates. It trades as Rigo, not Rigo's — older coverage uses the possessive, and the current name does not. Its documented non-alcoholic drink is That Cucumber Thing, built from cucumber, mint, lime and soda: a dry, herbaceous, low-sugar build of the kind that is much rarer on Honolulu menus than the tropical-fruit default, and one that works with salty Mediterranean food in a way a pineapple drink does not. The restaurant sits on the Kapahulu strip between Waikīkī and Kaimukī, a few minutes from Da Cove.
signatureDrinks: That Cucumber Thing (cucumber, mint, lime, soda)
venues.longDescription:
Rigo occupies 885 Kapahulu Avenue, on the corridor that runs inland from Waikīkī towards Kaimukī and holds a disproportionate share of Honolulu's good independent restaurants. The kitchen works a Spanish-Italian brief — tapas, wood-fired pizza, house-made pasta and smoky grill plates — describing itself as Mediterranean classics with a Hawaiian spirit. One naming note for anyone searching: the restaurant trades as Rigo, or Rigo Spanish Italian, and several older listings and articles still call it Rigo's. The possessive is not current.

Its non-alcoholic contribution is a single documented drink, That Cucumber Thing, and it is worth more than its simplicity suggests. Cucumber, mint, lime and soda is about as spare as a built drink gets, but the profile it produces — vegetal, cool, herbaceous, with almost no sugar — is close to absent from the rest of this guide. Honolulu's zero-proof drinks lean overwhelmingly on tropical fruit: pineapple, passionfruit, lychee, guava, hibiscus. Those are local, they are excellent, and they bring real acidity, but they are also all sweet, and a visitor working through the city's non-alcoholic lists ends up drinking a lot of sugar. A cucumber-and-mint build is the natural counterweight, and it is specifically what you want alongside salty, oily Mediterranean food — jamón, anchovy, blistered pizza crust — where a sweet drink actively fights the plate. That pairing logic is the same reason a dry sherry or a vinho verde works with tapas, and it is a genuine piece of thinking about what a non-drinker should be given with this particular menu rather than a default. The rest of the offer is standard soft drinks, which is why the venue sits at a three. Opening hours are limited and split across lunch and dinner services, so checking before travelling is sensible.
venues.pressQuote: Light and crisp with cucumber, mint, lime and soda, this drink paired perfectly with rich cheeses.

venues.name: Ripple Wine Bar
venues.description: Ripple Wine Bar's O'Bryonville outpost is a wine-focused room that treats non-drinkers as real guests rather than an afterthought. Alongside 40-plus wines by the glass, the bar pours Leitz non-alcoholic sparkling riesling and rosé — a genuine dealcoholized wine, not grape juice — plus rotating alcohol-free beer and wines. Two standing house mocktails round out the zero-proof list: the Ginger Garcia (ginger beer, apple, lime, soda) and the Althea (strawberry, pineapple, lemon, soda), both built to pair with charcuterie boards and flatbreads. It's the same menu run at the original Covington, KY location. Founded by Matt and Kathleen Haws in 2019, Ripple earned a spot on Wine Spectator's 2025 "Editors' Favorite Wine Bars" list, making it a comfortable, elevated place to order without the buzz.
signatureDrinks: Ginger Garcia (ginger beer, apple, lime, soda)
venues.longDescription:
Matt and Kathleen Haws opened the first Ripple Wine Bar in Covington, Kentucky, in 2019 at 4 West Pike Street, building it as a thoughtfully designed American wine bar that is half bar and half dining room. In August 2023 they opened a near-identical second location in Cincinnati's O'Bryonville neighborhood at 2000 Madison Road — same vibe, same hours and, per the owners, the same food menu. Wine director Molly Decker oversees roughly 43 wines by the glass and more than 100 bottles, and in October 2025 Wine Spectator named Ripple to its "Editors' Favorite Wine Bars" list alongside bars in New York, Paris, Florence and Tokyo, on top of the magazine's Award of Excellence.

For guests skipping alcohol, Ripple keeps a small but genuine zero-proof selection. The centerpiece is Leitz non-alcoholic sparkling wine — the German producer's dealcoholized sparkling riesling and rosé — poured so a non-drinker can still toast with something wine-like rather than settling for juice. The bar also stocks alcohol-free beer and non-alcoholic still wines. Two standing house mocktails complete the list: the Ginger Garcia (ginger beer, apple, lime and soda) and the Althea (strawberry, pineapple, lemon and soda), both designed to pair with the kitchen's charcuterie boards, flatbreads and petite entrées.

The O'Bryonville room is warm and intimate, open Monday through Thursday 4pm to 11pm and Friday and Saturday 4pm to midnight, closed Sunday. Reservations run through OpenTable and Resy, and walk-ins fill the bar. Because this is first and foremost a wine bar, the non-alcoholic lineup is compact — two mocktails plus the NA wines and beer — and the food menu shifts with the seasons, so it's worth asking your server what's current. It suits a date, a small group, or anyone who wants an elevated glass-in-hand evening without the alcohol.
venues.pressQuote: If you want the wine without the buzz, Ripple serves non-alcoholic Leitz sparkling riesling and rosé, or you can try a mocktail like the Ginger Garcia (ginger beer, apple, lime and soda) or the Althea (strawberry, pineapple, lemon and soda).

venues.name: Rita's Seaside Grille
venues.description: Hall family beachfront grille at the foot of Center Street near the Folly Beach Pier, run by the same group behind Halls Chophouse in Charleston. The kitchen serves scratch-made American fare, house-smoked barbecue, and coastal seafood. Its drink menu carries a small set of named mocktails priced at $7 alongside freshly brewed iced tea, sodas, frozen Jarritos, and cold brew coffee.
signatureDrinks: Rita's Remedy (iced tea, fresh ginger, lemon)

naMenuItems.name: Strawberry Fields
naMenuItems.description: strawberry purée, mint, lemon

venues.longDescription:
Rita's Seaside Grille is a Hall family-owned restaurant steps from the Folly Beach Pier, sharing ownership with Halls Chophouse in downtown Charleston. The laid-back beach-bar concept opens daily for breakfast, weekend brunch, lunch, and dinner, with live music often on the patio in the afternoons.

The zero-proof side of the menu lists four named mocktails for $7 each: the Strawberry Fields (strawberry puree, mint, lemon), the Garden Spritz (cucumber, basil, lime), and Rita's Remedy (iced tea, fresh ginger, lemon), plus Rita's Cold Brew Coffee. Freshly brewed iced tea, sodas, and frozen Jarritos round out the non-alcoholic options.

venues.name: Ritual
venues.description: Ritual, the late-night cocktail lounge that took over the former Alice space in Bryan Place in January 2026, gives non-drinkers a dedicated "Elixirs" section rather than a token Shirley Temple — four spirit-free cocktails built with the same intent as the full bar. The Elixirs were developed alongside the alcoholic list by Paul Ramon, named a Top 50 World Class U.S. Bartender in 2022, so they get the same modern-texture treatment (matcha cold foams, spiced infusions) as their spirited counterparts. The operating team frames the non-alcoholic program as a deliberate effort at "intentionality and inclusivity," not an afterthought.
venues.longDescription:
Ritual opened in January 2026 in the former Alice restaurant space at 1623 N. Hall Street, in the Bryan Place pocket of Old East Dallas. The sophisticated late-night lounge is the work of three hospitality veterans: Justin Kalhoff (Alice, The Standard Pour, Black Swan Saloon), Chris Evans (Green Light Social), and Cole Howard (a Komodo Dallas operating partner and former Hendy's on Henderson manager). The cocktail program was built by consultant Paul Ramon, who was named one of the Top 50 World Class U.S. Bartenders in 2022.

What makes Ritual notable for non-drinkers is a full, dedicated menu section of non-alcoholic "Elixirs" — four alcohol-free cocktails positioned to emphasize, in the team's words, "intentionality and inclusivity." Rather than an off-menu mocktail on request, the Elixirs are printed alongside the spirited list and get the same craft treatment Ramon brings to the rest of the bar, where signatures lean on modern textures like matcha cold foam and Biscoff-spiced infusions.

The lounge runs a late-night, evening-only schedule (roughly 5 p.m. to 2 a.m.), with light plates such as beef tartare, grilled cheese, cheese eclairs, salads and lobster rolls, plus live music midweek. The space keeps an exposed-brick, tiled-bar look, with a graffiti-mural bathroom by artist Leah Kirsch.
venues.pressQuote: The menu will boast a full list of non-alcoholic "Elixirs," in an effort to emphasize "intentionality and inclusivity."

venues.name: Ritual Kava Lounge
venues.description: Ritual is an alcohol-free kava lounge on North Dale Mabry in Carrollwood, open 10am to 1am every day, and it is programmed harder than most rooms in the category: silent discos, bingo nights and ping-pong tournaments run alongside the drinks. Seating is split between bean bags and bar stools, which suits both the study crowd in the afternoon and the social crowd at night, and the hosts, Dylan and Gloria, are the thing regulars mention first. The list covers kava, teas and coffee. IMPORTANT for readers in recovery: kratom is served here alongside the kava. It acts on opioid receptors and carries real dependence and withdrawal risk, unlike kava, so it is worth asking which is in your cup.
venues.address: 11127 N Dale Mabry Hwy, Tampa, FL 33618
venues.longDescription:
Ritual is an alcohol-free kava lounge on North Dale Mabry Highway in Carrollwood, open 10am to 1am every day, and it is programmed harder than almost anything else in the category. Silent discos, bingo nights and ping-pong tournaments run alongside the drinks, which is the difference between a room that sells an alternative to alcohol and a room that offers an alternative to going to the pub. The seating is split deliberately between bean bags and bar stools — the former for the afternoon study crowd, the latter for the evening social one — and the same space does both jobs across a day.

The thing regulars mention first is not the drinks but the hosts. Dylan and Gloria are named repeatedly in accounts of the place as people who know their regulars and look after them, and that is worth recording because it is the actual mechanism by which a third place works. A bar without alcohol has to give people a reason to come back that is not chemical, and being known by name is the strongest one available.

Kava is the ground root of Piper methysticum, a shrub native to the South Pacific islands, prepared as a cold water infusion and drunk socially across Fiji, Vanuatu, Tonga and Samoa for roughly three thousand years. It contains no alcohol. It tastes earthy and bitter, numbs the lips and tongue on the first mouthful, and is mildly sedative rather than intoxicating in the way alcohol is. Kava exhibits reverse tolerance, so regular drinkers usually need less rather than more, and a first visit is best paced across an hour or two. Alongside it the lounge serves teas and coffee.

Carrollwood sits north of central Tampa and is largely residential, which makes a 1am close here meaningful in a way it would not be downtown — this is the local, not a destination, and the people using it are mostly walking back into the same neighbourhood.

One disclosure belongs in the open rather than in a footnote. Kratom is served here alongside the kava, and the lounge presents both as alternatives to alcohol. That framing is true as far as it goes, and incomplete in a way that matters to the people this directory is written for. Kratom is the leaf of a Southeast Asian tree, Mitragyna speciosa, whose principal alkaloids act on the opioid receptors; regular use produces tolerance and a real withdrawal syndrome, several US states ban it outright, and concentrated 7-hydroxymitragynine products face active federal scheduling. Kava has no comparable dependence profile. Both are poured from the same bar, so ask which is in your cup.

venues.name: River Club
venues.description: River Club is a Mediterranean-coastal restaurant and bar on the Georgetown waterfront at 3000 K Street NW, serving mezze-style shareable plates drawn from Lebanon, Italy and Spain, with patio seating over the Potomac. It trades seven days with lunch, weekend brunch, dinner and a weekday happy hour. The drinks programme is notable for a dedicated zero-proof section, headed 0% Booze, whose cocktails mirror the food: a 0% Lemon Basil on basil-infused Seedlip Grove 42 with lemon, celery and celery salt; a 0% Sumac 75 on Freixenet alcohol-removed sparkling with sumac syrup, lemon and mint; and a 0% Farid Has to Drive with cucumber-and-fennel shrub and chinotto soda, all $15. Brunch adds 0% Aperol and Hugo spritzes on Undone. Peroni 0.0 is $9.

venues.longDescription:
River Club sits at 3000 K Street NW on the Georgetown waterfront, with patio seating looking over the Potomac, and it serves Mediterranean-coastal cooking - vibrant, mezze-style shareable plates drawn from the culinary traditions of Lebanon, Italy and Spain. It trades seven days a week across lunch, weekend brunch, dinner and a weekday happy hour, which matters more than it sounds: it means the zero-proof card is available at every service rather than only at dinner. Resy highlighted the venue in its 2025 roundup of Washington, DC non-alcoholic cocktails, noting that its beverage book is filled with zero-proof cocktails each influenced by coastal regions of the Mediterranean from Lebanon to Spain and Italy.

What distinguishes the list is that the zero-proof drinks are typed and priced as cocktails rather than filed under soft drinks. They carry the same $15 price as most of the spirited menu, they are built from named alcohol-free products rather than juice and syrup, and they occupy their own headed section of the printed card, 0% Booze, instead of a footnote. The current builds run a 0% Lemon Basil on basil-infused Seedlip Grove 42 with lemon, celery and celery salt; a 0% Sumac 75 on Freixenet alcohol-removed sparkling with sumac syrup, lemon and mint; and a 0% Farid Has to Drive of lemon, mint, cucumber-and-fennel shrub and chinotto soda. The brunch card adds a 0% Aperol Spritz and a 0% Hugo Spritz, both built on Undone's alcohol-free aperitif and sparkling. Peroni 0.0 is $9, and alcohol-removed sparkling wine is poured by the glass.

Beyond the cocktails the kitchen keeps a short non-alcoholic list of Acqua Panna and San Pellegrino at $9 and Mexican Coke, Mexican Sprite, Diet Coke, Topo Chico and the bittersweet Italian soda Stappi Red Bitter at $6, so a table that is not drinking still has range across a long meal. Reservations run through SevenRooms. Anyone visiting specifically for a drink from this list should know that the composition rotates: a zero-proof raspberry cobbler on Seedlip Grove 42 anchored earlier versions and is no longer served as of August 2026, and the current builds lean on sumac, shrubs and chinotto rather than on the Seedlip range alone.
venues.pressQuote: River Club's beverage book is filled with zero-proof cocktails, each influenced by coastal regions of the Mediterranean from Lebanon to Spain and Italy.

venues.name: Ro Sham Beaux
venues.description: Ro Sham Beaux is one of three Sacramento bars run by the Irish Hospitality Group, and all of them stock the same useful pair: the St. Agrestis Phony Negroni, a bottled non-alcoholic frizzante that is among the best ready-to-drink zero-proof products made, and Guinness 0. A group standardising its alcohol-free stock across venues is quietly valuable — it means you can walk into any of the three without checking first, which removes the research that usually precedes a night out for someone not drinking. Ro Sham Beaux is the Midtown J Street location, open from 2pm most days and noon at weekends.
venues.longDescription:
Ro Sham Beaux is a Midtown bar on J Street and one of three Sacramento venues operated by the Irish Hospitality Group, alongside The Snug and The Butterscotch Den. All three carry the same non-alcoholic stock, and that consistency is the reason to know about any of them.

The Phony Negroni from St. Agrestis is the standout product. It is a bottled non-alcoholic frizzante built to replicate a Negroni — bitter, herbal, faintly sweet, served cold from the bottle — and it is widely regarded as one of the best ready-to-drink zero-proof products on the market. Its virtue in a bar setting is that it requires nothing of the bartender: no technique, no specialist ingredients, no risk of the drink being made badly by someone who has never made it before. You get the same drink every time. For a non-drinker, reliability is often worth more than ambition.

Guinness 0 covers the beer case, and it is genuinely good — closer to the original than most non-alcoholic beers manage, because Guinness's character comes from roasted barley rather than from alcohol.

The wider point is the group standardisation. Most of the labour of not drinking in a city is research: checking menus, guessing, arriving prepared for disappointment. When an operator stocks the same alcohol-free products across three bars, that work disappears — you can suggest any of them without looking anything up.

Ro Sham Beaux opens at 2pm most days and noon at weekends, running to midnight on Friday and Saturday. The Snug in Midtown and The Butterscotch Den on Broadway keep later hours still.

It is worth being straight about the ceiling here. Two stocked products and some non-alcoholic cocktails is a solid neighbourhood offering, not a programme — there is no bartender developing zero-proof specs, no house-made syrups, nothing like the tepache work at Juju or the Lyre's builds at Kupros. The grade reflects that. What it is instead is dependable, which for a bar you might end up in three times a month is arguably the more useful quality of the two.
venues.pressQuote: Irish Hospitality Group (The Snug, Ro Sham Beaux, The Butterscotch Den): Phony Negroni by St. Agrestis, Guinness 0, and various NA cocktails.

venues.name: ROAM by San Chez
venues.description: ROAM by San Chez is a downtown restaurant at 250 Monroe Avenue NW from the family behind San Chez, the long-running Grand Rapids tapas house. It keeps what Experience Grand Rapids calls an extensive non-alcoholic drink menu, and the range is broader than most: hot teas and house drip coffees at one end, horchata and rotating house-made Italian cream sodas in the middle, and composed zero-proof drinks such as the Rosemary-Elderflower Spritzer — herbal syrup, lemon, soda and butterfly pea tea — at the other. The kitchen team has said publicly that it is glad to see the city offering more alcohol-free options in order to be more inclusive, which reads as a statement of intent rather than a marketing line.

signatureDrinks: Rosemary-Elderflower Spritzer (herbal syrup, lemon, soda, butterfly pea tea)
venues.longDescription:
ROAM by San Chez occupies 250 Monroe Avenue NW in downtown Grand Rapids and carries the name of San Chez Bistro, the tapas restaurant that has been a fixture of the city's dining scene for decades. The format is more casual and more all-day than its parent, and the drink list reflects that: rather than a short cocktail card, ROAM publishes a wide non-alcoholic range designed to cover a guest from a morning coffee through to an evening meal without ever handing them a soft drink by default. Experience Grand Rapids singles the restaurant out for exactly this, noting that it offers an extensive N/A drink menu that includes warm and cozy favourites like hot teas and house drip coffees.

The non-alcoholic list works in three registers. The first is hot and simple: house drip coffees and a tea selection, which makes the room usable in daylight. The second is the house soda program — horchata, and Italian cream sodas made in house in flavours that rotate, which are the drinks most likely to satisfy a guest who wants something sweet and cold without pretending to be a cocktail. The third is composed zero-proof mixing, best represented by the Rosemary-Elderflower Spritzer, which layers a herbal syrup with lemon, soda and butterfly pea tea; the tea is the interesting part, since it shifts colour with acidity and gives the drink the visual event that a spirit-free build otherwise lacks. Speaking to Grand Rapids Magazine, the restaurant said it was glad to see the city offering more alcohol-free options, to be more inclusive — a framing that puts the program in the context of who gets to feel comfortable at a table rather than in the context of a trend. Its downtown position, a short walk from the Amway Grand and from Max's, makes it a practical first stop on an alcohol-free evening in the centre of the city.
venues.pressQuote: ROAM offers an extensive N/A drink menu that includes warm and cozy favorites like hot teas and house drip coffees.

venues.name: Rob Roy
venues.description: Rob Roy is a Belltown cocktail bar at 2332 2nd Avenue, open since 2009 and owned by Anu Apte, who runs it with Chris Elford under their Canoe Ventures group alongside Navy Strength and Vinnie's Wine Shop. Rob Roy was a James Beard finalist for Outstanding Bar in 2023, and Apte herself was a James Beard semifinalist for Outstanding Professional in Cocktail Service in both 2025 and 2026. It was the first bar in Washington State to run its own ice programme. Its non-alcoholic drinks get a full printed section headed "Designated Drivers", six deep at $16–$17 and all marked 0% ABV: Silver Rush (Seedlip Spice 94, verjus, lemon, Giffard jasmine, salted honey), Cornucopia (Seedlip Notas de Agave, non-alcoholic Lucano amaro, Pathfinder, clarified in coconut), Ace of Cups (Three Spirits Livener, winter melon, Thai basil, ginseng), and three botanical elixirs — The Mood, Pick Me Up and Dream Maker. Bitburger Drive is $6. Note that three of those drinks use mood-active botanicals; see the full description. 21+ only.
venues.longDescription:
Rob Roy has been on 2nd Avenue in Belltown since 2009, and it did something early that shaped Seattle drinking: in 2009 it started ordering 300-pound blocks of ice, the first bar in Washington State to run an ice programme. Anu Apte owns it, and runs it with Chris Elford under their Canoe Ventures group, which also holds Navy Strength and Vinnie's Wine Shop nearby. The recognition is worth stating exactly, because it is often garbled: Rob Roy the bar was a James Beard finalist for Outstanding Bar in 2023, and Apte personally was a James Beard semifinalist for Outstanding Professional in Cocktail Service in both 2025 and 2026 — semifinalist in her case, not finalist or winner. Food is snacks only and cheerfully so: goldfish crackers $5, popcorn $6, old-fashioned beef jerky $9, and a $13 "Surf & Turf" that is the crackers and the jerky together. It is 21-and-over, and reservations are for large parties only — otherwise just walk in.

The non-alcoholic list is one of the deepest in Seattle and has a name that tells you the bar thought about it: Designated Drivers. Six drinks, $16 to $17, every one printed 0% ABV. Three are built like cocktails — Silver Rush downshifts a Gold Rush using Seedlip Spice 94 with verjus, lemon, Giffard jasmine and salted honey; Cornucopia is a Pimm's Cup rebuilt from Seedlip Notas de Agave, a house non-alcoholic Lucano amaro and Pathfinder, then clarified in coconut, which is real technique; Ace of Cups uses Three Spirits Livener with winter melon, Thai basil and ginseng. Bitburger Drive covers beer at $6. The other three deserve a note before you order. The Mood, Pick Me Up and Dream Maker are botanical elixirs rather than mocktails, built on things like lion's mane, yerba maté, damiana, guayusa and schisandra, and the menu sells them on effect — "blissful feeling", "euphoric feels", and in Dream Maker's case a limit of two per guest. No dosages are printed. None of that is alcohol or cannabis, and for most people they are simply interesting herbal drinks. But if you are avoiding anything mood-altering, order from the first three.

venues.name: Rochambeau
venues.description: Rochambeau is a French brasserie on Boylston Street in Back Bay, steps from Copley Square, with a street-level bar and a large dining room running from morning through late service. Its drinks list keeps a named non-alcoholic section rather than a token substitute, and the builds use real zero-proof products rather than juice. Red Lace is made with Tilden Lacewing, strawberry Persian rose, honey and egg white; Blueberries for Sal uses CleanCo non-alcoholic tequila with blueberry, mint, lime, orgeat and soda; the N/A Hugo Spritz is built on Giffard's alcohol-free elderflower with lime, mint and alcohol-free sparkling; and the Spritz Del Conte is an Italian-style alcohol-free spritz. The kitchen and bar also keep additional non-alcoholic wine, beer and spirits available on request.

venues.longDescription:
Rochambeau sits at 900 Boylston Street in the middle of Back Bay, a large French brasserie with a bar opening directly onto the street and a dining room that runs brunch daily and dinner every night. It is a room built for volume and occasion rather than intimacy, which is precisely why its non-alcoholic list matters: a table of six at a Back Bay brasserie is the exact situation in which someone not drinking ends up with a soda, and Rochambeau does not make them do that.

The alcohol-free drinks are listed by name on the same menu as the cocktails and are built with the same technique. Red Lace uses Tilden Lacewing, the Massachusetts-made non-alcoholic cocktail base, with a strawberry Persian rose element, honey and egg white for texture. Blueberries for Sal, named for the Robert McCloskey book, is built on CleanCo non-alcoholic tequila with blueberry, mint, lime, orgeat and soda. The N/A Hugo Spritz uses Giffard's alcohol-free elderflower with lime, mint and alcohol-free sparkling wine at $16, and the Spritz Del Conte is an alcohol-free Italian-style spritz at $15, listed with its residual figure of under 0.05% ABV printed on the menu, which is the kind of disclosure that lets a reader make their own decision. The house also notes that further non-alcoholic wine, beer and spirits are available on request by phone or email, so the printed list is a floor rather than a ceiling. Meet Boston, the city's official tourism organisation, included Rochambeau in its January 2026 round-up of where to get zero-proof drinks in Boston, alongside Backbar, Pagu and Alden & Harlow. Meet Boston grouped it with Backbar in Union Square, Pagu in Central Square and Alden & Harlow in Harvard Square, which puts Rochambeau among the small set of rooms the city's own tourism office points visitors toward when they ask where to drink without alcohol in Boston.
venues.pressQuote: Rochambeau's zero-proof drinks mirror the restaurant's refined aesthetic, with elegance that highlights citrus, floral notes, and subtle sweetness.

venues.name: Roll Up Herbal Bar
venues.description: Roll Up Herbal Bar is a dedicated zero-proof cocktail lounge beside the Gateway to the Smokies arch on Main Street in downtown Waynesville, about thirty miles west of Asheville. It serves mocktails exclusively, crafted with herbal infusions and house-made mixes and designed to either calm or energise. Its owner, Sam, is unusually clear about why it exists: she started it for one reason, to provide culinary beverages for people who are not drinking alcohol but crave the complexity of a well-crafted cocktail. She is an experienced bartender, and also an artist and a former theatre kid, which she says is why the drinks are built to look as good as they taste. The room is a small oasis — comfortable seating, magical décor, and a patio shaded by tall oaks — and it is a sit-down tasting lounge rather than a pop-up, typically open Thursday to Saturday from noon. It anchors the alcohol-free scene at that end of the region.
