venues.longDescription:
Sadie's occupies 1200 Villa Place in Edgehill Village, steps from Music Row, in the corner space that was Taco Mamacita until it closed in 2021. It opened that September under Red Pebbles Hospitality, the local group led by Howard Greenstone with Ken Levitan, whose other Nashville rooms include Adele's, The 404 Kitchen and the Jewish deli Shep's in Five Points. The cooking is Mediterranean-influenced American, built for sharing rather than around individual plates — sumac-roasted butternut squash stuffed with quinoa, kale and cranberry, crispy artichokes with dill aioli, chargrilled octopus salad, and a pistachio baklava made with local honey — and the room was designed to match, raw brick set against white stucco with muted tile floors and blush pink and mossy green accents. Service is unusually wide for the neighbourhood: lunch and dinner Monday through Friday, brunch from 10am at weekends, and a happy hour Monday to Thursday from 4pm to 6pm.

The non-alcoholic drinks sit in a section headed "Mocktails" and are priced flat at $8, with mocktail specials included in the Monday-to-Thursday happy hour rather than excluded from it. All three are built from fresh purées, citrus and house sodas rather than from a bought-in zero-proof spirit, which makes this a fruit-and-soda programme done properly rather than an attempt to imitate a cocktail. Pathos combines passionfruit and lime with a hibiscus ginger beer. Pineapple Express is the most composed of the three, working mint and almond orgeat with lime and pineapple soda so it drinks nutty rather than simply sweet. Guava Ginger pairs guava purée with ginger, lime and guava soda. The list does rotate: a Blueberry Butterfly appeared on earlier menus, and a Strawberry Lemonade of strawberry purée, lemon and soda was on the card through summer 2026 before being dropped, so check the current menu rather than arriving set on one drink. Two non-alcoholic beers, Athletic Brewing's Athletic Lite and an Untitled Art juicy IPA, round out the spirit-free options, which are available throughout service.
venues.pressQuote: The low-to-no ABV trend is also alive and well here, with sessionable spirits like the classic spritz mingling with alcohol-free riffs on the limonata and paloma.

venues.name: Sago House
venues.description: Sago House is a Duxton Hill speakeasy from three industry veterans whose weekly-rotating, market-driven menu of six classic cocktail styles always leaves room for a genuine non-alcoholic build. Its most talked-about zero-proof drink is the Yo Soy Elotes, a mocktail inspired by Mexican street corn (elote) that tastes uncannily of warm, buttered popcorn. Because the drinks list is rebuilt each week from whatever the team finds in local markets, the specific alcohol-free option changes, but a mocktail is a standing part of the offer rather than an afterthought. Co-founder Desiree Jane Silva has said the bar was never about making the best drinks so much as being friendly and approachable, which is exactly the quality a non-drinker is looking for.
signatureDrinks: Yo Soy Elotes - a non-alcoholic build inspired by Mexican street corn (elote) that drinks uncannily of warm, buttered popcorn
venues.longDescription:
Sago House was created during Singapore's 2020 lockdown by three hospitality veterans - Desiree Jane Silva (formerly of 28 HongKong Street and EC Proof), Jay Gray and Abhishek 'George' C. What began three flights up on Sago Street relocated in 2023 to a shophouse at 37 Duxton Hill, where the room was built almost entirely by hand, roughly 80% of it from upcycled materials, and wrapped in a mural by local Filipino artist Distort Monsters.

The bar's signature is a menu that never sits still: six drinks built around six classic styles - a short-and-strong, a sour, a highball, a tiki drink, a tropical drink and a Champagne cocktail - all rebuilt weekly from ingredients sourced in the surrounding markets. That same market-driven, low-waste approach carries into its non-alcoholic drinks; the standout is the Yo Soy Elotes, a mocktail inspired by Mexican street corn that drinks like warm, buttered popcorn, and which reviewers have singled out as one of the more memorable zero-proof pours in the city.

The accolades are substantial: Sago House won the Michter's Art of Hospitality Award at Asia's 50 Best Bars in 2023, and has ranked highly on both Asia's 50 Best Bars (as high as No. 10) and the World's 50 Best Bars (No. 32). Despite the recognition it stays deliberately unpretentious - a convivial, party-first speakeasy where the non-alcoholic option is treated with the same creativity as the cocktails.

Because the list rotates every week, the exact alcohol-free drink on any given night will change, but Sago House consistently offers at least one thoughtfully made mocktail, so non-drinkers are catered to as a matter of course rather than on request.

The hospitality is the point, and it is the reason to send a non-drinker here rather than to a more technically decorated bar. Co-founder Desiree Jane Silva told The Peak Magazine that Sago House was never about making the best drinks or getting too geeky with it, and that the goal was to be friendly, approachable, and not make anyone feel intimidated. Asia's 50 Best Bars voters agreed in 2023, giving the room the Michter's Art of Hospitality Award — an award decided by naming the single bar where a voter had the best hospitality experience, with no other criteria attached.

That matters practically. The most common bad experience for someone not drinking is not a poor mocktail; it is the pause, the raised eyebrow, or the sense of having made the evening harder for everyone. A bar whose entire reputation rests on how guests are treated at the door is structurally unlikely to deliver that. Staff shout a greeting as guests walk in and write names on the tables in chalk, a habit that started because the week's drinks were already being written on the windows.

The trade-off is unpredictability. Six drinks are rebuilt every week around six classic shapes — strong up, strong down, daisies, highballs, sours and tropical drinks — from whatever the team finds in the surrounding markets, so the specific alcohol-free build changes constantly. The Yo Soy Elotes is the one people remember, but do not travel for a named drink. Travel for the room, and ask what they have made this week.
venues.pressQuote: Sago House was never about making the best drinks or getting too geeky with it. We wanted to be friendly, approachable, and not make anyone feel intimidated.

venues.name: Saint Arnold Brewing Company
venues.description: Saint Arnold Brewing Company, Texas' oldest craft brewery, backs its beer list with a genuine house-made non-alcoholic line at its Beer Garden & Restaurant: Hop Spring alcohol-free hoppy sparkling water, cane-sugar Root Beer, and Ginger Beer, called out in their own dedicated 'Non-Alcoholic' menu section. Hop Spring is brewed from just carbonated water, hops (Citra and Amarillo), and phosphoric acid — zero calories, zero ABV — and began life as taproom-only 'Hop2O' in 2018 before its 2023 relaunch, and it's now canned for Houston-area grocery and liquor stores. It's a full-alcohol production brewery and restaurant rather than an alcohol-free bar, but non-drinkers get real, dedicated products instead of a soda-gun afterthought.

venues.longDescription:
Saint Arnold Brewing Company was founded in Houston in 1994 by Brock Wagner and Kevin Bartol, both Rice University graduates. Now billed as Texas' oldest craft brewery, Saint Arnold has twice been named the Brewers Association's national Brewery of the Year in the large-brewery category, in 2017 and again in 2023 at the Great American Beer Festival in Denver, where it also won gold medals for its Elissa IPA and Fancy Lawnmower golden ale. The brewery's production facility sits at 2000 Lyons Ave in the Near Northside, just north of Downtown Houston.

In July 2018, Saint Arnold opened an attached Beer Garden & Restaurant designed around six church-inspired 'chapel' murals by Houston artists — what co-founder Brock Wagner called 'a culmination of a pipe dream I had a long time ago but never thought it would be a reality.' The full-service restaurant serves scratch-made pizza, burgers, sandwiches, and bar food alongside the house beer, inside a dog- and family-friendly outdoor space with lawn games.

The non-alcoholic program grew out of that family-friendly bent: Saint Arnold started making its own cane-sugar Root Beer for the kids and non-drinkers who came along on brewery tours, later adding a Ginger Beer in June 2022. In July 2018 it also debuted a taproom-only hop water called Hop2O, popular enough that it was canned and relaunched under the Hop Spring name in January 2023 — an alcohol-free, gluten-free sparkling water made from carbonated water, Citra and Amarillo hops, and phosphoric acid, with zero calories and 0% ABV. All three drinks get their own 'Non-Alcoholic' listing on the Beer Garden menu alongside housemade lemonade, cherry limeade, iced tea, and coffee, and Hop Spring is now also sold in Houston-area grocery and liquor stores.
venues.pressQuote: Winning Brewery of the Year is pretty gosh darn gratifying. Winning a second one is unexpected because it's so rare.

venues.name: Saint Eve's
venues.description: Saint Eve's is a small, intimate cocktail bar on 12th Street in Park Slope, shortlisted at the inaugural NYC's Best Bars for NA Awards. It is deliberately tiny — the bar states it cannot take parties of six or more — which makes it the opposite of a destination and rather good as a place to sit and talk. It serves alcohol and does not publish a named non-alcoholic list, so the zero-proof drinking here rests on the bartender rather than on a printed menu; ask, and expect something built rather than poured. Open 5pm until close, seven nights. Mockingbird, South Brooklyn's dedicated alcohol-free bar, is a short walk away for anyone who wants a room with no alcohol in it.

venues.longDescription:
Saint Eve's is a small, intimate cocktail bar on 12th Street in Park Slope, and its size is the whole character of the place: it takes no reservations, and it is deliberately tiny, which makes it the opposite of a destination and rather good as a place to sit and talk. It opens at 5pm and runs to close, with happy hour from 5 to 7 Monday to Thursday. It was shortlisted at NYC's Best Bars for NA 2025 — the awards run a flat winners tier plus a shortlist, so shortlisted is the accurate word.

The non-alcoholic drinks sit under a heading printed, like everything else on the menu, in lower case: spirit free. There are three, all $13, and what distinguishes them is that each is built on a genuinely different base rather than three variations on one bottle. Days of future past uses Pathfinder with Giffard's non-alcoholic ginger liqueur, grapefruit, lime and a splash of soda — the ginger liqueur is the part most bars skip, and it gives the drink a heat and length that plain ginger beer does not. Don't call me shirley shaken is the joke on the list and the most constructed drink on it: green-tea-infused Seedlip Grove 42 with strawberry, Giffard's non-alcoholic aperitivo and lime, shaken rather than built, so it arrives with the texture a Shirley Temple never has. Alter ego runs a spicy-infused Seedlip Garden 108 with cucumber, mint, lemon and tonic, which is the long one to nurse. Between them they cover bitter, sour and fresh, which is about as complete as a three-drink list can be. One practical caution: the bar's own website gives two slightly different street numbers on different pages, 471 and 475 12th Street, with the second appearing next to a reference to sister restaurants — every other page uses 471, which is the address to go by, but it is worth confirming before travelling.
venues.pressQuote: A broader shortlist highlighted bars with strong NA options citywide, including Sugar Monk, Lobby Bar at Hotel Chelsea, Dante, Pearl's Social & Billy Club, Dynaco, Saint Eve's, Pitts and more.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Time Out New York, NYC's Best Bars for NA Awards 2025

venues.name: Saint-Germain
venues.description: Saint-Germain opened in 2018 in a Bywater double-shotgun house on St. Claude Avenue (the former Sugar Park pizza spot), founded by Drew DeLaughter, Trey Smith, and Blake Aguillard. It began as a French wine bar and small bistro and has since evolved into an intimate, multi-course tasting-menu destination, earning one Michelin star in 2025. The dining room runs by reservation a few nights a week, with an adjoining wine bar that takes walk-ins. The beverage program leans on natural wine, and the kitchen offers a curated, daily-changing mocktail menu built to complement the savory courses for guests who aren't drinking — a rotating zero-proof pairing rather than a fixed named list. It's one of the few Michelin-recognized New Orleans rooms that takes a non-alcoholic pairing seriously.
venues.address: 3054 St Claude Ave, New Orleans, LA 70117
venues.hours: Mon 5:30pm-10pm; Tue-Wed closed; Thu 5:30pm-10pm; Fri-Sat 5pm-10:30pm; Sun 5:30pm-10pm
venues.longDescription:
Saint-Germain occupies a converted century-old double-shotgun house on St Claude Avenue in the Bywater, and it holds a Michelin star — one of very few in Louisiana. It began as a wine bar and bistro from chefs Trey Smith and Blake Aguillard, who met working at Restaurant August under Michael Gulotta and went on to cook for him at Maypop and MoPho, and it has since narrowed to a ten-course tasting menu shaped by refined technique and whatever is in season. The dining room seats sixteen, with a maximum of four guests per table, and there is a back garden. The Times-Picayune's review captured the register better than any description could: the critic wrote that when he took the job he was promised no math, and yet there he was scribbling down numbers he would never memorise as the chef explained that the bread had fermented twelve hours while the butter was forty-nine days old. Service runs Thursday through Monday from 5pm to 10.30pm, and the building has four steps at the front and four to the garden.

For a non-drinker, the appeal and the caveat are the same thing: this is a wine-led restaurant that takes beverage seriously, and it offers non-alcoholic mocktails alongside its natural wine list — but it does not publish what they are. No named zero-proof drink, no ingredients and no prices appear anywhere on its site, and we could not confirm whether any non-alcoholic wine is poured, which at a restaurant built around a wine list is the thing worth knowing. What can be said with confidence is that a kitchen fermenting its own bread and ageing butter for seven weeks is not going to hand a non-drinker a glass of cranberry juice, and a ten-course tasting format all but requires a beverage progression of some sort. This is a venue to ring ahead about rather than arrive at hopefully — tell them when you book, and the pairing will almost certainly be built for you.
venues.pressQuote: When I took this job, I was promised no math. But there I was at Saint-Germain, surreptitiously scribbling down numbers I knew I'd never memorize, as the chef explained that the bread fermented 12 hours, while the butter was 49 days old.

venues.name: Sally O's
venues.description: Sally O's is a corner bar at 3531 Gough Street in Highlandtown from chef Jesse Sandlin, a Top Chef alum who took over the longtime home of The Laughing Pint after it closed in autumn 2019 and named the place for her grandmother, Mildred O'Dethal, known as Sally O. The kitchen cooks from scratch, including its own ice cream, and Baltimore Magazine singled out a Crabonara that mixes blue crab into the pasta in place of pancetta. Its printed "Spirit Free" section runs three built drinks at $10 each: Szechuan Blush (Ritual zero-proof gin, rosemary-szechuan-cranberry syrup, lime), a Pathfinder Old Fashioned (Pathfinder NA amaro, marshmallow syrup, orange twist) and a Zero Proof Spritz (Mionetto NA bubbles, Mionetto NA aperitivo, soda). Athletic's Free Wave and Lite are $5, a non-alcoholic Guinness is $8 and a Mionetto alcohol-removed sparkling is $10. Dinner runs Monday to Saturday from 5pm with a late-night menu Thursday through Saturday. Sandlin also owns The Dive in Canton.
signatureDrinks: Szechuan Blush (Ritual zero-proof gin, rosemary-szechuan-cranberry syrup, lime) $10
Pathfinder Old Fashioned (Pathfinder NA amaro, marshmallow syrup, orange twist) $10
Zero Proof Spritz (Mionetto NA bubbles, Mionetto NA aperitivo, soda) $10
venues.longDescription:
Sally O's is a corner bar at 3531 Gough Street in Highlandtown from chef Jesse Sandlin, a Top Chef alum who took over the longtime home of The Laughing Pint after it closed in autumn 2019. The name is her grandmother's: Mildred O'Dethal, known as Sally O. Sandlin was clear about what she wanted from the space — when it became available, she said, she felt strongly about creating a place the neighbourhood would feel comfortable in and want to patronise, which is a more modest brief than most chefs of her profile would set and the reason the room works. The kitchen cooks from scratch, including the ice cream, and Baltimore Magazine singled out a Crabonara that ingeniously mixes blue crab into the pasta instead of pancetta, arriving seasoned just so with thyme, heaps of parmesan and clumps of sweet meat. The Highlandtown Smashburger stacks chuck, brisket and short rib. Dinner runs Monday to Saturday from 5pm, with a late-night menu until midnight Thursday through Saturday, happy hour early in the week, and Sundays closed.

The non-alcoholic drinks have their own printed "Spirit Free" heading and all three are $10 — well below the cocktails, and each built on a real zero-proof base. Szechuan Blush uses Ritual zero-proof gin with a rosemary-szechuan-cranberry syrup and lime, so the szechuan pepper supplies the tingle that gin's botanicals normally would. The Pathfinder Old Fashioned is the most interesting: Pathfinder's non-alcoholic amaro with a marshmallow syrup and an orange twist, which is a genuinely clever substitution because marshmallow root brings the viscous sweetness that sugar alone cannot. The Zero Proof Spritz pairs Mionetto's non-alcoholic bubbles with its spirit-free aperitivo. Behind them sit Athletic's Free Wave and Lite at $5, a non-alcoholic Guinness at $8 and a Mionetto alcohol-removed sparkling at $10. Note the list turns over — a Sun Tropics documented in early 2025 is no longer on the menu.
venues.pressQuote: When this space became available, I felt strongly about creating a place that the neighborhood would feel comfortable in and want to patronize.

venues.name: Saltbrush
venues.description: Saltbrush on Grove Street keeps two named alcohol-free drinks whose names tell you what kind of bar it is: Queen of the Meadow — an old country name for meadowsweet, a bitter herb historically used in brewing — and Quivering Quinine, which points straight at tonic's defining bitterness. Both names advertise bitterness rather than fruit, which is unusual on a zero-proof list and a reliable signal that the kitchen is thinking about balance rather than sweetness. It sits a few doors from Tavolàta on the same block. Some local guides give a 6th Street address; the Grove Street address is the one recorded here — worth confirming before a trip. Closed Sundays.

venues.longDescription:
Saltbrush is a restaurant on West Grove Street in downtown Boise, and its two named alcohol-free drinks are worth a moment because of what they are called.

Queen of the Meadow is an old English country name for meadowsweet, a hedgerow herb with a long history in drinks — it was used to flavour mead and beer for centuries before hops took over, and it carries a faintly almond, faintly bitter character. Quivering Quinine names the compound that makes tonic water taste of anything: quinine is the bitter alkaloid from cinchona bark, and it is the reason a gin and tonic is refreshing rather than merely cold.

Both names foreground bitterness. That is unusual and it is diagnostic. The default alcohol-free menu leads with fruit — strawberry, passionfruit, pineapple — because sweetness is easy and inoffensive. Naming a drink after a bitter herb or a bitter alkaloid is a statement of intent: these are drinks designed for people who want something dry and structured, not a soft drink in a nice glass. Given that bitterness is the single hardest quality to deliver without alcohol, a bar advertising it up front is one that has done the work.

A note on the address: local coverage lists Saltbrush at 106 North 6th Street, but the more current address, recorded here, is 506 West Grove Street. It is worth confirming before a trip.

The hours are moderate — 4pm to 9pm through the week, to 10pm Friday and Saturday, closed Sunday. Being on the same block as Tavolàta makes the two easy to combine, and both are a short walk from the 8th Street bars. Grove Street and 8th Street together hold most of what this guide recommends, which makes downtown Boise unusually walkable for a non-drinker.
venues.pressQuote: Saltbrush offers thoughtfully crafted alcohol-free mocktails featuring fresh, botanical ingredients
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: This Is Boise, The Boise Area's Best Non-Alcoholic Drinks and Mocktail Spots, January 2025

venues.name: SAMU Matcha House
venues.description: SAMU is a fully alcohol-free Japanese matcha house and cellar door on Johnston Street in Collingwood, built entirely around stone-milled ceremonial matcha shipped direct from Japan. The room pours drink-in and takeaway matcha Thursday to Sunday and runs formal, appointment-only tea meditations led by a trained Chanoyu (Japanese tea ceremony) practitioner. There is no bar and no zero-proof cocktail list here, just single-origin tea as the entire ritual, which makes it one of Melbourne's clearest sober third-spaces. Samu is a Japanese matcha house on Johnston Street in Collingwood, milling its own stone-ground matcha from Kyoto and Kagoshima leaf and running formal, by-appointment tea meditations alongside its cellar door.
signatureDrinks: Stone-milled single-origin matcha, whisked to order at the cellar door (Thu-Sun, 10am-2pm)
Formal tea meditation — a seated, by-appointment matcha service (Wed, Fri and Sat)
venues.longDescription:
SAMU sits at 8 Johnston Street in Collingwood, about ten minutes from Melbourne's CBD, presenting itself as a premium Japanese matcha teahouse and cellar door rather than a cafe in the ordinary sense. Its matcha is sourced direct from Japan and framed around centuries of tea tradition, with the house's own SUKI Grade™ ceremonial tea as the centrepiece. It is completely alcohol-free by design.

The offering splits in two. The cellar door and takeaway counter operate Thursday to Sunday from 10am to 2pm, serving prepared matcha drinks and selling ceremonial-grade tins, scoops and accessories to take home. Separately, formal tea meditations run on Wednesday, Friday and Saturday by appointment only — a seated, guided session led by a trained Japanese Chanoyu expert that includes a welcome drink, a short art presentation, the exclusive SUKI Grade™ matcha and a seasonal Japanese sweet.

Named pours reflect the single-ingredient focus: a ceremonial "This Must Be The Place" matcha, the "4'33" SUKI Grade™ tea made from Kyoto-grown Samidori, Gokou and Asahi cultivars, and "Fear No Tea," a caffeine-free Tochu (Eucommia) matcha alternative for those avoiding stimulants. Every option is prepared without alcohol.

For a sober directory, SAMU is an honest outlier: it leans ceremonial and wellness rather than nightlife, and its daytime hours are limited. But as a place to meet, slow down and share a drink with no alcohol anywhere on site, it functions as a genuine alcohol-free social and ritual space rather than a bar merely tolerating non-drinkers.

The house is a working matcha specialist rather than a cafe that sells matcha, and the distinction shows in what it stocks. Its own labels are single-origin and stone-milled, drawn from Kyoto prefecture and Kagoshima and sold in small quantities — a suki-grade chaji matcha, a caffeine-free organic tochu, a Kagoshima saemidori — the sort of range that only exists where someone is sourcing leaf directly rather than buying a catering tin.

Two formats are worth knowing before you go. The cellar door and takeaway counter runs Thursday to Sunday from 10am to 2pm, which is a short window and the reason people arrive disappointed. The formal tea meditations run Wednesday, Friday and Saturday by appointment, and are a seated, guided service rather than a drink to carry away. For a non-drinker that second format is the interesting one: it is a booked, hosted, hour-shaped occasion built entirely around a drink that has never contained alcohol, which is a genuinely different way to spend an evening than looking for a bar that will accommodate you.

venues.name: San Simón
venues.description: San Simón is a moody, candlelit bar tucked down Tin Pan Alley in downtown Bend, the sort of room built for a slow evening, and its zero-proof options are made to hold their own against the cocktail list rather than sit below it. Open daily from 3pm until midnight — the latest consistent hours of any bar in this guide.
venues.address: 845 NW Tin Pan Alley, Bend, OR 97703
venues.longDescription:
San Simón sits down Tin Pan Alley, the narrow lane running off Bend's downtown grid that has become the town's small concentration of tucked-away bars and murals. It is dark, candlelit and deliberately slow — Visit Bend's guide pairs it with The Flamingo Room as the two rooms to choose when the evening calls for something unhurried — and its zero-proof options are made to hold their own rather than to fill a gap on the menu.

The case for it as an alcohol-free destination rests on two things beyond the drinks themselves. The first is atmosphere: a low-lit room where people sit and talk is a far easier place to not drink than a bright taproom where everyone is standing with a pint. The second is the hours. San Simón opens at three in the afternoon and runs to midnight every single day of the week, which is the most consistent late availability of any venue in this guide. Bend closes early — several of its best rooms shut at nine, and Boneyard's tasting room is done by seven — so a bar that is reliably open at eleven on a Tuesday is genuinely useful if you are looking for somewhere to go that is not a brewery.

We have not published drink names or prices here. San Simón does not publish its cocktail menu online, and its zero-proof list moves with the seasons like the rest of the bar's offering. What is documented, by Bend's own tourism board as of June 2026, is that the zero-proof options are treated as real drinks. Ask what the bar is making rather than looking for a printed section.
venues.pressQuote: when the night calls for something slower, san simon or the flamingo room are my go-tos

venues.name: Sana'a Cafe (Drumm Street)
venues.description: Sana'a Cafe's Drumm Street location opened in 2026 in a former Starbucks unit near the Embarcadero, and trades 7am to 10pm every day of the week. It is entirely alcohol-free, and the Bay Area Telegraph singled the fifteen-hour trading day out as the point of the place, describing it as a genuine evening destination rather than a morning latte stop. The menu combines familiar cafe orders with Yemeni specialities: pistachio, rose and Yemeni lattes, qishr made from the dried husks of coffee cherries, Adeni chai, Arabic light roast coffee and mofawar, with honeycomb pastries, baklava, milk cakes and savoury turnovers from the counter. For Financial District workers it is one of very few post-work rooms that is not a bar.
venues.longDescription:
Sana'a Cafe took 27 Drumm Street, near the Embarcadero, in 2026, one of several former Starbucks storefronts the growing chain has moved into as it expanded across San Francisco. The Bay Area Telegraph covered the opening in July 2026 and framed the cafe's trading hours as its defining feature: open daily from 7am to 10pm, a fifteen-hour stretch that the paper described as making it a genuine evening destination rather than another place to grab a rushed morning latte. That framing matters for a Financial District that historically offers office workers a choice between leaving early and going to a bar; Sana'a serves no alcohol at all.

The menu pairs the orders any American cafe would carry with the Yemeni preparations the group is built around. Qishr is the most distinctive: a hot drink brewed from the dried husks of coffee cherries rather than the roasted bean, spiced and served in small cups. Adeni chai, black tea cooked down with cream and spice, is the other traditional staple, alongside Arabic light roast coffee and mofawar. The espresso side of the board runs pistachio, rose and Yemeni lattes, and the counter holds honeycomb pastries, baklava, milk cakes and savoury turnovers. The Bay Area Telegraph noted that Yemeni coffeehouses nationally have adopted late hours as a defining characteristic, with some staying open until 3am, later than many bars in San Francisco. Sana'a's Drumm Street room does not go that far, but a 10pm close every night of the week, in a neighbourhood that empties at six, gives the city another alcohol-free place to sit with friends after dinner or work late over something spiced and sweet. The group has taken several former Starbucks units across the city as it has expanded, including sites on Market Street and Townsend Street, and the Drumm Street shop is the one closest to the Ferry Building and the Embarcadero waterfront, which makes it the most useful of them for anyone arriving by ferry or by Muni after work.
venues.pressQuote: Yemeni cafes have become increasingly popular across the Bay Area in part because they offer an alcohol-free place to gather well into the evening, whether that means catching up with friends, working on a laptop, meeting after dinner, or lingering over something sweet.

venues.name: Sana'a Cafe (New Montgomery)
venues.description: Sana'a Cafe is an alcohol-free Yemeni coffeehouse at New Montgomery and Howard, named after the Yemeni capital and open from 6:30am to 10pm on weekdays and 8am to 10pm at weekends. CBS News Bay Area profiled it in April 2024, with manager Sam Mardaei explaining that the team's aim was to bring Yemeni culture to the city. The list runs to signature Adeni chai, Sana'ani coffee, qishr brewed from dried coffee cherry husks, mofawar and Spanish lattes, alongside pistachio and rose lattes and a pastry counter of saffron milk cake, Biscoff desserts, baklava and honeycomb bread. The room seats a steady evening crowd of downtown workers and students well after the surrounding coffee counters have closed.
venues.address: 199 New Montgomery St, San Francisco, CA 94105
venues.longDescription:
Sana'a Cafe takes its name from the Yemeni capital and was operating on New Montgomery Street by late 2023, when The Oaklandside referred to it as the Yemeni coffee shop with a location on Montgomery Street in San Francisco that was preparing to open in downtown Oakland. CBS News Bay Area filmed inside the cafe in April 2024 for a segment on Yemeni coffee culture downtown; manager Sam Mardaei used the piece to talk about the depth of Yemen's coffee history, pointing out that the word mocha comes from the Yemeni port city of Mokha. The group has since grown into a small chain with further San Francisco sites and an Oakland roastery, but the New Montgomery room remains the busiest of the city locations.

The cafe serves no alcohol. It opens at 6:30am on weekdays and 8am at weekends and runs until 10pm every night, which places it firmly in the category of alcohol-free evening rooms rather than morning coffee counters. The drinks divide between traditional Yemeni preparations and the modern espresso bar. On the traditional side there is Adeni chai, black tea cooked with cream and spice; Sana'ani, the house black coffee; qishr, brewed from the dried husks of coffee cherries rather than the bean; and mofawar, spiced coffee finished with cream. On the modern side the shop is known for its Spanish latte and for pistachio, rose and Yemeni lattes. The counter carries saffron milk cake, Biscoff-layered desserts, baklava, honeycomb pastries and savoury turnovers, and the kitchen puts out light bites through the day. The address, a block from Yerba Buena Gardens and within walking distance of the Financial District, means the evening trade is a mix of office workers, students and people meeting somewhere that is not a bar. Mardaei told CBS that Yemen's coffee history runs deeper than most customers realise and that sharing it is the point of the business, a framing that fits the way the room is used: people stay for hours, and the cafe's usefulness comes as much from the 10pm close every night of the week as from what is in the cup.
venues.pressQuote: We are just trying to bring our culture, to the city, you know, into the states in general

venues.name: Sandfish Sushi & Whiskey
venues.description: A modern sushi-and-whiskey restaurant on 7th Avenue in the Melrose District of Phoenix, with a deeper non-alcoholic list than the format suggests. Several zero-proof drinks are built on Seedlip rather than juice: the Virgin Garden pairs Seedlip Garden with lemon, muddled cucumber and soda, and the Nordic Brace sets Seedlip Garden against hibiscus, lemon and a jalapeno-ginger note. The pairing logic is sound — the herbaceous, low-sugar register of a Seedlip Garden build sits alongside raw fish far better than the sweet mocktails most sushi restaurants default to. Open daily from 4:30pm in a neighbourhood worth arriving early for; the whiskey list remains the house identity.
venues.longDescription:
Sandfish sits on 7th Avenue in the Melrose District, a stretch of central Phoenix that has spent the last decade turning from vintage shops and neon signs into one of the city's more interesting eating strips. The restaurant pairs a modern sushi menu with a whiskey programme — the two halves of the name — and opens daily at 4:30pm, which makes it an evening room rather than a lunch one.

Sushi restaurants are usually a poor bet for anyone not drinking. The default non-alcoholic offer is green tea or something sweet and fruity, neither of which works with raw fish: sugar flattens the delicacy the kitchen has spent its effort on. Sandfish avoids that by building its zero-proof drinks on Seedlip rather than syrup. The Virgin Garden is Seedlip Garden with lemon, muddled cucumber and soda — herbaceous, dry, closer in register to a dry sake or a crisp white than to a mocktail. The Nordic Brace is the more assertive of the two, setting Seedlip Garden against hibiscus and lemon with a jalapeno-ginger edge that stands up to soy and wasabi rather than being erased by them.

That is a small distinction that makes a large practical difference. A non-alcoholic drink built to accompany food, rather than to substitute for a cocktail, is rarer than it should be, and it is the reason this entry sits above the many restaurants in the metro that will make you something sweet on request. Two things to note: the whiskey list is the house identity and the bar is built around it, so this is emphatically not an alcohol-free venue; and with only a handful of named zero-proof options, the range is narrow even if the quality is not, so this is a place to eat well rather than to work through a list.
venues.pressQuote: Within its Scandinavian-influenced interior, guests will enjoy a selection of hand-crafted sushi, carefully curated specialty rolls and whiskey pairings

venues.name: Sans Bar
venues.description: Founded in 2017 by Chris Marshall, Sans Bar is widely regarded as one of the first dedicated non-alcoholic bars in North America. Located one block south of the Texas Capitol, the downtown space is the cornerstone of Marshall's mission to create alcohol-free spaces that don't feel like substitutes. Marshall, a substance-use counselor since 2009 and sober since 2007, has been featured in The New York Times, Men's Health, USA Today, and has spoken at the Aspen Ideas Festival. Bar Manager Valentina, who joined in November 2022, overhauled the menu and now consults with bars and restaurants worldwide on their non-alcoholic programs. Beyond the bar itself, the Sans Bar Academy has helped launch over 40 alcohol-free bars and bottle shops across the United States, Canada, and Australia. The room hosts live music most Fridays at 8pm and rotating wellness collaborations through a partnership with Swift Fit Events.
venues.longDescription:
Sans Bar is the reason a lot of the venues on this site exist. Chris Marshall opened it in 2017, a block south of the Texas Capitol, and it is widely regarded as one of the first dedicated alcohol-free bars in North America — Visit Austin still describes it as the heartbeat of the city's sober community. Marshall has been a substance-use counsellor since 2009 and sober since 2007, and he built the room around a specific complaint: that the places available to people who had stopped drinking were church basements and coffee shops, neither of which is a night out.

His framing has stayed unusually generous. As he has put it, the bar is not anti-alcohol and does not think alcohol is bad; it respects people's decision to drink or not. The point was never abstinence enforcement — it was building an environment where you can connect with other people and not drink, which is a different and harder problem.

The drinks are treated as craft cocktails rather than consolations: the Pecan Praline Old-Fashioned, a spirit-free Mezcal Ranch Water, the Ume Moon, and a Garden Dandy built on Ritual Zero Proof gin with muddled cucumber. Bar manager Valentina, who joined in November 2022, rebuilt the menu and now consults with bars and restaurants internationally on their own non-alcoholic programmes.

The influence has travelled further than the room. The Sans Bar Academy has helped launch more than forty alcohol-free bars and bottle shops across the United States, Canada and Australia — which means a substantial share of the sober-bar movement traces back to one storefront in downtown Austin. Marshall has been covered by The New York Times, USA Today and Men's Health, and has spoken at the Aspen Ideas Festival.

One practical caution: this is not a nightly operation. Public hours are limited — Friday evenings, with live music most weeks at 8pm, plus event nights and rotating wellness collaborations. Check the schedule before making the trip.
venues.pressQuote: We're not anti-alcohol. We don't think that alcohol is bad, and we respect people's decision to consume alcohol or not drink alcohol. We're really focused on creating an environment where you can connect with other people and not drink.

venues.name: Sasha's Wine Bar on DeMun
venues.description: A DeMun-neighborhood fixture for more than two decades, Sasha's Wine Bar anchors a leafy Clayton block with a cellar of more than 4,200 bottles and a wine list curated by sommelier Denise Mueller. The zero-proof corner of that list is quietly excellent for a classic wine bar: NoZeco sparkling brut poured by the glass, Giesen alcohol-removed Sauvignon Blanc, and a trio of Leitz cans spanning sparkling Riesling, sparkling rosé, and Zero Point Five Pinot Noir. A dedicated N/A Cocktails section adds a house alcohol-free spritz, the St. Agrestis Phony Negroni, and Parch's Desert Margarita, while Athletic Brewing and Best Day cover non-alcoholic beer.
signatureDrinks: Leitz Eins Zwei Zero Sparkling Riesling
venues.longDescription:
Sasha's Wine Bar has poured for the DeMun neighborhood of Clayton for more than two decades, growing into a small St. Louis wine-bar family that includes Sasha's on Shaw, the casual sister spot Barrio down the block, and the intimate Cellar Bar upstairs on DeMun, open Wednesday through Saturday evenings. The original De Mun Avenue room remains the flagship: a cozy, all-day neighborhood hangout that opens at 11am daily and serves until well past midnight, with a showcased cellar of more than 4,200 bottles behind a long by-the-glass list.

The zero-proof program dates back years and is verifiably current. In January 2023, Sauce Magazine reported that certified sommelier and programs coordinator Denise Mueller had added a rotating selection of zero-proof wine across the group, and the DeMun menu dated June 2026 confirms the rotation continues: a Non-Alcoholic Wines section lists NoZeco sparkling brut by the glass or bottle, Giesen alcohol-removed Sauvignon Blanc from New Zealand, and three Leitz cans — Eins Zwei Zero sparkling Riesling, Eins Zwei Zero sparkling rosé, and Zero Point Five Pinot Noir. A separate N/A Cocktails section carries Shacksbury's Mountain Tonic, the St. Agrestis Phony Negroni, Parch's agave-based Desert Margarita, and a house-assembled N/A Spritz built from non-alcoholic aperitivo and alcohol-free sparkling wine, while the beer list ends with Athletic Brewing's Golden Ale and Best Day's hazy non-alcoholic IPA.

Sauce Magazine counted Sasha's among five St. Louis bars 'serving thoughtfully crafted nonalcoholic drinks,' and the DeMun room stays busy enough that reviewers recommend arriving early for a table or patio seat. Expect a lengthy wine list annotated for sustainable, organic, biodynamic, natural, and vegan bottles, a full food menu with weekend brunch, and a low-key, conversational atmosphere rather than a scene. For a sober or moderating guest, it is one of the rare old-guard wine bars in the region where you can order a zero-proof pour by the glass, a bottled NA cocktail, and an alcohol-free beer off the same printed menu, any night of the week.
venues.pressQuote: Led by certified sommelier and programs coordinator Denise Mueller, this bar group has added a rotating selection of zero-proof wine to their extensive wine portfolio.

venues.name: Saturn Room
venues.description: Saturn Room is Tulsa's tiki bar, on North Boulder downtown, and it opens at 4pm and runs to 2am every single day of the week — the most consistently available late-night room in this guide. Its alcohol-free build is the Apple Drop: a non-alcoholic apple vodka with pineapple, ginger, aromatic bitters, vanilla, lemon and cinnamon, which is a seven-component drink using a named zero-proof spirit as its base. Tiki suits this category unusually well, since the format is built on fresh juice, house syrups and spice with the rum as one element among many rather than the whole structure.
signatureDrinks: Apple Drop — non-alcoholic apple vodka, pineapple, ginger, aromatic bitters, vanilla, lemon, cinnamon
venues.longDescription:
Every day of the week, 4pm to 2am. No closed day, no shortened Sunday, no seasonal hours. For a reader who does not drink, that single line is worth more than most drink lists, because the recurring problem in every city in this directory is that the good alcohol-free options are shut exactly when you need them.

Saturn Room is Tulsa's tiki bar, on North Boulder Avenue downtown — full thatch-and-carved-tiki treatment, a long rum list, and the theatre that goes with it. The format is a better fit for alcohol-free drinking than almost any other kind of bar, because a tiki drink is fundamentally an assembly of fresh juice, house syrups such as orgeat and falernum, spice and elaborate garnish, with the spirit as one component among six or seven. Remove the rum and there is still a drink; remove the gin from a martini and there is not.

The Apple Drop demonstrates it. Non-alcoholic apple vodka forms the base, then pineapple, ginger, vanilla, lemon and cinnamon build the body, with aromatic bitters closing it. Seven components, one of them a purchased zero-proof spirit — meaning the bar has committed shelf space to the category rather than improvising with juice.

The presentation matters as much as the recipe here. In a room where every drink arrives in carved wood or ceramic under a cloud of garnish, an alcohol-free order is completely indistinguishable from everyone else's, which removes the small social friction that makes people stop asking.

Tulsa Remote ranked the Apple Drop among the city's must-try mocktails in January 2025. Saturn Room sits two minutes from The Tavern and Shuffles, so downtown Tulsa is walkable for a whole evening without drinking.

One caution about tiki rooms generally, since this guide recommends several: the format's house syrups are frequently made with rum or another spirit as a preservative, particularly falernum. That is a small amount and immaterial to most readers, but anyone abstaining completely should ask which components in a given build are alcohol-based rather than assuming a drink described as non-alcoholic contains nothing at all. Good tiki bars know the answer immediately.
venues.pressQuote: Apple Drop: NA apple vodka, pineapple, ginger, aromatic bitters, vanilla, lemon, cinnamon

venues.name: Savoy Society
venues.description: Savoy Society occupies the ground floor of Drayton Tower, the mid-century modernist apartment block on Liberty Street, and runs as a late-night bar and small-plates kitchen with a terrace. Its cocktail list is built on house ingredients — yaupon tea, house cordials, its own bitters — and the same components carry a handful of alcohol-free drinks, among them a spirit-free take on an old-fashioned made with yaupon tea and sugar bitters, a carrot, pineapple, coconut and lime colada, and a cold-brew-and-coconut build lengthened with tonic. It trades from mid-afternoon to midnight, later at weekends, and closes on Tuesdays.
venues.address: 102 E Liberty St Ste 109, Savannah, GA 31401
venues.hours: Mon 4pm-12am; Tue closed; Wed-Thu 4pm-12am; Fri 4pm-1am; Sat 3pm-1am; Sun 3pm-12am
venues.longDescription:
Drayton Tower is an anomaly in Savannah — a 1951 modernist apartment slab of glass and steel dropped into a city of eighteenth-century squares and Victorian brick — and Savoy Society runs along its ground floor on Liberty Street. The bar leans into the contrast: a late-night room with a terrace, global small plates, poke and ceviche alongside the drinks, open until midnight most nights and 1am at weekends.

The cocktail programme is built from house components rather than bought mixers, and the alcohol-free drinks draw on the same shelf. The most interesting is a spirit-free old-fashioned made with yaupon tea and sugar bitters — yaupon being the only caffeinated plant native to North America, and a genuinely local choice for a coastal Georgia bar. A Carrot Colada runs carrot, pineapple, coconut and lime, and a drink called Dock of the Bay puts cold brew with mint, coconut and lime under tonic, which is a much stranger and better idea than it sounds.

This listing is graded three rather than four. Savoy Society does not print a standing zero-proof heading the way Husk, Peregrin, Bar Julian, Water Witch and Ardsley Station do, and the three drinks above come from Savannah's tourism guide rather than from a menu that could be read live — the bar publishes its list as images. Given how many drink names in this city have rotated off since that guide was written, none are recorded here as signature drinks. What is well evidenced is that alcohol-free builds are part of the bar's normal repertoire rather than an off-menu favour.

A scheduling note: Savoy Society is closed on Tuesdays, opens at 4pm on weekdays and 3pm at weekends, and is one of the few kitchens in the Historic District still serving late.
venues.pressQuote: Conveniently located just below the sleek and modern vibes of Drayton Tower lives Savoy Society.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Visit Savannah, Where to Find Incredible Mocktails in Savannah

venues.name: Scarfes Bar
venues.description: Scarfes Bar is the World's 50 Best-ranked cocktail bar inside Rosewood London, a drawing-room-style room in Holborn hung with Gerald Scarfe caricatures and driven by live nightly jazz. Under Director of Bars Andy Loudon, its printed seasonal menus now fold serious zero-proof builds into the main list rather than hiding them on a footnote. The 2025 'Long Drawn Out Sip' menu spotlighted two alcohol-free originals among its 24 creations, led by the No-Cracker 0% (Amarico, Martini Vibrante and acorn soda) and the Lost & Found 0% (juniper hydrosol, Martini Vibrante, raspberry and iris cordial).
venues.address: 252 High Holborn, London WC1V 7EN, United Kingdom
signatureDrinks: No-Cracker 0% — an alcohol-free counterpart to the house Nutcracker, built with Amarico, Martini Vibrante and acorn soda
Lost & Found 0% — juniper hydrosol and Martini Vibrante with raspberry and iris cordial
venues.longDescription:
Set inside Rosewood London on High Holborn, Scarfes Bar is one of the city's most decorated hotel cocktail bars: it ranked No. 31 in The World's 50 Best Bars 2025 and was named No. 1 Best International Hotel Bar at Tales of the Cocktail 2024. The room is named for and hung with the work of British caricaturist Gerald Scarfe, styled like a grand, slightly surreal drawing room, with a roaring fire, deep armchairs and live jazz on the bill nightly from 8pm to midnight.

The bar's non-alcoholic craft is genuine and printed in the main menu rather than benched. For the 2025 'Long Drawn Out Sip' menu, the team under Director of Bars Andy Loudon built 24 originals across four chapters and, for the first time, gave two of them full zero-proof status in the core list: the No-Cracker 0%, an alcohol-free counterpart to the house Nutcracker made with Amarico, Martini Vibrante and acorn soda; and the Lost & Found 0%, combining juniper hydrosol and Martini Vibrante with raspberry and iris cordial. These are treated with the same clarification, cordial-making and carbonation techniques as the full-strength drinks.

Scarfes Bar rotates its concept menu roughly annually (the 2026 successor, 'Heroes & Villains', reimagines ten iconic figures across paired cocktails), so exact zero-proof serves change with each edition, but the alcohol-free line-up has been an anchored, priced part of the offering — non-alcoholic cocktails have run around £12. It's a high-end, occasion room where a non-drinker is handed something built with the same rigour as everything else on the list.

venues.name: Schlafly Tap Room
venues.description: St. Louis's original craft brewpub earns the title: when the Schlafly Tap Room opened in December 1991, it was the first brewery to open in the city since Prohibition. Three decades on, the restored brick landmark in Downtown West still anchors the Schlafly universe — and the brewery now makes two of its own non-alcoholic beers, NA IPA and NA Pale Ale, both under 0.5% ABV and part of the year-round lineup. The NA Pale Ale reimagines the 1991 flagship that started it all. Come for hefeweizen-battered fish and fries, Tuesday-night trivia and a genuine piece of American craft-beer history, alcohol optional.
venues.longDescription:
The Saint Louis Brewery was incorporated in 1989 by Tom Schlafly and Dan Kopman, who bought a burned-out building on Locust Street that had sat vacant for over 22 years and turned it into the Schlafly Tap Room, which officially opened on December 26, 1991. It was the first brewery to open in St. Louis since Prohibition — and, holding Missouri's first microbrewery license, the first new brewpub in the state since Prohibition as well. Schlafly still bills itself as the founder of St. Louis craft beer and the original locally owned, independent craft brewery in Missouri, and the restored brick Tap Room in Downtown West remains its flagship.

Schlafly is one of the few St. Louis breweries brewing its own non-alcoholic beer, and it makes two, both year-round and both under 0.5% ABV. The NA IPA delivers juicy, tropical IPA character with aromatic notes of mango and guava and a crisp finish; the NA Pale Ale is a copper-colored, non-alcoholic take on the 1991 flagship Pale Ale, smooth and balanced with slightly bready, caramel flavors from the malts. When the NA Pale Ale launched for Dry January 2024, trade press confirmed it was pouring into coolers at the Tap Room and at Schlafly Bottleworks in Maplewood — as the brewery put it, 'Pale Ale was the beer that started it all for us back in 1991, so it only made sense to offer a non-alcoholic option.'

The Tap Room experience is classic brewpub: hefeweizen-battered fish and fries, jagerschnitzel, the Tap Room Burger and pretzels with white cheddar sauce, plus trivia on Tuesday nights at 7pm. Feast Magazine's 2025 feature on how St. Louis breweries are adapting to a more diverse, sober-curious drinking scene featured Schlafly's longtime brewmaster, a sign of how seriously the city's original craft brewery takes the shift. One practical note: Schlafly's NA beers are packaged in cans rather than kept on the rotating draught list, so ask your server for the NA IPA or NA Pale Ale by name. Hours run Monday through Saturday from 11am and Sunday from noon, with the kitchen open until 9 or 10pm depending on the night.
venues.pressQuote: This non-alcoholic brew is available now across Schlafly's distribution as well as a few of Schlafly's brewpubs: Schlafly Tap Room in downtown St. Louis and Schlafly Bottleworks in the Maplewood neighborhood of St. Louis.

venues.name: Schofield's Bar
venues.description: Schofield's Bar is the eponymous City Centre venue of award-winning bartender brothers Joe and Daniel Schofield, set on the art deco corner of 1930s Sunlight House. Widely regarded as one of the UK's most decorated cocktail bars, it gives its non-alcoholic drinking a dedicated 'Temperance' section on the main menu, poured with the same care as its cocktails. Current alcohol-free serves include the Dove (rose, pink grapefruit soda, lime), El Ranchero (apple, nutmeg, lemon, vanilla, almond, soda), Fortuna (cranberry, ginger, raspberry, grenadine, lime) and a from-scratch Virgin Mary, alongside Lucky Saint 0.5%, homemade ginger beer and a spread of Fentimans.
venues.address: Sunlight House, 3 Little Quay St, Manchester M3 3JZ
signatureDrinks: Dove — rose, pink grapefruit soda and lime
El Ranchero — apple, nutmeg, lemon, vanilla, almond and soda
Fortuna — cranberry, ginger, raspberry, grenadine and lime
Virgin Mary — tomato, Worcestershire sauce, house spice mix, celery and lemon
venues.longDescription:
Schofield's Bar opened in 2021 as the homecoming of bartender brothers Joe and Daniel Schofield, who — in the bar's own words, with 'almost 40 years of combined experience' between them — returned to their native Manchester to open an eponymous venue after building their names in celebrated bars elsewhere. It graces the corner of Sunlight House, the art deco tower designed by architect Joseph Sunlight that was the tallest building in Manchester when it was completed in the 1930s: the decade of grand, luxurious cocktail bars whose spirit the room deliberately channels. In just a few years it has become widely regarded as one of the UK's most decorated cocktail bars, listed in The World's 50 Best Bars' Discovery guide and a fixture of Manchester's 'best bar' round-ups.

The bar is a handsome wood-and-brass corner room, cash-free and open from noon, that works as easily for an afternoon coffee as for a late-night martini (it serves until 1.30am). The drinks list — titled 'Fine & Classic Cocktails, Celebrated Libations & Other Fancy Drinks' — runs from immaculate classics (a Clover Club built on the brothers' own award-winning Schofield's Dry Vermouth, made in collaboration with Asterley Bros.) through an encyclopaedic spirits library to a shelf of books paired with cocktail 'companions'. Alongside the drinks there is a short food menu of British cheese and charcuterie, Nocellara olives and popcorn, plus an illy tea and coffee service until 9pm.

Crucially for non-drinkers, the menu carries a dedicated 'Temperance' section — 'a selection of carefully curated tipples prepared with the same love, care and affection as our cocktails' — built as proper zero-proof cocktails rather than mocktails on request. On the current summer 2026 list, four serves are poured at £8.95 each: the Dove, a floral, pale-pink mix of rose, pink grapefruit soda and lime; El Ranchero, a spiced orchard-fruit build of apple, nutmeg, lemon, vanilla, almond and soda; Fortuna, a tart long drink of cranberry, ginger, raspberry, grenadine and lime; and a from-scratch Virgin Mary of tomato, Worcestershire sauce, house spice mix, celery and lemon. The section rotates with the seasons — earlier 2026 editions featured a Club Tropicana (pineapple and passionfruit with a hint of Earl Grey) and a Frosty Toddy (honey, ginger and lemon) — and it sits alongside a genuinely useful low- and no-alcohol back bar: Lucky Saint 0.5% unfiltered lager, homemade ginger beer and lemonade, and a range of Fentimans elderflower, ginger ale and tonics. It adds up to a serious alcohol-free offering inside one of the country's most respected cocktail rooms.
venues.pressQuote: carefully curated tipples prepared with the same love, care and affection as our cocktails

venues.name: Sea Level NC
venues.description: Sea Level NC is a coastal oyster bar and seafood restaurant at 129 East 5th Street in Uptown Charlotte's First Ward, named for Sea Level, North Carolina, where the house oyster is farmed — the Sea Level Salt, medium brine and clean finish, at $2.50 each. The kitchen runs a Maine or Connecticut lobster roll at $32, chargrilled oysters at $20, a South Carolina tuna poke bowl at $30 and a miso-honey braised short rib at $42, with cocktails credited to Azure Cassidy and features from chef DJ Ivey. Weekday happy hour from 2pm to 6pm drops house oysters to $1.50. Its "spirit-free sips" section is priced well below the cocktails: the Passion Star Martini ($10, Undone Not Gin, passionfruit, vanilla simple, lime), Buzz Kill ($10, Lyre's non-alcoholic Italian Spritz, house-made tonic, simple syrup) and the Purple Sea Urchin ($8, pineapple, lime, hibiscus, demerara), alongside Athletic Free Wave and Upside Dawn at $5.50 and Heineken 0.0 at $4.50. The list rotates seasonally.
signatureDrinks: Passion Star Martini (Undone Not Gin, passionfruit, vanilla simple, lime) $10
Buzz Kill (Lyre's NA Italian Spritz, house-made tonic, simple syrup) $10
Purple Sea Urchin (pineapple, lime, hibiscus, demerara) $8
venues.longDescription:
Sea Level NC is a coastal oyster bar at 129 East 5th Street in Uptown's First Ward, and the name is not decorative — it takes it from Sea Level, North Carolina, on the Down East stretch of Carteret County, and serves an oyster grown there. The Sea Level Salt is a medium oyster with medium brine and a clean finish, listed at $2.50 apiece, and the sustainability-minded sourcing runs through the rest of the menu too: a Maine or Connecticut lobster roll at $32, chargrilled oysters with garlic butter and two cheeses at $20, a South Carolina tuna poke bowl at $30, and a miso-honey braised bone-in short rib at $42. Cocktails are credited on the menu to Azure Cassidy and kitchen features to chef DJ Ivey. Happy hour runs weekdays from 2pm to 6pm with house oysters at $1.50 — one of the better deals in Uptown. The dining room serves from 11.30am Monday through Saturday and closes Sundays.

The non-alcoholic drinks sit under a heading the bar calls "spirit-free sips", and they are priced well below the cocktails at $8 to $10, which makes ordering two across a long seafood dinner an easy decision. The Passion Star Martini ($10) is built on Undone's Not Gin with passionfruit, a vanilla simple syrup and lime — the vanilla is what gives it body where the spirit would normally sit. Buzz Kill ($10) combines Lyre's non-alcoholic Italian Spritz with a house-made tonic and simple syrup, so the bitterness is real rather than sweetened over. Purple Sea Urchin ($8) is the simplest and the best value, working pineapple and lime against hibiscus and demerara. Beyond the built drinks there is proper beer: Athletic's Free Wave hazy IPA and Upside Dawn golden ale at $5.50 each, plus Heineken 0.0 at $4.50 and San Pellegrino at $6. Note the list does rotate — a Nada Colada that appeared on earlier menus is no longer served.
venues.pressQuote: The Purple Sea Urchin, made with pineapple, hibiscus, lime, demerara, and passionfruit flakes, is a mocktail you'll want to sip on long after dry January is over.

venues.name: Seasons Rotisserie & Grill
venues.description: Seasons Rotisserie & Grill is a long-standing restaurant near Old Town on Mountain Road, with a rooftop cantina above the dining room, and its contribution to this guide is an elevated Shirley Temple — which sounds like a joke and is not. The Shirley Temple is the drink most often handed to adults who are not drinking, usually badly made from bottled grenadine and flat lemonade; a kitchen that takes it seriously enough to rebuild it properly is making a specific point about who it is serving. Open from 4pm most nights and 3pm at weekends, closed Tuesday.
venues.longDescription:
Seasons has been on Mountain Road near Old Town for a long time, a grill and rotisserie with a rooftop cantina, and it is the sort of established restaurant that a city's tourism board recommends without much fuss.

What puts it in this guide is a single item Visit Albuquerque records: an elevated Shirley Temple. That deserves more attention than it usually gets, because the Shirley Temple occupies a peculiar place in the life of anyone who does not drink. It is the default — the thing a bartender reaches for when told no alcohol, made from bottled grenadine, flat lemon-lime soda and a neon cherry — and it is served to adults constantly. It is also, done properly, a genuinely good drink: real pomegranate, fresh citrus, decent soda water, a proper brandied cherry.

A kitchen that bothers to rebuild it is making a statement about who it thinks is ordering. It says the restaurant has noticed that grown-ups drink this and has decided they should get something worth drinking, rather than the children's version handed over with an apology. For readers of this directory that is a more meaningful signal than another Seedlip-and-tonic would be.

This entry is graded three and honestly so. One documented drink, no published ingredients, no verified zero-proof section on the menu, and no non-alcoholic spirits programme confirmed. It is a good restaurant that treats the non-drinker properly, not a destination for the drinks alone.

The location is the practical draw: Mountain Road puts it within walking distance of Old Town Plaza and a short distance from Lost Cultures in the Sawmill District, which makes an Old Town evening combining the two entirely workable.

Open 4pm to 9pm Monday and Wednesday through Friday, 3pm to 9pm at weekends. Closed Tuesday.
venues.pressQuote: Seasons Rotisserie & Grill, near Old Town, serves an elevated Shirley Temple.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Visit Albuquerque, Where To Find Mocktails in Albuquerque

venues.name: Seaworthy
venues.description: Seaworthy is an oyster bar and seafood restaurant in a restored 1832 cottage on Carondelet Street in New Orleans' Central Business District, open since 2016. NOTE: it sits inside the hotel formerly known as the Ace Hotel New Orleans, which was rebranded The Barnett in 2024 and now operates under JdV by Hyatt — the restaurant kept its own name and continues to trade there. It built its reputation on wild-caught, sustainably harvested oysters from the Gulf and both coasts, plus an acclaimed cocktail program; executive chef James Whitehead came from sister property Maison de la Luz. Within the drinks list sit a handful of zero-proof options: Curious Elixirs No. 1, a non-alcoholic riff on a Negroni made with rhodiola and pomegranate, and a Lyre's Amalfi Spritz. Prices for the zero-proof drinks are not published online. Open 4pm to 10pm Sunday to Thursday and to 11pm Friday and Saturday, with an oyster happy hour daily from 4 to 6.
venues.longDescription:
Seaworthy opened in 2016 in a restored 1832 cottage on the 600 block of Carondelet Street, and has spent its reputation on one thing: wild-caught, sustainably harvested oysters from the Gulf and both coasts, shucked to order. Its own line is "come for the oysters, stay for the everything", and the everything includes a lobster roll on a brioche bun, shrimp and grits, boudin and gravy and a wagyu burger. Executive chef James Whitehead came across from Maison de la Luz. It opens at 4pm daily, until 10pm Sunday to Thursday and 11pm at weekends, with an oyster happy hour every day from 4 to 6 that halves the price of raw oysters.

One piece of orientation saves confusion on arrival. Seaworthy has always been described as the restaurant inside the Ace Hotel New Orleans, and much of the writing about it still says so — but the hotel is not the Ace any more. In 2024 the property's owner ended its management agreement with Ace and rebranded the building as The Barnett, now operating under JdV by Hyatt. The restaurant kept its name, its address and its own front door, and The Barnett's dining page still lists it as an active venue, so nothing about visiting has changed. Only the sign on the hotel has. For non-drinkers, the zero-proof offering is modest and bought-in rather than built: Curious Elixirs No. 1, a bottled non-alcoholic take on a Negroni made with rhodiola and pomegranate, and a Lyre's Amalfi Spritz. Neither price is published anywhere, and the restaurant's own menu page does not list its drinks as readable text, so plan to ask. The bar also keeps lower-alcohol session cocktails for people cutting down rather than cutting out, which is worth knowing but is not the same thing. Come here for the oysters and the room; the drinks list will meet you rather than impress you.
venues.pressQuote: Zero-proof refreshers include Curious Elixirs No. 1, a refreshing version of the classic Negroni with rhodiola and pomegranate; and Lyre's Amalfi Spritz.

venues.name: Sèchey
venues.description: Charleston's dedicated non-alcoholic bottle shop and tasting salon on upper King Street, founded in 2021 by Emily Heintz. The shop is a multi-brand specialty retailer carrying alcohol-free wine, beer, and zero-proof spirits alongside adaptogen and functional drinks, with complimentary in-store tastings to guide customers through the products. In July 2026 The Post and Courier reported that the King Street shop is closing, with Heintz planning to move the business out of South Carolina, and the 540 King Street unit is now listed for lease assignment. The website still publishes store hours, so call before making the trip.
venues.hours: Mon closed; Tue-Wed 12pm-6pm; Thu-Sat 10am-7pm; Sun closed

naMenuItems.name: Bittersweet
naMenuItems.description: non-alcoholic apéritif, sugar free

naMenuItems.name: Lyre's Dark Cane Spirit
naMenuItems.description: the premium non-alcoholic dark rum alternative

venues.longDescription:
Sèchey is a fully alcohol-free retail concept at 540 King Street in downtown Charleston, founded in 2021 by Emily Heintz. Part bottle shop and part tasting salon, it stocks premium non-alcoholic wine, beer, and zero-proof spirits alongside adaptogen-infused functional beverages, and offers complimentary tastings so customers can sample before they buy. The space is positioned as a modern, chic alternative to a traditional liquor store, geared toward sober and sober-curious shoppers.

Beyond the storefront, Sèchey runs Sèchey Noir, a separate line focused on THC and CBD products, and offers complimentary local delivery in downtown Charleston as well as event tastings.

The shop's future on King Street is uncertain. On 9 July 2026 The Post and Courier reported that the store is closing: Heintz cited South Carolina's unpredictable regulatory environment, a costly liquor-liability insurance requirement in the lease and high downtown rents, and said she plans to move the company to a state with a clearer framework. The 540 King Street lease, which runs to October 2027, has since been listed for assignment by Avison Young. As of early September 2026 the company's own website still lists store hours and tastings at the address, so the room may still be trading down its stock; anyone travelling for it should call ahead rather than assume it is open.

venues.name: Second Story
venues.description: Second Story is a Southern-Gothic craft cocktail bar and rooftop lounge on the upper floor of a century-old former Covington firehouse, opened in April 2023 by Lost Co. — the team behind Over-the-Rhine's Somerset and Alice — and voted CityBeat's Best New Bar. Beneath chandeliers and a giant artist-built tree that "grows" spirit bottles behind the bar, the menu keeps a small but genuine zero-proof lineup: house mocktails such as Clear Intent (lemon, lime, blueberry, pomegranate, mint) and Slow Burn (lime, pineapple, Fresno chili, soda water), a gin-substitute Clear Conscience, plus non-alcoholic Athletic Brewing lager and IPA. Note the bar also pours a THC-infused floral seltzer, so it's alcohol-free-optional rather than fully substance-free. Covington's largest bar patio makes it a comfortable place to gather without drinking.
venues.hours: Mon-Tue closed; Wed-Thu 4pm-12am; Fri 4pm-1am; Sat 2pm-1am; Sun 2pm-10pm
