naMenuItems.description: lemon, lime, blueberry, pomegranate, mint,

naMenuItems.name: Slow Burn
naMenuItems.description: lime, pineapple, fresno chili, soda water

venues.longDescription:
Second Story opened on April 28, 2023, as the latest project from Lost Co., the hospitality group behind Over-the-Rhine's Somerset and Alice, in partnership with a group of Louisville investors who also own the Flying Axes axe-throwing hall on the ground floor. The bar occupies the upper level of a century-old building at 100 West Sixth Street that once served as a Covington firehouse — and, over the decades, a music venue and logistics office. Lost Co. rehabbed the space into what CityBeat called "an artistic, Southern Gothic oasis for every sort of reveler," filling it with sparkling chandeliers, hand-painted murals, colorful floor tiles and a giant artist-built tree that appears to grow floor-to-ceiling behind the bar, its branches cradling bottles of spirits. There are deliberately no TVs; the room, its intimate nooks and Covington's largest bar patio are built for conversation. The bar was voted Best New Bar by CityBeat readers.

The drink list leans hard into imaginative seasonal cocktails, but it carries a real, if compact, non-alcoholic section for guests who want to skip the booze. House mocktails on the current menu include Clear Intent (lemon, lime, blueberry, pomegranate and mint) and Slow Burn (lime, pineapple, Fresno chili and soda water), each $10; earlier menus have featured an Orange Creamsicle (orange, cranberry, apricot, sage, bitters and orange blossom) and a Clear Conscience built on a non-alcoholic gin substitute, lemon, simple syrup and soda water. For beer drinkers, Second Story stocks non-alcoholic Athletic Brewing options in both a Mexican-style lager and an IPA. One caveat worth knowing: the bar also serves a THC-infused floral seltzer, so "alcohol-free" here does not necessarily mean substance-free, and the short mocktail list rotates with the seasons.

Second Story is open Wednesday and Thursday 4 p.m.–midnight, Friday 4 p.m.–1 a.m., Saturday 2 p.m.–1 a.m. and Sunday 2 p.m.–10 p.m., and is closed Monday and Tuesday; it takes reservations for small and large parties via its website and hosts a monthly market for local vendors. The rooftop patio and low-lit, plant-filled main room make it an easy recommendation for a date, a group outing or a designated driver who still wants something interesting in hand — reachable up the stairs at 100 West Sixth Street in downtown Covington, a five-minute drive across the river from downtown Cincinnati.
venues.pressQuote: Covington's Second Story bar, the latest vision from Lost Co., is an artistic, Southern Gothic oasis for every sort of reveler.

venues.name: Secret Admirer
venues.description: Secret Admirer is a downtown Des Moines cocktail bar on SW 5th Street that keeps rotating seasonal spirit-free and low-ABV options rather than a fixed pair of mocktails — a Santa Spritz of raspberry, cinnamon, apple cider and Topo Chico appeared on the winter list. Carrying both spirit-free and low-ABV matters, because they serve different people: someone who has stopped entirely and someone who is cutting down need different things, and most bars quietly assume they are the same customer. Open 4pm most days, from 10am on Saturday, and closing at 1am on Friday.
venues.longDescription:
Secret Admirer occupies a century-old boiler room at 110 SW 5th Street in downtown Des Moines, converted into a cocktail and patio bar — CITYVIEW called it the envy of local historic developers when it opened. The name came from the building's neighbours: the story the team tell is that it felt as though people had been secretly admiring the bar. It belongs to the DMDT hospitality group alongside Hello, Marjorie and Good News, Darling. CORRECTION TO OUR EARLIER LISTING: we had the wrong web address. The domain we published, with an s in the middle, no longer belongs to the bar and now resolves to a network security block page; the working site drops that letter.

What makes it worth a non-drinker's time is that the spirit-free drinks are a printed section rather than a courtesy, and they are priced below the cocktails — $10 against $13. The current list is a spring one, and the bar rotates it hard by season, so treat the names as a snapshot rather than a promise. No Ragret Spaghett is the interesting build: Best Day Brewing's non-alcoholic kölsch lengthened with a non-alcoholic aperitivo and lemon, which is a proper spaghett — the Italian bartender's drink of a beer with bitter aperitivo dropped into it — rendered alcohol-free without losing the bitterness that makes it work. Spring Kick runs non-alcoholic tequila with passionfruit, lime, jalapeño and Topo Chico. A Pesche strawberry mojito is $8, and Best Day's kölsch on its own is $6. The group's own view of the programme, from their events manager, is refreshingly unpretentious: they make them easy and drinkable, and people who don't drink alcohol say they have a good selection. One earlier winter drink documented here, a Santa Spritz of raspberry, cinnamon, apple cider and Topo Chico, is not on the current card — which is the clearest evidence that the rotation is real. The bar publishes no hours on its own site; check before travelling.
venues.pressQuote: A century-old boiler room in downtown Des Moines is the latest to become a cocktail and patio bar — and it's the envy of local downtown historic developers.

venues.name: Seed Library
venues.description: Seed Library is the Shoreditch cocktail bar from Ryan Chetiyawardana, the bartender better known as Mr Lyan, who reshaped London drinking in 2013 with White Lyan — the first bar to work with no perishables, no ice and no branded spirits. His later rooms, Dandelyan (named the world's best bar in 2018) and its South Bank successor Lyaness, have been fixtures of the World's 50 Best list. Opened in the basement of the One Hundred Shoreditch hotel at 100 Shoreditch High Street, Seed Library is pitched as his neighbourhood bar: less theatrical than the flagship, built around what the team call stripped-back analogue forms and a maker's touch — minimal fuss, maximum flavour, drawn from unexpected ingredients. It is a low-lit room with a pared-back, produce-led list. Its "Pathways" menu carries four dedicated non-alcoholic serves, and roughly half the full cocktail list can be rebuilt booze-free; named low- and no-alcohol drinks include the Hand-Rolled Spritz and Master Stock Plus.
signatureDrinks: Boozeless Coriander Seed Gimlet (Everleaf non-alcoholic aperitif, coriander seed cordial)
Boozeless Pink + Green Daiquiri (Seedlip Garden, nitro-ripened grape, lime)
Boozeless Orkney Breezer (Everleaf Marine, native tropical garum, rare-breed sheep, whipped citrus)
Boozeless Corn Yuzu Mule (Seedlip Spice, house hot sauce, cucumber, lime, ginger soda)
venues.longDescription:
Seed Library is the Shoreditch cocktail bar from Ryan Chetiyawardana, the bartender better known as Mr Lyan, who reshaped London drinking in 2013 with White Lyan — the first bar to work with no perishables, no ice and no branded spirits. His subsequent rooms, Dandelyan (named the world's best bar at the World's 50 Best Bars awards in 2018) and its South Bank successor Lyaness, have been fixtures of that list. Opened in the basement of the One Hundred Shoreditch hotel at 100 Shoreditch High Street (E1 6JQ), Seed Library is pitched as his neighbourhood bar: less theatrical than the flagship, built around what the team call "stripped-back analogue forms and a maker's touch" — minimal fuss, maximum flavour, drawn from unexpected ingredients.

The space is a low-ceilinged basement done in warm, retro tones — terrazzo tables, pine panelling and soft 1960s and '70s stylings — that Time Out called "a relaxed, impressively low-lit and supremely welcoming space". It is an over-18s room that takes walk-ins as readily as bookings, and at weekends the East London crew Diggers Dozen spin vinyl. Snacks lean on Lyan lore, including the returning White Lyan Magic Cheese first served at his original Hoxton bar.

The drinks arrive on a rotating "Pathways" list of eight serves, and — unusually for a bar of this billing — four of them are non-alcoholic, built with the same rigour as their full-strength twins rather than tacked on as an afterthought. The alcohol-free "Boozeless" pours (around £8–£9) shadow the main menu: a Boozeless Coriander Seed Gimlet of Everleaf's non-alcoholic aperitif and house coriander-seed cordial; a Boozeless Pink + Green Daiquiri using Seedlip Garden with nitro-ripened grape and lime; a Boozeless Orkney Breezer that swaps whisky for Everleaf Marine over native tropical garum, rare-breed sheep and whipped citrus; and a Boozeless Corn Yuzu Mule of Seedlip Spice, house hot sauce, cucumber, lime and ginger soda. The bar's boundary-pushing pantry — nitro-ripened grapes, koji, garums and fermented cordials — does as much work in the no-alcohol serves as in the spirituous ones. Menus change often, so past boozeless pours have also included a South Island Sour, a Banana Butter Swizzle, a Plum Wood Martini and a Green Juice, drawing on NA spirits such as Botivo, Sylva Orchard and Tropic All. Staff are well briefed and happy to rebuild almost any cocktail on the list as a booze-free version.
venues.pressQuote: Megastar mixologist Ryan Chetiyawardana – aka Mr Lyan – is behind Seed Library's menu, which features an unsurprisingly excellent and fairly bonkers selection of beverages.

venues.name: Selden Standard
venues.description: One of Detroit's most decorated restaurants — a 2024 and 2025 James Beard Award semifinalist for Outstanding Restaurant — Selden Standard treats its non-alcoholic drinks with the same seasonal, ingredient-driven care as its acclaimed wood-fired small plates. The Midtown dining room keeps a short list of named zero-proof cocktails like the bittersweet, ginger-tinged Beautiful Genius and the cucumber-mint-citrus Instant Karma, alongside non-alcoholic beer, house hopped water, and the amaro-inspired Casamar Club leisure soda from a local maker.
signatureDrinks: Rotating non-alcoholic beer & house hopped water
venues.longDescription:
Opened in 2014 on Second Avenue, Selden Standard helped define Detroit's modern dining revival and has since become a fixture of the city's fine-dining scene — a repeat James Beard Award semifinalist for Outstanding Restaurant (2024 and 2025) and a USA Today best-restaurant pick. The seasonal, wood-fired menu changes constantly around what local farms are growing, and the bar program follows the same philosophy.

That care extends to the zero-proof list. General manager Paul Fradeneck, a decade-plus beverage veteran, builds the non-alcoholic cocktails to stand on their own rather than mimic the spirited ones, leaning on pantry and kitchen ingredients to replace the mouthfeel and bitterness that alcohol provides. The rotating options include named mocktails such as the bittersweet Beautiful Genius and the cucumber-mint-citrus Instant Karma, plus non-alcoholic beer, house hopped water, and Casamar Club, an amaro-inspired leisure soda from a Detroit brand.
venues.pressQuote: It's actually harder to create a well-balanced, non-alcoholic cocktail than it is to make a traditional one using alcohol.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Paul Fradeneck, Selden Standard general manager

venues.name: Senia
venues.description: Senia is a fine-dining restaurant on North King Street in Chinatown, listed by The World's 50 Best Discovery and one of the most decorated kitchens in Hawaiʻi. Its non-alcoholic offering is a single drink, Mike's Mocktail, but it is a rotating one — the build changes every other month, with a lavender-honey version among those reported. That rotation is the point: it means the drink is developed alongside the food each cycle rather than printed once and forgotten, which is a different kind of commitment from a long static list. Dinner runs Monday to Saturday from 5.30pm, and the restaurant is closed on Sundays.
signatureDrinks: Mike's Mocktail (rotates every other month; a lavender-honey build among them)
venues.longDescription:
Senia occupies 75 North King Street in Chinatown, a few doors from The Pig & The Lady and a short walk from Lucky Belly, in what has become the most concentrated stretch of serious cooking in Honolulu. It is a fine-dining room by any measure — recognised by The World's 50 Best Discovery and a regular in Hawaiʻi restaurant guides — with a tasting-menu counter alongside the à la carte dining room, and it operates on a restricted schedule of Monday to Saturday evenings from 5.30pm to 9.30pm, closed Sunday.

Its non-alcoholic listing is a single drink, which would normally place it low in this guide, except that the drink is a rotating one. Mike's Mocktail changes every other month; a lavender-honey build is the version most often reported, but the whole point is that it does not stay the same. That structure is worth drawing out, because it is a genuinely different model from the one most venues use. A restaurant with a printed six-drink zero-proof list has made a stocking decision — it has bought the ingredients and trained the specs, and those drinks will be there in April as in January. A restaurant with one rotating drink has instead folded the non-alcoholic option into the kitchen's development cycle, so the drink moves with the seasons and the menu the way a wine pairing would. At this level of cooking that is arguably the more meaningful commitment, because it means somebody is thinking about the drink every eight weeks rather than having thought about it once. The trade-off for a guest is predictability: you cannot look up what you will be served, and if you dislike the current build there is no second option. For a special-occasion dinner in a city with no dedicated zero-proof cocktail bar, that is a reasonable exchange, and Chinatown's density means Lucky Belly's far deeper list is two minutes away if it is not.
venues.pressQuote: Its menu features a drink called "Mike's Mocktail," which, not surprisingly, is also really good.

venues.name: SereniTea Lounge
venues.description: SereniTea Lounge is a boba teahouse and cocktail bar on Milwaukee's East Side, occupying a long-vacant Downer Avenue landmark (the former Chancery) that it revived in January 2025 as the local brand's third location and first bar. By day it runs as a full teahouse with an extensive alcohol-free menu of fruit teas, milk teas and bubble-tea drinks built with tapioca pearls and bursting boba; by night it adds a cocktail program. For sober and sober-curious guests the entire boba/tea menu is non-alcoholic and available all day, with named drinks like the Horchata Taro and a house-brewed Sweet Thai. Because it also serves cocktails, wine and sake, it is a hybrid rather than a fully alcohol-free space.
signatureDrinks: Horchata Taro (layered boba, horchata and taro milk foam)
Strawberry Lemonade with strawberry bursting boba
Peach & Grapefruit with peach bursting boba
venues.longDescription:
SereniTea Lounge opened at 2569 N. Downer Ave. on January 31, 2025, filling part of the former Chancery space that had sat vacant since 2007. It is the third location for the Milwaukee-founded boba brand started by Manpreet Singh, who opened the first SereniTea in 2019 while finishing at Marquette University, and it is the brand's first to double as a bar, pairing a daytime teahouse with an evening cocktail lounge and lounge-style seating.

The non-alcoholic side is the heart of the concept. The standing menu runs deep on fruit teas, milk teas and bubble-tea drinks made with tapioca pearls and bursting boba: a strawberry lemonade with strawberry bursting boba, a peach-and-grapefruit with peach bursting boba, and a mango-passionfruit jasmine tea, alongside items like the Horchata Taro (layered boba, horchata and taro milk foam) and an in-house-brewed Sweet Thai. Every one of these is alcohol-free and available throughout the day, so a non-drinker gets the full menu rather than a single token mocktail.

Writing for Milwaukee Magazine in November 2025, Ann Christenson noted that "the teahouse serves many flavors of fruit tea and milk tea, smoothies and ice cream drinks," describing a room whose ambiance shifts from cafe by day to a more sophisticated cocktail lounge after dark. The venue also pours classic cocktails, wine and sake, which keeps it in hybrid territory, but the extensive, always-available non-alcoholic tea and boba program is what makes it a real destination for sober guests on Downer Avenue.
venues.pressQuote: The teahouse serves many flavors of fruit tea and milk tea, smoothies and ice cream drinks.

venues.name: Seroja
venues.description: Seroja is chef Kevin Wong's two-Michelin-starred Nusantara restaurant in the Duo Galleria at Bugis, and its non-alcoholic pairing is a genuine anchor of the beverage program rather than an afterthought. The roughly S$148 zero-proof flight is built to run alongside the S$288++ tasting menu, using fruit and vegetable trimmings that would otherwise be discarded. Named house infusions include a chestnut, watercress and lotus-root brew aged in an apple-wood barrel, and a pomegranate, mulberries and curry-leaf blend that plays sweet against savoury. This waste-conscious drinks work is part of what earned Seroja a Michelin Green Star. Chef Kevin Wong has said he could not connect with the other cuisines he trained in because they were not part of his DNA, and the drinks follow the same logic as the food.
venues.hours: Mon closed; Tue-Thu 6pm-11pm; Fri-Sat 12pm-2:30pm & 6pm-11pm; Sun closed
signatureDrinks: Infusion of chestnut, watercress and lotus root aged in an apple-wood barrel

naMenuItems.name: Non Alcoholic Pairing
naMenuItems.description: 108++lunch / 148++ dinner

venues.longDescription:
Opened by Klang-born chef Kevin Wong, Seroja celebrates Nusantara cuisine of the Malay archipelago and earned a Michelin star within roughly a year of opening. It was promoted to two Michelin stars in the Michelin Guide Singapore 2026. It has since become one of Singapore's most decorated modern restaurants, ranking on Asia's 50 Best Restaurants list (No. 31 in 2024 and No. 40 in 2025) and holding a Michelin Green Star for its sustainability practices. The restaurant sits at 7 Fraser Street inside the Duo Galleria near Bugis.

The reason to note Seroja for a non-alcoholic directory is its dedicated zero-proof pairing, offered at around S$148 as an alternative to the wine flight alongside the S$288++ Nusantara menu. The pairing is deliberately low-waste, drawing on fruit and vegetable scraps that the kitchen would otherwise throw away, and this circular approach is directly tied to the restaurant's Michelin Green Star.

Standout non-alcoholic serves include an infusion of chestnut, watercress and lotus root aged in an apple-wood barrel, which leans earthy and savoury, and a brighter pomegranate, mulberries and curry-leaf blend that carries Indian-spice notes. Because the drinks are house-made infusions built around the menu rather than bottled products, there are no commercial zero-proof brands to list; the program's strength is its kitchen-driven, ingredient-forward composition.

Seroja is a booking-led fine-dining room, open for dinner Tuesday through Saturday and for lunch on Fridays and Saturdays, with reservations handled through its website. It suits diners who want a serious, chef-composed non-alcoholic pairing rather than a walk-in cocktail bar.

The restaurant exists because of a decision Kevin Wong made about whose food he was cooking. He worked in fine dining in France, the United States and Singapore for the better part of a decade, rising to head chef at Meta, and told The Peak Magazine that those cuisines were something he learned as part of a career but could not connect with, because they were not part of his DNA. Seroja — Malay for lotus flower — is what he built instead, focused on Singaporean, Malaysian and Indonesian cooking across the Malay Archipelago.

That origin explains the drinks. A kitchen working with tamarind, coconut, pandan, curry leaf, kaffir lime and fermented pastes has a deep pantry of non-alcoholic flavour to draw on, and the pairing uses trimmings from that same pantry rather than buying in bottled substitutes. The apple-wood-barrel infusion of chestnut, watercress and lotus root is a savoury, tannic drink of a kind the zero-proof market simply does not sell; the pomegranate, mulberry and curry-leaf blend does the sweet-against-savoury work a wine pairing would hand to an off-dry white.

The low-waste method is not a marketing line either — it is the practice the Michelin Green Star recognises, and it is unusual to see it applied to the drinks list rather than only the kitchen. The room seats 24 inside Duo Galleria, interiors shaped after the islands of the archipelago, with serving ware made by regional craftsmen. Booking is effectively mandatory.
venues.pressQuote: Cooking the other cuisines was something I learned as part of my career, but I couldn’t connect with them. It wasn’t part of my DNA.

venues.name: Settle Down Tavern
venues.description: Settle Down Tavern is a supper-club-inflected bar and restaurant on South Pinckney Street off the Capitol Square, and it is one of the two downtown rooms Visit Madison names first when the question is where to find a mocktail menu. The bar shakes its non-alcoholic drinks in house rather than buying them in, and — usefully — stays open all day even when the kitchen closes for a reset between 2:30pm and 4pm, so it is one of the few Capitol Square rooms where you can sit with a drink mid-afternoon. Happy hour runs every weekday from 2 to 6pm. Closed Sundays; open to midnight Friday and Saturday.
venues.hours: Mon 4pm-9pm; Tue 11:30am-9pm; Wed-Thu 11:30am-10pm; Fri-Sat 11:30am-12am; Sun closed
venues.longDescription:
Settle Down Tavern opened on South Pinckney Street a few doors from Merchant and became one of the Capitol Square's reliable rooms — a bar and restaurant working in the Wisconsin supper-club register, which means brandy old fashioneds, a relish tray sensibility and food that does not apologise for being comfort food. It sits in a city block that also holds Merchant, Lucille and the Great Dane's downtown brewpub, which between them make the Square the densest concentration of credible non-alcoholic drinking in Wisconsin.

Visit Madison, the official visitor bureau, names Settle Down alongside Lucille as the downtown restaurants to check for mocktail menus, and Isthmus has noted that the bar shakes its own in-house non-alcoholic creations rather than pouring from a bottle. We have not been able to source the current drink names — the menu is not published in a form we can verify, and it rotates — so no named builds are recorded here rather than listing something stale. Ask at the bar; the programme is real, the specifics change.

Two practical details make it more useful than its neighbours for a non-drinker. First, the bar stays open through the afternoon even though the kitchen closes for a reset between 2:30pm and 4pm, so there is somewhere on the Square to sit with a drink at three in the afternoon — a gap most of downtown leaves open. Second, happy hour runs every weekday from 2 to 6pm, which in a supper-club room means the food specials matter as much as the drink ones. It opens at 11:30am Tuesday through Saturday, 4pm on Monday, runs to midnight on Friday and Saturday, and is closed on Sundays.
venues.pressQuote: Check out mocktail menus at downtown restaurants like Settle Down Tavern and Lucille.

venues.name: Seven Bro7hers Beerhouse (Ancoats)
venues.description: Seven Bro7hers Beerhouse in Ancoats is the Manchester bar of the Salford family brewery run by seven brothers, opened in 2016 on Blossom Street in the regenerated Ancoats district. It qualifies because Seven Bro7hers brews its own alcohol-free beer — AF Pale, a 0.5% hoppy craft pale ale — which is stocked across all of the company's Manchester beerhouses, this one included. Set over several levels with a ground-floor bar, a downstairs lounge and an outdoor patio, it pairs rotating house taps of Honeycomb Pale, Easy IPA and Helles Lager with burgers, gyros and bar snacks. The non-alcoholic pour is the brewery's own beer rather than a bought-in afterthought.
venues.longDescription:
Seven Bro7hers is a Salford family brewery founded in 2014 by the seven McAvoy brothers — Guy, Keith, Luke, Daniel, Nathan, Kit and Greg — who grew up watching their father home-brew in the cellar and turned the hobby into a business. The Ancoats Beerhouse opened in 2016 at 39 Blossom Street and was one of the group's first bars, planted in one of Manchester's most heavily regenerated inner-city neighbourhoods a short walk from Cutting Room Square. The brewery itself sits a few miles west in Salford, and the beerhouses act as the brand's shop window across Greater Manchester, alongside its 11 Central bar and microbrewery at Salford Quays and the Amber Alehouse at Manchester Airport.

The bar runs over several levels — a busy ground-floor room, a relaxed downstairs lounge fitted out with leather sofas, and a large outdoor patio for warmer days. Table bookings are taken for both food and drink, and the kitchen keeps things simple and beer-friendly with burgers, gyros and 'bar munchies' built to sit alongside a pint. Rotating house taps pour through the core Seven Bro7hers range — Honeycomb Pale Ale, Easy IPA, Helles Lager, Pilsner and a rotation of hop-forward IPAs — so the line-up shifts but stays firmly the brewery's own beer.

What earns it a place here is that Seven Bro7hers brews its own alcohol-free beer. AF Pale, launched in December 2021 as the brewery's first low-alcohol release, is a 0.5% ABV pale ale built to keep the hop character of a full-strength craft beer — pale and light, with citrus and fruity aromas and a clean bitterness — and it is vegan-friendly. From launch it has been stocked in 330ml cans across all of the company's Manchester beerhouses, the Ancoats site included, so the zero-proof choice at the bar is the same beer the brothers brew rather than a bought-in lager dropped on for form's sake. It is a modest but genuine non-alcoholic offering: one well-made house AF beer from a brewery that makes it itself, ideal if you want a proper Ancoats craft-beer night without the alcohol.
venues.pressQuote: The new release will be stocked on the Seven Bro7hers webshop and in all its Manchester-based beer houses from Monday 20 December.

venues.name: Seviche, A Latin Restaurant
venues.description: Seviche is chef Anthony Lamas's Latin restaurant on Bardstown Road in the Deer Park stretch of the Highlands, and one of Louisville's longest-standing serious kitchens — Lamas is a James Beard semifinalist and a familiar face from television. The bar makes a non-alcoholic mojito as standard and, more usefully, the staff will build a bespoke alcohol-free cocktail on request rather than pointing at the soft drinks. In a Latin kitchen that is a meaningful offer: the house already keeps muddled herbs, citrus, agave syrups and fruit purées for the cocktail list, so an alcohol-free drink starts from real components. Dinner runs seven nights from 5pm.
signatureDrinks: Non-alcoholic mojito (muddled mint, lime, sugar, soda)

naMenuItems.name: Chef's Favorite
naMenuItems.description: lyre's italian orange n/a aperitivo, lyre's classico n/a prosecco, lemon, ginger, orange bitters

naMenuItems.name: Kissin' Kate's Rattlesnake
naMenuItems.description: black cherry juice, lime, vanilla, lyre's classico n/a prosecco

naMenuItems.name: Jake Speitx (Non-Alcoholic Hugo Spritz)
naMenuItems.description: elderflower syrup, soda, lemon, mint, lyre's classico n/a prosecco

venues.longDescription:
Anthony Lamas opened Seviche on Bardstown Road in 2005 and has spent two decades making it one of the fixed points of Louisville dining — a Latin restaurant built on ceviche, Southern produce and a genuine cocktail programme, run by a chef who has been a James Beard Award semifinalist and a recurring television presence. The room sits in Deer Park, the stretch of the Highlands where Bardstown Road is restaurants rather than bars.

For a non-drinker the useful thing here is not a printed list — it is the kitchen's raw materials and the staff's willingness to use them. A Latin bar runs on muddled herbs, fresh citrus, agave and fruit purées, all of which are already prepped for the cocktails; the alcohol is one line item rather than the structure. So the standing non-alcoholic mojito is a real drink — mint muddled to order, lime, sugar, soda — and the more valuable offer is that the bartenders will build something bespoke if you tell them what you like. That is a different proposition from a bar with three fixed mocktails, and often a better one: you get a drink built for your palate rather than the one drink the bar decided non-drinkers want.

It is worth being straightforward about the limits. Seviche does not stock a deep bench of non-alcoholic spirits the way Proof on Main does, so a spirit-forward alcohol-free drink is not really on offer here; what you get is fresh, bright and built from produce. Dinner runs seven nights from 5pm, to 9pm most nights and 10pm on Friday and Saturday, and reservations are sensible at weekends. This is also one of the better entries in the guide for a group where only one person is not drinking, because the food is the reason everyone came.
venues.pressQuote: Seviche makes a non-alcoholic mojito, and staff can create custom non-alcoholic cocktails upon request.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: The Zero Proof, Louisville city guide

venues.name: Sexy Fish Manchester
venues.description: Sexy Fish is the glossy Japanese-inspired restaurant and bar that opened on Spinningfields Square in autumn 2023, inside the former Armani Emporium — a 200-plus-seat room designed as much as a bar as a restaurant, with large sea-creature sculptures by Damien Hirst and fish-shaped lamps designed by Frank Gehry. The kitchen turns out sushi, sashimi, seafood and robata-grilled fish and meat, and the bar earned a pin in the inaugural Pinnacle Guide 2024, one of only 37 bars selected worldwide. Its alcohol-free programme is treated as an equal rather than an afterthought: the Unity cocktail menu, launched in 2024, is built around 12 core flavour profiles, each printed side by side in an alcoholic and an alcohol-free version, so a non-drinker orders from the same list. Named zero-proof serves include a non-alcoholic Watermelon (£7) and a non-alcoholic Cacao (£10, on Everleaf Marine), alongside six low-ABV options.
signatureDrinks: Non-alcoholic Cacao (£10) — Everleaf Marine, cacao dark chocolate, vanilla, merlot grape juice, bitters
Non-alcoholic Watermelon (£7) — lemon, chilli, black olive, rosemary tonic
venues.longDescription:
Sexy Fish opened on Spinningfields Square in autumn 2023 inside the former Armani Emporium, a 200-plus-seat room designed as much as a bar as a restaurant. The interior is a spectacle in its own right, with large sea-creature sculptures by Damien Hirst and fish-shaped lamps designed by Frank Gehry, and the kitchen turns out Japanese-inspired sushi, sashimi, seafood and Robata-grilled fish and meat. The bar earned a pin in the inaugural Pinnacle Guide 2024, one of just 37 bars selected worldwide after an 18-month consultation process.

The reason it belongs on a non-alcoholic map is the Unity menu, launched in 2024. Rather than tacking a handful of mocktails onto the back of the list, Sexy Fish built 12 core serves that each appear as both an alcoholic and an alcohol-free drink, presented together on the same menu, plus six low-ABV options. As beverage lead Dominic North puts it, the team rejects the word 'mocktail' entirely, arguing it undermines the drinks; the alcohol-free builds use house-made tinctures and infusions rather than sugary shortcuts.

Named zero-proof serves include the Watermelon (£7), made with lemon, chilli, black olive and rosemary tonic, and the Cacao (£10), a coupe serve of Everleaf Marine, cacao dark chocolate, vanilla, merlot grape juice and bitters. A Manchester-exclusive Apple serve is offered in alcoholic, alcohol-free and low-ABV versions, and other core flavours on the list include Strawberry, Grapefruit, Honey and Sugar Snap Pea.

Open from noon until late seven days a week, it is a genuine special-occasion room where someone not drinking can order with the same seriousness as everyone else at the table.
venues.pressQuote: These are as far from the usual, overly sweet token gestures you might find in other bars.

venues.name: Sexy Fish Miami
venues.description: Sexy Fish Miami is the Brickell outpost of the London-born Caprice Holdings restaurant group, occupying a lavish, underwater-themed space featuring original Damien Hirst artwork. Beyond its Asian-influenced seafood menu, the bar program is notable for its structured non-alcoholic offering. In May 2024 the venue launched its "Unity" cocktail menu, built around 12 core flavor profiles each served in both a full-strength and a 0% ABV iteration — a near 1:1 alcohol-free mirror of the spirited list. The program was developed by Caprice Holdings' bar team, and the zero-proof builds lean on house-made tinctures and infusions plus named ingredients like Seedlip Garden 108 and London Essence Co. sodas. Miami-exclusive serves include Lime, Goldenberry, and Coffee (the latter inspired by the espresso martini and carajillo). It is one of Miami's most deliberately built NA cocktail experiences.
venues.longDescription:
Sexy Fish Miami is the Brickell outpost of the London restaurant group Caprice Holdings, occupying a deliberately lavish underwater-themed room hung with original Damien Hirst work. The food is Asian-influenced seafood; the reason it appears here is the bar, which runs what is probably the most systematically constructed non-alcoholic programme in the city.

In May 2024 the venue launched its Unity menu, built around twelve core flavour profiles, each served in both a full-strength and a 0% ABV version. That is a near one-to-one mirror of the spirited list, and the structural choice matters more than any individual drink. Most bars bolt two or three mocktails onto the end of a menu, which means a non-drinker orders from a different and shorter list than everyone else at the table. A mirrored menu removes that asymmetry entirely: the group orders from the same twelve profiles and some of them happen to contain alcohol.

The zero-proof builds use house-made tinctures and infusions alongside named products including Seedlip Garden 108 and London Essence Co. sodas, so the alcohol-free side draws on the same larder as the rest of the bar rather than on juice. Miami-exclusive serves include Lime, Goldenberry and Coffee, the last inspired by both the espresso martini and the carajillo.

The Greater Miami Convention & Visitors Bureau describes it as having one of the most extensive non-alcoholic cocktail menus in Miami, and the count supports that — more than a dozen refined mocktails, served in the same glassware as the cocktails.

It is a high-end restaurant with a full bar and Brickell prices, not an alcohol-free venue. But for a business dinner or an occasion where one person is not drinking, the mirrored menu is close to the ideal arrangement. Ask for the 0% version of whichever profile appeals rather than for the mocktail list — that is how the menu is designed to be used, and it produces a better drink.

A note on what this room is. Sexy Fish is a high-end restaurant with a full bar and one of the larger Japanese whisky collections in the country, so a non-drinker here is not in a protected environment — the 0% list is a genuine parallel menu, not a substitute for a sober space. What it does offer is a room where ordering nothing alcoholic carries no friction at all, which at this price point and in this part of Brickell is not a given.
venues.pressQuote: one of the most extensive non-alcoholic cocktail menus in Miami

venues.name: Shades Brewing
venues.description: Shades Brewing — which grew from a 500-square-foot Park City garage — brews craft beer on-site at its South Salt Lake taproom on Utopia Avenue; its bigger Ballpark "Engine Block" brewpub on 300 West closed in 2025 and that space now trades as an unaffiliated pub. For non-drinkers the brand's calling card is its "Stripped" mocktail menu, including the Stripped Geared Mule (pineapple, lime, lemon, mint and ginger beer), plus packaged non-alcoholic seltzers — a deliberate nod to inclusivity in an otherwise beer-forward room (note it is 21+). The NA offering is the mocktail program rather than an in-house 0.0% beer.
venues.address: 154 W Utopia Ave, South Salt Lake, UT 84115
signatureDrinks: Stripped Geared Mule (pineapple, lime, lemon, mint, ginger beer) — $9
venues.longDescription:
Shades built its name from a 500-square-foot Park City garage before settling into its South Salt Lake taproom on Utopia Avenue, where the beer is brewed on-site. A bigger Ballpark brewpub — opened April 2025 in the renovated "Engine Block" building with around 50 taps and a full kitchen — closed later that year amid a landlord dispute, and that space now trades as the unaffiliated Engine Room Pub & Bistro; the Utopia Avenue taproom is once again the place to drink Shades.

The non-alcoholic side is a dedicated mocktail program under the "Stripped" name rather than an in-house non-alcoholic beer, anchored by the Stripped Geared Mule that the Salt Lake Tribune singled out as a standout at the Ballpark room. Taproom hours are shorter than pub hours — afternoons into early evening most days — so it's worth confirming before a visit.
venues.pressQuote: I really enjoyed my mocktail, the Stripped Geared Mule ($9), made with pineapple, lime, lemon, mint and ginger beer. I'd never tasted that combination of pineapple and ginger beer before and I loved it.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: The Salt Lake Tribune, "Utah Eats" review

venues.name: Shangri-la Fair Oaks
venues.description: Shangri-la in Fair Oaks keeps three named alcohol-free drinks on the list year-round — Pineapple Cooler, Coconut Grotto and Lemon Roots — and expands for Dry January with Golden Earth, Bees Trees and non-alcoholic Stella Artois Liberté on top. The year-round three are the important part: seasonal menus that vanish in February are the standard failure in this category, and a permanent list is a much smaller promise kept properly. Fair Oaks sits about twenty minutes east of downtown, so this serves a suburb the central venues do not reach. Read the hours carefully though: closed Monday and Tuesday, and Sunday is an 11am-2pm brunch slot only.
venues.longDescription:
Shangri-la sits on Winding Way in Fair Oaks, a suburb about twenty minutes east of downtown Sacramento, and it maintains an alcohol-free list in two tiers: three drinks permanently, and additional ones during Dry January.

The permanent three — Pineapple Cooler, Coconut Grotto and Lemon Roots — matter more than the seasonal additions, and it is worth being clear why. The dominant pattern in this category is the January menu: a bar prints zero-proof drinks in the first week of the year, collects the coverage, and removes them by February. For someone doing a month-long challenge that works fine. For someone who has stopped drinking permanently, it means a venue's published list cannot be trusted in the spring, which is when the support actually matters. Three drinks kept all year is a smaller promise, honoured.

The Dry January expansion then adds Golden Earth, Bees Trees and non-alcoholic Stella Artois Liberté. Stocking an NA beer alongside built cocktails covers the other kind of non-drinker — the one who wants something familiar rather than something crafted.

The hours need reading carefully and are the main constraint: closed Monday and Tuesday, 5pm to 8:30pm Wednesday and Thursday, to 9:30pm Friday and Saturday, and Sunday only 11am to 2pm. That is a narrow set of windows, and the Sunday slot is brunch rather than evening.

Geographically it does something the rest of this guide cannot. Sacramento's alcohol-free depth is concentrated downtown and in Midtown; Fair Oaks is a substantial suburb with its own centre, and a venue there keeps a local from driving forty minutes round trip for a decent drink.

There is a driving argument specific to the suburbs as well. Fair Oaks is not walkable to anywhere, and anyone coming here is arriving by car and leaving by car. That is precisely the circumstance in which a bar with three real alcohol-free drinks changes the evening: the designated driver, who in most suburban bars gets a soda and an apology, can order something made properly and stay for the whole night rather than counting down. Suburban venues carry more of this weight than urban ones and get credited for it far less.
venues.pressQuote: Shangri-la Fair Oaks, year-round: Pineapple Cooler, Coconut Grotto, and Lemon Roots; Dry January adds Golden Earth, Bees Trees, and non-alcoholic Stella Artois Liberte.

venues.name: Shibam Coffee
venues.description: Shibam Coffee is a Yemeni coffeehouse at North Point Parkway in Alpharetta, opened in February 2025 as one of the first Yemeni cafes to reach metro Atlanta's northern suburbs. The brand was founded in Dearborn, Michigan, and Wasim Nasir is a co-owner of the Alpharetta shop. It serves no alcohol, and it trades to midnight most nights and 2am on Friday and Saturday — genuinely late for this part of the metro, and the reason the room fills up with groups rather than laptops after dark. The menu covers classic Yemeni coffee served in the traditional style alongside espresso drinks, and a set of house specialities including the Shibam Royal, strawberry and raspberry mojitos built without alcohol, dragon fruit lemonade and a pistachio iced latte. Desserts and Yemeni pastries are sold alongside.
venues.address: 4000 North Point Pkwy Suite 900, Alpharetta, GA 30022

naMenuItems.name: Black & Blue Berry Mojito
naMenuItems.description: blackberry and blueberry mojito with fresh mint (non-alcoholic)

naMenuItems.name: Mango Peach Mojito
naMenuItems.description: mango and peach mojito with fresh mint (non-alcoholic)

naMenuItems.name: Build Your Own Mojito
naMenuItems.description: choose your favorite fruit flavors for a custom mojito with fresh mint (non-alcoholic)

venues.longDescription:
Shibam takes its name from the walled city in Yemen's Hadhramaut valley, and the brand was founded in Dearborn, Michigan before expanding south. The Alpharetta cafe held its soft opening on 22 February 2025 in a suite at 4000 North Point Parkway, near the North Point Mall corridor, and 285 South covered it a few weeks later as part of a wider piece on the cardamom-scented wave of Yemeni cafes arriving across metro Atlanta in time for Ramadan. Wasim Nasir is a co-owner. The publication framed the arrival in exactly the terms that matter to anyone looking for somewhere to go that is not a bar: these rooms provide an alternative to alcohol-centric bar culture while transplanting a coffeehouse tradition from the other side of the world. Alpharetta had almost nothing comparable before it opened.

The operating hours are the clearest signal of intent. Shibam trades from 8am to midnight Monday through Thursday and Sunday, and to 2am on Friday and Saturday, which is later than most licensed venues in the same suburb. The room is styled as an upscale lounge rather than a takeaway counter, with seating arranged for groups. Classic Yemeni coffee is served in the traditional preparation, spiced and aromatic, alongside a conventional espresso bar. The house list is where Shibam differs from its Yemeni peers: the Shibam Royal is the signature pour, and the cafe runs alcohol-free strawberry and raspberry mojitos, a dragon fruit lemonade and a pistachio iced latte that has become the default order for first-time visitors. Yemeni desserts and pastries — including the milk cakes that travel with this whole category — are sold at the counter. Nothing alcoholic is served or permitted on the premises, which makes it a straightforward recommendation for anyone in the north metro who wants a late room with no bar attached.
venues.pressQuote: Shibam Coffee is the latest to join the scene, providing an alternative to alcohol-centric bar culture while giving local customers a taste of a coffeehouse culture that originates halfway around the globe.

venues.name: Shibam Coffee
venues.description: Shibam Coffee is an alcohol-free Yemeni coffeehouse that opened on 21 December 2025 at 5241 N Kedzie Ave in North Park, on the Kedzie Avenue corridor where several Middle Eastern cafes have opened within a mile of each other. It is the eleventh location of a chain that started in Dearborn, Michigan in 2022 and has since expanded through Ohio, Texas and now Chicago, and it imports its coffee beans and tea directly from Yemen. The menu is unusually deep on the traditional side for a US cafe, listing Adeni tea, mufawar, sana'ani, jubani, rad'ai and qishr alongside Saudi and Turkish coffee, an espresso list, non-caffeinated refreshers and a pastry case of sabaya, honeycomb and basbousa. There is no alcohol on the menu at all.
signatureDrinks: Adeni Tea (black tea simmered with cardamom and milk)
Mufawar (Yemeni milk tea gently infused with cardamom)
Jubani (bold Yemeni-style brew with a deep, smoky flavor and warming finish)
Qishr (Yemeni coffee-husk tea with ginger and spices)
Mojito (mint, lime and soda - listed on the menu as refreshing and alcohol-free)

naMenuItems.name: Mojito
naMenuItems.description: mint, lime, and soda—refreshing and alcohol-free.

venues.longDescription:
Shibam Coffee is named for Shibam, the walled Yemeni city of mudbrick towers often called the oldest skyscraper city in the world, and the chain leans on that heritage in its rooms and its cups. The company began in Dearborn, Michigan in 2022 and spread through Ohio and Texas before reaching Illinois; the North Park store, which opened on 21 December 2025, is its eleventh. Student reporters at the neighboring Northside College Prep, whose paper covered the opening in March 2026, noted the intricate light fixtures and wall art and quoted a Shibam employee explaining that the name is an ode to the Yemeni city known for its coffee. All coffee beans and tea are imported directly from Yemen to preserve the flavor profile the shops are built around.

The menu is organized by tradition first. The Yemeni tea section runs from Adeni tea - black tea simmered with cardamom and milk - through mufawar, a milk tea gently infused with cardamom; sana'ani, a spice-forward classic; jubani, a bold brew with a deep smoky finish; and rad'ai, lightly sweet and aromatic. On the coffee side there is qishr, the coffee-husk tea with ginger and spices, plus Saudi coffee with cardamom, Turkish coffee brewed unfiltered, and the house Shibam blend. A full espresso list, matcha, and non-caffeinated refreshers including a Mojito of mint, lime and soda that the menu itself flags as alcohol-free fill out the rest, and the pastry case carries sabaya, honeycomb bread, basbousa and milk cake. Nothing on the list contains alcohol. The cafe is listed as open from 7am to midnight every day, though at least one listing gives a 10pm close - either way this is an evening room, which is what makes it a genuine alternative to a bar on the far North Side. The chain also runs its own ordering app and an online shop selling the same Yemeni beans it brews, and it lists franchising alongside its store locator.
venues.pressQuote: Shibam, located at 5241 N. Kedzie, serves authentic Yemeni coffee along with pastries and teas.

venues.name: Shibam Coffee
venues.description: Shibam Coffee is a Yemeni coffeehouse on Brookpark Extension in North Olmsted, which the company lists as its Cleveland location. Shibam Coffee Co. began in Dearborn, Michigan in 2022 and now lists 22 cafes across ten states. It serves no alcohol and trades late; the company gives the hours as 7am to midnight every day. The menu divides into Yemeni coffee, Yemeni tea, an espresso bar and refreshers. Mufawar is Yemeni coffee with milk and cardamom, Qishr is a coffee-husk tea with ginger and spices, and Adeni Tea is a spiced milk tea simmered with black tea and cardamom. House specialities include the Shibam Royal, an organic mango smoothie with evaporated milk, the pomegranate-based Toot Shami, and a mint, lime and soda mojito that the menu marks as alcohol-free.
signatureDrinks: Mufawar (Yemeni coffee with milk and cardamom)
Qishr (coffee-husk tea with ginger and spices)
Adeni Tea (spiced milk tea with black tea, cardamom and milk)
Shibam Royal (organic mango smoothie with evaporated milk)
venues.longDescription:
Shibam Coffee Co. takes its name from the Yemeni city of Shibam, and the company began in Dearborn, Michigan in 2022. Its own site now lists 22 locations in ten states. The one it calls Cleveland is at 26745 Brookpark Extension in North Olmsted, on a short commercial street that Cleveland Scene described in 2024 as one of the quickest-growing Palestinian small-business hubs in Northeast Ohio, with twenty shops owned by Arab Americans opened there this decade. The coffeehouse suits that street: somewhere to sit once the errands are done.

The menu is the same across the company and is unusually complete on the traditional side. Under Yemeni Coffee it lists Mufawar, made with milk and cardamom; Sana'ani; Jubani; Rad'ai; and Qishr, a tea brewed from coffee husks with ginger and spices. Saudi coffee with cardamom and Turkish coffee sit beside them. Under Yemeni Tea come Adeni Tea, a spiced milk tea simmered with black tea, cardamom and milk, a plain Yemeni Tea, Moroccan mint tea and ginger tea. The refreshers are the part of the menu that works as an evening drink in place of a cocktail: the Shibam Royal is an organic mango smoothie with evaporated milk, with date syrup as an option; Toot Shami is pomegranate-based; and the mojito is mint, lime and soda, described on the menu as alcohol-free. Sabaya, a flaky layered pastry served with honey, is sold with honeycomb, milk cake and basbousa.

Nothing on the menu contains alcohol. The company's page for this location gives the hours as 7am to midnight seven days a week; some listings show an 11pm close from Sunday to Thursday, so check before a late weeknight visit. Either way it is open well after most cafes in the western suburbs have closed. Two other Yemeni coffeehouses, Qahwah House and Baladi Coffee House, are within about a mile and a quarter, and the company's site also lists a second west-side cafe at 25651 Detroit Road in Westlake, with opening hours still to be announced.
venues.pressQuote: creating room for a quick cup, a long conversation, or anything in between

venues.name: Shibam Coffee
venues.description: Shibam Coffee opened on Lancaster Avenue in West Philadelphia on the first Friday of Ramadan in February 2026, the first Philadelphia site for a Yemeni chain that runs thirteen locations nationally. It trades until midnight on Friday and Saturday and ten every other night, and its Instagram bio states plainly that everything on the menu is halal. The drinks are the Yemeni canon done properly: jubani made with coffee and coffee-cherry husks served with cardamom, ginger and cinnamon; adeni, a Yemeni black tea with cardamom, nutmeg and milk; mofawar, coffee with cardamom and cream; the house Shibam coffee, a light roast with husks, cardamom, ginger, cinnamon and cream; and a Saudi coffee with cardamom and saffron. The Philadelphia Inquirer covered the opening.

venues.longDescription:
Shibam Coffee opened on Lancaster Avenue in West Philadelphia in February 2026, timed to the first Friday of Ramadan — a deliberate choice, since the hours a Yemeni coffeehouse keeps are built around the evenings when people are out after dark. It is the first Philadelphia location for a chain with thirteen sites nationally, in cities including Pittsburgh, Dearborn and Columbus, and it takes its name from Shibam, the walled Hadhramaut city famous for its mudbrick towers.

The Philadelphia Inquirer covered the opening and set out the menu, which is the standard Shibam list. Jubani is made with coffee and the husk of the coffee cherry, served with cardamom, ginger and cinnamon. Adeni is the Yemeni black tea, brewed with cardamom and nutmeg and finished with milk. Mofawar is coffee with cardamom and cream. The house Shibam coffee is a light-roast Yemeni bean brewed with the husks and spiced with cardamom, ginger and cinnamon, then given cream — the most complete expression of the style on the list. The Saudi coffee is lighter still, with cardamom and saffron, and pale gold rather than brown. For anyone who wants something sweeter there is a lotus latte built on Biscoff cookie butter, and a pistachio latte.

What makes this a going-out venue rather than a coffee stop is the clock and the room. It opens at six in the morning on weekdays and runs to ten at night, and on Friday and Saturday it stays open until midnight. The Inquirer described the opening weekend as a reflection of the city's love for a growing cafe culture that has created cherished cultural spaces for immigrant, Muslim and diasporic communities — which is to say these rooms are full at eleven at night, and full of people talking.

On alcohol, this is one of the few venues in this category where the position is stated by the venue rather than merely inferred: its own Instagram bio says everything on the menu is halal, and the menu carries no alcoholic item. No kava, kratom or other psychoactives are served — caffeine only.
venues.pressQuote: Customers can sip on Yemeni cafe staples like jubani, made with coffee and the husk of coffee cherries, served with cardamom, ginger, cinnamon.

venues.name: Shorty's GoodTimes Bar
venues.description: Shorty's GoodTimes Bar — until recently Shorty's Pins x Pints — is a 10,000 square foot "retro-tainment" bar at 353 North Shore Drive with a 5,000 square foot patio, opened in February 2022 in the old Tilted Kilt space across from Burgatory. The draw is the games: eight duckpin bowling lanes ($15 per person per hour before 4pm, $20 after), pinball, vintage arcade machines, shuffleboard, bocce, foosball, cornhole, bubble hockey and camp-style fire pits outside. NOTE: the taco menu it opened with is gone from this location — North Shore now serves American pub food (wings $14.50, smash burgers from $14, sammies from $14.50), and tacos survive only as a Tuesday special at the separate Waterfront site. Its non-alcoholic drinks are built on Seedlip and printed on the menu: the Fauxjito ($8), Espressno ($8), Don't Call Me Shirley ($7), the Mock-Arita in classic or strawberry ($6) and JayNO & Ginger ($6). All ages are welcome before 9pm; after 9pm on Friday and Saturday it is 21-and-over.

venues.longDescription:
Shorty's is a 10,000 square foot games bar at 353 North Shore Drive with another 5,000 square feet of patio, opened in February 2022 in a corner that had housed the Tilted Kilt and Calico Jack's before it, across the street from its sibling Burgatory. Its own team coined the term retro-tainment for what it does, and the COO was clear about the order of operations: the magnet is the gaming, and then the beverage and culinary programmes are what they really want to show off. The gaming is substantial — eight duckpin bowling lanes, pinball, vintage arcade machines, shuffleboard, bocce, foosball, cornhole, bubble hockey, golden tee, basketball hoops, board games and fire pits outside. Duckpin runs $15 per person per hour before 4pm and $20 after. When ESPN's First Take broadcast from Pittsburgh in January 2026, this is where it came from, to a packed crowd waving Terrible Towels. Two things to know before going: the taco menu it opened with is gone from this location, replaced by American pub food, and while all ages are welcome before 9pm, it becomes 21-and-over after 9pm on Friday and Saturday.

For a non-drinker this is one of the more genuinely useful rooms in Pittsburgh, because the whole premise is that the activity is the point rather than the drinking — which is the single hardest thing to find when everyone else is having a night out. The zero-proof drinks are printed on the menu, built on Seedlip, and priced below the cocktails: the Fauxjito at $8 on Seedlip Garden 108 with apple juice, elderflower, lime and muddled mint; the Espressno at $8 on Seedlip Spice 94 with cold brew and demerara; the Mock-Arita at $6 in classic or strawberry; JayNO & Ginger at $6 on Seedlip Spice with honey, ginger syrup and ginger ale; and a Don't Call Me Shirley at $7, house-made grenadine topped with Sprite, which is a proper Shirley Temple made properly. One caution if you are checking online: the Waterfront location in West Homestead runs different recipes and prices under a differently named section, so confirm you are reading the North Shore menu.
venues.pressQuote: A packed crowd waving Terrible Towels and wearing plenty of black and gold welcomed ESPN's "First Take" to Shorty's.

venues.name: SHOUT
venues.description: An 18+, fully alcohol-free dance club at 32 Exchange Place in downtown Salt Lake City, opened on May 24, 2024 for the under-21 and sober/sober-curious crowd. Founded by Roger Muir, it runs as a themed-event venue rather than a nightly bar: a real dancefloor with fog and laser-light shows, a game area, and a separate video-gaming lounge. The bar is zero-proof, pouring mocktails and dirty sodas — the first mocktail is complimentary at each event — so check the schedule before heading out.
venues.address: 32 Exchange Pl, Salt Lake City, UT 84111
venues.hours: Themed dance nights, typically 9pm-midnight; 18+ — check schedule
venues.longDescription:
Founder Roger Muir pitched SHOUT! as an antidote to a nightlife landscape with few alcohol-free options for younger and sober Salt Lakers, telling ABC4 that the only current options for creating new social relationships are in swiping apps or hopping bars.

Beyond the dancefloor, the venue features a game area with card games and cornhole and a separate video-gaming lounge with couches and big-screen TVs. The bar is entirely zero-proof — mocktails and dirty sodas, with the first mocktail complimentary — and events run under rotating themes, typically from 9 PM to midnight.
venues.pressQuote: The only current options for creating new social relationships are in swiping apps or hopping bars.

venues.name: Shuffles Board Game Café
venues.description: Shuffles is a board-game café in Tulsa's Brady Arts District with a library of games to play in and a bar that builds proper drinks, alcoholic or not. Its alcohol-free entry is The Muggle — zero-proof rum, lavender honey syrup, lemon juice, ginger syrup and bitters — a five-component build that behaves like a cocktail rather than a soft drink. For anyone who does not drink, a game café is a structurally better night out than a bar: the evening has a shape that is not the round, and nobody notices what is in your glass. Open Tuesday to Sunday, from 5pm midweek and noon at weekends, to midnight on Friday and Saturday.

venues.longDescription:
The hardest part of not drinking is rarely the drink. It is the four hours of an evening whose entire structure is other people's rounds, and the low-level work of being the one person doing something different. A board-game café dissolves that problem completely, which is why Shuffles is near the top of this guide despite being neither a bar nor a dedicated alcohol-free room.

Shuffles sits on Archer Street in the Brady Arts District — Tulsa's downtown arts quarter — with a substantial game library you play from at the table. The evening's shape is set by whatever you are playing, so nobody is counting rounds and nobody is waiting for anybody. That is a genuinely different social experience from a bar, and it is the one most often recommended by people in early sobriety.

The drinks are made properly too, which is not a given in the format. The Muggle is built on zero-proof rum with lavender honey syrup, lemon juice, ginger syrup and bitters — five components, two of them house syrups, one a named non-alcoholic spirit. Lavender and honey against ginger and lemon gives it both floral lift and heat, and the bitters supply the finish that keeps it from reading sweet. Tulsa Remote named it in its January 2025 ranking of the city's mocktails.

A note on the bitters, since this directory is asked about it regularly: cocktail bitters are alcohol-based and a dash contributes a trace amount. For most readers that is immaterial; for anyone abstaining completely it is worth asking the bar to leave them out, which does not damage this particular build.

Open Tuesday through Sunday — 5pm midweek, noon at weekends, midnight close on Friday and Saturday. Closed Monday.

Worth adding for anyone visiting rather than local: Shuffles charges a small table fee for game play alongside the drinks, which is normal for the format and is what funds the library. It also means the room does not depend on drink sales to make its money, and venues whose economics do not require you to keep ordering are, structurally, the most comfortable places in any city to spend a long evening without alcohol.

venues.name: Shy Bird
venues.description: The Fenway branch of Shy Bird occupies a corner of the Fenway Center development on Brookline Avenue, a short walk from Fenway Park, and keeps the longest hours of the three: 8am to 10pm every day of the week. The Boston Globe reviewed it in May 2025 and singled out the zero-proof list. Six named alcohol-free cocktails are printed beside the house cocktails at $10 to $14, running from Cloud Nine with coconut, lime and club soda to two Tilden-based drinks, the Lacewing and the Tandem, plus a Tea-groni built on Gnista wormwood with a non-alcoholic aperitif and black tea. The bar also pours Ghia Aperitif and Gnista Wormwood as straight zero-proof sipping spirits and stocks non-alcoholic Best Day Brewing.

venues.longDescription:
Shy Bird Fenway is the third and largest of Andrew Holden's rotisserie restaurants, at 201 Brookline Avenue in the Fenway Center development between Kenmore Square and the ballpark. It runs a single continuous service from 8am to 10pm daily, with breakfast on weekdays, brunch from 8am at weekends, lunch through the afternoon and dinner from 4pm, which makes it one of the more flexible places in a neighborhood otherwise organised around game times. Holden previously ran Eastern Standard in Kenmore Square, a few hundred metres away, and the Globe's May 2025 review made the connection explicit while praising the drinks list.

The zero-proof section is the group standard, printed on the same page as the house cocktails: Cloud Nine at $10 with coconut, lime and club soda; Side Eye at $10 with hibiscus, orange and grapefruit; Strawberry Fields at $10 with strawberry, rhubarb, lime and ginger beer; the Tea-groni at $13 built on Gnista wormwood, a non-alcoholic aperitif and black tea; and the two Tilden drinks at $14, the Lacewing with cucumber, basil, lychee and juniper berry and the Tandem with American oak, lapsang, tart cherry and bitter orange. The Fenway menu goes a step further than its siblings by printing a 'Zero-Proof Sipping Spirits' block, offering Ghia Aperitif neat at $12 for its herbaceous bitterness and Gnista Wormwood at $13.50 for something bitter, aromatic and floral with citrus peel, which is a rare thing to find listed anywhere in Boston. Ghia Le Spritz and non-alcoholic Best Day Brewing in hazy IPA or electro lime lager round out the packaged options. The Globe's review also noted a hemp-infused Aplos sipper on the list at the time of writing. Holden also runs Branch Line in Watertown and previously managed Eastern Standard in Kenmore Square. The Kendall Square and South Boston branches pour the same six zero-proof cocktails, but the Fenway card is the one that prints the sipping-spirits block, which is worth knowing if a straight pour is what you want.
venues.pressQuote: Shy Bird has a truly impressive array of zero-proof cocktails, including a hemp-infused Aplos sipper and non-alcoholic beers.

venues.name: Shy Bird
venues.description: Shy Bird is an all-day rotisserie restaurant in Kendall Square from Andrew Holden, formerly of Eastern Standard, serving breakfast through dinner seven days a week. Its beverage menu gives zero-proof drinks their own printed section of six named cocktails, priced $10 to $14 against $14 to $17 for the full-proof list. Cloud Nine is coconut, lime and club soda; Side Eye is hibiscus, orange and grapefruit; Tea-groni is built on Gnista wormwood with a non-alcoholic aperitif and black tea; Strawberry Fields uses strawberry, rhubarb, lime and ginger beer; and two drinks are built on Tilden, the Massachusetts non-alcoholic cocktail house, as the Lacewing and the Tandem. Gnista Wormwood is also poured as a sipping spirit, and packaged zero-proof options include Ghia Le Spritz and Best Day Brewing.

Tilden Tandem (american oak, lapsang, tart cherry, bitter orange)

venues.longDescription:
Shy Bird opened in Kendall Square at 390 Third Street as the first of three locations from Andrew Holden, who previously ran Eastern Standard in Kenmore Square and also operates Branch Line in Watertown. The format is all-day: breakfast from 8am on weekdays, lunch through the middle of the day, brunch at weekends and dinner until 9pm or 10pm, built around rotisserie chicken and a wood-fired kitchen. Because it turns over from a morning coffee stop into a dinner room, its bar has to answer for people who are not drinking at every hour, and the beverage menu is set up accordingly.

The printed 'Zero Proof Cocktails' section runs six drinks alongside the twelve house cocktails, not on a separate card. Cloud Nine is coconut, lime and club soda at $10; Side Eye is hibiscus, orange and grapefruit at $10; Strawberry Fields is strawberry, rhubarb, lime and ginger beer at $10; the Tea-groni is built with Gnista wormwood, a non-alcoholic aperitif and black tea at $13; and two drinks use Tilden, the Massachusetts non-alcoholic cocktail producer, as the Lacewing with cucumber, basil, lychee and juniper berry and the Tandem with American oak, lapsang, tart cherry and bitter orange, both $14. Gnista Wormwood is also available as a straight sipping pour at $13.50, and the packaged zero-proof list carries Ghia Le Spritz in rotating flavours and non-alcoholic Best Day Brewing in hazy IPA or electro lime lager. The Boston Globe used the Kendall Square Tilden Lacewing as one of its reference points in a March 2026 piece on the rise of high-priced zero-proof drinks in Boston; the drink has since moved up to $14 on the house menu. Holden opened Kendall Square first and has since added the South Boston and Fenway branches, all three carrying the identical zero-proof section, and he also runs Branch Line in Watertown. Breakfast, lunch, weekend brunch and dinner all draw on the same beverage menu.
venues.pressQuote: In Kendall Square, Shy Bird's Tilden Lacewing offers a taste of cucumber, basil, lychee, and juniper berry for $12.

venues.name: Shy Bird
venues.description: The South Boston branch of Shy Bird sits on Old Colony Avenue near Andrew Square and runs the same all-day format as the original: breakfast on weekdays from 9am, lunch, weekend brunch and dinner to 9pm or 10pm, built around rotisserie chicken. It carries the group's full zero-proof cocktail section, six named drinks listed on the same page as the house cocktails and priced $10 to $14. The list runs Cloud Nine with coconut, lime and club soda; Side Eye with hibiscus, orange and grapefruit; Strawberry Fields with strawberry, rhubarb, lime and ginger beer; a Tea-groni built on Gnista wormwood, a non-alcoholic aperitif and black tea; and two Tilden drinks, the Lacewing and the Tandem. Packaged options include Ghia Le Spritz and non-alcoholic Best Day Brewing.
