Tilden Tandem (american oak, lapsang, tart cherry, bitter orange)
Tea-groni (Gnista wormwood, n/a aperitif, black tea)
Strawberry Fields (strawberry, rhubarb, lime, ginger beer)
venues.longDescription:
Shy Bird's South Boston location opened at 12 Old Colony Avenue as the second of Andrew Holden's three restaurants under the name, following the Kendall Square original and preceding the Fenway branch. It is the closest thing the group has to a neighborhood room: Andrew Square and the surrounding blocks of South Boston are residential, and the restaurant's hours reflect that, opening at 9am on weekdays for breakfast, running lunch from 11am, adding weekend brunch from 10am, and serving dinner until 9pm Sunday through Wednesday and 10pm Thursday through Saturday. The cooking is the same wood-fired rotisserie programme as the other two.

The non-alcoholic offering is the group's standard and it is a real one. The beverage menu prints a 'Zero Proof Cocktails' block of six drinks directly beside the twelve house cocktails, at $10 to $14 against $14 to $17. Cloud Nine is coconut, lime and club soda; Side Eye is hibiscus, orange and grapefruit; Strawberry Fields is strawberry, rhubarb, lime and ginger beer; the Tea-groni is built with Gnista wormwood, a non-alcoholic aperitif and black tea; the Tilden Lacewing is cucumber, basil, lychee and juniper berry; and the Tilden Tandem is American oak, lapsang, tart cherry and bitter orange. Tilden is a Massachusetts producer, so two of the six are locally made rather than imported non-alcoholic spirits. The packaged zero-proof list carries Ghia Le Spritz in rotating flavours at $11 and non-alcoholic Best Day Brewing in hazy IPA or electro lime lager at $8. For a neighborhood short on alcohol-free options outside coffee shops, a restaurant with six named zero-proof cocktails and a rotisserie is a straightforward answer for a group where not everyone is drinking. All three Shy Bird rooms print the identical zero-proof section, so a drink found here will also be pouring in Kendall Square and the Fenway. Holden previously managed Eastern Standard in Kenmore Square and also runs Branch Line in Watertown, and the Boston Globe has covered the group's zero-proof list twice, in May 2025 and March 2026.

venues.name: The Sick Stag
venues.description: The Sick Stag in downtown Nampa keeps two named alcohol-free drinks — a Sparkling Citrus Cooler and a Mock Mule — on a list that runs late, to midnight on Friday and Saturday. Nampa sits about twenty miles west of Boise and is a substantial city in its own right, largely absent from the metro's drinks coverage, so a bar there with printed zero-proof options is doing something the downtown Boise venues cannot: serving the people who live at that end of the valley without a thirty-minute drive each way. Craft Lounge is a few minutes away in the same town, so Nampa has two options rather than one.
venues.longDescription:
The Sick Stag is on 1st Street South in downtown Nampa, about twenty miles west of Boise in the Treasure Valley. Nampa is not a suburb in the commuter sense — it is a city of around a hundred thousand people with its own downtown — but it is almost entirely absent from the region's food and drink coverage, which concentrates on Boise's 8th Street and Grove Street blocks.

That is the argument for this listing. Two named alcohol-free drinks, a Sparkling Citrus Cooler and a Mock Mule, are a modest programme by the standards of Red Feather or Art Haus. But they are available to somebody in Nampa on a Tuesday evening who does not want to drive an hour round trip to sit in a Boise cocktail bar, and that accessibility is worth more than an extra ingredient.

The Mock Mule is the more reliable order of the two. A Moscow Mule is defined by ginger beer and lime, with the vodka contributing very little flavour, which makes it one of a small handful of classics that lose almost nothing in a zero-proof version. Ordering one is close to a guarantee rather than a gamble — useful in a venue whose drinks are not documented in detail.

Hours run 4pm to 11pm most days and to midnight on Friday and Saturday, closed Mondays. Craft Lounge is a few minutes away in the same town, which gives Nampa two options rather than one — a small thing, but the difference between somewhere to go and somewhere to go if it happens to be open. For anyone living at the western end of the valley, those two bars are effectively the whole local scene.
venues.pressQuote: Sick Stag features a zero-proof menu designed for creativity and flavor
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: This Is Boise, The Boise Area's Best Non-Alcoholic Drinks and Mocktail Spots, January 2025

venues.name: Sidamo Coffee and Tea
venues.description: Sidamo Coffee and Tea is a fully alcohol-free Ethiopian coffee house at 417 H Street NE, opened in 2006 by Kenfe Bellay and his wife Yalemzwed Desta. Bellay, known on the corridor as the mayor of H Street, died in May 2022, and Desta has run it since. The shop roasts its beans on site two or three times a week and pours single-origin Ethiopian coffees rather than blends - the Sidamo it is named for, the fruitier Yirgacheffe and the full-bodied Harar - alongside a wide tea selection. Its best-known fixture is the traditional Ethiopian coffee ceremony held every Sunday at 2pm, a ritual it has now run several hundred times. There is free Wi-Fi and a back patio. No alcohol is served.
signatureDrinks: Sidamo single-origin Ethiopian coffee, roasted on site
Ethiopian and conventional loose-leaf tea selection
venues.longDescription:
Washington has the largest Ethiopian population of any American city, and Sidamo is one of the places where that shows up as a room rather than a statistic. Kenfe Bellay and his wife Yalemzwed Desta opened it at 417 H Street NE in 2006, well before the H Street Corridor became a nightlife strip, and Bellay became enough of a fixture that people called him the mayor of H Street. He died in May 2022; Desta has run the shop since, and the notice the family posted still sits on its homepage. His own account of the ambition was deliberately small - a typical neighbourhood coffee shop, and that was all he wanted it to be.

What it actually does is more particular than that. The coffees are single-origin rather than blends, and they are roasted on site two or three times a week, which is unusual for a cafe of this size. The three that anchor the list map onto Ethiopia's best-known growing regions: the Sidamo the shop is named after, the fruitier Yirgacheffe, and the Harar, which carries the full-bodied mocha character the region is known for. Alongside them sits a wide tea selection, and the room keeps free Wi-Fi and a back patio, which makes it a working cafe as much as a drop-in one.

The fixture worth planning around is the traditional Ethiopian coffee ceremony, held every Sunday at 2pm and run continuously since the shop opened - Washington City Paper marked its five hundredth. The ceremony is the full version: green beans roasted in front of you, ground by hand, brewed in a jebena and poured in three rounds, with incense burning throughout. It takes time on purpose, and it is one of the few things in the city that gives a Sunday afternoon a shape without involving a bar.

No alcohol is served at any hour. The practical limits are the hours - 7am to 6pm, seven days - which make this a daytime and early-evening venue rather than a night out, and the location, which is at the quieter Union Station end of H Street rather than in the middle of the bar strip. Union Station is a short walk, and the streetcar runs along H Street itself.
venues.pressQuote: This is a typical neighborhood coffee shop

venues.name: Sidebar at Surdyk's
venues.description: Sidebar is the bar and brasserie in the back corner of Surdyk's Liquor and Cheese Shop on East Hennepin, the long-standing Northeast Minneapolis wine and cheese institution. It opened in September 2020 with chef Randall Prudden and runs a wine list drawn from the shop next door. Its non-alcoholic section is a properly built one rather than a footnote: four zero-proof drinks including two house builds — The Purple One, on a blueberry-poblano shrub with ginger, lime and grapefruit, and Mango Is Life — plus a Strawberry Spark made with Three Spirit's Livener, and a packaged list running from Leitz Zero Point Five pinot noir to Best Day's hazy IPA.
signatureDrinks: The Purple One (blueberry-poblano shrub, ginger, lime, grapefruit)
Mango Is Life (mango, orange, lemon, grapefruit)
Strawberry Spark (Three Spirit Livener, strawberry shrub, lime, orange)
venues.longDescription:
Surdyk's has traded at 303 East Hennepin Avenue since the 1930s and is one of the reference points of Northeast Minneapolis: a liquor store, a cheese counter and a deli under one roof. Sidebar opened in September 2020 in the back corner of the building, a sixty-seat room with a thirty-four-seat patio, with Randall Prudden — previously at Spoon and Stable, and at Alinea and Next in Chicago — in the kitchen. Its defining trick is that any bottle from the shop can be carried in and opened for an $8 corkage fee, which makes it one of the better wine rooms in the city. That context is worth stating plainly, because it is an alcohol-forward business: this is a bar attached to a liquor store, not an alcohol-free space.

What lifts it onto this list is that the zero-proof section is designed rather than tolerated. Two of the four non-alcoholic cocktails are house builds at $7, cheaper than the full-strength list rather than priced as a novelty: The Purple One works a blueberry-poblano shrub against ginger, lime and grapefruit, using the poblano for a low green heat that keeps it from reading as fruit punch; Mango Is Life is a citrus-forward build on mango, orange, lemon and grapefruit. Above them sit two drinks using non-alcoholic products — the Strawberry Spark at $12, built on Three Spirit's Livener with strawberry shrub, lime and orange and carrying caffeine, and a $9 pour of St. Agrestis Phony Negroni. The packaged list is unusually broad for a restaurant bar and reflects the shop's buying: Leitz Zero Point Five pinot noir in cans, Woody's non-alcoholic sparkling rose, Proxies crisp dry cider, and Best Day Brewing's hazy IPA. Service runs evenings Tuesday through Thursday, all day Friday and Saturday, and a short Sunday brunch. For a non-drinker the useful detail is the price ladder: the two house zero-proof builds sit at $7, below the packaged non-alcoholic beers and well below the full-strength cocktails, which is an unusual direction for a bar to take and makes an evening here cheap rather than penalising. The room is small, so booking ahead is sensible at weekends.
venues.pressQuote: Craving a "girl dinner" and an Instagrammable mocktail? Head to the back corner of Surdyk's Liquor & Cheese Shop and you'll find Sidebar.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Meet Minneapolis, Best Mocktails in Minneapolis

venues.name: Sierra Nevada Brewing Co. Taproom
venues.description: Sierra Nevada's East Coast home is a destination brewery and taproom in Mills River, south of Asheville, and it is one of the few local taprooms that brews its own non-alcoholic beer: the Trail Pass line (Trail Pass IPA and Trail Pass Golden, 0.5% ABV), made with a special yeast that leaves the beer near-zero rather than removing alcohol afterward, plus Hop Splash hop water. The non-drinker gets a genuinely brewed NA pint in a proper brewery setting.
venues.address: 100 Sierra Nevada Way, Mills River, NC 28732
venues.longDescription:
Sierra Nevada's Mills River brewery sits at 100 Sierra Nevada Way, about twenty minutes south of Asheville near the airport, and it is the company's East Coast home — a working production brewery with a taproom, restaurant and grounds attached, built on a scale that makes it a destination rather than a stop. The site includes a lower park area beside the river that the brewery calls a hidden gem, described as a peaceful pocket of nature made for unwinding, with cold drinks, light snacks, yard games and hammocks under the trees. That lower park closed in 2020 during the pandemic and stayed shut for five years, reopening with a ribbon-cutting and live music on 7 June 2025 — a rare piece of good news in a region that spent that period rebuilding.

Sierra Nevada matters to non-drinkers more than almost any large American brewery, because it committed to the category early and properly rather than adding one product late. Trail Pass is its non-alcoholic line, brewed at 0.5% ABV in an IPA and a Golden, and the brewery describes the Golden as inviting you to grab a Trail Pass and start a new adventure with miles of flavour, exploring fruity aromas and smooth malt. Hop Splash is its hop water — no alcohol, no calories, and hopped for aroma rather than sweetened. Between them that is three distinct non-alcoholic formats from one brewer, which is why Trail Pass turns up on so many other venues' lists, including several in this guide. One honest caveat: the brewery's own website could not be read during our checks, so while these are Sierra Nevada's own products and the taproom pours its own range, we could not confirm from a primary source which of them are on at Mills River on a given day. Worth confirming before travelling if a specific one is the reason for the trip.
venues.pressQuote: The Sierra Nevada Brewing Company is set to officially reopen its 'hidden gem' for the first time in five years this weekend.

venues.name: Silver Moon Brewing
venues.description: Silver Moon is a downtown Bend brewery with a busy events calendar — trivia, live music, comedy — and it stocks Downshift, a zero-sugar sparkling drink infused with terpenes and a trace of hemp-derived THC, as its alcohol-free-evening option. A good room to be in without drinking, though the flagship non-alcoholic pour here contains THC rather than nothing at all.
venues.longDescription:
Silver Moon is one of Bend's older breweries, on Greenwood Avenue at the top of downtown, and it has built its identity around being a room where things happen — trivia nights, live music, comedy, a taproom that functions as a small venue as much as a bar. For anyone not drinking, that programming is the draw: there is a reason to be there beyond the drink in your hand, which is most of the battle on a Friday night.

The alcohol-free option it is known for is Downshift, a sparkling drink with no sugar and no alcohol, infused with terpenes — the aromatic compounds that give hops, citrus peel and pine their smell — and a trace of hemp-derived THC under the 0.3% federal threshold.

That needs saying plainly rather than glossing. Downshift contains THC. It is not alcohol and the quantity is small, but it is an intoxicant, and for a large share of the people this site is written for — anyone in recovery, anyone avoiding all mood-altering substances, anyone driving back over the Cascades — it is not an alcohol-free drink in the sense they mean. Order it knowing what it is. Silver Moon also pours ordinary soft drinks and the taproom's non-alcoholic options extend beyond it, so there is a route here that involves no active compounds at all.

This pattern is common across Bend and Oregon more broadly: hemp-derived THC and CBD drinks are widely treated as part of the zero-proof category by local venues and local press. Reading the label is more necessary here than in most cities.
venues.pressQuote: it's sparkling, infused with terpenes and a touch of hemp-derived thc (under 0.3%). zero sugar, zero booze, and built for unwinding

venues.name: Simpl Things
venues.description: Simpl Things is an all-day cocktail and snack bar in Toronto's Parkdale neighbourhood, with beverages curated by owner and beverage expert Evelyn Chick. Its printed drinks menu carries a dedicated "Zero Proof" section of five named, priced, fully ingredient-listed non-alcoholic cocktails, built on brands like Seedlip Grove 42 and Martini's Vibrante and Floreale vermouths. Foodism.ca named Simpl Things among Toronto's best mocktail and non-alcoholic drink menus, crediting Chick's zero-proof cocktails with a level of skill and innovation that's cemented her reputation as one of the city's most talented beverage experts.

After School Root Beer ($10) — NOA Orange Liqueur, simpl Rootbeer syrup, Maison Perrier
Power Lunch ($12) — NOA Garden Gin & Sweet Vermouth, carrot, Rice Orgeat, NA Prosecco
Feathered Dreams ($13) — Seedlip Grove 42, Martini Floreale, Meyer lemon, aloe juice
Fin Soda Aperitivo ($10) — Orange, Raspberries, Cane Sugar, Grapefruit (Made in Montreal)

venues.longDescription:
Simpl Things is an all-day cocktail and snack bar on Dunn Ave in Toronto's Parkdale (South Parkdale) neighbourhood, with beverages curated by owner and beverage expert Evelyn Chick of Evelyn Chick Projects. The bar runs a dual-daypart concept — Italian comfort food by day, modern Asian snacks by evening — alongside handcrafted cocktails and natural wine, including a daily 3–5pm happy hour with $12 house cocktails and a Sunday discount on natural wines. It describes itself as "a cozy but vibrant space" built on the idea that "the moments that deliver the most joy in life are often simpl," and it has been named a "One to Watch" bar in North America's 50 Best Bars and listed among Canada's 100 Best Bars in 2025.

The printed drinks menu carries a dedicated "Zero Proof" section — tagged "non-alcoholic delights packed with flavour" — alongside the Simpl Legacy cocktail list, flights, and the wine and beer lists. It runs to five named, priced, fully ingredient-listed builds: the Rebel Without a Pour ($13, NOA Garden Gin, Martini Vibrante, simpl grenadine, acidified grapefruit), the After School Root Beer ($10, NOA Orange Liqueur, simpl Rootbeer syrup, Maison Perrier), the Power Lunch ($12, NOA Garden Gin & Sweet Vermouth, carrot, rice orgeat, NA Prosecco), the Feathered Dreams ($13, Seedlip Grove 42, Martini Floreale, Meyer lemon, aloe juice), and a Fin Soda Aperitivo ($10) of orange, raspberries, cane sugar and grapefruit — a canned aperitivo spritz from Montreal producer Fin Soda.

That program earned Simpl Things a place on Foodism.ca's roundup of Toronto's best mocktail and non-alcoholic drink menus, which credited Chick's zero-proof cocktails with "a level of skill and innovation that's cemented her reputation as one of the city's most talented beverage experts" — singling out a non-alcoholic tonic build as "crisp as pine needles and fresh as a mountain exhale" and the Fin Soda spritz as a nod to classic Italian aperitivo.
venues.pressQuote: "You're never going to get a second-rate mocktail if Evelyn Chick is on duty. The owner of Simpl Things shakes up zero-proof cocktails at her cozy Parkdale bar and restaurant with a level of skill and innovation that's cemented her reputation as one of the city's most talented beverage experts. Whether it's a non-alc tonic that's 'crisp as pine needles and fresh as a mountain exhale,' or a spritz inspired by classic Italian aperitifs sourced from Montreal brand Fin Soda, you're bound to be impressed by the cocktail wizardry at this neighbourhood staple."
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Foodism.ca, "9 of the best mocktail and non-alcoholic drink menus in Toronto"

venues.name: Sip 305
venues.description: Sip 305 is an alcohol-free drinks shop on SW 109th Avenue in Sweetwater, beside Florida International University's main campus, and it keeps unusually late hours for a cafe in west Miami-Dade: 7:30am to midnight Sunday through Thursday and 7:30am to 1am on Friday and Saturday. The entire menu is beverages and dessert. Coffees are ordered by name rather than by size, and the house list runs to the Macklemore, the Caramelcita, the Tuscan Trifle, the Cinnabon and the S'more, alongside Sunshine Sodas, smoothies, milkshakes, a Cuban Coffee poured as a sweetened double shot, and a build-your-own Choyo Coffee. A second Sip 305 trades on North Kendall Drive.
venues.longDescription:
Sip 305 occupies a small storefront at 636 SW 109th Avenue in Sweetwater, the Miami-Dade municipality next to Florida International University's main campus, and it is built for the hours that campus keeps. The shop opens at 7:30am and does not close until midnight from Sunday through Thursday, or 1am on Friday and Saturday, which makes it one of the few places in west Miami-Dade where a group can sit down over a drink late at night without walking into a bar. The company's own site carries no alcohol anywhere on the menu; the offer is coffee, soda, matcha, smoothies, milkshakes and cookies, full stop.

The drinks are organised as named house builds rather than as a standard cafe list. The coffee section runs to the Macklemore (vanilla and creamer), the Caramelcita (caramel and creamer), the Caramel Bean (caramel, vanilla and creamer), the Tuscan Trifle (tiramisu and creamer), the Cinnabon (cinnamon, white chocolate and creamer), the Cookie Dough (cookie dough, white chocolate and creamer) and the S'more (marshmallow and hazelnut and creamer), plus a Chai Latte, a Matcha Latte, a straight Cuban Coffee served as a sweetened double shot, and a Choyo Coffee that lets a guest pick a coffee style, two flavours and a creamer. Beyond the coffees the menu is split into Sunshine Sodas, Red Bulls, milkshakes, smoothies and a Lite & Fresh section, and the kitchen turns out cookie sandwiches filled with Nutella or cookie dough. A second Sip 305 operates at 9605 N Kendall Drive in Kendall, open from 6am to midnight daily. No press coverage of the shop was found at a verifiable URL, so none is quoted here. The address itself sits inside the City of Sweetwater rather than unincorporated Miami-Dade, confirmed against the US Census geocoder rather than taken from the mailing address, which is why the neighbourhood is recorded here as Sweetwater and not Westchester. For a catalogue of Miami that is heavy on kava lounges and hotel bars, this is a different kind of entry: a plain, late-opening drinks counter next to a large university campus, where nobody is drinking and nobody is expected to.

venues.name: Sitti
venues.description: Sitti is a downtown Raleigh Lebanese restaurant on South Wilmington Street in the Warehouse District, and its drinks list carries a dedicated "Spirit-free Cocktails" section with all three builds at $5 — among the cheapest properly made non-alcoholic drinks in the city. The list draws on Lebanese drinking traditions rather than mimicking cocktails: pomegranate molasses with honey, lime, ginger ale and soda in the Pomegranate Spritz, the mint-infused lemonade Limon Nana, and a passionfruit-and-ginger Lebanese Iced Tea. For the wine-shaped experience there is Leitz Zero from the Rheingau — the sauvignon blanc by the glass at $12, a sparkling rosé by the bottle. Open every day from eleven in the morning, to ten on weeknights and eleven on Friday and Saturday, which makes it a rare kitchen-led venue usable at lunch and late.
signatureDrinks: Pomegranate Spritz ($5) — pomegranate molasses, honey, freshly squeezed limes, ginger ale, club soda, over ice
Limon Nana ($5) — fresh lemon juice, mint-infused simple syrup, water, over ice
Lebanese Iced Tea ($5) — passionfruit nectar, ginger-infused simple syrup, tea, over ice
Leitz Zero Sauvignon Blanc — non-alcoholic white, $12 glass / $46 bottle
Leitz Zero Sparkling Rosé — non-alcoholic sparkling rosé, $52 bottle
venues.longDescription:
Sitti has anchored South Wilmington Street in downtown Raleigh's Warehouse District for years, cooking Lebanese food named for the Arabic word for grandmother. Its non-alcoholic offering is unusual in this metro for two reasons: it is properly cheap, and it does not pretend to be anything it is not.

The drinks menu carries a section headed "Spirit-free Cocktails" with three builds, each at five dollars. None of them is an imitation of an alcoholic drink. The Pomegranate Spritz is built on pomegranate molasses — the thick, sour-sweet reduction central to Levantine cooking — cut with honey, fresh lime, ginger ale and club soda. Limon Nana is the Lebanese lemonade-with-mint that appears on tables across the region, made here with a mint-infused syrup rather than muddled leaves. The Lebanese Iced Tea combines passionfruit nectar and a ginger syrup with brewed tea. These are drinks from a drinking culture that has always had good non-alcoholic options, served at the price they should cost.

For anyone who does want the wine-shaped experience, the list carries Leitz Zero from the Rheingau in Germany — the sauvignon blanc by the glass at twelve dollars or the bottle at forty-six, and a sparkling rosé by the bottle. Leitz is among the more respected de-alcoholised producers, and having it available by the glass rather than only by the bottle is the detail that makes it usable on a weeknight.

The restaurant was recognised for its non-alcoholic beverages in a 2023 local awards round, which is a rare thing for a kitchen-led venue rather than a bar, and the spirit-free section has stayed on the menu since.
venues.pressQuote: Sitti Authentic Lebanese, in downtown Raleigh, honors those ancestors and carries on the Lebanese tradition of welcoming guests with delicious food and endless hospitality

venues.name: Sixty Vines
venues.description: Sixty Vines is Uptown Dallas's wine-on-tap restaurant with a documented zero-proof program: a "Mocktails + NA Wines" menu section carrying four dedicated NA cocktails by name — Daylight Spritz, Garden Spritz, The Bright Side, and Blackberry Sage & Soda — plus a rosé, white, and red non-alcoholic wine list from Oddbird and Missing Thorn, all available year-round alongside 60 wines on tap. The builds lean on real zero-proof components like Seedlip Garden 108, Oddbird's Presence white blend, Jack Rudy tonic syrup, and Fever-Tree mixers rather than juice and garnish, so the wine-focused format extends to non-drinking guests rather than stopping at a token mocktail.

The Bright Side (blood orange juice, Jack Rudy tonic syrup, lemon, Fever-Tree club soda)
Daylight Spritz (Oddbird Presence NA white blend, grapefruit, agave, mint, Fever-Tree club soda, rosemary)
Blackberry Sage & Soda (homemade blackberry syrup, muddled sage, lemon, Fever-Tree club soda)
Missing Thorn Sparkling Rosé (non-alcoholic, Napa Valley)

venues.longDescription:
Tucked inside the Crescent Court complex in Uptown Dallas, Sixty Vines is primarily known for its 60-tap sustainable wine system, but it has quietly built one of the more complete non-alcoholic programs in the neighborhood. The NA options aren't relegated to a single token mocktail—the menu includes four purpose-built zero-proof cocktails and a dedicated list of non-alcoholic wines in rosé, white, and red, making it a genuinely usable stop for sober and sober-curious diners who still want a thoughtful, restaurant-quality drink experience.

The Garden Spritz is the signature NA build: Seedlip Garden 108 combined with honey, lime, fresh mint, and Fever-Tree ginger ale—herbaceous and light without leaning sweet. The Bright Side goes in a citrus direction, using blood orange juice, Jack Rudy tonic syrup, lemon, and Fever-Tree club soda for something closer to a sophisticated aperitif. Newer additions round the list out to four: the Daylight Spritz stretches Oddbird's Presence NA white blend with grapefruit, agave, mint, rosemary, and Fever-Tree club soda, while the Blackberry Sage & Soda pairs homemade blackberry syrup with muddled sage, lemon, and club soda. On the wine side, Sixty Vines carries Missing Thorn's alcohol-removed Sparkling Rosé—a Napa-produced NA wine that has earned critical praise from The New York Times and Food & Wine—offering a genuine wine-adjacent experience rather than a grape juice substitute. CEO Jeff Carcara has publicly highlighted the venue's Dry January mocktail and NA wine program as a priority for guests exploring mindful drinking.

Sixty Vines is a loud, open-plan space—high ceilings, communal-friendly tables, and a patio with valet service (complimentary at lunch and brunch, $12 at dinner). The vibe skews business-casual and is popular for group dinners and weekend brunch, which runs Saturday and Sunday from 10am to 4pm. Reservations through OpenTable are strongly recommended, especially on weekends. It's a good fit for mixed groups where some guests are drinking wine and others want something thoughtful in a glass—the NA program holds up to that scenario without anyone feeling like an afterthought.
venues.pressQuote: Sixty Vines Wine bar is offering zero-proof cocktails including Bright Side...Garden Spritz with Seedlip Garden 108, honey, lime, mint, & Fever-Tree ginger ale; and Missing Thorn Sparkling Rose.

venues.name: Skof
venues.description: Skof is chef Tom Barnes' Michelin-starred restaurant (star awarded February 2025) in Manchester's NOMA district, and it treats non-alcoholic pairing as a real proposition rather than an afterthought. Alongside the wine flight, diners can choose a dedicated botanical-driven zero-proof pairing (around £40) built course by course from meticulously house-made juices - such as a celeriac and lemon-thyme serve. The drinks program was developed with London consultant Zoe Burgess of Atelier Pip, and the kitchen also worked with local Track Brewing on 'Sidney', a light low/no beer meant to open the meal. For a fine-dining room of this calibre, a genuine printed NA tasting pairing makes it a standout for alcohol-free diners.
venues.hours: Mon-Tue closed; Wed 6:30pm-8pm; Thu-Sat 12pm-1:30pm & 6:30pm-8pm; Sun closed
signatureDrinks: Celeriac and lemon-thyme juice (a house-made serve from the non-alcoholic tasting-menu pairing)
'Sidney' - a light low/no citrus-toned lager brewed with Track Brewing to open the meal
venues.longDescription:
Skof opened in May 2024 in the Grade II-listed Federation building in NOMA, the regeneration quarter at the northern edge of Manchester's city centre. It is the first solo restaurant from chef Tom Barnes, a Roux Scholar and long-time Simon Rogan lieutenant who was executive head chef at two-Michelin-starred L'Enclume in the Lake District. The 36-cover room earned a Michelin star in February 2025 and was named Best New Restaurant at the Good Food Guide Awards and Newcomer of the Year at the Manchester Food and Drink Awards, cementing it as one of the city's most acclaimed openings.

What makes Skof notable for alcohol-free guests is that the tasting menu can be matched with a fully non-alcoholic pairing rather than a wine flight. Priced at around £40, the botanical-driven pairing puts the kitchen's extensive collection of house-made juices centre stage, with combinations such as celeriac and lemon thyme singled out as highlights. Barnes has been candid that a full wine pairing is not for everyone, and the no-alcohol option is designed as a considered, course-by-course alternative - not a single token mocktail. The wider drinks list, developed with Zoe Burgess of London consultancy Atelier Pip, also leans on lower-alcohol builds, sour beers and fermented juices, and the team collaborated with Manchester's Track Brewing on 'Sidney', a light low/no citrus-toned lager intended to open the meal.

The setting is a former Edwardian drapery warehouse with high ceilings, exposed brick and steel beams, giving fine dining an unpretentious, distinctly Mancunian ease. Service runs lunch Thursday to Saturday and dinner Wednesday to Saturday; booking well ahead is essential given the small room and its profile.
venues.pressQuote: Matching their passion for flavour and the deep consideration for every element of their guest experience with my similar approach to drinks has meant a collaborative experience and a beautiful menu.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Zoe Burgess, founder of drinks consultancy Atelier Pip, on Skof's drinks program

venues.name: SKY Waikīkī
venues.description: SKY Waikīkī is a nineteenth-floor rooftop raw bar and lounge above Kalākaua Avenue, with an open-air deck looking across Waikīkī to Diamond Head. It keeps three named non-alcoholic cocktails as a standing part of the menu rather than as seasonal specials: Dawn Patrol, built on a pineapple jalapeño shrub with lemon juice and soda water; Hapai Happiness, made with yuzu syrup, lime, basil and soda water; and Over the Pali. The shrub in the Dawn Patrol is the notable technique — a vinegar-based fruit syrup that supplies the sharpness a zero-proof drink normally lacks. It runs to midnight on weeknights and 2am on Friday and Saturday.
signatureDrinks: Dawn Patrol (pineapple jalapeño shrub, lemon juice, soda water)
Hapai Happiness (yuzu syrup, lime, basil, soda water)
venues.longDescription:
SKY Waikīkī occupies the nineteenth floor at 2270 Kalākaua Avenue, with an open-air deck over the middle of Waikīkī and a view running along the beach to Diamond Head. It operates as a raw bar and lounge earlier in the evening and shifts towards nightlife later, with a bar list that has carried the same three non-alcoholic cocktails long enough for them to count as fixtures rather than specials.

The drinks are better built than a rooftop bar's reputation would suggest. Dawn Patrol is made on a pineapple jalapeño shrub — a shrub being a vinegar-based fruit syrup, a technique that predates refrigeration and is one of the few reliable ways to give a drink without alcohol the sharp, mouth-watering quality that carries a cocktail. Vinegar supplies acidity of a different character to citrus, rounder and more persistent, and the jalapeño adds capsaicin heat, so the drink finishes long and dry rather than sweet. Hapai Happiness works a similar problem from another angle, using yuzu syrup for a floral, more aromatic citrus than lemon or lime, cut with basil for a herbaceous top note. Over the Pali completes the three. Between them they cover sharp, aromatic and long, which is more range than most bars manage with a spirit in hand.

The hours matter as much as the drinks. Honolulu's alcohol-free venues almost all close by seven or eight in the evening — the kava rooms and cafés that make up most of this guide are daytime businesses — which leaves a genuine gap for a night out. SKY runs 4pm to midnight Sunday through Thursday and 4pm to 2am on Friday and Saturday, so along with Ground Level Lounge and Vintage Books it is one of the few places in the city where somebody who is not drinking can stay out as late as everyone else. Being a rooftop, it is also the rare Waikīkī room where the view rather than the bar is the reason to be there, which changes the social maths for a table that is not drinking.
venues.pressQuote: Listed on its menu under Driving Tonight or Surfing Tomorrow is not one but three nonalcoholic cocktails.

venues.name: Smitten Kitten Cat Cafe
venues.description: Smitten Kitten is Hamilton County's first cat café, opened in January 2023 on East 96th Street in Fishers by Holly Moss of Westfield, working with her son Collin Fields and investor Al Wilkie. It is fully alcohol-free. The 2,500-square-foot space splits into a conventional café serving coffee, tea and snacks and a separate lounge of adoptable cats, where sessions run around $9 for thirty minutes or $18 for an hour. Coffee comes from Noblesville roaster Noble Coffee & Tea Co., and the lounge is built around a nine-foot custom cat tree made by 900 North Studios. Cats are placed through the Hamilton County Humane Society. It was Indiana's sixth cat café and the second in the Indianapolis area.
venues.hours: Mon 10am-6pm; Tue closed; Wed-Fri 10am-6pm; Sat 10am-2pm; Sun 12pm-6pm
venues.longDescription:
Holly Moss signed a five-year lease on a 2,500-square-foot unit in a strip centre on East 96th Street in August 2022, told the Indianapolis Business Journal she would open at the beginning of December, and — as almost always happens with a build-out involving live animals and a health department — opened in January 2023 instead. Smitten Kitten was Hamilton County's first cat café, Indiana's sixth, and the second in the Indianapolis metro after Nine Lives in Fountain Square. Moss runs it with her son Collin Fields and an independent investor, Al Wilkie, and staffs it with a dozen or so part-timers across six days a week.

The layout is the standard two-room solution the health code requires and the better cat cafés make a virtue of: a proper café at the front serving espresso, tea and snacks, and a sealed lounge behind it where the cats live. Coffee is from Noble Coffee & Tea Co. in Noblesville, with almond and oat milk as standard, and the pastries come from local bakers. Lounge time is booked in blocks — roughly $9 for half an hour, $18 for a full one — and the centrepiece is a nine-foot cat tree built to order by 900 North Studios. Adoptions run through the Hamilton County Humane Society. For a guide like this one the relevant fact is simply that no alcohol is served here and none is implied: it is a suburban room where the social offer is coffee and company, in a county whose only fully alcohol-free bar, Memento Zero Proof in Fishers, shut in 2024 and has not been replaced. The hours are daytime, closing at 6pm most days and 2pm on Saturday, so it is a morning or afternoon proposition rather than a night out, and the café is shut on Tuesdays. It is also worth being clear about what it is and is not. This is a coffee shop with cats, not a zero-proof cocktail bar — there is no named non-alcoholic drink list, no de-alcoholised wine and no NA beer, and nobody is going to build you a spirit-free negroni. What it offers is the thing Hamilton County otherwise lacks: an unambiguously alcohol-free social room where the reason to be there is not the drink. For a zero-proof menu in the same county you are looking at the two Orangily shops for retail or a drive down to Mass Ave, and the nearest alcohol-free evening room is The Mood on Mundy Drive, eight minutes north.
venues.pressQuote: It's just to hopefully get some more kitties into nice homes.

venues.name: Sneak CLT
venues.description: Sneak CLT is an intimate "sneakeasy"-style cocktail lounge in Charlotte's Elizabeth neighborhood, blending cozy elegance with a hip-hop and R&B music program. The bar maintains a dedicated non-alcoholic cocktail section with four named mocktails — each built with premium NA spirits including Lyre's and Seedlip — priced on par with their full-proof counterparts at $15 each. It is a standout option for sober-curious guests seeking a full cocktail-bar experience without alcohol.
venues.address: 2001 East 7th Street, Suite F, Charlotte, NC 28204

Slinking to Sicily (Lyre's Pink Gin, Lyre's Italian Spritz, orange rosemary syrup, lemon, club soda, NA sparkling wine) $15
Sneaky Link (Lyre's Blanco, Seedlip Agave, Lyre's Orange Sec, spicy oleo) $15
Midnight Bramble (lime, pineapple, blackberry, simple syrup, mint) $15

naMenuItems.name: Slinking to Sicily

naMenuItems.name: Cabernet Sauvignon
naMenuItems.description: ariel vineyards 2021 san jose, ca

venues.longDescription:
Sneak CLT is tucked at the back of the Pecan Point shopping centre at East 7th Street and Pecan Avenue in Elizabeth, next door to the long-standing Bang Bang Burgers, and co-owner Jamil Whitlow has a precise word for what it is. We're not a speakeasy, he told Queen City Nerve, we're a sneakeasy — a speakeasy is historically a hard place to find, and if you do find it you have to know someone who knows somebody to get there. The distinction is the point: Sneak is hidden but not gatekept. Whitlow is a spirits-industry veteran with more than a decade behind him, and what started as a deli-bar concept became a high-energy lounge with a hip-hop and R&B music programme. The room balances soft, vibrant wall treatments and gold accents against brown leather and moody lighting, and the kitchen keeps bar bites — fresh focaccia, a snack mix, D'Artagnan caviar. It opens at 5pm daily except Mondays, running to 2am Thursday through Saturday, with reservations through Resy.

The non-alcoholic cocktails are priced at $15, the same as much of the full-proof list, and three of the four are built on real zero-proof spirits rather than juice. Green Thumb uses Seedlip Garden with cucumber, honey, mint, lime and egg white — herbal and textured rather than sweet. Slinking to Sicily is the most elaborate, layering Lyre's Pink Gin and Lyre's Italian Spritz with an orange rosemary syrup, lemon, club soda and a non-alcoholic sparkling wine, so it drinks like a proper aperitivo. Sneaky Link combines Lyre's Blanco, Seedlip Agave and Lyre's Orange Sec with a spicy oleo, which is about as close to a full margarita build as a zero-proof drink gets. Midnight Bramble is the one made from scratch ingredients alone — lime, pineapple, blackberry, simple syrup and mint. Ordering one here does not mark you out: the same bartenders make them, at the same price, from the same station.
venues.pressQuote: Sneak CLT "clearly respects non-alcoholic options, too — a thoughtful touch for designated drivers or anyone avoiding spirits."

venues.name: Sneaky Pickle
venues.description: Sneaky Pickle is a vegetable-forward Bywater restaurant founded by Ben Tabor, a Marine Corps veteran, who opened the original on St. Claude Avenue in 2014. After a fire and a stint of pop-ups, it relocated into the long-idle former Maurepas Foods space at 3200 Burgundy Street, where it now runs two concepts under one roof: Sneaky Pickle serves a locally sourced, vegan- and vegetarian-friendly lunch, and after dark the same kitchen and bar become Bar Brine for dinner. Both emphasize produce from small local farms. For non-drinkers, the daytime menu includes a fresh sugarcane-juice cooler with ginger, mint, and lemon topped with club soda, and the evening Bar Brine program — built on house-made cordials, shrubs, and bitters — extends to named zero-proof options like the Seasonal Bitter, Summer Buck, and Shrub 'N' Soda.
venues.longDescription:
Sneaky Pickle is at 3200 Burgundy Street in the Bywater — worth confirming, because published guides still print two older St Claude Avenue addresses for it. Ben Tabor opened the original in 2014 and has been blunt about what he was doing: he used to say it was where vegetarians go to die, and that he offers one meat option on a menu that is otherwise entirely vegan and ninety-nine per cent local and made from scratch. His reasoning was never doctrinal — it is not that he thinks meat is evil, as some do, but that for health reasons he thinks less than twenty per cent of our diets should come from it. After a fire and a run of pop-ups, the restaurant moved into the long-idle former Maurepas Foods space, where two concepts now share one kitchen: Sneaky Pickle serves lunch Thursday to Monday, and every night from 5pm the same room becomes Bar Brine for dinner. Reservations open three weeks ahead.

Where Y'at's description is the accurate one: two businesses sharing one space, both committed to sourcing their food from small, locally operated farms. That sourcing is what makes the drinks worth a non-drinker's attention, because Bar Brine's bar runs on house-made cordials, shrubs and bitters rather than bought-in syrups — the same preserving instinct the name points at. The zero-proof drinks confirmed on the current list are the Seasonal Bitter, the Summer Buck and the Shrub 'N' Soda. A shrub is a drinking vinegar, fruit preserved in sugar and vinegar, and it is the single most useful thing a scratch bar can make for people who are not drinking, because the acidity gives a soft drink the sharp edge that alcohol normally supplies. A buck is the ginger-and-citrus format, dry rather than sweet. One practical limitation: the restaurant publishes its menus only as photographs, so ingredients and prices cannot be read online and the list rotates seasonally. A fourth drink documented in earlier coverage, a sugarcane juice cooler, could not be confirmed as current. Go, but ask at the bar rather than planning from the website.
venues.pressQuote: Located in New Orleans' Bywater neighborhood, Sneaky Pickle and Bar Brine are two businesses that share one space and both are committed to sourcing their food from small, locally-operated farms.

venues.name: Snug
venues.description: Snug is a 600-square-foot Irish pub in Irvington that opened on 2 January 2024 in a former hair salon, taking its name from the small private room in a traditional Irish bar. Jim Arnoldt runs it with Carey Shea and Timothy Barrett, and the shelves hold more than ninety Irish whiskeys, which is the most serious collection of its kind in Indiana. What earns it a place here is that the alcohol-free side is treated as part of the offer rather than a concession — the bar makes a seasonal alcohol-free punch and keeps non-alcoholic options alongside the whiskey and the Guinness. The room seats very few people, so it fills quickly on a Friday.
venues.longDescription:
A snug, in a traditional Irish pub, is the small partitioned room off the main bar — historically where women, clergy and anyone wanting a private drink sat. Jim Arnoldt named his Irvington bar for it, and then built something that genuinely is one: 600 square feet at 210 South Audubon Road, in a unit that was previously a neighbourhood hair salon, opened on 2 January 2024 with Carey Shea and Timothy Barrett as co-owners. The Indianapolis Business Journal called it Irvington's cozy castle of Irish whiskey, and the whiskey is the specialism — more than ninety Irish bottlings on display, alongside Guinness and Kilkenny on tap and Irish soda bread from the kitchen.

A bar that specialised in whiskey to that degree could reasonably have ignored the non-drinking customer, and Snug has not. Local coverage lists it as a place with a real alcohol-free offer alongside the whiskey — a seasonal alcohol-free punch made in-house, plus non-alcoholic options kept on the back bar rather than fetched from a fridge on request. The scale of the room is part of why that works: with this few seats the bartender is talking to everyone, and ordering a non-alcoholic drink here is a conversation rather than a transaction.

It is worth being clear about what this is and is not. Snug is a whiskey bar, the whole premise is a spirits collection, and the alcohol-free list is one punch and a handful of options rather than a printed zero-proof menu of the sort you get at Ball & Biscuit or The Inferno Room. If you are looking for a room where alcohol is not the point, this is the wrong entry. If what you want is to sit with friends who are drinking whiskey in a warm, small, genuinely convivial neighbourhood pub and have something decent in your own glass, Snug does that better than most, and Irvington — a historic east-side district with its own high street — is worth the trip out. Opens at 3pm on weekdays, midday on Saturday and 11am on Sunday, when it closes at 8pm.
venues.pressQuote: Irish whiskey is represented in more than 90 bottles of different brands displayed at Snug.

venues.name: SoBar at Alchemy Coffee
venues.description: SoBar is Richmond's alcohol-free speakeasy — a Friday and Saturday night concept that takes over Alchemy Coffee on West Broad Street after the espresso machines go quiet, with low lights, live music and a full craft cocktail list containing no alcohol at all. Operator Bobby Kruger built it as a real bar rather than a cafe staying open late: the drinks are named and composed, running from Something Blue, a blueberry-ginger mule, through the Not So Dirty Chai Martini, Cielito en Fuego, Lucid Sunset Spritz, Banana Bird and the High Priestess, plus a non-alcoholic dirty martini. With KavaClub now closed, it is the city's only regular alcohol-free night out.
venues.longDescription:
SoBar is what happens when a coffee shop decides the evening deserves the same care as the morning. From Friday and Saturday at 7pm, Alchemy Coffee's West Broad Street room changes character — the lights drop, live music starts, and the counter turns out a list of craft cocktails that contain no alcohol whatsoever. It runs until midnight. The rest of the week the same address trades as The Lab by Alchemy Coffee, a daytime cafe closing at 3pm, so the two identities barely overlap.

The distinction that matters for a non-drinker is between a venue that will make you something soft and a venue built for you. SoBar is the second kind. The drinks are named, composed and specific: Something Blue is a blueberry-ginger mule; the Not So Dirty Chai Martini borrows the savoury-spiced logic of the original; Cielito en Fuego, Lucid Sunset Spritz, Banana Bird and the High Priestess round out the list, and there is a non-alcoholic dirty martini for anyone who misses the ritual more than the ethanol. That is a cocktail menu, not a mocktail section.

Its importance to Richmond has grown for an unhappy reason. KavaClub, the West Main Street venue local press called the only alcohol-free bar in Virginia, closed in 2026, and Ceremony's Richmond bottle shop shut and moved to Norfolk. SoBar is now the city's only regular alcohol-free night out — a genuine bar atmosphere, with music, where nothing behind the counter contains alcohol.

The coffee-shop-by-day, bar-by-night model is worth noting as a pattern, because it may be how alcohol-free venues survive. A dedicated dry bar has to carry a full lease on evening trade alone, which is precisely the maths that closed KavaClub. Sharing premises with a daytime business removes that pressure: the rent is already paid by the espresso machine, and the evening only has to cover itself. The venues using this structure are the ones still standing.

Operator Bobby Kruger has talked about extending the concept to future Alchemy locations and exploring non-alcoholic wine production at Brambly Park. For now the practical advice is simple: it is two nights a week, 7pm to midnight, and worth planning around rather than dropping into. Anyone arriving during the day will find the cafe — The Lab by Alchemy Coffee, closing at 3pm — and not the bar.
venues.pressQuote: An alcohol-free speakeasy featuring craft zero-proof cocktails and live music, operating within Alchemy Coffee on Friday and Saturday nights.

venues.name: Sober Bar
venues.description: Sober Bar is a fully zero-proof bar and specialty coffee spot in downtown Gulfport — every drink on the menu is 100% alcohol-free. Opened in June 2026 after a run as a Tampa Bay pop-up, it's a New Orleans speakeasy-inspired room that pulls espresso, matcha, and kava-coffee drinks by day and pours craft zero-proof cocktails — Call Me an Ube, Red Widow, Linn & Juniper, Bee's Bouquet — on alcohol-alternative spirits by night, with NA beer and wine on hand. Owners Sean Hawthorne and Collin Horton built the room dark and moody rather than bright and wellness-adjacent, which is a deliberate signal about who it is for. Open 7am to 10pm midweek and to 1am at weekends — a genuinely rare thing for an alcohol-free venue.

venues.longDescription:
Sober Bar opened on Beach Boulevard South in downtown Gulfport in June 2026, after a period running as a Tampa Bay pop-up — a sequence worth noting, because it means the concept was tested against real customers before anyone signed a lease. Owners Sean Hawthorne and Collin Horton renovated the space into a moody room modelled on a New Orleans speakeasy, which is a deliberate rejection of how alcohol-free venues usually look. The default for the category is bright, clean and wellness-adjacent; a dark speakeasy says the customer is out for the evening rather than in recovery from one.

Every drink in the building is alcohol-free. The day trade is specialty coffee — espresso, matcha, kava-coffee builds — and the evening is craft zero-proof cocktails made on alcohol-alternative spirits, with names that would not look out of place on a full-strength list: Call Me an Ube, Red Widow, Linn & Juniper, Bee's Bouquet. Non-alcoholic beer and wine are stocked for anyone who wants the simpler thing, drawing on Ritual, The Free Spirits Company, Athletic, Guinness 0.0 and Heineken 0.0.

The hours are what make it function as a genuine third place rather than a novelty: 7am to 10pm Sunday through Thursday and 7am to 1am on Friday and Saturday. That span covers the morning coffee run, the afternoon work session and the Saturday night — the last of which is the hardest slot to fill without alcohol and the one almost every alcohol-free venue gives up on.

Gulfport itself is a small waterfront town southwest of St. Petersburg with an arts-district character, so this is a destination rather than somewhere to stumble into. Worth the drive: fully alcohol-free rooms that keep late weekend hours are rare anywhere, and this is the best-equipped one in Tampa Bay.
venues.pressQuote: With the name Sober Bar, we want it to elicit some curiosity with our customers because the words "sober" and "bar" seem like two conflating ideas.

venues.name: Soberish
venues.description: Soberish is an alcohol-free bottle shop and wellness boutique in Atlanta's Kirkwood neighborhood, founded in August 2023 by real estate attorney and entrepreneur Mehrnush Saadat. Built around the idea that "sober" means something different to everyone, the shop curates a predominantly women-owned selection of non-alcoholic spirits, de-alcoholized wines, aperitifs, and zero-proof beer alongside cannabis and CBD wellness products, barware, and gifts. Saadat personally vets ingredients for natural, low-sugar quality, and the store leans heavily on education, hosting weekly Saturday tastings so guests can sample before buying. Confirmed brands on the shelves include St. Agrestis (Phony Negroni), Lyre's, De Soi, Figlia, and Best Day Brewing. After celebrating its first anniversary in 2024, Soberish expanded with a second location at Serenbe in Chattahoochee Hills.
venues.address: 1963 Hosea L Williams Dr SE, Suite R103, Atlanta, GA 30317
venues.longDescription:
Soberish opened in August 2023 in Kirkwood, at 1963 Hosea L. Williams Drive, founded by Mehrnush Saadat — a real estate attorney who came to the business from outside hospitality. The premise is in the name: sober means something different to everyone, and the shop is built for the whole range rather than for one definition of it. Its own description is a destination for holistic wellness, blending education and inspiration in a warm, welcoming atmosphere.

The buying is unusually opinionated. Saadat vets ingredients personally, favouring natural and low-sugar formulations, and the selection skews deliberately toward women-owned producers — a curation decision rather than a marketing one, and rare enough in this category to be worth noting. The shelves span non-alcoholic spirits and aperitifs, de-alcoholized wine, zero-proof beer, and ready-to-drink cans, with St. Agrestis, Lyre's, De Soi, Figlia, Best Day Brewing, Renude and Nowadays among the confirmed names. Barware and gifts round it out.

Education is the operating model rather than an add-on. Weekly Saturday tastings let customers try before buying, which in a category where a bottle can run past thirty dollars and taste like nothing anyone wants is the difference between a repeat customer and a one-off. The shop passed its first anniversary in 2024 and opened a second location at Serenbe in Chattahoochee Hills, which remains listed.

One thing to know going in: alongside the non-alcoholic drinks, Soberish stocks hemp-derived THC products and functional mushroom items. Those are psychoactive and are a different proposition from a zero-proof aperitif, however adjacent the shelving. For anyone whose sobriety excludes all intoxicants — which is most people in formal recovery — the two categories need separating, and the staff are equipped to do it if asked. Saadat has said publicly that health and wellness sit at the front of what the shop does, and that is the frame to hold it to.
venues.pressQuote: I, especially as the founder, take health and wellness at the forefront of what we do, so I vet the ingredients to make sure that all the products we carry are as natural as possible.

venues.name: Sobr Market (Danforth)
venues.description: Sobr Market's Danforth location is a fully alcohol-free bottle shop in Toronto's Danforth Village, just east of Coxwell Avenue and outside the Greektown strip proper. It's a franchise of the Sobr Market chain — which also runs Toronto stores at The Well and Summerhill — opened in 2025 and run by owner Jenn. Every product on the shelves is zero-proof: non-alcoholic wine, beer, spirits and ready-to-drink cocktails, curated into vegan, organic, gluten-free, kosher and halal selections.

venues.longDescription:
Sobr Market's Danforth outpost is a fully alcohol-free bottle shop on Danforth Avenue in Toronto's east end, sitting just past Coxwell Avenue in Danforth Village — technically east of the Greektown strip that runs roughly between Broadview and Greenwood, though the shop is sometimes grouped in with that stretch. It's one of three Toronto-area Sobr Market locations, alongside the chain's stores at The Well and Summerhill, and unlike a licensed retailer with a small non-alcoholic shelf, the entire inventory here is zero-proof — there is no alcohol sold anywhere in the store.

The Danforth store is a franchise of the Sobr Market chain, opened in 2025 and run by owner Jenn. It's open daily from 11am to 8pm, with online ordering available through the location's own portal for local delivery or in-store pickup.

The shelves cover the full range of non-alcoholic categories: wines in red, rosé, white and sparkling styles; beers spanning IPAs, lagers, stouts, sours, and wheat and Belgian styles; and spirit alternatives standing in for gin, rum, whiskey and tequila, including bottles from Free Spirits. Beyond those core categories, the store stocks ready-to-drink cocktails, seltzers and functional beverages, plus curated collections for vegan, organic, gluten-free, kosher and halal shoppers — enough range to build a full boozeless bar cart from one visit.

venues.name: Society
venues.description: Society is Chris Lucas's ambitious fine diner on level two of the 80 Collins precinct, and its bar backs the food with a concise, sommelier-designed mocktail list built around native Australian ingredients. Time Out Melbourne singles it out as somewhere non-drinkers keep the full upscale experience, pointing to zero-proof builds that lean on strawberry gum, royal gala apple and leatherwood honey. It's a bespoke, kitchen-driven program rather than a can list, so the alcohol-free options sit alongside the bespoke martinis and vintage-spirit cocktails on equal footing. Time Out describes a concise but thoughtful mocktail list celebrating native Australian ingredients — strawberry gum, royal gala apple and leatherwood honey among them.
signatureDrinks: Native-ingredient mocktail list — built on strawberry gum, royal gala apple and leatherwood honey
venues.longDescription:
Society opened in the 80 Collins tower from restaurateur Chris Lucas (Chin Chin, Kisume, Yakimono) alongside chef Martin Benn and Vicki Wild of Sydney's acclaimed Sepia. Reached via the lifts on Benson Walk, it spreads across a grand dining room set beneath crystal chandeliers, a smoky mirror-ceilinged lounge bar, and adjoining spaces designed by local architects Russell & George in a blend of art deco, mid-century and brutalist detail. Broadsheet describes the room as one where jackets are taken at the door and service is "immaculate" - fine dining pitched at the top of Melbourne's CBD.

The bar is where the non-alcoholic offering lives. Time Out Melbourne's guide to drinking in Melbourne when you're not drinking highlights Society for a "concise yet thoughtful mocktail list" that celebrates native Australian ingredients - strawberry gum, royal gala apples and leatherwood honey among them. These are made-to-order builds designed with the same rigour as the venue's cocktail and wine lists rather than a bought-in zero-proof range, so the emphasis is on seasonal, house-composed drinks.

That context matters at Society: this is an a la carte fine diner where cocktails run from around A$26 up past A$145 for vintage-spirit pours, and the alcohol-free list gives non-drinking guests a genuine seat at that table rather than a soft-drink afterthought. The mocktails change with what the kitchen and bar are working with, so the native-ingredient theme is the constant rather than a fixed set of named drinks.

Society trades from the level-two space at 80 Collins Street, with the dining room open evenings through the week and daytime service later in the week; the precinct also houses the associated Lillian Brasserie and the Lounge Bar under the same roof.

The alcohol-free list is built from the same native pantry as the kitchen, which is why it reads as part of the restaurant rather than an accommodation. Time Out notes that Society's drinks are sommelier-designed and that a concise yet thoughtful mocktail list celebrates native Australian ingredients — strawberry gum, royal gala apples and leatherwood honey among them.

Those are not decorative choices. Strawberry gum is intensely aromatic and does the work perfume normally gets from spirit; leatherwood honey is resinous and slightly bitter, which is the quality that stops a zero-proof drink collapsing into sweetness. Used together they produce something with length, which is the property most mocktails lack and the reason people stop after one. In a room this size — plush, expensive and designed to be photographed — a short list executed properly is also more reliable than a long one, because every drink on it gets made often enough for the staff to make it well.
venues.pressQuote: A concise yet thoughtful mocktail list celebrates beautiful native Aussie ingredients like strawberry gum, royal gala apples, leatherwood honey and more.

venues.name: SODO Kava
venues.description: A fully alcohol-free lounge in Orlando's SoDo neighborhood pouring botanical teas, kava, kombucha, and house mocktails in a cozy, art-filled pool-hall setting. It draws a mixed daytime remote-work and late-night crowd looking for a bar-style hang without the alcohol. (Alcohol-free, though its kava and kratom drinks are mildly psychoactive botanicals, not strictly substance-free.)

venues.longDescription:
SODO Kava sits at 227 E Michigan St, Unit B, in Orlando's SoDo neighborhood, describing itself as a place to 'unwind and connect with an open-minded, authentic alcohol-free community.' The drink menu runs from botanical teas and kombucha blends to house mocktails like K's Hard Seltzer, Just Peachy, Humble Horchata, Island Palmer, Hades' Hex, Tropical Getaway, and Cacao Mama, served in a cozy room with a pool table and a wall of local art that's all for sale.

Worth being upfront about: SODO Kava is alcohol-free, but not substance-free. Alongside its teas and mocktails, the menu includes kava and kratom extracts - both legal, mildly psychoactive botanicals with their own effects - so it's best described as a spirits-free social space rather than a fully sober one.

Central Florida Lifestyle's 2026 Dry January mocktail guide singled out SODO Kava as 'a cornerstone of Orlando's sober-curious scene,' noting its drinks are 'layered and flavorful, often incorporating cacao, adaptogens, fresh juices, and herbal notes.' That range shows up on the full menu too, which stretches beyond the core kava and tea program into golden milk, matcha, and superfood add-ins like moringa, turmeric, and ashwagandha.

The Orlando location is open daily from noon until late (until 1am Friday and Saturday), with a sister location in Longwood that runs 24 hours, giving the metro's non-drinkers a genuine after-hours alternative to a conventional bar.
venues.pressQuote: A fully alcohol-free lounge that's become a cornerstone of Orlando's sober-curious scene.
