venues.longDescription:
Switchback has been part of Burlington's South End since 2002, brewing an unfiltered amber ale that became a Vermont standard, and it is employee-owned. Its place in this guide comes from a decision announced on 6 January 2026: the brewery installed a BrewVo de-alcoholisation system from Sustainable Beverage Technologies to bring non-alcoholic production entirely in-house.

The move followed the early success of Switchback N.A., which the brewery describes as having quickly proved to be more than a limited or experimental release. Rather than continue contracting the work out, it bought the equipment — and the investment goes further than its own label. With BrewVo installed in Vermont, Switchback now serves as the East Coast production location for BrewVo-manufactured products, brewing alcohol-free beer on behalf of other breweries and beverage brands that want it made properly and made close to home. That is an unusual level of commitment for a brewery of this size, and it means Burlington now has non-alcoholic brewing infrastructure rather than just non-alcoholic beers on a shelf.

BrewVo works differently from the thermal and membrane methods most de-alcoholised beers use: it is a multi-stage fermentation process designed to build flavour and body first and keep the alcohol from ever accumulating, which tends to avoid the thin, worty character that dogs cheaper NA beer.

For a visitor, the tap room on Flynn Avenue is a plain, comfortable brewery bar a few doors from Citizen Cider, and the Flynn Avenue corner of the South End is easily the densest concentration of alcohol-free options in the state — Switchback, Citizen Cider's Clean Mayor and Zero Gravity's Rescue Club all within a short walk. Open noon to 9pm Wednesday through Sunday, from 5pm on Tuesday, closed Monday.

Vice president and plant engineer Gretchen Langfeldt framed the reasoning in a way worth repeating, because it is the argument this whole category has been waiting for a production brewery to make: non-alcoholic beer is still beer, and it demands the same care, experience and respect for process. She also named the real bottleneck — that there is genuine demand in the category but not enough production capacity that prioritises quality — which is precisely why a mid-sized Vermont brewery buying this equipment matters beyond its own taproom.
venues.pressQuote: The beer is immediately recognizable. People don't experience Switchback N.A. as a substitute. They recognize it as the beer they already know.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Bill Cherry, President and Brewmaster, Switchback Brewing Co.

venues.name: Syndicate Kava Bar
venues.description: Syndicate Kava Bar is a fully alcohol-free kava and kratom bar in Miami's Wynwood Arts District, founded by Joyci Borovsky and Joey Roberts. Built "for the community of locals by those same locals," it runs like genuine nightlife rather than a wellness cafe: open until 3am daily, with a rotating events calendar that includes Tuesday open-mic nights, Thursday comedy, and a Saturday cabaret show. The bar pours brewed Fijian kava and kratom by the glass or growler, plus green/red/gold teas on tap and a roster of house-made kava and kratom mocktails. Signature pours include the Slutty Nectar (kava lemonade with watermelon, mint, lime, agave), Bitches Brew (a kava mojito), the Skinny Bitch, and Dasha's Kava Milkshake. A second Syndicate location operates in South Beach. Every drink is zero-proof — the venue serves no alcohol.
venues.longDescription:
Syndicate Kava Bar sits in the Wynwood Arts District and was founded by Joyci Borovsky and Joey Roberts on a stated principle: built for the community of locals by those same locals. What separates it from most alcohol-free venues is that it behaves like nightlife rather than like a wellness cafe. It runs until 3am daily, and the calendar is programmed rather than incidental — Tuesday open mics, Thursday comedy, a Saturday cabaret.

That programming is the substance of the argument. The hardest part of not drinking is rarely the drink; it is that the entire social architecture of a night out is organised around bars, and most sober alternatives close at nine and offer nothing to do. A room with a cabaret on Saturday and a 3am closing time competes with Wynwood on its own terms rather than offering an early, quieter substitute for it.

The pours are brewed Fijian kava and kratom, served by the glass or the growler, with green, red and gold teas on tap and a roster of house-built kava and kratom mocktails. The named drinks carry the same irreverence as the room — Slutty Nectar, a kava lemonade with watermelon, mint, lime and agave; Bitches Brew, a kava mojito; the Skinny Bitch; Dasha's Kava Milkshake. A second Syndicate operates in South Beach.

The caveat that belongs on every kava listing applies here and should not be softened: kava is psychoactive and sedating, with documented case reports of liver injury, and kratom acts on opioid receptors and carries real dependence and withdrawal risk. Everything served is free of alcohol. That is a narrower claim than nothing served having an effect, and for anyone whose reason for avoiding alcohol is recovery from a substance-use disorder, the difference is the whole question.
venues.pressQuote: Founders Joyci Borovsky and Joey Roberts fell in love with plant-based alternatives and the community that spawned over them as long as two decades ago

venues.name: Taano House
venues.description: Taano House is a non-alcoholic trailer bar parked at 1109 E. 6th Street in Austin's East Sixth entertainment district, with late evening hours that have changed more than once since it opened, so check its channels before going. Opened August 15, 2024 by University of Texas professor Geoff Smith and Joe Wes — co-founders of Austin-based Taano Elevated Beverages — the bar offers an unusual take on non-alcoholic drinking. Rather than focusing on traditional mocktails, Taano builds drinks around legal psychoactive plants like kava, kanna, blue lotus, and Amanita muscaria, aiming to deliver the relaxation and euphoria of social drinking through botanicals rather than alcohol. The cocktail menu was developed with Shaun Meglen, a mixologist and product education director for beverage distributor Southern Glazer's. Standout drinks include the Egyptian Mule (built on blue lotus and Amethyst's cucumber-ginger-serrano NA spirit), the Molly Martini (kanna with Lyre's NA coffee liqueur), and a 'mushroom wine' pairing Amanita muscaria with Oddbird NA wine. Visitors in recovery or anyone with substance sensitivities should note that the menu emphasizes psychoactive botanicals — this is a non-alcoholic experience, not necessarily a fully sober one.
signatureDrinks: Egyptian Mule (blue lotus, Amethyst NA spirit, ginger beer, lime, simple syrup)
Molly Martini (kanna, espresso, Lyre's NA coffee liqueur, Lyre's NA white rum syrup, vanilla)
Real Green Tea Shot (kanna, green tea, lemon, peach syrup, green spirulina)
Mushroom Wine (Amanita muscaria with Oddbird NA wine)
venues.longDescription:
Taano House is a non-alcoholic trailer bar parked at 1109 East 6th Street, in the middle of the East Sixth entertainment district, with late evening hours that have changed more than once since it opened — check its channels before going. It opened on 15 August 2024 from University of Texas professor Geoff Smith and Joe Wes, co-founders of Taano Elevated Beverages, with a menu developed by Shaun Meglen, a mixologist and product education director at Southern Glazer's. Its stated aim, in the founders' words to the Austin Chronicle, was to create drinks that promote relaxation, euphoria and sociability the same way alcohol does, but without its negative health effects.

That sentence is the whole proposition, and it needs reading carefully, because Taano House is not a mocktail bar. The drinks are built on legal psychoactive plants: kava, kanna, blue lotus and Amanita muscaria, the fly agaric mushroom. The Egyptian Mule combines blue lotus with Amethyst's cucumber-ginger-serrano non-alcoholic spirit, ginger beer and lime. The Molly Martini puts kanna with espresso and Lyre's non-alcoholic coffee liqueur. The Real Green Tea Shot is kanna with green tea, lemon, peach and spirulina. There is a mushroom wine pairing Amanita muscaria with Oddbird non-alcoholic wine.

This site exists in large part for people in recovery, so the distinction has to be stated flatly rather than implied. Taano House is alcohol-free. It is not substance-free, and it is not sober in the sense most recovery programmes use the word. Kava is a sedative; kanna is a mood-altering plant; blue lotus is mildly psychoactive; Amanita muscaria is a genuinely psychoactive mushroom whose active compounds are not the same as psilocybin but are intoxicating nonetheless. These are being served deliberately, as the point of the bar, not incidentally.

For someone who has stopped drinking but is not avoiding all intoxicants, that may be exactly what they are looking for, and the bar is upfront about what it does. For anyone whose sobriety means abstaining from mood-altering substances entirely, this is a venue to walk past — and knowing that in advance is more useful than a recommendation.
venues.pressQuote: We wanted to create drinks that promote relaxation, euphoria, and sociability the same way alcohol does, but without its negative health effects.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Geoff Smith and Joe Wes, co-founders

venues.name: Table Wine
venues.description: Table Wine is a neighbourhood wine shop on Atwood Avenue in Schenk-Atwood, and it carries what is generally reckoned the deepest non-alcoholic wine and spirits selection in the Madison metro — a distinction it inherited when Sober Social, the state's only dedicated all-NA shop, closed its Middleton storefront in February 2026. For anyone building a home bar rather than going out, that makes it the practical option: de-alcoholised wines, zero-proof spirits and aperitifs shelved alongside a serious conventional list, with staff who taste the range. It opens at noon daily and runs to 9pm Tuesday through Saturday, which is later than most bottle shops in this guide manage.
venues.longDescription:
Atwood Avenue is the spine of Schenk-Atwood, one of Madison's most self-contained east-side neighbourhoods, and Table Wine has been its wine shop for years — a small, well-curated room of the sort that survives on staff knowledge rather than shelf space. Its inclusion here is about a specific and growing part of that shelf: the non-alcoholic wine and spirits range, which Madison Eats Food Tours describes as extensive and which is, as far as we can establish, the deepest selection in the metro.

That was not always true, and the change is worth explaining. Until February 2026 Wisconsin also had a dedicated all-NA shop — Sober Social in Middleton, which carried more than a hundred non-alcoholic products and nothing else — and when its storefront closed, Table Wine was left with the deepest range anywhere around Madison. What a generalist offers is different in kind from what the specialist did. You can buy the de-alcoholised bottle and the regular bottle in one visit, which is how most mixed households actually shop, and the staff can tell you which non-alcoholic wine drinks closest to the Sancerre you already like because they sell both. For a couple where one person has stopped drinking and the other has not, that is often more useful than a specialist trip across the isthmus.

Practically, the hours are unusually good for a bottle shop: noon to 9pm Tuesday through Saturday, noon to 8pm Monday and noon to 6pm on Sunday, so you can call in after work rather than racing a 6pm close. Schenk-Atwood makes an easy pairing — the Herbiery's hop-free taproom is on Winnebago Street nearby, and Rooted In Sanity, the metro's only fully alcohol-free room, is a short ride west along Williamson Street. A shop, a brewery doing something genuinely strange and a kava lounge, all within a couple of miles, is a good afternoon.
venues.pressQuote: Table Wine in the Atwood neighborhood features an extensive NA wine and spirits selection.

venues.name: Taiyo Sun
venues.description: Taiyo Sun is a tiny, light-filled Japanese kissaten-style cafe run by Tats Kawabata on St Georges Road in Fitzroy North. It is alcohol-free by nature: the drinks list is built around whisked matcha — among the more talked-about in Melbourne — alongside a genuine curated tea menu (lapsang souchong, grapefruit green, sakuranbo cherry and blossoming jasmine flower) and Wide Open Road coffee with St David's Dairy milk. It is a quiet daytime cafe stop rather than a go-out-for-a-drink destination, but the matcha and tea program is real and well made.
venues.address: 394 St Georges Road, Fitzroy North VIC 3068
signatureDrinks: Matcha — whisked Japanese matcha (also served as a topping over homemade azuki red-bean toast)
venues.longDescription:
Behind an unassuming door at the base of a St Georges Road apartment block, Taiyo Sun is a tiny, light-filled Japanese cafe from Tats Kawabata. It trades in the spirit of a Japanese kissaten — a neighbourhood coffee-and-tea room — serving around ten light, Japanese-leaning breakfast and lunch dishes built on thick-cut white shokupan toast from Brioche by Philip, with toppings such as homemade azuki (sweetened red bean) and matcha powder, black-honeyed sesame paste, and hard-boiled egg with Japanese mayonnaise and melted cheese, plus vegetable curry with a cheesy toasted croissant.

The cafe is naturally alcohol-free, and its non-alcoholic offering is genuine rather than incidental. Matcha is the anchor — whisked to order and also dusted over the azuki toast — and has earned Taiyo Sun a reputation as one of Melbourne's better matcha stops. Beyond it sits a considered loose-leaf tea list including lapsang souchong, grapefruit green, cherry-flavoured sakuranbo and a blossoming jasmine flower tea, with espresso coffee from Wide Open Road roasters and milk from St David's Dairy.

The room is small and pared-back — only a handful of tables — so this reads as a calm, food-focused daytime cafe rather than a social drinking venue. For a sober visitor it is a reliable, well-sourced place to sit with a properly made matcha or pot of tea. As of mid-2026 it remains open and trading for daytime service.

venues.name: Taj A Sweet Cafe
venues.description: Taj A Sweet Cafe opened on Westheimer Road in Greater Uptown in September 2025 and keeps the most consistent late hours of any alcohol-free room in Houston: seven in the morning to midnight, every single night, with no weekday drop-off. It is a Levantine and Turkish sweets house rather than a Yemeni coffeehouse proper, though it serves Yemeni tea — the Adani, available by the cup or in a shared pot. The rest of the list runs to Turkish coffee, pistachio and Spanish lattes, a house soothing tea, and dessert-led drinks including the Biscoff Cloud and Tiramisu Dream. The published menu spans hot and cold drinks, oriental sweets, crepes and chocolates, and contains no alcoholic item anywhere on it.
signatureDrinks: Tea Pot (Adani Tea) — $21, brewed for the table
venues.longDescription:
Taj A Sweet Cafe opened on Westheimer Road in September 2025, and the reason it belongs on this list is the clock. It trades from seven in the morning until midnight, seven nights a week, with no shorter weeknight hours — the most consistent late closing of any alcohol-free venue in Houston. Most places that stay open past eleven do it only on Fridays and Saturdays. This one does it on a Tuesday.

It is worth being accurate about the category. This is a Levantine and Turkish sweets house rather than a Yemeni coffeehouse, and it should not be confused with the Yemeni rooms elsewhere in the city even though it shares their hours and their alcohol-free character. What it does share is the Adani tea — the spiced Yemeni black tea — offered both as a $5.95 cup and as a $21 pot brewed for a table to share. The pot is the tell: this is a room that expects groups to sit for a long time, and it prices for it.

Around the tea sits Turkish coffee prepared traditionally, a pistachio latte, a Spanish latte, and a house soothing tea. The dessert-led drinks are the other half of the business and are made without apology — the Biscoff Cloud and the Tiramisu Dream are closer to a dessert course than to a beverage, and the Taj Avocado sits in the same territory. That matters for the alcohol-free crowd more than it might seem: the thing most often missing from an evening without drinking is the final course that gives the night a shape, and a sweets house open until midnight supplies exactly that.

The published menu is unusually complete for verification purposes — hot drinks, cold drinks, oriental sweets, Turkish plates, savoury items, cakes, crepes and chocolates — and there is no alcoholic item anywhere in it. The Texas licence register holds no permit under the trade name. The evidence is therefore about as strong as it gets short of the venue saying the words itself, and it is recorded here as evidence rather than as a venue claim. The Houston Chronicle noted the opening in its October 2025 new-restaurants round-up.

venues.name: Takibi
venues.description: Takibi (Japanese for "bonfire") is a wood-fired Japanese restaurant and izakaya inside the U.S. headquarters of outdoor-lifestyle brand Snow Peak, in Portland's NW/Alphabet District, in a room built by Skylab Architecture around reclaimed century-old Douglas fir beams. By day it runs a ramen-focused lunch on long-simmered broths and snow-aged noodles; by night it serves wood-fired plates, sushi, sashimi, tempura and a rotating omakase with a vegan version alongside it, plus one of Portland's deepest sake lists, sourced from Niigata. The bar keeps a named non-alcoholic section of four drinks at $10–$13, built on real zero-proof bases rather than juice: Natsu Gori (Dr. Zero Zero amaro shaved ice, watermelon, lime, sweetened condensed milk), Swizzle Me This (Ghia, peach shrub, mint, salted lime soda), Early Bird (Seedlip, lemon, coconut cream, poppyseed, demerara, nutmeg) and Chura-Sun (Wilderton Earthen, caramelised pineapple, lime, demerara), with non-alcoholic beer at $6. Named an Esquire Top 25 US bar and a Portland Monthly Top 50 restaurant in 2022. The restaurant closed temporarily during 2024 and reopened that October.

Swizzle Me This (Ghia, peach shrub, mint, salt & lime soda) $12

Chura-Sun (Wilderton Earthen, caramelised pineapple, lime, demerara) $10
venues.longDescription:
Takibi — the word means bonfire in Japanese — is a wood-fired Japanese restaurant at 2275 NW Flanders Street in the Northwest District, built inside the United States headquarters of Snow Peak, the Japanese outdoor-lifestyle brand with more than sixty years of heritage behind it. The room was designed by Skylab Architecture around traditional Japanese timber framing and century-old Douglas fir beams reclaimed from a Portland-area warehouse, with dark wood floors, an open kitchen, a bar and patio seating arranged around fire pits. The restaurant closed temporarily during 2024 and Snow Peak announced its return that October, welcoming the community back with a relaunched kitchen; ramen is now led by Yoshimitsu Seki, who comes from Niigata prefecture, the birthplace of Snow Peak. By day Takibi runs a ramen lunch built on long-simmered broths and snow-aged noodles, and by night it becomes a chef-driven dining room of wood-fired plates, sushi, sashimi, tempura and a rotating omakase with a vegan version alongside it. It has been named to Esquire's top 25 bars in the United States and Portland Monthly's top 50 restaurants, both in 2022.

The bar keeps one of the city's deepest sake selections, sourced from Niigata, and gives non-alcoholic drinks their own menu section headed simply "N/A". All four are built with the same seasonal logic as the kitchen. Natsu Gori ($13) is a shaved-ice drink using Dr. Zero Zero amaro with watermelon, lime and a drizzle of sweetened condensed milk. Swizzle Me This ($12) combines Ghia with peach shrub, mint and a salted lime soda. Early Bird ($11) uses Seedlip with lemon, coconut cream, poppyseed, demerara and nutmeg. Chura-Sun ($10) is Wilderton Earthen with caramelised pineapple, lime and demerara. A non-alcoholic beer is listed at $6, though the menu does not name the brand. Travel Oregon, surveying the city for non-drinkers in November 2022, wrote that earthy zero-proof drinks are the perfect complement to the restaurant's Japanese-inspired, season-centred fare. Takibi serves Wednesday through Monday and closes Tuesdays, with lunch from 11.30am and the last dinner seating at 8.30pm; reservations run through Resy.

venues.name: Tall Order
venues.description: Tall Order is a New American bar and restaurant at 70 Beacon Street in East Somerville, opened in March 2025 by Daren Swisher and Joe Cammarata, who also run Daiquiris and Daisies in Boston. It occupies the former Thirsty Scholar Pub, a fixture near the Somerville-Cambridge line for close to thirty years before it closed in 2024. The drinks menu is deliberately split into full-strength, low-ABV and a section headed No Alcohol, so the alcohol-free options sit on the same page and at comparable prices rather than being relegated. Three named zero-proof cocktails are listed at $12.36 each, backed by non-alcoholic beer, non-alcoholic sparkling rose, a canned zero-proof negroni, hop water and fountain soda.

Blue Shroom (Oddbird N/A sparkling rose, blueberry, cardamom, mushroom)
Bitter Bali (Lucano and Giffard N/A bitter, pineapple, Gracenote cold brew)

venues.longDescription:
Tall Order opened in March 2025 at 70 Beacon Street, taking over the Thirsty Scholar Pub, which had traded on the site for nearly three decades before closing in 2024. The new operators are Daren Swisher and Joe Cammarata, who also own Daiquiris and Daisies on High Street in Boston. Boston Magazine reported the succession on August 22, 2024, framing Tall Order as a deliberately welcoming cocktail bar replacing the old pub, BostonChefs noted the opening in March 2025, and the Boston Globe reviewed it on May 29, 2025 under a headline about finding a bar for every taste. The bar's own reasoning about its alcohol-free offering has been made explicit in the press: in WBUR's April 30, 2026 report on Boston restaurants and no-alcohol cocktails, the position given was that in the current consumer climate a bar needs a substantial focus on lower-alcohol and no-alcohol cocktails.

That shows up in the structure of the menu itself, which is divided into full-strength drinks, a low-ABV section and a block headed No Alcohol rather than burying alcohol-free options at the foot of the page. The three named zero-proof cocktails are all priced at $12.36. Blue Shroom is built on Oddbird non-alcoholic sparkling rose with blueberry, cardamom and mushroom; 1,2,3,4 combines Earl Grey and verjus with vanilla, a mango foam and tajin; and Bitter Bali uses Lucano and Giffard non-alcoholic bitters with pineapple and Gracenote cold brew, Gracenote being a Berkshires-founded roaster with a Boston presence. A further block headed More NA Offerings carries Rescue Club non-alcoholic pilsner and IPA at $7.21, Oddbird non-alcoholic sparkling rose at $10.30, the St. Agrestis Phony Negroni at $11.33, Lagunitas hop water at $6.18, Saratoga sparkling or still at $10.30 and Maine Root fountain soda at $5.15. The kitchen runs a New American menu alongside, and the bar trades late: 5pm to 1am Sunday through Thursday and 5pm to 2am on Friday and Saturday.
venues.pressQuote: In the current kind of consumer climate in this day and age you need to have a substantial focus on lower-alcohol and no-alcohol cocktails.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Daren Swisher, co-owner of Tall Order

venues.name: Talula's Garden
venues.description: Talula's Garden looks onto Washington Square from the east side of the park, and is best known for a cheese programme that runs to a dedicated cave and a farm-driven seasonal menu. Its non-alcoholic offering is short but well made: The Perfectionist at $13 combines DHOS bittersweet aperitif with Töst alcohol-free sparkling, citrus, lavender and rosemary — an aperitif-style build with real bitterness and two herbs that place it alongside the kitchen's cooking rather than against it. Athletic Brewing's Run Wild IPA is $8. One house drink is a modest list, but the composition is serious and the setting is one of the more pleasant places in the city to spend a long evening.

Athletic Brewing Run Wild IPA ($8) — non-alcoholic

venues.longDescription:
Talula's Garden sits on the east side of Washington Square, with a courtyard that is one of the better outdoor rooms in central Philadelphia. The restaurant is farm-driven and seasonal, and its reputation rests substantially on cheese — there is a dedicated cave and a cheese list treated with the seriousness most restaurants reserve for wine.

That context matters for the single house non-alcoholic drink, because The Perfectionist is built as an aperitif rather than as a soft drink. It combines DHOS bittersweet aperitif — an alcohol-free Italian-style bitter — with Töst, a de-alcoholised sparkling made from white tea, white cranberry and ginger, then adds citrus, lavender and rosemary. Two things are worth pulling out. The first is the bitterness: an aperitivo's whole function is to stimulate appetite through bitter compounds, and a build that starts from a bittersweet base is doing the same physiological job as a Campari spritz rather than merely resembling one. The second is the herbs. Lavender and rosemary are both kitchen herbs here, not garnish, and using them in the glass ties the drink to a menu that leans hard on the same garden.

It pairs unusually well with the cheese programme, which is the practical reason to order it. Cheese needs acid and effervescence against fat; that is why sparkling wine works so well with it, and why still juice does not. A dry alcohol-free sparkling with a bitter backbone covers the same ground.

Athletic Brewing's Run Wild IPA at eight dollars is the other non-alcoholic option.

Honesty about the size of the list: one house drink and one beer is modest, and a group of non-drinkers will exhaust it quickly. What the restaurant offers instead is the setting and the meal — a courtyard, a long seasonal menu, cheese service that takes time, and evening hours running to ten every night with a Sunday brunch. For an occasion dinner where the point is the table rather than the bar, that is a reasonable trade.

venues.name: Tandem Coffee + Bakery
venues.description: Tandem Coffee + Bakery occupies a converted 1960s filling station on Congress Street in the West End and is the most loved cafe in Portland — nationally written-up, permanently busy, and entirely alcohol-free. Will and Kathleen Pratt roast their own coffee and the bakery turns out biscuits and pastries that draw a queue most mornings. It is a daytime room in the strictest sense, open 8am to 1pm and not a minute later, but within those hours it is the easiest place in the city to meet someone over a drink that was never going to involve alcohol in the first place.
venues.longDescription:
Tandem Coffee + Bakery is housed in a converted mid-century filling station on Congress Street in Portland's West End, and it is the cafe that comes up first whenever anyone writes about the city. Will and Kathleen Pratt roast the coffee themselves; the bakery, run alongside, turns out biscuits, pastries and cakes that account for most of the queue.

It earns a place in an alcohol-free guide for the simplest possible reason: it is a genuinely excellent place to drink something, and there is no alcohol involved at any point. That sounds trivial and is not. A large part of what a non-drinker actually wants is not a clever substitute for a cocktail but somewhere good to sit with a good drink, where the question never arises. Cafes of this quality do that better than any mocktail menu, because nothing about the transaction is a substitution.

The honest limitation is the clock. It opens at 8am and closes at 1pm, every day, and it does not bend. That is a bakery's schedule, not a bar's, and it means Tandem covers the morning and the very early afternoon and nothing else. Portland has a real evening problem for non-drinkers — Lava Kava is essentially the only room in the city keeping bar hours without alcohol — and no amount of good coffee at nine in the morning helps at nine at night.

Within its hours, though, it is a straightforward recommendation, and it sits in a walkable part of the West End near Bramhall and the Arts District. The company also runs a second location on Anderson Street with its own roastery, listed separately in this guide, which opens even earlier at 7am. Between the two of them, Tandem covers the whole morning across two different neighbourhoods.
venues.pressQuote: The Loaded Biscuits at Tandem — with jam and butter or pimento cheese — are legendary
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Portland Press Herald, The best bakeries and cafes in Greater Portland, March 2026

venues.name: Tandem Coffee Roasters
venues.description: The Anderson Street location is where Tandem actually roasts, in East Bayside among the breweries and distilleries that fill that end of Portland — which makes it a useful address to know. It opens at 7am and closes at 1pm, entirely alcohol-free, and it sits within a few minutes of several taprooms, so it works as the sober half of a morning in a neighbourhood otherwise organised around drinking. The coffee is the same carefully roasted product as the Congress Street bakery, in a plainer, more industrial room built around the roastery itself. It opens an hour earlier than the Congress Street bakery and closes on Sundays, so check the day before making the trip.
venues.longDescription:
Tandem's Anderson Street site in East Bayside is the working half of the business — the roastery, with a cafe attached. The room is plainer than the Congress Street bakery: concrete, sacks of green coffee, the roaster itself visible and often running. For anyone who cares how coffee is made rather than only how it tastes, it is the more interesting of the two.

The location is what earns it a separate listing. East Bayside is Portland's brewing district — Rising Tide, Austin Street, Lone Pine and a cluster of distilleries and cideries sit within a few blocks. It is a genuinely enjoyable neighbourhood to spend an afternoon in and a difficult one to spend it in sober, because almost every door leads to a taproom. Having a proper coffee roaster in the middle of it, alcohol-free by definition, gives a non-drinker somewhere to be that is not simply the corner of someone else's brewery.

The coffee is the same product as the West End bakery — Tandem roasts everything here — served without the pastry programme that draws the queues across town. Hours run 7am to 1pm Monday through Saturday, closed Sunday, so it opens an hour earlier than the bakery and shuts at the same time.

The same honest caveat applies as to any Portland cafe: this covers mornings, and Portland's real gap for non-drinkers is the evening. But if you are staying in East Bayside, or working through a day in the brewery district with people who are drinking, a well-run roastery a few doors down is a more useful thing to know about than another bar that will make you a lime and soda. It is also one of the few places in East Bayside where you can sit for an hour without anyone assuming you are between taprooms.
venues.pressQuote: They're distinguishing themselves by the atmosphere in the cozy East Bayside roastery and coffee shop

venues.name: Tartine Bistro
venues.description: Tartine Bistro occupies a small house on Old Detroit Road in Rocky River, the lakefront suburb ten miles west of downtown, and has been the west side's reference French bistro for years — croissants and quiche at the front of the day, steak frites and the rest of the canon at dinner, and a Sunday brunch that fills the room. Service runs from midday Tuesday through Saturday, which makes it one of the few kitchens on this list open across a long afternoon rather than only from 4pm. Its non-alcoholic drinks are seasonal composed builds at $13, the same territory as the cocktails: a Petit Autumn of cider, vanilla, maple, ginger and cayenne finished with apple butter and a bruléed apple, and a Mon Petit Coeur built on alcohol-removed red wine with cider, cinnamon and maple.
