venues.longDescription:
The Daily Kitchen & Bar is a Richmond Restaurant Group restaurant in the Greengate Shopping Center on West Broad Street in Short Pump, in Henrico County. The group opened it in 2017 as the second Daily. The first, on West Cary Street in Carytown, closed in September 2026 after 13 years; the group owns that building and plans a new concept there. Short Pump is now the one place to find it.

It earns its place in this guide with a short but real mocktail list, printed on the same drinks menu as the cocktails. There are six: the Cucumber Cooler (basil, cucumber, lemongrass, coconut water and soda), the Passionfruit Lime Soda (mint, lime, passionfruit and soda), a Strawberry Limeade (strawberries, lime and soda), the Coco-Mo (mint, lime, coconut water and soda), the Shrub Club, a rotating daily shrub with club soda, and Blue Ridge Bucha ginger kombucha from Virginia. There are two non-alcoholic beers on the bottle and can list as well: Athletic Brewing, either the Hazy IPA or the Golden Ale, and Stella Liberte 0.0%.

None of this makes it a destination bar. It is a full-service restaurant where someone who is not drinking can order a drink that was made for them, at lunch, brunch or dinner, without asking for anything off the menu. All of the other Richmond rooms in this guide are in the city itself, most of them in Carytown, Scott's Addition and along Broad Street, so this is the listing to know on the west side of the metro.

Practical notes: lunch runs from 11am on weekdays, brunch from 10:30am on Saturday and Sunday, and dinner from 4pm to 9pm every day. There is a patio, open when the weather allows.

venues.name: The Dandelion
venues.description: The Dandelion is a British-style pub off Rittenhouse Square, part of the Starr Restaurants group, done in the full country-pub register — snugs, patterned wallpaper, fish and chips, a Sunday roast. Its non-alcoholic provision is bottled rather than mixed, but it is honestly labelled on the printed beer list: Athletic Brewing's Upside Dawn golden ale at $7, marked non-alcoholic, and St. Agrestis's Phony Negroni. That is a shorter answer than a cocktail bar would give, and we grade it accordingly. What it offers instead is a proper pub that serves food all day and stays open to midnight on Friday and Saturday, where nursing a non-alcoholic pint attracts no attention whatsoever.
signatureDrinks: Athletic Brewing Upside Dawn ($7) — non-alcoholic golden ale, Stratford CT
St. Agrestis Phony Negroni — alcohol-free bottled aperitif
venues.longDescription:
The Dandelion occupies a corner of South 18th Street a block from Rittenhouse Square, and it is a Starr Restaurants take on the English country pub — several small rooms rather than one, patterned wallpaper, fireplaces, a menu running to fish and chips, shepherd's pie and a Sunday roast. It is a convincing version of the thing, and it is busy from lunch onwards.

The non-alcoholic offer is straightforward and it would be wrong to oversell it. There are no house-made spirit-free cocktails. What there is sits on the printed beer list, clearly labelled: Athletic Brewing's Upside Dawn golden ale at seven dollars, marked non-alcoholic, and St. Agrestis's Phony Negroni, the bottled alcohol-free bitter aperitif. Two options, both bought in rather than built.

We grade that a three rather than a four, and the reason is worth stating: a strong rating in this directory means a bar has done work — a named section, drinks constructed to order, an alcohol-free spirit used as a base. Stocking two good bottles is a lower bar than that, however good the bottles are.

What makes it worth listing anyway is the format, and specifically the pint glass. A pub is the single most difficult venue to attend without drinking, because the entire social architecture — rounds, the bar, the standing about — is built around the pint. Athletic's Upside Dawn served in the same glass as everyone else's beer solves that problem in a way no mocktail can, because nobody can tell and nobody asks. For someone newly not drinking, that anonymity is often worth more than a more elaborate drink would be.

The practical details help too. The kitchen runs all day rather than in sittings, so there is always food; the rooms are small enough to sit in for hours; and the hours run to eleven midweek, midnight on Friday and Saturday, with a ten o'clock weekend opening for breakfast.

venues.name: The Dive
venues.description: The Dive is a Canton cocktail bar on Elliott Street whose standing menu keeps a built non-alcoholic option rather than a soda pour: the Mockingbird shakes cranberry, lime and cinnamon honey with aquafaba and tops it with ginger beer, the aquafaba giving it the frothed body of a properly shaken cocktail.
venues.longDescription:
The Dive opened in November 2022 at 3123 Elliott Street in Canton, from Baltimore native and Top Chef alum Jesse Sandlin, who also runs Sally O's in Highlandtown. The building has been several bars before this one — Fuisine most recently, and the Regal Beagle before that — and Sandlin painted the exterior brickwork cobalt blue with a deep-sea diver on it, which is the clearest signal of the tone. Baltimore Magazine, reviewing it, noted what makes the room work: the purple booths filled with families, people walking dogs and pushing strollers, and the explicit sense that this was not going to be old men playing video poker by the bar. The food is unapologetic — hubcap-sized double pepperoni pizzas, a pickle pizza with Havarti, tiger sauce and dill, a fried bologna sandwich that is actually mortadella topped with fried pickles, and foot-long hot dogs under bacon-jalapeño relish or crab dip. It opens at 4pm Monday through Thursday and at 11am Friday through Sunday, serving until 1am every night, with the kitchen open until midnight and no reservations.

The non-alcoholic offering is one properly built drink rather than a list, and it is worth the trip for what it demonstrates. The Mockingbird, as The Baltimore Banner described it, is a zesty mix of cranberry, lime, cinnamon honey, aquafaba and ginger beer. Aquafaba is the liquid from a tin of chickpeas, and it is the vegan substitute for egg white — it whips to a foam and gives a shaken drink the silky body that zero-proof drinks almost always lack. Using it in a neighbourhood bar's single mocktail, rather than in a cocktail-programme showpiece, says more about the kitchen's standards than a long list would. One practical caveat: the bar's website is live but its menu pages currently show placeholder text rather than an actual menu, so the drink list has to be asked about in person.
venues.pressQuote: Their non-alcoholic creation, the 'Mockingbird,' is a zesty mix of cranberry, lime, cinnamon honey, aquafaba and ginger beer.

venues.name: The Dog Bar
venues.description: The Dog Bar pairs an off-leash private dog park with a full bar in St. Petersburg's Grand Central District — a USA Today "best dog bar in America" finalist. Alongside 30-plus rotating drafts, it keeps a genuinely curated non-alcoholic menu of mocktails and NA beers (plus a CBD seltzer), so dog owners who aren't drinking have more than a soda while their dogs run. The list runs to seven mocktails and eight non-alcoholic beers — the Nah'Chelada, Safe Sex On The Beach and a Virgin Mary among them — an unusually deep bench for a bar whose main draw is the dog park. A daytime crowd that has to drive a dog home is exactly the customer base most bars ignore.
venues.longDescription:
The Dog Bar combines a full bar with a private off-leash dog park on Central Avenue in St. Petersburg's Grand Central District — members bring their dogs, the dogs run, and the humans drink. It has been a USA Today finalist for best dog bar in America, and the format explains a great deal about why its non-alcoholic list is as developed as it is.

A dog bar is a daytime venue in a way most bars are not. People arrive at eleven on a Saturday, stay two hours, and then drive home with a dog in the car. That is a customer base with a structural reason not to drink, and the bar has responded properly rather than pointing at the soda gun: seven mocktails, eight non-alcoholic beers and a CBD seltzer, against 30-plus rotating drafts on the alcoholic side. The named builds have the same sense of humour as the room — the Nah'Chelada, Safe Sex On The Beach, a Virgin Mary.

I Love The Burg rated it in January 2024 as having one of the best mocktail menus around, listing the seven mocktails, eight NA beers and the CBD seltzer as the reason. Eight non-alcoholic beers is a genuinely unusual number — most bars carry one, occasionally two, and treat the category as covered.

Practical notes: it opens at noon Monday to Thursday and 11am at weekends, running to midnight or 1am, so it works across the whole day. Entry with a dog requires membership and proof of vaccination; visiting without one is straightforward. It is a full bar rather than an alcohol-free venue — but of everywhere in this city, it is the one where not drinking is closest to the norm rather than the exception.
venues.pressQuote: The Dog Bar has one of the best mocktail menus around. Choose from the seven mocktails, eight NA beers, or even the CBD seltzer.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Bob Carskadon, I Love The Burg

venues.name: The Donovan Bar at Brown's Hotel
venues.description: The Donovan Bar is the World's-50-Best-listed cocktail room inside Rocco Forte's Brown's Hotel in Mayfair, run by maestro Salvatore Calabrese and Director of Mixology Federico Pavan. Its signature achievement for non-drinkers is structural: the menu is built so that every section pairs four alcoholic cocktails with one full alcohol-free serve, given equal billing and treated as a real drink rather than a placeholder. The zero-proof builds are engineered to match the character and flavour of their spirited counterparts, drawing on bases like Seedlip.
venues.longDescription:
Named for the photographer Terence Donovan and hung with his black-and-white prints, The Donovan Bar sits inside Brown's Hotel at 33 Albemarle Street, one of Mayfair's grandest addresses. Since opening in 2018 it has become one of London's most decorated hotel bars, landing at No.92 on The World's 50 Best Bars list in 2023. The programme is led by Salvatore Calabrese, 'The Maestro' of the classic cocktail, alongside Director of Mixology Federico Pavan.

What makes it a genuine destination for non-drinkers is how the alcohol-free drinks are written into the menu itself. On the fairy-tale-themed 'Happily Ever After' list, every section presents five cocktails - four with alcohol and one without - so the zero-proof option is never an afterthought. Brown's has been explicit that the alcohol-free builds are designed to carry the same character and flavour profile as their spirited siblings, with equal respect given to the drinks and no placeholders on the menu; only the base changes.

Those non-alcoholic serves lean on contemporary distilled bases: Federico Pavan's Donovan Bar work has featured Seedlip Garden lifted with London Essence ginger beer for a dry, gingery finish, the kind of composed build you would expect from a bar at this level rather than a sugary mocktail. Expect the same crystal, garnish work and theatre poured for the alcoholic drinks.

The room is intimate and clubby - dark walls, low light, a small stage that hosts live jazz on weekends - and it keeps proper cocktail-bar hours, open from noon until midnight or 1am. It is a strong choice for a sober guest who wants an occasion-level Mayfair cocktail experience without compromise.

venues.name: The Draftsman
venues.description: The Draftsman opened on 21 June 2023 at 68 Patton Avenue downtown as the bar and restaurant of The Restoration Hotel, and it is a more relaxed proposition than a hotel bar usually is — there is a bowling alley in it, called Up Your Alley, run first-come-first-served by signing up at the bar rather than booked ahead. The kitchen is straightforward and well priced for downtown: deviled eggs with local farm eggs, pickled mustard seeds and bacon at $8, a short rib and chuck Draftsman Burger at $17, and a jalapeño buttermilk fried chicken sandwich with Alabama white sauce at $16. It builds its non-alcoholic drinks with the same care as the full list rather than treating them as an afterthought, leaning on zero-proof aperitifs like Ghia — the Clear Morning Spritz (Ghia Amaro, lemon, grapefruit, soda) and a spirit-free Phony Negroni — so the non-drinker gets a properly crafted cocktail in a real cocktail room. Open from 5pm Thursday and Friday and from 11.30am at weekends.

venues.longDescription:
The Draftsman opened on 21 June 2023 at 68 Patton Avenue in downtown Asheville, the bar and restaurant of The Restoration Hotel, and it is a more relaxed proposition than a hotel bar usually is — there is a bowling alley in it, called Up Your Alley, run first-come-first-served by signing up at the bar rather than booked in advance. The kitchen is straightforward and well priced for downtown: deviled eggs with local farm eggs, pickled mustard seeds and bacon at $8, a short rib and chuck Draftsman Burger at $17, and a jalapeño buttermilk fried chicken sandwich with Alabama white sauce at $16. It serves Thursday and Friday from 5pm and from 11.30am at weekends, running to midnight, and is closed Monday through Wednesday. Reservations run through Resy. The hotel reopened after Helene and posted its recovery notice in early November 2024.

The non-alcoholic drinks are handled differently here from most bars, and the difference is worth understanding before you order. There is no separate zero-proof section: the alcohol-free options sit inside the main cocktail list, each tagged "(N/A)" beside its name. That is arguably the better design — a non-drinker reads the same menu as everyone else, in the same order, rather than turning to a short appendix at the back. The Clear Morning Spritz ($12) is the best of them, built on Ghia, the Californian non-alcoholic amaro, with lemon, grapefruit and soda, so the bitterness is genuine rather than sweetened over. The Apple Cider Fizz ($10) is the simplest, made from apple juice with lime, ginger and soda. A Phony Negroni completes the list at $10. One small caveat: the Phony Negroni is the only drink on the entire menu printed without its ingredients, so ask what is in it if that matters — every other cocktail, alcoholic or not, lists what it contains.
venues.pressQuote: Their non-alcoholic drinks are more than just a mix of juices—they are crafted with the same care and creativity as their alcoholic counterparts.

venues.name: The Eddy
venues.description: The Eddy is Providence's most decorated cocktail bar — a perennial Best of Rhode Island winner for Best Cocktail List — and it handles non-drinkers better than any other room in the state. The menu carries a printed spirit-free section, and separately marks with an asterisk every cocktail that can be built without spirit, with the legend spelled out at the foot of the page. Athletic Brewing's non-alcoholic IPA is on the bottle list. Open daily until 1am.

El Angel ($9) — black currant, ginger shrub, lime, soda

venues.longDescription:
The Eddy sits on the street it is named for, in downtown Providence, and it has spent a decade as the bar other Rhode Island bartenders measure themselves against. It wins Best of Rhode Island's Best Cocktail List with the regularity of a fixture rather than a contender. What earns it a place here is not the trophy shelf but two structural decisions that make it genuinely usable if you are not drinking.

The first is a standing spirit-free section on the printed menu — not a seasonal special, not something you have to ask about. The second is more unusual and more valuable: an asterisk system. Cocktails on the main list that can be built without spirit are marked with a single asterisk, and the legend at the bottom of the menu spells it out plainly. That turns a two-drink section into a meaningful slice of the whole list, and it removes the part non-drinkers dislike most, which is having to ask a busy bartender to improvise and then hope.

The spirit-free builds themselves are made the way the rest of the list is made — around acid and bitterness rather than sugar. From Miles Away runs mint and passionfruit against ginger and lime over soda. El Angel is the sharper of the two, built on black currant with a ginger shrub, lime and soda; a shrub is a drinking vinegar, and it does the work that a bitter aperitif would do in the alcoholic version. Both sit at nine dollars, several below the bar's full-strength cocktails.

For beer drinkers there is Athletic Brewing's non-alcoholic IPA on the bottle and can list at seven dollars, alongside a deep local draught line-up from Rhode Island brewers. One practical note: published guides to this bar go stale fast. Three separate drink names credited to The Eddy in recent Rhode Island round-ups — a Mai Chai, an Autumn Gimlet and a Hibiscus Breeze — were not on the menu when we checked. El Angel was. Read the list when you sit down.
venues.pressQuote: a perennial Best of Rhode Island winner for Best Cocktail List

venues.name: The Edison
venues.description: The Edison is an upscale New American restaurant in Milwaukee's Historic Third Ward from the family-owned Benson's Restaurant Group, set in the ground floor of the restored 1914 Commission Row warehouse. Its speakeasy-inspired bar keeps a dedicated "Spirit Free" section on the standing drink menu, so non-drinkers get composed, named zero-proof builds rather than an afterthought. The lineup runs from a Seedlip-based garden cooler to a dessert-like Butterscotch Espresso Notini, and the restaurant is a featured stop on Visit Milwaukee's Mocktail Trail.

venues.longDescription:
The Edison is a contemporary New American restaurant and cocktail bar in Milwaukee's Historic Third Ward, opened by the family-owned Benson's Restaurant Group in the ground-floor space of the restored 1914 Commission Row warehouse at 322 N. Broadway. The kitchen leans into coal-fired butcher's cuts, seafood, and brunch, while a speakeasy-inspired bar anchors the drinks program. It sits alongside sister venues Bridgewater, Blue Bat Kitchen, and Onesto in the Benson's group.

The non-alcoholic offering here is a genuine, standing part of the menu rather than a seasonal special. The Edison's drink list carries a dedicated "Spirit Free" section with roughly half a dozen composed zero-proof options: the Summer Night's Breeze (Seedlip Garden, lavender syrup, lemon, and a Leitz non-alcoholic Pinot Noir float), the dessert-forward Butterscotch Espresso Notini (double-shot espresso, cream, brown-butter demerara, grated nutmeg), the Hidden Orchard (pomegranate, peppercorn syrup, lime, mint), and a Cinna-oat Iced Chai, plus Leitz Eins Zwei Zero non-alcoholic sparkling and still wines and canned UNDONE mocktails. Because the drinks are named and built with intent, an alcohol-free guest gets a full bar experience.

The Edison is a featured stop on Visit Milwaukee's Mocktail Trail, which highlights its "wide selection of spirit-free cocktails." As of 2026 the restaurant is operating on regular hours, with an active reservation system on its own site, current menus online, and steady recent reviews across Yelp and OpenTable. Reservations are recommended for weekend brunch and dinner.

venues.longDescription:
The Edison is Disney Springs' industrial-gothic showpiece, styled after a 1920s underground electricity factory turned illicit bar, complete with aerialists, a fortune teller, and steampunk decor. It sits in The Landing, Disney Springs' waterfront dining neighborhood in Lake Buena Vista at Walt Disney World Resort, and opened on New Year's Eve 2017. The restaurant is operated by Patina Restaurant Group, which runs several other Walt Disney World dining venues.

Its zero-proof menu is unusually deep for a themed restaurant and has its own printed "Zero Proof Cocktails" section: the Heart & Sol (Seedlip Grove 42, Seedlip Spice 94, housemade cinnamon cordial, pineapple, orgeat, Fever-Tree ginger beer) and the LZP (Seedlip Garden 108, cold-pressed watermelon juice, housemade cinnamon cordial, lemon juice, strawberry) both build on Seedlip's distilled non-alcoholic spirits, while the Botanic Sun uses the botanical non-alcoholic spirit Aplos Arise with muddled mint, pineapple juice, and lime juice. Rounding out the list are the playful Disco Melon Soda (cold-pressed watermelon juice, strawberry puree, Sprite, lemonade, served with a complimentary glow cube), Apple Propellant (apple cider, honey, lemon juice, ginger ale), Smoke & Mirrors (pineapple juice, lemon juice, lime juice, orgeat), and Springs Water (cucumber, mint, lime).

The Disco Melon Soda's complimentary glow cube is a signature bit of theater tying the drink to the restaurant's electricity-themed decor. A 2025 review in Main St. Magic called the Heart & Sol "bold, tart, complex" and the LZP "light, fresh, and a little unexpected," noting the zero-proof list offers "creative, elevated drinks that don't feel like an afterthought" compared to the typical mocktail treatment at comparable theme-park restaurants. The Edison also holds a 2025 OpenTable Diners' Choice award for "Great for Cocktails."
venues.pressQuote: The bar also offers a well-curated selection of wine, craft beer, and zero-proof cocktails for those who prefer a non-alcoholic yet flavorful alternative.

venues.name: The Eleanor
venues.description: The Eleanor is a Warehouse District cocktail bar whose zero-proof drinks are built with the same architecture as its spirited list rather than being simplified into juice. The clearest evidence is the Pass The Buck, which layers Almave — the non-alcoholic blanco agave spirit — with Giffard bitter aperitif syrup, a strawberry and Thai basil syrup, ginger, lemon and barrel-smoked black pepper. That is seven components doing the work alcohol usually does: the bitter aperitif supplies the backbone, the smoked pepper the finish. Visit Austin's official zero-proof guide singles the drink out. The bar keeps late Friday and Saturday hours and is walkable from the Fifth Street hotel cluster.
signatureDrinks: Pass The Buck - Almave non-alcoholic blanco, Giffard bitter aperitif syrup, strawberry-Thai basil syrup, ginger, lemon, barrel-smoked black pepper
venues.longDescription:
The Eleanor sits on West Fifth Street in Austin's Warehouse District, the downtown stretch where most of the city's late-night drinking happens, and it has built a reputation on a long and technically serious cocktail list. What earns it a place in an alcohol-free directory is that the seriousness extends past the spirited drinks.

The bar's signature zero-proof build is the Pass The Buck, and it is worth reading the spec closely because it explains the grade. It starts with Almave, the non-alcoholic blanco agave spirit developed with input from the tequila world, then adds Giffard bitter aperitif syrup, a house strawberry and Thai basil syrup, ginger, lemon, and barrel-smoked black pepper. Seven components, each doing a job that alcohol would otherwise do: the bitter aperitif gives the drink a spine, the ginger and lemon supply the bite, and the smoked pepper leaves the lingering warmth on the finish that a spirit normally provides. This is compositional bartending, not substitution — the difference between a zero-proof drink that feels like an adult drink and one that tastes like a soft drink with garnish.

Visit Austin, the city's official destination organisation, named the drink in its own zero-proof guide, which is a useful signal: municipal tourism boards are conservative about what they endorse, and the mention indicates the program is a standing part of the bar's identity rather than a one-off special.

Almave itself is worth a note for anyone building a home bar: it is a non-alcoholic blue-agave distillate created with Lewis Hamilton, and unlike most zero-proof spirits it is made from agave rather than assembled from botanical extracts, which is why it holds up in a drink built around bitterness and smoke instead of disappearing under them. Seeing it behind a bar is usually a sign the team has actually tasted the category rather than ordering whatever the distributor pushed.

Practically, the room keeps a narrow schedule — Friday and Saturday evenings only, running to 1am — so it works as a weekend destination rather than a drop-in, and that is worth checking before making the trip. It sits within a short walk of the Fifth Street hotels and the rest of the Warehouse District, which makes it a straightforward addition to a night out for a mixed group where not everyone is drinking. The cocktail list rotates, so confirm the current zero-proof options when you arrive rather than assuming Pass The Buck is still on it.
venues.pressQuote: The Eleanor, located in the Warehouse District, is known for its extensive cocktail menu, including the "Pass The Buck," which features Almave non-alcoholic blanco tequila, Giffard bitter aperitif syrup, strawberry-thai basil syrup, ginger, lemon, and barrel-smoked black pepper.

venues.name: The Elk Room
venues.description: The Elk Room is a subterranean, speakeasy-style craft cocktail bar in Harbor East known for a serious spirit-driven program. Its zero-proof entry, the Penumbra, is a composed build rather than a sweet afterthought — a wine vinegar shrub with yuzu juice, blueberries, thyme, black pepper and soda water — the kind of savory, acid-forward drink the bar's cocktail list is built on.
venues.longDescription:
The Elk Room is a subterranean cocktail bar at 1010 Fleet Street in Harbor East, opened in early August 2017 in the space that had been Ten Ten American Bistro, and operated by Atlas Restaurant Group. It is a small, deliberately hard-to-find room — entry through a peephole door, six seats at the bar itself, and a passageway that once led to a members-only cigar bar — and it built its reputation on a spirit-driven programme rather than on volume. Esquire named it to its Best Bars in America list in 2018. It opens nightly until 2am with live music Thursday through Saturday, and valet parking is available, which in Harbor East is worth knowing.

For a non-drinker the offering is narrow but genuinely made. The house zero-proof drink is the Penumbra, and The Baltimore Banner described its construction when it surveyed the city's mocktails in October 2024: a shrub-based drink combining wine vinegar, yuzu juice, blueberries, thyme, black pepper and soda water. That is a serious build — a shrub is fruit preserved in vinegar and sugar, and using one as the backbone gives a drink the acid and length that zero-proof drinks usually lack, while the black pepper and thyme supply the bite that alcohol would otherwise carry. It is the right approach for a bar whose whole identity is spirit-forward. Two honest caveats before you go. The bar does not render its menu in a form that can be read online, so the Penumbra is the only zero-proof drink documented and the current list has to be asked about at the bar. And its published hours and phone number differ between the operator's own site and the city's visitor listing, so confirm before travelling — the operator gives 5pm to 2am nightly.
venues.pressQuote: A shrub-based mocktail combines wine vinegar, yuzu juice, blueberries, thyme, black pepper and soda water.

venues.name: The Epicurean
venues.description: The Epicurean is an award-winning independent craft-beer bottle shop, and this Henry Street unit is the group's Ancoats flagship — its first city-centre store, opened in November 2021 next door to natural-wine merchant Kerb. Owner Simon Yarwood's shop packs more than 500 beers across nine fridges, and its low-and-no range is one of the deepest in Greater Manchester: a 'beer library' of alcohol-free options rather than a token shelf. Chilled 0.0–0.5% picks run from Big Drop's Galactic Stout and Beavertown's Lazer Crush to Tiny Rebel's Clwb Tropicana, Athletic Brewing's alcohol-free lager and Vandestreek's grapefruit IPA. It is a bottle shop rather than a bar, but for taking home a genuinely broad spread of alcohol-free craft beer it has few rivals in the city.
venues.longDescription:
The Epicurean began as a suburban craft-beer specialist under owner Simon Yarwood, building a following across Greater Manchester before opening this Ancoats shop in November 2021 as its first city-centre site. It sits on Henry Street in the heart of Ancoats, next door to natural-wine merchant Kerb, and trades as part of the group known as The Epicurean Beer People, which also runs stores in Chorlton, Didsbury and Heaton Moor. The Ancoats unit was fitted out from a blank canvas by manager and resident beer expert James Hodgson, who squeezed nine fridges into the space to keep a large chunk of the 500-plus range chilled and ready to drink.

The shop is wall-to-wall beer: floor-to-ceiling shelves and those nine fridges carry local heroes such as Track, Pomona Island, Squawk and Runaway alongside national names like Cloudwater, DEYA and Verdant and international rarities from Belgium, Germany, Norway and beyond. Staff knowledge is the selling point — it is the kind of place where you can describe what you like and be walked to the right can — and the stock deliberately spans vegan, gluten-free, low-alcohol and non-alcoholic beers, plus ciders from around the world, rather than sticking to hop-forward pale ales.

For non-drinkers the draw is the alcohol-free 'beer library', among the best suburban and city-centre NA coverage in Greater Manchester. Manchester Confidential singled the shop out for stocking the likes of Vandestreek, Beavertown's Lazer Crush, Tiny Rebel's Clwb Tropicana and Big Drop's Galactic Stout, and the current chilled low-and-no fridge backs that up: Athletic Brewing's 0.5% alcohol-free lager, Track's own Arosa 0.5% lager, Pomona Island's 'A Token Of Sweet Nothing' pale, Vandestreek's 0.5% grapefruit IPA, Beak's Nolia alcohol-free IPA and Warsteiner's 0.0% pilsner among them. Because it is a bottle shop the beers are sold to take away, with free local delivery on larger orders, but the breadth and turnover mean the alcohol-free selection stays fresh and genuinely current rather than a dusty afterthought.
venues.pressQuote: The Epicurean in Ancoats has a trademark beer library of options, stocking the likes of Vanderstreek, Beavertown's Lazer Crush, Tiny Rebel's Clwb Tropicana and Big Drop's Galactic Stout.

venues.name: The Fairmount
venues.description: The Fairmount is a long-running cocktail and wine bar in the Cedar Fairmount district of Cleveland Heights, a few hundred metres from Zhug, serving martinis, craft beer, burgers and pizza in a chic but unfussy room with a late-night menu from 10pm. Several non-alcoholic drinks sit on the standing menu, led by the Little Green One at $10 — cilantro, lime, pineapple, mint and jalapeño lengthened with Fever-Tree tonic over a Tajín rim, so heat and salt do the work alcohol would in a spicy margarita. It is savoury rather than sweet.
signatureDrinks: Little Green One (cilantro, lime, pineapple, mint, jalapeño, Fever-Tree tonic, Tajín rim)
venues.longDescription:
The Fairmount has been the Cedar Fairmount district's main evening room for years — a martini and wine bar on Fairmount Boulevard a few hundred metres from Zhug, drawing a mix of University Circle staff, Cleveland Heights regulars and people coming out of Severance Hall and the museums. The format is deliberately broad: a cocktail and martini list, craft beer, wine by the glass, and a kitchen turning out burgers and pizzas well into the night, with a dedicated late-night menu from 10pm daily. It is the kind of bar that works for a group that cannot agree on anything, which is precisely why its non-alcoholic options matter.

That list is short but properly built, and the general manager's explanation for it in Cleveland Magazine's 2026 mocktail guide is the plain one: people are becoming more health-conscious, and it is a nice option to be able to offer. The Little Green One at $10 is the drink to order — cilantro, lime, pineapple, mint and jalapeño lengthened with Fever-Tree tonic and served over a Tajín rim, so the heat, salt and quinine bitterness carry the drink the way tequila and salt would in a spicy margarita. It is savoury rather than sweet, which is the distinction that separates a genuine zero-proof build from a glass of juice, and it holds up across a whole evening rather than cloying after one. Two or three further non-alcoholic drinks sit alongside it and rotate.

Practically, the bar pairs well with Zhug for an east-side night out: dinner at one, a drink at the other, both walkable from the same Cedar Fairmount parking and both with something real on the menu for a guest who is not drinking. Published opening hours vary between listings, so call ahead if you are arriving early.
venues.pressQuote: People are becoming more health-conscious. It's a nice option to be able to offer.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: The Fairmount general manager, via Cleveland Magazine

venues.name: The Flamingo Room
venues.description: The Flamingo Room is a moody, candlelit bar on Century Drive built for lingering, and its zero-proof options hold their own against the cocktail list. Two named builds are documented — one a calming lavender, chamomile, ginger and CBD drink, the other a watermelon shrub and lime build that reads like summer in a glass. Open daily to 11pm, midnight at weekends.
signatureDrinks: Three Men in a Tub — watermelon shrub and lime
Calm the F**k Down — lavender, chamomile, ginger and CBD (contains CBD)
venues.longDescription:
The Flamingo Room sits in the Century Center complex on Century Drive, the road that runs west out of Bend toward Mount Bachelor and the Cascade Lakes. It is a dark, candlelit room designed for staying put — the opposite of Bend's bright, communal brewery taprooms — and it is one of the few bars in town where a non-drinker can settle in for a long evening without the drink in front of them being an afterthought.

Two zero-proof builds are documented. Three Men in a Tub is the summer one: a watermelon shrub with lime, the shrub's vinegar sharpness stopping the melon from turning cloying and giving the drink enough acid to last more than a few sips. The other, whose name the local press renders as Calm the F**k Down, is built on lavender, chamomile and ginger with CBD, and does roughly what the name promises.

That second drink needs a plain flag rather than a euphemism: it contains CBD. CBD is not alcohol and will not produce intoxication in the way alcohol does, but it is an added active compound rather than simply a botanical, and anyone in recovery who avoids all mood-altering substances should know that before ordering. The watermelon build contains none, and the bar's wider list includes plenty that does not.

Bend's zero-proof scene has a noticeable hemp and CBD streak running through it — several bars and breweries in town offer CBD or THC drinks alongside their alcohol-free options, which is a product of Oregon's regulatory environment more than anything else. It is worth reading the menu carefully here if that is a line you do not want to cross.
venues.pressQuote: both lean into that moody, candlelit vibe that makes you want to stay awhile, and their zero-proof options hold their own

venues.name: The Fox Bar & Cocktail Club
venues.description: The Fox Bar & Cocktail Club is a plush 1,000-square-foot craft cocktail bar in East Nashville's Inglewood stretch, tucked behind an Italian restaurant on Gallatin Pike. It opened on 28 September 2017 from Bryan Rushton and Andrew Cook, longtime music-industry friends and Massachusetts natives, in a room fitted out with reclaimed wood from Nashville-area houses. Food & Wine named it one of the 10 Best U.S. Bars in 2023, Eater Nashville made it Bar of the Year the same year, and USA Today's 2026 list called it one of the city's strongest cocktail programs. Its non-alcoholic drinks are built with the same technique as the full menu and, importantly, they rotate with the seasons rather than sitting still — the current three are the East Coast Inferno (Sanbittèr Red, orange juice, Old Bay, habanero, lemon), Pêche Mode (Almave Ámbar non-alcoholic tequila, peach, lime, salted honey) and Duck Hunt (duck fat Lapsang Souchong, The Pathfinder, cherry, BBQ bitters), all $12.

venues.longDescription:
The Fox Bar & Cocktail Club opened on 28 September 2017 at 2905B Gallatin Pike, hidden behind an Italian restaurant on the Inglewood stretch of East Nashville. It came out of a holiday conversation between Bryan Rushton and Andrew Cook, longtime music-industry friends and Massachusetts natives who had both settled in Nashville, and the room they built is small and comfortable rather than showy: roughly a thousand square feet holding a main bar, three high-tops, a few booths and a two-seat perch by the door, fitted out in reclaimed wood salvaged from Nashville-area houses by local makers 1767 Designs. The bar has drawn national attention well out of proportion to its size — Food & Wine named it one of the ten best bars in the United States in 2023, Eater Nashville made it Bar of the Year the same year, it took third in the Nashville Scene's readers' poll for best bar, and USA Today's 2026 list described it as one of the city's strongest cocktail programs. The kitchen sends out miso deviled eggs and a wagyu hotdog on a Japanese milk bun.

The Fox was among the first Nashville bars to treat zero-proof drinks as real cocktails, and the most useful thing to know about its list is that it rotates. The drinks change with the seasons alongside the alcoholic menu, so any list you find in an older article will be out of date — a good sign, since it means the non-alcoholic side is being rewritten rather than left to sit. The current three are each $12 and each built on a different idea. East Coast Inferno is the savoury one, combining Sanbittèr Red with orange juice, Old Bay seasoning, habanero and lemon. Pêche Mode is the softest, using Almave Ámbar non-alcoholic tequila with peach, lime and salted honey. Duck Hunt is the most unusual thing on either menu: duck fat-washed Lapsang Souchong tea with The Pathfinder, cherry and barbecue bitters. The bar keeps several hundred bottles in-house and has long given its bartenders wide latitude, so it is a reasonable place to ask for something off-list. Open Tuesday to Sunday from 5pm to midnight, closed Mondays.
venues.pressQuote: One of the best bars in the city, The Fox Bar & Cocktail Club in East Nashville is a dimly lit den that draws a crowd — reservations are a smart bet here.

venues.name: The George on Washington St.
venues.description: The George on Washington Street is a downtown Providence restaurant and bar with one of the broader non-alcoholic spreads in the city — three documented builds rather than the single token mocktail most rooms offer, covering a cucumber mojito, an alcohol-free margarita and a non-alcoholic sangria. Named on the Providence tourism board's own mocktail guide.
venues.longDescription:
The George sits on Washington Street in downtown Providence, a short walk from Trinity Rep and the Providence Performing Arts Center, which makes it a natural stop either side of a show. It works as both restaurant and bar, and its non-alcoholic offering is broader than most of the city's — three documented builds rather than the one that the majority of Providence rooms manage.

The three cover distinct ground, which is what makes the spread useful rather than repetitive. The cucumber mojito is the long, fresh option, built on muddled cucumber and mint for something you can drink slowly across an evening. The alcohol-free margarita covers the sharp, citrus-and-salt end, and it is the drink most often ruined by bars that simply pour limeade — done properly it wants fresh lime and enough salt to carry it. The non-alcoholic sangria is the one that suits a table sharing food, a fruit-and-spice build that stands in for a glass of red without pretending to be one.

Three builds is the threshold where a non-drinker stops having to order the same thing all night, which is why this sits comfortably at a three rather than the two we have assigned to the city's single-mocktail rooms. All three are named on Go Providence's own guide, published by the city's tourism board in August 2026 — the freshest source available for this metro.

We have not published prices or exact ingredient lists, as the restaurant does not publish its drinks menu online. The downtown location means it is well served by the Washington Street garages, and it is one of the few kitchens in the immediate theatre district that runs late enough for a post-show meal.
venues.pressQuote: Cucumber Mojito, Margarita, Sangria

venues.name: The Gin Joint
venues.description: A craft cocktail bar in Charleston's French Quarter, open since 2010 as one of the city's original spirit-forward bars. Alongside its gin-led list it keeps a small standing set of no-ABV mocktails, and its signature "Bartender's Choice" can be ordered zero-proof. The kitchen-style approach leans on house syrups, teas, and fresh herbs.
venues.longDescription:
The Gin Joint sits at 182 East Bay Street in Charleston's French Quarter and has operated since 2010 as one of the city's first dedicated craft cocktail bars. Its drink program is built around fresh ingredients, house syrups, teas, and herbs, and it runs on a no-reservations, walk-in model.

For non-drinkers, the bar lists named no-ABV mocktails including the "European Outlaw" (tea, raspberry, thyme, and ginger), "New Beginnings," and "The Unknown Coast." Its well-known "Bartender's Choice" can also be made zero-proof on request, letting alcohol-free guests get the same custom, made-to-order treatment as the cocktail list.

venues.name: The Gladly
venues.description: A Biltmore-area New American restaurant and whiskey bar open since 2013, The Gladly pairs a serious beverage program — 350-plus whiskies and a James Beard-recognized kitchen — with a permanent, menu-printed 'Zero Proof' section. These are crafted non-alcoholic cocktails built on real NA spirits like Seedlip and Lyre's rather than a token mocktail: the Hellfire works Seedlip Grove 42 with blueberry puree, orgeat, citrus, ginger beer and cracked black pepper; A Botanist Walks Into a Bar uses jalapeno-infused Seedlip Garden; Truth or Consequences is built on Lyre's Italian Orange with strawberry and grapefruit oleo. Phoenix New Times has repeatedly named it a go-to for alcohol-free drinks that are actually printed on the menu.

venues.longDescription:
The Gladly has held its corner of the Biltmore since 2013, a New American restaurant with a whiskey bar attached — or arguably the reverse, given a back bar carrying more than 350 bottles. The kitchen has drawn James Beard recognition, and the room works equally as a dinner reservation and as a place to sit at the bar, which is the relevant distinction for anyone who wants a proper drink without the drink.

What earns it a listing is that the alcohol-free options are printed. There is a standing 'Zero Proof' section on the menu, not a verbal offer, and the builds run on named non-alcoholic spirits rather than juice and syrup. The Hellfire pairs Seedlip Grove 42 with blueberry puree, orgeat, citrus and ginger beer, finished with cracked black pepper that keeps it from going sweet. A Botanist Walks Into a Bar infuses Seedlip Garden with jalapeno and lengthens it with grapefruit oleo, lime and soda. Truth or Consequences is built on Lyre's Italian Orange with strawberry and grapefruit oleo — an aperitif shape rather than a dessert one. There is a Fauxjito for anyone who wants the obvious thing done properly.

Phoenix New Times has named the restaurant more than once when surveying where in the metro alcohol-free drinks actually appear on the menu, including its January 2024 round-up. Two practical notes. This is a restaurant first, so the format assumes a table and a meal, and the bar is busy at peak. And the whiskey list is the house identity — the zero-proof section is a well-built part of a menu whose centre of gravity is emphatically alcoholic, which is worth knowing if you would rather not spend an evening beside 350 bottles of bourbon. The patio is the easier seat on that score.
venues.pressQuote: The citrus-forward non-alcoholic spirit Seedlip Grove 42 mixes things up with blueberry puree, orgeat, citrus, ginger beer, and cracked black pepper in The Gladly's rosy-colored Hellfire.

venues.name: The Golden Age
venues.description: The Golden Age is a Dupont Circle cocktail bar and restaurant at 1726 Connecticut Avenue NW, themed on the golden age of the American cocktail - the era of the late 1800s and early 1900s before Prohibition. It is a DC original from the Drinks With You group, which also runs Patina, Never Looked Better and The Mirror, and it pairs craft cocktails and fine food with a jazz-age room and recurring live programming, including regular jazz nights framed as an homage to Duke Ellington. Non-drinkers get their own headed menu, Beer, Wine & Non-Alcoholic, rather than a footnote: an Amaro Lucano & Soda built with N/A amaro, soda and lemon essence, and The Peacock Room, made with cider, lemon, sugar, NA bitters and sparkles, alongside non-alcoholic beer such as Kit NA Lager, plus NA ciders and wines.
signatureDrinks: Amaro Lucano & Soda (N/A Amaro, soda, lemon essence)
The Peacock Room (cider, lemon, sugar, NA bitters, sparkles)
venues.longDescription:
The Golden Age takes its name and its whole premise from a specific period: the decades between the first printed definition of a cocktail, in an 1806 Hudson Valley newspaper, and Prohibition, when the form reached maturity and cocktail bars became the meeting places of artists and thinkers. The bar's own framing is that it wants to present the origins of the classics before bartenders were forced into back rooms and speakeasies. It sits at 1726 Connecticut Avenue NW in Dupont Circle and is a DC original from Drinks With You, LLC, the group behind Patina, Never Looked Better and The Mirror. The jazz-age setting is backed by real programming - the team has talked about being part of a jazz revival in the city as an homage to local legend Duke Ellington, and live nights run regularly.

For a bar this committed to the spirits of a particular era, the non-alcoholic handling is notably deliberate. The drinks are not tucked into the cocktail card; they sit on their own menu, headed Beer, Wine & Non-Alcoholic, which means a table that is not drinking is handed a list rather than asked what they can have. Two zero-proof builds anchor it. The Amaro Lucano & Soda uses a non-alcoholic amaro with soda and lemon essence, and it is the more interesting of the two because amaro is the hardest category to reproduce without alcohol - the bitterness has to come from somewhere. The Peacock Room, named for the Whistler interior at the nearby Freer Gallery, is built from cider, lemon, sugar, NA bitters and sparkles. Beyond the cocktails the bar pours non-alcoholic beer from a rotating and mostly local selection, including Kit Non-Alcoholic Lager, plus NA ciders and wines. Resy has highlighted the spot for offering spirit-free and low-proof drinks - an ode to a Pimm's Cup, an Americano - alongside that range while classic jazz plays.

Practical notes. The bar is closed Sunday and Monday. It opens at 5pm Tuesday through Saturday, closing at 10pm midweek and 11pm Thursday through Saturday, so it runs earlier than much of Dupont. It is a short walk from Dupont Circle Metro.
venues.pressQuote: The Golden Age team is looking forward to being a part of a jazz revival in the city as an homage to local legend Duke Ellington
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Dupont Circle Business Improvement District, Jazz Nights at The Golden Age

venues.name: The Golden Tiki
venues.description: The Golden Tiki is a world-famous, immersive tiki cocktail bar tucked into Las Vegas's Chinatown corridor on Spring Mountain Road, open 24 hours a day and known for its shrunken-head collection, animatronics, and 1960s tropical-pop atmosphere. Beyond its rum-forward classics like the Navy Grog, the bar keeps a dedicated "Virgin Cocktails" section on its menu, so non-drinkers get crafted zero-proof options rather than an afterthought. The lineup includes the Tropical Vertigo (Kalinago Caribbean tea, cream of coconut, pineapple, lime, vanilla and grated cinnamon), the Coconut Pick-Me-Up (espresso, cream of coconut, vanilla and club soda), and an N/A Painkiller built on Dole soft serve with creamy coconut and grated nutmeg. The standout is the No-Groni, a non-alcoholic Negroni riff made with Lyre's Rose botanical spirit, Giffard aperitif, Lucano N/A, lemon and Fee Brothers orange bitters. The venue is 21+ and was voted Best Chinatown Bar in Las Vegas Weekly's 2025 Readers' Choice awards.

venues.longDescription:
The Golden Tiki opened in July 2015 in a strip mall deep in the Spring Mountain Road corridor of Las Vegas Chinatown, the work of Branden Powers, a longtime figure in Las Vegas nightlife who had been creative director at the Hard Rock Hotel and a tiki devotee for far longer than that. What he built is less a bar than an indoor theme park for adults: a Polynesian-pop fantasy crossed with pirate mythology, divided into named zones including Headhunter Village, Mermaid Cove, Pirates' Lair and the Golden Tiki Lounge, with a seashell waterfall, animatronics that include a talking skeleton, and a collection of more than forty shrunken heads mounted around the room. Those heads are the bar's signature: miniature celebrity likenesses sculpted by Terry Barr, among them Marky Ramone, Carrot Top and Robin Leach. The bar is 21 and over, it has been open twenty-four hours a day since the day it opened, and by its own account it has never once closed since. In 2025 Las Vegas Weekly readers voted it Best Chinatown Bar.

The cocktail list is rum-forward and classicist, running through Navy Grogs and the rest of the tiki canon, but the reason it earns a place in a non-alcoholic directory is a standing Virgin Cocktails section that gets the same treatment as the rest of the menu rather than being three sodas listed as an afterthought. The lineup includes Tropical Vertigo (Kalinago Caribbean tea, cream of coconut, pineapple, lime, vanilla and grated cinnamon), the Coconut Pick-Me-Up (espresso, cream of coconut, vanilla and club soda), and an N/A Painkiller built on Dole soft serve with creamy coconut and grated nutmeg. The standout is the No-Groni, a zero-proof Negroni riff built from Lyre's Rose botanical spirit, Giffard aperitif, Lucano N/A, lemon and Fee Brothers orange bitters. Combined with the twenty-four-hour licence, that makes The Golden Tiki one of the very few rooms in the city where a properly built zero-proof tiki drink is available at four in the morning.
venues.pressQuote: a one-of-a-kind Chinatown hot spot
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Las Vegas Weekly Readers' Choice 2025 (Best Chinatown Bar)

venues.name: The Goldfinch
venues.description: The Goldfinch is a dual-purpose bar on South Broadway from Denver hospitality veteran Iain Chisholm, which opened in 2024 behind Upswell Studios at 1842 South Broadway and now runs as a coffee shop by day and a cocktail lounge by night — its own team describes the model as drawn from Thai drinking establishments, with mornings light and airy and evenings darker and moodier. The interior is a Hollywood Regency and ski lodge fusion: leather couches and velvet chairs on black-and-white checkered floors, chandeliers, gilded mirrors, a VIP booth and a planted patio. The current non-alcoholic offering is modest rather than extensive: the Greenhouse Rickey N/A (Seedlip Garden 108, agave, fresh lime, cucumber, soda) and a Sober Carpenter alcohol-free blonde ale on the happy hour list, an N/A Mimosa built on Lunetta Zero sparkling wine at brunch, and a full espresso, matcha and tea programme from 6:30am. DJs play downtempo house on weekends.

venues.longDescription:
The Goldfinch opened in 2024 at 1842 South Broadway, set back behind Upswell Studios in South Denver, from hospitality veteran Iain Chisholm, who previously worked on Americatus and DADA Art Bar and lives a few blocks away. The bar runs two shifts out of one room, a model the team says it took from Thai drinking establishments: it opens at 6:30am as a coffee shop, light and sun-filled, and turns over in the evening into something the owners describe as darker, moodier and a little electric. The design is a Hollywood Regency and ski lodge fusion, leather couches and velvet chairs against black-and-white checkered floors, with hanging chandeliers, gilded mirrors, framed digital art, a VIP booth and a planted patio. Rotating DJs play downtempo house through evening service, which makes weekend brunch a livelier event than the hour suggests.

For a non-drinker the honest picture is that the daytime programme is the stronger half. The coffee and tea list is properly built: a Blueberry Matcha of premium Japanese matcha shaken with house-made blueberry syrup and the milk of choice, a Honey Nut Cheerio Latte on house brown sugar and honey syrups, a White Chocolate Strawberry Latte, a Honey Chamomile Tea Latte, a matcha lemonade shaken with grapefruit, pineapple or lemon juice, plus chai, London Fog and loose-leaf tea. On the alcohol side the current menu carries a smaller zero-proof selection than the bar's press coverage implies: the Greenhouse Rickey N/A ($10) of Seedlip Garden 108, agave, fresh lime, cucumber and soda, and a Sober Carpenter alcohol-free craft blonde ale on the happy hour list, plus an N/A Mimosa ($12) built on Lunetta Zero sparkling wine with fresh pressed orange juice at brunch. Westword's January 1, 2026 Dry January round-up described a robust mocktail selection and named an orange dreamsicle and the Goldwing, a zero-proof version of the house signature with pineapple, lime, bell pepper habanero syrup and egg white; neither appears on the menu as published now. The practical read for a non-drinker is that the morning and afternoon shift is the reliable one: the room opens at 6:30am on weekdays and 9am at weekends, the coffee programme is genuinely built rather than bought in, and the evening zero-proof list is currently short.
venues.pressQuote: This cocktail bar debuted last year, bringing a more elevated atmosphere and a robust mocktail selection to South Broadway. Order its orange dreamsicle or the Goldwing, a zero-proof take on its signature drink, which features pineapple, lime, bell pepper habanero syrup and egg white.

venues.name: The Green Door
venues.description: The Green Door opened in April 2025 as Greater Cincinnati's first fully alcohol-free "dry" bar, created by founder Christian Perry-Watt and the team behind Kentucky Botanicals Co. Every drink starts zero-proof: fresh craft mocktails you can enjoy as-is or customize with kava, THC, CBD, adaptogens or blue lotus. The moody, speakeasy-inspired room fuses Art Deco and Art Nouveau, with signature pours like "That Lavender Haze" (blueberry, lavender, citrus) and "The Spicy Mock-arita" (mango, citrus, habanero), plus non-alcoholic riffs such as "Not Gin + Tonic" and "Whiskey-ish + Soda." There are also canned THC seltzers, kava seltzers and mushroom elixirs, a small bottle shop, and a calendar of live music, DJs and wellness events. It's a 21+ room, just across the river from downtown Cincinnati.
venues.longDescription:
The Green Door is Greater Cincinnati's first-ever dry bar, opening on April 18, 2025 in downtown Covington, just across the Ohio River from Cincinnati. It was created by Christian Perry-Watt and the team behind Kentucky Botanicals Co. as what the company calls a "new kind of night out" — a fully alcohol-free space where no one has to choose between going out and staying off the booze. The design leans into a Prohibition-era speakeasy fantasy, all moody low light and a fusion of Art Deco and Art Nouveau detailing, a deliberate wink at the fact that this time the "dry" bar is the whole point.

Every drink here begins zero-proof. The core menu is built around handcrafted mocktails that guests can order straight or have infused with functional add-ins — kava, THC, CBD, adaptogens or blue lotus. Signatures include "That Lavender Haze," a soft floral build of blueberry, lavender and citrus, and "The Spicy Mock-arita," a mango, citrus and habanero riff on a margarita, alongside zero-proof classics like "Not Gin + Tonic" and "Whiskey-ish + Soda" made with non-alcoholic spirits such as London High and Looner Spirits. Beyond the bar program there are canned THC seltzers, kava seltzers, mushroom elixirs, and a small bottle shop for taking product home.

The room is open Tuesday through Sunday and closed Mondays — Tue–Thu 4–9pm, Fri–Sat 4–11pm, and Sun 2–9pm — at 5 E 8th St, with regular live music, DJ sets and wellness workshops filling out the calendar (the bar even ran a full slate of programming for Dry January). One important honesty note: alcohol-free does not mean substance-free here. Because drinks can be infused with kava, THC and other actives, entry is 21+ and the venue posts "Sip Safely" guidance about medications, pregnancy and dosing. Come for a genuinely sober night out — just go in knowing the optional infusions are the house specialty.
venues.pressQuote: We wanted to create something indulgent but mindful — where every drink is an experience and every night out leaves you feeling amazing.

venues.name: The Green Zone
venues.description: The Green Zone is a Middle Eastern craft cocktail bar at 2226 18th Street NW in Adams Morgan, founded by Chris Hassaan Francke, who opened the permanent bi-level space in July 2018 after running it as a pop-up. It draws on Levantine and Iraqi flavours - Francke sources rare ingredients such as sour grapes from Lebanese markets and visits his Iraqi family in Lebanon - and pairs house cocktails with Middle Eastern small plates. Because it is inspired by a region where many people abstain from alcohol for religious reasons, the bar treats the non-alcoholic list as a true equal, typically keeping at least eight no-ABV options on at any time: a Royal Jallab, a zero-proof Garibaldi, a Halal Spritz on St. Agrestis Phony Negroni, a Zeroodeh Swizzle and frozen mint or cucumber lemonade. Open to 3am on Friday and Saturday.

venues.longDescription:
The Green Zone began as a pop-up and became a permanent bi-level bar at 2226 18th Street NW in July 2018, in the middle of the Adams Morgan strip. Its founder, Chris Hassaan Francke, built it around Levantine and Iraqi flavours and around a point of view - the bar has never been shy about the politics implied by its name - and he sources accordingly, buying rare ingredients like sour grapes from Lebanese markets and visiting his Iraqi family in Lebanon. The recognition has been sustained rather than a single burst: a Tales of the Cocktail Spirited Awards regional top ten in 2019, Washington City Paper's Best New Bar staff pick, Garden & Gun's South's Best New Bars, Conde Nast Traveler's fifteen best bars in Washington, and Eater DC's list of the city's essential bars.

The non-alcoholic programme here is not an accommodation, and the reason is structural. The bar draws on a region where a great many people do not drink for religious reasons, so building a serious alcohol-free list is simply part of doing the concept honestly. In practice that means at least eight no-ABV options at any given time, and drinks that are their own thing rather than subtractions. The Royal Jallab is built on jallab - a syrup of carob, dates, grape molasses and rose water - and topped with pine nuts, raisins and pistachios, so it arrives as something to eat as much as drink. The zero-proof Garibaldi pairs Stappi Bitter Red Soda with fresh orange juice, which gets the bitterness a real Garibaldi needs. The Halal Spritz uses St. Agrestis's bottled Phony Negroni with orange blossom water and a lemon twist. The Zeroodeh Swizzle runs lime, cardamom and rose over crushed ice, and the Saudi Spritz is built on Vimto with lemon and ginger beer. Mint or cucumber lemonade comes frozen or on ice, alongside fresh-squeezed pomegranate and orange juice, and many of the bar's alcoholic drinks can be made virgin on request.

Practical notes. This is a late bar: closed Monday, then 5pm to 2am Tuesday through Thursday, 5pm to 3am on Friday, 2pm to 3am on Saturday and 2pm to 2am on Sunday - among the latest alcohol-free-friendly options in the city. The Washington Post has twice highlighted its alcohol-free cocktails, including in a roundup of spots with outstanding alcohol-free drinks.
venues.pressQuote: This 18th Street bar serves up cocktails based around the flavors of various countries in the Middle East

venues.name: The Guild House
venues.description: The Guild House is Cameron Mitchell Restaurants' farm-to-table dining room on North High Street in the Short North, and was awarded One Michelin Key in 2024. Its beverage menu carries a printed section headed ZERO PROOF, which is what separates it from the many Columbus restaurants that will improvise something on request. The section runs six deep: Mionetto alcohol-removed sparkling wine from the Veneto by the glass or bottle, an Orange Spritz built on a spiritless aperitif and the same Mionetto, a Citrus Ginger made with Seedlip Grove 42, lime and candied ginger, a Blackberry Smash of blackberries, pomegranate and fresh citrus, an Espresso No-Tini using Lyre's coffee originale with fresh espresso, brown sugar and cinnamon, and a rotating Athletic Brewing non-alcoholic beer. Prices sit between $7 and $11.

venues.longDescription:
The Guild House sits at 624 North High Street in the Short North and was Cameron Mitchell Restaurants' first farm-to-table concept, working seasonal and local produce through a creative American menu across breakfast, lunch, brunch and dinner seven days a week. It was awarded One Michelin Key in 2024, and it is one of the few Columbus dining rooms serving a full breakfast service from 7am and still pouring cocktails at 10pm.

What earns it a place here is the printed ZERO PROOF heading on the beverage menu. Columbus has a great many restaurants where a bartender will happily build something without alcohol if asked; a named section means the drinks have been costed, trained and put in front of every guest without them having to raise the subject. The list carries six entries. Mionetto alcohol-removed sparkling wine from the Veneto is sold by the glass at $11 and by the bottle at $44 — a genuine bottle option, which matters for a table where one person is not drinking. The Orange Spritz at $9 builds a spiritless aperitif into the same Mionetto. Citrus Ginger at $10 uses Seedlip Grove 42 with lime and candied ginger. The Blackberry Smash at $9 is the fruit-forward option, blackberries with pomegranate and fresh citrus, and is the drink local roundups tend to name. The Espresso No-Tini at $10 uses Lyre's coffee originale with fresh espresso, brown sugar and cinnamon, which puts a proper after-dinner drink on the non-alcoholic side of the list rather than leaving it to coffee alone. A rotating Athletic Brewing non-alcoholic beer at under 0.5% ABV completes it at $7. The pricing is worth noting: nothing on the zero-proof list runs to full cocktail money. Worth adding that the restaurant's daypart range is itself useful here. Because The Guild House serves breakfast from 7am, lunch, brunch at weekends and dinner into the evening, the zero-proof list is available across the whole day rather than only from a bar shift — so an alcohol-free spritz or espresso build is orderable at a business lunch as readily as at dinner. Reservations are advisable at weekends.
venues.pressQuote: The Guild House has alcohol-free menu options for when you're headed to happy hour. Choose from a lemon tonic, cherry ginger, or their Blackberry Smash.

venues.name: The Haymaker
venues.description: The Haymaker is a downtown Raleigh cocktail bar on Fayetteville Street, open since 2017 and reopened in early 2026 under new owner Glenn Shriver after a short hiatus, and its menu carries a section it calls Pick-Your-Proof: six house cocktails that can be ordered at zero proof, half proof or full proof — the bar's own claim is that it was the first to offer such a menu, and Raleigh Magazine put the zero-proof price at $8 against $14 at full strength. The six run from Mama Said Knock You Out on beets, herbes de Provence and citrus to Hello, Nurse! on orange blossom and blue matcha and The Rabbit of Caerbannog on carrot, black pepper and honey, and the zero-proof versions are printed choices rather than favours. Open late — until two in the morning Thursday through Saturday — with shorter hours on Sunday and Monday.
