venues.longDescription:
The Monarch Club occupies the penthouse of the Metropolitan Building, a neo-Gothic tower built in 1925 (long known as Detroit's "Jewelers' Building") that sat vacant for decades before its restoration into the Element Detroit hotel. The rooftop bar takes its cues from Detroit's mid-century rooftop lounges, with deep blue, red, and gold interiors, leather seating, and three outdoor terraces — The Tower, East Court, and West Court — that open onto 360-degree views of downtown, Comerica Park, and the Detroit River.

The non-alcoholic list is built as its own named section, "Zero Proof Libations," rather than a single token mocktail. The Golden Court mixes guava purée, pineapple juice, lavender syrup, honey, ginger ale, and Tajín; the Pea Tea SD is butterfly pea tea with lemon juice and honey; and the Root Chakra combines lemon, ginger, lavender, and tonic water. Athletic Brewing's NA IPA is also on offer for anyone who wants a zero-proof beer to go with the skyline view. Detroit Metro Times has separately singled out the bar's mocktail program in its roundup of the city's best non-alcoholic drink spots.

Downtown Detroit's rooftop scene is compact — the Monarch Club, along with a handful of hotel bars nearby, gives visitors a view-driven option that also takes sober and moderation-minded guests seriously, with dedicated non-alcoholic drinks built to the same standard as the cocktail list, not a syrup-and-soda afterthought.
venues.pressQuote: The Monarch Club might be known for its rooftop views of the city, but the cocktail bar has a selection of mocktails like the Coco Lassi, a fruity and spicy coconut drink.

venues.name: The Monroe
venues.description: A New American restaurant on the ground floor of The Julian Apartments in Creative Village, from Good Salt Restaurant Group owners Jason and Sue Chin, Orlando's first James Beard Award finalists (2025, Outstanding Restaurateur). The Monroe pairs nostalgic comfort food with a rotating, printed mocktail section built around house-made syrups and teas.
signatureDrinks: Pear-anoid Punch (Thai tea, orgeat, pear nectar, maple, lemon, ginger beer)
Chai Hard (oolong chai, turmeric, lemongrass-ginger honey, condensed coconut milk, cardamom-lime foam)
Pear-anormal Activity (lemongrass ginger tea, pear, almond, honey, lemon)
The Jackie Daytona (blood orange tea, cranberry, pomegranate, pineapple, ginger beer)
venues.longDescription:
The Monroe is a 4,000-square-foot dining and entertainment venue on the ground floor of The Julian Apartments in Downtown Orlando's Creative Village, featuring a main dining room, bar, lounge, semi-private dining area, backyard patio, and daytime coffee bar. The restaurant is named for Dr. William 'Monroe' Wells, a civil rights leader and physician who built the neighboring Wells'Built Hotel and South Street Casino (construction permitted in 1924 and 1926) to house African American travelers and touring entertainers during segregation, when no other lodging was available to them in Central Florida; the hotel is now the Wells'Built Museum of African American History and Culture in historic Parramore, which The Monroe supports.

The Monroe is the fourth concept from Good Salt Restaurant Group, led by owners Jason and Sue Chin, who in 2025 became Orlando's first-ever James Beard Award finalists, recognized in the Outstanding Restaurateur category alongside their other concepts (Seito Sushi, The Osprey, Reyes Mezcaleria, Sparrow Wine Bar, and Osteria Ester). Executive Chef Nikk Burton, raised in Queens and formerly of Disney's California Grill and Boardwalk Resort, runs the kitchen's nostalgic, childhood-inspired menu. The Monroe's own design and hospitality have picked up separate recognition too: Orlando Magazine named it 'Best Vibe' in its 2023 Dining Awards, and it has appeared on Eater's and Time Out's best-of-Orlando restaurant roundups.

The bar team maintains a rotating printed mocktail section alongside its coffee, tea, and cocktail programs. Recent seasonal builds have included the Pear-anoid Punch (Thai tea, orgeat, pear nectar, maple, lemon, ginger beer) and the Chai Hard (oolong chai, turmeric, lemongrass-ginger honey, condensed coconut milk, cardamom-lime foam), alongside the Pear-anormal Activity (lemongrass ginger tea, pear, almond, honey, lemon) and The Jackie Daytona (blood orange tea, cranberry, pomegranate, pineapple, ginger beer).
venues.pressQuote: The Monroe offers a rotating selection of mocktails, cocktails and craft beer throughout the year.

venues.name: The Mood Health & Wellness
venues.description: The Mood is a kava bar and botanical shop on Mundy Drive in Fishers, established in 2021 and the Indianapolis metro's first dedicated kava retailer. It was founded by a retired Eli Lilly immunopharmacology researcher, Dr. Hatfield, alongside Taylor Hatfield, and the front of the shop sells herbal supplements while a kava bar runs at the back with a free-to-play arcade and lounge attached. No alcohol is served. It is important to know what is on offer before you go: alongside kava the shop sells kratom-adjacent botanicals including blue lotus, kanna, klip dagga and mad honey, plus CBD, hemp-derived delta products and vapes. Kava contains no alcohol but is psychoactive and sedating, and the room is 21+.
venues.longDescription:
The Mood opened in 2021 on Mundy Drive in Fishers and bills itself as Indianapolis's first kava retail provider and educator — a claim that holds up, since the metro had no dedicated kava room before it. The founder is a retired Eli Lilly scientist, Dr. Hatfield, whose thirty-year career was in immunopharmacology and bioinformatics; he runs the shop with Taylor Hatfield, who came out of the e-cigarette and hemp trades. That pairing shows in how the place is set up: the front is a well-lit retail floor of herbal supplements and hemp products, and the back is a kava bar with a lounge and a free-to-play arcade, hung with work by Indianapolis artists.

Kava is served by the shell in rotating flavours — piña colada and pumpkin spice among them — and the staff are unusually willing to walk a first-timer through strength, onset and what the numbness on your tongue means. Nothing here contains alcohol. But this is not an alcohol-free café, and the distinction matters for anyone in recovery: kava is psychoactive and mildly sedating, and the same counter also sells blue lotus, kanna, klip dagga, mad honey, CBD, hemp-derived delta-8 and delta-9 products and vapes. The room is 21-and-over for that reason. Taken on its own terms it is one of very few places in the metro where you can sit for two hours in the evening, drink something with an effect, play a cabinet arcade game and never be offered a beer — which, since Memento Zero Proof closed in Fishers in 2024, is a shorter list than it was. Hours run midday to evening seven days a week, to 8pm on weeknights and 9pm on Friday and Saturday, which is early for a bar substitute but late for a shop. Two further notes for anyone weighing it up. First, kava has a learning curve: the taste is earthy and bitter, the effect is gradual, and the staff will tell you to drink a shell and wait rather than order three. Second, because the retail floor and the bar share a room, the atmosphere is closer to a wellness shop with seating than to a lounge, and the crowd skews toward people who came in for a specific product. If what you want is a fully alcohol-free room with no psychoactives in it at all, the cat cafés and Orangily are the better fit; if you want an evening drink that does something, this is the metro's only real option.

venues.name: The Muddy Root Kava Cafe | Gulfport
venues.description: The Gulfport branch of The Muddy Root runs 8am to midnight, seven days a week, on Gulfport Boulevard — a few blocks from both Low Tide Kava Bar and Sober Bar, making this small Pinellas beach town one of the densest concentrations of alcohol-free rooms per head anywhere in the United States. The group is explicit that it exists to offer alcohol-free alternatives, and the menu covers kava, botanical teas, coffee, mocktails and baked goods across the whole day. IMPORTANT for readers in recovery: kratom tea is prominently featured here, with its own dedicated section on the group's menu. Kratom acts on opioid receptors and carries dependence and withdrawal risk that kava does not. The two sit side by side, so order deliberately.
venues.longDescription:
The Gulfport branch of The Muddy Root runs 8am to midnight, seven days a week, on Gulfport Boulevard, and its location produces one of the more remarkable facts in this entire directory. Gulfport is a small Pinellas beach town of roughly 12,000 people. Within a few blocks of each other it supports this room, Low Tide Kava Bar, and Sober Bar on Beach Boulevard — three dedicated alcohol-free venues. That is very likely the highest concentration of alcohol-free rooms per head of population anywhere in the United States, and it is a useful corrective to the assumption that this category only works in large cities.

The group behind it operates five Florida sites and states its purpose directly: it exists to offer alcohol-free alternatives. The menu is genuinely all-day — kava, botanical teas, coffee, mocktails and fresh baked goods — which suits a small town where the same room has to work as a morning cafe and an evening social space because there is not enough population to support two separate businesses doing each.

Kava is the ground root of Piper methysticum, a shrub native to the South Pacific islands, prepared as a cold water infusion and drunk socially across Fiji, Vanuatu, Tonga and Samoa for roughly three thousand years. It contains no alcohol. It tastes earthy and bitter, numbs the lips and tongue on the first mouthful, and is mildly sedative rather than intoxicating in the way alcohol is. Kava exhibits reverse tolerance, meaning regular drinkers typically need less rather than more, so a first visit is best paced across an hour or two.

Gulfport itself is worth the trip for anyone in the Tampa Bay area who is not drinking. It is walkable, it has a genuine arts scene, and the three venues sit close enough together to make an evening of moving between them — which is the ordinary shape of a night out, and something almost impossible to replicate elsewhere without alcohol.

The standing disclosure for this group applies here in full. Kratom tea is prominently featured, with its own dedicated section on the menu alongside the kava. Kratom is the leaf of a Southeast Asian tree, Mitragyna speciosa, whose principal alkaloids act on the opioid receptors; regular use produces tolerance and a real withdrawal syndrome, several US states prohibit it outright, and concentrated 7-hydroxymitragynine products derived from it are the subject of active federal scheduling action. Kava has no comparable dependence profile. The two sit side by side at similar prices, so order deliberately and ask what is in the cup — a question the staff at this group are used to answering.

venues.name: The Muddy Root Kava Cafe | Orlando
venues.description: The Orlando outpost of the five-site Muddy Root group sits on Collegiate Way, directly in the University of Central Florida corridor, and runs 10am to midnight daily with a 2am close on Friday. UCF is the largest university in the country by enrolment, and a late alcohol-free room on its doorstep does real work for students who do not drink. The group positions itself explicitly as an alcohol-free alternative, with kava, botanical teas, coffee, mocktails and fresh baked goods across the day. IMPORTANT for readers in recovery: kratom tea has its own promoted section on this menu. It acts on opioid receptors and carries dependence and withdrawal risk that kava does not, so read the headers before you order.
venues.longDescription:
The Orlando outpost of The Muddy Root sits on Collegiate Way, directly in the University of Central Florida corridor, and runs 10am to midnight daily with a 2am close on Friday. UCF is the largest university in the United States by enrolment, with more than 65,000 students, and a late alcohol-free room on its doorstep does a specific and under-appreciated job: student social life is organised almost entirely around drinking, and the people who do not drink — for reasons of recovery, religion, medication or simple preference — are the ones with nowhere to go at 11pm on a Thursday.

The group behind it runs five Florida sites, with the flagship in Tampa and further rooms in Clearwater, St. Petersburg and Gulfport. Its positioning is explicit rather than implied: it exists to offer alcohol-free alternatives, and it says so. The menu is genuinely all-day — kava, botanical teas, coffee, mocktails and fresh baked goods — which is the right shape for a campus location where the same room needs to work as a morning study spot and a late-night hangout.

Kava is the ground root of Piper methysticum, a shrub native to the South Pacific islands, prepared as a cold water infusion and drunk socially across Fiji, Vanuatu, Tonga and Samoa for roughly three thousand years. It contains no alcohol. It tastes earthy and bitter, numbs the lips and tongue on the first mouthful, and is mildly sedative rather than intoxicating in the way alcohol is. Kava exhibits reverse tolerance, meaning regular drinkers usually need less rather than more to feel it, so a first visit rewards a slow pace across an hour or two rather than a single fast serving — advice worth taking seriously in a student area where the instinct may be to treat it like a shot.

Flamingo Kava sits a few hundred metres away on Corporate Boulevard, so the UCF corridor now has two alcohol-free rooms within walking distance of each other, which is more than most of Orlando proper manages.

One disclosure has to be prominent rather than buried, and the group's own menu makes it easy to state. Kratom tea is a promoted category here with its own dedicated section, not an incidental listing. Kratom is the leaf of Mitragyna speciosa, a Southeast Asian tree, and its principal alkaloids act on the opioid receptors; regular use produces tolerance and a real withdrawal syndrome, several US states ban it outright, and concentrated 7-hydroxymitragynine products face active federal scheduling. Kava has no comparable dependence profile. Read the section headers before ordering, and ask if you are unsure — the two sit on the same board at similar prices.

venues.name: The Muddy Root Kava Cafe | Tampa
venues.description: The Muddy Root's Parkedge Drive room opens at 7am on weekdays and runs to midnight every night of the week, and the group positions itself explicitly as an alcohol-free alternative rather than as a cafe with a sideline. The menu spans kava, botanical teas, coffee, mocktails and fresh baked goods, which makes it one of the more complete all-day propositions in the Tampa kava scene. It is the flagship of a five-site Florida group with further rooms in Clearwater, St. Petersburg, Gulfport and Orlando. IMPORTANT for readers in recovery: kratom tea is a prominent, separately promoted part of this menu, not an aside. Kratom acts on opioid receptors and carries dependence and withdrawal risk that kava does not — read the section headers before you order.
venues.longDescription:
The Parkedge Drive room is the flagship of The Muddy Root, a five-site Florida group with further locations in Clearwater, St. Petersburg, Gulfport and Orlando. It opens at 7am on weekdays and runs to midnight every night of the week, which gives it one of the longest trading days of any alcohol-free venue in Tampa Bay.

What distinguishes the group is that it positions itself explicitly as an alcohol-free alternative rather than as a cafe with a botanical sideline. That framing shapes the menu, which is unusually complete for the category: kava, botanical teas, coffee, mocktails and fresh baked goods. A room that can serve breakfast, a working afternoon, and a late evening from the same counter is doing something more useful than a specialist kava bar that opens at 4pm — particularly for anyone in early recovery, for whom the empty hours are often the daytime ones rather than the night.

Kava is the ground root of Piper methysticum, a shrub native to the South Pacific islands, prepared as a cold water infusion and drunk socially across Fiji, Vanuatu, Tonga and Samoa for roughly three thousand years. It contains no alcohol. It tastes earthy and bitter, numbs the lips and tongue on the first mouthful, and is mildly sedative rather than intoxicating in the way alcohol is. Kava exhibits reverse tolerance, so regular drinkers usually need less rather than more to feel it, and a first visit rewards a slow pace across an hour or two.

The location, on the north-eastern edge of Tampa near Temple Terrace, puts it within reach of the University of South Florida area, where Twist and Insomnia ISG cover similar ground. Between them that quadrant of the city is now well served, which was not true a few years ago.

One thing has to be prominent rather than buried, and to the group's credit its own menu makes it easy to state accurately. Kratom tea is a promoted category here with its own dedicated section, not an incidental listing — the group's site gives it a full explanatory block describing it as a versatile herbal tea, positioned alongside kava as a main beverage category. Kratom is the leaf of Mitragyna speciosa, a Southeast Asian tree, and its principal alkaloids act on the opioid receptors; regular use produces tolerance and a genuine withdrawal syndrome, several US states ban it outright, and its concentrated 7-hydroxymitragynine derivatives are the subject of active federal scheduling. Kava carries no comparable dependence profile, and a great many people choose kava specifically because of that. Read the section headers before you order, and ask if the answer is not obvious.

venues.name: The Neighbors
venues.description: A neighborhood store, cocktail lounge, kitchen and event space on the second floor of Audubon Park's East End Market, blending a Florida-maker retail shop with a full bar. The Neighbors runs a dedicated zero-proof cocktail section built around Seedlip, and its Lavender Pomojito won Orlando Weekly's 'Best Zero-Proof Cocktail' in the 2025 Best of Orlando awards.
signatureDrinks: You're Turning Violet, Violet! (blueberry, ginger, green tea, Aplós Ease non-alcoholic spirit)
Hot Spa (Seedlip non-alcoholic gin, lavender syrup, jalapeño syrup, vegan Fee Foam)
Theros (peach-infused oat milk, Seedlip Garden, rosemary)
Totes McOats (oat milk, Seedlip Garden, orange, lavender)
venues.longDescription:
The Neighbors occupies the second floor of East End Market, a former church on Corrine Drive that was converted into a food hall in 2013 and has since become an anchor of the Audubon Park Garden District. The Neighbors itself opened on November 5, 2021, a joint project of Freehand Goods owners Seth Daniels and Jacob Zepf, Domu owner Sean 'Sonny' Nguyen, and East End Market owner John Rife, pairing a retail shop with a cocktail lounge and kitchen. The upstairs shop stocks goods from Florida-based small makers, and the bar program is built to celebrate Orlando's individual neighborhoods.

Owner Jacob Zepf has described the alcohol-free program's growth from a niche afterthought into a core offering: 'We started with just two on the menu and now offer a full page of mocktails, non-alcoholic beers, sodas and some canned CBD beverages, as well.' Zepf has singled out Seedlip as the non-alcoholic spirit that mixes best for the bar's builds.

The menu's headliner is the Lavender Pomojito (lavender, pomegranate, mint, basil), which won Orlando Weekly's 2025 Readers' Choice award for Best Zero-Proof Cocktail in the Best of Orlando awards. Other named zero-proof drinks include You're Turning Violet, Violet! (blueberry, ginger, green tea, Aplós Ease non-alcoholic spirit), Hot Spa (Seedlip non-alcoholic gin, lavender syrup, jalapeño syrup, vegan Fee Foam), WPV (celery and grapefruit soda), Zephyr (ginger beer, lime, cinnamon), Theros (peach-infused oat milk, Seedlip Garden, rosemary), and Totes McOats (oat milk, Seedlip Garden, orange, lavender), alongside rotating canned mocktails and non-alcoholic beer in the retail cooler.
venues.pressQuote: We started with just two on the menu and now offer a full page of mocktails, non-alcoholic beers, sodas and some canned CBD beverages, as well.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Jacob Zepf, owner of The Neighbors

venues.name: The New Oxford
venues.description: The New Oxford is a multi-award-winning independent free house on Bexley Square in Salford, a restored 1830s corner pub famed among CAMRA members for its 11 handpumps of cask ale and a cellar of more than fifty Belgian beers. Its no-and-low range is unusually deep for a traditional real-ale house: Guinness 0.0 pours on draught alongside Erdinger Alkoholfrei, Asahi 0.0 and booze-free ciders, so a non-drinker is never left with a lone soft drink. It is a genuinely beer-led room where the alcohol-free choice sits on equal footing with the cask.
venues.longDescription:
The New Oxford is an independent free house at 11 Bexley Square, in the Chapel Street quarter of Salford that has become one of Greater Manchester's most concentrated stretches of independent food and drink. The pub dates from the 1830s and trades as a two-roomed corner house; a careful refurbishment restored much of its Victorian character — bottle-green banquette seating, an original 1800s clock with gold detailing and an early-1900s stained-glass window — while opening up the interior and converting the former kitchen into a snug. It is one of Salford's most decorated real-ale pubs, a repeat CAMRA award winner, with a central bar carrying 11 handpumps and over 20 fonts.

Beer is the whole point here. The cask line-up runs to nine changing beers plus two regulars — the house Moorhouse's New Oxford Pale Ale and Thornbridge Jaipur — sourced regionally with at least one dark beer usually on, and it is backed by a celebrated stock of more than fifty Belgian beers. The pub holds mini beer festivals at the end of most months, hosts live music at weekends, is dog-friendly, and spills out onto a partitioned drinking area in Bexley Square itself. It opens from noon daily, until midnight most nights and 1am on Fridays and Saturdays.

What sets it apart for non-drinkers is that the alcohol-free offering is treated with the same seriousness as the cask and Belgian lists. Guinness 0.0 pours on draught — a genuine tap pour rather than a can — alongside Erdinger Alkoholfrei, the classic Bavarian wheat beer in its de-alcoholised form, and Asahi 0.0, with booze-free ciders rounding out the range. Manchester's Finest singled the pub out in a January 2026 round-up of the city's best alcohol-free drinking, calling the offering "comprehensive". In a traditional 11-handpump free house that kind of depth is rare, and it means someone off the drink can settle in for the evening on a properly built round rather than a token soft drink.
venues.pressQuote: Their alcohol-free offering is just as impressive, with a comprehensive offering including Guinness 0.0 on tap, Erdinger Alkoholfrei, Asahi 0.0 and booze-free ciders too.

venues.name: The Nixer
venues.description: Billed as the Valley's first dedicated non-alcoholic bar, The Nixer (from Everything NA, LLC) is a craft zero-proof operation built into a repurposed horse-and-utility trailer that pops up across Phoenix at markets, concerts, and dry happy hours, with a home base on Grand Avenue. Rather than soda-and-juice afterthoughts, its bartenders — 'nixologists' — build layered NA drinks, many infused with adaptogens, nootropics, functional mushrooms, and CBD. The Nixer also works private events and corporate functions and offers ready-to-drink options, making it the metro's most visible flag-carrier for a genuine alcohol-free night out. Because it is mobile, check the Instagram for where it is parked before setting out — the Grand Avenue address is a home base rather than a nightly guarantee.
venues.longDescription:
The Nixer is a bar built into a repurposed horse-and-utility trailer, which sounds like a gimmick and functions as a solution. Phoenix had no dedicated alcohol-free bar; opening one as fixed premises means signing a lease against a market nobody had proved existed. Putting it on wheels meant the bar could go to where the people already were — markets, concerts, dry happy hours, wellness events, private parties — and let demand accumulate before bricks did. It is billed as the Valley's first dedicated non-alcoholic bar, operating as Everything NA, LLC, with a home base on Grand Avenue in the arts district.

The drinks are the argument. Its bartenders work under the name "nixologists", and the builds are layered rather than sweet — many of them infused with adaptogens, nootropics, functional mushrooms or CBD, which places the bar in the functional-beverage tradition rather than the mocktail one. The distinction matters to the audience: a person who has stopped drinking is usually not looking for fruit juice in a nice glass but for something that occupies the same place in an evening, with some of the same weight and ritual. Alongside the trailer the operation runs private-event and corporate catering and sells ready-to-drink options, which is how a mobile bar makes a year work in a city where outdoor events stop in June.

One thing this listing deliberately does not do is name an owner. The Nixer was co-founded by Tamara Wright and Bradley Bridwell, and reporting indicates it has since been acquired from its original owners — but the date and current ownership are not confirmed from a primary source, so no name is stated as current here.

Practical notes: because it is mobile, check the Instagram before travelling — the trailer's location changes, and the Grand Avenue address is a base rather than a guarantee of service on any given night. Everything poured is alcohol-free. A number of the builds contain psychoactive botanicals — adaptogens, functional mushrooms, CBD — so alcohol-free is not the same as substance-free, and it is worth asking what is in a drink before ordering it if that distinction matters to you.
venues.pressQuote: They co-founded The Nixer, a mobile dry bar that pops up at events and meetings throughout the Greater Phoenix area, offering booze-free beverage catering

venues.name: The Old Bar
venues.description: The Old Bar is a beloved live-music pub on Johnston Street in Fitzroy, open seven nights a week with gigs every night. In February 2026 it became one of just five Melbourne venues chosen to launch Heaps Normal's Original Draught - Australia's first non-alcoholic beer engineered specifically for tap - so gig-goers can order a fresh-poured alcohol-free lager at the same bar as everyone else. The NA anchor here is that Heaps Normal tap, a crisp Aussie-style lager, rather than a broad zero-proof list.
signatureDrinks: Heaps Normal Original Draught - non-alcoholic crisp contemporary Aussie lager, brewed with low-bitterness noble hops and toasted malt, poured fresh from the tap
venues.longDescription:
The Old Bar has been a fixture of Fitzroy's live-music scene for more than two decades, occupying a shopfront pub at 74-76 Johnston Street with a front bar, a back band room and The Old Bar Gallery upstairs. It runs gigs seven nights a week - single launches, EP releases, residencies and afternoon sets - and is regularly named among Melbourne's best small live-music venues. It's open 3pm-3am daily and is an 18+ room, with a nightly happy hour on pots from 3pm-8pm.

In February 2026, Heaps Normal picked The Old Bar as one of only five Melbourne venues - alongside Beermash in Collingwood, The Edinburgh Castle in Brunswick, Huzzah in Glen Iris and Brick Lane Market - to launch its Original Draught, the brand's first non-alcoholic beer brewed for kegs rather than cans. The launch on 20 February 2026 came with free pours from 5pm-7pm. Original Draught is a crisp, contemporary Aussie lager brewed with low-bitterness noble hops and toasted malt for an amber hue, tuned so its freezing point and mouthfeel hold up through a tap line.

For anyone who wants the pub-gig ritual without the alcohol, that tap is the draw: a fresh-poured alcohol-free lager in a proper glass, ordered at the same bar as the beer drinkers. Heaps Normal is an Australian NA-beer pioneer, and The Old Bar putting it on draught - poured, not cracked from a can in the fridge - makes it one of the few Melbourne live-music rooms where the non-alcoholic option comes off the tap.
venues.pressQuote: Serving it through the tap, it does really change the mouthfeel and the presentation.

venues.name: The Old Gold
venues.description: The Old Gold is a neighborhood whiskey bar and restaurant in North Portland's Overlook district, open since 2011 on N Killingsworth Street. It's best known for a sprawling whiskey list, a full food menu, and a craft cocktail program, and was named one of "Portland's Best Neighborhood Bars" by The Oregonian. Alongside its spirited menu, the bar keeps a genuine, named non-alcoholic cocktail list built on premium zero-proof ingredients: the Pathfinder amaro analog anchors the Peppino Garibaldi (a Garibaldi-style build with grenadine standing in for Campari), and Drømme Calm appears in lower-intervention drinks like the Prince Valium (a whiskey-free Gold Rush) and the Not Toddy. The zero-proof cocktails — also including the Lady Luck and Ginger Cooler — get the same care as the alcoholic ones, and NA beer options include Athletic Brewing. The bar is all-ages before 9pm daily.

venues.longDescription:
The Old Gold is a whiskey bar and restaurant at 2105 N Killingsworth Street in the Overlook neighbourhood, and it tells its own origin story plainly: we tried to open the Old Gold in 2006, and we actually opened the Old Gold in 2011. The five years in between were spent, in the bar's words, plotting and scheming and dreaming up a way to open a bar in its little corner of North Portland. Willamette Week reported in May 2016 that Ezra Caraeff had quit his post as the Portland Mercury's music editor after eleven years to open the place, and described a room where the focus rests squarely on the immense library of international whiskeys behind the bar, accessible via library ladder. There are whiskey flights, whiskey-and-beer pairings and whiskey-education classes, plus a front patio and a kitchen running hand-popped popcorn in five seasonings, chickpea-battered buffalo cauliflower, an elk burger with bourbon bacon jam, a panko katsu chicken sandwich and a vegan tofu banh mi.

For a whiskey bar, the zero-proof bench is unusually deep, and it is properly headed "Non-Alcoholic Cocktails" on the menu rather than buried under soft drinks. Peppino Garibaldi ($10) is a Garibaldi-style build using Pathfinder non-alcoholic amaro with orange juice and grenadine, served tall. Two drinks use Drømme Calm: the Not Toddy ($13) with honey syrup, lemon, orange juice, cinnamon and nutmeg, and Prince Valium ($12) with lemon and honey syrup over a large cube. Lady Luck ($8) is grapefruit, lemon, rosemary syrup, peach bitters and soda, and the Ginger Cooler ($6) pairs lime, honey syrup and black walnut bitters under ginger beer in a pint glass — with an honest note beside it offering to add Mellow Corn and make it a cocktail for $12. A separate non-alcoholic beer list carries Athletic Brewing Golden Ale, RationAle West Coast IPA and Happy Mountain ginger kombucha at $6 each. Usefully for families and under-21s, the bar states no age restrictions before 9pm daily, and happy hour runs Monday to Friday from 3 to 5pm.

venues.name: The Open Road
venues.description: The Open Road is an alcohol-free bottle shop on Penn Avenue in Garfield, founded by Mel Babitz and widely described as the country's oldest non-alcoholic specialty retailer. It began as a Dry January pop-up inside a downtown coffee shop in January 2020, took a storefront in Allentown in March 2022, and moved to the larger Garfield space — with room for an on-premise bar — in August 2024. Babitz says the shelves hold over 400 non-alcoholic beers, wines, spirits and ready-to-drink cocktails, with a deliberate emphasis on Pennsylvania producers including Jackworth, Two Frays, Cinderlands and Arsenal Cider House. IMPORTANT FOR ANYONE AVOIDING ALL INTOXICANTS: by the owner's own account roughly half the store is functional beverages rather than plain alcohol-free ones, and that half includes hemp-derived THC and CBD drinks, kava and adaptogenic mushroom products. Examples carried include a 10mg THC seltzer, a 20mg CBD seltzer, a hemp-and-lion's-mane soda at 3mg THC, and a kava spirit at 150mg kavalactones per serving. Everything is labelled, but alcohol-free is not the same as inert here — read the can.
venues.longDescription:
The Open Road began in January 2020 as a Dry January pop-up bar inside a downtown coffee shop, which makes it one of the oldest non-alcoholic specialty retailers in the country. Mel Babitz started it for a straightforward reason, and has said so plainly: she personally cannot drink alcohol, it does not get along with her body, and the project came from being in her twenties, wanting to go out and still have fun and even have a drink while she was at it. The pop-up became an Allentown storefront in March 2022 and moved to Penn Avenue in Garfield in August 2024, into a space a little over double the size with room to open an on-premise bar. The shelves hold over four hundred non-alcoholic beers, wines, spirits and ready-to-drink cocktails, and the buying is notably local: Jackworth, Two Frays, Cinderlands and Arsenal Cider House all sit on them. As Babitz points out, Two Frays is still the only craft brewery in Pennsylvania making non-alcoholic beer.

One thing has to be said clearly, because the shop's name and category would lead you to assume otherwise. This is an alcohol-free shop, not an intoxicant-free one. Babitz's own description is that half the store is dedicated to functional beverages that actually do something to your body — caffeinated iced teas, nootropics, adaptogenic mushrooms like lion's mane and reishi, and hemp-based drinks with CBD and THC. Those are real doses: a mango THC seltzer at 10mg of hemp-derived delta-9, a lemon CBD seltzer at 20mg, a hemp-and-adaptogen soda carrying 3mg THC with 6mg CBD and 2,200mg of lion's mane, a kava spirit at 150mg of kavalactones a serving. Every one of them is printed 0.0% ABV, which is true and is exactly the point of confusion. If you are avoiding alcohol only, this is the best-stocked room in Pennsylvania for you. If you are in recovery and avoiding intoxicants generally, you can still shop here happily — but read the label rather than the ABV, and ask, because the staff know precisely what is in everything.
venues.pressQuote: the country's oldest nonalcoholic specialty retailer, having opened in January 2020

venues.name: The Passport Cocktail & Wine Bar
venues.description: The Passport began as Pour Decisions STL, a mobile bar launched in 2020 by married duo Javia Gilliam-Sanford, a certified sommelier, and mixologist Kaje Sanford. After a hit two-year run downtown, the pair relaunched their travel-themed cocktail and wine bar in a two-story Delmar Loop space in November 2025. The globetrotting menu carries a dedicated Spirit Free section — ten alcohol-free cocktails built on Lyre's non-alcoholic spirits, from the yuzu-spiked Japanese Water to a zero-proof Zombie, Mai Tai, and Sicilian Margarita. With vintage mid-century furniture, an upstairs Equinox Lounge, and a sommelier-run wine club, it's one of St. Louis's most polished settings for a spirit-free night out.

venues.longDescription:
The Passport grew out of Pour Decisions STL, the mobile-bar company that certified sommelier Javia Gilliam-Sanford and mixologist Kaje Sanford launched in 2020. The husband-and-wife team opened their first brick-and-mortar in September 2024 at 1321 Washington Avenue downtown, filling the former Whisky on Washington space with photos from their travels and thrifted mid-century modern furniture. The bar's popularity outgrew the room: in November 2025 they relaunched The Passport in a two-story space at 6275 Delmar in the Delmar Loop, adding a kitchen for shareable small plates for the first time and an upstairs ruby-red Equinox Lounge that hosts wine-club gatherings and Vino and Vinyl Wednesday sessions.

The zero-proof program is a fixture, not a seasonal stunt. The current menu's Spirit Free section runs ten cocktails deep, all built on Lyre's non-alcoholic spirits: the Japanese Water (Lyre's agave spirit, elderflower syrup, fresh lime, sparkling yuzu), a Clover Club shaken with egg whites and raspberry, tiki-leaning Zombie and Mai Tai builds, a Sicilian Margarita with Lyre's Amaretti, a Cuba Libre, an Aperol-style spritz with Lyre's Italian Spritz and No-Secco, plus alcohol-free takes on the Old Fashioned, Margarita, and French 75. The lineup debuted as a Dry January menu in 2025 — Sauce Magazine highlighted its spirit-free Old Fashioned and Margarita — and St. Louis Magazine's relaunch coverage noted a mocktail lineup that spans from Japan to the Caribbean.

The Passport has drawn steady coverage from Sauce Magazine, Feast Magazine, and St. Louis Magazine since opening, first as a downtown 'first look' and again for the Loop relaunch. Expect a cozy, living-room feel with modern disco and R&B on the speakers, signature cocktails like From Mykonos, With Love and the caviar-olive Golden Martini for drinking companions, and a bottle program and monthly wine club curated by Gilliam-Sanford. It opens evenings Wednesday through Saturday, with reservations available online — an easy, dressed-up option for mixed groups where the spirit-free list gets the same craft as everything else.
venues.pressQuote: This January, The Passport Cocktail Bar and Bottle Shop invites guests to savor bold, buzz-free flavors with its new spirit-free cocktail menu.

venues.name: The Pearl
venues.description: A Central 9th Vietnamese street-food restaurant and cocktail bar opened in spring 2022 by chef-owner Tommy Nguyen, who rolled sushi at Takashi for years and helped open Rye, Post Office Place and Alibi's taco program before launching his own homage to his mother's cooking. The Southeast-Asian-inspired drink program extends to the non-alcoholic side: City Cast Salt Lake readers named The Pearl's bartender's-choice mocktails the best in Salt Lake City. It's a lively, no-reservations, 21+ spot with one of the city's best warm-weather patios, named one of Salt Lake magazine's 19 Best Restaurants of 2025.
venues.address: 917 S 200 W, Salt Lake City, UT 84101
venues.longDescription:
Tommy Nguyen's menu blends new and traditional Vietnamese flavors with bites like banh mi, hamachi crudo and caramel pork belly, plus a Sunday-night pho service and weekend brunch; Gastronomic Salt Lake City credited the kitchen with upping the ante for Utah bar food.

The cocktail list leans hard on Southeast-Asian aromatics, and that same care carries to the alcohol-free pours. Because the bartender's-choice mocktail is improvised on the spot, regulars treat it as a small surprise — different each visit — making The Pearl a reliable stop for anyone skipping booze without skipping the bar.
venues.pressQuote: Time and time again, The Pearl has the best mocktails in all of Salt Lake City. You can request the bartender special and they'll put something delicious together, each time different than the last. It's always a treat!
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Katie C., reader pick in City Cast Salt Lake
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: City Cast Salt Lake, "The Best Mocktails in Salt Lake," 2025

venues.name: The Penrose
venues.description: The Penrose calls itself the Upper East Local, and it backs that up with something almost no neighbourhood gastropub bothers with: a properly built list of eleven named non-alcoholic cocktails, published alongside the alcoholic ones rather than buried. Express Yourself is its espresso martini, Garden Tonic its zero-proof G&T, Peach Fuzz a boozeless bellini, Good Vibrations a no-alcohol negroni sbagliato, and Sunday Kinda Love a virgin bloody mary; there is also Lyre's non-alcoholic prosecco by the glass, plus NA beer. It serves alcohol too — this is a full bar, not an alcohol-free room — but it opens at 11:30am and runs to 4am daily, which makes it the most usefully late NA list in upper Manhattan.

venues.longDescription:
The Penrose sits on Second Avenue between 82nd and 83rd, and its self-description — the Upper East Local — is accurate about both its ambitions and its value. It is a gastropub with warm lighting and vintage fittings, the kind of room that fills with regulars rather than destination-seekers. What lifts it into this directory is that its zero-proof list is not a gesture.

Eleven non-alcoholic cocktails are named and built, and the naming tells you the kitchen understands what a person ordering them actually wants — not a fruit juice, but the shape of a familiar drink. Express Yourself stands in for an espresso martini. Garden Tonic is the zero-proof gin and tonic. Love That For You is the no-booze spritz, Peach Fuzz the boozeless bellini, Feels Like Summer the virgin mojito, That's Amore an almost-amaretto-sour, Sunday Kinda Love the virgin bloody mary, Stubborn Love a mule without the liquor, and Good Vibrations a no-alcohol negroni sbagliato, with Amor Prohibido rounding out the list. Lyre's non-alcoholic prosecco is poured by the glass, and non-alcoholic beer and sodas sit alongside.

The honest framing matters. The Penrose is a full bar. It serves cocktails, beer, wine and spirits, and the room will be full of people drinking them. For a lot of readers that is exactly right — the thing they want is to meet friends somewhere ordinary and not be handed a glass of orange juice — and for others, particularly anyone early in recovery, a fully alcohol-free room like Soft Bar or Mockingbird will be the better call. This guide lists both because both are needed.

What The Penrose offers that almost nothing else in upper Manhattan does is hours. It opens at 11:30am on weekdays and 9:30am at weekends, and runs to 4am every single night. The Upper East Side is comparatively bare for this category — the neighbourhood's dedicated non-alcoholic bottle shop closed, and there is no alcohol-free bar above 96th Street — so a room that will make you a properly constructed zero-proof drink at one in the morning is doing real work. Eleven options also means you can go repeatedly without ordering the same thing, which sounds trivial and is one of the most common complaints about drinking without alcohol in bars.

venues.name: The Perch
venues.description: The Perch is the rooftop bar above Local 11ten Food & Wine, a fine-dining room on Bull Street just south of Forsyth Park, set among the oak canopy rather than above a skyline. It runs a small seasonal cocktail list that has consistently included built alcohol-free drinks made from house shrubs and syrups — a strawberry-habanero shrub with basil and lime, a cucumber-and-lime shrub with cilantro and ginger syrup, a honeysuckle-and-white-pepper build with mint and lemon. Because the list turns over with the seasons and the roof only trades Thursday to Sunday evenings, weather permitting, it is worth checking what is current before making the trip.

venues.longDescription:
Savannah's rooftop bars mostly sell a view of the river or the historic grid. The Perch sells a view of the trees: it sits on top of Local 11ten Food & Wine on Bull Street, a few blocks south of Forsyth Park, and its terrace is level with the live-oak canopy rather than above it. The restaurant below is one of the city's long-standing fine-dining rooms, and the roof runs the same kitchen with a shorter bar list.

The alcohol-free drinks follow the kitchen's approach — house-made components, seasonal produce, nothing poured from a bottle of cordial. The versions documented by Savannah's tourism board give a clear picture of the style: a Strawberry Habanero built on a house strawberry-habanero shrub with basil, lime and soda; a Cue Ginger of cucumber and lime shrub with cilantro and a ginger simple syrup; and a Grapefruit Honeysuckle with white pepper, mint, honeysuckle syrup and lemon. All three are shrub-and-herb drinks, sharp rather than sweet, and they are constructed the same way the bar's alcoholic cocktails are.

This entry is graded conservatively at three rather than four, for two honest reasons. The alcohol-free drinks appear on a small rotating seasonal list rather than under a permanent printed heading of their own, and the specific builds above could not be confirmed against a current menu — the venue publishes its list as a PDF that was not readable at the time of writing. Elsewhere in this city guide, guide-sourced drink names have repeatedly turned out to have rotated off.

The roof is also the least reliably open venue in this guide: Thursday to Sunday evenings only, from 5pm, and weather permitting. Call ahead in summer, when Savannah's afternoon storms close it at short notice.
venues.pressQuote: Nestled above Local 11Ten Food & Wine, you'll understand why losing track of time at PERCH rooftop bar is easy.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Visit Savannah, Where to Find Incredible Mocktails in Savannah

venues.name: The Polished Pigeon
venues.description: The Polished Pigeon is San Diego's second dedicated alcohol-free bar, open in East Village since February 2026 and describing itself as a non-alcoholic temperance lounge, coffee bar and social club. Nothing on the premises contains alcohol. The drinks run to three printed sections — nine functional zero-proof builds from $13, six house specials at $15, and six spirit-free classics at $15 including an old fashioned, a manhattan and a whiskey sour built on non-alcoholic bourbon — plus non-alcoholic beer and wine and a full coffee menu from eight in the morning. It is women-owned and queer-owned, and the calendar is as much of the offer as the drinks: live music, an open-stage drag show, a women's recovery group and a Sunday afternoon social all run in the same room. Coffee and the functional list are served Tuesday and Wednesday until four; the full bar runs Thursday to Saturday until ten and Sunday until eight.
venues.address: 1450 Market St A1, San Diego, CA 92101

Old Fashioned, spirit-free ($15) — Sobour bourbonesque, bitters, orange
Kava flight ($18) — four pours, no substitutions: Kavahol, Mag, Kava Haven and a rotating pour
venues.longDescription:
The Polished Pigeon opened on 6 February 2026 in the former lounge of Black & Grey Atelier, an appointment-only tattoo studio on the ground floor of the Form 15 apartments at 1450 Market Street, and it is the second bar in San Diego where no alcohol is served at all. The founders, Kaylee and Crystal Clark, previously built the identity of the city's first alcohol-free bar in Hillcrest before a public falling-out with its majority owner; the local trade site SanDiegoVille covered the opening as the arrival of the city's second such room.

What matters on the ground is that the drinks list is deep and printed rather than improvised. The functional section runs nine builds between thirteen and fifteen dollars, each tagged for what it is meant to do: Breathe Easy and Basil Smash on aplós calme with CBD, The Glider and Clear Skies on a kava base, Wake Up Call and Spicy Piña under an uplift heading, The Pause on Sentia's GABA Red and Night ZZZ on Three Spirit's Nightcap under unwind. The house specials add six more at fifteen dollars, among them an espresso martini on Spiritless espresso liqueur and house cold brew, and a Golden Hour on Pentire Adrift with a house cordial. The spirit-free classics are exactly what the name says — old fashioned, manhattan, paloma, peach margarita, vanilla-lime gimlet and whiskey sour, built on non-alcoholic bourbon and tequila alternatives.

Beyond the cocktails there is non-alcoholic beer from Ted Segers, Good Liar and Gruvi, Gruvi red blend and Surely sparkling by the glass, three zero-zero shots at six dollars, and a four-pour kava flight at eighteen. The coffee side opens at eight every day it trades, which makes this one of the few rooms in the city that works for a morning meeting and an evening out without changing character.

Two things to know before you go. The bar serves kava and hemp-derived CBD alongside the alcohol-free drinks, both named plainly on the menu — no alcohol, but not free of every active ingredient, so read the tags if that matters to you. And the hours split: coffee and functional cocktails only on Tuesday and Wednesday until four, with the full bar running Thursday to Saturday until ten and Sunday until eight.

The programming is the other half of what this room is. The published calendar runs live music on weekend mornings, an open-stage drag show called The Aviary, a Sunday afternoon social, a women's codependency recovery meeting and a weekly women's group — the mix of nightlife and recovery support that a bar serving no alcohol can hold in one room and a licensed bar cannot. Collaborations with local coffee roasters and vendors fill the daytime slots. For anyone who has been looking for somewhere in San Diego to spend a Friday evening that is neither a bar nor a coffee shop closing at five, this is currently the answer in the east of downtown.
venues.pressQuote: San Diego's second alcohol-free bar, The Polished Pigeon, opens downtown this week

venues.name: The Portrait Bar
venues.description: The Portrait Bar sits inside The Fifth Avenue Hotel in NoMad, a maximalist room hung with portraiture that reads as considered rather than merely lavish. It won its category at the inaugural NYC's Best Bars for NA Awards, where the judges singled out an intimate maximalist setting paired with a confident non-alcoholic list — confident being the operative word, since hotel bars are where zero-proof menus most often collapse into a token pair of juices. It serves alcohol too. Hours are unusually generous for a room of this quality: 5pm to 1am through the week and to 2am on Friday and Saturday, seven days.

venues.longDescription:
The Portrait Bar is the bar of The Fifth Avenue Hotel, on West 28th Street in NoMad, and it belongs to the current wave of New York hotel bars that are genuinely destinations rather than amenities. The room is maximalist — densely patterned, richly upholstered, hung with portraits — and it commits to that register rather than hedging toward neutral hotel taste.

It is in this guide because it won its category at the inaugural NYC's Best Bars for NA Awards, judged in 2025 and covered by Time Out, which described an intimate maximalist setting matched with a confident non-alcoholic list.

Hotel bars are exactly where that recognition is hardest to earn. They serve a captive, transient audience, which historically has meant zero-proof options existed as a box to tick: a virgin mojito, something with cranberry, and a shrug. A hotel bar that has been externally judged to have a confident NA list is one that decided its non-drinking guests were worth the same attention as everyone else — and for a traveller, who has far less ability to research alternatives than a local does, that is disproportionately valuable. If you are staying in Midtown or NoMad and not drinking, this is the room that will not make the evening awkward.

The usual clarity applies: The Portrait Bar is a full cocktail bar and serves alcohol. It is listed here for the quality of what it will pour you if you are not drinking, not as an alcohol-free space.

Hours are strong. It opens at 5pm every day and runs to 1am Sunday through Thursday, stretching to 2am on Friday and Saturday. NoMad puts it within walking distance of Clemente Bar in the Flatiron and the Hotel Chelsea's Lobby Bar a little to the west, which makes a genuinely good non-drinking evening possible across three rooms without needing a train.
venues.pressQuote: Portrait Bar charmed judges with its intimate, maximalist setting and a short but confident NA list, including a standout non-alcoholic Ramos Gin Fizz.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Time Out New York, NYC's Best Bars for NA Awards 2025

venues.name: The Prado at Balboa Park
venues.description: The Prado is the restaurant inside the House of Hospitality in Balboa Park, a 1915 building from the Panama-California Exposition, and its bar card prints a Spirit Free heading with two named builds on Lyre's non-alcoholic spirits: an Italian Spritz NA with Lyre's Italian Spritz, Mionetto alcohol-free sparkling and orange, and a Prickly Pear Margarita NA with Lyre's agave blanco, prickly pear, lime and agave. A row of house sparkling lemonades sits beside them. Two named builds is a modest programme rather than a deep one, but they are printed, named and made from real non-alcoholic spirits rather than improvised, in a restaurant that feeds a very large number of people who are in the park with children, driving, or simply not drinking at lunchtime. The restaurant serves Tuesday to Sunday from half past eleven until eight, closed Mondays, on a terrace over the park's gardens.
venues.address: 1549 El Prado Ste 12, San Diego, CA 92101
signatureDrinks: Italian Spritz NA — Lyre's Italian Spritz, Mionetto alcohol-free sparkling, orange
Prickly Pear Margarita NA — Lyre's agave blanco, prickly pear, lime, agave
Sparkling Lemonade — strawberry, passion fruit, mango, pink guava or raspberry
venues.longDescription:
The Prado occupies the House of Hospitality on El Prado, the central promenade of Balboa Park, in a building put up for the 1915 Panama-California Exposition and now a national landmark. Its Spanish, Moorish and Mexican detailing, tiled fountains and courtyard terrace make it one of the more striking rooms to eat in anywhere in the city, and it is run by the Cohn Restaurant Group.

The alcohol-free offering is short and clearly labelled. Under a Spirit Free heading the bar prints two built drinks, both on Lyre's, the Australian range of non-alcoholic spirits. The Italian Spritz NA combines Lyre's Italian Spritz with Mionetto's alcohol-free sparkling and orange, which is the aperitivo shape done properly — bitter, orange-led and long. The Prickly Pear Margarita NA uses Lyre's agave blanco with prickly pear, lime and agave, and is the better of the two for anyone who finds aperitivo flavours too bitter. Beside them the menu lists house sparkling lemonades in strawberry, passion fruit, mango, pink guava and raspberry, which are simple, cheap and made to order.

Two named builds is a modest programme rather than a deep one, and worth describing as exactly that. What earns the listing is that they are printed, named and built from real non-alcoholic spirits rather than left to a bartender to improvise, in a restaurant that serves a very large number of visitors who are in the park with children, driving, or simply not drinking at lunchtime.

The practicalities matter here more than at most restaurants. The Prado is closed on Mondays and serves from half past eleven in the morning until eight, with a half past seven close on Sunday, so it is a daytime and early-evening venue rather than a night out. Parking in the park fills at weekends. The terrace is the reason to come, and it is worth asking for when you book.

The building holds more than twenty-two thousand square feet of indoor and outdoor space, including gardens, terraces and a ballroom, so the restaurant runs weddings and events alongside ordinary service and can feel busy in a way a neighbourhood room does not. The food is Californian with Spanish influences — the kitchen's own list of favourites runs to spicy calamari fries, red wine braised short ribs and a paella — and the sangria is the house drink on the alcoholic side. If you are visiting the park's museums for the day, this is the one sit-down restaurant on El Prado itself, which is worth knowing when everything else within walking distance is a counter.

venues.name: The Publican
venues.description: The Publican is the European beer-hall-inspired restaurant in Fulton Market known for its raw bar, heritage pork and house charcuterie, and its drinks list carries a named non-alcoholic section called High & Dry. Two built drinks sit under it at $12 each: What's French for "Pineapple", made with Giffard's spiritless pineapple and a house lime cordial, and Fleur de Sangre, which combines Giffard elderflower with a house lemon cordial and San Pellegrino Aranciata Rossa. A non-alcoholic hop water from Fair State Brewing Cooperative is listed at $8 within the beer list itself. Note that the bar offers an optional 5mg THC shot as a $7 add-on and stocks THC sodas separately; the High & Dry drinks are free of THC unless that add-on is requested.

venues.longDescription:
The Publican has anchored Fulton Market since long before the neighborhood filled with towers, and it still runs on the format it opened with: communal tables under a vaulted ceiling, a raw bar of oysters and shellfish, heritage pork, housemade charcuterie and vegetable plates, and a beer list built partly in collaboration with local brewers. The restaurant describes itself as blending the warmth of a European beer hall with the energy of Fulton Market, and it serves lunch and dinner seven days with weekend brunch from 9am.

Its non-alcoholic drinks are grouped under their own heading, High & Dry, printed with the cocktails rather than buried among the soft drinks. Both current builds use Giffard's spiritless range as a base and both are $12. What's French for "Pineapple" combines the spiritless pineapple with a house lime cordial - short, sharp and made to sit against fatty pork and salt. Fleur de Sangre is the longer of the two, pairing Giffard elderflower with a house lemon cordial and San Pellegrino Aranciata Rossa, so it drinks like a blood-orange spritz. Within the beer list, a Fair State Brewing Cooperative hop water brewed with citrus and galaxy hops is listed at $8 and 0.0% ABV, which gives a non-drinker something to hold in a room whose whole identity is beer. One caveat worth stating plainly: the High & Dry section offers an optional 5mg shot of Nowadays THC spirit as a $7 add-on, and the bar stocks separate THC sodas including a 5mg hemp option. Neither is included unless ordered, but anyone avoiding psychoactives should say so when ordering rather than assume. The restaurant keeps a two-service day, lunch from 11am and dinner from 4pm, with weekend brunch from 9am, so the High & Dry drinks are available at every service rather than only after dark. The beer list is one of the most closely followed in the city and is built partly through collaborations with local brewers, which makes the decision to place a 0.0% hop water inside that list rather than in a separate corner a deliberate piece of menu design. Food is farm-to-table in the original sense - oysters and shellfish from the raw bar, heritage pork, vegetable plates and charcuterie made in house.
venues.pressQuote: Enjoy “simple farmhouse fare” at this European beer hall-inspired gastropub.

venues.name: The Rendition Room
venues.description: The Rendition Room is a 1930s-style speakeasy hidden in the basement of Vitello's, the Italian restaurant that has served Studio City's stretch of Tujunga Avenue since 1964, entered through a door disguised as a bookshelf. The intimate, low-lit room leans hard into Prohibition-era Hollywood atmosphere, and the dress code is enforced rather than suggested: business casual or cocktail attire, with jeans, ball caps, shorts, T-shirts, sandals and athletic wear refused at any time. Its non-alcoholic list is headed "Spirits Away" and runs six drinks at a flat $12, all built on fresh juices and scratch sours rather than bought-in zero-proof spirits: Nectar of the Gods (watermelon, cucumber, scratch sour, lemon, seltzer), Eve on Earth (white cranberry, grapefruit seltzer, scratch sour), Pearadisio (scratch sour, pear, seltzer), Cloud 9 (pineapple, lemon, coconut, mango), Fauxjito (lime, mint, seltzer) and Spa Water (cucumber, mint, lime seltzer). Per Resy, the bar recently extended its NA offerings upstairs to its Rat Pack-themed lounge, The Velvet Martini, citing demand from younger guests. Vitello's Italian food can be ordered in the speakeasy, which is cashless.

Eve on Earth (white cranberry, grapefruit seltzer, scratch sour) $12
venues.longDescription:
The Rendition Room is a speakeasy hidden in the basement of Vitello's, the Italian restaurant that has served Studio City from 4349 Tujunga Avenue since 1964. Entry is through a door disguised as a bookshelf, and the room commits fully to its conceit: the bar describes stepping through into the 1930s, a time of elegance and secrecy, and holds an intimate, low-lit space of red light and a brick faux fireplace. The dress code is enforced rather than suggested — business casual or cocktail attire is required, and jeans, ball caps, shorts, T-shirts, sandals and athletic wear are not permitted at any time. Guests are encouraged to arrive in period-appropriate 1920s or 1930s dress, and the bar makes that worth doing: a 5% non-member surcharge applies to guests who are not members of Club Rendition, and it is waived for anyone who turns up in era-appropriate costume. Food comes down from Vitello's kitchen, including a blackened swordfish piccata, a short-rib and beef Prohibition burger and twin filet medallions with peppercorn sauce. The room is cashless and takes reservations through SevenRooms.

The non-alcoholic list is headed "Spirits Away" and priced flat at $12 for all six drinks. What distinguishes it from most speakeasy zero-proof lists is that nothing is built on a bought-in non-alcoholic spirit — these are fresh-juice and scratch-sour drinks, made the way the bar makes everything else. Nectar of the Gods combines watermelon and cucumber with scratch sour, lemon and seltzer. Eve on Earth pairs white cranberry with grapefruit seltzer and scratch sour. Pearadisio is scratch sour with pear and seltzer, Cloud 9 blends pineapple, lemon, coconut and mango, and the list is completed by a Fauxjito of lime, mint and seltzer and a Spa Water of cucumber, mint and lime seltzer. Manager Shelton told Resy in January 2026 that the bar had recently extended its non-alcoholic offering upstairs to its Rat Pack-themed lounge, The Velvet Martini, because of demand: we want all kinds of people to feel welcome and enjoy the speakeasy experience, even if they don't imbibe, she said, noting it is often younger guests who order them. Service runs from 5pm, to 9pm Sunday and Tuesday to Thursday and 10pm on Friday and Saturday.

venues.name: The Roosevelt Room
venues.description: Tucked inside a 1929 railroad warehouse in downtown Austin's Warehouse District, The Roosevelt Room has earned a reputation as one of Texas' defining cocktail destinations since opening in 2015. The 3,750-square-foot space holds up to 230 guests across two levels — a seated, table-service main bar downstairs with a 36-foot bar counter and surrounding booths, and a more relaxed mezzanine lounge upstairs available for walk-ins and private events. The cocktail program runs to 80+ drinks, anchored by the 'Classics Board' — a 53-drink timeline spanning seven eras of bartending history, from pre-1880s staples through tiki and into modern creations, each carefully reworked in the Roosevelt Room's house style. The non-alcoholic program sits alongside this rather than apart from it, featuring named NA cocktails like Glitter & Marigold, The Castaway, and the NA'Groni, plus a dedicated non-alcoholic spirits section on the back bar. The venue is full-service: alcohol is the main offering, but the zero-proof selections are crafted with the same precision as the rest of the menu.

venues.longDescription:
The Roosevelt Room occupies a 1929 railroad warehouse in Austin's Warehouse District and has been one of Texas's defining cocktail bars since it opened in 2015. The space runs 3,750 square feet across two levels — a seated, table-service main bar downstairs with a 36-foot counter and booths around it, and a looser mezzanine lounge upstairs that takes walk-ins. It holds 230.

The cocktail programme runs past eighty drinks and is anchored by the Classics Board, a 53-drink timeline covering seven eras of bartending history from pre-1880s staples through tiki to the present, each rebuilt in the bar's own style. That is a research project as much as a menu, and it explains why the zero-proof list is as good as it is: a bar that treats cocktail construction as a historical discipline does not suddenly stop thinking when the alcohol comes out.

Visit Austin called the zero-proof menu a technical masterpiece, and the drinks bear that out. The NA'Groni is built on verjus rouge and gentian tea — verjus for the sharp acidity of unripe grapes, gentian for the root bitterness that makes a Negroni a Negroni, neither of them a syrup. Glitter & Marigold works orange flower water, pistachio and vanilla. The N'artini uses Seedlip Spice with juniper tea, clarified Asian pear juice and Castelvetrano olives. The Castaway rounds out the named list, and there is a dedicated non-alcoholic spirits section on the back bar.

Clarification and gentian are the tells. Clarifying a juice strips the cloudiness and leaves a drink with the clean weight of a spirit-based one, and gentian supplies genuine bitterness rather than a sweet approximation of it. Both are labour, and both are what separate a zero-proof menu that has been thought about from one that has been assembled.

This is a full-service bar where alcohol is the main business, but a non-drinker here is ordering from the same kitchen of ideas as everyone else. Open daily from 3pm, with happy hour until 6pm.
venues.pressQuote: Tucked inside a 1929 railroad warehouse in downtown Austin, The Roosevelt Room has grown into one of Texas' defining cocktail destinations. Since opening in 2015, it has carved out a reputation not just for world-class drinks, but for setting a new benchmark in service and hospitality for the city.

venues.name: The Rose Garden
venues.description: An upscale cocktail lounge on 1st Avenue in downtown Phoenix, built around the conceit of a fairytale garden and its resident peacock, Penrose. The botanical theme runs through the drinks rather than stopping at the decor, and the non-alcoholic builds are made from the same components as the rest of the list: Seedlip Garden and Seedlip Grove worked with butterfly pea flower, lavender and fresh herbs. DiningOut Phoenix listed it among the metro bars worth visiting specifically for a mocktail in May 2026. It opens Tuesday through Sunday from 4pm, running to midnight on Friday and Saturday, and sits a block from the light rail — easy to reach without driving, and easy to leave when the rest of the group is still going.

venues.longDescription:
The Rose Garden sits on 1st Avenue in downtown Phoenix, a short walk from the convention centre and a block from the light rail, and commits completely to its own premise: an upscale cocktail lounge dressed as a modern fairytale garden, built around a mascot peacock named Penrose. It is the kind of room where the styling could easily have been the entire proposition — heavy foliage, deliberate lighting, a space designed to be photographed — and the thing that stops it being merely that is the drinks list, which takes the botanical theme past the decor and into the glass.

The non-alcoholic builds use the same components as the rest of the menu rather than a separate, simpler set. They are made on Seedlip Garden and Seedlip Grove — the herbaceous and the citrus expressions — and finished with butterfly pea flower, lavender and fresh herbs pulled from the same station as the spirited drinks. The practical effect is that the zero-proof options read as variations on the bar's house style rather than as apologies for it, which is unusual: most themed lounges treat the alcohol-free list as a compliance exercise. DiningOut Phoenix picked the venue out in its May 2026 guide to the best bars in the metro for a mocktail.

The hours suit a real night out by Phoenix standards. The bar runs to midnight on Friday and Saturday and to 11pm Tuesday through Thursday and on Sunday, closing on Mondays, and the downtown position means it works either as a destination or as the stop after something at the arena or the Orpheum. Two caveats. As with essentially every cocktail room downtown, this is a licensed bar with a full spirits programme — the non-alcoholic drinks are a genuine section of the menu, not the character of the venue. And the room is small and gets busy at weekends, so a group not drinking may still find themselves queuing behind one that is.
venues.pressQuote: the mocktails lean on butterfly pea flowers, lavender, and fresh herbs to create drinks that are just as lovely as the setting

venues.name: The Rosecomb
venues.description: The Rosecomb is a North Shore cocktail bar on Barton Avenue with the best-written alcohol-free list in Chattanooga: an entire mocktail menu, rotated regularly, with the current lineup named after Southern authors. The Grady Hendrix is built on holy basil, cucumber, lime, serrano and agave; The Natasha runs hibiscus and Bengal spice tea with ginger, pineapple and lime; and a mulled apple cider covers the colder months. That the mocktails get their own naming conceit, rather than being tacked onto the bottom of the cocktail card, is the tell — someone rewrites this list every time the theme changes. Open daily from 4pm, to midnight and 1am at weekends.
signatureDrinks: Grady Hendrix — holy basil, cucumber, lime, serrano, agave
The Natasha — hibiscus, Bengal spice tea, ginger, pineapple, lime
venues.longDescription:
A useful way to judge a bar's commitment to alcohol-free drinks is to look at how they are named. Most places call them mocktails and stop there. The Rosecomb, on Barton Avenue on Chattanooga's North Shore, gives its non-alcoholic list a conceit of its own and rotates it — the current lineup is named after Southern authors, which means somebody sits down and rewrites the whole thing each time the theme turns over.

The drinks justify the effort. The Grady Hendrix — named for the Charleston horror novelist — is holy basil, cucumber, lime, serrano and agave, a savoury, herbal, faintly hot drink with no interest in being sweet. The Natasha goes the other way: hibiscus and Bengal spice tea with ginger, pineapple and lime, a build that gets its body from brewed tea rather than from juice. In colder months a mulled apple cider joins them, which in a city at the foot of the Appalachians is the right seasonal answer.

What these have in common is that they are constructed from infusions, teas and fresh produce rather than assembled from bottled mixers, and that they are conceived as their own drinks rather than as subtractions from existing cocktails. Chattanooga's own daily newsletter, NOOGAtoday, has picked the bar out for exactly this in its round-up of where to drink without alcohol in the city.

The practical picture is good too. The Rosecomb opens at 4pm Monday through Friday and runs to midnight, 1am on Friday and Saturday, with a 2pm start on Saturday and an 11am to 4pm Sunday service — so it covers a weekday evening, a late night and a Sunday brunch, which few rooms in this guide manage. The North Shore location puts it across the river from downtown, walkable from the Walnut Street Bridge.
venues.pressQuote: This North Shore spot has options including The Natasha, made with hibiscus, Bengal spice tea, ginger, pineapple, and lime.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: NOOGAtoday, Local mocktails + non-alcoholic drinks in Chattanooga

venues.name: The Royale Food & Spirits
venues.description: A Tower Grove South institution since 2005, The Royale is the rare neighborhood bar that treats zero-proof drinkers as first-class citizens. Owner Steven Fitzpatrick Smith's corner gastropub — set in a building that has housed a bar since before Prohibition — prints a dedicated N/A cocktails section right on the menu: five house-built alcohol-free drinks, from the ginger-and-mint Functioning Bastard made with zero-proof gin to the beet-forward HeartBeet Spritz, backed by Athletic Brewing and Guinness non-alcoholic beers. Add one of South City's most beloved garden patios and a scratch kitchen turning out tacos and burgers, and it's an easy pick for mixed groups of drinkers and non-drinkers alike.

venues.longDescription:
Steven Fitzpatrick Smith opened The Royale in 2005 in a corner building on South Kingshighway that had housed a bar since before Prohibition, most recently the Reale Bar. A Saint Louis University graduate who had run a boxing gym in North City and worked events for the Riverfront Times, Smith modeled his gastropub on the great family-owned taverns of South City and the community-minded corner bars he admired in Milwaukee and Chicago. Two decades on, the bet has paid off: the Riverfront Times has chronicled how the bar became a gathering place for local politics and civic life, and St. Louis Magazine marked its 20th anniversary in 2025 with a profile of the South City landmark.

The Royale is one of the few St. Louis bars that prints a dedicated N/A cocktails section on its everyday menu. Five zero-proof drinks run $6 to $10: the Functioning Bastard mixes BARE zero-proof gin with ginger beer, mint, and Angostura bitters; the French 77 pairs lemon and lemongrass syrup with club soda in a champagne flute; What's Up Kid? blends freshly juiced carrot, lemon, and orange with a house hot-honey black-pepper syrup; Puttin' on the Fitz layers rosemary, pomegranate, lime, coconut water, and a splash of cranberry; and the HeartBeet Spritz tops house-pressed beet juice and a gin-inspired juniper simple with tonic. Non-alcoholic beer drinkers get Athletic Brewing's Upside Dawn golden ale, Guinness Non-Alcoholic in the 14.9-ounce can, and budget-friendly Busch NA.

St. Louis Magazine's guide to non-alcoholic cocktails singles out The Royale's handful of zero-proof riffs on classic cocktails, and the bar's backyard courtyard — a fixture of local best-patio round-ups from Sauce Magazine and Feast — is the place to drink them in warm months. Inside, the cocktail list nods to local geography with drinks like the Bevo Old Fashioned, Midtowner Manhattan, and River Des Peres, while the kitchen turns out fish tacos, brisket tacos, and burgers until 9 or 10 p.m. Expect weekend DJ nights, reservations via OpenTable, and a Tuesday closure; the rest of the week the room hums from lunch (or 4 p.m. early in the week) until 11 p.m. or midnight.
venues.pressQuote: This cozy neighborhood bar near Tower Grove Park has a well-earned reputation for crafting great cocktails.

venues.name: The Rum House
venues.description: The Rum House is a Caribbean-inspired taqueria and rum bar that opened on Magazine Street in June 2009, founded by Baton Rouge natives Michael Buchert and Kelly Ponder. The Uptown spot is known for island-style tacos and a bar stocked with over 200 rums. Its non-alcoholic offering is a named mocktail line developed with local personality Lauren Haydel of Fleurty Girl, which took off after one of her themed lemonade mocktails went viral during a high-traffic concert weekend. The mocktails are built on Free Spirits non-alcoholic tequila: the Heaux Ranch Water (lime, soda water), the Fleurty Faux-Rita (lime, agave, jalapeños), and the Teasequila Sunrise (orange juice, grenadine), available daily and during the weekday Island Time happy hour.
venues.longDescription:
The Rum House is a Caribbean taqueria and rum bar at 3128 Magazine Street, open daily from 11am to 10pm, and it has been on that stretch since 2009. The bar is stocked with a couple of hundred rums, the kitchen does island-style tacos, and chef Terri Savoie runs it. All of which makes the non-alcoholic list an unlikely thing to find here, and a genuinely interesting one, because it did not come from the bar alone.

The three zero-proof drinks are a collaboration with Fleurty Girl, the New Orleans clothing and gift company founded by Lauren Haydel, and they are named the way that partnership implies. The Heaux Ranch Water is non-alcoholic Free Spirits tequila with lime juice and soda water, sold under the line "heauxld the booze". The Fleurty Faux-Rita is described as all of the spicy kick with none of the hangover — non-alcoholic tequila, lime, agave and jalapeños. The Teasequila Sunrise is Free Spirits tequila with orange juice and grenadine, with the tagline all of the sparkle and none of the stumble. All three are built on the same non-alcoholic agave spirit, which is a sensible choice for a bar whose expertise is elsewhere: rather than assemble a scratch programme it does not have the bench for, it picked one credible bottle and built three familiar drinks properly around it. Haydel's own reason for doing it is the one that carries: she said she was thrilled to see alternative options in a city where alcohol is everywhere, which is as concise a statement of the problem New Orleans poses to a non-drinker as anyone has managed. The naming is unmistakably local and a little arch, and it changes the social register of ordering — asking for a Heaux Ranch Water in a room full of rum drinkers is a different act from asking for a mocktail. Prices are not published; the bar's own website is behind a security check that blocks automated access, so its current menu could not be read remotely.
venues.pressQuote: I am thrilled to see alternative options in a city where alcohol is everywhere.

venues.name: The Semi-Tropic
venues.description: The Semi-Tropic is a neighbourhood bar and all-day cafe on Glendale Boulevard in Echo Park, open since 2015 and named after the Semi-Tropic Spiritualists Association, an early-1900s utopian collective based in the hills at the north end of the neighbourhood. It is licensed, and its drink menu carries a titled Non-Alcoholic section with three shaken builds: Plantasia at $13, made with Amass Riverine, cucumber, cilantro, lime and yuzu soda; Pineapples in Stereo at $13, with Martini and Rossi Floreale aperitivo, pineapple, sugar snap pea and lime; and Garden Lemonade at $8, with fresh lemonade, lavender, chamomile, soda and butterfly pea extract. A wellness shot of ginger, honey, lemon, turmeric and black pepper is $7. The room is large and couch-filled, with an outdoor area and fire pits.
