venues.longDescription:
Three Dots and a Dash operates out of a subterranean space reached through a back alley off Clark Street in River North — and for non-drinkers, the experience is no less considered than it is for the rum faithful. The bar maintains a dedicated mocktail section on its official menu, and the kitchen behind it is serious: the team runs a full cold-press juice operation producing over 60 gallons of fresh juice daily, uses more than 30 house-made cordials and syrups, and explicitly avoids store-bought non-alcoholic spirits in favor of in-house creations built from spices, teas, and dried ingredients.

Beverage Director Kevin Beary, who has led the program since its mid-decade evolution into a World's 50 Best Bars-recognized destination, has extended that ethos to the zero-proof side. The Sunday Scaries combines coconut water, pandan, and sobacha tea for a quietly complex, earthy-tropical build. The Honeycrisp Nombie uses a house honeycrisp apple non-alcoholic amaro alongside verjus blanc and cinnamon — dry, autumnal, and textured in a way that reads nothing like juice. The Con Artist, an earlier addition that drew coverage from Time Out Chicago, leans on a Costa Rican single-estate cocoa nib tea layered with Chinese five-spice and cinnamon cordial for perceived bitterness and viscosity. The Bamboo Room, the intimate 22-seat rum bar tucked inside the main space, also carries its own NA options including the Coco-Nana and the Rising Tides with house-made spirit-free amaro.

This is a 21+ venue with no dress code, though the crowd skews toward people who dressed up a bit because the room rewards it — dark thatched-roof décor, ceramic tiki mugs, torches, and theatrical glassware set a tone. Reservations are strongly recommended, particularly on weekends when seating fills well in advance; OpenTable is the primary booking channel. The bar is good for groups who want a shared-format experience (the alcoholic side runs to large-format punch bowls), for sober guests who don't want to feel like an afterthought, and for anyone who wants to drink something that took real thought to build. The entrance through the alley and the staircase descent make the arrival part of the experience.
venues.pressQuote: One of Chicago's premiere tiki bars has added the non-alcoholic Con Artist cocktail to its menu, using a tea made with Costa Rican cocoa nibs and Chinese five-spice to create a drink that balances sweetness with bitterness.

venues.name: Three Notch'd Brewery & Craft Kitchen
venues.description: Three Notch'd's Scott's Addition taproom is the rare brewery that answers the non-alcoholic question with its own beer rather than a bought-in can. The Charlottesville-founded brewery produces Uncool, a full year-round non-alcoholic line, and pours it here on tap and in the fridge — including a Low Cal IPA that comes in around 40 calories. That distinction matters in a brewery district: ordering a house-brewed alcohol-free beer in a taproom is a completely different social experience from asking what they have without alcohol and being handed something from a competitor. The kitchen and the taproom keep normal brewery hours, to 11pm on Fridays and Saturdays.
signatureDrinks: Uncool - the brewery's own year-round non-alcoholic line
Uncool Low Cal IPA - non-alcoholic, around 40 calories
venues.longDescription:
Scott's Addition is Richmond's brewery district — a former industrial grid now dense with taprooms, cideries and distilleries — which makes it simultaneously the most fun and the most difficult part of the city to spend an evening in without drinking. Three Notch'd Brewery & Craft Kitchen, on West Broad Street at the district's edge, is the answer to that problem.

The brewery was founded in Charlottesville and has expanded across Virginia, and rather than treat non-alcoholic beer as someone else's product to stock, it brews its own. The Uncool line runs year-round, and the Richmond taproom pours it on tap as well as selling it cold from the fridge. The line includes a Low Cal IPA at roughly 40 calories, which is aimed squarely at the health-driven end of the category rather than the recovery end — a useful signal about who is actually buying non-alcoholic beer now.

Why this earns a higher grade than a taproom with a couple of imported cans: brewing your own alcohol-free beer is a real production decision. It occupies tank time, requires a different process, and only makes sense if a brewery believes the demand is permanent. When it is on draft rather than hidden in a fridge, a non-drinker in a brewery gets the ordinary experience — a glass poured from the same wall of taps as everyone else's — instead of the visible accommodation of a bottle handed over the bar.

The kitchen operates alongside, so this works as dinner as well as drinks, and hours run to 10pm midweek and 11pm on Friday and Saturday. It sits within walking distance of most of Scott's Addition, which makes it the sensible anchor for a group where only some people are drinking.
venues.pressQuote: Located in the heart of Scott's Addition, Three Notch'd Brewery & Craft Kitchen brings together fresh craft beer, elevated pub fare, craft cocktails, and one of Richmond's most energetic gathering spaces

venues.name: Three Sheets
venues.description: Three Sheets opened on Dalston's Kingsland Road in 2016, the work of brothers Max and Noel Venning, who came down from Manchester to build a bar around a stripped-back, ingredient-first philosophy. It first traded as Between the Sheets before the pair judged the name too suggestive. The room is tiny and deliberately spare — marble-topped tables, exposed brick and candlelight — with none of the theatre or clutter of a big-format cocktail bar; the focus is squarely on what is in the glass, and that discipline has earned it a place on The World's 50 Best Bars list. The menu is split into three "sheets" by alcohol strength, and the alcohol-free run rebuilds the classics properly: a booze-free whisky sour, negroni and espresso martini built on Belgian Opius NA elixirs, with three chillies infused in vegetable glycerin to restore the heat and viscosity alcohol would otherwise give.

venues.longDescription:
Three Sheets opened on Dalston's Kingsland Road in 2016, the work of brothers Max and Noel Venning, who came down from Manchester to build a bar around a stripped-back, ingredient-first philosophy. It first traded as Between the Sheets before the pair judged the name too suggestive and settled on Three Sheets. The room is tiny and deliberately spare — marble-topped tables, exposed brick and candlelight — with none of the theatre or clutter of a big-format cocktail bar; the focus is squarely on what is in the glass. That discipline has earned it a place on The World's 50 Best Bars list and a long-standing spot among London's most respected drinking rooms, and the brothers have since added a larger second site in Soho.

The list is organised into "sheets" that signal strength: One Sheet for lighter, lower-ABV drinks, Two Sheets for mid-strength and Three Sheets for the properly boozy — a structure that makes the bar unusually easy to navigate for anyone drinking less. Rather than treat alcohol-free as an afterthought, Three Sheets keeps a short, tightly edited zero-proof selection of roughly four drinks that mirrors the cocktail canon. Its alcohol-free classics run from a whisky sour and a negroni to an americano and an espresso martini, each built around elixirs from the Belgian Opius Distillery — a hand-made non-alcoholic spirit whose botanicals are formulated to act on the body (working on GABA receptors, comparably to ashwagandha) rather than simply imitate flavour.

The technique is what sets the drinks apart. For the alcohol-free negroni and americano the team infuses three different types of chilli into vegetable glycerin, which restores both the gentle heat and the rounder, weightier texture that alcohol would normally supply — thinness being the usual failing of a non-alcoholic cocktail. The result reads as a genuine drink rather than a soft-drink substitute. Anyone wanting low-ABV rather than fully alcohol-free is well served too, from the house-carbonated French 75 on the One Sheet list to a low-alcohol Rum & Plum built on Japanese ume plum liqueur. The zero-proof list is not always printed, so the standing advice is simply to ask — the bartenders will build it to the same exacting standard as everything else.
venues.pressQuote: Beautifully executed alcohol-free classics range from the whisky sour and negroni to the espresso martini, made with elixirs from the Belgian Opius Distillery.

venues.name: Thunderbolt
venues.description: Thunderbolt is a neighborhood cocktail bar opened in 2019–2020 by Atlanta-born owner-bartender Mike Capoferri, at the meeting point of Historic Filipinotown, Echo Park, and Downtown LA. The concept is Deep South-inspired — Southern-rooted flavors, a Southern food menu, an extensive Madeira selection — paired with high-tech techniques like centrifuge clarification. It ranked No. 24 on North America's 50 Best Bars 2025 and won that program's Ketel One Sustainable Bar Award for waste reduction and ethical sourcing. The bar runs a small but genuine named non-alcoholic program: zero-proof options include the Pride of Oxnard, School Night, the Lychee Daiquiri, and the Thumper (which incorporates a rare NA milk-punch), and the staff will build custom alcohol-free drinks on request. The room is casual and bright, with an open patio and a pink-and-green palette.
venues.address: 1263 W Temple St, Los Angeles, CA 90026
venues.hours: Mon 5pm-12am; Tue closed; Wed-Thu 5pm-12am; Fri-Sat 5pm-1am; Sun 2pm-12am
venues.longDescription:
Thunderbolt is a neighbourhood cocktail bar at 1263 West Temple Street, sitting at the meeting point of Historic Filipinotown, Echo Park and downtown Los Angeles, and pairing Southern-inspired food with a technically ambitious drinks programme that leans on clarification and other equipment-led techniques to make cocktails more sustainable, more efficient and more consistent. Its record at the World's 50 Best Bars is unusually sustained for a room this casual: ninth in North America and Best in the West in 2022, the Campari One To Watch award and number 66 globally the same year, number 10 and Best in the West in 2023, and number 8 and best bar in the western United States in 2024, alongside a StarChefs Los Angeles Rising Star bartender award in 2021. The bar states plainly that it is ADA accessible and a welcome space for all people, and the kitchen's best-known plate is a pimiento cheese burger with pickled green tomato.

General manager Camron Robertson thinks people misread the place as somewhere that would not suit a non-drinker. We have some fun NA cocktails, he told Resy in January 2026, but our bar staff is also really creative and can create something for you on the fly — which, at a bar with this much technique behind it, is a more valuable offer than a long printed list. The four named zero-proof drinks show the same methods as the full menu. The Pride of Oxnard is a sparkling drink built on whole strawberries, juiced and then clarified, combined with juniper and jasmine teas. School Night is a milk punch using Wilderton citrus and a measure of Wilderton bitter with passionfruit, orange and guava juices, chai and coconut. The Lychee Daiquiri uses rum extract with lychee, lime and salt in a frosted glass. Thumper is a savoury swizzle drawn from Thai red curry, made with fresh carrot and green apple juices, coconut, red curry and a non-alcoholic hemp amaro. Athletic's Upside Dawn lager covers non-alcoholic beer. Robertson's stated ambition for the list is texture — to scratch that itch that makes an NA cocktail taste like much more than just a juice drink. The bar opens at 5pm daily except Tuesday, from 2pm on Sundays.
venues.pressQuote: We have some fun NA cocktails, but our bar staff is also really creative and can create something for you on the fly.

venues.name: Tía Carmen
venues.description: Chef Angelo Sosa's modern Southwestern restaurant at the JW Marriott Desert Ridge runs a thoughtful non-alcoholic lineup alongside an agave-driven bar. Named zero-proof drinks include the Short & Spicy (aguachile, ginger, pineapple) and the Tall & Bubbly (prickly pear, hibiscus, sparkling apple cider), both drawing on the same desert-Southwest larder as the kitchen rather than defaulting to citrus and syrup. The non-alcoholic beer list reaches well past the usual single option, carrying Athletic Brewing's Upside Dawn and several Bravus Brewing beers — a rarity in resort dining, where the NA fridge is normally one lager nobody has checked the date on.

venues.longDescription:
Tia Carmen sits inside the JW Marriott Desert Ridge in north Phoenix, which ordinarily would place it in the category of hotel restaurants that exist because the hotel needs one. It is not that. Angelo Sosa — a chef with a national profile before he moved to Arizona — built it as a modern Southwestern room drawing on desert ingredients, and it has been treated by local critics as a destination in its own right rather than an amenity.

That matters for non-drinkers because resort dining is usually where alcohol-free options are worst. The bar here is agave-driven and serious, and the zero-proof drinks are built from the same regional pantry as the food instead of being handed off to a soda gun. The Short & Spicy runs aguachile with ginger and pineapple — savoury and hot, which is an unusual register for a drink without alcohol. The Tall & Bubbly is prickly pear and hibiscus lengthened with sparkling apple cider, and reads as Sonoran rather than generic.

The non-alcoholic beer list is the quieter achievement. Rather than one token lager, it carries Athletic Brewing's Upside Dawn alongside several beers from Bravus, which means a guest who wants a beer with dinner has an actual choice of styles. In a resort context that is genuinely rare, and it is the sort of stocking decision that only happens when someone has decided the category matters. Two caveats: this is a full-service restaurant with a substantial agave programme, not an alcohol-free venue, and the Desert Ridge location means a drive from central Phoenix and resort pricing when you arrive. If you are staying at the JW Marriott it is downstairs; if you are not, treat it as a destination dinner rather than somewhere to drop into for a drink, and book — the dining room fills on weekends and the bar is small.
venues.pressQuote: Desert Ridge scores a culinary bullseye with this sexy, modern Southwestern restaurant from celebrity chef Angelo Sosa

venues.name: Time Out Market Boston
venues.description: Time Out Market Boston is a curated food hall at 401 Park Drive in the Fenway, assembled by Time Out's editorial team from local chefs and restaurants, with two bars at opposite ends of the room serving the whole market. Those bars run a seasonal alcohol-free programme developed by Meghan Murphy, the market's assistant general manager and mixologist, built on house-made syrups rather than bought-in mixers, and rotated through the year in the same way as the cocktail list. Alongside the named drinks the bars keep a standing set of alcohol-free options: Sam Adams "Just The Haze" non-alcoholic beer, TOST sparkling rose, kombucha on draft from Luluna in Pawtucket, root beer, cream soda, Culture Pop and fountain soda.
venues.longDescription:
Time Out Market Boston opened in the Fenway at 401 Park Drive as the American outpost of a format Time Out began in Lisbon: a food hall whose tenants are chosen by the magazine's own restaurant critics rather than let to whoever will pay, so the hall functions as a physical version of the city's editorial coverage. The Boston market runs a mix of kitchens from established local restaurants across a large open room, with two bars positioned at opposite ends, and its own description of the bars is that they pour unique, seasonal cocktails alongside a curated list of food-friendly wines and an all-star, all-local beer list, with plenty of non-alcoholic and low-alcohol options available. Because the market opens at 8:30am and runs to 10 or 11pm, the bars serve a much wider span of the day than a conventional cocktail bar, which is part of why the alcohol-free list is developed as seriously as it is.

That programme is the work of Meghan Murphy, the market's assistant general manager and mixologist, and is built around house-made syrups. The drinks rotate seasonally: Lavender Lights combines a lavender syrup with lemonade and a splash of soda, shaken and strained into a Collins glass over cubed ice, topped with sparkling water and garnished with lavender and a lemon wedge. The Vanilla Fig Cooler is built on Q Grapefruit Soda with fig-peppercorn and vanilla syrups. The Blackberry Ginger Fizz uses Q Ginger Beer topped with a blackberry-ginger syrup and lime juice. Winter Warm Spell is the most cocktail-like of the set, combining pineapple juice, coconut cream and lime with a jalapeno syrup and alcohol-free bitters. Earlier menus have carried No New Friends, made with turmeric and hibiscus teas, agave, lime and aquafaba, and The Razzle Dazzle, with blood orange, almond orgeat, cinnamon and ginger beer. Murphy's stated position is that there is no reason to miss out on the fun just due to alcohol, and the standing range backs that up: Sam Adams "Just The Haze", TOST rose, draft kombucha from Luluna of Pawtucket, Rhode Island, root beer, cream soda, Culture Pop and fountain soda.
venues.pressQuote: There's no reason to miss out on the fun just due to alcohol.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Meghan Murphy, assistant general manager and mixologist, Time Out Market Boston

venues.name: Tipping Point Restaurant & Terrace (Hotel ZaZa Memorial City)
venues.description: Tipping Point Restaurant & Terrace is the all-day American restaurant and rooftop terrace at Hotel ZaZa's Michelin Key-rated Memorial City property, open from 6:30am into the early morning daily. Its printed bar menu carries a standing Mocktails section of three $12 zero-proof drinks built from fresh produce and syrups rather than dealcoholized spirits: Verdant Chill, Blush Garden Fizz and Golden Hour Paloma. Houston Press singled out the restaurant's 'short but polished alcohol-free lineup' in its January 2026 Dry January guide.

venues.longDescription:
Tipping Point Restaurant & Terrace occupies the ground floor and poolside terrace of Hotel ZaZa Houston Memorial City, which was completed in 2017 and is owned by developer MetroNational, a west-side companion to the original Hotel ZaZa in Houston's Museum District. The restaurant overlooks the hotel's rooftop Beach Club pool in the Memorial City neighborhood near CityCentre, serving contemporary American food from Dinner, Bar, Brunch and Morning menus, Sunday-Thursday 6:30am-12am and Friday-Saturday 6:30am-1am, with live music on the terrace Saturday nights.

Hotel ZaZa Memorial City received a Michelin Key in the Michelin Guide's inaugural 2024 North American hotel selections. Tipping Point is the hotel's flagship restaurant.

The restaurant's published bar menu keeps a standing Mocktails section alongside its Cocktails, Martinis and Wine lists: three $12 builds -- Verdant Chill, Blush Garden Fizz and Golden Hour Paloma -- made with fresh fruit, herbs and sparkling water rather than spirit alternatives. Houston Press's January 2026 Dry January mocktail guide called out Tipping Point's alcohol-free program by name, describing it as 'a short but polished alcohol-free lineup.' (Note: that same article describes two other zero-proof drinks -- a Blueberry Gin Sour and Zero Proof Margarita using Ritual Gin/Tequila -- attributed to Tipping Point; neither appears on the restaurant's current published bar or drinks menu, so they are not listed here as standing offerings.)
venues.pressQuote: Tipping Point offers a short but polished alcohol-free lineup, including a Blueberry Gin Sour with Ritual Gin and egg white, plus a classic Zero Proof Margarita with Ritual Tequila, lime and agave.

venues.name: Todo Bien
venues.description: Todo Bien is a tiki tequileria tucked into the UnCommons development in southwest Las Vegas, where lead mixologist Rylen Komeiji builds an intentional lineup of non-alcoholic drinks alongside the bar's tequila, mezcal and sotol cocktails. The roughly 1,300-square-foot space leans into a tropical-meets-Mexican aesthetic with lush hanging greenery, patterned textiles and an altar-candle-lit patio. Komeiji's zero-proof creations are designed around dominant fresh flavors rather than sugar, and have been singled out by local press, including a Las Vegas Weekly feature on the city's top mocktail-makers and a 2025 Las Vegas Magazine roundup of the valley's best no-alcohol drinks. The aim, in his words, is to "make everyone feel included," whether guests want spirited drinks or refreshment without alcohol. It's a strong pick for someone who wants a genuine craft mocktail in a stylish bar setting rather than a soda-and-juice afterthought.
venues.address: 8533 Rozita Lee Ave, Ste 110, Las Vegas, NV 89113
venues.longDescription:
Todo Bien is a tiki tequileria in the UnCommons development in southwest Las Vegas — a mash-up of Polynesian tiki convention and Mexican agave culture that in less careful hands would be a gimmick and here is mostly a coherent bar. The room runs about 1,300 square feet and is dressed accordingly: lush hanging greenery, patterned textiles, and a patio lit with altar candles. The spirits list goes deep on tequila, mezcal and sotol with a well-chosen cerveza list beside it, general manager Curt Knickerbocker runs the floor, and Rylen Komeiji leads the bar. The name is the thesis — todo bien, all is good — and the bar has built programming around Mexican cultural events rather than treating the theme as decor.

Komeiji's non-alcoholic drinks are the reason the bar is worth a specific trip for someone not drinking. They are designed around a dominant fresh flavour rather than around sugar, which is the single most common failure of a mocktail, and they are named and listed like everything else: the Crotch Kick, the Melon Pepino, the Sandia Frambuesa, the N/Alote and the Sundown Sipper. Local press has repeatedly singled the program out, including a Las Vegas Weekly feature on the city's best mocktail-makers and a 2025 Las Vegas Magazine round-up of the valley's best drinks without alcohol. Komeiji has framed the intent plainly, telling Las Vegas Weekly that people are drinking a little healthier and that what the bar wants to do is make everyone feel included. For a guest who wants a genuine craft zero-proof drink in a stylish bar rather than a juice served apologetically, this is one of the strongest options outside the Strip. The bar is closed Mondays and opens at 4:30pm the rest of the week, running to midnight and to 1am on Friday and Saturday.
venues.pressQuote: One of the great things to come out of the pandemic is people are focusing more on quality over quantity and also just drinking a little healthier. What we want to do is make everyone feel included.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Rylen Komeiji, lead mixologist, Todo Bien

venues.name: À Toi
venues.description: À Toi is a 1920s Paris-inspired speakeasy and cocktail bar in Toronto's Entertainment District, hidden behind a pearly pink oyster bar inside a historic 1920s boutique hotel. It's part of the COC (Coffee, Oysters and Champagne) hospitality concept, and takes its name — French for "to you" — from an inside joke between the hotel's builder, French millionaire Antoine Mercier, and his wife, Isabel. Alongside its raw oyster and classic-cocktail menus, À Toi runs a standing, six-item zero-proof cocktail list, all $16, built on Giffard Alcohol-Free Liqueur as the base spirit.

venues.hours: Mon closed; Tue-Wed 5pm-11pm; Thu 5pm-12am; Fri-Sat 5pm-1am; Sun closed

Ce N'est Pas Une Sortie — honey, lemon, lavender, jasmine, soda ($16, Giffard Alcohol Free Liqueur base)

1920s Orchard — watermelon cordial, lemon, white peach Red Bull, soda ($16, Giffard Alcohol Free Liqueur base)

venues.longDescription:
À Toi is a 1920s Paris-inspired speakeasy and cocktail bar tucked inside a historic boutique hotel on King Street West, part of the COC (Coffee, Oysters and Champagne) hospitality concept. Per venue lore, the building was put up in the 1920s by French millionaire Antoine Mercier as a gift to the city, with the hotel's name — à toi, French for "to you" — an inside joke between Mercier and his wife, Isabel; Mercier reportedly died during construction under circumstances that were investigated but never resolved, and Isabel completed the build, centering it on the lobby bar that carries the hotel's name. Canada's 100 Best summed up the effect on its 2023 list of the country's best bars, where À Toi ranked No. 20: "The pearly pink oyster bar is merely a front for a lavishly embellished speakeasy with layers of secret chambers." Inside, the room leans into rich jewel tones and 1920s glamour, pairing an extensive raw and dressed oyster program with classic cognac, absinthe and champagne-forward cocktails, plus a late-night comfort menu of poutine, grilled cheese and a banquet burger.

The bar sits at 214 King St W, on the border of the Entertainment and Financial Districts near St. Andrew subway station. It's open Tuesday through Saturday from 5pm to 2am and Sunday from 8pm to midnight, closed Mondays, with reservations taken through SevenRooms; the venue also hosts private events, weddings and corporate parties.

À Toi runs a standing, six-item zero-proof cocktail menu, every drink $16 and built on Giffard Alcohol-Free Liqueur as the base spirit rather than treated as an afterthought pour. The list spans the Garden Daiquiri (cherry, honey, grapefruit, lime), Ce N'est Pas Une Sortie (honey, lemon, lavender, jasmine, soda), Bébé Picante (watermelon, lime, fire tincture), 1920s Orchard (watermelon cordial, lemon, white peach Red Bull, soda), Best Friends (blueberry rooibos tea, peach, lemon) and Old Flames (plum, lime, honey, ginger beer) — a named, priced, ingredient-listed section that puts the zero-proof list on equal footing with the bar's alcoholic cocktail menu.
venues.pressQuote: The pearly pink oyster bar is merely a front for a lavishly embellished speakeasy with layers of secret chambers.

venues.name: Tongue in Cheek
venues.description: Tongue in Cheek is a long-running New American restaurant and bar on Payne Avenue on Saint Paul's East Side, known for a heavily vegan-friendly kitchen and a bar team that builds to order. Its non-alcoholic offering is listed as The Placebos, a set of zero-proof drinks spanning several flavour profiles that can also be ordered as a flight, and the bartenders will build a custom alcohol-free drink to a described flavour profile rather than pointing at a fixed list. The bar also makes beer cocktails that can be built non-alcoholic — the Passion of Cayenne, with passion fruit, cayenne and jalapeno salt, works on Athletic Brewing's Upside Dawn.
signatureDrinks: The Placebos (zero-proof flight across several flavour profiles)
Passion of Cayenne (passion fruit, cayenne, jalapeno salt, Athletic Brewing Upside Dawn)
venues.longDescription:
Payne Avenue runs north from Saint Paul's East Side into Payne-Phalen, and Tongue in Cheek has been one of its anchors for years — a New American restaurant with an unusually deep vegan and vegetarian menu, a tasting-menu option, and a bar that has always been more ambitious than the room's storefront exterior suggests. It trades Wednesday through Sunday, daytime into the evening, which makes it one of the few places on this list that works for an early dinner as well as a late one.

The non-alcoholic offering is structured around a named set called The Placebos, spanning several flavour profiles and available as a flight so that a table can taste across the range rather than committing to one glass. Underneath that is the part that matters more: the bar builds to order. Rather than handing a non-drinker a fixed list of three sweet options, the bartenders will construct an entirely alcohol-free drink to a described flavour profile — bitter, herbaceous, sour, whatever is asked for — which is the same service a full-strength guest gets. Visit Saint Paul's guide to drinking without alcohol in the city describes it as a bar that "makes great use of its talented beverage team in building any drink, including those without alcohol." Separately, the bar runs a line of beer cocktails, several of which can be built non-alcoholic; the Passion of Cayenne combines passion fruit, cayenne and jalapeno salt over Athletic Brewing's Upside Dawn golden ale, giving a zero-proof drink with the bitterness and carbonation that make beer cocktails work. This is a licensed restaurant with a full bar, and the non-alcoholic programme is a real but modest part of it rather than the centre — the strength of the offer is the bar team's willingness to build rather than a long printed spirit-free list.
venues.pressQuote: This Eastside bar makes great use of its talented beverage team in building any drink, including those without alcohol.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Visit Saint Paul, Where to Drink When You're Not Drinking

venues.name: Tony's Siesta
venues.description: Tony's Siesta on Brooklyn Avenue keeps mocktails on the menu year-round rather than wheeling them out for Dry January, and the list includes a build using non-alcoholic rum. That first detail is the one worth caring about: a great many bars discover zero-proof drinks every January and quietly drop them by March, which is precisely when someone who has actually stopped drinking needs them. A permanent list is a different kind of commitment. It also runs to 2am seven nights a week, from 4pm on weekdays and 2pm at weekends. That puts it among the latest alcohol-free-friendly options in the city, alongside Idle Beer Hall a few doors away.
signatureDrinks: Year-round mocktail list including a non-alcoholic rum build
venues.longDescription:
Tony's Siesta is on Brooklyn Avenue in River North, near the Pearl and a short walk from Idle Beer Hall and Isidore. It is a bar rather than a restaurant, and it keeps mocktails on the menu all year, including a build using non-alcoholic rum.

The year-round part is the whole point of this listing. Every January a wave of bars discovers the alcohol-free customer, prints a Dry January menu, collects the press coverage, and quietly removes it in February. For someone doing a one-month challenge that is fine. For someone who has actually stopped drinking — which is a permanent condition, not a seasonal one — it is worse than useless, because it teaches you that a venue's published list cannot be trusted in March. A bar that carries the same drinks in July is making a much smaller promise and keeping it, which is worth more.

The non-alcoholic rum matters for a related reason. Rum is one of the harder spirits to substitute convincingly — its character comes from sugar, funk and barrel age rather than from botanicals — so a bar stocking an NA version is buying a specialist product with limited use rather than reaching for the nearest syrup.

The hours are among the best in the guide: 4pm to 2am Monday through Friday, and from 2pm at weekends, every day of the week. Combined with Idle Beer Hall next door, Brooklyn Avenue gives a non-drinker two genuinely late options within a couple of minutes of each other — and in a city where much of the alcohol-free provision closes by seven, that is the most useful thing on this page. The Pearl is a short walk north, so an evening can start with dinner there and end here without anyone needing to drive.
venues.pressQuote: Tony's Siesta serves mocktails year-round, including a NA-rum option.

venues.name: Topside
venues.description: Topside is the rooftop restaurant on the 14th floor of Hotel Revival in Mount Vernon, with panoramic views of the Washington Monument and the Baltimore skyline. Its non-alcoholic program is a formally named one — “Zero Proof, Zero Judgment,” created by bartender Anna Welker — and it runs as a full spirit-free menu rather than a single token pour. The drinks are built on gin and tequila alternatives with house ingredients like pineapple shrub and Aztec chocolate bitters; the signature Yellow Balloons layers cinnamon-infused ginger turmeric tea with pineapple shrub and grapefruit bitters. Rotating cans from the Baltimore non-alcoholic brand NOPE round out the list alongside NA beer and wine, and the program was successful enough to draw its own local TV coverage.
venues.longDescription:
Topside sits on the 14th floor of Hotel Revival at 101 W Monument Street in Mount Vernon, in what was the Peabody Court Hotel — when the hospitality group took the building over, the smart move was to use the panoramic windows at the top of it, and the result has the best view of any dining room in Baltimore, taking in the Washington Monument and the harbour beyond. Baltimore Magazine described a room that feels airy and modern with light woods and geometric accents, on a loose beer-garden theme. The kitchen leans local and seasonal. Dinner runs 5pm to 10pm Monday through Saturday and to 11pm on Sundays, with weekend brunch from 10am and happy hour weekdays from 4pm to 6pm. Valet parking is available at the hotel and walk-ins are taken subject to space.

The non-alcoholic programme has a name that tells you the intent — Zero Proof, Zero Judgment — and it is written into how the bar describes itself: elevated American cooking with handcrafted cocktails, local beers and booze-free creations built on regional flavours. That framing matters more than it might sound, because a rooftop bar with a view is exactly the kind of venue where a non-drinker most often ends up holding a soft drink while everyone else has something considered. The documented house drink is Yellow Balloons, which Baltimore Magazine described as spicy and built from cinnamon-infused ginger turmeric tea, a pineapple shrub and grapefruit bitters — a shrub-and-tea construction rather than a juice mix, which is what gives it length. Two caveats worth having in advance: the bar does not publish a drink-by-drink menu online, so the current zero-proof list has to be asked about at the table, and Yellow Balloons itself was documented in early 2025, so treat it as the house style rather than a guarantee. Hotel Revival currently lists Topside as its rooftop restaurant alongside its cafe and karaoke room.
venues.pressQuote: Innovative recipes include the spicy Yellow Balloons (cinnamon-infused ginger turmeric tea, pineapple shrub, and grapefruit bitters).

venues.name: Toro Toro
venues.description: Toro Toro is the pan-Latin steakhouse on the ground floor of the InterContinental Miami at 100 Chopin Plaza, part of chef Richard Sandoval's group. Its non-alcoholic list is not a footnote on the cocktail card but a separate menu, printed and linked alongside the lunch, dinner, bar, drinks and wine lists as "Zero Proof". The restaurant runs it under Sandoval's group-wide Art of Zero Proof programme, which the company describes as flavourful, beautifully crafted drinks showcasing culinary artistry, creativity and elevated indulgence without alcohol. Named builds include the Espresso Maíztini, a spirit-free reworking of the espresso martini, plus the Garden Grove and a Grapefruit Sour. RESIDENT called it one of the city's most extensive zero-proof lineups in December 2025. The dining room runs to 11pm Tuesday through Saturday.
venues.longDescription:
Toro Toro occupies the ground floor of the InterContinental Miami at 100 Chopin Plaza, on the downtown bayfront between Bayfront Park and the Miami River. It is a Richard Sandoval restaurant, pan-Latin in format, and it trades from noon until 10pm on Monday and Sunday and until 11pm from Tuesday through Saturday. For a guest who is not drinking, the structural detail that matters is how the drinks are presented: the restaurant's menu page lists Lunch, Dinner, Bar Menu, Drinks, Zero Proof, Miami Spice and Wine List as separate documents, which means the alcohol-free options are ordered from their own menu rather than requested off-list from a bartender.

That menu sits inside a programme Richard Sandoval Hospitality runs across its restaurants under the name Art of Zero Proof, which the group describes on Toro Toro's own site as celebrating flavourful, beautifully crafted drinks showcasing culinary artistry, creativity and elevated indulgence without alcohol. Named builds documented in December 2025 coverage include the Espresso Maíztini, an alcohol-free remix of the espresso martini that leans on corn as well as coffee, along with the Garden Grove and a Grapefruit Sour. RESIDENT, surveying twenty Miami venues for Dry January 2026, placed Toro Toro at the head of the list and wrote that each drink is built with technique and depth. Full ingredient specifications for the individual builds are not published on the restaurant's public menu page, so this entry records the names only rather than guessing at what is in them; a guest should expect the list to rotate. The restaurant can be reached on (305) 372-4710 and posts as @torotoromiami. Two further details are worth recording for anyone planning a visit. The first is that the Zero Proof list is one of seven separate menus the restaurant publishes, sitting alongside the wine list rather than beneath it, which means the alcohol-free order does not depend on a server improvising. The second is that Toro Toro publishes a Miami Spice menu — the city's late-summer prix-fixe programme — alongside its regular lists, so the room's pricing changes in August and September. Reservations run through the restaurant's site and by telephone.
venues.pressQuote: Toro Toro offers one of the city's most extensive zero-proof lineups.

venues.name: Torra Tea
venues.description: Torra is a Scottish high-tea room and bar off Dishman Mica Road in Spokane Valley, opened in August 2024 by Kathryn Soady — the name is Scottish Gaelic for "from the castle". It pours close to forty loose-leaf teas across black, green, white, yellow and herbal, served hot or iced, and builds tea-infused lemonades and mocktails from the same leaf as the cocktails on the other half of the list. Food runs from scones and finger sandwiches for afternoon tea to short ribs and meat pies. The room is gilded and glamorous rather than cottagecore, with white-linen service, and it is open Tuesday to Saturday from 11am to 8pm.
venues.address: 11205 E Dishman Mica Rd Suite 104-C, Spokane Valley, WA 99206
venues.longDescription:
Torra opened in August 2024 in a shopping district off Dishman Mica Road in Spokane Valley, and it is a genuinely odd and welcome hybrid: a Scottish high-tea room that is also a craft bar. Owner Kathryn Soady named it with the Scottish Gaelic for "from the castle", and fitted it out in gilded, streamlined glamour — chandeliers, deep earthy tones, curated artwork, crisp white linen — rather than the floral cottage look the format usually attracts.

The tea list is the substance of it: close to forty loose-leaf teas across black, green, white and yellow, plus a wide herbal range, served hot or iced. Almost as many whiskeys sit on the other side of the bar, and the two halves talk to each other — the same leaf that goes into a pot goes into tea-infused lemonades and into the mocktails, which are built rather than poured. For a non-drinker that structure is the appeal. In most bars the alcohol-free list is a smaller, worse version of the main one; here the tea programme is the deepest thing in the building, and ordering from it is ordering the house specialty.

The food runs the full range of the format, from freshly baked scones and finger sandwiches for a proper afternoon tea through to short ribs and meat pies for a heavier, pub-inspired meal, which means it works as dinner rather than only as an afternoon stop.

This entry is graded three rather than four: the mocktails are documented by the Spokesman-Review and the Inlander as part of the drinks list, but the individual builds are not published in a form that could be read for this guide, so none are recorded as signature drinks. The tea programme is the reason to come and it is verified in detail.

Open Tuesday to Saturday, 11am to 8pm. Closed Sunday and Monday.
venues.pressQuote: Torra means 'from the castle.' I really want my guests to feel like they've had an experience from the castle.

venues.name: The Town Company
venues.description: The Town Company is the flagship restaurant inside Hotel Kansas City, the Unbound Collection by Hyatt property in a restored downtown landmark at 12th and Baltimore. Led by James Beard-nominated executive chef Johnny Leach and executive pastry chef Helen Jo Leach — alumni of Del Posto, Momofuku, and Eleven Madison Park who relocated from Portland to open it — the restaurant centers a seasonally rotating menu on a white-oak-burning hearth and a network of local farmers. Its bar program includes named zero-proof cocktails alongside the spirited list: the "Clear Headed," built on Ritual's rum alternative with Earl Grey and smoked vanilla, and a zero-proof piña colada made with hearth-roasted pineapple, mint, coconut water, and lime. The NA pours are crafted with the same hearth-and-seasonal approach as the kitchen.
signatureDrinks: Clear Headed (Ritual rum alternative, Earl Grey tea, smoked vanilla)
venues.longDescription:
The Town Company is the flagship restaurant of Hotel Kansas City, the Unbound Collection by Hyatt property that occupies the old Kansas City Club building downtown — a 1922 landmark on the National Register of Historic Places, converted into a hotel and opened as a restaurant on 15 October 2020. The room was built around an open-hearth, wood-fired oven with its own art deco bar alongside, and the cooking runs through it: Clara Bow rolls proofed and baked in a cast-iron pan and served with cultured butter and a roasted carrot dip, lamb skewers combining grilled leg, braised tongue and house-made sausage with roasted aubergine purée and honey vinegar, and an angel food cheesecake with black sesame ganache and a pomegranate-poached pear. Executive chef Johnny Leach has been recognised by the James Beard Foundation in three consecutive years, named a semifinalist for Outstanding Chef in 2023 and for Best Chef: Midwest in 2025; his wife Helen Jo Leach runs pastry and was herself a 2025 semifinalist for Outstanding Pastry Chef.

The non-alcoholic drinks are treated as a named part of the bar rather than an afterthought — the restaurant calls them "no proof" options, which is a small signal that someone chose the language deliberately. The one that has drawn attention is Clear Headed, built on Ritual's rum alternative with Earl Grey tea and smoked vanilla: tannic and smoky rather than fruity, and designed to sit alongside the wood-fired cooking rather than to imitate a cocktail. KCUR singled it out when mapping where to drink well without alcohol in Kansas City. Two practical caveats. The restaurant does not maintain its own web presence any more — its address now redirects into the Hyatt booking system, which does not publish the drinks list — so the current zero-proof options are best confirmed on arrival. And note that published sources disagree about the building's street address, since the hotel occupies a corner with entrances on both 13th Street and Baltimore Avenue.
venues.pressQuote: You can stay Clear Headed (one of The Town Co. signature 'no proof' options) with Ritual's rum alternative, Earl Grey tea and smoked vanilla.

venues.name: Track Brewing Co Taproom
venues.description: Track Brewing Co is one of Manchester's most celebrated modern craft breweries, and its taproom sits inside the working brewhouse on the Piccadilly Trading Estate, minutes from Piccadilly station. The 2,000 sq ft room pours 20 keg and 3 cask lines straight from the tanks that brewed them, with a beer garden for sunny days and Slice Culture pizza through the back half of the week. For non-drinkers, the draw is Sonoma AF — the 0.5% alcohol-free version of Track's flagship Sonoma pale, brewed in-house and poured by the pint from a dedicated alcohol-free spot on the draught menu.
venues.address: Unit 18, Piccadilly Trading Estate, Manchester M1 2NP
signatureDrinks: Sonoma AF — 0.5% alcohol-free pale ale (Citra & Mosaic), poured by the pint
venues.longDescription:
Track Brewing Co is among Manchester's most respected modern craft breweries, built on a reputation for hazy, hop-forward pales, IPAs and DIPAs. In 2021 it moved into a 10,000 sq ft home on the Piccadilly Trading Estate, a few minutes' walk east of Piccadilly station, and carved a 2,000 sq ft taproom out of the working brewhouse. The open-plan room seats around 80 beneath a colourful, Wes Anderson-ish fit-out, with the fermentation tanks sitting within arm's reach of the bar — so the keg pouring into your glass often came off the tank just metres away.

Twenty keg lines and three cask pumps run the length of the bar, alongside wines, spirits and soft drinks, and the taproom is both dog- and child-friendly. There's a beer garden for the Manchester sun and Slice Culture pizza slung from the kitchen through the second half of the week, making the place feel as much a neighbourhood local as a brewery tap.

The alcohol-free draw is Sonoma AF, the 0.5% version of Track's flagship Sonoma pale ale. Because it is brewed in-house rather than bought in, it keeps the beer's signature Citra and Mosaic hop character — bright citrus and light tropical notes over a soft malt base. It sits in its own alcohol-free slot on the taproom's draught menu and is poured by the pint, so non-drinkers get the full post-work-pint experience rather than a token can from the fridge. With the full-strength Sonoma a near-permanent fixture on cask, the AF pour is a genuine like-for-like swap: the same beer, without the alcohol.

venues.name: Traveler's Table
venues.description: Traveler's Table is a globally-inspired restaurant in Montrose, open since 2019 and built around dishes gathered from world travel — soft-shell crab fried rice, duck pad see ew, chiles en nogada, Nigerian suya skewers, Brazilian cheese bread — with a cocktail list that follows the same passport theme. It won Houston Press's Best of Houston 2025 award for Best Steak Night and has appeared on Food Network's Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives. For non-drinkers it prints a dedicated "No Proof" section of two spirit-free builds on Ritual Zero Proof alternatives: La Vida Tranquila, made with Ritual's tequila alternative, hibiscus simple, lime, a hibiscus salt rim and a candied hibiscus flower, and To Have And Have Not, built on Ritual's rum alternative with passion fruit, mango, mint, lime and soda. Both are $12, the same price as the alcoholic cocktails — a deliberate parity. The Montrose patio is the draw.
signatureDrinks: La Vida Tranquila (Ritual tequila alternative, hibiscus simple, lime juice, hibiscus salt, dehydrated lime, candied hibiscus flower)
To Have And Have Not (Ritual rum alternative, passion fruit, mango, mint, lime juice, soda, dehydrated lime, mint sprig)

naMenuItems.name: La Vida Tranquila
naMenuItems.description: ritual tequila alternative, hibiscus simple, lime juice, hibiscus salt, dehydrated lime, candied hibiscus flower

venues.longDescription:
Traveler's Table opened in Montrose in 2019, built around dishes gathered from travel — soft-shell crab fried rice, duck pad see ew, chiles en nogada, Nigerian suya skewers, Brazilian cheese bread — with cuisines spanning Latin America, the Mediterranean and East and Southeast Asia. The cocktail list follows the same passport conceit. The restaurant won Houston Press's Best of Houston 2025 award for Best Steak Night on the strength of its $30 Tuesday globetrotting steak special, and has appeared on Food Network's Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives.

For non-drinkers there is a dedicated section headed "No Proof", with two spirit-free builds on Ritual Zero Proof alternatives. La Vida Tranquila takes Ritual's tequila alternative into a hibiscus simple syrup with lime, served with a hibiscus salt rim, a dehydrated lime wheel and a candied hibiscus flower. To Have And Have Not uses Ritual's rum alternative with passion fruit, mango, mint, lime and soda, finished with dehydrated lime and a mint sprig.

Two things about those builds are worth drawing out. The first is hibiscus, which appears twice in one drink — as a syrup and ground into the salt on the rim. Dried hibiscus is genuinely tart rather than merely fruity, closer to cranberry than to berry, and blending it into a salt rim means every sip opens with sour and saline before the sweetness arrives. That front-loaded acidity is exactly what a zero-proof drink needs to avoid tasting flat. The second is the garnish work. Dehydrated citrus and a candied flower take preparation days in advance, and a kitchen that does that for its non-alcoholic drinks is treating them as menu items rather than as an accommodation.

Both are $12, matching the price of the full cocktail programme — a deliberate parity that says the labour is the same.

The lively Montrose patio is the main draw, and the format suits a mixed table: dinner is served nightly with weekend brunch from ten in the morning, running to eleven on Friday and Saturday. A 2026 Houston Restaurant Weeks menu beginning in August confirms the restaurant remains active and current.
venues.pressQuote: Steak night goes globetrotting at this eclectic Montrose gem, where Tuesday evenings usher in a passport of flavors for $30 a plate.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Houston Press, "Best of Houston® 2025: Best Steak Night"

venues.name: Traveling Mercies
venues.description: Traveling Mercies is a third-floor oyster and cocktail bar in Stanley Marketplace, the converted aviation factory on the Denver–Aurora line, opened in 2024 by James Beard Award-winning chef Caroline Glover with Nelson Harvey. It was a James Beard semifinalist for Best New Bar and named one of Esquire's Best Bars in America in 2024. The bar runs a descriptive non-alcoholic menu that Westword singles out as friendly to newcomers — the Fizz, which the paper reports as "silky and pleasant, much like a milkshake", and the "childlike, verdant and bright" Ocean Water, made with seaside botanicals, ruby red grapefruit and citrus. The food is raw bar and comfort classics: oysters, shrimp cocktail, wedge salads and rice pudding.
venues.hours: Mon closed; Tue-Thu 4pm-9pm; Fri 4pm-10pm; Sat 3pm-10pm; Sun 3pm-9pm
signatureDrinks: Ocean Water (seaside botanicals, ruby red grapefruit and citrus)
The Fizz (described by Westword as silky and pleasant, much like a milkshake)
venues.longDescription:
Traveling Mercies sits on the third floor, west side, of Stanley Marketplace at 2501 Dallas Street — the former Stanley Aviation factory that straddles the Denver–Aurora boundary in the Central Park area, close enough to the city line that most of its trade is Denver-side. It opened in 2024 from Caroline Glover, the James Beard Foundation Award-winning chef behind Annette in the same building, with Nelson Harvey. The bar landed immediately: a James Beard Foundation semifinalist for Best New Bar and one of Esquire's Best Bars in America for 2024, and a 2025 James Beard semifinalist again.

The format is an intimate oyster and cocktail bar. The food is a raw bar built on oysters and shrimp cocktail with a nightly tackle box sampler, set against deliberately unfussy comfort classics — wedge salads, rice pudding — and the cocktails focus on aperitivos and rum with a coastal-leaning wine list behind them. Where the bar differs from most rooms of its calibre is that its non-alcoholic drinks come with the same descriptive treatment as everything else, which is what Westword picked up on in its January 2026 guide, recommending it as somewhere to go "for a descriptive mocktail menu that's friendly to newcomers". The paper named two: the Fizz, which it quotes as "silky and pleasant, much like a milkshake", and the Ocean Water, described as "childlike, verdant and bright" and built from seaside botanicals with ruby red grapefruit and citrus — a composition that reads as designed for the oysters rather than borrowed from a soda list. The bar is closed on Mondays and opens at 4pm Tuesday to Friday and 3pm at weekends, closing at 9pm or 10pm. For anyone in the Central Park, Stapleton or northwest Aurora part of the metro, it is the most serious drinks room within walking distance, and the non-alcoholic list is written so that a first-time non-drinker can order from it without having to ask what anything is.
venues.pressQuote: Options include the Fizz, which is 'silky and pleasant, much like a milkshake,' and the 'childlike, verdant and bright' Ocean Water made with seaside botanicals, ruby red grapefruit and citrus.

venues.name: Trick Dog
venues.description: Trick Dog is a cocktail bar at 3010 20th Street in the Mission, opened in 2013 by Josh Harris and known for elaborately designed, fully themed drink menus that the team reinvents roughly every six months. Harris is sober, and the bar deliberately integrates zero-proof drinks into the same menu sections, with the same creative names, as the full-proof list rather than isolating them as a separate category — so a non-drinker gets the identical ordering experience. Past alcohol-free builds include Puppy Pose, a creamy green milk punch with wheatgrass, yogurt and non-alcoholic spirits, and the Wydah, built on Ritual Tequila Alternative and Wilfred's aperitif. Trick Dog was named Best U.S. Cocktail Bar at the 2025 Spirited Awards and has twice won World's Best Cocktail Menu.
venues.longDescription:
Trick Dog opened in 2013 at 3010 20th Street in the Mission and has spent the decade since as one of the most-copied cocktail bars in the world. Its defining trick is the menu itself: roughly every six months the team scraps the list and rebuilds it around an entirely new conceit, designing and printing the object from scratch, so that the menu functions as a piece of graphic design as much as a list of drinks. The bar has twice won World's Best Cocktail Menu and was named Best U.S. Cocktail Bar at the 2025 Spirited Awards. It opens at 4pm daily and runs to 2am on Fridays and Saturdays, and doubles as the waiting room for Flour + Water across the way, which is part of why it is consistently full.

Founder Josh Harris has been sober for years, and that shapes a non-alcoholic programme built on a specific and unusual principle: rather than grouping zero-proof drinks into a separate section at the back, Trick Dog folds them into the same menu sections as everything else, with the same invented names and the same design treatment. A non-drinker ordering here is not visibly ordering from a different list. Kane's December 2023 survey in The San Francisco Standard put the reasoning plainly, reporting that "for Josh Harris, the Mission hot spot's sober founder, it's important to integrate nonalcoholic drinks into the menu rather than isolate them as a standalone category." Because the whole list is rebuilt twice a year the specific drinks turn over, but past alcohol-free builds show the ambition: Puppy Pose, a creamy green milk punch made with wheatgrass, yogurt and non-alcoholic spirits, and the Wydah, which layers spirit alternatives including Ritual Tequila Alternative and Wilfred's aperitif. The practical consequence is that the zero-proof options should be treated as a guarantee of approach rather than a fixed menu to plan around — whatever the current theme, there will be drinks on it made without alcohol.
venues.pressQuote: Trick Dog is a ridiculously popular bar (and Flour + Water waiting spot) in the Mission that serves creative cocktails that are actually good (and not just pretentious).

venues.name: Trina's Starlite Lounge
venues.description: Trina's Starlite Lounge is a Somerville lounge that opened in the Winter Hill neighborhood in 2009 and built its reputation on dive-bar food done carefully — dressed-up tater tots, baked mac-and-cheese and Southern-inflected comfort cooking — served in a small, booth-filled room that trades until 1am on weeknights and 2am at weekends. Its non-alcoholic offering is currently narrow. As of August 2026 the bar's published drinks list carries no mocktail, zero-proof or spirit-free section, and the only alcohol-free item on it is Notch Non-Alcoholic Pils from Salem, Massachusetts, at $7. The Boston Globe featured the bar in a January 2025 round-up of $5 booze-free cocktails, but that program is no longer listed. Seating is first-come, first-served, and a Sunday brunch runs from 11am.

venues.longDescription:
Trina's Starlite Lounge opened in Somerville's Winter Hill in 2009 and has spent more than fifteen years as a neighborhood lounge and industry hangout — the kind of room where kitchen staff turn up once their own shifts have ended. It is credited locally with helping popularize dressed-up bar food, loaded tater tots and baked mac-and-cheese and Southern-inflected fried chicken among them, well before that became a standard restaurant move, and the cooking is still the reason most people come. The space is small, dark and booth-filled, run first-come first-served with reservations taken only for Valentine's Day, and it keeps genuinely late hours: 5pm to 1am Monday through Thursday, 5pm to 2am on Friday and Saturday, and 11am to 1am on Sunday, when brunch runs until 3pm.

For non-alcoholic drinkers the picture has narrowed, and it is worth being precise about it. The Boston Globe included Trina's in a January 2025 round-up of spots serving booze-free cocktails, singling out a $5 mocktail list that ran to a Phony Negroni and a floral drink built on Fluere Botanic Blend. As of August 2026 that program is no longer on the published menu: the bar's own drinks list has no mocktail, zero-proof or spirit-free heading anywhere on it, and the single alcohol-free item is Notch Non-Alcoholic Pils from Salem, Massachusetts, listed at $7 alongside the draught beers. That is a real option and Notch is a well-regarded Massachusetts brewery, but one non-alcoholic beer is the whole of it. Anyone arriving expecting a made-to-order alcohol-free cocktail should ask at the bar rather than assume the Globe's list still stands. The remainder of the drinks menu is a rotating cocktail program, draught and canned beer, and a short wine list. The bar sits at 3 Beacon Street, a short walk from Inman Square on the Somerville side of the line, and takes phone enquiries during service if you want to check what is pouring before making the trip.

venues.name: True Chesapeake Oyster Co.
venues.description: True Chesapeake Oyster Co. is an oyster bar and restaurant in the restored Whitehall Mill complex at 3300 Clipper Mill Road in Woodberry, opened 17 September 2019 and sourcing from its own farm — co-founder Patrick Hudson began oyster gardening with his father, and chef Zack Mills was named Maryland's Chef of the Year for 2025 by the Restaurant Association of Maryland. Baltimore Magazine gave it Best Happy Hour in its 2024 Best of Baltimore awards. Its non-alcoholic offering is the deepest of any Baltimore restaurant here, covering all three formats: six built drinks under "Spirit Free Cocktails" — the Goose ($9, non-alcoholic bitter apéritif, pineapple, lime, molasses), a St Nalder Spritz ($11), The N/A-torious F.I.G. ($9), a Northside ($8, lemon, lime, mint, sugar, club soda), a Palmer Thyme ($6) and St. Agrestis's Phony Negroni ($10) — alongside six non-alcoholic beers and four non-alcoholic wines by glass and bottle, including a Steinbock Zero sparkling rosé.

St Nalder Spritz (NA bitter apéritif, NA sparkling wine, club soda, orange) $11

Northside (lemon, lime, mint, sugar, club soda) $8
Palmer Thyme (iced tea, lemon, thyme simple syrup) $6
venues.longDescription:
True Chesapeake Oyster Co. opened on 17 September 2019 at 3300 Clipper Mill Road, in the restored sailcloth factory of the Whitehall Mill complex in Woodberry, and it is the rare oyster restaurant that also farms the oysters. Co-founder Patrick Hudson was born and raised in Baltimore and began oyster gardening with his father; shucker Nick Schauman co-founded it with him, and chef Zack Mills — from Davidsonville, a 2007 French Culinary Institute graduate who was sous chef at Bourbon Steak in Washington under Michael Mina — runs the kitchen. Mills was named Chef of the Year for 2025 by the Restaurant Association of Maryland. The dining rooms have wraparound bars made of pressed oyster shell and an elevated copper shucking station, and the house oysters come from the company's own farm — a huckleberry at $2.75, a chunky dunker at $3. Baltimore Magazine gave it Best Happy Hour in its Best of Baltimore 2024 awards, singling out $2 oysters and 25 per cent off bar snacks, Tuesday to Friday from 5pm to 7pm.

The non-alcoholic list is the deepest of any restaurant in this guide's Baltimore section, and it covers all three formats. Six built drinks sit under "Spirit Free Cocktails": the Goose ($9) on a non-alcoholic bitter apéritif with pineapple, lime and molasses; a St Nalder Spritz ($11) pairing that apéritif with non-alcoholic sparkling wine; The N/A-torious F.I.G. ($9) using a house fig jam with lemon and ginger; a Northside ($8) of lemon, lime, mint and soda; a Palmer Thyme ($6) built on iced tea; and St. Agrestis's bottled Phony Negroni at $10. Six non-alcoholic beers follow, from Guinness 0.0 to Athletic's Cerveza Atlética and a Deschutes Super Stoked. Most unusual of all, there are four non-alcoholic wines by the glass and bottle, including a Steinbock Zero sparkling rosé and Le Naturel Zero Zero. For a room built around raw shellfish, having genuine sparkling wine without alcohol is the single most useful thing on the list. Note that a drink previously listed here as a Baltimore Southside does not appear on the current menu.
venues.pressQuote: Maryland's first oyster farm restaurant turns into a happy hour hangout with $2 raw and roasted St. Jerome Creek oysters, terrific cocktails, plus 25 percent off on bar snacks.

venues.name: True Food Kitchen
venues.description: True Food Kitchen in Preston Center runs a printed Zero-Proof Cocktails section alongside its seasonally driven food programme, built with recognised non-alcoholic spirits rather than juice-and-soda standbys. The Spicy Clean Margarita leans on Clean & Co. zero-proof tequila with pineapple, lime, jalapeño and mint — a credible riff on the bar's signature cocktail. The Sparkling Sangria uses Lyre's Sparkling as its base, and the Hangover Rx, off the cold beverages list, combines pineapple, orange, honey and coconut water. The kitchen serves weekend brunch from 10am, takes reservations through OpenTable, and skews family-friendly, which makes it a straightforward choice for a table with mixed drinking preferences.

venues.longDescription:
Tucked into the open-air Plaza at Preston Center — a walkable retail and dining destination at Preston Road and Northwest Highway — True Food Kitchen runs one of the more substantive zero-proof programs among Dallas full-service restaurants. The dedicated "Zero-Proof Cocktails" section on the menu isn't an afterthought: it features multiple named, ingredient-forward drinks built with recognized NA spirits rather than juice-and-soda standbys. The Park Cities location draws a crowd that skews health-conscious and active, and sober-curious diners fit in seamlessly here without the usual awkwardness of asking a server to improvise.

The Spicy Clean Margarita leans on Clean & Co. zero-proof tequila with pineapple, lime, jalapeño, and mint — a credible riff on the bar's signature cocktail that holds its own on complexity. The Sparkling Sangria uses Lyre's Sparkling as its base, rounded out with pineapple for a festive, wine-adjacent pour. Off the cold beverages menu, the Hangover Rx — pineapple, orange, honey, and coconut water — is a longtime house staple worth ordering with brunch. No individual bar director has been publicly named for this location; the program appears to be developed at the brand level and executed consistently across the chain.

True Food Kitchen stands out in Dallas's zero-proof landscape less for novelty and more for consistency and approachability. This is a sit-down restaurant that does weekend brunch (Saturday and Sunday starting at 10am), accepts reservations via OpenTable, and skews family-friendly — reviewers note it works well for groups with mixed dietary needs or mixed drinking preferences. The interior runs lively and open-concept; patio seating is available and noticeably quieter on weekdays. Dress is casual. For anyone navigating a dry stretch who still wants a composed cocktail experience at a proper table, this is one of the most reliable options in North Dallas.
venues.pressQuote: "Plenty of interesting non-alcoholic drinks grace the menu alongside alcohol-infused options. Try the Hangover Rx: a refreshing mixture of pineapple, orange, honey and coconut water."

venues.name: True Laurel
venues.description: True Laurel is a cocktail bar and restaurant at 753 Alabama Street in the Mission, opened in 2017 by the team behind the Michelin-starred Lazy Bear — chef David Barzelay and bar director Nicolas Torres. Its drinks are built from house-made syrups, shrubs and ferments made with California produce, and the same pantry drives a rotating non-alcoholic list that always carries several zero-proof options, including the Bay Bay Bubbler (California bay laurel, dealcoholized tequila, quinine) and Spice & Everything Nice. The bar has a heated parklet on Alabama Street that stays usable in Mission fog. True Laurel ranked No. 17 on North America's 50 Best Bars in 2025, rising to No. 14 in 2026, and won the Ketel One Sustainable Bar Award in 2024.
venues.hours: Mon closed; Tue-Wed 4pm-10pm; Thu 4pm-11pm; Fri 4pm-12am; Sat 11am-12am; Sun 11am-10pm
venues.longDescription:
True Laurel opened in 2017 at 753 Alabama Street in the Mission as the bar project of the team behind Lazy Bear, the Michelin-starred tasting-menu restaurant — chef David Barzelay and bar director Nicolas Torres. It functions as a full bar and restaurant rather than an annex, with a food menu of its own and a heated parklet on Alabama Street that keeps it usable through Mission fog. The bar ranked No. 17 on North America's 50 Best Bars in 2025 and rose to No. 14 in 2026, and it won the Ketel One Sustainable Bar Award in 2024 — an award that is directly relevant to how the drinks are made, since the sustainability case and the flavour case are the same one here.

True Laurel builds from house-made syrups, shrubs and ferments made with California produce, using trim and by-product from the kitchen rather than buying in flavour, and that pantry is what the non-alcoholic list draws on. Because the ingredients are made in-house rather than purchased as dealcoholized bottles, the zero-proof drinks are not thinner versions of the cocktails — they are made from the same components. The list rotates seasonally but always carries several alcohol-free options, among them the Bay Bay Bubbler, built on California bay laurel with dealcoholized tequila and quinine, and Spice & Everything Nice. The Infatuation, in its guide to drinking in San Francisco when you are not drinking, recommended the bar specifically for this: "When you require a non-alcoholic beverage and more fresh air than your open apartment window can supply, find your way to True Laurel in the Mission. The heated parklet is the perfect perch to zone out and let your eyes mindlessly track the cyclists zooming up and down Alabama — all while having a drink from their seasonal menu made with a booze-free spirit, chamomile, pink peppercorn, and pear vinegar." The bar is closed Mondays and opens at 11am at weekends, so it works for a daytime drink as well as a late one.
venues.pressQuote: When you require a non-alcoholic beverage and more fresh air than your open apartment window can supply, find your way to True Laurel in the Mission. The heated parklet is the perfect perch to zone out and let your eyes mindlessly track the cyclists zooming up and down Alabama—all while having a drink from their seasonal menu made with a booze-free spirit, chamomile, pink peppercorn, and pear vinegar.

venues.name: Trung Nguyen Legend Coffee World
venues.description: Trung Nguyen Legend Coffee World is the first U.S. location of one of Vietnam's best-known coffee brands, a 4,700-square-foot, roughly 130-seat cafe that opened on Houston's Bellaire Boulevard in March 2026. There is no bar and no alcohol anywhere on the premises -- the entire drink program runs on traditional Vietnamese coffee, tea, and milk-tea specialties. Its three signature brewing styles, the Zen, Roman, and Ottoman, plus a viral whipped-egg coffee, anchor a menu built for lingering rather than drinking. Co-owners Harry Nguyen and David Ho designed it as a slower, more social alternative to a quick-service coffee counter for Houston's Vietnamese community.
signatureDrinks: Vietnamese Egg Coffee (dark roast coffee topped with whipped egg cream)
Zen Coffee (coffee brewed and served warm in a mini kettle)
Roman Iced Milk Coffee (espresso served over ice with condensed milk)
Ottoman Iced Milk Coffee (Turkish-style coffee finished with copper service)
venues.longDescription:
Trung Nguyen Legend Coffee World opened at 11754 Bellaire Blvd in Houston's Alief/west Asiatown corridor on March 21, 2026, following a March 10 soft launch and a lion-dance grand-opening celebration. It's the first U.S. location of Trung Nguyen Legend, one of Vietnam's largest coffee brands, and co-owners Harry Nguyen and David Ho believe their 4,700-square-foot, roughly 130-seat cafe is the brand's largest in the country. The pair signed the lease back in 2022, and construction delays pushed the opening back several years before the space finally welcomed guests, according to the Houston Chronicle. Nguyen, who has also run Vua Bun Bo in the same shopping center, said he and Ho wanted to build the kind of slow, social coffee spot for family and business gatherings that Houston lacked.

The cafe serves no alcohol at all -- every drink on the menu is coffee, tea, or a milk-based specialty. The core of the program is Trung Nguyen's three signature brewing presentations: the Zen (coffee brewed and served warm in a mini kettle), the Roman (espresso served over ice with condensed milk), and the Ottoman (Turkish-style coffee finished with copper service), priced roughly $5 to $10 depending on the blend. Alongside those sit a viral Vietnamese egg coffee (dark roast coffee topped with whipped egg cream), coffee with sea salt cream, pandan lotus seed tea, Legend milk tea, oatmilk matcha, and a tiramisu latte, plus fruit teas and smoothies.

Co-owner David Ho backpacked across Vietnam to develop recipes before returning to help run the kitchen, and the cafe has begun adding food to its coffee-only opening menu -- beef and chicken pho and a Vietnamese sandwich (banh mi) are now listed on its website, with bo ne also planned. Sitting on the Bellaire Boulevard corridor of Alief, in the heart of Houston's west-side Asiatown, the cafe has quickly become a gathering spot for the local Vietnamese community as well as a broader crowd drawn to its viral, Instagram-ready coffee presentations.
venues.pressQuote: When discussing business or hanging out with our family, finding a place like this was difficult. We felt like Houston needed one.

venues.name: Trust
venues.description: Trust is the Hillcrest restaurant that started chef Brad Wise's group, cooking over an open flame on Park Boulevard, and its drinks card prints a Spirit Free section of five. Two are finished products — St. Agrestis' Phony Negroni at fifteen dollars and Athletic Brewing's Upside Dawn at eight — and three are made in house at eight dollars each: a grapefruit and strawberry lemonade, a honeydew and lemongrass limeade, and a vanilla whip cold brew. Pricing the three house drinks at eight dollars, against fourteen to eighteen for a zero-proof cocktail elsewhere in the city, is a deliberate choice about who is welcome at the table. Dinner runs Wednesday to Monday from five, with brunch on Saturday and Sunday from nine until two, which is when the cold brew makes the most sense. San Diego Magazine has given the restaurant awards for best brunch, best service and best new restaurant.
venues.hours: Mon 5pm-9pm; Tue closed; Wed-Thu 5pm-9pm; Fri 5pm-10pm; Sat 9am-2pm & 5pm-10pm; Sun 9am-2pm & 5pm-9pm
signatureDrinks: St. Agrestis Phony Negroni ($15) — the bottled non-alcoholic negroni
Grapefruit Strawberry Lemonade ($8) — made in house
Honeydew Lemongrass Limeade ($8) — made in house
Vanilla Whip Cold Brew ($8) — made in house
Athletic Brewing Upside Dawn ($8) — non-alcoholic golden ale
venues.longDescription:
Trust opened on Park Boulevard in Hillcrest and is the restaurant that started chef Brad Wise's group, which now includes Fort Oak, Cardellino and Rare Society. Its own description is plain about what it is: a neighbourhood restaurant, bold flavours cooked simply over an open flame, built on relationships with local farmers and purveyors. San Diego Magazine has given it awards for best brunch, best service and best new restaurant.

The Spirit Free section on its drinks card is five deep and splits neatly in two. The bought-in half is strong: St. Agrestis' Phony Negroni at fifteen dollars, the bottled non-alcoholic negroni that is genuinely bitter rather than sweet, and Athletic Brewing's Upside Dawn golden ale at eight. The house half is three drinks at eight dollars each, and they are the reason this list is worth describing rather than just counting — a grapefruit and strawberry lemonade, a honeydew and lemongrass limeade, and a vanilla whip cold brew. None pretends to be a cocktail. They are made in the kitchen from fruit and herbs, priced like soft drinks rather than mocktails, and they are the honest answer for a guest who wants something good without paying cocktail prices for a drink with no spirit in it.

That pricing is worth dwelling on. In a city where zero-proof cocktails now routinely land between fourteen and eighteen dollars, a restaurant that puts three made-to-order non-alcoholic drinks on the list at eight is making a choice about who it wants at the table.

The practical details: the restaurant is closed on Tuesday, serves dinner from five until nine or ten, and runs brunch on Saturday and Sunday from nine until two — which is when the cold brew makes most sense. The room is loud and busy at weekends and reservations are the safer route. Like the rest of the group, this is a licensed restaurant rather than an alcohol-free space.

Trust is also the easiest of the group's rooms to visit without an occasion. It sits on a busy stretch of Park Boulevard with parking on the street, the bar takes walk-ins, and the menu is built for sharing rather than for a formal three courses. The open flame does most of the cooking — the restaurant's own line is that it believes in bold flavours cooked simply over fire, and in buying from local farmers and makers. For a non-drinker, the combination of a genuinely bitter bottled negroni at fifteen dollars and three made-to-order fruit drinks at eight covers both ends of the evening without a compromise in either direction.
venues.pressQuote: We’re a neighborhood restaurant, at our heart. A place for our community to gather, to celebrate, to raise yet another glass in a toast to good tidings.

venues.name: Tucana Tiki Bar
venues.description: Tucana Tiki Bar is Birmingham's tiki room, and it rewrites its mocktails as a seasonal exercise rather than leaving them fixed — Bham Now covered a brand-new January menu built around a refreshing lineup of them, with a Wanna Pear Up? among the drinks. Tiki is a format that suits alcohol-free drinking better than most: the category is built on fresh juice, house syrups, spice and elaborate presentation, so removing the rum leaves more behind than removing gin from a martini does. Open daily from 4pm, to midnight most nights and 1am on Friday and Saturday.
venues.longDescription:
Tiki is quietly one of the best formats for drinking without alcohol, and Tucana is Birmingham's tiki bar. The reason the format works is structural: a tiki drink is mostly fresh juice, house-made syrups such as orgeat and falernum, spice, acid and a great deal of presentation. Rum is one component among many rather than the backbone. Take it out of a martini and there is nothing left; take it out of a mai tai and you still have a complicated, aromatic, well-garnished drink.

Tucana works that advantage deliberately. Rather than keeping a static pair of mocktails, it rewrites them with the seasons — Bham Now covered a brand-new January menu built around a lineup of them, with a drink called Wanna Pear Up? among the new arrivals. Seasonal rotation is the signal this directory weighs most heavily, because it means someone is doing the work again every few months rather than printing two drinks once and forgetting them.

The room itself is the full tiki treatment, which is worth mentioning for a specific reason: elaborate glassware and garnish are not decoration in this context, they are the thing that makes an alcohol-free drink socially equivalent to everyone else's. Nobody at the table can tell, and nobody has to explain.

This listing records one drink name from the January menu; the current list will have moved on, which is the point of a seasonal programme, so it is recorded as evidence rather than as an order.

Open every day from 4pm, to midnight Sunday through Thursday and 1am on Friday and Saturday. It sits west of downtown near the Parkside district, a little apart from the 2nd Avenue North cluster, so treat it as its own stop.
venues.pressQuote: Tucana Tiki Bar has introduced a brand-new January menu featuring a delicious lineup of refreshing mocktails

venues.name: Tula's Kitchen
venues.description: Tula's Kitchen is a restaurant on Wyoming Boulevard in north Albuquerque, a sister brand to the New Mexico pizza institution Dion's, and its drinks list is built entirely without alcohol: teas, lemonades, Italian sodas, coffee mocktails and house soft drinks. That is unusual for a full-service restaurant — not a bar with a zero-proof section but a dining room where the whole beverage programme is alcohol-free, so nobody at the table is drinking anything anyone else cannot. Open 11am to 9pm through the week and to 10pm on Friday and Saturday, seven days.
