venues.longDescription:
Tula's Kitchen is on Wyoming Boulevard in the north-east of Albuquerque, and it is a sister brand to Dion's — the New Mexico pizza chain that is close to a state institution. It is a family restaurant rather than a bar, and that is exactly why it is here.

New Mexico Magazine's survey of the city's non-alcoholic drinking includes it for a beverage list made up of tea, lemonade, Italian sodas, soft drinks and coffee mocktails, with no alcohol on it. The distinction from everywhere else in this guide is worth drawing out. Most venues here are licensed rooms with a good alcohol-free section, which means a non-drinker is choosing from a subset while everyone else chooses from the whole. At Tula's there is no subset — the whole table is ordering from the same list, and the question of who is drinking what never arises.

For certain readers that is the single most valuable property a restaurant can have. Someone recently sober, or in a family with children, or simply tired of the small negotiation that happens at every table, gets an evening where the issue is structurally absent rather than politely managed.

The coffee mocktails are the most interesting part of the list — coffee brings bitterness and body, the two things alcohol-free drinks most often lack — though the individual builds are not published, so none are recorded here and the entry is graded three.

Open 11am to 9pm Sunday through Thursday and 11am to 10pm on Friday and Saturday, seven days a week with no closed day. It is well north of the Old Town and Nob Hill clusters, so it serves its own neighbourhood rather than a night out downtown — which, for the families it is built for, is the point.

venues.name: Tulum Botanical
venues.description: Tulum Botanical is a fully alcohol-free kava and kratom lounge at 1620 East 7th Street in Central East Austin, a few minutes from downtown. Also listed as Bula Tulum Kava & Kratom, it serves kava, kratom and botanical elixirs in a tropical-styled room, and states that everything it pours is 100% organic and rigorously tested for purity and safety, sourced from farms in the Pacific Islands and Southeast Asia. Rather than a conventional cocktail list, the bar is built around effect: staff invite guests to say how they want to feel and are guided to a blend from there. It is open daily from noon to midnight, and doubles as a community space with poetry night on Sundays and an open-mic music night on Wednesdays. Kratom in particular is a psychoactive substance with a contested risk profile, so this is an alcohol-free room rather than a substance-free one.
venues.longDescription:
Tulum Botanical occupies 1620 East 7th Street in Central East Austin, a tropical-styled kava and kratom lounge that also trades as Bula Tulum. It is fully alcohol-free and open every day from noon to midnight, which puts it directly against the East 6th and East 7th bar strip at exactly the hours that strip is busiest — the practical value of a room like this is that it is open when the alternative is a bar.

The sourcing claim is the strongest thing the venue says about itself: 100% organic, rigorously tested for purity and safety, from farms in the Pacific Islands and Southeast Asia. In this category that is not marketing boilerplate. Kava quality varies enormously with cultivar and processing, and kratom is an unregulated product in most of the United States, sold with wide variation in alkaloid content between batches and vendors. A venue that tests and can say where its material comes from is making a meaningful claim.

The ordering model is unusual and worth knowing before you arrive. There is no conventional cocktail list to read; the bar asks guests to describe how they want to feel and recommends a blend from there. Drinks are pitched as calming, energizing or mood-enhancing. That is a candid description of what is on offer, and it makes the next paragraph more rather than less necessary.

This is an alcohol-free room, not a substance-free one, and the distinction is sharper here than at most venues on this site. Kava is a mild sedative that should not be mixed with alcohol or sedating medication. Kratom is a different substance altogether, acting on opioid receptors, and it carries a genuinely contested risk profile that includes physical dependence and withdrawal with regular use. For someone in recovery — particularly from opioids — that is not a footnote, and a bar organised around choosing a substance by desired effect is worth approaching with that clearly in mind. Ask what is in a drink and say plainly what you are avoiding.

Beyond the drinks it functions as a community space, with poetry on Sunday nights and an open mic for musicians on Wednesdays.

venues.name: Turner's Cut
venues.neighborhood: Autry Park (Allen Parkway & Shepherd Dr, Montrose/River Oaks edge on Buffalo Bayou)
venues.description: Turner's Cut is Ben Berg's opulent, Gilded Age-inspired steakhouse in Houston's Autry Park, and its bar list carries a genuine four-drink zero-proof program built on Seedlip and Cut Above non-alcoholic spirits rather than an afterthought syrup-and-soda pour. The same $12 mocktails — Strawberry Rose Refresher, Spiced Pear, Margfreerita, and Kosnopolitan — are shared with sister restaurant Prime 131 under the Berg Hospitality Group's beverage program, and were independently confirmed by multiple Houston Dry January roundups.
venues.address: 811 Buffalo Park Dr, Suite 160, Houston, TX 77019
venues.hours: Mon closed; Tue-Thu 5pm-10pm; Fri-Sat 5pm-11pm; Sun closed
signatureDrinks: Strawberry Rose Refresher (Seedlip Grove 42, Monin strawberry rose syrup, simple syrup, Fever-Tree club soda)
Spiced Pear (Seedlip Spiced 94, Monin pear syrup, organic honey, Fever-Tree ginger beer)
Margfreerita (Cut Above Total Zero Proof agave blanco, Monin mango syrup, agave, Fever-Tree club soda)
Kosnopolitan (Seedlip Grove 42, cranberry juice, fresh lime juice)
venues.longDescription:
Turner's Cut opened in June 2024 in Houston's Autry Park development, the newest steakhouse from Ben Berg's Berg Hospitality Group, which also runs Turner's, Prime 131 and B&B Butchers. Executive Chef Chelsea Cummings leads the kitchen with regional culinary director Pablo Peñalosa, serving rare cuts of American and Japanese wagyu and Kobe beef in a Gilded Age dining room of leather walls, soaring ceilings, antique chandeliers and white-glove service.

Despite a full bar and an extensive wine list, the restaurant runs a genuine named zero-proof programme at $12 a drink, and the compositions are more considered than a steakhouse needs them to be. The Strawberry Rose Refresher uses Seedlip Grove 42 — the citrus expression, built on blood orange, ginger and lemongrass — with strawberry rose syrup, simple syrup and Fever-Tree club soda. Spiced Pear switches to Seedlip Spice 94, the allspice-and-cardamom bottling with a long bark-like bitterness, against pear syrup, organic honey and Fever-Tree ginger beer; that is the one to order with beef, since the warm spice and ginger heat cut through fat the way a red wine's tannin would. Margfreerita is built on Cut Above's zero-proof agave blanco with mango syrup, agave and club soda, and the Kosnopolitan returns to Grove 42 with cranberry and fresh lime.

The use of two distinct Seedlip expressions rather than one bottle across the whole list is the tell. Each expression has a different botanical profile, and choosing between them per drink is the same decision a bartender makes between gin and whiskey — evidence the list was built rather than assembled.

CultureMap Houston, Bayou Beat News and Hot in Houston Now each independently confirmed the identical four-drink list during Dry January 2025 coverage, noting it is shared with sister restaurant Prime 131 across the group's beverage programme — which means the recipes are documented and trained rather than dependent on one bartender.

The restaurant sits in Autry Park, a fourteen-acre mixed-use development on the western edge of Buffalo Bayou Park at Allen Parkway and Shepherd Drive, bridging Montrose and River Oaks just west of downtown. Dinner only, Tuesday to Saturday.
venues.pressQuote: Both Prime 131 and Turner's Cut have four signature zero-proof cocktails at the ready for Dry January observers.

venues.name: Twist Kava Cafe
venues.description: Twist opened on Bruce B Downs Boulevard in 2014 to fill what its founders saw as a gap for a proper kava bar and coffee shop in the same room, and that hybrid is still the pitch — locally roasted coffee on one side, handcrafted kava on the other, plus herbal teas. It runs 8am to 11pm through the week and to midnight on Friday and Saturday, close enough to the University of South Florida to draw a study crowd in the afternoons and a social one after dark. No alcohol is served. IMPORTANT for readers in recovery: kratom sits on this menu alongside the kava. It acts on opioid receptors and carries genuine dependence and withdrawal risk, which kava does not, so ask before ordering.
venues.address: 14937 Bruce B Downs Blvd, Tampa, FL 33613
venues.longDescription:
Twist opened on Bruce B Downs Boulevard in 2014 to fill what its founders identified as a specific gap — Tampa had coffee shops and it had kava bars, and it did not have a room that did both properly. Twelve years later that hybrid is still the pitch: locally roasted coffee on one side, handcrafted kava on the other, herbal teas across both. Its own line is that it is a coffee shop with a Twist, which is exactly as much of a pun as it sounds and reasonably accurate.

It runs 8am to 11pm through the week and to midnight on Friday and Saturday, in New Tampa, close enough to the University of South Florida to draw a study crowd through the afternoon and a social one after dark. No alcohol is served. The dual programme is the reason it works across that whole span: an all-day coffee operation gives people a reason to be there at 10am, and the kava gives them a reason to still be there at 10pm.

Kava is the ground root of Piper methysticum, a shrub native to the South Pacific islands, prepared as a cold water infusion and drunk socially across Fiji, Vanuatu, Tonga and Samoa for roughly three thousand years. It contains no alcohol. It tastes earthy and bitter, numbs the lips and tongue on the first mouthful, and is mildly sedative rather than intoxicating in the way alcohol is. Kava exhibits reverse tolerance, meaning regular drinkers typically need less rather than more to feel it, so a first visit is best paced across an hour or two rather than rushed.

The pairing of kava with serious coffee is more thoughtful than it first appears. The two occupy opposite ends of the day and opposite ends of the effect, and a room that does both well can hold someone from a morning working session through to an evening with friends without ever offering them a drink. For a lot of people in early recovery, having one place that covers the whole day is worth more than having three places that each cover a slice of it.

One disclosure belongs plainly on the page. Kratom sits on this menu alongside the kava, as it does across most of the Tampa Bay scene. Kratom is the leaf of a Southeast Asian tree, Mitragyna speciosa, whose principal alkaloids act on the opioid receptors; regular use produces tolerance and a real withdrawal syndrome, several US states prohibit it outright, and concentrated 7-hydroxymitragynine products derived from it face active federal scheduling. Kava has no comparable dependence profile. Ask before ordering if you are avoiding it — the staff here are consistently described as knowledgeable and willing to explain.
venues.pressQuote: We serve coffee, but we're a coffee shop with a Twist

venues.name: Twisted Roots Kava Brewery
venues.description: Twisted Roots is the busiest alcohol-free room on Hollywood Boulevard by a wide margin, and it trades like a bar: 8am to 2am at the start of the week, 8am to 3am Thursday through Saturday, with a happy hour from 4pm to 8pm. The interior is done as a jungle, the shelves are stocked with board games, the WiFi is free, and both dogs and children are welcome. The drinks programme is organised by origin — awa from the South Pacific islands, Japanese matcha, South American coffee. IMPORTANT for readers in recovery: the fourth pillar is Maeng Da Kra-tea, which is kratom, sold here under a tea name as it is across most of Florida. Kratom acts on opioid receptors and carries dependence risk that kava does not; the distinction is not cosmetic, so ask before you order.
venues.longDescription:
Twisted Roots is the busiest alcohol-free room on Hollywood Boulevard by a wide margin, and it trades on a bar's schedule rather than a cafe's: 8am to 2am from Sunday through Wednesday, and 8am to 3am from Thursday through Saturday, with a happy hour running 4pm to 8pm. The interior is done out as a jungle, the shelves carry board games, the WiFi is free, and both dogs and children are welcome — a combination that makes it work as a family afternoon and a late night out from the same fit-out.

The drinks programme is organised by origin, which is unusual in this category and tells you something about how the room thinks. Awa comes from the South Pacific islands — awa is the Hawaiian name for kava, and using it signals a bar that knows the drink's provenance. Matcha comes from Japan. Coffee comes from South America. Kava itself is the ground root of Piper methysticum, prepared as a cold water infusion and drunk socially across Fiji, Vanuatu, Tonga and Samoa for roughly three thousand years. It contains no alcohol. It tastes earthy and bitter, numbs the lips and tongue on the first mouthful, and is mildly sedative rather than intoxicating in the sense alcohol is. Because it exhibits reverse tolerance, regular drinkers typically need less rather than more, so a first visit is best paced across an hour or two.

Hollywood Boulevard runs from downtown to the beach through one of the denser drinking strips in Broward County, and Twisted Roots sits on it alongside Elixir's original Harrison Street room and Club Kava a few blocks south. Between them, this stretch of Hollywood has quietly become the strongest alcohol-free cluster in the county — better served than Fort Lauderdale proper.

The fourth pillar of the menu requires its own paragraph, because the naming actively obscures what it is. Maeng Da Kra-tea is kratom. "Kra-tea" is a contraction of kratom, and Maeng Da is one of its best-known strain names; the tea framing is standard across Florida and genuinely easy to misread as a herbal infusion. Kratom is the leaf of a Southeast Asian tree, Mitragyna speciosa, and its principal alkaloids act on the opioid receptors. Regular use produces tolerance and a real withdrawal syndrome, several US states ban it outright, and concentrated 7-hydroxymitragynine products derived from it are under active federal scheduling. Kava carries no comparable dependence profile, and a great many people drink kava specifically because it does not.

None of that makes Twisted Roots a bad room — it is a genuinely good one, and it is entirely alcohol-free. It makes it a room where you should read the menu headers and ask what is in the cup before you order.

venues.name: The Twisted Tail
venues.description: The Twisted Tail is a Southern-leaning whiskey bar and live-music room on Headhouse Square, and its zero-proof drinks are unusual in reaching for the serious end of the non-alcoholic aperitif market rather than for syrups. The Zero Proof Ginger Spritz at $13 is built on Ghia, the bitter Mediterranean aperitivo whose gentian and elderflower give it genuine astringency. The Zero Proof Chili Margarita, also $13, uses Aplós — an alcohol-free spirit made with adaptogens — against Persian lime, habanero and sea salt. Both are priced level with the bar's alcoholic cocktails, which is a deliberate statement about the labour involved. The room runs to midnight on Friday and opens at ten on Sunday.
signatureDrinks: Zero Proof Ginger Spritz ($13) — Ghia Bitter Aperitivo, ginger
Zero Proof Chili Margarita ($13) — Aplós Chili Margarita with adaptogens, Persian lime, habanero, sea salt
venues.longDescription:
The Twisted Tail occupies a corner of Headhouse Square in Society Hill, working a Southern menu against a deep bourbon list, with live music downstairs most nights. It is, in other words, a whiskey bar — which makes the composition of its two zero-proof drinks more interesting than it would be anywhere else.

The Zero Proof Ginger Spritz is built on Ghia, and that choice tells you the bar took the category seriously. Ghia is a Mediterranean-style bitter aperitivo made with gentian root, elderflower, ginger, yuzu and riesling grape juice concentrate; gentian is the same intensely bitter root that gives Aperol and most amari their backbone. A spritz built on it has real astringency rather than sweetness, which is precisely the quality that makes an aperitif work before food and precisely what juice-based alternatives cannot produce.

The Zero Proof Chili Margarita uses Aplós, a newer alcohol-free spirit built with adaptogens — botanicals such as ashwagandha marketed for their calming effect — against Persian lime, habanero and sea salt. It is worth being clear about that ingredient for a readership that includes people in recovery: adaptogens are herbal rather than intoxicating, and this contains no alcohol, but anyone who prefers their drinks entirely free of functional additives should order the spritz instead.

Both drinks are thirteen dollars, level with the bar's alcoholic cocktails. That parity is a choice and generally a good sign — the bottled alcohol-free aperitifs these use are expensive, and a bar that absorbs the cost rather than discounting the drink is treating it as a cocktail rather than as a consolation.

The hours suit a proper night out: four in the afternoon to midnight on Friday, an eleven o'clock Saturday opening that runs to midnight, and a ten o'clock start on Sunday for brunch. With live music downstairs, the evening has a structure that does not depend on rounds.

venues.name: Twisted Totem Kava Bar
venues.description: Twisted Totem trades noon to 2am, seven days a week, on North 7th Street, under a slogan that leaves nothing ambiguous: zero alcohol, all vibes. It describes itself as a watering hole with no bar-tab hangover, and the room is fitted for staying — custom wall art, comfortable seating, big TVs and games consoles. The kava is graded House and Premium by size, with Island Warrior as the signature build. IMPORTANT for readers in recovery: kratom is a headline category here, not a footnote — Crushed Leaf Tea, Jamaica, Unkie Palmer and the house Josh Juice are all kratom drinks. Kratom acts on opioid receptors and carries dependence and withdrawal risk that kava does not, so order by name rather than by vibe.
venues.longDescription:
Twisted Totem trades from noon to 2am, seven days a week, in a unit on North 7th Street in north Phoenix, under a line that removes any ambiguity about what it is: zero alcohol, all vibes. Its own description is better than anything written about it — a watering hole with no bar-tab hangover. That is precisely the gap the kava format fills, and this room fills it more literally than most.

The fit-out is built for occupying rather than passing through: custom wall art, comfortable seating, big TVs and a couple of games consoles. The venue calls itself a friend-and-family spot and programmes events through the calendar. What that produces is a room where people arrive without a plan and stay for a few hours, which is the specific social function alcohol usually performs and the hardest one to replace.

The kava is graded and properly presented. House Kava and Premium Kava are offered across several sizes, and the signature build is the Island Warrior. Kava is the ground root of Piper methysticum, a shrub native to the South Pacific, prepared as a cold water infusion and drunk socially across Fiji, Vanuatu, Tonga and Samoa for roughly three thousand years. It contains no alcohol. It tastes earthy and bitter, numbs the lips and tongue on the first mouthful, and is mildly sedative rather than intoxicating in alcohol's sense. Kava exhibits reverse tolerance, meaning regular drinkers typically need less rather than more to feel it, so a first visit rewards a slow pace across an hour or two.

Phoenix now carries a real spread of these rooms — Kawana on Thomas Road, Kavasutra on Thunderbird, Lighthouse over in Tempe and the two Mad Hatter sites in Ahwatukee and Mesa — and Twisted Totem's contribution is the latest close in the group and the most straightforwardly bar-like atmosphere.

The caution here is unusually easy to act on, because the menu names the drinks rather than hiding them behind categories. Crushed Leaf Tea, Jamaica, Unkie Palmer and the house Josh Juice are kratom drinks, not kava. Kratom is the leaf of Mitragyna speciosa, a Southeast Asian tree, and its principal alkaloids act on the opioid receptors; regular use produces tolerance and a genuine withdrawal syndrome, several US states ban it outright, and its concentrated 7-hydroxymitragynine derivatives are the subject of active federal scheduling. Kava carries no comparable dependence profile, and a great many people come to kava bars precisely because of that difference. Here, the practical advice is simple: order the House Kava, the Premium Kava or the Island Warrior and you are drinking kava; anything from the tea side of the board is a different proposition, and the staff will confirm which is which.
venues.pressQuote: Kava is a sacred beverage, and one business placing authenticity at the forefront is Twisted Totem Kava Bar

venues.name: Two Frays Brewery
venues.description: Two Frays Brewery is a Garfield craft brewery founded by husband-and-wife team Mike and Jen Onofray that brews its own non-alcoholic beer on-site — its first NA brew (2022) is billed as Pittsburgh's original non-alcoholic beer. At least a couple of its own 'Near Beer' pours are always on the menu, recently the Finicky Beast NA West Coast IPA and Fruity Pebbles NA fruited blonde on tap and in 4-packs, and on the first Monday of each month the taproom goes fully non-alcoholic for 'Mod Mondays' with the Pittsburgh Teetotal Initiative. It is a full brewery (not alcohol-free), so its regular craft lineup runs alongside the NA options.
venues.hours: Mon closed; Tue-Thu 4pm-9pm; Fri 4pm-10pm; Sat 1pm-10pm; Sun 1pm-8pm
venues.longDescription:
Two Frays is a small Garfield brewery on Penn Avenue run by Mike and Jen Onofray, a husband-and-wife team, in a 120-year-old former Star Soap building — the old hand-painted Star Soap billboard is still on the side of it, alongside a ceramic mosaic. Their French bulldogs, Zeus and Iris, appear on the beer can labels, and the patio is dog-friendly. Jen Onofray has described the intent as staying true to their vision and making sure the community knows this is their space, and the brewery has worked at being a genuine neighbourhood hub rather than a destination taproom.

What makes it matter well beyond Garfield is that it brews its own non-alcoholic beer, on site, and appears to be the only craft brewery in Pennsylvania doing so — a claim made not by the brewery but by The Open Road, the alcohol-free bottle shop a few blocks away that stocks half the state's non-alcoholic output and would know. The origin story is refreshingly unstrategic. In the brewery's own telling, when some of their customers asked whether they would ever brew a non-alcoholic beer, they did not ask why or scoff and say no — they said they thought they could, why not, and gave it a shot. That first brew landed in 2022. Mike Onofray framed the audience simply: these are for the designated driver, or someone who has to work tomorrow. The current alcohol-free line runs a West Coast IPA called Finicky Beast and a fruited blonde called Fruity Pebbles, both sold in cans through local retailers as well as poured in the taproom. Two honest caveats. The names rotate — an earlier pair of alcohol-free beers went under the name You Do You, and the brewery has also made a Half Way There hoppy amber at 0.9% ABV, which is low-alcohol rather than non-alcoholic and would not qualify under Pennsylvania's 0.5% line. And the taproom menu is not readable online, so confirm what is actually on tap before travelling for a specific beer.
venues.pressQuote: In this industry that's declining, nationally and locally, NA is the only growing portion.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Mike Onofray, co-founder of Two Frays Brewery

venues.name: Tzuco
venues.description: Tzuco is chef Carlos Gaytan's Mexican restaurant on State Street in River North, opened by the James Beard Award winner who was the first Latin American chef to earn a Michelin star, and its cocktail list carries a Spirit Free (Non-Alcohol) section on both the dinner and bar menus. Three drinks sit under it: Daydream, a long build of cucumber water, lime juice, chia seeds and aloe vera juice at $12; On Thyme, made with a non-alcoholic agave spirit, thyme, strawberry, lemon and soda at $15; and an NA Cosmopolitan combining a non-alcoholic agave spirit and an orange aperitif with lime juice, prickly pear syrup and cranberry juice at $15. Seedlip Notas de Agave is also poured neat by the ounce alongside the tequila and mezcal list.

venues.longDescription:
Carlos Gaytan opened Tzuco at 720 N State Street in River North, naming it for Huitzuco, the town in Guerrero where he grew up. Gaytan is a James Beard Award winner and, as the restaurant states, the first Latin American chef to achieve a Michelin star; the cooking sets Mexican technique against French training, and the restaurant describes its own approach as an austere experience in which richness comes from the purity of ingredients and the story of their origin. The dining room runs dinner six nights a week with weekend brunch service, and the bar keeps its own menu.

The non-alcoholic offering is set out under a Spirit Free (Non-Alcohol) heading that appears on both the dinner list and the bar list, sitting directly beneath the tequila and mezcal cocktails rather than in a separate corner. Daydream is the lightest of the three, a $12 build of cucumber water, lime juice, chia seeds and aloe vera juice with real texture to it. On Thyme, at $15, uses a non-alcoholic agave spirit with thyme, strawberry, lemon and soda - the closest thing on the list to a long agave highball. The NA Cosmopolitan, also $15, combines a non-alcoholic agave spirit and an orange aperitif with lime juice, prickly pear syrup and cranberry juice. Beyond the mixed drinks, Seedlip's Notas de Agave is available neat by the ounce at $9 for 1.5oz and $12 for 2oz, listed in the same block as the whiskies and amari, which means a non-drinker can order a pour and sit with it in the same way as everyone else at the table. Aguas frescas - horchata, jamaica and tamarindo - are $6, and there is a full soft list beneath that. The restaurant serves brunch on Saturday and Sunday from 10am to 2pm and dinner every night except Sunday's earlier close, and the Spirit Free block appears on more than one of its menus rather than on a single card, which is the practical difference between a program and a gesture. Micheladas and a full aguas frescas list sit immediately alongside it for anyone who wants something simpler.
venues.pressQuote: expect beautifully plated Mexican dishes with a touch of French flair, plus a handful of zero-proof drinks that speak the same language

venues.name: Uchi Dallas
venues.description: Uchi Dallas is the Uptown / Oak Lawn outpost of the contemporary Japanese sushi brand founded by James Beard Award-winning chef Tyson Cole, which opened here in June 2015 as the third Uchi location. Set on Maple Avenue (with sister izakaya-cocktail bar Uchiba upstairs), it pairs hot and cold tastings, sashimi, and seasonal omakase with a genuinely built-out zero-proof program rather than a token mocktail. The current menu carries a standalone "Zero Proof Cocktails" section of six named drinks built on premium NA spirits — including the Zero Crush (Crodino, yuzu, Oddbird sparkling, soda), Mitsu Mitsu (Ritual ZP gin, rosemary, yuzu honey), Akabanaa (Ritual ZP agave, hibiscus-lime), and Jonetsu (Ghia, passion fruit, habanero) — alongside dedicated zero-proof beer (Athletic Brewing Free Wave, Best Day Kölsch) and Oddbird non-alcoholic wines.

venues.longDescription:
Uchi Dallas is the Uptown outpost of the contemporary Japanese restaurant group founded by James Beard Award-winning chef Tyson Cole, which opened at 2817 Maple Avenue on 1 June 2015 as the third Uchi location. The kitchen runs hot and cold tastings, sashimi and seasonal omakase, with the group's izakaya-style sister bar Uchiba upstairs, and the room offers valet during dinner service. Service runs Sunday to Thursday 4pm to 10pm and Friday and Saturday until 11pm, with happy hour every day from 4pm to 6pm.

What sets Uchi apart for non-drinkers is that the zero-proof programme is built to the same specification as the rest of the bar rather than tacked on. The menu carries a standalone "Zero Proof Cocktails" section of six named drinks, each constructed on a real non-alcoholic base. Zero Crush ($13) uses Crodino with yuzu, Oddbird zero-proof sparkling wine and soda. Mitsu Mitsu ($12) is Ritual zero-proof gin with rosemary and yuzu honey. Akabanaa ($12) pairs Ritual zero-proof agave with a hibiscus-lime agave. Jonetsu ($14) is the boldest, combining Ghia with passion fruit and habanero. Shokuzen ($12) layers Giffard aperitif with Oddbird zero-proof red wine and a citrus oleo, and Carajillo Cero ($14) builds espresso, golden syrup and vanilla over Ritual zero-proof agave and Oddbird red. The support around those drinks is equally serious: zero-proof beer runs Athletic Brewing Free Wave and Best Day non-alcoholic Kölsch at $8 with Sapporo Premium at $7, and Oddbird non-alcoholic wines — a blanc de blancs, a white blend and a Grenache-Syrah-Mourvèdre — are poured at $14 a glass or $55 a bottle. Most notably, the zero-proof drinks are included in happy hour rather than excluded from it, with the Sapporo at $3 and the Mitsu Mitsu at $6 between 4pm and 6pm daily. Restaurants that discount their alcoholic drinks and leave the non-alcoholic ones at full price are common; this is the opposite, and it is the clearest signal of how the programme is regarded in-house.

venues.longDescription:
Uchi Houston is the Montrose outpost of chef Tyson Cole's Japanese restaurant group, Hai Hospitality. Cole, who won the James Beard Award for Best Chef: Southwest in 2011, opened the original Uchi in Austin in 2003; the Houston location followed in 2012 inside a converted building on Westheimer Road, becoming an acclaimed omakase and contemporary sushi destination in its own right.

On June 17, 2025, Uchi Houston relaunched its beverage program with a full bar for the first time, developed under Hai Hospitality beverage director Jason Kosmas (a co-founder of Employees Only in New York) and staffed by bartenders Liah Crumbley and Carley Rice. Alongside new spirits-driven cocktails, the relaunch introduced a dedicated zero-proof section and expanded low- and no-ABV options -- as Kosmas put it, guests "will also enjoy the same robust selection of wine, sake and beer, as well as low- and no-ABV cocktails."

The zero-proof list runs seven cocktails deep: the Mitsu Mitsu (Ritual ZP gin, rosemary, yuzu honey), Akabanaa (Ritual ZP spirit, hibiscus, lime, agave), Shokuzen (Ritual aperitif, zero-proof wine, citrus oleo), Zero Spritz (Crodino, yuzu, de-alcoholized sparkling wine, soda), Orenji Yuzu (orange, yuzu, sparkling), Jonetsu (passion fruit, lychee, lemon), and the Ube Coconut Boba (coconut water, ube, coconut foam, boba). The bar backs these with Athletic Brewing's Upside Dawn and Free Wave NA beers, a non-alcoholic Sapporo lager, and three Oddbird non-alcoholic wines (Blanc de Blanc, Presence, and a GSM blend).

The program has drawn local notice: CultureMap Houston featured Uchi's three Ritual-based zero-proof cocktails in its January 2026 Dry January roundup of the city's best spirit-free sips, noting the drinks "pair seamlessly with its Japanese-inspired menu."
venues.pressQuote: Uchi fans will also enjoy the same robust selection of wine, sake and beer, as well as low- and no-ABV cocktails.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Jason Kosmas, Hai Hospitality Beverage Director

venues.name: Uchi
venues.description: Uchi is the Wynwood location of the Japanese restaurant group founded by chef Tyson Cole, on NW 25th Street, serving lunch and dinner every day of the week. The bar keeps a standing non-alcoholic section rather than a single token drink, and the builds are made to sit alongside the sashimi and hot plates rather than to imitate cocktails: the Inari uses Seedlip Grove with lychee, lemon and yuzu; the Raba is a tangier build of passionfruit and ginger topped with soda; and the newest addition, the Ube Shima, works ube with coconut milk and pineapple. Non-alcoholic beer has also appeared on the list. Happy hour runs daily from 5pm to 6:30pm, and the kitchen serves until 11pm.
venues.longDescription:
Uchi opened its Miami location at 252 NW 25th Street in Wynwood; the group was founded by chef Tyson Cole and now trades in several US cities. The Miami room runs a full daily service — lunch from noon to 3pm, dinner from 5pm to 11pm — with a happy hour every day from 5pm to 6:30pm, which is a useful detail for anyone who wants the bar without the full tasting-menu commitment.

The non-alcoholic list has been a fixture here across at least two years of published coverage, and it changes. As documented in December 2025, the three named builds are the Inari, which pours Seedlip Grove over lychee, lemon and yuzu; the Raba, a tangy build of passionfruit and ginger topped with soda; and the Ube Shima, the newest of the three, combining ube with coconut milk and pineapple. A January 2024 survey by Miami New Times recorded a partly different line-up at the same bar — the Yebiso, built on a non-alcoholic tequila with passionfruit, ginger and soda at $13, and the Inari at $8 — alongside a non-alcoholic IPA on the beer list, which suggests both that the section is long-standing and that individual drinks rotate. The group's Instagram is @uchirestaurants and the Miami location posts separately as @uchi_miami. Uchi's sibling restaurant Uchiko trades on Miami Beach and runs its own, different alcohol-free list. Pricing is worth flagging because it is unusual: in the 2024 survey the alcohol-free builds ran from $8 to $13 while the restaurant's cocktails sat well above that, so ordering off the non-alcoholic list here does not carry the price penalty it does at some Miami bars. The restaurant takes bookings on (305) 995-0915. For a guest planning a Wynwood evening, Uchi sits within a few blocks of R House, Rosemary's and Double Knot, all of which run documented alcohol-free lists of their own.
venues.pressQuote: This upscale Japanese restaurant in the heart of Wynwood is whipping up some delicious mocktails for those who want to take a break from alcohol without sacrificing the taste.

venues.name: Uchibā Dallas
venues.description: Uchibā is the second-floor cocktail bar above Uchi in Uptown, and it runs the deepest zero-proof programme found in Dallas: four separate non-alcoholic sections covering cocktails, beer, wine and other drinks. The n/a cocktails include the Mitsu Mitsu with Ritual Zero Proof gin, yuzu, honey and rosemary, a Nattsu Sour built on Lyre's Amaretti with lemon and cherry, a hibiscus margarita on Ritual's tequila alternative, and Little Bird on sanbitter with pineapple and lime. The n/a beer list carries Athletic Brewing Run Wild and Best Day Kölsch, with dealcoholised Oddbird wines available by the glass or bottle. Open 5pm to 11pm daily.

venues.longDescription:
Uchibā sits on the second floor above Uchi on Maple Avenue, and where the restaurant below is a sushi destination, Uchibā is a cocktail bar with a kitchen. It also happens to run the most complete non-alcoholic programme this directory found anywhere in Dallas — not one section but four, printed as n/a cocktails, n/a beer, n/a wines and n/a beverages. That structure is the whole story: four headings means the bar has accepted that a non-drinker's choices should be as wide as anyone else's, rather than picking one drink to be the answer.

The cocktails are the reason to make the trip. Mitsu Mitsu builds Ritual Zero Proof gin against yuzu, honey and rosemary; the Nattsu Sour uses Lyre's Amaretti with lemon and cherry, giving the nutty, sour profile that non-alcoholic lists almost never attempt; and the hibiscus margarita runs Ritual's tequila alternative into hibiscus agave and lime. Little Bird, built on sanbitter with pineapple and lime, covers the bitter end. They are priced identically to the alcoholic cocktails, which is a fair signal of how the bar regards them — and a rarer signal than it should be, since pricing is where most venues quietly rank the categories.

Beyond the cocktails the depth is unusual. The beer list carries Athletic Brewing's Run Wild IPA, Best Day Brewing's Kölsch and Sapporo's non-alcoholic lager; the wine list offers dealcoholised Oddbird by the glass or bottle, including a blanc de blancs and a GSM, which means a table sharing bottles does not have to leave a non-drinker out. Service runs 5pm to 11pm every day, so it works as a late drink after dinner elsewhere as readily as a destination in itself. For anyone who wants a genuine cocktail-bar evening in Dallas without alcohol, this is the strongest single answer in the city.
venues.pressQuote: Uptown Japanese cocktail bar will offer two mocktails: Little Bird with sanbitter, pineapple, lime, for $16; and Mitsu Mitsu with Ritual zero proof gin, yuzu, honey, rosemary for $12.

venues.name: Uchiko
venues.description: Uchiko is the Miami Beach sibling of Uchi, set on Purdy Avenue in Sunset Harbour and open for dinner only, from 5pm to 11pm seven nights a week. Where Uchi in Wynwood leans on Seedlip, the Uchiko bar builds its alcohol-free drinks on Ritual: the Akabanaa pairs Ritual's tequila alternative with lime and a hibiscus agave, giving the drink a genuine bitterness rather than relying on fruit sugar, while the Raba is the cleaner and tangier of the pair. RESIDENT wrote in December 2025 that the drinks are built to complement the menu rather than compete with it, which matches how the pair are constructed. Sunset Harbour is a walkable pocket of Miami Beach away from the Ocean Drive crowds.

venues.longDescription:
Uchiko trades at 1759 Purdy Avenue in Sunset Harbour, the low-rise pocket of Miami Beach around the Purdy Avenue marina, away from the Ocean Drive strip. It is the sibling concept to Uchi — the same Japanese restaurant group, a different menu — and unlike the Wynwood location it does not open for lunch: service runs from 5pm to 11pm, seven nights a week. For anyone building an evening on the Beach without drinking, the practical advantage of Sunset Harbour is that it is a walkable few blocks of restaurants rather than a strip of clubs.

The bar's alcohol-free section is short but properly constructed. The Akabanaa is the anchor: Ritual Tequila Alternative with lime and a hibiscus agave, a build that uses the bite of the non-alcoholic spirit and the tartness of hibiscus to keep the drink from reading as a soft drink. The Raba, which also appears in a slightly different form on the Wynwood menu, is described as the cleaner and tangier of the two. RESIDENT covered the restaurant in its December 2025 Miami round-up and wrote that the zero-proof selections reflect the restaurant's refined approach to flavour, and that they are built to complement the menu rather than compete with it. Ingredient detail beyond that is not published on the restaurant's own site, so the Raba is recorded here by name only rather than with a guessed specification. No phone number is published in this entry; reservations are handled through the restaurant's website. The location posts under the group account @uchikorestaurants. Sunset Harbour itself is worth knowing about for anyone avoiding the bar strips: it is a compact grid of low-rise blocks by the marina rather than a nightlife strip. Uchiko's neighbourhood is recorded here as Sunset Harbour rather than the broader South Beach because the two read very differently on the ground.
venues.pressQuote: Uchiko's zero-proof selections reflect the restaurant's refined approach to flavor.

venues.name: Uchiko Plano
venues.description: Uchiko in Legacy West carries three separate zero-proof sections — cocktails, wine and beer — which is more structure than most Dallas restaurants give the category. The cocktails include the mitsu mitsu on Ritual Zero Proof gin with rosemary and yuzu honey, an akabanaa built on Ritual's agave spirit with hibiscus and lime, and a tsuchi mule using the Scottish botanical spirit Feragaia, an unusually adventurous choice for a suburban dining room. Dealcoholised Oddbird and Wölffer Estate wines are poured by the glass, and the beer list carries Athletic Brewing, Best Day and Sapporo 0.0. Note this is the Plano room; Uchi Dallas is listed separately.
venues.address: 7801 Windrose Ave Ste H150, Plano, TX 75024
signatureDrinks: mitsu mitsu (Ritual Zero Proof gin, rosemary, yuzu honey)
akabanaa (Ritual zero proof agave, hibiscus-lime agave)
venues.longDescription:
Uchiko is the Austin sibling of Uchi, and its Legacy West dining room brings the same farmhouse-Japanese format to Plano. Like the Uchi group's other Texas rooms it treats zero-proof drinking as a full category rather than a courtesy, printing three separate sections: zero proof cocktails, zero proof wine and zero proof beer. Splitting the offer into three headings rather than one is not cosmetic — it means someone has thought about the fact that a person who has stopped drinking has not stopped wanting different things on different nights.

The cocktails are built on real non-alcoholic distillates. The mitsu mitsu uses Ritual Zero Proof gin with rosemary and a yuzu honey; the akabanaa runs Ritual's agave spirit into a hibiscus-lime agave; and the tsuchi mule is built on Feragaia, the Scottish botanical spirit, which is an unusually adventurous choice for a suburban restaurant and the clearest sign the list was assembled by someone who tastes widely. A zero crush made with Crodino and non-alcoholic sparkling covers the aperitivo end, and a tinto de verano combines Oddbird's GSM with Feragaia.

The wine section is what makes this worth a detour for anyone who has given up alcohol but misses wine with food. Oddbird's dealcoholised blanc de blancs, white blend and GSM are poured by the glass alongside a Wölffer Estate sparkling rosé — a proper by-the-glass programme rather than a single token bottle, at a restaurant where the sake and wine lists are central to the experience. Pairing across a tasting-style Japanese menu is precisely the situation where a lone mocktail fails and a range of wines does not. Service runs from 4pm daily, to 10pm most nights and 11pm on Friday and Saturday. Note that Uchi Dallas, listed separately in this guide, is a different restaurant in a different city; this is the Plano room.
venues.pressQuote: Plano restaurant will offer Akabanaa with Ritual zero proof agave, hibiscus-lime agave, & lime; Mitsu Mitsu with Ritual zero proof gin, rosemary, yuzu honey; Shokuzen with zero proof pinot noir, Giffard aperitif, citrus oleo; and Tsuchi mule with Feragaia spirit, yuzu, and ginger beer.

venues.name: UnBAR Cafe
venues.description: IMPORTANT CLARIFICATION — UNBAR SERVES ALCOHOL. UnBAR Cafe is a Black-owned cafe and evening hangout on Larchmere Boulevard, opened on 20 January 2020 by Melissa Garrett-Hirsch and built around the social experience of a bar for people who are not drinking. We previously implied it was alcohol-free; it is not. It runs a wine offering alongside its non-alcoholic drinks, and the owner's own framing is precisely the point: people can bring their friends and have a good time, participate in karaoke, trivia and cards, and their friends can have the alcoholic beverage — but they don't have to. A mixologist who specialises in non-alcoholic work makes the drinks, and the rest of the menu runs to espresso, smoothies, soup and light, health-conscious food. The interior is deliberately domestic — green and purple walls, positive art, inspirational quotes lettered where you will read them — described by its owner as a loved one's living room, and the room programmes comedy, game nights, karaoke and poetry. PLEASE NOTE: its website is currently broken and its published phone numbers disagree across listings, so confirm hours on its social channels before travelling.
venues.longDescription:
UnBAR Cafe opened on Larchmere Boulevard on 20 January 2020, weeks before the pandemic closed everything, and it has become one of the most quietly important rooms in Cleveland for people who do not drink. Melissa Garrett-Hirsch built it around a simple observation about how sober socialising actually fails: it is not that non-drinkers have nowhere to buy a soft drink, it is that they have nowhere to bring their friends. Her own description of the fix is the clearest statement of the idea anyone in this guide has offered — people can bring their friends here and have a good time, they can do karaoke, trivia and cards, and their friends can have the alcoholic beverage, but they don't have to. She describes the space as being like a loved one's living room, and it looks like it: green and purple walls, positive art, inspirational quotes lettered where you will actually read them. The programming does the rest, with comedy, game nights, karaoke and poetry. Her regulars' verdict, which she repeats with some affection, is that they hate telling people about UnBar because they do not want it to change.

One clarification is needed, because our earlier entry implied more than is true. UnBAR is not an alcohol-free venue. It serves alcohol, running a wine offering alongside the non-alcoholic drinks, and it hosts events aimed at sober audiences within a space that is licensed. That does not diminish it — arguably the opposite, since a mixed room where a non-drinker is genuinely catered for is harder to build and more useful to most people than a fully dry one — but it is a material fact and we had it wrong. What earns the listing is that the non-alcoholic side is made by a mixologist who specialises in that work rather than being an afterthought behind the coffee machine, alongside espresso, smoothies, soup and a light, health-conscious food menu. Two practical cautions. Its website is currently broken, serving an error page under a mismatched certificate, so there is no authoritative online menu to check. And its phone number is listed three different ways across directories. Its social accounts are active and are the reliable place to confirm hours before you travel.
venues.pressQuote: My intentions were to create a space where you walk through the door and you get a virtual hug. I wanted to create an environment where you feel safe.

venues.name: Uncle Nicky's Italian Specialties
venues.description: Uncle Nicky's is an all-day Italian café on South Lamar, open 10am to 10pm every day of the week, working the northern-Italian bar-café tradition in which coffee in the morning and aperitivo in the evening come from the same counter. That model suits a non-drinker unusually well, and the house keeps named alcohol-free drinks on the printed list: the Porch Swing and the Fluffy Orange Mule, both named by Visit Austin's official zero-proof guide. The aperitivo format is what matters here — an Italian café is one of the very few settings where ordering something soft in the early evening is completely unremarkable, because the room was serving cappuccino an hour earlier. A deli counter runs alongside.
venues.longDescription:
Uncle Nicky's Italian Specialties runs on the northern-Italian bar-café model, which is worth understanding because it is the whole reason the place works for someone who is not drinking. In Italy a bar is a café: the same counter serves espresso at eight in the morning, a sandwich at one, and an aperitivo at six, and nobody treats the switch as a change of venue or a change of intent. Uncle Nicky's imports that structure to South Lamar, opening at 10am and running to 10pm seven days a week.

The practical effect is that the aperitivo hour — the part of the evening a non-drinker usually has to navigate — happens in a room that is still recognisably a café. Ordering something alcohol-free at 6pm in a cocktail bar marks you out; ordering it at an Italian counter that was serving cappuccino an hour earlier does not. For anyone newly sober, or pregnant, or simply driving, that difference is more useful than a long mocktail list.

The named alcohol-free drinks are the Porch Swing and the Fluffy Orange Mule, both listed in Visit Austin's official zero-proof guide. The Mule in particular is a sensible piece of menu design — the alcoholic original is defined by ginger and lime rather than by the vodka, so the non-alcoholic version loses very little in translation, which is not true of most spirit-forward classics.

The deli side of the business runs alongside, so the room is as much a shop and a lunch spot as a bar. The grade is an honest 3: two named drinks, well chosen, in a setting that does a lot of the work. Worth confirming the current list, as café menus rotate more often than bar menus do.
venues.pressQuote: Uncle Nicky's: Porch Swing; Fluffy Orange Mule.

venues.name: Understory
venues.description: Understory is an immersive, ingredient-driven craft cocktail bar tucked into the Sky Deck at Del Mar Highlands Town Center. The concept is themed around the hidden world beneath the forest canopy, and that ecology motif runs through the drink names; guests can order food from the surrounding Sky Deck restaurants and pair it with Understory's tableside cocktails. Within its broader program, the bar maintains a small but deliberate non-alcoholic section built with the same care as the full-proof list — led by the signature Boisduval's Marble (blue lavender, black tea, lemon, kava, non-alcoholic Creole bitters, and aquafaba fizz for texture), alongside builds like the Lustrous Copper and Crimson Fruitcrow. It's a polished North County date-night and cocktail destination.
venues.address: 12841 El Camino Real, Ste 209-210, San Diego, CA 92130
venues.longDescription:
Understory sits in the Sky Deck at Del Mar Highlands Town Center, and it is themed on the understory itself — the layer of the forest that lives beneath the canopy, in the shade of everything taller. That ecological conceit runs through the room and, more usefully, through the drink names, which are drawn from butterflies, birds and plants. The format is unusual and worth understanding before you go: Understory is a bar rather than a restaurant, and guests order food from the surrounding Sky Deck restaurants and bring it to the table, pairing it with cocktails made tableside. That makes it a genuinely flexible destination for a group with different appetites.

Within the wider programme the bar keeps a small, deliberate non-alcoholic section built with the same care as the full-proof list. The signature is Boisduval's Marble — named for a butterfly — which combines blue lavender and black tea with lemon, kava, non-alcoholic Creole bitters and an aquafaba fizz for texture. That drink is a good illustration of what separates a considered zero-proof build from a poor one: black tea supplies tannin, the Creole bitters supply the aromatic bite, and the aquafaba supplies the weight and foam that alcohol otherwise provides, so the finished drink has structure rather than just flavour. Alongside it sit the Lustrous Copper and the Crimson Fruitcrow. San Diego Magazine's Kelly Davis singled out the same drink when covering the county's no-ABV options. One note for readers in recovery: the Boisduval's Marble contains kava, a mildly sedating South Pacific botanical that is alcohol-free but psychoactive — worth asking about if you would rather avoid it, since the other two builds do not use it. Open daily, late on Fridays and Saturdays. Del Mar Highlands sits well north of the city proper, so this is a North County destination rather than a San Diego one, and the Sky Deck format means a group can eat across several kitchens and still drink together at one table.
venues.pressQuote: Del Mar's Understory includes three alcohol-free offerings on its ecology-themed menu, including Boisduval's Marble — blue lavender, black tea, fresh lemon, kava, non-alcoholic Creole bitters, and, for texture, aquafaba fizz.

venues.name: UnderTow
venues.description: A tiny, immersive below-deck tiki bar themed around an 18th-century sailing voyage, UnderTow is a Phoenix cult favorite — and its menu runs a genuine lineup of spiritless tiki drinks built with non-alcoholic 'liquors' rather than just juice. The house alcohol-free spirits are distilled by the Century Grand team upstairs and used across all three of its concepts, so a zero-proof order here is the same programme on a different base. The Shipless Sailor is the one to know: a rum substitute worked with cinnamon, clove, orgeat, hibiscus, lime and pineapple. Now under the Barter & Shake group, with a second location in Gilbert; reservations are essentially required for the cramped, transportive room.
venues.address: 3626 E Indian School Rd Suite 100, Phoenix, AZ 85018
venues.longDescription:
UnderTow is reached by a staircase down from the Century Grand complex on Indian School Road, and the descent is the point: the room is built as the below-decks of an 18th-century sailing ship, portholes showing water and weather, ceiling low enough to matter. It seats very few people, runs in timed sittings, and had a cult following in Phoenix well before the two bars upstairs existed. Reservations are not a formality here — walking in is rarely an option.

Tiki is the hardest category to do without alcohol, because the classic builds lean on rum for body and the obvious substitute is more fruit juice, which produces something closer to a smoothie than a drink. UnderTow avoids that by using the non-alcoholic spirits the Century Grand team distils in house, the same ones running through Platform 18 and Grey Hen Rx. The Shipless Sailor is the clearest example: a rum substitute layered with cinnamon, clove, orgeat, hibiscus, lime and pineapple, which keeps the spice and the weight that make a tiki drink work rather than just its sweetness. Phoenix New Times named the drink when it surveyed metro bars with real alcohol-free options in January 2024.

The practicalities matter more here than at most bars. The room is small and hot by design, sittings are timed, and there is a second location in Gilbert if the Arcadia one is booked out — which it usually is. And the venue is a full-strength tiki bar: the spiritless builds are a proper part of the menu rather than the character of the room, so expect to be surrounded by rum drinks while not having one. For anyone who finds that hard, the room upstairs at Grey Hen Rx is quieter, better lit and pours from the same house-made alcohol-free range.
venues.pressQuote: The seafaring Undertow's Shipless Sailor starts with a rum substitute and incorporates warming spices such as cinnamon and clove, along with orgeat, hibiscus, lime and pineapple.

venues.name: Union Jack Pub
venues.description: Union Jack Pub is a long-running British-styled pizza pub on Broad Ripple Avenue, and one of the neighbourhood's fixtures. Its non-alcoholic offer is narrower than a cocktail bar's but properly made: the Elderflower Garden builds Seedlip Garden — the pea and garden-herb expression of the London non-alcoholic distillate — over an elderflower simple syrup and tonic, which drinks like a proper gin and tonic substitute rather than a sweet mocktail. It is an all-day room, open from 11am on weekdays and 10am at weekends, which makes it usable for lunch as well as an evening. The company's Speedway location, open 41 years, closed permanently; the Broad Ripple pub is the one still trading.
signatureDrinks: Elderflower Garden (Seedlip Garden, elderflower simple syrup, tonic)
venues.longDescription:
Union Jack Pub has been part of the Broad Ripple furniture for decades — a British-themed pizza pub on Broad Ripple Avenue, in a neighbourhood whose reputation is otherwise built on late bars and a strip of nightlife that is not friendly to anyone avoiding alcohol. It is on this list for one drink, made well. The Elderflower Garden uses Seedlip Garden, the pea, rosemary, thyme and spearmint expression of the London non-alcoholic distillate, over an elderflower simple syrup and tonic. That is the correct construction for a gin-and-tonic substitute: the botanical distillate does the aromatic work that gin would, the tonic brings the quinine bitterness, and the elderflower keeps it from tasting thin. It is one of four venues on this list pouring Seedlip, and Indy Maven named it in its round-up of the city's best mocktails.

The practical value here is the hours and the format. Most of the credible zero-proof lists in Indianapolis are in evening bars that open at 4pm or 5pm; Union Jack opens at 11am on weekdays and 10am at weekends, serves pizza all day, and takes families. For someone not drinking, a pub you can go to at lunchtime is a different and often more useful proposition than a cocktail bar you can only reach after dark.

One point of confusion to head off. Union Jack Pub ran a second, older location in Speedway near the Motor Speedway for 41 years, and that one has closed permanently — it still appears in circulating guides and on map listings. The Broad Ripple pub at 921 Broad Ripple Avenue is the one trading. Note the street number: some published guides give 924, which is the opposite side of the road. Broad Ripple is a mile north of the SoBro Orangily bottle shop up the Monon Trail, and Cholita is two doors along the same block, so an alcohol-free afternoon in this neighbourhood is straightforward to assemble.
venues.pressQuote: Elderflower Garden — Seedlip Garden, elderflower simple syrup and tonic.

venues.name: UP on the Roof
venues.description: UP on the Roof is the rooftop bar at the top of North Main in downtown Greenville, looking out over Main Street and the Blue Ridge beyond it, and it keeps a booze-free drink as a menu staple rather than a seasonal special. The Walk the Line is built on lemon and pink grapefruit juices with a blackberry simple syrup and club soda — a long, tart, low-sugar drink rather than a sweet one, which is what actually works across an evening on a rooftop. Open from 3pm most days, 11am from Thursday, and running to midnight or 2am at weekends, seven days a week.
signatureDrinks: Walk the Line — lemon and pink grapefruit juices, blackberry simple syrup, club soda
venues.longDescription:
UP on the Roof occupies the top of the building at 1 North Main, at the head of Greenville's main street, with the Blue Ridge escarpment visible on a clear day. It is the kind of room a group ends up at, which makes what it pours for the non-drinkers among them more consequential than a specialist bar's list would be.

The Walk the Line is described in the local drinks coverage as a staple rather than a special, and that word is the important one. A seasonal mocktail is a marketing exercise; a staple is something the bar has decided it will always be able to make, which means the components stay stocked and the staff stay trained. Anyone who has turned up somewhere on the strength of a drink they read about and found it rotated off will recognise why that matters.

The build itself is sensibly designed for the setting: lemon and pink grapefruit juices, a blackberry simple syrup and club soda. Two citrus juices rather than one give it real acidity, the blackberry supplies colour and just enough sweetness, and the soda makes it long. On a hot rooftop in the Carolina summer, long and tart is the correct answer, and it is the opposite of what most bars reach for when asked for something without alcohol.

The hours are among the best in this guide. Three in the afternoon to midnight Monday through Wednesday, an 11am start from Thursday onwards, and 2am closes on Friday and Saturday — seven days a week, no closed day, and open through the afternoon when most of Greenville's cocktail rooms are still locked.

It sits a few minutes' walk from Oak & Honey, Crafted and STIR, at the opposite end of Main from Juniper.
venues.pressQuote: A staple mocktail called Walk the Line is booze-free and features lemon and pink grapefruit juices, blackberry simple syrup, and club soda.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: TOWN Carolina, Mocktails for Dry July

venues.name: Upstairs Circus
venues.description: Upstairs Circus LoDo is the original location of the DIY workshop-meets-bar concept, opened in 2010 in Denver's historic Lower Downtown district at 1500 Wynkoop Street near Union Station. The space pairs a full bar serving craft cocktails, mocktails, beer, and wine with a rotating menu of 25+ hands-on creative projects — jewelry making, leather working, woodworking, art, and home décor — that guests work on at their own pace while drinking. The format is reservation-based: book a seat, pick your project from the menu at check-in, get supplies and photo tutorials plus on-demand staff help, and take your finished piece home. The non-alcoholic offering is a headed section of the bar menu rather than an afterthought: Free Spirited, marked no alcohol, lists five drinks at $8 — the Pineapple Palm Reader, Berry Go Round, Tumblin Peach Tea, Lion Taming Limeade and the jalapeno-spiked Pepper Pantomime — with Athletic Brewing's Free Wave hazy IPA poured alongside at the same price, roughly half what the cocktails cost. The concept has since expanded to Austin, Minneapolis, and a second Denver-area location in Greenwood Village, but the LoDo location remains the original.

venues.longDescription:
Upstairs Circus LoDo is the original location of a concept its founder describes as DIY workshop meets bar, opened in 2010 by Kelly Johannsen at 1500 Wynkoop Street in Denver's historic Lower Downtown, a block from Union Station. The format is reservation-based and unusually structured for a bar: guests book a seat, choose from a rotating menu of more than twenty-five hands-on projects at check-in, and are given the materials and photo tutorials to work through them at their own pace, with staff available on demand. The project list spans leather working, wood working, jewellery making, art and home decor, and finished pieces go home with the guest. Drinks are served throughout rather than before or after, which is the whole point of the format: the bar exists to keep hands busy and conversation going for the two or three hours a project takes.

For non-drinkers this matters more than it might at a conventional bar, because the activity, not the alcohol, is the reason to be there, and the room is one of the few places downtown where an evening out has a built-in purpose that does not depend on drinking. The full bar pours craft cocktails, beer and wine alongside a named non-alcoholic section on the LoDo bar menu. The published Upstairs Circus bar menu carries a section headed Free Spirited and marked no alcohol, holding five drinks at $8 each: the Pineapple Palm Reader with pineapple, vanilla simple syrup and ginger beer; Berry Go Round with lemonade, grenadine, strawberry preserve and soda; Tumblin Peach Tea with tea, simple syrup and peach preserve; Lion Taming Limeade with soda, lime, mint simple syrup and cherry juice; and the Pepper Pantomime, a spicy margarita substitute of lime, ginger beer, pineapple and jalapeno. Athletic Brewing's Free Wave hazy IPA is the non-alcoholic beer, also $8. Do303's Denver and Boulder non-alcoholic guide still recommends a Snake Charmer of grapefruit juice, lime juice, simple syrup and tonic here; that drink is not on the published menu as of August 2026, so do not go expecting it. FOX31's Dry January listicle put the mocktails in the $7 to $8 range, which is roughly half what the cocktails cost. The concept has since expanded to Austin and Minneapolis and to a second Denver-area location, but the Wynkoop Street room remains the original and the largest of the project menus. The LoDo room is closed Mondays, opens at 3pm midweek and from late morning at weekends, and sessions are booked rather than walked into, so a group planning a sober night out can hold a table in advance without negotiating anything at the door.
venues.pressQuote: The idea behind Upstairs Circus is 'DIY Workshop Meets Bar.'

venues.name: Urban Farmer
venues.description: Urban Farmer is the steakhouse inside the Logan Hotel on Benjamin Franklin Parkway, and its drinks menu carries a printed section headed "No Proof Cocktails" rather than burying the alcohol-free options among the soft drinks. The Cadillac Shirley Temple at $12 is the one worth ordering — house grenadine and verjus with lemon-lime soda and a cherry, where the verjus does the job a dry wine would. The Crimson Fizz pairs cranberry with a cranberry shrub and Fever-Tree ginger beer, and the Fauxpresso Negroni builds St. Agrestis Phony Espresso Negroni into cold brew with orange. Athletic Brewing's Upside Dawn covers the beer side. The kitchen serves from seven in the morning until half past eleven at night.

venues.longDescription:
Urban Farmer occupies the ground floor of the Logan Hotel on Benjamin Franklin Parkway, working a farm-to-table steakhouse format — dry-aged beef, a cheese cart, a long wine list. It is a hotel restaurant in the good sense: open from seven in the morning to half past eleven at night, every day, which makes it one of the more reliable late kitchens in Logan Square.

The drinks menu carries a printed heading, "No Proof Cocktails", and the builds under it are more considered than the category usually gets in a steakhouse. The Cadillac Shirley Temple is the standout, and the joke in the name is doing real work: a Shirley Temple is the archetypal drink handed to whoever is not drinking, and this version rebuilds it seriously. House-made grenadine replaces the bottled syrup, and verjus — the pressed juice of unripe grapes — supplies the sharp, wine-like acidity that the original completely lacks. That single ingredient is what turns a children's drink into something an adult can hold through a steak dinner.

The Crimson Fizz runs cranberry against a cranberry shrub with Fever-Tree ginger beer, doubling the fruit in two forms, one fresh and one preserved in vinegar, which gives it a much longer finish than juice alone. The Fauxpresso Negroni is the after-dinner option, taking St. Agrestis's Phony Espresso Negroni — a bottled alcohol-free amaro-style aperitif — into cold brew and orange.

On the beer side the house pours Athletic Brewing's Upside Dawn golden ale, which is the reliable non-alcoholic beer to find on a list where the alternative would be a soft drink.

The practical case here is the occasion. A steakhouse is where anniversaries, business dinners and family celebrations happen, and it is precisely where a non-drinker is most conspicuous — the wine is the ritual, and declining it is visible. A printed section with four named options, one of them explicitly designed to be a grown-up version of the drink you would otherwise be handed, removes that friction entirely.

venues.name: Urban Grub
venues.description: Urban Grub is a Southern seafood-and-grill restaurant in Nashville's 12 South neighborhood, opened in April 2012 by Jay Pennington and Billy Inman inside a renovated former carwash at the corner of 12th and Gilmore. Branded "Fresh Fish & Fine Aged Meats," the kitchen pairs Southern traditions with a flavored-up tweak — fresh-shucked oysters, smoked and grilled meats, and seafood. The bar maintains a named non-alcoholic program highlighted by local guide Nashville Guru for its "extensive selection" of zero-proof options. The current card runs four at $10 under a Non-Alcoholic Cocktails heading: a Fauxspresso Martini on Switters nitro cold brew with vanilla clove, Defying Gravity (Seedlip Agave, Lyre's Italian Orange, lemon and house grenadine), a Not Aperol Spritz on Lyre's Italian Orange with NA sparkling wine, and a Free Spirit of grapefruit, ginger syrup, lime and ginger beer — alongside non-alcoholic beer from Athletic Brewing (Lite, Golden Dawn, and Run Wild IPA) and other NA pours. It's a lively 12 South spot where non-drinkers have a real menu to choose from.

venues.longDescription:
Urban Grub sits at 2506 12th Avenue South, on the corner of 12th and Gilmore in the 12 South neighbourhood, in a building that spent its earlier life as a small carwash and took thirteen months to convert. It opened in April 2012 from Jay Pennington, who runs operations, and Billy Inman, who shaped the look of the room, and it trades under the banner "Fresh Fish & Fine Aged Meats" — a Southern seafood-and-grill hybrid built around a fish programme and a wood grill, with fresh-shucked oysters, smoked and grilled meats, and a dining room that stays busy and loud in a part of town where that is the point. Service runs late for the neighbourhood, from 4pm to midnight Tuesday through Thursday and from 10.30am on Sundays for brunch, with reservations through OpenTable.

For non-drinkers the relevant fact is breadth rather than invention. Local guide Nashville Guru singled the bar out for an unusually extensive range of non-alcoholic options, and the list it recorded is deeper on packaged drinks than most restaurants manage: three Athletic Brewing beers — the Lite, Golden Dawn and Run Wild IPA — alongside a BrewDog hazy IPA, an Untitled Art dragon fruit sour, Original Sin sparkling cider, an Infruition sparkling Earl Grey and a Thirst Mutilator hop water. That is a genuine range of styles rather than one token non-alcoholic beer, and it means a non-drinker at a table of drinkers has something to choose between across a long meal. The same source records built mocktails including a Fauxpresso Martini, a Not Aperol Spritz and a Free Spirit of grapefruit, ginger syrup, lime and ginger beer. One honest caveat: Urban Grub does not publish its bar menu in a readable form on its own website, so the mixed drinks above come from a local guide rather than the restaurant, and a second listing site shows different mocktails entirely. The packaged non-alcoholic range is well attested; the specific mocktail names are worth confirming with the bar when you order.
venues.pressQuote: Urban Grub can seem a little over-the-top with all the exposed wood, fire features and tables and booths tucked into every corner of the restaurant, but they still manage to do it right.

venues.name: Urban South Brewery
venues.description: Urban South Brewery, founded in 2016 by Jacob Landry and Kyle Huling, is the largest brewery by volume in New Orleans, anchoring a taproom on Tchoupitoulas Street in the Lower Garden District that welcomes families and hosts children's birthday parties. It was the first brewery in the city to brew a non-alcoholic version of its own beer. The NA program is built around two in-house 0.5% ABV brews: N.A. Holy Roller, a hazy IPA using the same Mosaic, Citra and Centennial hops as the flagship, and N.A. Charming Wit. PARENTS AND NON-DRINKERS SHOULD KNOW: the same beverage page also carries a "THC Beverages" section of nine hemp-derived THC seltzers at 5mg per can — Grapefruit, Black Cherry, Tangerine Ginger, Peach Spritz, Watermelon Spritz, NOLA Cola Classic, NOLA Cola Root Beer, Lemon Lavender and Lime — listed immediately above the "Non-Alcoholic" heading, with no warning or age-policy text published nearby. The two categories are labelled separately but sit side by side. The taproom serves smash burgers, with happy hour weekdays 3 to 6pm.

venues.longDescription:
Urban South was founded in 2016 by Jacob Landry and Kyle Huling, two LSU graduates, and is now the largest brewery by volume in New Orleans. Landry's account of why is worth hearing: the seed was planted during a year he spent in Europe, where he understood for the first time how big the chasm was between the beer his ancestors drank and the mass-market stuff he grew up with in South Louisiana. Huling brought a decade in beer distribution and a lifetime in the city. The taproom is at 1645 Tchoupitoulas Street in the Lower Garden District, serves smash burgers from its in-house Urban Smash counter, runs happy hour weekdays from 3 to 6, and is genuinely set up for families — it advertises private parties and children's birthdays. It opens at 11am daily, until 9pm most nights and 10pm on Friday and Saturday.

It was the first brewery in New Orleans to brew a non-alcoholic version of its own beer, and the two it makes are both 0.5% ABV. N.A. Holy Roller is the one that matters: a hazy IPA using the same Mosaic, Citra and Centennial hops as the flagship Holy Roller, at 60 IBU, and the brewery's own line is that it lets you keep your halo polished without sacrificing flavour. N.A. Charming Wit is the wheat beer counterpart. Neither is priced on the website. There is something worth flagging for anyone bringing children or avoiding intoxicants generally. The same beverage page that lists those two non-alcoholic beers also carries a THC Beverages section immediately above the Non-Alcoholic heading — nine hemp-derived seltzers at 5mg of THC per can, in flavours including NOLA Cola, Lemon Lavender and Peach Spritz. The headings are distinct and the dose is printed on each line, so the labelling is not misleading. But the two sit adjacent on one page in a taproom that hosts children's parties, and no warning or age-policy text appears near either section. Read the heading above whatever you order.
venues.pressQuote: Urban South Brewery will unveil a non-alcoholic version of their Holy Roller Hazy Juicy IPA on Friday, just in time for designated drivers to have a new beverage option to ring in 2024.

venues.name: UrbanMama505 Kombuchery & Elixir Bar
venues.description: UrbanMama505 is a kombuchery and elixir bar on Central Avenue run by Julie Morrell and Ted Archuleta, brewing its own kombucha from organic teas and pouring it as flights — lime, lavender, rose hips, and a Black Guatemalan made with cold-brew coffee. Nothing served contains alcohol. Morrell's framing of why it exists is the clearest statement of this directory's premise anyone has made: the culture always asks what you're drinking, and they want people to know that does not always mean alcohol. The hours are narrow — Friday and Saturday only — so plan around them. The building is a plain cement-block unit on Central, easy to drive past.

signatureDrinks: Kombucha flight — lime, lavender, rose hips, Black Guatemalan (cold-brew coffee)
venues.longDescription:
UrbanMama505 operates out of a cement-block building on Central Avenue, and it is a kombuchery first — Julie Morrell and Ted Archuleta brew the kombucha themselves from organic teas — with a bar attached rather than the other way round.

The flight is the format that makes it work as a social venue rather than a shop. Four small pours across lime, lavender, rose hips and a Black Guatemalan made with cold-brew coffee gives a table something to compare, discuss and work through, which is most of what a round of drinks actually provides. Kombucha itself is well suited to the job: it is sour, faintly funky, lightly effervescent and genuinely complex, closer in character to a natural wine or a sour beer than to a soft drink, and it is one of the few things a non-drinker can order that rewards paying attention.

Morrell's line to New Mexico Magazine is the best single articulation of this directory's premise that its research has turned up. The culture is always asking what you're drinking, and she wants people to know that does not always mean alcohol. The problem was never thirst; it was the question and what answering it costs you.

One honest technical note: kombucha is a live ferment and contains trace alcohol, typically under 0.5% and comparable to a non-alcoholic beer. For most readers that is immaterial. For anyone abstaining completely it is worth knowing rather than discovering.

The hours are the real limitation and they are tight: Friday 11am to 4pm and Saturday 10am to 2pm, closed the rest of the week. This is a daytime, weekend proposition — a Saturday-morning stop rather than an evening out — and it should be planned as one. Check before travelling, as small producer hours move.
venues.pressQuote: Our culture is always saying, 'What you drinkin'?' We want people to know that doesn't always mean alcohol.

venues.name: Valkyrie
venues.description: Valkyrie is downtown Tulsa's serious cocktail bar, on Reconciliation Way, open 4pm to 2am six nights a week and closed only on Monday. It has treated zero-proof drinks as part of the programme for years rather than as a recent addition — a Don't Text Your Mex of spicy house ginger beer, strawberry syrup, lemon and basil appeared in local drinks writing back in 2020, and the current alcohol-free entry is the NWA, built on orgeat, cream and lemon. Both are house-made from the bar's own components. It is one of three downtown rooms in this guide keeping a 2am licence, which makes late sober nights in Tulsa genuinely possible.
