venues.longDescription:
Valkyrie has been the reference point for cocktails in Tulsa for a decade, in a dark room on Reconciliation Way at the edge of downtown, and it is one of the few bars in this guide that was thinking about alcohol-free drinks before the category became fashionable.

The evidence for that is in the archive. When Tulsa's drinks writing first made the argument for zero-proof cocktails, Valkyrie's contribution was Don't Text Your Mex — a spicy house ginger beer with strawberry syrup, lemon and basil, built entirely from the bar's own components. The current entry is the NWA, an orgeat, cream and lemon build, which is a much harder drink to make well than it looks: cream and citrus want to split, and holding them together is a technique problem rather than a recipe one.

The argument for why any of this matters was made best by Nathan Young, a long-time Tulsa bartender who had been sober six months when he put it to The Humble Garnish: hospitality is hospitality, people are at a bar to enjoy the environment and have conversations, and a bartender should make sure those who are not drinking feel just as included. That is the whole case for this directory in two sentences, made by someone standing behind a bar in this city.

The practical value is the hours. Valkyrie runs 4pm to 2am Tuesday through Sunday, closed only on Monday, which puts it alongside Saturn Room and Starlite as the three downtown rooms where a non-drinker can still be out at one in the morning.

This entry records the current named build only. The earlier drink is described above as evidence of a long commitment rather than as something to order — the list has moved on in the years since, which is what a live programme does.

One practical note about the address. Reconciliation Way was renamed in memory of the 1921 Tulsa Race Massacre, and the bar sits at the edge of the Greenwood district, with the Greenwood Rising history centre a short walk away. It is worth knowing what neighbourhood you are drinking in, and it makes Valkyrie an easy pairing with an afternoon that was not built around alcohol in the first place.
venues.pressQuote: Hospitality is hospitality. People are at a bar to enjoy the environment and have conversations. A bartender should make sure those who are not drinking alcohol feel just as included.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: The Humble Garnish, Spirit of Inclusion

venues.name: Van Ryder
venues.description: An 11th-floor rooftop bar atop the Le Méridien Salt Lake City Downtown, opened in February 2023 with a Western-saloon aesthetic. Its non-alcoholic program is unusually deep: a dedicated "Proofless Cocktails" menu (the Honey Badger Redux and Meet Me in The Garden, both around $11) plus a separate "Proofless Beer" list. Director of Libations and Service Elyse Evan has put the zero-proof program at roughly 15% of total sales, with NA beer running 25-30% of all beer sales. The spirit-free builds get the same care as the full rooftop cocktail list, served against floor-to-ceiling skyline and Wasatch Range views.

venues.longDescription:
Van Ryder sits on the top floor of the Le Méridien hotel in downtown Salt Lake City's West Quarter, pairing an indoor lounge of floor-to-ceiling windows with an outdoor terrace and fire pits overlooking the city, the Wasatch Range and the Great Salt Lake. The drinks lean into Utah spirits and locally sourced, house-made syrups.

The zero-proof side is a genuine focus rather than an afterthought. In a 2023 Utah Stories feature, the bar's libations director said its popularity has only kept climbing, and the menu carries both proofless cocktails and a standalone proofless beer list, so non-drinkers get a full, intentional lineup alongside the rooftop's signature cocktails.
venues.pressQuote: I would estimate around 15% of sales go toward our zero-proof program. Our zero-proof beer selection really holds its own at 25-30% of our total beer sales!
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Elyse Evan, Director of Libations and Service at Van Ryder

venues.name: Vanderpump Cocktail Garden
venues.description: Vanderpump Cocktail Garden is reality-TV personality Lisa Vanderpump's glamorous open-air-style cocktail lounge at Caesars Palace, tucked between The Colosseum and the entrance to The Forum Shops on the Las Vegas Strip. The space is styled as an elaborately decorated garden with sparkling chandeliers, lush florals, and pink-hued opulent decor, and it draws a steady celebrity-fueled, Instagram-driven crowd. Beyond its hand-crafted signature cocktails, the menu includes a dedicated "Mighty Mocktails" section of zero-proof drinks, so non-drinkers get crafted options rather than an afterthought. House mocktails include the Garden Goddess (mint, matcha, pineapple, lemon, and aquafaba for a velvety foam) and the Caesars Berries (raspberry, mint, hibiscus, lemon, coconut, and soda), both made with the same garnish-forward attention as the alcoholic list. The kitchen pairs the drinks with decadent small bites, with the goat cheese balls a widely cited favorite.
venues.address: 3570 S Las Vegas Blvd, Las Vegas, NV 89109

Caesars Berries (raspberry, mint, hibiscus, lemon, coconut, soda)
venues.longDescription:
Vanderpump Cocktail Garden opened on 1 April 2019 at Caesars Palace, the first Las Vegas venue from the restaurateur and reality-television personality Lisa Vanderpump. It sits on the Strip between The Colosseum and the entrance to The Forum Shops, and it was designed by Vanderpump with her husband Ken Todd and creative director Nick Alain, the same collaborator behind her Los Angeles bar Tom Tom; Alain handled the lighting, fixtures and furniture. The result is an indoor patio dressed as an al fresco garden — sixteen-foot olive trees, sparkling chandeliers, lush florals and a great deal of pink — and it draws exactly the celebrity-adjacent, camera-forward crowd that suggests. The kitchen sends out decadent small plates alongside the drinks, with the goat cheese balls the most consistently cited order in the room.

For a bar whose whole identity is built on the theatre of a cocktail, the zero-proof handling is better than it needs to be. The menu carries a standing Mighty Mocktails section, which means a non-drinker orders from a named list rather than negotiating with a bartender. The Garden Goddess is built from mint, matcha, pineapple and lemon with aquafaba whipped in for a velvety foam; the Caesars Berries combines raspberry, mint, hibiscus, lemon and coconut with soda for bubbles. Both arrive with the same garnish-forward presentation as the alcoholic list, which matters more than it sounds in a room where the drink is substantially the point and where holding something that looks like everyone else's is the difference between being at the party and being adjacent to it. Visit Las Vegas, the convention and visitors authority's own publication, named the Caesars Berries among the seven must-try mocktails in the city. The garden opens in the afternoon most days and runs late Thursday through Saturday.
venues.pressQuote: You'll find handcrafted mocktails in a decadent and romantic space at Vanderpump Cocktail Garden at Caesars Palace. Order the Caesars Berries, a blush-colored mix of raspberry, mint, hibiscus, lemon, coconut and soda for bubbles.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Visit Las Vegas (Las Vegas Convention and Visitors Authority)

venues.name: VASO Rooftop Lounge
venues.description: VASO is a rooftop lounge above Bridge Park in Dublin, at the north-western edge of the Columbus metro, serving Spanish-inspired tapas with skyline views over the Scioto. It took gold for Best Rooftop Dining in CityScene Magazine's 2025 Best of the 'Bus reader poll. The cocktail menu carries a dedicated no-proof section rather than a single token drink, and the builds use proper non-alcoholic spirits: Everybody Loves Juniper is made with Lyre's London Dry, a house tonic syrup, lemon and soda; the Spice Orange combines Seedlip Citrus with fresh lime, orange and ginger beer; and the house VASO G&T is offered zero-proof with Seedlip Garden, bergamot, lavender, juniper and tonka bean over sparkling Mediterranean tonic. The bar opens at 4pm on weekdays and 2pm on Saturdays.

venues.longDescription:
VASO occupies the roof of the Bridge Park development at 6540 Riverside Drive in Dublin, the affluent suburb at the north-western edge of the Columbus metro, where the Scioto River bends between the old village and the new mixed-use district on the east bank. The kitchen works Spanish-inspired tapas, the room is glass and terrace, and the view is the selling point — enough of one that CityScene Magazine readers voted it gold for Best Rooftop Dining in the 2025 Best of the 'Bus poll.

What distinguishes it for a non-drinking guest is that the cocktail menu carries a standing no-proof section built on real non-alcoholic spirits rather than juice and soda. Everybody Loves Juniper is the current anchor: Lyre's London Dry, the zero-proof gin, with a house tonic syrup, lemon and soda — a drink assembled from a made tonic rather than a bottled one, which is the detail that separates it from a supermarket gin-and-tonic substitute. The Spice Orange runs Seedlip Citrus against fresh lime, orange and ginger beer, giving a longer, warmer drink. And the house VASO G&T, the bar's signature, is offered in a zero-proof build with Seedlip Garden, bergamot, lavender, juniper and tonka bean lengthened with sparkling Mediterranean tonic — an aromatic, layered thing rather than a simple substitution. The pattern across all three is that the alcohol-free versions are specified on the menu with their own ingredient lists, so a guest can order by name. Practical notes: the bar opens at 4pm Monday to Friday and 2pm on Saturdays, runs happy hour on weekday evenings, and the kitchen shuts an hour or two before the bar does. It is a thirty-minute drive from downtown Columbus with no direct transit. For anyone weighing whether the drive is worth it, the honest summary is that VASO is a view-and-occasion room first: the tapas are good, the terrace is the reason people book, and the zero-proof list is deep enough that a non-drinking guest is not left choosing between sparkling water and a sugary substitute. Reservations are strongly advisable at weekends and through the summer.
venues.pressQuote: VASO Rooftop Lounge took gold in the CityScene Magazine 2025 Best of the 'Bus reader poll for the Best Rooftop Dining category.

venues.name: Vector Brewing
venues.description: Vector Brewing is a family-owned Lake Highlands brewpub that brews all its beer in-house on a seven-barrel brewhouse, but it also runs a real 'Not Beer' program for people who aren't drinking. The taproom keeps a rotating bench of non-alcoholic beers — Bero's 0.0% West Coast IPA and Noon Wheat, Rationale Brewing's Japanese-Style Dry and Mexican Cerveza, and Sam Adams Just the Haze — alongside Noble Coyote nitro cold brew, kombucha, espresso and tea. Because the scratch kitchen and coffee bar open at 7am, a non-drinker can order a nitro cold brew as easily as a pint, and the kid-friendly 'Half Pints' patio play zone makes it a low-pressure hang rather than a beer-geek-only room.

venues.longDescription:
Vector Brewing opened in the heart of Lake Highlands in summer 2020, founded by husband-and-wife team Craig and Veronica Bradley. Craig spent six years brewing at Lakewood Brewing before launching Vector, where every beer is made in-house on a custom seven-barrel Deutsche brewhouse tucked away right behind the bar, with two barrel-aging rooms — one dedicated exclusively to mixed-fermentation and oak-aged beers.

Alongside its house draft list, Vector keeps a dedicated 'Not Beer' menu for people who aren't drinking. That includes a genuine bench of non-alcoholic beers — Bero (the 0.0% brand backed by Tom Holland) in Double Tasty West Coast IPA and Noon Wheat, plus Rationale Brewing's Japanese-Style Dry and Mexican Cerveza and Sam Adams Just the Haze — as well as Noble Coyote nitro cold brew on tap, kombucha, cider and a full espresso-and-tea program. Because the coffee bar opens at 7am and runs all day, ordering a cold brew instead of a beer is completely normal here.

The atmosphere is built for families and designated drivers, not just beer enthusiasts. The outdoor patio has a 'Half Pints' play zone for kids, and on weekends Vector serves brunch from 11am to 3pm with sourdough pizzas, migas and gravy pizzas. It's the kind of neighborhood brewpub where choosing an NA beer or a nitro cold brew over a house IPA never feels like a compromise.
venues.pressQuote: Vector offers a whole menu of 'Not Beer,' gluten-free options with the latest from Trinity Cider, Stem Ciders, kombucha, and Noble Coyote nitro cold brew.

venues.name: The Velvet Hippo
venues.description: The Velvet Hippo is a third-floor rooftop bar on Orange Street in downtown Durham with the most complete non-alcoholic menu in the Triangle. Its drinks list carries a standing section headed "Tomorrow-Friendly" — six named zero-proof builds, each priced and specified like the full-strength cocktails beside them, from a Lyre's Italian Spritz to a Ritual tequila-alternative Hot Tropic with a smoked-chilli salt rim — backed by a proper bank of finished alcohol-free product: Athletic Brewing beers, Freixenet and Giesen wines, the Lyre's range and Ritual. The rooftop opens at four most days and noon at weekends, with the kitchen running late Thursday through Saturday. Discover Durham singles it out for a non-alcoholic menu that rivals anything with a proof.

It's Britney, Spritz ($12) — Pallini 'Limonzero' limoncello, Freixenet alcohol-removed sparkling wine, soda water
Hot Tropic ($12) — Ritual Tequila Alternative, guava nectar, lime, fresh jalapeño, simple syrup, cinnamon-sugar smoked chilli salt rim
Girl Dinner ($10) — prickly pear and passionfruit purées, coconut cream, fresh lime, vanilla syrup, soda

The Peach Blossom ($9) — lavender syrup, lemon juice, cranberry, Goslings ginger beer, peach bitters
venues.longDescription:
The Velvet Hippo occupies the third floor and roof of a building on Orange Street in downtown Durham, and it is the strongest licensed non-alcoholic programme in the Triangle by a clear margin. What distinguishes it is not that zero-proof drinks exist on the menu but that they are given their own standing section, their own name, and the same treatment as everything else: "Tomorrow-Friendly", six builds deep, every one of them priced and spelled out ingredient by ingredient.

The list is genuinely varied rather than six versions of the same idea. Two are spritzes built on alcohol-removed sparkling wine — one on Lyre's Italian Spritz with an orange wheel, the other on Pallini's Limonzero limoncello and Freixenet. The Hot Tropic is the ambitious one: Ritual Tequila Alternative with guava, lime and fresh jalapeño, served with a cinnamon-sugar and smoked-chilli salt rim. Girl Dinner is a rich, fruit-forward build on prickly pear, passionfruit and coconut cream with no NA spirit in it at all, which matters for anyone who would rather avoid spirit analogues entirely. She Is The Moment runs Lyre's Pink London Spirit over muddled blackberries, and The Peach Blossom is the cheapest and simplest at nine dollars — lavender syrup, lemon, cranberry and Goslings ginger beer.

Behind that list sits an equally serious stock of finished alcohol-free product, which is the part most rooftop bars skip. Athletic Brewing's Run Wild IPA and Atlética Mexican-style copper are both on, alongside Freixenet's alcohol-removed sparkling, Giesen's de-alcoholised New Zealand sauvignon blanc, the Lyre's spirits range and Ritual's tequila alternative. So a non-drinker can order a cocktail, a beer, a glass of wine or a spritz and get something considered in every case.

One practical note: the bar's official site is velvethippodurham.com. A similarly named domain, thevelvethippo.com, serves a broken menu page and is not the venue's — a trap worth knowing if you are checking the list before you go. The rooftop opens at four most days and noon at weekends, with the kitchen running late Thursday through Saturday. One of the six, Girl Dinner, contains no non-alcoholic spirit at all — worth knowing for anyone who would rather avoid spirit analogues entirely.
venues.pressQuote: dedicated non-alcoholic menus that rival anything with a proof

venues.name: Velveteen Rabbit
venues.description: Velveteen Rabbit is an award-winning craft cocktail bar and one of the very first cocktail bars to open in Downtown Las Vegas's Arts District, known for its artsy interior, boutique spirits, vintage furniture, pink patio, and constantly evolving seasonal menus built on house-made botanicals and syrups. The bar maintains a dedicated 'Non-Alcoholic Cocktails' section on its drink menu, with house creations priced at $14 each that are as carefully composed as its full-proof drinks. The current conspiracy-themed menu carries four zero-proof builds: The Midnight Idol (verjus, fig & chamomile syrup, thyme, coconut milk, lime, aquafaba, tonic), Resurrection (NA gin, jasmine, blue spirulina, coconut, lemon, iris water, aquafaba, orange bitters), Lemur's Tale (NA tequila, guava, baobab-lychee syrup, vegan lime meringue), and the 27 Club (NA tequila, cilantro-infused NA sauvignon blanc, pear and lime oleo, orange bitters, mint and lemon oil); earlier builds Shadows in the Garden and The Empress have rotated off. Patrons can optionally add a spirit to a non-alcoholic build for an additional charge, and non-alcoholic beers from Athletic and Coors are also stocked. The bar is located at 1218 S Main St and is open daily from 5pm.

venues.longDescription:
Velveteen Rabbit was opened in 2013 by sisters Pamela and Christina Dylag, who took over what Forbes Travel Guide described as the forlorn wreckage of a burned-down furniture store on South Main Street and turned it into a dark, inviting Victorian-era parlour. They kept the fire's burn marks in the room and built around them with hand-stencilled walls, a shattered-mirror wall, mismatched vintage furnishings, velvet-covered couches, moody work by local artists, and a wide satiny wood bar fitted with purse hooks. Christina had worked as a hostess and server and kept an extensive home bar, but had never tended bar professionally before the two of them opened the place; the sisters drew their template from bars they had visited in Portland, Oregon and in Tokyo. It was one of the first cocktail bars in an Arts District that at the time still badly needed rehabilitation, and the sisters ran it as a community room from the start, collaborating with local artists on events and teaching bimonthly beginner cocktail classes built around the French 75, the whiskey sour and the Old Fashioned.

Each seasonal menu is built on fresh produce and house-made botanicals and syrups, poured alongside eight rotating beer taps and a boutique spirits list, with a magical pink outdoor patio off the back. The non-alcoholic cocktails are a standing, clearly labelled section of that menu at $14 apiece, composed with the same care as the full-proof drinks rather than being improvised on request. The current conspiracy-themed list carries four zero-proof builds: The Midnight Idol (verjus, fig and chamomile syrup, thyme, coconut milk, lime, aquafaba, tonic), Resurrection (NA gin, jasmine, blue spirulina, coconut, lemon, iris water, aquafaba, orange bitters), Lemur's Tale (NA tequila, guava, baobab-lychee syrup, vegan lime meringue), and the 27 Club (NA tequila, cilantro-infused NA sauvignon blanc, pear and lime oleo, orange bitters, lime, mint and lemon oil). Earlier builds Shadows in the Garden and The Empress have since rotated off. A spirit can be added to any zero-proof build for a surcharge, and non-alcoholic beer from Athletic and Coors is stocked.
venues.pressQuote: One of the very first cocktail bars in the Arts District, where locals visit to explore the bar's constantly evolving menu of creative drinks featuring house-made botanicals and syrups.

venues.name: Vena's Fizz House
venues.description: Vena's Fizz House has been the centre of gravity for alcohol-free drinking in greater Portland since 2013, when it opened on Fore Street as a bar where every drink was zero-proof. That original room closed and the business moved to the Dana Warp Mill in Westbrook, where it now trades as a craft mixer and mixology shop — shrubs, bitters, syrups, tools and the ingredients that make a good non-alcoholic drink possible at home. It came close to closing entirely in 2025 after twelve years before new owners stepped in to keep it going, with the founders helping. Note the hours are strictly weekday business hours, and Westbrook is a twenty-minute drive from downtown Portland.
venues.longDescription:
Vena's Fizz House opened on Fore Street in Portland's Old Port in 2013, and it did something almost nobody was doing then: it served a full bar menu in which every drink was zero-proof, built on house shrubs, bitters and natural ingredients rather than syrup from a gun. It was years ahead of the category, and for a long time it was the reason Portland had any alcohol-free reputation at all.

The Old Port room did not survive. It closed around 2021, the business shifted toward e-commerce and mixology supply, and the physical operation moved inland to the Dana Warp Mill in Westbrook — a converted textile mill about twenty minutes from downtown Portland. Then in 2025, after twelve years, the owners announced they were closing for good. New owners took it on instead, with the founders staying involved, and the Westbrook operation continues.

What it is today is a shop rather than a bar: craft mixers, shrubs, bitters, syrups, glassware and tools, sold to people building drinks at home. That is a narrower proposition than the original, but it is arguably the more useful one, because the hardest part of drinking well without alcohol is not finding a bar that will make you something — it is having anything decent in your own kitchen. A shop stocked by people who spent a decade making zero-proof drinks professionally is a rare resource.

Two practical notes. First, this is Westbrook, not Portland — it folds into the Portland metro for our purposes, but it is a drive. Second, the hours are strictly business hours, 9am to 5pm Monday to Friday and closed at weekends, which is unusual for a drinks business and catches people out. The company has also been reported working on a new Portland location in a converted West End church; worth watching, but not open at the time of listing. If it opens, Portland regains a genuine alcohol-free bar in the centre of the city for the first time since the Fore Street room closed — which would change this guide substantially.
venues.pressQuote: Born out of a love for seltzer, Vena's Fizz House in Downtown Portland, Maine is made to feel like a old-fashioned soda fountain spot

venues.name: Verde
venues.description: Verde is the restaurant and terrace inside the Pérez Art Museum Miami in Museum Park on Biscayne Boulevard, with a terrace looking straight across Biscayne Bay. Its alcohol-free list runs to three named builds rather than one — a Boba Passion Fruit, a Coconut Cooler and a Gingerberry Smash — all built around fresh fruit and spice rather than around substitutes for spirits. RESIDENT covered the restaurant in December 2025 and wrote that the drinks are part of the larger sensory experience and that the setting encourages guests to linger. The hours follow the museum rather than the restaurant trade: closed Tuesday and Wednesday, with a late Thursday service until 8pm.
venues.longDescription:
Verde is the in-house restaurant of the Pérez Art Museum Miami at 1103 Biscayne Boulevard, in Museum Park on the downtown waterfront. The dining room opens onto a covered terrace facing east across Biscayne Bay, which is what RESIDENT means when it writes that the setting encourages guests to linger. Because it operates inside a museum, the hours track the institution: 11am to 4pm on Monday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday, a late Thursday service until 8pm, and closed on Tuesday and Wednesday.

The alcohol-free list carries three named builds, which puts Verde ahead of most single-drink hotel bars in this batch. The Boba Passion Fruit brings tapioca pearls into a passionfruit base, the Coconut Cooler is the longest and most refreshing of the three, and the Gingerberry Smash pairs ginger heat with a berry blend. RESIDENT documented all three in its December 2025 Miami survey and wrote that at Verde the drinks are part of the larger sensory experience, that the options lean into freshness and balance, and that the setting encourages guests to linger. Full ingredient specifications are not published, so the drinks are recorded here by name only. One correction worth logging: the same article places Verde in Allapattah, which is wrong — the Pérez Art Museum is on Biscayne Boulevard in Museum Park, at the northern edge of downtown, roughly three miles east of Allapattah. The restaurant posts as @verdemiami. Two practical notes. The Thursday late service until 8pm is the only evening in the week the terrace is open after dark, and the restaurant is closed on Tuesday and Wednesday, so the window for a visit is narrower than the address suggests. The restaurant takes bookings on (786) 345-5697.
venues.pressQuote: Options like Boba Passion Fruit, Coconut Cooler, and Gingerberry Smash lean into freshness and balance, enjoyed against sweeping views of Biscayne Bay.

venues.name: Verdigris
venues.description: Verdigris is an upscale cocktail bar and lounge inside the Park Place development in Leawood, Kansas, opened in spring 2020 by owners David and Noelle Manica with the team behind Kansas City's Monarch Bar. The room is themed around verdigris — the green patina of weathered copper — and the menu organizes drinks as classic, light, rich, and imperial cocktails. The non-alcoholic offering is built into the cocktail list itself: several signature drinks are explicitly marked "available non-alcoholic," meaning the bar builds spirit-free versions of named house cocktails to order. Confirmed spirit-free options on the 2026 menu include the Green Maiden (cucumber, snap pea, green tea, ginger, lime), the Ibisco (hibiscus, pineapple, lime, orgeat), the Aqua Regia (orange, turmeric, aperitif, strawberry seltzer), and the Whiskey Bramble. The packaged non-alcoholic pour is the 0.0% Lagunitas Hoppy Refresher. Verdigris was voted Best Johnson County Bar in Kansas City Magazine's Best of 2026.

venues.longDescription:
Verdigris is a cocktail bar and lounge at 5245 W 116th Place in the Park Place development in Leawood, opened in 2020 by David and Noelle Manica under their Exit Strategy group — the team behind The Monarch Bar, The Mercury Room and Jade Jaguar. The move across the state line was deliberate: so many bars with good cocktails on the Kansas side are still restaurant-focused, the team said before opening, and Verdigris was built as a drinking room first. It bills itself as Johnson County's premier cocktail bar and lounge, and prints the definition of its own name on the menu — the bright bluish-green patina that forms on copper by atmospheric oxidation. Bennett Hofer directs operations with Abigail Lee as head bartender. Food is bar food done well: whipped goat cheese with honey and blackberry compote at $13, birria tacos at $15, a two-patty cheeseburger at $15, smoked popcorn at $5. Happy hour runs every day from 3pm to 6pm, and parking is free on the street or in the adjacent covered garage.

The non-alcoholic approach here is different from most bars and worth understanding before you arrive, because it is easy to misread. There is no separate mocktail list. Instead, five cocktails on the seasonal menu are printed with the note "available non-alcoholic" directly beneath their ingredients, meaning the bar will rebuild those drinks zero-proof to order: Green Maiden ($16) with cucumber, snap pea, green tea, ginger and lime; Ibisco ($16) with hibiscus, pineapple, lime and orgeat; Aqua Regia ($15) with orange, turmeric, aperitif and strawberry seltzer; Whiskey Bramble ($14) with blackberry and lemon; and El Diablo ($14) with crème de cassis, ginger beer and lime. The advantage is that you get a full seasonal cocktail rather than a short fixed list. The limitation is that the standing "Spirit Free" section on the printed spirits list holds only a Lagunitas Hoppy Refresher at $5 and a Mexican Coke or Sprite at $4 — so ask for one of the five by name rather than asking generally what is non-alcoholic.

venues.name: Vesper
venues.description: Vesper is a James Bond-themed cocktail and tapas bar that opened in September 2020 in Atlanta's Glenwood Park, just off the BeltLine, from owners Damien McGee and Jon Tilley. The dimly lit, mid-century-inspired lounge — hunter-green walls, jewel-toned velvet seating — leans into Ian Fleming lore, from the namesake Vesper martini to a full "00 Proof" zero-proof cocktail section that the bar builds with the same care as its spirited list. Nearly every mocktail is anchored by Ritual Zero Proof non-alcoholic spirits, with a few using Lyre's. Named alcohol-free options include the Not So Stormy, Bonito, a zero-proof Old Fashioned, Slo Gin Fizz, Paloma and a "Nigroni." The kitchen serves American and Spanish-leaning tapas meant for sharing, indoors or al fresco. Open daily from 5pm.
venues.address: 924 Garrett St SE, Suite D, Atlanta, GA 30316

venues.longDescription:
Vesper opened in September 2020 at 924 Garrett Street in Glenwood Park, just off the BeltLine, from owners Damien McGee and Jon Tilley. The concept is James Bond, pursued further than a theme bar usually bothers to: hunter-green walls, jewel-toned velvet, mid-century lines, and a name taken from the Vesper martini Ian Fleming invented in Casino Royale. Opening a cocktail bar in September 2020 was its own kind of gamble, and the room has outlasted the circumstances.

What earns it a place here is the zero-proof section, which the bar calls 00 Proof — the Bond usage, and a signal about how it is treated. This is not a courtesy list of juice. Nearly every drink on it is anchored by a Ritual Zero Proof non-alcoholic spirit, with a few built on Lyre's, meaning the drinks are constructed from a spirit base the same way the alcoholic list is. Named options include the Not So Stormy, the Bonito, a zero-proof Old Fashioned, the Slo Gin Fizz, a Paloma and a Nigroni.

The Old Fashioned and the Nigroni are the tell. Both are spirit-forward, bitter, stirred drinks with nowhere to hide — no citrus, no sugar, no bubbles to cover a weak base. A bar that puts those on a zero-proof menu is making a claim about its NA spirits and its own technique, and it is the kind of claim most bars quietly avoid by offering only shaken, fruit-driven drinks. Bitterness is the hardest quality to reproduce without alcohol and the one that makes a drink read as adult.

The kitchen serves American and Spanish-leaning tapas built for sharing, indoors or on the patio, and the bar opens daily at 5pm. For a non-drinker this is an ordinary cocktail bar that happens to have done the work — which, on a night out with friends who are drinking, is often exactly what is wanted.

venues.name: Via Vecchia
venues.description: Via Vecchia is a grand Italian restaurant in a restored Old Port building, and its bar programme extends properly to the alcohol-free side with the N/A-groni — a spirit-free Negroni riff built from gentian, cherry bark, grapefruit and juniper, served over a single large piece of clear ice with an orange peel. Every element of that build is doing the job the alcohol would: gentian and cherry bark supply the bitterness Campari normally brings, juniper stands in for the gin, and the clear ice and garnish mean the drink arrives looking exactly like the one everyone else ordered. Dinner service runs from 4pm daily in one of the Old Port's grandest rooms.
signatureDrinks: N/A-groni - gentian, cherry bark, grapefruit, juniper, large clear ice, orange peel

naMenuItems.name: French Bloom, "Le Rosé" Non-Alcoholic Sparkling Wine, France NV

venues.longDescription:
Via Vecchia occupies a restored building on Dana Street in the Old Port, and it is one of Portland's more theatrical dining rooms — high ceilings, marble, a long bar, Italian cooking served with some ceremony. Its cocktail programme is described as merging old-world sophistication with new-world flavours, and unusually the alcohol-free side got the same treatment.

The N/A-groni is the proof, and its specification rewards a close read. A Negroni is defined by bitterness, and the reason most non-alcoholic versions fail is that they replace Campari with something sweet and red. Via Vecchia instead builds the bitterness from gentian — the root that gives Campari and most amari their backbone — and cherry bark, which adds a woody, faintly medicinal depth. Grapefruit supplies the citrus edge, juniper stands in for gin's aromatic spine.

The presentation is the other half of the job. It is served over a single large piece of crystal-clear ice with an orange peel, which is exactly how the alcoholic version arrives. That matters more than it should: a great deal of what makes a drink satisfying is the object in your hand, and a non-drinker handed a highball of something pale while the table drinks from heavy rocks glasses is reminded of the difference every time they look down. Same glass, same ice, same garnish removes that.

Dinner service runs from 4pm daily, to 10pm most nights and 11pm on Friday and Saturday. It sits in the heart of the Old Port within a couple of minutes of Hunt & Alpine and Andy's, so a group can move between them easily — and unusually for this city, all three have something real for the person not drinking. For a visitor staying in the Old Port, that cluster is the single most useful thing to know about this city.
venues.pressQuote: One of the most unique and fun elements of Via Vecchia is its apéritivo program, the Italian version of a happy hour
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Portland Press Herald, Bar Guide, May 2021

venues.name: Vibehaus Kava Bar & Lounge
venues.description: Vibehaus is an alcohol-free kava lounge in downtown Hallandale Beach, open 9am to 2am every day, with an outdoor lounge area and free parking for guests. It is programmed as a night-out venue rather than a cafe — live music and events run through the week — and the drinks are billed as signature kava and K-drink cocktails rather than as wellness shots. Two things are worth knowing before you go. Hookah is served, so the room is not smoke-free. And IMPORTANT for readers in recovery: the K-side of that cocktail list is kratom, whose alkaloids act on opioid receptors and carry a genuine dependence and withdrawal risk. Kava, the South Pacific root the venue is named for, does not work that way. Both are poured here, so ask which is in your glass.
venues.address: 118 NE 1st Ave Ste g, Hallandale Beach, FL 33009
venues.longDescription:
Vibehaus sits on NE 1st Avenue in downtown Hallandale Beach, at the southern edge of Broward County where it meets the Miami-Dade line, and it is programmed as a night-out venue rather than as a daytime cafe. It opens at 9am and runs to 2am every day of the week, with an outdoor lounge area, free parking for guests, and live music and events through the week. It serves no alcohol at any point.

The drinks are presented as signature kava and K-drink cocktails — built, mixed and named, rather than poured as plain shells — which is a sensible read of an audience that is largely coming for a night out rather than for a botanical ritual. Kava is the ground root of Piper methysticum, a shrub native to the South Pacific islands, prepared as a cold water infusion and drunk socially across Fiji, Vanuatu, Tonga and Samoa for roughly three thousand years. It contains no alcohol. It tastes earthy and bitter and numbs the lips and tongue on the first mouthful, and its effect is mildly sedative and sociable rather than intoxicating in the way alcohol is.

Hallandale Beach is a useful location for this directory to cover. It sits between the Hollywood cluster to the north and the North Miami rooms to the south, on a stretch of the coast that is dense with condominium towers, casinos and conventional bars, and it has had no dedicated alcohol-free social venue of its own. Vibehaus fills that gap, and its late hours mean it functions as a genuine alternative on a night out rather than as somewhere to go instead of going out.

Two things should be known before visiting, and neither is a reason to avoid the room so much as a reason to arrive informed.

First, hookah is served here, and it is a significant part of the offer rather than an afterthought. The room is not smoke-free. For anyone avoiding tobacco and smoke — including a lot of people managing recovery alongside a respiratory condition — that matters as much as the alcohol question.

Second, the K-side of that cocktail list is kratom. The abbreviation is standard across South Florida and is genuinely hard to decode from a menu board. Kratom is the leaf of Mitragyna speciosa, a Southeast Asian tree; its principal alkaloids act on the opioid receptors, regular use produces tolerance and a real withdrawal syndrome, several US states ban it outright, and concentrated 7-hydroxymitragynine derivatives face active federal scheduling. Kava has no comparable dependence profile. Both are poured here from the same bar, so order by name and ask what is in the glass.

venues.name: Vice City Kava
venues.description: Vice City Kava is a fully alcohol-free kava and kratom bar in Miami's Coral Way neighborhood, wrapped in an unapologetic 1980s "Miami Vice" aesthetic of neon, vaporwave lighting, and retro nostalgia. Its stated mission is to offer relaxation, energy, and euphoria through kava and kratom "minus the booze, pressure, and weird vibes." The bar pours traditional strained kava sourced primarily from Fiji, kratom teas, herbal infusions, and nitro cold brew, alongside light food like Belgian waffles and ramen. Beyond drinks, it leans hard into community: weekly trivia, open mics, live music, "Around the Tanoa" gatherings, and a free "Sound Library" of instruments and recording gear. The venue is listed by BestKavaBar as the #1 kava bar in South Florida. It operates daily, 9am–3am, and runs a second location ("The Warehouse") elsewhere in Miami.
venues.longDescription:
Vice City Kava sits on Coral Way and commits entirely to a 1980s Miami Vice aesthetic — neon, vaporwave lighting, deliberate retro nostalgia. Its stated mission is unusually plain-spoken: relaxation, energy and euphoria through kava and kratom, minus the booze, pressure and weird vibes. That last phrase does real work. Much of what makes drinking culture hard to leave is not the alcohol itself but the pressure and the awkwardness of declining, and naming it directly is more useful than most wellness marketing manages.

The pours are traditional strained kava sourced primarily from Fiji, kratom teas, herbal infusions and nitro cold brew, with Belgian waffles and ramen from the kitchen. It runs 9am to 3am daily — an eighteen-hour day covering the morning, the working afternoon and the small hours, which very little else in Miami manages without alcohol as the organising principle.

The community programming is where it goes furthest: weekly trivia, open mics, live music, Around the Tanoa gatherings named for the communal kava bowl, and a free Sound Library of instruments and recording gear. Lending instruments to customers is not a normal bar amenity — it is a statement that the room is for doing something rather than for consuming. BestKavaBar lists it as the number one kava bar in South Florida, and a second site, The Warehouse, operates elsewhere in the city.

The caveat that belongs on every kava listing applies here and should not be softened: kava is psychoactive and sedating, with documented case reports of liver injury, and kratom acts on opioid receptors and carries real dependence and withdrawal risk. Everything served is free of alcohol. That is a narrower claim than nothing served having an effect, and for anyone whose reason for avoiding alcohol is recovery from a substance-use disorder, the difference is the whole question.

venues.name: Vicia
venues.description: Vicia, the vegetable-forward flagship of Tara and Michael Gallina's Take Root Hospitality, has been collecting national accolades since it opened in the Cortex Innovation District in 2017 — most recently a 2026 James Beard Award finalist nod for Outstanding Restaurant. The seasonal, farm-driven cooking that made Michael a Food & Wine Best New Chef in 2018 extends to the glass: Vicia offers a year-round non-alcoholic selection spanning mocktails, wines, and beers. The signature Garden Toddy stirs n/a bourbon with opal basil, green shiso, spearmint, marigold, honey, and lemon — a zero-proof drink as garden-obsessed as the food. Dinner runs Tuesday through Saturday in a light-filled space at Duncan and Boyle.
venues.address: 4260 Forest Park Ave., St. Louis, MO 63108
venues.longDescription:
Vicia opened in 2017 in the Cortex Innovation District, the flagship of husband-and-wife team Michael and Tara Gallina, who met while working at Dan Barber's famed farm-to-table destination Blue Hill at Stone Barns in New York. Their St. Louis restaurant — its entrance at the corner of Duncan and Boyle, on the edge of the Central West End — puts vegetables at the center of the plate, building menus around seasonal ingredients from local farms. Vicia became the cornerstone of the couple's Take Root Hospitality group, and nearly a decade in it remains one of the city's defining dining rooms, offering both à la carte dining and a 'Let Us Cook for You' tasting experience Tuesday through Saturday evenings.

The beverage program treats non-drinkers as first-class guests. In its January 2025 guide to zero-proof drinking in St. Louis, St. Louis Magazine reported that Vicia 'leans into the spirit-free trend,' expanding its selection of non-alcoholic beverages to be offered year-round, with options that include mocktails, non-alcoholic wines, and beers. The signature Garden Toddy shows how much intention goes into the category: n/a bourbon layered with opal basil, green shiso, spearmint, marigold, honey, and lemon — the same garden-driven sensibility that defines the kitchen, translated into a zero-proof glass. For a fine-dining restaurant of this caliber, a standing year-round commitment to spirit-free options is still rare, and it makes Vicia one of the most comfortable reservations in St. Louis for anyone skipping alcohol.

Few St. Louis restaurants can match Vicia's résumé. Michael Gallina was named a Food & Wine Best New Chef in 2018 and was a James Beard Award finalist for Best Chef: Midwest in both 2019 and 2020; in 2026, the restaurant itself was named a James Beard Award finalist for Outstanding Restaurant, one of the highest honors in American dining. As St. Louis Public Radio put it that spring, 'Vicia, the farm-to-table spot in the Cortex District of the Central West End, has received numerous accolades since it opened nine years ago this month.' Expect warm, polished service, a menu driven by what local farms are harvesting, and dinner Tuesday through Saturday from 5 to 9 p.m., with reservations through OpenTable.
venues.pressQuote: Vicia also leans into the spirit-free trend, expanding its selection of non-alcoholic beverages to be offered year-round.

venues.name: Victoria Bar
venues.description: Victoria Bar is a mostly-vegan restaurant and cocktail bar in North Portland's Humboldt neighborhood and an early local champion of the spirit-free movement — roughly a third of its cocktail menu is dedicated to non-alcoholic drinks, built on NA spirits like Wilderton, plus Athletic non-alcoholic beer.
venues.longDescription:
Victoria Bar is a (mostly) vegan neighborhood restaurant and cocktail bar that opened in 2015 at 4835 N Albina Ave in Portland's Humboldt neighborhood. It was founded by bartender Lisa Victoria Hare in partnership with the Lightning Bar Collective (behind Bye and Bye, Jackknife and Sweet Hereafter), and is named for her middle name. The cocktail list is themed after the film The Princess Bride, with drinks such as Florin and Inigo Montoya, and the kitchen serves a largely vegan, gluten-free-friendly menu alongside two covered, dog-friendly patios.

Victoria was an early adopter of a dedicated non-alcoholic section and has been recognized by Portland Monthly as "an early pioneer of the spirit-free movement." Its zero-proof menu is built with the same care as the full bar and leans on Oregon and craft NA brands: the Beautiful Stranger pairs Wilderton Lustre with lemon, cucumber and ginger beer, while Crazy For You is a Moscow Mule riff with For Bitter For Worse aperitif. Other spirit-free options include Into the Groove, a Virgin Piña Colada, and Live To Tell, and the NA list is rounded out by Athletic non-alcoholic beer, kombucha and cold brew. Portland Monthly reports the NA program accounts for roughly 10 to 20 percent of the mixed drinks sold on a given night.
venues.pressQuote: An early pioneer of the spirit-free movement, neighborhood cocktail bar Victoria was one of the first spots in town to sport a dedicated NA section on its menu.

venues.name: Vintage Books
venues.description: Vintage Books is a speakeasy and restaurant hidden behind a vintage-bookstore facade on Waialae Avenue in Kaimukī — not Chinatown, as several guides have it. The styling is Prohibition-era with a tropical bend, and the spirit-free drinks are built to the same specification as the rest of the list rather than improvised. The Nogroni is the clearest evidence: Seedlip Garden, Giffard sirop aperitif and Lyre's aperitif rosso, finished with orange oil — three genuine zero-proof products layered to hold the bitterness a negroni drinker actually wants. The Kaimuki Cruise runs lychee, lemon, mango and Sicilian lemonade, and a botanical London Tonic sits alongside them.

venues.longDescription:
Vintage Books trades from Suite 101 at 3660 Waialae Avenue, on the Kaimukī strip, behind a facade got up as a secondhand bookshop — the bar and restaurant are through the back. The conceit is Prohibition-era, softened with tropical flourishes appropriate to where it actually is, and it functions as a full restaurant as well as a bar, with brunch service at weekends from 10am to 2pm and dinner from 4pm. A note on location, because it matters for anyone navigating: several published guides place Vintage Books in Chinatown. It is in Kaimukī, several miles east, and the confusion probably comes from its own Kaimuki Cruise appearing on lists of downtown drinks.

The spirit-free list is the most technically serious in Honolulu, and the Nogroni is the reason. Most zero-proof menus collapse into sweetness, because sugar and acid are what remain once the spirit is gone and genuine bitterness is hard to build. This one goes the other way, layering three separate commercial zero-proof products — Seedlip Garden for the herbaceous top, Giffard's sirop aperitif and Lyre's aperitif rosso for the bitter-sweet Campari-and-vermouth register — and finishing with expressed orange oil, which is the aromatic step that makes a negroni read as a negroni before it is tasted. Stocking three zero-proof lines at once is a real inventory decision, not a gesture. The Kaimuki Cruise sits at the other end of the range, built on lychee, lemon, mango and Sicilian lemonade for something bright and tropical, and a botanical London Tonic covers the guest who wants length and bitterness without sweetness. Together they cover the three things a spirit-free drinker normally cannot get in one room. Kaimukī also puts the bar within a short walk of Leahi Health, which makes the neighbourhood the most complete alcohol-free stretch in the city outside the kava rooms.
venues.pressQuote: Spirit-free options are also available.

venues.name: Vintage Kava
venues.description: Vintage Kava is an alcohol-free kava bar on Reems Creek Road in Weaverville, ten miles north of Asheville, and it is larger and more room-like than most in the category — a Main Bar Room, a space called The View, and the Elysium Lounge, with live music and local art throughout. It opens at 9am and runs to midnight, or 1am on Friday and Saturday. Kava flights are offered for anyone wanting to taste across preparations. Its standing locally rests on more than drinks: it hosts the annual Kava Campout, has been recognised by the Town of Weaverville, and served as a gathering space for the community during Hurricane Helene.
venues.longDescription:
Vintage Kava sits at 141 Reems Creek Road in Weaverville, about ten miles north of downtown Asheville, and it is one of the more substantial kava venues in the Carolinas — not a counter with seating but a multi-room bar. The layout runs to a Main Bar Room, a space the venue calls The View, and a separate Elysium Lounge, with live music programmed regularly and local artists' work on the walls. It opens at 9am every day and closes at midnight, extending to 1am on Friday and Saturday. No alcohol is served at any point.

What sets it apart from the Asheville kava rooms already listed here — Sovereign Kava and Elevated Kava Lounge, both downtown — is its position in a small town rather than a tourist district, and the depth of its relationship with that town. It runs an annual Kava Campout. It has received recognition from the Town of Weaverville. And during Hurricane Helene, which devastated western North Carolina in September 2024 and cut power and water across the region for weeks, it functioned as a gathering space for the community. That is a stronger claim on a place than a good drinks list, and it is the reason the venue's own material talks about community involvement before it talks about kava.

The drinks themselves are kava-led, and the venue offers kava flights for anyone wanting to taste across preparations rather than commit to a single shell — a sensible option for newcomers, and the same approach the better kava bars elsewhere have converged on. Kava is the ground root of Piper methysticum, a shrub native to the South Pacific, infused in cold water and drunk socially across Fiji, Vanuatu, Tonga and Samoa for roughly three thousand years. It contains no alcohol. The taste is earthy and bitter and it numbs the lips and tongue on the first mouthful; the effect is mildly sedative and sociable rather than intoxicating in alcohol's sense. Kava also displays reverse tolerance, meaning regular drinkers generally need less rather than more to feel it, so a first visit rewards a slow pace across an hour or two.

For anyone staying in Asheville, Weaverville is a straightforward drive up US-19/23 and worth it for a room that stays open to midnight without a bar tab. For anyone living in the northern Buncombe County towns, it is simply the local — and one of very few places in the area open that late on any given night.

venues.name: Violet's
venues.description: Violet's is a neighbourhood bar and restaurant at Clement and 24th Avenue in the Outer Richmond, running dinner nightly and weekend brunch under new ownership. Its zero-proof drinks are grouped under their own menu heading, The Pure Pour, and priced at $14 against $14 to $15 for the alcoholic cocktails. Five are listed: House Finch, built on Giffard aperitif and Mionetto's non-alcoholic aperitivo with passion fruit, vanilla, lime and tonic; Paradiso Beach, with Giffard orgeat and coconut, grapefruit, lemon and cinnamon; a Venetian Spritz of Mionetto aperitivo, Giffard aperitif and club soda; a Phony Negroni; and a Falso Amaro. Athletic Brewing's IPA is stocked at $8. The kitchen runs cioppino, fried chicken and other Richmond comfort cooking.

venues.longDescription:
Violet's sits on the corner of Clement Street and 24th Avenue in the Outer Richmond, a stretch of the city where the drinking options run mostly to long-standing Irish bars and where a full cocktail programme is unusual. The restaurant changed hands and reopened under new management, keeping the room's bar-forward layout and adding a kitchen that leans on San Francisco standards — cioppino, fried chicken, weekend brunch — rather than on anything more fashionable. It is a short walk from Ocean Beach Cafe, which makes the western end of Clement one of the few parts of the city where two venues with serious alcohol-free lists sit within a few blocks of each other.

The non-alcoholic drinks are set out under their own heading, The Pure Pour, and cost $14, which is level with the $14 to $15 charged for the full-proof cocktails — a detail that says more about how seriously a bar takes the category than any amount of menu copy. House Finch is built on Giffard's aperitif syrup and Mionetto's non-alcoholic aperitivo with passion fruit, vanilla, lime and tonic. Paradiso Beach is the tropical entry, using Giffard orgeat and Giffard coconut with grapefruit, lemon and cinnamon. The Venetian Spritz combines Mionetto's aperitivo with Giffard aperitif and club soda for a lower-sugar aperitivo-hour drink. A Phony Negroni and a Falso Amaro round the section out for anyone who wants bitterness rather than fruit. Below the cocktails, the beer list carries Athletic Brewing's IPA at $8 next to Original Pattern and taco truck lagers. The restaurant serves dinner from 5pm every night, with brunch service from 10am on Saturday and Sunday. Two of the five drinks — the Phony Negroni and the Falso Amaro — are aimed squarely at the bitter end of the spectrum, which matters in a category that usually defaults to fruit and sugar, and the presence of a named house build on Giffard orgeat and coconut shows the bar is treating its non-alcoholic syrups as cocktail ingredients rather than as sweeteners. For the western half of the city it is the deepest zero-proof cocktail list outside Ocean Beach Cafe.

venues.name: Virago Spirits
venues.description: Virago Spirits is a Richmond distillery whose tasting room pours non-alcoholic versions of several of its own cocktails, built around flavours including smoked raspberry, vanilla, orange and pecan. A distillery is the last place most non-drinkers would expect to be catered for, which is exactly why it is worth knowing: the same people who develop the spirits build the zero-proof serves, using the syrups, infusions and technique the bar already has. It trades Wednesday to Sunday afternoons and evenings, closing at 9:30pm, and it makes the distillery tour circuit that runs through Scott's Addition workable for a mixed group — turning what is usually the worst afternoon of the year for a non-drinker into an ordinary one. Ask what they are pouring zero-proof when you arrive, as the serves follow the house list rather than a fixed menu.
signatureDrinks: Non-alcoholic versions of the house cocktails — flavours including smoked raspberry, vanilla, orange and pecan
venues.longDescription:
Virago Spirits is a Richmond distillery producing rum, gin and liqueurs, with a tasting room attached in the Scott's Addition area. On the face of it, a distillery tasting room is the least promising venue in a city for someone who is not drinking — the entire purpose of the room is to sample distilled alcohol.

Which is what makes its non-alcoholic offering interesting. Virago pours zero-proof versions of several of its own cocktails, drawing on flavours including smoked raspberry, vanilla, orange and pecan. These are not bought-in mocktails; they are built by the people who develop the spirits, using the same syrups, infusions and technique the bar already keeps behind the counter. When a distillery does this it tends to do it well, because flavour construction is the whole business — the only thing being removed is the ethanol, and everything else that makes a drink interesting is already in the building.

The practical value is social. Scott's Addition has become a distillery, brewery and cidery trail, and it is a genuinely enjoyable afternoon — unless you are the person in the group who cannot participate, in which case it is several hours of watching other people taste things. A tasting room that pours you a considered smoked-raspberry serve while everyone else works through the rum flight changes that from an endurance exercise into a normal outing.

Hours are limited and worth checking: closed Monday and Tuesday, 4pm to 9:30pm Wednesday to Friday, from 2pm on Saturday, and 2pm to 6:30pm on Sunday. The grade is an honest 3 — the drinks are real and made in-house, but this is a distillery tasting room rather than a venue with a standing zero-proof menu, so ask what they are pouring when you arrive. The staff develop the spirits themselves, so the answer is usually more interesting than the question deserves.

venues.name: Virtue
venues.description: Virtue Restaurant & Bar is chef Erick Williams's acclaimed Southern restaurant in Chicago's historic Hyde Park neighborhood, opened in November 2018 as his first solo concept. Williams was named James Beard Foundation Best Chef: Great Lakes in 2022, becoming the first Black chef to win in that category, and Virtue is listed in the MICHELIN Guide. The kitchen centers thoughtful, hospitality-driven Southern cooking, and the bar carries a dedicated "zero-proof" section for non-drinkers. Current spirit-free offerings are house-made rather than bottled brands: the Sorrel Fizz (hibiscus, rosemary, vanilla, sparkling water), The Hummingbird (basil, lemon, soda), and the Coconut Woman (coconut cream, pineapple, lime). It's a smaller but real NA list at a full-service Southern restaurant, well suited to those who want a considered alcohol-free option alongside a notable dinner.

venues.longDescription:
Virtue Restaurant & Bar opened in 2018 at 1462 E 53rd Street in Hyde Park, chef Erick Williams's first solo restaurant after years running kitchens for other people, and it became one of the most decorated rooms in the city almost immediately. In 2022 Williams made history as the first Black chef to win Best Chef: Great Lakes from the James Beard Foundation, and the restaurant has held a Michelin Bib Gourmand. The cooking is Southern in the full sense — regional, specific, unhurried — running biscuits with pimento cheese and local honey at $12, fish and grits built on blackened red drum with Geechie stone-ground grits and crab étouffée at $35, short rib with creamed spinach and caramelised onion gravy at $42, and a bone-marrow-buttered New York strip at $69. Damarr Brown leads the kitchen as chef de cuisine and Becky Pendola runs pastry. The dining room seats up to seventy for private events and is ADA accessible, and service runs Tuesday to Sunday from 4pm, closed Mondays.

The bar keeps a section headed simply "zero-proof", and what makes it worth a non-drinker's attention is that the three drinks are drawn from the same cultural well as the food rather than being generic mocktails bolted on. The Sorrel Fizz ($9) is the clearest example: sorrel is the hibiscus drink of the Caribbean and the Black Atlantic, traditionally spiced and served at Christmas, and here it is built with hibiscus, rosemary and vanilla over sparkling water. The Hummingbird ($9) is the lightest of the three, just basil, lemon and soda, and functions as the drink to order across a long meal without palate fatigue. Coconut Woman ($12) combines coconut cream, pineapple and lime into something richer and more dessert-adjacent, and shares its name with the Harry Belafonte calypso. At $9 for two of the three, they are priced well below the cocktails rather than at parity — unusual in a restaurant at this level, and it makes ordering a second one an easy decision.

venues.name: Volare Italian Ristorante
venues.description: Volare is a long-running Italian restaurant on Frankfort Avenue in Clifton, named Best Italian Restaurant by readers of Louisville Magazine three years running, with a seasonal menu built on locally sourced produce and house-made pasta. Its place in a non-alcoholic guide rests on one thing done properly: the bar builds Spiritless Manhattans, using the Louisville-made non-alcoholic bourbon Kentucky 74 in place of rye or bourbon. A manhattan is a spirit-forward, stirred, undiluted drink — the hardest category to render without alcohol and the one most bars refuse to attempt — so a restaurant offering it as standard is making a real claim. Dinner runs seven nights from 4:30pm.
signatureDrinks: Spiritless Manhattan (Spiritless Kentucky 74 non-alcoholic bourbon, vermouth-style aperitif, bitters)

venues.longDescription:
Frankfort Avenue through Clifton is one of Louisville's genuine restaurant streets — a long run of independent rooms rather than a nightlife strip — and Volare has been near the top of it for years. Readers of Louisville Magazine named it Best Italian Restaurant three consecutive years; the name means to fly, the menu changes seasonally around locally sourced produce and house-made pasta, and the service culture is the old-fashioned kind where the same server looks after you all evening.

Most Italian restaurants with a bar will make a non-drinker a sweet fizzy thing. Volare builds Spiritless Manhattans, and the distinction is worth spelling out. A manhattan is spirit, aromatised wine and bitters, stirred and served up — no citrus, no soda, nothing to hide behind. It is the single hardest classic to render without alcohol, because the whole drink is the spirit's weight and the bitters' edge. Doing it means owning a non-alcoholic bourbon good enough to carry the glass, and Volare uses Kentucky 74, made across town by Spiritless using reverse distillation to strip alcohol from a finished distillate while keeping its caramel and oak. That a neighbourhood Italian restaurant in Louisville offers a stirred, spirit-forward, alcohol-free drink as a matter of course says something about how far the category has travelled in this city.

For planning: dinner service only, from 4:30pm seven nights, running to 10pm Sunday through Thursday and 11pm on Friday and Saturday. Reservations are advisable at weekends. Clifton puts three other entries in this guide on the same avenue — Fork & Barrel at 1722, Pizza Lupo at 1540 — so an evening on Frankfort Avenue is one of the easier ones in Louisville to plan around not drinking.
venues.pressQuote: Volare serves Spiritless Manhattans.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: The Zero Proof, Louisville city guide

venues.name: Vue de monde
venues.description: Melbourne's most celebrated fine diner, perched on Level 55 of the Rialto, offers a dedicated non-alcoholic pairing (A$120 per person) built to match its multi-course Chef's Tasting Menu. Developed by the Vue de monde sommelier team with the crew from the neighbouring Lui Bar, the pairing runs on sans-alcohol cocktails, prestige teas and custom-made beverages rather than off-the-shelf zero-proof bottles. A separate tea pairing (A$150 per person) journeys through rare and exclusive teas served as carbonated, blended, cold and warm infusions. Vue de monde prints two alcohol-free flights against its wine pairings: a $120 non-alcoholic pairing built with the Lui Bar team, and a $150 tea pairing sourced the way a sommelier sources wine.

venues.longDescription:
Vue de monde is one of Australia's benchmark fine-dining restaurants, occupying Level 55 of the Rialto Towers at 525 Collins Street in the Melbourne CBD, with floor-to-ceiling views stretching from the Docklands to the Dandenongs. Founded by chef Shannon Bennett, the restaurant serves a modern, native-ingredient-driven degustation and remains a fixture on Melbourne's best-restaurant lists into 2026.

The non-alcoholic offering here is a genuine, considered course-by-course pairing rather than an afterthought. Priced at A$120 per person, it is designed to sit alongside the Chef's Tasting Menu and was created as a collaboration between Vue de monde's sommeliers and the bartenders at the venue's adjoining Lui Bar. The line-up is built from sans-alcohol cocktails, prestige teas and beverages made in-house specifically for the pairing, so it changes with the menu rather than pouring commercial NA products.

Guests who want to go deeper on tea can instead choose the dedicated tea pairing at A$150 per person, which moves through rare and exclusive teas sourced from around the world and served in carbonated, blended, cold and warm forms. Both routes give a fully alcohol-free diner a drinks experience matched to the food at the same level of intent as the wine list.

The room is a special-occasion destination: reservations open roughly three months ahead and sell out quickly, and service runs across dinner Wednesday to Saturday with lunch added on Fridays and Saturdays. For non-drinkers, it is one of the few Melbourne kitchens at this altitude, literally and figuratively, that treats the zero-proof pairing as a first-class part of the menu.

Two separate alcohol-free flights is rare at this level, and both are priced on the same page as the wine. The non-alcoholic pairing, at $120 per person, is described by the restaurant as a collaboration between the Lui Bar team and its own sommeliers, showcasing sans-alcohol cocktails, prestige teas and custom-made beverages designed to elevate the chef's tasting menu. The tea pairing is charged separately at $150 per person.

The tea programme is the more unusual of the two. Vue de monde says its approach to tea emulates a sommelier's approach to wine, running a dedicated acquisition model to source unique leaves and blends from specialist tea houses with a focus on rare and exclusive teas, and the pairing is built to explore tensions between carbonated, blended, cold and warm infusions across the arc of the menu. That is a description of cellar work, not of a hot drink at the end of dinner. Against wine pairings that run from $220 to beyond $500, the alcohol-free options are also the least expensive way through the room — worth knowing, because at this price level non-drinkers are usually charged as though they were drinking.

venues.name: W.A. Frost and Company
venues.description: W.A. Frost & Company is a Cathedral Hill institution that opened in December 1975 inside the historic 1889 Dacotah Building, originally home to William A. Frost's pharmacy. Long known for its tree-canopied patio, award-winning wine list, and contemporary American cuisine, the St. Paul mainstay also runs a genuine zero-proof program. Its Cocktail Hour menu carries a dedicated "No Proof Cocktails" section priced at $8, currently listing the Blueberry Buzz Tonic, the Wilfred Spritz, and the Strawberry Gimlet. The bar additionally pours non-alcoholic and low-proof options such as the Evening At Frost, built on Gnista Wormwood and house-made spiced orange syrup. Set among the grand Victorian mansions of Cathedral Hill, the restaurant pairs its no-proof list with the same atmospheric, white-tablecloth setting that has made it a special-occasion destination for decades. The NA list is real but compact — a handful of named drinks rather than a full menu.
venues.hours: Mon closed; Tue-Thu 12pm-10pm; Fri 11am-12am; Sat 10am-12am; Sun 10am-9pm
venues.longDescription:
W.A. Frost & Company opened in December 1975 inside the 1889 Dacotah Building on Cathedral Hill, the space that originally housed William A. Frost's pharmacy. Half a century later it remains one of St. Paul's defining special-occasion restaurants — known for a tree-canopied patio that is among the most beautiful outdoor dining rooms in the state, an award-winning wine list, contemporary American cooking, and a white-tablecloth setting among the grand Victorian mansions of the neighbourhood.

A restaurant with that profile and that wine list has no particular commercial need to bother with zero-proof drinks, which is precisely why the fact that it does is worth recording. The Cocktail Hour menu carries a dedicated No Proof Cocktails section priced at $8 — notably below what the room could charge — currently listing the Blueberry Buzz Tonic, the Wilfred Spritz and the Strawberry Gimlet. Beyond those the bar pours non-alcoholic and low-proof builds including the Evening At Frost, made with Gnista Wormwood and a house-made spiced orange syrup. Gnista is a Swedish producer whose Floral Wormwood is one of the few non-alcoholic products with genuine bitterness and length, and pairing it with a house syrup is the work of a bar that has thought about the problem rather than bought a solution.

It is honest to describe the scale accurately: this is a real named list but a compact one, three or four drinks rather than a full parallel menu. What it buys a non-drinker is the ability to sit on that patio, at a table marking an anniversary or a birthday, with something in a proper glass that costs what it should. At a restaurant of this vintage and formality, that is worth more than a longer list somewhere less special. Open Tuesday through Sunday, with weekend brunch.
venues.pressQuote: WA Frost serves refined bistro fare in a soaring cathedral space

venues.name: WAKUDA
venues.description: WAKUDA is the two-Michelin-starred chef Tetsuya Wakuda's traditional-meets-modern Japanese restaurant inside the Palazzo lobby at The Venetian Resort, created with 50 Eggs Hospitality. Known for omakase, sushi and a late-night menu, it also runs a genuine zero-proof beverage program: its bar uses Lyre's non-alcoholic spirits to build an array of tropical and Japanese-inspired mocktails. Named non-alcoholic drinks include the Matcha Colada (Lyre's spiced sugar cane, ceremonial matcha, pineapple, lime, coconut), the Hosaka Fever (Lyre's spiced sugar cane, pineapple, green tea, lime), Geisha's Garden (lychee, butterfly pea tea agave, lime, Fever-Tree club soda) and Cure. The restaurant also houses the Golden Gai Cocktail Club, a Shinjuku-inspired lounge serving handcrafted drinks and Michelin-quality bites. It was named 2025 Gold Winner for "Best Sushi" by the Las Vegas Review-Journal.

venues.longDescription:
WAKUDA opened on 25 June 2022 in the Palazzo lobby of The Venetian Resort, the first American restaurant from Tetsuya Wakuda, the two-Michelin-starred chef behind Waku Ghin in Singapore. It was built with 50 Eggs Hospitality, and the concept traces back to a 2016 trip its founder John Kunkel took to Tokyo and a late night in Shinjuku Golden Gai, the warren of tiny bars that gives the restaurant's own cocktail lounge its name. The finished room seats 264 and is really several rooms: a main dining space, a private dining room, a bar and lounge, a private sushi room, a secret bar, and an outdoor terrace. The kitchen runs omakase, sushi and a late-night menu built on seafood flown in from around the world, and Las Vegas Review-Journal readers named it the 2025 Gold winner for Best Sushi.

The reason it belongs in a non-alcoholic directory is that the bar treats zero-proof as a category to build in rather than a request to accommodate. Its non-alcoholic drinks are constructed on Lyre's non-alcoholic spirits and pull from the same tropical and Japanese vocabulary as the rest of the list. The Matcha Colada is built from Lyre's spiced sugar cane, ceremonial matcha, pineapple, lime and coconut; the Hosaka Fever from Lyre's spiced sugar cane, pineapple, green tea and lime; Geisha's Garden from lychee, butterfly pea tea agave, lime and Fever-Tree club soda; and a fourth, Cure, rounds out the section. The Las Vegas Convention and Visitors Authority's own guide to must-try mocktails in the city singles out the Hosaka Fever specifically. Attached to the restaurant is the Golden Gai Cocktail Club, the Shinjuku-inspired lounge serving handcrafted drinks and Michelin-quality bites, which means a guest who is not drinking can spend an evening here in the bar rather than only at a dinner table. Service runs daily from 5pm to 10pm.
venues.pressQuote: The bar uses Lyre's nonalcoholic spirits to create an array of tropical and Japanese-inspired drinks. Try a Hosaka Fever with Lyre's Spiced Sugar Cane, pineapple, green tea and lime.

venues.name: Wakuda
venues.description: Wakuda is a modern Japanese restaurant and sake bar in the Tower 2 lobby of Marina Bay Sands from two-Michelin-starred chef Tetsuya Wakuda, and one of the resort venues carrying the alcohol-free 'Zero Edit' list. The zero-proof builds lean on Seedlip: Berrylicious reworks the clover club with Seedlip Grove, cranberry, strawberry, raspberry and rosemary, while Lady Marmalade layers Seedlip Garden with osmanthus and orange. The drinks are served at the bar (open daily until midnight) alongside bar bites, giving non-drinkers a genuine named menu rather than an afterthought.

venues.longDescription:
Wakuda opened in the lobby of Marina Bay Sands' Hotel Tower 2 as the more contemporary counterpart to chef Tetsuya Wakuda's flagship Waku Ghin. The Australia-based, two-Michelin-starred chef describes the room as 'a bold, artful collision of time and culture,' pairing traditional Japanese technique with French method and a design-forward interior. Wakuda is listed in the Michelin Guide Singapore, and its bar runs daily from 11:30am to midnight with bar bites from mid-afternoon.

The non-alcoholic offering comes via Zero Edit, Marina Bay Sands' resort-wide alcohol-free program that places sophisticated zero-proof drinks across its signature bars and restaurants rather than relegating non-drinkers to soft drinks. At Wakuda the Zero Edit list is built around Seedlip's distilled non-alcoholic spirits: Berrylicious is a fruit-forward riff on the classic clover club, combining Seedlip Grove with tart cranberry, sweet strawberry and raspberry and a grassy note of rosemary, while the citrus-forward Lady Marmalade marries Seedlip Garden with osmanthus and orange.

Because the drinks sit on the same bar menu as the alcoholic cocktails and are matched with the same bar bites and setting, the zero-proof options function as a real, named part of the experience for guests who aren't drinking - a hotel-bar NA program anchored by a marquee chef and a recognisable global NA brand.
venues.pressQuote: The alcohol-free Zero Edit beverages at Marina Bay Sands compromise nothing - and are for everyone

venues.name: Wallace Dry Goods
venues.description: Wallace Dry Goods is Ardmore's first fully non-alcoholic bottle shop, opened in early 2024 by owner Robin Cummiskey on the Main Line at 1 West Lancaster Avenue. Styled like a traditional bottle shop — shelves of "whiskey," wine, gin, and mixers — it stocks zero liquor; everything is alcohol-free. The shop sells NA spirits, beer, wine, cider, mixers, bitters, syrups, and ready-to-drink cans, plus barware, so non-drinkers have the same tools to build cocktails at home. Brands carried include Ghia, Ritual Zero Proof, Cut Above, Seedlip, Lyre's, Athletic Brewing, Abstinence, and Mingle Mocktails. A daily in-store tasting bar pours rotating samples and the occasional craft mocktail, and the shop hosts classes and events. Wallace Dry Goods was named Best Non-Alcoholic Bottle Shop in Philadelphia Magazine's 2024 Best of Philly awards.
