venues.longDescription:
WLVS Den Kava Lounge is a fully alcohol-free kava bar at 5447 South Rainbow Boulevard, Suite E7, in Spring Valley — southwest of the Strip in a Rainbow Boulevard strip mall, not downtown, despite several listings filing it in the Arts District. It bills itself as Nevada's only licensed kava bar, and is the current branding of the lounge that launched at this same address in 2019 as 9th Island Kava Lounge. Kava is worth describing plainly, because the audience for a bar like this includes people in recovery: it is a psychoactive botanical from the Pacific Islands, prepared as a water infusion of the root of the kava plant and drunk socially in place of alcohol. It is not alcohol and contains none, but it is mildly sedative and it is intoxicating in its own right, which is a distinction that matters if you are avoiding intoxicants of every kind rather than avoiding alcohol specifically. It is served here in the traditional way — shells, quads, thirty-seven-ounce Big Bula jugs, half-gallons, gallons and Tanoa bowls — brewed fresh daily in rotating flavours including horchata, blueberry and peach.

Alongside the kava proper is a specialty list of teas and functional drinks, some of them micro-dosed with kava and some with none at all: WLF MNT Tea (white tea, fresh peppermint, agave), the stronger Trainwrckr Tea, Cup of Joe (cacao, ashwagandha, eight mushrooms, red tea, micronised kava, agave), Cocao, and Night Cap (magnesium, lemonade, ashwagandha, micronised kava, vitamin C). The house GOLD'n BULA is marketed as the strongest kava shot available without resorting to harmful extract. A daily happy hour from 3pm to 6pm takes half off all shells and teas, Trainwrckr excepted. The lounge doubles as the unofficial Las Vegas Star Trek headquarters, with custom themed drinks and monthly watch parties, and fills the rest of its calendar with live music, board games and karaoke. Nothing alcoholic is served at any hour.
venues.pressQuote: What I like about WLVS DEN KAVA is that it gives people a place to hang out socially without making alcohol the center of the experience.

venues.name: Wooden City
venues.description: Wooden City is the Birmingham room of a small restaurant group that also runs in Chattanooga and Tacoma, on Morris Avenue in the restored warehouse block downtown, serving wood-fired pizza and small plates seven nights a week from 5pm to 10pm. Its sibling in Chattanooga carries five separate zero-proof drinks on the printed menu, which is the deepest restaurant list in that city; the group's house approach to the category is the reason this room is listed here. The Morris Avenue setting — cobbles, iron canopies, no through traffic — makes it one of the more pleasant places downtown to eat without drinking.
venues.longDescription:
Morris Avenue is a preserved nineteenth-century warehouse street in downtown Birmingham — cobblestones, cast-iron canopies, no through traffic — and Wooden City occupies one of its ground floors. It is part of a small group that also operates in Chattanooga and in Tacoma, serving wood-fired pizza and shared small plates in a room that fills every night of the week.

The reason it is in this guide is the group's approach to alcohol-free drinks, which is documented in detail at its Chattanooga sibling: five separate zero-proof builds printed on the menu, including a Fizz of berries, coconut cream, cinnamon, nutmeg and soda — the deepest restaurant list of its kind in that city. Five is a section rather than a gesture, and a group that has done that work once tends to carry the recipes and the training across.

This entry is graded three and carries no signature drinks, which is the honest position. What has been verified for the Birmingham room specifically is that it is trading normally and belongs to the group; the individual drinks on its own menu could not be read for this guide, and this directory does not transplant one location's drink list onto another's page. Treat the Chattanooga list as an indication of what to ask for rather than as a promise.

The format helps regardless of the drinks. Shared plates set the pace of an evening by the food rather than by the round, which is a substantially easier social setting for someone not drinking than a bar counter where the rhythm is set by everyone else's glass.

Dinner runs 5pm to 10pm seven days a week — including Sunday and Monday, when several of the better bars in this guide are closed, which makes it a useful fallback as well as a destination.

venues.name: Wooden City
venues.description: Wooden City is a downtown Chattanooga restaurant on Broad Street serving wood-fired pizza and small plates, with a bar that carries five separate zero-proof drinks on the menu — the deepest printed alcohol-free list of any restaurant in the city. The one worth ordering is the Fizz, built on berries, coconut cream, cinnamon, nutmeg and soda, which uses warm baking spices and a fat to give an alcohol-free drink the weight most of them lack. It serves dinner seven nights a week from 4:30pm, running to 9:30pm and 10pm at weekends, with a daily happy hour from 4pm to 5:30pm.
signatureDrinks: Fizz — berries, coconut cream, cinnamon, nutmeg, soda
venues.longDescription:
Five is an unusual number of zero-proof drinks for a restaurant to print. Two is a gesture; five is a section, and it means the kitchen and bar have had to build, cost and train on each one. Wooden City, on Broad Street in downtown Chattanooga, carries five, which makes it the deepest restaurant list of its kind in the metro.

The standout is the Fizz. Berries, coconut cream, cinnamon, nutmeg and soda is an odd-looking specification until you understand the problem it is solving: alcohol carries weight, warmth and aromatic lift in a drink, and when you remove it what is left usually tastes thin and cold. Coconut cream restores the body, the baking spices supply the warmth that alcohol's burn would otherwise provide, and the soda keeps it from becoming a dessert. It is a genuinely well-engineered drink rather than a fruit juice with a garnish.

The restaurant around it is a wood-fired pizza and small-plates room, well regarded locally, and the format helps: shared plates and a long table are a much easier social setting for someone not drinking than a bar counter is, because the meal rather than the round sets the pace of the evening.

NOOGAtoday, the city's daily newsletter, picked the Fizz out specifically in its guide to non-alcoholic drinking in Chattanooga, which is the corroboration this listing rests on alongside the menu itself. The other four zero-proof drinks rotate and are not recorded here.

Dinner runs from 4:30pm every night of the week, to 9:30pm Sunday through Thursday and 10pm on Friday and Saturday. Happy hour is daily from 4pm to 5:30pm, which is a useful window if you want the room before it fills.
venues.pressQuote: Five zero-proof drinks are on the menu at this downtown restaurant, but the one that caught our eye is Fizz, made with berries, coconut cream, cinnamon, nutmeg, and soda.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: NOOGAtoday, Local mocktails + non-alcoholic drinks in Chattanooga

venues.name: Wooden Robot Brewery
venues.description: Wooden Robot Brewery is an urban farmhouse craft brewery founded in 2015 at 1440 S Tryon St in Charlotte's South End, with a 15-barrel brewhouse, two bars, a biergarten, a scratch kitchen and a coffee bar. Queen City Nerve readers voted it Best Brewery in 2024. Its taproom lists a Non-Alcoholic section holding an N/A Beer at $6, Walker Brothers kombucha at $6 and sodas from $2, plus a rotating shelf of non-alcoholic cans from Untitled Art and Athletic Brewing. IMPORTANT: three further items on that same Non-Alcoholic list — Five Flowers ($8), 420-Rita ($14) and Blueberry Yum Yum ($14) — are hemp-derived THC and CBD drinks rather than plain mocktails; Five Flowers is a THC/CBD cooler brand, and the bar's "Hightails" are built with a Calmezzi THC/CBD elixir. They contain no alcohol, which is why they appear there, but anyone avoiding intoxicants should order the N/A beer, kombucha, soda or coffee instead.
venues.address: 1440 S Tryon St, Suite 110, Charlotte, NC 28203
venues.longDescription:
Wooden Robot Brewery was founded in 2015 by two friends, Dan Wade and Josh Patton, blending Belgian farmhouse tradition with American craft brewing on a 15-barrel system at 1440 S Tryon Street in South End. Wade's brewing and Patton's business background built what the brewery itself calls a beloved Charlotte institution, and Queen City Nerve readers voted it the city's Best Brewery in 2024. The brewery has been through a great deal since: Wade died in an accident at the brewery in February 2024, and Patton concluded his involvement in October 2025 to pursue work outside North Carolina, with the wider Wade family stepping into a larger ownership and management role to carry it on. The South End site is more than a taproom — two bars, a biergarten, a private event space, a scratch kitchen cooking with North and South Carolina ingredients, and a coffee bar that opens at 8am on weekdays. Dogs are welcome on the patios.

The taproom prints a Non-Alcoholic section, and it needs reading carefully, because it mixes two very different things under one heading. The straightforwardly inert options are an N/A beer at $6, Walker Brothers kombucha at $6, sodas from $2, and the full coffee bar — plus a rotating shelf of non-alcoholic cans that has included five Untitled Art varieties and Athletic Brewing. The other three items on that list are not mocktails. Five Flowers ($8 for 12oz) is a THC and CBD cooler brand rather than a house drink, and the 420-Rita and Blueberry Yum Yum ($14 each) sit alongside the brewery's "Hightails", which are built with a Calmezzi THC and CBD elixir. All three are alcohol-free, which is why the brewery groups them where it does, and for some people avoiding alcohol that is exactly what they want. For anyone in recovery from anything else, or simply not looking to be altered, the distinction matters more than the heading suggests — so order by name, not by section.
venues.pressQuote: Best Brewery — Winner: Wooden Robot Brewery

venues.name: Wooden Ship Brewing
venues.description: Wooden Ship Brewing is a small neighbourhood brewery and fifty-seat taproom on West 44th Street in Linden Hills, with a garage door, big windows into the production floor, and a dog- and child-friendly room. All its beers are gluten-reduced. Its non-alcoholic offer is broader than most taprooms': a house hop water at 0.0% built on Centennial and Au Tropical hops, canned non-alcoholic beer from Untitled Art and Deschutes, and — the part worth knowing — specialty non-alcoholic cocktails including a shrub seltzer, a hibiscus margarita and a dill seltzer, each of which can be ordered at 0% rather than only in its alcoholic version.
signatureDrinks: Hop Water (0.0%; sparkling water, Centennial and Au Tropical hops)
venues.longDescription:
Wooden Ship Brewing sits on West 44th Street in Linden Hills, in the south-west corner of Minneapolis where the neighbourhood commercial strips are small and the taprooms are scarce. The room seats about fifty: big windows out to the street and in to the production area, a garage door for warm weather, and a stated policy of being dog-friendly, kid-friendly and, in the brewery's own phrasing, YOU-friendly. Every beer it brews is gluten-reduced, which already makes it an unusual stop for anyone drinking around a dietary constraint. The taproom runs seven days, from 2pm on weekdays and midday at weekends, closing at 10pm most nights.

The non-alcoholic side is worth setting out precisely, because a state tourism listing has described Wooden Ship as having launched two non-alcoholic brews of its own and the brewery's published beer list does not support that. What the brewery's own page does list is a house Hop Water at 0.0% ABV — sparkling water dry-hopped with Centennial and Au Tropical, which gives the citrus and tropical aroma of an IPA with none of the alcohol, sugar or bitterness — plus canned non-alcoholic beer from Untitled Art, whose Italian-style pilsner is on the list, and Deschutes' Fresh Haze non-alcoholic IPA. Beyond beer, the taproom makes specialty cocktails that are offered at either 0% or 10% ABV, so the shrub seltzer, the hibiscus margarita and the dill seltzer can all be ordered with nothing in them: a genuine choice at the point of order rather than a single token option. Northstar Kombucha, house sodas, apple juice and La Croix cover the rest. This is a working brewery with a full-strength tap list and is graded as a modest but real non-alcoholic offering, not an alcohol-free venue. For anyone planning a visit around the non-alcoholic options, the practical point is the cocktail list rather than the beer: being able to order the same seltzer or margarita build the rest of the table is drinking, at 0%, is a materially different experience from being handed a can. The hop water and the non-alcoholic cans are priced in line with the rest of the list.

venues.name: Worthy Brewing Company
venues.description: Worthy's Hop Quencher is hop water — hop aroma and bitterness brewed without alcohol, calories or sugar — and it has become a warm-weather staple in Bend for exactly the moment a full beer is too much. The east-side brewery pairs it with a hop garden, an observatory and a big patio, open to 11pm at weekends.
signatureDrinks: Hop Quencher — hop water; hoppy, crisp and alcohol-free
venues.longDescription:
Worthy Brewing sits on the east side of Bend on Bellevue Drive, with a hop garden, a greenhouse and — unusually for a brewery — its own observatory, the Hopservatory, with a telescope open to the public on clear nights. It is a big, family-friendly site with a large patio, and its contribution to Bend's alcohol-free drinking is Hop Quencher.

Hop water deserves explaining, because it is the most interesting thing to happen to non-alcoholic drinking in a brewery town and it is still unfamiliar to most people. It is not beer with the alcohol removed and it is not a soft drink. It is water infused with hops — carrying the aroma, bitterness and resinous character that hops give an IPA, with no malt, no fermentation, no alcohol, and essentially no calories or sugar. The result tastes recognisably like the smell of a hoppy beer, without any of the body. For someone who misses an IPA specifically because of the hops rather than the alcohol, it is a closer match than most non-alcoholic beers manage, and it is dry rather than sweet, which is where NA soft drinks usually fail.

In a town where the post-ride, post-climb, post-float beer is a genuine social ritual, Hop Quencher slots into the ritual exactly. It is the drink for a hot afternoon on the patio when a full pint would end the day rather than extend it.

Worthy pours it alongside its full-strength range, and the site's scale — patio, gardens, family space, observatory — makes it one of the easier places in Bend to spend a long afternoon without the drink being the point. The observatory keeps its own separate schedule, so check before making a special trip for it.
venues.pressQuote: worthy brewing's hop quencher has become one of my warm-weather staples. hoppy, crisp, and wildly refreshing

venues.name: Wren House Brewing Co.
venues.description: A beloved neighborhood brewery on N 24th Street in central Phoenix, Wren House is known for some of Arizona's best IPAs — its flagship hazy, Spellbinder, took a Gold Medal in the Juicy/Hazy IPA category at the 2020 Great American Beer Festival. It also brews a zero-proof Non-Alcoholic Spellbinder at 0.5% ABV, built on the same Citra, Mosaic and Cascade hops with increased kettle hopping for bitterness and a dialled-in dry-hop ratio aimed at tangerine citrus. Axios Phoenix named it among the local non-alcoholic beers worth seeking out for Dry January. Note that the standard Spellbinder is alcoholic — ask specifically for the NA version.
venues.longDescription:
Wren House operates out of a converted bungalow on N 24th Street in central Phoenix, in the Encanto/Green Gables area, and has the feel of a neighbourhood operation that happens to be very good rather than a destination brewery that happens to have a patio. Its reputation rests largely on Spellbinder, the hazy IPA introduced in 2017 that became its flagship and took a Gold Medal in the Juicy/Hazy IPA category at the 2020 Great American Beer Festival — a category that is among the most crowded in American brewing, which makes the medal a real one.

The relevant thing here is that the brewery makes a non-alcoholic version of that same beer. Non-Alcoholic Spellbinder comes in at 0.5% ABV and is not a separate, lesser recipe: it uses Spellbinder-selected lots of Citra, Mosaic and Cascade, with increased kettle hopping to carry bitterness through the lower gravity and a dry-hop ratio tuned toward tangerine citrus. Those are the two problems that sink most non-alcoholic IPAs — thin body and a sweet, wort-like finish where the bitterness should be — and addressing them deliberately is the difference between an NA beer that exists and one worth ordering. Axios Phoenix included it when rounding up local non-alcoholic beers for Dry January.

For a non-drinker the practical value is the same as at any brewery that brews its own: you are drinking the house product, poured by the people who made it, rather than a national brand kept in the fridge as an accommodation. One caution worth repeating because the names are nearly identical — the standard Spellbinder is a full-strength IPA. Ask explicitly for the non-alcoholic version, and check the can or the tap list rather than assuming. This is a working taproom with a full beer programme, not an alcohol-free venue.
venues.pressQuote: That was maybe always the goal of Wren House, to find that medium between what people want and what we want
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Preston Thoeny, Wren House head brewer

venues.name: Writers Bar
venues.description: Tucked into the front corner of Raffles Hotel Singapore's Grand Lobby, Writers Bar runs a genuine printed list of eight non-alcoholic cocktails served in proper stemware. Bar manager Konstantine Arzumanov's zero-proof builds include the Emin Pasha, an Arabic-influenced old-fashioned of Seedlip Spice 94, miso, orgeat, gum and demerara syrups and orange-blossom water, and the Strike Slip, a clarified serve of Lyre's White Cane, sencha, soursop and calamansi. The NA drinks are composed with the same care as the bar's literary-themed alcoholic cocktails, not treated as an afterthought.

venues.longDescription:
Writers Bar occupies the front corner of the Grand Lobby inside Raffles Hotel Singapore, the 1887 colonial landmark and national monument on Beach Road. Behind a gleaming brass counter, the grandly arched room is dressed in palm-leaf wallpaper, tufted leather sofas and objets d'art, trading on what Food & Wine called its 'gentleman explorer' energy. The bar's cocktail programme is themed around the celebrated novelists who passed through the hotel's doors, and Writers Bar appears on The World's 50 Best Bars' 50 Best Discovery guide.

The non-alcoholic offering is a real, named part of the menu rather than a token nod. Bar manager Konstantine Arzumanov, who brings more than a decade of luxury-hospitality experience from Abu Dhabi and the Seychelles, has built eight zero-proof cocktails served in the same beautiful stemware as their spirited counterparts. The Emin Pasha is a zero-proof, Arabic-influenced old-fashioned named for the Ottoman explorer, combining Seedlip Spice 94 with miso, orgeat, gum and demerara syrups and a dab of orange-blossom water. The Strike Slip is a luminous clarified drink built on Lyre's White Cane spirit with sencha, soursop and calamansi.

LeRoy Chan, Raffles' assistant director of food and beverage marketing, has framed the approach around treating alcohol-free guests as seriously as any other: nonalcoholic cocktails made with thought and served with the full ceremony of the room. For non-drinkers, Writers Bar is one of Singapore's strongest hotel-bar options for a considered zero-proof serve in a genuinely storied setting.
venues.pressQuote: Guests are delighted to see nonalcoholic cocktails made with thought, served in beautiful stemware.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: LeRoy Chan, Raffles' assistant director of food and beverage marketing

venues.name: Wyrd Sisters Taphouse & Brewery
venues.description: A primarily women-owned Park Circle taphouse and brewery that quietly opened December 2024 and held its grand opening in early 2025, founded by Thad Wellington, Brittany Slechter and Jess Wellington. Alongside its always-changing house brews and roughly a dozen guest drafts, the inclusive beverage program lists meads, wine, non-alcoholic brews and "alcohol alternatives" so non-drinkers have real options. It bills itself as Charleston's only 21+ brewery, with a large yard where leashed dogs and kids are welcome.

venues.longDescription:
Wyrd Sisters opened in the Park Circle neighborhood of North Charleston in December 2024, the project of Thad Wellington and Brittany Slechter, who met at Frothy Beard's Summerville taproom, along with Jess Wellington. The space carries a punk-metal aesthetic and an explicitly inclusive ethos where, as the owners describe it, flavor comes first and style is an afterthought.

Beyond house brews and outsourced guest drafts, the menu deliberately makes room for people who aren't drinking: meads, wine, non-alcoholic brews and alcohol alternatives are part of the lineup. The non-alcoholic selection complements the beer program rather than functioning as a dedicated zero-proof concept, but it is a documented, intentional offering.
venues.pressQuote: We offer meads, wine, non-alcoholic brews, and alcohol alternatives so everyone can enjoy the Wyrd Sisters experience.

venues.name: Yacht Club
venues.description: Yacht Club is a 2021-founded neighborhood bar in Denver's Cole neighborhood, co-owned by McLain Hedges and Mary Alison Wright. The 'anti-club club' concept sits at the crossroads of upscale cocktail haunt, natural wine bar, and beloved dive bar — with hot dogs and dim-sum-style snacks rounding out the food offering. The bar debuted on the World's 50 Best Bars list in 2023 and won the Ketel One Sustainable Bar Award at North America's 50 Best Bars the same year, recognized for sustainability initiatives including fermentation programs that extend the shelf life of seasonal ingredients. The non-alcoholic program is featured on the menu under 'soft bangers' and has been covered in detail by Visit Denver's December 2025 spirit-free roundup (the Paradise Waits — green pineapple, Lyre's white cane, celery, lime, curry leaf) and Sober Bars Finder's Denver mocktails feature (the Friends In Low Places — Three Spirit Nightcap, Late Harvest Verjus, coffee, N.O.T. Chocolate Vinegar). The split-based, wine-forward cocktail philosophy that defines the alcoholic menu extends to the NA program: thoughtful, ingredient-driven, and far from the standard mocktail playbook.

venues.longDescription:
Yacht Club opened in 2021 at 3701 North Williams Street in Cole, a residential pocket north-east of downtown, from co-owners McLain Hedges and Mary Alison Wright. The stated concept is an anti-club club, and in practice the bar sits at the intersection of three formats that usually stay apart: a technical cocktail bar, a natural wine bar, and a dive. Hollywood Frank's hot dogs and dim-sum-style snacks are the food. The bar debuted on the World's 50 Best Bars list in 2023 and took the Ketel One Sustainable Bar Award at North America's 50 Best Bars the same year, recognition tied to fermentation and preservation work that extends the usable life of seasonal produce rather than to any single drink. Esquire named it to its Best Bars in America list and Westword named it Best New Bar, both in 2023, and Eater Denver includes it among its essential Denver bars. The room is open from 4pm to 2am six nights a week and closed on Tuesdays, which makes it one of the few high-end cocktail programmes in Denver still pouring at closing time.

The non-alcoholic drinks live on the menu under the heading Soft Bangers (N.A.), and they follow the same split-base, wine-forward, faintly contrarian logic as the full-proof list. Paradise Waits ($10) is the most-cited of them: Lyre's White Cane with green pineapple, celery, lime, curry leaf and salt. Freebird ($12) builds Pathfinder against a bitter aperitivo with pineapple, lime, salt and soda. Coconono ($12) is coconut cordial with lime, mint and sparkling tea. The YC N/A Spritz ($10) runs Seedlip Garden with strawberry, magnolia, verjus and tonic. A Suze Tonic N/A ($9) and a cold brew and tonic ($6) round out the section. Visit Denver's December 20, 2025 spirit-free guide argued that the bar's cocktail obsessiveness carries directly into the mocktails, naming Paradise Waits, and the bar's pricing supports the point: the zero-proof drinks are cheaper than the spirited ones but are not simplified versions of them. The section is short by design rather than by neglect: four built drinks that turn over with the rest of the menu, plus two lower-effort options for anyone who wants something long and bitter without a full build. Because the bar keeps late hours and takes no reservations, it also functions as a place a non-drinker can arrive at 11pm and still be served something considered.
venues.pressQuote: Consistently ranked among the best bars in the country, Yacht Club brings an eccentric high-low vibe that feels very of the moment...That same geeky cocktail charm bleeds into the mocktails, where you'll be just as happy sipping the Paradise Waits with green pineapple, Lyre's white cane, celery, lime and curry leaf as you would a cup of the Kool-Aid du jour.

venues.name: Yarra Botanica
venues.description: Yarra Botanica is a two-level floating bar and eatery moored on the Yarra River at Riverside Quay in Southbank, pouring a 100% Victorian beverage list through a Drink Victorian partnership. Its non-alcoholic side is genuine if moderate: alcohol-free beers from Melbourne's Hop Nation and zero-alcohol spirits from Four Pillars sit alongside AF spritzes, RTDs and mocktails. The riverfront room, all-local produce and skyline views make it an easy low-proof stop rather than a dedicated zero-proof destination. It is a floating bar on the Yarra, pouring Victorian-made drinks through a partnership with Drink Victorian, with non-alcoholic beer, cocktails and alternative wines all on the list.
venues.address: North of 4 Riverside Quay, Southbank Promenade, Southbank VIC 3006
venues.longDescription:
Yarra Botanica is a two-level floating bar and eatery built out over the Yarra River, moored just north of 4 Riverside Quay on the Southbank Promenade in the heart of Melbourne's arts precinct. Guests jump aboard for casual drinks, shared plates and pizzas with spectacular city-skyline views; the kitchen sources around 90% of its food from local suppliers, and walk-ins of all sizes are welcome across the two decks.

The drinks program is the venue's signature: a 100% Victorian beverage list assembled in partnership with Drink Victorian, spanning signature spritzes, boutique beers and locally made wines. The non-alcoholic offering runs the same all-local logic. Per sitchu's Melbourne non-alcoholic bars guide, the list includes alcohol-free beers from Hop Nation and zero-alcohol spirits from Four Pillars, and the venue's own listings add AF spritzes, RTDs and mocktails to the mix.

The range is real but moderate rather than a printed zero-proof anchor menu — the NoLo Life directory rates its alcohol-free and low-alcohol selection a 3 out of 5. For an alcohol-free visitor, that means a dependable handful of genuine local NA beers and spirits plus mixed non-alcoholic builds, poured in one of Southbank's more distinctive riverfront rooms.

Yarra Botanica is open Monday to Wednesday from midday to 10pm, Thursday until 11pm, Friday to 1am, Saturday from 11am to 1am, and Sunday from 11am to 11pm.

The setting is the draw, and it is genuinely hard to replicate: a floating bar on the Yarra in the middle of the city. Pub With No Booze puts the appeal plainly — who would not want to sit on a floating bar on the river drinking non-alcoholic beverages — and notes that Yarra Botanica gives you plenty to choose from, with beer, cocktails and alternative wines all available alcohol-free.

The sourcing is local by design. The bar partners with Drink Victorian to pour a line-up made in the state, running from signature spritzes to boutique beers and Victorian wines, with a range of non-alcoholic options alongside. For a non-drinker that combination is unusually good value: the thing you are paying for is the position on the water and an hour in the sun, neither of which is improved by alcohol, and the drink in your hand is made forty minutes away rather than shipped from Europe.
venues.pressQuote: A 100% Victorian beverage menu that includes an alluring assortment of non-alcoholic options.

venues.name: Yellow Door Taqueria
venues.description: The original Yellow Door Taqueria is in Lower Mills, the mill village at the southern end of Dorchester Avenue where Boston meets Milton, and it is the room that made the group. Cali-Mex food, a margarita-led bar and a dining room that runs to 11pm most nights and midnight Thursday through Saturday. The alcohol-free list is the same three named drinks the group pours across its restaurants, all $10 and made with fresh juice rather than a mix: Mango Vibes Only with mango, pineapple, coconut, agave and lime; Stitzer's Paloma with a house rosemary syrup, fresh grapefruit and lime juices and soda; and Sober Baddie with pineapple and hibiscus, vanilla, toasted coconut, lime and soda. Jarritos are $4.

venues.longDescription:
Lower Mills is a distinct pocket of Dorchester, a nineteenth-century mill village strung along the Neponset River at the Milton line, and Yellow Door Taqueria at 2297 Dorchester Avenue is one of its anchors. It was the group's first restaurant before the South End and Providence openings, and it retains the neighborhood-room feel: a bar that fills with regulars, a dining room that turns over families early and groups late, and a kitchen serving Cali-Mex tacos, bowls and shareables. Hours run to 11pm Sunday through Wednesday and midnight Thursday through Saturday, with brunch from 11am at weekends and lunch on Thursdays and Fridays.

The drinks matter here because this part of Dorchester has almost nothing else with a printed alcohol-free list. Yellow Door pours three named mocktails at $10, the same ones as the group's other rooms, and they are built from hand-squeezed juice and house syrups rather than from a bottled mix. Mango Vibes Only is mango, pineapple, coconut, agave and lime, the sweetest and most tropical of the three. Stitzer's Paloma is the useful one for anyone who normally drinks a paloma: house rosemary syrup, fresh grapefruit and lime juices, soda, and enough bitterness from the grapefruit to stop it reading as juice. Sober Baddie is pineapple and hibiscus with vanilla, toasted coconut, lime and soda. Jarritos in assorted flavours are $4. The programme has no non-alcoholic spirits behind it, which is why it is graded as a real but modest offering rather than a serious one, but the drinks are named, priced against the cocktail list rather than the soda list, and made to order at a bar that expects to be asked. The South End restaurant on Harrison Avenue pours the same three drinks, and the Boston Globe used the group as its case study in March 2026 when reporting on how far Boston restaurants have pushed the ambition, and the price, of their alcohol-free lists.

venues.name: Yellow Door Taqueria

The kitchen is Cali-Mex and the bar is built on margaritas, but the non-alcoholic list is a real one rather than a bottled soda. Three named drinks are $10, all hand-squeezed rather than poured from a mix: Mango Vibes Only combines mango, pineapple, coconut, agave and lime; Stitzer's Paloma uses a house rosemary syrup with fresh grapefruit and lime juices and soda; and Sober Baddie layers pineapple and hibiscus with vanilla, toasted coconut, lime and soda. Jarritos in assorted flavours are $4.

venues.longDescription:
Yellow Door Taqueria began in Dorchester's Lower Mills and expanded into the South End at 354 Harrison Avenue, in the Ink Block development on the edge of the neighborhood where it meets the expressway. The format is Cali-Mex: tacos, bowls and shareables, a room that fills after work and stays busy through the evening, and a bar organised around margaritas. It keeps later hours than most of the surrounding restaurants, serving until 11pm Sunday through Wednesday and midnight Thursday through Saturday, with brunch from 11am at weekends and lunch on Thursdays and Fridays.

The reason it is listed here is that the group deliberately rebuilt its alcohol-free offering. The Boston Globe reported in March 2026 that Yellow Door had replaced a short list of soft drinks and faux margaritas topping out at $7 with hand-squeezed, fresh-fruit mocktails at $10, and the current menu bears that out. Mango Vibes Only combines mango, pineapple, coconut, agave and lime. Stitzer's Paloma is built on a house rosemary syrup with fresh grapefruit and lime juices topped with soda, and is the closest thing on the list to the bar's own signature drink without the tequila. Sober Baddie layers pineapple and hibiscus with vanilla, toasted coconut, lime and soda. All three are $10 against a cocktail list in the mid teens, and Jarritos in assorted flavours are $4 for anyone who just wants a cold soda with tacos. The programme is modest in size and there are no non-alcoholic spirits behind it, so it is graded as real but not serious; what it does have is fresh juice, house syrups and three drinks that a bartender will make properly rather than apologise for. The group also runs the original Lower Mills restaurant in Dorchester and a location in Providence, and the same three mocktails are poured at each; a Mission Hill branch has closed.
venues.pressQuote: They have replaced an alcohol-free menu limited to soft drinks and faux-margaritas that topped out at $7 with multiple hand-squeezed, fresh-fruit derived mocktails priced at $10.

venues.name: Yellowbelly
venues.description: Yellowbelly, the "Sea & Spirits" restaurant and craft cocktail bar that Travis Howard and Tim Wiggins opened on Lindell Boulevard in 2018, pairs coastal-inspired seafood with one of St. Louis's most deliberate zero-proof programs. Four alcohol-free cocktails hold a marked "(N/A)" spot on the menu at $10 — the Belly Bump, Piña Co-Nada, Toothless Tiger and Jungle Feather — drawing on the hydrosol "botanic waters" Wiggins developed so alcohol-free drinks keep real flavor and mouthfeel. Best Day Brewing's N/A Kölsch covers the beer side. St. Louis Magazine's guide to nonalcoholic cocktails counts this buzzy Central West End spot among the city's best places to drink without drinking.

venues.longDescription:
Travis Howard and Tim Wiggins, the team behind Retreat Gastropub, opened Yellowbelly in September 2018 in the Citizen Park building at 4659 Lindell Boulevard in the Central West End. The concept is "Sea & Spirits": a coastal-inspired seafood restaurant — ceviche, crudo and whole fish alongside comfort plates — welded to a craft cocktail bar built around sugarcane and agave spirits. Celebrity chef Richard Blais was brought in to help develop the opening menu, but the identity of the place has always belonged to its bar: Wiggins runs the beverage program, and in 2020 the pair added Lazy Tiger, a dedicated cocktail bar in the lush space next door.

The zero-proof side is a signature, not an afterthought. In early 2021, Feast Magazine covered the launch of Yellowbelly's nonalcoholic cocktail line, for which Wiggins developed a blend of hydrosols, or "botanic water" — distillations of fresh leaves, fruits and flowers meant to give alcohol-free drinks the flavor and mouthfeel of the real thing. That technique is still on the menu today: the current list marks four N/A cocktails at $10 — the Belly Bump (pineapple, coconut, turmeric, ginger beer, nutmeg), Piña Co-Nada (fresh pineapple, coconut cream, lime), Toothless Tiger (peppercorn hydrosol, serrano chile honey, lime, Tajín) and Jungle Feather (N/A aperitif, pineapple, lime) — plus Best Day Brewing's nonalcoholic Kölsch at $6.

The room has stayed relevant well past its opening buzz. In a March 2025 feature, Sauce Magazine called Yellowbelly and Lazy Tiger "a dynamic duo in the Central West End," describing Yellowbelly as tropical, trendy and fun with the bar and kitchen equally yoked, and St. Louis Magazine's roundup of the city's best nonalcoholic cocktails praises its creative, crowd-pleasing drink list. Expect a lively, beachy dining room, dinner Tuesday through Saturday with a Saturday brunch, happy hour Tuesday–Friday from 5 to 6:30pm, and reservations on Resy — with the sister cocktail bar Lazy Tiger sharing a wall if you want to keep the night going.
venues.pressQuote: Yellowbelly is tropical, trendy and fun, with the bar and kitchen equally yoked.

venues.name: Yemex Bakehouse & Specialty Coffee
venues.description: Yemex Bakehouse & Specialty Coffee opened in west Houston on 11 February 2026, founded by Rawan Alsagheer and Efrain Ayllon — a couple who both left tech careers with no culinary training to build a Yemeni-Mexican cafe. The signature drink is the areekano: a double espresso poured over chilled water, sweetened with a house-made syrup and topped with cream, cheddar cheese, honey and black sesame seeds, a translation of the Yemeni date-and-cheese dessert areeka into a cup. Alongside it sit a cafe de olla latte, an Adeni chai brewed with a house spice blend and piloncillo, and single-origin Yemeni pour-overs from Al-Haimah and East Haraz. The kitchen bakes cafe de olla rolls and a black lime Danish. It trades to midnight on Friday and Saturday, and is closed Mondays.

venues.longDescription:
Yemex Bakehouse & Specialty Coffee opened in west Houston on 11 February 2026 with a premise no other coffeehouse in the city is working: Yemeni coffee tradition and Mexican coffee tradition on one menu, treated as equals rather than as a novelty crossover. It is the personal project of Rawan Alsagheer and Efrain Ayllon, a couple who both previously worked in tech and neither of whom had culinary training — they told the Houston Chronicle they wanted to build something that represented their two backgrounds.

The areekano is the drink that explains the place. A double espresso is poured over chilled water, sweetened with a house-made syrup, then topped with cream, cheddar cheese, honey and black sesame seeds. The cheddar sounds like a stunt until you know the reference: areeka is a Yemeni dessert built on dates, honey and cheese, and the drink is a straight translation of it into a glass. Order it first, and order it cold — it is built as an iced drink.

The Mexican half of the list runs through a cafe de olla latte built on a house-made syrup of the traditional spiced coffee with cinnamon. The Yemeni half runs through the house Adeni chai — black tea with a house spice blend, milk and piloncillo, the unrefined cane sugar that also ties it back to the Mexican side — and a spiced honey latte. Behind both sits the most serious part of the offer: single-origin Yemeni pour-overs, currently a Haimi anaerobic lot from Al-Haimah near Sana'a and a Bany Murah from East Haraz. Yemeni coffee is among the oldest cultivated in the world and among the hardest to source; a cafe putting two named lots on a pour-over bar is making a real statement about where it sits.

The bakehouse half of the name is not decorative either. The kitchen turns out cafe de olla rolls and a black lime Danish — black lime being loomi, the dried lime that runs through Gulf and Yemeni cooking, which is an unusual thing to find in a pastry case anywhere.

The practical notes: closed Mondays, open from eight the rest of the week, and running to midnight on Friday and Saturday, which makes it a genuine evening room rather than a daytime stop. On alcohol the evidence is unusually complete — the entire published drinks menu carries no alcoholic item, the pastries are halal, and the Texas licence register holds no permit under the trade name anywhere in the state. Note for accuracy that the retail centre at this street number does contain a separately licensed liquor store, an unrelated tenant.
venues.pressQuote: build something unique that represents us and our passion, our background and everything
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Rawan Alsagheer and Efrain Ayllon, Yemex founders, to the Houston Chronicle

venues.name: Yeppa & Co. Beltline
venues.description: Yeppa & Co. Beltline is an Italian bar and restaurant on Auburn Avenue in the Old Fourth Ward, directly on the BeltLine's Eastside Trail, from Pietro Gianni and Stephen Peterson of Storico Fresco and Forza Storico. The menu takes its cue from Rimini on the Adriatic coast, and the drinks list carries a zero-proof section that fits the aperitivo format properly rather than awkwardly. The house Spritz swaps prosecco and bitter liqueur for Lapo's non-alcoholic aperitif with soda, and Amore e Passione runs Floreale non-alcoholic aperitivo with passion fruit, lemon and soda. There is a large covered patio with fire-pit tables and outdoor seating alongside the trail, so the alcohol-free order works in the same setting as everyone else's.
venues.address: 667 Auburn Ave NE Suite 120, Atlanta, GA 30312
venues.hours: Tue-Thu 5pm-11pm; Fri 5pm-12am; Sat 11:30am-12am; Sun 11:30am-11pm; Mon closed
signatureDrinks: Spritz (Lapo's N/A aperitif, soda, no prosecco)
Amore e Passione (Floreale N/A aperitivo, passion fruit, lemon, soda)
venues.longDescription:
Yeppa is a Romagnol exclamation of delight, and the restaurant group behind it — Pietro Gianni and Stephen Peterson of Y Hospitality, previously responsible for Storico Fresco, Storico Vino and Forza Storico — built the concept around Rimini, the seaside city in Emilia-Romagna. The BeltLine location sits at 667 Auburn Avenue NE in the Old Fourth Ward, opening straight onto the Eastside Trail with a spacious covered patio, outdoor seating, fire-pit tables and strings of lights, which is where most of the trade happens in good weather. It serves dinner Tuesday through Friday from five and adds weekend lunch from 11:30am, running to midnight on Friday and Saturday.

Aperitivo is the format, and that is precisely why the non-alcoholic list works here rather than feeling like a compromise. An Italian spritz is a structural drink — bitter, effervescent, low in sugar, drunk before food — and it survives the removal of alcohol better than almost any other cocktail category. Yeppa's house Spritz drops both the prosecco and the bitter liqueur and rebuilds it on Lapo's non-alcoholic aperitif lengthened with soda, keeping the bitterness and the colour. Amore e Passione is the floral counterpart, made with Floreale non-alcoholic aperitivo, passion fruit, lemon and soda. DiningOut, surveying Atlanta's zero-proof bars in 2026, judged that both Yeppa outposts carry a zero-proof section that fits the aperitivo ethos perfectly. The kitchen runs handmade pasta, wood-fired dishes and Adriatic-leaning seafood alongside. The restaurant is fully licensed with a substantial wine programme, so it sits at four rather than five, but the zero-proof drinks are named on the printed menu, priced as cocktails and built behind the same bar — and on a stretch of the BeltLine where most patios are drinking-first, that matters. The Eastside Trail runs past the door, so the room draws walkers and cyclists coming off the path as well as booked tables, and the patio is the part of the operation most people encounter first. A second Yeppa operates in Buckhead Village under the same ownership with the same zero-proof section but longer daytime hours; we list the two separately because they are distinct addresses with distinct kitchens and schedules.
venues.pressQuote: Both the Beltline and Buckhead Village outposts of this Rimini-inspired Italian bar have a zero-proof section that fits the aperitivo ethos perfectly.

venues.name: Yeppa & Co. Buckhead
venues.description: Yeppa & Co. Buckhead is the Buckhead Village outpost of the Rimini-inspired Italian bar and trattoria from Pietro Gianni and Stephen Peterson of Y Hospitality, and it keeps longer hours than the BeltLine original — open from 11:30am seven days a week and to midnight on Friday and Saturday. The room is a Formula One-themed bar and dining space in the Buckhead Village District. The same zero-proof section runs here: a Spritz rebuilt on Lapo's non-alcoholic aperitif with soda and no prosecco, and Amore e Passione made with Floreale non-alcoholic aperitivo, passion fruit, lemon and soda. Because the kitchen opens at lunch, this is one of the more reliable places in Buckhead to get a properly-built alcohol-free aperitivo in the middle of the day.
signatureDrinks: Spritz (Lapo's N/A aperitif, soda, no prosecco)
Amore e Passione (Floreale N/A aperitivo, passion fruit, lemon, soda)
venues.longDescription:
The Buckhead Yeppa sits at 306 Buckhead Avenue NE in the Buckhead Village District, the walkable retail block off Peachtree, and it is the second of the two Atlanta locations from Pietro Gianni and Stephen Peterson — the Y Hospitality partners behind Storico Fresco, Storico Vino and Forza Storico. The concept is the same: an Italian bar and trattoria drawing on Rimini, the coastal city in Emilia-Romagna, with an interior that leans into a Formula One motif and a bar that anchors the room. What differs is the schedule. Buckhead opens at 11:30am every day of the week and runs to eleven, or midnight on Friday and Saturday, where the BeltLine site is dinner-led and closed on Mondays. That makes it the more useful of the pair for anyone who wants a drink over lunch or in the middle of the afternoon.

The zero-proof list carries across from the BeltLine location, and it works for the same structural reason: aperitivo drinks are built on bitterness, dilution and carbonation rather than on the warmth of alcohol, so removing the alcohol costs them less than it costs a spirit-forward cocktail. The house Spritz is assembled with Lapo's non-alcoholic aperitif and soda, without prosecco, keeping the bitter-orange profile and the colour that makes it look like everyone else's glass on the table. Amore e Passione is the floral, fruit-led alternative, built on Floreale non-alcoholic aperitivo with passion fruit, lemon and soda. DiningOut's 2026 zero-proof round-up covered both outposts together and judged the section a good fit for the format. Food is handmade pasta and Adriatic-influenced cooking, and there is a full wine list, so this is a licensed restaurant with a real non-alcoholic option rather than an alcohol-free room — a four on our scale, listed separately from the BeltLine site because it is a distinct address with its own hours and its own kitchen.
venues.pressQuote: Both the Beltline and Buckhead Village outposts of this Rimini-inspired Italian bar have a zero-proof section that fits the aperitivo ethos perfectly.

venues.name: Yixing Xuan Teahouse
venues.description: Yixing Xuan Teahouse is a Chinese teahouse and tea merchant at 78 Tanjong Pagar Road, founded in 1989 by Vincent Low, a former banker who came to tea through a friend, and run today with his daughter Charlene. It serves no alcohol at all. The tea menu runs to more than thirty Chinese and Taiwanese teas brewed gongfu-style at the table, from a S$8.50 Beauty of the East oolong the house calls its signature to three grades of Da Hong Pao, aged Gong Mei white tea and Feng Huang Dan Cong, with dim sum as pairing. Tea appreciation workshops run regularly and the shop sells around fifty loose-leaf teas and teaware. It opens until 9.30pm on Fridays and Saturdays.

venues.longDescription:
Yixing Xuan has been on Tanjong Pagar Road since 1989, which makes it one of the longest-running teahouses in Singapore and a contemporary of Tea Chapter a few streets away. Its founder, Vincent Low, left banking after a friend introduced him to Chinese tea, and the business is now a father-and-daughter operation with Charlene Low, who leads many of the workshops. City Nomads described them in 2018 as a passionate father-daughter team who have spent three decades raising awareness of the joys, history and proper methods of drinking Chinese tea. The format is the classic one: a pot brewed at your table in the gongfu style, repeated infusions, and staff who will walk you through what you are tasting if you ask. Tea appreciation workshops cover the basics from plant to palate, and the retail side stocks about fifty teas across white, green, oolong, pu-er, black and flower categories, along with Yixing clay pots and other teaware. Prices on the tea menu start around S$8 a pot, with a S$5 charge for a second person sharing.

The house signature is Beauty of the East, a Taiwanese oolong at S$8.50 with honey-fruit aromas and a bittersweet finish. The Wuyi rock teas are the other strength: Da Hong Pao in standard, premium and prestige grades from S$9 to S$16, and Rou Gui at S$12.50 with its smoky, oak-like aroma. Beyond those there is Ti Kuan Yin, a Fujian Yinzhen Baihao silver-needle white tea, a 2009 aged Gong Mei white tea, Hangzhou Long Jing in two grades, Bi Luo Chun, osmanthus-scented oolong, jasmine pearls and a hand-bound Dragon Pearl flowering tea, plus Feng Huang Dan Cong in Duck Shit and Honey Orchid cultivars from the shop. There is no wine, beer or spirit anywhere on the menu, which is why it is graded here as a genuine alcohol-free destination rather than a cafe with a tea list. The limitation is the clock: it closes at 8pm Monday to Thursday and 7pm on Sundays, stretching to 9.30pm only on Friday and Saturday, so it works as an early-evening alternative to a bar rather than a late one. Reservations and workshop bookings are taken through the website.
venues.pressQuote: For the past 30 years, the passionate father-daughter team – Vincent and Charlene Low – have been raising awareness of the joys, history, and proper methods of drinking Chinese tea at their homey tea house.

venues.name: Yours Truly
venues.description: Yours Truly is the cocktail bar inside the AC Hotel by Marriott on Bishop Street, in Honolulu's downtown financial district. It publishes a dedicated Zero-Proof section on its own menu — a distinction worth drawing, because a printed section means the drinks are costed, trained and stocked rather than left to whoever is behind the bar. Three named builds anchor it: She's Blushin', made with spiced rich cranberry, lime juice, mint leaves and club soda; Manila Bae, which puts pineapple juice with tamarind syrup, lime juice and citrus syrup; and Stamped Strawberry, muddled strawberry with lime, basil and club soda. Fever-Tree mixers are stocked for simpler orders.

venues.longDescription:
Yours Truly occupies the ground floor of the AC Hotel by Marriott at 1111 Bishop Street, in the middle of Honolulu's downtown business district — a part of town that empties in the evening and where the bar trade is largely hotel guests and people staying on after work. The room is polished and low-lit, tucked away enough to be worth finding, and it is built to be lingered in rather than passed through.

What distinguishes it for a non-drinker is structural rather than atmospheric. Its published menu carries Zero-Proof as its own named section alongside the cocktails, wine and beer, rather than appending a mocktail or two to the bottom of another page. That distinction does real work: a section on a printed menu means the ingredients are ordered every week, the specs are trained into the staff, and ordering one does not require a negotiation with the bartender. The three standing builds are properly composed and priced accordingly, at $14 to $18 — the same order of magnitude as the alcoholic list, which is itself a signal that the bar treats them as equivalent products rather than as consolation. She's Blushin' works a spiced rich cranberry base against lime, mint and club soda for something tart and long. Manila Bae is the most interesting of the three, using tamarind syrup — sour, faintly funky, and a Filipino pantry staple — against pineapple, lime and citrus syrup, which gives it the savoury edge that fruit-forward zero-proof drinks usually lack. Stamped Strawberry is the simplest, muddled strawberry with lime and basil lengthened with soda. Fever-Tree mixers are stocked for guests who want something plainer. The venue does not publish opening hours or a phone number on its own site, so booking through the reservation system is the reliable route.

venues.name: Yunta Nikkei
venues.description: Yunta Nikkei is Charlotte's first Peruvian-Japanese (Nikkei) restaurant, opened in 2022 by the Viva Chicken team in South End, blending raw ceviches, tiraditos, and handmade maki with an intentional zero-proof cocktail program. Beverage director Ashley Sarkis built a dedicated mocktail menu anchored by premium NA spirits including Seedlip Garden and Amass Riverin, earning Yunta a spot on Yelp's top 25 mocktail programs in the U.S. in 2024 — the only North Carolina restaurant on that list. Guests can choose from named zero-proof cocktails like The Gardener and Isle del Sol alongside NA beer, making it one of Charlotte's strongest NA options in a full-service restaurant setting.

venues.longDescription:
Yunta Nikkei is Charlotte's first Peruvian-Japanese restaurant, at 2201 South Boulevard in South End, from Randy Garcia and chef Bruno Macchiavello — the hospitality veterans who opened the Peruvian rotisserie concept Viva Chicken in Charlotte in 2013 and built a cult following from it. Nikkei cooking is the cuisine that emerged from Japanese immigration to Peru, and it is the natural home of raw fish handled two ways at once: ceviches and tiraditos alongside sushi technique. The restaurant calls itself a gastro barra, and the room matches — an industrial, modern space with a sleek fluted wood-panel wall and a lush covered tropical terrace. The menu runs a crabocado causa at $16, a ceviche trio at $39, lomo saltado at $30, a New York strip at $68 and a duck tamago at $72. Queen City Nerve readers named it Charlotte's Best South End Restaurant in 2024. It opens at 4pm on weekdays and from late morning at weekends, with reservations through Resy.

For a non-drinker the important structural fact is that Yunta prints a section headed "Mocktails" on its main menu, four drinks deep and priced at $11 to $12 — meaningfully below the cocktails, and sitting in the same place on the page as everything else. The Gardener and Isle del Sol are both $11, with Flor de Sauco and Blushing Rose at $12. The names point at what the kitchen does with produce: Flor de Sauco takes its name from elderflower, and the list leans on the same Peruvian aromatics — black mint, aji, citrus — that run through the food. Asahi Dry non-alcoholic beer is $5.50 for anyone who would rather have a beer with raw fish. One caveat worth stating: the restaurant lists its mocktails by name and price without printing ingredients, so if a specific allergen or a particular flavour matters to you, ask rather than assume — and the list rotates with the kitchen's seasonal produce.
venues.pressQuote: I believe having non-alcoholic options on my cocktail menu is vital. There are many times when people can't, or choose not to drink alcohol. Having non-alcoholic options available gives guests a safe alternative to enjoy thoughtfully crafted drinks.
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Ashley Sarkis, Beverage Director, Yunta Nikkei
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Yahoo News / AOL (Yelp Top Mocktail Spots feature, 2024)

venues.name: Z Co-Space & Kava Clubhouse
venues.description: A coworking-meets-kava-bar hybrid in Orlando's Mills 50 district, running as a daytime workspace and coffee/tea bar that shifts into an alcohol-free social lounge by night. Its pitch is simple: kava is 'the buzz without the booze.' (Alcohol-free, though kava is a mildly psychoactive botanical, not strictly substance-free.)
venues.longDescription:
At 1413 Haven Dr in Orlando's Mills 50 district, Z Co-Space & Kava Clubhouse blends a coworking space, coffee shop, and tea house with a kava bar. By day it functions as a productivity hub with workspace and wifi, open to members and non-members; by evening the same room becomes a lounge pouring handcrafted kava, its signature Z Tea mocktails, kombucha, coffee, exotic teas, and hookah.

The alcohol-free pitch centers on kava producing a relaxed, social buzz without alcohol's downsides - no hangover, no impaired driving - but it's still a mood-altering botanical rather than a plain herbal drink, so guests wanting a fully substance-free visit are better served sticking to the coffee, kombucha, and tea side of the menu.

The venue has built a strong local following, holding a 4.67-out-of-5 weighted score across more than 400 reviews on BestKavaBar, with regulars singling out drinks like the brown sugar oat milk latte. Z Co-Space runs daily drink specials, local DJs, and recurring social, art, and networking events, and is open Monday-Friday 9am-midnight and Saturday 10am-midnight, closed Sundays.

venues.name: Z Tiki Kava Bar
venues.description: Z Tiki is an alcohol-free tiki lounge in the Hourglass District, and it is a night venue in the full sense — closed Monday and Tuesday, open from 5pm midweek and from 3pm at weekends, running to 2am on Friday and Saturday. The room is fitted with soft lighting, plush seating and natural wood, and the entertainment is real rather than incidental: a blacklight pool table, karaoke every Friday from 10pm, and stand-up comedy nights. Kava is served at a notably low price point for the city. IMPORTANT for readers in recovery: kratom is on the menu alongside it. Kratom acts on opioid receptors and carries dependence and withdrawal risk that kava does not, so order deliberately. (As of late September 2026 Z Tiki appeared to be temporarily closed, and the bar had not posted on Instagram since May, with no reason given — check before you go.)
venues.longDescription:
Z Tiki is an alcohol-free tiki lounge in the Hourglass District, and it is a night venue in the fullest sense — closed entirely on Monday and Tuesday, opening at 5pm midweek and at 3pm at the weekend, running to midnight early and to 2am on Friday and Saturday. A room that does not bother opening until the evening is making a statement about what it is for: this is not a cafe that stays open late, it is a bar that happens not to serve alcohol.

The fit-out supports that. Soft lighting, plush seating and natural wood give it the register of a cocktail lounge rather than a wellness space, and the entertainment is real rather than incidental — a blacklight pool table, karaoke every Friday from 10pm, and stand-up comedy nights. Those are the things that fill the hours alcohol usually fills, and they are the reason a room like this works as a Friday night rather than as a worthy substitute for one.

The kava is served at a notably low price point for Orlando, which matters more than it might sound: one of the quiet barriers to alcohol-free socialising is that the alternatives are often priced like a treat rather than like a round. Kava is the ground root of Piper methysticum, a shrub native to the South Pacific islands, prepared as a cold water infusion and drunk socially across Fiji, Vanuatu, Tonga and Samoa for roughly three thousand years. It contains no alcohol. It tastes earthy and bitter, numbs the lips and tongue on the first mouthful, and is mildly sedative rather than intoxicating in the way alcohol is. Kava exhibits reverse tolerance, so regular drinkers usually need less rather than more, and a first visit rewards taking it slowly.

The Hourglass District, on East Michigan Street south-east of downtown, has become one of Orlando's better small neighbourhood scenes, and Z Tiki sits alongside SODO Kava and House of Mana a short drive away — giving the southern half of the city a genuine cluster rather than a single outpost.

One disclosure belongs here plainly. Kratom is served alongside the kava. The two are poured from the same bar across most of Florida and are easy to conflate, but they are not the same class of drink. Kratom is the leaf of Mitragyna speciosa, a Southeast Asian tree, and its principal alkaloids act on the opioid receptors; regular use produces tolerance and a genuine withdrawal syndrome, several US states ban it outright, and its concentrated 7-hydroxymitragynine derivatives face active federal scheduling. Kava carries no comparable dependence profile. If you have come to a kava bar specifically to avoid substances with a hold, order by name and ask what is in the cup.

As of late September 2026 Z Tiki appeared to be temporarily closed, and its Instagram had been silent since May, with no reason or reopening date given. The hours above are the last ones the bar published; check its Instagram before making the trip.

venues.name: Zanti Cucina Italiana
venues.description: Zanti's River Oaks bar keeps a standing "Zero-proof" section on its permanent cocktail menu, not just a seasonal add-on: Berry Brezza, Mora di Zanti, Piccola Rita and Senza Fashion, built on Seedlip Garden, Seedlip Notas de Agave and Cut Above Non-whiskey (each $15, matching the alcoholic cocktails). Each January the bar layers in Dry January specials such as La Mora di Zanti, Marg No Rita, Panoma and Tiki Good. Houston outlets DiningOut and Click2Houston (KPRC) each named the zero-proof list in January 2026 Dry January roundups, evidence of a maintained program rather than a one-off.

venues.longDescription:
Zanti Cucina Italiana opened its second location in Houston's River Oaks Shopping Center in November 2022, following the original in The Woodlands in 2019. Founder Santiago "Santi" Peláez runs the roughly 7,700-square-foot room on West Gray Street with director of operations Stefano Ferrero and executive chef Hilario Zamora. Zanti holds Wine Spectator's Best of Award of Excellence, granted in 2024 for its extensive Italian-focused wine list.

That award is the useful context for what follows. A restaurant whose reputation rests on a serious wine programme has every commercial reason to steer guests toward the bottle list, and most such places offer non-drinkers nothing. Zanti instead keeps a permanent "Zero-proof" section of four drinks, each at $15 — the same price as the alcoholic cocktails.

The builds are properly constructed. Berry Brezza and Mora di Zanti both use Seedlip Garden, the herbaceous expression built on pea, hay, spearmint, rosemary and thyme; the first takes it into raspberries, lemon and soda, the second into hibiscus, blackberry syrup, lemon and mint. Piccola Rita uses Seedlip Notas de Agave, the tequila-facing bottling, with lime and orange juice.

Senza Fashion is the one that shows the programme is serious. It rebuilds an Old Fashioned on Cut Above Non-whiskey with maple syrup and — critically — non-alcoholic bitters. Standard cocktail bitters run to 35–45% alcohol by volume, so an Old Fashioned made with ordinary bitters is not an alcohol-free drink, however non-alcoholic the base spirit. Sourcing zero-proof bitters costs more and takes effort, and doing it is the clearest signal a bar has thought about who is actually ordering these drinks.

Each January the bar layers Dry January specials over the standing list, including La Mora di Zanti, Marg No Rita, Panoma and Tiki Good. Both DiningOut Houston and KPRC's Click2Houston named Zanti in their January 2026 Dry January round-ups, citing the West Gray address and the Seedlip-based drinks — evidence of a maintained programme rather than a seasonal gesture. Open from eleven most days, to eleven at night on Friday and Saturday.
venues.pressQuote: The new year can still be one of dolce vita at this buzzy Italian restaurant in the River Oaks Shopping Center.

venues.name: Zen Room Kava Lounge
venues.description: Zen Room Kava Lounge is widely cited as Minnesota's first kava bar, a fully alcohol-free social space on West Kellogg Boulevard in downtown St. Paul. Rather than coffee or cocktails, the lounge is built around ethically sourced specialty kava — the calming Pacific-island root beverage — plus nootropic and hemp-derived botanical drinks, traditional teas, and snacks. It positions itself as a calm, mindful place to gather, read, or connect, marketing kava as "a social beverage without a next-day hangover," which makes it a genuine fit for sober and sober-curious guests. The menu blends prepared kava drinks served in traditional shells and bowls with espresso-style and tea options, plus sugar-free and dairy-free preparations and build-your-own blends. It carries a 4.9-star Yelp rating across 100-plus reviews, with praise for its sourcing, knowledgeable staff, and atmosphere.
venues.address: 342 W Kellogg Blvd, Saint Paul, MN 55102
venues.longDescription:
Zen Room Kava Lounge is widely cited as Minnesota's first kava bar, and as of 2026 it remains the only dedicated kava lounge in the Twin Cities — a fact worth stating plainly, because the surrounding metro of some three and a half million people has produced exactly one. It sits on West Kellogg Boulevard in downtown St. Paul, is fully alcohol-free, and is built around ethically sourced specialty kava rather than around coffee or cocktails with kava added as a novelty.

The menu blends the traditional and the modern. Prepared kava is served in traditional shells and bowls — the Boula Bowl is the sharing format — alongside espresso-style preparations, traditional teas, a warm spiced chai, and a kava Mai Tai for anyone wanting something closer to a cocktail in feel. Mud Water, the coffee-alternative mushroom blend, is poured too. Sugar-free and dairy-free preparations are available, and the bar will build custom blends, which matters for a drink whose earthy, peppery base taste is the main thing that puts newcomers off. Beyond kava the lounge carries nootropic and hemp-derived botanical drinks and snacks. It runs to midnight on Friday and Saturday and to 10pm the rest of the week, and it carries a 4.9-star Yelp rating across more than a hundred reviews, with the recurring praise falling on sourcing, staff knowledge and atmosphere.

The lounge markets kava as "a social beverage without a next-day hangover," and positions itself as a calm, mindful place to gather, read or talk. For readers in recovery the honest description matters: kava is the ground root of a South Pacific shrub steeped in water, containing no alcohol whatsoever and drunk socially across the Pacific for roughly three thousand years — but it is genuinely relaxing and mildly intoxicating on its own terms. If what you are avoiding is alcohol, it is a direct substitute; if what you are avoiding is intoxication of any kind, it is worth knowing what you are ordering.

venues.name: Zén
venues.description: Zén holds three MICHELIN stars in a restored Bukit Pasoh shophouse, and it runs one of the most serious non-alcoholic pairings in Asia. The zero-proof programme is priced at around S$250 per person — set against the wine flight rather than discounted below it — and it is rebuilt whenever the kitchen changes its menu, so it tracks the food course by course instead of recycling a fixed set of juices. The drinks are constructed rather than poured: a sparkling aperitif of heirloom tomatoes and red plums, a Peach with Pepper made from aged peaches juiced and fermented with oxalis stems, and a white wine alternative of fermented quince, apple, pear and lemon finished with toasted pecan and walnut water.
signatureDrinks: Peach with Pepper - aged peaches juiced and fermented, with oxalis stems and pepper
White wine alternative - fermented quince, apple, pear and lemon with toasted pecan and walnut water
Sparkling aperitif of heirloom tomatoes and red plums
venues.longDescription:
Zén occupies a restored shophouse on Bukit Pasoh Road and is the Singapore sibling of Frantzén in Stockholm. It carries three MICHELIN stars, which places it at the very top of the city's dining hierarchy, and the format is a long tasting menu served across multiple floors of the house. For a guest who is not drinking, the relevant fact is that the restaurant treats the non-alcoholic route as a full parallel programme rather than a concession.

The pairing runs at roughly S$250 per person. That price is deliberate and worth understanding: it sits alongside the wine flight rather than beneath it, which is the clearest possible statement that the zero-proof drinks are not a cheaper fallback. The programme is also rewritten whenever the kitchen alters its dishes, so what arrives is matched to the food on the night rather than assembled from a standing list. That is a significant amount of ongoing work, and very few restaurants at any level commit to it.

The drinks themselves are built with fermentation and extraction rather than simple juicing. Documented serves include a sparkling aperitif made from heirloom tomatoes and red plums; a Peach with Pepper, in which aged peaches are juiced and fermented before being combined with oxalis stems and pepper; and a white wine alternative of fermented quince, apple, pear and lemon, finished with toasted pecan and walnut water to give it the weight and nuttiness that a wine would otherwise supply. These are savoury, structured drinks designed to cut and complement across a long menu, not sweet ones — the fermentation supplies the acidity and length that would otherwise come from wine, and the nut waters supply the weight.

The restaurant has also moved into bottling its non-alcoholic work in white, red and orange styles, which suggests the programme is treated as intellectual property rather than as a service obligation. For a non-drinking guest the practical implication is simple: this is one of the few three-star restaurants anywhere where declining the wine flight does not mean accepting a lesser version of the evening. Booking is essential and should be made well in advance, with the pairing requested at the time of reservation so the kitchen can plan the sequence.
venues.pressQuote: The non-alcoholic drink pairing offers eccentric combinations that work.

venues.name: Zephyr Southern Brasserie
venues.description: Zephyr Southern Brasserie is the lobby-level restaurant and bar of Hotel Phoenix, the first major project delivered at the Centennial Yards development in downtown Atlanta. The cooking crosses French brasserie technique with Southern ingredients, and the drinks are run by mixologist Thandi Walton, whose rail-themed cocktail list is named for the site's railway history. Her non-alcoholic menu is titled Zero Judgement, and the named pour from it is Butterflies on the Rail — butterfly pea flower, lemon, blackberries and an egg white foam that gives it the texture of a proper sour. The restaurant serves from 6:30am to midnight seven days a week, and a separate 32-seat room, Bar Z, pours the same drinks list.

venues.longDescription:
Centennial Yards is the redevelopment of the railway gulch that separated downtown Atlanta from Mercedes-Benz Stadium for decades, and Hotel Phoenix is its first major completed building. Zephyr is the hotel's signature restaurant, sitting at lobby level at 70 Centennial Olympic Park Drive NW and taking its name — like most of the drinks list — from the passenger trains that once ran through the site. The kitchen works a French brasserie framework with Southern ingredients: spicy fried chicken with stone-ground grits, collard greens and pickled vegetables; shrimp biscuits with avocado and maple; endive salad with smoked chicken, green apple and whole-grain mustard; deviled eggs and cornbread with smoky tabasco butter. It serves from 6:30am to midnight every day, which makes it one of the longest-trading rooms downtown, and a 32-seat bar called Bar Z runs off it.

Thandi Walton runs the beverage programme, and her cocktail list keeps the railway conceit going with drinks like The Gulch Resurgence and the Boxcar Burn. The non-alcoholic drinks are grouped under their own heading — Zero Judgement — which is a deliberate signal to guests rather than a filing convention, and DiningOut's 2026 zero-proof survey judged that the menu earns the name. The named drink from it is Butterflies on the Rail: butterfly pea flower for the colour shift, lemon for acid, blackberries for body, and an egg white foam that gives it the head and mouthfeel of a classic sour rather than the thinness of a juice. It is the only alcohol-free drink we could confirm by name, so it is the only one listed here; the rest of the Zero Judgement list rotates and we have not published names we could not verify. Zephyr is a fully licensed hotel restaurant, so it sits at four, but the non-alcoholic section is titled, run by a named bartender and available every hour the room is open.
venues.pressQuote: Acclaimed mixologist Thandi Walton runs the beverage program at Hotel Phoenix's lobby-level restaurant and bar, and her 'Zero Judgement' menu earns the name.

venues.name: ZERO Cocktail Bar
venues.description: ZERO Cocktail Bar bills itself as Canada's first non-alcoholic cocktail bar, pairing a full bar with an in-house bottle shop on Carlton Street in Toronto's Cabbagetown. The menu runs to fourteen named zero-proof cocktails - from a Power Serve of alternative whiskey and ginger beer to a Sorrel Negroni of hibiscus and spiced sorrel - built on NA brands including Free Spirits, Ghia, DR ZERO and Noughty. A retail bottle shop stocks NA wines, beers and alternative spirits alongside a café menu of hot and cold coffee drinks and pub food like loaded fries and grilled cheese.
