Le Marg — "Crossip's vibrant citrus and spice with the earthy warmth of Free Spirit Alternative Tequila for a zesty, full bodied sip."
Aperitivo Spritz — "Zesty grapefruit and bittersweet orange lead into Ghia's herbal complexity, lifted by bubbles and a clean, dry finish"
French 57 — "Bright and elegant, Sober Spirits Gin and Undone French Aperitif come together in a lightly bitter citrus lift"
Gooseberry Forest Gin Fizz — "Tart gooseberry and citrus lift Everleaf's woodland herbs and resinous notes, finished light, dry, and effervescent"
Stressa Sour — "Juicy orange and lemon lift floral hibiscus and amaro bitterness, softened by DR ZERO herbal warmth."
Mauby Old Fashioned — "Soft smoke, mauby bark bitterness meet caramelized spice and herbal bitterness"
Sorrel Negroni — "Rich bitterness meets vibrant hibiscus and spiced sorrel, unfolding into a dry, aromatic Negroni-style finish"
Soulful Sorrel — "Rich, ruby pour inspired by Caribbean tradition, opens with tart hibiscus and warming spice, layered with gentle citrus and a rounded velvety finish"
Hibiscus Bitter — "Zesty lemonade meets CROSSIP Hibiscus' floral bitterness, vibrant, balanced citrus, complex"
venues.longDescription:
ZERO Cocktail Bar sits on Carlton Street in Toronto's Cabbagetown and describes itself as Canada's first non-alcoholic cocktail bar - a combined bar, tasting room and bottle shop built around what the venue calls "Curated Experiences. Curated Bottles. Crafted Cocktails." The team frames the concept around the shift toward mindful drinking, citing that up to 30% of guests at Canadian events aren't consuming alcohol and up to 51% of Canadians are mindfully consuming it.

The cocktail menu runs to fourteen named, zero-proof drinks built on alternative spirits and NA brands. The Power Serve pairs an alternative whiskey with ginger beer for "a spicy, crisp serve with depth, bite, and a lively ginger snap," while the Le Marg leans on Free Spirit Alternative Tequila and Crossip for a "zesty, full bodied" citrus pour. The Aperitivo Spritz builds Ghia's herbal complexity with grapefruit and bittersweet orange, and the French 57 pairs Sober Spirits Gin with Undone French Aperitif for a lightly bitter citrus lift. The Sorrel Negroni and Soulful Sorrel both draw on hibiscus and Caribbean-style sorrel for bitter, spiced, citrus-lifted pours; the Stressa Sour and Hibiscus Bitter add DR ZERO and Crossip Hibiscus bitterness to citrus bases; and the Mauby Old Fashioned uses mauby bark bitterness with caramelized spice for a soft, smoky, Old Fashioned-style riff.

Alongside the bar, ZERO runs a retail bottle shop stocking NA wines, beers, alternative spirits and botanicals - including Noughty Rosé - plus a café line of hot and cold coffee drinks and a short food menu of loaded fries, hand-cut fries and grilled cheese. The venue also runs cocktail mixology classes, seasonal pop-ups around Toronto (including Sankofa Square and the Waterfront Underground Night Market), guided Sunday hikes, and a "Behind the Bar" podcast. Over Here Toronto named it among the city's best, writing: "If you're serious about the zero-proof life, this is your Mecca. It's a dedicated, alcohol-free bar, tasting room, and bottle shop all rolled into one."
venues.pressQuote: If you're serious about the zero-proof life, this is your Mecca. It's a dedicated, alcohol-free bar, tasting room, and bottle shop all rolled into one.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: 17 Best Non-Alcoholic Bars in Toronto (Zero Cocktail Bar & More)

venues.name: The Restaurant at Zero George
venues.description: Fine-dining restaurant and bar inside the boutique Zero George Street hotel in Ansonborough, selected for the 2025 inaugural MICHELIN Guide American South. Lead bartender Casie Fennell built a dedicated zero-proof pairing menu that runs alongside the nightly tasting menu for $50, roughly half the cost of the wine pairing. The non-alcoholic lineup spans house creations and premium NA wine, and guests are welcomed with a Lynn's Spritz mocktail of lemon, honey and basil.
signatureDrinks: Garden Suite Spritz (hibiscus, blackberry, zero-proof sparkling rose)
Lynn's Spritz (lemon, honey, basil) welcome mocktail
Dirty Chai Espresso Martini (N/A dessert cocktail)
Italian Soda with sweet corn and salted vanilla
venues.longDescription:
The Restaurant at Zero George occupies a boutique hotel built in 1804 in Charleston's Ansonborough district and serves a multi-course fixed tasting menu Tuesday through Sunday. Beyond the dining room, its bar pours zero-proof cocktails year-round, including a summer Garden Suite Spritz of hibiscus and blackberry topped with a zero-proof sparkling rose.

The standout is a full non-alcoholic beverage pairing built by lead bartender Casie Fennell to mirror the tasting menu, offered for $50 versus the wine pairing's higher price. Pours have included a Wolffer "Spring in a Bottle" N/A Rose, an Italian Soda with sweet corn and salted vanilla, a Cacao Old Fashioned made with orzo malt, and a Dirty Chai Espresso Martini dessert cocktail. According to the Post and Courier, N/A sales tripled in the first six weeks after launch.
venues.pressQuote: People think they'll be missing out by not being able to drink, but we are saying, 'Hey, we made this menu special for you.'
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Casie Fennell, lead bartender at Zero George, quoted by Kalyn Oyer

venues.name: Zero Gravity Beer Hall
venues.description: Zero Gravity's Pine Street beer hall is the taproom of the brewery behind Rescue Club, one of the earliest craft non-alcoholic beer lines in New England. Rescue Club was launched in January 2021 as a collaboration between Zero Gravity and Citizen Cider co-founder Kris Nelson, and both expressions — the IPA and the pilsner, each under 0.5% ABV — are stocked in cans at the beer hall alongside the full draft list. The brewery dry-hops the IPA again after the alcohol is removed, which is why it tastes like a hop-forward beer rather than a compromise. Open 8am to 9pm daily, to 10pm on Friday and Saturday, with food, an outdoor patio and dogs welcome outside.
signatureDrinks: Rescue Club IPA — non-alcoholic, under 0.5% ABV, dry-hopped after de-alcoholisation
Rescue Club Pils — non-alcoholic pilsner, under 0.5% ABV
venues.longDescription:
Zero Gravity was founded in 2004 in the hearth room at American Flatbread in Burlington and moved into its own Pine Street facility in 2015. The beer hall there is a large, plain, well-run taproom — Green State Lager, Conehead IPA, Madonna Double IPA and a long rotating list — and it is also the home of one of the earliest serious non-alcoholic beers made by a New England craft brewery.

Rescue Club launched on 2 January 2021 as a separate brand, developed with Kris Nelson, a co-founder of Citizen Cider, and it started with an IPA. The technical detail that matters is what happens after de-alcoholisation: the beer is dry-hopped a second time and then pasteurised, which restores the aromatic hop character that the alcohol-removal process strips out. That is why Rescue Club reads as a hoppy beer rather than as hop-flavoured water, and it is the same trick the better NA brewers have since adopted. A pilsner followed. Both sit under 0.5% ABV and both are available in cans at the beer hall.

For a visitor the practical value is that this is a proper brewery taproom where the non-alcoholic option is made by the same people who made everything else on the board, sold at the same counter, in the same room, with no separate menu or apology attached. In a beer city like Burlington that is a meaningful thing to be able to do with a group.

The hall opens at 8am seven days a week — genuinely, for coffee and breakfast — and runs to 9pm, or 10pm on Friday and Saturday. Food is served daily, there is indoor and outdoor seating, it is first-come first-served with no reservations, and leashed dogs are welcome on the patio.
venues.pressQuote: I was hanging out talking to people, everybody with masks on, and there I was drinking these non-alcoholic beers the whole time. And that felt really good. People need to be able to have another option, an alternative. I like it even more than I thought I would.

venues.name: Zero Lounge
venues.description: Zero Lounge is a Y2K-themed bar off Hollywood Boulevard, open Wednesday to Sunday from 7pm and running to 2am at weekends. It is licensed, and its menu carries a titled Mocktails section alongside the cocktails: Tamagotchi Tea, made with green tea, hibiscus syrup, lemon and agave; the Saved By the Bell-ini, built on Ritual non-alcoholic gin with peach puree, agave and soda water; and Slime Time, with lime juice, agave, cucumber, mint and ginger. The room is decorated with Furbies and neon, the DJ booth is built to look like a teenager's bedroom, and the programming runs to trivia, karaoke and DJ sets. Happy hour runs 7pm to 10pm daily. The Infatuation reviewed it in 2025.
venues.address: 1710 N Hudson Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90028
signatureDrinks: Tamagotchi Tea - green tea, hibiscus syrup, lemon, agave
Saved By the Bell-ini - Ritual Gin (NA), peach puree, agave, soda water
Slime Time - lime juice, agave, cucumber, mint, ginger
venues.longDescription:
Zero Lounge is a themed bar on Hudson Avenue, half a block off Hollywood Boulevard, and the theme is the early 2000s executed without irony or restraint. The Infatuation covered it in February 2025 and was clear-eyed about what it is: neon-lit, Furby-decorated, playing Ke$ha remixes, with a DJ booth designed to look like a teenager's bedroom, and in the reviewer's words pure absurdity and absolutely not for everyone. That is a fair warning and also, for a certain kind of night out, the entire appeal. The programming leans social rather than reverent - trivia, karaoke, DJ sets - which tends to suit groups where not everyone is drinking, because there is something to do besides drink.

The bar is licensed and the cocktail list is the main one, but the menu carries a named Mocktails section rather than burying non-alcoholic options in a footnote. There are three. Tamagotchi Tea is the simplest and the best-balanced: green tea with hibiscus syrup, lemon and agave, tart rather than sweet. The Saved By the Bell-ini is the one built like a cocktail, using Ritual's non-alcoholic gin with peach puree, agave and soda water - a bellini in shape, with the botanical bite the fruit needs. Slime Time is lime juice, agave, cucumber, mint and ginger, which is a mojito-adjacent long drink and the most refreshing of the three. The bar also notes on its own menu that the seasonal cocktail list rotates and is posted to its Instagram, so the mocktail line-up is worth checking before you build an evening around a specific drink.

A few practical points. The bar is closed Monday and Tuesday and does not open until 7pm on any day, running to midnight on Wednesday, 1am on Thursday and 2am Friday through Sunday. Happy hour is 7pm to 10pm daily, though the posted happy-hour prices cover beer, wine, well drinks and a spritz rather than the mocktails, which stay at menu price. It is walkable from the Hollywood and Highland Metro B Line station, which matters more than usual here: this is a part of Hollywood where parking is expensive and the surrounding blocks are busy late.
venues.pressQuote: the DJ booth is designed to look like a teenager's bedroom

venues.name: Zero Proof Lounge
venues.description: A fully alcohol-free lounge in Glendale and one of the only true sober bars in the West Valley — the entire menu is non-alcoholic, spanning botanical-tea cocktails and kava-based builds that mimic familiar drinks: a Zero 'Bull, a Blushing Lemon, a kava Pina Colada, a kava White Russian. Founded by Alanna and Chloe, the room deliberately blends kava bar, speakeasy and upscale lounge, with dim lighting and red LEDs rather than the clinical feel a lot of sober spaces settle for, and it runs weekly open mics and live music. Important: it serves kratom as well as kava. Both are alcohol-free and both are psychoactive — this is an alcohol-free room, not a substance-free one.
venues.address: 5150 W Olive Ave Ste C114, Glendale, AZ 85302
venues.longDescription:
Zero Proof Lounge occupies a suite on West Olive Avenue in Glendale, which puts it in the West Valley — a part of metro Phoenix with almost no alcohol-free nightlife at all, and a forty-minute drive from the downtown cocktail bars that dominate every list of the city's zero-proof options. Its existence is the point as much as its menu: for a large stretch of the metro it is the only sober bar there is. Founders Alanna and Chloe built it on the premise that connection, celebration and a night out do not have to be organised around alcohol, and pitched it at anyone exploring mindful drinking, living alcohol-free, or simply wanting a different kind of evening.

The room reads as a deliberate hybrid: part kava bar, part speakeasy, part upscale lounge, with dim lighting and red LEDs. That matters more than it sounds. A great many alcohol-free venues default to the aesthetics of a cafe or a wellness studio — bright, clean, faintly clinical — which signals recovery rather than a night out, and quietly tells the customer what kind of person they are assumed to be. Building a dark, low-lit lounge instead is a decision about dignity.

The menu runs botanical-tea cocktails alongside kava builds shaped like familiar drinks: the Zero 'Bull, the Blushing Lemon, a kava Pina Colada, a kava White Russian. Programming is weekly rather than occasional, with open mics and live music, which is what turns a bar into a place people return to. It opens daily at 2pm, running to 10pm on Sunday and Monday and to midnight the rest of the week.

One thing to be clear about before going. Alongside kava, the lounge serves kratom. Both are alcohol-free; both are psychoactive, and kratom acts on opioid receptors and carries documented dependence and withdrawal risk. For anyone in recovery that is a material distinction — this is a room without alcohol, not a room without substances, and it is worth deciding in advance which of those two things you are actually looking for. The staff are reportedly straightforward about what is in each build if you ask, which is the right way to handle it.
venues.pressQuote: We created this space because we believe that connection, fun, and celebration don't need to revolve around alcohol
venues.pressQuoteAttribution: Alanna and Chloe, founders, Zero Proof Lounge

venues.name: ZERO ZERO
venues.description: ZERO ZERO is a natural wine shop in Miami's Little River neighborhood, opened in June 2024 by Nicole and Adam Darnell, the couple behind Boxelder Craft Beer Market. Alongside its organic, biodynamic, and low-intervention wines, the shop houses "Zero Proof," a dedicated non-alcoholic micro-shop that the owners bill as "Miami's first and only retailer specializing in nonalcoholic beverage offerings." Rather than mixing drinks on site, Zero Proof is a walk-in bottle shop: the focus is "nootropic, adaptogenic, and functional beverages, as well as interesting offerings that feature a slug of flavor," spanning ready-to-drink spritzers and non-alcoholic wines, tequilas, and vodkas to take home. The Darnells frame the concept around inclusivity — providing those who don't drink with, in Adam Darnell's words, "equally exciting and delicious options." The shop also stocks goods and tinned fish, with parking behind the building.
venues.longDescription:
ZERO ZERO opened in Little River in June 2024, run by Nicole and Adam Darnell — the couple behind Boxelder Craft Beer Market, which is to say people who built a business on alcohol and then built one on its absence. The shop is primarily a natural wine retailer dealing in organic, biodynamic and low-intervention bottles, and inside it sits Zero Proof, a dedicated non-alcoholic micro-shop the owners bill as Miami's first and only retailer specialising in non-alcoholic beverages.

That it is a shop rather than a bar is the point. Most non-drinking happens at home, and the practical obstacle is supply: a supermarket stocks one alcohol-free lager and nothing else, so the alternative to a glass of wine on a weeknight is a soft drink. A retailer carrying non-alcoholic wines, tequilas and vodkas alongside ready-to-drink spritzers changes what is possible in a kitchen rather than only on a night out. The stated focus is nootropic, adaptogenic and functional beverages plus, in the shop's own phrase, interesting offerings that feature a slug of flavour.

The framing the Darnells give it is worth recording because it is the argument this whole directory rests on. Adam Darnell describes the aim as providing those who do not drink with equally exciting and delicious options — not a consolation, an equivalent. Housing that inside a natural wine shop rather than a separate sober storefront makes the same point structurally: the non-drinker and the wine buyer shop in the same room.

Goods and tinned fish round out the stock, and there is parking behind the building. It is a retailer, not a bar — there is nothing mixed on site and nowhere to sit and drink it. Little River has become the centre of gravity for this in Miami, and ZERO ZERO is a large part of why.
venues.pressQuote: We understand that not everyone wants or is able to consume alcohol, and we want to provide them with equally exciting and delicious options.

venues.name: Zhug
venues.description: Zhug opened on Cedar Road in the Cedar Fairmount district of Cleveland Heights in 2020, the eastern-Mediterranean concept from Douglas Katz — one of the most influential chefs in Cleveland over the past twenty-five years, and the man behind Fire in Shaker Square before it — now operated with Todd Thompson under the Edgewater Hospitality banner. The cooking runs through hummus, wood-grilled vegetables and mezze built around the Yemeni chilli-herb sauce the restaurant is named for, and the dining room does dinner six nights a week, closing Sundays. Its drinks list gives non-alcoholic cocktails a permanent place in its own numbering rather than a separate mocktail box: two N/A builds on Ritual and Monday zero-proof spirits, a rotating pair of house gazoz — Israeli-style fruit-syrup sodas — plus non-alcoholic beer and sparkling rosé.

venues.longDescription:
Zhug opened on Cedar Road in the Cedar Fairmount district of Cleveland Heights in 2020, the eastern-Mediterranean concept from Douglas Katz — one of the most influential chefs in Cleveland over the past twenty-five years, and the man behind Fire in Shaker Square before it — now operated with Todd Thompson under the Edgewater Hospitality banner. The cooking runs through hummus, wood-grilled vegetables and mezze built around the Yemeni chilli-herb sauce the restaurant is named for, and the dining room does dinner six nights a week, closing Sundays.

The beverage list is unusual in Cleveland for giving non-alcoholic drinks a permanent place inside the menu's own naming system rather than a separate mocktail box at the bottom of the page. The Zhug N/A No. 2 is built on a Ritual gin alternative with lemon, jade and chardonnay vinegar, the vinegar supplying the sharp finish a spirit would otherwise give; the N/A No. 3 uses Monday non-alcoholic whiskey with jalapeño, hibiscus, lemon and ginger beer for a longer, hotter drink. Alongside them sit the house gazoz — the Israeli-style fruit-syrup sodas that have become a signature — with No. 8 a sparkling pear shrub with cardamom and No. 10 a sparkling blueberry with lavender and lemon. The numbers rotate with the season, so the list is a live one rather than a fixture. Non-alcoholic beer, non-alcoholic sparkling rosé, mineral water and coffee drinks fill out the rest.

Cleveland Magazine's 2026 mocktail guide listed the N/A No. 2 at $12 and the gazoz at $11, both several dollars under the alcoholic cocktails. Between Zhug and its sibling Amba in Ohio City, Edgewater Hospitality is now the most consistent multi-restaurant group in the city for named, printed non-alcoholic drinks, which makes either a safe booking for a table where only some people are drinking.
venues.pressQuote: The N/A No. 2 pairs a Ritual gin alternative with lemon and chardonnay vinegar, while house gazoz drinks layer fruit syrups into soda water.

venues.name: Zig Zag Café
venues.description: Zig Zag Café is a landmark cocktail bar at 1501 Western Avenue on the Pike Place Market hillclimb, open since 1999 and housed in the 1910 Fix-Madore Building. It is internationally recognised as a pioneer of the classic cocktail revival, and it is where bartender Murray Stenson rediscovered the Last Word — a Prohibition-era drink that had fallen out of memory after the Second World War, which he found in a 1951 book and put back on a menu, from where it spread to New York, San Francisco, London and eventually everywhere. Its own description of the room is accurate: a low, sultry glow over the dining room, a verdant patio, and a house soundtrack of jazz, cumbia and highlife. Its non-alcoholic drinks are printed under "Zero Proof Drinks" at a flat $15: Daybreak (Yu No non-alcoholic gin, lemon, pineapple cordial, Giffard non-alcoholic spritz liqueur), Jardin Sauvage (mint, lime, ginger, Midnight Sun non-alcoholic aperitif), Rose-Colored Glasses (Roots non-alcoholic bianco vermouth, grenadine, grapefruit, bitters, non-alcoholic sparkling wine) and Dark Horse (Dr. Zero Zero non-alcoholic amaro, lime cordial, Giffard aperitif syrup). Open 5pm to midnight daily; 21+. Live jazz Sunday to Wednesday.
venues.longDescription:
Zig Zag Café opened in 1999 on the Pike Place Market hillclimb, in the 1910 Fix-Madore Building, and it has a genuine claim on cocktail history. The original owners hired Ben Dougherty and Kacy Fitch to build a credible drinks programme, and the two later bought the place. Around 2002 Murray Stenson came over from Il Bistro because, as he put it, they wanted to focus on classic cocktails. What happened next is the bar's monument: Stenson found the Last Word — equal parts gin, chartreuse, maraschino and lime — in Ted Saucier's 1951 book Bottoms Up, the only place he had ever seen the recipe, and started making it. A visiting bartender took it to New York, from where it went to San Francisco and then London and then everywhere. The cocktail historian Robert Hess's verdict on the bar is the fair one: it basically put Seattle on the map from a cocktail standpoint. Stenson was named the country's best bartender in 2010, left in 2011, and died in September 2023. The room today is what its own site describes — a low, sultry glow over the dining room, a verdant patio, and a soundtrack of jazz, cumbia and highlife — with live jazz Sunday through Wednesday. The kitchen is real: oysters at $25 the half dozen, a burger at $23, dry-aged flank steak at $44.

The non-alcoholic drinks get their own printed heading, Zero Proof Drinks, priced flat at $15, and the construction is exactly what you would hope from a bar with this pedigree — four drinks built on four different non-alcoholic houses rather than one bottled shortcut. Daybreak uses Yu No non-alcoholic gin with lemon, a pineapple cordial and Giffard's non-alcoholic spritz liqueur. Jardin Sauvage is the fresh, herbal one: mint, lime and ginger against Midnight Sun non-alcoholic aperitif. Rose-Colored Glasses is the most ambitious, layering Roots non-alcoholic bianco vermouth with grenadine, grapefruit, old-fashioned bitters and a non-alcoholic sparkling wine, which gives it the length and the lift of a proper aperitif cocktail. Dark Horse is the bitter one, on Dr. Zero Zero non-alcoholic amaro with lime cordial and Giffard aperitif syrup. The bar is 21-and-over and opens at 5pm every day.
venues.pressQuote: Zig Zag Café is internationally recognized as a pioneer of the classic cocktail revival.

venues.name: Zola
venues.description: Zola is a live-music bar and restaurant on Main Avenue in downtown Spokane, a room built out of salvage and oddities with bands most nights. Its mocktail list is the most deliberately constructed in the city, and the reason is personal: head bartender Sheldon Moore expanded it after getting sober, and holds the alcohol-free drinks to the same standards as the cocktails — measured pours, proper technique and real non-alcoholic spirits, with Figlia among his preferred bases. His stated aim is drinks with some bitterness and structure rather than another sweet soda, which is the complaint most non-drinkers have about bar menus. Open from 4pm, to midnight midweek and 1am on Friday and Saturday, closed Sunday.
venues.longDescription:
Zola is a downtown Spokane institution of the eccentric kind — a live-music bar on Main Avenue assembled out of salvage, with a Ford pickup mounted in the room and a band on most nights of the week. It is not where you would expect to find the most rigorous alcohol-free drinks programme in the Inland Northwest, and that is precisely what it has.

The credit belongs to head bartender Sheldon Moore, who got sober in 2023 and then set about rebuilding the mocktail list from the position of someone who has to drink from it. His diagnosis of the problem is the one every non-drinker recognises: going out, you can only order so many Pepsis, so many Sprites, so many flavoured lemonades. What he wanted instead were drinks with some bitterness to them, something that hits a little harder — the structural quality that makes a cocktail worth ordering slowly rather than draining.

His standards for the category are specific and worth repeating, because they are the difference between a mocktail programme and a garnish. Proper measurements, not free pouring. Good non-alcoholic spirits rather than syrup and soda — Figlia's range is among his preferred bases. And an acceptance that a customer paying cocktail prices for an alcohol-free drink is entitled to the same attention to detail and the same full-mouth flavour that the alcoholic version would deliver.

The result is a list that has grown steadily rather than sitting static, and a bar where asking for something without alcohol does not change the level of service you get. In a music venue, where people are in the room for three or four hours at a stretch, that matters more than it would somewhere you stop for one round.

Zola opens at 4pm and runs to midnight Tuesday through Thursday, 1am on Friday and Saturday, and 10pm on Monday. Closed Sunday. Live music is the default, not the exception, so check the calendar.
venues.pressQuote: Going out, you can only order so many Pepsis, so many Sprites, so many flavored lemonades.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: The Inlander, on mocktails becoming a menu standard

venues.name: Zunzibar
venues.description: Zunzibar is the coastal American restaurant and bar attached to Zunzi's on Drayton Street, with a large outdoor patio, live music programming and a dog-friendly policy, open from 11am to 11pm and later at weekends. Its bar keeps a mocktail list in regular rotation, and the house standard is the Pineapple Express — built on Ritual Zero Proof's non-alcoholic rum alternative with peach purée, pineapple, almond milk, cane sugar and lemon — which staff describe as the most-requested alcohol-free drink in the room. The long daily hours make it one of the easier places in the Historic District to get a considered zero-proof drink at lunchtime.
signatureDrinks: N/A Athletic Brewing Run Wild IPA
Spring in a Bottle N/A Non-Alcoholic N/A Sparkling Rosé

naMenuItems.name: Spring in a Bottle N/A Non-Alcoholic N/A Sparkling Rosé
N/A Athletic Brewing Run Wild IPA

venues.longDescription:
Zunzi's is a Savannah institution — a South African-influenced sandwich counter that grew a following long before the Historic District had a restaurant scene worth the name — and Zunzibar is the full-service bar and dining room that grew out of it on Drayton Street, where the historic grid meets the waterfront. It is a patio operation as much as an indoor one: shareable coastal plates, live music, dogs welcome, and a room that stays busy from lunch onwards.

The bar's alcohol-free drinking centres on one well-known build. The Pineapple Express is made with Ritual Zero Proof's non-alcoholic rum alternative, peach purée, pineapple, almond milk, cane sugar and lemon — a creamy, tropical drink that reads as a piña colada's more interesting relative. Staff have told Savannah Magazine it is the most-requested mocktail in the house, which for a room with this much foot traffic is a meaningful volume signal rather than a menu claim.

The grading here is deliberate. Zunzibar is recorded at three rather than four: the bar clearly makes alcohol-free drinks as a matter of routine and uses a real non-alcoholic spirit to do it, but there is no standing printed zero-proof section the way there is at Husk or Peregrin, and the current menu published on the venue's own site does not itemise the mocktails. The Pineapple Express is well enough sourced to describe; the rest of the list is not, and is not invented here.

What Zunzibar offers that most of this guide does not is timing. It opens at 11am seven days a week and runs to 11pm, or midnight Thursday through Saturday, so it covers the middle of the day when the city's better cocktail bars are still locked. There is also a Hilton Head Island location, which is closed; this listing is the Savannah restaurant only.
venues.pressQuote: Our Pineapple Express is hands down the most popular requested mocktail.
venues.pressQuoteSourceLabel: Savannah Magazine, The Buzz on the Growing Mocktail Trend

venues.name: Zydeco Kitchen & Cocktails
venues.description: Zydeco does elevated Southern-leaning comfort food in downtown Bend with a strong zero-proof lineup alongside its house cocktails, and it pours Crux's NØ MØ non-alcoholic IPA on the beer list — so both routes are covered for a non-drinker at dinner. Open daily from 4:30pm.
venues.longDescription:
Zydeco has been one of downtown Bend's dependable dinner rooms for years, doing elevated comfort food with a Louisiana lean, and Visit Bend's zero-proof guide groups it with Bar RBC and Dear Irene as the trio of elevated dining rooms in town that give alcohol-free drinks real attention.

What makes it useful in practice is that it covers both routes a non-drinker might want. There is a zero-proof lineup alongside the house cocktails, made by the same bar team from the same ingredients. And separately, Crux's NØ MØ non-alcoholic IPA is on the beer menu — which matters more than it sounds, because a restaurant carrying the local brewery's NA beer rather than a national brand is a signal that someone chose it rather than defaulted to it. Between the two you can have a cocktail-shaped drink before the meal and a beer with it, which is the ordinary pattern of an evening out and the thing most restaurants make impossible without alcohol.

The room sits on Bond Street in the middle of downtown, a short walk from Deschutes' public house and Bar RBC, and it is a popular choice for a special occasion — the sort of place people book for anniversaries and celebrations rather than a weeknight.

We have not published drink names here. Zydeco does not publish its cocktail menu online and the zero-proof list moves with the seasons, so anything specific would be a guess. The NØ MØ pour and the existence of the zero-proof section are the durable facts. Kitchen hours are relatively early by bar standards — last orders around half past eight most nights.
venues.pressQuote: rounds out the trio with elevated comfort food and a strong zero-proof lineup
